name: MULLET MADJACK
detailed_description: Your HEALTH is TIME You must KILL to get more TIME A HIGH-OCTANE-ACTION SHOOTER, 90% ARCADE FUN, 10% roguelite. In this future, MAN and INTERNET have merged into a new being. This being needs DOPAMINE every 10 SECONDS, or else it will DIE! • ARCADE FUN! You are MULLET MAD JACK, and you must kill enemies to refill your 10 SECONDS OF LIFE! • Beat handcraft stages at random full of exciting new obstacles at each chapter! • Memorize each room and compete for better times! • Cleverly build your character every FLOOR, in a fully-fledge NARRATIVE with small roguelite elements. • Defeat the mysterious masterminds and experience the ultimate OLD SCHOOL ANIME plot! KEY FEATURES: • Fast Arcade feel full of dopamine rush like the old times • A fully animated campaign with old-school anime cutscenes • 50+ Power ups that change the way you can play the game. • You can play the game forever in random levels on ENDLESS MODE • A CLASSIC MODE with no TIMER if you want a traditional campaign • Unbox a digital/virtual BIG PC GAME BOX from the 90's • 15 trading cards and more than 50 point shop items • Relive the bloodshed from 80's and 90's ACCESSIBILITY: Full controller support, Ultrawide support, key and button rebinding, Mouse sensitivity, Purple blood mode, disable camera shake and flashes, custom AIM options, custom volume controls for sfx, music and voices.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't see a single reason not to try Mullet Mad Jack.  I disagree with those who compare the game to Hotline Miami, for this game is less about hardcore and more about a sense of flow. In general, the concept of boomershooter where you are given 10 seconds to pass the level and the only way to increase the time is to kill enemies is very interesting. Because time limits in games usually annoy us, but Mullet Mad Jack makes it incredibly addictive mechanics, it's extremely hard to get away from the gameThe game runs for about 3 hours and after passing all you can do is start it again on a higher difficulty. And for me that's the only drawback of the game.Unfortunately there are very few similar games, I primarily think of Post Void. And to me, it's one of the best shooters I've played in years, and I'll be looking forward to the new content.

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forward to this game coming out, and it's everything I hoped it would be and more.The game was clearly made with love by developers who appreciate 90's video games and anime. The animation and art style really brings the world to life and game play is frantic and fun. The game does have a loose story in it's campaign mode, and checkpoints are separated out by every 10 floors that you go up. There's an endless mode to jump into for instant insanity, and even a nice little old school PC game unboxing that the game uses to display it's manual, which I think is really cool for someone who enjoys the days of having boxed PC games.All in all, if you like anime, 90's old school boomer-shooter style FPS games, or rouge-likes in general, then this is a no-brainer. The devs delivered one of the best games of 2024 imo and deserve the support.FEAR THE MULLET!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I was a bit hesitant at first when I heard and saw the game and its older demos. 10 seconds to live?  I already hated timers in games before, because in most games they were just put there for arbitrary reasons that don't usually contribute to the game itself except for the fact to speed up the player and create a fake sense of urgency, with very few of them actually integrating the timer into the gameloop. Mullet Madjack on the other hand, stretches those 10 seconds into pure dopamine as the game puts it.And it ain't lying. The guns feel great, destroying your enemies with speed and precision or obliterating them with the melee finishers or weapons feels amazing. There's very few guns and I feel like some overlap, but thats not the point. All guns are good, though I wish the SMG didn't kick like a mule even with the upgrades.The game doesn't have a lot of content, because its not made to take away your days and nights. It knows what it is: an Arcadey corridor shooter, actually I'd compare this game to Time Crisis but instead of having lifes your timer is your life, each time you get shot it goes down. Its quality is shinning in everything, from the amazing artstyle, to the tight gameplay. It also has multiple difficulties, I personally finished it on the Challenging difficulty as it was the one described "As the devs intended", and even though some levels took me a few tries, they were not impossible. Playing in that difficulty also taught me how to play by using every single mechanic: Shooting, Sliding, Kicking and Finishers.That game is not just the campaign, the game is the campaign and its Endless Mode. Which unlike other roguelikes, here the upgrades you pick are also on a timer: They only last 10 floors. Which I can see myself playing from time to time one or two endless runs when I feel like it.Game is well worth its asking price if you like these kind of indie games, which with games like Animal Well and the like we need more of. Genuine passion went into these by a small group of developers and are worth experiencing!

_childDocuments_.review: I started out loving this game. After finishing it, I still like the gameplay loop, but this game feels unfinished. I’d skip this at full price. The good things: Music is fantastic, guns are great (except the pulse rifle, it feels like trash), swords are fine but not my favorite. The loop is really fun to fly through levels and kill robots while dodging obstacles. The anime style starts out really cool.The bad: The levels never get interesting or frankly even challenging. The bosses are TERRIBLE. Seriously, completely awful. Too simple and easy. A couple are interesting, but there are only 7 (if I counted right) and most are dead brained to fight. The story by the end was grating. It becomes really cringey slop that was very disappointing. They created an interesting atmosphere with a good concept and style, and wasted it on horny nerd garbage. The last chapter and cutscene(s) are by far the most off putting part of the game. It’s some socially awkward 18-year-old boy energy. Awful.At the end of this game, I was really unsatisfied. None of the style paid off and the gameplay never matured. Feels like the game is over as soon as it ramps up.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the main story of this, and I loved every bit of it!   While the main game itself isn't that long, it's very action packed!   It's 2D visual anime style really pops out at you in the best way.   The story is you have the rescue the big time influencer princess from the evil robots inside a giant building.   You have to progress through 1 floor at a time and kill robots you encounter as you make your way to the next elevator.  But there is a catch:   You have 10 seconds to live.The main way you get more time to live is by killing the robots.  You can get extra time by killing them in more stylish ways, such as headshotting them, putting a knife through their head, or by kicking them into an electric fan.  Be careful though.   You also LOSE extra time if a robot shoots you too.  When you reach an elevator, you're given the chance to rest and pick a new weapon, or equip a mod that boosts you stats in some ways.   Such as a chance for bullets to ricochet off walls, immunity to acid floors, being able to duel wield weapons for a short time,  and tons more!   But if you die , you lose all of your upgrades and have to start back at the last checkpoint.   There is a certain balance between not being too reckless, and not going too slow either.The good thing I love is this game is very welcoming to players of ALL skill types with tons of difficulties to pick from.   There's the standard difficulty I mentioned, but if you're not as skilled, you can pick an easy mode where you have more time (Or no timer at all if you want)      For those looking for a challenge, you can pick a harder mode where bosses do extra damage and there are less helpful items to find in the levels.   And if you're a real nut, you can play the perma death mode where you have to beat EVERY floor in the game with ONE LIFE.   NO CHECKPOINTS!   But if you can pull it off, you get to be in the worldwide leaderboards!There's some extra stuff you can do and unlock after beating the main game, but I'll leave that for you to discover if you're interested, which you SHOULD be if you love cool FPS.Ready?   Destroy these damn robots!

_childDocuments_.review: Only played 15 mins so far... 10/10. This is hands down one of the best shooter/roguelikes I've played, totally sold on it. It's like Hotline Miami on steroids. Every level has a 10 second timer that increases with every kill and headshot. It's strangely compelling and says so much about modern society and the current state of the internet. 11/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★☆☆☆ (2/5)A running game where you also shoot robots.This is a game with an identity crisis. It advertises itself as a shooter, but it rewards players who reach the end of the level the fastest. As a result, the player is more focused on spotting environmental kills or shortcuts than on blasting away foes. The anime style is really well done, and players who enjoy high scores would love the rating system, but it becomes too repetitive too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so incredibly addictive and if anything, I just wish it had something more to offer than endless mode. What it is, is a fast-pace score based shooter with level randomisation. You end up at the bottom of the building and you are suppose to save the girl who got kidnapped. Twist is, you have only 10 seconds on the timer (more on lower difficulty) and as you kill enemies, you get some additional time - but be careful, getting hit takes the time away. If the timer reaches 0 - you die and return to the previous checkpoint. You get a checkpoint every 10 floors. Completing a floor allows you to pick an upgrade - at the end of a chapter, there is a boss. And that's pretty much it... and yet this game is just so fun to play. An despite what I consider to be a bit high of a price (in PLN at least), the experience was just so intensive with almost no padding anywhere, that I have no problems but to recommend it. It's fantastic... just short!
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best shooter I've played since DUSK (sorry Boltgun, you're still great).Newcomer tips:- Play on Normal first.- The Bulldozer upgrade is useless once you get to floor 71. The enemy it effects does not spawn from that point forward.- I would recommend a Hard playthrough, not just for the achievement. It forces you to learn the game and try new upgrades.Critiques For Devs:- Lasers feel like they do way too much damage. The half-damage upgrade for lasers is basically required.- Endless pits aren't fun. Losing on floor 79 to a pit is the definition of rage.- The sub-machine gun is barely viable on the lower difficulties, impossible to use on the higher difficulties.- The "Talking Protag" upgrade seems bugged to be always on, as Jack will make comments intermittently throughout gameplay normally.Otherwise, this game is really fun, and I enjoyed both the gameplay, music, and art style immensely. The fun extras such as the Oh-My-Goshi speedrun, endless mode, and virtual unboxing really show the passion of the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: A wild, thrilling, adrenaline fueled ride.I had seen a bunch of coverage of this game in its earliest stages and thought "Eh, the aesthetics slap, but I don't know if that whole constantly-refuel-10-seconds-of-life thing is for me"And then I noticed they had a demo. I did the whole thing in one sitting and immediately bought the game.Once you get the flow of it (which it is very gentle at introducing), it is basically dopamine reward fueled machine of swift dancing and rythm, and I am here for it.It's fairly short but very replayable given the high variation in builds and difficulty you can roll for. Tuning a game so that it's challenging, but not so ball busting hard that you go URGH and uninstall it on failure is a delicate balance, and I think they've mostly succeeded here.The aesthetics are on point, beautiful art, banging music. It has a Big PC Box Unboxing Experience option in the main menu that is full of fuzzy warm feelings. The Voice Acting is also absolutely on point for circa 1996 Anime OVA English Dub, it's spot on. Some may find the Streamer lady grating, in which case you can mute her immediately from the same screen where she shows up, but I personally love the touch.Man, what an exciting ride. The story mode is fairly short on normal difficulty, it took me about 2.5 hours to make it to the end in a few sittings and retries, but I don't feel like the game is over and can be shelved yet. I just want to do it again.Basically, give the demo a go, if you have a good time, you're gonna love the full thing.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: I saw neon colors everywhere. A women on a small screen screamed orders at me to buy, attack, or die depending on what the people wanted to see. I shot hundreds of robots and other horrors as I fought my way through endless corridors, searching for my princess. Eyes twitching and muscles spasming, I guzzled down liters of fizzy drinks to feed my endless need to be the perfect consumer. I committed acts of violence and horror live for adoring fans as part of an endless quest for likes.  I confronted the moral quandries and hypocrisy of late stage capitalism, and I grappled with the knowledge that I too am just a cog in this machine and if this society ceased to exist then so would I. So anyways, once I got the dosage on my meds adjusted, I started the game and it was pretty great. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I sure do have the temerity to leave a thumbs down after 15 minutes of play, and I'll leave the comments on (thanks in advance for the awards). Besides the very-fun graphics and Brock Samson vibe (which do a fair amount of work), I found nothing to recommend this game- and if you don't think the first 15 seconds are fun, probably none of subsequent 15 second-fills are going to change your mind. I didn't get it. I like shooters, boomer shooters, and roguelites. This is an arcade game first, which borrows snippets from those genres. It occurs in 15-45-second snapshots of action. They're cool looking, but I don't find them very fun.The game is dead simple- you've got WASD and right/left click - and dash. Sprint, shoot, kick, shoot- and then you died or you accidentally finished the floor (although as far as I can tell, your best bet is to finish the floor ASAP in all cases)The visual expression really is top-notch, but go watch cartoons if that's what you're looking for, because the gameplay is paper-thinWhen you look at a 97% score like this one, that (apparently) falls roughly in a genre-set you like, it feels like a sure thing... but this didn't even seem compelling enough to merit a full hour of play.Not for me, and I'm a little baffled by the over-the-moon reviews. Anyway I've spent more time writing this review than I did playing the game, so time to hang it up.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing review, I want to straight out say that damn this is definitely not worth what it is now, even at its lowest recorded price! It's really hard to recommend this toanybody that isn't already knee deep into playing indie games or loves busting money. Whilst I really do appreciate the unique style and aesthetic, besides that I can't really give it alot of praise. In some cases the visuals in this game is very jarring, especially the 3D animated cutscenes that puts jack in the fore-front. You can distinctly tell, compared to the rest of the scene he is 3D which completely ruins any immersion you have. Even at the game's best selling point it kinda fumbles, which sort of tells you how the rest of it will turn out. I'll chuck dot points cause I'm not bothered writing alot. 1. Generated maps play out mostly the same and often times you see the same tile/set every run with negligible deviations between floors. 2. The game's bosses aren't particularly interesting, and sometimes flat out the easiest part of the game. 3. Guns feel lack-luster or don't particularly stand out. There's more feeling in my imaginary 12 gauge in my mouth than the in-game shotgun. 4. End of floor upgrades were okay, nothing horrid or interesting. Aside from the weapon upgrades or extra time ones they mostly feel negligible.5. Enemy variety is poor. You mostly see the same enemies throughout the game. No visual changes based on the floor either unfortunately. 6. Music is okay. I'm generally open to all sorts of music but this is rather forgettable. The main menu music was kinda neat.7. The game isn't particularly challenging even on the hard modes. A magic monkey was piloting my brain more then I was piloting it. That's how disengaged I was.8. I like the main antagonist's voice I thought he was fun to listen to.9. The meta-narrative about hyper consumerism and 4th wall breaking was a bit cringe sometimes.The overall and lasting impression is faded and fleeting for this one. I thought after playing the demo the game would dramatically improve in a lot of its weaknesses but it didn't. To me, it felt like the demo with a few extra sprinkles on top. Not worth the price, I personally cannot understand the overwhelmingly positive for this one. (08/08/2024)TLDR; Not worth it at all. Just play the demo as you get mostly the same experience there.

I get that it's supposed to be like an arcade game, but it's not that interesting to play because of these things. Also there is a lot of jank where you get stuck on geometry, which absolutely kills any fast paced "arcade" game. If you want something in this kind of vein but with actual depth, play Neon White instead. Also, the developer is an overly sensitive salty manbaby/babyman that acts really hostile to people who offer polite and very valid constructive criticism on the message board. Earth to game developers on Steam! That is part of what the message boards are there for. If you can't handle constructive criticism, then you're in the wrong business friendo. Sorry you think that anyone who points out the glaring issues in the gameloop just "doesn't understand the game". Nah dude, your game gets boring way too quickly, sorry. This is what I originally wrote on the message board, to which the developer said it was pretty much my issue alone (yet, if you look at the other negative reviews, they say very similar things):Okay good game overall so far (I'm only on chapter 8, however I feel like that is far enough to make this assessment), but there are certain things that (in my opinion) hold it back from being great/amazing. These are things which prevent it from being something that I would fully recommend to my friends who are like me and enjoy these kinds of games.1. Lack of variety level to level.I don't mind the format where there are individual chapters with 10 levels each, but I think the level design needs to have a bit more variety chapter to chapter. A lot of the levels/floors feel very much the same in each chapter except for very minor additions like lazers or giant fans.2. More permanent upgrades would be nice. seems like they cap pretty early on, which seemed a little bit strange to me. I know this game isn't a strict rogue-lite/like, but it would be nice to have more permanent upgrades and ones that are a little more interesting. It makes the game feel very small.3. If I exit the game and come back to it later, don't make me do the tutorial for that chapter again. I actually hate that. At least allow players to actually skip it. We've seen it, we don't need to see it again (and again).4. Make the skip buttons actually work. They don't work, at least for me (perhaps someone can shed some light on this). They somehow work for the full cutscenes, but not for the dialogue.5. If there is no boss fight for that specific chapter, don't include perks that impact boss damage for the perk pool for that chapter. If I am trying the game on different difficulties and replaying chapters, I shouldn't have to remember which ones have a boss and which ones don't when like 85% of them do. _childDocuments_.review: Nice game.MULLET MADJACK is not a rhythm game, even the music gives some strong beats. What makes this game stand out from regular FPS is the health bar is measured by time. You are given 10 seconds to live, to refill it you need to kill before time runs out, a good concept similar to 2011's movie In Time.I‘ve beaten the campaign on normal difficulty, the key point is  . Sure time is limited, but don't forget to keep your pace, try to eliminate enemies rather than escape your way through, because every hit will deduct your valuable time. My advice is take this game as a regular FPS, clean the area (or most of the enemies) before moving on to the next, but in a timely manner. 10 seconds is not that short, you can use a timer to have a good feeling if you are unsure, just do not panic. Good luck.At the end I made it to 30+ floors in the prize claiming section, not knowing it is actually an endless run, and eventually rewarded a sneaker as promised. For the story mode, every 10 floors you will face a boss, the boss fight is easy compared to 10 floors of non-stopping killing. This is intense even if each floor is only 30-50 seconds long, but with the ticking clock and groups of enemies, concentration is required to beat a level, especially a gameover punishing player to restart from floor 1. At the end of each floor you can choose 1 out of 3 temp upgrades ranging from new/upgrade weapon to abilities like double jump, special kill (headshot/crotch kill!!!) for extra time, or environment helper, or boss life deduction etc., this adds a taste of raffle. My favorite goes to that tier 3 Uzi which offers unlimited ammo. This is as good as a cheat to largely reduce the difficulty, because loading takes time, and time is everything in this game.The campaign is 3 hours long, kudos to devs for not extending it into a 9 hours gameplay because after 30 floors there's nothing new, the rest are just refine your skill, repeat each level to prepare the final boss fight on the 90th floor. The campaign ended before I tried out every upgrade and got bored. $19.99 can be expensive for a 3-hour game, but the excitement is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what happens when you take a bunch of good stuff and throw it in a blender. The fast, unrelenting, perfectionist inducing, loop of violence and general aesthetic offered by Hotline Miami, a hint of Katana Zero in comedic energy and visual flair, and finally, a WHOLE lot of Post Void. (Later referred to as PV) The time mechanic, frantic gun play, and general structure are clearly heavily inspired by PV. I don't think this is any secret or something they're trying to hide either considering the most useless and bizarre upgrade from that game rears its ugly head here too, IYKYK. Just wanna preface by saying no shade to PV, it's a game I haven't finished and have only borrowed off a buddy for an hour or two but I had far more fun here and need to accentuate why that is. If you gotta choose, I'd grab this one but they're both good in their own right.  The reasons why I like MMJ more are mainly stemming from the inspirations I listed earlier, which i’ll discuss later, but the key piece here is the boot. The boot is the best part of this game.  I have an inkling that the developer's knew this considering sneakers are the primary reward. The dash in PV is pretty brief and doesn't have any invulnerability or damaging properties. This works well considering the level design is far more chaotic and difficult to navigate, enemies are built to slow you down and make the time mechanic more of a fear than an adrenaline booster. (At least from my experience and taking into account the more abstract and eerie art direction) I assumed this game would be the same so I spent half of the first floor just kinda tapping sprint for quick little boosts until I realized how you’re actually supposed to play. Now I need to break the thought here to establish something important. It was mentioned earlier in regards to PV, level design. To my knowledge the game is pretty much entirely randomly generated but no matter what the layout is with quick reactions no sidetracking or stuttering is required. The game rewards cooler, more difficult kills with more time. Headshots, nut shots, Doom Eternal style finishers (Made available by picking up items lying around), and most prominently, environmental kills. The way you’re supposed to dash is long strides gotten by holding the button. When you past the peak of your momentum, dash again. Continue this rhythm to make a mad dash towards the exit, mowing down anything in sight along the way. You can indulge in the boot with two methods: dashing into something or right clicking. Dashing into things automatically booting enemies really lets that rhythm cook. Most of the enemy placement is built to condition you into knowing when to shoot and when to boot. Environmentals nets you time, ammo in the clip, and a sweet, sweet dopamine hit. The coolest moments I’ve had in this game are times where I can look at a layout and not even think about an enemy in front of me. I can walk through a corridor knowing who I can just walk into and boot which just leaves nailing what I actually have to aim at. This type of decision making is only encouraged by a later enemy type that can’t be shot. You have to use a finisher or whip out the boot. The rest of the gameplay is solid. I like all of the weapons outside of the Plasma Rifle and MAC-10. Going through them, the swords are good. The main difference between the two from what I could decipher is that  is pure damage and  was able to freeze enemies. Freeze was good for beefier foes from a distance since all you needed was a nice boot to the head to take’em out after but I still preferred being able to just kill from range without needing to run over and finish the job. Biggest boon of swords is taking out locked doors and their upgrades being really solid. The shotgun gets all the positives of a sword from longer range but more tactful reloading is needed since the animation is pretty damn long. Pistol and Rifle are my favorites, putting them in the same category since I don’t have much of a preference between them. They’re the most satisfying to do well with,  The MAC-10 is the easiest weapon to use, it didn’t feel very satisfying no-braining my way through with it. It’s a good weapon and all and at a visceral level feels better after upgrading but still didn’t jive with what I like about the game. The Plasma Rifle slows you down. The game is about going fast so nah. It’s good and all but it’s just kind of a turn-off. If it was a normal boomer shooter I wouldn’t really have complaints about it at all but honestly I dunno why it’s here. The first time I used the railgun was the final boss. It’s fun, I kinda like it, but again it’s pretty slow. If you wanna get better at using the boot it’s a fun challenge though. There aren’t any specific upgrades or anything I feel inclined to talk about. Most of them are pretty good, some of them are kinda useless and I dunno why they exist, some of them are things I wish were there on default. They almost make me wish this game would get DLC to further flesh out the pool, maybe add a new weapon? Compound bow? Chainsaw? The soundtrack is good, not as good as the inspirations I listed earlier, but they’re all easy on the ear, lo-fi, synth bangers with some slick chip-tune tracks mingled in.  Final note on the soundtrack, just thought it was a neat reference, but the song “JankenPOW” sounded a lot like “” to me. Moving on, the visuals are pretty spectacular. There’s some iffy looking stuff in the later cutscenes and I guess I’m not a big fan of some of the voice acting but I like Jack and that’s all that really matters; considering he’s the only one you can’t mute or skip without turning voice volume off. From a surface level perspective that’s all I can criticize. When it comes to stuff I want to praise? Just look at it. The only thing I really wanna note here as a little extra praise is the subtitles. Assuming this is a neat little reference to older anime translations back in the 90’s some of the text just flat out isn’t what’s being said. Same general message, it’s not like Ghost Stories adlibbing, it’s just a little bit off here and there which was fun to notice. It was consistent enough I felt like it had to be an intended decision rather than a bunch of typos.Hopefully you’re convinced that it’s worth your time. One of the few times I’ve seen a game, thought it was cool, waited for launch day, and it was actually good.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - Amazing 3.5 hours Normal	- The gameplay is a fast paced boomer-shooter similar to 'post-void' with story arcade mode and an endless roguelite mode. 	- Designed to test your skills, with every 10 floors presenting additional enemies and obstacles that require strategic thinking and quick reflexes.	- The controls are highly responsive, making precise movements and actions possible, which is crucial given the game's difficulty.	- Rogue-lite upgrades per every level give a sense of variety, keeping the game fresh.	- The story light yet is captivating, with a mix of humour and drama that keeps you invested in saving 'The influencer princess'.	- Dark undertone of 'consumerism', addiction to dopamine and futuristic dystopia.	- Vibrant saturated graphics, with detailed environments and character designs that bring a retro 90's anime feel.	- UI is intentionally loud and obnoxious which may seem like a negative but only adds to the challenge, feeling and style of the game.	- If you're money conscious and looking to play just for story\completion?  It's 3.5 hour story and very light. It's not worth purchase until half price sale.	- If you like the gameplay loop of a boomer shooter and want to do endless runs and focus on getting better with the escalating difficulty? I'd say it's definitely worth it.	- The Difficulty options are honest and explain well which difficulty is right for you to start with. 	- Story mode is very forgiving on Normal mode and has Checkpoints every 10 floors (floor takes approximately a minute).	- The game is hard, so be ready for a tough but rewarding experience.	- The game is meant to be played multiple times in escalating difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: It was late at night, I had just finished my 4000th playthrough of Mullet Mad Jack, my favorite game of all time. I decided that I was going to attempt to beat my endless record of floor 300, getting my life soda (Actually monster...XD) and readying myself for a long night of playing with zero sleep. As I begin my playthrough, beating levels in under 30 seconds as usual, I start to hear strange noises coming from somewhere outside my house, thought I ignore it. Nothing can stop me from playing Mullet Mad Jack, I have to pay attention to every single item, every single enemy, and keep on top of the game. Floor 20, the noise becomes louder, as if it's gotten into my own home. Though like before, I can't investigate, I have to focus. Floor 30, as I finish mopping up the enemies, I hear my own door slowly creak open. Was it my mother telling me the game volume was too loud? Was it my father coming back with the milk and cigarettes? I look back to see the man himself, Mullet Madjack."Mullet Madjack?", I said in shock, my mouth drooling, "What are you doing here?"He took a step forward, "I noticed your appreciation for my skills, and I just wanted to come in and give you some of my heart because of that."Hearting...my posts? I couldn't believe it. "Oh-thank you so much, I'm so glad-""Not yet, and I didn't meant that kind either." He said, taking off his belt. "On the bed, I can lay down the 'rules' for you."Oh my god, was he being serious? I felt my heart start to beat like his during gameplay, my face slowly warm to the color of a bloodied screen, and with joy I nod. I crawl to my bed as he follows after, us both hopping on."I won't lie, you have grown a beautiful mullet, but it isn't what I'm interested in, bucko." He said chuckling, now stripping down my pants. I anticipated his banhammer, grabbing onto my sheets tightly. Suddenly, I feel my mullet grabbed and my head pulled back, the icon now thrusting deep inside of me. With each thrust I moan only louder and louder, losing my grip and letting him control me to my will. As he's about to climax, I hear him scream,"THIS IS HOW WE KEEP THE FORUMS CLEAN!"My insides are filled with his matrix juice, and my mullet is finally let go, my body going slump against the bed. He hops off the bed, walking to the door."I would love to show my fan some appreciation, but I gotta shadowban myself before I get any views from your mother."He runs off, leaving me filled to the brim with shock mixed with happiness, as well with my mother screaming in horror at what happened to me.On a serious note, what the ♥♥♥♥ is with this trend of locking difficulty achievements so that when you complete a higher difficulty, you don't get awarded the difficulty achievements below it? I shouldn't have to play each individual lower difficulty when I should of just gotten it from playing on the hardest one. That ♥♥♥♥♥ boring, just give them all to me instead of making me go through each.It's a good game though.

_childDocuments_.review: I went through the entire game, got all of the achievements for it. If you like the 90s, going fast, dopamine, cool shoes, Gianni or just kicking serious ass? This is the game for you.Pros:- Cool anime-style visuals (both with the gameplay, and anime-ted scenes!)- Fun weapons (level 3 shotgun is a hard carry if you ever get it)- Good enemy variety to shake things up- Upgrades that allow you to play how YOU want- Semi-random floor generation- Near Infinite Replayability- AMAZING soundtrack- Both steam achievements and secret ingame awards for pushing yourself through challenges- Cool one liners and words of wisdom, all spoken by Jack himself.Cons:- When you play as much as I have, you begin to hear the same 6 combat tracks over and over. This is not an issue with base game but instead one if you choose to replay over and over.- The 'streamer' girl can be muted so you don't hear the between floor chatter, but story crucial lines cannot be muted. Guess you can only hide for so long :/- The 'Mr. Brain' (I think that's his name) character ended up being more annoying than fun. He has some good scenes but I feel like he was too on the side for me to properly get invested in him. Perhaps that's just a me thing though.- If you restart a chapter you're forced to do the brief introduction sequence. I wish there was a way to skip this and get straight into the carnage.Aside from the mentioned cons, this game is a must play if you enjoy any kind of action shoot-em-ups like hotline miami or superhot. The fast paced slaughter-fest that is Mullet Mad Jack is guaranteed to make you feel like a 90s badass hero.

_childDocuments_.review: It would genuinely be hard to write this game a bad review.  At it's core it's a very, very simple premise: run through the level, murder everything, get to the end.  Hotline Miami immediately springs to mind in both the speed of the gameplay and at least some of the plot.  That's really it.  It's all super well done, looks great, sounds great, and plays great.  There's just no fat on the bones here to get worked up about: the game is easy to play, easy to spend a few hours with, and just as easy to put down.For anyone who might look at it and worry it's perhaps a bit too hardcore, the basic challenge is pretty easy, I blew through the normal difficulty with only a small hiccup during Chapter 7 where I kept falling into pits.  It wasn't really the fault of the game, I just kept doing it.  Kicking it up a notch to the developer-intended pain it did spin back around and immediately kick my teeth in so yeah, if you want a soul-crushing challenge you can find it here, but if you just want some light skill-based shooting in a fast-paced package, the game obliges there as well.As I said at the top, it's hard to write anything but a good review for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a seizure/10I played the Demo and had a lot of fun with it.The gameplay is pretty simply in and of itself. Move forward (with branching paths and shortcuts etc) and kill stuff to refill your life.What had me like the demo so much was the overall quality in presentation.When the game launched, i was at first put off a bit from the quite steep price compared to, for example, Post Void, a game i also enjoyed enough to play through.But then i thought that i liked the demo enough to anticipate the release, looking forward to play more and deeper into the content, so i still gave it a shot.After only 5 minutes i felt the price was worth it.The quality in all areas is top notch. It oozes details and style. But its not just glamour and bling covering up hollow gameplay.It really lives everything it does. It comes with Anime Cutscenes, Synth Pop/Electronic Music and fun, detailed and interesting visual presentation.It doesnt bombard you with pointless effects and lighting to trick you believing its an active game, it places all the effects and details in a way they make sense being there.This is also true for the gameplay.The game offers about 8 or so difficulties, including a permadeath mode, something i wish more games would have (looking at you Amid Evil), as it motivates me to replay once im beyond normal mode (im a pleb).Even if i never manage to beat it.The gameplay itself is deep. You "climb" 10 stages of killing robot dudes. After each stage you get to choose an upgrade, which is a new weapon or an upgrade, adding more time, allowing better combos to gain more time, or more ammo in your magazine etc.The clue here is, which is why i think its great, you can specialize or go broad.I started with a 25% larger magazine and went up to 75% during my first run.But i could also have added other stuff for better combos.Theres also style upgrades, like an upgrade that your protagonist does oneliners.Ending a run, allows you to pick one permanent upgrade (like keeping the last stage upgrade for the next run or adding lvl2 weapons).So theres enough depth and replayability from that alone.The gunplay also is varied, having melee, dash, kick, environmental damage and headshotting.The game features several chapters.I can fully recommend it, at this price, its incredible.It convinced me after just 10 minutes that this is worth the price.Its not just Post Void, its a far more expansive Post Void with 500% increased production value, style and quality.Its a bit less of a drug experience asking you what you do with your lifetime and a bit more content rich.Still questioning my life choices, but with more stable mentality.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: Super fluid and satisfying gameplay, amazing interesting graphics, great music and sounds. The game feels like Doom, Hotline Miami, and maybe Superhot but takes only the best and cuts the fluff creating an extremely streamlined gameplay loop that is one of my favorite movement shooters ever. The story is very on the nose and comical but is still well written in spite of how little dialogue there is.This is a must buy for anyone that likes stylish, fast paced movement shooters and great music!!
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: Ooooh yes, this is a great Game!I will keep it quite short here.Mullet Mad Jack is basically Post Void but better. And no, I don't want to hate on Post Void. The idea was great but to be honest, Post Void was a pretty unforgiving Game.So let me explain... Post Void is basically an Ego Shooter where you have a VERY limited time to get through a level. Time goes down if you do nothing or get hit, time goes up if you kill enemies. So it is a VERY fast moving Game. You have to run, shoot, HIT and make it to the next level and if you finish one level, you can choose one of three upgrades.Also it has a very distinct psychedelic look that is quite awesome (U-Comic Style) but in motion it can be very tiring on your eyes.And it is unforgiving as heck.Don't worry, this is not a Post Void Review but I just wanted to mention it because Mullet Mad Jack improves on almost everything that Post Void did. (But Post Void was there first :) )So, Mullet Mad Jack is basically the same but better. Same principle, you have 10 seconds, this is your life. You get hit, seconds get taken away. You shoot/hit/kick/combo enemies, seconds get added.There is enough variety that it doesn't get stale. You have your "typical" Arsenal of Weapons: Pistol (which I played 90% of the Game), Shotgun, Submachine Gun, Assault Rifle, Plasma Rifle, Railgun.All of those feel great to use except for the Submachine Gun which has a little too much recoil.Inside the Levels - which here are floors of a skyscraper (Nakamura Plaza) - you can also find one hit melee Weapons that are a one time use after pick up and they refill your time completely.And there are environmental hazards where you can kick your enemies into or make them explode another way.I don't want to spoil all the mechanics here, actually it is quite simple.So my first experience in my first 20 minutes was: "Oh man, this is as unforgiving as Post Void, I am probably getting frustrated, also I feel too old and my reflexes are not what they used to be."If you have a similar experience, I urge you to press on. Shortly after the Game klicked.It was not about the speed and precision (as the Game even tells you) but more of a flow state that you have to get into. And when you are into that zone, you really flow and it really klicks.Yes, you will die, it's part of the fun. But right after you die, you will want to get back into it."Just one more attempt."By the way, this Game is also basically a roguelike with a handful of roguelite elements.Without spoiling, there are 3 Upgrades, that you can upgrade 2 times each, which stay forever after unlocking them. This is the roguelite element. The Roguelike Element is, that after every floor you get to choose one of 3 upgrades (which you can later re-roll) and those upgrades are lost when you die.Also: This Game has Episodes and Checkpoints, this takes away a lot of frustration. Basically every Episode has 10 Floors and usually a Boss at the end. After each Boss, you get a checkpoint and your Game is saved. If you - for example - die in floor 6, you will get thrown back to the start of the Episode, so the first floor.This Game references the 90s many times, but the vibe is more of an 80s vibe here. The artstyle is very crisp (as you can see from the pictures or videos) and somewhat Anime influenced, don't want to say too much about that, but it looks really cool.Music is also very fitting and does the job well of pumping you up throughout the Floors. Not much variety though but also it doesn't really need it.You can play it in bite sized chunks or just try and push through. Both works fine.Also, of course the Game isn't very demanding so it will run well probably also on older machines. I finished my first playthrough on Challenging in about 5 hours, got 37 of 48 Achievements in that short time. Usually in some Games, I have no interest in revisiting those Games, but Mullet Mad Jack stays on my hard drive.I want to dabble a bit more in the endless mode, also now that I have a grasp on the Game I want to beat it on hard mode as well. So as of writing this review, it's been around 5 hours of pure fun and it will likely be even more.At this Point you probably could've guessed, this is a total recommend from me. I also encourage you to get Post Void as well, so that you can see where this Game stems from. You can get it pretty cheap, way under 5 Bucks on Steam.Btw., I asked the Dev if I could by any chance contribute to this amazing Game (translation wise), so IF that is going to happen and I can do it, I will also edit this review here with a little note, because I don't want anyone to think the positive review is because of that.So yeah, get your Mullet on and violently shoot some robots...Addendum: Right after finishing the review, I jumped straight back in (even missed my Bus) and played Endless Mode until Floor 31. Just wanted to say, this is really addicting and also soooo satisfying with the Headshots (you get a little ping sound, I live for that).Okay, I'm out...

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing art and presentation can't hide that the gameplay loop gets stale quite fast, as you're rushing through the same randomly connected map modules, with the same object and enemy placement. Having the roguelite aspect (select 1 of each 3 random power ups after each floor) allow for deep/amazing/rewarding synergies would be a great way to solve the repetition, but unfortunately that's not the case in Mullet Madjack.Although one of the devs has stated the game is not a roguelite/-like, one of the main features of the game, as being advertised on the page is:  The power-ups are presented in typical roguelite fashion: 3 random 'cards', of which you can select one, yet there are no actual 'clever builds' to make. Being able to create awesome synergies through power-ups would actually make the repetitious gameplay loop a lot more fun & interesting.So, if the game actually distances itself from the roguelite aspect, what's left? A fast paced FPS that feels a bit like a light-gun game, that get's repetitive fast, because it doesn't have the aspects of what makes a boomer shooter good, like Dusk and HROT for example.All in all, and considering the price I can' t recommend. The game just doesn't offer enough currently to keep it fresh, fun and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary: 10/10It's basically a shooter like Duke Nukem but with a bit of a twist and set in a dystopian future with an old school anime vibe.  The story is short overall, but the gameplay is fast and satisfying, with a variety of weapons, power ups, and game modes to try out, all accompanied by a sweet soundtrack.  Absolute blast.  Highly recommended! The Full Review:It's the future, and the internet and AI have evolved to a point that robots have essentially taken over the economy, with powerful Robo-Billionaires owning much of the wealth.  Humans are subject to streams of content and advertising, with the most successful humans being massive live-streamers.  Or, in your case, a MODERATOR.Moderators are tasked with taking down key Robo-Billionaires, and in your case, rescuing the woman known as the "Influencer Princess," who has been kidnapped by one of the most powerful of the Robo-Billionaires. Working through an app/company known as PEACE CORP., you're supplied with weapons and power-ups to complete your mission, but there's a big catch: you only have ten seconds of life. In order to extend the timer, you have to keep your live stream audience entertained; their Likes pump dopamine into your veins, which apparently humans in this future need a constant supply of in order to live. Therefore, you have to kick, shoot, and otherwise dismantle the robots standing in your way, swiftly and with style.The gameplay is very fast-paced, and perhaps too much for those not accustomed to first-person-shooters.  There are A LOT of colors, special effects, and other visual noise flying by as you navigate the hallways filled with robots.  Fortunately, the developers have included a wide range of difficulty settings, including an option that makes the game play more like the original DOOM or Duke Nukem games.  So even if the intended way to play isn't your style, you may still find the game enjoyable on one of those other difficulty options. Regardless of if you play the game in "Boomer Shooter" mode or go all out on Hard mode, I personally recommend that you do give Mullet Mad Jack a try because this game has style.  The soundtrack is a banger and the visuals really makes the game stand out. And while the story is short, I did find it very intriguing, particularly because it feels like it's trying to make a comment on we as humans are so hungry for stimulation and content here in the internet era.  Nowadays we're bombarded with so much media and developing AI to further increasing levels of sophistication, that Mullet Mad Jack almost feels like a satirical take what the future could be.  In any case, the game is hella fun to play.  I love the music, I love the style, and the juxtaposition of the futuristic setting and the old-school anime art direction is just really cool, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game held back by a few issues.  To start, this is one of the most engaging audio/visual experiences I have EVER experienced.  Truly, it is remarkable.  The mastery of the 80's anime artstyle is so satisfying.  From the UI to the animations to the menus and even the interactive in-game manual (!!) it is a huge treat.The core game loop is also masterful.  It really is a pure concentrated shot of dopamine and the game is very self-aware of it.  So what's the problem?  Well, have you ever played a game that gave an amazing first impression, but the more you played it and examined it, the more you began to see its flaws?  Unfortunately that is this game to me, so I'll try to go beneath the surface and explain some of the issues I had with it.-Identity crisis-This game is listed as 90% arcade, 10% roguelite.  I'd say yes that is true on first impression, but the more you play, the more you begin to see how the game never fully commits to being either.  The core gameplay loop does feel like 90% arcade (the roguelite perks don't last indefinitely and are minor), but the problem comes more in the level design and progression.  Ironically, in some ways the level design is LESS arcadey than many roguelites.  Most roguelites have you play a collection of biomes and in each biome is a randomized set of procedurally generated arenas/rooms.  This game does not really even do that, but instead, almost every single room in the game can occur at ANY part of the run, and will be repeated over and over at any point, like shuffling through a deck of cards.  Every 10 floors, the game introduces a new hazard such as lava floors or lasers, and sometimes some unique room layouts, but the reality is you will be shuffling through the same rooms during the ENTIRE run, albeit with a few new hazards.  So not only does it not have a level progression of arcade games (a stream of novel content from beginning to end but the same game every time you play), but does not even have as strong a sense of biome progression as in roguelites.  This not only moves the game more away from the feel of an arcade game, but leads to an overall diminished sense of progression during the run.  This issue unfortunately also is exacerbated by other issues.-Pacing-Despite this game being about a flow of constant forward progression, the actual pace of the game feels tedious.  Each floor lasts about 15-60 seconds and there is an incredibly dense amount of player actions that occur in that brief time.  After every floor, the game goes through the standard congratulations, the female character gives you some quips, and you choose your perk for the next floor.  It kind of feels like doing high intensity lifts in the gym for 30 seconds but then pausing for 10 seconds after each set.  For a game being about the "flow state", this creates a less than desirable flow from floor to floor.  This is also made worse by the overall pacing of the campaign.  After 10 floors, you fight a boss then move onto the next chapter, where the game does a "tutorial floor" to introduce the new hazard/enemy type.  At first this setup seems fine, but because each of the 10 floors plays out exactly the same (due to randomly shuffling rooms that occur repeatedly at every part of the run), those 10 floors end up feeling more like a slog and much longer than they actually are, especially due to the constant breaks in between each floor.  By the end of campaign, it really starts to feel like you have been running the same 20 second core game loop over and over for several hours, albeit with a few new hazards.  It feels like the game could've benefited more from a genuine arcade progression by trimming the campaign down in length and also having more of a true level progression system where most if not all the rooms are locked to specific chapters.  I don't think the campaign warrants being 3-4 hours and 100 total floors considering the lack of true level progression, and unfortunately does not make the game an effective arcade game (which typically is cleared within 25-45 ish minutes).  There is also I think a pacing issue with the "side missions" that occur.  Around 3 or 4 times during the campaign, the game breaks into a kind of playable cutscene or a new gameplay type segment, such as a sniper section or car section.  Some of these sections don't have gameplay and consist of walking through an empty house.  While beautiful and memorable, they will inevitably slow the game down for future runs and further move the game away from a pure arcade game.  Inversely, the unique gameplay segments (like the sniper section) do not stay long enough in order to effectively break up the monotony of the core game loop.  I think the campaign could've been shortened, transitions sped up, and these additional gameplay type bits could've been lengthened and expanded on to better break up the monotony.-Difficulty systems/balance-My major issue is that the game in my opinion does not open up in higher settings as the dev claims, but instead the opposite. With most great games, in higher difficulties the strategy and gameplay systems blossom into its full beauty, but in this game, it confines the player more.  For example, in higher settings you literally HAVE to headshot enemies or kick them into environmental hazards to refill your constantly draining time/life meter, because normal kills won't fill it up.  This is a problem, because this new genre of "booter shooters" is about getting into that flow state, albeit through a very "one-track" way of thinking.  Flow state gaming is very satisfying of course, but when it is such a one-track-think dopamine rush, it can quickly devolve into fatigue and monotony.  In other flow state games, you may notice that the most satisfying flow states occur at both a physical and mental level, where you are able to establish that exhilarating synergy between complex strategic decision making and physically executing the strategy with clinical precision.  The flow state in this game in higher difficulties confines the game more into just a blistering pace of rapid, near perfect accuracy of headshots while dashing through tight corridors and rooms that often line you up for the shot as soon as you open the door.  There's nothing inherently wrong with that, but it would have been nice for the higher difficulty settings to open the game up more into both a physical AND mental flow state.  The game just doesn't really have much of any sense of strategic decision making, it is more about being able to recognize what enemy type and room you are dealing with as instantaneously as possible and then muscle memory takes care of the rest.I could go on more, but I think I have started to scratch at some of the ways I think the game will not hold up as well as I'd desire for long term commitment.  I definitely believe the game will be very successful, because I think a lot of what is here is nothing short of genius.  This game I think does deserve and will achieve its high status as a beloved title.  Its swagger, aesthetic, instant gratification, and core game loop are undeniable.  For me, it just happened to be one of those games that doesn't quite hold up as well on further examination.  To summarize, the three major issues for me lie in it neither fully committing to being a great arcade game nor roguelite, its numerous pacing issues, and difficulty systems that confine an already one-track mind game into a corridor racer head shooter game.  I will likely still try and clear harder difficulties, but I think the brilliance of the dopamine kick did start to desensitize too quickly, turning some of that fun factor into a tedious dopamine "ritual".  And the game does break the 4th wall by explicitly depicting video games as functioning as a kind of masturbatory dopamine kick to "consoom" and fill our boredom of our meaningless lives.  I just do not agree that the best games devolve into such.

_childDocuments_.review: The 1990s were a halcyon age of video games.When you bought a game back then, you were getting the complete experience. You weren't tricked into spending stupid amounts with free admission, you weren't convinced that endless grinding for garbage was acceptable under the auspice of it "getting better" as you unlock further garbage, and there wasn't a widespread internet for you to further your stupidity with dumb ideas delivered by loudmouthed hacks convincing you that these predatory tactics are ok.Back then, games needed to be bad ass. Even the games for kids, like Mario and Sonic. In Mario, you're going into another world to shoot fireballs at dinosaurs. In Sonic, you were fighting an army of robots using living creatures as batteries. The exception was Bubsy, those games were anus.But, Mullet MadJack is not anus. Mullet MadJack is awesome. Mullet MadJack will kick you in the teeth for underestimating it. And you'll love it. The premise is simple: You have 10 seconds to finish a level. You can kill robots to get seconds back, you can get pick ups that add more time, as well, but you still need to be moving and killing and putting all these robots into their place. At the end of an area, you fight a billionaire and kill them. These billionaires have enslaved humanity through the use of social media and they need to die. So, remember that the next time you say you get your news from social media; it just means you're a moron that is a slave to robot billionaires. You should have figured that out, though, since most people disseminating news on the internet are just losers, like you, screaming at their phones and acting outraged over dumb stuff that doesn't matter.Mullet MadJack is not dumb stuff, it's awesome stuff. At the end of each level, you pick an upgrade that has effects like slowing time, turning soda cans into grenades, giving more time back for kills, and even giving you a new weapon. Joy is rinsing out hallways of robots with a shotgun using the ricochet and penetrating chance power ups.To be clear, this is NOT a boomer shooter. This is something fairly unique. It's an arcade game crossed with a shooter that has extreme emphasis on movement. It's all tweaked together to perfection and feels outstanding to do just that. Move fast, dash through the air, gun down enemies, stab them, chug down soda, and keep on doing it. Kick them into giant fans, into neon lights, through doors, become the action movie hero you wish you were.That's really what Mullet MadJack feels like; an action movie you get to play. It's Die Hard after a case of Jolt cola. It's Terminator 2 if the T-800 was given a jetpack. It's the Matrix without the insufferable fans who just discovered its core themes are similar to Plato's Allegory of the Cave.Visually? Gorgeous.Action? Perfect.Soundtrack? Flawless. In fact, that's what DLC should be. Let me buy soundtracks.So, basically, if you don't get Mullet MadJack? You're just wrong. You've made a mistake. You're bad. Know how bad? This game is, basically, a Discord moderator's fantasy come true and you can't even handle that. Exactly. That's how bad you are. I don't care how good you are at souls-likes, anyone can read broadcasted attacks. I don't care what you have in whatever skinner box multiplayer vehicle game you play, those are bad and you should feel bad.Mullet MadJack separates the plebes from the patricians.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: BE ADVISED: This one is SHORT. There's an endless mode, but there's only so much the game throws at you before it starts to feel very limited. I had all of the achievements in under 10 hours.I crushed the game on the recommended difficulty in just under 4 hours, and I'm not the best at shooters. If you're not sure if a rouge-lite shooter is something for you, I would probably point you towards something like Roboquest first, which has a little more game for the price tag in addition to offering a little more in the variety available in your run builds. That being said, it was still a really good time and I'm honestly very excited to see what the devs might do with this kind of style in the future. It looks great and plays well, and while the gameplay premise of playing off of a timer isn't entirely original, it's still a lot of fun here. Sometimes the linearity of the levels is a little much and it feels like you can run through it, and the bosses aren't the best, but for 20 bones it wasn't a bad time.For the price, I'd give it a high 3 or low 4 out of 5 for at least hooking me for a while and nailing the presentation. A great first outing for the studio. Would love to see a deeper experience with this aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal, I am filled with utter joy to see something so neat executed in such a clean way.I'm a huge fan of this type of arcade "try to get as high a score as you can" type of shooter and very few games have scratched that itch for me.Devil Daggers, and Hyper Demon are the only two that come to mind, and while those are great, this is for sure different than those, there's a lot more appeal here for people who aren't coming just to beat their own time.The campaign is lovely, it's a bit short, but only because I wish there was more, it's got a delightfully silly story with a wonderful aesthetic, and it's a great way to teach you if you are looking for that arcade repetition while also having it's own unique content separate from endless.The gameplay itself is fast and simple though with a lot of room for creativity, with plenty of simple environmental methods of killing enemies, and room layouts you'll probably start to remember your own methods for.It's fast, really fast, and that simplicity also helps it escape being difficult to understand in all the chaos.Art is fun, character designs are a highlight for me, really love Mr. Bullets design in particular!Music is really good, although tragically you won't be hearing many tracks play out as you finish most floors in 20 seconds, but it serves the game well for this, I just wanna hear it more.I also wanna touch on how it's updated, because there's something really cool here I don't see often.There have been some changes already that fundamentally change the ease of which one gets a high score, and very often I see this avoided due to it often nullifying high scores. HOWEVER, these changes fundamentally made the game more enjoyable.Most of my complaints with the gameplay on release were changed shortly after and are no longer gripes I have.I for sure recommend it, it's one of the best things to come out this year and it has a lot to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRDoes the game look great? Absolutely.It presents the 90's Old-taku, ultra-violence theme perfectly. The game is fittingly ridiculous in every way. Nothing about the presentation is bad. But this game needed purposefully designed levels and not procedurally generated ones.It's one of those games that works great on paper but I think the biggest problem with it is that it is a rogue-like and as you progress through the game it's mostly the same rooms (a few different rooms are added) and they just add different enemies or traps to those existing rooms.When you have a game that requires as much twitch decision making as this, then I just don't think procedurally generated levels are the best platform for this combat design. You often find rooms being repeated over and over during the same level, some of the rooms really needed more testing, the wallrunning rooms get you killed all the time because you just jump over the walls, or accidentally slide off the map because you were trying to melee something.My biggest reasoning, however, for why I think this needed to be purposefully designed levels is how the sequencing of rooms can hand you a win or get you killed. Sometimes the rooms come together perfectly and your just running forward and shooting whatever you see (possibly how the game is supposed to feel) other times you end up with so many tight turns , corridors and enemies in blind spots that you aren't even sure what killed you. Some of the things they start to add to the rooms also feels like it doesn't really work for this game. The biggest things being the laser mines. You're character does not control precisely, he doesn't need to normally, but the laser mines require precise movement, except when they end up around corners or in blind spots, then you just walk into them by accident.The upgrades also feel wonky, with the biggest problem being the weapons. The railgun is too slow for this game, the plasma gun pushes you back when it fires, making you too slow for this game and I still don't know what's wrong with the katanas but they just don't feel right. You have to charge up the swing for them but that feels very out of place in this game, and half the time it doesn't even kill the enemy and you don't know if that's because you missed or because it didn't do enough damage.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MAD JACK is a dizzingly fast-paced, stylish FPS, that, in an age where Retrowave games are not exactly hard to come by anymore, stands out for its adherence to a twisted themepark version of 1980s Anime. It's more Hotline Miami then Doom, easy to pick up, but definitely difficult to master.In the 2090s, humankind and the internet have merged into the flawed "♥♥♥♥ Media", and now literally cannot survive for more then ten seconds without constant dopamine flow. You are Jack, a man with a weakness for lollipops, an itchy trigger finger and a hairstyle that no one before him save perhaps Solid Snake has been able to pull off. Jack is a "Moderator", who's job it is to destroy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robot billionaires quickly and violently, with your antics streamed live for all to see. Their likes are injected directly into your bloodstream, keeping you alive for a few seconds longer with every kill. Your goal is to rescue the "Influencer Princess", a cute green-haired gal with billions of followers and a strong resemblance to Yui Takanaka of the 80s OVA Megazone Two-Three. She is held captive in the familiarly named Nagatomi Plaza by the bombastic Mr. Bullet, voiced of course by Gianni Matragrano hamming it up as usual.First and foremost, MMJ is FAST. Stages can take less then a minute and the entire campaign took me maybe three hours, accounting for many restarts in the markedly more difficult second half. As previously mentioned, you typically have at most 10 seconds to live (a certain roguelike perk can extend this by 1 second, while in the Endless mode you get LESS maximum seconds every ten floors) Getting damaged tends to take off a few seconds. Kills tend to restore 1 second, while more creative kills- headshots, environmental kills, and even robo-nutshots give more. Drinking Soda restores the full 10 seconds, as does using a finisher kill using items picked up from the environment- knives, pipe wrenches, crowbars, even a copy of (Insert Favorite Manga Here). You start with a fast-firing revolver, and can obtain other weapons between stages, along with a selection of roguelike-style perks. Completing a floor gives you a selection of three perks, and every ten floors you face a boss- the timer is disabled on the boss floors, instead giving you a traditional finite health percentage. After defeating a boss you get a checkpoint, and death will only send you back to the last checkpoint, though you will lose all your perks.SPOILERS FOR PLOT BELOW.Gameplay wise, MMJ excellent. But it has a lot of tonal whiplash and in the end I'm not sure what I'm meant to take away as a message, if it was trying to have one, and it may not have been. A cinematic and intense final boss encounter and genuinely cute ending segues directly into your first endless run and after that is an incredibly bleak Reason-You-Suck speech by the tutorial gal/handler/girlboss character that was honestly rather disheartening. As much fun as I had with MMJ, I don't know at the time of this writing if I would play it again, and this is a game where one of your start-of-level barks is "Let's kill some billionaires!"... but then has a "No billionaires were harmed in the making of this game" message in the credits. Well, why the ♥♥♥♥ not?If that doesn't sound like it would bother you that much, know that MULLET MAD JACK is an incredibly tight, fun and brisk experience and worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't see the appeal. Every room plays the exact same, its your average shooter with a 10-second time limit. The style is nice, its very fast-paced, but the variety in upgrades and rooms just killed it for me. I'll probably still finish the game, but its just... very repetitive for what it is. When you find a roguelike/lite you are usually looking for replayability, and good variety of upgrades. This has neither.Also, the game will constantly remind you that you are 1 difficulty higher than standard. It feels like the game is mocking me for dying on the higher difficulty. Every 2 deaths my screen will show this little "Hey btw you are on hard mode you can turn that down". It was fine the first time, but when you say NO to something 5-10 times in a row it gets annoying, almost downright patronizing.Can we have an option to turn off these useless upgrades like "the protag will say some one-liners" because it was funny the first time, but seeing that "upgrade" just makes me take a deep sigh in realizing that I just wasted an upgrade option for nothing. "Mark where the end level door is" really? in the game where you have essentially a single direction to go? "Slide faster on ramps" might be cool but its useless for bosses.Weapon balance is all over the place. Pick up the railgun/uzi/pistol to insta-lose.I really hope that there is more in store for the game, because the core gameplay loop is good. But other than that, you probably won't be playing this game for more than 5-10 hours.Edit: it just gets worse. I went down to "Normal" because I was sick of the constant difficulty reminder, and now its telling me EVERY SINGLE DEATH to switch to a different difficulty. I've unlocked a few upgrades that ruin the visual clarity of the game (add them to the useless list). I don't understand why the developers felt the need to make a main boss turn-based? In this game??? It really broke the pacing for me, and the post-rpg moment was lackluster at best.I've just realized there is no way to turn off the environment-based tips that show up EVERY time you come across an object in the environment. They take up a good 1/4 of the top of the screen, and tell me information I already know. This doesn't change at higher difficulties, why?Do the devs never want you to die in this game? Are you just meant to speedrun through the story spamming leftclick, rightclick, repeat? I don't understand the patronizing. Every second of this game just wants you to beat it without any issue, no learning, just go down to the lower difficulty! It really makes me angry every single time I die. Roguelikes should feel fair and rewarding when you die. It might be fair, but every time I die, I'm being told "skill issue". Its a really simple fix and its a real wonder why it isn't like this before: only show the notification after a streak of deaths. If the player closes the notification, DONT SHOW IT AGAIN.rocket science.Aside from that, there's typos, unfinished upgrade text ("after killing an enemy, boost damage for seconds". How many?), FPS issues at later stages, and visual clarity is a joke. Honestly I can't understand the hype at all.Edit 2: I finally finished the game, and boy, I wish I hadn't. Turns out  Yeah. It's really bad. Why not just have the ending be a link to your Deviantart profile? Doesn't help that the main lady you are trying to save is voiced by the EXACT SAME voice actor as the Peace Corp lady. Also... Rock, paper, scissors. REALLY? I want whatever the devs were smoking when they thought this section was a good idea.This is by far one of the most overrated games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in-f*ckin-tense! And absolutely worth the $20, in fact I wish I got it prior to the Steam Summer Sale because buying it on sale feels like stealing it...Combat flow is the name of the game here, and goodness gracious does it flow. When you learn the controls and get yourself into a rhythm it's incredibly easy to lose yourself for hours with this game and the level and enemy designs help keep you alert. There's plenty of playstyles for different people here as well, despite the 10 seconds you can be slow and methodical as you clear out rooms, but blasting your way to the end as fast as possible is also viable and actually heavily encouraged. Different weapons will compliment your playstyle in ways you might not even think of. For example I went through majority of the campaign blind firing into enemies with the SMG which was hella fun, then when I unlocked endless mode I ended up picking up the more precision based Rifle, which then led to practice lining up head and nut shots which led to faster and more efficient times. You'll constantly pick up new ways to play and extreme levels of dopamine when you get just a little better.The aesthetic is also amazing, the unabashed throwback to 80's style anime and over-the-top gore that surrounded it in that era is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and the animations compliment it well. There's some questionable CGI at parts that honestly isn't even a negative since it feels like it's a callback to said anime. The one-liners that Jack says sometimes never fail to get a chuckle out of me and frankly The Streamer, aka the Shop Gal, never once got on my nerves as she kinda melds in with the rest of the game and accents it well. The cyberpunk-esque theme is also amazing, and the HUD really shines with the older 80's style take on cyberpunk and the more freaky styled body alterations (for example, the cell phone that has a blood tube connected to Jack's arm.) The music also lands right at home with the rest of the aesthetic, and while it wasn't a large focus for me, due to being enamored by the combat, it still adds to the experience and wraps it up in a gorgeous chrome bow.The story is deceptively simple and yet explores some rather harrowing themes about the modern day... like most cyberpunk inspired stories do. The Streamer and Mr. Bullet do a wonderful job at portraying their sides and both really make you feel like Jack really is trapped in a dystopian future, both due to the writing and their respective VA's work. Depending on your skill level and difficulty choice, the story portion of the game may take you 2-3 hours to complete. I personally played through and Challenging difficulty which is the experience the devs intended you to play on, and while there were some frustrating moments in there, it was mostly skill issues on my part and I was able to power through them.So all in all, this game is absolutely incredibly and I cannot recommend it enough. The aesthetic and gameplay loop is super addictive and is absolutely worth the $20. I would go as far as to ask that you wait for the Steam Sale to be over so that you can buy it at full price because the devs have absolutely cooked up a friggin' masterpiece.So yeah, I'm gonna go back in to kick ass and lick lollipops! Also shout-out to Gianni Matragrano for his amazing work as Mr. Bullet, the way he screams MULLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEET will forever be ingrained in my brain.

_childDocuments_.review: Hurry up and buy Mullet Mad Jack if you like cyberpunk, outrun music, 80's / 90's aesthetics, anime of any kind, or indie video games. That's automatic. Read on if you aren't already buying this wonderful game.What's the game like? You're an elder millennial whose mom left him in a mall arcade with five bucks for the next hour and you just put a quarter into Smash TV, Revolution X, and Out Run at the same time. You take a sip of the flat, diluted soda you've been clutching before you stick it on the cabinet with your stash of quarters stacked on the hard, plastic lid. It plays something like that, anyway.How's the story? You're in the story of Quarantine, Doom, Rise of the Triad, and Duke Nukem 3D on a beige CRT monitor with a VGA graphics card on a Pentium II. Your friends are coming over later to watch The Sandlot on VHS but when your parents go to sleep you're going to put on Judge Dredd or Tank Girl. The story's good.Is it worth the money? Well, I don't wear my JNCOs anymore. Those little sunglasses with the small lenses look good on Venjent but anachronistic on me. My CD collection is in the bottom of a box somewhere, slowly delaminating while I refuse to finally throw them away now that Spotify completely replaced everything. But those things were so worth the bygone era they were a part of, an era I was fortunate enough to be a part of before too much of the stuff in those cyberpunk stories came true and the lifestyle of Mullet Mad Jack's weird social media dystopia parody was a little too real.Buy this game. Play this game. It's basically perfect.
