_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's alright!Basically a roguelike with a short campaign that exists to onboard you into endless mode. You have 10 seconds run through a series of randomly arranged pre-fabricated rooms until you reach the exit to the next floor. Getting kills or healing items adds to your time, so you run around blasting robot guys until you pass 10 floors to reach the boss.The gameplay loop is satisfying but starts to get repetitive. The core loop of shooting robots feels great, especially when you get in the groove. All of the guns feel punchy and distinct and the death animations are over the top and fun. You fall into a nice flow state where you're churning through rooms.There aren't enough room combinations, so you can go through the same rooms multiple times in a row. It doesn't help that there's no variation in the visuals. I personally had no desire to move on to endless mode after beating the campaign. Upgrades also feel tertiary. They don't have much impact on your run and there's not much variety.The presentation is solid. The art direction is peak 90s cyberpunk satire. Big neon signs, mullets, and chunky 90s tech smashed together with modern devices like smartphones. Dialogue is hit or miss. I chuckled a couple of times, but some of the satire doesn't hit. Sometimes feels like you're talking to that friend who thinks streamers are more important than they actually are.TLDR; A nice way to kill an afternoon but it's held back by a lack of gameplay variety. Art direction is good though. You'll know if this game is for you from the trailer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly short, (I beat it in about 4 hours) but does include an endless mode for continued fun. The story is very cheesy and the dialogue gets a little repetitive, but that's really not what people are here for anyway. The story mostly boils down to: go rescue the damsel in distress because capitalism, dopamine rushes, and evil robots, but unfortunately, you get an unskippable cutscene at the end of the game that feels incredibly pretentious. The game could have hammered its point home through the world building but instead, decided to beat the player over the head with one annoying cutscene that feels completely out of place given how short and skippable most cutscenes in this game are and how fast paced the gameplay is.It's incredibly fast paced, if you avoid the slower weapons. The SMG, katanas, and revolver are all pretty fast paced, as well as the laser rifle, although I didn't really care for that one. The shotgun is a little slow and the railgun slows the game down to a crawl and really isn't viable because of that at the higher difficulties. Most of the weapons feel good. The katanas can be tough to justify due to their inflexibility against almost all of the bosses, but can be swapped out right before a boss fight. They do trivialize the early game levels, as most of the guns feel clunky due to having to reload all the time, something that can be fixed through in game upgrades.The upgrade system is random. You're given a weapons option that can also contain an upgrade to your current weapon, a stat boost, and a hero modifier (most of which are either gaining more time for certain kills or softening the blows from traps) after every level you beat. Sometimes, you get locked in to some terrible upgrades. The laser rifle just feels bad. It doesn't do anywhere near the damage it needs to to feel good to use. Combine that with "talking protagonist" and "silent protagonist" being potential upgrades and some random stat boost like "chance for bullets to pierce through enemies" while you're using a sword, and there are some times the upgrades straight up don't feel rewarding. That being said, some of them feel great. There's nothing like getting 100% ricochet chance and watching SMG bullets flying all over the room or upgrading your revolver to have infinite ammo. The unique life system feels great. While limiting in the kinds of weapons you can viably use (stares at the railgun), it encourages fast gameplay. Did I mention this game was fast? The only issue I have with it is that the game is very vertical and there are some issues with tiny ledges stopping you from falling straight down and sometimes getting stuck on top of enemies that are sprites. The ledges were minor annoyances but usually, getting stuck on top of an enemy meant immediate death, which was rather frustrating. Other than that, the running and gunning is a ton of fun. The movement feels fast and almost all the weapons feel good.The art style is really cool. While it is also a point of frustration due to the sprite art and verticality, it looks like a comic book and works well, well, mostly, with the gameplay and works very well with the cheesy story. The colors really pop and make it easy to shoot at the things you're supposed to be shooting at in a split second and the art is full of detail most people are just going to fly by.This game is a blast and then it's over. I have a few minor gripes, but overall, it's a ton of fun and doesn't overstay its welcome. And if you want to keep playing, there's always an endless mode on offer that will keep the bullets flying

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is fast action in its purest form.This is an FPS stripped down to only those intense, frenetic firefights of movement and trigger finger reaction in an endless, glorious loop. The game itself actually mentions Flow State, and that's exactly what it delivers!This is one of those masocore games you play for the challenge. As such, the Attempt - Fail - Reattempt gameplay loop doesn't keep you waiting; you're back in the fight to try again immediately. It's easy to sink hours into MMJ  a good way.Aside from being the tightest action game I've played all year, MMJ also has heaps of style. _childDocuments_.review: Absolute peak run and gun fun. Mullet Mad Jack brings the retro aesthetic, and arcade-y feeling from the 80s and 90s into a fast paced, non-stop, fun ride, you won't want to miss. It is a game anyone can play and have a great time, but that also brings forth skill expression. The more you play it, the better you'll get at it and the more you'll be able to execute cool combos as you blitz through the levels.The story itself is relatively bare bones, however that's far from a downside. This is a game that embraces the insanity of its CyberPunk Universe. It's here for a great time, not a deep philosophical one, but that is not to say the story has nothing to say, it just won't be the thing that stick with you for a long time.Once you're done with the Story mode, you can dive into the Endless mode and this is where the game fully embraces its arcade-like nature with leader boards and fun that will only end when your skill can't carry you any further.It would be hard not to mention the thematic aspects of the game, since it boldly chose the CyberPunk aesthetic. While the game is by no means breaking any graphical fidelity standards, the way it stylizes itself and uses visuals as well as music is truly noteworthy. For an indie game, it is one of the most beautiful and thematically consistent games on the market. It's obvious the team had a solid vision for what they wanted to achieve and thanks to that it makes many other super realistic games look ugly by comparison. This is a videogame that feels like a videogame and it is an absolute blast.For Hammer95's first title, Mullet Mad Jack is a shot of brilliance and hopefully a great sign of what is to come for the Studio if they keep polishing the talent they already have. Now, your have 10 seconds, moderator. Destroy these damn bots!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's grease up and dive into the absurd world of "MULLET MADJACK," a game that cranks the insanity dial way past 11 and snaps the knob off. This isn't just a game; it's an 80's hair metal album cover come to life, complete with more bullets and mullets than a truck stop in the deep South.Mullet MadJack is the hero we didn't know we needed. Imagine if Rambo stopped taking life so seriously and decided to party hard instead. That's MadJack for you. He's all about spraying bullets with the finesse of a firehose at a cat bath, and his one-liners? They're cheesier than a high school prom in Wisconsin, and twice as entertaining.Now, let's talk gameplay. This no-nonsense FPS is as straightforward as it gets—think of it as a guided tour through a fireworks factory that's currently on fire. With roguelike elements that keep things fresher than a pair of socks straight out of the pack, you'll never get bored, no matter how many times you play.In conclusion, MULLET MADJACK isn't just a game; it's a high-octane, face-melting, mullet-flapping adventure that's as ridiculous as it is addictive. It's a power trip wrapped in anime visuals with the subtlety of a sledgehammer at a glassware convention. If you're in the mood for something utterly absurd and fantastically fun, then buckle up, buttercup. MadJack's got a bullet with your name on it, and it's coming in hot.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void goes 80s anime with this one. Mullet Madjack is just straight addictive fun. The perfect dopamine rush to kill a quick hour playing. It doesn't take long to beat, not that it should given the premise, but it's very replayable given the number of difficulty options and endless mode. It oozes style all throughout. You can see all the references to classic anime like Akira, Fist of the North Star, maybe Patlabor? The soundtrack is catchy synthwave which feels appropriate. The takedown animations are quick and brutal. Gives me that DOOM Eternal feel. The art style is really beautiful. It's colorful cyberpunk with impressive animations and campy voice acting. Levels look somewhat different, but are functionally identical all things considered. There's a decent variety of enemies and weapons to keep the experience fresh. The fully upgraded railgun is extremely powerful. It's just fun to power through levels completing them in 20 seconds or less. It's not a very deep game. After playing last year's phenomenal Deadlink, that showed me how to do a roguelite shooter very well. As a roguelite, Mullet is a little light on upgrade options between floors. You see a lot of the same options and they're not that exciting. Bosses are extremely easy. I think I died twice altogether fighting the bosses. This game is easy to learn and easy to master honestly. It doesn't take long to get familiar with the game's pattern for each floor. I still really enjoyed it and I do recommend it if you really liked Post Void. I definitely enjoyed this more. I'd say it's maybe better to get on sale like $15. (7/10)

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a fantastic fusion of the adrenaline rush hyperviolent gameplay of Hotline Miami and classic FPS gameplay, all wrapped in a delightful 80s/90s anime OVA aesthetic. It sounds like a strange elevator pitch, but it works quite well overall. If that alone has piqued your interest, I recommend you download the demo and get straight into it.The basic concept between Mullet Madjack is that you have 10 seconds (on Normal) to reach the end of a level before you flatline. Taking out enemies or completing certain movement tricks will give you more time, whereas taking damage will reduce it, resulting a constant need to keep moving and on the offensive. You can jump, dash, kick doors in and use one-off melee weapons to help you in this endeavour, finishing a level/floor results in the roguelite option of picking and upgrade or new weapon from a selection of three. In practice, it's nothing too revolutionary, but it's a solid combination of all these elements together. You complete 9 floors, a boss on the 10th floor, rinse and repeat.The default difficulty, Normal, offers you 10 seconds of initial life and it's a solid entry point to learn the evolving mechanics of the game across the 80+ floors of the complex - not too hard, not too easy. There's lower and higher difficulties for those who want a range of options, but there is one curious and deeply accessible option: no timer mode. Rather than making the game a race against the clock, 'no timer mode' changes the flow to something closer to a traditional boomer shooter, which works quite well as well. Lastly, an endless mode is available if you're keen for a full roguelite experience. A Normal run will take about 3.5-4 hours, but I'm definitely keen to jump back in.This is all supported by a very robust set of aesthetic choices. Mullet Madjack nails the look of 80s/90s anime OVAs and the synthwave soundtrack just reinforces that. The visual and in-game references to things like Bubblegum Crisis definitely brought a small to my face, and I'd argue that the the visual/aural component of the game is its strongest feature.The only weakness I'd highlight is that in some ways, it feels like there could just be a little more to the campaign content and a little extra polish with the weapons. I'm nitpicking as the experience is already quite solid, but an expansion campaign, a few more weapons and a little polishing of some of the weaker weapons could definitely go a long way. The roughly 4 hours it took me to complete a Normal run were definitely all killer, no filler, and the game still offers a fair bit with its alternative modes and the option for endless mode.I will say however, that this game sits in a nice little niche in terms of its contemporaries. I still consider Neon White to be the best of the FPS/puzzle fast-paced games of this era, but this offers something a bit more action-heavy. Likewise, a lot of the aesthetic appeals of Ghostrunner are replicated here, but without the inherent frustration with parts of that game (case and point: boss battles). If this sounds like your jam, you're likely going to have a good time with Mullet Madjack. I still feel that an expansion could do wonders for the game in due time, but it's definitely a great game as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages to take a bunch of very well known and familiar genre's, themes, etc and mash them all into one unique experience. You can find plenty of games that tick some of those individual boxes but Im confident you wont find one that ticks them *all* as well as Mullet Madjack does.A fast paced love letter to 90's anime and mullets. Everything going on blends together so well and satisfies the senses in a way I havent seen in many other games. Combat is brutal and buttery smooth, the sounds are pure dopamine, visuals are captivating, and the gameplay is butt cheek clenching madness.My favorite part about it all is that, while it is very fast paced which is reinforced by the 10 second timer constantly ticking away for every second you dont kill someone, you dont have to be a adderall pumping Apex Legends pro to be good at this game. As one of the tool tips explain: "It's not about being the fastest, but to dance and flow through the enemies!". It lets the game be intense and keep you at the edge of your seat while also not feeling too rushed to make something happen and just, as the game says, flow through the levels.I hope to see more from the dev(s) and maybe even an expansion to the Madjack universe. They have a really good character here. A mullet wearing, lollipop sucking, one liner spitting gunman just sounds like a protagonist that belongs with the likes of Duke Nukem, Caleb or Lo Wang. More games starring Madjack, whether this same style or not, would surely be a hit and something I would personally be first in line to try out.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is a fun, fast-paced FPS experience oozing with style that ends just as quickly as it starts. The game and its levels are structured like a roguelite, with rooms, enemy placement, and upgrade choice varying randomly between each level and each attempt. Although "vary" may be too strong a word for this game as the possible changes between each level are so minuscule that the game feels exactly the same the entire way through. Granted that constant state is a fun one, it feels good to blitz through rooms keeping up your combo, it looks great, sounds great, but there is no variety in the gameplay at all. Outside of the charming cutscenes that separate the different chapters in the two-hour-long campaign, your experience will not vary. There are additional score attack gamemodes that change the rules of the game and challenge you to make it as far as you can, but it's just not enough of a difference to be worth the time. And for $20 I tried to get as much time out of this game as I could, my playtime that you see now is how long it took for me to get every single achievement. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent fast paced game that retains playability with a good skill ceiling. Extremely stylistic and beautiful at that, alot of things happening at once though can be distracting for some but I had no issue. Easy to pick up, with a moderate amount of skill required to master. It in many was can be described as a 90s anime version of the game Post Void, but that game definitely has a higher skill ceiling and is much more difficult on the eyes. Fun campaign though not long, replayable with the randomized layouts as an option and higher difficulties. The endless mode is alot of fun as well and a huge attractive piece to this primarily roguelike game, the campaign section has more roguelite elements with a few permanent upgrades for that mode since its meant for progression, learning aspects of the game, and the fun little story. Absolutely delight of a game and well worth $20, plenty of replayability and fun to be had. Certainly less so than something like Binding of Isaac, but they are very different games.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, MULLET MADJACK sounds simple enough. A kidnapped pop icon princess held hostage at the top of an eight-story tower. You—her mad and mulleted would-be-rescuer—at the bottom, with 10 doors standing between you and the tower’s next floor. Reach the floor’s next door and you’ll receive a new weapon or temporary upgrade. Get through all 9 doors and then kill the floor’s boss and you’ll receive a  upgrade. Die at any point, however, (even seconds before reaching the floor’s final door!) and it’s back to that floor’s very beginning. So far so good, right?   Well, it would be if MULLET MADJACK was a by-the-book cover shooter you could slowly dink ‘n’ dunk your way through as you gradually scale the tower. But Mr. Madjack has a quick trick up his sleeve... or, rather, a syringe up his vein. For you see, in this dystopian robobillionaire future that looks and sounds a heck of a lot like a roided-up 80’s anime, we lowly retrohumans cannot survive without dopamine, and your employer/streaming contractor—the ironically ultraviolent Peace Corp—has decided the best way to keep its viewers engaged (and alive!) is to manually hardwire you into a short-term life support system and stream the results, meaning you only have 10 seconds to reach the next door. Kill something along the way and you’ll get a few seconds back, even more if you kill ‘em creatively. Get shot, however, and you’ll lose a few seconds, and (in case you forgot) you don’t have many of those to spare. Now, if you’ll permit a quick tangent, last August I reviewed a nifty little Boomer Shooter called Turbo Overkill, which I considered to be—at the time—the most fast-paced and relentless combat I had experienced since middle school (those kids were so mean). However, Turbo Overkill, what with its spacious level designs and objectives that demanded occasional backtracking, looks about as fast as freeze-dried turtle turds when compared to the claustrophobic, straight-line, time-sensitive intensity of MADJACK.  But speed isn’t everything, and while MADJACK’s 10-second gimmick goes a long way to creating compelling gameplay, it doesn’t mask  of the game’s flaws. For example, during my 80-floor ascent, I only recall facing a handful of distinct enemy types, and more lethal than their weapons was their ability to get in my damn way by clogging up tight passageways.  Equally repetitive is the dialogue, as after the intro there are only maybe 20 more voice acted lines in the entire game, 10 of which are screamed at you by your manic Peace Corp moderator on every floor, nine of which are Mr. Madjack’s watered down Duke Nuke’em knockoff one-liners about lollipops and soda, and the last of which is the final boss screaming “MULLLEETTTTT!!!” over and over again. There are also a ton of meh platforming sections scattered about each floor, and nothing took the wind out of my high-speed sails faster than killing my way through five minutes of enemies only to barely miss a jump right before the last door and get sent back to the floor’s very beginning. I know, “Get good!” but goodness was this a consistently annoying recurrence during my playthrough.   But, whenever I did get mad at MADJACK, it didn’t take long for the game’s enjoyable visual aesthetic and fun soundtrack to pull me back in. As noted earlier, the game draws heavy stylistic inspiration from the Akira-era of original video animations, and I never grew tired of its bright lights and hyper-saturated gore. As a UI nerd, I also geeked out over MADJACK’s immersive menus and diegetic health bar in the form of your phone, which combines with energetic, arcadey damage notifications popping up all over the screen all of the time to create a mesmerizing, even suffocating experience. I also appreciate the option to increase, reduce, or even turn off your level timer, as each setting can completely transform the way you approach levels and allow you to say, focus on killing everything as opposed to scream sprinting past everyone as I often did.  Everything else in MADJACK ranges from okay :/ to okay :). The boss fights are intense if unspectacular exclamation marks at the end of each floor. Meanwhile, the tower’s level designs have a handful of fun touches, like air duct shortcuts you can Kool-Aid Man your way through, and environmental hazards like poison and lava you can unlock resistances for (or, better yet, just jump dash over entirely). But even as the later floors begin adding lasers to dodge and advanced door locks to disable, the end product still ends up feeling like eight unconnected floors of comparable difficulty as opposed to something that truly builds upon itself. Ditto that for the fast and loose story, which is so busy being silly that it misses an opportunity to expand upon its characters or insane premise in any meaningful way.  But you're not here for serious, unless you’re serious about bisecting evil robots with a giant fire katana. So, for $20 and after adding in the game’s endless mode that’s tied to a leaderboard, I think MULLET MADJACK presents solid value, so I’ll give it an aggregate MEGA score of 3.31/5 (full scoring breakdown from “Plot” to “Sound” available in video form). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a weird game that I'm unable to recommend.The map variety is non-existent and the game is barely legible, the UI is clunky and overdesigned and will often lead to your untimely death by covering up the important parts of the game, the game is not difficult at it's core, it's just not all that playable if played the way it's intended. The hitboxes aren't tight and the level design is samey but not samey enough to be learned by heart. It's a good looking game but that's about all it is. The weapon balance is all over the place and if you're aiming for higher difficulties you'll likely find yourself going back to the only viable weapon in game, the fully upgraded starter pistol which lets you finish levels in a normal amount of time (20-30 seconds) and kill enemies in a speedy manner.The gameplay is horridly shallow and the more interesting gameplay altering upgrades ( such as the grappling hook or environment items) fall short because the game wasn't built to accomodate them. In short, if you've finished the DEMO which is available, you've seen most if not nearly all of what the game has to offer.Compared to other fast paced shooters on the market which fill a similar niche such as Deadlink or Roboquest, Mullet Madjack leaves a lot to be desired, the developer insists that this game has nothing in common with either of those titles but I beg to differ, there's way too much overlap not to take it into consideration. If you're a fan of wild visuals and weird shooters, MMJ might be up your alley, certainly not mine. I decided to embark on a journey to finish the game on HARD and then INSANE but I simply got bored of it, dropped the game for a few months and came back to finish it alongside the rest of my backlog and decided to drop it again. MMJ feels like an early access title sold as a finished product with a healthy dose of identity crisis. I'm not sure where the overwhelmingly positive reviews are coming from because the game is simply undercooked. It falls short in comparison to actual modern boomer shooter such as DUSK, Forgive me Father, ULTRAKILL, Project Warlock, Fortune's Run and many more, I can only attribute the positive reviews to the game's visuals.I urge you to download the DEMO and consider if the free portion of the game ( which is more or less everything this game has to offer) is fun enough to be played through 8 times over for the game's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty, very stylish - I feel like the design is a love-letter to a foray of different 80s/90s anime tropes, and honestly that was what got me in immediately. Sadly a run or so later, and I didn't feel like it was for me. I think that it deserves the praise it's getting! This is more of a review for those who are looking for a boomer shooter and instead got an incredibly high-octane arcade shooter. It's got minor RNG (I wouldn't even call it roguelike) elements with the floor "upgrades", but it really is just a twitch combo-shooter with a single weapon of choice. Done very stylishly, but is more of an arcade shooter than what I was expecting - essentially something more DOOM-like.Also as others have mentioned, it's all procedurally-generated, which sounds neat on paper, but for something that requires such twitch-mechanics and near-perfect shots at higher difficulties, I could see that being fun if there were a pattern to learn. Instead it does feel a bit more like "hope for the best, shoot for the worst" sort of situation things could get into.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. "Boomer Shooter" is a terrible tag, "Fast-Paced" is what this game is, it is basically Post Void with an 80s aesthetic. Essentially, you get random super-fast paced linear levels, then a boss every 10 floors, and the goal is to always be doing moving and shooting enemies in the head. If you're expecting something like Warhammer 40k Boltgun or Prodeus, you should look elsewhere. This is moreso for people who really like the fast parts of Ultrakill and just want more of that.Gameplay: There are 7 weapons - Plasma rifle, SMG, Rifle, Revolver, Shotgun and 2 variants of the Katana. While I want to really like the Katana, you take damage from touching most enemies, and you need to get close to use the katana. The 2nd or 3rd boss, Chainsaw Guy, is a hard counter to the Katana as well (unless you throw it) which I thought was unbalanced. The powerups are not that well thought out. Especially for a genre like this that is just corridor after corridor of dopamine, I think it should be a cardinal sin to introduce percentage based improvements as powerups. I want more effects on my screen, give me a powerup that shoots a rocket after every 2nd shot or gives me a 1-hit shield every time I kill an enemy. There is no reason for there to be a triple-jump powerup, or a powerup for navigating through the map. It's ridiculous.Soundtrack + Visuals: Great. Not much to add except it is a lot easier to get your bearings than you think. After the first few levels you just naturally lock in.Plot: Not non-existent but might as well be. I will say the Chapter 4/5 stuff does not need to be there. I'm only here to zoom past the levels, the whole "walk around your room while this bar fills up" is a terrible design choice. This is not the genre to tell a deep story. Overall cool game

_childDocuments_.review: ++ Cool visuals and retro-style++ Unique premise++ Very fun gameplay+ Amazing final chapters+ Good music+ Fun "unboxing"-- Way too expensive-- Missing overall varietyThis game is pretty cool, but I really cannot recommend it outside of a sale.The good points are numerous: the gameplay is amazing and just a ton of fun, its fast, brutal, varied and intuitive. The visuals are cool and charming and the music is all around pretty good. The overall premise is very unique and extremely fun to engage with, as it is woven into the gameplay masterfully (10 secs till death). The game goes into overdrive during the last chapters culminating into a great final boss fight.The biggest problem however, and the reason why it is a hesitant recommendation: The story took me 4 hours to complete. F O U R. That's pretty weak for 20 Euros, in my opinion. I would have loved some kind of escalation like in the last chapters, but all you are left with is the endless mode, which is not THAT motivating to be honest. Another big negative point concerns the missing variety: You shoot the same enemies with the same guns, running through the same levels, while getting the same upgrades, which have little impact.Talking about voice lines: the VAs did a great job, no questions asked. Sadly there is almost no variety here as well, before every boss I started spam-skipping the voice lines, as they are ALWAYS the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. You only have 10 seconds to beat each level but killing enemies grants you extra time. Stylish kills (like headshots, nutshots, and special finishers) reward extra time. The enemies themselves are fairly simple but blasting through the levels is thrilling. After each level, there's a sort of roguelike-esque progression where you can change weapons, upgrade your weapon, or unlock different abilities like double jump/nutshots grant you extra time. The colorful graphics combined with the hyper-violent gameplay and the cheesy one-liners of the protagonist (who is about as subtle as Duke Nukem) is perfect. I also really liked the 90s anime-style cutscenes/characters. The story starts off simple (you must save the princess) but actually becomes pretty profound at the end. Beating the game once is pretty quick (I played on normal mode) but there are a few different difficulty levels and an endless roguelike mode. I'll definitely play more of this game at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: TL-DR: Very well polished breakneck paced shooter albiet short story length.Pros:+ It has a Demo, that went a long way to get me to decide to buy it.+ The 90's anime aesthetic really comes to life within the game. Character designs are great!+ Fast paced and addictive fun. The games theme of "Dopamine" really fits and they did it justice.+ Multiple difficulties for novices and experienced FPS players alike.+ It's great to play as a gigachad protagonist in a 2024 game. Rare to see these days in modern indie gaming.+ It's one of those games where the gameplay seems overwhelming at first, but then it "just clicks" and you will be blasting and dashing your way through floors.+ Excellent sound design. Music very fitting for the game also.Cons:- Very short story. Completed in 2 sittings on the easier 15 Seconds of life mode. I died way too often on Normal mode in the demo. I am very glad this easier mode is available but you will blast through the story.- Floor checkpoints were a bit too spaced out. I get that each floor takes a minute to beat, but this design choice solidified my decision to play on the easiest mode. I can see it get frustrating to do floors over and over again. - Can't be played for long sittings, the flashy visuals will go for your eyes.Overall, it's a welcome addition to the FPS genre! If only the story was longer, but many will enjoy the "Endless Mode" the game has on offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is another sleeper hit of 2024 that came out of nowhere for the most. At first glance, it's not hard to make comparisons to Post Void, simply by being a corridor boomer shooter. However, I find Mullet Madjack to be a bit more forgiving, as it’s easier to read the level layout and the patterns of enemies.The game immediately oozes charisma with its highly stylized visuals that transport you into a 90s anime, with lots of references to 90s pop culture and retro shooters. You even get to unbox a big box version of the game in-game that introduces you to the game. Accompanied by a great selection of synthwave tracks, an idiosyncratic sense of humor, and high-octane gameplay, Mullet Madjack achieves exactly what it promises and doesn't shy away from letting you know:YOU NEED THAT DOPAMINE HIT.And, you probably want to enslave yourself to that Peace Corp lady, but that’s another matter.Mullet Madjack has 9 chapters that can be completed in about 2.5 to 3 hours. Each chapter consists of 10 floors, and you have only 10 seconds to reach the end of each floor. Each kill adds to your lifespan, and if you get creative, you get rewarded. It plays like a roguelite: if you die, you go back to the start of the chapter (the first floor). However, you get to keep some permanent unlocks, and they let you keep one of your best upgrades. There is more than enough variety in unlockables (guns, environmental items, and so on) to keep the flow going.The game always has some tricks up its sleeve with twists. While levels evolve with more traps and enemies, you’ll soon recognize the pattern, as it doesn’t change much within a chapter. However, since it only takes about 30 to 50 seconds to complete a level (usually), you get a mental reset soon enough and probably won’t mind that. Bosses are fun overall, and there are some surprise gameplay sequences that are great callbacks to retro shooters. The game also cleverly ties the ending to its endless mode. With the addition of different difficulties for the story mode -if you want to suffer more- and endless mode for the leaderboards, you get fair amount of replayability.All in all, Mullet Madjack is a very clever parody, but above everything else, it is great entertainment. Go kill some billionaires, handsome.★★★★☆

On normal the difficulty curve is decent although there were a few places where it felt like it unfairly spiked. Fortunately the designers did we'll in providing a virility of difficulties you can swap into at any time - unlike certain other indie games which crank the difficulty to un-fun & waste unskilled players time. _childDocuments_.review: Simple but addicting gameplay. If you enjoy boomer shooters or arcade games, this is a must have. A timeless addition to the genre. A peak example of 90's anime style, it is a self-designated "FPS OVA". Despite being incredibly fast-paced, I find myself wanting to stop and inspect every asset; the attention to detail is astounding. The world and art direction take inspiration from movies like Akira and They Live, the mechanics from games like Brutal Doom and Post Void. It satirizes and glorifies its own style, mocking both the protagonist and the player in their quest to save an influencer and obtain a virtual pair of sneakers.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. Great aesthetic, very good production values. Fast paced game play, and a very interesting ten seconds to live mechanic which ensures you keep the action going.It has some roguelite / like mechanics, but I would definitely not call this game a roguelite / like game since there is actual progression and chapters.To summarize the game, 1. Chapters are divided by ten short levels or floors each.2. You have ten seconds to live in each floor, but you keep up the counter by killing enemies.3. You can select an upgrade from a random assortment of three between floors.4. You face a boss on the tenth floor of a chapter, without a timer.5. If you die at any point during a ten floor interval, you start all over with zero upgrades from the first floor of that particular chapter.6. Beat the boss and the chapter is cleared. Move on to the next chapter. Upgrades are reset in between chapters.Give the demo a try if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: A stylish, somewhat punishing, but addictive 90s-inspired shooter. It's a short game, but the swift, high-octane nature of the gameplay, as well as the RNG of the levels, provides great replay value. The range of weapons and perks, as well as the randomness of the levels, ensure that no two run feels the same. This game follows Mullet Mad Jack, a character based on the likes of Duke Nukem, who may spew cheesy one-liners or be a silent protagonist (it's up to you) as he shoots, kicks, and finishes off robots to save his damsel-in-distress. You fight through 10 floors, encountering a boss at the end of each, risking having to start at the checkpoint all over if make a mistake. The story is rather bare-bones, but that's fine; it's very much an unapologetic love letter to the video games of the 1990s, and I love that.I highly recommended this title for any FPS-lovers, novice or veteran, and I have every faith this will be remembered as one of the best shooters of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: I like being able to see what the hell I'm doing. This game encourages speed, but you will end up going so blindingly fast that everything becomes a blur and you're gonna be pumped full of shots from enemies before your brain can even register what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on. There's "fact-paced" and then there's "seizure inducing". This is the second.  Why bother trying to aim and actually shoot something when mashing dash and attack is just as effective? I should not have to seriously consider dropping the difficulty to "accessibility" mode just to make sense of the blur of the neon river rushing past on my screen. Why use a gun when you literally don't have the time to meaningfully aim at anything because you're instantly knocked down to 1 second of life the frame you enter the room?I really wanted to like this game, but as it stands now I feel genuinely ripped off by a game that I find barely playable. I'd love to put more than 2 hours in to give it an honest try, but blame Steam for that one. I spent $20 and walk away with a headache and a feeling like I got gyped. Not a good impression. Could I have tried the demo first? Sure, but too often the demo isn't representative of the final product, so I'm not about to waste my time with them.

_childDocuments_.review: *AT THE BOTTOM OF THIS REVIEW IS SOME SPOILER CENTRIC DISCUSSION*Yeah, its pretty ♥♥♥ dope.Had this one on my radar for a while. Gameplay is fast and frantic. I've heard some people describe it as an FPS Hotline Miami. I think thats probably a little inaccurate since the timer-based life system changes the way you play quite dramatically compared to Hotline Miami's one hit kill system. Though the fast time to kill and vibrant aesthetic probably contributes to that comparison heavily. New mechanics are added every ten floors which help keep up the variety. Most of the weapons also feel great (except the plasma gun, not a huge fan of that). The game looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous. It's a very unique style that I still notice despite the rapid pace of everything. I would recommend bumping up the FOV as it made me a little motion sick at the default 60. The game also runs fantastically. A unique detail that I appreciated was the unboxing experience you can find in the menu. It's somewhat unnecessary, but really commits to the bit, is quite funny and surprisingly detailed.I have two points that could be construed as a negative. Firstly, like an OVA, this game is short and sweet. I've not touched endless mode yet, but the main campaign took me around 3.6 hours according to steam. However, this is a case of quality over quantity. There is plenty of replayability with endless mode and the additional difficulty modes. Basically don't be a d**k and refund the game. They clearly worked very hard on this and you're a terrible human if you do. Overall, I think the base game could be a bit longer (which will tie into my critique around the plot), but it absolutely does not overstay its welcome. Despite it's short length, its well paced with its gradual introduction of new mechanics.*SPOILER CENTRIC DISCUSSION*Secondly, I would have liked to see some additional story content as I feel like the story sets itself up for something a little more nefarious, but doesn't really go there. The story probably wasn't central to this game and I get that. But it feels incomplete or that potential is wasted. Given that you see a second building as you progress, the constant fourth wall breaks and the dialogue poking at darker concepts like death, the afterlife and consumerism, I was expecting some twist like, the influencer princess being the villain and the final boss is actually aware of the metaphysical f**kery going on. Or theres additional set of floors like the inverted castle in Castlevania. I'm just spitballing here and there could always be potential for an update or DLC. I could also just be massively misenterpreting the intent. Regardless, the story is still a good time. I like the hidden jokes/gags in the levels and that unboxing thing.*END OF SPOILER DISCUSSIONOverall, despite its short length, I'd genuinely recommend this at full price. It's clearly full of passion, has insanely fun gameplay, has a wonderful audiovisual presentation and does have replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little conflicted on how to feel about this. Its hard to tell what the intended pace is. Sometimes being just a bit methodical makes sense since you can more readily deal with threats and go for bonuses, but other times enemies will hitscan you to near death immediately so it feels like you have to bust in as quickly as possible and hope something doesn't kill you immediately. It makes me wonder if having a health bar separate from your timer might have been the better way to go to help control the pace a little more, but I also  see people being able to pace themselves a little with no issue so maybe these are just personal issues. Otherwise, the game is stylish and knows exactly what its inspired by and how seriously it takes itself. If the initial pitch seemed enjoyable to you then odds are it'll be do the job. It also has a demo so there's no harm in sampling either.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Graphics and music are good, sound design is acceptable, gameplay is good for 15 minutes and then doesn't develop at all and is insanely repetitive. After about 20 minutes you will see little to nothing that is new or interesting other than some cutscene lore/story stuff with a few different sections. The whole game is basically an autoscrolling shooter. You hold W and dash through the level while clicking heads, occasionally needing to jump, or move to the side briefly to hit a vending machine to heal. There are upgrades but they get wiped every 10 levels so... ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ There are also some perma upgrades but its just ♥♥♥♥ like adding some rerolls and unlocking max weapon level. Enemy variety is horrible, adding an extra enemy after some bosses, but you don't play any different. Hold W, shoot enemies in the way. It's mind numbing, and not in a good way. You don't even get the courtesy of new environments to play in, it's minute differences that change almost nothing, and all looks the same. I was very pleased in the first 15 minutes and then 10 minutes later I was getting lost. Wanted to persevere through it for a full review but idiotically dying resets you to the 1st level of your stage (You die in 47, you go to 41, 37 go to 31, etc). So then you just endure MORE of the SAME tedium. You can't even call it replaying the levels they are so similar, you are basically just given more levels to do. On the Challenging difficulty, the greatest threat to your life is boredom. Both of my 2 deaths were me just zoning out, one during a bossfight that instakills you in melee (he was a chainsaw man I guess), the other because i was just not paying attention to enemies, and the timer killed me because I wasn't killing enough. I don't get all the positivity. it is pretty mediocre. 3/10EDIT: Oh yeah, the price. 20 bucks? Really? Even Dead by Daylight is a better use of 20 bucks, and that ♥♥♥♥ will make you never want to play a multiplayer game again.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is an exceptional achievement in what it sets out to do, offering an innovative yet nostalgic approach based on familiar mechanics. It combines the classic style of Doom, the frantic gameplay of Ultrakill, and the strategic depth of Hades, granting the player remarkable freedom to explore and understand their own limits.The fast-paced floor-based structure delivers a highly satisfying game design experience. _childDocuments_.review: Ultra-stylish, edge-of-your-seat boomer shooter bliss.Mullet Madjack takes Post-Void's basic gameplay formula, spices it up with some bells and whistles (such as melee finishers and wall running), and packages it all in a neon-soaked, semi-randomized campaign (as well as an endless mode for roguelike purists). The gameplay is fast, and it's hard, with a relentless push-forward momentum that demands you kill to survive. It's ceaselessly exciting, and the devs have included generous accessibility options to make sure everybody can experience the game in a way that's fun for them. Add in a banger synthwave soundtrack, god-tier A/V juice, and copious heaps of personality (including laugh-out-loud one-liners from the player character and a hilarious "unboxing" feature available from the main menu), and Mullet Madjack is an absolute winner. FPS, roguelite, and action fans should be all over this game.  This is a very easy recommend for what is already amongst my favorite games of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: The exhausting popularity of  “boomer shooters’ has began waning at the candle of creativity. Dripping into this pool of saturation is “Mullet Mad Jack’’  a celebration of nostalgic revery. Naive arcade game-play tributed with two button mechanics (shoot or sprint) predominantly drive the ruthless yet repetitious game-play loop. All ensnared by the vibrant but tiresome cultural aesthetics of 80's. Supporting this feathered frontier is a superficial roguelite system. Upgrades provide mostly banal amendments, lacking creative consequences and development. Maintaining playability remains safely conservative.  The juxtaposition of this rudimentary approach demands more depth. Without any sense of risk, reward or strategy, the arcade gun-play becomes more evidently shallow.  “Mullet Mad Jack’’ is a basic package, indulged by its own bravado rather than developing comprehensive mechanics. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The main "campaign" itself is very brief and the progressing addition of more difficult and varied challenges make it entertaining. It's like if a 1980s anime fan and who is big into vaporwave took DMT and came up with the idea whole cloth. The style and the anime hottie negging you the whole time is inpressive on it's own and for price it is cheap for what it is. If are are the target market it is exactly for you. I finished the epilogue which really doesn't feel like an epilogue and just the last chapter of the story where the developers by way of the negging anime girl basically call you a dopamine fed slave with contempt and daring you to keep playing I find myself a bit disturbed by. In part because she is exactly correct and that I am seeking idle dopamine drips as I march toward the grave at my final level.It makes me envious of the Mullet in the shape of a man. Because I can pull of business in the front. But not the party in the back.

_childDocuments_.review: HAMMER95 bravely woke up one day and answered the question "What if Post Void was actually good?" with MULLET MADJACK: ANIME ACTION. The game’s a really fun corridor-shooter roguelite (and roguelike if you play Permadeath) with quirky elements absolutely, absolutely oozing with ardent admiration for both faced paced shooters like the previously alluded to Post Void, but obviously Hotline Miami and 80s/90s series like GitS, Akira, and Gunsmith Cats. It has a lot going for it, but also has a decent number of drawbacks that can be looked over in the grand scheme of things just due to how fun and charismatic the game is as a whole.Pros+ Asthetic: Artstyle and music were knocked out of the park+ Pretty addictive and fun; feels good to play+ Zany and charmingNeutrals/ Pretty costly for the content on display (20 bones for 3-4 hrs) with most of the cost behind "replayability" (which might rightfully not be everyone's cup of tea)/ Hira, kata, and some kanji/JP vocab required to get that “extra immersion” factor (plus knowledge on popular culture but that’s already a given) – imo it’s a lovely touch but might leave some people in the dark/ Rooms can get quite repetitive and "feel same-y" after a while (since you'll repetitively go through them), although this is by design as HMR95 want you to remember the layouts of the room (as mentioned in the difficulty screen)Cons (-) and Nitpicks (・)- Final boss fight can feel very underwhelming and anticlimatic (excluding the outro segment that's just flavor), the dude has like literally 3 attacks and only 1 phase and can be beat in like around a minute or less lol- VERY noticeable audio cut-outs and glitches when things get hectic (to the point of annoyance) - “Seconds gained” popup can block enemies; died due to being unable to see enemies because of this a couple times, felt very cheap- Some upgrades lack info and could benefit from having an “info popup” if hovered over – EX: Weapon upgrades are one of the few things that carried over between checkpoints if you reach the next checkpoint, seeing higher tier weapons requires leveling them up while equipped, what exactly do crits do (double damage?), no mention that the grappling hook heals, etc.- One liners that can be annoying for some; muting LOCKED BEHIND AN UPGRADE for whatever reason??? Really dilutes the upgrades pool, should just be a game setting.- The sniper segment is very discombobulating and a bit nauseating; could benefit from both having a crosshair pre-ADS (to know where you will aim at) and having less "scope" take up the sides of the screen - Screen glitch artifacts effects should be able to be toned downed/disabled in settings (still occur with the “screen flashes” setting disabled)- For a game quite heavy on replayability, lacking a Custom Difficulty option is disappointing (ex: No Timer vs Second Lifespan, kill second reward, max HP, boss/enemy damage, soda/item frequency, etc.)- Katanas feel quite weak (long swing time, lackluster long-range solution, can't benefit from a lot of upgrades)- Some upgrades are just straight-up too weak (You telling me picking up items further and sliding faster is as good as ricocheting bullets and extra max HP? Or laser kills should still only give 1 extra second when head/nutshots also give 1 extra?)- Enemies are a bit hard to see from far away – they appear a bit blurry and low-res (this might just be an engine/artsyle thing but I swear I feel like there’s some post-processing getting in the way here)・Finishers don't mention the free reload (on top of the heal)・Argument can be made to swap the default kick (Shift) and kick w/item use (R Click) binds (this can be rebinded anyways)・Tooltips cannot be disabled (sure need to know to hold W on a slide to go faster for the 60th time)・Life Vest shouldn't take an upgrade slot on No Timer (but instead a side option - it wastes a slot that could've been used on something else)・Art of War passive should be changed to proc at max hp instead (rewards aggressive play instead of passive play)・Railgun should have innate enemy/glass pierce・Endless should show how many floors an upgrade has before it expires on the upgrade screen・Lack of a “quick restart/continue” option (by skipping having to press space at loading screens)・Spelling errors sprinkled in here and there (notably so in the credits and manual)・ Finishes/sodas still show seconds (instead of HP) healed on No Timer (sometimes rarely shows HP healed text in testing)・Wallrunning billboards have an invisible wall behind them, preventing you from climbing over them from behind・If more and more upgrades keep getting added (like they already have been), the upgrade pool are just going to get more diluted and would eventually benefit from something to combat it (ie: being able to choose your upgrade pool and exclude ones that you don’t like – but this might “shift the point of the upgrades being random” and just more of a personal opinion)7.5 - Streamer is my wife; she doesn’t engage in infidelity or polygamy btw

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, if you're a fan of 80's anime, or solid and fast paced FPS action, then just go ahead and get this one and enjoy!The fast gameplay is straightforward with a solid design and focus, with a fun twist to keep things lively and intense without being too annoying or tedious. Plus, the variable difficulty helps one to learn the overall mechanics, while also being available to crank up the scale when appropriate.Major props to the beautiful art and design, as it's a fun and colorful homage to the classic anime of yesteryear. Plenty of fun references to catch without being overbearing. Top notch job with the smooth and detailed animations as well. Also, big points for showing off the "unboxing" experience in all its rendered glory.Gotta appreciate the excellent music as well, with plenty of nice tracks throughout the stages, along with a terrific main menu theme. The sound design is also great, with fitting impact, explosions, and other effects feeling appropriately suited to the action. Also, love the performance from the voice actors, with their characters being appropriately over-the-top and fitting for this setting.As for any major issues or bugs, I didn't really encounter much aside from a few frame rate hiccups between loading screens, and one time when the game refused to let me continue to the next floor. Overall, you won't be disappointed by picking up this title. It keeps things short, sweet, and fun with loads of style, and doesn't rip you off like a modern AAA studio - let's leave that for the robillionaires.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there, allow me to introduce you to my game of the year: (Here is the link to my YouTube review if you’d rather watch that)Mullet Mad Jack is a rogue like unlike anything you’ve ever played before. Soaked in neon featuring a wild mix of 90s japanimation and synthwave aesthetics, you enter a dystopian future where killing robo billionairs is the norm and it is live streamed to a large audience. Enter Jack, part mullet, part man, part potato and soda lovin’ machine, he is here to traverse 80 floors of nonstop action in an effort to rescue a social media influencer known as “the princess”. The number one robo-billionaire has kidnapped her in order to draw out her virgins blood to summon a god, and Jack is the only person that can save her.   Jack is given a measly 10 seconds to live on this adventure, and he has his handy dandy cellphone attached straight to his bloodline and his heart pumping him full of endorphins and life as he kills enemies left and right. Mullet Mad Jack is a traditional FPS in a sense, you’ll be running and gunning with various weapons, but the twist is every kill and style of the kill gives you seconds back to keep living and keep shooting your way through floor after floor of the Nakamura Plaza. You’ll encounter various enemy types ranging from your typical sharpshooter, to drones, to mecha enemies that will chase you down, and even chainsaw weilding baddies that you have to place a shot on perfectly to get past (please don't get me started on the chainsaw guys, they’re the biggest obstacle and led to more deaths than I can even remember). Jack has to make it through ten floors at a time in which he will regularly flip out screaming “WHY IS IT ALWAYS TEN FLOORS?!”, and at the end of every tenth floor is a boss waiting to challenge your ability to dodge, jump and shoot to victory. The unique thing about the boss fights is you’re not timed by 10 seconds during them, but rather a life meter that starts at 99% and dwindles as you take hits. After every ten floors things stay fresh and the game introduces new enemy types, new traps, and new abilites for you to keep the blood flow running. My one and only complaint with this entire game is that floors and layouts tend to repeat constantly, but in the end it doesn’t really matter because you’re moving at such a fast pace and the action is so intense that you don’t really notice.   The game offers the main campaign, but also an endless mode where you fight through floor after floor until you die to place your best time on the leaderboards against other players. It also offers a slew of difficulty modes ranging from a “boomer shooter” mode where you are not timed and can play as you desire, or others such as easy, normal, and perma death mode which also has a leaderboard. As of review week I’ve already been chasing other content creators scores nonstop and I know its something that is going to keep me hooked for a long time.  So, when it comes to the visuals and sound part of the game, it is purely orgasmic. This may be a bit bias, but if there was ever a game made specifically for me, it would be Mullet Mad Jack. It has a blend of 2D and 3D art style to it, and it’s absolutely beautiful. Invoking pure 90s anime aesthetics crossed with synthwave and cyberpunk vibes and visuals, Mad Jack is a feast for the eyes and the neural synapses. I know we already discussed gameplay, but the end game of the campaign mixed with the visuals and voice acting and everything else going on made me feel something no other game has ever made me feel, and the best way I could describe it is “Emotionally Horny” when trying to talk about the game to friends.  Audio wise Jacks voice actor kicks ass, and there is literally a 90’s protagonist upgrade you can get that makes him spout off one liners nonstop channeling his inner Duke Nukem or Ash Williams. The voice over work for your handler and all the other characters are top tier as well. Synthwave music accompanies you nonstop throughout all the action, and it is truly top tier stuff for the genre. Weapons all sound punchy and hit hard, notably the shotgun, which is one of the best feeling and sounding shotguns ive fired in a game in a long time. This entire game is a sensory treat.  All in all, Mullet Mad Jack is a very strong contender for my game of the year. It features Enticing roguelite gameplay that keeps you hyper focused and wanting more and more, presenting that traditional *one more run* feeling. It has references to so many greats in pop culture, one being Metal Gear which is a huge deal to me. I mean come on now, what game lets you assassinate someone with a copy of your favorite Manga? Not one that i can remember. If you’reconsidering checking out this game, I highly recommend it, you will not be disappointed, and thats a promise. After all, you want to rescue the beautiful princess and claim your prize of badass sneakers, right?

_childDocuments_.review: It's like an ADHD shooting gallery rogue-lite-lite, where you get to pick an upgrade at the start of each level and you lose all upgrades when you die, but here you only go back to the beginning of the chapter instead of the beginning of the game. You have ten seconds to live, getting shot lowers those seconds, but killing enemies gets you seconds back and if you kill them in stylish ways like headshoting them or kicking them into THE VOID, you get extra seconds, and if you just stay still or take too long the seconds keep ticking down to death anyway, so you're constantly ping-ponging between almost death and full health every other room, the level design can kill you almost as fast as the enemies. The trap and enemy variety is great and ups the difficulty ante with each chapter, but unfortunately the bosses sucked, and it sucks there is an upgrade that lowers boss health when half of the bosses are just gimmick fights where the health doesn't matter, it's pretty much a nothing upgrade that wastes a possible upgrade slot on every floor. But otherwise, it's a pretty fantastic game, it's not about going fast so much as about dancing through enemies and level layouts, going from room to room dodging bullets and traps, while fighting the urge to just give in to the ADHD and just mash your way through everything while staring at the pretty colors.So in that sense, it's pretty much an edging simulator. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it on normal lenient difficulty (2s per kill) - finished first 3 chapters on true normal (1s per kill), but reconsidered as I wasn't having much fun retrying whole chapters at floor 8 or 9 and at the time I didn't realize how shallow and short the game is.Fantastic presentation, atmosphere, and absolutely adorable with it's dialogue and story.But the gameplay is severely sub-par. It leans hard on it's speed gimmick because it would not be a good game otherwise.Buy only if you understand that this game is all looks and almost no substance. I decided on a non-recommended verdict because I can't see myself recommending this as a game, only as a general experience.FPS game where you have 10 seconds of life and each level is mostly a linear corridor that takes around 40 seconds to finish. If you were really cool at math you'd know that you're about 30 seconds of life short to finish. That's ok, not all of us will finish before our life ends.But since this is a game and it actually wants you to play it there is a method of restoring your time. You just need to engage in various methods of carnage. Shooting enemies dead, kicking them into doors, explosive barrels, electric fences or exposed wires will all increase your time.After each level you will get to choose 1 upgrade or weapon because this is a roguelike-like. You fight a boss after 10 levels and boss fights don't have the timer. After that you get to new chapter. There are 9 chapters, but last one is just a boss fight and epilogue.The story? You are a Moderator, basically a robot hunter. You have an app on your phone that lets you compete in mercenary work and you current job is to save a female pop-star hottie from robot billionaires who want to use her to their nefarious deeds. Your reward if you complete the task before other Moderators? A new fancy pair of sneakers.There are a total of 7 weapons (that I've seen) consisting of 2 types of katanas, pistol, shotgun, uzi, railgun and plasma gun. You can only have 1 weapon at a time and if you select a new one on level up - you replace the current one. Each weapon also has 3 levels and you can upgrade them by selecting them again on new level.Whole 80s neon presentation is really well represented here. Just look at the trailers, the game really sells itself based on looks. Everything from ingame levels to animated cutscenes are fantastic.Special mention because they are really cool.One thing annoyed me, but the rest of the game works as you'd expect without any technical issues.Speed is a gimmick. It can be enjoyable, but the game around it should have been more than it is.It can be finished in less than 4h even if you die sometimes.And this 4h worth of content is really stretched out anyway. Levels barely change throughout the game, some new hazards are added like laser gates or mines and an odd new enemy sometimes, but nothing crazy is done while progressing through the levels. Only 2 enemies require you to fight them differently and even then all you need is kick them before you can do damage.Item variety is also lackluster. You lose upgrades after each chapter and upgrades are very small % increases to different things. 5% move speed? 10% crit chance? 3% chance of your shots exploding? WOW, what great choices!!! Do you seriously think that 5% movement speed is going to really change up the game?Guns are cool, but even those get old very fast because you still fight same enemies in same way over and over because of the speed gimmick.Each level is also just a glorified hallway, again, because of the speed gimmick. You can't have complex doom levels and keep the speed gimmick.If you land on an enemy, you will slide off them. I died multiple times because an enemy's head would slide me off into a bottomless pit and force me back to the start of the area where I had 0 chances of getting back fast enough to not run out of time.It was the cause of probably like 5 restarts and pretty far into the chapter too.This game really needed something more in terms of gameplay design. Having played through on the lenient mode I have no desire to advance to the harder difficulty because there's nothing here to experience past the presentation. It needed Isaac's style itemization with interesting and powerful combinations and varied enemy types that would require different approach depending on what items you have... oh but that would eat into the speed gimmick, yeah?The speed gimmick is at the center of the problems here. There are definitely people who will be able to enjoy this on a very basic level just for the experience of mastering it's mechanics. But for anyone else this is a very pretty game with a gimmick in place of substantial gameplay.I'd give Mullet Madjack a 9/10 for presentation, and a 3/10 for the gameplayBuy only for the graphics and atmosphere. I can't even fault it for costing pretty penny for how short on content it is because the graphics and cutscenes alone must've cost a lot of money, but I can't just recommend this when there's so little substance in it.Maybe if you're a huge fan of the speedrun-FPS subgenre then you'd have a different opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I've said my whole life than I'm a mechanics first gamer. I love cool worlds and good stories, but how a game plays trumps all for me. Even having not remotely finished it as I write this, I can say that Mullet Madjack is one of the mechanically tightest games I've played in years. It'll challenge you (at least on the intended difficulties) but you'll be in flow state the whole time and instantly going "one more run" whenever you die.You should just look at the trailers to get a sense of the game play as trying to describe it won't do it justice. The vibe is 80s anime through and through and the devs clearly knew exactly what style they wanted and nailed it. It's fast, fluid and vicious, laying on new traversal mechanics and enemy types every ten levels, which is when it also checkpoints for future run. This isn't really a roguelite, but it does share some similar elements of that in terms of per-run upgrades with permanent ones added after each checkpoint. Levels are so fast that even if you fail, you don't feel you've lost a ton and at least in my case, I less wanted to be frustrated and more just wanted to jump right back in. I will say that sometimes, you will suddenly die and not realize why as encounters are so rapid, you won't always get clear damage feedback. Some might get frustrated by this, but it didn't happen to me much and I was fine to not worry much about it and just restart.Beyond the campaign, there's also an endless mode and other modes besides you can unlock, with more listed as coming in the future and voted by the community to boot. This is something they clearly intend to keep supporting for a while. There's also leaderboards for those modes, which is another great addition.I'm 45 and games like this show me that I can still hold my own in fast and frantic titles, which is perhaps the best compliment I can give it. This is definitely going to be one of my favourite games of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I highly recommend this game for its price, but mostly for those seeking a fun shooter with an emphasis on dashing through levels, rather than any rogue or rogue-lite where subsequent runs will vary in playstyle like Streets of Rogue. Also Streammer is best waifu (Yes, that is how she is referred to in the art book)Pros: Easy to play, hard to master. Beautiful retro graphics, fun voice acting.Cons: Replay value is limited for a rogue-liteMullet Mad Jack is an incredibly fun and challenging first person shooter with an 80s retrofuturistic design based on 80s anime and rogue-lite elements.Its controls are much like Doom and Duke Nukem, but instead of exploration, it has an emphasis on moving through levels as quickly as possible in one smooth mad dash, using the environment as well as your shooting skills to your advantage. Your countdown is your health bar, with damage from enemies subtracting precious seconds while killing enemies refills your counter. Most levels will be completed in under a minute, and the game is so fast-paced and chaotic that it is easy enough to mistake it for a rail shooter. You kick enemies into fans, explode barrels, use your weapons to annihilate enemies as soon as you enter the room. Besides enemies, it also has a strong emphasis on first person platforming, asking you to dodge lasers, wall run across chasm, and avoid pools of acid and lava to reach the level's end point.Your gameplay will eventually come down to producing as smooth a mad dash as you can muster through a level, using the rogue-lite elements, such as exploding bullets or extra seconds, in order to more easily accomplish that.That all said, it has limited value for a rogue-lite, since levels are functionally the same in terms of your play style. Indeed, most of the weapons operate similarly enough that playing through the game with new weapons will hardly feel worth it. It is strange to say this in a game that features a Katana, a shotgun, and a rail gun, but it is true.Most of the replay value comes in mastering the gameplay more than in varying how you complete your runs.

_childDocuments_.review: Way back in the before times (of 2020) a little indie game called Post Void came out that was far better than it had any right to be for how simple it was. Go fast, hit headshots, fill your decapitated head with juice from the blood of your enemies which lets you live just a little bit longer. I'm sure there was games before Post Void that did what it did, although maybe slightly less anti-epileptic than Post Void, but Mullet Mad Jack is the evolutionary followup to Post Void and it ramps up every element of Post Void's core gameplay to 999 with an overload of lights, dopamine, 90s anime aesthetics and crazy ass robo-goons. Any faults that MMJ might have (and there are some) are more or less moot points because of the overwhelming amount of absurd and high quality art direction that you run by at 200MPH on your mad dash to the checkpoint. This is a rare instance of the trailer for a game not accurately depicting how batsh*t insane the game can be especially if you really try gunning it through the levels. A slightly more methodical approach can definitely improve your survival rate but good lord is it fun just blasting through a level like a cannonball. The basic premise for anyone who didn't get it is that you have 10 seconds to live which is granted to you by an I.V. from your phone, you are being livestreamed climbing the tower and killing Robillionaires, and the more the "chat" loves you the more it feeds Jack dopamine through the I.V. which you get from getting kills, headshots, environmental kills and a hundred other things. The gameplay loop is more or less a boomer shooter style mad dash to the exit of each level trying to time your kills to keep as much uptime as possible. I will say that there are a few enemies and obstacles that are a bit frustrating to combat beyond the point of fun (looking at you lasers that can't be jumped through safely without going at turtle speed, although you can just kick people into them to shut them off). I streamed the game on my Twitch channel originally and for the sake of that I had the difficulty on "Normal" and it proved to be a lot because talking and walking is a bit hard, but I finished the game offline (the last like 20ish floors) and was easily able to crank the difficulty up to the hard/challenge zone. I would encourage you to play on this difficulty as it is very fair if the game has your full attention and you're never so far from a checkpoint that deaths are too punishing. The developer intended difficulty was a blast. Words cannot describe how much of a, for lack of a better phrase, dopamine overload this game is. There are some stumbles with some lackluster bosses (excluding the final act), some middling upgrades and some minor bugs, but the off the walls aesthetic that gets shot straight up your nasal cavity every floor is more than enough to make up for it especially at 20 bucks full price. _childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a perfected blend of style, fast-pacing and intuitive gameplay in an ultra condensed package.Disclaimer: the game was played on the "Challenge" difficulty, which in-game is represented as the intended way to play the game by the developers.At first, it may seem like this FPS is just press forward and shoot whatever is on the way while you pass through the rooms. But the player will quickly learn that even if a ten second clock is ticking constantly, one must take a moment to assess the situations and take quick decisions about how to clear the rooms effectively (With high countdown number and taking the items to perform executions). Doing this process at first may prove difficult due to how fast the game and the protagonist moves, the constant or immediate reaction of the enemies and the countdown, but after mastering it, it feels just like watching an Action Film, pure awesomeness.The visuals are clear and give the player the needed feedback to take quick decisions on the flow of the gameplay, while also looking awesome on static screenshots, how can this game look so good??? The music also acompanies the gameplay and the cutscenes perfectly, truly a love letter to the era.Even if the game looks daunting or too easy for you, the game offers several difficulty levels that range from "No countdown mode", and the hardest modes which decrease the Countdown seconds, give less seconds as a reward for killing enemies, enemies do more damage, etc...I think the only reason one would not try this game is because he/she doesn't like the aesthetics.9/10 would rescue the princess again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game took POST VOID and expanded on it PERFECTLY. Don't listen to the people who say it's a blatant ripoff (most of them are probably just baiting clown reactions tbh). I also saw some complaints about the game being short. That is only the case if you play on a lower difficulty the first time around, or if you refuse to replay the game. Speaking of replayability, this game is super fun to player over and over again. This is one of those titles I could easily see being a real cabinet I would find going into an arcade. Playing this game gives me the same feeling as finding an awesome arcade cabinet and gluing myself to it for hours. This is where its replayability comes from. If its easy to you, you'll find yourself replaying it just to get a better score or time. If its hard to you, you'll replay it for the challenge.If you enjoyed playing POST VOID, or just like fast time-based shooters like Neon White, you'll love this game too.
