_childDocuments_.review: is a fast paced boomer-shooter roguelite set in the year 2095.The game is set in the year of 2095 in which robot billionaires have taken over the world and humans are highly addicted to dopamine. The player controls Jack who is a so-called moderator who was hired by Peace Corp. to rescue the Influencer Princess who is being held hostage in a massive skyscraper filled with killer robots. The princess is located 10 floors above you and you only have 10 seconds to reach the exit of each floor, sounds easy right?I played the demo of  earlier this year and it instantly hooked me despite not being a huge fan of boomer-shooters but the fast paced action and the setting itself just made me like the demo a lot when I played it.The game itself was released not too long after I’ve played the demo and I purchased it fairly shortly after the release. The game feels good. It’s fast paced and the gameplay loop is straight forward: Your timer ticks down, killing robots gives time – dopamine goes brr; or something like that.Quite honestly the story itself is okay but nothing special, right? It kind of has the whole Mario vibe. You finish the 10 floors; you defeat a boss and the princess is  on another floor. Despite this sounding a bit whack, the story has certainly its moments, especially the epilogue and the whole premise of the game itself is quite interesting.The gameplay loop is satisfying. The bosses are quite simple but can be a challenge on higher difficulties. Clearing a floor gives you an opportunity to buy new guns or new passive effects and defeating a boss grants you some permanent upgrades – so pretty standard roguelite elements that mix well with the whole fast boomer-shooter gameplay.The upgrades that you get after every floor feel fair and nice. If you have a good gun and some good upgrades you will probably do more than well – especially in the endless mode in which your timer gets reduced by 1 second every 10 floors which makes the game harder after you’ve reached floor 40 since you will only have 7 seconds to complete the level; that means that getting hit and not instantly killing a robot could be fatal.The art-style, the graphics, the music and the overall vibe of the game are great. It’s essentially a retro anime with a beefy male protagonist that yells those 90s action movie slogans every so often.The length of the game isn’t too crazy either. It took me around 3 hours to finish the game which is alright since there is the previously mentioned endless mode in which you can unlock some more cosmetics and if you like to go for achievements there is a few of them that require you to play through the game on higher difficulties and such – so there is replay value for sure. I hope that there will me some more content update in the future though.Speaking of different difficulties: There’s also a difficulty which removes the timer and changes the gameplay from a fast first-person-shooter to a boomer-shooter that let’s you play the game without needing to worry about the timer and such. I personally think it’s a nice idea but it’s certainly not meant to be played like this but it might be fun for some people that have beaten the game already and want to try something new. There’s also an achievement for completing the whole game in that mode. Is  worth your money? Yeah sure. It depends on what you want from a game.If you go after the whole “1 Euro = 1 Hour” thing I’d say that it’s best to buy it on sale if you only plan on playing through it once without messing around with harder difficulties or with the endless mode.For me personally, I bought it with the 20% off deal and I have to say that it’s worth it for me. I will probably mess around with the endless mode a bit and hope that the developers add some more content in the future since it’s a pretty good game that has a cool setting and great aesthetics.There should be a demo available so you could just mess around with that before you decide on getting it or not.“” - JackIf you found this review helpful, feel free to visit my  page.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is a fun, fast-paced boomer shooter, with a very stylized 80's aesthetic. I enjoyed my 9 hours I got out of it, even if I don't think I'll play it again. After beating the game, there isn't a lot of incentive to replay other than beating your high score. There aren't enough weapons and abilities to make experimenting with combinations worthwhile. The only reward to unlock is a new skin for your shoes, something you only see when you kick an enemy. The irony is, the game is not subtle about making fun of the dopamine-triggering gameplay loop that boomer-shooters rely on, yet there isn't a whole lot to keep you coming back for more. It feels like there was supposed to be more to the game that never got fleshed out, and probably never will be. The animations and cutscenes are great. The voice acting is not. I wanted to like the main villain because the character design is neat, but then he opened his mouth. The game seems to want you to take him seriously, so it's unfortunate that his voice actor in particular sounds like a 4chan edgelord with VoiceMod. At the end of the day, I got my $20 worth, but there are a lot of other games I got a lot more gameplay out of for $20. I would buy it in a bundle or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a game I had to play for about 15 minutes to understand its premise, and I just don't like it. The game prides itself on being an anime, but feels more like a soul-less parody of anime (like something you'd see on Newgrounds, or that one episode of South Park) than something made by people who actually like anime. The only thing anime about this game is the fact that the protagonist is basically the result of going to an artist and asking them to draw the guy from City Hunter from memory. The only thing that feels anime about it is the absolutely godawful voiceacting, which does in fact sound like the kind of horrid dub jobs companies would crap out for a quick buck. Quick **** you to Vic Ireland. The opening cutscene has the Akira bike slide (HEY GUYS, REMEMBER AKIRA? THAT QUIRKY 80S ANIME FILM?) and a pan over a bumper sticker on the protagonist's car that reads "Shonen", presumably to remind us that a 12-year-old could probably make a more original game than this.Anyway, this game isn't a shooter - it's one of those infinite runner games. You have a 10-second time limit that extends by killing enemies.. except on higher difficulties where only environmental kills count. Even on the lower difficulties, the guns are useless unless you are constantly landing perfect headshots all the time, because otherwise the enemies are bullet sponges who can eat an entire magazine to the chest and not flinch. No, the solution here is to simply spam the "kick" button and kick all the enemies into the giant fans/explosive barrels/exposed electrical panels they're standing directly in front of. On any difficulty below "hard", you can win the game by setting up an auto-clicker on the kick button and holding W. On the harder difficulties, the game is an infinite runner about kicking the right enemies into environment hazards while ignoring everything else. There are also roguelike upgrades, which are for the most part the single most milquetoast thing ever: you can get a whopping 3% chance of one of your bullets (which, on harder difficulties, you are NEVER GOING TO USE) exploding if you shoot an enemy with it, or "up to" 5% faster movement speed. About the only upgrades that are worth it are the ones that give you more time for kills, the rest are so negligible they might as well not exist.The best thing you can do with this game is make like the editorial board at Weekly Shonen Jump and axe it from your hard drive, preferably getting a refund on the way.

_childDocuments_.review: No-nonsense first person shooter that did what Doom 2016 did - chose a genre and kept everything relatively simple. The game is fast paced adrenaline rush that doesn't leave you much time to think. And that's the beauty of it. You're not supposed to. This game is meant to be played like your very life depends on you moving as fast as possible - which it technically does; within the game world, that is.Right from the start you go in hard and fast; like a macaque hopped up in dozens of different illicit drugs up to its eyeballs with a fully loaded AK-47 in its hands. The colorful aesthetics, the music, and the sounds design are straight up from the '80 and '90 that hits a boomer like me like a 30 ton 18 wheeler going down the highway at 120 mph! The game is visually gorgeous, and any friend of beautiful 2D-art is going to be enjoy shooting, kicking, smashing and slicing their way through this game as the game's dopamine addicted protagonist. As you beat each floor, you get to choose an upgrade from three randomly selected ones, until you beat the a boss at every 10th level, after which you can choose a permanent upgrade before losing the temporary ones. This repeats until you reach the end, after which you unlock the next stage. There is an endless mode for those, who want to keep on going after beating the game or even before it, so fear not - you can still keep the carnage going for as long as you like. The levels are all proceduraly generated, so no two levels should be quite the same.I'm not going to spoil the plot to anyone reading this, what little there exists within the game, but I do have to say it is straightforward but ingenious at the same time. But nobody is going to play this game for its plot. You are going to play it for the gameplay. Though some of the mechanics in the game are bit clunky, like the wall-running that feels like you're grinding your face against the wall while you're doing it, they get the job done and that is all that matters to me in the end.If you're looking for a fast and fun shooter that doesn't require you to think much - just react fast and be quick to aim and shoot - this is the game for you. Clearing a floor takes from somewhere between 30 to 55 seconds, and clearing a stage (10 floors) is around ten minutes approximately - after which the game saves your progress, which allows you to quit the game and come back later. Also, if you die before the boss stage, you get booted back to the first floor of the stage, with all your upgrades lost into the void - forcing you to earn them back as you fight your way back up.All in all, I found the game a fun experience and would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of old '80's and '90's Anime, fast old school first person shooters, and/or just adrenaline junkie.

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had with a movement shooter in a while. Excellent visuals, great soundtrack, satisfying sound effects for every weapon, witty one liners, and MULLETS. The game has it all.There's even a button just for giving the player an interactive experience of opening up a big game box with all the goodies inside as though you were actually in the 90's unboxing your new acquisition, which is a very specific kind of novelty that you'll spend 3 minutes on at best, but one that I appreciate nonetheless.I'd also like to highlight the fact that despite the game being built around randomly generated levels, you can still turn on a switch that makes it so the levels follow a specific order, as well as a general timer for a speedrun, as opposed to having to rely solely on each chapter's individual timer.This game also marks the quickest I've ever aimed for 100% achievements, at roughly 5 days. Though I do have a few criticisms. One of them being that the levels look a tad similar to each other. Even if makes sense that the scenery looks similar, on account of the game taking place inside one individual building, the fact still stands that it IS a videogame, so some rules can be bent. I also think that there should be more enemies in the game, since after a while it can feel a bit too repetitive, specially in Survival Mode and it's variants.I also believe that stackable upgrades should actually stack in the upgrades menu, as opposed to stealing multiple slots all to themselves, which just clogs up the table, and ruin builds.The Railgun and Plasma Guns look too similar to one another, given how distinct every other weapon looks in the game, it irks me that these two in particular are near identical, specially when they both play very differently. I also think that there should have been some more variety between the aforementioned weapons upgrades as well as Rifle, since as it stands, the Rifle is pretty much preferable to the Plasma Gun almost every time on account of both of them receiving an infinite ammo upgrade, but the Rifle benefitting from more damage, as well as a grenade at maximum level (even if I do have grievances with it, as detailed below). Speaking of, said grenade I feel should be set to a button (perhaps middle mouse button, since it serves no function in this game), and not a random timer, as the times it's shot at nothing tend to outweigh the times it's made to actually hit something.I also appreciate the fact the developers have since added more game modes for further replayability, including, but not limited to, making the Sniper segment playable separately, which was a weird ommission from the base game. (The new voice lines are much appreciated as well!)In conclusion, if you like running against a clock that's constantly trying to kill you while you slice, shoot, dash and kick those DAMN robots to the sound of 90's inspired tracks, while pondering about the effects of excessive consumerism on "retro humans" and the commodification of death, then you might want to give this a shot. Just be prepared to die and to be made fun of for it by a sassy anime lady... A LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long while since a game managed to disappoint me as much as this one.I wanted to love this game, because I've been a shooter fan since the '90s and this looked promising. But in my opinion it flopped hard.The story is... Terrible. Perhaps the single worst story I've encountered in a video game. Basically, you're meant to save a popular streamer who got kidnapped, and your attempt is aired live as well for everyone to enjoy while the stream's host spams you with dated memes that don't even fit what's going on. You only have 10 seconds to live, but every kill or cool action gives you... life juice or something.It's also incredibly easy. I played on Challenge difficulty, actually died on the tutorial... And that's it. I died once there because I didn't demolish a vending machine (which refills all your HP/Time/survival gimmick) but then I made it all the way from level one to the first boss with no death. Then I quit, feeling... pretty much nothing, which isn't common for me. Nothing makes me want to go back to it. I played literally 20 minutes and beat 12.5% of the game. 5 of those 20 minutes were the main menu and cutscene.And sure, I could try one of the two harder difficulties, but speaking of levels... There are 80 of them, each lasting 30 seconds, and they're "randomly generated" - as in, they're all the same, somehow. And even if they weren't, well, it's not like you can enjoy the scenery -  after all. Besides that, it's also your standard roguelike, and each level gives you a reward, such as new weapons or stat improvements.But really, stick with the default pistol, dash a couple times, spam left click on the first enemy you see, dash again, repeat for the 5-6 more enemies you'll encounter and boom, level completed. That's the gameplay. The bosses are different and you've got extra time for them at least, but they don't save this game. There were better indie shooters released in 2024.And this game is so easy to fix, too: Write a proper story for it, make levels longer and actually different... That'd already make me go from 1.5/5 to 3/5 stars. And honestly, make roguelike optional - among all the memes in this game, its core mechanic is the most tired trend and adds nothing of value here. This game is trying hard to have an identity of its own but simply copied what's been succesful in other indies (and also borrowed the small streamer's starter pack for its visuals).Only play this if you're in love with the vaporwave aesthetic. I guess. I spent more time writing this than I played the game I'm writing about, and this was more entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: Manages to scratch that same itch of an ultra fast paced FPS roguelite with a visual assault on the senses that I loved in Post Void. Despite the maximalist super saturated colours, it is quite readable to make out the enemies and items (to the point where you don't need the enemy or item scanner upgrades), and there are even melee executions like Doom to increase your life. The story is pretty old-school and kind of sexist in using a big-boobed "virgin" damsel in distress as plot motivation for a stoic, 80s style badass hero but she becomes an actual character by the end. However, I did lile the epilogue and plot continuation to the endless mode and your PEACE CORP handler has good voice acting. The upgrades are a lot of fun in that you're looking forward to beating the levels to keep building up your powerups and modifiers to glean more seconds of life and stronger weapons, even if a shotgun, SMG, or katanas can be enough from start to finish. The levels can get very repetitive in their layouts to the point where you can notice the same five variations of the levels and enemy positions, but when you're in a flow state of speeding past the level (because you only have ten seconds to live in a very Crank-like premise), you don't mind just bopping robots in your quest to kill robobillionaires. The cyberpunk commentary is nothing new but the motivation to get a new set of sneakers is very satirical of 80s and 90s toy crazes, and the humour keeps up until the end. Even some of the bosses are gilarious like a turn-based battle or playing rock-paper-scissors with your tamagotchi. The bosses are much easier than expected and the hardest bits are actually the laser obstacles, but the game definitely gets easier as you progress, gaining permanent upgrades such as being able to keep your latest weapon or any upgrade into the next run. I do want to play more of the endless mode and upgrade all the weapons, but also katana-only runs are completely viable much like Superhot. I played on Normal and will go for the harder difficulties for replayability. It's easy to recommend if you're into anime, arcade FPSs, and some of the other games mentioned here.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is yet another one of those games that I wish I liked, but... I really just can't. Not a terrible idea at face-value: An FPS runner game, with rogue-like elements and hammy, retro-style anime visuals. But in practice, I've found this game to be kinda blah and un-engaging. I get the appeal of falling into a "flow-state" (HI, HOTLINE MIAMI!), but I never successfully got there with MMJ. Much of that comes down to the chaotic visuals and hud, which makes it more difficult to play than it needs to be. I'm not stranger to crazy boomer-shooters, but these games need to make an effort to design their visuals so you can process the situation at a glance, and I don't think MMJ succeeded in that effort (did they even make one...?).Also, this game likes to think that it's satirizing some kind of 90's anime aesthetic, but really, it's just screaming obnoxious things at you through its hectic pacing and... well, by actually screaming at you over dialogue :PSadly, MMJ is just one of those games that had a seemingly great idea that didn't really pan out in a real-world scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: This game is fun. Buy it. Do it.Ć̶͓o̴̧̭͌̉n̶̞̊s̷̫̰̿u̸̮̍͆m̶̺̈ḛ̵̯̚For the rest of us, the game is fun! The artwork is perfect, colors are bright and vibrant, speed is your best friend and your best enemy, guns are meaty and satisfying, soundtrack is amazing, the lore is not extensive but it is satisfying, making for a great setting.The good:Levels are autogenerated based off a set of templates, which can create its own set of challenges or advantages. And the more levels you do, the more hazards come into play. Because dying is quick in this game, being able to have not repeat the same level over and over is nice, but there's also the option to not have it being randomized, so you can master a map if that is what tickles your fancy. The timer is a very nice mechanic. You only have 10 seconds to live, even less if you take damage, but you can recover seconds by killing and just... Being badass. You nailed a headshot in midair? You get yourself an extra second to live, on the house. You kicked a robots to an industrial fan? That leaves a mess, but was badass, one more second.At the end of each floor, you can can get one of a selection of random upgrades, which could be guns, upgrades to said guns, speed, of just being more manly. Keeps each run different from the one before, and forces you to a different style of combat depending of what upgrades you get. The Bad:There's not enough! I did beat the game under 8 hours, on the Challenging difficulty, and I could've beaten a lot quicker if I didn't suck at games. Nonetheless, there's the need for more. A sequel, maybe a different character, different guns, new enemies, but still having you killing billionaire robots and perhaps even the peace corp. I even got some names to donate for a potential sequel:Mohawk Johnny RageMildly Angered SalarymanPonytail Chainsaw CarlFlattop Crazzy Frank, with two Z.Finally, the BR dub is just nice. I did only play briefly with BR dubbing, because I'm just so used to have everything in English, I don't consume any BR media these days and living abroad just distances me further from roots, but after reading about it, I gave it a try, and hearing voice actors that were part of my childhood was quite something.

_childDocuments_.review: After noticing this game in my recommended and deciding to pick it up, I have to say that I fell in love with this game so fast. I love the retro 80's Anime style, the music that slaps so hard to killing enemies, and the chaotic and goofy story and premise this game has. Looking at the trailers, I expected this game to be fast paced action. But THIS is really fast paced, as in having to worry about making every second count while you run and gun your way to the end of each floor is by far the most exciting part. The weapon selection was fine for the most part (although I wasn't a fan of the plasma rifle), the variety of guns and power ups can help you complete each floor easier. The story for this game is nice and short. The over the top humor and chaos never made the story feel boring, and it never outstayed its welcome. So if anyone is looking for a little bit of challenge, retro vibes, and some fun destruction. I'd say give it a try.

The guns are powerful, fun, and the fast paced nature of the game makes the whole bit that you're walking down corridors the whole time feel a lot better than it might have otherwise.  The highlight, I think, are the kills you do with your finishing moves.  They are pretty varied based on what items you pick up, and quite fun.  The roguelike nature of picking up upgrades at the end of each level is alright, though I didn't find them awesome until the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the game, and this should be the moment when I am the most hyped about the game. Instead, I am disappointed.I like anime, I like rougelites, and I like... Variety. And the last is something that this game severely lacks.Have you played the first floor? Congratulations, you have seen about 80% of what the game has to offer. Sure, it adds new enemies, but do not offer much in terms of different approaches. And the environment changes, but not much, and it is not like you will notice the difference anyway given the pace of action. The story is shallow, which is to be expected, but so is the gameplay.Tired of wiping the same looking floors? And they literally look the same, since they utilize a _very_ small number of sections as well as a tiny set of regular enemies. Well, from time to time the game offers a very short one time different gameplay mode - because it does not know how to keep you engaged with its core mechanics. And the bosses are extremely boring: all of them (beside one which is nearly a joke) are made by formula "shoot it until it dies". Moreover, they use a regular shooter format, not the main "shoot something every 10 seconds", so they noticeably break the flow.The left hand consists of a low resolution hand sprite with a higher resolution sprite of phone and fingers. A small detail, but it really irks me.It might be possible that I fell victim to my own high expectations, but I hoped to see a bit more than a flashy attraction. But this is just it, an attraction. Higher difficulty level are dumb, since they change the time balance but not enemy behaviors.If you want this game for the sake of flashy entertainment - sure, go ahead. But be warned that it might run out of steam disappointedly quickly, even before the credits start rolling.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a bit. Gets tedious after awhile... you get a pretty clear preference for weapons after maybe level 40 and each weapon only gets three levels, each of which only unlock the next level by continuing with them, but you do keep that unlock level when you resume, so if you get the shotgun to level 3 it'll always be level 3 in the future. Personally, I found the railgun the primary game breaker, instant kills on everything but kunoichi, super long range (not always a great thing if you're killing stuff at a distance but you move so fast it doesn't matter) and has a blast to take out locked doors. Pistol is reliable til the end if you're good at headshots. Etc. Shotguns don't seem to claim headshot bonus so harder to use in higher difficulties. Most bosses are pretty lame, but I liked one (floor 3 boss I think). Levels have very clearly repeating layouts after a time, so you know exactly how to move in the three "fall to your death" possible areas (forward, don't shoot the glass floors, run on wall, run forward and there's usually a chainsaw guy waiting in the middle of the fork... shoot him and jump across as one example). Game gets real preachy at the end. Most of the time you can skip cutscenes, but if you go through the credits, you're subjected to a solid two minutes of forced clicking to get through a tirade. Meh. The social commentary ain't wrong, but as the one scene you can't skip, it's real lame too. I actually found Post Void in the reviews for this game and probably enjoyed it more from a stylistic perspective, refuses to outstay its welcome. But if you went the opposite direction and you want Post Void, much longer (one set of 10 levels basically the same as the entirety of Post Void) toned down into a more straightforward cyberpunk style with a sassy protag in an anime themed hellscape, this'll keep you busy for an hour or so. There's an infinite mode that lets you try to go zen and kill forever, and that's solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, a game that has a highly repetitive gameplay loop, a single gimmick, and not a lot of variation will get slammed in Steam reviews and fail faster than one of 's levels. But this game makes it all work.There isn't a whole lot of game (git gud and you can reach the credits scroll in 2 or 3 hours) but the tongue-in-cheek humor, fast pace, secrets, and unlocks offer enough to hold your interest and keep the replayability pretty high. Multiple difficulty settings ensure that you're enjoying the game the way you want with maybe some incentives to try a harder setting... but no pressure.Some people will be drawn to the "anime on VHS" style to everything. I'm in that age range where anyone into what was "JapAnimation" at the time only had access to VHS dubs of dubs of dubs of stuff and pickin's were slim. I guess where I am going with this is that, sure, this game gets the feel almost right but it does so upon the shoulders of classic animation that time is about to forget. It's pretty on the nose, too. If you dig the main menu's loop then you'll want to find and watch:- Bubblegum Crisis- Riding Bean- Akira- Dirty Pair- MADOX-01- Dominion Tank Police- Megazone 23- City Hunter- Gall Force

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, but has a myriad of little things that all build up to major annoyances.- Chapter transitions are really long and require an excessive amount of text skipping, spam-dashing, or in one case, standing around waiting for a timer to expire.- Skipping text not always consistent.- Combos get you killed in Hard Mode because you need to wait for the combo to cash in before you actually get time back.- A LOT of pointless powerups. Why do you need an exit marker? Or see items through walls? Almost everything is a straight line so you know where to go, and items stand out pretty obviously. Talking protag is just fluff. The powerup that turns explosive canisters into ice ones is a questionable downgrade. Even the Shield Dash and Boss Damage bonuses are useless on Chapter7, as shield enemies don't appear there and Chapter7 has no boss. Too much powerup pool dilution.- The Level3 pistol upgrade says it lets you shoot as fast as you can pull the trigger, but there is a pretty low cap on the firerate. It also loses the damage bonus from Level2.- You will get shot the moment you open a door and there's nothing you can do about it. Enemies have instantaneous reaction and will shoot you the nanosecond the door is registered as open. The amount of runs that end from these is ridiculous.- Kicking enemies into lava/acid/lasers only count as basic kills instead of environmental ones, which means trying to pull off stylish kills in Hard Mode penalizes you instead.- Kicking enemies is inconsistent and does not always flinch them. You will get stabbed/shot in the face a LOT for trying to use the intended combat mechanics. And again, on hard mode this is a death sentence.- One of the chapters gives you a glitch effect on-screen which is extremely chunky and disorienting. There are options to turn off debilitating effects, but not this one. Guaranteed migraine inducer.- The sniper rifle zoom/scope is rubbish and never zooms to where you're pointing. Not sure if this is intentional since it's for a boss/joke fight but it's still very annoying.There are a lot of good things about the game. If you are playing on normal mode or the no-time mode, it's a mostly chill playthrough with some goofs and gaffs. The difficulty spike comes from the very unbalanced RNG, of which the harder difficulties are not balanced around at all.Maybe with time and updates these will get improved, but currently doing the harder difficulties is just a speedrun to find the point where you hit alt+f4.

_childDocuments_.review: In a very distant future, humanity has merged with the internet and is ruled by a cruel robot billionaires known as “robillionaires”. Our hero, Mullet Mad Jack, is a robo-killer called moderator with the objective of saving a hostage locked up on the 10th floor of a tower. The problem is that Moderator only has 10 seconds to live and constantly needs dopamine in order to survive. The only way of extending his life is by killing robots, thereby holding the interest of the viewers of a brutal livestream show. The plot is a bit simple, but it’s narrated in a really fabulous way, with a very distinctive ‘90s cyberpunk anime style that is simply gorgeous. There is also a lot of environmental storytelling such as wall posters, graffiti, tv screens and vending machines, but unfortunately you don’t really have time to stop and admire them. There are also some over-the-top moments that take place during boss fights or when you get closer to your objective, with funny dialogues and meta-references. Speaking of which, I recommend reading the in-game digital manual (yes, they still exist) with all the story, characters and gameplay descriptions, which also unlocks a new weapon as a form of thank you for unboxing the manual and legally owning the game.Gameplay-wise, Mullet Mad Jack is a great mix of FPS games like ,  and , but with a distinctive roguelike progression that makes it more similar to , a lesser known game that is equally worth playing. Each level is a race from start to finish as you run, dash and destroy enemies to gain more life time. You start with one weapon and through each floor you can swap between random weapons and upgrades. While you constantly need to check your available time, you also need to take care of your health and quickly restore it by destroying vending machines and getting a drink. Dying means losing all weapons and upgrades, as well restarting the chapter you are playing, which is made of 10 levels (floors). There are 10 chapters in total and each one adds more gameplay elements, such as environmental hazards, new enemies and mechanics (wall running for instance). Overall, it’s a really fast-paced and adrenalin-fueled gameplay structure, with each level lasting around 40 seconds – 1 minute depending on your speed and ability. This can make the game incredibly short or slightly longer depending on your skills, but in my experience the length is adequate, even if the difficulty at the default setting isn’t really enough for someone who loves this kind of games. Fortunately, there are more difficulty options that can reduce your life time and increase the enemy damage, so the game can get really challenging if you want. Speed runners will also have a fun time climbing the global leaderboard, which can be accessed from the main menu. Technically there is a lot of replayability here, including a separate Endless Mode, and hopefully the game will be long supported with updates and DLCs, yet the thing that didn’t entirely convince me is the level design. Despite the beautiful aesthetic of each level, they tend to be a bit too similar, with the same type of generic assets, corridors, doors, vents and acid lava pits. I was also expecting enemies to be more varied, especially during the later chapters, because despite their beautiful cybernetic design the same ones are too often repeated through each level. Boss fights are different and cool enough, but as you can image, they don’t last for too long.Overall, Mullet Mad Jack is a very addictive game that will easily capture your soul with its beautiful anime visuals and dystopian cyberpunk story. It’s an FPS filled with adrenaline, violence and nostalgia for the ‘90s that doesn’t last too long unless you play at higher difficulties or want to test your speed running skills against your friends and the entire Steam community.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is a first person shooter that gets right to the point: kill robots to get more time and complete the stage. This simple premise is clothed in an eye-popping retro anime artstyle that will grab your attention at every moment.While the basic gameplay is straightforward, the means at the player's disposal are numerous. Various upgradeable weapons including gatling railguns and elemental katanas give you ample room to get creative. Upgrades obtained between stages can be synergized into powerful combinations. For example, one upgrade spawns more explosive barrels, another gives you bonus time when you explode enemies, and yet another gives your bullets a chance to explode. Breaking up the lightning-fast combat are boss fights, many of which require the player to think outside of the box to overcome.Mullet Mad Jack's Endless Mode gives the player a quick way to enjoy the game's adrenaline-pumping action in a more direct fashion and is a great way to play once you complete the story mode. The game is a labor of love and the developers clearly put a lot of care into making it. Having completed Mullet Mad Jack, I find myself eager to keep picking it back up, whether to complete harder difficulties or enjoy more heart-thumping action!

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in about 3 hours. I want to say I like it but I just can't. Strange that this game is getting overwhelmingly positive reviews. Here is a break down:Game play 5/10Definitely not a "boomer shooter". The game encourages speed over exploration or interest in more complex fights than just going fast. There is some fun in learning the rhythm but it becomes repetitive quickly. Certain guns ruin the run, never pick plasma gun or rail gun.Trying to make a "build" like other rogue likes isn't really a thing. Just gotta go fast! Style 9/10Love the retro anime style. The bright colors and vapor wave is great. Only complaint is the amount of things that can pop up on the screen all at once. Story 5/10This is disappointing because I see parts that could have been really interesting. The main bad guy is good and his evil plot is unique. There are mixed ideological messages throughout the game. That in itself isn't a problem it just didn't make any sense. The ending monologue about the shoes was way too long and terrible.So maybe it's just not my kind of game, clearly there are people who love it. tldr:Zoomer game. Speedrunner game? Not much to the game. Finished it in 3 hours and endless mode does not interest me.

_childDocuments_.review: Received the game as a gift from a friend.That said, at time of writing, I have completed 100% of Steam achievements, though I still have a few more pairs of shoes to get. I've done endless mode up to floor 53 as well.So, as for whether I recommend it: yes, as long as you're a fan of this kind of game. So to start, the positives:The Action: blood pumping, wild, stimulating, my dopamine needs have been drowned. You can approach it a few ways, regardless of your skill level. If you're a button masher that slams the shift key & swings a katana like a one legged blender, you'll be happy. If you've got the reaction time and reflexes of a robot to catch headshots with a railgun as you move at full speed through hallways, you'll love it.The Art: In gameplay, the game is crisp, in cutscenes they have that special old school anime vibe to them that is absolutely perfect. It's that perfect combination of vaporwave, old school anime, and retro gaming vibes that it scratches that something special for me.The voice acting: Personally, I love it. All the Duke Nukem style one liners, the Peace Corp commentary, Mr Bullet screaming "MULLET", its' all just so perfect that it both brings you back in time and puts a smile on your face.The Bad:The Story Length: This is really the only thing I can find any sort of real issue with. I would have liked the story to go longer, but that said, I don't fault the dev for this, because for an indie dev's first game on steam, All of what you get is just so great. So really, my only direct critique is: I'd love to have more (but then again, doesn't everyone).Really, I think the game is amazing. But, I do think it isn't for everyone. Some people like a game to relax with, I don't feel relaxed playing this game, I feel absolutely pumped and hyped. I played it late at night, and when I stopped I felt more awake than I did when I started.That said, watch the gameplay a bit. If after one minute of gameplay (approximately 1~4 floors of the story mode) it seems like the game for you, I'd absolutely recommend it.I sincerely hope to see more of this developer's work in the future (and I hope the robillionaires are willing to throw their cash at him) because if they ever make another game with the same vibes (does not even need to be the same exact type) I would absolutely buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is not only a great potential masterpiece of a 2024 shooter but for me personally it's one of the better rogue-likes! The titular Jack is what you get in the form of a Macho anime Husbando if the T-800 and Big Trouble In Little China's Jack Burton did a Dragonball fusion with this Jack being a lollipop chomper like Kojak rather than a stogie chomper like Duke Nukem. Like Duke himself though you occasionally get the option via stage completion pickups to give Jack the ability to spew out one-liners. There also level completion purchases for weapons and weapon upgrades. From shotguns, SMGs, Doom style plasma guns, and even Quake 2/OG Shadow Warrior style rail guns, as well as a weapon or two to unlock after completing the game the first play through. You also have a melee weapon in a Katana sword where with upgrades you can do Scorpion or Liu Kang from Mortal Kombat style fire abilities or Sub-Zero style ice abilities. They're two different achievements that involve shooting enemies in the groin in an obviously more brutal fashion than Johnny Cage simply doing his nutcracker split punch! There is also a Classic Super Mario Bros. style reference when you finish the first two floors after completing the boss fights. Out of the nine total boss fights; three of them are rather unique compared to the rest of the six. The old school anime in a cyberpunk-world atmosphere was another appeal for me alongside me being an old school first person shooter enthusiast. My Steam friend in the YouTube famous Zlimbratski himself recommends MULLET MADJACK as do I!

_childDocuments_.review: A game so dedicated to its retro-80s-gamer-nostalgia aesthetic it has an attract mode (look it up, youngin'). Soon as I saw that and heard the opening theme I knew I was in for a treat. The older I get, the more partial I find myself to tight, focused experiences like Mullet Mad Jack. The synthwave soundtrack, neon-saturated visuals, and fast paced gameplay all make for an enjoyable arcadey experience that almost makes you forget you're playing what is technically an FPS roguelike (as opposed to a meticulously crafted "boomer shooter"). Whether you play for five minutes or five hours, you can feel like you made progress, as the game saves after every ten floors you clear, a process that doesn't usually take more than fifteen minutes. However, because Jack only has ten seconds to live, I often found myself focusing on keeping the ten second timer (that also doubles as a health bar) maxed out at all times, often to the exclusion of nearly everything else; this is a game where you can spend the entire time staring at the timer, and next thing you know, you've blinked and the credits are rolling. Despite these minor complaints, I still highly recommend it, and kudos to the devs for releasing the soundtrack AND and an artbook; not enough devs do that these days.

The game also has a 'no timer' difficulty level for those players who would like to take their time and experience the game as a classic 'boomer shooter'—an cool option to have, in my opinion. Loved the game; props to the devs for making such fluid and responsive gameplay with some really stylish aesthetics!

_childDocuments_.review: A great, but rather short experience best enjoyed at a sale, I think. It's definitely worth a pickup if you ever have a chance to play it as this game absolutely oozes style through it's 90's anime inspired retrowave/cyberpunk aesthetic with a VHS filter on top of it all to really bring home an authentic feeling experience that makes you feel like you're playing through a 90's action anime -- with all of it's hijinks. So what's it like? It's rogue lite boomer shooter, but I would argue that it's a "puzzle shooter" in a way. A lot of the system mastery of this game comes from the ability to quickly recognize patterns and capitalize on those opportunities via the various environmental death hazards present in each floor.This unfortunately means that mastery of the mechanics will come rather quickly once that pattern recognition sets in, and the only way to really "do more" with the experience is basically be able to interact with these patters quicker. It's admittedly a bit shallow for my liking, and it wears off its welcome fairly fast. For the people who absolutely want to push this game to it's theoretical mechanical limits though, the endless mode is available to give you a more traditional roguelike shooter experience. As for me? I enjoyed it. It was a solid game with very charming visuals, but the lack of meat really keeps this game from being anything over a 6/10 for me personally.

_childDocuments_.review: pros: - the live streamer "dopaminepunk" setting is unique and kind of cool- the retro anime aesthetic is cool- the gameplay rewards playing stylishly a lot, you rely on stylish kills to stay alive. it keeps you on the move constantly, theres no time to think you have to make quick snap second decisions to try to stay alive.a lot of your success comes down to instinct. very dynamic and fluid. - the extreme commitment to linearity is refreshing compared to most modern games, even including modern fps games. sometimes you dont care about exploring for the nooks and crannies in each stage you just want to run forward, shoot stuff and kick ass and thats exactly what you do here. - gunplay feels very frantic, weighty, intuitive and visceral. it really nails the "kickass" feel of boomer shooters and action games to a t- fun as ♥♥♥♥- fun as ♥♥♥♥cons:- level design lacks variety and makes the game feel somewhat repetitive. each level feels samey, same enemies, same hazards. you do get new types of "rooms" after completing each chapter(like the lava room for example) but the majority of the time its the same corridor with fan hazards, electric vents, exploding barrels and soda can machines. - bosses are extremely weak and dont feel rewarding to beat- there are some balance issues with the upgrades. the triple barrel shotgun overshadows pretty much every gun in late game, turning it into a point and click fest. it is essential for handling the shield enemies. the 3 second slowdown upgrade is basically a cheat code. its almost impossible to lose once you find that as it gives you the time you need to dodge anything and shoot anything in sight within those 3 seconds. if you also get the permanent upgrade that lets you choose which one to keep, you can hold onto the 3 sec slowdown for however long you want. - story had a lot of potential with the unique and interesting streamer/corporation based premise but completely squandered it for a generic mishmash of the "the princess is in another castle" and "the ritual to open the gate to hell will be complete muahuahuahuha" tropes. i dont think this is that big of a deal since this is clearly a very gameplay focused game however. overall, this game is still EXTREMELY fun to play, despite some of these pet peeves i have with it. if you love video games, and if you love action games or arcade fps, you have to play this. i would give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Here you are, riding your crimson car, waiting for your next call that will send you on your next mission where you will destroy another thousand of robots for the amusement of the crowd. In ancient times, people like you were known as "Gladiators," but now you are called "Moderators." A bloody wire is inserted into your body like a shackle, filling your body with dopamine to keep you alive for longer than ten seconds. Yes, you are truly a   of this eternal coliseum. However, to some extent, your fate is more in your control than that of the young maiden who is captured by a wealthy but twisted robot in search of something beyond reality. However, I wouldn’t take his faith seriously, because he’s just an instrument of entertainment like you, right?Fight in an ever-changing labyrinth against an "iron mass" that seeks to reduce your life timer to two zeros. But, ironically, this "iron mass" is your life source, right? To survive, you must dance this deadly waltz, sweeping from room to room, leaving destruction and death in your wake. Shoot'em in the head (or anywhere else), kick into traps, tear into pieces or simply destroy them all so that the crowd rejoices at this farce and gives you more of this ambrosia called “like”! Fortunately, your masters generously rewarded you with a rich arsenal of chaos. From the ancient sword of honor to a futuristic blaster of control! Also, every tool in your way became a torture device for those machines! So much carnage, and for what? For a pair of fancy boots? And here you are, cut from a network of bloodlust, into the darkest place before your big challenge. Don't you think that is strange? No one can give you that "dopamine nectar" to support your short life, and here you are, still breathing even after ten seconds of silence. Oh, sorry, I forgot that you don't have time to reflect on that trivial topic! Now you have a big bad boss to demolish. Well, you've passed this test and head to the next room, but... what did they say in that old game? "Your princess is in another castle"! And that bloody cycle begins anew. New floors, new deaths, new mockery... Until you've finally reached that so called "ROBILLIONER", ripped his shell and saved that lady called "Influencer"... But is this truly the end of this nightmare? Do you really have this "final goal"? Or is it actually just a false "promised land", and now you are stuck in this cycle until the crowd gets tired of you?Do you actually do all of this just for a pair of shoes? Or do you just want to save that girl you barely know? Or are you just frustrated with this farce, but just can't break free of that cursed cycle and just take it out on these robots to distract your mind from despair?Well, for now, this cycle is unbreakable. The endless maze of violence is still full of iron prey. So take that gun and sink into a dopamine rush! Right now, is the only thing you can do, my mighty Retro-human!"

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a great arcade shooter that blends quirky humor with fast-paced action. The game's vibrant pixel art style immediately captures your attention, evoking a strong sense of nostalgia for classic 80s and 90s video games while having detailed environments, characters that pop with personality and beautifully animated cutscenes. The soundtrack is equally impressive, featuring catchy, upbeat tunes that perfectly complement the high-energy gameplay. The gameplay feels great, the guns have great impact and the enemies explode with impact. The timer keeps you engaged and on edge the whole time and they've done an amazing job of keeping the pace high while not feeling overwhelming. I think this is a must play for any fan of shooters.9/10 (Amazing)

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is an adrenaline high that's over almost as soon as it starts. Every level is a rush and getting into the flow state feels great, and the passive upgrades have you feeling pretty powerful by the end of each 10-level chunk. My only complaints are that enemies just kind of stand around and the game overall is quite easy. Not every game needs to be a crucible but I wish there was a little more meat on the challenge bones here. It's also  short; I beat the campaign in a little over 2 hours on the "Challenge" difficulty. I'll leave it up to you on whether or not the game's price reflects value. This is possibly the first game whose endless mode doesn't feel entirely tacked on. The core concept of ascending a building floor by floor is the perfect fit for a never ending murder frenzy and I actually enjoyed my time with it. Most FPS in this style that do an endless mode wall off some base levels and vomit enemies at you which I'm never inclined to bother with.

_childDocuments_.review: Is there anything better than just stumbling over a videogame that turns out to be awesome? Currently out for the count with Covid, I found myself browsing Steam to add to my ever-increasing backlog, and this anime-inspired gem just leapt out of the screen. Sporting a sexy 80's anime aesthetic (the game says 90's but this looks more like Bubblegum Crisis or Riding Bean to me), complete with VHS-style artifacts, Mullet Mad Jack is an anime fan's FPS dream come true. Set in a cyberpunk future (depicted as only 80's/90's anime could dream of, all neon colours and graffiti) humanity is unemployed while AI robots (Robillionaires) live the good life. Mad Jack is tasked with rescuing an idol that has been kidnapped and must ascend 10 floors to get the girl, while kicking robot ass. However, you start with just 10 seconds to live, each kill granting precious seconds of extra life as you race to the exit utilising all the skill, speed and violence you can muster. The game has an incredible sense of urgency thanks to the pumping soundtrack, smooth graphics and corridor style gameplay. Your can shoot, kick and slide your way past your enemies, using environmental items like fans or electric boards to kill your enemies, or just headshot the robo-thugs for a clean kill. Every level you progress allows you a power up, but die and it's back to the first floor to try all over again. This decidedly brutal reset makes every kill just that bit more important.Mullet Mad Jack's presentation is what drew me in, but it was the adrenaline that kept me hooked all night. The upgrades allow you to customise your play style, kills are immensely satisfying and most importantly, my own deaths were entirely due to my own mistakes (or let's be honest, mad panic as things get hectic and I'm just missing every shot!) so it never feels frustrating despite the punishment of a total reset on dying.A special mention for voice actor Kat Dannes, she's perfect as your sassy operator who seemingly delights in both your successes and failures and just brings the game to life.I think this might also be the first time I've kicked myself for just buying the vanilla version of the game, because the soundtrack by Fernando Pepe and Mateus Polati is superb. I'll be keeping an eye out for a vinyl release because the retro-futuristic smooth opening alone makes it deserving of a place in my collection, but it's all absolute gold. It makes me want to crank it up on the car stereo and just cruise around at night. Ultimately, I adore this game. It runs smooth as silk on the Steam Deck, so good news for blasters on the move. Honestly, I just want more of everything - a physical special edition release, LP, artbook, all of it. It's pure fun and I can't recommend it highly enough. The studio is now on my watch list.

_childDocuments_.review: 'If Hotline Miami was an early 90's action OVA.' It definitely captures that same feeling of having to move fast and time your kills to the music. Punishingly difficult when things don't go your way, but a massive power trip when you get everything just right. The mechanic of only having 10s seconds of life (extended by kills) also plays really well into that. Still, similar to Hotline Miami, it also kinda loses it's meaning (at least for me) after you've beaten the story once (took me 7 hours, probably less if you don't suck at FPSes like i do), so keep that in mind. Still, for the time I played, I was completely in awe, and I really think this game is one-of-a-kind in every sense of the word and not just as throwaway figure of speech. The over-the-top and darkly humorous story and setting, synthwave-inspired soundtrack, stupidly cheesy one-liners and the 90's OVA aesthetic all play work really together other and so, I was completely absorbed for the whole of my first playthrough, and the game will likely leave an impression on me long after I've stopped playing it.My only two gripes, are firstly the environmental hazards and jumping, which while not directly fatal, still eat your timer away and I've had so many good runs completely ruined just for walking carelessly into a laser fence or messing up a jump. Thankfully, there's no real downsides in losing and going again until you get it right.  The second gripe, which is the major kicker, is the same as I also have for Hotline Miami, namely that I don't feel much of a reason to play more after beating the story for the first time. For myself, the normal difficulty is already hard enough, the next difficulty above that feels just plain unfair, so forcing myself to beat my head into wall to 'git gud' just does not inspire me.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially had many issues with this game. The repetitive four different rooms, the predictable enemy spawn locations, the limited selection of like three guns and swords, the few available power-ups, the extremely short levels, and the sound design all frustrated me. However, after playing for more than three hours, I realized I was wrong about most of these concerns.The short levels serve a purpose: they act as checkpoints that give you a brief respite before the kill timer starts again. The repetitive level design, with its close and confined claustrophobic spaces, encourages you to use the environment strategically, maneuver around enemies, or swiftly shoot them to progress to the next room. The consistent enemy spawn locations allow you to anticipate where enemies will appear, saving you from spending too much time searching for them. The limited selection of guns is intended to help you become proficient with these weapons, offering opportunities to upgrade or trade them in. While I still believe the game could benefit from more weapons, I understand the developers' rationale for their decision.One area that still needs improvement is the swords; throwing them doesn't feel powerful enough, even when aiming for headshots. On the positive side, the movement in this game is superb. Everything feels swift and flashy, with each bullet and slash registering impactfully, so you know which hits connect and which do not. The kill timer, reminiscent of the movie "Crank" and the multiplayer game mode in old-school Call of Duty games, is implemented very well here. Speed, movement, accuracy, and precision are crucial and incentivized.That being said, I still think the game is a bit pricey for the amount of content you get. However, it's worth purchasing if it genuinely looks like something you will enjoy. Keep in mind, the story isn't the focus here; in fact, the dialogue often pokes fun at itself and the fact that you're playing a protagonist within a video game. Although the game’s description and doesn't explicitly state this, it’s essentially a roguelike. Make sure you're aware of this before diving in so you don't expect a narrative and linear experience like Hi-Fi Rush. If there is anything I could compare this game to, I would say it's essentially a fps version of hotline miami, with boomer shooter and roguelike mechanics.Overall rating: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: My laptop is certified trash and I'm still able to play this game, which is something I'm very grateful for, so thank you to the devs for that. Also, I am currently on chapter 6 because of the performance issues caused by my own hardware and also by being, as the kids say these days, "bad." I might even swallow my pride and bump the difficulty down so I can finish the game this weekend, might not, who can say? Anyway.As probably a lot of folks might have, a friend introduced this to me via Alpha Beta Gamer and I was hooked on the whole visual aesthetic and gameplay loop. Admittedly, I did not play the other game that's similar to this that I imagine served as part of the inspiration for this and I will have to check that out later, but this is not about that game. Continuing on, I tried out the demo and enjoyed what was available to me, particularly the way the weapons were balanced. The only one I didn't "click" with by the end of it up to the full release was the SMG and that's entirely on myself. I value taking things out very quickly when I'm playing an FPS in general (and this game's central gimmick with the timer values it more so) and the shotgun serves that purpose well and it felt like beaning someone in the head with some SMG fire didn't instantly down them, but then again, the enemies are made of metal.As mentioned previously, I am extremely grateful that the devs have some settings in the options menu that can let my toaster play and I've run into lag spikes only in instances that they would be expected (hi, level 3 shotgun with max reload bonus) and it's been very responsive otherwise. The new enemies and hazards introduced in chapter 3 and beyond are refreshing after spending quite a bit of time with the demo, although the wallrunning prop did take me a brief moment to understand what was being asked of (you just rub against it and you will pop up once you reach the end of the track; don't mess up). Also, the laser traps are dastardly, but in a good way since some players might be all about the speed and it's effectively a speed trap to get you to pause for a second and really think about what you're doing.The new weapons that weren't in the demo, the railgun and the plasma rifle, I've had some fun with. The railgun especially just melts the more irritating standard foes but you have to watch out for the kick because that could invite trouble. The PR, to me, feels like an SMG I can gel with.But my love is with the shotgun and how I can simply turn my brain off (for the most part) and destroy everything in front of me. This shotgun easily enters the top 5 of video game shotguns because it has real range and good hitstun whenever it doesn't instantly destroy the enemy. I do enjoy all the weapons quite a bit, but I always found myself switching back to this thing because it's just so cool.On the story so far that I've reached (up to Chapter 6), I was not truly expecting so much from it, but it's still pretty good given, you know, everything. I do recommend anyone who's played so far to check out the in-game unboxing option because there's even more things to learn about the background that brings some more texture to the world, which I dug.As for things to improve, I've been seeing that some people have been having some performance issues, but I would assume the devs are aware of the situation and will address that in due time. The only other thing I would recommend is perhaps giving a few more concessions to those with photo-sensitivity issues (I am not personally affected by this, but I do have friends and associates who are), but I would want those people to speak up more about that as they would know more than I do on that matter so that the game could have more of an audience, and I do ultimately understand if it proves to be too difficult for the devs to do that considering other things they might want to take care of first and foremost.Bottom line, this game's good if you're able to pick up what it's putting down and as long as you're not at risk with flashing lights, it's definitely worth the price of admission.

It's crazy how indie devs can make better games than multi million dollar corporations, no battle passes, dlcs on realease, or any other anti consumer practises, just pure art.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: This can't be an indie game. This game is dripping with personality and charm. It is so so so good. I have not had this much fun with a FPS in a while. Loaded with unique mechanics, awesome visuals, and good old fashion cutscenes. The story is actually really really good. I could watch a movie based on this game. As long as it is exactly like the game that is. I don't have any complaints about Mullet Mad Jack either. From the gameplay, the shooting, the music and even the voice actors, its really hard to believe this is Indie. You want a fast paced first person shooter that does its own thing and breaks up the monotony of most fps games, look no further!!
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: So you're telling me that a group of people took the underrated and underappreciated core game play loop of "The Club", gave it some rouge-lite elements, polished the controls to a mirror sheen to where if I screw up I KNOW it's my fault, set it in a 90's anime, gave it a retrowave soundtrack - AND IT LETS ME SHOOT BILLIONAIRES IN THE ♥♥♥♥?!I don't know where the story is going to go at this point and frankly, if that aspect of the game falls a little short (Which I don't see happening, it seems like they had a clear vision) - I will not mind. The presentation is so unbelievably well done, they deserve recognition for that alone.Is this a candidate for "indie game of the year"?I'd be lying to your face if I wrote "Probably Not."
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS AMAZING!The pure adrenaline shooting, the synth-wave tracks, the old-school references and jokes! I am always getting first the narrator upgrade :)The gameplay feels sweet and smooth, so many builds possible I want to try!  I beat the story and still want to try more and get better, feels challenging and rewarding.So buy this game, worth every cent!
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is a single-player fast-paced FPS that brings you directly inside a CLASSIC ANIME. Power up your character and reach the last floor; Beat your best time or try again. Haste makes waste… OF YOUR ENEMIES!

name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions
detailed_description: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a gamified focus tool, set to a soothing lofi soundtrack. Discover and collect Spirits, customize your cozy virtual space, and facilitate your real-life tasks with a collection of handy features designed to improve concentration and ease stress. CHILL LOFI BEATS AND SOUNDS Soft, soothing lofi music and dynamic soundscapes such as pattering rain and crackling fire provide the perfect background ambiance to relieve stress and unwind. All music in game is courtesy of Homework Radio and fully stream-friendly, perfect for featuring on youtube or twitch as a pleasing background. SHOW OFF YOUR STYLE Customize both your character and your bedroom to suit your mood, selecting from a multitude of fashion, hairstyle, color, and room decor options. From hoodies to horns, bookshelves to boba teas, fairy lights to fireplaces, there’s dozens of options available for you to flex your unique personality and style. ADORABLE SPIRIT COMPANIONS Explore different combinations of room activities, soundscapes, and decor options to lure out the mischievous Spirits that populate the world. Discover and collect them as you focus on your tasks. You'll never be alone with a Spirit companion by your side. And yes, every Spirit can be petted too! BEGIN YOUR PRODUCTIVITY JOURNEY Utilize built-in productivity tools, including a to-do list for organization, a pomodoro timer for focused work sessions, and a habit tracker and journal to foster a healthy routine. Earn XP for practicing good habits, unlocking more goodies over time - from new character & room cosmetics, to hints to help discover more Spirits, being productive has never been so rewarding! KEY FEATURES Listen along to a carefully curated catalog of chill lofi beats, with a selection of themed playlists for every mood and occasion; Stay organized using integrated productivity tools, including a to-do list, pomodoro timer, habit tracker and journal; Create your own avatar. Choose from a variety of hairstyles, outfits, color options, and more to bring to life your own unique Spirit City persona; Spruce up your room to design your ideal cozy retreat, swapping between different wallpapers, flooring, furniture and wall decor; Immerse yourself with interactive soundscapes that change the world in real-time to suit your preferred vibe, from the pitter-patter of rain on a window to the crackling of a toasty fireplace; Decipher hints to lure curious spirits out into the open with the right combination of game settings, unlocking them as your future companions; Earn XP and level up over time, and by using the game’s features to their fullest. Unlock new cosmetics and customization choices as you progress; Stream your sessions worry-free thanks to the game’s fully stream-friendly music library - perfect for co-working streams or as a background on Twitch or Youtube; Expand your song catalog with the built-in web player, providing even more options for the musically adventurous; Enhance your everyday activities. Spirit City: Lofi Sessions offers a pleasing and distraction-free space for you to better enjoy and concentrate on your work and hobbies.
