_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this game is not your normal video game. It is very much a productivity game that encourages healthy habits, reminders and a safe place where you can write out your thoughts.With that in mind, it is an absolutely wonderful game. I recently found myself being drawn to lofi when I was in my college years and anytime I need a calming escape and can't find myself outside, I drift to lofi. Spirit City has a few lofi stations that you can choose from depending on your mood, along with ambient sounds that you can mix and match to create your ideal sound. It far succeeds my expectations on the sound-front.The "gaming" portion comes from using given hints to discover new spirits! This is a fun little portion and requires patience when you're luring one out. Besides having the cutest spirits with the most meaningful descriptions, you can customize them AND yourself!There isn't much to say on the productivity front: it does well for studying or general productivity management. From timers to checklists, it has it all!Overall, this game is amazing for what it is! When I start up school again, I can't wait to use this wonderful little game to help manage my scattered brain and stress. I highly recommend it if you study frequently!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.user: D I I G I T D O L L
_childDocuments_.review: As someone who likes the idea of journals/tracking/lists etc, I'm very not the best at keeping up with them in an app or paper notebook. This game/tool is very easy for me to keep up on my computer while working, doing chores, or even just playing games. I constantly have my to do list visible and the timers help to remind me to take breaks every so often. The vibes are cozy, the art is cute, and I love all the Spirits. I very much look forward to what else will be added in the future. There is so much potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a giant to-do app with a pomodoro timer, weekly habits log, journal. You can customize your avatar and put them in various task areas. Has helped me a lot when I need to do homework or chores around the house. You earn credits by having the game open and can use those to buy colors to paint your room, outfits, accessories, and different decorations.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: A really pleasing app to run in the background, I really recommend it for studying or working. The pomodoro timer and the task list is actually useful, while the lofi playlist and sound options can relax you and help you focus. The visuals are gorgeous, I hope we can get more interior design and character options in the future, but for now it is more than enough as it is.I really like that the additional items are NOT micro-transactions. Unlocking things with an in-game currency that you can get for playing the game is something I always loved in games and I'm glad this app is sticking to that instead of making us spend more irl money.One thing that would be nice though, is to have a "Dynamic" setting for the lighting, where the game would automatically change according to your PC's system time. It kinda bothers me when I look at the app at 8PM and it's still on the morning setting. (if there's a toggle for this somewhere and I just didn't find it, pls someone let me know!)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I was used to pomodoro apps but I quickly got bored of it, using it was more a punishement than a motivational tool to be proactive. Also finding the proper background sound (music or ambiant) for my work was an additional task where I wasn't always inspired for.This "game" is the perfect task tool as there are rewards which motivates me to work into small tasks with regular breaks to create real focus moments and removes the hassle of searching for a playlist or background sound.I really like it and now I use it regularly to be productive. I check if I unlock the spirit only during breaks which is a good motivation to complete my work.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: The first session was fun, but not a lot of doing stuff in the outside world happened as I was too distracted by decorating my Spirit City room. Second and third days were pretty productive tho. Turns out bribing me to do basic chores with the prospect of cute digital pets works really well. The music and soundscapes are also exactly what I needed.Windowed mode is weird, it seems anchored to the center of my main monitor so I can't move it to one side and have access to my lists while I'm looking at Word or whatever.ETA: Turns out there's only seventeen levels worth of spirits to catch at the moment. So I tapped out the game part of the program pretty early. Having difficulty motivating myself to use the program without them tbh, even if the tools are useful and the music is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Spirit City: Lofi Sessions for a while now, it's a great productivity tool! While I haven't used the habit tracker as much, the to-do list and pomodoro timer have become part of my daily routine.The lofi music is stunning and helps create a calming and focused atmosphere that's perfect for studying or working. Watching my character study alongside me adds an extra layer of motivation,Overall, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is an excellent tool for anyone looking to enhance their productivity. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a gift for those of us with ADHD/focus issues. I get so excited to launch this every day and knock out tasks with cute bops playing in the background. Seeing a version of myself be productive and living her best life also encourages the real me to be productive and live my best life.From a gameplay standpoint, I REALLY appreciate how the devs designed this.  Perhaps I've been scarred from other games, but I really expected to have to repurchase the same item for each separate area if I wanted it there and thats not the case at all. Once you spend your tickets on one item, its available in each location its available in the room. Its nice to not be nickel and dimed for my in-game currency.  The art style, animations, and customizations available are phenomenal.  I usually have this launched in the background almost 24/7 now. I cant wait to see what else the devs have in store for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I am SO in love with this game! It helps me take better care of myself! I love the functionality and the aesthetics. Functionality: I have a really hard time focusing. I also don't want a bunch of different apps to help keep me focused. This game combines 4 different productivity and trackers into one without being overwhelming. The to-do list, pomodoro timer, habit tracker, and journal are so easy to use and you can hide them at any given time. The music and sounds help keep me focused while not be too overstimulating. I love being able to change what I'm wearing, my spirit companion, the way my room looks, and the time of day at any given time!! I am so thankful for this game and see myself utilizing it every single day for a very long time. Huge thank you to the developers for making such a great, functional, and helpful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Useful for my ADHD butt forgetting to stretch my hands while drawing...If you dig the "LoFi Girl" vibes but want to customize your experience, this is a fun option ^^ Helps me stay on task with the pomodoro timer, and having a checklist of 'To-Dos' (even if they're as simple as 'Finish flat colour on piece X') is also really nice. That feeling of accomplishment is really good for us non-functioning-dopamine-transmitter-owners :P
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I throw this game up whenever I need to get something done or am hosting a co-working night-- it's actually really good at simulating parallel play, which is great for my brain and getting things done. The spirits are charming, but don't get in the way and I love decorating the room and unlocking all of them! The music is perfect and I love the option for importing your own via youtube (though I don't use it much bc of youtube ads). My only complaint is that the timer doesn't automatically do breaks-- you have to set up a timer loop. But other than that it's pretty perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute way to sit down and organize the things I need to do each day. Whether I use it after work or on a free day, it makes it easy to stay on task with timers, check lists, and even a journal. I love all the outfits you can collect and that you can change the color of your spirit companions. There are lots of options for decorating your room as well. The music on the playlists make great background music while I'm working on stuff. All in all, I'm happy I came across this little organizer game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutly love this game (or "tool") and it's actually the first thing I launch on my pc every day since i have it.In my case, it runs perfectly with any other game/browser page in the background (it might not for every one though, but the devs are still working on optimizing it at the moment I write this review).
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and calming productivity tool/game. Helps you create an individual space to provide a soothing background for focusing on tasks with an increasing variety of unlock-able options to decorate with. Continued responses to user feedback with free updates from the devs means this charming game keeps getting better all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I love this "game"! It helps with my studying, or well anything I need to focus at. It was extremely fun to play and find all the spirits. Buuuut it needs more... like a lot more. The spirits are too easy to find and you can run through them in a few hours. The customizations are good, but once you find the outfit and room design you want the in-game currency is basically useless, and you get A LOOOT of it. Again, I love this game a bunch. I would be absolutely okay if they started selling cheap DLC packs or something to keep the game interesting. It just currently does not have enough stuff in it to keep people's attention after a few days.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the pinnacle of kozy games! Spirit City Lofi Sessions motivates you to stay productive with tons of calming and soothing elements (a comfy home environment, asmr sounds of your choice). The spirit companions are also a nice addition. Thoroughly enjoying the lofi experience thanks to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: A friend of mine brought this game to my attention and I'm really happy they did. I love to have this on my personal laptop while I'm at work and the body-doubling aspect of it really helps. I have my avatar working right along with me while I manage the electronic resources of my institution. The music is great (and I was really pleased with the Spring playlist); the perfect music to chill to, to be energized to, and more. I loved collecting all the spirits and look forward to more of them being released as the game continues to run.I have very few dislikes or issues with this game. Maybe a nitpick or two: I wish the to-do list had a "To Do" and a "Done" section, just to keep it a smidge more organized. I also wonder if the to-do list and the daily task list could be combined? That's about it, and to be honest, the devs put out a questionnaire earlier this year, asking for feedback (which I did fill out) so obviously they are interested in the users' experience and in making changes/adaptions to feedback. They've shared upcoming aspirations and overall I think this is a great product. I really enjoy it and would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game! It helps me as my body double while I do other tasks around the house. Hopefully in the future we get a little cute cleaning animation for our character.    The spirits are absolutely adorable and I love that you can change them to different color palettes. I also really enjoy getting to customize so many aspects of the room to suit my mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review of any game on Steam, and I have to say that it is AMAZING so far. It is far more of a productivity tool than a game at the moment, but the gaming elements have been huge motivators. I personally love character and home customization so that has been a big motivating factor for playing and finding spirits. I also love that you can customize the spirits' colors! The music choices are wonderful and I love the option to stream from online as well. There are some things I would like to see optimized or added over time. For example:-An option to switch the clock from 24 to 12 hour.-Daily tasks reset every day, and/or multiple task lists that can be saved and reused.-The option to save and reuse timers.-UI customization (colors, styles, etc. Similar to the character and room customization).-More activities in each location and/or custom activities (changing color of laptops, books, etc. Again, similar to all other customization).-Unlockable rooms/areas of the home to hang out in, such as a garden or living room.Ideally I would love to see this game out on mobile as well (with the ability to link accounts) so that I could take it with me to my workplace, but I know things like that don't come so easily. :)Overall, I am loving this so far and would 100% recommend it to anyone who is motivated by cute creatures, customization, and chill music.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy game that helps you relax while doing work on the computer. One of my favorite parts about the game is how easy it is to customize your character and your room. I also love the music controls and the sound adjustment for the ambient environmental noises. I love listening to a thunderstorm with strong wind and rain while a fireplace crackles, and the forest outside has critters making noise.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm one to always listen to Lo-Fi while working on things. I do love that I can pair it with other sounds like keyboard clicking, fireplace, thunderstorms and rain. The creatures and avatar are such a cute bonus! I hope that more spirits will be added in the future, maybe even other areas that could be near the sea for ocean wave sounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an author and I'm always playing lofi in the background to help cut through any noise in my home. I also have two littles and will put lofi on the main TV while we all work on our own things. Having this makes it so much more personal and my kiddos love switching out the pets (and collecting them) while also changing up the character. I also love the task list which I use every day to help balance my household tasks as well as tasks in my writing. The sprint timer is also a HUGE win for me as I use it for writing sprints and sometimes cleaning sprints with the kids. Being able to change the lighting and layer the different sounds has also been a gamechanger. Matching my mood with the sounds has been so fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a wonderful help for either working on personal projects or chores! Seeing my avatar also working or relaxing with a spirit helps keep me going! I really like all the spirits, seeing them do different things too. I also really love the representation in the game-when I saw the mug with the asexual colors I yelled "Ace mug!" and bought it without thought. The to-do list is also wonderful since it helps me keep track of everything I'm working on and want to do. For anyone wanting to get more done in their lives, I highly recommend picking up this game! I hope the developers keep working on it to add more spirits and more things for both avatars and spirits to do!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a nice game, it really helps me to relax or to focus. The tunes are carefully selected, they're not only smooth but also stable, kind of like the perfect music for a yoga session. I wish I had discovered this game earlier.There are other productivity games out there with Pomodoro timers, I have been searching for that, but many of them are designed to distract more, making the game itself more engaging than actually helping me focus. This one, however, is perfectly aligned with what I need because I tend to procrastinate, and I really don’t want to spend time playing actual games.Just a few suggestion:- It would be nice if the room had a small aquarium or fountain with various fish that we can choose from- An animated music box would be nice with more holiday songs for people who will celebrate holidays and new years alone haha-probably a chat room for people who are active using it and just want to socialize a bit- Window with a view of a sparkling pond or moving river- And a larger window to see the city lights, stars, sun, pond, river, garden, whatever.- More options to choose the Pomodoro alert sound and an option to make it transparent.- Why is there no dog?
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on a whim because I love "gamifying" productivity. It's pretty simple and not too involved, so I love having it on in the background while I'm researching or working on pretty much anything. Plus, the ability to create different soundscapes is great for providing some inspirational ambiance for writing. I am hoping they add more to the game soon, and I have high hopes for that after the recent update!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit city has been a very useful tool for me while working, especially on the days I struggle with procastination and being productive. Here are some of my pros and cons:Pros:+ A lot of room custom options+ The soundboard affects the enviroment outside, such as rain sounds makes it rain outside+ I can choose the time of day+ I can make checklists ingame and categorise them+ Ingame timer, very useful+ Does have a habit tracker and journal too. Do not use those but they are still very neat+ The spirits are very cute + They update regularyThe Cons:- The avatar customs are a bit lacking, not many hair and head gear options yet- Halloween clothing was a bit dissapointing, no witch robes and skelly hoodie? :c
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This game has helped me become so much more passionate about my art and making sure that I stay on tasks! I finish every piece I start and even have my character doing art at her desk to mimic me lol. Halloween update is adorable, especially the new spirit friend that I found. 94hrs played and counting. Love love LOVE Spirit City + even bought for a friend. Can't wait for future updates!! xoxo
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: This is already a good tool for having a non distracting busy screen, that syncs ambient sounds and visuals with your lofi music and tracks. So yes it's worth it, I already gifted someone else a copy as well.I feel it could be improved with other features though:-Perhaps a stereo system option or something that displays a functional synthesizer? -Ability to play tracks directly off your PC for offline use, and not only from youtube.-An easy/accessible "Mute all" button so I can mute it quickly when needed. One that mutes music, sound, etc- even if using it's browser for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it so far! I have ADHD and work from home and as you can imagine, it's easy to get distracted. A lot of times I find myself scrambling to finish my work at the end of the day because time just seems to get away from me. I bought this game to help me focus and have been using the timer feature. 15 minutes of work, 5 minutes of web browsing. Truly made me realize that I have no natural gauge for how much time has passed because I will think "surely it's been 15 minutes" and then I look over to my laptop where I have this game running and the timer is not even 30% down yet. Very cute graphics and I like the various customization options. The spirits are very cute!! I do feel like it's maybe a bit too easy/quick to collect stuff but that's okay, I primarily got this game to help me focus and it does that very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Love this productivity tool! I took it to school and showed my class. The AU students loved the parallel activities and every student responded to the visuals. If I wanted them to sit at the table and work I would show the avatar at the desk working and if I wanted them to sit quietly on the carpet I could show them that too. Reading time was great - they were all focused on their book including the avatar.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: If you struggle like me to keep on track with task you need to get done, this is for you!I've managed to stay on track with getting things done. The music is a vibe, so relaxing. I love how you can customise your room, your avatar and even pick which spirit to have and have a few options colour wise too for them.I highly recommend! Such a great way to keep on track and focus on those tasks you just need to get done :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed how this game feeds my brain serotonin while I do less-rewarding tasks! It helps me work for longer and stay on task better, since now completing my tasks feels like part of the game! I love all of the decor options and unlocks that you get for just completing tasks you need to complete anyways (checking items off of your to-do list gives you experience points towards leveling up, which earns you more tickets to purchase decor and customization options.) I never find the music they provide distracting, but if you aren't a fan of the current track playing, or you have a specific one that you want to listen to, the game has very conveniently-placed UI for changing the music without entering a single menu screen. The slider options for layering different sounds over the main track might be my favorite feature. I love the sound of wind and rain to be loud, the thunder to be quiet, the sound of typing to be medium, and a crackling fire that's barely audible. Or sometimes I want the sounds of a creek and crickets chirping. This game truly offers all you would want in a create-your-own Cozy-Lofi situation, and I adore it. Can't wait to see what else they come up with to make this game even cozier.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting much of a game, don't bother. HOWEVER... out of all the "cozy, productivity tool and pomo timer masquerading as a game" ...games that have popped up recently, this is the most promising and most enjoyable experience I've had. It doesn't (yet?) have Twitch integration or plug into any external productivity tools or systems but it's a nice starter pack if you're just getting into that space as well. Plus figuring out how to find the spirits while getting things done is just super fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: ADHD and Autism can make navigating the working day challenging, and over time, the importance of a focused workspace has become apparent and has lead to me making many changes to my environment to work with my conditions rather than against them. After just 6-hours of use, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions has already proven to be an invaluable tool for day to day task management. The tools available, including, a to-do list, pomodoro timer, the ability to note new habits, and a journal, have made breaking down my day into manageable chunks so much more convenient and have helped me to begin identifying areas I have improved in and areas I need to work on.The video game aspects of Spirit City: Lofi Sessions serve as incentive for committed and focused study, rewarding you with XP per minute and with each discovery of a new spirit. XP earned increases your Spiritographer rank, giving you access to new spirits to unlock in your Spiritdex. The clues given, are not only a fun way of building each spirits individual character, but, also involve exploring the UI, which is a great way of gaining familiarity with all the available options. Spirit Credits earned can be spent on unlocking a variety of cosmetic items for your avatar and your in-game workspace.Like many others, the Lofi Girl YouTube channel has been the go to for easy listening music. Spirit City: Lofi Sessions, rolls a great productivity app and soothing Lofi playlists into one. For anyone looking for a fantastic productivity tool, with beautiful art, and oozing with character, I cannot recommend Spirit City: Lofi Sessions enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Why would you buy this when there are plenty of streams for lofi available? - After thinking about this for some time, I finally decided to try it and see what difference this little tool / game can make.Are the number of available tracks limited? - No, the game provides some curated playlists (that I personally really like) but also offers the ingame browser. It allows you to listen to almost everything that is available as regular lofi streams and videos as well. Are there other important limitations? - Yes, I am missing the ability to add local files and manage my own playlists. I hope this will be added at some point.Now that the most important things are clarified: The game itself does provide the cozy atmosphere that is promised. Customizing the character and background acts as the better video background. UI elements can be hidden. The gamification of working is enjoyable and really helps you keep on track. There are no sudden actions or anything distracting so far. You can keep the game open on another monitor or even minimize if you need the space. The integrated features are minimal but helpful - Creating a simple task list, the integrated timer for learning breaks, and habit tracking.What I wish for:- More playlists - as many as possible :)- Ability to add my own songs and playlists- More background customization and settings (e.g. city roofs, village, forest camping)- More stats and long time achievements for even 100s of hoursSo if you are still on the fence, just try it. The distraction potential is smaller than by using the browser. I like to keep live chat away and ignore video recommendations this way.One important thing at the end:If everything appears blurry at the start, go to settings and set resolution scale to 100% (which really should be the default).

_childDocuments_.review: Just in case you're somehow reading this and don't already know: This isn't a game, it's a productivity tool with some gamified elements. But don't let that stop you from checking it out, especially if you're someone who like me, can have issues with focus.If you've ever watched some lofi music YouTube channels, you've probably seen those cozy looking environments and animations that play over them. This basically allows you to make your own one of those environments. You create a character and use "currency" you earn by levelling up to buy elements to customize your environment. There's a few lofi playlists built-in (though they aren't very large), plus a built-in web player you can use to play any music you can find on the web. There's no direct integration with music apps like Spotify of YouTube Music. I generally like the playlists, though some of the songs have a bit of a sadder or more melancoly tone to them, which can be harder to listen to if you're going through something. There's also a ton of sounds effects you can add in to various levels and intensities to make a relaxint soundscape. Some of these will also affect the visual environment, which is a nice touch. I would also like to see more options to customize the environment, though the developers have said they plan to add more over time.You level up by just spending time with the software running, or by completing tasks you set for yourself or pomodoro timers, which you can customize to your liking. Once you level up, you'll unlock a spirit you can find by putting your character in a certain location, doing a certain activity for a while. The clues are super simple and it won't take long to unlock everything. More spirits are also needed, which they also say are coming.There are other functions like a journal, but I don't recommend using it as a primarily journalling application as you can't export anything out of it so anything you write is locked to this software.I also want to shout out some smart features they've added, like the ability to customize what frame rates it runs at both focused and unfocused, which can lower the demands on your system when you're running it in the background. It also works well in windowed mode. However, a real frustration is that your "game state" doesn't save between sessions. So if you were at a certain point in a playlist, it'll always go back to the first track of the default list when you start up next. This feels like an easy thing to patch, but I'm not programmer.This is most definitely not for everyone, but if you're into the idea, you'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Has potential but feels a bit bare bones as it is. Was looking for something functional, gamified, and has all the study tools in one place, and most importantly, actually lets you focus instead of demanding your attention.Props for not tethering the player and being actually AFK, BUT it has issues in terms of both functionality and game aspects. The interface is rigid and you can't customize it as much as you would like (e.g. time display size/location, timer style, no built in alarm/reminders that you can set, etc.), and despite advertising the quality of being cozy and customizing the space to suit you, the cosmetic/color options (player appearance, room, decor, clothes, accessories, spirits) are very limited. Also would really would like an option to set your timezone and have it reflect the hours in game. Having to manually change it between morning/night is disruptive. For a game that's meant to be cozy, the entirety of it was mildly unsatisfying. There's also really not that many spirits to discover which was a bit disappointing.I'll still use it, but it's okay at best as it lacks a lot of tools and interface options. Maybe with some feature and content updates that provide more expansive tools/customization for interface, cosmetics, and spirits, it'll be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 10/10, helped me get my ethics essay finished 4 days early all while listening to some good tunes and background noise. I've used plenty of productivity applications before to varying degrees of success. The vibe in this is unmatched. There's a low-pressure environment that helps keep things less like a work-like taskmaster atmosphere and more of a personal goal-oriented drive to do what you want to do for your life; not in the name of productivity for productiveness sake, but in the name of self-driven action. This atmosphere is achieved with the different soundscape options and great music playlist options, supplemented by the ability to pull whatever songs you'd like from YouTube. Sometimes, I'll just use rain and thunder noises for background noise while I get some schoolwork done. The to-do list is fantastic, simple, and effective. The timer is also simple and effective, though I'm not sure how the break function works on it, It still does the job for me to be mindful of how much time I'm spending doing whatever task or taking however long of a break that I need to. I've also been using the journal function which has been very helpful in getting my thoughts straight. It would be nice if it gave you extra blank space when you've reached the bottom of the page during your writing, though.As far as the customization options go, the spirits you collect are charming and well designed. The clothing and room options are also sufficient and charming, and for me, not overwhelming or too distracting from the productivity parts of the application. Looking forward to future content to be realized, if that's planned, or possible DLC in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so happy that this popped up on my steam summer sale. It was an impulse purchase that I am very pleased with.I was pleasantly surprised by how fleshed out this app is right out of the gate. They have a hearty number of different sound effects and soundtracks to help you focus on the task at hand. You're able to custom mix the volume levels for sound effects to make the perfect mix of white noise. Some of the sound effects even add atmospheric graphics to the room,  such as rain in the window, which is a nice touch. The songs are chill, and not too distracting which is a problem other similar apps seem to struggle with. The graphics are a delight. The character animations are really smooth. There are a lot of LGBTQIA items you can customize with, and we love to see the inclusion. The UI is very intuitive and it is easy to alter my to-do list and habits. I find myself looking forward to doing my daily tasks so I can discover new content. The app is definitely in its early stages in development. They have a good starting catalogue of home decor and clothing to customize your space, but I feel like there is a lot of untapped potential and a lot of room for growth. I would love to see them expand their selection with a little more goth and witchy customization options to make my little lo-fi space feel more like home. Some of the flat UI graphics have some pixel artifacts around the edges, such as the spirit bar level indicator, but a little polishing will fix that right up. I’m looking forward to how the developers will build on this foundation in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely outstanding. Instead of Lofi on Youtube, you play Lofi via this game. However, you are given the ability to customize the girl to your liking as well as her bedroom. The options are somewhat limited but there is a good amount, and the possibility of the developers adding more is there. On top of having a reasonably good size of songs to play from by choosing your album, you can also add sound effects such as rain, or the cackling of fire from your fireplace, or the sounds of keys being typed. You have various pets (spirits) that you can unlock in your room by having your character do tasks under certain conditions. TLDR; This is Lofi music with the option to add sound effects and customize the girl and her bedroom to your liking. Easy 10/10, highly recommended for Lofi enjoyers.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is less a game and more of a productivity tool with gamified elements. You have in-game to-do lists that you can freely customize, an in-game timer function, and a nice selection of low-key music and relaxing ambient noise. The game elements are that you get experience points for spending time in the game and using its built-in functions daily, with leveling up rewarding you with in-game currency to spend on customization items for your avatar and room, as well as completing passive objectives to unlock new pet options. It's humble in scope, but I've found it works for me for focusing on the task at hand and making sure I do so regularly. Perhaps the in-game pet options could have a few less-fantastical options, but that's a small nitpick and only a matter of personal taste. I got more or less what I wanted from this game and will continue to "play" it for the foreseeable future, and I'm looking forward to future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really a game, it's a productivity tool with some traits of a game :) In Spirit City: Lofi Sessions you create your cute anime-style 3D avatar and their apartment, set up your soundscape and you catch adorable pun-named spirits (that you can choose as your companions, let's not forget about that!) by completing certain activities.As for the productivity tools: you can add multiple to-do lists, set up habits and even write a journal all inside the app. You even have a customisable pomodoro timer!I don't always need these tools, especially pomodoro timers don't usually work for me and I'm not even a fan of lo-fi music but in Spirit City somehow it all comes together and it just... works! I don't understand this magic but I'm not going to question is as long as it does its job, which is helping me focus when everything else fails.20/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I sat on this review for days as I hate leaving any negative reviews. Ultimately, I had to post this.I'll start with the positives:- The art style is cute and the models are solid. I love the inclusion of animal horns and the like.- Homework radio is a great YT channel, so having their music as default is perfect, however I wish there was more variety.- The spirits are cute.Now the negatives:- If you're going to have larger sizes in a game...make it actually apparent. My skinny character just got a pot belly and widened slightly, which looked a bit odd and not how someone would actually look.- Please allow us to shuffle all songs. I heard the same song about 3 or 4 times in the space of an hour because it limits to one playlist.And the big one:If you're going to have a productivity tool that you want to gameify, don't just give up on content after approximately 20 hours of useage and plonk a few level achievements at the end. The actual usage of this tool was lost as soon as the last spirit was found (which for me was about 15-20 hours in). The rest of the game is just cranking up hundreds of hours to get the final 3 achievements. I have a friend and he sat the game idling for days (refreshing each day to get the bonus exp) in order to get the level 50 achievement (approximately 245 hours).What is keeping me using the app if I have nothing to really engage me in those last 230 hours?Instead of sitting this game open, using cpu, I could just put a free lo-fi radio playlist or radio station on in the background and have a checklist and pomodoro timer on my phone, all free tools. I feel like the final 3 achievements were just slapped there as an afterthought to get people using the game more.Does the cuteness of the art style really justify the price for things that are readily free? Yes, it compiles them into one program, but is that program worth it? In my opinion, no. I feel terrible writing this review, but I feel like these are things a lot of reviewers aren't talking about.UPDATE: I wanted to see exactly how long it would take to unlock all the furniture, spirit colours and clothing items.I've now clocked over 270 hours and I've only unlocked the furniture and about half the spirit colours. I'm now going to give up on this because it's not worth trying to 100% it more than just getting the achievements. I'm not event using it for its intention at this point, i set it going and go downstairs to actually work with proper time management tools.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this task manager & idle spirit catching combo! Within the first couple hours of playing the game, I've already hit rank 7 and managed to catch 6 spirits! I LOVE the designs and descriptions for the little spirit buddies, and I'm *really* hoping there'll be more to catch in later updates. I have rampant ADHD and hate silence, so this effectively kills two birds with one stone for me!My Pros & ConsCons:- Character Customization is Rough. I see very limited options for POC hairstyles, I'd LOVE to see some braided hairstyles for both straight and curly hair types, a better tool for custom colors (give us a custom two-tone option for eyes/hair/skin/etc!)- PLEASE overhaul the body sliders! If you put the body weight slider to max, it kinda just look like playdough or like the character shoved a pillow into their clothing. Maybe a spider chart-style slider for body types would be nice (pear-shaped, hourglass-shaped, apple-shaped, broad shouldered, etc etc since people carry weight and mass in different ways.- I can definitely tell at some points when the ambient tracks loop around, but if I keep it low enough to just drone on in the background, it doesn't really matter I guess. It'd be nice to have a bit of variation in the ambient tracks as well, maybe different bird calls play depending on the time of day? Owls at night, Bird songs in the morning, maybe a seagull call? I'd really looove to see an ocean ambiance with a coastal background!Pros:- The habit tracking and journal features are really nice touches. It allows me to not only track my journey while trying to quit nicotine, but also allows me to remind myself of things like plans for going to dinner with friends, or things that occurred in my D&D games that I want to save for later.- You can adjust all of the ambiance elements to your liking, and the default lo-fi playlists on the program are decent too, but all are optional! Being able to play music through their youtube player is also a nice workaround if you just want to use your own playlists.- The spirits are too stinkin cute! I love the option to buy additional skins for them with in-game currency, and I will say it again, I love the lore being built around them! I would absolutely adore an opt-in mechanic where you need to take care of your buddies like feeding them, hydrating them, bathing them, etc as little reminders to also feed & hydrate yourself, I could see it as a great motivator to ppl with eating disorders. Maybe a little happiness meter or something, if your pet is sad or sick, it's probably because you aren't taking care of it/yourself!- It doesn't require internet connection! I can Spirit Hunt on the go!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a genius idea of a game. True, there isn't a lot of direct/active gameplay such as you might find in your more typical games like The Long Dark or Grocery Store Simulator (both of which I also recommend you try; The Long Dark is gorgeous with in-depth lore and gameplay with legitimate survival mechanics and an active dev team while Grocery Store Simulator is a lot of fun alone or with others and also has an active dev team so far), if you enjoy lofi music in the background or just like games that let you relax without demanding much brainpower, this is perfect for you. It's also a good game if you like natural ASMR (the sound of a fireplace; the sound of a cat purring; the sound of thunder or wind or rain, etc). It's the best game-not-game you'll probably ever find. If you like lofi, this is the perfect game to meet your needs.You can customize your character's appearance to a fair degree and there are a lot of clothing options to choose from. You can pick between skins for your spirit pet and customize your room quite a bit, from the walls to the decorations down to the furniture. By simply spending time in the game, completing daily tasks, or leveling up your spiritographer rank, you earn tokens that can be used to unlock some pet skins and customization options for the room or character's clothingYou can choose between sound effects you want to listen to while the music plays or silence them entirely, or you can choose to keep the sound or visual effects of the sounds without activating one or the other. These can be played at the same time as the lofi music you pick, or you can silence the music and just listen to the sounds. You can also opt out of any sounds and just chill with the music. The volume and level of the sounds and music are also independent of one another so you can adjust them as you see fit.The graphics are beautiful for what it is and controls are easy to get the hang of since it's just clicking things. I've been listening to Halloween music with a nighttime cityscape out the window, with visuals and sounds of wind, rain and thunder to relax to and it's actually nearly put me to sleep twice already because it's so peaceful.I'm not great at reviews but basically what I'm saying can be summed up like this: Give the game a try if you like customization and relaxing sounds/music with smooth, lofi visuals. Whether you're into the lofi scene, or you just want music/sounds you can relax to without putting a lot of brain power into it, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of a tool than a game, but since i've had it, it's been instrumental in helping me focus on doing work. Being able to play music and add in sound effects like fire crackling, keyboard noises, crickets or birds singing- and adjust the volume of each independently- lets me create a soundspace that's unobtrusive but helpful to keep my brain occupied.The timer feature is brilliant and I wish i'd thought of it earlier, and all the customization and personalization options help me create a space that's perfect for relaxing in while i'm working on my projects. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: A very good gamified productivity tool! I really like that besides the usual pomodoro timer and a to-do list that such tools usually have, it also has a habit tracker and a journal.I'm also impressed by the quality of Spirit City considering it was made by only 3 people, and to make it even better, the developers are pretty quick to react to suggestions or bug reports. There are plenty of fun things to do besides just focusing on productivity. You can customise your avatar, decorate your room, and collect different spirit companions. There's an ability to change the time of day, try a variety of different relaxing sounds, and have multiple soundtrack playlists to listen to as well. I enjoy how you can make your character do different activities in the room, such as relax with the laptop on the bed, knit by a fireplace, or draw at the desk. I hope we get even more of these activities in the future, though.Personally, out of all the similar apps I've tried, I think this is the one that actually encourages me to be more productive than any other and gives me motivation to keep opening it whenever I'm trying to get some things done. The only things I'm waiting for are more spirits to collect and even more customisation options.Overall, if you find use in productivity tools or want to chill with some cute and relaxing idle game, then you should definitely give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a focus and management tool ideal for people who need something in the background that keeps track of tasks, goals, dairy entries and more.The team are the type who constantly listen to feedback, produce new content and make it very clear that they care about their user base.What exactly does spirit city provide?A character customisation with constant added content to help you make your avatar unique to you. While I wish they offered piercings and tattoos, the head accessories such as horns and ears make up for that.You customise your room with a variety of colours, patterns and themes. You can change how your shelves, lights and walls appear. With either cute plushies, pretty candles or some nice books (and more).My all time favourite is probably the spirit animals you can befriend by fulfilling specific requirements. And depending on where and what task you're avatar is doing, your spirit companion will often mimic you c:The are several music playlists for you to use to help you focus, from spooky vibes to more chill lofi beats. There are also sounds effects like white/pink/brown noise, fireplace sounds, ocean waves and more. So if you don't like music, you have some calming background noises instead. Everything can be muted, so if you prefer your own music playlists you can do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 would recommend. Great gamified alternative to just having YouTube up on a lofi stream.-Tab for free-form journal-To do list-Pomodoro-style timer (that has basic timer and break customization)-Weekly habit tracker (though as of now, it doesn't save/track once you manually clear the week)Devs also seem to take feedback seriously and work to add quality of life features, so far.As far as aesthetics and game concept go, I LOVE it! Great for someone like me who likes to change the visuals up a lot. Also the sound effects you can choose to layer over the soundtrack and the toggle for environmental impact (ex: I can have lightning sounds with OR without the flash based on the vibe I want whenever, or the sound the fireplace without the fireplace being lit-up) is a WONDERFUL feature.I just hope they add more spirit companions in the long-term, because I already unlocked them all T_TThough, all of them are so cute and the in-game currency is definitely useful to unlock all the different spirit skins.TLDR - so worth the money; came for the spirit animals/aesthetic and ended up checking tasks off my list just for the satisfaction of "playing the game" and getting the achievements <3 Accidental productivity, for the win!

There are barely any hairstyles, no skirts, barely any eyes and eyebrows  can't preview items you buy, can't change color of clothes. _childDocuments_.review: I've only recently learned of Spirit City through a wholesome games list. I was instantly drawn into the stress free aspect, along with the cute character design, clothing, decor and Spirits of the "game". I phrase game the way I do because this is more of a productivity/management app. With my first launch, I came to learn that there's a timer, to-do list, habit tracker, journaling, and the ability to listen to music! Whether you want to listen to their in-game playlist, or from their built-in YouTube player. Live or premiere videos are NOT supported, and while their in-game music is safe to stream, streaming audio from their built-in app may result in a copyright strike. The timer, to-do list and the habit tracker have been a HUGE help in my everyday life. I struggle due to many personal, private issues, and even the most basic/simplest of tasks can be absolutely crippling and daunting. I've found myself sticking to a routine so much better than I have in years, coupled with another self-care app I use in conjunction. You're rewarded XP for every minute you spend doing your habits/routines/tasks, which in turn grant you levels. These levels grant you Spirit Credits, which can be used to purchase and customise your in-game character, Spirit companion, and room! These levels also grant you access to discover a new Spirit to find. There are currently 21 Spirits to discover at the time of my review, each are extremely unique and adorable. Each come with a few different colours/versions of them to be purchased, some being Holiday themed! The variety of activities and poses enhance so much in your cosy, little space. You can set your own ambiance, mood, atmosphere, and so much to your liking, creating the perfect, cosy mood you're looking for! Their in-game journal has also helped me TREMENDOUSLY. I love the idea, concept, vulnerability, private aspects of writing/keeping journals. That being said, I struggled to even get myself to write the smallest entry, I found myself able to engage myself more into actually writing out my feelings/thoughts. The journal is rather basic in terms of sorting, customising, and topics to choose from if you so desired at the time of this review, but it is still super helpful! Spirit City has actually improved aspects and qualities of my life I did not think would return soon/at all. Although I still struggle, Spirit City has been an ABSOLUTE lifesaver. I am extremely satisfied with my purchase. I am beyond thankful and happy I was able to find out about Spirit City, and Mooncube Games. If you're someone who struggles with day-to-day things like myself, desire a cosy place to relax and ease away your stress, or you just enjoy the calming, gentle, stress free aspect of it as a whole, I highly recommend giving Spirit City a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so hear me out on this. This tool (it is only a game in the way that rewarding yourself with a candy bar if you finish your workout is a game) is relatively straightforward. You can make checklists, start Pomodoro-style timers, track a routine schedule, and write in a journal. It also has some sounds you can mix in and some songs.The data isn't protected in any way from peeping on the local computer, tasks don't have reminders of any sort, and deleting things doesn't even have a confirmation dialog.With that said, I still love this software. It can be configured to consume very little power, and the customizeable avatar and background make it a really nice little idle toy. Moreover, it DOES have a timer, and a task list, and a journal which can be used for keeping track of sticky-note kinds of things. Additionally it comes with several hours of great lofi focus music, and a surprisingly versatile noise generator. For the price they're asking, it's actually *cheaper* than most dedicated noise generators, or even a single lofi album.As such, it is now my go-to tool for helping me focus and for decorating any screens that find themselves unused on my computer for a particular project. Plus the new customization they've given to the room really have helped me liven up my virtual office space, which I've been enjoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start my review, I want to apologize for the slowness in getting reviews out, which is unusually rare for me.  This will be explained in a bit more detail in my review, but this should be rectified now that I have obtained all of the achievements. ^^ is a productivity app with a gaming (specifically, creature collecting) aspect developed and published by Mooncube Games.  When you first start, you're greeted by Lenny, the resident spirit companion who appears as a kitty and is your starter companion.  Lenny talks you through a brief tutorial, and you can customize your avatar as well as your room.  Also, you start off with some spirit bucks, which is the game's currency from which you can purchase skins for spirit companions, clothing items, and room features.  (For the record, there are no in-app game purchases.)  Once you finish the tutorial, you can play  however you like.  As there isn't really a story here, I'll go right into the gameplay.  As I explained earlier, you can customize your avatar, room, and spirit companions through the use of spirit bucks.   is mainly a productivity app, which means that you can use it to organize your tasks, journal your thoughts, and use a pomodora timer to time activities (as well as to remind you when to take breaks).  Also, there is a wide range of music track selections (lofi beats) that you can relax to as you work.  However, there is a creature collecting aspect as well.  There are various spirit creatures that you can capture, and as Lenny explains in the tutorial, you can lure these creatures via clues that are given in the Spiritdex, a spirit creatures guide.  Creatures will be brought out, depending on the time of day (morning, afternoon, evening, or night), current activities (ranging from writing to knitting), and/or sound effects.  In addition, there is a leveling system, and you can level up by collecting various spirit creatures, logging in daily, checking off a daily task, and using the pomodora timer.  Of course, there are Steam achievements and at the time of this review, Steam trading cards are available, too.Now that I've gone over the gameplay, I'll move onto my thoughts.  I love that there is such a productivity app available that has relaxation and cute aspects to it.  Having spent lots of time on  (at the time of this review, over 237 hours :o), I understand why it has gotten lots of praise.  It helped me to focus and complete my tasks, as I was very busy for the past couple of months with work-related tasks.  The productivity tools are definitely useful.  As for the creature collecting aspect, I really loved finding all of the spirit creatures.  They're so adorable, and a couple of my favorites are Moonpaw and Earlybirb. ^^Also, I love the selection of music tracks.  They vary from the slower paced beats to the more upbeat ones.  Also, you can upload your own customizable tracks.  In regards to the art, the style is beautiful and cute, and I love how the colors feel bright and just pop out.If there are any complaints that I have, it has to be with obtaining all of the Steam achievements.  Although most of the achievements were very doable, the ones that I found the most frustrating were the level achievements since there are only a limited number of spirit creatures that can help out with that.  They were the reason that it took me so long to complete  and to get a review out.  As a reviewer who values fully completing a game and/or app before I write up a review, since I'd personally feel that I would be taking shortcuts, cheating readers to do otherwise, I found it a bit frustrating.    To give the developers credit, though, they have listened to such feedback, and I found that gaining experience went by a little faster after a major update.  The developers have stated that there will be future updates, which probably means more spirit creatures and perhaps other ways to gain experience.  I want to state that although I was able to obtain all of the Steam achievements, I didn't purchase all of the cosmetic options since I'd have to be at over level 100 (at least) to be able to do so. :oOverall, would I recommend ?  Well, let me experiment a little with my recommendation:Although I did enjoy  (for the most part), I think it could use a bit of tweaking in regards to gaining experience, so that it feels like a joy rather than a slog to use.  However, I am looking forward to future updates, especially on obtaining more future spirit creatures.I want to give a major thank you to Mooncube Games for the review copy.  It did take me a long time, but I think it was worth it and I'll love to return to . ^^Also, if you want to read another excellent review from someone who obtained all the achievements and has written up a review as well as uploaded a youtube video explaining  and whatnot, please click on the link .  Of course, I obtained permission from the reviewer to post the link, and I recommend following his curation and especially, his youtube channel. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if I have the words to express how helpful this is.I came in with no expectations and I was very sceptical about it helping me in any way. A friend who swore by this as an effective study help and way to organize gifted it to me while singing praises like "I wish I had this at the start at Uni..."But again, I was sceptical as... Well it's just a bunch of methods I already have tried irl with little to no success to reduce my stress or organize my workflow. But I gave this little thing a shot and well... Here I am. Have some soothing music + background noise and actually able to DO ♥♥♥♥. I actually can sit down and do my big ass assignments for Uni without having a breakdown and starting to play games as a coping strategy. Hell it's probably pathetic to admit publically, but this actually helped me getting out of bed as well as starting to brush my teeth again and kicking some depressive habits. All because I did a lil' habit and didn't want to disapoint the lil' cute avatar I made and their pet.Is this experience perfect? Of course not, as much as I love the habits system it's also my biggest fault as I would personally prefer if it wasn't "Wipe it clean at the end of the week". Might not be great for everyone, but I would really like to be able to look back at previous weeks to check how my habits have become... well habits. And everytime you boot up if you have one playlist prefered over another you have to start it up yourself. The complaints are obviously minor, but y'know. Still thereBut either way I would highly recommend it for anyone doing any sort of work on a computer. Even if you don't want the tools you can replicate with a calander or sticky notes, I would still recommend it for the ambiance sound customization as well as the relaxing music. It's just kinda perfect work studies in my experience.Sorry that I'm all over the place and for whichever lost soul decided to read this whole thing :p

_childDocuments_.review: While I do enjoy this game, I have a few things I'd like to point out. Pros:*Having the pomodoro timer is a great addition, although I really wish you could adjust the sound of the alarm. I can barely hear it, and when I'm focused, I forget that it even went off.*Having a place where you can track your tasks and journal is great. I don't personally use them, but it's a good feature for those who use it as a tracker.*Personally, I use it most for the simulation of body doubling. Having it run in the background has actually helped me work on some things.*The spirits are very cute.*And you can pet them, even if its just a simple click.Cons:*The content within the game is very limited. There's only so many spirits you can unlock and its super easy. It really only takes a few hours to get them all. There's a fairly limited selection of clothes and things you can change about your room, I generally keep my customization the same anyway. I kind of wish there were other environments to visit, like a cafe or a park.*There's only a few playlists available with maybe an hours worth of music each and it gets boring to listen to the same ones over and over. Sometimes the same track will play right after it ends. Sure there's the in-game browser, which can be nice, but as someone else already pointed out, it doesn't have adblocker capabilities. I just pause the music as soon as I open the game and open up YouTube separately.*After reaching level 30, it now takes me my full day to level up. I understand it's an idle type game and that shouldn't really matter, and it really doesn't. But when you've done all you can do, getting to level 50 is really the last thing to do at all. It's just a small nitpick.*Some of my settings revert, specifically the v-sync being enabled.I honestly wish that there was a workshop for this game so people could make custom graphics for certain things. Even a modding community. As it stands though, I have genuinely used this everyday. I have it running in the background all the time, even now. I like using it as a body double, it really helps me, instead of having to search YouTube for one that I like before starting a task.EDITAs of the Halloween update, there has been a lot of changes. Your room now has so much more customization options, including things you weren't able to before. There are new spirits that have been added and I'm looking forward to more. I'm so glad this application has been updated and that the devs behind it seem to really be listening to their playerbase. There's also a new Halloween playlist, but that's really all that's been added music-wise.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommendedSee this as a customizable Lo-Fi gamified tool, and not as a game. It does wat it tries to do extremely well. Things that Lofi Sessions include:- Lo-Fi music player and browser player (for YouTube for example). Does not have a spotify option as of now.- Pomodoro timer- To do list- Habit tracker- Journaling tool- Customizable room and characterThe tools are basic, but I don't think theyre trying to replace more elaborate versions of the tools you can find in other apps. Its a nice way to centralize them.Everything looks really pretty and customization feels very satifsying. I really like that you can play youtube music, because Lo-Fi itself isn't usually my go to genre for working.Overall, Ive already used it a lot and found myself feeling oddly organized. That is rare. There are just a few minor quality of life things that could be improved:- When the pomodoro timer is done, the jingle is quite inaudible sometimes. When you have the game running in the background because you're working on the same PC-screen and are not visually aware of the timer, it's easy to miss your break - When making a journal entry, the entire entry can be deleted with just one X button. There's no warning, so one misclick can instantly delete a day's worth journaling. A warning message before deletion could fix this.- when putting together the habit tracker, it is not possible to rearrange the order of the habits after putting them in, as is possible in the To-Do list. Adding this feature would improve the tool a lot. These are just really minor peeves in an otherwise awesome tool. I am really looking forward to future content!

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and cozy!  It's not the kind of 'game' I can see helping me with my ADHD issues in the long run; but in the short-term, while it's still novel, it's helped with my time management and productivity tremendously.  On that basis alone, I'd recommend it to others, and am very happy with the purchase. Because it is a small team, I don't think we'll get massive new features anytime soon; but in the long-term, my dream wishlist would be a lot more rewards and unlockables for completing tasks, and spending time on them. 'nuff said.If you always wish you had a customized ambience manager at your fingertips, this is definitely the game you're looking for!

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to play this game as a demo before buying, and highly enjoyed it even back then! The current release (1.4) is a vast improvement upon everything started in the demo, and really enjoy all the fun additions and QOL bits. I bought it to play while working on programming and art, listening to some nice music with ambiance effects is always something that helps me focus. The incorporation of a youtube search bar fro music also makes it so much more versatile, and I love all the extra sound effects built upon the original! The pompodoro timer, journals, and tasklists are also very helpful for keeping my direction. I have quite a bit of fun dressing up my avatar and room before setting them up to do a task similar to mine.The additional gameplay loop of getting new spirits is also pretty satisfying. However, I am VERY appreciative of the ability to mute the sound effect since it takes me out of it. It's pretty simple doing the different hinted requirements to get a new buddy, but allows some encouragement to try new effects and lighting. My only qualms are cosmetic related, such as a lack of hair options (There are quite a few, but none quite like my midlength style), a lack of food items other than ramen (plenty of drinks though),  and you cannot resize the pompodoro timer to be smaller. The first two are cosmetic and of no real consequence, and you can hide all UI elements if you want with a different option so the pompodoro doesn't even matter much.Ultimately, this is highly recommended from me. Useful for studying, focusing, etc, especially for people who LOVE soundscapes, it's also a bit of a fun game for people who love dressups and room decorators, and has a unique gameplay aspect for the spirit hunting that's nice and passive. The lofi music and soundscape is the largest draw in for me, as you can even just make musicless ambiance or even play a youtube video with these new effects over it. Having my little guy doing the same tasks as me helps me mirror and stay focused, and then I put him on a break whenever I'm taking one too. Also Hedgelog is still best spirit ftw.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Was I skeptical? sure, did this live up to the hype? For me personally, yes! I'm a very visual person and I need lots of visual stimulation on at once to keep my attention, this provided a way for me to do that through my desktop while working! I am a writer and just today I have finished a good chunk of work I needed done with the help of this lovely game/ tool. I tend to get very overstimulated by some lo-fi and or background noise because stuff like rain, wind, or thunder are too loud and distracting, but Spirit City: Lofi Sessions fixed that by simply applying volume sliders to those things! the art style is lovely and the customization and spirits are a solid 10/10! Be warned, though, that this app game is a bit big and takes quite a few background resources! I will also warn that there is no (current) ability to link to things like spotify, but youtube is an option. The tools provided are very compact and nice to have all in a central app (especially the journal and to-do list because I lose my physical ones) But, if you tend to be pretty organized and minimal with things like timers, notebooks etc, then this app game might not be essential for you!! Well that's my piece! do with that as you will!! cya my diggity diggity dawgs!

_childDocuments_.review: The thing about all the other productivity apps/programs/etc is that they're needlessly elaborate, even the "simple" ones. My ADHD can't afford the executive function to figure out, optimize, and memorize an entire system unless I'm dying, especially when the whole point is to streamline and take the hassle OUT of a schedule. So far, Spirit City has been e x a c t l y what I've been trying to find for years. A To Do list, a timer, a habit tracker, and a little ambience to enjoy with a cute creature. No more, no less, and actually ADHD friendly.Great, simple interface, a small but well executed and thoughtful number of options for customizing the room, sounds, and various effects to create the atmosphere you want. Sometimes you don't need a bunch of convoluted elements, but a small handful of elements done well. Super excited to the update in a couple days, I'm really rooting for these developers. Oh, and they get a ton of bonus points for the pride flag options as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this. _childDocuments_.review: Strengths:- great core concept- nails main aesthetic goals- sensible basic toolsWeaknesses:- tools are basic only- can be quite resource-intensive for a productivity aidAs per other reviews, Spirit City is a focus/productivity tool with light gamification.You can array your in-game character in a variety of ways, doing a variety of things; different combinations of activity, place, time, and sound will slowly lure in new spirit companions to hang out with. By luring spirits, running the task timer, and checking off your to-do list, and simply by having Spirit City open, you gradually level up, which opens up more spirits to be summoned. All of this happens to music from a range of lofi playlists and/or streamed from YouTube through the in-game browser, plus your choice from a pretty wide selection of background noises, from rain / fireplace / distant streets to sizzling cookery or just white noise. First off, this is a great idea! And Spirit City looks great, capturing the particular aesthetic it takes as its goal. (If you dislike the various topoi and codes associated with 'lofi', this is…not something for you.) The music's a fun, gentle selection which I genuinely enjoy working to, and I'm impressed by the set of background sounds you can layer in, and by the precise volume control offered per-sound. And I think most of the spirit companions are adorable, though this is probably a matter of taste. There're a good number of them, so if you set yourself to lure one new one a day you can keep that up for a while. I'm probably older than the average Steam user—let's just say I was alive for some of the Cold War—and I am as far as I know dully neurotypical, so please look at other reviews for other accounts of how helpful or not this app is for a range of different people. But for my experience, the pomodoro timer here works well, and the basic to-do and habits lists have their uses. There's an in-game currency for buying more clothes and interior decor, but there aren't in-game transactions with real money (thank goodness!), and the in-game currency seems (so far, to me) plentiful enough unless you want to buy everything immediately.I don't know whether this next thing is a deliberate choice or an omission, but I also  the fact that the program just loads in to the main room; in this day and age, it's great to open anything and not immediately get five spuriously urgent notifications for DLC/features/news to the face—so, thank you to the devs for not doing that, and long may it continue.At present, anyone buying this should know that the productivity tools are fairly basic. You can date your to-do items if you want to, and set up multiple to-do lists, but I've not found any within-list sorting functions. The habits menu is a fairly bare-bones prototypical week structure. Neither has any time-within-day granularity. There's a journal you can bung text into, but there's no organisational diary or calendar, as far as I can discover. There's no goal-setting.You should also know that there're what you might call some rough edges in the experience, little things that might grate after a while. For instance, the built-in timer never seems to remember its settings once I close Spirit City. Many of us will have standard ways of working (e.g. 3 x 25-minute work sprints with 10 minute breaks, or whatever) and it's a little bit of a chore to be tuning the timer whenever I open the program. The timer also only makes one sound when it goes off, and to be honest that sound could stand to be more obtrusive—I've read through it without noticing while in a flow state once or twice.One other caveat is kind of inherent in the project: unless you have a computer with at least a bit of muscle, Spirit City will take a non-trivial amount of resources to run in ways that more routine (and more fully-featured) productivity software won't. I don't think this is an optimisation problem, and there's an option that lets you cut the target framerate when the program's not in focus (great idea! bravo). It's just in the nature of a project in the Unreal Engine that you can't, say, toss this onto an ancient laptop at the side of your desk in the way that you can with other, more boring focus/productivity tools. Many people reading this will no doubt have hulking gaming machines which will let them run Spirit City on a third screen without really noticing anything (or whatever). But if that's not you, be alert to the trade-off involved in in running this.Those're my only hesitations about Spirit City. Several of these might well improve with further development, though I don't think you should necessarily spend money on potential alone. So, at the time of writing (September 2024), this's a pomodoro timer with some pretty basic to-do features, and an excellent, charming aesthetic. If that sounds worth the price to you, I happily recommend it.
