_childDocuments_.review: When I first stumbled upon Spirit City: Lofi Sessions through a cozy gaming group on Facebook, I wasn’t sure what to expect. The post that introduced me featured a player who had left the game running in the background, only to find her husband had given her character a beard — a cute and hilarious moment that caught my attention. The comments were brimming with admiration for the game’s art, and soon enough, I found myself diving into this charming little world.At its core, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a productivity tool wrapped in the aesthetic of a cozy game. What makes it stand out is its unique blend of task tracking, lofi beats, and the delightful collection of “Spirits” and decorations. I honestly didn’t think I’d enjoy it as much as I do, but its approach to productivity is surprisingly effective. You’re encouraged to set tasks, and while you wait for a Spirit to appear, you end up focusing on real-world goals—working, studying, or cleaning—just to pass the time.The magic of the game lies in the subtlety of its design. Rather than being a game you’re glued to, it lets you engage with life around you, all while keeping you hooked on what’s next. The slow-paced waiting for Spirits to appear and the anticipation of new decorations for your cozy little abode make for a perfect blend of relaxing gameplay and a sense of accomplishment. It somehow encourages productivity without being forceful, turning "waiting" into a motivation to get things done.The art style is wonderfully soothing, with its warm color palette and soft animations that transport you to a peaceful urban haven. The lofi soundtrack is, of course, a huge highlight. It creates a mellow background vibe that’s perfect for staying focused or unwinding after a long day. I find myself leaving the game on while I work, as the music and visuals create a sense of calm, and the steady appearance of Spirits adds just the right amount of distraction to keep things interesting.I’m eagerly awaiting new content and can’t wait to see what kind of decorations and Spirits the developers come up with next. If you’re looking for a unique way to stay productive or simply want to enjoy a soothing atmosphere while organizing your tasks, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a delightful experience that I highly recommend. It’s not just a game—it’s a companion for your everyday life.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is both a game and productivity tool, where players can create their avatar, discover and befriend Spirits, and make use of things like to-do lists, a Pomodoro timer, and a habit tracker and journal—all with built-in lofi playlists and customizable ambient sounds!Here’s a little bit about why I love and use Spirit City: Lofi Sessions --I’m not only a VTuber, but I’m also a published author. When I’m writing or editing, I always need music alongside rain and crackling fire sounds to help me relax and focus. Until Spirit City: Lofi Sessions, this meant keeping several browser tabs open on my other monitor for that purpose. Unfortunately, I tend to get distracted very quickly if my browser is open, so this always resulted in me losing focus for hours at a time. Scrolling social media ends up eating so much of my time when I can’t focus.All-in-all, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions has been a great boost to my productivity. The music in-game is stream-safe, so it’s perfect for cozy co-working streams. If you don’t need to worry about stream-safe music, there’s also an in-game music browser so you can select your own tunes to listen to.While I don’t have much in the way of critique for the game, there are some things I would like to see! I think it would be fantastic if we could import .VRM and similar models in place of the character creation, and I’d also like to see some in-depth twitch integration, such as shared task lists.Of course, I would like to see more things like more hairstyles and other cosmetic pieces for characters as well—especially long hair—but I do think they’ve started with a great and diverse selection for launch! If there’s anything you’d like to see them add to the game, they have a Suggestions & Ideas section in their Discord—so make sure you voice any ideas you have there!If you have limited monitor space, such as a single monitor; if you put Spirit City: Lofi Sessions into windowed mode, you can use Windows Key + Arrow Keys to move the game around, including having it vertical on half your screen. So, if you can’t have a full window up, try and see if split screen will work for your workspace!Overall, I think Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a wonderful productivity tool and game, well worth the investment. If you struggle with focus, or would simply like cozy little friends to join you while you work, I highly recommend giving Spirit City: Lofi Sessions a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Spirit City if a game isn´t what you´re looking for. What is it then?TL;DR Your own custom Lofi Stream with the added extras of nice sounds, visuals and productivity tools.I suggest checking out Let´s Plays, there are a couple on YouTube and Steam´s video page with no commentary. They´ll give you a good look at what you´re getting. That mostly being a nice ambiance through a cute mostly customizable, animated screen saver with a couple of productivity tools and background music along with a few different sounds, keyboard typing, rain, or Fireplace crackling for example (with customizable loudness). There´s also collecting Spirits and customizing things of course. But while they are the game aspect, they´re only a fraction of the experience. If you get Spirit City only for them, you´ll end up somewhat disappointed and bored. Personally, I think they´re just meant to add to the ambiance and give you some motivation to get used to the app, not be the focus. That´s because YOU and your real life tasks are the focus. So keep in mind that a game meant to stop you from getting distracted, won´t shower you with gameplay and complexity. And that´s perfectly fine!Look into my gameplay:With minimum effort, I managed to get all Spirits in under 2 days. More or less half using it (setting it up, reading up on the spirits and customizing), and for the rest, leaving the game running in the background. I got to level ten on the first day and I believe level 14 and thus all the spirits on the second day. It does slow up, I´m level 16 now on day three, but since I have all the spirits I really don´t mind. Also because you get more than enough spirit credits, the currency you get for leveling up.The Customization:Btw don´t worry about spending your spirit credits, the first couple of levels gave me enough to customize everything to my liking, room, pet, and character. I´ve spent maybe 2k, that´s worth 4 levels. (You still can´t preview before buying, so I´ve bought a couple of wallpapers for 50 Spirit credits each messing around) I have 6k currently.Honestly, I was a little disappointed with the customization myself. For example, after reading a review praising the options for male characters, I thought it´d be fun to try making one. That along with keeping an aesthetic probably made everything harder. Taking the eyes, for example, the ones without lashes make up exactly one-third. (4 eyes out of 12) The biggest eyes without lashes are quite smaller than the ones that do have them. I personally think they look a little weird.But even though things are kind of sparse in general, and you can mostly only choose from limited presets, even picky me ended up satisfied. (Sadly character creation only has a pastel color wheel without saturation options. only a slider to muddy your color to grey max. Careful btw, you only have the option to accept the color you made, so don´t mess with the wheel unless you´re sure you want to change it)The Conclusion:This isn´t a game overflowing with content. That´s okay. It´s a really cute app that helps you stay motivated and focused on your real-life tasks instead!CUT THE DEVS SOME SLACKPlease keep in mind that this game just had its full release this month. It´s still a fairly new indie game and with the three-developer team, I´m impressed with what we did get. I´m looking forward to further updates. As of writing this, the developers already released an update with 2 more hairstyle options.I can´t wait to see new spirits and more customizability options, but that´ll only happen with enough support from our side.

_childDocuments_.review: While I think this product is a little simple and content light, I still want to leave a positive review as I think it's a great idea which I wish there was more of, and I want to encourage them to keep building on it. I'm currently struggling with what I'm pretty sure is ADHD or some other mental ailment which is extremely disruptive to my life, and makes it very difficult to work or carry out tasks. The best way I can describe it is feeling like I have a familiar sitting on my shoulder yelling at me when I'm doing something it doesn't want me to do. It makes things as simple as replying to emails feel like a massive, draining effort. I'm told the waiting list for triage, never mind treatment, is 12 months. I saw this, and downloaded it as a tool to help, and it does seem to do that. I feel like I'm progressing on a game while I'm working on something, and the game does not constantly demand my attention. Unlike other idle games, there's no incentive to click on things to speed it up, nor incentives to constantly reset the game to boost the rate the numbers go up. You just leave it running, occasionally changing the setup to unlock a new creature, listen to perfectly chosen chill music, and that's about it. That's exactly what I need.My concern is that this will not last very long. I've had the game running for 6.5 hours, and unlocked 12 out of 18 available creatures already. I have all the money I need to set up the room how I want it, meaning any more cosmetics I unlock are just for the sake of it. No new features have been unlocked yet, so I think that's all there is. I can see myself hitting a ceiling in a few days. I see the game has had some free updates, which is good, but I'm concerned any meaty content updates will arrive in the form of paid DLC, which is not great (though the devs have said they won't lock productivity tools behind it at least). I think the game needs some long-term goals. Big unlocks that cost a lot of currency, which reward you for establishing good habits. These could be new activities for the avatar to do, new locations to travel to (with new spirits to unlock there) or similar. I also think that the productivity tools like the to-do list and timer, while great, are too basic. I want to group tasks by work/personal, for example, but all I can do is make a list and reorder it at the moment. So to summarise:- great idea, does what it's supposed to, please flesh it out more.

_childDocuments_.review: The art is cute, the atmosphere is nice, it works great for co-working streams (so far anyway), and it has a pretty useful variety of soundscapes. Plus, the devs seem pretty intent on updating it, albeit slowly. That said, this is a game you're (presumably) supposed to leave on for hours and hours at a time, so IMO progress needs to be WAY slower. I like the other features enough that I'll likely still use it when I'm out of stuff to unlock, but I feel like I'm going to unlock everything in the game in less than a week of using this for work.

_childDocuments_.review: im drowning in all the new room cosmetics (positive), send help, someone throw me a life raft.Jokes aside: Spirit City LS is a really great "game", although it's best to call/view it as more of a hybrid lofi-fi player productivity app with a bunch of customisation (but for the purpose of this review, we'll call it a game). Not only does this game provide a pretty solid roster of Lofi to listen to, but SC (Spirit City) also allows you to use an in-built Web Music Browser (Youtube), so you get to listen to all your favourite songs and whatnot through here! On top of this, SC provides a selection of background/white noise that you can toggle on and off, which is a great help to those who might need/use background audio to concentrate (me). When you aren't running Spirit City in the background (either just to vibe or to study/work), you'll get the opportunity to spend your in-game currency (which you gain naturally from logging in, levelling up, and completing tasks) to customise and decorate both your room and your character! And oh boy are there already a good amount of customisation options available (plus updates will probably bring M O R E), so you'll def be content. Not only do you get room and character customisation, but you also get to collect little dudes (creatures) who'll hang out with you while your character chills out in the room.If you have the spicy brain (neurospicy) then this might be a great thing to nab and just have in the background while you work on something, it's honestly helped me a good amount (anyways, back to my tasks I go with Lofi and rain cheering me on)

_childDocuments_.review: is essentially a customizable Lofi girl with a productivity tools and creature collecting. This non-game allows you to customize your own Lofi character, choosing their appearance, the room's decor, what activity they're doing, the music station from a selection, the outside conditions, and the spirit accompanying them. The developer has already added a few updates, so we'll see more spirits, decorations, and avatar customization items over time if there isn't an option you want yet.Just like the original Lofi Girl, you are supposed to use this program while doing something else such as cleaning or homework. Creatures are collected by having certain outdoor conditions met and activities your avatar is doing while the game idles, so if you're running it solely to collect them and not doing anything else, you're basically doing it wrong and may be waiting a long time.The aforementioned tools are a to-do list, timer, habit tracker, and journal. Using these tools and having the game idle earns you in-game currency to buy decorations and clothing as well as experience points to level up and gain access to more spirits.Overall, while not perfect, this is a cute program. I am all for the gamification of life improvements and look forward to seeing what they release in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The 1.4 update has added a huge amount of extra customisation for the room decor, from furniture to knick-knacks. The themes throughout are centred around cosy and cute, but at the same time you can make some pretty austere set-ups if minimalist is more your thing. It's worth the base price now, whereas before it was a little light on customisation options. In terms of productivity tools, of course there's going to be more intricate and nuanced ones out there and the ones in here are fairly simple - a journal, a task list, a weekly habit tick sheet, and a pomodoro timer. I can't see any export tools for all the extensive journal entries you could write, so do with that what you will. But if you're looking to be able to customise the girl in the studying girl lo-fi vids, and put your own spin on the background the avatar works in front of, then this is where you can do so. Soundscapes and playlists are limited. The new update has added some of the more major ones (ocean sounds, running water) but if you're looking for something you can adjust to suit your very specific preferences you're better off using a soundboard in the background and running the game over the top. Same for the music if lo-fi playlists aren't for you. I do like a bit of lo-fi, and the playlists they have in-game are both pleasant and unobtrusive, which is what you want if you're using the game as a focus tool. Sometimes I run my own in the background because the in-game web browser doesn't have an ad-blocker on it. Is the game worth the base price? IMO - yes. Will I be able to make the character look like me/my imaginary friend/my character? Probably. Maybe. A young and cute version of them yes. There are options for male, female and enby, with all colours available to use as skin tones. Facial feature range is extremely limited - this is not the BG3 character creator. Spirit City has a definite style which is quite clear from the trailers, so do bear that in mind.tl;dr - there's better time management tools out there, but if you want something that mildly gamifies your background music experience with the ability to customise your avatar, collect spirit mascots, and the aesthetic of the game appeals to you, then Spirit City 100% delivers on that front.I'm looking forward to seeing what the devs do next in terms of dlcs and future content.

_childDocuments_.review: If you asked me a few months ago, I wouldn't have recommended Spirit City: Lofi Sessions yet. There were many spirits to collect passively, and some customization options, but that was about it. And tool-wise, there wasn't much either; once you collected all the spirits, you were mostly at the mercy of leaving the program open for hours to accumulate EXP in hopes of leveling up for tickets to buy a few things. But I held out hope for the promises the developers made.And I'm so glad to tell you that they made good on their word! I wholeheartedly recommend Spirit City: Lofi Sessions now if you're looking for a tool to help you be more productive while also giving you the joy of personalization!To start with, there's a lot more customizability now as compared to before; instead of just a bed, desk, cushions and rugs along with the wall and floor to change, pretty much every aspect of the tool is customizable, with a lot of options and color variations!The method of earning tickets is better now too; I don't debate on opening the tool to leave it running for hours, just for 500 tickets if i manage to level up. You earn 1 ticket a minute now! So any period of having it open is still productive, and it incentivizes opening the tool since there's a definitive reward for doing so, regardless of for how long.The productivity part is what I was most happy about; the task window is now resizable, and has a calendar for due dates as well as tabs to separate different tasks! All I can ask for to improve this personally is a permanent calendar. All in all, Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a calming, fun tool that has vastly improved my productivity, and now that the devs have started delivering on their promises and have been adding more things to the tool, it's been improving more and more with each update, and I'm glad to get to see it grow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just the perfect gamified productivity aid. Make your own cute little lofi avatar, customize a gorgeous little room for them to be in, and then create your Perfect Soundtrack For Success. Do you like lofi music? Multiple playlists already there for you. Do you like a different lofi playlist? It has a built-in youtube browser that you can play other music from without tabbing in and out and getting distracted. Do you like various soundscapes to fill the silence or add to your music? There are options for different weather sounds (wind, rain, thunder, crickets) or indoor sounds (fireplace, record white noise, keyboard clacks, food sizzling) or even just white/brown noises that you can select. AND they change your environment! Choose rain and a crackling fire? See rain out the window and the fireplace roaring to life. Choose wind and thunder? See the trees outside swaying and the clouds flicker with distant lightning.It's got built-in productivity tools like a customizable pomodoro, a to-do list, a habit tracker, and a journal. It's become part of my daily routine to open this in the morning and plan my day in it and with it, and then I use it to complete the tasks I need with body-doubling and the perfect soundtracks for my mood and activity.I *love* this. It's cute, it encourages you to Get Things Done, and it gives you incentive to Get Things Done with little tokens you can use to buy new outfits or housing decor. Also, doing different tasks in different spaces can earn you cute little (also customizable) pets to keep you company!10/10, so excited to see what more the devs will bring to this, but already delighted by what we have today.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, cute game where you can collect little guys that don't do anything besides being an extra decoration for the room you're decorating. _childDocuments_.review: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a nice little indie game/productivity tool - it combines basic productivity features (to-do list, timer, habit tracker, and journal) with a cosy aesthetic, relaxing lofi music and cute spirits/pets. You customise an avatar, decorate the room and have your avatar do activities in the room alongside their chosen spirit companion. Spending time in the game and completing productivity tasks will increase your level, which allows you to buy more decorations and clothing as well as find new spirits. It positively reinforces productivity with this loop.As the game stands at launch, it is good but there are some areas that could be improved upon. For instance, improving the functionality of the productivity tools or adding new features to them - they are relatively basic. However, the developers have stated that they plan to continue to support the game with updates and new content (including new spirits!) so it is likely that the game will only get better from here on out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and love games where you can customize a character to look just like yourself, "Spirit City Lofi Sessions" is going to charm you right out of the gate. One of my favorite things about this game is how spot-on you can get your avatar. From hair color to style, it feels like you're creating a mini digital version of yourself, and I’m here for it! Not to mention, your spirit companion can also be personalized—there are two free cat skins that look almost exactly like my cats.The room decoration aspect is another big win for me. There aren’t a ton of items to choose from initially, but I’m hopeful more options will unlock as I level up or with future updates. I'd love to see a "Barbie core" room in bright neon pink, Tiffany blue, mint, lavender, and white accents! More "cute kawaii" items, please, and a bit less of the "cottage core" vibes. The game lets you adjust the lighting, and my favorite setting is "afternoon," where everything pops in bright, colorful tones rather than muted ones.You level up by simply spending time in your room, clicking around, taking photos, and listening to lofi tunes. I won't lie—I usually play on mute while watching TV. The music isn’t my main draw; it’s the dress-up and design elements that keep me engaged. Plus, the game is currently on sale for under $10 on Steam, making it well worth checking out.However, here's the catch: the game needs more content. It’s a slow burn, which is perfect for playing in short bursts—an hour here, an hour there. But once I’ve customized my character, room, and spirit friend to my liking, I don’t feel the urge to keep changing things unless new dress-up and design items are added. After about an hour of play, I can already sense the potential for burnout if the game doesn’t get regular content updates.In summary, Spirit City Lofi Sessions has a lot of charm, especially if you love customization and cozy vibes, but it needs more depth to keep players coming back for the long haul. For now, it's a cute, low-commitment game that’s worth the price if you're looking for something light and relaxing. Fingers crossed for more updates to keep the magic going!

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit City is probably the best tool I have found for staying on track with work and is a recommended pickup for anyone, regardless of if you are a student or not.It is not as if the game has no issues and is perfect from release. The character customization is a bit more limited than I would like, the YouTube music player can be annoying sometimes (which is actually mostly YouTube's fault), and sometimes there are clunky animations for the activities. I would also like to be able to have certain background effects on without the noise. For example, sometimes I find the fireplace sound annoying and hard to tune out when reading. However, the effect is beautiful and really suits the room that I have made, and I cannot currently have one or the other.These complaints are completely drowned out by how good the rest of the game is. The music provided is fantastic, and even if you are not a fan, there is the YouTube player where you can use your own music. You can also just put your music on Spotify or your browser and have it running outside of the game with no issues. The timer function and to-do list are useful and have been given various QOL updates. There is also a journal if you don't keep a physical one. It can also just be used for random thoughts. The decoration is cute, as is the character customization. Both are frequently updated and the dev team is fantastic. I recently had an article that I was struggling to sit down and actually write; this game got me motivated enough to finish it.  Spirit Cities does its job. Buy it. Trust.If anything else, this game is worth it just to support the dev team. They are always super responsive to feedback, they work diligently on the game, they are inclusive, and no new content is put behind a paywall. Buy it. Trust.I am not a paid sponsor. Buy it. Trust.

_childDocuments_.review: This Idler/ Time tracker does a lot of things right, I love running it in the background when I need to complete my tasks and to keep myself from getting destracted or wandering of mid task. There are a lot of Idlers, yes. But from all I "played" till now I enjoyed this one the most. The leveling System gets kinda slow over time after you reach Rank 30, and even after nearly 200 Hours in I am "only" at 45, so you don't reach lvl 50 that fast and I think that's a good thing - other than some of the other Idlers where the requirements are "Be 24h in the Game" or "Be 100h in the Game". I love the slow pace at which you earn XP for the time you spend working at your Tasks and even when I reach Rank 50 I will continue to use this one. What does Spirit City offer?- A daylie and weeklie task tracker- Setting a individual Timer- A Journal for writing with 12 different prompts like: "What's on my mind this morning?" or "What can I do today for my physical and mental healt?" and "Free Writing"- Five Lofi Playlists and a Web Music browser- 10 different Sounds you can lay over the Lofi Music for aditional atmosphere - Customizable Charakter and different Clothes- 4 different Places in your Room where you can put your character for aktivities with two - three activities like Reading, writing, drawing, knitting- Customizable Room- Adorable Spirit Companions that are also customizable with different desings (You find these by luring them out with the right settings as hinted in the Spiritdex)All in all I really like the features and how the devs implimented them in the Game.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game so far! Whether you are looking for a productivity helper or just a chill little game you can make an avatar in and listen to chill music, I highly recommend it!!-2 body sliders for masc/fem and thin/thick builds-Nice variety of hair and eyes (including natural black hairstyles and a headscarf!), with a palette of colors for skin, hair/eyebrows, eyes, and horns. The palette has some standard colors but also some cool multicolor/gradients. If you don't like those options there's a full color picker as well.-Nice variety of clothing/accessories available from the start, more can be bought with the in-game currency. There's no microtransactions, you earn the in-game currency just by playing the game and completing tasks.-Various aspects of your room can be customized, and you can buy more decoration variants/colors with the in-game currency.-Everything is preset colors though, which isn't a big deal for me because there's a pretty nice variety.-No spoilers, but the in-game tutorial does a good job of explaining how you get spirits and there's a hint system too that's really nice!-The spirits are all super cute and have various color variants you can unlock with the in-game currency, as well as a Spiritdex with lore about each one!-Small spoiler: -Really solid, has multiple "activities" you can have your avatar do, with a few locations around the room. Not every activity can be done at each location, but the availability/selection makes sense.-Multiple productivity assistants: Habits, To-do List, Timer, and a Journal for writing whatever you'd like!-Multiple themed playlists of Lo-fi music provided by Homework Radio, along with a in-game browser that opens YouTube if you have a specific playlist/music you want to listen to.-Multiple sounds you can play solo or alongside the music with their own volume slider, some of which affect the ambience of the room/landscape.-4 times of day to choose from that affects the lighting and outside landscape.-There's no free camera to look around the room/change the angle, you're locked in based on the activity you're doing, although there is a "whole room" option to zoom out and see the entire room. I would love to be able to move the camera around on my own to see more of the details in the room closer and from different angles.-When you click on the custom color picker in character customization it doesn't remember your current color, it just goes back to the default white/grey, and there's no way to back out of the color picker. I was showing my partner and had to force close the game so I wouldn't have to redo my skin color.-Hiding the UI doesn't remove the timer widget at the bottom right of the screen.Overall I think it's a solid game/productivity helper and it's well-priced! Definitely glad I picked this up!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a pretty big proponent of the Pomodoro technique since the pandemic forced everyone to work and study from home for a time; so this tool built-into a Steam game is pretty great. I recommend this for hardcore productivity nerds who like cozy vibes. I'm not a fan of lofi, but the tunes here aren't bad, and you can always use the web browser player to just play what you want.That said, this is clearly geared towards teens through college students, and lacks a lot of character customization for older players (30's and up) or those that work from home. There's also no customization for various disabilities (hearing devices, wheelchairs, prostheses, etc.). So there's only really "diverse" representation at a very surface level (LGBTQIA+, skin tones), but nothing deeper than that. Hairstyles and body types are surprisingly limited. I found collecting spirits very fast and ran out of "things to do" to motivate me to focus and use the tool more heavily, and wish there was more variety for characters, spirits, and room decoration. I didn't find myself using the journal feature since I'm a pen and paper kind of person; and like others, wish there was a calendar sync. I'm hoping a lot of the suggestions that have been coming through reviews and Discord will be added in future updates since this tool really is a "diamond in the rough" scenario. :)

_childDocuments_.review: ✅Great productivity tool✅Relaxing ✅Cosmetic customization✅Good ambient music options➖Could use more masculine clothes/postures➖No ability to favorite songs➖Ironically the in-game browser doesn’t work for the actual Lofi Girl streamGame World: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions (SCLS) only really has a single “level” of the game world, which consists of a bedroom. This isn’t the kind of bedroom where kinky stuff happens, no siree, this is the kind of bedroom where you get stuff done! The room in SCLS consists of a very customizable space where the player can partake in various comforting activities. You can opt to change anything from wallpaper to floor, all the way to lighting, time of day, and ambient sounds. You choose whatever works best for you when it comes to background noise. Narrative: There isn’t much narrative here, it's kind of like “You Need a Budget” having a story when that’s clearly not the intended purpose. There are some spirit animal-type things that you can read and learn more about, but that’s it. Length: As long as you want, this is intended to be a background, almost idle, game, so this varies greatly. Controls: Simple left clicking with KBM setup, you navigate menus with the mouse, nothing complex. Mechanics: There’s some good mechanics here. First that is unique to the type of game SCLS is, you have the spirit animals. How it works is you have a clue, something like “You’re hearing some odd noises by the fireplace when it's dark out.” You then know that you have to spend some time near the fireplace after setting the light level to night time. After a random amount of time (something like ~15min for me on avg), you get a cosmetic pet and an achievement. Aside from the pets, the only other mechanic is collecting cosmetics. You have a daily reward for using your timer and notes, then you accumulate levels every minute spent playing. Overall, if I just have Youtube open anyways with the Lofi soundtrack on, which I often do when working, then having this game open is a no-brainer instead. I do like the mechanics, and while there could still be a ton of better idle options, it's still more customizable than a simple Youtube stream. Difficulty: No difficulty here, this is chill time. Quality: Graphics are decent. Kind of looks like a PS3 game, but it's cartoony enough that it doesn’t look bad. UI: I found the UI slightly confusing at first, but after finding a spirit animal or two, it started to become natural. There is something wrong with the in-game browser though, I can watch any Youtube videos through it, but ironically streams seem to be blocked, which is exactly what Lofi Girl is. Performance: No issues and I found background performance to be negligible. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: The sound effects are great. You have a lot of options available ranging from things like waves or thunderstorms to rain and even white noise variants. When it gets close to lunch you can even play grill sizzling sounds! Music: Great. I love the Lofi ambiance when I’m working and this program delivers in spades. There are a ton of songs to choose from, and you can even watch Youtube videos if you run out. I would estimate there to be somewhere around 5-7 playlists each containing 20-30 songs. Aside from the usefulness as a background program, I cannot think of a reason to “Replay” this in the normal sense, in the same way that you would not replay an idle game. Props to achievements though. A solid piece of software, though I struggle to call it a game. I feel like this has definitely increased my productivity since trying it out. If you are a fan of music in the background while you work, I highly recommend it. You can find my curator page here:

name: Chronique des Silencieux
detailed_description: Set in 1970s southern France, you play a rookie private eye tasked to dig out the secrets of a stubborn old man. Think on your feet while you follow your leads : ask questions to witnesses, detect their lies, hypothesize why and finally confront the silent ones running from their past. A Strange Request You are entrusted with the peculiar case of Victor Dousvalon. This old history professor is known for shrouding his past life in secrecy, even from his own daughter Catherine. But an apparently harmless accident motivates him to hire you to help Catherine trace back the steps of his life. Why can't he simply tell her his own story? Why does Catherine, who has been so distant with her father these past years, suddenly want to know about him? Your first case will decidedly be a delicate one... Anything Goes to Break the Silence! Get engrossed in the handy work of a detective : search through family papers, ask personal questions, call at inopportune times, and be generally nosy. Head First Investigation No watching characters think for you, this is your time to prove your deductive powers. Choose leads, follow them to the end or stop when you think you’ve got the right idea. But you'll need to be convincing to push the silent ones to talk! A People’s History Piece together the lives, the choices, and the tragedies people are running from and walk a mile in their shoes. Discover History, not from a bird’s eye view, but from the ground, where folks have to continue living and coping, each in their own unique way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a very good detective game. First, I should point the superficial flaws: The game is extremely buggy. Every other time I opened the journal (something that is necessary very often), I ran into either a game-crash or a softlock, which required me to restart the program. To the game's credit, I should point out that it autosaves constantly and I did not have to replay any segments due to this. But even so, having to go back through all the start menus about once every hour is not an ideal gameplay experience.Another superficial flaw is that the game is difficult to read. The text stored in the journal is of a font that is thin enough such that some pieces of the letters do not show up at all at the game's default resolution. In addition, the size of the text characters and spacing of the letters makes it difficult to read the text at a glance. The testimonies cannot be zoomed in on at all, and some of the documents' text was still illegible even when viewed at full zoom. There is a slider in the option menu labeled "text size," but after messing with it a bit, I cannot claim to know whether or not it actually affects anything.Finally, there's the important stuff: the detective gameplay. Simply put, the game gives you insufficient evidence or guidance. Many times throughout the game, I found myself unsure what question I was even supposed to be answering. Due to the mechanics also not being clearly explained, I found myself unsure what I was suppsed to be doing at any given time. Here is one example in particular that stands out to me: the "Connections" feature is explained as a way to find connections between evidence and testimonies, with no more info given. So, when I attempt to connect a testimony saying that someone is named "Veronique" with the name "Veronique" that appears on a document, I expect to get some sort of feedback, but no. The game does not let you prove that that document relates to that person, because who the document belongs to isn't one one of the question the game wants you to answer, and you're expected to just know that. Once I did get past all the glitches and manage to use the ingame hint system, it did give me a vague idea of what question I needed to answer, but not much more than that.More egregious than this, however, is that the deductions themselves rely on extremely shaky evidence. At first I assumed that the evidence was just well hidden or illegible, and the logic convoluted, but those assumptions were shaken when I played the section of the game where we went over a few conclusions with detailed logic (which the player was still providing). Playing through this section, it became easily apparent just how ♥♥♥♥ this game's logic really is. The clearest example:  For reference, one of the statements that that deduction relies on consists of a single throwaway line. Another question in the same sequence is literally unnkowable, and the game's indended? solution requires reinterpreting one of the words into something clearly not intended by the person asking the question so as to change the question into an answerable one. If the game gave any indication that this is what you are supposed to do, or at the very least given me more than one chance to input the correct answer, this might have been a cool puzzle. But it does nothing of the sort.I did not continue playing the game after this first confrontation. I suppose it is possible that the game suddenly becomes better about some of these things in the following chapters, but I find that highly doubtful.

_childDocuments_.review: A detective game with a great atmosphere, a deep and moving story. and lines full of character. What I liked is that you really need to actively investigate and find discrepancies in the different testimonies and documents, so that piece by piece you can complete the puzzle and understand what happened. You then make hypothesis that, if true, will unlock the secretive character’s padlocks. In each chapter you then have a confrontation à la Ace Attorney. A very fresh game, also with very nice animated scenes and a great soundtrack, all in all a delightful indie gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game would have done a lot better in reviews with more playtesting before release.  I waited until I saw the developers made multiple updates and patches before playing and I’m glad I did.  I didn’t run into any tech issues.I really enjoyed the game, but ohhhh is it hard!  You play as a young detective trying to discover the secrets of those around him.  Lots of interesting characters and stories of life in France during and after WWII and the French Resistance.  You collect conversations and documents and then you need to make correlations and deductions to be able to open the chapter’s final confrontation and reveal.  Most of the time I could tell what was going on, but what was difficult for me was picking the exact lines to correlate or my deductions would get a ‘that’s true, but …’ response, telling me I needed to make a bigger jump in my conclusions.There is an automatic save upon exit and the game is completely mouse driven.  This is a game for those who like serious deduction games with very little hand holding.  There is a senior detective that can help you, but it will cost you points.  It had a complicated story of war, choices, family, and repercussions.  I liked this game it very much.  I would recommend it to those who like reading and making deductions and getting caught up in a historic period in time.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely have a soft spot for detective mysteries, so Chronic seemed to be certainly something that was exactly the kind of game that I would enjoy. In most parts it is, but in some parts, not so much. It’s a prime example of a title you’d love to love, but the game itself does its damndest to break your heart.The game begins when our main character arrives at Bordeaux in search of his uncle. Right off the bat we learn that our uncle is in jail, so we need to start sniffing around so that we can get him out of there.We gather evidence, talk to people in hopes for clues and most importantly, connect the dots -literally. The core gameplay feature of Chronique is deduction. You have to do your own research, and conclusions based on that. It’s the biggest strength of the game, but also its greatest downfall.You can link evidence on people, and getting it right will reveal more dialogue options, for example. You advance the story through the means of gathering evidence, linking it, and then presenting your conclusions which in turn opens up new dialogue options, which lead to new evidence, and new linkable material.Linking pieces of evidence together and making deductions based on that is really interesting, but on many occasions the game does fight you on this. I understand that as we are playing a game, there just can’t be unlimited alternatives to these kinds of situations, but in many cases the game does require a rather specific solution which is very easy to miss.The game is fortunately very logical at least in the most parts, so gathering clues and connecting them to others is very fluent. The sense of progression is always present, and generally you have a good idea on what you’re supposed to do next.The story takes place in 1960s France, and I rather enjoyed it. There are some grammar errors in the script, but nothing too major. The detective work and the gameplay that accompanies it connects to the story extremely well, and I’m really impressed by the fact that the gameplay does not feel one bit superficial.The game also looks really beautiful. The art direction reminds a lot of old Tintin graphic novels, which probably isn’t an accident. Graphics are accompanied with a soundtrack that has a distinct 60s vibe in it. The game nails audiovisuals spot-on.Chronique is set on an isometric perspective, which does create a set of problems. Moving the character is a chore, in both mouse and keyboard. Because the perspective is locked, you need to press down two arrow keys to move the character in a straight path, and if you use a mouse, you better have your clicking fingers greased up. The camera is so close to the ground, that you’ll be constantly clicking in order to move from one place to another.The game was also riddled with bugs at launch. The developers have been ironing them out with a respectable pace, but during my playthrough the game did crash a couple of times, and there were a few softlocks as well.In conclusion, Chronique does have its moments, but they are unfortunately overshadowed with some technical issues and problems in the game’s logic. Fortunately, these are things that can be fixed, and it seems that the developers are dedicated to patching up their creation.Chronique has a lot of promise, and the core idea is excellent. It’s a shame that the execution is not quite on the par of the idea itself. It’s a very decent detective game with great ideas for gameplay. If you can overlook the issues mentioned previously, it’s definitely a title worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me a lot of the boardgame/gamebook Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective. Most of your time will be spent poring over collected testimonies and documents to find connections and contradictions, and there are a lot of said testimonies and documents. I spend a lot of time reading and rereading them to find what the game wants me to. Progress can therefore be pretty slow. You can spend a lot of time without feeling like you are making much progress, and you may want to step away from the game at times and come back later to look at things with fresh eyes. There is a hint system, though it is often of limited help.If this sort of meticulous searching doesn't sound interesting to you, I don't think you are likely to enjoy this game, and it will probably have less mass appeal that a lot of other detective style games. If it does sound interesting to you I would suggest giving it a shot. There is not much else out there like it.The game could also use some extra polish in various areas, but the developer seems pretty responsive and has been pushing out many small bug fixes and improvements since launch about a week and a half ago.Also, for what it's worth, I was a Kickstarter backer of this game. I don't know how or if that has affected my review.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it so bad. I found this game under recommendations for games like ObraDinn and Golden Idol. Unfortunately, it is not like them at all. It takes about 30 min for the actual game to start, in the beginning you're just walking around, getting to know the situation and clicking through not so well written dialogue. By the time the first puzzles started I was already not invested, so the fact that it's not a deduction puzzle, but more like reading comprehension task disappointed me even more. This first slow bloated part seems to be there just to stretch the time, so that you don't return the game. I really dislike this approach, so I ended up returning the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game primarily in French, so I cannot comment extensively on localization issues. Occasionally, I referred to the English translation to make sure I had understood the text correctly, and I found it reasonable.Overall, I enjoyed Chronique des Silencieux, and I liked the detective work and the puzzles. It is not a particularly easy game, but I was able to complete most of my leads without any hints. The exploration is also fairly open-ended. The game reminds me of Lamplight City, except it is not possible to actually come to a completely incorrect conclusion.The game is stymied by many bugs, the most egregious of which is faulty game logic and assumptions about player progression. (In the Prologue, my leads page contained information that I had not actually found yet. Later, in Chapter 2, Eugène reveals some details in his meet-up with Yves that I suspect I was not supposed to know yet, although I did already have some inklings of what he discussed.) However, the developer has been extremely responsive to bug reports, which I appreciate.

_childDocuments_.review: The most confounding crime here is why the game is so unknown.But seriously, the game has a lot going for it. I love the animated look, the characters are surprisingly expressive during conversations. Menus are easy to read and mostly smooth to navigate, which is important when you'll spend so much time there poring over evidence.The story is good so far. It's rare to get a straight up detective story like this that also has proper detecting gameplay; usually its one or the other. History and geography play a factor too, it is a genuine period piece that uses the setting and I'm sure the developers' own knowledge and experience to give an earnestness to it all.Others have noted the issues. The English translation can sometimes be awkward, though not enough to impact the story or your deductions (that I've seen). Most of the difficulty so far has not been from failing to understand the mystery, but not knowing how to register that knowledge with the game to fully explore all the leads. Finding just the right lines to compare can be time consuming, though it does at least feel like detective work and putting things together is rewarding. It can sometimes just feel arbitrary when one connection is fruitless and another yields progress.Still, the investigation mechanics themselves are good. I like how open the connections and hypothesis systems are, it lets deductions feel more like your own and less guided. The confrontations where you use your evidence to corner a suspect are a fun gamification of the classic detective speech.Overall I think this is worth a try for anyone interested in detective games, so long as you accept some jank and frustration are a part of the process. There is a hint system now, and you're allowed to make mistakes, so don't let the reviews about difficulty put you off.Will update if my opinion significantly changes as I get further.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an investigative game with rich historical roots and a slow-burn detective narrative, Chronique des Silencieux is worth your time. Set in post-war France, the game places you in the shoes of Eugène, an amateur sleuth, tasked with unraveling complex webs of deception. The game stands out for its attention to detail and immersive environments, blending 1960s French culture with a jazz-infused soundtrack that adds to the noir vibe​.However, the game can be quite challenging. It's filled with long conversations, detailed document analysis, and a myriad of clues to piece together. Keep in mind that while it offers plenty of depth, it can also test your patience with its slow progression. If you're up for a challenge and enjoy detective games with historical context, the game can be very rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, because I love detective games like Ace Attorney, Danganronpa, Golden Idol, etc. However, I'm at the first confrontation and so far I felt that finding the right connection is more a matter of luck than anything. For example, I thought one hypothesis concerning the drugs was obvious. In fact, I got it right on my first try. However, before I was allowed to make it, I had to find a connection that felt less decisive than several other better pieces of evidence. The confrontation is similar in that several sentences could be used to prove or contradict the same thing, except only one seems to be accepted as correct, making it more of a guessing game than anything.Perhpas I'll play it again at some point, but I'm not confident that the game's connections become less ambiguous later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: This debut game does so much incredible work and features so many aspects, from its writing to its art to its facial animations to its dedication to making the player feel like a real detective, and it nails so many of these aspects, truly delivering a special experience for anyone with a love for point-and-click adventure games. However, to actually get through the title, a player is going to have to deal with several major issues that make Chronique des Silencieux kind of a pain to play. I genuinely loved my time with this gem and I dearly wish I could just point to some of my favourite characters and the beautiful art style and beg everyone to give it a shot, but in its current state, some people just aren’t going to have the patience for it.That being said, the animation (particularly for the characters) is stellar, the gameplay is deeply engaging (if at times frustrating), and the story is well worth experiencing. If you have the patience for an involved point-and-click, this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: Kickstarter backer here (thus no star on the right).What a wonderful game.Even though it is set in the 1970s, the main theme of the game is the events that took place throughout WW2, the things people are silent about, the things that left a mark on them, and that's exactly what you end up investigating: because what happened in the past still paints the present. Thus, I can't describe the game as an entertaining one; moreover, I couldn't play it in a relaxed or tired state: you have to be alert, you have to read carefully what people say to you, you have to peruse documents you found. You know, a detective. And mind you, there are plenty of dialogs and topics you can talk to people about. And all of them are relevant to the big picture.All three cases are carefully connected, and bit by bit you're unveiling the life story of the mysterious man, Victor.It took me 15 hours to solve all three cases. Also, there is a hint system, and don't be afraid to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: So I played this game over the course of a few days. I really enjoyed it! Chronique des Silencieux has a really good flow of events. Talk to a bunch of people and look for clues, review your information, make deductions and finally confront the guilty party with your knowledge and catch them in their lies and contradictions. The music and the likable characters made this game a joy to play through. I actually almost didn't finish this game due to a glitch at the finale of the game, however the game dev responded to my inquiry extremely quickly and managed to fix my save so I could complete my run. It was a great experience that, if you like puzzling together a complete picture from lots of small, interconnected pieces of information I highly recommend checking out this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: You’d better have a good memory if you don’t want to spend hours reading through long blocks of text over and over again in Chronique des Silencieux, searching for that one piece of information that just might connect to or contradict another. The good news is that it’s all presented in a beautiful, evocative period setting with interesting characters, providing enough motivation to keep digging into their backgrounds. Sadly, the occasional graphical glitch, faulty translation and overly demanding deduction requirements make the gameplay experience much harder than it should be. Pierre Feuille Studio has the right idea and introduces a great concept for detective games, but they should have tested and polished it up further before releasing. To their credit, during my 14-hour playthrough they released several updates that gradually improved certain issues, making the third part of the game smoother than the first two. It still wasn’t perfect, but it’s moving in the right direction, so here’s hoping it will get there so more people can enjoy the intriguing elements lurking beneath the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronique des Silencieux

_childDocuments_.review: Set in 1970s southern France, you play a rookie private eye tasked to dig out the secrets of a stubborn old man. Think on your feet while you follow your leads : ask questions to witnesses, detect their lies, hypothesize why and finally confront the silent ones running from their past.

name: Blasphemous 2
detailed_description: Mea Culpa Reborn New Expansion coming soon! DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION INCLUDES Blasphemous 2 - Full Game Blasphemous 2 - Digital Artbook Blasphemous 2 - Original Soundtrack About the Game The second scripture in the Blasphemous series portends the return of The Penitent One, with a story that continues from the free Wounds of Eventide DLC for the original game, where The Heart in the sky heralded the return of The Miracle and foretold the birth of a new miracle child. Awakened in a strange new land, and displaced from his final resting place, The Penitent One is thrust back into the endless cycle of life, death, and resurrection, with no other option than to explore this perilous new world and uncover its long-forgotten secrets. Hordes of grotesque enemies stand in your way, awaiting final judgement by the brutal hand of the Penitent One, with titanic twisted bosses also lurking in the darkness, waiting for their chance to return you to the grave from whence you came. Taking them down won’t be easy, but with Blasphemous 2 offering more chances to customise and improve your skill set, along with several new unique weapons to wield with righteous zeal and unending fury, victory might just be within grasp. Ultimately, only one thing is certain… Penance Never Ends Explore a fuller Non-Linear world Having awoken in a strange new land, your journey starts anew in a series of enchantingly grotesque landscapes, oozing Gothic charm and littered with unforgiving traps. How you tackle the labyrinthian world remains at your discretion, there is no wrong turn to be made, only scores to settle Savage Combat The Penitent One shows no mercy, and with a series of new weapons offering new moves, brutal executions, and expanded combos, destruction will rain on any that stand in his way Customize your playthrough your way Blasphemous 2 offers up new ways to play, with the ability to customise and improve your base skillset, alongside several new unique weapons to unleash devastating attacks on enemies Grand Intense Boss Battles Hordes of monstrous foes stand between you and your goal; twisted bosses with unique attack patters and sundering abilities will put your skills to the test as you fight to stand triumphant when the dust settles Explore a deep new world A whole new world awaits, bustling with mysterious new NPCs to interact with, some will offer aid, some will ask for it, and others will send you on death defying missions to obtain long forgotten items. With so much to see and do, the stories and myths you encounter will help you unpick the games myriad of secrets, granting you a deeper understanding of this strange new world

_childDocuments_.review: Solid stuff again. Amazing art, fantastic soundtrack, tight controls and very good level design. This game is even more Souls-y than the previous one and that's a good thing. I just wish there were fewer gauntlets, especially towards the end you get locked in a room with N waves of enemies a lot, didn't particularly enjoy those.Otherwise, this is a worthy addition to your Metroidvania collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like all the people saying this game is a direct improvement over the first never actually liked the first at all. Almost every change Blasphemous 2 makes causes the formula to be significantly less interesting and unique. They made it significantly easier, the platforming is basically non-existent now, parrying barely matters anymore, the world and story feel sanitized compared to the first game, the areas feel way less distinct with almost none having any gimmick to make them play different than the others, and a bunch of other little things that make the game feel so much sloppier than the first.It's also fairly buggy and hits you with a crazy difficulty spike right at the end. Made me wanna give up because the game didn't feel nearly as worth it to see through as the first which I did everything in. That game's not perfect but it had so much more personality and charm. This game feels like the team saw people complaining about how the game was too hard or the platforming too annoying so they just massively scaled back everything anyone ever had an issue with and in doing so made a pretty generic metroidvania. Seriously, the game doesn't feel anything like the first. There's a certain tone(?) that's missing now and that goes for more than just the visuals or story, the whole game feels more like a diet version of the first, almost like it should've been the first in the series before they found what worked and leaned into it.  Anyway, it's not bad, it's still fun to play, but it's a much less interesting experience. There's a million other methroidvanias, why would you play this one over something else when it does nothing new and actively stomps out its own identity from the first? I guess that's what I mean when I say it seems like the praise is from people who never liked the first, there's a lot you have to not really care about in the first game for this more bare bones approach to seem better by comparison. If that's you, and you never like the first, try this one out, maybe it'll hit that sweet spot for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend a game in good faith (ha) when it's fundamentally broken. The DLC makes softlocking your game very easy to do. Or you might get some enemies with lingering hitboxes. Or you might get bosses that kill you while you're in a cutscene. Or you might have enemies suddenly do double damage due to another hit box bug. Or you might be unable to progress due to a well known crashing bug. The list goes on and on and on. Huge shame too, because at its core this is an amazing game, ruined by bugs and crashes. And the devs are running fixes at a pace that would make a snail jealous.

_childDocuments_.review: if you're like me, you came here looking for a good castlevania clone. you heard that this sequel was much improved from the first, polishing out all of it's major flaws. you maybe even heard the sweaty tryhards complaining that this was way too easy, which is probably the best advertisement a game can get. if you're like me, and thought this was going to be "blasphemous if it was fun", then you were totally lied to.this is just 2d darksouls. again. a genre designed to waste your time, to piss you off. and trick stupid people into believing they "overcame a challenge" because they beat some unfun boss. a boss with too big a healthbar and that deals out too much damage. nobody is proud of you. nobody cares. everyone has beaten that boss. because it's just a timesink. artificial difficulty. a game design trend that has already plateaued and is dying, as people grow up and realize they want games with difficulty settings (and accessibility settings).to be fair, the game has better action and aesthetics than the first. and it DID fix a lot of the horrible pit/spike issues that plagued blasphemous 1. but it isn't enough. just like the first, the game is fun for the first three or so bosses. the enemies are tough, but nothing feels particularly unfair. think shovelknight. but then suddenly there's a difficulty spike, and the game starts playing like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. normal enemies twoshot you, and are all built like tanks. this is embarrassing game design. this is devs not knowing where else to take a game, so they just up enemy health and damage. none of this would be bad if there were difficulty settings, but these are trend-chaser devs. this whole genre is built upon being streamerbait. if you aren't getting paid to play these, there is nothing for you here.this is the worst genre ever made. stay away. salty tryhards will clownaward this review because it hurt their delicate feelings. because they need to continue believing that beating a singleplayer game will impress someone, when in reality we're all laughing at them. ♥♥♥♥ soulslikes. ♥♥♥♥ this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous was, my any metric, an excellent game.Blasphemous II took that formula and instead made absolutely everything worse. Much is bloated: There are new weapons, which have no business in the lore of the game. The dialogue is excessive and rambling. The weapons have to be upgraded considerably more. There’s more busy work: get more tokens, find more items, etc. You get Tears of Atonement, but… you don’t need them? Why even have them?When not bloated, it was changed for who knows what reason:The cut scenes are animated differently and cartoonish, which gives a ridiculous atmosphere. The character sprite movement is rendered differently and (I’ll be honest, this criticism is a personal complaint) annoying.You can’t attack upward any more. This game feels like the developers went back to the drawing board and decided to tweak things- not because they needed to be fixed, but just for the sake of changing them.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is a MASSIVE improvement over the first, it's still a long way to go.PROS:No more instant death spike traps literally everywhere all over the game. there are much much less of them and they dont instant kill you, only deal some damage.Getting alternate endings no longer basically requires you to replay the entire game!Fast travel is less painful this time around... kinda.The default keybindings for PC when from "Literally the worst i have ever seen by a mile" to "only like the 4th worst i've ever seen"The Artwork of the whole game is still beautiful.CONS:Get ready to fight the same enemy over and over and over again. this game has so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ arenas it's not even funny. The big guy with the hammer that explodes upon striking the ground being his literal only attack? get ready to fight him as a "mini boss" like 50 times. Thats not a joke.This game definitely has some straight up padding build into it.Once you get all the powers there is nothing that tells you where all the secrets are so if you wanna get the "true ending" get ready to check every single spot in the whole game because you dont know what your missing!On death you take semi-permanent mana bar reductions. This was a bad idea 15 years ago in Demon Souls but the devs thought "lets do that anyway!"There are 3 weapons you can choose from and swap freely but because you basically have to spec into one specific weapon and give it bonus damage and effects there might as well just be one. complete waste of dev time.The talent tree is still terrible, it might even be worse. basically the made a complete move set and then just removed stuff... seemingly at random... and called those missing pieces a "talent tree". Also because you have a talent tree for each weapon but they cost the same resource so you will just put all your points into the one weapon you actually use and the very quickly cap it leaving talent points completely useless for the rest of the game!Weapon design is back to the old fashion "jump attacking is better because you can still move while in your the air" i cant remember who originally started this (maybe as old as like Castlevaina 1) but it was a bad idea then and is still a bad idea.The first game was already pretty light on story and this game basically said... lets have even less of it!

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a noteworthy sequel that successfully builds upon the foundation laid by its predecessor. The visual design continues to be a standout feature, with meticulously crafted environments that immerse players into a dark and eerie world.The gameplay improvements are immediately noticeable, particularly in the realm of combat. The controls feel more polished, resulting in a smoother and more engaging experience when facing off against various enemies. The expanded array of weapons and abilities provides a satisfying layer of depth to the combat mechanics, and the boss battles remain a highlight of the game.The narrative takes a deeper dive into the lore of the Blasphemous universe, offering players a more intricate and nuanced understanding of the game's world and its inhabitants. However, it's worth noting that the game doesn't shy away from exploring controversial themes related to religion, which might be off-putting to some players.Overall, Blasphemous 2 maintains the atmospheric qualities that made its predecessor stand out, while introducing refinements that enhance the overall gameplay experience. It's a game that caters to those who appreciate a darker, more challenging adventure, and its execution makes it a commendable sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 Yet another solid 2D platforming adventure, this time around feeling less like a SoulVania and more like a traditional MetroidVania.Blasphemous 2 looks fantastic with it's pixelated graphics, you really can't fault the art work and the way the game looks, It is just flawless.The Story takes place I am guessing 1000 years after the events of Eventide (Spoilers I wasn't good enough to beat it) and there is a new miracle that is taking place alongside the original penitent one. Gameplay - Blasphemous 2 takes everything it knew from the 1st game and pumps it up to 11, with 3 weapons in your arsenal this time and weapon memories there is a whole lot more stylish combos and weapon swapping mid-combat to make yourself look god-like but in 2D (similar to DMC) Blasphemous 2 feels less weighted and more feathered, you can really tell the Devs made the character feel much lighter and easier to control this time around apposed to Blas 1 where everything feels overly heavy and sluggish to pull off. New Bosses: The Bosses within my run of Blasphemous 2 while they were original in there designs and what they throw at you, they just felt way too easy this time around having 3 weapons of choice to decide how you want to play around the traits some of the bosses have. I personally used the daggers most of the game as I like the challenge and I prefer the quick in and out for a couple of jabs without taking any damage, The Sword was my 2nd choice and felt similar to the first game with a few new additions and some extra damage and elemental buffs and lastly the Swinging Mace thing, Really didn't like this thing, it hits hard as nails if that's your kind of thing but for me it was just too slow and locked me into animations I would like to get out of much faster.The New statue system: Now this is a nifty new feature, 8 Statue blocks all that can be filled by a mad array of statues all with their own perks and even combos that can be made to benefit your playstyle even more. I for example using the daggers found a perk that allowed me to use a Stinger and have a clone follow my stinger up to finish off enemies that just barely survived. If that wasn't good enough with the dagger again when I healed I gained my Electric meters back from healing allowing me to go on a rampage doing tons more damage to my enemies. There are still aton more to discover but I personally liked them.The Map Design: It felt alot softer, A lot lighter this time around like ♥♥♥♥ hadn't just hit a fan, the dark tones of the first game seem almost lifted but this didn't dampen my experience with Blasphemous 2 alot of the areas were original by design and gave me alot of challenge and fun going through them. Secrets: The sheer volume of secrets in this game like most MetVania games is insane and you can't hope to find them all without some help or knowing exactly what it is you're looking for so I really enjoyed this aspect of the game.Overall: Blasphemous 2 is one hell of an improvement over the original and I am grateful we even got a 2nd game because I Wasn't so sure we would get a sequel. The gameplay is amazing, the puzzles and locations are all amazing, YOU DON'T DIE from falling off ledges or into spikes anymore allowing you to relax when you make a mistake doing some platforming, the Devs just put some proper TLC into Blas 2 and made it hella great. Couple minor notes, the game does have some visual bugs, there were many a time I would save and A flame would appear by my legs and follow me everywhere until I lit Veredicto on fire then it would disappear. The only other bug I have encountered is the in game timer has bugged out on my start screen.Ah and lastly this is a real issue...the contact damage in this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke, if you get cornered you are just dead, the I-frames for being hit are less than a second and within that time you just get juggled in a corner until you die. It happened to me a few times and it's dead annoying there are also some enemies you have to jump over and CAN'T slide through this is also dead dumb game design as you will not be able to dodge and you will take one hell of a hit from the enemies I am referring too.10/10 even with the little bugs and aggros.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing followup to the first game. Undisputed GOAT in art, character design, and music for metroidvanias, no question.Although I really enjoyed the second game I'm looking forward to a more polished experience in a couple years with updates and DLC. I played the first game on release and in its final form and both times were a blast too. This game starts off with a MUCH smoother gameplay experience with all its mechanics and movement feeling about as tight and responsive as any side scroller gets.I encountered a couple easily reproducible bugs that bothered my gameplay:1) When you die in this game it blocks part of your mana bar. I understand that now you only get back some of your loss so that it builds up over time (2% per death if you collect your corpse) however if you get your body while your reduced mana bar is maxed you don't get ANY of it back, and the full 20% you lose on death stays blocked. By casting one spell before collecting you get the whole thing back. It was really disappointing to see this 100% repeatable bug exist almost a year after release.2) When you swing on the same frame that you get knocked down, you take another swing when you stand up. More or less minor bug but when you use the big mace it has a very long attack time and can kill you. Again, very simple to re-create and TGK should have fixed it by now.A couple other criticisms:- Significantly less gorey than the first game. There is still some very disturbing imagery (Cesareo will be forever burnt into my mind) but it doesn't hit the same as the first game.- Much easier game overall. The combat is very fluid and allows for a lot of experimentation. If you fully explore the map you'll find yourself very overpowered quickly. Some of the early bosses were challenging but once you get some leeway in how you build your character the rest are a pushover. Eviterno excepted...- Lacklaster executions. Executions are about 10% as satisfying in this game. Executions seem to be offered completely at random instead of having a high chance to occur after a block (probably because you can't block with one of the weapons) and don't feel satisfying. They felt unfinished because most of them have the same animation of vines squishing your enemy instead of the slow, methodical beat down into an impale or beheading that the first game lingered on beautifully.This is a fantastic game. Nobody else in the business is making bosses and beautifully written NPCs based on religious imagery in such a captivating way. I'm still really sad that I didn't contribute enough to the kickstarter to get the art book for the first game but I will absolutely be shelling out for the new volume that's being released soon. The Blasphemous series remains one of my favorites of all time and I can't wait to come back for the inevitable DLC that offers new bosses, hard mode, NG+, skins and whatever else TGK wants to throw in.
