_childDocuments_.review: This game is, without a doubt, a huge step forward from the first Blasphemous. Pretty much every aspect of game design here feels like a refinement; it’s as if the devs took every mechanic of the first game under close inspection and fundamentally improved what had to be improved. Because let me tell you, as much as I liked Blasphemous I for its style, music and presentation, that game was heavily flawed. Movement and platforming felt clunky, the game was extremely backtracking-heavy (even for a Metroidvania), elemental gameplay features were bound to equippable items… it just felt more like a first draft for me and not a polished game. All of these points are addressed in the sequel in some way. Movement feels much more fluid and precise, I never had any issues with the platforming; I even enjoyed some of the more demanding platforming challenges. Backtracking is still a thing in this game but at least the game now displays on the map if a quest can be progressed and where which was a huge help. Also, i-frames and dodge distance, among other things, are fixed and can’t be altered by equipping some random item. So, on the mechanical side of things, I couldn’t be happier. Boss battles are still extremely challenging, the level design is still some of the best in the genre and the various progression systems (which are thankfully somewhat simplified compared to the first game) still feel motivating.Aesthetically, this game is at least on the level of Blasphemous I, if not better. The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous and the designs are unlike anything you can find in any other game. It is at times hard to fathom what insane designs the artists for this game came up with. There is some batsh*t crazy stuff in here, some genuinely beautiful scenes and some of the most gruesome and grotesque imagery that I’ve ever seen. You can tell that the devs were inspired by catholic motifs and biblical themes that were twisted to create a unique kind of horror. These meticulously crafted pixel art designs are the star of the show here. For some reason, the devs decided to replace the pixel art cutscenes of the first game with 2D hand-drawn animations. These still look great and they successfully convey the vibe of the world but I can’t help but feel that something was lost here. Yes, the cutscenes in Blasphemous I were shorter and simpler but they also fit right into the world of the game. Here, I feel like there is a clean cut between in-game graphics and the style in those cutscenes (kinda like in early 3D games) and I completely understand fans of the first game being appalled by that. I for one didn’t mind too much as I do see the beauty in these new designs but I get it. When it comes to music, all I can say is that Carlos Viola, the composer for the first game and this one, is back and he’s greater than ever. That man is a straight-up genius and the devs owe him so much as the music carries the atmosphere of the game at least as much as the art style. This is a Spanish game and the setting is inspired by Spanish history, culture and, of course, the country’s relationship with religion, specifically catholicism. The music reflects that perfectly. Think Diablo II but more subtle, more suspenseful, with a reliance on violine and piano music. Mostly, that results in some quiet and melancholic tunes like  or one of my favorites . It’s not always dark and depressing though. There are pieces like  or  that feel alive and pumping while retaining that dark undertone that permeates everything. Overall, it’s just a masterclass in music composition which is a rare sight in a small indie game such as this. Same goes for the voice acting and voice direction. My god, what a treat that was. Do yourself a favor and play this game in Spanish with subtitles in your preferred language. It is such a vibe. Truly amazing to learn so many different ways to pronounce “Penitente” :D As for story and writing, there isn’t too much I can say. It is just as cryptic as the first game. The lore is vast and deep and there is so much to learn by reading item descriptions, talking to NPCs and just… looking at the environment. I honestly didn’t spend too much time with this aspect of the game as the concepts discussed here are rather abstract and a lot, and I mean a , is open for interpretation that I just felt overwhelmed at some point. I do see myself coming back to this game for a second run and taking it all in though as I feel the game really shines here. For a casual first run, you don’t need to engage with the lore of the world too much to get a sufficient grip on the story, another major improvement over the first game. There were moments in the game that frustrated the hell out of me. Two times I nearly dropped the game. Blasphemous II is hard, it is unforgiving and it requires you to sit down, observe, learn and apply. If you’ve read my Shadow of the Erdtree review, you know that this isn’t really my preferred way to approach boss design. Blasphemous I had some hard-hitting bosses too but some of the bastards in this game made me tear my hair out. Still, if you practice patience and are open to learn and improve, you will overcome everything this game throws at you. For me, after hitting my head against a wall that was a mid-game boss for about an hour without progress, it really made a huge difference to go explore some more and level up my abilities. In a similar fashion, for some of the end-game challenges, it really helps to try out different setups with various combinations of equipabble items. There are always ways to mitigate difficulty in this game and you do feel a difference. What doesn’t really make a difference is the weapon you choose to fight with. There is some wasted potential here. At the beginning of the game, you can choose between three weapons, a fast but weak set of sword-and-dagger, a heavy-hitting but slow war censer (yup, a ) and a sword that’s kind of a compromise between both. In principle, that is a cool idea. There are some situations where one weapon is more useful than the others and there are entire puzzles bound to the usage of a specific weapon which is nice. For the most part though, I just stuck to the sword and was fine with that. No real incentive to change tactics, no boss battles that require you to switch weapons mid-battle or anything, just three ways to approach the game. Again, I like to have some variety but they definitely could have done more with this. I’m glad I didn’t drop the game in the moments of my deepest frustration. Blasphemous II is a bliss from start to finish with the occasional hurdle in between. I encountered some glitches, even some crashes and I am not on-board with every game design decision made here. Nonetheless, in the search action genre that is overflowing with titles, this one stands out. The art and music are drop-dead beautiful, the game feels great to play, it is motivating, it is challenging and it paints the picture of a truly cryptic but intriguing world informed my religious motifs and a retelling of themes founded in catholic mysticism. I deeply hope that our penitence is far from over.

_childDocuments_.review: About a year ago I already played the first part and was amazed, fascinated and addicted of this game. I really was looking forward to the second part and I haven't been disappointed! The game is just as awesome as the first part. When you've played the first part before, you might think it's a bit easier. Well some parts or bosses of this part really might be easier, but then there are some who will drive you mad ^^ But overall the difficulty is challenging, but just as the first part it's quite hard but always fair. So when you're patient enough and try a boss over and over you will make progress and finally beat them. It's a must play for everyone who already played the first part and I recommend it for everyone who love 'Metroidvania' style games. I can't wait for a DLC or Blasphemous 3 ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a great example of learning from experience.What Blasphemous 1 did well, Blasphemous 2 does just as good if not better, all while improving on the shortcomings of its predecessor.The art is still absolutely gorgeous and the music is great. The combat is way more fluid and has a lot more variety, thanks to the weapon arsenal at the players disposal.While there is still a ton of stuff in the inventory, it isn't nearly as cluttered as it was in Blasphemous 1With secrets and questlines and whatnot the game has a ton to offer and is honestly a lot of fun.I do have a few gripes with the game after playing through it 100%-This game is insanely backtrack-heavy, and not in a good way. You choose 1 of 3 weapons at the start, each does something different to get through obstacles.Flail: Rings bellsRapier: Teleports through mirrorsSword: Destroys wooden blockadesOn your path through the first mainstory objectives you will acquire the other 2 weapons, but will find a LOT of spots which require a combination of 2 or maybe even all 3 weapons, which you certainly won't always have at your disposal on first traversal or the areas.Then there are abilities, which improve your mobility, which in combination with your weapons will be needed to solve puzzles and find secrets.All of that wouldn't be that bad, if there was some kind of item (even if it near endgame) which shows all secrets on the map. But there is NOTHING like that. So you better place markers everywhere.-Later on enemies tend to spawn and gang up on you in the most annoying groups, perfectly assembled to make you fly around, unable to move, dodge or fight if you get caught in something once. There is just too little post hit invulnerability or at least invulnerability to getting thrown around.-Bosses aren't balanced very well. I don't think the game is hard overall, but the bosses certainly don't get progressively harder. The last boss in fact is probably the easiest aside from the tutorial boss. It's a little weird to have a super easy time, get pounded afterwards and then do fine again.-It is basically a Blasphemous trademark, but the sidequests and objectives are often as cryptic as they could be. This isn't inherently bad, I enjoyed having to figure stuff out and try what could work. Just wanted to point it out, since I believe many people prefer to be given at least some kind of direction.Nonetheless, the game plays extremely well, and I had a ton of fun throughout my journey. It took roughly 17 hours of focused gameplay to get 100%, and was definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Inferior to the original in every way. The story/lore felt really forced. They were obviously just trying to capture what made the first game unique but tried way too hard. The fight design seems to have suffered from the game having 3 weapons this time. They obviously needed to balance the fights to ensure every weapon was viable. This resulted in most fight being extremely easy with the exception of Eviterno which went the entire opposite direction and is the worst designed fight I've seen in the genre. The sudden difficulty spike with that fight is part of the problem but phase 2 overall is just horribly designed. Metroidvania fights are supposed to be clearable with just reaction and observation. Eviterno is contradictory to that entire concept. Eviterno forces you to memorize the 2nd phase. The fact that you can't skip cutscenes in a 2023 game is also extremely bizarre and just feels like lazy programming. The fact that the inability to skip cutscenes hasn't been  patched in the 7+ months since launch says a lot as well. The first game was fantastic except for the convoluted ending unlocks. This game is just worst in every way. It even still has a convoluted ending unlock even though literally no one enjoys that.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, huge upgrade from Blasphemous 1 in terms of combat, traversal, and general gameplay mechanics. This feels a lot smoother than the first game, with a lot less bugs and issues. They really nailed it with the 3 weapons system, and they did a great job of making sure you'd have to use all 3 of them to get through the game. Sound design and soundtrack, just like the first game, is fantastic. Graphics are gorgeous, the art style is what attracted me to the first game initially, and this one looks and feels even better.When it comes to the lore, Blasphemous 1 has the upper hand, which is not to say this game's story isn't good, it's great. But, the first game's story captured my attention like very few other games, and I fell in love with the lore and mythology they were building with it. This game's story feels a little less thought out. Without giving away any details, the idea of the game's final act makes less sense when you consider the *true* ending of Blasphemous 1.Besides that, there are very minor gameplay issues that kind of annoy me, like the collectibles hunting, and trust me there's a lot of it. I'd really recommend marking on the map whenever you find something you can't access initially and you have to come back to later, it'll save you so much time.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is to Blasphemous 1 what Mega Man X2 was to Mega Man X. Mega Man X2 is bottom line the better game with new movement tech (double jump, air dash) and just more of everything, while Mega Man X will always be the more memorable, classic experience which left the bigger impression when it first came out.That being said, B2 is a near perfect Metroidvania and worthy successor. It's still lacking a few features that B1 already received post-launch through free DLCs (like NG+), but B2 in its release state already has way more replay value than vanilla B1 had. Personally, I enjoyed the 3 different weapons and altarpiece system most, letting you experiment with different playstyles and specializations. Those alone were motivation enough for me to finish the game 4 times already... ;)There are also a few things I didn't like, but those are minor and most of them could easily be fixed with future updates. I will then remove them from this list:- Partially unskippable dialouge- Partially unfitting music (e.g. crown of towers)- Too many cage fights where you fight waves of enemies. Some proper minibosses instead would have been nice.- Too many fetch quests.- Some quests require the player too die over and over, which is annoying because... - The game is too easy for veterans and there are no difficulty options yet.- Weapon upgrades can feel like downgrades depending on the player's preferences. Thus, the player should be able to deactivate unlocked weapon upgrades at will.- Weapons lose their charge upon weapon switch, penalizing players who want to incorporate multiple weapons into their combat style.- It takes too long to turn around, causing the player to sometimes attack the wrong direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: With a very original setting and a design that is bold and does not follow the standards, the original Blasphemous is a very ambitious game in the tired "metroidvania" genre. It is far from perfect and its flaws are very well-known, but even with the rough parts it is a game that I think it is worth playing.Possibly due to the flaws of the first game, the sequel overcompensates and the end result is a rather standard game in the genre. The platforming is better, but still is  not particularly interesting, and it is what I expect of any random game of the genre (double-jump, air dash, etc).  The combat has more variety (three types of weapons with skill trees) but most enemies can be stun-locked just by using the basic attack so there there is little challenge, not to mention the small variety of enemies(for the most part of the game, the only enemies that may cause trouble are the skeletons with chandeliers).  The story and setting feels less memorable, and the map design is more linear with the exception of the first few hours. Even the excellent Spanish VA of the first game is replaced for a fairly standard one (with the single exception of the battle arena lady).It is actually a good game, but instead of challenging and surpassing the ambition of the first one, the developers decided place it safe at every opportunity and the result is just another good but forgettable "metroidvania" game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The fighting is fun, outside a couple enemy types when you want to use specific weapons.  My issue with this game and the previous is...the story and structure. The story doesn't make sense from the start, so I just don't pay attention after about 10 minutes of playing.  Everything is weird and unexplained, much like the mission progression, if you can call it that. This is a game where you will be backtracking and doing the same areas over and over and over again.  I can't stand that in games. I can do it a couple times, not 3 or more. It gets so annoying going over the same areas just to see if there is something there that you can get now that you couldn't before. Guacamelee has this same thing but in my opinion done so much better. This game is cryptic, if they give hints at all. It just seems like you just stumble around forever hoping to bump into something important. Or, you can look up stuff online, which is what I end up doing in this game anyway, so I don't know why I bothered trying to play it normally, I knew from the first one that this was going to be the case.  (ps, I don't want to get to the final boss without finding all the stuff first, or else what is the point of finding stuff)There are a couple obvious things, but many are not. I just hate wasting the limited time I have searching the same areas looking for something new. I'm at a point right now, where I am going to have to look up where to go next because IDK. I seem to be blocked off of all the paths, and now I'm sick of looking for something to have changed, or maybe it was one little spot I missed. Another problem with this game, if you miss something it can result in you have to backtrack even more...yay, because the second part of the quest is now in an area you already went through 4 times before.  If this game was more straightforward it would be great. But right now, all I can tolerate is the combat...but even that has issues but they are rare, like requiring you to switch weapon types midfight, and of which have different moves if you use R1...I have only used the one weapon I chose in the beginning for all the combat. However, later, there are enemy types that require you to switch to the other weapons to interact with the environment to dodge projectiles.  I can't stand that. I just want to fight with the weapon i want to use.  I shouldn't have to use a specific weapon to complete the fight (mirrors against the enemy throwing 4 homing red orbs and slashes if you jump). One other thing with the weapons, is that you can upgrade them which is neat, but some upgrades cause certain swings to take twice as long to finish...and you can't dodge until you finish swinging fully....yuckIm sick of the metroidvania's....lets get back to something more fun. Wandering around like a jacka** isn't fun...meanwhile you have to look at all the stuff you can't get yet or places you can't go to.   This is a middle thumb, because of the aggravating map structure and cryptic bs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game adds mechanics that where lacking in the previous one, making it a more finished and polished game than the previous one. Still, I felt like it tried to over compensate when explaining the plot, losing a bit the souls-like experience of just exploring and trying to find yourself around.I enjoyed it as a kid like I have not enjoyed a game in a while. If you like metroidvania/souls-like games this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's technically a better game than the first Blasphemous, but it also feels like it sanded down some of the interesting edges in the process. It's not as gory or horrific, the cutscene art style is jarring, and the executions feel like an afterthought this time. I also encountered a few distracting bugs a few months after release (sometimes the music just doesn't start in places, and will start playing randomly again while you're in the same area).However, the combat, skill trees, and bosses are all a big improvement. The game also looks amazing. I slightly prefer the first one overall, but this is still a great metroidplatformervania.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the best pixel art and animations I had seen. It's music is celestial, and it's sound design it's on point. Then there are it's game mechanics, who blend perfectly with the combat, it's weapon system, and it's enemy design to deliver exiting fights!I am not even half way through the history to have something to say, but so far it's storytelling and world building had been phenomenal, at pair with the first game. I can already tell this is another masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 although having issues when compared to its predecessor is a fantastic game definitely worth playing.Let me list off the positives first, the mixed then the bad! This will include slight spoilers or talks of later game objects and the like too.-The combat is highly addicting, the variety of builds you can do with the figures, prayers and prayer beads is insanely high especially when you factor in the 2 weapons you can collect in the game. -Missable Quest rewards can be retrieved from a merchant, although minor it prevents you from being unable to 100% your save which is great for completionists.- The artstyle, while the game does have drawn cutscenes instead of pixel cutscenes it doesn't detract from the experience in my eyes and genuinely the cutscenes are fantastically made and admittedly if you want to make them a wallpaper as well they'll look fantastic! I do appreciate how the cutscenes as well give off a Renaissance feeling as well-The story and its endings feeling very conclusive and fulfilling to see. Alot of games recently feels like your efforts in the story doesn't pay off however in Blasphemous 2 the endings especially the "true" one feels rewarding to witness and like your efforts actually feeling like they worked towards a great finality (or a bad one with Ending Bs)-The OST. This OST is easily one of the most beautiful ones I've heard in a game. The intensity, the somberness, the peacefulness. All clearly displayed in every piece of music in this game in a very classical manor too which I adore! It's truly great and makes some fights feel even more tense than they'd be without it!The Mixed!-Bosses feeling geared heavily towards one weapon over the others. I do enjoy how each boss has a specific strength that a weapon can counter or turn to a weakness it does hurt your build if you have one geared towards a specific weapon like Verdicto the giant incense mace for example since there is a few bosses who favor parrying and agile swings over a heavy mace, not to say it's impossible but it definitely is more difficult in some sections. I don't absolutely hate it however which is why I am mixed on it since someone out there will guaranteed hate it instead of being slightly annoyed needing to swap everything quickly to have an easier time with a boss.-The bosses, although I enjoyed every fight against all of the bosses they suffer from not having as memorable designs as the first game, having more laxed combat mechanics to work with and just generally feeling easier which isn't a bad thing but isn't exactly the greatest either. They still feel great to fight at the end of the day and some are VERY memorable, which is why it's so mixed for me.-Convoluted steps to achieve the "true" ending, this is mainly just me but getting the item needed to achieve it was very confusing and although I can see how someone might instantly pick up on it but for me I had to get some help to actually get the items. It does feel rewarding however to get the necessary item for the ending however which is why I don't hate it.The Bad-The Cherub collectibles. I don't need to explain it, collectibles aren't fun to go through, especially if they give important items that make the game easier or more fun.-The Golden Cherub platfroms not being more shown that they're a naturally unlocked ability. You see so many golden particles early on so atleast for me I began to think I can get the ability needed to make those platforms appear early and that I just need to find it only to figure out it's actually a pretty late game ability which was infuriating. Atleast for me. This is DEFINITELY just a me thing.-Lack of invincibility frames when hit, obviously this is preventable but at times I found myself hit in a corner by multiple enemies and being unable to escape due to the lack of invincibility frames and ending up dying quite a bit.The final verdict! Overall Blasphemous 2 despite having elements I am mixed on or actively dislike there's a reason I played through this game so much in a span of a day! It's a extraordinarily well crafted game and it doesn't disappoint at all especially if you're a fan of the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Strict improvement of the first game in almost everything. Combat retains the visceral brutality of the first but improves the feel and satisfaction by leaps and bounds. Boss fights are thrilling and unpredictable. The first game mainly found difficulty by making the bosses have a million health and last forever, but they are now much more rewarding in that the fights are much more a test of skill than patience. My only complaint so far is that the cutscenes are a very weird stylistic mismatch with the rest of the game. The aesthetic of the game is very grimy, dark and disturbing with contrasting scenes of opulence, whereas the cutscenes are clean and almost anime-adjacent. I don't think this would have been as big of a complaint if the first game hadn't already done the cutscenes perfectly to match the rest of the game.Overall, if you like metroidvanias or souls likes or cool ass art you'll mess with this
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and traversal have improved greatly, they are far more fun, intuitive, and challenging to master than the first game. That's why it makes me so mad that the writing took such a massive hit in return. If the theming and stories matter to you, the original is the definitive experience. If more refined and complex, if uncreative, gameplay is what matters to you, then this game is the definitive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: For those who aren't comparing it to the first: it's an amazing game. Top marks all around, with the only flaw being that contact damage is too high. I regularly listen to the soundtrack, and the artsyle is as good as it's ever been.     For those who are comparing it to the first: the combat is faster, more complex, and with a higher power level, at the cost of being much easier. And by complex, I mean the player is able to switch between three weapons, equip two spells (as opposed to one and a preset spell), and has access to the new 'Altarpiece of Favors' system, alongside everything from the first game. Blasphemous 2 loses the somewhat grounded combat of the first game in exchange for something that's a bit more standard, but still excellent. The soundtrack is perhaps easier to listen to, but not nearly as atmospheric. The world also felt much less oppressive than the original Custodia.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Among the history of sequels to good games, there are bad sequels no one wanted; there are sequels everyone called for but never had; there are sequels nobody expected but turned out great.  is…the sequel we don't really need, but it's nice to have anyway, though with too many missed opportunities perhaps. was unique; it was its own thing in many ways: its gameplay and art style, its writing and its atmosphere, while janky at times, set itself aside from many other generic Metrovania games. The sequel, while still a great experience that could keep players entertained for a solid 20 hours, simply feels a lot more generic.In the first game, it was a blast that for the whole game there was only one weapon and no double jump. It was a board decision for a modern Metrovania, but they successfully designed the whole map and combat around that and worked great. In the second game, while combat and exploration are much more fluid, it also feels less creative. Movement abilities are kind of expected: double jump, mid-air dash, grappling; 3 weapons are also kind of expected: a given standard similar to the previous game, a slow heavy hitter, a fast and agile one. The game is still fun, and to be honest, a lot less frustrating to play, but it lacks its own identity often.The art direction in the first game was bleak and muted, which complimented the atmosphere of the game and the story well. The pixel art in the second game is a lot more vivid and colorful; while nice to look at, it feels superficial and lacks inspiration. The Spainime cutscenes, while beautifully done, feel out of place. The story has more handholding; it becomes a quite explicit and blantant "kill 3 bosses then kill 5 more bosses" structure.All in all, this game on its own is not bad. It is more polished and accessible, with more balanced gameplay and presentation. It is still a cool Metrovania, pleasant to play. However, if you are going to look for the unique charm from the first entry, sadly that is not included. All the supposed improvements in the end didn't work too well together to elevate the sequel further——the Miracle works in mysterious ways indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 improves upon the predecessor on almost everything while keeping some of its weaknesses, 8.25/10CONS:* Less distubing and gory artstyle, cutscenes are fine but don't blend well with pixel art* Blood prayers overperform everything else and most prayers have been nerfed* you lose 4 itmes to get one ending and no ways to recover themPROS:* Instakill spikes and pits are finally gone* way better platforming and controls* gorgeous and vastly improved pixel-art with beautiful environments* spells more are more fun to use* new weapons are great and linked to platforming* harder then the first blasphemous with vastly superior bosses* one boss is the hardest thing on this franchise and will kick your @ss real good

_childDocuments_.review: I beat both games 100% and it breaks my heart to say that this one is inferior to the first one in far too many ways, with absurd contact damage, and never reaching the peak design that was WoE Crisanta. In fact, they somehow only went downhill after Wounds of Eventide.I have done several playthroughs of the first game and I don't think I'll be playing this one more than once unless a DLC comes out, but hopefully that happens after they iron out the flaws this game already has, such as Odon's sound still being broken 6 months after release, or getting softlocked in pressure rooms because enemies decided to just fly away6/10

_childDocuments_.review: A buggy, tedious slog.I will preface the review by listing out the positive:The pixel art is great. The soundtrack is great. That's it.The bad:The game is a series of boring, easy bosses separated by sadistic and tedious platforming and combat sections.Towards the end of the game you get a closed of arena battle with enemies spawning in every two rooms, sometimes at the end of very tedious and insane platforming sections.Whoever designed crimson rain should go to some kind of psychologist to sort out his issues.What's worse is that the game has many soft locking bugs that ♥♥♥♥ you over:Bugs:One of the bosses has a glitch in which you just die. There's nothing you can do about it, 50% of the time you just die when the battle begins. It's not an attack or anything, just instat 100% damage death.Another boss fight, Svsona, I got stuck in her hitbox somehow unable to move for the whole duration of the battle even after the boss moved from that location.During one of the mandatory inescapable battle arenas, one of the flying enemies just went off screen making it impossible to kill it and progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: No I wouldn't recommend this game, there's some stuff to like, the art direction and the level design is mostly OK, but the combat is drudgy, clunky and annoying, in particular, parrying and certain mechanics "pause" the game for a split second and just feel awful, chain parrying also never works.  In this type of game typically the more I play, the more I want to play, but I'm having the opposite experience here, I'm just getting annoyed by the mechanics of the game, they just get in the way of enjoyment.  The "punishment" for dying in particular might be the worst iteration of the "souls" corpse run mechanic, instead of taking your currency, they take away your ability to use spells, inherently taking away your "extra" avenue for fun.  I also find the story to be absolute drivel, I quite literally have no idea what the hell is going on, it's either pretentious hipster nonsense, or it's just regular nonsense, but I can't tell.I wanted to like blasphemous 2, but I really, really don't, go play "bloodstained" instead, if you want a metroidvania, or grime, if you want a soulsy-metroidvania.  I'm giving this thing a 65%.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Best metroidvania I've played. Takes everything good about the first game and uses it as a springboard to create something truly exceptional. The art, music, boss design (both thematic and mechanic), the incredible interconnected world and its rewarding secrets, the opportunity for combat customization and mastery the expanded weapon/prayer/altarpiece system offers - the developers seemed to know exactly what needed to be changed from Blasphemous 1, yet the innovations they brought to the table blew my expectations out of the water.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: [Disregard time played - much of it was spent AFK while I did other stuff] The art direction in this game is fantastic, but in full honestly, I can't say I'd recommend this game. Far too much of the game is based around finding hidden collectibles, and there are a TON of these things.First off, in the obligatory Metroidvania playstyle, there's a lot of unlockable mobility skills - dodges that let you go through certain walls, weapons that let you activate certain objects, and abilities that let you grab walls and hooks. Unfortunately, until you get those abilities, you have to just ignore every single one of these things you see, because you can't do anything with them until you unlock the ability. As a player, it's obnoxious to be exploring a new area and constantly run into passageways that you can't explore again and again and again because you haven't unlocked the necessary ability yet. It's almost Donkey Kong 64-esque.When you eventually unlock the ability, you'd better be prepared to do a lot of backtracking. For most of the game, you're only allowed to teleport between specific Gates and there aren't very many of them spread around, so you'll be legging it constantly through areas you've already explored. This becomes absolutely UNBEARABLE about midway through the game, when you hit a dead-end because you don't have a specific power-up unlocked yet, so you have to turn around and backtrack through every single area in the game, searching for the way towards unlocking that power-up. At one point, I spent almost 2 hours searching for the next area to go to, because it was actually ONE SINGLE UNMARKED corridor in a far-off part of the map that I was meant to go to.Keeping things spoiler-free, you will almost certainly receive Ending B upon finishing the game. To obtain Ending A, you have to collect ALL the collectibles in the game. Normally in a game with this many collectibles, the game will provide you with a map/radar of some sort after you've found MOST of the collectibles, to help nudge you towards the last remaining few - but not this game. The map is absolutely barebones and provides no hints about remaining collectibles, or even information about collectibles you've already found. The only thing the map provides are Pins, so if you haven't been manually marking every single collectible you've found since the start of the game, your only alternative is to look up an online guide and go re-check every single area to find the ones you missed - and some of them are EASILY missable.Lastly, from a lore standpoint, I never really felt engaged. So much of the games story is vague, as you travel around hearing about the Miracle and see all the weird NPCs affected by it, most of which will ask you to go find a bunch of collectibles for them. A dying woman laying in a bed, surrounded by mourners? Go find my 5 daughters. A mysterious, extremely tall nun-creature? Go find my 8 sisters. A gigantic man breastfeeding a baby? Go find 6 seeds of wax. A two-headed Jester with burning shoes? Go find me 12 boysenberries. I actually made up that last one, but it makes just as much sense as any of the other NPCs you'll come across. They're just there for the sake of being there, with very little plot relevance (if any). But don't forget: you HAVE to go collect all their thingamajigs if you want to see the REAL Ending,Also, as a minor gripe, the penultimate boss of the game comes with two unskippable cutscene segments that you have to sit through every single time you die to them. Upon completing the game, I pretty much just felt relieved that it was finally over.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers advertised this game as a more "pure metroidvania" but so much of the design feels like the opposite.Instead of the more free-form exploration players did all throughout Blasphemous 1, the second half of Blasphemous 2 has you progress through a set order of levels one at a time. Progression becomes extremely linear with the game telling you what to do and where to go, the opposite of what the metroidvania genre is known for. These levels aren't even accessible before the second half. They are literally placed in spots of the world where there was nothing previously.This issue also played a part in making exploration feel much less interesting compared to both Blasphemous 1 and other metroidvanias. When going through the first game, I found myself enjoying simply exploring the very interconnected world. It wasn't uncommon to uncover new areas and items, and many sections looped back to previous levels or the main hub. These aspects of the first game's world design feel very lacking in Blasphemous 2. That feeling of enjoyment from uncovering new areas and items didn't happen nearly as much in this game and the world is not nearly as interconnected. I think Blasphemous 2's second half is worse, but the first half still didn't live up to what Blasphemous 1 offered.Letting you cycle between three different weapons is an alright addition, but it never really felt fleshed out in the combat or platforming. It's not necessarily bad, but doesn't do nearly enough to make up for the world design issues I mentioned before.All of this while charging $40 CAD. This is more than the first game, most other indie games, and many other metroidvanias. I loved the first game and wanted to love Blasphemous 2, but the game ended up being very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is targeted towards a broader audience, with a noticeable emphasis on accessibility. The gameplay has been made simpler, the storyline is clearer, quest markers assist in navigation, and characters communicate their needs more directly. While these changes are undoubtedly favorable for casual players, dedicated fans of the initial game (myself included) might find themselves a bit let down. Nevertheless, it remains an exceptional game well worth the investment. I can't help but feel a tad disappointed that the developers chose to prioritize wider appeal instead of staying true to the unique qualities that defined the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying, if you're interested in Blasphemous 2 and haven't played the first one GO PLAY THE FIRST ONE! It's a great metroidvania that is arguably better than 2 in a few different ways. They're both great, but you should not skip the 1st one to rush to the second! They're both incredibly competent games and it would be a shame to miss the 1st one. Have two delicious cakes, not just one.Blasphemous 2, while a bit buggy and questionable in some design choices, is overall a very enjoyable and refined metroidvania experience. The weapons, upgrades, and passive status system allows you to do a lot of mixing and matching and the traversal mechanics are used consistently through. All this while playing through the beautifully done pixel art of the game, it's unlike many others and has a level of quality unparalleled by other metroidvanias and modern pixel games.That all being said, I did mention bugs, and yes, it is buggy. From bosses who have their music and sounds turn off, to soft locks, to other things, I ran into quite a few bugs I had never ran into in the previous title. I'm not too salty about these, and game making is hard, but I hope for the next title these bugs are ironed out especially given how this game has had a year or so of release time and these bugs are still not resolved.Some of the design choices are also questionable to me. Some correlate to bugs but others are just basic stuff like unskippable cutscenes (You should always be able to skip cutscenes, especially repeated boss ones). Also missable questlines and npc choices. There are also a few levels (like the final one) where I wasn't all too impressed by the layout.Overall though, great game. Like I said at the beginning GO PLAY THE FIRST ONE FIRST! It's worth your time and rather than it feeling like a slog of doing the same thing it feels like more of what you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Like SOTN? Then this is the game for you. Takes much inspiration from the game that started it all and adds its own spin. Now this is not your dads SOTN. Each enemy has its own way of attacking so you need to think before you attack, or you will get your butt handed to you. Its is much less cryptic than Blasphemous one so you will understand what you need to do as you progress. Many secrets are hidden in this game so if you take your time you will find most of them (Im still missing one o_O)This game is as good as it looks if not better. Don't hesitate to buy this if you're thinking about it. You will have alot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania and an excellent sequel.They have addressed some of the most annoying shortcomings of the first game and introduced lots of new features and mechanics. Some notable improvements such as a double-jump, better wall-climbing, a variety of different weapons (in place of Mea Culpa) each with unique abilities and much more. And yeah, spikes no longer kill you with a single hit.The art has been elevated to an even higher level than in the first game, which was already visually stunning. The music, while not exceptional, is still great. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 had a lot of quality life improvements over the 1st one that I think at the end of the day, took away some of the charm of it. In the first one every little relic would make your character slightly less clunky and potentially improve your movement, here instead you get defense bonuses against different things. I'm a sucker for bit art, so I was a little sad to see the creepy cutscenes in bit art to be replaced with art (that was great looking) similar to Hades. I can see why some people argue that the 2nd one is "easier" than the first (except a sudden spike in one of the last bosses). Overall, if you liked the first one, you'll probably enjoy this one. My biggest gripe was that finding the cherubs got bugged for me and 2 didn't get properly marked so I couldn't get one of the endings because of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Everything the first part of Blasphemous did good, this one makes better. This time you have different weapons to choose from, a lot more nice metroidvania movement abilities and no missables achievements, which I'm totally a fan of.I totally inhaled this game and I hope, The Game Kitchen will make more great metroidvanias in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Combat feels amazing in this one, multiple weapons really keeps it fresh I actually don't much care for light-heavy attack combos like the first game and prefer having less to think about and less wasted design space on combos I won't ever use. There are still a lot of eureka moments in this combat system, and the three bosses I've fought so far were fun to figure out once I figured out how to increase my health so I stopped dying in 3 hits. I'm 4 hours in and have all the level 1 upgrades in my preferred weapon and it's great. I did find out that I screwed myself out of a future health upgrade by giving two health upgrades to the health upgrader at once when I finally figured out what the chalices were for instead of arbitrarily sacrificing health in a cup in front of her in between them, which is the kind of goofy game design I remember from getting the true ending in the first game. Map is pretty good too, and I love the first three bosses so far. Definitely going to finish this one. Hope there's a New Game + down the line with the basics unlocked out of the gate.Quite a few flaws though. There's always a weapon that goes a looong time without use outside of platforming(Ruego for me), and there's a really annoying bug with activating Veredicto if you activate the flames while standing. I'd wait for an update before buying outright, I don't think it's really worth full price right now(though snap it up if on a large markdown). I got it as part of Humble Choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a "barely recommend". If you liked Blasphemous 1, you'll not like this as much, but still enjoy it. If you haven't played the games, this one being (generally) easier is a good entry point.Good stuff:• Graphics are still some of the best pixel art around; cutscenes much better especially with CRT filter• Platforming is much more interesting this time around• Two types of prayers at any one time are great• Superior customization options for the character• New control scheme takes getting used to, but is tighter than the first• Audio is much better than the first; sound effects really hitBad stuff:•Lots of glitches not present in the first game and still not fixed 4+ months post-launch. Game often crashes at launch, there can be a loss of control of the penitent one as the animation for igniting the hammer/bell fails to load; sometimes, you cannot smash through the people-barriers with the dive bomb attack until you reload, sfx can get caught in loops on boss fights, and most annoying: A persistent glitch in which guilt is not lost at all upon recovering your fragment still hasn't been fixed.• Imbalanced difficulty. Most of the game is substantially-easier than the first, but there are random spikes that are absurd.• Enemies are now bullet/sword sponges, generally. Enemies from B1 that went down in a few swings with even level 3 Mea Culpa now take 6+ hits, and there are not nearly as many weapon upgrades. Despite that, the game is easier, so it's just tedious.• Upgrading health, flasks and fervor is needlessly convoluted now and much more tedious to do.• The sword remains the most useful of the three weapons, and the other two border on useless save for traversal or specific enemies.• Weaker plot, by a lot• They got lazy on executions. In the first game, every enemy had a unique execution. In this one, most of them all get finished in the exact same way.• Although the graphics are better, it has an inferior overall aesthetic to the first game.• Spikes and pits aren't an instant death anymore -_-• Second half of the game is very linearIn a nutshell: If you liked the first game, you will still enjoy playing this one despite its issues, but unlike the first game (which I played through 4 times) this game will have to get some absolutely amazing DLC (and bug fixes!) to make you want to play it again after you beat it.It's just not as compelling as the first game, which I believe is the best metroidvania ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played this right after the first game, and was pleased to see that there were three weapons! They can be used interchangeably once they are obtained.  This is a nice change from the first game. They also control various mechanics, so depending on which you pick first, you could access different things earlier on. Not that it matters much. And there are almost too many thing to interact with that require upgrades. Rooms are covered with them, so I ended up taking a lot of screenshots for revisiting at a later date. This made traversing the world interesting and exciting. There are a ton of shops to buy things at and NPCs to upgrade so they can upgrade you. And there are so many upgrades to collect. Makes the game super rewarding.Just like the previous game, the pixel art and animation are top notch. There are also some animated cutscenes that are actual animation and not pixel animation. I did find the pixel cutscenes in the previous game to be really well done and pretty awesome, but these ones are really high quality. The music is reminscent of the first, some songs with the same instrument line up but different tunes. Really quite good and matches the mood of areas really well.I was glad to see some familiar areas as well. I was beginning to wonder how Cvstodia could be so different, though I guess it's possible as much time has passed.I know this game wasn't quite as challenging as the first game, and perhaps a bit less mysterious, but the actual level design, unlocks, and mechanics, I found to be  much more enjoyable. The previous game had a lot of missable things and it was possible to lock yourself out of the canon ending. Nothing like that happens in this game so you can play without worrying. There is even a vendor who will sell stuff that you did lock yourself out of.I was glad that there is a slide down ladder mechanic. Not being able to dismount downward in the first game irritated me. I realized a few hours in, by accident, that if you dash on the ladder you fall straight down. Not sure if that's how it was in the first game though.Some issues:1. The music would randomly stop playing, and then randomly start playing again.2. After obtaining an item, menus are not available for about 4 seconds, which is annoying.3. It was clear how much a prayer cost in the first game. This game doesn't not create lines to indicate the cost. Which can be frustrating trying to use a spell in a boss and not having enough, as you waste time attempting and there is a brief animation.Overall, this is a fantastic game. I got about 26 hours, 98% in game completion, and 67% achievements. The asking cost is more than fair, but on sale it's a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly well made game. It has pretty much everything what the first game offered and more.More ways to customise your playstyle (prayers, weapons, altar pieces). Controls are smooth and combat is fair.Graphics are still just as solid and beautiful and the cutscenes are amazing.I really really enjoyed the soundtrack. In more than one area would I stop for several minutes just to take in the music. Many of them made it into my playlists.If one uses the map and the markers well, they should have little trouble of exploring the map and get most collectibles, or know where to go after unlocking a new skill to open previously locked pathways.Some quests might need a guide but none are too tedious to complete.Overall, I highly recommend this game if you enjoyed playing the prequel.

_childDocuments_.review: - The story is  frustratingly convoluted, with every line drenched in unnecessary euphemistic and circumlocutory terms. _childDocuments_.review: The first, Blasphemous, is one of my favorite games with it's bulky movement, amazing palette and meditatively paced music. Sadly, someone in charge of the art direction really dropped the ball with the sequel.The first culprit is the cutscenes and it's strange to think they got past pre-production. It's not that they look bad, they're just so far removed from the core identity that was built up from the first game and that trend continues throughout.Everything now feels more like a cartoon from the get-go and it doesn't blend well with the religious motifs at all. There's just not the same weight to the world anymore. The tone isn't meant to be as depressing this time around, with the sequel feeling more saturated and bright. But they just went too far in too many places. The characters feel less developed, seeming out of place with this new brighter vision, like they didn't quite manage to capture that same spark.Gameplay wise, the sequel feels slick and faster but not methodical anymore. Gone is that feeling of slowly pacing along to the music when traveling, making rooms feel more like a sequence of platforming trials than actual locations with history you visit. Penalties are removed for doing things wrong and the harsh reality of the world is just kinda gone with it. Item placement has less restraint and purpose, removing a lot of the visual story-telling and mystique the first game had. Everything was down to earth like it was doing more with less. I could easily turn a blind eye to the gameplay changes. Because that's not why I bought it in the first place, I bought it for the art and mentality behind pulling off a theme to completion, something I really respected and admired about the first one.There are plenty of people out there who will enjoy this game as their first time in the universe and that's great, but I can't help but feel they shifted their target audience or outspoken members of the team from the first one lost some creative control over the project. With whoever was in charge of the art direction for the sequel understanding it only on a surface level or was just too willing to make compromises with the publisher to try to franchise it for a wider appeal.It just ends up feeling kinda shallow, leaning way harder into style over substance, diluting the atmosphere, mature themes, Catholic Spanish fused iconography until it's more family-friendly and easy to digest, it's a shame because that very dark and heavy religious focused identity was their own and it stood out from the other half-cooked attempts on the market.I hate not being able to recommend this, but presentation wise it feels watered down.But hey, at least the soundtrack is still pretty righteous.

_childDocuments_.review: I for one was very excited for Blasphemous 2, the original game was, and still is one of my favorite metroidvanias, and now having finished B2, I can only express disappointment. Firstly, the story. In the first game there was a very clear reason why you were the Penitent One, you are going to do penance like so many before you, and stop the big bad guy who's making things wrong in Cvstodia, there was a driving force making you care about the events unfolding before you. Meanwhile in the 2nd game there's really no reason for the Penitent One even being there, he just kinda trails along because the miracle, I guess... and let's throw a lot of adjectives at the player to make their task seem important. It just doesn't have the same sticking power and makes the whole ordeal seem very meandering and pointless. And don't even get me started on the cutscene animation.. eugh.Now let's talk about the areas themselves, apart from a few standouts, I can only go through so many ruined temples/castles before it starts to become samey. In the first game they managed to make every area distinctly their own style along with having their own enemies, but in B2 all of them just blend together and the recycled enemies REALLY don't help at all.As for the general difficulty, it has been dumbed down and the often brutal platforming of the first game is completely absent in the 2nd one. Enemies are generally fun to fight but I noticed some have way more health/damage than they probably should. The bosses were pretty easy, I don't think I ever died to one more than 10 times. as for the new weapons you're given, they all lack a real personality to them compared to the Mea Culpa, but they're all sufficiently fun to mess around with. Oh and one more thing is the bugs. Now this is not something I'd usually complain about, but this time I just expected a little more polish. Multiple times I'd switch areas and the game would just refuse to load them, leaving me with a black screen and a forced restart. Likewise on the occasion I couldn't even START the game, and on other occasions when switching weapons the previous one would still be visible on my character. I know these are the kinds of things to get patched out eventually, but they should've just done the due diligence from the get-go.In conclusion, the game is fun at parts but lacks the unique personality of the first game in terms of story, area design and enemy variety. I'd say play it but only when it's gone on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked the first one, the second isn't gelling with me. _childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 builds upon the interconnected world of its predecessor with even more intricately designed areas and hidden secrets. Backtracking remains essential, and the game still rewards those who thoroughly scour every corner. The areas are more unique than in the first game, but it is more linear overall.The controls in Blasphemous 2 are tight and responsive, continuing the need for precision in platforming and combat. The combat system is further refined, with an arsenal of three weapons (four with the DLC, each with multiple different moves and individual progression. Parrying returns, but it's only present on two of the weapons. The platforming feels more fluid compared to the original, and it's less punishing now. The design of platforming and puzzle challenges is exceptional, making clever use of the different weapons.Blasphemous 2 offers a more engaging progression system, with meaningful upgrades that enhance both combat and exploration. Beyond the traditional health and flask upgrades, the game introduces unique abilities that significantly alter how you approach obstacles and enemies. While some progression elements still revolve around finding keys to unlock new areas, the game does a better job of making these discoveries feel rewarding and impactful.The dark and immersive world persists, deeply rooted in religious and cultural themes. Like before, the supporting cast of characters adds depth to the world, with rich backstories and connections to the main plot. Environmental storytelling is as strong as ever, with the world itself telling a haunting and compelling story. The bosses feel like they have more personality than the bosses from the first game.Blasphemous 2 pushes its pixel art to new heights, delivering stunning visuals that are both grotesque and beautiful. The level of detail in the environments, character designs, and animations is exceptional, with each area exuding a unique atmosphere. The religious and gothic imagery is more pronounced, creating an even more memorable and immersive visual experience. While many dislike the non-pixelated cinematics, I like how they look.The soundtrack of Blasphemous 2 remains haunting and atmospheric, perfectly complementing the game’s dark themes. The compositions are more varied, with some tracks standing out as particularly memorable for me.Blasphemous 2 seems to prioritize fairness over difficulty, and I'm here for it. The game introduces new mechanics and enemy types that keep players on their toes, and while there are still occasional difficulty spikes, the overall experience feels more balanced. Boss battles are a standout, each offering unique challenges and requiring different strategies to overcome. The punishment for death remains fair, with ample opportunities to recover guilt fragments without excessive frustration, though I don't like how guilt builds up even if you recover every fragment you leave after death.For me Blasphemous 2 offers more replayability than its predecessor, with multiple weapons to use and a NG+ mode. The game is packed with content, including side quests, hidden areas, and collectibles. While the core experience is unlikely to change drastically with each playthrough, the variety of builds and paths you can take ensures that the game remains engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a great game - however, it hasn’t really surprised me in any new way (compared to the first game) and somehow, the game just felt somewhat “rushed”, i.e. developers made the sequel as quickly as they could.Sure, the game does introduce three weapons but you end up collecting all of them throughout your playthrough anyway. The music doesn’t pull the same strings as the first one did - it just seems to lack character.Nearly a year after the release, when I had played the game, it still had bugs. One of them was so bad that it deleted my Save file, so I had to search the web to find the fix. Fortunately, I managed to restore my 14-hour save file.What I will definitely give the game a credit for are the bosses. They’re very well designed: the attacks are clearly telegraphed and for any souls veterans, it’s quite easy to learn their moveset.All in all, this is a very safe sequel. It lacks a number of things that made the first one stand out so much for me: memorable boss fights, weird & ominous enemies & moody soundtrack.If you’re on a lookout for a great-looking metroidvania - this is the one. However, if you’re a huge fan of the first game, you may not like what the sequel has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: It really sucks to give this one a thumbs down because it certainly wasn't a _bad_ game per say, but I'm pretty disappointed at how it compares to the original, especially for $40. I really loved the first game for a ton of reasons, and ended up picking this up over several of the other big name games releasing currently.Here's a couple of particular things that are bugging me:- Cutscene art is changed from the old pixel style to a out of place cartoonish style. Kind of a baffling change.- The parry/execute system - one of the things that made B1 so much fun to play - has been cut back and deemphasized significantly. This is perhaps the single most baffling change to me.- The sheer amount of copy/pasted enemies from the original, which wouldn't be as bad if there were more original enemies thrown in there. But as is, I have to guess that at least half of the enemies are unchanged from the original.- To make matters worse, the enemy variety in any given region is super repetitive. I don't recall this being an issue in the first game, but there's just a lot of similar halls with similar groups of enemies present here.- The new animations, where they do exist, seem very lazily done. The original game had detailed visceral death animations, but this one seems to slap a dozen keyframes into half a second resulting in overly fast and undetailed animation.The new NPCs and bosses are creative and interesting, and disturbing, and the change to 3 weapons is also an interesting one but I can't help but feel this could have easily just been a DLC for the first game.If you're a superfan of Blasphemous, I would consider picking this up on sale at some point. Otherwise, I find it hard to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 emerges as a triumphant sequel, enhancing every aspect of its predecessor to deliver an exceptional gaming experience. The shift towards a purer Metroidvania style is a welcome change, although a touch more originality in gameplay and ability design would have been appreciated. Despite this, the game doesn't falter in execution, offering a well-balanced challenge and a more accessible experience than the first installment. The narrative continues to intrigue, weaving a cryptic yet fascinating tale that demands attention. Gameplay-wise, the transition to a more agile protagonist with precise controls and new abilities significantly enhances both combat and exploration. The level design showcases greater variety and creativity, moving away from the linear corridors of the past to offer distinct regions with unique mechanics. Weapon variety adds a refreshing dynamic to combat and exploration, each with unique properties and uses. The enemy roster is more diverse, and boss battles are a highlight, featuring intricate patterns and phases that capitalize on the protagonist's improved mobility. Graphically, the game is a feast for the eyes, with reimagined characters, detailed environments, and an art direction that beautifully pays homage to Andalusian culture. The soundtrack, once again composed by Carlos Viola, is exceptional, with catchy, flamenco-inspired tunes that perfectly complement the game's atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this all I have left to do is the final boss. My map is at 99%, I found every cherub, every prayer, upgrade etc. without a guide at 14 hours. 2 of those hours were trying to solve one part of a riddle because I was having a complete mental blockThe game is obviously fun, but it's extremely easy and falls into the pitfall of so many other modern metroidvanias, where all the backtracking is just for money or upgrades you wont use/need. This becomes apparent very early, so really the game is completely linear and after you get all 3 weapons and all 4 traversal skills, you go back to all the areas you marked on your map that needed some kind of movement in collectathon tedium. Don't bother going back until you have all the skills too because most backtracking items need 2 or more, so you'll just waste time if you don't wait. The devs give you every movement skill you need in the same area, so there's nothing like SotN where you had to search for the double jump in a separate area and go back.There were only 2 bosses I died more than twice at and as said before, I didn't even have my health upgrades until the end because they simply weren't needed. The original blasphemous had super easy bosses too but had the worst platforming in gaming on release (if you know, you know) so they improved movement, but didn't accommodate for it. The biggest challenge you'll have is hopping from a few mirror with one weapon, then ground slamming with another.The last gripe is that NPCs are not nearly as memorable as the first. The first game is worth playing just for the art and characters you meet, but they're much more mediocre this time around.I could recommend the game for under $15, but at full price it's really not worth it. Maybe when they add freeLC like in the first game and it has more meat it'll have more value

_childDocuments_.review: game has been a lot of fun but the negative reviews definitely have a point (but dont let that stop you from experiencing it for yourself) its somewhat missing the charm of the first game. im still having a great time with it so far. the movement is less clunky and i appreciate the QoL changes. if youve never played the first one, i think youll love this. if youre coming into this after the first, it might feel like its lost a little bit of soul. i would say im disappointed but i might of had too high expectations. the dialogue is definitely not as well written and i miss the mia culpa a lot. sure the new weapons provide cool platforming/puzzle stuff but im not the biggest fan of them. when i read about the new cutscenes i thought "it can't be that bad" but they feel so out of place. why would you choose to go for that smooth kind of animation compared to the gritty pixel art cutscenes that really gave the game character?  makes no damn sense to me. outside of the artwork/dialogue, i really think the combat could of been improved upon way more. more variety in attacks would of done a lot for the game and at times the combat is a tad too easy. the execution animations are reused from the first game and a lot of the enemies share the same generic one. a lot of missed opportunity imo but this version of blasphemous does seem like it will draw in a more mainstream audience for sure. i will say the platforming is more enjoyable and i enjoy the level design. anyway, all that being said:overall i say give it a go and at least you can refund it on steam if you arent feeling it. 2 hours is more than enough time to make that decision imo. or if you arent in a rush, hold out until a future sale. i still think its a great game and worth at least trying

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO CLOSE to finished, but it absolutely needs one last quick pass on polish before it's ready. The same was true of the first game, which just got better and better after each DLC rollout; I assume it'll be the same for this one later down the line. For right now though, there are *just* enough glitches, lack of consistency and rough edges that my frustration hit bizarre spikes throughout my playthrough. Spoilers below:Double-jumping 'into' half-block-high areas meant to be climbed into will kill you instantly.Inputs are dropped juuust often enough during input-heavy sequences (ie boss battles) that the game will force you to miss dodges.There are only two or three enemy attacks that can be dodged ONLY in the air, NOT along the ground, while very similar attacks from other enemies or stage hazards can be dodged along the ground. We're trained for 10+ hours, told that just sliding through it is fine, but all of a sudden that training goes out the window for a very select few attacks.Timing on the 'flower' attack of the final boss is tight enough that I had to clear the flowers 5 times before he dropped his shield my first time through. It's tight enough that the only way I could realistically get through it with a Sarmiento build was to switch to Veredicto and tank damage, rushing them as fast as I could.The semi-final boss and the final boss are the only two that force you to sit through at least a portion of their dialogue before attempting again, paired with a needlessly-long walk back to the final boss. It's inconsistent with previous bosses, and pointlessly time consuming.All that being said, once these issues are addressed, it'll be nearly flawless from a gameplay perspective. It's a fair amount more challenging than the first game (minus Isidora), but once they reduce dropped inputs and polish with some quality-of-life for retrying bosses, it'll be fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Boss fights are not very hard, except for the previous-to-last boss, which is suprisingly (in a good way) difficult. Not sure why the last boss is so easy tho.I'm also quite sick of these "find brothers, sisters, daughters" etc stuff, which gives you almost nothing worthy, but required tons of time. Search-n-find with no clear purpose other than to stretch your playtime.Same goes for side quests. I've spent some time reading thru all the 5-letters lore only to find that the reward is a spell which costs all your mana and has its effect for like 2 seconds.The dialogs feel completely GPT generated based on a prompt like "generate pompous religious nonsense". Even the last boss when died started praising (???) some new world. Like wtf dude, you're craving suicide be the player or what?And of course the plot is all about suffering and torture and death. Not love or pleasure or anything good.The aren't very many skills, and even then 2/3rds of them are just bad.The UI controls are super awkward, like why do you need THREE different sets of keys to navigate left from right? I mean, make it five! At least you'll succeed in something, like confusing me.The basic movement abilities are reduced. No double jump, no air dash, no wall climb, etc, until you collect a certain "tribute" (unlock the ability to finally be able to make some moves). But these are all scattered all over the map, and you're forced to face some areas which you KNOW you can't access, and you KNOW you'll get the ability to do so on the other side of the map, so you KNOW you are forced to either go thru all the map AGAIN after beating the boss (or just before), and place million map markers to return to these area later. And you'll only find useless junk like in there anyway (like 3k souls).And there is no reason to visit these areas once you've reached the final boss. You can just go and kill him, nothing in those dozens of hidden spots will give you anything worthy.So, these spots feel forced and annoying.Like "haha player, we KNOW you want to grab that shiny junk, and we KNOW you need a double jump for it, but suck it, you won't get it, just stand there and look. crave for that cheaply earned ability (which is on the other side of the map tho) that we took from you by a magic of game design".
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyable experience! It lost a bit of the original's flair*, so I can see B1 being remembered longer. However, the platforming is fluid and combat more varied with 3 weapons. It's a fun time! Maybe 2 being fun and pleasant compared to 1 is a "bad" thing, but I'm not here to analyze that. If you liked zipping around in Hollow Knight, you'll love Blasphemous 2! If you loved the slow, methodical, grueling Blasphemous 1 ... you're probably going to be disappointed. Try it anyways. -* A few things I think factor into B2 not feeling the same: Faster land traversal (a double-edged sword), no pixelated cutscenes, & less execution animations.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: "Cheap" is the only thing that comes to mind when playing this game. The lore is cheap, the plot is cheap, the world-building is cheap, the gameplay is cheap.- The lore is nothing compared to the previous game, and for a very precise reason: the story was over to begin with. The first game came full-circle already, what is there to talk about now? "The miracle" this, "the miracle" that, yeah we get it, fancy and ominous church-y slop, the dialogues are so needlessly convoluted they end up telling the player nothing new about the world. - Same for the plot. When the lore is already poor, you can't have a rich storytelling. "The miracle is having a son" sounds like some Spanish telenovela. Uninspired and cheap, aimed at milking the first game's aesthetic and name just to sell a second instance. - The world-building is nonsense. There is absolutely no artistic cohesion between any of the areas, the enemies are mostly recycled assets from the previous game, and the new enemies look like some cartoony parody of themselves. The previous title created a complex, coherent and awe-inspiring world, making it feel alive with its rich lore, every enemy design was coherent with its surrounding, the items you found had detailed descriptions that would help explain what was going on, the whole thing was inspired by real-world art and traditions, respectfully reinterpreted and portrayed in a delicate frame. This? This is literally "look, spanish-y flamenco, so cultural! Look, famous painting reference! Veeeery culture, yes! Spanish!" Cringe AF.- The actual gameplay is just another mediocre metrovania, like many out there. Meh. The level design is simple enough, most of your powers and weapons are pretty much situational or just plain useless, and the whole thing feels like a chore. The first one was difficult as hell compared to this, the platforming time trials, and the bosses, holy crap. There was challenge there. Here? I chopped everything up in little more than 3 hours, couldn't even care to kill the enemies at one point, I just run through them. Booooriiiiing. Sad to see that this is a recurring theme coming from small indie studios. They strike gold thanks to talented artists, devs and storytellers, and then they just sit there. It's almost like they don't realise what made their work successful in the first place, and they end up repeating themselves. Just make a new game with a new world, this well is dry already.
