_childDocuments_.review: I played Blasphemous 2 directly after completing the first game and I didn't expect them to be so different! Where Blasphemous one felt more like a Soulslike with Metroid elements, Blasphemous 2 is quite clearly a Metroidvania.Unlike the first game your upgrades aren't just simple items that make platform appear or make you immune to poison but instead are mobility upgrades such as double jump, air dash, and wall climbing. A major difference is that the game was designed so that you must find all of these upgrades to advance deeper and deeper into the game. It's a classic case where you find a new power-up and then backtrack to explore more of the map.The combat in Blasphemous 2 is also quite a bit different. With all of the mobility upgrades it's much faster and in my opinion easier. Instead of needing to learn timings to parry like the first game you can instead reliably dodge almost all attacks in the game. It's kind of a shame but the risk feels too high for parrying in this game and the reward is far too small and sometimes the knockback prevents it from being worth it at all.  There are three weapons in this game as opposed to just the sword in the first game and all of them are fun to use with unique perks and playstyles.  You pick one weapon at the start but you end up needing all three as they offer unique interactions with the environment that are required to progress. They all have separate upgrade skill trees and by the end of the game I was able to max two of them out. You can swap between the weapons at any time in combat which is fun when you prefer one or the other against a specific enemy.Secrets in Blasphemous 2 was much, much easier to find in my opinion which is probably the result of all the mobility power-ups being a requirement to progress in the game. You aren't going to get locked out of finding most things because you missed something in the first hour or two of the game like Blasphemous 1. There's still a lot to find here though and I think if exploration is your thing you won't be disappointed by the amount of content in this game.The art and sound was just as fantastic in this game as the original. I do miss some of the creepier body horror designs from the original but there were plenty of unsettling looking npcs, bosses, and enemies. I feel like this sequel had less gimmicky bosses than the original and the boss fights were much more consistently good, even if some of them were a bit on the easier side. The penultimate boss is quite the difficulty spike!If the gameplay of Blasphemous 1 wasn't your thing you might want to check this one out if you're a Metroidvania fan because I thought that overall it was fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, 100% took me 26 hours. I am not really great at making reviews, so I will keep it simple. The story is almost non existent, and so are most of the character you meet alongside of your journey. Feels rushed, and because of that, it's a bit of a step down, in many ways from the previous one. Far less love and passion was put in it. From music, story, game play to animation. The best way to describe it, as if they made this game, to bring more audience to play the first one. I really want this studio to keep making great games, and that why I'm strongly recommending you play the original Blasphemous game instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: While I did like the combat mechanics more, I overall felt this was such a let down of a game. I had hopes this game would fix the problems I had with 1, and it did, but in return just frustrated me more in other ways.Exploration was sluggish and slow in 1 in my opinion, and they have fixed it here with less instant-kill environmental traps, movement abilities, and handy QoL features, but now most of the areas are too forgettable and samey. Just felt like I was flowing from one area to the next before it could leave an impact on me.Some of the NPC character designs were neat, but overall also forgettable and uninteresting. Same with a lot of the enemies, which I just avoided near the last quarter of the game as much as I could because fighting them got too repetitive. Boss designs were good for the most part, though.End was a big let down as well, just a big, "that's it?" moment for me. Enough so that I didn't bother going back to get what ever other ending is available and finish clearing the map.Disappointing all around, would recommend spending your money elsewhere unless you just desperately need a metroidvania fix. If it weren't for the strange biblical character designs and macabre imagery while riding on the coat-tails of popularity from the first game, I don't think anyone would give this game the time of day.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't understand some of the negative reviews. For me Blasphemous II is better than its prequel in every thinkable way: The new game mechanics, the bosses, the weapons and its skills, the way the world is built (much more labyrinthic and metroidvania-esque than in Blasphemous I) and the overall quality of the pixel art (Characters, Maps, Animations). For me, Blasphemous II is one of the best games of this genre I’ve played in a long time. A huge improvement compared to the first entry!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel! Platforming has been expanded with  three new weapons that double as tools to navigate the world. Music especially boss themes will get your heart pumping  - looking at your boss music Lesmes - and the retro art style is gorgeous as ever. I feel like the art team really wanted to outdo themselves here. All around a labour of love worth your time and money no questions about. Pick up the game with the recently added Mea Culpa DLC while you're at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played Blasphemous 1 and loved it. Blasphemous 2 has a nice balance on the difficulty of the game like certain areas and bosses. You might feel easier in some areas or bosses because you have seen it in Blasphemous 1 but the new areas and bosses might be slightly harder. The lore and music is amazing as always. A good 20+ hours of gameplay and more if you want to 100% it. A very solid and well made metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

Didn't know this game was made in 1998 when that ♥♥♥♥ was still cool.Great game otherwise but majorly ♥♥♥♥♥ over completionists who don't look up guides before hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through roughly 50% of the game I experienced a gamebreaking bug. From a saving point I kept falling down under a bridge, and could not get out or up in any way. Thus, all my progress was lost and only way was to restart the game, which I will not bother with doing after all that playtime.And no, using the spell to go back did not work.Otherwise the game was great, although hard. _childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Game kitchen is cooking.They succeded in improving many of annoying game mechanics like having to run around all the time - it's way easier to teleport through areas than in B1.My opinion on B2 changed dramatically after reaching about 50% of the game. With double jump and air dash, weapon and spell upgrades it gets VERY interesting and versatile.The resonance mechanic with statues is done very well.At first I was disappointed because I didn't like the colorful anime cinematics which do not really fit the dark mood and they also toned down on the brutality of execution scenes. I also didn't like that it's easier than B1 and spikes do not kill you instantly. Kinda like the "one missstep and you are dead, don't have to die" fear :)But maybe I'm just saying this because I have played B1 right before that (same problems with Ori 1+2). You already know the mechanics from the first game so obviously the second game seems easier.The fire mace is clearly the OP weapon choice in the beginning BUT the sword takes the cake when reaching midgame - it's sooo much fun to use in combination with spells. Rarely use rapier. Anyway, this game will slowly grow on you and once it does it will not let go
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Its more of the first game but just better in every way. Movement isn't as stiff, there are a lot of QoL changes, such as giving the player the ability to see health bars innately, instead of locking it behind a rosary bead, and overall just making the map better.There are also 3 weapons to choose from now, each with one of the melee abilities we saw from the first game (charge attack, dash attack, and ground slam) they are also very unique from one another, giving options on how you want to fight.ALSO SPIKES DON'T IMMEDIATELY KILL YOU
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very good Metroidvania game that continues the Story of Blasphemous 1.Accessibility is better than the first one but for veterans it is also a let down cause the game is too easy with very few exceptions. The look and the Soundtrack are again top notch.An very enjoyable experience especially if you dont have too much time for videogames on hand.You can 100% it in under 20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: 1st game is better. The only real thing this sequel improves upon is the gameplay, and clunky mechanics of the 1st game. Visually the 1st game looks better, has a better story, better lore and far more memorable bosses and locations. Don’t know why they decided to limit the bosses in the sequel either, there’s like 7 bosses in total and only about 2 are decent fights. With that said though, still an enjoyable game. Just falls into that same boring Metroidvania trope that the 1st game didn’t have.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Massive improvement over the original game in almost every way. You can tell the devs listened to the feedback of the first game and trimmed the stuff that didn't work while improving on what did work. Blasphemous 2 is how to do a sequel right.I've read some people saying the game is too easy compared to the first. IMO Blasphemous 2 strikes the right balance of 'medium' difficulty for a game of this genre. Most bosses didn't take me more than 5-10 tries to beat and each have visible tells in their animations to let you know how to dodge or counter them. This was fine, as they were still fun to fight and no boss really stood out to me as being bad.Platforming is way, way, way, improved thankfully. There's no more touching the sides of a ledge during a jump and clipping through it. They also removed a lot of the insta death spike sections so when you fall you teleport back to the ledge and lose a fraction of your health. Platforming feels precise and snappy now.Pixel art and music are gorgeous.They also removed the opaque and esoteric relic hunting of the first game. The first game felt like hunting for those relics was just meant to softlock you out of the 2nd half of the game to needlessly pad the game time out but that's no longer the case. You find everything you need to progress much more fluidly by just exploring the world and playing the game.Overall Blasphemous 2 is a very solid addition for Metroidvania fans. 8.7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: In some ways this improves over the first, but it falls short in others. Overall, there's a lot to love here. In terms of improvements: the movement and abilities are much more fleshed out and they are a lot of fun to use. Exploration, secrets, and quests are just the right amount of obscure, with a few of the possible quest lines being buried in item lore descriptions. Visually, it does not quite live up to the harrowing body horror of the first, but it is still successful in creating a feeling of a complete, strange, and grueling world with a handful of memorable NPCs and set piece encounters. Bottom line: it is a fun and engaging world to explore.The biggest negative is that the game is too easy, which makes my favorite boss in the game into a huge difficulty spike at the very end. Platforming is also much easier, and I missed the presence of insta-death spikes a la Castlevania. Also, I ran into a number of visual bugs, like enemies freezing mid-animation before dying and one of the weapons having some bugged animations. Also had a few deaths to bugged screen transitions where I died for no apparent reason. I've also read that some quest lines can bug out, but I did not experience that.In all, my complaints are minor and the experience of playing the game more than makes up for them. Strongly recommend for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: A solid metroidvania with solid platforming, lots of stuff to collect, and npcs actually doing something when you fully complete their quest lines. It's worth getting the secret ending, and no shame if you need a guide to do it (like me!). It's worth the purchase and I hope to see more from these devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It took almost 18 hours for me to get through a first playthrough and get ending B while exploring 99% of the map. This is much better than the first Blasphemous in almost every single important (gameplay) aspect :1. There are actual movement upgrades this time around (after all it's a metroidvania). Some platforming sections are actually fun. Movement is actually well implemented in boss fights, esp. in bullet hell segments;2. The Prie Dieu fast travel upgrade isn't hidden behind some obscure donation machine and it's easy to get relatively early (the downside is that the teleportation gates become useless reaaaal quick);3. Boss fights are almost all much harder than in the first instalment (with one very important exception, see below);4. If I remember correctly, the first Blasphemous was locked at 60fps. I played this on 144hz and it was perfect;5. Combat is much better (you're actually rewarded for parrying and not getting hit).There are however a few misses in Blasphemous 2 :1. I really enjoyed having to stick my blade into walls to climb, instead of having the wall latch on the same input as the dash;2. The final boss is so easy it's not even funny. This was a problem in the first game as well but it's even worse in the sequel as some earlier bosses are actual choke points;3. The cutscene style they went with doesn't suit the game at all;4. Would've liked to see the return of the silvered lung of Dolphos and some poison sections;5. Still don't understand the point of the guilt mechanic. It's like in Dark Souls 2 where you're punished for dying by making your next attempt even harder. Had to beat most of the tougher bosses without using a single prayer.9.1/10 hoping for a 3rd one
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Bigger, better, avoiding the mistakes of its predecessor, Blasphemous 2 is one of the most faithful to its tenets, sequels we've seen in recent years. Its solid gameplay and intriguing level design and exploration are some of the reasons why we fell in love with this genre, in the first place.Read more on:

_childDocuments_.review: Having just gotten both endings i can safely say this this game is undeniably a step up from the first (with the first, naturally, being an amazing game in of itself, especially after all the updates it received). This game had me loving the combat again, three new weapons to play around with as well as skill trees??? consider my love obtained. The majority of the boss fights were very enjoyable (especially the second to last one).My only gripe is that ending A is rather annoying to get considering you need to get all 33 cherub's/ caged babies to get one of the items needed.This game is absolutely worth playing
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel to the first game, Blasphemous 2 improves on nearly every aspect where the original fell short, while bringing enough new elements to the table to re-invigorate Cvstodia. First and foremost are the QoL changes, such as not dying immediately from a spike trap or pitfall, and being able to unlock traveling between shrines much more coherently. Additionally, the level design feels much more modern than the original, and the dungeons all feel detailed, fleshed out, and fun to explore. The story is also far easier to follow, which is beneficial to casual players.                                                                                                         That said, there are some aspects where the original remains supreme. Noticeable from the opening cutscene, Blasphemous 2 lacks the gritty themes of the original, made obvious by the change in artstyle. The atmosphere feels especially generic and bland when compared to the desolate and plague-ridden environment of the first game. Though this could be attributed to the plot, as the Miracle has been gone from Cvstodia, this in of itself serves for a less interesting premise than the original. There is no more aura of mystery -- nothing to discover in terms of story or lore. I felt far less involved in the world and lore of the game as I played than the original.    Regardless, Blasphemous 2 was certainly a very enjoyable experience. Each dungeon somehow improved in quality, and the excitement upon reaching the final zone was palpable. Although I miss the Mea Culpa, the combat feels smoother than the first game, with more options and unique features. Marks of Martyrdom are also a smart addition, as weapon upgrades don't simply require more tears of atonement. The gameplay improved solidly from the first game, with the exception being the somewhat linear progression. This isn't that big of a deal though for me, as there's plenty of metroidvania in the game already.      In conclusion, I'd definitely recommend this game. The story isn't bad on its own -- it only falls depressingly short when compared to the masterpiece of the original. The gameplay is invigorating and exciting, and it's a fun time all in all.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very good metroidvania.The game design and character evolution have changed quite a bit since the first opus. It can be unsettling at first but the diversification of builds is nice. I think some balancing may be required between the different weapons. The censer might be too powerful compared to the other ones.There are some audio bugs that can be bothering at times (no music sometimes, no bgm on a boss fight)But overall, I enjoy my time on the game.So, it's a "yes" for me. gg wp
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: A Very Solid sequel with enough to offer! Graphically, The game looks as beautiful and disturbing as the first with a little more added to itThe new 3 Weapons system is a refreshing twist and a solid story reason too. They also serve a purpose in the world so you'll often switch. Speaking of which, Switching is responsive which is a plus because they'll be some platforming involved so its important! One thing I don't like is how a lot of things weren't as "open" as the first. To me i felt that there was a bit of "hand holding" or other things locked behind story progress where you HAD to go to one area to open up another and get power ups and such to back track and find other things. Also the final boss seemed a bit lackluster, especially due to the other boss before it being such a pain. Other than that - I'd say its worth a try, if you've played the first one, You'd enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot, I don't know if I can compare it with its predecessor since I liked both with their differences, beautiful settings, very disturbing and interesting boss design, the mechanics of the new weapons are very fun, the only thing I can have a complaint It's the low level of difficulty, but for everything else, I would play it again. The wait was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: An overall upgrade compared to the first title.Boss fights, and even the enemies are well designed and punishing for the average souls-like enjoyer, but should not be to difficult for the general metroidvania enjoyer as well.Playstyle differs significantly depending on your preferred weapon archetype. I opted to go with Sarmiento & Centella (Rapier and Dagger) for the entirety of the game, which rewards greed and risky play through the need to squeeze every possible hit in, and abusing invincibility frames as much as possible. Veredicto (Censer) serves as the best alternative, being safest due to it being slow and hard hitting with great range. Ruego Al Alba (Sword) offers a balanced solution, which unfortunately did not work well for me as both extremes have significant advantages compared to it.Puzzle-solving is easy but fun, primarily due to some agility required.Exploration is painless, only later in the game once easier ways to travel are unlocked. These are within standard expectations for any good metriodvania in the market.The only negative for me is that the cutscenes are almost being of a different aesthetic as compared to the grotesque art style seen throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of graphics and overall fidelity, this is a notable improvement over the original.But in terms of world/story/characters/plot, Blasphemous 2 falls sort of it's predecessor. I'd go so far as to say this feels like the main team didn't have any ideas for a sequel, so they handed it off to a new group.The new weapons add verity, but the one handed sword is still the best due to block and parry windows. In fact, the mace can't parry at all. So even with the extra range I found myself almost never using it.Several animations have been missing since launch. I've been caught in the floor, and had an enemy get knocked off screen that couldn't return. Both incidents requiring me to quit and re-load.And this might be more personal, but if you're going to add a time stop power to your game please make the rules consistent. In short, works on everyone including bosses, but won't stop projectiles even from regular enemies. If the enemy is mostly done the animation, it will still launch the projectile. Sometimes stopped enemies won't hurt you when you touch them, and sometimes they do.Overall, I'd recommend the first one over the second.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same, which is initially enough, but as this drags on, it becomes clear that it's all very phoned in.There just doesn't seem to be much to it. The game's size seems comparable to the original base game, but a lot of the map traversal seems trivial. The game holds your hand so much more than the first, even telling you exactly where you need to go at all times, which completely kills that Metroidvania sense of adventure. Backtracking seems kinda bleh, as while upgrading your flasks is worth it, it doesn't feel like much of a reward overall. Tears of Atonement come in abundance and there's little to purchase with them.Outside that, there's QoL changes in some aspects like easy warping, but they still kept major annoyances from the first game, like the grief system, where you lose max fervor, which basically renders your major spells uncastable, and all this achieves is constantly making you warp back and forth to the NPC that wipes it. Vague, ridiculously named items return, attached to NPC quests and vendors, none of which feel all that rewarding, except this time they are actually spelled out rather obviously in the lore descriptions. Chokepoint enemy battles return to a major degree, inflating the game's playtime because there's just not enough meaningful encounters in this game. The boss battles all have very annoying unskippable intros, incredibly egregious for the later boss battles requiring multiple tries.Speaking of which, the bosses... are interesting in a design aspect, but they're all ridiculously easy, mostly because of the games 3 weapon system and upgrades. If you just beeline the one weapon, you are mostly too powerful for these bosses.Until you're not, which leads me to the finale of this game and the Eviterno boss. Straight up, whoever designed this nonsense should be fired. It's like putting an Armored Core 6 boss into DS2. Striaght up, unadulterated, nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent sequel to the first one. I liked that the exploration depends on the weapons you've acquired. The environments are enjoyable to look at. The regular enemies are challenging enough. The bosses are amazing, even though on the first few tries, it appears that only dumb luck can help defeat them. A few more tries, and their move sets and counters to those moves start to make sense. After that, every incorrect action feels like a player error and not the game being cruel or unfair.Also, selecting the correct weapon for the boss fight makes a huge difference.Using the built-in marker system, I found 32 out of 33 angles on my own before using a guide to finish that quest.One thing I wish is that there was an option to completely skip the boss cutscene after seeing it for the first time. Even though they are mostly short, hearing that some guy is the first Penitent for the 10th time (skill issue on my side, I guess) was a bit annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. They played it pretty safe, its very similar to the first game, but just like the first game the catholic imagery is great. The fights are fun and challenging enough, but not so difficult that they get frustrating. The next to last fight has a significantly harder difficulty than the rest of the game, but it just took a little longer than i would have liked.If you liked the first one, you will like this one. _childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Blasphemous game was really good, although not something I was all that interested in. Its exploration didn't have much in terms of movement upgrades, a criticism I held for it. It wasn't something I thought was a bad thing, it just wasn't something I enjoyed as much as a Metroidvania fan. Even with that the first game was excellent. Blasphemous 2 evolves from the first game and takes a different direction for their exploration which could be off putting for some. Much like the changes from Axiom Verge 1&2, Blasphemous 2  brings in some methods of movement and offers the player a choice of 1 of 3 at the start. This makes it so the game can have different experiences for repeated playthroughs, at least at the start of the game. You eventually get all 3 weapons but this change was a welcome one in my opinion. Visually and narratively the game does not disappoint. The lore is extremely rich in the series although I'd be lying if I said I really understood it. From my perspective the Miracle seems needlessly cruel. The Quest of penance also seems fairly cruel as well. perhaps that's the point of the game, but I'm not entirely sure. Its hard for me to decipher what the game wants to say since I'm not as familiar with Catholicism, the game's clear inspiration. To me it looks like Zealotry and suffering. Beyond that I couldn't say. Perhaps I'll read or watch someone smarter than me explain it. There's a lot to unpack with this one to really understand what its trying to really say.Gameplay is smooth and being able to swap between 3 different weapons was enjoyable. Although the Mace wasn't all that useful against bosses most the time while being really useful against flying enemies. The Saber was a pretty good generalist weapon having a good counter and strong arc preventing smaller enemies from tripping you up. The Rapier and parrying dagger were the best in my opinion. Strong damage output if you could get them going and great battlefield movement. Its weakness was it struggled against smaller enemies sometimes and getting hit often would mean its damage wasn't as strong as the saber. Although if you could block well and prevent yourself from being struck it could clean up rather well. At least that's my opinion. I'm also a big fan of timed blocks in Metroidvanias. Blasphemous has a rather satisfying black as well which really rewards your skill. Overall big fan!The Music of the game was just awesome. A couple of the songs I kinda want to download for a playlist. I really enjoyed them. The game is also kinda hard. I struggled for a while and one boss made me put the game down for a couple of weeks. I'm not always in the mood for extremely hard games and I'm not the biggest fan of Boss fights. I like them as set pieces or narrative pieces. Some of the bosses here were a little on the frustrating side which isn't to my liking. Most were good though. Fun and challenging.Overall its a great game. Deserves the praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: A good sequel so I would recommend for those that enjoyed the first one. Interesting lore, engaging story. The best improvement being the combat system and movements. Really cool new character building mecanics.However I did not enjoy it as much as the 1st one for these reasons :- The cutscenes style are, as for me, out of touch with the blasphemous world. Even if I can tell there were efforts put into them, they just do no fit the game imo.- Some bosses desgins are quite forgettable- Really cool new character building mecanics-- Overall really enjoyed this game and diving into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Horrible game in terms of difficulty balance mainly due to the wooden and slow movements of our hero. Complicated controls make it difficult to enjoy the game.It is also basically a copy of the first one with a few improvements (3 weapons instead of one), but still the gameplay is predictable and tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game. It feels for the most part like the game that the developers wanted to make the first time around. Blasphemous 2 overall better than Blasphemous but it has it's own issues. The map to me feels less fleshed out than in the original game but I still had a fun time exploring it. There are also music and SFX bugs in the game. I think the best parts of this game are the multiple the weapons that you can upgrade, the combat, and the rewarding experience for exploring, to find lots of items to help you on your journey of penance. The art and cutscenes are beautiful like in the original and the item lore is very good. I do miss the gory imagery of the first game. This game feels a lot tamer than the original but I wouldn't consider that a negative. I look forward to the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game almost non-stop on switch when it first launched and I was amazed at the improvements: Multiple weapons, More enemy designs, more epic boss fights, fully voice acted, and incredible level design. Looking at the basically completed map at the end of the game put a smile on my face basically being an homage to Castlevania: SOTN excellent map. This game is a fantastic Metroidvania and it seemed to go unnoticed with the 2023 onslaught of games but this is up there with the best of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias out there. The combat system has been greatly improved compared to its predecessor. _childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best metroidvania games out there.The controls are improved in comparison to the first game. Controlling The Penitent One feels like a Castlevania game.There are more weapons this time, and they are all fun to use in combat, but they are also useful to solve puzzles and for map traversal.This time, all of your relics that give you abilities to traverse the map are equipped automatically.  There was no reason for them not to be turned on by default in the first game.Speaking of the map, it is huge, full of secrets, platforming challenges and puzzles. It is a joy to explore the map in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a sequel done right. It takes everything that made the first game great and expanded upon it heavily. I played through the entirety of the first game before diving into the sequel and my only real complaints regarding the original were the options for mobility and the lack of weapon variety. These issues are masterfully answered by the new weapons presented in the sequel, which both broaden the means in which you can engage combat as well as providing new means of traversal. The interconnected map is excellently tied together and while there is a range of variety I found no bosses in the game to be poorly designed. Just like the first game the setting is gripping and dripping with personality. I absolutely devoured this game when it came out, I just could not stop playing it. Blasphemous 2 is a master class not only as a modern Metroidvania but what sequels should aspire to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll go in saying that i really wanted to like the game, and gave it a pretty good chance. The way the game plays is fine, everything feels good, combat for the most part is fine, i'd even say good. Side scroller metroidvenia games are my absolute favourite genre, so i would like to think i know what im talking about and can pick out the good and the bad in these types of games. im not gonna talk about the good, because theres not much to it; the game looks great, feels nice to play, and honestly i cant say much else. For the things i didnt like, they are a lot more prevalent in my time playing. Exploration doesnt feel very rewarding, especially when i would say most of it is behind a double jump of some type of ability, all to often i would get to the end of some path and i found nothing except a dead end i couldnt do anything with, and i explored all i could, promise. i didnt get terribly far i dont think, probably about halfway? However im kinda just done with the game.Another thing i feel is that the player is weak for too long and it just kinda stays that way. i found my second bile flask pretty early and then never saw one again, i maxed out all 3 weapons pretty fast (being the upgrades available, never found a way to unlock the next tier of upgrades for any of them) and they just stayed that way for a long while, most exploration that you can actually do rewards you with basically nothing meaningful, best you get is a mark of martydom which again, isnt that great. This is also shown with the enemies, most are fine, some are just annoying and seem to be intentionally made that way, and some enemies are just way too tanky for god knows what reason, not hard to fight, the fight is just too long, your bound to make a mistake sometimes and thats the point, which i think just isnt good design. The game seems to want you to stay weak, which is just kind of annoying cause it just feels like your not progressing your character while the game steadily increases in difficulty.Finally, contact damage....idk why people put this crap in side scrollers anymore when the enemies have actual attacks, its a scourge, and if it is in your game it should do barely any damage; but often it feels like when i touch an enemy its basically doing half the damage of one of its actual attacks. its just super annoying, especially when some enemies have so much carry through with their moves they just like, land on you sometimes and stagger you, and then do a move you cant do anything about cause your staggering. It feels bad leaving a negative review on a game that a lot of people say is good; but i just dont see what you all see. Theres just too many things that i feel are constantly there that are kinda lame at best and garbage at worst.

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best metroidvania games ever made for sure most annoying issues are gone and youre left with great exploration and fun platforming that never really borders on the too hard or unfair feeling traps are not insta kills anymore eitherits a spanish chatolic nightmare fuel filled world in pixel art and the creativity with designs is insane combat is fast and fun with several weapons and comboes to do could maybe do with an option to turn up the difficulty a bit if you wanted to but at the end of the day its not too easy either it has several ways to customize your stats with rosary beads and figures with comboes that unlock special interactions as well and a lot of collectibles that reward you as you get more of them not just when you get em all so its worth the time the quests could have been a bit better but they are never really the focus and thats about the only gripe i have with it so overall amazing game 9,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed most of the game even though it was a bit more linear than the first game.(Maybe it felt more linear because of the markers) The bosses where the highlight of the game as I felt that the fights themselves were a massive improvement compared to bosses from the original game as all of the fights felt very clean with little to no cheap moves. Only issue was with the penultimate fight where the boss had two phases one which was very easy and the second being a massive jump in difficulty. Both of these fights I feel would be fine on their own but the combination of both of the fights made me feel like the fight as a whole lost a lot of quality because of this decision. I found that I had to get a lot of health upgrades which I did not previously need for previous fights as I felt i could learn the patterns quite fast with the other fights since you could always jump into the action and the boss would not change up a lot. When it came to learning the penultimate fight it became a cause of frustration because to get to the second part of the fight I would have to wait 1 minutes and 30 seconds just to be killed in like 10 seconds. It's not that the boss is unfair but it can be quite annoying to try to learn it since the fight is so long. The rest of the bosses were absolutely amazing and I thoroughly enjoyed the rest of them. Really happy with the inclusion of a double jump and air dash as it made movement feel a lot better than the first game and the diverse weapon choices was a great decision. I personally started with fencing swords but then transitioned into the normal sword later on as it felt the best to use in my opinion. Overall I would give this game an 8.5/10 I'm sure the developers may add further updates to the game that will increase the quality which may make some of my complaints obsolete but so be it. I would highly recommend this game for people wanting to get into the metriodvania genre as I feel as though it is a game that is easy to pick up compared to something like hollow knight where it is a little less linear.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell, nearly everything in this game has improved from the original, with the exception that there are two endings. But there's a DLC coming, and I played the original + DLC.The graphics are slightly better, still pixel art, still beautiful sprites. Beautiful music, and really great ideas for level design.In Cvstodia, one gets constantly in awe. Each 5-15 minutes, I found a new area, a new impressive background, a new music theme. The density of content of the game is as good or better than the first one.I saw two endings, as I did in Blasphemous 1, and it took me  give or take, basically the same amount of time as with Blasphemous 1. Only my Steam Deck counted the total time, as I have played this game mostly offline, during trips and flights and so on. Perfect game for a handheld, by the way.This game incorporates a bit more mechanics and a bit more sophisticated combat than the first one, and there are three particularly nasty mechanics borrowed from fighting games, that can be make or break for you:- Auto-combo: once the combo gets started, it cannot be stopped, so the enemy has plenty of time of kicking your ass. You better learn to avoid combos or time them really well.- Short jumps: they are possible, depending on how long you press the jump button. That's a blessing and a curse: in some cases, the developers force you to make short jumps as the only way to evade certain attack.- Stun: being hit stuns you and sends you back spinning a bit. A very lucky succession of enemy attacks can send you spinning into spinning into more spinning. You can be so unlucky as to die of one hit, without being able to press a button.How did reviewers see any of these mechanics as "too easy" or "easier than the original", is beyond my understanding. The actual % of players that got the achievements speak for themselves.I owe you an apology, Eviterno. I was not really familiar with your game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is packed to the brim with great content that both metroidvania and souls-like fans are going to enjoy, saw a review about this missing the mark and being nothing like the first game but i just don't see it.The lore is easier to understand than the first game but not worse in any manner; the world and the atmosphere, which in the first installment were already great, have greatly improved since; the combat and platforming are outstanding, with 3 weapons to choose from with all of them being viable and unique in their own right; and the customization for your character being perhaps my favorite feature about the game. The rosary now is used to gain defensive stats or various utilities, while the offensive capabilities are moved to 2 different mechanics, one of which is the weapon upgrade system which has been overhauled and has become way more varied and fun while the other is a brand new system in which you can swap different stat boosts and offensive abilities that go in pair to forge exceptionally strong and unique combinations to play around with.This game is seriously so much fun and a great improvement over the first, with my only real complaints being the fact that almost every enemy hit knocks you straight on your ass making a few areas just tedious to get through and the number of enemy types and execution animations being a bit on the low end, but other than that i can't bring myself to think anything negative about this game, it's a great buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been eyeballing the negative reviews ever since it came out and a lot of them mention some sort of degradation in its atmosphere and aesthetic. Im here to tell you thats generally not trueOne thing you first need to understand before playing Blasphemous is that its an artistic experience first and a game second. The first game was clunky, most combos unwieldy, build making nonexistent and cheese tactics rampant. The most striking part of blasphemous was its style. I dont think ive seen something so blatantly inspired by christianity or baroque. This remains true for Blasphemous 2, however most people dont seem to figure out we arent in a post apocalyptic desert land anymore. The issue with the cutscenes isnt their more livid and bright apparence in contrast to the dark and gritty tone of B1. No, the issue is that theyre clearly low quality. Some characters in these cutscenes move like we are in a western kids cartoons, as if theres an animator just dragging jpegs behind the scenes. Its genuinely poorly made. The style too is somewhat generic, which doesnt help its case. The issue here isnt the tone, its the execution of this new, non apocalyptic tone which is otherwise done amazingly in other parts of the game (the cities are full of npcs and sprites of people going about, you can pretty much find 2 or 3 guys living their lives in most areas).On the sprite work, its the same improvement we have seen from base game to Stir of Dawn. Everything is golden, smooth, skeletal and gorgeous. Though where B1 was more somber, B2 is very bright and livid, as I said. I think a good way to put it is B1 being Caravaggio and B2 Moreau.My only real complaint is the music, which so far is a shell of its former self. Im currently listening to the entire ost and theres no excuse: its just bad, its a dowgrade, hardcore artifical and souless. I dont know what happened to Carlos Viola but all these instruments sound straight out of a program (while as in B1 it sounded like you could just pick up a guitar and shred a saeta de altos balcones). Not a single one of them compares to al compás de tus contornos or baile de violetas. The entire ost feels like a remixed ten piedad. I dont think im biased towards the flamenco, because even the flamenco songs in B2 suck so far. (CHECK EDIT PLEASE)The executions, I did notice they standardized them to mostly a single animation, though larger enemies do get a custom one. I dont really mind but it is bittersweet, as I wouldnt even dream of asking so many animations for three different weapons.The gameplay feels much more fluid. Ive only tried the incense so far but even the heavy weapon is more maneuverable than Mea Culpa. I had my grips with relics in the previous game, as they were a worthless time consuming feature, so it was a pleasant surprise theyre part of the weapons now. You dont need all three to progress through the game it seems, but to unlock all collectibles, yeah, get ready to swamp weapons frequently. One thing I do appreciate is how balanced it seems so far. You dont need a fast weapon to absolutely style on a boss. Hell, even prayers are easier to use now with how much fervor is generated. Combos are now a real thing,Overall, even with my gripes with the cutscenes and specially the music, I could never bring myself to not recommend Blasphemous 2. Its the perfect 8/10, a more accessible version of B1 even.(EDIT) As I played more and more the music grew on me. The piano gives a more "civilized feel" to songs like Del Santo Nombre. While I still think a good part of the ost sounds like filler, songs like Corona de Siete Azahares are definitely at the top of blasphemous osts. I think my previous take was msguided by a few forgettable pieces which even B1 had, so Im retracting this take, the soundtrack is perfectly fine.Also, one thing I want to add, this game is insanely fun. Weapon swapping in the middle of a boss fight is insanely, INSANELY rewarding. Picture swapping between incense for reaching two enemies and barely pulling off your sword for a quick parry. I can see this game will have some crazy stylish boss battles, you can expect some youtuber gremlin to master it within a week or so

_childDocuments_.review: Read the full review on Gameffine:Tl;dr-Blasphemous 2 is the perfect sequel fans could ever ask for. The sequel doubles down on everything Blasphemous is beloved for, and then proceeds to add a slew of new features. The result is a beautifully rendered action platformer with challenging combat, varied character builds, rewarding exploration, a plethora of side content and some great music. I would have liked to see more epic screen-filling boss fights, some post-campaign modes and reasonable regional pricing, but I guess the last wish is not up to the developer. Team17, if you’re reading this, fix your prices. Blasphemous 2 is a gem of a game otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. They've retained, for the most part, what made the original game such a good one, although the tone seems not quite as dark and disturbing as the previous entry. Combat feels much better than in the previous one.However, the game has had sound issues for players for at least the past six months, causing areas to lose background music, and even in some extreme cases, enemy attack sounds. Unfortunately this sound bug seems to negatively affect some of the weapons, causing them to get queued and playing even if you get up from a knock-down. Needless to say, this makes the game far harder during these segments, as you can't count on sound cues.And despite the Steam forums saying the issue is under investigation, nothing seems to have happened for the last six months. It is solely due to these sound issues and the team's apparent lack of interest in fixing the problem, that I am not recommending this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is easily one of the best sequels I have played, and definitely one of the best Metroidvanias of the last few years. The Game Kitchen took all criticism that people had about the first game and then reworked most of those and fixed the problems. You have a clear goal and purpose from the beginning, the movement feels very smooth and responsive, the combat is engaging, the exploration and the world are interesting and easy to do due to a very good traveling system. Combining main weapons with exploration mechanics is nothing short of brilliant and refreshing for a genre that seems to repeat itself very often. The world is still dark, sad, and mysterious without being overly depressing. The music is fantastic and every track fits the areas in a very soothing way for the player, and the pixel art is simply breathtaking.Ultimately, I can only recommend this game to anyone interested in a good experience and a very well done video game. If you disliked the first game, you will really like this sequel, and if you (like me) also liked the first one, then you will probably fall in love with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun. Faster game play. Weapons and upgrade system is vast and easy to use. More Metroid than the last. This is going to be a hit, but I prefer the simpler weapon and game play in the first. I also prefer the atmosphere and music in the first, yet some levels with it's music in 2 are more jaw dropping and intense. I had to pause myself and stare at the screen to take it all in. The story isn't sucking me in. He returns to stop what was going to manifest after 1 was completed. It's a bit of an excuse to have The Penitent One return. The game is deep, but only after some time and upgrades. After playing at 56% on the map and getting the double jump, the game opened up enough to revisit areas and find loads and loads of stuff and connecting areas. The dash ability will render levels from annoying to suddenly easy. A win. Just don't like the "caged fights" while getting some items. Ugh! The cartoons too. Not my thing for this game. The artwork is beautiful enough not to use Saturday morning animation (looks like the Castlevania cartoon). I also find it very odd the penultimate boss is ridiculously stronger (took me 3 days until I learned I had a "time stop" prayer) and more difficult than the final boss (took me 20 minutes). I think that is the theme of the game, with the "dragon" being stronger. The ending was also a little abrupt. Great fun, but I might not come back to play the crap out of this like I did with Blasphemous.(edit) ...and the funny thing is that NOW I can't stop playing this on my more portable console. It's growing on me as the better of the two. Get the DLC because it will add a vast amount to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a great Metroidvania. I enjoyed the first Blasphemous, but if I were to rate it, I would give it a 7, due to the lack of progression and the 'clunkiness' of the gameplay in some sections. Blasphemous 2 is a solid 9. The developers have taken all the feedback to heart and improved their creation in every aspect, truly commendable. The gameplay is flawless, with a sense of progression that keeps you glued to the screen, and an even more inspired artistic style, with backtracking handled perfectly. I hope the sales have been great because I really want to play a Blasphemous 3!Some minor negatives I feel compelled to add (but very personal):a) Half of the bosses are challenging and exhilarating, while the other half are just frustrating.b) I love trying to complete all the Steam achievements, especially in a Metroidvania, but personally, I always prefer achievements that I can complete in a single run of the game and that I can still achieve after defeating the final boss. I hate having to Google what I need to do to avoid ending the game at 99% because of an achievement that I can't/won't get at this point (true story).

_childDocuments_.review: I truly wanted to enjoy this game. The first one is one of my favorites, right up there with the greats like Hollow Knight. This one felt like either a very big DLC or a fan-made game using ripped off assets from the first.PROS:1. Combat is still good. Better, some might argue. The Mea Culpa is back (kinda) and still functions generally the same, along with two new weapons. One's faster and weaker, the other slower and stronger. Different weapons for different playstyles and enemies. I can respect that. 2. Platforming just IS better, not arguably better. The abilities you get in the second half of the game are automatically equipped instead of having to waste a slot in your rosary knot. I think that's how it worked in the first game, it's been a few months, I can't remember exactly.3. The environments are beautiful, and the pixelated art style is still very good. It still adds to the shock of watching an enemy turn into a puddle after an execution.CONS:1. Like I said in the beginning, this feels like a rip-off of the first game, or just a very lazy DLC. The executions were one of the best parts of the first game, because every enemy had a unique one. In this one, the enemies returning from the first game kept their execution animation and most (if not all) of the new enemies have a generic execution. It feels so lazy.2. The cutscenes. if you want to call them that, are completely unnecessary and out of place. They're jarringly HD in this pixelated game, don't serve any purpose besides showing you one thing that's different, and don't last any more than 5 seconds apiece. Compared to the style fitting cutscene in the first game where the Penitent One filled his helmet with blood and put it on, it just (again) feels so lazy.3. DS2 Scholar of the First Sin levels of mobs. They're EVERYWHERE all the time, and you're constantly having to dodge 2 or 3 attacks simultaneously. Not difficult in and of itself, but it makes attacks impossible to get in without taking 1/4th of your health.4. The bosses. This one is my biggest gripe. The bosses in the first game were AMAZING. Stunning to look at, just difficult enough, perfect ratio of "react accordingly" to "maybe memorize this attack pattern". Almost every boss in this one feels like you NEED to learn the attack pattern and you NEED to do it perfectly every time. I'm currently fighting the last boss, I'll update this when I beat it if that's possible. The final boss has 2 phases that I've seen so far (if there's a third, I won't do it), and they're both just some human sized dude, I'd honestly mistake him for a mob enemy if he didn't have named health bar. The first phase has 3 different attacks and they aren't bad to dodge. The second phase also has 3 (unless you count his string of attacks as separate, then he has 5), and every single one of them does at least half of my health bar EDIT: I just hadn't gotten past the halfway point in his second phase. ♥♥♥♥ this boss END EDIT. Even if I had more health, which I'm sure I missed at least one or two somewhere, they'd do at least a third. He puts them together so fast I can only get 2 swings in before I have to dodge and let him run his course. And he's a damage sponge like you wouldn't believe.And this isn't the only boss I've felt this way about. The salt conflagrant or whatever the Hell his name was feels exactly the same, and he just straight up summons mob spawns to annoy you during the fight. Svsona spent the entire fight flying, except when she would come to the ground and 2 shot you if you were too close. None of these fights feel well balanced and the victories never feel well earned. It's never "That was tough, but I'm glad I persevered" like in other souls games. It's always "that was unnecessarily difficult for no reason and I'm glad it's done just so I don't have to do it again."I truly want to love this game. If I'm missing something or doing something wrong, please let me know. As it stands though, this is one of the only games I would not recommend to people. If you liked the first one and are considering getting this one, please use this as a word of caution.FINAL EDIT (hopefully): So the boss I was talking about ended up not being the final boss, jokes on me. I changed up my play style and he was a little easier, maybe that was the play from the beginning. I still can't recommend it, which hurts me so much. I truly wanted this to be amazing. I'll probably still go for the 100% all achievements in the future just because I hate myself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a sequel should look like to an already amazing first game.  Aside from the true ending Crisanta fight in the first game, the bosses and enemies are notably more difficult and intricate.  Still riddled with bugs, but not nearly as much/as badly as its predecessor.  Weapon variety made not only the combat so much more fulfilling, but also the way their attributes are utilizes in puzzles and secrets is sure to somehow give this game even more replay-ability than the first which I have poured 100 hours into.  The translation of only being able to use a few relics in the first game and now instead just having them as abilities, more unique skill trees for all weapons, the preference variety of combat strength provided by alterpieces- all of it helps to make this a great sequel.  Although the art and cutscenes were beautiful and higher quality and the story being solid- I do miss the pixel art from the first game and do think the story of the original was alot more in depth, interesting, sophisticated, and dark.  This game- while still having its fair share of violent/mature content- definitely also paled in comparison to the first game in terms of things like executions and the deeds of the miracle.  Overall great game, fantastic ending.  Probably one of the best metroidvanias of all time.  Also, please add a hard mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the first game for the first time about two weeks. The art design and music were immaculate, the combat was serviceable, but the insta-death platforming became an annoyance by the last 50% of the game that only grew worse due to the significant back-and-forth you had to do at that point. Couple this with the scarcity of checkpoints/teleport points and I found the last half of the game to be a significant slog. Ultimately, I felt the game was above average with plenty of room to improve itself. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did it improve in the sequel. Literally every issue I had in the first game was stamped out.  If I had to pick any negatives, they would probably be the following. Gone are the pixel art cut scenes which have now been replaced by a very simply stylized cartoon-like animation. Not only did I quite like the original pixel art, it is very jarring going from the highly detailed pixel art in-game to the cartoon counterpart. Very apparent during the final boss which looks absolutely incredible during his fight but very simple in the subsequent cutscene. Not the end of the world, however. Some of the later end bosses felt a little too overtuned to my taste. Windows for retaliation and parrying were pretty small for the high damage they deal. It wasn't insurmountable, but there were definitely moments where I was going “come on”. And, I would have loved the little Castlevania-like bestiary. Maybe a little lore blurb to a given enemy, number of times we've fought it, where they are located, weaknesses and strengths, etc. Would have been a wonderful little extra touch. Again, not the end of the world.I gave the first game a 7/10, which I thought was appropriate as it was an above average game. This game is an easy 10/10 if one ignores my little nitpicks – no lower than a 9 otherwise. Easily the best indie metroidvania out at this time. Based on the good ending of this game, the chances of a sequel are a little lower than expected unless they focus on a different penitent. However, after this, my focus will definitely be at attention for anything The Game Kitchen decides to do next.Playing this gave me the same ecstatic joy I'd get playing the modern castlevania games, which are some of my favorite games. It is great to know that that the metroidvania aesthetic still lives on in the indie space as Konami is doing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with it.  As with the prior game, highly recommend playing with the Spanish audio.

_childDocuments_.review: Newcomers to the series will probably love it, and Blasphemous 1 (B1) fans may like it a bit less. The common B1 fan perspective that the game is a bit casualized rings true for me.Combat: certainly improved coming from B1. Combat feels good, though the hitstun and knockback can feel dumb at times as you're bounced around. In general the combat is engaging enough. Problem is battles with normal enemies is pretty meh, and the game doesn't throw you into many situations where there's a lot going on, and there aren't unique sparsely-used enemies to keep it exciting. This is part of what made enemies in Symphony of the Night (SotN) so fun - the random crazy monster you only see once or a couple times in the whole castle. Most bosses are pretty fun, but there aren't enough and they're too easy. SotN also had more areas with tons of different enemies colliding and creating interesting clusters of action.Upgrades/metroidvania progression: There are endless NPCs you need to revist after you find x item, so you can get improved gear, health and etc. Cool, and almost required in games like this, but mostly they aren't exciting. There are a few fun spells to play with, but otherwise no improvements are exciting. Most of them are like "10% more damage", or "spells cost less". Again unlike SotN, none of them are exciting especially as you scan over the insane array of fun weapons items and spells to be found in SotN.Difficulty: Way easier than I expected. I may have to revisit B1 to be sure, but this game is easy. Only 1 boss in the whole game gave me trouble. Another boss took me a few tries. All the rest took 1-2 or so. This made me sad because in memory blasphemous 1 was much harsher and I actually had to try. In this, equipped properly, sometimes you can even just tank hits without thinking about it. If you're what I could consider an average gamer, it will probably be only slightly harder than described above.Aesthetic and cutscenes: This is where B1 fans are upset including myself. The art style has completely changed for B2 compared to B1, at least in the cutscenes. They now lack the raw brutish grit of the first game. Instead everything's sort of heavenly and angelic. The artist isn't doing a bad job, but I agree that the new style completely clashes with the gameplay's aesthetic and takes away from what really sold B1. These new cutscenes remove me from the grim world I was hoping for.Writing: The writing is similar enough, but maybe too extreme in its dialect. Maybe it's just my own crappy brain, but the writing is just unnecessarily difficult to read. Much of the time it takes several readings of a sentence to even know what they were trying to say because it's over-the-top wordy. Basically it seems like they should be writing poetry... not characters discussing something that may not be grand at all. Far too grandiose for my tastes and just makes the story annoying to follow sometimes. I like what they're doing but it goes too far to the point of being tiresome to translate.In general I'm a little disappointed because after being in awe of B1 I was expecting a masterpiece. The game is definitely pretty good, but I guess I was expecting too much.  Still, don't get me wrong, I had lots of fun playing. I just was hoping for a more faithful sequel. I haven't found a metroidvania as good as B2 in a long time and this is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have decided to change me initial review after having played and completed the game with both endings. I will leave the original review--of which was rated negative--below this review for anyone interested, as I do feel some of those criticisms are present. I think Blasphemous 2 is an absolutely wonderful game, as long as you don't compare it to its predecessor, the original Blasphemous. Blasphemous 2 keeps a lot of the original's elements, such as the metroidvania style of gameplay and the art design and direction, but loses a lot of other core components of the first game. Instead of following a linear upgrade path like the original, you stay at a relatively equal power level from start to finish, only unlocking minor damage boosts through allocating resources to get minor upgrades on weapons and using trinkets to empower specific tools more than others, which makes for a unique system where the starting enemies can be just as dangerous as they were when you first met them, even at the end of the game. On the discussion of weapons, there are 3 of them, each with a unique playstyle. However, I feel that in an attempt to make all weapons equally viable, they make windows for attack easy for even the heaviest weapon, resulting in a system that doesn't make the player rely on the different weapons available to them. I literally never used the rapier & dagger because I found its damage output inferior to the flail. Only on the second to last boss and one type of enemy did I ever even use the sword, and the spells in this game are also vastly superior to any melee weapon available, much like the first game. Upgrades to things like health and mana are relatively easy to find, requiring basic intuition and general exploration to find, with a couple items locked behind more difficult tasks and convoluted questlines, making them much more readily available than the first game, which I personally think is an improvement. Bile flasks are also notably less available in number, and are more coveted in the second game, which makes for a situation where the player is always persuaded to play more carefully with bosses and enemies, however Prie Dieus are much more numerous as a result. Areas do generally feel smaller and more easy to traverse, which is something I personally don't like, as the original game felt more large and daunting, but I could just be imagining things. Areas do tend to feel quite small and quick at times though. Traversal is easier as movement is generally improved from the first game, feeling more fluent and pleasant, and it is also more forgiving, with instant death obstacles like spikes now being completely nonlethal and only doing a small portion of the player's health. Movement upgrades are more linear and are simply added on as the game progresses, unlike the original where a lot of the movement items were locked behind exploration and sidequests, which I preferred more compared to the second game. It should also be noted that the art in this game is some of the best pixel art I've ever seen, and if it hasn't already won awards, it absolutely should with its beauty and depth. The cutscenes were good too, but I found them inferior to the first when portraying characters. When they show environments and scenery, the cutscenes were absolutely amazing to me though. Difficulty is a little controversial, but I found the game relatively easy to complete outside of a few examples. Bosses have consistent movesets with timings that can be quickly learned, making them feel fair, as they can be overcome with time and dedication. Some notable bosses for me included Orospina and Afilaor. I found the Odon fight at Sunken Cathedral to be outright unfair with how he spams his ability to spawn enemies, making the fight downright painful and unpleasant to do. Eviterno's second phase was difficult to learn and keep up with because of his sheer speed and sometimes hard to read patterns, but with enough time I did come to learn his behavior and moveset. I appreciate this game more now, but I do not feel like it is the kind of game I hoped it would be. It feels more like an attempt to mimic the first game while making itself more available to the general public, which I think was a poor move, as the majority of the audience is likely fans of the first game. It's an enjoyable and gun game, but I don't believe it should be held to an equal regard as the first unfortunately. I still recommend it to anybody interested, but don't come in with heavy-handed expectations for the sequel if you are a fan of the elements of the original. If you re interested in further information on my opinion, I highly recommend you read my previous review.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The following was my original review for the game:I will be honest, Blasphemous is one of, if not my favorite game of all time. I know my opinion differs from many others, and I don't think Blasphemous 2 is a bad game to any extent, but I just can't find myself enjoying it the same way I enjoyed the original. Blasphemous 2 feels 'off' in many ways compared to its predecessor. The new cinematics that are drawn in a smooth, clean, and almost cartoonish way are extremely different from the gritty, realistic pixel art cutscenes of the original game, which I feel gave the original a lot of flavor. The subtlety of Blasphemous' figures, lore, disturbing art, and religious portrayal feels like a miserable mockery of its former self, as if they were creating these--albeit impressive and amazing sprites--just for the sake of making weird designs. The same extends to the somewhat overly flamboyant dialogue, which feels complex for no viable reason other than to sound extravagant and mysterious--although that is just how I perceive it. Although, at least for the Spanish voice acting, which is what I played with, it was superb, however the dialogue remained convoluted. Another issue I felt was quite blatant was the apparent brevity of the areas within the game. Most of the areas feel dogpiled within the 2 and a half hours of the game I had played (I now have played around 6 and a half, and my opinion has not changed)--of which I feel I discovered around 7 of based off memory alone. The areas within Blasphemous 2 feel too short-lived to truly capture my attention and interest, as they passed so quickly, I could not fully enjoy their theming and enemies. On an unrelated note, if you are looking for the harsh, unforgiving, and extensive platforming that, I feel, helped the original game stand out a bit more, it is not as apparent in Blasphemous 2, and is much more lenient, with a greater focus on combat. It's a far different experience than the original Blasphemous, although it isn't necessarily a bad thing.Again, I'm a certain type of player, and I hold different values with this game than others. Don't let my comments dissuade you if you feel otherwise, and I encourage you to try this game for yourself if you truly want to, as it could be a positive and engaging experience if you don't emphasize what I've talked about in this review. I will likely continue to play the game, and i will update the review if I come to feel different about the game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to get a key for this game, and I went into this game having played the original Blasphemous about 2-3 months ago, so the experience from the first was fresh in my mind; a game with a fantastic presentation, but somewhat average gameplay. So how does Blasphemous II compare? Quite simply, the game improves upon Blasphemous's formula in almost every way. The game still maintains Blasphemous's strong presentation; the visuals, music, symbolism, and themes are all on point at all times. You still have gorgeous pixel art, intriguing if not disturbing character design, and a mysterious atmosphere with plenty of lore to uncover. But the most notable thing about Blasphemous II is the tremendous improvements to its gameplay formula. I had described Blasphemous's combat as being "slow", "clumsy", "lacking oomph", and having a "stop-and-go" pace, but absolutely none of that is true of Blasphemous II. The combat gives you so many more options right from the start; having your choice of three different weapons, one emphasizing speed, one emphasizing power, and one emphasizing balance, allows you to approach the game with different strategies rather than being locked into one style like with Blasphemous, which also aids replayability. But you're also not barred from getting the other weapons, and you can instantaneously switch weapons mid-combat, so as the game progresses, so too does the amount of ways you can approach combat. Each weapon having a distinct skill tree lets you further expand each weapon's options in combat, and they have no shortage of flair with numerous weapon skills for high damage or areas of effect. And I can safely say, with all of the tools available to you.. the combat flows so much better, in a continuous rhythm of offense and dodging. Everything still has a feeling of weight behind it and feels very methodical, but it all feels just a bit quicker, more refined, and less clunky. But it's not just the combat that's much improved, as the platforming has seen a similar glow up. Old staples from the first game such as wall climbing and ledge grabbing are much quicker and more responsive, allowing your exploration to be at a much more satisfying pace. Not only that, but progression through the game affords you new tools to enhance your mobility and exploration options, not only for platforming but for combat as well. So not only is the pace of exploration more satisfying, but you have new ways to execute in ways you never could in the original Blasphemous. It's also worth noting that one of Blasphemous's most unforgiving elements, the dreaded spike pits, have been overhauled; no longer are they an insta-kill, but instead deal damage before placing you back on your last safe platform. So they remain an obstacle, but are no longer an unforgiving one. Now, let's talk bosses. Compared to Blasphemous, I admit that I found there was less visual diversity amongst bosses, as a significant number of bosses do tend to be humanoid bosses. But while they may not be as visually memorable as the Blasphemous bosses, who had far more bizarre appearances, they more than make up for it with much more mechanical depth. I criticized the Blasphemous bosses for being either too simple or too RNG-dependent, but all of the bosses in Blasphemous II felt much more balanced. They stand out for mechanics that are designed to test your evasion and ability to react on the fly. I honestly don't think there was any boss in Blasphemous II that I outright hated; every boss felt fair and balanced, and had a consistent level of quality. The game does still have some small gripes, such enemies sitting on top of you and damaging you multiple times in quick succession, and some backtracking due to the size of the map (which does have some workarounds as you progress through the game). But none of it takes away from the gameplay experience as a whole, as I found myself enjoying the game from start to finish, something I can't necessarily say was always true of Blasphemous. Blasphemous II is a shining example of how to do a sequel; it preserves everything that was great about the original, while improving on the original's weaknesses. As someone who had a somewhat lukewarm reception to Blasphemous, Blasphemous II was an absolute joy to experience. I'd put it right up there as one of the greats for any lover of Metroidvanias. It is absolutely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent metroidvania. Compared to the first one, the platforming is MUCH better, the story is more coherent, and the new visual assets and mobs are less inventive and well-drawn. It also stops being an actual metroidvania after the first part, with new areas unlocking in the order you need to beat them for plot reasons. All in all, it's both a very decent and beautiful game that successfully explored the ideas of the first part — and a soulless sequel that may be a labor of love (I can't read the developers' minds), but sure as hell doesn't feel like one.Which makes  hard to evaluate.You don't need to play the first game to understand the second. The grim Catholic setting where God became twisted and bestowed inexplicable horrors on humans that they're supposed to accept with gratitude is good and fits a souls-like metroidvania well. The mechanic of not actually losing souls is odd — you might as well do, it makes the game a bit easier where it really didn't need to be. The exploration is fine, and it does feel like a giant adventure at first. I expecially loved the dark chariot that can carry you to otherwise inaccessible parts of the map — you really feel like you've stumbled upon a secret when you do.I liked how QoL upgrades like travelling between bonfires are locked behind collectibles, and some areas (looking at you, Sacred Entombments) were sheer fun to explore.The fights are also fun. You now have three weapons to choose from, each with its own gimmicks — and each also serving as a way of traversal. That makes your original weapon choice influence the routes you can take, which is an interesting idea, and sometimes it makes sense to switch (and learn) different weapons for different enemies.In other words, the core of the game is all right.But the scope gives the impression of a bit of a cash grab — it's not impressive. Way too many enemies are just recolored versions of each other. Very open in the beginning, the game becomes almost linear in the latter half (and by "half" I do mean half — only the first three bosses can be finished in any order), and it's very clear it struggled for more content. There are too few bosses, none of them secret. Same as the first game — but, unlike its predecessor, in  most bosses are just... humanoids. Decently fun gameplay-wise, but very uninventive visually and in terms of story.Same with some mobs. It's hard to put a finger on what is tasteful and what isn't — but the gentle yet horrifying art direction of the first game is just , everything is simpler and more on the nose.And it's just... blindingly obvious how much worse the new pixel art is compared to the first game. Some mobs and bosses (like Afilaor) look like they're from a different game entirely, with no detail, bright contours and plain colors. The same can be said for the animated movies — they help with the story, but the style is so mundane. still holds together due to reusing a lot of assets from the first game — which is fine. I just with the new additions were of the same quality. But they're not — and thus we are left with this odd sequel: decent, fun, and soulless. It fits my tastes, so I enjoyed it, and since spikes no longer insta-kill, there was no unnecessary frustration.But it doesn't have the spark of the original. And that's a shame.
