_childDocuments_.review: Caveat Blasphemous cultor!The game is nice and some rough edges of the predecessor have been smoothed out, but in my opinion in parts it lacks exactly this rich and melancholic atmosphere Blasphemous 1 (B1) was bleeding out of its every pore. There are of course rich moments of immersion to this game and the first meeting with the Procession of Shadows is still sending shivers down my spine because of this fantastic mixture of visuals, text, music and voice overs. But these moments are rare and that is a shame in my eyes, for it is not for the lack of great content. There are lots of interesting "boss" enemies you meet on your journey through this game that would have deserved some kind of story or introduction. In B1 I remember being excited to finally confront Our Lady of the Charred Visage after getting to know all the hints about her past and her cruel fate. Here it just seemed the first three bosses were kind of introduced whilst the following five or six weren't worthy of even a short speech or an announcement. Instead of tending carefully to a delicate story as it was done in B1, it seems the focus has been shifted to weapon styles and cage fights. Latter ones already annoyed me in the first game. The split to three different weapons wasn't my kind of thing, either. Maybe because in my opinion it wasn't really adding to the game since there were a lot of special attacks in the first game already and the forced on rapid switching in the end wasn't really fun in my eyes. Last of all I have to say, that the cutscenes with their plain, straight comic-esque style are just sad and to me were an unwelcome interruption. In B1 they were wonderful scenes, also made of pixels and pixels and I greatly enjoyed them as an addition to the game's storytelling. The in-game art here is wonderful btw. in B2 and it is worth playing for the visuals alone. I would have loved a wallpaper pack of some sorts with the backgrounds of this beatiful game. I'd even pay for it. All in all I have to say, that Blasphemous is without a doubt very beautiful in itself but shallow compared to the predecessor storywise.

_childDocuments_.review: From style to substance, Blasphemous 2 is an all-around top-notch metroidvania. The game's difficulty overall hits a satisfying level of challenge. The theatrical boss fights provoke intense duels where dodging well-telegraphed attacks becomes more rewarding as you practice. (That complement does not extend to the disgrace that is the final boss.) Blasphemous 2 also provides a lot of freedom with playstyles as well as opportunities to offset the difficulty via brief bits of backtracking. Whenever I felt I needed a break from a boss, I had options for restrategizing or at least other corners to inspect.Blasphemous 2's richly grotesque pixel art conveys a depraved world that's as beautiful as it is vile. Exploring each of these elaborately crafted environments was a huge motivator for exploration. The next-level sprite animation bring all the hideous creatures to life and gives your attacks tactile impact.The insta-swappable trio of weapons with (mostly) unique movesets cleverly enables great depth accessible at the press of a button. Instead of only touching a single weapon, I found myself using each of them relatively equally as I continued to play and learn the weaknesses of enemies and bosses. Other systems like the slew of magic attacks and variety of offensive/defensive charms also bring more options to the table and are an enticing reward for exploration.While I failed to engage with the story in the slightest, the religious horror that seeps from every crack of this shattered world doesn't need a concise form to convey the greater tone of its apocalyptic events. It's not the best style of storytelling if there's a point you want to actually get to, but it's weirdly perfect if your goal is to make the player feel like an outsider trapped inside a mad dream.For both its visceral presentation and the engaging layout of its world, Blasphemous 2 has got to belong up there in the pantheon of the highest-quality metroidvanias. As a sequel, it makes great technical/visual advancements to an already head-turning style. The game also streamlines many aspects of the original’s gameplay and it heavily upgrades the diversity of combat. Blasphemous 2, with a couple of boss-related barriers, was a consistent source of immersion. Traversing new areas always put me into that lovely state of methodical exploration. The combat and platforming made me feel in control of how I interacted with the world. Blasphemous 2 knows how to grasp your attention and it's a must for anyone deep into the world of the metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: When talking about games there are few things that I love more than being proven wrong. I love totally underestimating a game and later have it kick my ass and make me eat my terrible insidious words. One could even say that I have been Blasphemous towards this series HEHE.~ Estimated reading time 5-6 mins ~I am of course referring to my review of the first game. I gave it a pretty bad and short review. I didn't give it a chance honestly. The thing just didn’t click with me but after experiencing a masterpiece like the second one, I am really glad I gave it a chance - and I thought poor little old me just wasn’t into metroidvanias. In reality, maybe I just needed to be exposed to a masterpiece to understand. An utter piece of art. I played Momodora: Reverie of the Moonlight just before this and it definitely lit a fire for metroidvanias. Blasphemous II made that fire explode into a barrage of difficult, but enjoyable bosses, and a Jackson Pollock of dark fantasy and Spanish religiosity.I really came into this game with a strange soup of expectations. I do really have a resistance for these types of games, and I had sort of given up on them. However, it’s always difficult to turn the other cheek to people giving a game so much praise. Especially when the game has a mix of some themes and genres I love. The first thing that I accepted when starting the game was that understanding the the story at this moment was a pointless endeavor, a mere trifling matter. Having skipped most of the first one (pls forgive me), I begun my journey almost completely in it for the gameplay. I was already sort of familiar with many aspects of the game and I had enjoyed a plethora of lengthy video essays going over some of its themes. So, my mind was made up.The game wastes absolutely no time to hit you with its great visuals and vibe. The intro screen has some great movement to it and even the color palette instills weird feelings in you. You immediately understand what the game is about. You feel the hopelessness and the angst of a world that is decaying more and more. It’s very darksouls in its vibe, but it feels like a breath of fresh air in many ways. Like most great art, it critiques ideas or even whole sections of society and in this instance I feel like its critique is geared more towards the Spanish brand of Catholisism (which is also manifested by showcasing beautiful spanish inspired compositions and which some are honestly 10/10 songs). I am sure that there are tons of people who could talk for hours about the innerworkings of what the game is critiquing with more knowledge and poise than me about this lol, so I think I’ll just mention that its critique exists.Once the game figuratively splashes some Cvstodia (name of the game’s world) water on your face, it drops you into its world and promptly gives you the option to gain one of three weapons. A heavy one, a light one and a balanced one. Loving the big-bonk-ooga-booga character builds, I had to go with the heavy hitting one (huge mace-like spiky ball with chain). They all have lovely latin sounding names and are upgradeable (like most things on this game) - and in a very dark souls fashion the game almost immediately throws a boss at you! The battle is definitely winnable on the first try and honestly it’s a fantastic fight. The boss is aggressive and hits hard, but the openings are very big, allowing you to hit hard back. The movement is very fluid and nuanced and the overall mechanics do not betray the player. It was love at first sight.Very shortly after installing the a couple of ball hits on the boss’s skull(lovely sentence I know), the world opens up and starts giving you choices. You can decide where to go and what to do and for me this was a very surprising experience. I was never used to this much player freedom in a metroidvania, but I was excited (albeit a little overwhelmed already). There are weird NPCs to talk to, Prie-Dieus (this game’s bonfires) to discover and STUFF to upgrade. The first town, a world hub of sorts, is located very near to the first boss - “City of the Blessed Name” - name enveloped in mysticism and man, do the NPCs live up to its name. I was definitely not ready to experience the best voice acting in any game ever. This should be the new gold standard for weird souls-like games. The voices in the game always display a regal tone, but always shady in nature and the words themselves are exquisitely selected. It’s as if the devs took special care into the world building via dialogue. Whether it’s a humble wood sculptor, a floating hand (of which there are atleast a couple) or a huge three meter tall apparition of sorts, they all seem like they received very loving care in their design.As you start advancing the game and upgrading your stuff, the difficulty starts ramping up. However, it always felt very natural and very well paced (this could have been due to the specific choices I made to progress as well since there is player choice in where to go). You start obtaining spells and key items that you’re not really sure what they do, but thankfully this is a game that rewards experimentation and exploration. There are many hidden places and items everywhere - and it was just that specific choice to follow all the alternate routes where I started to realize how expertly interconnected the world is! I am aware that this may be something that’s even a feature of metroidvanias, but as someone just getting into them, it felt amazing that the game respected the player's time so much. Backtracking was never something I loved doing, but here it’s something that’s very fun and very rewarding to do. There are always more collectibles to get and more upgrades to unlock - and the best thing is that collectibles almost always end up affecting gameplay. Again, the game really respects your time.I felt like the designs of bosses and enemies were insanely good (both in visual and gameplay-wise), although none were extremely challenging to defeat. Out of the 11 (12 depending on who you ask) unique bosses in the game, only about 3 gave me a really hard time and maybe only one made me wanna rip my hair out a bit - and that’s really good! I wish the ratio for difficult bosses in souls-like games was more like this. Once you understand the nuances of the movement and really get into the upgrade system, the whole thing becomes a toughish, but very enjoyable experience. Having said that I don't think I can articulate well enough why these type of games are so special and so appealing to me. They just are.This is a very special game that does many very well and doesn’t have much if at all objectively wrong with it. Aside from the expected frustration of difficult games, the overall experience was almost therapeutic at times. I know I speak for many when I say that souls-like games are very meaningful and very satisfying to play, and this game definitely falls into that category. If you are like me and are not into metroidvanias, I urge you to reconsider them! I believe that you’d be doing yourself a disservice if you skip this game (or the first one) based solely on that. Please don’t be like me.Excitedly, I’d love to give this game a 4.5 brilliant golden hearts out of 5 💛💛💛💛P.S. thanks game for not punishing me if I die and for letting me have 6000 map markers all at once

_childDocuments_.review: I want MORE Blasphemous! In reality, it's a good game, BUT nowhere near as good as the first Blasphemous. Here are some pro and cons.Blasphemous 1:PROS:- Atmospheric world building that connects. Every place you go to seems to tell a story and flows from one to the other. It's dark, moody and you can feel the story seeping through the background.- Violent. It's gory alright. The executions are Mortal Kombat level and are chunky and fun. Even when you are not killing things, everything from enemies to NPCS to backgrounds are violent and gross. Love it. A stark contrast to the Christian imagery and themes.  - Story is awesome. A bit hard to follow but with a little item description reading, everything works out to tell a story rife with guilt, strife, pain and glory. - Animations. Man, the animations are super. From your character sheathing his sword to Boss's simply breathing. Everything is pixel porn. The cut scenes are done in this really janky, dark pixel art style that is so unique. The animators really took their time with making everyone have character. - Multiple endings and more re-playability. After I finished the campaign there was so much more to do, to my surprise. CONS:- It's hard. This game may take some practice. Boss battles are not for the faint of heart.- No customization in looks or weapon. One weapon only.- Something else maybe, but I can't think of it.Blasphemous 2PROS:- Combat is very fluid and responsive compared to the first game.- More weapon customization. - Graphics are better?CONS:- Barely any executions. Like maybe 4. Those gory executions made this game unique. Where did they all go?- Not very violent. Apart with some outliers, this game really toned down the violence. Did people complain and they toned it back? Not sure, but it's not very violent or dark or gritty.- Lack of atmosphere. All the areas and backgrounds are disconnected and do not flow with narrative. Kind of like a Dark Souls 2 situation. - NPC are bland with not personality. Animation has gotten worse with no personality.- Endings stink. They kind of leave you hanging with no real resolution. Also, nothing else to do after the game ends. - No real atmosphere.- Cinematic art style has changed to something softer. No bueno. Maybe the developers plan on fixing these issues later? Blasphemous 1 did release a bunch of DLC that made the game better so maybe that will happen. Again, I like this game, but the first Blasphemous is so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very good game, better than the original. I do have a few minor nitpicks though. One is that the game feels like it’s afraid to have to miss something, and you end up having to go to every area and fight every boss in the main game. There are no real secrets or optional stuff aside from collectibles/ side quests that involve collectibles. The game also becomes very linear in its second half. The bosses were fun but fairly easy (barring the second to last one) due to the expanded arsenal of abilities and weapons, and had really cool designs. While the game fixes the  janky movement of the first game, it still suffers from similar problems that the first game did in terms of combat. The enemies are very simple, and while fighting several at once in different combinations provides some fun combat, the extensive arsenal of tools you get with the more complex weapon system make it really easy to just delete enemies, since a lot of the spells and weapon abilities are very OP. the challenge of the enemies mostly came from if they either had high damage or the ability to stunlock you into a wall. The weapon system is really cool and all 3 weapons are really fun, but it’s very easy to become overpowered, which might be a problem if you are looking for a challenge. I recommend it if you like the first game, or want a decent metroidvania experience if you are a fan of the genre. Or if you just like the artstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying, as much as I didn't enjoy the first game's last 10-15%, I actually enjoyed 100% of this one (well, 97% to be exact).Good:- Combat is great and fluid. Most of the bosses are challenging enough- No death pits (only lose a portion of your health instead)- Level design and metroidvania progression is modern and a lot more instinctive than in the first game- Traversal is smooth and vastly improved (without spoiling anything, metroidvania traversal powers are a lot more in line with other modern entries in the metroidvania genre)- A lot of fast travel options which makes backtracking a lot easier in the long run- True ending locked behind collectables that you can find without a guide- The OST is, in my opinion, also better than the first game'sBad:- The art is fine, the game went for a more generic art style and lost a bit of the flair of the first game- The story is meh (told more directly than the first game, so I enjoyed it a bit more as I'm not a fan of Souls-like storytelling where you have to read all the subtext of items to make sense of 10% of the story/world)Overall, Blasphemous 2 feels like a modern metroidvania whereas the first Blasphemous felt like an experiment in the genre. I understand why people who loved the first game's flair and aesthetics would be disappointed with this one, but IMO it is overall a better designed and more enjoyable metroidvania game.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, really good 2D metroidvania/soulslike, improved sequel to the first game.However, there are a two glaring issues that almost made me thumb this down, all of them entirely avoidable and frankly baffling:The biggest issue is the boss design.Most bosses are laughably easy and can be beaten first try. In a game of this kind, that's just horrible.But a few bosses are very hard. Which is fine and welcome. Unfortunately, all bosses come with UNSKIPPABLE CUTSCENES. And with hard bosses, you'll see them again, and again, and again, and... it will drive you utterly insane.Just make them skippable after the first time, like all other games of this kind do!The other issue is that in some areas, altars (this game's "bonfires") are spread out extremely wide and so for some tougher areas or bosses you'll have to backtrack significantly.Elden Ring had "checkpoints" in front of most bosses for a reason, a hint this game should have taken.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first; still very good.  Tips I wish I knew going in: Finding 6 of the 9 hidden sisters unlocks fast travel at every bonfire. High priority.Talk to the green girl as soon as you see her every time, and agree to have her help. If you leave the screen before talking to her or say no at any point, you fail her quest. You can still get the item rewards from her quest a different way, but c'mon. "Guilt" is complex now even though it looks the same as the first game. You do NOT recover all guilt when you corpse run. You always accumulate a small % even after you recover. Higher guilt not only eats your magic bar, but also increases enemy damage AND currency drop amounts. Removing guilt with the guilt npc is a questline. I don't like this because it makes repeat boss attempts annoying, but better to know what it's doing than not.You can create synergy effects by combining certain idols in a window. This will create a little symbol between both idols.

_childDocuments_.review: I was heavily anticipating , and I was not let down.  is a fantastic Metroidvania that improves on its predecessor in essentially every way. The new weapons allow for different combat styles, which helps keep the game fresh, but also provide you with new traversal abilities that you'll need to master if you plan on clearing the map and finding everything. The platforming is also much improved from the previous game, and becomes a strength here.I love all the new features they added as well. There are many more ways to customize your build, buff your weapons, or beef up your defenses for a particular fight. I love the music, which is often eerie and atmospheric, but changes tempo in the flow of battle creating intense scenarios. As with the first, the boss fights were my favorite part of the game, they're thrilling and a great test of your abilities. Personally, I found the difficulty to spike and dip kinda randomly. The penultimate boss was very challenging, but I beat the final boss, and the three bosses prior to the penultimate boss all on the first try. Meanwhile, one of the early game bosses was pretty difficult, and most of them took at least a few attempts. Although, that could just be me getting into the flow of the game, I'd love to hear about others experiences with it. My second favorite element was the exploration. Every time I unlocked a new ability, I immediately ventured across the map, stopping at every location I had marked that was now accessible. This was super enjoyable, and finding all the game's secrets unlocked some huge quality of life features that made everything far less time-consuming. My only real complaint is that blocking/counter attacking felt pretty useless and buggy. I found that about 50% of the time I blocked/counter attacked, the attack wouldn't do any damage to the enemy, or I'd end up inside of the enemy's body and get chain hit for a large portion of my health. I highly recommend dodging instead as it's a far more viable strategy.Overall, I'm really pleased with , they improved upon everything I had issue with in the original, and did even more ultimately creating one of the best Metroidvania's on Steam, and certainly the best I've played this year (probably the best I've played since ).I'd say more, but my playtime speaks for itself; I can't remember the last time I bought a game on day 1, and essentially beat it within 24 hours (honestly might be the first time I've ever done this). I highly recommend .

_childDocuments_.review: As a Gen X gamer returning to the Metroidvania genre since Symphony of the Night in the 90's, I found Blasphemous 2 reminiscent and thoroughly enjoyable. Its accessibility struck a perfect balance, offering challenge without being overly difficult. The map marking feature was a lifesaver, aiding navigation significantly.The graphics were excellent, although a touch more color depth with native HDR support would have been appreciated—I relied on Windows AutoHDR. The music was great, though occasionally it stopped playing. Sound effects were impactful, especially on a home theater setup.Playing with an Xbox controller felt natural, and while I couldn't follow the story well, it didn't detract from my enjoyment. Perhaps playing the first game would have helped in that regard.After 40 hours, I achieved 97% completion and explored 99% of the map, experiencing both Ending A and B. I'm more than satisfied and eager to support the developers by purchasing the first game and any future releases in the series.Many thanks to the developers for crafting such an engaging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: For me this was a highly enjoyable experience, a good but slightly unbalanced metroidvania.Balance and difficultyThe exploration in this game as a metroidvania is great, but the normal enemies you face as you explore are very easy to deal with. The platforming is also very easy, there are very few even lightly challenging platforming sections. Overall this makes the exploration part of this game rather relaxing compared to other metroidvania games where the danger of death hangs over you quite often. For me this was a good level, since I enjoy the exploration in itself and dont mind that it is pretty easy. The bosses however are hard, a perfect level of challenge in my opinion, they get harder the farther you get and the second to last boss really took me a lot of tries to clear.Storytelling and questlinesThe setting and atmosphere is great, as well as the voicelines in the game. I don't care at all for the story in the game though and I don't understand it at all. Its very confusing, convoluted and uninteresting. Its like they made it confusing for the sake of being confusing. Sadly the same is true for the sidequests, there are a lot of items and characters in the game that you just don't know what to do with. There are basically no hints in the game about it either, what this means is if you want to clear a lot of the sidequest or do a true ending clear you need to follow a guide. Huge minus for me, I want a well balanced challenge that is possible for me to figure out without having to google, in that regard they failed.Overall its sits around a 7.5 score for me, as a metroidvania its a success (pure exploration happiness) and the bossfights are great but everything besides that is mediocre.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. Doesn't compare in artstyle to the first game. The Penitent One is downgraded, the weapon animations aren't as tight, the animated cutscenes don't have the pixel art infused punch of the first game. The executions aren't very creative in comparison to the first game. I would have liked additional executions for enemies brought back. Unique executions performed with button combinations.The soundtrack is nice. The NPCs are neat though they don't have the aura of dread that the first had.I have heard that the game gets better towards the middle and end. Blasphemous was good from the start. I do not have the time I used to have. Slim reasons to play this over replaying the first game and I say that after having 100 percented the first. I still look forward to DLC but I'm not getting my hopes up. Maybe I'll just go and play SOTN or Aria of Sorrow again.

_childDocuments_.review: Every quality that the first game had, the unsettling atmosphere, the eerie music, the disturbia, the shock value, the gory kill animations, the extremely morbid flavor text of every item?This game pretty much took all those good qualities and threw them out the window.I am extremely sad to say this, but B2 is a very very basic metroidvania shadow of its former self. Also, I was hoping for better more intricate combos and more complex enemies. The concepts of the weapons was really good, but their move sets executions are very....empty and bland. I will however give credit for the creativity of each weapon being their own unique "key" to unlocking specific roadblocks. But that was about as creative as it got. Most of the new enemies are meh. The majority of the special-kill animations are recycled and the ones that ARE unique have nowhere near the graphic level of gore the first game had, which is sad. Everything that made the 1st game awesome was basically not transferred over or amplified and it is a huge letdown after spending so many months looking forward to this sequel. I was hoping for a true sequel to Blasphemous. B2 was a massive let-down. My expectations were too high it seems.I really hope you guys make a 3rd game and I hope it has more of what made the 1st one so great. You still deserve credit for the 1st game being as awesome as it was. I hope that in a threequel you can redeem yourselves after this one. But I'm still happy that you guys made the first game, so thank you again for it.Also, I'm quite insulted at the fact that this was made to be played on PC and yet you released it without coding into the controls the ability to keybind buttons to the mouse? And I'm stuck using the U and O keys to navigate the menu? How awkward is that? Not comfortable or intuitive U.I at all. Shame on you.I was hoping this game would wow me as much or more than the 1st did. It did not. Not impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but the first was better (except for the insta kill spikes) IMO, if you haven't played the original get that one first. Art/music was great, new weapons were fun to use but I felt like I spent too big of a chunk of the game picking things up and then running them back to their respective NPC, as opposed to just playing the game. This one is also a lot easier than the original, cold be a pro or a con. some strange but not game breaking bugs are also in the mix. Great game and definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the 1, you'll love 2. It expands on almost everything from combat to exploration to QoL changes. There's some reused assets, and some of the environments are just more of the same, but hey, really not a big deal in a combat-based metroidvania. It's almost a perfect sequel.My biggest complaint with Blasphemous was the Jank. It was just a game that didn't feel fully polished; The art was more important than visual clarity, or certain enemies didn't feel fully tested, or hitboxes were off. A little jank is no big deal, though it would cause me to put the game down for a few days from frustration.What makes Blasphemous 2 almost a perfect sequel is that a lot of this jank is still here. Sometimes you'll parry an attack and end up inside the enemy, getting hit anyway. Sometimes you'll parry, but some other attack will hit you, or even the enemy you parryed will recover before you do. Some enemy attacks knock you around, some don't, but damage has nothing to do with it, so you might take half your health in one hit and keep running. There's i-frames, but only until you get back control, so in some encounters you can get stunlocked. One early boss creates massive flame pillars, and yet you can be half standing in them and take no damage.While I love this game, and the original, it rarely feels like I stop playing because I was done. More because I'll get one or two too many moments of jank and just lose my motivation to play

_childDocuments_.review: First half is outstanding, one of the best designed and assembled 'vanias I've ever played. Take the heavy hitter when you start, the other weapons are useless; other than that, everything delighted me. Beautiful art, immersive music, fascinating (if vague) story. Back half, after Odon, is an absurdly punishing nightmare of speedbumps designed to stretch out the gameplay. If you're the kind of person who never finishes games, grab this; the first 4-6 hours are wonderful and I adored them, so you'll have fond memories.When you hit Odon though, just give up. It's not worth eighty deaths just to see the back half of the game, which clearly got less testing - I ran into multiple egregious bugs, including one that I'm pretty sure killed Yerma despite me doing nothing to cause that. The bizarre Yerma fetch quest in question is also obvious padding - this character is clearly an 'easy mode,' so why is there a puzzle attached to 'easy mode' that you can silently fail, by doing something that isn't indicated in-game, killing the NPC? Huh?There's no story, no interesting themes after Odon, just pointless slog through poorly designed levels (there's at least one backtrack path you can open up that's literally useless; it's easier to just go the normal route) and eventually it dumps you into a miserable gauntlet they clearly made in one weekend of crunch and never playtested. It's full of spikes, new enemies that constantly teleport and two-shot you, pixel-perfect jumping puzzles, devil-may-cry locked-door monster arenas *with holes in the floor you can get knocked into,* and zero saves. If you make the tiniest mistake you do it all over from scratch.Seriously, everything after Odon is tangibly designed to prevent reviewers from calling this "wonderful, if short." They preferred "huge letdown and still pretty short" I guess. Is there a GOTY award for "worst disappointment"? If so, it gets my stamp of approval.

Combat is solid.I did run in to several bugs like audio glitching or some animations not working especially on the mace weapon or getting hit when I shouldn't have. I also really hate that some boss dialogue or intros are unskippable especially when they are talking for 20 seconds.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning pixel art metroidvania with relatively smooth gameplay, a large world, great music, great lore, and a plethora of different kinds of enemies, items, item upgrades, and side quests to come across; however, occasional difficulty makes this game most likely inaccessible for casual players.The visuals of the game are stunning; there are many different kinds of areas with great-looking environments and characters, and the pixel art animation too is high quality. Background music is great and fits locations and boss battles. The audio effects too are punchy, and all the dialogues have quality voice acting.The game has a pretty OK character progression system; you unlock new abilities in a quite satisfying manner. You will eventually get three different weapons with upgrade trees to max out, as well as magic spells. The game also has a stat-modifying item system. There is also a nice fast travel system, and later in the game you get even more options for fast travel, which is a nice bonus for completionists.Gameplay is focused on platforming and brawling. Level design feels a bit like playing a Shantae game. There are platforming skill sequences and ambushes, and the levels are never too messy or labyrinthine. On the other hand, difficulty can be off-putting for a casual player. If you would like to simply enjoy the pixel art and story, platforming skill sequences may already be too much for a casual player, let alone the boss battles. Boss battle difficulty is probably easy for enthusiasts but too difficult for a casual player. Even after getting all the health and weapon upgrades, some boss battles can be on the tougher side, as most bosses have a large hitpoint pool and move and shoot a lot, while your health is depleted relatively quickly if you take hits. I wish there was a difficulty setting, I barely made it through the toughest bosses.The game has nice options for full-screen and scaled windowed modes, and game controller work without any issues. I had some issues with achievements unlocking, some boss battles glitched once or twice, and fast travel back to the city sometimes made the player invisible, resulting in a need to reload the save file. Negatives: there is no difficulty setting (how hard can it be to add such in 2024?), neither is there a new game plus mode, nor is there any kind of gallery to replay or practice bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it impossible to digest and review Blasphemous 2 without doing so in direct relation to the first Blasphemous game. I know that’s not necessarily fair to B2. I also know that you, dear reader, might not even care about the particulars of how B2 may or may not be better than B1. Nonetheless, though, it feels impossible to disentangle the second game from the first, so that’s how I’m going to break this review down.Buckle in, because this review is way longer than it should be. Don’t want to read all this nerd gobbledygook? I’ll spare you the trouble – Blasphemous 2 is fun; you should buy it! While it has its blemishes, it is, overall, a competent and enjoyable Metroidvania. If you want some in-depth criticisms, though, read on. -----------------------------------Let’s start with the good:The most immediate thing Blasphemous veterans will notice is that B2 offers an expanded arsenal of weapons. Unlike B1 (the weaponry of which is defined by the Penitent One’s lone weapon, the sword Mea Culpa), B2 offers players their choice of one of three weapons upon gaining control of the Penitent one, with the unselected two weapons being subsequently findable in the game world. Each weapon has its own feel in combat, as well as a unique skill tree and constellation of supporting items to further define its niche. In terms of buildcraft and combat variety, this relatively expansive arsenal offers a wealth of options for players to sink their teeth into throughout B2.To accompany the wealth of weapons is a new character progression system called the Altarpiece. The Altarpiece features up to 8 unlockable slots, grouped into four pairs of two, in which the player can slot in Figures for passive bonuses. The effects of these Figures vary drastically, from providing damage boosts to certain weapons or elemental damage types, to increasing potion efficacy or fervour (mana) generation, to offering enhancements to very specific mechanics of particular weapons. Matching two figures in one of the four slots also activates a Resonance (if the combination is eligible), which are synergistic additional effects that provide a boost related to the set that the figures are from or, in some instances, provide an entirely unique, build-defining ‘Special Resonance’. In totality, the Altarpiece provides character customization far deeper than anything available in B1, and, in tandem with the returning (albeit slightly simplified) rosary bead system, lend a deeper, more complex RPG feel to B2, which I think is very welcome.The other keystone change in design from B1 to B2 is that B2 is more of a “real” Metroidvania. In B1, there were a select few relics you could find to access new areas and secrets with various items and upgrades. However, these were few and far between, and, invariably, simply caused new platforms to spawn in certain locations, rather than granting the player new transversal abilities. They also didn’t particularly gate progress through the main story. In B2, that completely changes: genuine MV staples like double jumping, air dashing, and more provide that genuine MV feel, granting a sense of unfolding exploration and increasing freedom of movement. And, in a stroke of genius, each weapon in the Penitent One’s arsenal also acts an additional “key” in the MV sense, being associated with clearing certain obstacles or activating certain environmental objects, shaping how you navigate the world of Cvstodia. The increased MV bona fides are a welcome addition to B2, especially for the contingent of MV fans who felt that B1 wasn’t a “true” MV. Plus, it’s just fun to zoom around! Those are some of the key highlights. Let’s move onto the lowlights:It pains me to say this, but B2 simply does not capture the mystery or horror of B1. Part of that is unavoidable – B1 had the advantage of mystery and novelty simply by being the first entry in the series. It has the natural privilege of introducing Cvstodia and its lore first. However, the disappointing truth is that B1 was also gritter and more untamed than B2, brimming with personality in a way B2 isn’t. B1 was full of impossibly creative and disturbing tragedy at every turn, backed up by a shocking and gory visual style; the atmosphere was, and remains, unlike anything I’ve seen in any Metroidvania game. I will never forget Socorro’s questline, or the story of Our Lady of the Charred Visage – they are superbly imaginative and, beyond their mere shock value, offered genuinely haunting narratives that stand out in my mind as some of my favorite samples of discrete storytelling in any medium.In contrast, B2 feels toned down both narratively and visually, with fewer moments of both wonder and disgust. In B1, there are monsters roaming the world because of the horrors unleashed by the Miracle. In B2, there are monsters roaming the world because it’s a video game. There are flashes of the narrative brilliance of B2, such as Lesmes’ opening dialogue in his fight, but not one segment of the story is memorable in the same way that B1 is. An angel simply shows up and tells the player, “Hi, you’re the chosen one, please go fight these bosses so you can beat the game,” and you’re on your way. Quite honestly, it feels lazy, and the result is a very lacking sense of immersion. In B1, you felt like a lone warrior, small and relatively powerless, stumbling through a conflicted land on an unwitting quest to salvage what little remains of the grim world you find yourself thrust into. In B2, you’re simply a generic player character on a quest to beat the big baddies, lacking the gravitas and breadth of B1. This watered-down design permeates into aspects like boss design and zone aesthetic, the likes in which in B2 are, writ-large, less memorable than B1.My gripes extend beyond these atmosphere and narrative, though. There are genuine gameplay frustrations present, too. Contact damage is out of control, ping-ponging the player about with the slightest brush with an enemy pixel. Very often you will find yourself stunlocked in a corner, at the mercy of enemy AI to back off lest you find yourself respawning at the Prie Dieu momentarily. The expanded weapon arsenal is also extremely unbalanced, with the Veredicto, the censer weapon, offering nearly thrice (if not more) the range and AoE of the other two weapons. The progression path in B2 also becomes strictly linear after clearing the first three bosses – especially disappointing since freedom of progression and the ability to explore anywhere was a key strength of B1.At the end of the day, I cannot shake the feeling that Blasphemous is a better game, or at least a better EXPERIENCE, than Blasphemous 2. For as many strides forward that B2 makes – and it does take several important steps forward – it takes more steps backward. The best way I can describe the dynamic is that B1 was more than the sum of its parts. It was an evocative, special experience yet to be imitated by any other game. Conversely, B2 is the sum of its parts – not more, to less – but those parts are, generally speaking, pretty good, so the game remains fun and worthwhile. It’s also not entirely fair to compare B2 right now to B1 – B1 had plenty of problems on launch and enjoyed several years of postlaunch support to add content and polish. If B2 receives the same support (and I suspect it will), it will also improve as a game. However, B2 simply lacks the spark of B1 due to fundamental narrative and aesthetic choices, and I do not think B2 will ever capture the same magic of the first game.So, all of this being said, is Blasphemous 2 a good game? Yeah, I loved it! There are some moments of frustration and clunkiness here and there, but B2 is still a very fun game with good exploration and a unique, if watered down, visual style. If Game Kitchen is inclined to make a Blasphemous 3 that polishes the gameplay of B2 and captures the atmosphere of B1, we may see the best Blasphemous yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the first one was great. Boy, oh boy, did I know nothing! Once again, the atmosphere comes out of every pixel, the music is exceptional (that Orospina fight!!!), and the gameplay itself is enhanced with new mechanics - changeable weapons and altarpiece that create even more viable builds. My only complaint is that some of the side quests felt a little too short, but otherwise I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the original, the sequal has fabulous arts direction and great ambiance in general. The combats are fun, and the exploration is good enough. I still find the lore pretty confusing and the story quite mediocre, but overall, the gameplay is good enough to carry all. The biggest issue though is the unskippable cutscenes during final boss fight(s). They made zero sense in a game that requires so much grind, die and retry. So close to be a great game. Still recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just one sentence - Elevated Temple challenge room. A terrible game design in this one part ruins the game. I do not know whether and how the devs playtested this and what they had expected a player to feel, but this is just a plain bad game design in my opinion. More than that, I've been locked out of my ability to perform complex spells by constantly dying, and the system does not even allow you to restore the mana level to the minimum necessary for that - I have to travel all the way back to 'buy my guilt' back. Perfect way to ruin a game by a single badly designed location - have no motivation whatsoever to continue playing through this.The first game was perfectly balanced, challenging and enjoyable, and in the second one the devs suddenly decided to adopt the worst possible practices from the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Already like it better than the first one. Despite loving souls likes and metroidvanias, I kept getting bored with 1. The artstyle is immaculate to be sure, but I found the combat lacking and the one weapon to be pretty bland and not fun to use. Same for the level design and most enemies. The few bosses I fought were good tho. It seems the devs agreed because you immediately get to choose from 3 different weapons with drastically different approaches to combat. We now have direct access to charged strong attacks (tho still no basic combos afaik) and even a temp buff you can apply for one of the weapons. The pixel art is still amazing and refined, it also looks smoother overall possibly due to more frames of animation being added. Unfortunately, the guy who did the last game's amazing pixel art cutscenes left the studio apparently annnnd instead of using their profits to hire a new artist they....outsourced the job to an anime studio....okaaaay? I guess that's what I'd do too? Apparently, that was the one talented pixel artist they knew despite recent indie games being filled with pixel art that was on par with their cutscenes (Conscript and The Last Faith games to name a few). In short, the cutscenes look awful. It's jarring af to have these amazing in game pixel art characters and set pieces and then it cuts to a budget Saturday morning cartoon from the 70s during an animators artist strike (think the worst animated classic scooby doo episode you've ever seen). It's bad. There's no detail, and barley any shading, the style is drastically different from the last game AND the rest of this game. Like who tf signed off on this after they watched them? Did no one do QA there as the anime studio was creating them?? They look like anime, not Blasphemous and it's not even close. But that aside, it seems great and better than the first from a gameplay perspective so if you bounced off the first maybe try this one....or those other two games I mentioned. Tbh, the Last Faith and Conscript are being slept on hard with better gameplay and/or narrative but Blasphemous got all the internet clout due to its unique Spanish catholic weirdness (most of which is now gone anyway but whatever)
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry to write a bad review on this game but I was really disappointed from the experience.I'll start with the positive because it's really  a bad game. Firstly it is shown that the art and animation team worked a lot harder than the QA team (more later), because the visuals in this game is amazing and even above my expectations (which was high after the first game...). Secondly the world design and the metroidvania elements were great, the backtracking was fast and all in all the movement around the map wasn't tedious as many games make it, and the world was immersive and fun to explore.  Lastly the combat system felt good and was a nice upgrade to the last game with the weapon switching mechanic. Now, what made my experience negative was the bugs... I played this game almost half a year after lunch and I was shocked to see  still in the game. From player animations not playing to boss rooms without sound, rooms without music and even game breaking camera bug, where you can't see your player. All this and I even didn't tried to break the game, I don't know what the game testers were doing but its clearly shows that not enough. Another thing that I want to mention is the boss fights. In my opinion the bosses in this game, which I think is a big part of a metroidvania, weren't very fun... The music was meh and the flow of the fight was annoying in some and boring in other. Also they sometime make it extra annoying when there are unskippable cutscense in reentries to a boss room.All in all  it's just that my experience was negative. I wanted to share it because my expectations were high for this one, I really loved the first game and this studio in general.Looking forward for the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It captures the magic of Blasphemous whilst improving on almost all aspects.There are now three different weapons that can be swapped between at will. This adds so much more complexity to combat as well as having far more useful skill trees to accompany them. Each weapon can be used for unique puzzle mechanics throughout the world which breaks up the pace of combat nicely.The boss and enemy designs hold up just as well as the original game, and the platforming is far tighter and responsive. The story and ambience were not quite as good, but the game-play more than makes up for it.9 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Better music, gameplay, bosses and platforming. I enjoyed the story of the first one more. The art in the blasphemous 2 is exquisitely done. This is pixel art at it´s peak. I would have preferred the cutscenes to have also been done in pixel art like the first one. There were some bugs but with some patches and maybe some DLC down the line it will be fixed. The best change we got is that spikes no longer insta kill you and the alterpiece system. Game very good :)-=8.2/10=-
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The return of the Penitence was announced, and here we are again.Sequel obligated, things have both changed and stayed the same.The biggest highlight for me is the completely new weapon system, it makes mastering the combat harder because it is more complex with 3 whole different movesets and equipment types.But it's not too required either since as a whole the game is easier, especially with the flexibility in build crafting through icon synergy.While the game feels easier, that doesn't mean it is easy, and one boss(duo) made me really use different weapons during the battle.I wish it was more explored, but maybe it would've made the game way too hard in average, hopefully we get that as extra content updates! It terms of exploration, it's once again a huge improvement with no more painful inventory swapping of traversal abilities, most are inherent to the three weapons and we get extra movement options as a bonus!The start feels more open, but sadly the second act suffers from extreme linearity, I wonder if it was impossible to make it open and keep the balance.The areas had each their theming and feel, it was pleasant to wander around, especially with the better hazards that aren't instakill anymore.There is a stiffness in the combat and some moves which is familiar. Learning to tame the avatar is part of mastering the game.The death system is less punishing, but you'll frequently stay with a debuff for a while and best to clean it before bosses. I miss the more unique executions, they were great in 1, it felt a little something was missing here with most being generic.The menu UI controls suck, wish it was better configurable.The length is fairly equal to the first before all the post-game content updates, so hopefully we get more of those for prolonged value.Overall a very solid experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first metroidvania I have ever really played.  I dabbled in Metroid Dread before but didn't make it very far.  But I have to say, I truly enjoyed my time with Blasphemous 2.  The "weirdness" in the story and environments as well as the challenging but fair game play kept me engaged throughout.  I'm even thinking of trying another game in the genre now, maybe the first Blasphemous, Ori, or hell, maybe it's time to actually make a solid run at Dread.  :)Either way, if you have any interest at all in metroidvanias I really can't see how you can do much better than this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I played the original Blasphemous but this sequel, Blasphemous 2 is a solid game. : This time around, you have three different weapons with their own skill trees for different abilities. I really had a lot of fun trying out the different weapons and each one seems to work better for certain situations. I really enjoyed the Ruego al alba which has mystic abilities and a very strong parry. Overall, the combat gets more entertaining as you upgrade your weapon abilities and it feels fluid. You also have prayers and quick verses along with your weapon combat. : You have a very large map to explore the world, lots of secrets in the game, and it is easy to travel around for the most part. This one is a more linear gameplay with showing the next area for your objective but you can still explore other parts of the map and find secrets, upgrades, other content, etc. : To start off, a lot of the bosses are not too hard and the enemies are fair to fight against. There is a big difficulty spike right halfway through around the sunken cathedral area. I personally had to scout for a lot of weapon, health, rosary, and fervor upgrades. I did not feel like it was a chore to scout out these upgrades as it was enjoyable to traverse through other areas and secrets. A lot of the boss fights were fun to fight against and it did not feel like there was artificial difficulty in the design. There was always a counter that would work against a boss. A lot of people say the 2nd to final boss is too hard but he is one of the 2 final bosses, what do you expect? It took a lot of tries but when you learn his moves and learn how to parry him, he becomes much more bearable. Overall, the enemies and combat feel good and the boss design is fun. They do re-use some of similar enemies from the original Blasphemous earlier on in the gameplay which was a little lackluster. The bosses are interesting and fun to fight against but I feel the original Blasphemous had more captivating and better designed bosses. Also, the final boss for Blasphemous 2 is a little dull difficulty wise : The story felt pretty engaging and it was enjoyable for the most part. I feel a bit disappointed they went with the animation in the cut scenes which felt a bit duller instead of the pixel art from the original game. With the bosses, there are cut scenes which are not skippable which does make for an annoying time. I'm not sure what bugs are in the game but I did encounter one that would not let me get all the lullabies I picked up for a quest along with being locked out of certain achievements if you did not grab certain items for npcs. : Blasphemous 2 is a good sequel to the original Blasphemous. There are some improvements to Blasphemous 2 while also the original Blasphemous performed other parts of the game design a lot better. I would highly recommend playing the original Blasphemous and then playing this sequel if you want a good souls-metroidvania game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is fun, but truth be told, I'm a little disappointed in the sequel compared to the first game.  It lost some of the cool atmosphere and “WTF?” reaction-worthy moments that made the first Blasphemous such a treat to push through until the end.The bosses aren’t as cool looking (actually, they seem pretty uninspired this time around,) the enemies were reused too much in the game (recolored skins,) and the combat challenge rooms you get locked in were way too prevalent. The first game forced you to learn how to parry and attack.  This time I just brute-forced my way through and smashed everything with the mace since its range and damage was the best choice for everything.  Most importantly, there are barely any boobies in it this time around…  disappointing.  The waxy old man is not enough boob for us refined gamers.That said, I still played it until the end, which I wouldn’t do if I didn’t like the game.  Its fun, but as a sequel it feels like it comes up short.

_childDocuments_.review: blasphemous 2. metroidvania soulslike. i've played the first one till full achievements. this one too. let's dive in.good:- if you liked the first game, chances are you'll like this one too, it's more of the same thing with more qol- worldbuilding, voice-acting, art and music as per usual, some throwbacks to the first game are cute- rosary beads for defensive stats and altarpieces for offensive stats is so much better than trying to crunch both within 8 bead slots- new quick chant essentially allows you to have 2 prayers active at the same time, which is what i wanted from 1- i didn't know how much i wanted double jump and airdash for the penitent one... it feels glorious- some traversal mechanic attached to weapon you are currently holding is cute, but more on this later- achievement are a lot easier to get in a single playthrough (looking at you, crossing souls from 1)- second final boss spoiler bad:- it has been a very long while since i played 1, but 2 feels a lot faster to get through, maybe i'm just used to the dev's 'formula' at this point- the game feels like it's missing a lot of content. i feel like there should be a lot more questlines and secrets? more hidden rooms? i know most of the hidden rooms in 1 were just stat upgrade rooms so cutting those out in favor of having stat upgrades be actual key items does feel better.- i really didn't want to have to complain about this because i had the same issue in 1... but man, they are good at making ICONIC second final boss fights (crisanta my beloved), and then just... whimper out for the actual final boss. escribar eventually got fixed in 1 and became a fun fight but my point being, man this final boss.. yeah yikes bro, it's just very boring and almost an insult with how easy it is. - since some traversal abilities are attached to weapons, there are only 4 actual 'abilities' you can gain over the course of the game, and what do you mean i have to acquire wallgrab... did the penitent one just... forgot how to?- some of the mid game bosses are so easy that they feel unfinished, this might be a personal issue- the veredicto + timestop cheese is actually too strong, kinda nullifies the 'no hit' achievement when you can do it easily with the cheese, disappointing they somehow didn't see this coming lmaoknowing them, in a few months they will come out with a massive update that adds in more content and tweaks encounters, because they have done exactly that for 1. coming from play 1 recently though, it's a slight let down, but i'm chill, these guys can cook and i just need to wait for them to serve. a lot of people are saying this game is a cashgrab compared to 1, but honestly, this was what 1 looked like on launch, the reason why 1 was so great is because of the updates they made to it., which is the same score i gave when the first game first launched lmao, the updates in 1 eventually pushed it to a 9/10 for me so i expect the updates for 2 would change my score too.

_childDocuments_.review: To find peace is to be in your coffin as the sole and last penitent. To find peace, momentarily, is to lay down, and as the figure of the sinuous mists let those in dark cloth carry you away. Pray, penitent one, to find peace, momentarily, is to play Blasphemous 2This game is what sequels should be, I never felt like being in a new world that isn't the same Blasphemous world, the game said to me: "I am here, I never left you, and your penance is far from over". Yet, every time I entered an area, new or not, a feeling of awe, relief, or anxiety washes over me, the music and the visuals in this game are nothing short of mesmerizing, sad, sorrowful, twisted, and mysterious, for such is the world of the Miracle.Traversing and movement are so fun, you have your double jump, your dash, air dash, and other means of climbing, hanging, and the like to get to where you want to get. There are two ways of teleporting across the vast map, to get where you want to get. Some of the enemies are vicious, and some of the bosses... the music once again does a lot of heavy lifting that isn't a must but a most welcome addition to building up the hype around them, to let you know that this is your moment, where those so-called servants of the Miracle, where they come for you, where you go at them, for you have to defeat them, to get where you want to get.You have 3 weapons now, to smite those who are out to get you, with multiple magical abilities to aid you in destroying those who are out to get you. Yet, the world of the Miracle has friends as it has foes. Many devout believers and also sinners will be of company to you, company and camaraderie to assist you in besting those who are out to get you. The music, just like the first game, is a ray of light that pierces your ears straight to your very heart, to your very being. When you hear it... when you hear those very lightweight tunes of music touching your inner self, you know that you are playing Blasphemous. Still, the music never overdoes it. It knows when to halt when to let the world speak to you when to alleviate you, and when to bring you down.Sometimes, you have to stop and contemplate the world, the people, the faces, the signs, the sky and what it holds, the events that took place, the misery, the shame, the fears, and the joys.Never mind how harsh the world is! Shards of beauty, innocence, and hope lay around the world for the penitent one to come, welcoming him in their loving arms, for his journey, ever seemingly appearing to be his and his alone, it never is, for there might be one Miracle, but there are many penitents.

_childDocuments_.review: An honorable sequel to a masterpiece that is the first game. The platforming and movement are improved. There are more Quick Verses, but Rosary Beads are boring (mostly just resistance stats). There is a plethora of enemies and the bossfights are as cool as they were in the first game. The art style is breathtaking as expected. Locations are very interesting and very well designed, but some are kind of underused, for example Basilica of Absent Faces. When I thought I've seen it all, you still manage to surprise me. I am not that fond of three weapons mostly because they are significantly less interesting than Mea Culpa. Overall, good game. I hate pre-ordering games, but this is a rare occasion where I did and I do not regret it a bit. Cannot wait for the DLCs, especially the new game+ one.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 takes everything great about the original, and provides a breath of life with fresh ideas, quality of life changes, and other improvements. Highly recommend giving this a shot if you enjoy metroidvanias, souls-likes, or both (and even if you don't, I hate Dark Souls, but this game is amazing).Only one minor bug that I found (an animation sometimes didn't play when activating the Veredicto ability, so the character just stood still input locked, not like you would be able to move anyway even if the animation was playing).

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is perfectly serviceable its a huge disappointment from the first game. The game doesn't have the same charm as the first one did especially with the change in cut scene animation which clashes with the look of the game and makes it seem really cheesy. It also feels like the difficulty of the game has gone down drastically. Enemies are too easy to avoid and the environment isn't punishing enough. I was gutted when I fell on some spikes and saw you just lose a little health and spawn where you were last standing (previously was an instant death). Just overall the game feels like a downgrade from the original and if you are looking for the original but better you'll have to look elsewhere.Also they removed resolution selection so it doesnt work proper on ultrawides (this is fixed)Edit after almost 10 hours: My thoughts have pretty much not changed. I kept trying to give the game a chance but honestly it still just feels like a shell of the original. While the original gave off a very grave desolate feeling this one doesn't elicit any feeling. None of the bosses seem to be foreboding and the normal enemies never feel like a challenge waiting for me just an annoyance. As much as it sounds like a negative the clunk of the originals visuals plays much more into the atmosphere. In blasphemous 2 the entire game artistically is too polished and vibrant.As far as gameplay its fine but it very quickly gets trivialized once you unlock the double jump and dash ability as they allow you to cheese through every fight from then on making the already fairly easy bosses even easier. It feels like combat took a backseat in order to focus on how cool you can move around the map. The addition of movement abilities make the game also feel more linear as after the first 3 bosses there's only one way to progress. I still stand by instant death being removed as a fault since it feeds into the game being watered down in difficulty.All in all the game doesn't hit the same mark as the original and feels very forgettable. They reuse enemies like crazy and overall feeds to the blandness of each section. Never once did I feel like a challenge was too much and had to go fight something else this has likely been purposeful since after you get all 3 weapons the game becomes linear. I also generally just feel like it's lost the charm that made the original one of my favorite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 plays almost exactly like its predecessor; it's not a big leap, but it doesn't need to be because the basic pillars are already there. It builds on that with some small, welcome changes like three different weapon sets that are perfectly integrated into exploring and reaching new places. My favorite was the Rapier/Dagger Combo that slices through enemies lightning-fast, and they especially helped a lot during later boss fights, particularly with the parry and block mechanics.What particularly stands out for me is the grotesquely designed game world and characters. I also call it the black metal aesthetic. For example, there's an NPC who feeds a baby with wax through a breast he cut off from his wife who died after childbirth and sewed onto himself. This is his penance imposed by the Miracle, just like many others who suffer a similar absurd fate. Also, the sense of place is beautifully done. From a distance, you see a cathedral hanging upside down on a mountain, winding its way through a valley, and you can actually visit that cathedral. Or a basilica that has sunk into the sea, but through your actions, it becomes visitable again through a reflection, and this reflection also has a gameplay component.My biggest criticism is still the very monotonous soundtrack. While it thematically fits the Spanish-Christian-inspired setting well through its choice of instruments, it lacks punch and melodies. The only time I was musically pleasantly surprised was during a boss fight when, as the battle duration increased, the instruments became faster and more imposing. This is completely missing from the rest of the game.Ending A is really special and it's the perfect farewell to the Penitent One, and I got goosebumps during the last cutscene. The after-credits scene also heavily implies a DLC or even a sequel with a beloved character, and I'm all in for that. Well done, Game Kitchen!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a Blasphemous 1 fanatic I finished it through and through 4 times at 150% so here are my generic thoughts. These may or may not be positive it's up to you to decide if it's a pro or a con. The review may seem overly critical but you shouldn't be detracted from the fact that this is a good game that just missed the bar the older game made by 1 inch. I suggest waiting to get it at discount around 20-25$ USD.- Controls remain tight but move execution is too complex. I wish I could map Parry to a specific button or both types of prayers. I will have to fix this using Steam Input unfortunately.- Overly complex controls to accomodate XBOX style controllers. I have a 6 button controller and my 2 extra buttons are dead because its impossible to remap them. A lot of the in game flourishes youre allowed to perform with your weapons is just fluff and useless and never as good as just flailing your opponents to death.- Weapons offered are extremely unequal and imbalanced (Flail is best, Sword 2nd, Rapier dead last)- B1 had a specific path you followed and a clear goal, this one feels more freeform.- Game settings screen oversimplified (No resolution choice for example). Lacks depth.- Pixel cinematics replaced with cartoon FMVs, the quality of the cinematic is better but it detracts from the horror theme.- Severely toned down difficulty overall (Platforming the most, bosses also, teleport to town and around plentiful).- Soundtrack isn't worse quality, but the songs offered do not fit as well the theme of the world the first had. The best example is Mother of Mothers area. Overall the music is softer without tension and more ambiant.- Revisit of a lot of areas covered in the first game feels a bit lazy- Prayers are mostly just as useless as the first game and only there for eye candy if you get bored of flailing stuff- No wokeness in-game (We dodged a bullet there, Game Kitchen is severely woke)Play it and don't worry too much, but this isn't a clear step up from the previous one.EDIT: I'm so sorry I forgot to say this, just like my first review:"My great guilt"

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is an incredibly beautiful and atmospheric game. Frequently, I found myself just coming to a halt in an area and letting all of the atmosphere soak in. The backgrounds, each oozing character and style, the music, the subtle ambient sound effects... it all comes together to make a truly immersive experience, something which could finally fill the demon's souls ps3 edition shaped hole in my chest.And that is only the atmosphere - underneath is an incredibly fun combat system with more depth than the first instalment, fun bossfights and engaging puzzle platforming. Also, the amount of secrets and optional challenges to discover and master was very fun.Highly recommended to anyone who enjoyed the first game, souls fans and people who enjoy their games with a hefty dose of atmosphere!

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 1 remains one of my favorite games and I was excited to see what the Game Kitchen Delivered next.The sequel far exceeded the first and my expectations, by increasing the complexity and speed of combat and making the Platform and metroidvania elements FAR superior. The result is an engrossing, hard to put down experience that I blasted through in 3-4 sessions.The art work, as always makes the game as much a piece of art to be admired, as it is a fast paced combat heavy game. Astounding animations, bosses and environments mean this second journey to Custodia is even more exciting than the first. The music by Carlos is as stunning as always, and is one of the few game soundtracks I listen to while I'm working.What else is there to say? It's the iteration of an already amazing game. Better combat with more weapon options, and tying weapons to traversal options is absolutely genius. Cannot wait for future dlc

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would rate this game neutral.  If there wasn't already a precedent that was far superior (i.e. Blasphemous I), then I might go as far to rate this positively, but since we already know what the series is capable of, this game was a disappointment overall.  The gore and graphical elements, as well as the atmosphere were heavily watered down.  The three weapons added for some interesting dynamics, but found myself only using the mace in most situations.  The Marks of Martyrdom were kinda....not very interesting, and the weapon development felt almost irrelevant.  Lots of backtracking until you can find the warping between save points.  Bosses were far less inspired, and overall character development was lacking.  Overall, I felt this experience to be relatively hollow compared to the first one.  Last boss kinda sucked the big one too.  I beat the game, got both endings, but don't really ever see myself returning back to this one for any reason to be honest.  I'd give it a 6/10. Maybe would be worth it at $15-$20 bucks maximum, but nothing more than that.  Just kinda overall disappointed with the game.  Sure, it was playable.  Sure, it was a typical metroidvania in every sense of the term.  But was it notable enough to recommend.  Not really.  Play it if you must, but know that you're not going to get nearly the type of experience you would expect out of this kinda game, given the original was so fresh and tasty.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a game I kinda didnt expect to happen. I love Blasphemous 1, and was exited when this game was announced. Overall this game was satisfying, but left me wanting a little bit more.Overall I think that 2 is the strictly "better" game. The world design and the gameplay are straight upgrades from 1, and in a metroidvania those are some of the most important factors. The biggest change here is that there is three different weapons, which all play completely differently, and interact with the world in unique was in regards to puzzles/platforming. This game also included a custom marker system in the map which I personally think should be a requirement in every metroidvania.I can't help but feel as if something is missing however. To start, I think the traditional animation cutscenes are a massive step down from the cutscenes in the first game, all thought the in game pixel art is still fantastic. I can't exactly place my finger on it, but something in the spirit of 1 feels missing here. Nothing was as strikingly grotesque in this game in my opinion, and while the lore was still in depth and interesting, it felt slightly too detached from the first game.I did have some issues with bugs, from sound effects and music completely cutting out, to some soft locks here and there, but nothing to ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good game? No.Is this a bad game? Also no.What makes this game good? Well, the gameplay is solid, the pixel art is beautiful, and the soundtrack is very enjoyable. There's more metroidvania elements in Blasphemous 2 too, such as a wall jump and weapon abilities.What makes this game bad? The *story*, man. Everything that was great about the first game was just thrown out the window. This game starts off with an egregious mistake. Somehow... the Penitent One returned. This completely takes away from the gravity and satisfaction of the true ending of Blasphemous. When this game was first hinted, I was REALLY hoping you'd play as Crisanta. Her redemption in Blasphemous made her the obvious choice for the next protagonist. Nope. She dies in the opening scene. Wow. But maybe this won't be so bad... right? Nah, the world of Blasphemous 2 shares little to no resemblance to the intriguing and immersive world of Blasphemous. All the delightfully disturbing imagery of things such as trees and ash that was ubiquitous in Blasphemous are just... gone, the new weapons have no relevance to the plot like the Mea Culpa, the setting is nowhere near as interesting, and there are no meaningful side characters to interact with. The only consistent imagery I've seen in Blasphemous 2 is with hands, but giant hands aren't exactly disturbing like a humanoid goat skull tree monster.To put it in shorter terms, in Blasphemous, I really felt like I was experiencing an adventure in an immersive world. In Blasphemous 2, I'm just playing an action platformer with cool art.What a disappointment. This feels like a half-baked reboot rather than an actual sequel.
