_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the game and gotten both endings, I feel like I'm in a better position to explain my feelings about this game, so I've decided to update my review.I don't have much to say about the gameplay. But, though I would generally agree that it's better than the first, I do have a few complaints: The new weapons are a gimmick. There was only one boss fight in which I found myself switching between weapons. It would've been better to either force the player to use only one of the weapons throughout the game (thus locking them to a certain play style), or to have a singular weapon that we could equip different skills to. Alas, these weapons turned out to be little more than glorified relics. That's not all. Thanks to these things, blocking as a game mechanic, while still there, has become rather unintuitive to the point I almost never used it. Fortunately (unfortunately), outside of a few boss fights, you don't need to block either: enemies have been declawed and most of your battles consist of being swarmed by them rather than focusing on a few, dangerous ones. You'll spend most of your time dodging instead. Overall it feels like combat has been dumbed down, not improved.Art wise, aside from the most obvious issue, which is the cutscenes (they're done in a completely different style to the rest of the game, breaking the immersion), the style has been maintained. The quality, however, has not. The drop is most noticeable in some character sprites, but it also affects the environments, many of which are uninspired and far too bright for the context in which they are supposed to exist. But these things aren't deal breakers for me. Perhaps the most problematic aspect about the art is the fact that there are no execution animations for most enemies, and I'm not sure why. Hopefully it's something that will be fixed eventually, unless they are trying to make the game into a family-friendly experience, for whatever bizarre reason.Something that DLC and patches unfortunately can't fix, though, is the writing. It's superficial at best.I was intrigued by the lore and characters in the first game. Yes, I did die hundreds of times on those stupid spikes and pits, but because I wanted to see more of it, I pulled through, and it always felt rewarding. There's no such thing in Blasphemous 2.The characters are all hollow. They seem to be in a rush to prove just how many big words they know, all with no meaning attached to them. A lot of your time will be wasted by long, overly pompous, pointless sentences that add nothing to the story. This disease has unfortunately also spread to the item descriptions, through which you get to know much of the lore. I read every single one of them religiously in the first game -- here, I just gave up mid game.Some people complained about giving the game a negative review with just a couple hours of play time. Well, let me tell you: even a few minutes of playing is enough to notice how the atmosphere is just... gone. Cvstodia is no longer a dark, twisted place -- the religious themes are toned down, characters are unidimensional, and the plot is just ridiculous. Even the weapons seem to lack any reason to exist, they're just given to you without any explanation. There is no reason to be attached to them like there was with the Mea Culpa. I'm baffled that they resurrected the Penitent One just to make him battle the League of Penitents™. They spent more time giving them cool designs than writing their characters.On the first game, you had a reason to do what you were doing. Your will and that of the Miracle both coincided. Here, anyone could have taken your place.I'm not sure what's gone wrong with the game, since it doesn't seem like anyone left the team. The writing however, is atrocious, and I find it suspicious that no one is credited for it like in the first game. Who wrote this? And why has there been such a change in direction?This game feels like it was made by someone who doesn't understand what made the first one so great. It's a mockery of it, like bad fan fiction.It's extremely depressing to see how nearly every positive review of it never even mentions the writing. I thought that was the soul of Blasphemous... it never occurred to me that I was in the minority.All that aside, that isn't to say that Blasphemous 2 is a bad game, it isn't. And if I had never played the first game, I wouldn't have disliked it so much. But I did play it.Sure, Blasphemous 1 was a flawed experience, but even so, all of its elements worked together in harmony. It was a work of art.Blasphemous 2... is just a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a terrible letdown in every aspect but menu graphics and menu navigation! The atmosphere of wonder and horror is gone, the writing is atrocious (where the first one was outright poetry!), the story pales into  nothingness compared to the first one; Enemy variety is nonexistent: you'll see recolored and reskinned enemies in every area, the best part is the usage of old enemies from part one but all new enemies are boring and terribly animated because of this and of the almost identical ruin backgrounds, that you forget in a day, each location looks and feels the same, whereas in the first Blasphemous you mostly will remember some areas and encounters forever!Music builds no tension and falls flat.The difficulty is laughable - there is no engagement on any level. Compare any frame of the first to any frame of the second and you will notice the difference: this one will not highten your imagination or mesmerize you with it's incarnations of the miracle like the first one did - and even if this is story related, it is no excuse to use all this lazy animated enemies with their poor framecount and a story so far from intersting as they did. Another worst part are the bosses which are amazingly uninteresting: mostly terribly animated human characters straight out of a saturday morning cartoon but even more uninteresting and bland.The violence, nudity and blasphemy is toned down too, the finishing moves are replaced with a catch all thorn animation which is the same for most enemies and covers the execution. It feels like cencorship or cowardice towards the epic store.Then this game gives you 20 or more rooms where you are locked in and have to fight THE SAME spawning waves of enemies till you succeed or die instead of mid bosses or anything interesting and due to the new weapon options and combat you can buttonmash through these encounters which is a shame compared to the first Blasphemous where every encounter had a trick or hint or interaction or pattern to learn. This is just a hollow shell, a shadow of greatness - maybe alll planned with future DLC's in mind, to spread the content - it is a shame and you should not listen to good reviews of this, they are objectively wrong or blindsighted - when playing BP 1 I had to stop and take photos every 5 minutes to show them to friends - I did not make a single photo this time and when I showed part 2 there was no reaction but silence. wWen I presented part one there was awe and joy and interest on the face of the people I showed it. _childDocuments_.review: This is really hard to write and further proof that Valve desperately needs to let us have a middle point between yes and no. I *love* Blasphemous 1. I was beyond excited for Blasphemous 2. The problem is, the veneer falls off the game rather quickly. I'd only recommend getting this game if you REALLY love the first one. Here's why:-All of your movement abilities have been split up across 3 weapons for the sake of making the game more complicated. It leads to clumsy weapon switching during fights.-The combat is not great. Enemies are basically damage sponges and the Penitent One is make out of sugar glass. In Blasphemous 1, if I died I knew how I screwed up and I could adjust. In Blasphemous 2, the Penitent One is slow, clumsy and unresponsive while the game constantly throws you into locked rooms that spawn in mobs of enemies. More than once he's thrown out an attack when I have hit jump and he *constantly* doesn't dodge when prompted. It feels like a half attempt at a character action game for the enemies but a Soulslike for the Penitent One. Just mismatched.-Bugs. So many bugs. Enemies get knocked out of screen but still spam projectiles. If you try to set the heavy weapon on fire while standing still, you get frozen in place. Moving from location to location can cause the music to not start and it's just silent. The map will constantly show you in the wrong position. Then, again, incorrect inputs galore. Oh, and picking up an item and wanting to see what it does? You gotta wait. Why? No idea. Just wait.-I get that it's a 2D Soulslike, but... Dear lord, they need to explain mechanics better. You still have to fight back to reclaim your dead body, but if you've died enough times you still get punished for it. Huh? I thought I encountered a bug. I had no ideas I was supposed to upgrade my weapons in a tab in the pause menu after Blasphemous 1 had a shrine. I'm willing to put the weapons on me for not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in the menu, but c'mon...Ultimately, I've shut the game off in frustration more than a handful of times now compared to zero in the last game. I'll probably beat it, but I'm not sure how much I'm going to enjoy it. This game is definitely coasting on my love of the art style and atmosphere at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Other than maybe the art style of the cutscenes, atmosphere and some of the boss designs, Blasphemous 2 is a straight upgrade on Blasphemous 1. - The controls are muuuch better, the platforming is more satisfying and there are no more instadeath spikes. - The two new weapons weren't as good as the sword for combat in my experience, but they at least had a function with some of the platforming. - The bosses in Blasphemous 2 are good, some are great, the only reason I give the edge to B1's bosses is because they were a little more creative. Most of the bosses in B2 are humanoids so it was missing that bit of weird monster killing that B1 had.- Music is always a matter of taste and I enjoyed the music in B1, but I would say the music in this game is more memorable.- Some of the collecting gets frustrating and tedious at times. There are a few collectables in this game that take far too long to achieve. The game needs some kind of system unlocked at the end of the game to let a player know when they have found everything in a room, otherwise you can spend literal hours backtracking and checking every room in the game for a small collectable. - There are also a few collectables that just require grinding and that's no fun. Nobody wants to grind in a metroidvania. But overall I really enjoyed Blasphemous 2, when I saw the change in art style I was initially put off, but as I played it more I realised how much Blasphemous 2 improves on the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR of my review: Honestly a great game. More of Blasphemous with some more mechanics, polish and story/lore progression. If you are interested in seeing any negatives that might turn you off check the bottom.Now the longer version:Having played and enjoyed the first one quite a bit I was excited to play the sequel. I can honestly say I am quite happy with it.I got the game and in around 20 hours I managed to 100% and get all achievements. This is something I don't usually do unless I really enjoy the game or the achievements are very simple and easy to get. I would say playing completely blind I managed to get map exploration to around 90-93% and achievements to around 80% or so. Finished up with some assistance from guides.Blasphemous 2 is a sequel some people might not enjoy as much as I did. The game in my opinion has done a decent job implementing and polishing up new mechanics in combat and movement, however it remains familiar to the first game. In my case I would say I am happy with that, same way I was happy with Remnant 2. For both games I enjoyed the original game and having a sequel that polishes some rough edges and provides more of the same is exactly what I wanted.Majority of my playtime was on my first save, exploring the world, combat and secrets. Around 23 minutes are on my second save speedrunning to get the speedrun related achievement. For people interested in specific parts I would split this review in a few parts: Combat, Movement, Exploration, Music and Story,First of: CombatThe combat of Blasphemous 2 I would describe as similar to the original with some more options. You are presented with 3 weapons from the get go and picking any one of them only locks you out of the other 2 until you find them while exploring. After you find them switching them happens with a press of a button and is instant, there are no mid change combos but switching being instant lets you play with whatever you want whenever you want. I would say the 3 weapons they went with are a safe but decent approach. You have a heavy flail, quite good range, highest stun chance, lowest attack speed and trading a parry option for the ability to ignite the flail for more damage. The next weapon are dual wielded rapier and dagger/shorter blade. This is the fastest option you have, trading per hit damage for lightning fast attack speed, parry option only if you perfect parry so you don't get knocked back and near zero stun(I might have been able to proc a stun on an enemy once with these weapons). The last option is the middle ground, a one handed sword that plays the closest to the original game, medium damage, medium attack speed, medium stun chance, a normal and a perfect parry option. The sword is the balanced option of the game and the one I used the most as it felt very familiar to the first game.Up next: MovementThe movement was very responsive and enjoyable. There is a good mix of abilities you acquire directly for your character and movement involving some of your weapons. In combat movement usually utilizes the character movement options for bosses and both character and weapon mechanics for combat rooms. All and all a solid movement system.Next: ExplorationI would say the game has pretty good exploration. A metroidvania after all the world is filled with locations you can discover early and return later to access with new abilities. The world is also very well connected and traversal is quite fast combining character movement, weapon movement and unlockable both static teleport points and checkpoint to checkpoint teleportation if you progress the collectibles and NPC quests. Running around felt fast and with enough places to teleport to if needed helped with not feeling lost or bored having to traverse the game.Up next: MusicSome people would turn off music and play with either their own music or no music/sound at all. For me music can add a lot to games. I would honestly say the music in this game is amazing. A lot of the zones have superb music tracks that I would sometimes just sit and listen to as they are very enjoyable. The music is composed in such a great way that I listen to  it even outside the game. Quiet places have serene music compositions allowing you to stop and enjoy the locations and combat and boss encounters have quite dynamic and hype tracks. A great soundtrack all around.Lastly: StoryThe story picks up right after the first game, however it seems there is a significant time gap between the events unfolding as indicated by some places and characters. The storytelling is well distributed between cutscenes, dialogue and of course the staple of soulslike and souls inspired games item descriptions. If you only sit and watch the cutscenes and character dialogue you would still be able to get the general idea of the story. Item descriptions build more of the world and its events. As a lot of the game is still vague you can draw your own conclusions on events and engage with the community in lore crafting and deciphering the meaning of different parts of the game. I quite enjoyed the story and I am happy with it in its initial version. The first game did get DLCs that expanded more of the lore and perhaps the same would happen here. I am eager to see if there is more.The final part would be any negatives or nitpicks that might be important for some people:The only parts I would deem as negative or lacking for some people would be some of the things I find as fine.The familiar feel to the first game, some people like me would see this as getting more of the thing you already liked, but I know some people look towards sequels for new and improved aspects in every department of the game so this is a warning for anyone who is expecting a completely different game. This is still Blasphemous, it feels close to the first game and more of what made the original great, for some it just might be too close.Difficulty - I would say personally I was ok with the difficulty of the game, however I can recognize that the game does have some pretty big spikes at a few points and overall you don't have the situation of feeling like a god cutting down everything and being unstoppable, enemies in later zones scale with you and remain threatening and some bosses do require a fair bit of concentration to get down and figure out. I know some people enjoy starting off weak and becoming near godlike in the end. Here you have your upgrades and you access more and more options but it's far from becoming a walk in the part even with upgrades. The game remains demanding and respects its difficulty and its players.Bugs - I encountered only 2 bugs in my 20 hours, both of which I would call minor and not really hard to fix. Both bugs just needed me to exit to the menu and load in again, taking just a couple of seconds to do and returning me to the last checkpoint so not losing more than a minute or two of progress. First bug was me somehow falling out of the map during one of the bosses. I am not sure how I managed to do it as I never managed to replicate it after that on the same boss or any other boss. The second bug I encountered was my character despawning, I was able to somewhat move and attack as I still heard the noises for it but the camera would not move. This bug happened while I was teleporting and alt tabbed the game. It might have been a bug with the game loading in assets while going in and out of focus, however this bug also happened only once and I couldn't get it to happen again even after alt tabbing a lot while loading. All and all nothing major or game breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent follow-up to an awesome title, if I would have to put it in one sentence. But I will nerd out for a bit:For those expecting an equal or more challenge compared the first game, you guys might be slightly out of luck, as I think this is a step down in terms of Boss Difficulty. Take it from somebody who is bad at timing and probably have very slow reflexes -- this game is more forgiving. It won't be a breeze but I think it's easier to get the attack patterns down with this one. I'm not so sure of the quantity of boss fights but I think its a respectable amount considering the first game. Well that's about it for the things that I didn't like. Here are some of the things that I actually loved about the sequel:1. The inclusion of different weapons achieves a lot of things: (1) the selection of weapon varies the path you take on your journey, although pretty minor, (2) it introduces build variety unlike the first game, and (3) it adds the additional traversal challenge. On top of the usual movement upgrades, the three weapons layer in additional movement mechanics making exploration additionally challenging. It doesn't over-exaggerate on platforming challenge unlike the first game slapping on a DLC to repair a mirror. 2.  Speaking more on build variety, the altarpiece mechanic further provides ways to upgrade your preferred play style, including builds that reap off the Guilt System. 3. Quest design is more straight forward and there are few miss-able things unlike the first game. Luckily they aren't tide to any achievements. For trophy hunters going in blind, there is probably just one trophy that you might need a second run for -- too bad there isn't a new game plus yet. Quest design introduces some new mechanics but it also retains some of the familiar once such as Cherub Hunting, Combat Arenas, and such.4. Art and sound design remains superb, though I'm not exactly a fan of the cartoon animations the developers decided to go with here. I'm hoping that they add in those additional graphic upgrades that make the game even more retro.  Pretty excited for the DLC to drop, until then I will probably figure out a way to get that time trophy that I missed in my first run. This is a 9 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat till now. Multiple mechanics than the first game had, animations are really smooth this time around, many weapons and abilities to learn, and the graphics man... I can't wait to find more about the unravelled and grim yet goldish world of Blasphemous and find all the secrets that the characters hold. Get this one if you like pixel games with a grim world and dark characters, and an intriguing story. Probably one of the best metroidvania games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania all around and well worth the price of admission! Pros:-The OST is worth the purchase price alone.-Sprites and backgrounds are gorgeous, and art design really does feel unique. There is incredible detail.-Many memorable characters—looking at you Cesáreo.-Movement feels good.-Travelling is not arduous, and you have plenty of reasons to return to areas.-Hits feel right in terms of sound design, animation weight, and visceral timing.-Wide variety of playstyles possible thanks to weapon/prayer/alterpieces.-Compelling story that is as esoteric as the theme—not everyone's cup of tea though.-Plenty of secrets and easter eggs to find (for the explorers out there).Cons:-Boss difficulty is a bit inconsistent—some are surprisingly easy others are steel walls that require being more finicky with builds and playstyle.-Some of the cutscenes and lead-up animations cannot be skipped for some bosses; and, this is annoying when having to do multiple attempts to beat a boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 1 is a weird little game. Is it a metroidvania? Of course. But... It's not got a great emphasis on upgrades, exploration is usually just health and it's clunky and has some jagged sharp edges. But a fantastic first effort imo.Blasphemous 2 is like the devs said 'ok guys, we learned literally every lesson, let's make an amazing sequel'. And they have.Combat? Fluid. It has a small issue or two (I don't like not being able to dodge with the flail if I'm attacking because it's damage does not make up for this)  but past that, having THREE weapons that all play wildly different, and their own skill tree AND unique ability for each... Plus something abilities wise for exploration which I'll get into later... It's good stuff.The npcs, the art, the music? As good as the original. Which is to say absolutely brutal and amazing. From wax filled towers to vistas of a huge lake with candle lit city behind it... From lady's who's faces are stone and matrichical skeletons. To brides in coffins and priest slugs breathing fire... It's great.The exploration? They learned SO much from the previous game. Not only is there a new thing to do on each map screen (or close to. A lot but not overwhelming) WITH your map letting you drop 8+ symbol types on most any square... You're constantly thinking 'oh hey I see a *thing I wanna do* and I can't reach/dodge/fly' up there. I better take a note of that' and the rewards for exploration are, 80%, amazing. Sure you'll get currency or upgrade points but most of the time it's good, important stuff. Items for quests, statutes for massive buffs, prayer beads for passive but substantial buffs... Or, and this is always my favorite, a brand new npc being tortured by the miracle in some gruesome way. Oh and each weapon has its own progression ability. From mirrors that teleport you to bells that reveal hidden platforms and fleshy wooden barriers (wood? Wax? Idk. It bleeds though...) each weapon has a unique ability. So replayability and even which path you take depends on the player. I could start with the sword and end up in the palace. Or I could start with the flail and end up in the sand tombs.... Or even way up in the sky, but not higher than the upper city, unseen but waiting for you to lower it) Overall, it's scratched the metroidvania itch in a way I forgot I needed. This is what I hope more metroidvanias do; refine refine refine. Uniqueness is fun, yeah. Having a weird movement ability or a wacky combat system is great... But if you don't have unique ideas? That's fine. Just make your systems really good. I don't care if I just unlock a double jump and a 'see the hidden platforms ability' in more games... Just make it so it's FUN using the abilities and exploring and combat. Make it good or make it unique.I wouldn't call blasphemous 2 unique. I'd say it's a lot of staple metroidvania abilities and such. But that's not a bad thing. It's a fantastic game and barring the final section being bad (which I'm just about at, I suspect) it's truly one of the greats of 2023, and it's been an INSANE year.Oh. Well. There are some cons. Mainly in a few bugs and a few enemy types stun locking you which is annoying. So... Not 10/10, but few games can be. 9/10, highly recommended for metroidvania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Easier than Blasphemous 1, mostly due to pits/traps no longer causing instant death.I think the combat and QoL stuff is almost universally better. The exploration is perhaps a little worse because the relics are no longer as unique or interesting as they were in B1. Overall still a fun game if you like metroidvanias, I am optimistic it will be as good as the 1st after a few rounds of updates/free DLC similar to the original's post-release development.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This review is being made on LAUNCH DAY VERSION. My comments, critiques, and praises may change down the line.Gamplay: 8/10. Feels more fluid than the first, feels more dynamic and free. The weapon variety is a very warm welcome that I really love. Only real issue I will proclaim is that certain enemies can stun lock you from full to dead, and practically all of them can do that if you are touching a wall due to how jank the collision damage is right now, but past that I am loving it so far.Music: 9/10. You definitely get the Blasphemous music vibe from the first. Different enough to enjoy the music differently, but similar enough to make it stand out among other games. It has it's own soundtrack theme that is hard to find work anywhere else and it's a pleasant experience.Graphics: 10/10. I have said it before to my friends with Blasphemous 1 that it is the golden standard for pixel art and animations in games, and they took that for this game and just gave that statement more evidence to support it. I've seen some people complain of the new art style for the cutscences being more of a catoon-y style rather than pixel, but I actually support this choice since the animation looks far better in this than their cutscenes in one. (SPOILERS FOR BLAS 1) The biggest point I have for this is in Blasphemous 1 how you have a cutscene killing the High Wills and the animation in pixel just looks...not good. So while others complain, I find the style change for the cutscenes welcome.Difficulty: 8/10. This is probably subject the change through time, but I find the game to have a good balance of difficulty, even if there are a few outliers of being a pushover or being a borderline nightmare. Not really much else to say other than it feels find so far and feels like a Blasphemous game.Bugs: I have found very very few bugs or glitches, but the few I found where not welcome. The one I found that was the most annoying and consistent is that if you are in hallway encounter and die, there is a 40-50% chance of not being able to recover your guilt fragment since it never drops one. This will be edited accordingly though.Overall: I recommend this game. I still would suggest waiting roughly 2 weeks or so just so that they can iron out the tiny wrinkles, bugs, and maybe balance changes. The only thing I pray they change is the contact damage issues of being infinite stunlocked if you are against a wall and not being able to save yourself. Outside of that, it's a great game that will be worth it when the patch iron is all hung up and finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable game! I did not enjoy the first game that much, not saying it was bad, it was ok. But Blasphemous 2 seems amazing. I'm glad you have more than one weapon and the combos and abilities are really well thought of. I just unlocked my 2nd weapon, only 4 hours into the game and I don't feel bored at all. The level designs are amazing (as were in the first one too), the enemies are great and finally the penitent one feels amazing too. Not too OP, and the enemies are not too OP either. So far, the game hasn't felt it was being unfair to me and its good to see devs working hard on making a game that is challenging but fair. That is not easy to achieve, so far I've only faced one boss, Orospina Lady Embroiderer and I think I died maybe twice or thrice against her before I memorized the pattern. All in all, the game feels amazing, and I can't wait to unlock more powerful combos and spells as I progress in the game! Definitely one of the best indie games this year. I play tested the last faith (it was only a demo) and well it was quite bland and boring to be honest. So, once again hats off to the devs for making a very engaging and fun to play metroidvania game!

_childDocuments_.review: As an ardent fan of the first game, there is something special missing from the opening hours of Blasphemous 2; something captivating and personal that made you want to see through your journey from start to finish almost immediately upon awakening as The Penitent One. In B2, you're resurrected for reasons, and with little fanfare, undoing the gravitas of the true ending of the original and undercutting the significance of the destruction of the Mea Culpa, your weapon from Blasphemous 1. In return, you get to hunt down three mediocre replacement weapons which serve a dual purpose in traversing the world, signaling more of an emphasis on platforming than combat. Narratively, the story is supposed to take place 1000 years after the first game, yet starting areas are full of several enemies lifted from it, with the same palettes and movesets. After about four hours it all just starts feels like more of the same. I think I'll wait for the inevitable DLC and final updates before jumping back into this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is similar to the first in being a Metroidvania but improves upon the last in almost every way. One of the complaints I had in the original was the upgrades not changing the movement or having minimal use and while sure it made it so you didn't need any to beat the game i prefer the sequel's approach, In which you can choose between 3 weapons a lightweight middleweight and heavyweight weapon. BUT each has more then just a unique move set they also act as a upgrade to solve puzzles and locked areas. for example the dual fencers weapon allows you to teleport in the direction a mirror statue is facing which make the upgrades more then the areas they lock like the air dash is multi-purposed, as movement and exploring. And once you made your choice of weapon the other 2 are scattered about to find later. one minor issue with this is depending on which weapon you chose decides which area you go 1st, 2nd and 3rd giving the game too much linearity. and not just the opening act as well! After all weapons have been obtained you still aren't given much agency as to explore you have a set path to go until the end of the game (similar like Metroid fusion). which while the level design hasn't changed to drastically between both i still think that is one of the leg ups the first has over 2.Man blasphemous 2 really isn't beating the ''easy boss'' allegations huh? yeah i hoped they'd be better and to give credit they are (they do more damage) Plus i died to them more. but i think it comes down to the easy boss patterns not truly utilizing the potential (hopefully if there is post launch content it will be improved). i do think the areas are amazing to explore with the immaculate pixel art they really outdid themselves plus the music is even better. the music is Blasphemous 1 was nothing like i had heard before in feel, but each track did kinda blend together in my head i couldn't tell you which music was from what area. Blasphemous two has a more varied soundtrack all the while not sounding out of place.In my original review I didn't touch on the story of the game (the lore is confusing) but comparing the two i would definitely say blasphemous is in a whole other ballpark with the Miracle and high wills story left me blown away with a plot I'd never seen before. with the High wills controlling the Miracle punishing people for doing good and the people wish for suffering. and the second is basically just the first but worse is every way with the miracle (free from the high wills) still making people suffer without a good reason. in blasphemous one seeing all the weird and quite frankly grotesque ways they change. and in 2 since most people don't believe in the Miracle after 1000 years it showing up feels random and that's because it is. The reason for is because some kid wanted the golden clouds to have a beating heart and now that heart has the son of the Miracle.  Not to mention the confraternity of the salt is pretty bland as well. Now for miscellaneous rapid fire points that didn't fit anywhere else. The wall climb is much better. Same with collectibles (the alter pieces and martyrdom marks). The economy is almost perfectly scaled except for the martyrdom points needed you will always be around 15 -20 needed before the game is over because the amount you can get from chests is not the full amount to unlock everything (they can also be gotten by grinding). the rosary beads just copy and pasted with a resistance of little, medium, and large for every damage type. they made hidden walls easier because you will hear whispers when there is one nearby but those are only for the sisters. It's dumb how one and I mean one of the cherubs is in a hidden wall none of the others are. when i played (it could be fixed when you read this) i sometimes got a bug where the music wouldn't play for an area or boss luckily it only happened twice. areas have more creative gimmicks. the weapons have skill trees. the enemies are not stun locked as much.I feel overall this game is better is most respects but I can't help but feel like something was lost along the way. As standalone game it also holds up well. But in spite of this i can't help but feel i had a more memorable time (not necessarily more fun) with blasphemous 1 mainly because I had no idea what to expect going in but as much as I try to be objective I can't deny my judgement is clouded still even so my final verdict is 9.1 Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> Superior in almost every aspect from the first title; faster, more enjoyable to play, with a more varied world to explore, and skills & abilities that make more sense. All of what while being the brutal souls-like metroidvania you're expecting. -----------------------------------------Dear lord, I actually completed the game from start to finish in a single session. So much to recap but let's see.Blasphemous II is finally here, the sequel to the brutal souls-like metroidvania inspired by games of the genre, the Spanish Easter Week culture and many other art references that culminated into a dark, crude world where the designs of The Miracle are above all and everyone. This sequel follows the events of the first game (probably centuries later, maybe even more) and you take control of The Penitent, who silently journeys into a world still ruled by the sacred words and inevitable punishments.This game is basically superior on everything from the first title. So many lessons were learnt, and it shows. I will try to mention the most relevant ones for both newcomers and people who played the first game:- Visually, the game is equally stunning. While we say goodbye to pixel art cutscenes, the new ones are also very good and there are more of them. As for the rest of the game, expect many more varied areas, much more easily identifiable. For some people it might come as a handicap, though, as the game is a bit less dark that the previous game.- The soundtrack is super good too. It still catches on going along with the environment while having that Spanish touch into it. I can see myself burning the OST on Spotify in the following days.- Gameplay is where the game has seen the most changes, for the better. Blasphemous 1, while great to play, felt like Dark Souls 1 in terms of being heavy, stiff and slow. This sequel fixes every of that and offers you a much more fluid gameplay, with many more combat options, as well as easy-to-understand build systems while also keeping the mysterious aura on every item you collect. You can choose between 3 different weapons at the beginning of the journey, which will only matter temporally as you will unlock the rest while progressing through it. Everything just feels faster in the way that it makes sense.- Length of the game is very similar to B1. It took me around 11h to complete, with 98% map exploration. I am very experienced with the genre so I believe the average should be 14h or so, which is completely fine for a metroidvania.- Boss fights are, like in the first game, very good. Patterns are easy to recognize, and fights are fast and satisfying. While the new combat variety might make the game easier, it will still provide a decent amount of challenge.- Exploration is better than in B1, in the sense that it is clear what skill you might be missing in order to reach certain places, and there are also even sound clues in order to find secret paths. You won't escape the classic fake walls though, so there's a high chance you'll keep mashing lots of them.- Spike pits no longer instakill!! Screw that on metroidvanias.Overall, there is a reason why I beated the game in a single session. I just couldn't get enough of it. Every new area, every new NPC I interacted with, every new upcoming boss fight or sidequest, I just had to know where that led to. This is an amazingly faith sequel, with many lessons learnt from a game that was already excellent. Grab this without any fear because this penitence has been great once again.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a very solid sequel to the original game, and for the most part I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. It does of course have a few flaws, but I'll sing it's praises first. Artistically, Blasphemous 2 is gorgeous. The pixel art is so intricate and atmospheric, with every area being incredibly well defined in terms of color scheme, background art, and area design. Character design and animations are also excellent, each NPC is distinct and unique, which characterizes them very well and makes them memorable, which helps significantly when all of their names seem to be a paragraph long. The music was also very solid,  I really loved the background music in the Crown of Towers. Finally, gameplay wise, the actual exploration and combat were generally very, very satisfying. Without spoiling too much, each weapon is pretty well executed in terms of move set, and without too much effort it's pretty easy to make some really unique and interesting builds around the weapons. This makes combat encounters and bosses very satisfying to rip through, especially in conjunction with the brutal death animations. These tight and snappy attacks, coupled with world design chock-full of collectables and upgrades, makes the early-mid game very, very addicting. Unfortunately, the game begins to weaken in the late game, which is where I have a few gripes.For the most part the pacing of Blasphemous 2 is pretty solid, with proper routing it doesn't take long at all to start feeling very, very powerful. Unfortunately, by the late game, however, things stop feeling brutal but fair, and instead feel unjustly punishing. During my playtime I did my best to specialize with a certain weapon, upgrading it and utilizing the available collectable buffs, but by the end I found my damage output still quite underwhelming. Many enemies get really tanky near the end, and the "final area" in particular is deeply frustrating, with only a single save point in an obnoxiously long platforming/combat gauntlet. Additionally, the penultimate boss of the game is a massive step up in difficulty, with an enormous health pool, insane damage per hit, and very minimal windows for retaliation. Additionally, for whatever reason, the late game bosses don't skip their intro cutscenes on repeat attempts, so you have to sit and listen to him ramble before each and every fight. It ultimately really hurt the combat experience at the end, less so for the difficulty and moreso for how sluggish it felt to retry.I also had some gripes with the actual 100%ing experience, for the most part the collectables feel pretty good and are very rewarding. But at the end, when I was looking for ten hidden symbols throughout the world and grinding out the last three upgrade points for the last weapon upgrade, the grind set in and ended up bittering the once sweet taste of exploration. It's a more minor gripe since reaching 100% completion is not required, but the hidden symbols in particular were absolutely unfair without a guide.Ultimately, Blasphemous 2 is an excellent sequel to the first game, and while the experience is soured a bit by some genuinely unfair challenges at the end, it nonetheless is an overall very satisfying metroidvania experience. I'd give it an 8/10, only brought down by a few low points. If you loved the first game, Blasphemous 2 is absolutely a worthy sequel that you should be sure to pick up.(I do miss the skins and NG+ challenges though, hopefully they appear in a later update but I wish they'd shipped with the base game.)

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm a Catholic seminarian (a priest-in-training) and a fairly squeamish gamer, so at first glance the Blasphemous franchise should repel me away to make prayers of reparation; but it somehow positively intrigues me. Religious/lore reasons below if you like, but first a proper review...Gameplay wise, it's fantastic. It's a slick metroidvania with difficult but very satisfying combat. For context, I came to B2 right after Hollow Knight and the two compare favorably. My one main critique is that there are too many frustrating dead ends/ability locks in the mid-game, but it makes up for it in the exhilarating exploration of the late-game. The art and music quality are on point as well all throughout, and with my 30+ hours at this writing I have completed the story, a good amount of the side quests, and I'm starting in on the DLC.***** Religious/Lore Take*****I've seen commentors claim that Blasphemous' setting and lore "nails" its depiction of Catholicism. Not really. I would say that it nails a very specific Spanish Gothic aesthetic within Catholic culture, and that is just what the developers have set out to do. As such, though the game has plentiful echoes of Catholic art and devotion, it feels more like playing through a grotesque Renaissance painting, or a work of Francisco de Goya (an explicit inspiration for the devs) rather than an homage to sacred art itself. The developers have more or less acknowledged this, and have also (to their credit) said they do not seek to offend any real world religions and so have refrained from depicting Jesus, the cross, or any specific Saints.Ironically then, the games are so fictionalized and stylized away from Catholicism that it might not actually qualify as blasphemous. "The Miracle," the spiritual antagonistic(?) force of the series, is clearly not God, it's not even a god, but more like a Freudian "super-ego" created by the collective guilt-ridden psychology of the setting's inhabitants. But even though its religious sensibility is twisted and over-exaggerated, the series occasionally is able to tap into a very human catharsis of spiritual guilt and dread in a meaningful way. Further, some lines are genuinely beautiful and maybe even approach real devotion (in this game I found this particularly with the confessor and the rosary-maker). All of this is to say that I have found value in Blasphemous' religious setting even as a man of faith. That said, I would still definitely put the series in the not-for-everyone category, and I would be even more selective in recommending it to my fellow Christians. It is also unabashedly macabre and gory, albeit in pixel art form, which makes my recommendation even more hesitant. For what it's worth, I actually bought B2 precisely because they toned those parts down compared to the first game, which I haven't played beyond the demo out of regard for my emotional health. Lol. So take that as you will.In the end, I don't mind a game which depicts and appropriates Christian symbolism. I don't even mind a game which explores the dark and overwrought parts of human religious impulses. The thing I mind, my ultimate critique of "Blasphemous," is that the game doesn't give corresponding attention to the forgiveness and hope provided by faith, which is in fact the actual point of the Gospel. In being mindful of the cross and death, we ought to be just as mindful of the Resurrection and life. So, even while I continue enjoying Blasphemous, I'll ever be on the lookout for games which give more space for that larger, better story.So, yes, "sorrowful be the heart, Penitent One;"But as Jesus says: "Blessed are the sorrowful, for they shall be comforted."

_childDocuments_.review: When this game came out, I bought it instantly, and I don't remotely regret it. This game improved some of my issues with the first one being you don't have to sacrifice flasks in order to upgrade you healing, and as far as I know there aren't any missions that will time out because you progressed too far in the main story. The traversal is super fun, the weapons all have there own special traits and uses, and once again, the pixel art and music is just plain amazing.   The fast travel was kinda fixed, . I also love with alter pieces and rosary beads you can take on the game any way you want to. I do however have one issue with the game, and that is the bosses.   They felt way easier to me than the first games bosses. it could just be that alter pieces give you a huge boost so it just feels easier in comparison. However where the bosses in the first game truly felt unique and served a purpose in the overall lore. Of course the bosses in this game serve the lore as a whole, but I feel like they left less of an impact on me unlike the first game.   In conclusion I do think this game is an improvement when it comes to full on game-play, but could use a bit of tweaking when it comes to story and lore. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Huh.First impressions after beating it--While I have to say, that this is a sturdy and solid follow up to the first game, it is noticeably easier. This could be the addition of ability upgrades in this game, or it could be the content in general. It could also be, that when I played through the first game, there was a lot of DLC that had been added over the years.Whatever the case: that difference in difficulty might determine how much you enjoy this sequel, relative from the first game.Personally, I'm a little bummed that it wasn't challenging enough. I remember feeling like a champ when I finally beat some of the bosses in the first game (Isidora comes to mind). The last boss here was a TOTAL pushover. It took me two tries, and then it was over. The platforming also felt a lot easier. To clarify: the platforming in this game FEELS great, but I think the challenge was less present. Some of the most fun I had in the first game were the timed platforming challenges. Here, they're noticeably absent.All that in mind: it's still a fantastic game. It makes a lot of improvements on the first, and comes out the gates swinging. If you were a fan of the first, you'll most likely enjoy it as well. I just wish I had gotten more of a catharsis out of beating it, like I had before.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I'm not a Souls-like connoisseur, the first game did give me an appreciation for the genre and I had a lot of fun playing through the sequel. It feels much faster and slightly easier, but I'm not sure if that's simply because I'm more used to the game's flow this time around. _childDocuments_.review: Great art. Dark, baroque, sinister and absurd. I don't have the vocabulary to describe it adequately. It was a pleasure to see it all. Technically, I encountered a few bugs: some missing animations, teleportation broke a few times requiring me to restart my game, some small things. Not serious or common enough to prevent me from finishing the game. The combat was overall satisfying, with a few caveats. Contact damage is not ideal when there are some enemies that can spawn directly on top of you (northwest area, you'll know the ones), or glide into you randomly. The trial-and-error in determining which things can be dodged through and which can't is a bit annoying. The pacing and balance is a bit uneven. Weapon upgrades appear at strange periods. None of the bosses are terribly difficult, especially with the massive health and healing upgrades that are a bit too loaded towards the mid-late game. There's a mid-game duo boss that doesn't work very well when you haven't yet acquired some of the defensive abilities that would make it more controllable, and many of the late game bosses have entirely too much projectile spam in lieu of attack patterns (this is perhaps more just a personal taste thing). I do appreciate the general boss and enemy variety. The decision to make the final health and fervour upgrades completely missable based on some minor actions the player can take near the start of the game with little context is foolish, especially in the face of the rest of the quests and items being mostly self-solvable without looking up a guide and acquirable from a specific NPC if they're missed. It stands out as a mistake. There's a little bit too much metroidvania backtracking. I'm glad the map gives you options to mark spots to come back to later, at least, and the final few sweeps are accelerated by all the fast travel options you end up with. Despite the (mostly minor) issues above, I enjoyed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to a great game. Genuinely felt like a perfect "safe" sequel. "Safe" because this is still undoubtedly just more Blasphemous. Practically everything in the first game makes a return in this direct sequel, but with improvements across the board. You get more weapons, more stat boosting items, more NPC's to be shocked by, better areas, better exploration, better enemies, better upgrades, and the list can go on I'm sure. Easily surpasses the sequelitis for me, I do think this is the better game overall even if the novelty of the original keeps it a close contest.Now to rant about my thoughts on main portions of the game, i'll start with the bosses. They are just about as interesting to look at and learn as they were in the first game's base version. I don't know if the post release stuff from the first game will be surpassed. The individual areas have seen some of the largest improvement in my opinion. The rooms took more interesting shapes and the layouts were more fun to navigate. The start of the game had some really open ended progression but things die down heavily in the mid game where areas start opening up one by one instead of at the same time like I think would have been more interesting. This eventually forces you into following what feels like a pretty defined route. Having three weapons is amazing, especially because you don't have to use all three in combat. You can pick a favorite like I did and just get good with it. The use of all three weapons in traversal is fantastic though and it makes for some of the more interesting movement puzzles. Speaking of movement, it feels very similar to the first game, just better. More consistent and smoother overall. And with the addition of some new movement options it was much more varied than the first ever was. I do miss stabbing the walls to climb though, even if that system resulted in a ton of deaths for me, just felt unique I guess. The combat feels the same way. It's the same, but more consistent and smooth, and of course you have three different weapons to work with. There's also loads of new enemies and better use of enemy variants to kept it fresh for far longer. There is a lacking number of unique executions though which is a shame. The music is about as good as in the first game, overall very atmospheric. The visual presentation seems to have not skipped a single beat excluding two things. Firstly, the world in this game supposedly has a giant heart in the sky but you never see it the background sky box. Thinking about it now that ♥♥♥♥ should be up there looming over our entire playthrough as some sign of the danger to come. Secondly, the cut scenes being in a different style did feel weird, but it's such a non issue for me that I hardly remembered to mention it here. Everything else looks absolutely fantastic. Backtracking was so much better in this game, from the increased density of stuff in every room to the improved layout of the world and placement of fast travel rooms. Much less frustration getting from point A to B and back again. Finally the story and characters. Both were great. The writing is still weird and fun to listen to and the voice acting is a lot better than the first game overall. The characters are all still a wonderful mix of horrifying and mysterious and most were really good. I think the fist game will always have a leg up in this part because of how unique it was when it came out. This game is just as good, it's just no longer the first to do it. There's more I could mention like the improved variety in spells and stat boosters, but generally speaking if the first game had it this game has it too, with some form of improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: If you told me Blasphemous would have a sequel four years ago, I would laugh at you and ask if you were high or something. And yet, here we are. Blasphemous 2 has been released, and it's more polished, darker and weirder than the first one, and even more gorgeous in terms of art style. It's the same deal with Nioh 2 and Remanant 2: sequels that are basically just the first game but with way, way more content. Blasphemous 2 takes in all the criticism from the first game and improve upon it. I am not just talking about number tweak. The lacking of character build, the annoying platform issues, and the metroidvania identity crisis, all have been resolved in this wonderful sequel. Well, I suppose if I have to say something negative about Blasphemous 2, it would be that if you don't like the first one, you will not enjoy the sequel either. It is still the same game, fundamentally. However, I would still recommend this game to those people simply because of its sheer improvement.Looking back at Game Kitchen's previous works never cease to amaze me. The improvement they have from The Last Door to Blasphemous is phenomenal. From simple background drawn from simple line works, to a full-blown melancholy scenery made with delicacy and wonder, it is undeniable that the studio has out-done themselves over the years. But here comes the sequel. Somehow, Game Kitchen finds a way to improve even further. The background detail of Blasphemous 2 is really something else. Every stage is beautifully crafted. Various degree of solemnity can be seen from each level. The City Of Blessed Name is layered with a warm color of lighting with the doves taking off, conveying a divine and hopeful atmosphere. My favorite scene is probably the starting area of the Choir Of Thorns. It is ominous road to the Crown Of Towers. The dark color and the thorny decoration apply a sense of dread. Once you push pass the shrubs and forests, you are greeted with an open view. A great lake sits calmly in front of you. You notice something different about the lake. The reflection of clear surface seems off. It depicts a night sky and a lively city on the far hill, yet when you look up there’s nothing there. This scene is full of mystery, and at the same time delivers an unspeakable sense of wonder that only Blasphemous and Game Kitchen can pull off.Immediately the first improvement jumps right in. The first game does not have much weapon variety. Mea Culpa is your only sword throughout the whole game. It makes sense lore wise, but I wish there were more. And now in Blasphemous 2 there are three weapons for you to choose. Ruego Al Alba is basically Mea Culpa with a curse sword appearance, but its function is far from identical. With Blood Pact ability, this curve sword can enhance its attack with additional range, damage, and even heal yourselves for the damage you deal. Veredicto is the heavy hitter, a chained hammer made with incense. It has the longest reach and delivers the heaviest punch of the three. It's power is further increased by lighting the incense on fire. Sarmiento and Centella sports a faster attack and a deadly dash attack which is great for repositioning. With repeating strikes, this rapier and dagger can even conjure up some lightning damage. Needless to say, the new weapons are welcoming features. What I love even more is that each weapon comes with one metroidvania style perk. The perk is baked into each weapon's moveset, meaning it can be used to open new areas or cut some hole on your enemies. The human tree trunks can only be penetrated by Ruego Al Alba's high-air plunge attack; Veredicto can ring the special bell to summon the formless platforms and thin the iron doors; Sarmiento and Centella allows you to zoom through the floating mirrors and reach higher level. This is a recent feature which I fall in love with during many years of playing metroidvania, and I am glad Blasphemous 2 jumps on this trend.→Spanish dub has a solemn touch to it, and I love it.→Again, NPCs are intriguingly weird.→Soundtrack is equally good as the first one.→A lot of secrets and collectibles.→That indie games gallery easter egg.→Traps no longer one-shot you, rejoice!→: There are certainly more ways to improve your playstyle in Blasphemous 2. Each weapon has unlockable movesets and some general upgrades in the responding skill tree. Rosary beads have been cut down on quantity and focus on survival and defensive traits. And the new feature, Altarpiece is something worth investing into. It functions similar to Rosary beads, but instead of survivability, it serves as offensive customization for your weapons and prayers. Each figure has different attribute to boost your performance, and I am not talking about a measly 5% boost like the first game. It is 10% and the number can go even higher with right combination. Yes, combination is a thing for the Altarpiece. Combines certain figures together can create some crazy synergies. For example, putting The Anointed One(increases the strength of Veredicto) and The Purified One(Increases Fire damage) together gives Veredicto new attack effect that whenever you attack with the incense active, every swing sends out four fire orbs that explode. There are more synergies that focus on each weapon and even your Bile Flask for you to discover.→: With all these new upgrades also come with a catch. Most of the critics I come across say that the game is a little too easy comparing to the first game, and I have to agree. It is an extremely delicate line to balance. You want to give players the power they deserve, but you also need to keep both the power and enemies' toughness in check to create a balance difficulty. Sadly, Blasphemous 2 is struggling to find that balance. I will be honest. I never feel challenged during my playthrough up until the second to last boss fight.→If two or more enemies manage to run into you when you're knocked down, prepare to take a ridiculous amount of contact damage before you can reposition to safety.→Some descriptions for the puzzles can be cryptic to deduce.中文小簡評→續作出來的比我想像的還快，瀆神2就好比遺跡2和仁王2，擁有一代的基礎但是更多玩意兒！→把一代有的缺點一一改善並且逐一加強，玩過一代你會更愛。→美術風格更上一層樓，每個場景都是充滿黑暗宗教氣息，既神聖又詭譎。→三把武器任君挑選，各自有優缺點，值得一提的是三把武器都各有類銀河系惡魔城的技能，可以解鎖更多區域，又能拿來打怪。→西班牙配音有股不可言喻的肅穆感。→NPC真的是無法想像的怪(讚美。→背景音樂好聽。→諸多隱藏道具及收集任務，各自有相對應的獎勵。→獨立遊戲畫廊小彩蛋。→讚嘆主，陷阱不會秒殺你啦！→本作擁有更多方式來客製化玩法，升級上下限遠超一代，然而這是一把雙面刃，過度強化帶來的是暴力輾壓過關，瀆神2的難度因此比一代低許多。→如果有兩個敵人在你被擊倒時站在你身上的話，除了吃上大量接觸傷害外完全無解。→有些解謎敘述過於艱澀難懂。

_childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: 31/36 CherubsThe Context:Some games ooze charm. Others ooze style, or atmosphere. Blasphemous 2 just oozes. What it oozes I'm not sure, could be blood, pus, wax or honey. One thing's sure though, it's a blessing from the Miracle, and if you look past the grotesque, what awaits you is an excellent followup to the original holy experience.The standout for me was how much more smooth the Penitent One controls, both in platforming and combat purposes. With 3 new weapons to swap between, along with several additional mobility options, the difference is noticeable (Think early Castlevanias vs. Aria of Sorrow).  Don't get me wrong, I love both styles, I just think that this closer fits the style of exploration the devs intended with their world design.Not everything has changed, though. The prayer spell system returns, as do the equipable prayer beads to create your build. This is augmented by the statues you can equip for a build that affect anything from a certain type of damage to healing to guilt (a real thing you need to manage). Altogether, it lets you craft a much more personalized build that fits your style, and is definitely a boon to the game.One aspect I don't think was recaptured was the gothic, religious art of the original. There are glimmers here and there, but overall it seems a bit watered down compared to the almost Goya-istic (not a word) style of the original. I don't think it's enough to weigh down the sequel beyond the original, but I can see the argument. Personally, I found this to be an improvement over the original, fitting much closer to the vision of the Metroidvania that I saw laid out there. While some style choices may ruffle some feathers, I think it's a worthy followup, the Circle of the Moon to the Simon's Quest of the first.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 major problems with the sequel.  The battle system isnt as tight as the first because they balanced it for 3 weapons and lets be honest, its way easier.  Also, having a blinking spot on your map telling you where to go was a huge mistake.  It completely ruined the aspect of getting lost in the world and just exploring.  And the 3rd major issue is the lore isnt as thorough, mostly noticable in the lore options under items and prayers.  Some are so simple it really just says "wind is scary."   But overall, still a good game.  They just made the mistake of aiming for more wide appeal in some aspects and it watered down the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviewers have mentioned, this game is fun but will leave you slightly disappointed if your are seeking the same feeling the original Blasphemous. Combat is fun and the platforming is interesting- especially with the Mea Culpa DLC. The music is beautiful as always. The bosses are interesting and don't feel like carbon copies of what we saw with the first game.That said...-The NPCs are forgettable. One of the things that I love about the first game are the characters that populate the world and make it feel so much more alive. Gemino, Rendeto, Soledad, just to name a few. This game has very few in comparison, and they don't really expand the lore of Cvstodia. A lot of time has passed since the Penitent One died, surely some lore can be woven into these characters like they were for the first group. But sadly no- they are all very flat in comparison.- Replayability is much lower. In the first game, you could unlock a number of skins which were tied to challenges that, while frustrating at times, kept the play fresh. Once you finish Blasphemous 2, you can start new game plus, but there are no aesthetic rewards for doing so. - This is more of a nitpick, but I dislike the animated cut scenes. They are so jarringly different in style from the rest of the game, it kind of breaks the immersion a bit.Do I think this game is worth playing at least once? Yes.Do I think future DLCs can help address some of my concerns? Absolutely.Do I think Blasphemous 2 holds a candle to the original at all? No. Not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is Blasphemous but with everything taken to the next level: improved movement, better level design, fun and more diverse combat, amazing music, fair but still challenging boss battles, the best pixel art ever made on a videogame, and a really good feeling of what a metroidvania has to be, which sometimes Blasphemous lacked it. The developers really learned a lot and made an amazing sequel, absolutely better in every aspect than the first game, which was already very good.If you liked Blasphemous, then you will absolutely love Blasphemous 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game on my switch and now making a playthrough on pc.The good:-Soundtrack is on par with B1 and serves well for the context of the story.-Movement is massively upgraded, making it a delight to transverse the world. Sadly you unlock the full potential of movement options very late in the game.-diversity in Weapons is really good tailored and really good for replaying the game with different initial options.-Environments are better than B1, the team really got a grasp in what they can improve with the backgrounds as there was more focus on the actual game now that the cutscenes are animated.-QOL improvements are good in this game, Prie Dieu upgrades now are locked behind quests instead of money paywall making it more engaging to actually going to explore the map instead of farming tears This game is a really good sequel, sadly B1 feels more complete even without 2's movement, weapon diversity and QOL improvements. The bad: -Executions were a major selling point in B1 making it engaging to actually try to engage with enemies in the intense backtracking that these games provide. In B2, executions are sparse and i may have done as much execution as my first 5 hours on B1. A lot of executions are now very generic and not even near the uniqueness of B1; i understand that with 3 different weapons the challenge of making unique executions is higher but now that the pixel art in the cutscenes has been erased they should've keep this major selling point that made B1 so unique. Damn it even feels like i should play B1 again now just to enjoy the executions.-Hidden rooms, a metroidvania staple, are cut down from B1 in a 60% for how it feels. Now limited to a few specific questlines and replaced with parkour-themed timed door challenges. -This game feels somehow easier than B1 for me. Double jump and airdash serves right for movement since B1 is kinda sluggish in terms of movement without bead upgrades, but in combat feels like an excuse to put as many enemies with ranged attacks or janky hitboxes in the same room just for annoyance. Bosses feel easier too, while in B1 i had to repeat some bosses a significant amount of time or go outta my way to get upgrades to rival the damage output, in B2 that feeling is just non-existent. Relying on Veredicto when things got tough never failed to me.-Hitstun lock is back baybee and it seems there's no fix to this, but yeah, annoying AF. They made a good work with it in executions, making enemies don't aggro you while you're executing an enemy so they aren't on top of you when the execution is over for a free hit. But damn a few invincibility frames in the get up animations could have serve this without tampering difficulty that much.-Lore and story seems toned down. Yes, it is still the same Church/Bizarre nightmare fuel experience, but NPCs feel way less involved in the story. While B1's story revolved around how the miracle impacted sorrow and repent was much more engraved in the world. This time the story is way less captivating, i guess making the miracle the main subject again left the devs with less options in how to make the world alive and top the abr that B1 set years ago.-Tears of atonement are not a main "thing" in the game now, i have 100k+ and never got any trouble with buying any item at any point of the game, making them less important in a not so rewarding way, specially if you tie the new guilt system to them. Overall B2 is a good game, a good sequel, but the fact that B1 outshines this game in a lot of the things that makes this franchise so appealing is kinda disappointing to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the first Blasphemous game, but while playing the sequel i couldn't help but be disappointed and angry at how they handled some elements of the game. Apart from the art style the game just feels bland. They completely crushed the "soul" of the first game and replaced it with generic metroidvania elements and for the most part boring level design.The game does improve on some things compared to the first one, like the combat and the fact that you have 3 weapons at your disposal. There aren't any miss-able quest this time around. Also the altarpieces and weapon skill-trees are cool additions. Sadly these came at a cost of making the rosarie beads completely uninteresting and 2 of the 3 weapons having bugs that I found.Due to people complaining about insta-kill spikes in the first game, the devs removed the insta-kill element from them in the second game ( I personally didn't like this decision, but I do understand that people were annoyed and frustrated by the spikes). The problem with this is that it makes traversing the different areas less interesting and tense especially because most of the platforming sections are gone as well and the ones that remain have little to no weight or danger behind them.  The devs tried to fix this by adding more enemies to rooms and imo way too many challenge rooms. This would have probably helped if the enemy variety wasn't so lacking.Obviously some enemies were taken unchanged from the first game (which is totally fine) but the problem lies with the fact  a lot of the enemies are just recolours of themselves with the element of the enemy being changed or them having an extra little addition to their attack. This just makes it feel cheap and recycled. Another part which adds to the laziness of it all is the fact that there are almost no unique executions in the game. I saw like maybe 5 different executions because most  of the enemies have the same boring execution + triggering executions is harder and less consistent. Sadly, even though game has been out for almost a year, common and easily found bugs have still not been fixed. I encountered bugs were in some areas the music cut out randomly and i had to fast travel to get it back. Worst of all, one of the bosses you have to fight has his music AND sound effects completely cut out which you can't fix from what I've tried. Obviously this completely ruins the atmosphere and feel of the fight. Another thing which I noticed is that when you stop time (through the use of prayers or altarpieces), projectiles and flying enemies don't stop, but keep moving in the direction they were moving. This actually led me to being stuck in one of the challenge rooms because a flying enemy went off screen and never came back. Lastly, as stated above, I found bugs with 2 of the 3 weapons in the game. The most apparent  one was with the mace, where there is an animation error when you try to light it while running, this makes the lighting animation cut out and freezes the character in place until the mace is suddenly lit. The second bug was with the rapier weapon specifically with the skills "silver cross" and "cross of the tempest". You're supposed to be able to use the "silver cross" skill anytime you want in the air, but for some reason I had to spend a diamond (Verdadera Destreza) point to use it. Because of this, the upgraded version, "cross of the tempest" which actually had to use a diamond (Verdadera Destreza) point, just didn't work no matter what I tried.Overall, if the game wasn't tied to blasphemous 1 then it would be a decent game. Unfortunately, since it is a sequel that imo for the most part is a downgrade of the original. For that reason i can't recommend the game especially if the developers will continue down the same path and make the series worse. I just can't support that.PS: The final boss has an unnecessary difficulty spike with a couple of lines of unskippable dialogue every time you fight him, which is just annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 has gripped me right from the beginning with its mesmerizing artstyle and evident passion. As I navigate through its haunting world, I'm already captivated by the attention to detail and the darkly immersive atmosphere. The UI system is sleekly integrated, and the cutscenes are like chilling pieces of visual storytelling.I'm only at the start of this journey, and I can already tell that Blasphemous 2 is something special as well as the first entry in this series. I'll be updating this review as I progress, but if the initial minutes are any indication, I'm in for an unforgettable experience.I already played Blasphemous 1 on the Nintendo Switch which was a blast to play, so I recommend playing the first title of this series before playing the second.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 emerges as a refined sequel, surpassing its predecessor in both combat and exploration. The game shines aesthetically, with more detailed backgrounds and a greater diversity of areas to explore. The music is enchanting and perfectly captures the emotion of each setting. A significant change from the original is the shift from entirely pixel-based cutscenes to hand-drawn animations. While this might initially feel off-putting to some players, it effectively details the characters before transitioning to the pixel art graphics.CombatCombat has received substantial emphasis and expansion. Players no longer wield the Mea Culpa, which, while missed for its versatility, is replaced with three new weapons that offer diverse combat options:Veredicto (Hammer): A slow but powerful weapon capable of smashing walls and ringing bells for traversal.Ruego Al Alba (One-handed Blade): Allows for counter attacks and plunging attacks, which also destroy roots found on the ground.Sarmiento and Centella (Sword and Dagger): Enables fast attacks that increase in damage with a higher combo counter and allows the player to dash through mirrors.Additionally, prayers have been greatly improved, offering more variety and being available sooner in the game, allowing players to experiment with them faster.PlatformingPlatforming has been made less frustrating, with spikes no longer instantly killing the player. However, it has also become more challenging, requiring players to switch between weapon mobility skills to access different areas. Although it feels better than in the previous game, the increased complexity will challenge players more.Enemy VarietyEnemy variety is a standout feature in Blasphemous 2. Encounters are generally more difficult than in the first game, with enemies dealing more damage, having more varied attacks, and frequently using ranged abilities. The enemy placement is excellent, making every room feel challenging in the best way.Player Equipment and LoadoutsThe player equipment and loadout system has undergone significant changes. The number of rosary beads that can be equipped has been reduced to five, but the game introduces up to eight equipable altarpieces, which need to be changed at a specific NPC. Although I wish these could be changed at rest points, this system offers more overall build variety, which is a net positive.A major change is the introduction of defined damage types that enemies can resist. This adds more complexity to the system, as altarpieces can alter how these damage types interact with enemies.Boss FightsEvery boss has a short introduction that cannot be skipped, which can make repeated attempts more annoying than necessary. A particular boss, Eviterno, toward the end of the game, is notably challenging and forces players to skip through dialogue each time. This has been a point of frustration for many players and needs to be addressed by the development team.Missing FeaturesNotably, Blasphemous 2 lacks a New Game+ feature, which was a highlight of the first game after an update. This mode imposed specific penalties on the player character, forcing them to interact with the game differently. Despite its absence, the game remains highly recommendable, and I hope the developers add this feature in the future.ConclusionBlasphemous 2 is a worthy successor, delivering a polished and diverse experience. The improvements in combat, platforming, and the equipment system add depth and complexity, while the enhanced aesthetics and music elevate the overall atmosphere. Despite some minor drawbacks, such as the limited flexibility in changing altarpieces and the frustrating boss intros, Blasphemous 2 stands out as a challenging and rewarding game that fans of the series will greatly enjoy.
