_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's fun, it's good and it's worth the price BUT the first Blasphemous is superior. If you're thinking about buying this game (and I recommend you do) consider the following first. -Blasphemous has INFINITELY better artstyle, especially custscenes. The new ones seriously don't match the tone of the game and you might think at some point that you turned on Crunchyroll by accident. You can thank Team17 for that, as the animator mainly responsible for cutscenes in B1 was Russian and he left the studio when Team17 forbid distribution of games in Russia.-Blasphemous 1 lets you explore a bit more and is more of a proper metroidvania. This one is pretty linear, you cannot wander into a late game area, because it simply is not there and only appears with progress. You also know where to go at all times, as objectives are now marked on your map.-Eventually you get to posess all three weapons. I thought really hard about choosing my weapon at the beginning of the game, and it turned out to be in vain, as you get all of them pretty early on. Weapon skills from the first game have been divided between 3 new weapons. You liked to have the option to parry and dash attack? Well now one weapon can parry, and the other can dash attack. It really doesn't matter, as you can focus on one weapon and steamroll through the entire game. -No i-frames, contact damage, ridiculous knockback - not only it's really easy to ♥♥♥♥ yourself over by poor positioning, the game tries to ♥♥♥♥ you over in some places. I died more times to contact damage than I'd like to admit. Enemies can spawn right onto you, which wouldn't be that problematic, if not for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ knockback, which can stunlock you right into the corner. This is extremely applicable before you get any upgrades, as a couple of times you get locked in a room with 2 charging enemies that you CANNOT jump over.-Boss balancing isn't there yet. The majority of bosses are REALLY easy and can be taken down in under 3 attempts without tryharding. On the other hand, some late game bosses become ridiculously difficult.-YOU CANNOT SKIP INTROS BEFORE BOSSFIGHTS! I don't know who came up with this, but it's one of the worst things about this game. Let me watch it once and then skip it whenever I want, Jesus it's not that difficult. With some changes, it could be just as good or better than the original. As it stands, it's very serviceable, but not "up there". They will probably drop some DLC at some point, so it has potential. Having said all that, In Blasphemous 2, spikes and falls no longer insta-kill you, so it may be a better game after all lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time for 90% of the game but the second-last boss was a massive difficulty spike coupled with ~40s of unskippable cutscenes. This was very frustrating and my initial review of this was a no.But since I had a good time for most of the playthrough, I'd really like to voice to the devs that cutscenes should be skippable for bosses. And 40s of unskippable scenes for one boss is too much. It was more Blasphemous and I think the combat in this was overall better than in the first. So after having had a few weeks to cool off, I'd ultimately recommend this game, but I do agree with others that the difficulty on bosses can feel all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome sequel to the first game, although the story was less compelling as the first (I believe it's due to the lack of normal NPC questlines). This isn't necessarily a bad thing, because the additional map size is totally worth all the work into it. I was agog at the scenery and detail, especially in the forest and sheet city areas (iykyk). Like, this game is worth the art alone. I also really appreciate the new ability to mark things on the map which was a huge help.Also, fair warning, the last two bosses of the game are extremely obnoxious and not like the rest of the bosses in the game, so I recommend not sticking to one weapon. Use the whole game to practice different moves, weapons and spells so the end game won't be such a pain. Additionally, if you are going to try to go for all the cherubs, I recommend marking the ones you find on your map as you go through them to avoid the pain of trying to find the last ones in end game as well.

Now the serious motives in the game are undercut by the childish scribbles during the cutscenes. I WILL PAY FOR THE DLC THAT GIVES ME AN OPTION TO CHOOSE THE ORIGINAL ARTSTYLE. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10 A great time! Blasphemous 2 takes elements from Castlevania, Elden Ring, Bloodborne and even Disney's Aladdin for the SNES to make a great experience. Now I'm not positive they took inspiration from any of those games but it sure felt like it. The music was enjoyable and the game looked beautiful. To top it all off it was much easier than the first. I mean, I was killing most bosses within 1-3 tries. I recommend this to anyone interested in a wonderful metroidvania and it might even be worth checking out over the first game as a warm up to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a worthy successor, that you can still play without having played the predecessor. Lore wise it is similar to a souls-like, you wont understand anything the first time you play it or without looking up some stuff. The second I started playing, muscle memory kicked in and it played just like Blasphemous I. You will recognize a couple of enemies as well. The upgraded art style of the cut scenes was unusual at first and I feared to lose a bit of the grim feel, but it turned out to be not to be a bad decision at all. The things you loved about Blasphemous I you will get more of. I personally loved the little moments when you realize what just happened to the characters and what consequences your decision just triggered. The new possibility to choose and level different weapons is a good addition, especially when the game encourages you to use all of them. Overall everything I expected, with good additional mechanics and lore, so that it does not feel too copy-pasted. The only thing (that I didn't like in the first game as well) is the kind of overwhelming skill and inventory system. It still has its reason and roots in the lore, which is why I still don't think it is that restrictive.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel that delivers everything that made the first game great and more on top of it. Like with the first, it is a fantastic Metroidvania with a difficulty that is certainly punishing, but sits in a nice sweet spot where it feels beatable with the right combination of skill and knowledge, never demanding absolute perfect precision at all times. I'd take any "too easy" complaints with a grain of salt. Like "dead game" people say that about literally every game on steam pretty much all the time, so you'll need some more in depth details to properly ascertain the difficulty for yourself.Some nice quality of life changes help take some of the frustration from the first game out (such as no more instant death spikes).Art and music are once again top notch. The animated cutscenes are beautiful, the pixel art as lovely as it is macabre, and the music is fantastic (though as of writing there's a bug that causes it to sometimes vanish for a time. I hear they're working on it though.)While I'm normally not that big on lore, I do wish a little more was explained in how things have changed between the two games as some areas lead to some interesting implications, but seem to lack any explanation (though perhaps I missed it.)All in all, as long as you like these kinds of tough Metroidvanias, I'd say it's a great game with nothing really to complain about. If more content is released for Blasphemous 2, I'll certainly be interested in that, but I'm also quite satisfied with what it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 was amazing. If you liked the first one, getting this one is a no-brainer.It's essentially more of the same, and that's the best thing about it.Gorgeous art, atmospheric music, tight controls, fulfilling combat and varied boss fights. (Although one of the boss fights is WAY harder than the rest, which I found a bit odd. It required very cheesy tactics for me to beat.)There's a lot to explore and a lot of secrets to be found, so completionists get to enjoy the awesome setpieces in some depth.The main difference compared to the first game is that there are now three main weapons which cater to different playstyles. You can also experiment with various builds, as each weapon has its own skill tree with some global modifiers, and there are new equippable items that boost different aspects of the main character, the weapons and prayers etc.The only minus for me was that there were a few bugs here and there, but nothing game-breaking or anything reloading a save wouldn't fix.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.2Compare to the previous game, this game is improved in a lot of way.Graphic - Graphic is mostly the same as the prequel and I think theres's some improvement but not very obvious. Classic 2D platform graphic.Gameplay The gameplay is expand a lot, on the first game it only have one sword, and we got three diffferent type of weapon. and can suit different playstyle, also the combination of weapons to traves and open gates are really a creative mechanic. I do enjoy it. the movement also feels more smooth and more flashy. Really good improvement imo.Area and Map designThe map design is same as last game, make sense but I feel less complicated, the first game's map is so complicated is kinda hard to know where am i and where to go. so that's a improvement to me. overall the Areas are well designed, especially the mirror city, really a rare design and it's pretty creative. the last area feels really long with no shortcuts, that's kinda annoying, but overall is pretty good. Boss design and Enemy placementThe enemy placement are pretty good, some rooms have some crap enemy placement, like two giants with others. that feels pretty unfair and not fun. But overall is pretty decent.Now the Boss design, oh man where do i start it. it is complicated, I would say most of bosses are well designed, but have some outliners. one of example of a good design boss are the final boss(eviteno), very comfort area, not mob summoning, just sword vs sword, very fair and reasonable fight. I would give the final 2 boss fight a 10/10. but some bosses like odon and benedict are just the opposite, one is summon mob in mid of fight and all have contact damage, other is platforming during the fight and half of the time she is at a place where you can't hit her. so mostly is well done but some bosses are annoying.StoryTBH I barely understand what is the first game even saying, but the second game's story is way clear and have no problem to understand. i would say is an improvement to me. Overall i give this game a 8.2 out of 10, mainly the bad boss, some ♥♥♥♥ enemy placement and contact damage. but greatly improved than the previous game. buy it on a 20% sale is fair to me.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a good game until the Eviterno boss fight. Very frustrating and odd choice in significant difficulty spike vs. what the whole game prepared you for. I wouldn't say the boss is hard. Rather he is cheap, with small open windows, lighting fast movement, screen clutter, waiting through the dialogue, and just other tedious aspects to this. I really enjoyed my time otherwise, and would give it a thumbs up other than this one part. It is so frustrating that I just had  to put this down after so many attempts. Before you say git good, learn his mechanics, etc I get it. As a souls borne veteran this just doesn't work for me and I don't have the time or  the patience to do it. I've gotten close a few times and probably could get through it if I did nothing but concentrate on it for an hour but that is just not up my alley. Hopefully the devs realize there are some issues with this fight that could be addressed fairly (e.g. you get hit with a fire wall and on recovery you get hit again, there is no time to dodge or recover)Edit: I was finally able to beat Evitreno after concentrating for one hour. I still hold by that it was an odd choice in difficulty spike. You basically steamrolled through the entire game (Veridicto is OP). This boss fight would have been more palatable if the rest of the game was more challenging and getting you to dodge and parry more. I changed my review to thumbs up. The thumbs down was due to sheer frustration,

_childDocuments_.review: The game improves on many of the minor issues in the original while bringing some excellent improvements. There are two primary bugs that exist though: map location and guilt. Sometimes the map won’t show your location correctly. I even had the map just not populate. You can fix this eventually though by closing and reopening the map once or twice until it’s right. The big issues is guilt. When you go back to where you died to pick up your guilt, it sometimes won’t remove the guilt on your fervor bar. This forces you to pay to have it removed. It’s been half and half for me. Works half the time and other half the time it doesn’t. Really should fix this soon or it seriously hampers gameplay. Other than that, I am really enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks about the same as the first game. Sword has an almost identical moveset, some of the enemies are exact copies. That's not encouraging.Got to a boss that required me to kill one enemy, then a second boss, then kill both at the same time.Now I really am not a fan of gank fights where I'm getting attacked by two people at once especially when one is firing ranged attacks at me while I'm trying to fight something else. Half the time I couldn't even see the little guy's attacks because the big guy's flame tornadoes were covering the screen. The hardest part of the fight was actually seeing what was hitting me at that point.What got my attention was the fact that even though I kept grabbing my body after each attempt my mana kept going down. Turns out the fight was getting harder every time I lost. I was losing mana and defense every death, body recovered or no. If I wanted to fix it, it cost me xp and a LONG ass trip back to town.Absolutely not a fan of that mechanic at all, I'm already losing to the boss why handicap me further and then charge me XP and time for my trouble? If you're going to copy the dark souls formula maybe actually take the time to understand why it works first.The best part was finally beating the boss and my reward was that my defense and mana were still gimped and I didn't even get something useful for my time. Dark Souls knew better than to do that, why don't these guys?

_childDocuments_.review: When I first reviewed this game, I gave it a thumbs down, because I had just rage quit it after getting killed by the worst boss ever for about the 150th time.  I have since then finished the game and I have had some time to reflect, and I would say that this game definitely deserves a thumbs up, but the last two bosses did leave a bad taste in my mouth.  The second to last boss is literally the most unfair boss that I have ever played against.  The actual final boss is kind of a pushover once you figure out his patterns.  It would be nice to see a future patch even out the difficulties a little more. But for most of the time playing Blasphemous 2, I was legitimately loving it.  It is a huge improvement over the first game.  Better level design.  Three great weapons instead of one, and each weapon is useful.  The weapons allow for all kinds of different approaches to your enemies, and the game is long enough that you will get to try all of them.  The collectibles are huge in number and high in quality.  Exploration is fun and it helps make the game addictive.  There are more upgrades to your abilities than there were in the first game, and that gives Blasphemous 2 much more of a traditional Metroidvania feel than its predecessor.  Falls into spikes and pits are no longer insta-death (Thank God).  The enemies are also more fun to fight.  The enemies that were the least fun to fight in the first game have been removed in favor of some new enemies that are very fun to fight.  The boss battles, up until the final two, are fantastic – they typify what a boss battle should be in a game like this. Blasphemous 2 is just as wonderful in its art direction and its animations as its predecessor, with the lone exception being that they, for some reason, neutered the executions in this game pretty badly.  The music is top notch once again too.  This game is one of the most improved sequels that I have ever played…. …until that boss.  And if you have played this game, then you know exactly the boss that I am talking about.  The most brutally difficult and punishingly unfair boss that I have ever experienced in a video game.  It is at that point that your 15-20 hours of consistent progress and addictive flow comes to a raging halt.  This boss has two full health bars and three stages on the second bar, with a short cut scene in the middle for good measure.  And by the time that you finally defeat the guy, you will have memorized that cut scene backwards and forwards.  The first time that I played this game it took me, no kidding, maybe 150 tries to beat the guy.  When I finally did, I had maybe two pixels on my health bar and no healing flasks left.  Some of his attacks are so grotesquely unfair that the only way to avoid getting killed by them is to just hope that you get lucky and that he doesn’t use them many times.  It’s truly awful and I’m not exaggerating when I say that this penultimate boss almost singlehandedly ruins what, up until then, is a nearly perfect experience. After you defeat that guy, you go to the final boss, thinking that it must be some sort of epic difficulty confrontation.  And he is al pushover.  Once you figure out his patterns (he only has a few different attacks), you can easily beat him on the 2nd or third try.  I don’t know how you could design a game so near-perfect for the first 98% of it and then stumble so badly with such horribly calibrated boss battles. The final sequences of this game are so profoundly disappointing, and they really left a bad taste in my mouth. The story in Blasphemous 2, like the first game, is largely gobbledygook.  There is, of course, The Miracle.  The Miracle apparently causes nothing but suffering but people still refer to it as a “miracle” for some reason.  You are the Nameless – er, um – The Penitent One, a silent coneheaded guy who is doing penance for some unnamed sin or crime.  An infertile couple is granted a child but apparently that child is diseased or deformed or something, and there is an elevated city above the main city in the game, and a gigantic beating heart there, and you have to defeat 3 bosses to access that city and then beat five more to get five keys to let some birds out of cages – Christ I don’t know.  Like its predecessor, Blasphemous 2 opts entirely for style over substance when it comes to telling its story, preferring to cloak the plot in layer after layer of cryptic dialog and symbolism that makes absolutely zero sense.  There are youtube videos that attempt to untangle this bowl of narrative spaghetti but if I have to watch youtube videos to understand the basics of your plot, then you have failed miserably as a storyteller. Do I recommend Blasphemous 2?  Yes.  Strongly?  No.  In some ways, it is the most improved sequel that I have ever played.  But at a few crucial times, it practically begs you to uninstall it.  For what it’s worth, I have finished it twice, which is fairly unusual for me, so it can’t be bad.  I am hoping for a third game in this series, warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: Just the first game but EVERYTHING is slightly worse. Constant overblown hitstop on attacks messing up your timing and making the game feels like its stuttering. Two interact buttons, why?. Annoying bosses. Annoying awfully designed traversal. The cinematics arent in the pixelated style anymore which makes them looks like a fan made flash cartoon. Every area is 50% stuff you can do now and 50% "Haha you dont have that ability yet come back in 2 days if you even remember this was here!!". Sound glitches where enemy sounds will just stop playing some of the time. Half of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemies are just reused from the first game. The story is somehow even more convoluted than the first one and most of the characters just yap at you about vague "Doth the Miracle eons ago saw fit to rend upon mine flesh these 3 marks... whenst you find all 30 chalices of slime release me from my sin and let me rest" and what they mean is "Come to me when you find this collectible and ill increase your mana or whatever". This game doesn't inspire any kind of wonder or excitement or self reflection on what you did wrong when you die, you just kind of sit back and sigh because the only emotion this game brings out of you is defeated resignation

_childDocuments_.review: Significantly worse combat. Combat abilities from the first game are now spread out over 3 weapons, with each weapon feeling like a lesser version of the Mea Culpa (The primary weapon in the first game). Each weapon feels terrible in their own unique way; the mace cannot parry, the rapier gives a damage bonus which is lost if you take even the smallest amount of chip damage, and the short sword is a copy and paste of Mea Culpa, but without a lunge attack, or charge attack.On top of that, the weapons are buggy. The short sword has a falling plunge attack that will randomly not work (even if the player has enough height), and the mace can ignite and do extra fire damage, but the animation doesn't play half the time, causing the game to stutter. I have never had such frustrating combat in a metroidvania before. My intention was to play through Blasphemous 1 and 2 back to back, and while I had a great time with the first game, the second is a disappointment. I wish I could refund this game. I had a plethora of other issues with this game, but I am way to drained to type anymore. Do not buy this game, its not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: For now the game follows the *true ending* of blasphemous 1. As the game goes on you will get used to it.When I complete the game (get all achvs and 100%) I'll come back here and do a full review.For now, it's looking as good as the first game and I can't wait to play through it again and again.Edit: Just got all achvs for the game; the first one took me 70 hours to get all achvs, the second (as you can see by my playtime) took me 30. _childDocuments_.review: This game was great! I loved it. One of the weapons is obviously much stronger than the other ones, but it was still fun beating the hell out of everything with it. I would say this is a slight improvement on the first one. The bosses were all very unique and fun. I had to stop at the second to last boss, which happens sometimes (or the last one) because he was definitely a lot harder than the other ones, as I have heard. _childDocuments_.review: Not nearly as impactful as the original but still a solid metroidvania with a strong character and aesthetics. The multiple weapons are a nice addition and puzzles, upgrades, and quests are less obtuse. I put a negative review only because it is so similar to the original and because all I remember is the unskippable cutscene before the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: So far about halfway done (propably?) with the game.. only minus I have with the game is downscaling/streamlining of gore kills (which may be good or bad thing depending on the player experiencing it). First game had all sorts of gruesome ways the Penitent one (player) could end their opponent, Now you have the ability to do that.. but many of them have been thrown under an umbrella of "create a cocoon of thorns and squeeze". Granted that not all of them are like this.. some are as remarkably gruesome and they were in the first one.. but all too often you meet the same "cocoon and squeeze" animation. Does this take away from the game? Absolutely not.. a casual player wont even see the difference and instead the few special animations feel like cream on the cake.All I can say is that Blasphemous 2 is a great sequel for blasphemous 1. Now I feel like playing it again just for the kicks (and since there is dlc which I havent yet played).

_childDocuments_.review: I had really high expectations on this sequel and partially they have been satisfied. Blasphemous 2 follows the formula of the previous game with a more fantasy setting and with just one and enourmous difect: the Eviterno boss fight. Christ, I've always loved challenging bossfights but that's too much: unpredictable movesets, too much damage done and bugged damage hitboxes. I hope they fix all because it would be a waste.

_childDocuments_.review: I would definitely recommend this game to others. Having played, and beat, both games, I was not disappointed by the amount of play and style of either. I did have to look up how to solve two side quests (envelope (minor hints) and symbol room (the whole solve)) yet by that point I had already completed everything else and was just going for the achievements factor. _childDocuments_.review: Slightly better than the first game in a lot of ways and less impactful in others. I generally think the first Blasphemous was a solid Metroidvania that got a lot of free points for its incredibly unique atmosphere, but suffered a lot from its very clunky platforming and half-baked combat mechanics. I can safely say that Blasphemous 2  much better than the first, especially when it comes to platforming, though it's ironically weaker in the aspect that made the first instantly memorable: its atmosphere.For anybody unfamiliar with Blasphemous, the game is essentially is a Souls-like/metroidvania set in Custodia, a Spanish Catholic-themed land filled with all kinds of Boschian horrors. You play as the Penitent One, a warrior sworn to silence who struggles against the Miracle, an eldritch entity that inflicts cruel and unusual punishments on the people of Custodia. It's got most of the hallmarks of metroidvania exploration and platforming, with some very light Soulsborne combat thrown in. It's like Hollow Knight, if Hollow Knight was half as fast, half as long, half as hard, and everybody waxed poetic about God.The upgrades Blasphemous 2 brings to the table mostly concern the platforming and the combat. You can quickly swap between three weapons, each with their own set of moves and traversal mechanics. To navigate a puzzle, you might swap between all three in quick succession, avoiding or fighting enemies along the way. Once you get the hang of weaving in and out of each weapon type, platforming is pretty smooth and satisfying, a far cry from the inelegant jumping in the first game.You can also upgrade your weapons if you want to specialize in one or two for combat, using them in conjunction with equipped items to make a kind of poor-man's RPG build. Compared to Hollow Knight, where your equipped charms can make an enormous difference in how you play, the "builds" in Blasphemous 2 largely enhance a weapon's existing strengths, making the whole system feel a little tacked on.What I would've preferred instead were more incentives to switch between the weapons mid-combat. Toggling your weapons is pretty seamless, so why not design some bosses in a way that requires you to swap between weapons to move around the stage or avoid attacks? That'd probably be a bit at odds with the weapon specialization that the game encourages you to shoot for, so it seems like a bit of a missed opportunity.Exploring the map itself is also great, though only for the first half of the game. After you acquire all three weapons and beat the first round of bosses, the map railroads you rather than opens up. This makes collectibles very easy to acquire too. I wound up getting the true ending in the course of finishing the side quests, which all involve collecting items hidden throughout the world or fighting enemy gauntlets. There isn't much backtracking or item combing, as the game does a pretty good job of signaling where and when you'll be able to progress in a given area. On one hand, this is nice as it avoids a lot of time spent reading guides or desperately posting on Reddit asking for advice. On the other hand, it makes the game… pretty easy.The first Blasphemous has a reputation for being hard, and I'd argue it's more due to that aforementioned clunky platforming. Now that it's been cleaned up, I found Blasphemous 2 kind of a cakewalk. The platforming is smooth and satisfying, but there is no equivalent of the Path of Pain from Hollow Knight, something (optional) to truly test a player's skill.The bosses are mostly fun, yet the hardest one for me, the penultimate boss, only took 4-5 tries. I breezed through the final boss on a single try. I was fuming by the time I was finished with Escribar in Blasphemous 1, though your mileage may vary on whether or not the easier difficulty is a good thing or not.Otherwise, all the things that hit from Blasphemous 1 still hit here: the music somehow manages to top the first's arrangement, the pixel art is still gorgeous, the general aesthetic is to die for. That being said, some of the artistic decisions baffle me a little.The pixel art may still be gorgeous, but it's a bit less detailed in 2, and there's more of a reliance upon animated cutscenes. In my opinion, they really clash with the aesthetic. None of it really compares to the Penitent One slapping on a helmet full of blood, or Escribar's visage slowly opening over the course of the game.The enemy design, while still good, also doesn't hit as hard for reasons I can't quite place. Some areas in the game feel a little more generically fantasy, like the sunken temple or the spooky forest, and (this may just be me) the color palette of the game feels lighter. These are small items, though they add up over the course of the game.The only part of the game that I found totally negative was its increased emphasis on story. A lot of people might herald this as a welcome change from the obtuse delivery of the original, which I can respect, but all the extra conversations and cutscenes only served to remind me how goofy the game's dialogue is. It may be because I specialized in renaissance history, and especially religious history, during college, and am biased as a result, but it feels like the game uses a lot of Catholic buzzwords without unpacking them. Everything feels very belabored and put upon, like purple prose that's masquerading as "authentic" because of its unique aesthetic.It's not bad by any means, but compare it to something like Legacy of Kain, where the purple prose serves to illustrate more fleshed out characters, as opposed to just rambling about guilt and sin and holiness to pad out every voiced line of dialogue. The first game was charming precisely because it was so minimalistic. Add heaps of cutscenes and optional quests to that and you really drive home that there's more setting than story behind most of it.Anyway, most of those complaints are pretty small. If you liked Blasphemous 1, you'll like Blasphemous 2, because it's just that game, but slightly better in most regards.

_childDocuments_.review: A very, very solid title for Metroidvania lovers. Game-play elements are built on top of what the first part did. The world map is slightly more complicated and bigger than before, but becomes easily accessible for backtracking once you've progressed farther in the game.If you're a seasoned Metroidvania player, this game is not the most difficult of them all. I would say it's of "medium" difficulty when considering a game like Aeterna Noctis to be much harder. Only one boss took more than 5-10 attempts to beat.There's enough "precision" platforming to go around but it's not over done at all.The music is spectacular, the pixel graphics are excellent and the whole concept / theme of the game is very, very, well executed. Hats off the dev for parts 1 and 2. I eagerly await part 3.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is one of those sequels that's two steps forward, two steps back.  The presentation's great as ever; nice animation, good music, very moody ambiance, nice sound effects, the fantastic Spanish audio included from the start.  The minute to minute gameplay is well improved from the first; the Penitent One controls more smoothly, the new movement mechanics are well implemented.  The new weapon trio is great; outside of changing the early game and affecting what secrets and paths you can take contingent on your starting choice, they all have different styles, and let you lean into the parry-and-counter style of the first game, a rapid fire high risk/reward dual wield set, or just ignore blocking entirely and crush things with the censer (which I used for almost the entire game and adored).  Letting you equip a "quick" prayer and a bigger effect together mean a lot less menuing to deal with situations you encounter.  Splitting character "equipment" into altarpieces for general character customization and the rosary beads for general resistances and bonuses is a good way to handle things.  Some of the nice QoL features from the first game's DLCs also show up and make things smooth going as well, like altar teleporting.  B2 is a lot of fun to just run around and fight in.That said, while the specific moment to moment gameplay is a marked improvement, the game also falls apart compared to the first game in some fairly significant and damaging ways.  After a strong opening act, Blasphemous 2 goes extremely linear in a fashion that doesn't live up to the first game and takes a lot of the joy of exploration from getting new tools and upgrades away.  The boss design is fairly uninspired.  A lot of the general creepy religious-monkey's-paw aesthetic and design from the first game is lacking; the NPCs mostly feel like retreads or just imitations of the first game, which means that the sequel doesn't have that same level of oppressive dread that kept the first game going (the animated cutscenes, which are good quality animation, also feel like they're working at odds to the pixel artwork style).  Quest design is abysmal; it really doesn't matter what choices you make in dealing with NPCs, because at the end of the day you can just go buy the other quest reward(s) you didn't get based on your handling and get everything anyway (the only missables I'm aware of are a bonus health/fervor upgrade for dealing with the related NPCs in a specific fashion).  And while the first game's alternate ending (pre-DLC) was somewhat esoteric to unlock, it also didn't force you to effectively 100% the map to get either.I'm hopeful they can elevate Blasphemous 2 with DLCs like the first game, which ended in a far, far stronger place than it began.  I still mostly enjoyed my time with Blasphemous 2, and would recommend it for Metroidvania fans or folks who liked the aesthetic of the first game but bounced off the extreme difficulty curve (or the spiked pits), but as it stands right now I'm going to be far more inclined to go do another NG+ cycle of the first game than play through Blasphemous 2 again.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting a long time for blasphemous 2 to come out since I'm a fan of the first part of the game.What can I say?There are minuses, did not like that artifacts now clearly show you which of them does what, that is, you can not read the description, you can immediately see which one is better. Also as far as I remember in the first part you could put more rosary beads.Also developers for some reason in this part decided to remove the human bones that were in the first part scattered throughout Custodia. Each bone wanted to find and find out what its history is, and it gave us more information about the lore of the world. I would like to see a DLC that would add the bones with the history of the people they belonged to.The history of the world would like to open more strongly, to know what happened during this thousand years.Many people liked that now you don't die when you fall on the spikes, I still liked it better when the penitent died falling on them, it made me play more carefully.I would also very much like it would be that the screensavers were in pixel graphics, and so in the first part in the pixel, in the second graphics in the screensavers are similar to vector, I would like that the developers would stick to one style. For some reason in this part there are no skins on the penitent, yes I understand that they changed only his coloring, but still hope that in the future it will be corrected.Now the pluses, visually all locations are very beautifully looked, and as it seemed to me that they became more than in the first part, I want to explore everything everywhere well, characters and enemies are also drawn perfectly, there are no questions)Three types of weapons, and each of which can be pumped, and naturally the tactics of battle with each weapon will be different. But still miss the mea culpa.Musical accompaniment on high, as in the first part.I liked that in addition to artifacts added tree statuettes that also give various positive characteristics of the character.My verdict, the game is beautiful, I wish the developers would release DLC that would tell more about the lore of the game, as well as would give the third true ending, and further continuation of the game.So fans of the game, put a like on my review, maybe then the developers will see it, and we will wait for DLC, as well as blasphemous 3 with its unique atmosphere of the world, and unique music.And who hasn't bought the game yet, make sure you buy it, support good developers and good game:)And may your heart be in sorrow, penitent one.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Blasphemous 2, I really liked the smooth gameplay and the choice of 3 weapons. It's an easy recommendation for any Metroidvania lover but i can't help but feel it is a downgrade from the first game. I don't mind the anime cut-scenes i actually enjoyed them. In the 24 hours that i played it i only finished it once with both endings. I know that mea culpa was disentegrated as per the canon ending of the first game, i still prefer the sword over the 3 new weapons. Bosses are tougher and more challenging imo in this game and i enjoyed overcoming them especially that mf Eviterno (the penultimate boss) at the end which reminds me of the final boss of the game F.I.S.T (forged in shadow torch). I encountered the same bugs as some people did which is sometimes music stops out of nowhere and sometimes whenever i enter an area it doesn't show me the name of the area i only hear the music of the new area. WTF do you mean i can not hit above me vertically only can hit diagonally when i am in the air???? for some reason the tall enemies with mace reminded me of the villains of the basketball match in space jam movie :D

_childDocuments_.review: +The graphics and audio are nice.The combat is fun, easy to pick up, and generally smooth.The map is well-made, easily customizable, and it's easy to return to specific places for thorough exploration.The Metroidvania system is well-implemented.Decent playtime.Fairly easy, not stressful.-The story is just okay.The bosses lack a bit of flair in both their gameplay and design, and they are easily forgettable.Even though they are in the minority, some "quests" won't be completed without a wiki.+/-My playthrough of the first game was a long time ago, but I remember the feeling of playing a 2.5D Dark Souls, which I didn't feel at all with this one.Almost all the fights are relatively simple, with death having almost no impact anyway, which can be seen as a downside. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, this seems like a decent sequel. However, there's a few issues that might make you want to buy it on sale, or set a timer so you can make use of the Steam return policy. (Since there's no demo.)1. When you start the game, you have to choose one of three weapons, without enough time to get a proper feel for them. (Unless you want to sit there fighting the training-dummy / -ghost and not, you know. playing the game.) Very unusual for a game that otherwise lets you swap out powers, equipment, etc basically at will. (Or at least in town or a shrine.)2. The cutscenes are all high-res cartoons, instead of being pixellated like the ones in the original, or like the rest of the game, UI, etc. Somewhat jarring.3. In the cutscenes, the actors also sound (to me) a lot more pompous? Maybe the voice direction or scripting was just a bit worse this time around.It's not a bad game by any means, but definitely feels more like it's just "OK" this time around.

_childDocuments_.review: If Blasphemous 1 was gourmet food with amazing desserts (DLC updates) then this feels like video game junk food in comparison.It's a decent game but it's vastly overshadowed by its prequel and the standards it set. Difficulty is lukewarm at best, Story is hardly present - more of a mediocre excuse for one, not even the NPCs you meet on your journey are particularly memorable at all.The game is -fun- in terms of receiving a constant stream of metroidvania dopamines until you get the 100% map completion, but that's about it. Get upgrades, collect items, explore the map, light platforming, hack and slash enemies with a couple bosses thrown into the mix (out of which even the somewhat challenging one took <10 attempts in total). Before you know it the game's over and you feel like you've sat in one of the many metroidvania treadmills out there rather than something that even attempted to come close to the lightning in a bottle that was Blasphemous 1.Each of my criticisms are things that the original game perfected from the get go, so it's a real shame that this game feels like an AI-created sequel. None of the believable world building or atmosphere has been carried over and neither has the quality of the satisfyingly challenging gameplay.I initially defended the game considering everyone had B1 to get used to the rough game formula so all of those reports of "game too easy" are to be taken with a grain of salt; but after finishing the game and seeing the incredibly lackluster ending(s) I'm inclined to agree that overall this is a disappointing sequel to a dearly beloved indie metroidvania that managed to elevate itself from the rest.This one just feels like one of the many forgettable ones instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics – 7/10Sound –910Gameplay – 9/10Story – 6/10Replayability – 8/10Overall – Blasphemous II takes the formula from Blasphemous and many other pixel art style Metroidvania games and really turns it up a notch. The exploration feels fun, and all things considered; this game has many combat improvements from the first game. The combat feels smoother and flows much better than the previous game, you’re also presented with different ways to play with the three different weapons and how different they feel from one another. Your choice of starting weapon lends to a unique style of exploration as many of the map unlocks are hidden behind additional weapon abilities, this means that you’ll never unlock the map the same way twice on further play throughs. The boss fights can feel frustrating at times, but the mechanics are fair and just take a bit of getting used to.  Highly Recommended. 🖥️ System Specs Intel i9 13900K | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 FE | DDR5 32GB RAM | Alienware AW3423DWF 3440 x 1440 165Hz

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first one, this is a pretty cool metroidvania with some unique qualities but I just can't recommend it without caveats. First the good: the very weird and disturbing religious tone is still awesome and the graphics are amazing.The combat starts out a bit slow, but it gets fast and fun as you level up. Discovering secrets and new paths is fun. Sometimes you are stumped about where to go next however, but that's how it goes in a metroidvania.The bad: everything feels just a bit worse than in the first game. Story-wise, less is more guys! The first one gave you some space to experience the world in a good pace. This one there is a lot of exposition.The combat is a bit more tedious as enemies feel very spongy. I ended up basically skipping entire screens of enemies as it was just not fun to hack away at them for minutes. In the endgame it improves a lot but that's no excuse, I should want to kill everything that moves because it's fun throughout the whole game, like in the first one! And finally the difficulty: It is all over the place. It felt much easier than the first one at first. Bosses were better as it usually only took 4-5 tries to figure them out, which is the sweet spot for me. But then the final boss has such a large spike that I actually just lost interest in the whole ending. It is not fun to grind a boss for half an hour inching away at his life with fully upgraded gear. If you like this kind of games you will have some fun, but it left a sour taste in my mouth for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW WILL BE EDITED THROUGHOUT MY PERSONAL GAME PLAY As someone that went into this game with the intention to 100% it and being obsessed with the first game, things are not looking good. Speaking on only an hour of game play, so far I am not loving this nearly as much as the first game. The best way I can list my grievances is to, well, make a list. To simplify, it's going to consist of a couple subjects and I'll start with things changed from the previous game, and things that were just straight up removed.Changes>Cartoonish drawn cutscenes that have a jarringly different style from the game itself>Unique executions are nonexistent for some new enemies with most of them sharing the same animation >Movement has a very weird and flighty low-grav feeling while feeling like you have way less mobility>Voice acting and dialogue quality seems to have plummeted drastically compared to the first game where each line felt like it was given by the character and not just someone playing a character>Parrying enemies now has layered timing beyond just one result of a riposte. If done at the incorrect time, it'll only do a partial parry, resulting in you being pushed anywhere between 1 to 5 inches across the screen, this new addition has has resulted in my being kicked out of a room an INNUMERABLE amount of times if the parry timing is slightly off, only a perfect parry will allow you to do a riposte.Removed>Air Impulse/Latern Jumping has been removed from the game! This was my favorite combat/movement mechanic from the previous game and its removal is tragic to me

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't too crazy about the original Blasphemous, so I was a bit hesitant to check out this game.  I'm glad I did.  This is an improvement in every way on the original, and the result is an excellent, well-crafted metroidvania that is enjoyable the whole way through.  The bosses are all great, if a bit on the easy side for the most part, the areas are fun to traverse and explore to find secrets, and the puzzles and platforming challenges to get extra experience points, quest items, and other upgrades are satisfying to complete.  As with Blasphemous 1, this game has lore for each item and spell you pick up if you like diving deep into that and getting some background on the story and world.  I have no big criticisms of the game, I think it's excellent at what it tries to do, and overall a very strong metroidvania that anyone who enjoys the genre would like.  There are a few nitpicks I have, such as some animations not playing properly, the music acting oddly at points, disappearing for a bit and then coming back in all of the sudden, and the presence of one major glitch that made it so I had to redo a combat trial for one sidequest twice, but it seems to be a decently rare occurrence,  so most people probably won't have issues with it.  None of these detract from the overall experience in any way that would ruin it, although the glitch can make it a bit tedious on the off chance it does happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I find this to be a very good game, although it doesn't feel right to say it's miles better than the first one. -The artstyle is still amazing, but i don't like the overall look of the game ( for example the HUD), it looks like it'a a mix of two different styles and I'm not crazy about it. - There are now three weapons; it's cool to use them all in different ways and it also works very well for the platforming side of the game, which was kinda wack in the first one. _childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is an exceptional game and, in my opinion, one of the finest Metroidvania titles out there. While the game doesn't bring significant innovation to the Metroidvania formula, its impeccable execution and one of the most captivating settings/art I've seen make it a strong recommendation for anyone interested in the genre or looking to try a game within it.- The Setting: This is the standout feature - incredibly unique, drawing inspiration from Spanish Catholicism with elements of horror and gore. It's simultaneously horrifying and oddly comforting. You'll find it hard to look away from the absurd and messed up design of some of its NPCs. Tip: Put the VO in Spanish language for extra immersion- The Pixel Art: Arguably the best I've seen in recent years. I often found myself stopping to look at the views. Many screens could easily pass as paintings in their own right.- The Music: Several pieces are stuck in my head. Once again, the Spanish influence shines through, with Spanish guitars and rhythms that are wonderful.- The weapon system: I found this aspect very intriguing and well-designed, with each weapon offering unique combat options while also helping in exploration - Combat and platforming are generally tight and enjoyable, making backtracking and searching for new items a satisfying experience- Steep Difficulty Spike Towards the End: There's a significant difficulty spike with the second-to-last boss (and the area just before it). While I usually embrace a good challenge and don't mind repeated attempts on bosses, the fact that this boss has unskippable dialogue and cutscenes - albeit not very long - nearly made the fight unenjoyable. Still, the boss fight itself, while challenging, was fun to learn and satisfying when I finally beat it. Just be aware that this might not be your cup of tea and could become frustrating towards the end of a long playthrough if you're not particularly into this type of encounter.- Story/Lore: I expected an ambiguous and subtle/soft world-building approach (common in the Metroidvania/Soulslike genres), which the game succeeds at to some extent. However, some aspects left me somewhat unsatisfied. In particular, some of the bosses didn't receive the narrative depth I had hoped for, making it challenging to connect with their backstories.This is a phenomenal game, absolutely worth playing, and I'll be eagerly following whatever the team does next!

_childDocuments_.review: Fiiinally just got the last achievement (Flawless Penance, done on the final boss because I'm stupid) of this beautiful game.I adored the first, and the sequel has lived up to and exceeded the expectations set by it.The 'multiple weapons' was not exactly what I had imagined, but it's done in a unique and very metroidvania way, and it adds a lot to the game. Most of the bosses felt very fun and engaging, especially as you gain more abilities and progress further in the game.I have thoroughly enjoyed exploring the beautiful, beautiful pixel art world of this game, and the combat is even better than it was in the first. I believe pretty much every bug I encountered when I first started playing (within a week of release) have been fixed by the time I finished.I am a little sad there's no NG+, but I imagine that will come in time - I also assume there may be more (paid or more likely free) DLC added down the line, but I am not certain of that.I enjoyed the story, the cutscenes and all the NPCs. The VO was great - in both English and Spanish. The sound design in general is amazing, it adds a lot to the combat and gameplay, and the soundtrack is yet again beautiful.Definitely recommend, for fans of the first game, and for fans of both soulslikes and metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: Even aside from the remaining bugs, I do feel this game is roundly a downgrade from the first, which was a game I wasn't expecting to like but ended up enjoying a LOT lot. And it's not like 2 is particularly worse than 1 in any major ways... just a lot of little ways that add up. And, don't get me wrong, it's still GOOD, quite good - but, it's like going from a 9/10 to an 8/10. The magic just isn't there this time.Specifics? Well, one, I'm just not thrilled about having three weapons. I think the weapons, individually, are all good, all have their uses, I bounced between them all fairly regularly, and the puzzles and platforming involved with each of them are pretty fun, too! But... none of them feel as versatile or as -good- as your standard blasphemous 1 sword. All the different moves that game had got doled out between the sword and the daggers in this one, with the mace kinda just being its own thing, so I always feel like I'm playing with an incomplete kit - and parrying, while, one, feeling nerfed in this game, also just doesn't feel as useful - I swear bosses have way more unblockable magic attacks than they used to, or attacks you can't really counter even if you can parry.I'm also not a fan of all the extra steps the game adds to powering up this time around - it was already true of some upgrades in the last game, true, but now even basic health and mana increases require you to drag quest items to NPCs, which are a lot more spread out than they were last time, too. And the game still has as many obtuse puzzles and quest items as before, though at the very least nothing truly missable this time. Rosary beads feel less useful, basically just existing as two or three tiers of the same few defensive capabilities and all the cool ones got doled out to the altarpieces instead, which, okay, fair, and those can be pretty fun to play around with - once you unlock the ability to change them from save points, anyways.Bosses do feel roundly harder in this game, and combat is generally faster-paced as a result of the higher level of movement you have, and I'm mixed about some of them - more aerial bosses than last time, I feel, which COMPLETELY nerfs the sword and its reliance on ground combos, and doesn't feel great with the daggers or mace, either, though the mace generally fares best in the air out of all three. Oh, by the way, the enemy bounce is just. Gone. Not even something you can eventually get back. I miss it so much. Was a cool, fun mechanic that had both platforming and combat applications. Anyways, so Odon is the worst boss across both games, easily. I just. Do not think mob fights are ever fun - dude would be fine on his own, but the addition of enemies, even relatively weak but numerous ones, suggests the devs thought the boss wasn't interesting enough on its own (it was - the pre-fight proved that imo). And the battle arenas, carried over from the first game, also feel like a mess this time - instead of themed areas with different arenas, you get one bare-bones arena and a random scattering of enemies, which are already more palette swap-y than they were in the first game, usually two or three different elemental varieties of the same enemy types.And, my least favorite change - the back half of the game is COMPLETELY linear. The first half? Very open, and very fun. The back half, new areas literally don't appear until you kill the boss of the previous one. And I really don't get why it had to be that way. The areas themselves are cool and fun, but being ghost train ridden through them all in what was originally a wide-open exploration game just feels baaad.I gripe but, again, I had a lot of fun with this game - the combat, when it works, and that's most of the time, is really fun and a fresh take on the first game's combat, and the introduction of new movement abilities, often integrated into the fights, goes a long way in facilitating that. And the platforming and puzzles are better than ever here - no instakill spikes or pits this time, for one, but the bigger toolset of moves just leads to more interesting platforming. Though I lament the loss of really clever stuff like falling in pits to go to lower areas and take shortcuts or get treasures you couldn't otherwise get but, ehh, the novelty of that would probably wear off if they repeated it. I still think this game is a good fun time, worth its asking price etc. but it doesn't feel as "special" as the first game did, or as unique - just another good metroidvania with the lightest of light souls-like elements.

_childDocuments_.review: "Plasphemous 2" is a visually stunning masterpiece that continues to captivate players with its mesmerizing pixel art. The intricate details and hauntingly beautiful landscapes immerse players in a world of dark beauty and despair. The introduction of new weapon mechanics adds a refreshing layer of versatility to the gameplay, allowing players to experiment with different combat styles and strategies.The game's non-linear storytelling and the introduction of new mysteries create an enthralling sense of exploration and discovery. Players are constantly challenged to remember their steps and retrace their paths to uncover hidden secrets and unlock new areas. This non-linear approach adds depth and complexity to the gameplay, keeping players engaged and eager to explore every corner of the game world."Plasphemous 2" is a testament to the power of pixel art in conveying emotion and atmosphere. With its innovative weapon mechanics, non-linear storytelling, and captivating mysteries, it offers a gaming experience that is both haunting and unforgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that I ask for in a metroidvania.Some fans of Blasphemous 1 will hate it, due to how different it is at points. Three weapons, human-sized bosses, different art direction, lesser difficulty level, and so on. Other fans will love it for those same differences. Three weapons means more combat variety. Human-sized bosses will sport different movesets and feel faster-paced at times. Different art direction is a matter of taste. Lesser difficulty level is partly because spikes no longer 1-shot you like the cheap bastards they are.The game is different from Blasphemous 1, and I think whether or not you enjoy it is going to somewhat hinge on whether or not you're okay with something different. 2 isn't a perfect game. The enemies don't always feel as cool as they did in the first game. Some of the bosses feel easier, too. And sure, the art is different. But it also has things like greatly enhanced combat, cool levels with fun music, some neat lore, and some bosses which, thought not always the hardest, were genuinely cool, and a joy to fight.This game is different. If you're okay with that, and want a good metroidvania with some fun action and great music, you'll have a good time. If you're looking for Blasphemous 1 all over again, you won't get that here. Personally, I'm okay with that, but maybe you're not, and that's fine too. But me? I recommend it. Like, a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was negative, but my friends convinced me to change it to positive since I liked the game. I hope you still take the time to read my criticisms.Ok, im lying. I do recommend this game. But, I have to leave a negative review. This is great game, but its such a downgrade compared to it's predecessor, I have to leave a negative review because it erks me that it has a high percentage of positive reviews. This game has a lot of what made the first game great. If you're like me and loved the first game, you'll enjoy this game. It's more of what you loved, and is a great metroidvania.But the first blasphemous is a masterpiece. Not acknowledging that this is a downgrade is a disservice to the love put into the first game. To get the least important complaint out of the way: this game is buggy. Twice I jumped while charging the flail attack and got stuck in the charge until i restarted the game. Sometimes the flail's little animation to start the fire doesn't play, and I just get stuck standing there. No spoilers, but a character who appears during some boss fights tanks the fps when they show up. Next, the art. The beautiful, gritty pixel art cut scenes of the first game gone and replaced by still, unmoving hand-drawn stills. While the art is good, and I'd have no complaints had I not played the first game, it PALES in comparison to the first games incredible cut scenes. The new art feels cartoony and really does not fit the majesty of the playable world. The animations of the enemies clearly have less love put in. Not focusing on the old crone who has a glitch in her animation so that sometimes two of her frames overlay each other, there's other places its clear less time was put in. Way less enemies have unique executions. Many just stay in their hitstun animation while you summon a cone of vines around them to crush them ( a copy, pasted animation).Lastly, this game reuses enemies way more than the first. It especially sucks because the devs insisted on reusing the giant brutes who tank damage like crazy. I never remember feeling like any enemies were sponges in the first game.This game is great. But these devs can do better than great. I started this game because recently a coworker asked me if I think any metroidvania is as good as Hollow Knight, and blasphemous was my answer. But I couldn't say the same about blasphemous II. They were clearly ambitious, and the weapon system is awesome. This game is so good, but it could have been better. My guess is that the devs had time constraints, since they licensed with much bigger companies for this game. I always worry, when games have less time put into stuff like animation, that devs will see that and think no one cared about animation. The first game is art. I hope the devs release an update revamping these flaws, so blasphemous II can stand with it's parent as two of the greatest metroidvanias ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: GOTYBoth this, and B1 are this weird ephemeral sort of game that I can't truly put into words why I love them so. It's the atmosphere and the music and the combat and the voice acting and everything ever put into a game. I could go on and on about every perfect step that both games in this series took.The soundtrack for this game is genuinely beautiful, I'm even willing to argue perfect in every sense. Every area was a new song, and a new 5 minute break from me to just sit there and be marveled at every single instrument and note.The visual designs of enemies never missed once, it was all clear, and crisp. I could tell when they were attacking and the visual cue of an attack was better telegraphed than any 3D combat game I could think of.The voice acting is amazing. Both English and the native Spanish dubs are amazing. It all just sounds so well and each voice a perfect match to what I see on the screen.My only real complaint is maybe the lack of *meaning* behind the weapons in this game. B1 had this insane lore behind the most basic sword that the Penitent One had, made even deeper with the DLC. B2 on the other hand just gives us 3 weapons, and beyond the text blurbs they have in the inventory, and the statue carvings you can get relating to each weapon, it seems not much was actually imporant about them. They're *just* weapons, as compared to B1's Mea Culpa being this insane piece of craftwork that I get even really explain without spoiling that games story.It doesn't seem really fair to compare a game to it's predecessor, but with a game that is a direct sequel like this, it's warranted, at least a little. It's still amazing though, all of it is.10/10 on all fronts

_childDocuments_.review: My first encounter with the work of The Game's Kitchen was with their point & click pixel art adventure: The Last Door, a game that to this day I still like very much. However, it doesn't end there, as I later played its sequel and was even more enchanted with the world they had created, and with the continuation of a very enigmatic but captivating story. So what does this have to do with Blasphemous 2? When the developers announced the first, I was excited thinking that perhaps it would be a new installment on The Last Door’s saga, and that it would delve deeper into the world behind the "veil" (I recommend playing The Last Door to understand this, sorry!), but I found myself with something quite different and that tried a new approach; a bloody and unforgiving world in which I immersed myself, and ended up amazed. Blasphemous exceeded my expectations and those of the general public, and even if it was of a completely different genre to what I knew from the team, I loved how they approached it. Now I find myself once again in this situation, with a sequel that proves once again that the developers have it clear when it comes to continuing their sagas. Blasphemous 2 far surpasses its predecessor, adding new mechanics and improvements that elevate the experience to a new level, and that left me very satisfied. This time, the story will take a different course; the miracle will give birth to a new event, and the Penitent one will wake up from his rest to once again put on his shoulders an arduous task. But standing in his way will be the Achicofradía, a group of penitents who were welcomed by the miracle as its defenders; an arduous and very fitting challenge for our character. If I can add anything, it is that without a doubt the religious setting is maintained and deepened, and it’s an aspect that really catches my attention.As in the first game, the  will be revealed to us little by little, with a lot of cryptic dialogue and at the hands of several new characters. On the other hand, we’ll also have some side quests, assignments and legends that we can follow if we want. In my case, I got quite lost in the world looking to complete these "quests", although some are easier to track than others. Overall, I really enjoyed this section, the narration is interesting and the fact that there is voice acting for the characters made me enjoy the experience so much more. On a side note, this sequel also features different endings; I'll leave it at that.The  remains fairly similar from the first game, being the classic metroidvania gameplay, with platforming, combat and exploration being the main focus. However, the character's movements felt more fluid and precise this time around, and there are several other new tidbits I'd like to comment on; by the way, we finally have a double jump! But what impressed me the most was that we now have three weapons at our disposal: the classic sword, dual blades, and a mace with a chain (my favorite). Each of them has its own characteristics, such as different attack speed or movements, and they have skill trees to improve their repertoire of techniques or increase the damage inflicted by them. But the most interesting thing about this is that they also have unique mechanics for exploration; an example would be the mace, with which we can ring huge bells that materialize surfaces or open certain doors. Having them interact both with combat and exploration left me ecstatic, truth be told.Beyond our arsenal of weapons, we’ll also have rosary beads; objects that will give us passive bonuses such as more defense against physical attacks, to give an example. We can also make use of prayers, divided between chants and verses; powerful spells and prayers, among which we’ll find from electric or blood attacks, to gigantic pillars of light that will rain judgment on our enemies. But something that stands out a lot, along with the new weaponry, is the Retablo de Favores and the carved sculptures that can be equipped on it to grant us powerful advantages, and which have special combinations depending on the ones they’re paired with. This addition, while quite similar to the rosary beads (as both are passive systems), I quite liked and it felt more interactive, letting me try out different statuettes to see if I could get those combos unlocked. In short, there are varied systems and mechanics that are very entertaining, and make the section feel robust and very complete.In terms of , the game returns to that beautiful pixel aesthetic, with muted and gloomy tones that create a very unique atmosphere. In addition, we’ll also be able to see animated cinematics, both in digital and pixel art, which are super neat and feel great from start to finish. The design of characters and bosses maintains that peculiarity that represented so much of the first game, the panoramas and environments are desolate and hopeless at times, and everything is very bloody, raw; I loved it. The   is excellent, just like in the first game. From suspenseful and calm melodies, to more lively ones between combat and dangerous areas; and in my opinion, those that make use of masterfully played guitars stand out a lot. The voice acting, both in Spanish and English, was impeccable and very immersive, and it is one of the few times where I have constantly changed the language of the voices to appreciate the differences. Both sections, visual and audio, left me fully satisfied, and absorbed in this particular world. In , Blasphemous 2 gives us a new and interesting story, improves practically all its aspects and mechanics, from exploration to combat, and even gives us at last a real double jump ability, which affirms it as a full-fledged metroidvania! I must admit that I had a couple of moments where I felt a bit bummed, like being hit in the middle of the getting up animation (which in "challenge" rooms, where many enemies spawn, can be a pain), and having to replay some cinematics several times when losing against the bosses they belonged to (although this is fixed by getting good haha!); but, all in all, I was delighted with the game, and I feel it was a marvelous sequel. Without any hesitation, I invite you to enter this religious world, and do your penance; whether you are a fan of the previous game or not, I think you can appreciate it either way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more approachable than the first one in regards to combat and story, and there are more things in place to prevent you from soft-locking yourself out of side quests. This one feels like its better for casual metroidvania players than the first, and its better for people that are here for the combat rather than the exploration. The exploration feels more rewarding in this one in my opinion. The side quests are generally shorter and less tedious than the original, primarily because there are less collectibles and items needed for upgrades and what not. Over all, I think this one is better made than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I must say, as a very big fan of MetroidVanias, and more of a fair-weather fan of the "souls-like" aspect, I was hesitant to try this one out. Boy, am I glad I did.I will start by saying I never played the first one (and I've since started playing it), so coming to this completely fresh and having watched a few reviews, I can definitely recommend this game.The controls are fluid, intuitive, and responsive. The difficulty is tough, but fair. The penalty for dying isn't as steep as it may seem, and there's a good deal of secrets and lore to uncover.I've read complaints from others about how this game changed the animation style for the cutscenes from the first to the second game, and for me personally, I didn't mind it. Some said it jars you away from the "pixelated" retro feel; but you can take this how you will, I didn't find it all that annoying or intrusive.The bosses are fun, just tough enough to keep you trying, but not so frustrating that you just have to give up. This game is all about learning enemy techniques and avoiding, countering, or outsmarting them. Each new area offers lots of stuff that's just out of reach (as is typical of the genre), and the map screen lets you add various markers so you can remember to come back later.The incentive for finding secrets is pretty nice too, makes going back for 100% completion much more approachable. This game also added 3 different weapons, as opposed to the main weapon used throughout the game. You start off by choosing one of the three, leaving you to progress through the game to find the others (and you will need all of them to fully progress, so don't fret).After having put in about 20 hours through this game and near 100% completion, I can say that this was one time I didn't mind picking up a game that was sure to kick my ass in spots. You should do the same, you won't regret it.Just don't drop your guilt...

Furthermore the speech bits are unskippable; just have a retry option and skip the pointless bits. Shame, 1st was great, this is a huge let down.

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to say I was disappointed. Lets start with the great stuff.Pixel art is fantastic, the music is wonderful. There are some gameplay elements that I think are very cool and there are interesting locations.-I had a bug where the Unfinished Lullaby NPC would never speak to me, have the items and no dice.-The time stop is jank as all hell. Boss behaviors going weird, appearing and disappearing hitboxes, some stuff doesn't stop and some stuff does. Its all over the place. Does not feel good.-Second to last boss has a simple first phase that you have to do and then watch a cutscene to get to the tough as nails second phase every time. Serious drawback, made me very frustrated.-And the story. The story was my favorite part of the first game. The game was grusome because it was about pain, about suffering and asking why culturally we seem to revere it by making this suffering grotesque and calling it a miracle. The tone was quite somber. Thematically it was rich and had multiple facets playing out across its world.This game seems to lift the gruesome aesthetic and setting then throw elements together, I can't get a bead on what this game has to say. It seems to revel in the visual style because it can, not because the story has something to discuss related to it. Maybe I just don't understand this game, but I came away not understanding the plot or the themes, and those were elements of the game I was REALLY looking forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the first one, so definitely had to give this one a go. A lot of reviews complained that the second half was too linear. It is indeed linear, but you gain abilities that you can use throughout the first half to re-explore and pick up the goodies that you missed. I actually like version 2 more than Blasphemous 1. You get a double jump and an air dash. This improves the gameplay a lot to me. The weapons being tied to traversal was a bit annoying at first until I collected them all. Having skill trees for each weapon is great. The game is basically an onion, so as you progress more and more layers get revealed. Solid recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I really was shocked to see so much negativity posted on the discussion board of B2.  B1 created high expectations and the sequel has surpassed every one of them.  It seems so many people expect a sequel to be a carbon copy of the first game with new content.  That is DLC friends.  Sequels are supposed to be innovative to keep a franchise fresh.  If you don't like the animated cutscenes, go play B1 again.  There is no reason for hate, it runs and plays smoothly and has it's own unique feel while keeping the lore intact.  The price tag is well worth it.  4.5/5 game
