_childDocuments_.review: Here's My Review For Hollowbody. There are minor spoilers so if you care stop reading here (the game is enjoyable if you must know, especially if you like old horror game style). The game isn't very long if you just focus on the story and maneuvering past enemies. I beat it in about a little over 4 hours while reading texts you can find for world building and looking at all the cut scenes. It was a neat game that gives you the vibes of a silent hill game with some elements of resident evil and other older games in the genre (maybe a little obscure too). The atmosphere is done really well and the tone of the game suits it very well too. I enjoyed the art-style of the characters and enemies. It was an overall enjoyable experience for me. I very much recommend this game to anyone interested in this genre. The positives: -Gameplay is great for those who enjoy old school horror games. Even includes tank controls-The voice acting is good and serves the story well. -The game has extras like first person mode, big head mode and harder difficulties for replayability. Have to beat game first to unlock of course.  -A good price for whats there and not a very long drawn out game-visual damage. Can see how damaged you are without needing to go into menu to see health.-Some hidden secrets and things to see that you have to go out your way to access but nice addition. The negatives: -Melee did not seem to work correctly. Never got to swing any of the melee weapons because I just couldn't.  -Some of the dialog in the documents you find have some typos or worded very strangely. -Not many, if any, boss battles and very little enemy variety.-have leeches that run along the ground but they don't really attack you unless you literally stand still.  -music will cut out at times but nothing too distracting.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I really get into writing this review I'll just say: buy it. Seriously, just buy it.  Block out like 5 hours, get in a dark room and just go.I'll start with my small list of things that are technically criticisms (but I think could be fixed pretty easily) since I wanna just gush about this already:-There are a few times in the game where it wants you to press A (or E if you're on keyboard) to further the dialogue and then there are times where you'll see the A prompt but then it'll auto continue and it's never super clear why that is. Could be an easy fix, small issue in the grand scheme of things.-There's a few times where a small amount of items/doors can be a littttttle hard to see due to the camera angles, but again another small issue that can be easily fixed.-There are a small handful of items that require a ridiculously precise angle to grab. That can absolutely be fixed with a few tweaks so I'm sure before long it'll be fixed!-The map has the typical red door on the map means locked and blue means good. I would have liked to see red for locked, blue for good, and some other color for doors that are inaccessible. I know in other 2000's eras games they'd mark it with an X, so maybe that?Now my only two gripes:-The combat is a little... clunky. Specifically the melee weapons honestly. Bit of learning curve when it comes to learning how far away you can be to hit enemies, and the act of hitting them looks a bit strange some times and feels a bit strange too. I think the guns are perfectly fine, maybe could use a bit more weight to them in the animations but again totally fine! -My other gripe is the lack of  Spoilered that because some people really don't want to know how many of something there is, just to be safe.  NOW, onto what I really want to get to, the positives!!-LOVE the music. Feels right out of a early 2000's horror game without feeling dated in the slightest. Couple pieces in there that could be real classics down the line.-Nails the blend of PS1/Early PS2 graphically. Looks like someone found a copy of a lost 2000's horror game that never got published till now.-The atmosphere, WOW. From the moment the game boots up I'm sold. Never been across the pond but it looks and feels very authentic and like a real place that could exist. Dark, grimy, claustrophobic at times.-Said atmosphere is backed up by the phenomenal sound design. The pounding rain, the moans of an enemy just around the corner, a baby cry as you stomp out one of the creatures. Great great stuff.-I was not anticipating voice acting so that was a lovely surprise! And another surprise, it's really good! I really enjoyed it, I thought for sure it was going to just be a text filled adventure. Especially love Mica's voice, and the voice over the phone. Great work.-Speaking of in game characters, great premise, pretty good execution. Have only gotten one ending so far, but I plan to go back and get the other endings/other achievements I'm missing. Had a good time reading the hidden journals/letters/articles spread across the game. Also the signals, cool way to show a bit of the before times without doing something big and grandiose.-I'm always an absolute sucker for horror games that have lots of puzzles that are just "oh now how in the world do I do this/get over there?" and you gotta find random items to get through, some fun ones in here. Hopefully in a future sequel/future horror game you do there'll also be more conventional puzzles, similar to the  puzzle. That was my favorite in the game!That all being said, I give the game a strong 8. Great atmosphere, sound design, story, music, characters, plenty of little puzzles... if you're a fan of early 2000's horror games ala SH2, you'll love it!Playing this feels like getting in on the ground floor of a future star developer, especially since it was essentially built by one person! As someone who spent two years building a decent 4-5ish hour game for my friends in RPG Maker, I'm unbelievably impressed with what you were able to accomplish here. Here's to the success of this and any future games!

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game completely by accident via survival horror Twitter; I wasn't a backer, but I thought it was interesting and was waiting on the release since I played and loved Chasing Static. I've only played through the first part so far, so take my review with a grain of salt - I will update upon completion.I think we gotta remember what this game is - It's an oldschool Silent Hill/ResE 2000s/PS2-worship nostalgia game, with all the associated clunk and cheese - manage your expectations accordingly. We're going for SH dead-wife melodrama with polygonal butts and heavy atmosphere. Leave your raytracing, particle physics, and 200-hour AAA sandbox games at home. I appreciate that they updated the setting with some BladeRunner vibes and a world that isn't just Foggy Sadtown Times With Mr. Sadman (tm)-It's nice to see a game like this that isn't just a bad SH clone and has some creativity in the setting. It feels like it pays a little homage to all the cheesball sci-fi games and B-Movies of the 2000s, which was unexpected but a welcome addition. There are parts where you're running past abandoned mechs or viewing "ancient" future tech and it adds a fun layer on top of the standard horror vibe in most SH clones.I love fixed-camera games and have been thirsting for them to come back, and I think Hollowbody does a great job with that idea and has an overall very pleasing cinematic flair to it. You can tell a lot of stylistic intentionality went into the visual decisions, though I think a bit of functionality is sacrificed at times - such is the nature of fixed cam so I am not mad at it. You can tell visual aesthetics are the dev's strong point and leaning into the SH-style meditative melancholy does the game a lot of favors and hides a lot of blemishes.I don't think it's that much worse to play with a keyboard/mouse either, so if you can't afford a console controller I don't think it's a dealbreaker - you should try the game anyway. It's a little clunky but it feels a lot like the PlayStation classics it wants to reference,  so it feels ok even though it's imperfect. Playing with keyboard reminded me a lot of running ResE on desktop emulators in HS in the 2000s.Hollowbody does feel a little style-over-substance. Once you get done being impressed with how much it feels exactly like a specific flavor of 2000s survival horror game, there's not so much left afterwards - I am not very far in yet but I will say the plot feels a little cliche and limited storywise; from reading other reviews it's not the longest gameplay either. I'm seeing folks saying they are finishing the game in under 5 hours in some cases. It also does feel a bit derivative at times - I know we all love Silent Hill but I also have already played Silent Hill and would love to see the dev get weirder with it. Chasing Static (the dev's other game) was great because it also referenced B-Horror Sci-Fi like The Thing etc so it felt unique while still having that nostalgia vibe we all crave. There was also the whole static-y audio thing taken to an extreme where it went past being a bit and started to feel like another character. Holllowbody doesn't have anything like this so it falls a bit short once you start looking more closely.The world could have more surprises and easter eggs to discover too - not only to build B-plots but also to reward folks who instinctively look under every rock in a game. You gotta know your audience after all, and some of us are gonna be out here trying every door and poking every trash can and corpse, even if there's never anything there. Please respect my mental health diagnoses enough to give me a treat for it.However, again, this is also about managing expectations - a solo dev built this in Unity and it's referencing an era where games had a limited scope and usually one main, often underdeveloped, plot thread. So the limitations do feel stylistic to some degree. That said, when you're looking at things like SH2 or ResE as inspiration, you can still do a lot of implied worldbuilding and story expansion if you write your game well - I feel like Hollowbody lacks a little depth in this regard and isn't quite fully baked. I would also say gameplay things feel a little unpolished beyond a stylistic choice - the HUD for interacting with objects can be clunky and the menu is very Unity 101. Some parts of the terrain block you when there's no reason you shouldn't be able to walk over them, and some ammo boxes, etc are glitchy. Combat is also ROUGH and movement can be a pain- please do yourself a favor and turn on tank controls. I know it's a solo dev but I would think that this kind of thing could be handled with a few more hours of work and testing. I am sure it will be updated over time and I know they wanted to get the game out, but I'd be slipping if I didn't mention it.All said, I think it's very solid for what it is, so again: I'm not mad at it. I came here expecting a diet SH2 clone riding on the coattails of the oldschool graphics nostalgia wave, and Hollowbody delivered an interesting combo of those ideas with a couple fun updates. I'll give it a 6 or 7/10 and will be happy to update that as bug fixes etc come in. It met my expectations and is a job well done, especially for one dude manifesting it out of pure commitment to the bit. Definitely worth checking out - and while you're at it you should check out Chasing Static too. They're both worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is an absolute gem of a survival horror game, capturing the perfect balance of tension and atmosphere without relying on cheap jump scares. From the moment I started playing, I was hooked by its eerie, decaying world. The environments are stunningly detailed, with a gritty, dystopian feel that really immerses you in the setting.What struck me the most is how well the game builds tension. I was constantly on edge, but never to the point where it felt overwhelming or exhausting. The atmosphere alone does most of the work, keeping you alert and uneasy. The puzzles and resource management add just enough challenge to make you think strategically, and I loved how combat wasn’t always the focus—sometimes it’s smarter to avoid a fight.It’s mind-blowing that this game was developed by just one person. You can feel the passion and care in every detail, from the story to the voice acting, and even in the pacing of the save points. I didn’t encounter any bugs, which is rare these days, and it’s clear the developer put a lot of effort into polishing this game.I’d recommend Hollowbody to both seasoned horror fans and those new to the genre. It’s not about shock value, but rather about crafting an experience that keeps you engaged and a bit on edge throughout. I’m genuinely having a blast playing, and I can’t wait to see what this developer creates next!

_childDocuments_.review: I am LOVING this game. Let me explain why;First off, I see a lot of people comparing it to RE1R and such, this is NOT resident evil. Resident Evil has and always will be a bit faster and more action packed. RE1 was def slower, but you still had a lot of combat encounters. There are far few in this game. What this IS is a love letter to survival horror, and the gameplay falls more in line with Silent Hill 2. It is much slower, relies on atmosphere, and likes to use combat encounters when it's least expected. There have been tons of times where no warning, the camera would switch, and I would see an enemy looming over me. The atmosphere is INTENSE. Part of survival horror is knowing how to use sound effectively, specifically knowing where to use silence, and this game strikes that balance borderline perfectly. There are some areas where the only sound is your footsteps and it is HARROWING. The only place I would have suggest to maybe tone down the music would have been outside because when I turned the music to mute, it was terrifying and really drove home that feeling of isolation. The voice acting too is superb. Within the first three hours there was a scene that literally made me cry because of how it was written and the heartfelt and emotional voice acting.The puzzles are pretty hard! The very first puzzle I encountered there was something to throw me off and the second I had to look up a guide because the solution is not something I would just think of, but once I did, it made a weird sense. Some of the puzzles definitely have that "Silent Hill 2 use the can-opener on the can to get a lightbulb" logic.There are not too many negatives I have for this game. There are glitches, such as every melee weapon I have used with the exception of the starting one sometimes glitches out animation wise and will stop swinging in a wide open area, mid swing, causing me to get hit. It also will randomly un-equip my weapons sometimes after coming out of a menu. One thing to keep in mind is this is made by ONE person, who truely understands what makes an emotional survival horror game great.This is an amazing buy, for under $20 USD, even off discount, well worth it. Can't wait for my other playthroughs and to try to 100% the game.Updates after finishing 100%:I would have preferred a few more boss battles like  but overall it blew me away. For $15 we got a game that most AAA developers (or lets be real AA or indie devs since AAA devs have abandoned horror with the exception of Capcom and shockingly Konami) struggle to emulate, let alone create. The ambiance, the feeling of isolation, everything is so well done. I even found myself turning the music down all the way when outside for a bit because the silence and footsteps really drove it home. The puzzles tripped me up slightly, and one even had me pulling my notes app to make note of things. It feels big in a decent way too, the city feeling like the streets are never-ending and you just hope you don't hit a dead-end.Endings discussion ahead:Overall I absolutely loved the game. I'm extremely grateful that 100% it was not insane like for instance, RE1Remake. I played through it 3 times. Once on normal, once on easy (to get all the documents and signals), and once on Punishing for the best ending in the game (there is no argument to that, if you say otherwise, you are incorrect.)My final thought is that after you beat the game PLEASE, PLEASE  it gives a completely different vibe and makes you appreciate the world-building so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish steam would allow a neutral review, BUT, I am going to give this a positive as there are more positives, at least for me, than negatives. I got this game after watching Avalanche Reviews and beat this in under 5 hours (4.2 to be exact). The atmosphere and graphics are all great, the puzzles are nicely done (although I feel after the first 'real' puzzle in the apartment they all became a little easier). Gameplay is alright - I wish the ranged weapons in the game had more 'oomph' to them sound-wise. Melee combat is a little wonky to get used to but it works. The thing for me is the storyline - the template for it is there but it kind of gets lost in translation after the first half of the game and I wish it was more fleshed out. There are certain areas in the game where you think can be accessed but turns out there's no way to access them (ie. the sewers portion). Not sure if dev forgot that it was there and did not create a way to unlock/get through them, but hopefully a future update can fix this? Overall I would give this game a 7/10. Perhaps the dev can also add additional content to flesh out the story a little better is my only criticism.

_childDocuments_.review: An overall great love-letter to survival horror games past. It's gameplay on the surface is more adjacent to Silent Hill, but it has a fresh enough presentation to make it stand on its own merits. It's level design is a bit lacking, and I could see players getting potentially lost  during certain areas of their journey. There's a decent bit of replay value baked in with a New Game + mode as well as post-game unlocks and multiple endings.All-in-all, if you're in the market for a new survival-horror experience, you can't go wrong with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody pulls off the vibe of classic survival horror games from a solo developer who truly loves the genre. Puzzles, combat, but more importantly the ENVIRONMENT. The environmental storytelling and camera work are the strongest aspects of the game for me. The main character's story wasn't the most engaging but the stories you come across from the voice messages and the paying attention to the details in the world gave me the feeling of exploring a real place and discovering short stories of people long past.I only got one of the the game's multiple endings (Riven) so maybe the main story gets explained better. But if you're reading this and want to get absorbed into a world, give Hollowbody a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a brilliant love letter to a lost era of survival horror. The seamless blend of third person - fixed camera angles works so well and is at times capable of appearing prerendered despite being entirely real time. The English setting is extremely refreshing and is brought to life by an incredible cast of actors. Hollowbody's presentation is top notch.It took me around 3 hours to finish but that runtime was packed with variety. Hollowbody is at its best when you're exploring areas and slowly unravelling their webs. However I did end up stockpiling ammo expecting to use it all in a final encounter but it ended up not being necessary. Combats by no means the focus of the game but I was hoping to unleash everything I'd collected in the climax. Regardless - an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed the 5 hours I spent playing Hollowbody, the atmosphere is pretty good, there are quite a few really good sections, and while it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥, hitting dudes with melee is quite satisfying. The game is also really good to look at, honestly the game looks so pretty, this is what I wish devs would aim for when making "PS2 graphics games" it's really nice. Voice acting was pretty solid too, very british lolNow for the cons, the game has like 2 solid puzzles and the rest are "combine these 2 items next to the thing to open the thing" puzzles, not much engaging tbh. And this might differ from person to person, but I felt like the game was showering me with bullets and healing items, was at like 55 pistol rounds, 16 shotgun shells and like 9 healing items at some point lol kinda makes you lose the feel of "survival horror" at that point but I get it, your average player might screw it up and lose all their ammo and healing items and then give a bad review for the game, understandable but I wish it was kinda toned down a bit cuz I think I finished the game with like 12 healing items and only shot my shotgun twice throughout the game lol enemies are pretty generic without much variation but I guess it's okay since it's going for that silent hill vibes not the RE feel. Also there is a bit of jank here and there, quite a few invisible walls and the music would cut off for a split second I think to reset the loop or something lol I don't mind these things but some might find them annoying. Also the map ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ keeps rotating on its own for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason it's infuriating lolanother thing that bothered me is on the "free-cam" sections which are like 80% of the game, you have to press the left stick to re-orient the screen to look forward instead of just using the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ right stick cuz the game is so afraid of being labelled a 3rd person action game I guess? I dunno but it felt annoying having to press L3 constantly to fix the camera while moving R3 did ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The endings also suck ass, there was so much potential here but oh well.It might sound like I hated the game but I actually quite enjoyed it, and for the price it's a really enjoyable experience, i'd give it 7/10, really wish some things were done better but what we got is a really good experience that kept me quite engaged throughout, I never felt like I wanna rush to finish the game and be done with it like how I feel with most games these days. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A mini budget Silent Hill that goes from average to a great game thanks to excellent presentation - the audio and visuals of Hollow Body are fantastic.Typical horror activities. Search for supplies, solve a few puzzles, fight some monsters between. Ranged combat worked good and melee combat felt inconsistent, but its not a big deal. Game alternates between indoor areas and foggy Silent Hill streets, minus the fog.Plays fine, nicely paced at 5hrs, has multiple endings and a harder difficulty. Set your expectations in line with a one person made game and you wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I immediately knew that Hollowbody was a game made with people like me in mind. The obvious inspiration comes from PS2-era horror games like Silent Hill 2 and Resident Evil 4, but there's more subtle inspiration that feels like it draws from movies that I love, like 28 Days Later and Blade Runner. I've loved every moment of the 90s-style video game revival that we've had for the past few years, but I'm even more excited to see this as-of-yet fairly underrepresented 2000s revival. The dream of 2004 is alive, it's well, and if Hollowbody is any indication, it's going to go far. I'm only an hour in, but I know I'll be spending more time with this game as soon as I can. Also, this was all made by ONE PERSON?! Buy it, love it, and tell all your friends about this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody embodies (excuse the pun) a lot of what you would expect from a PS2-inspired Survival Horror. From narrow hallways to open streets, the environment gives you the feeling of an area long abandoned, but still hiding secrets. Mica must scour this landscape in search of her friend.I think this game handles the genre well, and I only had couple real hangups with the design overall. Firstly, the environments didn't really seem to connect with our main protagonist. It felt like someone exploring someone else's world without any real reflections on the character themselves. Secondly, the design of the sewer "puzzle" left me visibly upset as I felt robbed of the chance to complete what was laid before me, with zero indication if I had interacted correctly or wrongly. It felt miserable to leave that area, unsatisfied.Overall, I still recommend this game. It doesn't take any new strides in storytelling or mechanical depth, but as it is made by a single developer and at a $17 price tag, it's a no-brainer for any fans of survival horror. It has replayability, secrets, and multiple endings that all bundle well into an interesting, if simple, package.You can also find my video review here: Well done, Headware Games. I look forward to what you work on next.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful homage to games like Silent Hill, fixed camera angles, tank controls, feels clunky in a 'good' way. Some derpy camera issues here and there, but nothing game ruining for me. Beat the game in about 3.5 hours, and that was with me getting stuck on a puzzle or two.  None of the puzzles are very hard or mind blowing, but just enough to keep you engaged. I felt the games default difficult was WAY too easy. I also wasn't sure how to actually do melee combat because I missed the first tutorial for it until WAY later in the game when I got it figured out by accident (Basically if you have a melee weapon out and you try to melee without an enemy nearby, your character ALWAYS just stomps. They will only swing their weapon when youre close to an enemy)   I only had to heal 4 times in the whole game, and had surplus ammo by the end. I know I can new game+ the difficulty up, but I don't know that I really want to play the whole game again. I kind of absorbed everything by the end. Also, there is multiple endings it seems, so if you're into 100%ing games, you're in for a treat, and there's an unlockable first person mode to make the game a whole other experience when you beat the game. All in all would reccomend if you dont mind the 15$ price tag for a 3~ hour experience (if you only clear it once). Enjoyed my time with it, thank you Nath for making this wonderful game <3

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a fun nostalgia trip to the PS2 era of horror games and one that can be recommended to genre veterans although with some caveats. It took me a bit over 3 hours to beat the game on the "Intended" difficulty on a playthrough that involved a fair amount of optional exploring around so don't go in expecting a long game. That being said there are at least a couple different endings and once you beat the game you unlock NG+ that allows you to select a harder difficulty mode "Punished" along with some other NG+ things so there is some minor replay value there.What does the game do well? I think it often managed to nail the atmosphere especially when it mixes in some psychological horror elements, the derelict city setting is quite nice and the semi fixed camera angles are well implemented.So what about the not so good things then? I think one big point especially genre veterans will find on their first playthrough is that the game is sort of lacking that "survival" part of survival horror as there is plenty of ammo and healing items to go around as the game barely ever forces you in to situations where you need to fight thanks to the easily avoidable and rather passive enemies.Another negative point I would say is that the pacing has some issues especially in the early parts of the game, as well as one section that sort of drags on a bit too long in the latter half of the game. To some degree I would blame the level design and the borderline useless map for some of the pacing issues as well.Overall I would recommend this to fans of the genre if you don't mind some of the flaws / issues listed above.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: First off, that this is a single developer game is mindblowing.I'm all about atmosphere in games, and especially in horror titles it's crucial. I'm thrilled ro report that Hollowbody nails it on every front. The lo fi but very effective visuals, the naturalistic but still surreal urban decay, the bits of environmental storytelling sprinkled throughout that help paint the backstory of the dreary setting, the minimalistic but effective music and sound design - they all converge into something really special. It's never diluted, it's densely packed with suspense and atmosphere, and the fixed camera jumps take me back to the late 90s early 2000s titles that scared the living daylights out of me back then. It's a bit of Alone In the Dark and a bit of Resident Evil and a bit of Silent Hill, but actually more than the sum of its influences. Hollowbody is a thing of its own and it's beautiful. Happy to have supported it early. Will help crowdfund / buy anything else Headware puts out there. You can tell when a game is a product of passion, not focus groups and marketing pitches. This is 100% the case.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have any issues with your resolution not being in the preset options, you can set the resolution yourself manually!To do so in Windows you can go into RegEdit/Registry Editor - HKEY_CURRENT_USER-Software-HeadwareGames-Hollowbody and modify the values using decimal the Screenmanager Resolution Width_h and Screenmanager Resolution Height_h entries (not the default ones).The game will likely have your resolution set by default but if you change any settings and it isn't in the options menu, you'll have to refer to this fix! If this doesn't work you might be able to delete the current settings and have it reset to default values. Thanks Nath for helping me with this fix and for giving us this stellar game!

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric throwback to the PS2-era of survival horror games. With a unique world and premise that uses a dystopian scifi setting as the backdrop for a creepy story that almost feels like fantasy at times. Its setting and tone are VERY reminiscent of Silent Hill 2, as well as the gameplay. It is ultimately about the story though, which can be completed in about 4-5 hours. Fans of more involved survival horror may find this lacking in complexity of combat and puzzles, though it does offer higher difficulties, New Game+, and other modifiers upon completion.This game's strength is in its atmosphere. It seems to want you to take your time in exploring, and studying, the sights of the ruined city it takes place in. The darkness, the constant storm, and great soundtrack had me immediately immersed in an oppressive atmosphere that never let up until it was over.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have finished the game and yeah it's a recommendation for sure. It's not perfect, I have some issues with a few sequences (One in particular is just pointless and very much intended to be so () and some definite BS with one big enemy placement near the end of the game that caused me to lose progress. Not too much since the game is fairly short, but it felt pretty BS the way I died. Otherwise I wish the story was a bit more developed. We kinda get to the end in a way that feels random. I wish the game was also a bit longer. It's great, but it does feel like part 1 of a bigger story. Which is to say I hope we see more of the MC or at least the world in general. name: SILENT HILL 2
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition [Deluxe Edition - Contents] ・SILENT HILL 2 ・Digital Artbook ・Digital Soundtrack ・Pyramid Head Mask（pizza box） The mask is a skin that applies to James (the main character) in the game. About the Game Having received a letter from his deceased wife, James heads to where they shared so many memories, in the hope of seeing her one more time: Silent Hill. There, by the lake, he finds a woman eerily similar to her... 'My name… is Maria,' the woman smiles. Her face, her voice... She's just like her. Experience a master-class in psychological horror―lauded as the best in the series―on the latest hardware with chilling visuals and visceral sounds. High-end Graphics and Sound With ray tracing and other cutting-edge technical enhancements, the world of SILENT HILL and its unsettling ambiance is even realer than before. And with the inclusion of new, immersive soundscapes, you'll feel like you're standing in the thick of it. Larger Environments Explore locations and buildings that were once inaccessible, or are newly added in the remake. Enjoy the same acclaimed story, even while you experience the town of Silent Hill with fresh eyes across an expanded map. Over-the-shoulder Camera The remake moves from the original's fixed-camera viewpoints to an over-the-shoulder perspective, putting you closer to what James sees, for a more thrilling, more immersive experience as you explore the town and come face-to-face with monsters. Evolved Combat Gameplay Familiar weapons like the steel pipe and handgun make their return, but now with an updated combat system. Avoid attacks with carefully timed dodges, aim down sights, and more, making monster encounters more engaging and nerve-wracking than ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is my favourite piece of media.  I had hopes that Bloober could re-imagine the original in a unique and special way but I have been completely taken back by how incredibly well made this remake is and just how much it makes me feel like when I played the original.  Remake captures the beauty, melancholy and total fear that the original instilled in me decades ago and I absolutely love it.  It now stands alongside the original as my favourite game.  The only downsides for me are that the early moments meeting Maria just do not hit the same way they did back then, though portrayal of her character here does improve as the story progresses.  Also, cutscenes are locked at 30fps and whilst its a very fluid 30fps, its still jarring.  The music is stunning, the environments are the grittiest and most haunting I have ever seen in a game and the overall design shows just how far Bloober have come. This remake will happily provide me with another great way to experience this incredible story and world for a long time to come and I am very much looking forward to hopefully seeing more remakes like this of all the earlier Silent Hill games.  Congratulations to Bloober, they have excelled here and done the Silent Hill series justice.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to apologise to bloober team for thinking they couldn't pull off a good SH2 remake but they somehow did?!?they've managed to create an almost completely faithful remake while adding in new areas, puzzles, better combat and even building on some of the lore theories the original game had without making them feel out of place. the only real issues I have with SH2make is that it gets very combat heavy compared to the original and needed a bit more enemy variety to keep it fresh IMO, the other issue is with stuttery performance on all platforms (thanks unreal engine 5) switching to DX11 helped but its still far from perfect so keep that in mind.UE5 ♥♥♥♥ aside as someone who actually played OG SH2 and doesn't get mad over "DEI chins" on twitter I would highly recommend this even if you're a newcomer to the series (but please play the team silent games)

_childDocuments_.review: RE2 is my favourite survival horror game due to its schlock factor and memorable characters SH2 has always been a very close second due to how it handled adult themes of loss grief and guilt, needless to say, I think the RE2 remake while not 100% faithful to the original game it was stellar and became my gold standard for remakes moving forward, I think Silent Hill 2 now holds that crown.At first, like many I was hesitant and skeptical of Bloober team's ability to take on the Herculean task of Remaking Silent Hill 2, I was worried that the themes and scenes wouldn't be treated with the same degree of respect and heaviness or would be toned down to such a degree due to modern tastes that they would all but be left out entirely,I was Wrong, they absolutely knocked this game out of the park, its modern but in the right ways while retaining the core of The OG.in terms of performance, this game gave me Zero issues which is a rarity these days for any new game coming out as they usually arrive in varying degrees of unpolished, unoptimized and downright broken, I can say in my whole time with SH2R i had 2 frame dips because of the stupid Epic installer launching whilst playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Shock to many, but I found myself not being a fan of the OG (and yes, I tried playing the enhanced edition years ago). The gameplay didn't click for me whatsoever.But.. I bought the remake after a long time of waiting in excitement after seeing the trailer because I genuinely did want to get into SH2. And I was hooked right away. Beautiful graphics, an absolutely eerily enthralling atmosphere, sound design that truly makes you just as tense as James surely is and level design that just constantly has you thinking and piecing things together. I had a lot of fun pretty much the entire way through.I also was just so unbelievably intrigued with the mystery that the narrative presented. Who really is James? What is Silent Hill? Who is Angela? Who is Eddie? Who is Laura? Who is.. Mary? Is she really waiting for James? And seeing all of those questions be answered as the mystery unravels, and with the truth eventually being revealed in what is now one of my favorite twists in anything ever -- it was an absolutely unreal first experience. Now, writing this, I've watched and read a good amount of stuff on the series and it's characters. I've replayed 5 times and 100%'d it. I love it.I would recommend this to anyone in a heartbeat who's looking for their entry into not only the horror genre but also Silent Hill as a series, because I know now that I'm invested.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and WOW, Bloober Team knocked it out of the park. This game is not to be considered a replacement of the OG, but a celebration of the original while feeling so brand new and different. Every major area in the game has been completely changed while keeping the same puzzles intact, while adding new ones as well, and the new puzzles are such a welcome change, loved most of them. Bloober also managed to do all of this while keeping the same major story beats the same. The dialogue remains unchanged for the most part, with more of a, natural delivery. The natural delivery could somewhat be a downside for some and not for OTHERS, but they still have this somewhat dreamy, slow charm to them. This game is awesome. Hoping for more bangers soon from Bloober Team, they deserve all the praise they are getting now and congrats to them for making doubters become believers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure this game received a warm reception because the bar has been set so absolutely low for this series. While the art direction is pretty good, and I do like some of the more minute and style changes, the gameplay is awful due to the addition of verticality as a mechanic. It wasn't difficult to proceed in the original -- your map updates with what is blocked off and not, so either explore somewhere you haven't been yet or figure out a puzzle. With the verticality, your map is updated, but NOT with possible entry-holes, windows you can smash, ledges you can climb... meaning you will be spending A LOT of time either looking through every corner to find out just how the hell you're supposed to get anywhere or looking up a guide only to find out you missed some poorly lit wall you could break with a pipe five minutes in the opposite direction. And that's just not enjoyable whatsoever. It's not like the original was 'fun' necessarily, but I wouldn't call it frustratingly boring either. I got halfway through the game and just couldn't bother anymore. And that's not even getting into the performance issues. Have fun having 5 FPS during a scene with only one prop for reasons you do not understand in a game you spent $70 on. I wouldn't recommend this for a fan. And I DEFINITELY would not recommend this for anyone new to the game -- just play the original ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it still holds up.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game since the news of a possible remake of the legendary series have appeared in the Internet. Unfortunately, I didn't play the original game when it was released 23 years ago and I was very excited when I found out about the serious development on this remake! This particular game will appeal to both fans and those just getting to know the series. If you are looking for the game that have a special, unique atmosphere that will be remembered forever, then I definitely recommend this game for purchase.I am a fan of the Silent Hill series and my favorite parts are the first 3 parts. I also believe that these 3 parts are the best example of "psychological horror" genre games. Silent Hill is: depth of plot, psychological insight, quantity and quality of raised problems, interesting characters with tragic stories, heartbreaking soundtracks...Oh yes, let me say a special word about SH soundtracks. Akira Yamaoka is a God of music! His compositions brought this series to life. I was happy to find out that he's also working on the remake. Soundtracks from the 2nd part are my favorites and it wouldn't be as emotional and exciting journey if it wasn't with his music.So, now specifically about the game. There is a generally linear game divided into different locations, where you can fight enemies with different types of weapons (melee weapons, pistol, shotgun and rifle) and avoiding their hits, have to look for items or solve puzzles () to open access to the next levels, but you will also have a small opportunity to walk around the city/current location without any problems (except for the doors that are locked at certain stages and, well, enemies you probably don’t want to face). After all, every time I passed another house or room, I wondered, “who lived here and what really happened?” No matter how dead this city is in the story, its streets are still alive with all of those details and that is beautiful in its own way! . There are several types of enemies in the game with their unique “features”, which you get used to over time, but sometimes because of the number of enemies it is very easy to miss a hit or even a few and end up dying. That is why in this game it is important to watch the enemies' movements and calculate timings correctly. This series was never about a cool combat system, but the developers managed to get rid of the old, sometimes quite funny mechanics and make something of their own, which most of the time looks not very impressive and dynamic, but which is very suitable for Silent Hill series as a whole. In addition to the usual enemies, there are few boss fights, which, from a story perspective, look good, but they are not too challenging especially with a lot of resources you have.. Those who are not familiar with the story of the original, then if briefly and without spoilers I will say that the main character receives a letter from his wife, who asks him to meet at a “special place” in Silent Hill. Silent Hill is a small town, which used to be a popular tourist spot, until a terrible tragedy happened in it. Unfortunately, the second part gives us very little information about the origin of the town and the creatures in it, this information is in other parts of the game and there will be spoilers, so I can only say that the tragedy is associated with people who for the sake of their goals went very far and in the end because of them a lot of people died...Anyway, throughout this particular history we encounter enemies and meeting several characters who either just talk to us about their problems or accompany us like Maria did. In the original series, Maria has never caused me any sympathy, but developers did smth that really got me attached to this character. There are 8 endings in the game, so your actions and your "play style" will be important if you want to achieve one or another ending. At the end I can say that the SH is a very complicated and completely untypical story, especially in the genre of horror. So whatever your experience, it will be in your memory forever.. In my opinion, this game is not as scary as the Outlast series and there are few jump scares, but there are other types of horrors. For example, each location has its own tragic story and the horror you see there, is on the surface/in the enemies or in the details that you have to find around. In addition, some locations were creepier, especially in the dark as there are all these creepy and sometimes unexpected sounds and enemies that only add an atmosphere of horror. There is another frightening element: the boss fights or chases where you have to think and do smth very fast and try to not die. of the game is great and walking around the city, making a bunch of beautiful and atmospheric screenshots is normal reaction. I am also exciting to try the “90’s” graphic mode during the second play through, but there are more modes in the settings. However, there is one minus and this is an optimization. I do not have powerful computer and unfortunately, I had to find a combination of settings that would allow me to play with a smoother picture and more FPS. For the overall picture of the game, it is a minor minus, cos my game has never crashed or freezed at important events/fights and I think that developers will solve important problems with the new patches.To those who say that the remake turned out to be bad, I can answer that it is very difficult and even wrong to compare the remake with the original (), because the original part came out more than 20 years ago and at that time people felt completely different emotions playing games. No matter what, I can never imagine a better remake of SH2 than we see now from the Bloober Team. I could go on forever about how great the Silent Hill series is. Thank you so much Konami and Bloober team for all these emotions, I am looking forward to the next remakes of SH1 and SH3!P.S. I thought that Digital soundtrack from Deluxe Edition contained more music tracks :( I hope we will get more in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is a big fan of the original and not so much of a fan of Bloober Team, I approached this game with some apprehension. I ended up buying the game on the off chance that it was at least entertainingly bad. On the contrary, the game is a perfectly fine remake and nothing more. It borrows heavily from the Resident Evil 2 school of game remaking for better and for worse. The town of Silent Hill itself is impressively rendered in high resolution and fog as dense as ever. On the other hand, there is more renovation than a fresh coat of paint. Voice acting is a lot less awkward, combat is more fluid, etc. etc. Ordinarily, these would be welcome changes for nearly any other game. However, with Silent Hill 2, I find that the original is a game strongly characterized by the ways it is, whether intentional notwithstanding, contains flaws in the experience. I know that we had practically no chance of getting a big budget horror game in 2024 with tank controls and fixed cameras. I know that some of the original SH2 cast are weirdos and probably not worth bringing back to reprise their roles. Nonetheless, I wish that Bloober Team had sought out more interesting creative compromises than just largely copying the homework of Capcom's RE remakes. This game is not as bad as it could have been. Far from it, in fact. However, it still resides in the shadow of both its own potential and the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s been a very very long time since the original came out, so an old beloved series like this was always going to present a challenge. But considering the difficulty in obtaining a copy legitimately or even having the knowhow to emulate it properly, it was in danger of falling further into obscurity, and more recent projects either being either lackluster or outright cancelled (P.T on the PS3), the idea of a Silent Hill remake was always going to ruffle some feathers.I was introduced to the series with Silent Hill 1 through a Playstation demo disk, which I was blatantly too young to understand, and it terrified me. But it stuck in my head for a long time which made me come back to the series to overcome it – and it quickly became one of my favourite series in gaming. I must have done around 10 playthroughs of SH2 alone – and I can fully vouch for this remake.I was apprehensive going in, but Bloober has done a fantastic job bringing the series to life again to allow a new crowd of fans to see the atmosphere, tone and horror of Silent Hill. These aspects have been nailed, and while the game is significantly different in terms of its map design, the original content has clearly been respected and considered. New things have been tried, but all are in keeping with the gameplay loop you’d expect from a Silent Hill game.To touch on differences between the OG game and the remake – firstly the controls have been massively modernised, which presents the first minor issue with the game – James is very agile and enemy attack patterns can be learned, which can make combat feel less about survival than the original. It feels as though you’re expected to rise to the challenge of the combat and running away seems a lot harder – considering enemies can follow you to different rooms now, and the corridors feel like they have less space. Enemies are also much more agile and even react to you in unexpected ways, like running, hiding and setting up ambushes. I don’t dislike this though, it’s just different.The controls are more akin to something like Callisto protocol or the RE4 remake, over the shoulder reactive shooting with a dedicated melee and dedicated firearm button essentially. All modern day QoL improvements which some may feel take away some of the feeling of helplessness that added to the horror elements of the original game, whether it was intended or not!The visuals are gorgeous. The trademark fog of Silent Hill drifts and billows in the rustic dilapidated streets, looming around every corner and obscuring the shifting shapes of enemies staggering around. Massive creepy looking makeshift walls blocking off the exits, layers of corroded metal. There’s some really cool graphical features too like leaves and discarded trash floating around in the streets, and fabrics blowing in the wind. A lot of attention to detail has been made in the games design, and it shows, it really is quite beautiful in its own oppressive way.The characters and writing, in my opinion, have been improved somewhat. There are slight things that are worse in the remake, but I think it boils down to preference. The acting/writing wasn’t great in the original, and even worse in the HD collection. But the uncanny voice acting added to the otherworldly feel, so it’s hard to say whether this was intentional or not. A lot of that is gone in the remake, but it sounds more natural now. The additional characters are more empathetic in some ways, but overall again Bloober did a good job. You’ll hear a lot of arguments regarding the characters, specifically Maria and Angela, but a lot of them are bad faith arguments either from people more invested in the culture wars than Silent Hill as an IP, or the sort of people where nothing would ever impress them over the originals. My own personal negative of the new characters was that Maria seemed a bit too human considering the dubious nature of her existence. In the OG game she seemed like a demon/snake wearing human skin, and this came across in the way she spoke. Angela seems better though, sorry to those who disagree, but in this she actually seems like a 19 year old and not the 40 year old I thought she was meant to be in the original.With all that said, Silent Hill 2 is a great remake and I highly recommend it. I’d love to see SH1, 3 and even The Room remade in this same way, and I never thought I’d say it, but it’s clear Bloober have respected the IP, respected the fans and did a good job making this a reality. Cheers!Pros:Gorgeous world design that considers multiple previous entries in SH.Perfect sound design made by the OG Akira Yamaoka, and radio / menu sounds fitting of the original games and decent voice acting. (Also I’m pretty sure they used the radio sound from P.T which is awesome)New content for returning fans of the OG with lots of nods and easter eggs to older games.Very respectful to the original game.Good gameplay, though there’s clearly more focus on facing enemies rather than running from them.Enemies now have variants which is a much needed element to the game.Cons:The odd janky animation sometimes, when James picks up items etc.Maria seems more human and less demon this time around.Some traversal microstutter. Unfortunately a fairly common UE5 issue. There are some fixes you can find in the guides section on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly excellent remake of an all time classic.  I originally went in with low expectations - I don't like Bloober as a company, I haven't enjoyed any of their previous projects and especially with The Medium (which was a Silent Hill-esq successor)  leaving an incredibly sour note regarding the teams attempt at more serious themes/topics. The early footage looked... Rough to say the least, the combat trailer made the game look like a really REALLY poor-man's Last of Us or even Resident Evil 2-4 Remake. Some of the lighting and facial animations didn't fit what the original game was conveying so from the start I wasn't looking forward to this, however I'm happy to admit I'm quite pleased with SH2Remake.The game looks fantastic, I can barely fault Bloober's attempt at bringing Silent Hill 2 to the modern era, they handled the story surprisingly well and with a good amount of care for the source material - James, Angela and Mary/Maria's story was told just as well as the original if not better due to the new voice actors (I vastly prefer the original Mary performance.) I honestly wish more remakes were in-line with this, midway through the game I started to draw more and more comparisons to the recent Dead Space remake and honestly after finishing my first playthrough I'm happy to stick to those comparisons.  The expanded levels, entirely new areas splintered across here or there were all largely enjoyable to go through and experience, the remixed takes on classic areas were well done, the expanded town even was a genuine improvement over the original. It now feels like an actual place instead of a glorified spooky hallway, more buildings to enter and loot for supplies, new puzzles and notes/diaries for worldbuilding. I'm genuinely surprised at how I felt about SH2, I can recommend it for both new and old fans. Props to the devs at Bloober for once.

_childDocuments_.review: They did a phenomenal job and this is one of the best survival horror games I've played in years. It reminds me a bit of RE2 Remake, but that's not a bad thing.Let's not ignore the elephant in the room. The maps are reimagined, but that doesn't detract from them. Most areas have excellent design. I was thrown for a loop a few times and got lost even though I can usually map these areas out pretty good in my head. In their reimagined forms, I could see places like Woodside Apartments or Brookhaven Hospital in the real world.The combat system has been overhauled but never feels broken like in Homecoming. The decision to keep this from becoming a walking sim like Shattered Memories was a good one.Monsters have been improved in their design and have new attack behaviors. The number of times I caught a glimpse of a Mannequin behind walls and furniture was hilarious in a good way. It also made me feel like there was a semblance of skill by not triggering them. Using caution when going around blind corners is recommended because this isn't Call of Duty.Not only that but more of them are lurking around than ever. Sometimes adding too many enemies will eliminate the horror and turn it into an action game like Resident Evil 4, but I feel it's masterfully done here. I'm a Silent Hill veteran, and the monsters gave me some trouble. The prison was incredibly daunting. The enemy count was ridiculous, and if this was Silent Hill 3 with the Closers, Scrapers, and Double Heads, I'd be running for my life, which is what I would say if the monsters here weren't brutal.The monsters in the original could usually be juked or easily dispatched, even in hard mode, but that's not the case anymore. Try that, and you'll get chased down and clomped over the head by a Nurse's pipe or Mannequin. These changes are understandable because the original was too easy. Can we please have Silent Hill 1 and 3, Bloober Team? I just can't get over how good this is. I thought it would disappoint like many others, but no. This is one of the best Konami-published games in years.I don't know how I feel about the new voice acting. Some of the script is lifted from the original but there are a few new cutscenes. Angela looks and sounds more like a teenager now, as does Maria for some reason, and I love her flirty eyes. Don't get me started on the new Eddy who doesn't seem as mean spirited as the original but is more dimwitted. He also has a better boss fight that doesn't end in three seconds.I think most of the changes are welcome. Health pickups have received a rework. Health Drinks and Ampoles are now found inside Health Kits rather than them acting as medium heals. I don't know about easy mode, but bullets are scarce on normal and above if you aren't using the Chainsaw to destroy everyone. Sure, you can kill every monster you see, and I usually try in the originals even though combat isn't the focus in these games. I didn't try to pick every fight I found here, though. My aggressive play style turned into a more passive, and I avoided most fights for once.I'm not one to get scared, but I'll admit that the monsters and environments were creepy. I would love to see Bloober Team's take on the Otherworld from the other games. As usual, the music sounds like nothing else and is great. The usual ambience is great and assaults your senses as it should. Most monsters sound squelchy and like vile insects.Dodging is a new feature but isn't used to the degree of becoming a Souls game. Though I'd love a souls-like game with a Silent Hill theme, I'm glad that's not what this turned into because this game has a critical job. It needs to reinvigorate the Silent Hill name, and I think it'll more than accomplish that. I'll beat this game dozens of times as I did the originals.I loved the puzzles. Some of them are based on the original, and some are new. I think the Coin Puzzle and Hanged Men were some of the best. Some later levels reminded me of Zelda dungeons and got complex, but I'm here for it. Bloober Team, if you keep this up, you'll be my favorite developer. I feel like I've waited almost twenty years for Silent Hill to be good again, and now it is. Recommend if you're a fan of horror games or Silent Hill, but there's sadly no unlockables except the Chainsaw.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I approached Bloober Team with a degree of skepticism, not due to doubts about their standing within the horror genre—where their craft is somewhat unique and the reputation is well-deserved—but because I felt they had yet to truly reach their full potential. They didn't have 'it'. While their past efforts have shown promise, they never quite captured that elusive quality that defines masterpieces. Should Silent Hill 2 (SH2) indeed represent their artistic maturation as a process in self-realization, I welcome it wholeheartedly. Nevertheless, I still anticipate an original title from Bloober Team that transcends their previous work, which has often been considered as budget titles. As for KONAMI and SH franchise in general, let's not repeat history. Those familiar with the franchise know all too well the mishandling and stagnation that plagued the series (and the KONAMI itself) for years. Yet, one cannot help but hope that Konami has at last found a way to inject fresh vitality into its veins. Perhaps this is just a stepping stone for KONAMI to get back in the business. Though I was initially apprehensive about the project, I did not believe from the outset that it would devolve into disaster. On the contrary, the director’s comments conveyed a clear sense of passion and expertise, suggesting a deep understanding of what made the original a masterpiece. As Silent Hill 2 is a story that lives in interpretations how it is directed is everything and it only gets only heavier when you realize the topics it tackles. Fortunately, the remake not only preserves much of the artistic integrity that defined the original (keeping all the sinistry and creepiness around the town intact) but also succeeds in modernizing the gameplay. Furthermore, it expands upon the existing content, introducing new areas (which increases the playtime significantly) while implementing QOL improvements that enhance the experience. While the fixed camera was a notable part of the og (and most of the games during that era, defining new approaches to utilize for storytelling) SH2 is also successful with its generic over the shoulder camera. Evil finds new ways to sneak onto you.One thing that is notable with this remake is not only they tried to deliver a sense of familiarity but also challenged it by adding new layers of interpretations. One of them is the bold assumption of that you already have gone through the events of Silent Hill. The only slight issue lies in the performance—microstutters and occasional frame rate dips, which, despite some efforts at fine-tuning, have proven difficult to resolve. This is exclusive to 4K though (in my case). While I was able to achieve 50-60 fps overall, it would tank a lot and sometimes get completely broken and require a full restart (which is frustrating as you know SH2 uses an old save system and that means you need to replay the same stages after the last checkpoint). Nevertheless, the overall performance remains satisfactory and the game is most definitely playable at 2K (above 70 fps, DLSS Quality & Epic presets, 3080ti). A more significant concern, however, is the introduction of a modern health indicator: a red screen (aka low health vignette) signaling the character’s weakened state. I strongly recommend disabling this feature, as it not only disrupts immersion but also conflicts with the thematic intent of the game. In a narrative where the "In Water" ending—one that requires the protagonist to endure significant damage—is largely regarded as canon by fans, this red paint thrown onto your screen feels frustratingly out of place. I can sense it getting worse in the darkness (i.e. most of the game) and especially in the Otherworld. A more organic approach is to monitor James' physical animations, which offer a better immersive representation of his deteriorating condition [don't worry they are explicit and readable enough]. Playing the game without any hint will probably do wonders as you must rely on the visual & audio cues and they did some clever job at that. At its core, Silent Hill 2 remains an unparalleled work of art, a narrative imbued with layers of meaning, all interwoven through the lens of personal turmoil, with the game unflinchingly disturbing the player while conveying its own cognizance of torment and grief and to this very day still stands as a poignant exploration of the human psyche.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played Silent Hill 2 before and you can run this well, it is well worth it.  The game looks beautiful.  The story is - well, Silent Hill 2, the best of the series (RIP) - so, so, good,   The ambient soundtrack is good and the sparse music uses much of the melodies of the original Akira Yamaoka OST so it is also amazing.  The voice acting has been vastly improved over the original, and is better than many other games.   The map highlighting things you may have missed is an absolute lifesaver because I was lost several times.  Ranged weapons are pretty good.  Combat is serviceable, but not great.  There are a few criticisms I do have though: I feel like the areas can becoming overly long.  You feel the middle of the game where you go through several large areas twice basically and the puzzles you need to complete to get through have you checking everything.  Despite this, sometimes it feels like you're railroaded in a direction and you'll just miss something and end up relying on the map to point things out, which I am glad it does.  I finished the game with a couple key items that I didn't use.  I guess I'll look them up in a guide.  The formulaic jumpscares by the few enemy types get annoying,  The flashlight does that horror genre thing where it flickers when you're looking at an enemy and it does it Every. Single. Time.  And it can actually make you lose track of an enemy and miss shots.  This being a survival horror game, that can be costly depending on your combat difficulty.  Melee combat is clunky because it's a series of dodges and counters where enemies can end up behind you and you won't be able to see what's happening because of the aforementioned flashlight and the camera.    The melee attacks have seemingly inconsistent hit stun; if you run into an enemy and hit them the camera and weight feels good, but sometimes it feels like they recover nearly instantly and counterattack while you are stuck in place.  Some attacks have the enemy flying across space to get you when you should be well out of range.  The saving grace is that dodging gives seemingly infinite i-frames; this is NOT Dark Souls combat.I will admit that I was torn on this game because I played the OG PS2 Silent Hill 2 and loved 2 and 3 most of all and have been sad to see Konami laying all their properties aside for years to fester or releasing mobile trash and pachinko machines, but Bloober didn't really try to reinvent the wheel and instead tried to tell the story and make a good survival horror game and I think they achieved that.  70 dollar price aside, if you like the genre and are looking for a beautiful new toy, I would recommend playing this classic in this format.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely superb remake of a classic survival horror gem!The atmosphere in this is on point, and managed to scare me so much that my first playthrough took much longer than I expected, because I needed to take breaks often to get my heart rate down. The game is longer and more padded than the OG SH2, where you need to spend longer time in some areas than previously needed. I did enjoy exploring, even though pissing my pants, so I didn't mind this. The combat is definitely improved from the OG, but it still doesn't feel like an 'actiony' type of game and doesn't take away from the atmosphere. Some of the monsters have gotten a serious upgrade, and will ambush you when you least expect it. Many boss fights have also changed - in my opinion, these changes make sense but also make the game more challenging in some ways. This game is really beautiful and the fact that Akira Yamaoka came back to work on this is amazing, the score is great as one would expect, with new renditions of the classic tracks from the OG SH2. This game feels respectful to the OG SH2, and I'm happy that I've now experienced both. I don't feel that this remake can replace the OG, but it's just a new version of the story, that is a great addition to the franchise. I really hope that we can get more remakes of the other Silent Hill games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill holds a place in my heart and mind that few games do. The essence of what it's trying to convey is what most books or films ache to express with a fraction of the efficacy. One of my best friends listened to the soundtrack non-stop with me and expressed his love for the series as a whole for years until he convinced me to just try SH2 out and see how I felt about it. There was a moment where i literally fell out of my chair as a genuine reaction to a unexpected moment. He claims that, and holds the games effective nature over me and our friend group to this day, and I do NOT disagree. I was floored - No Pun intended, the game just put me in the state of mind that I had a purpose, and I needed to find out what was going on, humans by nature of very curious beings, and the pacing feels flawless for it. A story beat that demands urgency, yet everyone around you seems lost, but Something keeps pulling you in.       Beating the game for the first time on PS2 was a heart wrenching and cathartic experience. Before playing it, my favorite horror game was Resident Evil 4, and this games tone was on another level considering it came out 4 years prior and had the themes that most drama films have, combined with interactive gameplay  I'd say this is one of the more effective experiences ever created to depict the psyche and mental illness, or conceptual ideas that you don't simply 'get' from most mediums of entertainment. It's thought provoking, meaningful, tragic, immersive, engaging, and horrifying. It's actually safe to say it feels like its incomparable to most games purely because what its trying to say transcends video games and hits a nerve that most people can latch on to and understand and put into their own trauma and frame it around ones fractured perspective.       So far this remake has hit it out of the park and gone above and beyond my expectations, painstaking detail, absolutely gorgeous visuals with an added layer of exploration to the town that doesn't feel overbearing or 'collectathon' - ish with its added content. Nothing feels padded so far, nothing feels out of place. It feels like SIlent Hill modernized in a way that I desired. I just made it to the Apartments. A few performance hitches, but nothing crazy to detract, and nothing that has pulled me out of being entirely immersed. Some details have completely thrown me off guard and made me jump all over again, phenomenal so far.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played Silent Hill 2 on the HD Collection a couple years back through Xbox BC, (Yes I know I played the worst version of the game, I am sorry I will play the PS2 version one of these days), I was hooked from the very beginning. The atmosphere, the sound design, the themes, and the characters were all so ominous yet mysterious at the same time. Because of this, I consider this to be my favorite survival horror game, and one of my favorite games of all time. Now that I have done at least one play through of SH2R, I can say that this version of the game is also amazing. I was worried that some parts of the atmosphere that defines Silent Hill would be gone with the modernization. Add Bloober Team to the mix, and that spelt out a recipe for skepticism. This time, however, Bloober Team stepped up their game and created something that I would define as a love letter to one of the best survival horror games of all time, with some new twists. Despite the fact that it has been a couple of years that I have played the original version of SH2, I do remember a decent amount from it, and I was very surprised at the changes they made, like how certain events happen at different locations in the remake, but I was even more surprised at how Bloober was able to manage keeping the plot almost (if not) 1:1 to the original game. With this in mind, I consider the remake to be a "movie based on a book" situation where there are changes made for the movie (or in this case, the remake) in order to make things flow better. Even if that is the case, Bloober has added some collectibles that references the old puzzles or key locations from the original, which is a nice touch. Stuff that I was worried that would be removed from the remake (like the pitch black environments in the levels or the supernatural sounds coming from....somewhere inside the building you are in) are intact, which means that I can be anxious again but with raytracing :). Combat now feels fleshed out and not as clunky as the OG game. With the addition of dodging, I felt a lot more in control and I found it easier to fight groups of enemies. The shooting also is more fluid and feels a lot more familiar to an FPS (or is it a TPS? Whatever tomato tomato). I think the only problem I had with this game is the stuttering, but I heard there are mods to fix that, so that should good on that front, although it should be patched officially. Besides that, my 4070 SUPER (with Quality DLSS, raytracing on, at Epic settings) handles this game like a champ and makes the game look gorgeous (Obviously, this can change depending on your setup). With this in mind, I definitely recommend playing SH2R, as it is a game that will make you nervous as you roam around the streets of Silent Hill. It will make you want to dig deeper into the town and witness the journey of James Sunderland. I would also recommend play the original one, whether through emulation, the PC port (with the enhanced mod), or on the original hardware (you could also play the HD collection version like I did, but it's the HD collection....so yeah), as the way the OG plays and feels is completely different to the remake. (Plus you can see what things changed from the original). I love this game (and the series in general), and I want everyone to be able to experience Silent Hill 2 for the first time like I did when I played it for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an OG fan and you're on the fence - don't be. The original game is preserved in this remake, but Bloober have also injected their DNA, including plenty of expanded areas, dialogue and more to keep things fresh for returning fans of the seriesVisual design is incredible. The re-designed monsters are pure Masahiro Ito gross body horror at its best with some unexpected new tricks (the Mannequin has been dialled up to 11!) and of course the sound design is everything you would expect from Akira YamaokaThe voice acting is superb. Hearing and feeling the emotion that didn't quite come across in the OG due to tech limitations of the time has been amazing. I can't say much for fear of spoilers for newcomers, but there have been parts where my change of feelings towards certain characters has surprised meI DESPERATELY hope this success prompts Konami into a true remake of the original Silent Hill!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for some time for this game and was super excited to finally play it. My current run isn't finished yet, but I can say that it so far did not disappoint!! The game itself runs smoothly aside from some few in-between frame drops, but these fix themselves very quickly so this is more a nitpick. The town looks gorgeous and is fun to explore, I really enjoy the way the map works in this game. It's simple but easy to navigate. The combat is again rather simple, but it feels smooth and is easy to understand. As for the settings in this game I just want to say that I love how accessible they made them. I see a lot of games that some people (me included) can't play for various different reasons. Settings feature for example, special subtitle fonts for people with dyslexia amongst many other options. Contrary to making the game simpler, you can also change stuff to make the game more difficult like for example turning off all types of hints (ex. no icon to interact with) so you can shape the games difficulty and accessibility to however you prefer which I adore. It may not be something big, but it means a lot to me. If there was something I'd improve upon so far it'd be the companion AI. Sometimes the AI will run into a wall because of a scripted event or run in-front James when fighting, which can be a bit bothersome, but this will hopefully be fixed in the future. _childDocuments_.review: Cutscenes rendered in real-time and locked at 30 FPS, transitioning into gameplay at 120 FPS, is jarring. It's 2024, and they still haven't learned... There are plenty of cutscenes, and some transitions visually feel like they're lagging due to the drastic drop in frame rates from 120 to 30. Nope, it's a negative review until this gets fixed. I was so baffled by it that I spent ten minutes combing through the options, convinced there had to be a toggle for it. There is already a mod to remove this lock, and using it makes a night-and-day positive difference. To make matters worse, even cloth animations, like curtains, are locked at 30 FPS—it's just painful to watch. The last time I saw something like this was in the Horizon Zero Dawn port, but thankfully, that got patched after several updates.I just finished Until Dawn (2024), and aside from a few pre-rendered cutscenes, everything ran at 120 FPS. It was simply amazing. You might think it’s an unfair comparison, but I would argue otherwise. Both games are horror. Both are remakes. Both originally had fixed-camera setups, and their remasters do not. Both use Unreal Engine 5. And finally, both were released in the same month. Yes, Until Dawn is mostly an interactive movie, but the remaster allows for a lot of exploration. The levels are pretty big, and they look stunning. Visually, Until Dawn looks better to my eyes. Silent Hill 2 remake looks good, but nothing about it is particularly impressive. What makes it worse is that, despite not looking extraordinary, the game has performance issues. Even with Ray Tracing off, the frame rate fluctuates in simple scenarios—and let’s not forget the occasional stutter. Meanwhile, Until Dawn ran at a locked 120 FPS on my machine with everything maxed out. Oh, and Until Dawn didn’t lock its cutscenes to 30 FPS while looking perfectly cinematic and in-line with the gameplay.If you want a better comparison, let’s look at Alan Wake 2. I’m pretty sure the Silent Hill series was one of the many inspirations for that game. It was released a whole year ago—it looks several times better than Silent Hill 2 and runs at a locked 120 FPS on the same machine, with everything maxed out. Not only do the cutscenes run at 120 FPS, but Alan Wake 2 also has an incredible Ray Tracing implementation, including reflections. For instance, in Silent Hill 2, with everything maxed out, you still can’t see your character’s reflection in random mirrors around the world (I’m not talking about the intro mirror—there’s one, for example, in Wood Side Apartments). I mean, with RT, you do see some dark shape in a mirror, but I wouldn’t call it a reflection. Furthermore, Alan Wake 2 has far superior writing, while Silent Hill 2 stuck to the original script from 2001—back when professional-level writing in games was rare.Here’s how I see it: As of today, Silent Hill 2 costs EUR 69.99, has ugly locked cutscenes, and only OK visuals—but it does have replayability. Until Dawn remake also costs EUR 69.99. It looks and performs better, and it has replayability. Then there’s Alan Wake 2. It looks better than both, has much better writing and story, decent length, and replayability (a second playthrough is almost a must to advance the story)—and it costs EUR 49.99. You do the math.And yes, I understand nostalgia. I played Silent Hill 2 back in 2002. It was an amazing game that terrified me and stood out among others at the time. But today? Honestly, I expect better performance and visuals—and, most importantly, more engaging writing.
