_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is by far one of my favorite horror games, and I can confidently say that this remake is both true to it's original material, and also a breath of fresh air. Now that it's here, I can say it's a great new way to get into the town of Silent Hill. This franchise means a lot to me, and Bloober Team overcame the odds and delivered an experience that feels almost unreal, even for a second time.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of emotions playing this game, as I did with the original. Aside from the updated graphics and more modern camera angles and combat style, it kept all of the creepiness, beauty and sadness. While there are slight differences to the original in terms of where some things are located and what sorts of things you have to do to proceed, the main story and major elements are the same. Where it differs, there are a number of throwbacks to the original in terms of easter-eggs and interactable "memories of the past", however (encounter all in a single play-through for an achievement). Overall, I think the developers did an excellent job balancing its faithfulness to the original game while providing a new experience.I could not recommend this game enough to those who are a fan of the series or simply anyone who enjoys horror games, especially those that heavily feature mystery and psychological elements. Definitely a worthy addition to the Silent Hill series.

_childDocuments_.review: As a angsty teenager I have spend ungodly amount of hours on this game. I was completely obsessed with it. Listening to OST in loops, nocliping through levels to find anything hidden, scrolling through forums to know more and to discuss with people interpretations. My irl friends were utterly annoyed of me yapping about this game over and over again. So when remake was annouced I was scared. I felt like someone want to take those memories and feelings I had, throw them away and replace with something new and "better". I went into defensive. Avoiding anything related to this game to not let myself hate it.It relased. I bought it. Went into 5 min into a game and I was raging hard. Uninstall, refund. ♥♥♥♥ game. Nothing beats original.Then I went for a long walk to think about my feelings. No one can take away my memories and feelings I had. No one can take away my love I had all these years ago. Someone loved this story like I did and had opportunity to told it again. Because every good stories should be retold for next generations.More open minded I bought it again and started playing.Is it a good game? Yes. Is it a good Silent Hill game? Yes. Is it a good SH2? No. Little details of the story are missed. Acting is bad, voice deliveries are bad. Dreamlike feel is missing. Moments that should hit hard are meh. Or at least it is for me because every line of dialog, every scene and even little face expressions. All of those are burned in my mind forever. So maybe acting is not that bad? Maybe those moments still hit hard? I will never know. Overall it's a good game. Worth money and time spend.sidenote:F@#$ Unreal Engine! This piece a !@#$ crashed like milion times. Stuck in infinite loadings and froze hell knows how many times. Please Devs! Never make anything on this s!@# engine. I beg you. It looks pretty, but its more unstable than me when i was nineteen. TL;DRBig fan had to drop nostalgia gogles to be open minded and had fun in a good game, but also had his patience tested with unstable game engine. 10/10

The biggest upgrade to me  i can say, is the combat. I was using a dualsense controller with haptic feedback on and lemme tell you it elevated the experience. _childDocuments_.review: Initial marketing material for this game did NOT do it any justice. Even I was super skeptical until I actually played for myself. A lot of love went into this game and it's evident after the first play through. 2 additional endings that are new content to SH2 entirely, leaving it at 8 total possible endings. While some enemies feel too aggressive at first it ends up coming together fairly well for the 2nd half of the game. The re-imagined boss fights are wayyyy more than what I expected Bloober to be able to do. Feels like the same quality as RE4 remake, just not as flashy with what you can do in combat while still being satisfying to use weapons. Overall spent about 30 hours on the first play through just combing through Silent Hill in a way we haven't been able to before. It was damn near perfect. Some questionable voice acting/direction decisions, but overall I can accept that this isn't a replacement of the first game and it's magic. Just an awesome love letter to the series and I'm glad we got this. Highly recommend and would be open to them eventually revisiting SH1 properly.

_childDocuments_.review: Bloober Team delivered an impressive remake! Aside from some nitpicks here and there, it's a fun experience with thoughtful nods to the original. Despite my nitpicks, it is definitely one of my favorite games of 2024.- Stunning updated visuals- The soundtrack is AMAZING, I LOVE Akira Yamaoka though so I'm biased- Improved voice acting and facial animations enhance emotional impact- New puzzles align with the original's spirit- Enhanced combat system- Engaging New Game + options and achievements- Immersive sound design and atmosphere- Full Sony Dualsense controller support (currently intermittent though.. you need to jiggle mouse to reactivate the enhanced features)- Expanded lore with intriguing implications- Predictable tension-building after puzzles- Pacing issues in Toluca Prison and Labyrinth, to the point where I just began running to every objective without exploring- Repetitive combat loop and some forced encounters- Some redone cutscenes lose impact due to odd visual choices and script changes (A certain "death" scene for example..)- Unreal Engine 5 traversal stutter, like a plague of locusts..- In addition to the stutter, unstable performance and with raytracing enabled expect framerates between 45-60 FPS (there are tweaks you can make to increase performance, but at a visual effects loss that compromises the atmosphere)Recommended for survival horror fans, even those new to the series. For future Silent Hill games, combat could use more variety and strategic options. Tighter pacing would improve replayability, especially considering the game's multiple endings. Buy if you enjoy Silent Hill or atmospheric survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh. I kind of feel like ♥♥♥♥.It might have to do with the fact that I pounded energy drinks until 4:00 so I could finish this game. I couldn’t help it, though: I had to see this thing through.I forgot how much I  . I mean, a lot of the early games in the series hold a place in my heart. But it was  that I obsessed over. I loved recounting the story for people who would never be able to stomach actually playing the damned thing. I even used to have a plot analysis I printed off from GameFAQs that moved with me from state to state. So, even when I couldn’t access my PS2 to play the actual game, I could read over the plot analysis. I’d steep myself in the plot beats, sinister twists, secret endings, fan theories, source materials… Like tonguing a sore tooth, I’d find some ill-begotten solace in this.Because that’s kind of what  does, isn’t it? It gets caught under the player’s skin like a shard of glass that breaks off and is impossible to remove without digging. It is synonymous with illness and ending. Lust and corruption. Terror and beyond.Yeah. I feel like ♥♥♥♥. But I’m happy to feel this way again.We old folks were cursed to look on in horror as Konami degenerated into a pile of dog puke in the 2010s. And, though I’m less familiar with the circumstances, I know Bloober Team has had their share of issues as well. So, when the  project was announced, it was met with much gnashing of teeth. Konami had already bungled a remaster of the game in the years before the announcement, so there were very few people who had any faith in this project. The players had every right to feel this way; the original  is, without exaggerating, a cornerstone of horror (not just in games but in the genre ) and every attempt to recreate the magic of the original game has fallen on its face.But, somehow Konami and Bloober Team have found a way to hit that vein again. Even as a guy who just wanted to replay  after all these years and had my fingers crossed that it would be good the entire time, I’m floored by what I just experienced.They’ve managed to capture the feel of playing the original game while modernizing everything about it. The oppressive atmosphere always keeps the player on edge – even with updated combat mechanics, there is no guarantee of safety here. Every staircase, every room, every corner is an opportunity for Silent Hill to strike at the player. Whether it’s an enemy waiting for James behind a cardboard box so it can spring out like a trap or the environment suddenly, inexplicably collapsing further in on itself like a singularity, this is a long, crushing trek through a world that hates you and wants to see you suffer… just like it’s supposed to be.All of the ingredients that made the original stand tall like a looming behemoth are here. The sound design was the first thing that caught my attention. I think it says something that the music that plays as James first explores Silent Hill got my heart racing and set me on edge. It’s that beautiful dissonance of exploring a quiet, misty town while discordant music thunders through the speakers, landing squarely in the player’s gut. Skittering that makes the skin itch, crashes from nowhere and everywhere, mumbling voices when no one’s in the room with you. It’s all here and it’s all perfect.And every character has as much punch as they did in the original. Or, dare I say, even more so: I don’t remember Eddie making my skin crawl as much in 2001 as he did in 2024. Some of it is his model, sure; his constant sheen of sweat makes him appear unwell and gives the player the impression that he reeks of something putrid. But it’s his pointed taunting and teasing that truly seeps into the player. And they completely nailed Angela’s transformation. As the story progresses and her dreamlike dissociation begins to peel back, her cold defensiveness comes forward. The tables turn: she’s no longer trapped in a room with James, James is trapped in a room with her. And the player feels it.One of the things that had people worried before the game’s release was the combat. PlayStation released a “combat reveal” trailer that sent a lot of people flocking to their keyboards to share their outrage that Konami and Bloober Team turned the main character into a monster-killing-machine. You see, the combat in the original  intentionally felt awful. James isn’t a trained soldier – he’s a guy who finds a two-by-four on the ground and is using it to survive. But fears about this aspect of the game turned out to be unfounded; every encounter has the potential to be the last one if the player is caught off guard. A little more fluidity helps ease things along without making the monsters feel like cannon fodder.Of course, the story is one of the game’s greatest strengths and much of it remains untouched here. None of the minor changes made in this version detracted from the story whatsoever. The one thing that might be missed that is tangentially related to the story is the original’s fixed camera perspective. The over-the-shoulder camera in the remake works great, but the exemplary camera direction is now mostly limited to cutscenes. It’s unfortunate, but it’s a necessary change.I don’t count it as a negative, but this game is  compared to other modern horror games. Considering the price of admission, I didn’t mind the extended playtime at all. On top of that, I think it was handled extremely well. In the original  games, it felt like at least half of the doors the player came across were locked with no way to unlock them. In the remake, however, a lot of those locked doors are now unlockable from the other side. This means that, as the player progresses through the environments, they are opening shortcuts they can use when they need to backtrack later on. What starts as a meandering trek through the hospital (or wherever) turns into quickly zipping from place to place to solve puzzles as the level progresses.Honestly, I think the length of the game adds to the oppressive feeling of the environment itself. Sometimes it feels like it’s never going to end… and I think that’s the point. You, the player, begin to lose hope that you’ll ever find refuge, right alongside James.That neatly brings me to the most important question anyone should be asking: is the game scary? And, um, yeah, it scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. There are multiple parts that are going to linger in my mind for far longer than is healthy. Without getting into spoilers, there is a scenario at the beginning of the Labyrinth that had my pulse pounding and left me short of breath. The final stage was so eerie that it ruined the color yellow for me. And scouring the desolate locations around the town felt so realistic that it reminded me of the times years ago when I explored abandoned buildings and retroactively made my memories scarier. This game is just as devastating as the 2001 version, if not more so. not only managed to retain the feel of late-90s/early-2000s survival horror games while bringing it up to current standards, but it also managed to dredge up the feelings of true terror that, I think, only comes from horror games. So, yeah, I recommend this game. I recommend it so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. It quickly and handily became my Game of the Year. However: if you’re thinking about pulling the trigger on this one, keep in mind that this game is not fun. It’s not supposed to be. If you don’t like the idea of being subjected to pervasive, creeping dread that will slowly burrow into you until your insides feel wrong and your own skin doesn’t feel right on your body anymore… maybe skip it? It might make you feel like ♥♥♥♥. But, if you’re like me and you’re chasing that feeling, buy it right now. Do not hesitate. Jump down the hole.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake is nothing short of a masterclass in psychological horror, brilliantly reimagining the 2001 classic for modern audiences while preserving the soul of the original. Developed by Bloober Team in collaboration with Konami, this remake is a haunting experience that will linger long after you’ve put down the controller.Graphics and Atmosphere:The visual overhaul is absolutely stunning. Every texture, from the dilapidated buildings to the eerily realistic fog, feels meticulously crafted. The town of Silent Hill feels alive, or rather, decayed in a way that draws you in and unnerves you at the same time. The lighting system is incredible, with shadows creeping and shifting in ways that make you constantly question what’s lurking in the dark. It’s a visual feast of dread that perfectly captures the oppressive and melancholic atmosphere of the original, while pushing the boundaries of what next-gen hardware can do.Sound Design and Music:Akira Yamaoka’s legendary score returns, enhanced with more nuance and depth. The iconic theme still sends chills down your spine, and the new ambient sounds breathe life into every corner of Silent Hill. The distant echoes, unsettling whispers, and the screeching static of the radio are not just heard – they’re felt. The sound design is so immersive that I found myself on edge even in moments of silence, expecting something terrible to happen at any second.Story and Characters:The heart of Silent Hill 2 has always been its deeply psychological and emotional narrative, and the remake stays faithful to that. James Sunderland’s journey to find his wife Mary is just as poignant and disturbing as ever. The improved facial animations and character models add an extra layer of emotion to the story, making each interaction feel even more impactful. You feel the weight of James’ grief, guilt, and confusion as if they were your own. The supporting cast, especially Maria, is brought to life with even more complexity, making the story’s twists hit harder than before.Gameplay and Mechanics:Combat remains secondary to the atmosphere, but the controls have been significantly improved for a smoother experience. The subtle adjustments to gameplay mechanics – like improved camera angles and more responsive movement – ensure that the remake feels modern without losing its classic survival horror roots. The puzzles are still satisfyingly challenging, but the quality-of-life improvements (such as easier inventory management and clearer objectives) help avoid unnecessary frustration.Enemy Design and AI:The monsters, iconic in their symbolism and grotesque designs, are even more terrifying thanks to the enhanced graphics. Pyramid Head, in particular, is more menacing than ever, embodying the darkest parts of James’ psyche with an unsettling presence. The AI has also been tweaked to make enemy encounters feel more dynamic and dangerous, with unpredictable movements and attacks that keep you on your toes.Final Thoughts:Silent Hill 2 Remake, brought to life by Bloober Team and Konami, is a triumph in every sense of the word. It delivers on the nostalgia of the original while updating the game for a new generation, balancing modern improvements with a deep respect for what made the original so beloved. It’s a harrowing journey into the human mind, exploring themes of grief, guilt, and redemption in a way that few games have ever done before. Whether you’re a long-time fan or a newcomer to the series, this remake is an absolute must-play.Rating: ★★★★★ 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: JC Kitan (experienced consumer of the survival horror genre)I can imagine the painstaking stages the Blooper team had to go through to translate a work of art like Silent Hill 2 (Jurassic one xD). Moreover, it was too big a bite, but did the result remain the same as the original, or even better... To begin with, I must say that I had a phenomenal experience and the development team honestly SUCCEEDED in translating the old format!Of course, like any product of modern horror in gaming, this remake suffers in terms of deciding how to transfer the older masterpiece to modern players (I mean the generations born after the nineties). The sufferings of this remake are not so much on the artistic level (visual, sound and narrative), but more on the level of playing the game itself (the so-called gameplay). Is it that important, it definitely is, because unlike the movie, we set the plot, we decide which direction to go, we are the curators of the story...I will carry out this review quantitatively and based on crucial parameters, I will present the initial evaluations as well as the explanation of why I think so. At the end, i will give a final CLIMAX rating that will surprise some. All in all, even though it is a remake of a masterpiece - of the masterpiece of the same name - I feel obliged to give an opinion about the game outside of scholarly discourse.1. Narrative overview / Rating: 8.0/10Synopsis of the story: The story begins three years after the questionable and painful death of the wife (Maria) of James Sunderland (the main character of the game). James receives a mysterious letter from her inviting him to return to their "special place". Visiting that special place (the city of Silent Hill itself) it becomes obvious that this is not the city he remembers - it is mysterious, dangerous and disturbing, full of various creatures from nightmares that constantly follow him. His search for Mary leads him to face not only the horrors of the city itself, but also the darkness and secrets within himself.Such a blasphemous attempt to describe the synopsis of the story without simultaneously creating a "spoil" is rare. Overall, the story holds up very well, and it's clear from the start that the developers are experienced connoisseurs of the original story and all the potential repercussions that the characters in the game face. Dramatically, the remake begins identically to the original and keeps the "old school" treatment, but at times, speaking of the technological development of video games, it tries too hard to modernize certain scenes, which loses the basic charm of the most important parts of the game. The problem lies not in the way of monologic and dialogic, or even diegetic narration, but in the way of framing the scene. Previously, scenes had so-called "dutch" corners and totals were present (in the context of the film plan). The remake does not allow that risk, and forces more close-ups (than those mentioned), which loses the surreal magic and even the Lynchian spirit that the Japanese forced in the original game. Of course, there is everything that I criticized, but not in the places where it should be. Given that it is a remake and therefore an extended experience of storytelling and playing the game itself - the new inserted scenes look phenomenal and fill the gaps of the original, and sometimes they also problematize and create a bigger QUESTION about what is happening and in which direction the mystery will go.In addition to the narrative, it is important to mention the acting. The actors did a phenomenal job with their characters. The main character James Sunderland has never looked better than he does now. The other characters are wonderfully reimagined, as well as the way they are set up - in opposition to the main character. The acting is on point! The direction is not...I know that for some it sounds pointless to analyze film grammar in a game, but this is a game that responds as an undisputed multimedia work. After all, all games nowadays strive to have phenomenal direction. However, whoever directed the original scenes went too far. At times it seems as if the director, i.e. the game director didn't know if he wanted to force a surreal spirit or a psychological foreplay between the characters. The combination of multiple genres in the SH franchise is not a bad thing, but it is awkward in terms of direction, because you don't know exactly if something is purposefully poorly executed, because it is not moderated with the remaining scenes that are super done. It is important to note that the Japanese are extremely awkward when it comes to storytelling, so their original games had that charm, but when a westerner remakes a Japanese game, it becomes very difficult to understand whether the author refers to his own style or tries to combine original and your own, create a new result. Certainly a very difficult task, but I am satisfied if nothing else.2. Atmospheric (un)opportunities and perfect visuals / Rating: 10/10In terms of graphics and the visual atmosphere itself, the game does not make mistakes. In this parameter, the remake was given an honorable place to be better than the original itself. The way the fog and hail concept has been improved is mind-blowingly killer! Most of them, mostly as I write, criticize some aspects of the atmosphere, like it's too dark a game or something like that - NO! It's not dark, increase the brightness if you use HDR. Adjust the brightness based on your monitor. I'll just say it.The stage space has been filled with new details, from where you can clearly see that the space was once alive and filled with details of a past life. There are a lot of psychological attributes in the stage space that play with the main character, testing him. A GREAT job again!3. Soundtrack/Sound Design / Rating: 8.5/10As someone who has been emulating SH music and sound design for years, I have to be critical here. Let's start with the sound. The sound is completely school-made, precise and designed in the spirit of the original. So what's wrong... Well. The incorporation and relationship of SFX and music is wrong. Whenever there is no music, the design is at its best, however, when the music starts, the way it's mixed, I can barely hear it. Is it school - it is... However, SH is a pure improvisation of the relationship between sound and music, and here it is lacking. If I were to analyze the sound separately from the music, I would give the sound a 10/10 and the music a 6-7,Music - khmm... I wonder why there was a need to remake the music itself. Honestly! Let's be real! Where the problem arises - in the music... Listen to some of the main tracks, like Laura Theme, Null Moon or Heaven's night. The instruments are almost missed, it sounds identical, but the uncanny experience that was present in the original is missing due to the so-called trip/hop lo-fi arrangement. 4. Game design/Level design/Puzzles / Score: 10/10There is no need to write so much here, because this is a unique experience, both for new players and for people who have crossed the original many times. The way the world is designed from a gamer's point of view should be the basic manifesto for any new survival horror game ever, especially if someone decides to remake an older game. So, the levels are full of creepy (un)opportunities, new but at the same time improved puzzles. It's a truly unique experience and kudos to the Blooper team!In this section, another compliment to the developers - "Congratulations, you did a better job than Capcom with the remakes of the Resident Evil franchise"!Conclusion:All in all, Silent Hill 2 - Remake is a great game - RATING: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Stutter Hill 2 Deluxe Unpatched Edition. Seriously, don't know how the overall consensus of the game is overwhelmingly positive, or how you'd be hard pressed to find any negative reviews online. Buyer beware, unless you have a really high end machine because I have multiple pc's to test this on, it's not worth it at all. The base game is great and what's there is a fantastic framework for a game of the year contender, but it's wrapped up in Unreal Engine 5 stutters for everyone else. Considering how slow Konami has been on rolling out updates for Metal Gear Solid Master Collection, because that was it's own mess, I'm not too optimistic on how fast they can fix this game's problems. So I would wait on this game for God knows how long before you buy. Litterly, there's no benefit of being an early adopter these days, so just don't, unless you want your first playthrough to be a dissapointing mess.Edit: After playing the game more, I would say this game prefers Nvidia graphics cards, so if you have a low mid range PC, your AMD card will absolutely not work. But if you have like a 3060, it should run for the most part but traversal stutters are going to happen regardless. It's playable on Nvidia. AMD? Well just have a beefy one. Still I'd recommend on sale unless you really just want to jump on the bandwagon because I am enjoying the game. To give you an idea, on a lower end AMD card, the game ran like Callisto Protocol on release. With a less powerful Nvidia card, it was an actual playable experience. So if you can wait, wait. If not, take the game as it is, it's still very fun. Gpu's tested are the AMD 6700s laptop gpu (doesn't perform well at all) and the Nvidia 2060m (which had a pretty playable experience), then of course very little problems on a AMD 7900 xtx. Mostly played the game on the 2060m. Upscaling used on all builds with low settings. Sometimes i would come across 15fps for the traversal stutters, and if I waited it would go away (2060m). Ran the game on fsr ultra performance on all builds and on the 2060m I'd usually get around 60fps with dips every once in awhile. There is also a potato mod for this game that really makes it playable on anything, but you'd have to add reshade to make it look decent. 😂 And that mod is called Demake on Nexus Mods.P.S. Oh and last but not least NO CLOUD SAVES

Goes to show that Bloober Team CAN make a  survival horror game (i.e. limited resources, grounded combat, fairly challenging puzzles, mystery, unsettling stuff over jump scares).I have some complaints, though:-Some hidden graphical options (dig around the .ini files to turn off some annoying effects)-Mouse sensitivity can't go down 0.25 without digging around files using a hex editor-No effective way to turn off mouse acceleration (not even found on the in-game settings)-$70 price tag with no regional pricing-No Born From A WishI want this franchise to live again. I want to see more (fairly priced) Silent Hill games in this format, whether in the form of remakes or new entries.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original for the first time this year. I loved it so much I played it three more times, and I understand why some people claim it to be one of the best horror games, hell, one of the best games of all time. My expectations were already set, and the hype was building up.I have to say, this game... it's amazing! I love the new layouts and puzzles, they're actually brain teasers so I feel good about actually figuring out the solutions beforehand. I love the combat, it feels nice to fight the enemies and honestly, the bar for combat in the original was so low that any slight improvement would have been 10 times better, the game aged in a lot of areas, and combat was one of them. So when I started hitting enemies and shooting them, I knew that this game was good, because it FEELS good to shoot them.I just finished the Brookhaven Hospital, and I have to say, the story has evolved and changed in ways that I cannot be mad about, it still fits the themes of the original story, and even expands upon it to my surpirse. I even saw a teaser for Born From a Wish, so I hope they add that to the game. While I have some minor gripes with a couple of the scenes, at this point its just being nitpicky and you have to accept that changes will be made for better or worse, but most of the time for the better in my opinion.The one thing I do need to complain about is the optimization. I had to look up online and mess with internal files to be able to get the damn thing to run slightly above 60 FPS, and I have a brand new computer that surpasses the recommended specs. So honestly, my only complaint is that I hope they optimize and patch the game so it runs smoother, but other than that? This game so far is a slam dunk and Bloober should be damn proud of the work they put into this. So many details that true fans of the series and especially the original game are realized here and put even when a lot of people will not notice them, they gave it their all with this game.If by the time I am super satisfied with how they did Toluca Prison, and whatever ending I get is amazing, I am more than happy with my purchase and fully recommend this remake to old fans and people who have never played a Silent Hill game, it will be worth your money for the amazing story alone.P.S: I am more than welcoming the idea for Bloober to work on 1, 3, and 4 with how good this remake is.Edit: Just finished the game, ABSOLUTE CINEMA! They even fixed the fps issue I had, but some visual bugs are still present, but they're trying. I definitely loved this game

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure this could have been done much better. Had an fantastic time from start to finish. Extremely faithful, yet still refreshingly new/updated. Only have a few "criticisms". The biggest one (and this is only minor), is that looting/searching is a bit touchy sometimes. I played the first play through without any prompts on screen, and searching some of the areas (the kitchens in the apartment stand out the most) was sometimes frustrating. James' head would clearly look to "something" straight in front of him, but I had to position myself in a certain spot/position perfectly in order to be able to actually interact with things at times. Another example is the save spots. I couldn't use them if I was too close. I had to take a step back in order to be able to interact with them.Secondly, the game limits backtracking without warnings. As an early example, once you get inside the apartments and the doors close, you cant go back out. Again, playing without prompts caused me to trigger a cutscene on some doors that cut you off from back tracking. I saved often on my first play through, so reloading a previous save made this practically a non-issue, but it is still something to point on in case this helps anyone.EASILY a 9.5/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve never been a fan of Bloober Team. Layers of Fear, Blair Witch, and the Medium were big misses for me. When it was revealed Bloober was given the reigns for a Silent Hill 2 remake, my heart sank. My expectations were extremely low but I know I had to play the remake seeing as how the original Silent Hill 2 has been (and still is) my favorite game of all time.Their other games I mentioned above always do a nice job with atmosphere & aesthetics, but fumbling original narratives about mental illness was always a known concern for many.Bllober did their homework for SH2r here and it shows. To my amazement they did a fantastic job keeping the die hard SH2 fanatics like me happy. For sure not perfect with its flaws (an occasional voice line and having to wiggle away from enemies that have no arms to grab you) but the extent of my gripes are minimal. The updated boss fights/redesigns by Masahito Ito and the remixed/new music by Akira Yamaoka are fantastic contributions from the OG Team Silent crew.I still do not care for their original IP’s or believe in their ability to make an original story for existing IP’s such as Blair Witch… but they were given a chance by Konami to remake one of (if not) the best horror game of all time and adapt it to a modern audience. It’s damn strange for me to admit this but…. Bloober knocked it out of the damn park.

_childDocuments_.review: It was nice to see a «Leon Kennedy» but without Face App again. After beating every RE I ran out of horror games and Silent Hill 2 was a breath of fresh air. Foggy, with threatening silence, mysterious air. The story itself is interesting and confusing at the same time, it makes you make assumptions, baffles you, during the whole game I asked myself lots of questions and even after completing the game I have some questions left. Games that make us think are adorable and unique. All the puzzles are fascinating and solvable without searching for answers on the Internet. Special attention should be paid to the ambience. Sounds are so real, I strongly recommend playing in headphones.The only disadvantage of this game— I couldn't play it for more than 2.5 hours in a row, just because my brain was tired of constant puzzles, scary sounds and a terrifying atmosphere. But it's not the game's problem, isn't it?This game completely lived up to my expectations. Can do nothing but recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews but I wanted to make it known how great this game was. I know some people were mad about some of the more corny dialogue being removed but it's absolutely for the best. The voice actor choices for all the characters were fantastic. It's hard to describe but they all feel like REAL people. Not actors delivering lines, like actual human beings if that makes any sense. Than combined with the fantastic facial animations for the characters means all that cheesy extra dialogue where people state how they feel is conveyed with motion and facial expressions that were just not possible on the PS2.Bloober team did a fantastic job in honoring this game by keeping so much of it true to the original while bringing into the modern age of gaming. As said before, dialogue is retooled, WHILE STILL KEEPING MOST OF THE ORIGINAL TEXT. So many of the lines in the original have been simply redone word for word by the new voice actors and it has a much more intense and serious tone. Watching the two games side by side the original almost seems like a parody.As far as combat goes, while certainly not the most advanced or innovate thing, the inclusion of a dodge mechanic makes fights feel more visceral and lethal for both parties involved instead of just standing there whacking each other or just evading enemies. Each enemy feels like it could actually pose a threat if not respected. Visually the game is amazing. The town of Silent Hill, in my opinion, could not look better. I will say I had issues maintaining 60 fps at 1440p but thats most likely due to my 3060 gpu. I've had an issue as I've gotten older and games become more realistic of being able to "read" the screen. The sheer amount of detail in some titles makes it hard to distinguish what you are looking at. I'm a big fan the sharpening option in games. I mention this because whatever combination of contrast in textures, lighting, and sharpening made this game look INCREDIBLY detailed while still being easily visually digestible.Sure some people may be upset with the launch price of $70 but lets be clear here. We purchased games for $60+ in 2001. Accounting for inflation $60 in 2003 is equal to $106.10 in 2024. If anything games have not kept the pace with inflation while at the same time skyrocketing in terms of production cost. To be clear, if every game was somehow released at no cost I wouldn't be upset, but I'm not mad that some developers need to raise the price a bit. I really hope Bloober team continues to remake the rest of the series, because currently this one stands out as the best by far.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a solid remake actually. There's big revamps to a lot of areas of the game and the boss fights are also improved a lot which is pretty cool, there's a couple of extra cutscenes here and there also and some new areas not seen in the original.The voice acting is pretty good although I prefer some of the line deliveries of the original over this one and even some lines were taken out entirely which is unfortunate, other than that though its passable. The combat isn't too bad, its mostly a lot of dodge timing which can be frustrating when enemies have delayed attacks and taking damage really sucks on hard difficulty, if you really suck at dodging in games you're not going to get far at least if you try playing on hard. The puzzles are quite good I do like how they've improved and expanded upon some of the puzzles in the original and even scrapped some puzzles in favor of better ones so that's pretty good, there are a few challenging ones but the further you get into the game the easier they get in my opinion.Visually it is very nice and impressive looking even on low graphics settings although there can be some odd visual bugs when you're on the lowest settings and have frame generation stuff on. The hair is the main problem for me its so ugly and glitchy looking if you don't have high settings so it does take you out of the experience a bit unfortunately.There are some things here and there which feel a bit like maybe low budget or just maybe not given enough time for more polish which is a shame, some animations and little details are a bit janky which is unfortunate but oh well. The game itself runs sort of okay but its plagued with constant framedrop issues which can be annoying at times, outside of that though it does run a lot better than most new games that are coming out these days, on lowest settings and frame generation I'm able to get between 70-120fps in most areas so its pretty decent compared to stuff like alan wake 2 which I could only get like 30fps on, and this is at only 1080p, I can't imagine how bad it must be at higher resolutions. But yeah its not too bad, could be better but yeah pretty much the main thing that kills the game is the framedrops, they really need fixing. The game also crashed for me twice which kinda sucks, once at the end of a boss fight and once just opening some door somewhere.I do like how they've changed some things around in the game but other times I feel like ah man I wish they would've kept this in. Overall though I definitely think its a very good remake and I am glad that it exists so people who weren't able to play the original can experience the game. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a faithful remake of one of my favorite games ever. Even though it removes the Dutch Camera Angles, they still make the game feel claustrophobic and tense with the third-person camera. The story largely stays the same, with a couple of the story beats fleshed out or put in a slightly different order. The original game had a very Japanese feel to horror, where most of the characters are in this numb sense of reality, while the remake feels much more Western, where most characters seem like they are actively suffering and in emotional distress. Overall this is my game of the year. I didn't think Blooper team could do it, but they over-delivered. If you've never played Silent Hill 2 or you grew up playing it as I did, this is a great way to experience the horrors of 2001 on modern systems.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blooper Team did the unbelievable and I am truly amazed by how the remake HAS the soul of the original in it's core. Everything, from the mood, the setting, the story and most important (for me, at least), the MUSIC and sound design is perfect. Simply game of the year and nothing will change that.Thank you for letting me relive the experience I had playing the original back in 2001.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much of a change...still can't be arsed to finish the game... (Tacomo Prison atm, bit over the half). Finished Unitl Dawn and very close to finish Metaphor...This month we got two horror titles competing with nostalgia: Until Dawn (Remaster) and Silent Hill 2 (Remake).  Both are using the problematic Unreal Engine 5, one game does everything to make it a good experience, the other sends you on a technical nightmare. + good but no stellar presentation (mostly bland)+ great, eerie soundscape+ good voice acting+ good mouse controls+ mature story() little improved gameplay, true to the original or a bit boring, your call- very stretched playtime (a bit too old school, you spend most of your time looking for ammo and text snippets)--- Constantly present UE5 stuttering, no matter what you do (highend machine or lowest settings won't help to ban it totally)Both, SH2 and Until Dawn do little to improve the original game's gameplay which isn't exactly contemporary any more. Until Dawn is a mix of walking sim and interactive teen slasher movie, while SH2 is a successor of the 90's horror survival genre including all it's unfortunate perks which feel very old-fashioned nowadays: slow movement (at least good mouse control in the remake), few weapons and sparse ammunition, text snippets, few NPCs, repetitive areas that hold little more than ammo packs or healing items and a few odd but very linear riddles.You can say, the game is true to the original. That would be ok, if it wasn't riddled with UE5 stuttering and right now there is NOTHING you can do about it, WHATEVER others try to tell you (or themselves) in their reviews. If I go for it I can get 100+ FPS out of the game when lowering the more demanding graphic items. Sadly this is entirely meaningless if it's not a smooth ride. The game can have a few some seconds but the next little or bigger hickup is always around the next corner (sometimes the same corner). While it's not unplayable, I do not find it very enjoyable. And since the story is good but strongly stretched over lengthy explorations of maze-like structures, it feels like a chore getting to the end. I'm at 13h and about half through the game atm. I've played 30+h Metaphor while taking a break...While there are some fan fixes to improve quality and performance (like RT and ghosting), they won't get rid of traversal hickups which are worse on lower CPUs. Still, if you intend to buy I highly recommend checking for game mods on Nexus.The Silent Hill 2 Remake's STEAM rating rides on sympathy for the devil while Until Dawn is driven by Anti-Sony gamers' protest. While Until Dawn makes no fuss about being a cheesy and simple horror game, it does a good job delivering great presentation and not overstaying its welcome. A lengthy shader compilation at start prevents stuttering for most of the game, I only saw short FPS drops at complete scene changes. Whenever it counts (like QT events), the game is set to fixed camera angles to maximize performance. Overall, I'm having a shorter but better time there. Since I have no emotional binding to Silent Hill 2, I can't quite see it as the survival masterpiece others declare it to be. Mainly, it's boring meandering through mostly empty streets and buildings, looking for sparse ammo and notes left behind. While the dev made an excellent job at bringing the desoiate and dreadful town of Silent Hill to modern times, they can't harness UE5 and deliver a smooth gaming experience. Considering the dev's previous titles, I doubt we will see meaningful fixes for the game. Instead of stellar game reviews watch Digital Foundry's Tech Review, they don't mind telling you the truth about the performance.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiple pain points right now. 1. No Cloud Saves in 2024. I have a 14900kf / 4090 desktop and an ROG Ally. I can't play on both due to no cloud saves (moving saves around defeats the purpose.) This should be a launch feature of any game anymore and yet we keep seeing developers still refusing to support it day 1, if at all. So far I don't believe there is any proof they will add them. 2. Performance really is terrible. All the complaints about stutter are factual and anyone saying they don't get them is lying. They are also probably the same people who can't tell the cut scenes are 30fps but not even a smooth 30fps. It also flips in and out of cutscenes and they are rendered pretty low so least in my case you go from super clean graphics to potato graphics back to super clean. It's a harsh transition. 3. Interacting with some stuff is a pain. Seems like whatever you are standing in front of that can be interacted with has to be near the center of the screen or otherwise you can't touch it. I never got around to playing the original so was pretty excited for this and if I didn't get a nice discount by buying a key I probably would have waited for a sale as in it's current state it's not worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes...Finally a game about the average male loneliness experience Okay, all jokes aside. Silent Hill 2 Remake is possibly the greatest Silent Hill we've had since The Room back in 2004. The amount of passion and attention to detail made by Bloober Team in this cannot be understated. While keeping most of the story intact it expands upon it. The combat still feels clunky but in a modern way which is exactly what Silent Hill is. It's a experience you live first and THEN a fun video game. The atmosphere is something I haven't seen in the AAA space since the PS2 era and that's both nostalgic and comforting to know. Easily one of the best Survival Horror in years and the return of one the most important games of this mediumThanks Bloober Team for resurrecting Silent Hill

James was out here breaking Pyramid Head's ankles.

_childDocuments_.review: Found my wife and a backup wifey too, 10/10As a huge fan of the original Silent Hill 2, I think Bloober really did a phenomenal job and somehow pulled off improving upon something I always considered near perfection. Cutting it brief because we all got places to be, but 5 of my favourite things about the remake: Vastly expanded areas and exploration, with many references to other SH games, making for a more seamless-feeling Silent Hill game. How cool is it to be able to revisit iconic SH locations?Additional lore which adds some context and relevancy to the characters and the symbolism you see throughout the game, without it feeling dumbed down or over-explained. The game's sensitive topics are handled with maturity as well, which was initially a concern of mine. The combat, while still 'janky', is arguable the best the series has ever had. The bar for this was admittedly very low but hey, the combat surprised me with how satisfying it feels.I have to say, the vast amount of accessibility options included is impressive, and goes beyond the minimum standard for a lot of horror games. Huge kudos to Bloober for that.And last but not least, the characters, bosses, puzzles and areas have all seen major glow-ups that make the original counterparts almost seem forgettable. (And yes, it pains me to admit this!)Some negatives:- Could do with a performance patch or two. Even with my 4090 and powerhouse CPU, the game occasionally stutters a little. No big deal at all, but the PC version is clearly in need of some optimization.- The item pickup/interaction prompts were driving me insane, and can be very buggy at times. One of the items in a drawer, I couldn't pick up at all in fact. To make the matter worse, during crucial moments like boss fights, you can't spend seconds standing at an item spamming / angling yourself to hit the pick-up prompt.- I did admittedly feel like the pacing of some of the later areas in the remake wasn't quite as good as the original. Going from the hospital, to the prison, to the labyrinth with all segments being substantially longer than in the OG, felt a bit overwhelming. The remake could probably have benefited from being slightly trimmed down in the prison & labyrinth, to give you a little bit of a breather.- As amazing as the accessibility settings were, I did feel like some elements of the UI and game text could do with additional resizing options as well. This is me nitpicking though, and it's very possible I may have missed activating the right setting somewhere.All in all, please go play this game, it was and still absolutely is the golden standard of how a psychological horror game should be.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought a game could move me so deeply... As I learned more about its story, I realised how much I resonated with the character of James. Unfortunately, I couldn't empathise with him due to his actions, but I was truly affected by experiencing such a well-crafted narrative. My connection to James and the story is somewhat tied to my personal life, but that doesn't make the game any less impactful; in fact, the way it was executed makes it even more compelling. Looking at the events through the lens of my own experiences, this game wasn't just about James and the other characters confronting their traumas; for me, it was also a confrontation with myself. It turned out that this kind of personal journey was exactly what I needed all along. I may not be as deserving of punishment as James, but I too have made bad decisions that I felt warranted it... In 2019, my girlfriend was diagnosed with cancer. Of course, we weren't married like James and Mary, and I didn't experience the challenges of living together or caring for someone who was ill, but it was still awful. I wanted to help her as much as I could, even if it was a slim chance of her marrow responding. Besides offering psychological support, I felt powerless, and this process was wearing me down. She seemed to try to distance herself from me, and my biggest regret was allowing that to happen. I had grown distant from her; we felt like strangers, and we weren't letting the gap between us close. She made that decision entirely for my sake, and I accepted it, succumbing to my own selfishness. I should have been there for her; I shouldn’t have accepted that I didn’t need to be by her side. This game made me realise that I still can't forgive myself. I wish I could receive a letter from you too... At that time, I couldn’t do anything for you, but I would throw myself into hell for you now.  James and I are both examples of the worst kind of people; don’t be like us.

_childDocuments_.review: The only game where walking two steps in the fog feels like running a marathon! I’m still trying to figure out if I’m playing a horror game or participating in ‘who’s gonna have a heart attack first?’ Even the monsters are probably on stress leave by now. 😂Now it’s the real time for the review 6 November 2024 10:25 PMSilent Hill 2 is not just a game; it changed the way I see the world, especially the people in our lives. They represent scattered pieces of ourselves: our emotions, passions, love, and hatred. Each person in our life is a piece we’ve chosen to be there, reminding us of our inner selves. It’s natural to see reflections of yourself in your surroundings — a friend passionate about games, reflecting your playful side, another who is sad and depressed, mirroring painful truths in your life and mind, one who is angry, and another who is compassionate.Silent Hill chose James to uncover his true nature. It’s a game that understands what emotions would be like if they were alive. You see “Eddie” as anger and impulsiveness, always thinking of killing and getting rid of others, a character full of tension who denies his actions and tries to escape responsibility. “Angela,” on the other hand, represents the broken family issues, lack of trust, and discomfort. And then there’s “Pyramid Head,” the embodiment of murder turned into a punishment for James. In the end, it stops chasing him when he accepts the reality of what he’s done.Ultimately, Silent Hill is the one that chooses its victims, not the other way around. It clung to James tightly, trapping him in a cycle that lasted for 20 years. I’m sure the soil of Silent Hill dug up Mary’s memories when James buried her in the cemetery at the start of the game, using those memories to punish him for his actions.What a game and concept that competes with the fiercest of modern games! All the ideas and stories have been lost, leaving only competition through shallow technologies and graphics. Truly, every era has its own defining moments. I hope the age of excessive tech passes quickly, and we return to telling powerful, meaningful stories.

Overall, the Silent Hill 2 remake is a triumph that pays homage to the beloved classic while ensuring it resonates with both new players and longtime fans. _childDocuments_.review: First the map layout for building is bonkers.  The hospital has no operating rooms but a pool, with the locker room two hallways away.  Instead of signs pointing to radiology, oncology, orthopedics, etc.  The signs are for the cafeteria, stairs, lounge, pool, etc.  The non corrupted buildings are nonsensical which then doesn't make the corrupted buildings feel more confusing and profound.  It never feels like your exploring the town and falling down a rabbit hole.  You feel pushed to the next objective, that never feels strong enough to warrant your character putting himself in this much danger.  Through the original game you keep pushing on trying to figure out the central mystery of your wife.  In the first Act James decides his wife isn't there and this was pointless.  The enemies with target you without having seen you.  The enemies also appear from nowhere.  I checked a wall to make sure there was nothing hiding behind it.  I was blocking the door and went back thinking I had missed a first aid box and now there was a monster waiting where there hadn't been 3 seconds before.  The game encourages you to learn how to take lower enemies down with melee, where as the first game it encouraged you to run, because James isn't a skilled fighter/killer and you were very short on supplies.  It puts white fabric strips around places you can progress without a door.  However the Hospital is covered in White fabric.  At one point it go so dumb I just had to start laughing.  This games is just not that good.  It's a C+.  If we hadn't had our expectations so low with bloober team than more people would be seeing the flaws.  But everyone's just so happy it's even in a playable state that they're treating Bloober like they built a masterpiece, and all they did was not take a c**p on it.  Sigh.

_childDocuments_.review: The horror remake everyone has been waiting for.  We got Resident Evil 4, we got Dead Space, so the franchise king of horror had to make a return.  Who better than Blooper to give it the flavor we all have waited for.  Resident Evil 4 remake is the better game but when it comes to horror, Silent Hill 2 wins by making you feel uncomfortable and at times not want to continue.  And it repeatedly does this after taking breaks.  Took me around 17 hours exploring every inch and corner.  The boss battles were better than expected, with some really nice twists.  It feels like a brand new game in third person, and the puzzles are well balanced.  The combat is decent and can sometimes literally be a hit or miss.  The performance dips randomly but becomes unplayable at the last boss.  I had to drop from all high settings at 4k to medium 4k midway and then the last boss I had to put everything on low and switch to 2k.  The other cons are the current dayer dress up a girl so the horny man doesn't want to jerk it.  The characters also look quite different,  but for those that want to get mods and get back clothing and characters from the original, can do so.  No more jerking it to the big titty nurses but that's okay because the gameplay makes up for it, easily a 9 out of 10.  The story is phenomenal. Silent Hill 1, 3 and 4 remakes from the same team is a must!

I highly recommend picking up this game for new and old Silent Hill fans.  This game will be a very strong contender in future horror games if they maintain the formula they used making this masterpiece.

The frame rates are pretty low even on good hardware, most of the buildings are just decoration and not accessible which is a bit lame nowadays. Ammo and health stuff is extremely scarce, but they have implemented a nice difficulty selection system. James does not comment anything but important points or items in the game in contrast to the predecessors. So far I encountered only a very limited number of enemies.A highly debated point are the appearences of the characters which have been changed, or modernized if you like. Some like it, some hate it. Angelas looks a little bit goofy now, but James, Mary, Laura appear quite natural and ok. No improvement, no backstep in my opinion.Voice acting is very good, the mood is true Silent Hill like, the scarce resources are like survival horror is intended to be. Many more buildings of the town can now be visited, windows can be destroyed and, as already mentioned, the graphics are fantastic. The music is mostly identical to the original game, a very good choice. The rotten buildings are rich in details.Despite some flaws Silent Hill 2 Remake is a true Silent Hill game and shouldn't be missed!

_childDocuments_.review: To me, the original is a masterpiece, I really wanted to give this remake a 10/10, and up until about half-way through I was, but then the cracks began to show. It’s unnecessarily long, and too many things just don’t work for me as well as they did in the original, namely the scene direction, the writing, the cutscenes and the OTS camera style. It feels like an action game with very little character and repetitive encounters. The original had repetitive enemies too, but the atmosphere, music and scene tone always kept you feeling uneasy. The remake however is not something I would describe as tense or unsettling or even scary, but rather as predictable scripted and extremely linear like a kids roller coaster. The side characters also don't have the same presence in this one as they do in the original. They either overact in their cutscenes or underact their performances. The game at many points just feels boring, and the cutscenes drawn out and not as impactful. It feels like you’re playing a zombie game, not a psychological horror. It also holds your hand way too much, not allowing you to combine items that wont work and always guiding you to where you need to go by either bright lights or environmental "damage" not letting you get lost. It's far too linear and there are way too many heal items and ammo on standard anyway. Boss fights are a lot more fun though, but still they have very simple mechanics and are not challenging at all and often just make the game feel like an action game or just resident evil remake. I think if they at least kept the original fixed camera the game would feel a lot more tense, unsettling and atmospheric, as if you're always being watched.The puzzles were okay, my favorite was the labyrinth cube because after completing the rotten area I headed back and found the cube was still the same as before and the previous path hadn’t closed, which I soon found out meant my game had softlocked. Now I had to solve the real life puzzle of how to get around this. At first I had little success, until someone said to download the previous version from the steam console. That worked and I felt more satisfaction than I had the whole game so far. I could now push on to finish it, and finish it I did.The more I write this the more I realize this game just isn’t what it could have been. I can’t really recommend it to someone who hasn’t played the original. Your first experience of this story should be done right. Go play the enhanced edition on PC first and then come back, relax and check this game out just for fun.  Overall, some things work, but most of the changes for me just don’t, which takes away from the depth of the narrative and the experience.I give it a 6/10 for effort.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a massive survival horror fan haha yeah i guess you can say im pretty cool (ladies calm down).  I have played through them all resident evil, fatal frame, siren, garfield kart furious racing... yeah i guess you can say im quite the gamer. I was known as Mr. Survival Horror for most of my life. The first 3 Silent Hill games speak to me in a way that no other games really do... the fog, the uncanny valley, weird twin peakes esque dialouge, early 2000s music and vibe. The first 3 silent hill games i hold very near and dear to my heart ESPECIALLY the second one ill never forget playing silent hill 2 for the first time, i cried like a little baby wanting to suckle on my mothers tit. I had never been more moved by a game, the story wasnt anything super original but the execution of it and how it utilised its atmosphere, game mechanics to portray the feeling of dread and guilt and explore themes of abuse were so effective and potent and really stuck with me as a person. There was me BEFORE silent hill 2 and me AFTER silent hill, it almost felt like losing my virginity all over again. When i heard of the remake i could have jizzed my pants from the sheer amount of excitement i felt, boy was i lubed up and ready to play this game. I saw the trailers and while promising a little bit of doubt was planted more and more but after playing it i can safely say, not only is this a faithful remake it is also just a damn ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good survival horror game. I Feel so bad for the people over at bloober team because the amount of pressure to get this right would have made any man start balding and suffer an erectile dysfunction. I assumed they would have took the easiest route and done a 1:1 remake of the original game but that is not AT ALL what this is. They have took areas in the original game and completely expanded them and took their own twist on them and 9/10 these often are way better then the original imo.PROS:Exploration: i feel like this one is very subjective because the original i found at times to be a bit too frustrating because exploration was super ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ confusing and more often then not i found myself completely lost. In the remake the settings have a bit more of a linear approach to them NOW they arent like ubisoft type linear, you can still explore and get lost and have to check room to room like classic silent hill but the map is way more helpful, and its easier to find where you are meant to go.Puzzles: All the iconic puzzles in the OG are still here and even added upon and imo made even better like the coin puzzle in the apartments is WAY better in this version. There are also tons of new puzzles bloober added that are super fun and interesting to solve.Boss Fights: The boss fights are WAY WAY better in this version of the game especially abstract daddy. I wont spoil but that boss fight let me stunned at how they used it to tell a disturbing story, bloober really took the original ideas of the boss fights in the og and improved them.Environment and settings: Bloober really smashed it out the park like babe ruth hitting a home run with the enviorments in this game ESPECIALLY the otherworld holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ i could ejaculate at the otherworld. Some of the enviorments here are genuienly unsettling and places like the hospital are built upon so much more then the og imo. Enemies: This game is way harder then the og the enemies can kill you way easier and really actually pose a threat (compared to the og that even a zygote could beat it) this really makes the game more terrifying and anxiety filled as the enemies are way more dangerous and sneaky. Some times those killer legs will hide behinds walls to jump out at you, these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sentient legs are the bane of my existenceMixed:Story: very much hits the same beats as the og with some different paths a long the way and  i was a big fan of most of those changes until the last half with the game. Sadly imo they just did not hit the mark when it comes to the latter halfs story, this is very much a hollywoodified version of the og and so some of the camera choices, voice acting, and music choices kind of ruin the punch some of the original scenes had. Specifically the leave ending felt really weak compared to the original. Some of the decisions resulted in some of the story not hitting as hard as the original did IN MY OPINION. Apart from that i really respect what bloober did with the story 90 percent of it i would say is better then the original but the latter half of the game is where the story starts to fall apart for me.The original was lightning in a bottle it captured that eerie, disturbing, uncomfortable, twin peaks esque vibe perfectly. You felt like everyone you met was a disturbed individual detached from reality, the original even with simple stuff like composition are super emotionally effective. In the og leave ending its one static shot behind james and its a single shot after of the grave yard while mary reads the letter. Its subtle but effective and hits like a ton of bricks, the remake while good doesnt really hit the same emotional depth the original did. EDIT: After playing through this game some more i think the added emphasis on combat works in some aspect but can be incredibly frustrating and annoying because this is such a heavy exploration game. There are parts of this game where you need to explore to find key items but those areas are so padded out with so many enemies, that it makes exploring some of these areas incredibly frustrating. Some areas simply have too many enemies and make it impossible to explore areas without killing them. Also the more i get familiar with the game the more linear it feels, if you aimlessly walk around 7/10 times you will find out where you are meant to go. I get that they are just modernising the game by making it more linear and implementing more standard current day game mechanics but the more i play it the more linear it feels and more gammey it feels. Not saying this is good or bad, but this feels very gamey compared to the originalBasically if the original never existed this game would easily be a 9/10 experience but compared to some of the magic of the og it comes a bit pale but still easily a strong 8/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Love' doesn't feel like the right word.Silent Hill 2 is a bitter, dark, ugly, and beautiful portrait that understands everything that's worth hating and loving in humanity. Bloober Team have done a magnificent job translating the classic into the modern era. Some things are lost; I miss the fixed camera angles, and the cheesy voice acting, but these are facets worth giving up on, in my view, to see Silent Hill live on. Nothing in its substance- its brutality, its pain, its honesty- is bled away in this remake, as I truly expected from something made in a time where people are progressively obsessed with not offending anyone, even themselves. It stands as such a stark contrast to modern game design, where everything is sanded down and simplified. Silent Hill trusts the player to figure things out, to the point where its puzzles becoming bizarrely abstract, yet entrancing all the same. Every aspect of the game is doused in symbolism, in metaphor and purpose, that even the weakest parts act as the soles of a goliath. A singular example of artistic achievement in the medium. It doesn't focus on content for content's sake; the original skeleton doesn't even feel like it was visualized as a product or a way to make money, but as a means of expressing something from the soul. That expression still echoes today.There are arguments to be made about how much merit a remake can truly deserve. At the end of the day, even the very best can only bring an original excellence in line with current expectations. I cannot ascribe the quality of Silent Hill 2's writing or design to Bloober Team, much as I would like to, but, at the same time, I'd like to point at the sheer difficulty they must have faced in reimagining a 23-year-old game. The fact that they succeeded on any level is testament to their capability, and with the degree of faithfulness and reverence they obviously handled this with, I fully look forward to their future work with delight. It deserves the very best praise that I can give it: that it is Silent Hill 2, and not a drowned reflection. One of the best experiences of any year. I loved it.

_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: The remake largely sticks to the narrative of the original and yet manages to present itself in a refreshingly new and innovative way. The gameplay feels very solid and modern. The controls are fluid and responsive. In a combat situation, for example, you can react instantly and defend yourself or dodge to avoid major damage. You can even cancel an attack animation by pressing dodge which is a big win for me. The combat system in general feels perfect to me, better than the original I would even say which felt very clunky at times. While the game takes you from one level to the next in a linear fashion - which is by no means a negative in this type of game - you have a lot of room for exploration within the levels and can pursue your urge to pick up loot. Most of the time you are rewarded for this.Graphically, the game also gets full marks from me. I would particularly like to emphasize the facial expressions, most of which look incredibly realistic and natural, not least because the actors have done a fantastic job here. The atmosphere also benefits from the graphics. I often stood in long, sparsely lit corridors and had to pause for a moment because it just looked so good.Finally I would like to mention the sound design. Silent Hill games have always been absolute masterpieces when it comes to sound design. In the remake, the original has also been used as a guide. There are new sounds and music here and there but they integrate perfectly into the gameplay. In my opinion, it was absolutely the right decision to let Akira Yamaoka work his magic on this game again. Personally my biggest plus point is the sound when you pick something up which has been changed a bit but still reminded me immediately of the sound from back then.For me, the remake is a perfect success. Props to Bloober Team, who have outdone themselves with this one. I hope Konami and Bloober build on the success and remake SH1, SH3 and SH4 too!10/10, my personal GOTY!
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 10 hours in and I legitimately think this is the best horror game I've played in my entire life hands down. The spirit of the original SH games was captured perfectly in this remake and the game is filled with substance and little details to make every moment unsettling.I was lucky enough to have played the original series on PS1 and PS2, and can 100% recommend this remake to any old fans of the series, or first time players alike.  This game is a must have.

_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Now I don't remember much from the original series, I've played and finished at least SH1 & SH2 but from the first sequence, those that're familiar with PS1/PS2 era you feel the immediate atmosphere that is so is wonderfully nostalgic from the dark depressing tone and unmistakably soft yet hopelessness with the music! Only just hit the apartments that's going to be the inventable maze to traverse but so far so good! After coming away from the Medium, I was sceptical about Silent Hill 2 being handled by Bloober Team but I have to say they nailed it: the tone, vibe and feeling. I was so convinced it was going to be subpar after the initial combat trailer that made it look so floppy so long ago. Release looks and feels much more tighter which is a relief! You can tell this was a labour of love. It is incredibly realised in Unreal Engine 5. Even if it's not the greatest for performance, I freakin' love the opening area staring down the road of tree's with all the reflections. Despite being shrouded in fog the entire dang time, this game is stunning. I have hitches and micro-stutters but admittedly I do have everything cranked with Raytracing with a R7 3700x|4070ti so YMMV but inherently, there's performance issues. Lastly ultrawide support out the box but be sure to get the mod to unlock the frame-rate and get those cutscenes looking the best they can! Grab a controller, a good pair of cans, flick the lights off and strap in for a nostalgic time! Or if it's your first rodeo, the unsettling experience that is, Silent Hill.Here's to you Bloober Team, you deserve this!
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played Resident Evil 1&2 when I was a kid but never got around to any of the Silent Hill series. I know, I'm a horrible person. So glad they remade this. This now sits at the top of my favorite horror games. The pacing is great and maintains the old classic horror vibe where there is a LOT of silence, exploration, and ambiance, peppered with small enemies, and then something reminds you of your place in this world. Nothing like the trend over the last decade or so - where there's a Big Bad /constantly/ chasing you and bursting through walls like the damned Kool-Aid Man. That isn't horror, that's just action. This, however, gives you just the right amount of peace, so that when it's taken away you are psychologically damaged a little bit every time. It's lovely. I'm so glad that Bloober didn't feel the need to turn the game into a 10-hour foot chase, as some other franchises have done.Speaking of ambiance, the sound design on this is absolutely top notch. I'm a sucker for audio atmospheres and this has the quality of audio atmosphere to match the absolutely gorgeous prop and world design. Definitely recommend some good headphones with this.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing recreation of a classic gem. While this is an amazing remake and it feels faithful with amazing new visuals and gameplay improvements, I will say the optimization is where this game falls short. I've seen many different experiences from a wide assortment of players with diverse computers, and it is not feasable that a 4090 can struggle to run this game. I can get it to run comfy enough for me on a 3060 and a Ryzen 7 5800x, but its a shame that the best this game can run with everything set to its lowest is a rough 70-80 for me.I think personally that the quality of the game itself outweighs its poor optimization, and that's why I like it. My only true complaint about the game is the fact that cutscenes are restricted to 30 fps, even though the cutscenes are ingame and not preloaded. In summary, releasing a game for $70-80 with a 2 day early access when the game is poorly optimized is a horrible decision on Konami's part, and the game should have been delayed. But alas, this remake is beautiful and had so much effort put into it on Bloober's part and it's amazing they listened to the feedback they got and defied expectations. I'm still happy it released on Oct. 7 however, and I think Bloober team deserves praise for their work.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 remake of a 10/10 game. Loved my first playthrough and can't wait to play it again.The narrative, locations and events are extremely faithful to the original game, and only ever enriched or expanded upon. If you played the original & remake of Resident Evil 2 you would have noticed the significantly gutted B scenarios. This is not the case in the Silent Hill 2 remake. Every element of the original game has been captured.The combat is a lot harder than the original game, and mostly consists of dodge and counter-attack. As I progressed through the game I learned the enemy attack patterns and combat became a lot easier. I have seen criticism around this combat compared to the original, but in my opinion, the combat in Silent Hill has always been its weakest point and this change makes it much more engaging and panic-inducing. I started the game on Hard difficulty combat and quickly lowered it to Normal after getting my ass kicked.I played with puzzle difficulty on Hard which cannot be changed mid-playthrough. I made a poor life choice here. I don't know if I'm just dense, but sometimes, even after looking up the solution online, I couldn't understand why it was the solution. I recommend sticking with Normal difficulty puzzles.The voice acting is significantly improved upon over the original, and the soundtrack sounds fresh, and still makes me want to crawl into a shoe box.The visuals are immersive and maybe an 8/10 for 2024, but I think this game could've benefit from a path tracing implementation. Performance is poor though, most of the time my frame-rate was unstable. It was just good enough to be playable but this depends on your specs and settings.This is a big game. A lot bigger than the original. It took me 24 hours played to complete - but I am admittedly slow at completing games in general. It is not obvious to me where my additional time in the game was spent, but none of it felt like filler content. That said, I haven't played the original for probably over 20 years.
