_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is a game that is very dear to me. Though I did not have a PS2 to play it, I remember staying at my friend's place to play the game circa 2001 (wow, time long gone). It was a game that came out after 9/11 and made a massive impact because of how bad that month got.	How does the Remake hold up to the original? Well, a quick summary of the original is needed.	Silent Hill 2 follows as a sequel that can also work as a standalone game. You don't need to know about Silent Hill 1, but having it makes the game all the more attractive due to the town's history and dark undertones.It is a game that is not focused on combat (save for exceptional instances or boss fights). It is a psychological horror and a slow burn at that. It builds; it hints at secrets held within the town and James' (protagonist) past.	For first-timers, the game provided multiple endings based on unknown actions that the player performs, more so with the New Game+.	While James has access to weapons and firearms, he isn't the greatest, and that is okay. As a character, he is just an ordinary man, nothing special, nothing grand: not a special forces member, not a space marine, but a guy. This lack of polish in his combat style adds to the tension, to the fight or flight aspect of what makes us people.	Do we go ham and bash everything we see, or avoid them and find our Mary?	The voice acting and the animations were very stilted, purposefully, to add to the surreal nature of the world. Of course, some things do feel a bit like "Twin Peaks" in terms of how cheesy they sound. Animation involved the use of motion capture, which further led to the odd nature of the character's emotions.How does all of this come together in the Remake?SH2R, to keep it short, does a decent job of utilizing the Unreal Engine to give us a gorgeous game. The landscape is imposing, and the re-imagined designs of the creatures look spectacular, thanks in part to having the original creature designer of Team Silent helping to assist - (Masahiro Ito)	This, coupled with the incredible sound design of yet another Team Silent member - (Akira Yamaoka) - which can be heard in every object breaking, every footstep, not to mention the music and ambiance, all come together to make for a tense atmosphere.	When it comes to the creatures, Blooper Team gives us a few additional variations of each of the creatures. These creatures are generally faster and more aggressive. Many will close and grapple with James and horribly disfigure this poor guy.	Many of the bosses have had adjustments made to them to take them from the simple, plodding sods that they were and turn them into genuinely frightening creatures hunting after you.	Unfortunately, with all of these changes made to the Remake comes baggage.	Graphics—While gorgeous, the game is undoubtedly unrefined for many people. Even I, with an AMD and 4080 graphics card, had game crashes, major stuttering, and odd graphical glitches. Fixes have helped in some places, but I had to resort to modifying the engine in order to keep it smooth. Typically, I've had no trouble running the game at Ultra, but again, certain moments suddenly stutter, most likely due to something z-fighting in the distance or such.	Combat- James has more freedom of movement and a dodge function, but as you run into the more aggressive enemies, this can become extremely difficult. The enemy's speed and numbers can quickly overwhelm you; this is most apparent in the Otherworld. Blooper did try their best to provide a level layout that gave us the ability to squeeze through cracks and escape or even trap these creatures. Still, again, you run into so many of them that it can become a wild circus of you trying to zip between the enemy just to make some breathing room. The 2nd variation of creatures is faster and meaner and often will grapple you and punish James horribly, and in greater difficulties, it leads to a lot of game-overs since the camera's sluggishness tends to fight against you at the worst times.	Boss Fights- Most of them are generally fair, but you will find yourself in at least 2 of them where the enemy's speed and actions can often catch you off guard and scrambling to try and reload your weapon(s). Now, I didn't mind it, but I can see this becoming aggravating for others, and take into account that I play casually for fun, not for achievements.	Character models—Yes, I will include this because certain aspects bug me as a 3D artist. Angela and Mary, while the body models are fine, I have issues with the pudding faces because, for one thing, that isn't precisely how the anatomy works, plus it takes away from the fact that they are supposed to be alluring. Angela's beauty is tied to her tragedy, while Maria's beauty is tied to James's history.	I'm mixed about James himself. On the one hand, he is a little too Leon Kennedy-looking. Honestly, I prefer the look of the original James, as again, it felt like an every-man. I do give credit to the team for providing small details to James as the game continues, such as looking tired, having dirty hands, etc.	Audio- Honestly, I really can't say anything against it. I really enjoyed the re-imagining of the soundtrack and how faithful it is to the original. Again, that isn't really fair since the original artist worked on it. The ambiance and foley effects are fantastic, and honestly, I feel I can leave it there.	The biggest sin of this game, for me, is that it comes to a moment where it really begins to overstay its welcome. The change in enemy numbers and combat ends up becoming a speed bump that gets in the way of the story's momentum, and that is what troubles me most. The story provides you with fantastic depth, and you want to move on, but then a lot of combat begins to filter in between you and the next bit of the story. For me, it was when I got to the hospital's Otherworld that I started to get exhausted from fights, to the point that it slightly mired my thoughts with the Prison, which took a moment to set aside my thoughts on the hospital, the Prison introduced a new variation of one of the enemies that I both loved and hated. I loved it because of the use of the creature, and I hated it because it was designed for a character that reacts faster and doesn't fight the camera to aim at this thing.Final Thoughts and Future InstallmentsHonestly, I give this game a fair B- to B+. Certainly, it isn't the original, and when it is at its best, it hits that B+, but at its worst, it gets that B-.	It is a great game, and Blooper did an outstanding job, mainly translating a game that so many of us loved for its atmosphere to 2024. I do feel that they could have allowed this game to bake just a little longer in the oven.	In the end, I would give Blooper a chance to bring us a refined Silent Hill 1, and if that does well, Silent Hill 3. I hope that they will perhaps try to put more emphasis on the player's progression from story elements to story elements, as opposed to enemy/boss fight to enemy/boss fight.Final Final ThoughtsThe Endings get a C- for not giving us the proper goofy joke clips in the Dog Ending. Seriously, it goes straight to credits. You couldn't even just rip the old silly ending slideshow for us?

_childDocuments_.review: After Kojima's Silent Hill was canceled, Konami faced a lot of criticism because, first of all, Kojima is a genius, and secondly, the short demo P.T. turned out to be incredibly successful (I liked it as well). I had little doubt that Kojima's Silent Hill would have been great. But Kojima and Konami parted ways like ships in the night, and the project was shelved - until recently.Konami decided to entrust the game to Bloober Team, the studio responsible for games like Blair Witch, Observer, The Medium, and Layers of Fear. Interestingly, I liked each of these games in its own way, but to be honest, they were all B-tier games, and they even had performance issues. (The Medium, for example, would cause even powerful graphics cards to struggle when it had to load textures in two worlds simultaneously.) Overall, it’s hard to call their games masterpieces or extremely popular.However, the game turned out to be awesome - almost perfect, but not quite. It’s clear that resources weren’t unlimited, but it’s also clear how carefully and diligently Bloober Team worked with what they had. There aren’t a ton of enemies or enemy types, but I think they’re well-made and thoughtfully designed. The same goes for the bosses. The locations are often maze-like, reminiscent of Resident Evil, but what I really liked were the puzzles, not all of which were super obvious or as straightforward as in RE.Things got worse when the first gameplay trailer was shown. It featured clunky, jerky animations straight out of 2008, which fueled doubts about the game, and everyone started expecting a disaster.Even though the game keeps you on edge and really captures that Silent Hill vibe, by the end, you start getting tired of the formula: shoot something, find an item, solve a puzzle, repeat. The game isn’t too long, but this repetitiveness makes it feel longer than it actually is. There are also some issues with freezing, but as Digital Foundry explained, this is related to Unreal Engine 5. Even if you lock the framerate at 30 FPS and the frames remain stable, there are still noticeable stutters. (For some reason, I didn’t get the claimed 60 stable FPS; I had drops to 40 FPS and, at one point, even to 30.)In conclusion, I think everyone got exactly what they were expecting: the game has great puzzles, decent action, and a thick atmosphere. I really enjoyed it, and for those who are still undecided about buying it - I highly recommend it.I hope the sales will be good, and we'll be looking forward to the next remake from Bloober Team!

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailers for the Silent Hill 2 Remake, I was honestly shocked. I mean, I was like, “Whoa, are they finally making a new game for the PS3 after all these years?” Yeah, it really looked that bad. After what I saw, I gave up on following this game and once again completed my Silent Hill 2 playthrough ritual, which I do once every 3-4 years.(Thanks for nothing, Konami)I watched the latest gameplay videos that came out 1-2 months ago, and well...it actually looked good. Sure, it seemed a bit action-heavy, but it was something that could be given a chance. So, a few weeks before its release, I pre-ordered the game. I've been playing for a few hours now (okay more like 7-8 hours but who's counting?), and the game actually looks great! The action part? Yeah, it’s more prominent than in the original, but so far, it hasn’t really been a problem. It feels like they’ve stayed true to the original, which, for me, is way more important than fancy graphics or cutting-edge mechanics. After all, I have yet to come across a game with a storyline as well-written and emotionally devastating as Silent Hill 2. The game is going well so far, and I hope I won't be disappointed.Long story short, this remake is definitely worth reading Mary's letter again in its new-gen version guys.Thanks Bloober Team.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: A master of atmospheric horror is back, and it's pretty! Bloober Team has done a phenomenal job with this remake. I remember playing bits and pieces of the original game back when it came out, but I was pretty young at the time and I found it way too terrifying to finish. Although I plan to complete the game this time, it's not for lack of effective scares. The overall sense of unease and outright horror this game creates is almost unmatched, in my opinion. The visuals are great. Graphically, this is a very demanding game, but I'm about an hour in with no real hiccups so far. And the sound design....truly one of the highlights of this game. I highly recommend playing this game with headphones if you're brave enough.Overall, I cannot recommend this game enough for fans of the horror genre, but it's not for the faint of heart.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say much as I've only played an hour, but the last time I pre-ordered a game it was a disappointment (Cyberpunk 2077) so I'm a bit scared this time. No pun intended. Runs quite well on a 5800X and 4070 with ray tracing on so far. Sound over headphones is great, especially the voice acting.Update: Some tweaks needed as I got some stuttering here and there. RT switched off for now.Update 2: It's platin now after 3 runs in 42 hours. I didn't have a single crash within that time. Thx bloober team for the beste remake I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Going to preface that I never played the original Silent Hill 2 so I'm not able to draw from that to influence my feelings on this remake, so this is my first real experience with the game story. That said, to me, this was a fantastic game and a real breath of fresh air for the season. In contrast to the Resident Evil games that normally blow up the charts, having this slower more methodical approach to horror is really nice. If anything I would say that they should have backed off the combat a bit more and just let us explore the spaces. I can say that cause the world they have built (rebuilt in this case) is well fleshed out and visually extremely interesting. Even just exploring feels very creepy as you look through the town. I'm probably going to echo what a lot of people are feeling, but it does drag on a bit too long and could have used some tightening just to help with a more consistent feeling throughout. The combat just isn't as interesting as they may have thought, so it would possibly benefit from having some more exploration scenes. Story is of course super interesting and very bleak, exactly what you would want. Without having the context of the original game, I was full invested in seeing what was happening and trying to read into everything you encounter. All in, I would highly recommend this game. It's a fantastic survival horror experience that I think fits well into the modern landscape.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: Having an absolute blast so far.Bloober cooked, and they delivered a fantastic remake. Faithful to the source material, it expands it further and there are little easter eggs everywhere about the old locations where things used to be that you can interact with.The first encounter with Pyramid Head literally sent chills down my spine...A game that I've loved and learned down to the last detail is managing to scare me again like it did back then... It's absolutely WONDERFUL!3 hours in so far, just reached the Blue Creek Apartment complex... And I can't stop playing!EDIT:Same day, 16 hours later... I literally couldn't stop playing, I went for a full run... Holy God, this is an absolute MASTERPIECE. Bloober did it. They brought Silent Hill 2 in this era, with spot-on accuracy to the source material!I didn't think they could, but they did! 10/10 from me, easily. Being SH2 my all-time favourite game, I can say without any doubt that this is unbelievably good!MUST BUY!
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna try to keep this short and sweet--this is a fantastic and very well-made remake. Graphics are amazing. Lighting effects among the best I've seen in a modern game of this kind. Excellent soundtrack and just amazing sound design in general.With that said I'm going to warn you about one thing: the endgame sections of the game are EXCRUCIATINGLY long. Pretty good pace in the beginning and midgame. But once you reach the endgame you'll be begging for it to be over. I get that players want to feel like they "got their $70 worth" but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, bro. I feel like most of us should be happy with a quality game that we can get 12-15 hours of solid content. More hours doesn't always equate to "getting your money's worth". I said what I said. But overall, terrific job by Bloober. Thanks for giving us far more than our money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has only played the original once a few years back, it was already one of my favorite horror games of all time. When I heard the announcement of the remake i was unimpressed, how could you remake what was already perfect? The trailers hadn't impressed me and I was set to ignore it and hear what other people thought of it. But once it came out and saw "overwhelmingly positive" and read that bloober team actually did it and some people were calling it "better than the original" I had to buy it. As someone who doesnt buy games on release EVER anymore spending the 70USD was a big moment. Right away the voice acting and graphics blew me away. The fog looked incredible and the atmosphere was spot on. I was weary of the third person perspective because I always liked the use of fixed camera angles in survival horror. But it felt good and I feel didn't ruin the atmosphere, although I might still prefer the fixed camera. Combat has been IMMENSLY overworked, with a dodge that adds atleast a little bit of complexity to what used to be sit and mash with no risk of getting hit. The guns feel awesome to use and and the bosses were fun. If you even remotely like silent hill or enjoyed the resident evil 2 remake I would say you would love this. Im now hoping they go back and remake 1 and 3 as those would be amazing to see get this treatment.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: An honest remake but it needs some tweaking gameplay wise its not very precise and that's a bit problematic on hard mode combats. Otherwise the game is good, the original is an intemporal masterpiece that can't be replaced but that version has good ideas. The atmosphere is very good, sound design is phenomenal. The level design is better than in the original. The story is remade well, James' VA killed it ! The other voice actors are good too, my only complain story-wise would be Maria's VA, but I dont think its because of her skills but more about the acting she was told to do.In conclusion : Its a good remake, you can't replace the original with it but its a fresh new take on a 20 years old game with some unique qualities like the recent Resident Evil remakes and its thousand times better than the Alone in the Dark reboot released earlier this year for example. I would still recommand to play the original first for those discovering the franchise, and playing the remake afterward.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing Silent Hill 2, this game is amazing, I think Bloober team ticked every box imaginable. Story telling 10/10Puzzles and level design 10/10Graphics and gameplay 10/10Left speechless after completing the game, will definitely play through it again. If you're on the fence just buy it don't hesitate.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 8 hours in but I have been enjoying the game so far. Feels like classic survival horror that I fell in love with 20 years ago.As for anyone crying about "changes", nothing feels changed from this game. Everything feels much better both mechanically and graphically. Environments are better. Characters look better. Having the ability to share an old franchise with the youth of today while dressing it up nicely to make it feel better and more in line with the games and technological/mechanical advancements of today's market.The game feels great. It looks great. It runs really well on my system as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most other remakes, this one is here instead of a good port, not alongside it. Which is in bad taste. So is the superstitious grifter nonsense stating that remakes diminish the originals or deter people from them. I enjoyed the remakes of late, so I can't agree with the simplistic "iterations bad" position. Even when sometimes people use one as a replacement for the original, we shouldn't be control freaks about it. I think that more often it happens due to the lack of a streamlined alternative rather than the core idea being cursed. You can't make an average Joe jump through hoops like emulation. That's why companies should stop the practices that deprive people of access to the originals on the same platforms. It's on Konami & Co.To break and reassemble something as delicate without it showing cracks was an impossible task for Bloober, to begin with. Or maybe painting over the cracks is the real problem. Anyway, I had to put my money where my mouth was and play it. To a big fan, there’s no bigger fan who knows better. I thought it would be a soulless cash grab, but while the ludicrously expensive fan project doesn't deserve to bear the name, it shows more respect for its roots than the outsourced trash that came before it. To show you what I mean, look no further than all the "options of respect" in the menu. Original devs and actors in the credits, a filter to apply the 90s colour palette, and other UI tweaks to bring it closer to the source. Not to mention the overall polish. As if to apologise for the arrogance of stamping their names on the franchise.Bloober are tone deaf when it comes to writing, but their eyesight is mostly fine. Beautiful dilapidated environments all around. The Otherworld is the strongest suit, flaking and menacing. The public bathrooms and garbage piles are sublime. The fog crawls behind you like a predator about to pounce, then creeps away when you turn to look. The hospital, the hotel, and the town itself are filled with finer details, adding to the sense of heartbreaking abandonment. Alas, the prison reminded me of The Suffering more than Silent Hill. Used to be bleak and unsettling, banging on your soul, now it's just dark & spooky. The Blue Creek Apartment is bland and your encounters with Pyramid Head there feel weak. Is it the direction? Maybe also the sound design. The music is good, but the refined ambience is too easy on the ears to be truly unnerving. Even the radio is toned down.The remake can terrify, albeit, it failed to oppress my psyche. It's not about fear alone, it's about grief. I replayed SH2 many times. One would think there was nothing left to fear or feel at that point, yet I had to drop out in the middle of my fourth playthrough because my nightmares got worse and my unceasing grief for the game's motley crew started to stress me out. It was a game where having a breather felt even more suffocating than being chased by monsters. Just being exposed to it felt wrong. Its influence keeps growing, torturing me into loving my nightmares. As I love Silent Hill. The only games where a fictional character's death struck me down. Every time. The remake couldn't reproduce it. I had fun, but I didn't feel a thing. It's not on the new appearances alone, they changed more than that.This game's crap is extremely realistic, and so are its characters. All in all, I saw no sense in the re-designs. Stop giving me lessons, I ain't gonna learn a thing from you. The original intent is more important than trying to correct the general public's beauty standards. That said, people's faces here aren't as repulsive as some say, only deglamorised. Except James is a f#ckboy for no reason. He's still rocking that where's-my-wife drip, still doesn't roll up his sleeve before digging deep in sh#t. Still, this isn't him... we'll get to it. Maria reminded me of Jon Lovitz, but her cougar mannerisms remain, which is narratively important, and she has more lines to flesh her out. But she's less creepy for that, and where are her cloudy eyes? She didn't need to feel more real or have her feelings over-explained.The new voice cast is fine. Like other things, the polished acting seems off to an old fan. Again, I have a problem with James. Aloof and uncharismatic, the old one made every dialogue awkward to sit through. It emphasised the feeling of loneliness. Guy Cihi's inner emptiness was miles ahead of Luke Roberts' formulaic theatrics. It's not just him, there's something about the new direction that made conversations less uncanny. Look, there were few people in Silent Hill and we couldn't even find solace in their company, unable to establish a meaningful personal connection through a character whose mind roams elsewhere. They all kept their distance, showing how a sick mind works, pushing others away in a time of need to drown in solitude. That impression is lost when they don't seem as mad in their antics.Thankfully, the glistening monsters are still hot enough to symbolise. Your first encounter and many more have changed places. A stickler in me is full of indignation, but did I really want to be able to predict everything? Here, the game played with my expectations, caught me off guard. I didn't like the revisionism, even if I don't feel strongly about it. Just as I'm not sure how I feel about some encounters being over-directed. The abundance of movie-like scripts serves the tension, yet also seems cliche and goes against the vibe of an uncontrolled nightmare Team Silent perfected. Yet, the pacing is on-point, with the downtime spent on phenomenal puzzles, the best in the genre.Better than ever, if fact, and so is the violence. Silent Hill’s combat was a balancing act between satisfying and indulgent. After all, it all looks like domestic abuse. Bloober exercised restraint by adding snappier movement, dashes, yet nothing more. The fights are bloody visceral. It's hard to time dodges, the combat has that unpredictably ragged rhythm. It's a brutally simple system that doesn't overplay its hand. Monsters now act more cunningly, pack a punch, and tank damage on Hard. Dealing with more than one in close quarters often means certain death. Gotta respect their patterns and avoid when possible. Not just to save time but to live.They relentlessly follow you around since there's no concept of different screens! No pausing to view a map or heal. Boss fights are so good now, always leaving me on my last legs. As, frankly, every other nurse. The original wasn't that challenging, so I took this as an improvement. If a Silent Hill game can't kick my teeth in mentally, I let it do that by other means. Until you get a gun, that is! The ammo starvation is real, but you're drip-fed properly. And still, it's not that easy to hit the twitching fiends. The need for resources made for a great scavenger hunt. I liked the mechanic of smashing windows in cars and shops to get in or just maraud some goodies. I feel like I just beat a fun flick in the vein of The Evil Within. That's the problem.I can see now that Bloober aren't fiends, they're fans. It matters, for this is the first attempt in 20 years that I didn't hate. Leaving a decent impression, the remake fails to capture the melancholic essence of a grieving nightmare that made Silent Hill hit so hard. But while it ringed hollow to me, I can't ignore the sincerity or deny the fun I had. Can one really draw a comprehensive picture by retelling Mulholland Drive or convey Pavarotti by humming Nessun Dorma to a friend? Bloober got the lore, but couldn't hit the notes, occasionally replacing raw emotion with melodramatic slop. Should I blame them? The team did well but couldn't achieve the impossible - be Team Silent.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: I had never played the original 2001 release of Silent Hill 2, although I did watch a full playthrough with all the endings multiple times on Youtube before playing this remake. I was part of the skeptics that had doubts on whether Bloober team and Konami could really pull this off correctly, and I waited through the first week of the game's release to check reviews and impressions. In short, I had plenty of reasons to have my foot back when it came to this game.However, just like the twist in the story herein, Bloober team and Konami proved my concerns futile: this game is a Masterpiece, through and through. No ends or buts, after playing this game for nearly 40 hours across multiple playthroughs (default and NG+) and getting all of its achievements, this is a must-have title on everyone's Steam library. While I still find the industry's new $70.00 standard price off-putting, and that this game is a remake of an existing classic Masterpiece, I would still purchase it at full price.As far as some points of criticism or discussion, initially the game ran like crap, tons of hitches and stutters, and no Nvidia Frame-Gen or AMD Fluid Motion to speak of. The game has been patched since to fix most stutters, and Frame-Gen/Fluidd Motion paired with your preferred upscaling solution is a win-win. Game feels smooth, responsive, and looks gorgeous still. And the benefit of Frame-Gen's implementation here is that it makes the 30FPS cutscenes into 60FPS smooth-as-butter monents to watch and enjoy.I should note that I am playing on 4K, with the highest settings selected except for DLSS on Performance andd Frame-Gen on. I am running on an AMD 7950x3D CPU and an Nvidia RTX 4090, both watercooled, and the game now runs at 4K often above 100FPS, with some more demanding areas ddroping to around 80FPS with the previously indicated settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake is one of the best horror game I ever played. Easily being in company of great horror games like Soma, Amnesia A Dark Descent, Resident Evil 7. The game centers on James Sunderland a man who travels to this creepy, foggy town called Silent Hill after he unexpectedly receives a letter from his dead wife.  The whole game consists of you exploring the town in search for your wife and solving the mystery which is a treat in its self because at the end you are thoroughly surprised by the truth. The best thing game has to offer is the unparalleled atmosphere. It transports you so easily in the world of the game. It is one of the most immersive games I ever played. From the emotional roller-coaster you experience as you tag along with James on his surreal, psychological journey, to the creepy vibe of the foggy, monsters infested town's streets or the depressing, dark hallways and buildings.  The games's characters are some of the best I have seen in all my gaming experience with incredibly fleshed out-believable personalities, not being the one dimensional boring characters you see in most games rivaling the ones in the masterpiece of game that is Last of Us. You actually begin to care for them or feel sorry for them or get uncomfortable because of the depressive, unhinged behaviour shown. Other important aspect of the game are the puzzles which are a nice addition which fit perfectly with this weird, deranged tone of the game. The puzzle are not easy-necessitating some use of your brain which is nice thing, some of them being really unique and interesting. The combat is challenging enough that is not boring and not so hard that you get frustrated. You get plenty of supplies if you explore carefully all the places. You never feel like you are low on ammo if you use it wisely and combine shooting with melee attacks when the situation makes it possible. The dodge mechanic helps greatly in this regard. But you have to be careful not to get overwhelm by enemies in tight, smaller spaces. The sound and music is again some of greatest out there contributing perfectly to the unsettling , immersive atmosphere of the game. From the random creppy sounds haunting the deserted building's halls, streets to the well done soundtrack. Promise of the Forgotten is my favorite song which i kept listening much after finishing the game while still pondering on what I experienced in this amazing game.  The game visuals are great. The game is made in Unreal Engine 5, has Ray Tracing and all the bells and whistles when it comes to modern gaming graphics. I found myself often taking breaks from doing the next objective and admiring the environment, making screenshots and taking in the creepy vibe of the game.The only issue at the time I played the game was the performance problems and the existing traversal stutter which hindered a bit from what was already a amazing experience. Overall Silent Hill 2 Remake is a masterpiece of horror design with some of the best creepy atmosphere offering an unforgettable experience, great-interesting story and fully fleshed out characters, great sound and visuals but with some performance problems. I would rate the game a 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent remake, and a truly unique experience. I would recommend this game to any fan of survival horror, whether you are new to the franchise or a die hard Silent Hill fan.The original Silent Hill 2 is a revered game and for good reason, everything from the atmosphere, setting, story and characters captured my attention from the start. I had never played the original, but had heard much of the praise that game received, and after playing through the remake I understand why. Silent Hill 2 has the most unique and consistent atmosphere/setting than any survival horror game I have played. Silent Hill is more than a setting, it is a character in itself with depth, themes, and personality.I think Bloober team did an excellent job recreating what made the original game so special. The symbolism, themes, story, and atmosphere all masterfully work together to craft an experience that sticks with you long after you complete the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's great, like all good remakes it gives the opportunity to play Silent hill 2 but in a different way rather than being a full reboot or just a graphical remaster.Honestly, everything I had any reservations about has so far been decent to great, if you like the original, this incredibly faithful and if you're new to the series, it's a fantastic opportunity to start.If I had to force myself to find issues, I would only be thinking of good things that maybe could have been just a tiny bit better had they been given infinite money and time, which is ridiculous.If anything, any of the "drawbacks" (if they can even be called that) come from almost trying to be too faithful, but even those are purely a matter of personal preference.The atmosphere is fantastic, the visuals, especially the fog continue to impress, the facial animations are great along with the VA's behind them. I'm honestly so happy for Bloober being able to pull this one off, especially how much unnecessary ♥♥♥♥ they got after the first trailer.

_childDocuments_.review: Best game i've played this year (story/gameplay/atmosphere/whole package wise).I don't like survival horrors - they're usually become more annoying than scary as you progress. In SH2 Remake, the tension, horror elements, puzzles, fighting mechanics, story - all of his is so masterfully balanced. I never felt underpowered/unbalanced, but at the same time, even with 20+ healing items in my pocket, I felt so fragile, that I'm constantly being oppressed, with a huge sens of depression and surrounding danger.What surprised me the most - there is a very little usage of usual "jump scare" mechanics - the game relies more on psychological horror/fear. I love the story - the ending is one of the best plot twists I remember in my video game memory.Highly recommend this to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: FoV cannot be changed.Vignette cannot be disabled.Chromatic aberration cannot be disabled.Mouse acceleration cannot be disabled.Anisotropic filtering is tied to the same setting as texture quality.Controller rebinding is non-functional. Several functions use the same button by default, if you bind any other function to one of these buttons, it unbinds all other functions assigned to that button. They only way to fix this is to revert to default settings.Recommended specs are inaccurate and performance is terrible. My PC is well above the recommended specs and I can barely get a stable 60fps in the starting area on low/medium settings, and even then there is a noticeable amount of stuttering.Cutscenes are locked to 30fps.I'm sure the gameplay is good, but these issues are completely unacceptable in a $100 game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical (and honestly worried) when I heard that Bloober Team was working on Silent Hill 2 as their games are hit and miss but oh my goodness. I will gladly eat my words and say that I was wrong to doubt them, they absolutely nailed this remake! It is genuinely creepy and scary! You can tell these folks are big fans of the original game themselves, they even added neat easter egg nods to the original, if you find one you'll know what I'm talking about! For me, this is a much needed breath of fresh air, I haven't felt genuine fear from a movie or video game in a VERY long time. The detail that they put in the environment is breathtaking! They did make changes and add to the story to make it a bit long which I appreciate. I'd love to say more but I wouldn't want to spoil anything for a curious reader but I will tell you, if you're thinking of pulling the trigger on this one and don't know anything about Silent Hill? DO IT. This game is regarded as possibly the greatest psychological horror game of all time and for good reason. Akira Yamaoka has also returned delivering his amazing soundtracks as well and my goodness the sound is GOD tier! The ambient music SIGNIFICANTLY compliments and expresses the area or combat its incredible. I would definitely trust Bloober Team with a Silent Hill 1 and 3 remake if they'd be down! Playing with headphones late at night in a dark room is the way to do it!Silent Hill 2 Remake slaps tits!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a better pc than I do, you'll love this game! Yeah, this is really unfortunate, but my pc is moderately decent. _childDocuments_.review: Bloober Team accomplishes something that I have never seen before — taking a perfect masterpiece and somehow enhancing it even further. While it is of course a different experience from the original game, this for me is the definitive version of . Team Silent's original work in 2001 was a gripping thriller; a psychological horror with depth that could only be found in this medium. While I was skeptical prior to the game's release, Bloober Team perfected staying true to the original while tweaking certain aspects to be just that much more better. They say don't invent the wheel, but Bloober Team somehow made lightning strike twice. 10/10. My game of the year, and probably one of the best video games I have ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill is one of the most beautifully crafted games and there aren't ANY games out there that are like it. This game is unique, even the OG games have such an enchanting appeal that will just hook you onto the game in a heartbeat. This game can really call out to you and make you feel connected to it, to the atmosphere.. to the characters and to their pain and suffering that they have gone through. Silent Hill really does an amazing job at capturing you and keeping you engaged within the game. its simply a perfect portrait, amazingly painted to the littlest detail. The horror, sadness and suffering, grief and guilt aspects of the game are amazingly described and shown in characters such as James, Maria and Angela.I am so thankful that the devs have given us such a beautiful, aesthetically pleasing and true adaptation from the original game. Silent Hill 2 remake is truly one of the best remakes of the year. When you get into Silent Hill it will always remain with you and will always be a part of you, a truly unforgettable journey into this psychological horror themed game. Its worth any amount of money

_childDocuments_.review: This remake of  deserves to go down in history as a shining example of why you should never judge a game’s book by its perceived cover. It feels like for the last year, all the impressions I’ve ever heard or read about this game has been how it was destined to fail, how it was going to disrespect the source material, and it would likely dumb things down for idiot casuals.Lo and behold, those of us who have experienced the game in its entirety have seen the light, or rather the absolute darkness that Bloober Team had surprised us all with.I want to start with the source material breakdown, because as someone who has been actively listening to SH2’s OST for the last 23 years, as well as revisiting James Sunderland’s sad journey at least two dozen times over the course of that time, I found myself smiling like a teenager in 2001 all over again, because not only did the game bring out the big-guns when it came to paying attention to most of the iconic moments (yes, I know, there was ice cream instead of pizza), but it elevated a lot of weaker aspects of the original. Exploration of the town is expanded in the best way possible, combat has been drastically improved, and every boss has been turned into a glorious horrifying recreation that tests your mettle and ammo supply in a way that feels truly survival horror.James’ journey has never felt more dreary and exciting.Immersion has reached an all-time high, and I genuinely hope that Bloober Team is going to be behind any future Silent Hill releases, as they just . I HIGHLY advise you use a Dual Sense controller (add gyro bound to L2 if you want some smooth aiming while you’re at it), because the way the vibration has been utilized made my skin crawl in several subtle ways. Yamaoka’s legendary audio has been preserved and simultaneously bolstered by so many new, exciting ear-gasms that I hope you won’t spoil for yourself before jumping into this, blind. Even the subtle changes like the way Mannequins don’t instantly trigger your radio leads to so many great sweat-inducing moments throughout.Combat is a colossal win, here, and I want to qualify that statement by saying: This game should, in my opinion, end the conversation about whether good combat makes a game less scary. The answer is: It doesn’t. I don’t know how it plays on normal mode, but Hard mode (IMO the way this game deserves to be played) absolutely makes the combat a joyful time. Fighting enemies never felt boring to me thanks to the variety of maneuvers the monsters can do, along with giving you fun dodge mechanics, but I also made a habit of avoiding fights as much as I could, simply because the slightest error in dodging instantly costs you precious consumable heals. There were several instances where I thought I had the combat down, with “Welp, I’ve got XXX bullets and xx healing now, what could go wrong?” Only for later boss encounters to eat three quarters of those resources, leaving me sweating over my imminent predicament. The best attribute to combat is: Your guns are not toys to have fun with, they are constant, dwindling compromises. Do you spend a rifle round head-shot on a knife-nurse? Or risk missing handgun bullets as she twitches toward you? Or risk lots of damage going full-melee? These are the choices you are constantly making, and it feels great.Seeing SH2 in this new blaze of glory feels like the happy ending we deserved, as fans. You owe it to yourself to dive into this one if you want a genuinely superb survival horror experience. I have zero regrets paying the full price, and as much as I cherish my time with the original, I believe we now have a superior version, and I loved every moment of it. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a AWESOME remake with so much love and care put into it. The acting, the characters, the bosses, the environments, the sounds. ALL of it is just a amazing love letter to the OG SH2 while also mixing in some fresh original ideas by Bloober Team. The combat is a really nice blend of simple to understand but difficult to master and feels really satisfying. You can also play the whole game without attacking an enemy like in the original which gives you more of a choice to either fight or just run but you can and will get overwhelmed if you're not careful. I am overwhelmed with joy to be able to say that I can recommend any new fan of the series to play this game to really GET what Silent Hill is about and it brings me even more joy that Silent Hill is finally being talked about again. Give this game a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: (Will update this review after completion)This remake is, in my opinion, everything silent hill fans could've hoped for. Silent hill 2 has for a long time now been my favourite horror game of all time and one of the best stories in a videogame ever told. When this remake was announced I was concerned with Bloober team heading the project after their handling of trauma and guilt (core concepts in silent hill) in their game The Medium. I am happy to say they really outdid themselves and perfectly captured the raw emotion in this game.The atmosphere is perfect, extremely surreal and dreamlike. You never feel comfortable but at the same time it is welcoming and makes you want to delve further into the mystery. They really did a good job of the fog, masking things that are even a few feet ahead of you so you never quite know what is lurking a few steps away.The sound design is phenomenal, there are often moments of whispers that sound like they are coming from right next to you and it really keeps you on edge and jumpy. The music of silent hill 2 was always a strong part of the game so I was thrilled to see Akira Yamaoka return for the music and he honestly killed it. The new songs are just as good as the original but have been edited and improved.The graphics really are top-notch, the raytracing looks gorgeous especially when you get the flashlight and are roaming the apartments. The area it covers is almost strangled and kept narrow which really adds to the fear, you can't always make out what is just outside of your field of view. The performance could certainly be better which I imagine will be fixed with patches but on a gaming laptop with a 3070ti and i7 11800k I was able to run the game maxed out with dlss on ultra performance and consistently maintained ~60 fps at 2560x1600 with only occasional dips in graphically intensive sections.The performances from the voice actors are great, you can really feel the sorrow and guilt in James' voice and Maria's flirty playfulness is unsettling but at the same time reassuring. I doubt they will top the original voice actors especially when it comes to later scenes as the performances in the first game really were something special that money just can't buy but we will see upon completion.The combat is a huge improvement upon the original and enemies actually feel like more of a threat. The AI is out of this world, especially for enemies like the mannequins who will often scurry out of site only to be hiding around the next doorway where they will suddenly jump out at you. This really adds to the fear factor compared to the original. The shooting feels good and encourages you to preserve ammo as James' is not a trained marksman so you will often find shots hard to place.The character designs for the enemies are spot on. They retain that almost wet-look and are not pleasant to look at. However, James' and Maria's designs leave a little to be desired. I miss the badges on James' jacket, especially because I made my own jacket of the original but this is hardly a big deal. For Maria though I really do not understand the redesign, there was nothing wrong or offensive with the original and part of her very character is that she is supposed to be over-sexualized. But again, this is hardly that big of a problem.The puzzles are fun and engaging and haven't been too difficult so far. The garbage chute puzzle in the apartments left me pretty confused in the original but through prior experience I knew what to do, I'm not sure whether new players would have this problem or not.The game is littered with references to the original as well as previous silent hill games which was a really nice touch.Overall, I am really satisfied with this game. Bloober team have genuinely achieved the impossible here and truly tested their mettle. Silent hill fans are infamously hard to please and for the game to be this well-received proves they really were up to the task. I think I will always end up preferring the original but that's just how these things go. But this is a really worthwhile remake and definitely as good a way to experience the game and encourage new fans of the series.If your a fan of survival horror, emotional stories with subtlety where it's up to you to read into the meaning of things, and games with an uncomfortable and surreal atmosphere then I can't recommend the silent hill 2 remake enough.Top marks from me.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never played the original, diving into Silent Hill 2 Remake was a fresh experience and it’s a visually impressive game that ran on my PC without any issues. However, I have to add that I own a high end system, which may be why I did not suffer from stutering etc. as a number of people seems to have. The eerie, fog-drenched environments and detailed character designs make the game immersive and visually striking, with plenty of creepy moments that kept me engaged.However, I did feel somewhat let down by the storytelling. It felt minimal, and I often found myself moving through enemies and solving puzzles without fully understanding the purpose behind my actions. This lack of narrative depth diminished my connection to James' journey and the overall story.After the 16-17 hour mark, the game started to feel repetitive. The enemies, puzzles, and mechanics remained largely the same, making the latter part of the game less engaging. While Silent Hill 2 Remake is definitely fun to play and visually stunning, it falls short in storytelling and is somewhat repetitive.Overall: Silent Hill 2 Remake is a good game that’s worth experiencing, but it could benefit from more narrative depth and variety in gameplay mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what you think it is: It's a very loyal, modern remake/update. Nothing groundbreaking here.There is Unreal Engine jank or optimization that can be done. Maybe it's my rig w/ a 3070 and external ssd but I'm locked at 30 fps and still stuttering on medium settings. And that's fine. Bloober has done a good job worthy of the praise they've received. Their most notable additions they've made are designing more instruction and pathing that makes the puzzles more of a fun minor obstacle then something you need to open a wiki for. Voice acting is better than it's ever been (much better than the genuinely bad dub in the hd remasters). Team Silent always had good cut scene direction: The acting here finally makes a western version shine. Not sure if they used a stage or mocap or key framing but it all looks good. The combat is more complex now then swing when an enemy gets close but not by much. If you've played Silent Hill Homecoming: it's that. You'll still feel better just trying to run past enemies and fight when you have to. Classic survival horror as it should be.None of these improvements fundamentally improve the experience of SH 2. That game has charm this one doesn't. They are equal at best and honestly I'd rather play the original. But that doesn't mean I want Silent Hill to die. I don't consider myself much of a fan of the series. And 2 is honestly maybe my least favorite of the games I've played (1,2,3,4, homecoming, downpour, p.t).I bought this because my best friend insisted it was a masterpiece on the level of RE 7. It is not. But I'm still no disappointed i bought it. I'm just disappointed I bought a game I already own. Konami,If you give us more Silent Hill, I'd like a new game please.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This isn't Silent Hill 2 from the old days. What it is however is an expertly made recreation by a talented devoted team that respected the original enough to not crap over its legacy. A high quality Silent Hill 2 Fan Remix, if you will. Not meant to replace the classic by any means, but more to act as a companion piece to the original I love.I'm pushing 40. I am a survival horror fan of the golden era which spawned some of the best and most definitive survival horror games ever created. To level with you, dear reader, gaming as a hobby has been losing its appeal to me for a while now. Quality horror games are also few and far between, and it's more likely I'll get my fix from a smaller or independent developer (Tormented Souls, Crow Country, Withering Rooms, ...) than from a bigger studio handling a bigger franchise. You bet yer arse I was skeptical about a Silent Hill 2 remake. Especially after Konami had milked the franchise dry with the godawful low quality spin-off train wrecks like Origins, Homecoming, Shattered Memories, Downpour. I was convinced the franchise was dead & beyond saving, and that no developer could ever resuscitate it successfully.Well...I'm glad to be proven wrong here. As of writing, I've completed Silent Hill 2 Remake 100% with all eight endings. As protective of the original Silent Hill games as I am, I don't feel the Silent Hill 2 Remake has altered or tampered with its source material in such a way that would ruin the experience. In fact, quite the opposite, much of it has been enhanced. However...Is it perfect? No. There are a handful of things that bother me, most of it can be remedied by giving the NexusMods page a visit and fix that goofy looking Angela face. What cannot be fixed is the somewhat downplayed sexual themes (thanks to DEI companies acting like the permanently offended puritanical conservative morality police, meddling with things they don't understand) and some of the voice acting; James has too much of that Hollywood gasping-at-every-line thing going on.Otherwise, honestly, I'm beyond satisfied with this remake. Does it replace the original? No. It's damn close... Silent Hill 2 is a classic. But there is definitely room for the remake to act as a what-if companion piece.Now, I am rooting for a proper definitive Silent Hill (1999) remake in this style. I think Bloober Team can do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake holds the reins of the original while losing its grip in quite a few spots that, although they don't ruin the experience, hinders its enjoyment from the source material. It does a great job at recreating the environment, atmosphere and tension the original brings right down to its core. Silent Hill has never been more eerily beautiful with its blood smeared streets, pockets of puddles and abandoned, barricaded stores littering the town. The sound design is incredible with the original sounds from the strange creatures, the radio spiking in its frequency when so much as a cockroach is munching at your feet, and the exploration and discovering the neat little nods/flashbacks to the original stating "We didn't forget!". Bloober has managed to be faithful when it comes to exploration and gathering your next key item, with some slight mix-ups for puzzles and solutions thrown around that may or may not intrigue people who have played the original. But, while I want to say the game is perfect, it's not.The voice acting ranges from absolutely horrible to generally pretty good, and personally I think the fault is with the original script. Any time Maria and James are interacting with each other, it feels fake. The original has very cheesy, borderline terrible voice acting that managed to be very charming for the time. Trying to replicate that in 2024 sounds bad, real bad. It isn't natural, it feels like they're reading directly from a paper in front of them and it manages to make me cringe at how off it feels. But, shortly after the initial meet-up, you're thrown into a brand spanking new cutscene of Maria talking about letting yourself be loose as you enter Heaven's Night. It's entirely new dialogue with nothing to go off on, and it shows. It's clear, its showing emotion, exploring Maria's character as this sexy, easy going personality that will stop at nothing to gaslight you into paying attention to her more. It feels as manipulative as the original without needing to copy her and I love it. But it's a "damned if you do, damned if you don't" scenario. Change it too much and people will whine its not like the original. Keep it the same and people will question why you should get it in the first place, and that feels like a lot of what the remake is. They played it fairly safe without changing the story beats but adding new ones in to try and squeeze a bit more out of the little time you already get from existing characters without it being too overwhelming. I adored those cutscenes when they came on [even though I think the casting of the characters were a little off], and I wish they showed off more considering how much longer the game overall feels. Combat is another damned if you do. The original had some terrible combat issues with it being too basic. Swing, swing, swing, stomp. Shoot, shoot, shoot, stomp. It got the job done and allowed you to explore with ease aside from key bossfights. The remake improves on it, but not enough. Adding active dodge frames, meatier hits, and aggressive enemies, even more so if you're in the Otherworld, are great additions. But throwing in almost quadruple the enemies, multiple at once in tight corridors or rooms can feel like a hectic mess. I was shocked when I was in the middle of the apartment building and already achieved a trophy to kill 75 enemies with melee. That's nearly as much as an average player will kill in the original in less than 3-4 hours! To me it feels like padding in some areas when you walk into an area with corpses, only to grab an item and have them revive and sometimes be forced to combat them. Nothing in the game was overall hard, as the dodge gives so many iframes it's difficult to be whacked the second you learn a pattern. Most of my injuries were the Mannequin Legs creeping around corners or beside items that I was too impatient to notice before grabbing said item. The combat became too rock-paper-scissors too fast for me personally, as most enemies followed the same patterns the next time you fight them. Swing, swing, swing, dodge, dodge, dodge, swing, swing, stomp. It boiled down to being too basic too fast, but Silent Hill never had good combat to begin with. I'm not sure if I prefer the original or the remake's combat, but they've done their best and I suppose that's all I can ask.Bossfights may have gotten the biggest improvement over the original, though! Pyramid Head is as slow and deadly as ever, Flesh Lip breaking out of his rustic bedframes to use them as appendages was a real shock, and the rest of the bosses continued to surprise me in ways I was pleasantly okay with. It's hard to get into too much detail without spoiling them, but I'm happy with the direction they took.Overall, the remake doesn't replace the original for me. The original has better voice acting, heart wrenching moments that do a great job at making you sob, something that the remake doesn't. The reading of the entire letter, James & Maria's separation, James' frustration at doctors being unable to cure his wife. The emotions are raw, heartfelt and very real emotions people in these situations. The helplessness and loneliness of sadness and impending doom. They managed to fail at these parts heavily but created new ones that I think will stick with me regardless. The remaster has better exploration, the graphics are superb and the sound design is something I haven't heard in a game yet, and it's gorgeous. They're both good games on their own, and I'm happy to be wrong about this game. The second I saw Bloober's name to be revealed as the lead developer on the project, I was a cynical person. But they proved that once in a blue moon, they can make a good game.And obviously, Akira Yamaoka ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocked the show. Absolute legend.

_childDocuments_.review: Please read the first sentences fully. I won't say I'm a die hard Silent Hill fan boy, I never played any Silent Hill game other than P.T. That wasn't my exposure to this franchise though. I first watched Pewdiepie play Silent Hill 1 years ago when I was under 10 or something. I then went on to Silent Hill 2, then 3, then skipped 4 and learned all about the IP getting passed around and then pt and so on until this remake, never actually playing a single one, but know everything about each installment. I love Silent Hill, it's genuinely the best horror game out there. (SH 1 is my favorite)I never played any Silent Hill game, but man there are some actually really bitter "fans" that have. This remake has a handful of issues in comparison to the original. Honestly, the two female faces looking masculine (the prominent gripe and also mine too somewhat) isn't even a big deal when you realize that the ost is altered (by Akira Yamaoka himself mind you) into strange versions of the original ost. Laura's theme for instance sounds so weird when you know how the og piece sounds like, and don't even get me started on how Peace & Serenity was completely removed from the game. I made sure to listen for that specifically and I didn't hear ♥♥♥♥ of it.The voice acting is also kind of alright, they try to keep the uncanny feel from the og with the realistic approach of the remake. It seems pretty fine but not better or worse than the og, just different. James' va does great though I won't lie.There are a few changes to scenes which, really I didn't mind, the notorious bowling alley scene is gone, but really I don't care. I care though that Eddie acts different in the remake, in the og he was kind of humane, here he is outright psychotic from the get go, with about no expression other than dead eyes and a monotone voice.The creepy scene with Maria in the labyrinth also was butchered, the og was so great at using the shading for her face. Here it's just another cutscene in between gameplay with no impact.Combat is actually fine though, it really isn't a big deal that there is a dodge button, I mean cmon man thats your biggest concern? It's not an action game just because it has a dodge button. They give you enough to fight back and enough to be afraid of. The darker halls in the remake sometimes make you want to not even move forward, they nailed the horror aspects here and I at times, I won't lie, it kind of reminded me of PT. Which is a really good thing, I wouldn't be surprised if bloober took from that.I also was scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of the performance, and ya it's really bad. I have a 12th gen intel core i5, rtx 3050 with 4gb, 16gm of ram in an asus tuf gaming laptop. I'm telling you this is the only game I get stuttering this bad in. At times the game just fixes itself and then ♥♥♥♥♥ itself again, then repeats. It's so damn annoying that I don't even want to do new game+ just because of the stuttering problems. I here that it's mostly an UE5 problem and that means no fixes for this anytime soon.I just finished the game by the way so all my thoughts are poured out here in no real order. I knew everything about sh2 from 2001, the story still hit for me (except for when peace and serenity didn't play, I was so disappointed). I got the Leave ending btw. When they decide do fix more of the performance problems i'll go back and get the 2 new endings too, just because. Also, I think another studio should handle future remakes for silent hill. Bloober tried and succeeded, not with flying colors though honestly. It's just better if a more understanding developer team took over (for sh1 remake if that's coming anytime soon).I know there's a lot of people that don't like opinions from others that never even touched the original game. Honestly, I couldn't care less (I probably know more  about sh as a whole than they do actually), but mostly because theyre stuck in a never ending loop of playing the same old games forever. Constantly despising anything that gets released, good or bad. I cant stand that. Not everything is crap, you just know what is and what isn't. SH 2 remake at the end of the day is a very satisfying game.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game holds a special place in my heart, I was introduced to Silent Hill, Resident Evil, and Parasite Eve through a friend I had when I was around 11 years old, him and I were super obsessed with these games and would often play pretend that we were in the games with our own stories (I know, some cringey ♥♥♥♥ right?) Anyways, playing 1, 2 and 3 originally on PS and PS2 I can confidently say that I've had enough experience playing these games over and over again and have always felt a connection to the stories and the characters, I'm pretty sure last i played SH2 was around 2014? so it's also been a while since I've played it. Now for my actual review of the game lol. I was skeptical at first hearing the news 2 years ago because I didn't want a game I hold close to my heart get this "upgrade" that many of the AAA studios like to do because often I feel they aren't done right and they're soulless compared to their original. I was even more skeptical when initial game play footage came out, it didn't look right to me and it felt too fast paced? I was so used to seeing the clunkiness of the original and thought they'd treat it like the RE2 or 3 remake and I didnt want to be doing combos on the nursed personally. I can confidently say that none of my concerns have come true and it feels very faithful to the original, I love the voice acting, I love the combat and I love the facial expressions when you're in cut scenes it all feels natural, I can feel the hope slipping away slowly every time I see James in a cut scene as the game progresses, his concern for Angela, his weariness of Eddie and his confusion(? didn't know the right word) of Maria, it all feels so right. The environments are exactly what I wanted when it comes to the remake, it's gloomy, eerie, and often times bizarre, Bloober Team really captured the essence of Silent Hill when it comes to the fog, it is my favorite part of the game, its so disorienting walking around and have an enemy sneak behind you because of fog (and just it hiding around a corner or under a car) to cut things short, the main buildings you end up going to are phenomenal, the puzzles are as good as I remember, enemies are sometimes a pain in the ass but in a good way and the combat just feels right, one thing that i do hope for is bloober to add a mode where it controls and looks like the original (camera angle and combat mostly) and maybe some outfits? I havent finished the game yet so who knows. Oh and pyramid head is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool in this game they did him justice. TY FOR READING THIS FAR IF YOU HAVE, MUCH LOVE♥ PLEASE BLOOBER REMAKE SH AND SH3!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: i'm a oldschool survival horror purist, original sh2 is one of my favorite games of all time. and yet, i still consider this remake to be an absolute masterpiece. it's right up there with the original 4 team silent games, and it may actually be the best remake i've ever played. disregard any negativity in regards to this being made by bloober team, because they nailed pretty much everything. in many ways, this could be called "resident evil 2 remake but for silent hill". tho actually it's much better, and more faithful to the original game.and YES this is fully playable on steam deck. i just beat it multiple times in portable mode, zero crashes. set everything to low/off, resolution scalability to 75%, and resolution to 1152x720. you will usually get around 30fps, and the only thing that will look iffy is your hair and jacket zipper. everything else looks fine, the art direction is so good that it still looks great. also you can turn on supersampling tsr low to get smoother gameplay in return for some visual compression.this team def should remake sh1. and 3. etc. also a new one.

_childDocuments_.review: ''Bloober team... you made me happy.''An excellent game that remains faithful, expands and is even better than the original in many aspects.This game is an absolute MUST play if you're a fan of horror games,+Ambience: This game will drive you INSANE with the excellent sound design and visuals, it's oppressive, anxiety inducing and it's definitely going to cut your breath in half while playing.+OST/Sounds: Superb, from the background noise to the music every single sound has been made to perfection, I'd recommend playing with good headphones so you can experience the depth and richness of the sounds and music!+Story: The story has been kept the same BUT, it has been expanded a bit more in a meaningful and rich manner, in no way it feels bloated or too on the nose. The tweaks in the dialogue are justified and fit perfectly in this remake+Combat: It has been remade into an on the should camera that makes you feel claustrophobic, but at the same time every single hit that you put on the enemies feel like you've hit them really good! way better than the original+Puzzles: Every single puzzle from the OG is still here but arranged at a different pacing + new puzzles that are very well made!I have very few gripes with the games and are as follows:-Performance: Rocking a 3060ti and I should be able to max the game at 1080p with RT and DLSS, but there's a fair bit of stuttering and frame drops lasting for around 1-2minutes + there's some distracting pop-ins, but the latter is mostly an UE5 issue that's plaguing every single game,-Combat: Some zones in the game probably feel slightly overpopulated with enemies-WHAT DO YOU MEAN NO PHOTO MODE??? THIS GAME IS AMAZING TO LOOK AT!Bravo to bloober team for bracing their belt and tackling this BEHEMOTH of a legend in gaming history and made a faithful and amazing remake of the most important games of the 2000's!

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game it is a piece of art that stands out in gaming for its storytelling and writing. Few games have had such a tight narrative fueled by symbolism that really keeps you moving through the game and the balance between these two things really sets Silent Hill 2 apart from other media. For a franchise that is famous for its setting I was really driven to complete this game by the strong writing of the characters, the dynamics between them, and the mystery of the main character. James is an excellent POV for this story and is such an amazing vessel for exploring human nature and driving criticism of our modern ways of living. Commentary on death, sex, forgiveness, selfishness, loss and purpose are common themes throughout story telling but Silent Hill 2 makes me feel like I am thinking about them for the first time again. James, Laura, Angela, and Mary will remain in my heart for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that tries to keep you scared not with jump scares, but with atmosphere.For the first few hours, I was thrilled. By the middle of the game, the excitement faded. By the end, I just wanted to find out the conclusion as quickly as possible.Let's start with the pros:+ Captivating atmosphere of abandonment, emptiness, and hopelessness.+ Excellent sound and music.+ The combat system. I can really feel the impact when I hit enemies, and how they take damage.+ The enemies. They dodge and use various movesets. Not just "dummies."+ Voice acting for the characters. Emotions are conveyed well. It sounds natural, not forced.+ Very beautiful graphics. The interiors are gorgeous. I wanted to explore everything, to look at everything.+ Interesting lore. I actually wanted to read the notes.+ The endings. They're interesting too and put a conclusion to the hero's story. There are 8 endings in total. I got the standard "Leave" ending.Now, the cons:- The main downside is the excessive length of the game. Throughout the game, we're running from one corner to another, and then we run through the same corners, just in an alternate reality. There's so much of this that the main plot is almost lost. The ugliest, most boring, and least interesting location is the mazes. The mazes are monotonous, with no interesting story, and are just identical tunnels.- Few enemy types. Very few enemy types and a lot of locations. This creates a sense of repetition. The same opponents appear in all locations of the game.- The side stories are underdeveloped. For example, about the patients in the hospital or the residents of the apartment complexes.- The idea with scattered photographs, which have numbers written on the back, was not fully developed. I thought throughout the game that it was part of some puzzle, but it turned out to be a useless collectible item.- Poor optimization. To get a stable 60 FPS, you have to tweak the settings a lot, and there will still be stuttering and frame drops.Conclusion:The game is worth the money. The developers really put effort into it. You can feel the soul of the project. Despite the flaws, I strongly recommend playing this game. I don't think the developers will remake the other parts, because in this remake, they've shown everything they could, and other remakes would just be dull repetitions of this one, like with the Resident Evil 3 remake.

_childDocuments_.review: The Silent Hill 2 Remake is a masterpiece that brings new life to one of the most revered horror games of all time. The developers have done an incredible job of preserving the original’s haunting atmosphere while updating it with modern graphics, sound, and mechanics that make it feel fresh and immersive.From the moment the game begins, you’re enveloped in an eerie, oppressive ambiance that pulls you right back into the desolate, fog-laden streets of Silent Hill. The visual overhaul is breathtaking: the enhanced graphics allow for more detailed environments, nuanced lighting, and shadows that add a layer of realism and dread to every location. The infamous fog has been beautifully reworked, making every encounter feel as though it could hide something terrible just out of sight. The audio is equally mesmerizing—Akira Yamaoka's score has been re-recorded with a modern polish that retains the original’s haunting melodies but feels even more resonant and chilling.One of the standout elements of this remake is the character work. James Sunderland’s story remains as psychologically complex and tragic as ever, but the updated facial animations and voice acting add new depth to his emotions, allowing players to feel more connected to his journey through guilt and grief. The other characters, too, are portrayed with an intensity that makes every interaction impactful and every storyline twist hit harder.Gameplay mechanics have been modernized in a way that respects the original game’s pacing and challenges but feels smoother and more accessible to new players. Combat has been refined, making it more responsive without sacrificing the tension and vulnerability that make the encounters so terrifying. It’s still more about survival than action, and every enemy feels like a genuine threat, especially with the enhanced AI and disturbing redesigns of classic monsters like the unsettlingly iconic Pyramid Head.Silent Hill 2 Remake is a love letter to fans of the original and a perfect entry point for newcomers to experience one of horror gaming’s greatest stories. It’s atmospheric, deeply emotional, and terrifying in all the best ways—a testament to what a remake should be. It’s hard to imagine a more respectful and effective update, and it firmly establishes Silent Hill 2 as a timeless piece of horror history. This is survival horror at its very finest.Thank you so much!
