_childDocuments_.review: I'll try and keep this kinda spoiler free. There will probably be minor ones here and there but nothing that will destroy the game to a new player at least. Now, lil bit of history, I played Silent Hill 2 to death back on my PS2 when it first released and it was one of those games that took a while to grow on me. I preferred Silent Hill 1 and 3 back then as they were more focused on why things were happening in the town and not a specific case like this. However anyone who has even typed "Silent Hill 2" on YouTube will see just how much of a lore rabbit hole the game has.So I've been waiting for this remake since I first heard it was coming and as a first impression, it was honestly a great re-imagining of a classic psychological horror game. I'll try and break the review into sub categories as I usually do and go over each point.Story - 10/10If there is one thing that will always be damned near perfect on this game it is the story. The pacing is generally pretty good and it's not just James' story that is unfolding over the course of the game as you meet Angela, Eddie and Maria over the course of the game. All of these plots culminate in some really dark payoffs and really paint the bleak picture this game presents. In comparison to the original game, I'd argue the story is better here as new points are elaborated on which answers some questions but rightfully bring up whole new ones which I'm sure the lore afficianados will be talking about for decades to come like with the original. The game takes place over several areas and gradually get further detached from reality as we proceed.Characters - 9/10 The characters are generally good, the voice actors for the most part are good at what they do. I particularly liked James' voice actor in this version, even over the original as he truly sounds like a man worn down by depression and hopelessness as he is supposed to be through the advancement of his story. Angela was a bit hit or miss. In some regards she was better than her original actress but in others the performance felt a bit wooden however it wasn't really enough to detract much from the experience. What you will come to realise is that none of these characters are particularly good people and the town itself is exceptionally good at bringing out the worst in the people it summons, including James. There are no heroes in this game!Graphics - 9/10The graphics are a massive upgrade from the original and even ran damned near flawlessly on my mid-range rig. There were a couple of moments where the camera played silly buggers when backed into a wall during combat but these are avoidable. New areas look great and the otherworld areas in particular feel more unique than previous titles which is also a plus.Audio - 10/10Now this is one area where the game really shines. The original OST and sound design is legendary and the game for the most part pulls much of its inspiration from there. Sometimes lifting sounds and music directly from the 2001 game which is not a bad thing. I mean if it ain't broke, don't fix it. Some of the music and monster sounds, particularly in the second half of the game give me goose bumps just thinking about them. The sound bars that play after combat with an enemy in such places really gets the hairs on my neck standing on end. So if a psychological game can do that, then clearly the sound is in the right place. Gameplay - 8/10 The gameplay for the most part is good, the combat is vastly improved over the old tank controls and bludgeoning until things die mentality of the 2001 version. Being able to dodge and having the RE4 over the shoulder cam is a big improvement when it comes to appreciating both combat and simply exploring. Exploring is also a fun thing to do as there is so much to find. New players getting to grips with new experiences and the old veterans finding easter eggs of the previous game is always a fun time. Puzzles are also pretty good too as they arent simply lifted from the original and have been reimagined. None are particularly taxing but they are interesting enough to keep your attention.The biggest plus though is the boss encounters, fights such as the "Abstract Daddy" being true high points of the game and are how psychological experiences are supposed to be.Replayability - 9/10There are 8 different endings to be found here so there are many paths for you to take with small gameplay changes. You can get 1 of 3 endings on your first run but starting a New Game+ unlocks the ability to find 5 more, 2 of which are exclusive to the remake and definitely worth pursuing. I went out of my way to 100% the game and it took me about 48 hours of gameplay to do as some endings were harder to trigger than others. So in conclusion, is the game worth buying? If you are a fan of the new Resident Evils and enjoy the classic Silent Hill games then absolutely. Even if you havent played the original and are looking for an unsettling game to play in the dark, then this one totally fits that mold. The game as it stands at time of review definitely deserves it's "Overwhelmingly Positive" status on Steam. If you arent sure, then wait for a sale, but this is one of the few games I'd say is worth it's retail price. Hopefully with the amount of sales achieved, the developers may make a remake of the original Silent Hill which I will have on my wishlist from day dot!

My only real criticism here is I think letting you go outside so much in the apartment stage was a mistake; the OG had a very claustrophobic and dark atmosphere that made that area a 10/10 on the horror scale.The combat is actually somewhat challenging now and the few big bads of the story actually feel like proper boss fights instead of just bigger enemies that take slightly more bullets to put down. Again, I am not a superfan of SH2 and consider it somewhat overrated in a lot of regards but this hooked me enough to make me want to replay it for the other endings.The only downside is the performance, which can be really ugly in certain areas, even with DLSS enabled. Clean up that and Team Bloober has itself a winner.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something blasphemous about the very idea, as if SH2 popped out onto store shelves as a perfect object destined for greatness and a hundred billion YouTube video essays. But the game sold beneath expectations, only gathering its modern reputation over time. Worse yet, developers Bloober Team had recently gone from rising star horror devs to punching bags with the reception of  and  All of which makes it all the more miraculous (and shocking to me, frankly) that  is actually really good, man.The biggest changes are expanded levels, surprisingly decent combat, and a more naturalistic take on the characters. The expanded levels can be a little  long at times, with a needlessly draggy and pointless detour to an abandoned theater being one of the most baffling. But when you start getting the layouts down (if you're a freak like me who replays survival horror games multiple times) they start to go by quick. The designs themselves are longer, sure, but they're also . More complicated and twisty than the designs in the original. While they're not necessarily better, they bring a lot of welcome new flavor to the game. The combat, too, is less clunky than that of the original. While it doesn't quite reach the limb-shooting panic of the  remake, it's still a lot of fun to hear a monster rear up for the attack, preemptively dodge, and earn yourself a free whack with an iron pipe without getting hit once.Finally, there's the way the characters are animated and performed in this game. We need to let go of Guy Cihi as James Sunderland, because Luke Roberts brings a complexity and exhaustion to the role that Cihi could never dream of. Every character is played much more naturalistically than in the original; they look more like human beings than dolls, deliver the same dreamlike script in a way that feels shockingly grounded--Lynchian in the actual sense, not just Lynchian in the "kinda weird!" sense. This slight move in the direction of realism has caused the dumbest people on the internet to get mad about the portrayal of Angela, who appears like a fairly attractive normal person as opposed to a smooth PS2 woman. If you can't find an above-average imaginary woman hot in a video game, I don't know what to tell you. Your horny game is weak and you will not see Horny Valhalla. Get on my level, chumps.I've unlocked all but the last new ending, "Stillness," because I'm just straight-up having a good time. It feels good to get good at the combat. I always love the vibes of just walking around my favorite evil little town, you know? Two decades have passed, but  is still my special place. Maybe it's waiting for you too.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience! Silent Hill 2 is gripping from start to end. This was my first Silent Hill game, I went in as blind as possible avoiding story spoilers and it was worth it all. It was a harrowing experience - in the best way possible. Bloober team did a fantastic job with the visual effects and the style of the game. Very impressive. I hope that they continue to deliver high quality work going forward now that they have shown what they are capable of!If you want to go in completely blind stop reading here because I want to talk a little bit about the endings - or rather how you get them. In short, every action you take in game is being judged. Both in combat and out of combat actions have consequences to your ending. The game is constantly assessing James' mental state and what his likely frame of mind is at every given moment and that calculation will ultimately determine your fate. I thought that I got "the bad ending" but after reading more into it, it just happens that was the appropriate ending for the way that I played, it is "my" ending. I think this is such a cool and interesting detail and knowing this after the fact really helped me appreciate the game and how it ended for me.Very highly rated, I hope that this wins some awards in the upcoming awards season.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting this game I was very sceptical. Konami, Bloober taking this on this massive game, Angela looking as she did...don’t get me wrong other things looked great like the environments but then I heard doubts about the combat and I was just not sure what to expect.I can confidently say that so far this has been a major win. No spoilers and I’m only up to meeting Laura outside the apartments. The three things I recall that are key to a successful remake are: stay true to the original, develop that with twists, like new locations, monsters like crimson heads in RE1R, and QOL updates. This game has it all.+ Echoes: locations in the remake that are a nod/thumbs up for OG fans. It’s such a small thing to add but it means a lot.+ Switching weapons and healing on the fly. You can even switch melee and ranged just by using a different button, no witching required.+ Exploring through smashing windows and checking drawers etc. Not ground breaking but just makes you work that bit harder inside of just having stuff lying out in the open.+ Puzzles are in many ways the same but evolved. I LOVED what they did with the coin puzzle in the apartment for example. The same, but with a twist.+ Combat is better that the OG. I love the OG but the combat was very wooden and static and it wasn’t the strongest trait of the game and it didn’t mean to be. This game has monsters hiding or running away and then suddenly coming to life. They’ll parry and counter you making combat much more intense. I’m having fun doing melee only so far. Is it the best combat? Hard to say but I hope the doubters feel their feedback has been listened to.+ Strange photos: picking up random photos with numbers on. Not sure what that’s about but it’s fun to explore and hunt them down.+ James and Eddie feel like they are different but within their character boundary so to speak. They may be subjectively better/worse but objectively they are different in their own way and that’s fine, I can believe they are who they are meant to be.+Environments look GORGEOUS. Sometimes I do feel there’s a bit of a bubble around me but it’s nothing like SHHD collection. The town feels more windy, leaves and rubbish blow through the town, it’s so much more alive. It seems that the rain goes through James, maybe there’s something I can do to address that but this seems kind of a minor issue.+ The settings is taken right out of RE4R. You can customise so much and see how it will look in game.+Achievements are always good and of those that aren’t hidden there look to be some standard ones and also ones for OG fans. Won’t spoil but if you like to explore and do things in the OG, try them in the remake.+ The camera. Some might not like that you can move the camera (not sure). I though love that you can move the camera. Being able to look up and see the trees towering above you or the apartment block looming high makes you feel like you’re in the town.And so on to the negatives:-Angela still feels like she could be so much better in her facial appearance (maybe modders can fix it on Steam). At first I felt her lines felt rushed but listening again I’d say no. She sounds like she lacking confidence and her body language is on form, but she just seems to not be the character she is in the OG. It’s not a massive problem, certainly not as bad as I feared and she is a relatively minor part, unlike say James. I don’t think that this is a VA issue, it’s a director issue.- Laura came across somewhat aggressive in the trailer and I’ve yet to see this in game but she has yet to win me over with her performance.- The frame rate. Sounds like I’m not the only one and it’s not unplayable, my pc was fairly high end 5-6 years ago but maybe I’m pushing it that bit too hard. I’ve tried a few setting recommendations from reddit but my pc can run in the high 50’s and then every now and then take a giant dump and run as low as 7 fps. I’m confident that tweaks to settings or a patch can address this. Again, this is a hiccup but not something I’d say was obnoxious.If I had to give this a rating I’d say probably 9 out of 10. Will update this if I deem it necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: LONG FORM REVIEW: Silent Hill 2 2024To say that we live in a strange media landscape in the moment might be putting it lightly. Across the political spectrum, flame wars between anyone and everyone that is looking to be offended shape what media gets made, what gets canceled, what remains unseen. And it’s not just one side that’s worse than the other, no. It’s the naive youth culture that creates permanent immaturity in social media, where people who tend to have less life experience than they should screech their opinions. Add on to this, the concept of the remake. Remakes piss people off. I had extremely cautious optimism when this game was finally announced, I assumed it would most likely be okay, a 7 out of 10 game, filled with remember this and check out that. Silent Hill 2 means a lot to me, for most people there is a piece of media that hits them hard, means something to them, and this is one of mine. I played the game originally at 18, in the midst of probably the lowest point in my life. Fresh out of high school, no direction, no idea what to do next, and most of my friends were slowly fading away or revealing their true colors. That game hit me hard in a way that was pretty much just, man, it’s time to start going somewhere and doing something. I registered for the ACT the evening after beating this, to just get going. So, yeah, cautious optimism. It will probably be okay, nothing amazing right?I was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wrong. Let’s be honest, the first thing. The change in camera angles and combat changes. The original SH2 is not a hard game. In fact, the combat is now in my mind, probably one of the worst aspects of the original game. It’s god awful, and low stakes. Every single boss fight is a face roll. Yeah. In the remake combat is TERRIFYING. You are on the seat of your pants every single fight, and watching the telegraphs from the enemies, because you will get your ♥♥♥♥ knocked down fast if you’re not dodging. The camera angles are immersive. Beyond compare as well. The old style camera angles, while great for the time, the cinema like quality of it all, just don’t hold up as well in 2024. And the boss fights. Oh man. The boss fights in this remake are insane. Whereas in the original it was shoot something about 4-5 times and occasionally move, these fights now are dynamic. The thing I could compare them to the most would be like fighting a colossus in Shadow of the Colossus. It’s an event, walls are breaking, your dodging and trying to time reloads, the arenas are changing constantly. Of particular note, the Abstract Daddy fight, just. You have to experience that. And the context around that fight, I won’t spoil whats going on, what trauma spawned that monster, but the battle combined with the context, it’s so great. And yet, the point of Silent Hill isn’t the combat. But at the same time, you never feel like you’re an action movie star. You feel like you’re fighting for your survival. They nailed making the combat work, and injected high stakes, while also conveying the feeling that this town is haunted by old gods, and you’re going to have to scrape tooth and nail to survive, you’re not a fighter, and you don’t have a clue what you’re doing. Graphically, this game is amazing. Just, put this on the fastest SSD you have, and it pretty much solves any hitching issues. My 5600mbs Gen 4 SSD did the trick. It’s just gorgeous, that first descent in the town is one of my outstanding moments in games in a very long time. Just the sounds and the graphics and the atmosphere. Good lord, the sound. This game better win sound design of the year from several award shows. This game made me jump from that alone more times that I would imagine. As I’m typing this, there are a few pricks whining about how this game is DEI, woke trash. So, for this game, it’s right wingers turn to ♥♥♥♥♥ and moan. For another game, it will swap sides, but for now its them. And I don’t understand where this is coming from, but it’s really not that many people. This game is obviously a remake made by people that loved the original game, and did their damnedest to deliver an experience that reflects that. Everything is faithful to the original, except some minor outfit changes, which, honestly, doesn’t matter and needed to be changed. Which leads to the best part. This remake is faithful while changing every single point of progression and puzzle in the game. That’s right. It’s a whole, brand new experience, while still having the same locations. Nothing from the original game, progression and puzzle wise, is solved the same way as the original, meaning I had a fresh, entirely new experience. I can’t believe that I’m saying this one, but, given the state of survival horror games, and how far we come, we’re eating well the past few years. Capcom has been knocking it out of the park, a ton of indies that I will be talking about have been amazing too. But, this game, if this game didn’t have the connotations of being a Konami game, the overblown (in my experience, maybe you will experience worse) performance issues, the weird “woke” complaints that people who should touch grass can’t admit that they’re being stupid about, I think people could admit what I’m about to say. This is the crown jewel of survival horror. Long may it reign, and may we receive more. 10 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I must admit I had serious doubts about this remake, much like many other longtime fans of the series. I couldn't imagine Bloober Team successfully handling such a monumental title. I've always held the first three Silent Hill games close to my heart, with Silent Hill 2 standing out as the best of the trilogy.The Silent Hill 2 remake by Bloober Team delivers an impressive take on James, with his character design and voice acting standing out as exceptional. The game's visual fidelity is stunning, bringing the eerie world of Silent Hill to life in ways that surpass expectations. Akira Yamaoka's music and sound design are masterful, once again creating a haunting atmosphere reminiscent of the 2001 original. Though the fog isn't quite on par with the original, I personally found it to be far better than anticipated and a great addition to the remake’s overall atmosphere. I also found the redesigned UI to be sleek and incredibly customizable, a nice touch for modern players.However, it's important to note that this is not a flawless remake. My biggest issues lie with the character designs for Angela, Laura, Maria/Mary, and Eddie, which are far from satisfying. The voice acting, too, is a major letdown, which nearly detracted from the overall experience for me. These two aspects alone could have brought any other game down to a much lower score, but because Silent Hill 2’s story remains so deeply compelling, they don’t drag it below a 9/10 in my eyes.Bloober Team exceeded my expectations, and despite my gripes, I enjoyed my 101 hours with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Day 10 of the October Horror Reviews: Silent Hill 2 (Remake)Guilt is a prison. A bitter, cold prison that shackles your conscience and forces you to make a decision: Do you want to confront the suffering you may have caused, take responsibility and lighten your burden... or choose to wallow in that guilt, and expect the world to simply forget, or one day consume you?James Sunderland is on that journey, but he doesn't realise it. His every expression, every close-up shows a face that's wracked with guilt, tired and lost. He submits readily to the environment, he throws himself into every opportunity to face harm, because it's not just the town that's punishing him - he's punishing himself. The nightmares he faces are representations of every aspect of his psyche, critiquing his mindset through the journey leading up to him making that decision that threw him into this very town in the first place.Silent Hill 2 is a nostalgic game for me, and Bloober Team - having faced many doubters through the lead up to this release - really captured what made the original game so captivating. As dumb as it sounds, I played the original when I was ten. I was at my grandmother's house, and my uncle had the game on his PS2. He was in the apartment, and I simply picked up from where he left off. Had no idea what I was doing, but something about the use of dark colours, the sombre tone, the way I couldn't really tell if a step forward was really a step forward - I felt that same tension here. And I got stuck on the same place I was stuck on all those years ago, and it still took me a bit of time to figure those parts out. The thing is, being stuck here doesn't feel unearned - you don't get frustrated. You tolerate the lows of the journey, even those that are your own failures, because you know that James' destination, no matter if it ends in water, or in a full circle, or in a release... it all feels like catharsis.The nitty gritty of it is that the visuals are great - the new aspects to several bosses, even though they're not new, they feel welcome, they feel like they're made with love and appreciation for what made the original game so tense. There are even areas where you're treated to throwbacks to the original game - it's beautiful. The combat feels desperate, you actually feel the intensity of each of James' hits, this is a man fighting for his life. Each boss, each encounter, you question the necessity in a very visceral way, because you can just run around most of the enemies. Puzzles are just as tricky as I remember, not too hard, not too easy. A lot of the classic puzzles were beautifully remade. There were little bugs here and there, but nothing gamebreaking, if you encounter any issues with the sound, I think I had to go into audio, change the output to something else and then back to the default, and it would work like a charm again. Bloober, you did good. Thank you for honouring what made the original Silent Hill 2 so special. 9.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: From the very first moment you step into the fog-shrouded forest, Silent Hill 2 Remake pulls you into its haunting narrative with an almost tangible atmosphere. The game expertly captures the essence of psychological horror, staying true to the original while enhancing it for modern audiences.The remake excels in creating an immersive environment. The atmosphere is thick with tension, amplified by a superbly curated soundtrack and chilling sound effects that keep you on edge. Every audio cue feels meticulously crafted, contributing to an unsettling experience that lingers long after you've put down the controller.The characters are well-defined, with the protagonist feeling more relatable compared to other iconic survival horror figures like Leon Kennedy from the Resident Evil series. The emotional depth and psychological complexity of the story make it one of the most compelling narratives in the genre.The game offers intriguing puzzles that challenge you without breaking the immersive flow of the story. With multiple endings to discover, Silent Hill 2 Remake encourages multiple playthroughs, rewarding players with different perspectives on its haunting tale.Bloober Team did a splendid job revitalizing this classic, but I'd still recommend playing the original to fully appreciate the nuanced differences. Overall, this remake is a masterpiece and a peak example of psychological survival horror done right. Whether you're a returning fan or new to the series, Silent Hill 2 Remake is an unforgettable experience that stands out in today's horror landscape and in my humble opinion the most important horror game in history.

_childDocuments_.review: Even 2 years after the first Silent Hill Transmission it still feels surreal that this game even exists. Not only is this a return to the Silent Hill franchise that Konami has left dormant since that god awful HD collection and the tragedy that was the cancellation of Silent Hills and its subsequent de-listing of PT, but it's a remake to arguably the best entry in the series. And if that wasn't enough, it's a remake made by Bloober team of all studios, which they have had a tenuous track record of releases. So how is it that in spite of all the odds, Silent Hill 2 Remake is not only a good horror game, but an incredible remake that succeeds in nearly every category? So first, how is the game itself, just based on its own merits outside the original? Well unsurprisingly it feels pretty modern, yet familiar if you've played the classics from this genre. It's a third person OTS action game with an emphasis on exploration, combat, and puzzle solving. The game is split up into multiple indoor areas you will be exploring, not unlike dungeons in Zelda, and the town of Silent Hill acts as the hub area which connects them all together. Each dungeon-like area will consist of exploration and puzzle solving, with a good amount of combat thrown in, but they will also contain cutscenes which progress the story. Some of these areas will even cap off with a boss fight at the end, which strengthens the Zelda dungeon comparison. Since this is a survival horror game, exploration is a necessity since most of the the health items and ammo you find lying around is hidden off the beaten path. Outside a couple of boss battles however, I never found myself too low on ammo and health, and its abundance did hurt some of the tension this game otherwise builds up very well. Puzzles are another core pillar of the experience, and I'm happy to say they're well designed and hold up to past entries. Many of them did challenge me to think outside the box, but I never found them too obtuse, and that's a very fine line to tread so I respect the effort the designers put into them. Then, there's combat. And let me say this one surprised me. Horror games in the past have had a reputation of poor combat systems since they were never integral to the experience, and I went into this game expecting no different. But that's not the case here, the combat in Silent Hill 2 Remake is surprisingly fun! It's not as polished as something from a AAA game, there's still some jank. But even after 16 hours in I never found combat boring, and that's thanks to the newly introduced dodge mechanic. James can now dodge enemy attacks like he's in a souls game, and enemies will telegraph their attacks, while also keeping their patterns varied. There's a real skill curve to the combat, and over the course of the game I got better at consistently avoiding taking hits. I jived so much with the combat that unless I was low on health I always chose to confront most enemies instead of avoiding them. You might argue this clashes with the intent of a horror game being to make you feel vulnerable, but the Silent Hill series always relied on its atmosphere to scare you instead of trying to overwhelm you with enemies. It's roughly twice as long as the 2001 original and while that might be a good thing for most players, the third act of the game starts to lose some of its momentum, though not to the extent where I felt it was outstaying its welcome. Story is as strong as the original, and it is for the most part pretty faithful. You take control of James Sunderland who returns to Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his wife, Mary, to come meet him there. Not too unusual, until you account for the fact that James's wife has been dead for 3 years, and you're here to find out if she's really alive and waiting for you. Along your journey you will encounter other characters who were "called" to Silent Hill, each for their own reasons. Silent Hill 2 doesn't shy away from challenging topics like abuse, suicide, depression, and mental illness, and I find it handles them quite tastefully while also never being too explicit about it. This game hides its themes behind a heavy use of metaphors just like the original, and it's largely this reason the 2001 game has endured such a strong legacy as a cult classic in survival horror. The remake respects the source material in this regard, but never plays it too safe, and isn't afraid to take slight artistic liberties in its character designs. Slight spoiler ahead, but there's even a scene showing an interaction between Maria and James at Heaven's Night, which is wholly original to this remake. The interaction is not just a bit of fan service showing us a more intimate interaction between James and Maria which we haven't seen in the original, but it also serves as a bit of character development for James. I want to avoid specifics, but if you've already watched the scene you'll know what I'm talking about. Overall, Silent Hill 2 is a strong remake and a great Silent Hill game that is faithful to the original, but also isn't afraid to modernize the parts that aged and expanding on what worked. Bloober team obliterated everyone's expectations through what I could only internally rationalize as them making some kind of deal with the devil, and I guess that's at least partly true since Konami did publish them. We know more Silent Hill is coming down the pipeline, whether those titles come to fruition or live up to even half the quality of the remake is impossible to determine now. What I can say for sure is that we finally have Silent Hill 2 Remake, and if that's all we ever get, then as a longtime Silent Hill fan who's been burned by high expectations for years, it was well worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 3 hours of Silent Hill 2 Remake at the time of writing, as well as that I have not played the original game (only seen videos). but I want to talk about this game regardless.This game from a visual standpoint and especially comparing it to the original, is beautiful. It uses Unreal Engine 5 and to give a clear idea on how beautiful it is, in my opinion it looks better than Demons Souls on PS5. There are so many high quality textures, puddles, character models, shadows, and so on. Because of this the game's atmosphere is also incredible and easily my main draw to the game. The original was already known for it's atmosphere, ambience, and tone and in this remake it is no different. In some ways you could say it is better than the original though I don't want to claim that it is. The fog obscuring your vision, the wind sound effects and other sounds effects that play in the background, the colorless-ness of the world, as well as the dark/depressing tone the game gives off keeps you immersed within the town of Silent Hill as you walk around.As for gameplay, much like Alan Wake 2, Dead Space, Callisto Protocol, Resident Evil, etc. it is basically just a Resident Evil clone with different factors in there of course (like no real inventory management) but it's more or less the same fundamentally. It's probably most like Callisto Protocol since that game is mostly melee-focused like this one. Is the gameplay the most disapointing part of the game so far for me? Yes. Does that mean the gameplay is bad? No, far from it, in fact it is really good anyway. So why complain about it if it's good? Well as a person who has played the Dead Space Remake, Resident Evil 4 Remake, Alan Wake 2, a little bit of Callisto Protocol, and other games like those. I suppose I was hoping that since recently alot of AAA horror games have been more or less very similar, this remake would try to be different fundamentally from RE in some way (which I suppose it technically is?) I don't know what exactly I was hoping for but something different I guess. Now once again, none of this means the game is bad at all and im not trying to rail on it by comparing it to RE. After all RE's gameplay is still great to this day so therefore Silent Hill 2's gameplay is still great to me. Plus the overall game in the 3 hours I played (up until the Apartments) is a masterpiece so far. So I don't really have a right to complain about it at the end of the day.I don't have much to say about story and plot, like I've said before, I've only played 3 hours. I'm only almost done progressing through the Wood Side Apartments. But so far the story has been 'intriguing' is the word i'd like to use. I'm interested to see where it ends up. I intend to edit this part and this entire review in general the more I play until I get at least one of the endings (I know there are multiple.)The last thing I'd like to talk about, which is part of the reason I started this review this early on, is the performance. As of right now (10/12/24 or 12/10/24 for most other parts of the world) The game's performance is not too great at all. I had to look up the settings online that I needed to have on 2k resolution (2560x1440p) to maintain a 'stable' 60fps which was fine around the start of the game, but now at the Apartments it's has boggled down to more or less 40fps. It could just be because I'm on 2k resolution but I see plenty of people complain about the performance who are on lower settings and resolutions. So I think in general the game is not optimized well on PC. It's no Jedi Survivor launch performance, but I recommend people who are interested in buying this game to at least wait a week or two before paying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ $70 to get the game. Most likely by that point Bloober Team will have at least rolled out a patch or two for performance.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a perfect game, but it is a perfect exercise in bottling the essence of old school survival horror and modernizing it for today's audiences.I, like many, was fairly skeptical when I heard that Bloober would be taking on this remake, but having now finished the game, all I can say is: what an achievement.If you're a fan of survival horror/horror games, and especially if you came up playing old school survival horror like I did (think fixed camera angles and clunky tank controls), you owe it to yourself to play this game. Just about everything this game has to offer is downright excellent, and the only complaint I can think to level against it is that the pacing drags just a bit at times. But still, even that only serves to remind me of those survival horror games of old that I grew up loving.This game deserves your time and money. I cannot recommend it enough. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: this is damn good, damn good!!! as someone who didn't grow up with the OG, but having played it for the first time in my 20s, i enjoyed the OG as having a PlayStation past but also a deep infatuation with the lore, music, sound design, world design, etc. of silent hill that i had learned of from external references. i played it, and loved it, really with no complaints considering the point in time it was made. when this remake was first unveiled, my excitement was profound because i love this franchise so much - even if this game was bad, i still would have enjoyed it - but too bad... it was perfect. i think that someone who hasn't played the original will want to compare it to resident evil, and likely complain about the lack of enemy variety - but even with a 25+ hour playthrough, i still wasn't fully evading enemies and taking damage (they hit hard on hard difficulty! which is good!) - but even then, if you remember a certain corridor enemy that also appears in SH3, you will be pleasantly surprised with what Bloober did with that enemy here! So enemy design, awesome - combat is super punchy (i love the sound design of curb stomping enemies, James' voice actor did great) - and combat was fun, fair, and had no instances of me screaming "BS" to some hitbox shizz. Atmosphere and music, sound... more oppressive than the OG, i was scared out my britches the whole dang time, and all the homages to the OG triggers/scenes were a nice touch. I love what they did with Maria, her dialogue was a nice tension relief between the Apartments and Brookhaven, It's hard to view this game without the lens of the original (which i think is pretty much perfect) - and with even that considered, i thought this was a perfect game (A LOT OF GAMEPLAY compared to the original, looks beautiful, great combat, oppressive atmosphere, etc.) but even as a standalone without the legacy of the original game, this definitely stands on it's own with things that it does even better than Resident Evil Remakes with the sound design, combat (i think this game's combat was great... and combat, even if it's not the premise of the game, should still be good obviously) - Bloober team needs the blessing to get us Silent Hill 1, 3 (PLEASE), and 4 remade as well, because it can only get better from here. This was a great game, and i wish i could forget it and play it again. It really blew my balls off, really good stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to suggest this game, I cannot. It's a 70 dollar version of a game you can get for free from abandon ware sites with an extra 8 hours of padding. It claims to be a remake, but puts very obvious references to the originals in a form of a blatant, slap in the face objects placed in the location, and a musical cue that can be equated to a set of jingling keys. Not to mention that the wide array of weaponry available in the original have been completely stripped down to a single melee weapon, and only the original 3 guns. Not to mention the inventory has been rendered obsolete thanks to hotkeys and healing being on a single button. They also somehow managed to make the game control worse than the original. Combat was clunky in the original, but every mistake was your own. You didn't have James taking up 2/3rd of the screen All of the atmosphere has been completely stripped down and filled with block push puzzles, and obvious, white sheet marked traversables. All while James grunts and groans in your ear the entire game. Silent hill is one of my favorite game series (though I'm not the biggest fan of 2), and to see it done this dirty just makes me wonder "why blooper?" They tried to take everything that the Resident Evil remakes made good while removing everything that made Silent Hill originally better than that series. Instead of buying this game, I suggest going to , and simply playing the original PC version of restless dreams.

_childDocuments_.review: Blooper Team did a mostly good job in remaking this game.The story itself remains unchanged and faithful. The soundtrack was made by Akira Yamaoka, who also worked on the original. It is slightly different, but still faithful. For better or worse the game is much more streamlined. Whereas in the Original, you would easily find yourself getting lost due to how open the map is to you, and how it does not hold your hand at all. This one does, and by doing so it changes how most of the game is played compared to the original. However, one major change that I really did not like, was Mary's Letter at the end of the game. They added extra fluff, that the letter really did not need. The original was perfect in that regard, and the remake takes away from the feeling by adding more to it.The level design is good but more streamlined, the puzzles are the same in concept but easier than the originals, and there is much more focus on combat then the original. Combat in the original was more an afterthought in my opinion, they made combat easy and gave you ample ammo and you can skip most of the enemies presented to you. In this one, you will be forced to engage in combat at many facets of the game against regular enemies, and the ammo economy, at least in the beginning, was sparse. By the end of the game I had ample amounts of ammo, and health drinks/syringes, but that is mostly because I used melee primarily, and was going for one of the other endings of the game. Those with familiarity with the original may find themselves disappointed with these changes. Blooper did add a ton of options to customize the game experience such as making combat light, so some credit for that at least. The voice acting in the remake is far better than the original for all characters EXCEPT for Mary. When I finished the game and Mary's Letter was being read, I did not feel the same emotion as I did when I heard it in the original. Mary's VA in the original did a phenomenal job, and especially during the reading of the letter. It invoked such strong emotion, and i'm pretty sure everyone who played the original can still hear the line "You made me happy" in their head. Sadly the reading for the remake is not that great. Not only did they change the letter as I mentioned prior, but also, in my opinion, the VA did not do as good a job in the reading to invoke such strong emotions. Overall, I do feel like this is a good remake, many will enjoy it. Do yourself a favor though, and also play the original Silent Hill 2. There is still a ton of merit only found in that game.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions after 2hrs and reaching Woodside ApartmentsTLDR: if you are new to the series, buy it, is the best way to experience Silent Hill to date. If you played the original, expect some minor changes that may surprise for the good or bad (subject to the experience of the player). The game is faithful to the original but also expands in several aspects, like sidequests in other buildings previously locked in the original game, similarly to what has been done in Resident Evil Remakes.Combat feels more impactful, you can see each strike made to the enemy (scars, blood, etc)  and also when James is injured is clearly visible. New puzzles have been added and the already existent are slightly changed in favour of better location and pacing.Performance wise, played on a RX 570 4gb (old graphics card) with locked 30 fps, medium settings and 1080p. If you have the program lossless scaling can help to reach 60fps with frame generation and keeping good image quality.Bloober Team did an excelent job and this game deserves its place alongside with other good remakes like Resident Evil 2. Hopefully Konami keep this quality for future projects (looking at you Metal Gear Solid Delta).

_childDocuments_.review: well i'll be damned.....they really pulled it off. I had every intention of writing this remake off due to my love for the original and my distrust of Bloober Team, but honestly I'm glad I was wrong because instead of a cheap cash grab, we got an honest love letter to the original game. Boss battles are improved big time (particularly the fights with the Abstract Daddy and with Eddie) the charafter performances do a great job of making the dialogue more serious while still keeping that dreamy/uncany tone, the sound design and music still delivers....almost every aspect of this game delivered. The only big mark against it is the performance which is admittedly a pretty big black eye on an otherwise solid remake. Definitely play this one, but maybe wait for a couple performance patches first.

_childDocuments_.review: The Silent Hill 2 remake by Bloober Team is a masterclass in horror gaming, delivering an experience that is both genuinely terrifying and visually stunning.🌟Terrifying AtmosphereFrom the moment you step into the fog-laden streets of Silent Hill, the game grips you with its oppressive atmosphere. I recommend using the 90's mode. Bloober Team has meticulously crafted every detail to ensure that the sense of dread is palpable. The dense fog, eerie silence, and sudden, unsettling noises all contribute to a feeling of constant unease. The environments are designed to keep you on edge, with every shadow and corner potentially hiding something sinister.🌟Genuine ScaresThe remake excels in delivering genuine scares. The tension builds gradually, with the game using psychological horror elements to keep players on their toes. Encounters with enemies like Pyramid Head are as terrifying as ever, with improved AI making these moments even more intense. The game doesn’t rely on cheap jump scares; instead, it creates a sustained sense of fear that lingers long after you’ve put down the controller.🌟Gorgeous GraphicsVisually, the Silent Hill 2 remake is breathtaking. The updated graphics bring the town of Silent Hill to life in a way that was previously unimaginable. The use of ray tracing makes the game look almost like a movie. The character models are incredibly detailed, and the animations are smooth and lifelike, enhancing the overall immersion.🌟Overall ImpressionThe Silent Hill 2 remake is a triumph for Bloober Team, successfully capturing the essence of the original while enhancing it with modern technology. The terrifying atmosphere, genuine scares, and gorgeous graphics make it a standout title in the horror genre.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game for sure. As a person who tried playing the very first silent hill when it came out and was too terrified to continue it was nice to finally experience a game from this series. The revamped combat definitely helps in making a bit less terrifying because you're not fighting horrible controls and a camera boss at the same time. It's still very scary and gets under your skin despite that at times with well placed enemies and the ability to trick you into letting your guard down. Story is good and the puzzles my wife really enjoyed solving them. Both combat and puzzle difficulty was standard and I think that's good enough for me because I really can't handle horror games lol but this has helped me get over that quite a bit.The graphics are beautifully done and equally as disturbing/scary but the only really bad thing about this game is the god awful performance by default (6800xt/5600x/32gb ram, Ultrawide 1440p) most likely due to Unreal Engine 5. The mods "Silent Hill Optimizer" and "Enhanced Silent Hill" found on nexusmods helped a lot to maintain a consistent 60+ fps. There is one area though towards the end of the game that no matter what you do even if you drop everything to low fps will drop to 20fps and below and possibly cause crashes. Thankfully enemies in that area aren't really a threat to you by that time as you know how to deal with them or just have enough resources to make it a non-issue. I paid full price for about 23-24 hours but this game does have replay-ability in the form of new game+, higher combat/puzzle difficulties, and many different endings and a time challenge achievement. I'm satisfied with what I got but I feel like the $70 charge was trying to take advantage of the nostalgia factor of the silent hill games (also I personally still don't like the idea of games now costing $70) and due to the performance issues I would say wait for a discount at some point unless they get fixed some how. Still a really big recommend from me if you've never played a silent hill game before or just like horror games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece. From the story, acting, music, to the gameplay—it’s all perfect. As a huge fan of the original it's clear from playing this game that Bloober Team truly understood Team Silent’s vision. there is so much passion put into this game it makes me want to cry. It was so important that Bloober team got this remake right to bring Silent Hill 2’s story and characters to a new generation of gamers, and I genuinely believe they did it justice.The original will always hold its own, but this remake captures everything that made the original so so amazing and brings it to the modern age.This is horror done right. I’ve played horror games for years, to the point where I’m desensitised to gore, jump scares, and un-killable enemies, but the Silent Hill 2 remake had me jumping out of my chair at several points and each time it was unscripted, regular gameplay. The enemies are soo creepy and unsettling that you always feel on edge when you know they are nearby. Never have I felt so tense playing a game. For the best experience, I highly recommend playing on hard mode.The sounds and music in this game is just the chef's kiss that really brings everything together and make this game the masterpiece it is. From calming and melancholy to down right hostile, the sound design in this game deserves it's own separate review.The story telling is on point but you really have to read between the lines to understand what's happening. New players are going to finish the game with a lot of questions, but once you do some digging and read up on everything, upon a second play-through you will pick up on so may little details you missed the first time. Whether it's the placement of items, the symbolism behind the monsters or even just noticing subtle shifts in the characters movements and facial expressions when talking with each other, once it all comes together you will be blown away (and likely chronically depressed). subtlety is lost in a lot of horror these days with the monsters and mystery getting explained to the viewer but with this game, all the information you need hidden in plain sight for you to figure out and interpret yourself. This game touches on some very heavy themes but handles them with a lot of care. Does a perfect remake exist? Yes. It's this. It took me 35 hours to complete one play through because I just kept stopping to soak in the atmosphere and sounds of this beautifully bleak and sombre town. I hope this remake inspires and moves people for the next 20 years, just as the original did for me. It’s a 10/10 experience and a must play game for lovers or horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is a game that should be amazing. The atmosphere is haunting, the story is deep and layered, but actually playing it? It’s an absolute chore. From shortly after you start, it feels like the game is less about horror and more about throwing endless, pointless puzzles at you. You’re not immersing yourself in psychological terror — you’re spending hours trying to solve convoluted puzzles just to unlock the next door. And guess what? That door? It leads to another puzzle.The horror aspect, which should be front and center, is completely overshadowed by this ridiculous barrage of puzzles. It’s like the developers thought, “How can we stretch a two-hour story into a twenty-hour game? Oh, I know — let’s force players to constantly backtrack and do fetch quests labeled as puzzles to get a key, that leads to another key, that unlocks yet another puzzle!”By the time you manage to stumble your way through these tedious tasks, the story feels like an afterthought, a distant backdrop buried under layers of frustrating gameplay. And the worst part? It completely kills the tension. Any sense of fear or dread evaporates the moment you realize you’re just solving another boorish and needless puzzle for the umpteenth time.If you’re thinking about playing this game for the story or atmosphere, save yourself the headache. Watch a two-hour cutscene compilation on YouTube. At least then, you won’t have to deal with the mind-numbing, soul-sucking grind that this game disguises as "gameplay."

The pasting of the game is great and its never to slow nor fast never gives you to much to chew at a time especially getting around Silent Hill or the different creepy unsettling areas you explore in the game.  Over all game looks great plays great, story line is great highly recommend it to anyone who's looking for a nice horror, unsettling story to get dragged into.Congratulations to Bloober Team for proving everyone wrong (Including myself)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review by saying: I'm a man born in the 90s. In Eastern Europe no less. Silent Hill 2 is a part of my DNA. The TL:DR is: I think they did it!This won't become the definitive version of SH2, but it holds up for someone who holds the original in high regard, and it would be a great game to pick up for a newcomer to the series.There's a lot to go through, so I'll break down the review into several topics.The story in the remake is pretty much unchanged, with a few minor additions that serve as either clarifications of ideas that were already present in the original, or flavor. This was probably the biggest concern leading up to the release of the remake, given Bloober's... spotty track record. But I am happy to say that all of the story beats still hit right, and all of the themes are handled with a similar amount of care and attention as in the 2001 version.The characters, too, changed very little in the way they are . What did change was the cast: both the voice actors and the MoCap actors make the characters in the remake a lot less stilted, closer to actual human beings. Which could have been bad! A large amount of the original's impeccable vibes were courtesy of the strange and uncanny way the characters behaved. However, I didn't think it detracted from the story in any way. It's still not exactly a  portrayal, it's just a little more grounded.In fact, given the switch to the 3rd person fixed perspective, I think this was a good choice. James' lack of emotion in the original served to separate him from the audience. The player wasn't necessarily meant to associate with James, merely follow him on his nightmarish journey. With the new perspective that may have been boring. This time we  James, and being able to see that he is, in fact, feeling  made it easier to embody him as a player.I don't have much to say about any of the other characters, other than that 99% of the time the actors did their jobs well. I thought there were a couple of lines of over-acted dialog here and there, but mostly I had no complaints.I'm going to say this: the remake knocks the original OUT OF THE WATER in terms of visual design. Not just graphics: it's hardly shocking that a game released in 2024 looks better than the one from 2001. But the  that went into crafting every inch of the world is amazing. SH2 had a desolate look of a half-remembered dream: it was a suggestion of a place, and the environment served more as a way to establish the mood with the color palette than to give much dimension to the world. The remake, on the contrary, has hands down THE BEST depiction of decay I have ever seen in any game. Or any piece of media for that matter.The peeling paint on the walls, the dust, the litter and debris: long after you stop actively noticing these details they are still making the places you traverse  real even when they are actively defying the laws of reality. The remake somehow gets away with generally having an  oppressive atmosphere than the original, and the way the world around you looks and feels weary and dying adds a heaviness to it that works amazingly well to enhance that.I genuinely think that developers being from Poland actually helped a lot in crafting the visuals. Maybe it's a stretch, but Silent Hill here looks like a cross between idyllic, if disheveled, small town Americana and any number of depressing, crumbling towns in Eastern Europe and Russia, whose veneer of Soviet glory is slowly degrading into existential nothingness. I would know, because I grew up in one of those. :DAlso, this thing has the most gorgeous fog effect ever.Yamaoka's brilliant soundtrack is almost the same, so there isn't much to say there. Although I like the new version of "Promise" less - it lacks the purity of the original.The in-game sound design, however, is the second reason why the remake is one of the most effective yet subtle horror games I've ever played. Very few things are in-your-face , but the unsettling sounds that saturate the game's environments will keep you on the edge of your seat. You will hear enemies long before you see them, and the sounds they make are so creepy that seeing them will often be a relief. Silent Hill is never  silent, and every sound has a purpose, a place within the larger atmosphere of a particular set piece. Headphones are pretty much mandatory for playing this game.So, I know the decision to go 3rd person was controversial. Was it necessary? I don't know. I could see the argument that modern players would struggle with tank controls and fixed camera angles, but I also have seen a large number of "retr-aux" survival horror games that came out recently with similar or identical presentation, and they seem to be doing fine.Either way, I don't hate the 3rd person, and once you accept it, it's easy to see how many other changes serve to make the new perspective work better.For example, the remake is a lot more combat-heavy. Enemies can follow you into rooms now, the hallways have a lot more stuff to get tripped up on, and avoiding confrontation generally seems to be less of an option. And that makes a lot of sense once you realize the enemies in SH2 . They are unsettling and stressful to deal with, sure, but the actually scary part is the  of a threat. The reimagined mannequins that aren't picked up by the radio until they attack are a great (and extremely annoying) addition for that reason.So, if you could easily run past enemies in the remake like you could in the original, and the 3rd person perspective allowed you to see them coming more easily, a lot of the tension would have been lost. And I think the combat mechanics Bloober went with hit a good balance. I played the new  recently, and trust me, there were SO MANY ways in which this game's combat could have been worse! It's still nowhere near "robust", and I don't think it was meant to be: it's a janky, stressful dance that goes on just long enough to release some adrenaline, but doesn't turn SH2R into a game  fighting monsters.The only new element that bothered me a bit were the collecta-thons. Just like every single other game on the market, there is a mandatory inclusion of not one, but two different categories of collectibles. They are, of course, completely optional, and as far as I can tell don't provide anything other than an achievement for completing them, but in a game with such meticulously maintained atmosphere the collectibles felt like a forced, immersion-breaking video-gamey intrusion no one asked for.The remake is a slow burn of a game. A first playthrough can easily take 1.5x if not 2x the time it took to complete the original. Not all of this additional time is used well.The time spent on the actual streets of Silent Hill has been expanded, but still feels too short. I understand that the foggy streets probably run the risk of starting to feel all too similar all too soon, but for such an iconic environment it felt underused. The Otherworld sections, on the other hand, take longer, but don't do anything with the extra time they weren't already doing. None of it is bad enough to be a deal breaker, but it could have used some fine-tuning.There are very few games that I ever consider playing more than once. Life is short, and there are so many new things to experience! The privilege is reserved for games  connected with me.I played the original SH2 two or three times. I don't know if I will end up playing the remake more or less. But I know I will be back to this town. Because, you see, I got this letter from my wife...

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having a few technical flaws, the Silent Hill 2 remake is both a great game and an amazing remake that stays in the tone of the original game, but manages to expand a lot of its story and gameplay mechanics. It also upgrades the game's visual quality drastically, making it more serious and graphically impressive.As for the cons of this remake, I can say that it seems to be very inconsistent with its performance. And when I say "inconsistent" I mean that there are some unpleasant traversal stutters in some areas, despite the fact that I have mostly stable frame rates that rarely drop below 80 fps and there are some massive frame rate drops in some areas that feel really bad, like dropping from 100 fps to 60 fps and so on. I use the highest graphical settings and ray tracing + DLSS set to "balanced" on 1440p to achieve this experience so I am not entirely sure if more "optimized" settings will make the game run better, with less stuttering issues and fps drops. Despite that I honestly don't want to sacrifice the stunning visual quality for a little bit of extra performance that is already acceptable, according to my standards.Overall I can totally recommend this game to horror games fans and people that like Silent Hill games, because it is an absolute masterpiece. The rating that I can give to the Silent Hill 2 remake is 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of the original, or even have been curious about playing it, you owe it to yourself to pick this up. Everything else is SH2 cranked up to 11; masterful voice acting, redone boss fights that actually feel compelling, an absolutely amazing amount of additional world-building not present before.

The combat isn't great, but it works. Anyone that says the combat in the original is good is lying, the combat in the remake is 100x better.

_childDocuments_.review: A positive negative review, or a recommendation to get it on sale.It's mostly fine. Story and scenario changes and additions range from inconsequential, to needless padding, or in the absolute worst case taking me out of the experience entirely. That would be the abstract daddy boss fight, which has become a scripted chase sequence. Very hollywood. There was very little new here that impressed me or seemed to justify the enormous money and time expenditure of a remake. Perhaps I'm simply bitter over how little gaming and entertainment have evolved over the past twenty years. Perhaps a remake of 3 would be more interesting, being the most rushed and uneven of the classic trilogy?Combat is atrocious. Even though the title emphasises exploration and ambience over action, an observance of action game fundamentals could have only furthered their cinematic aspirations. It's the typical euro dev pitfall. Fancy motion captured animations ruined by enemies having to moonwalk the last distance to land their 'locked-in' attack, excessive shaky cam, and a magical dodge button so generous pyramid head's knife can visibly clip you without dealing any damage.Furthermore, the behavior of the mannequin enemy pushes the whole structure of the game into 'monster closet' territory. To those unaware, this is NOT a feature of traditional survival horror, but later games, like Doom 3, and that absolute piece of garbage Dead Space. In these games, ambushes are inevitable and unpredictable, so the player proceeds for the duration in a blase state of tactical unpreparedness, knowing that any effort to turn the tables and be proactive in hunting down the foe is a waste of time. They can only react. It's not quite at that level in SH2r, credit where it's due, and it's only one enemy type out of several. But  the dead space likeness ties in to the next complaint all the same.I'm being charitable to assume the creation of a combat system even shallower than the original was unintentional. With this game's audience, it's hard to say. The professional critic response was predictable, as always. But the fanboys are truly rabid. I wonder if the enthusiasm comes from younger gamers who follow certain streamers, who have parasitically attached themselves to the franchise despite it being a quiet low-key experience completely antithetical to their awful content. And there's something sad about seeing reddit snack-photographers absolutely lose it over this game, because while their fun doesn't affect your fun directly, they are the type of people who are likely going to be put in charge of designing the next one. It's going to really suck.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me clarify, although I'm marking this as Not Recommended, I think Bloober did an amazing job. It's just that the original is far superior to the remake in a way that cannot be understated.The game is bloated to high heaven, with the biggest offenders being the Apartments and Labyrinth. The Blue Creek apartments are way too long. Instead of it being a single labyrinth now you have three sections, one of which is a combat test which does not belong at all in a Silent Hill game.Gameplay is alright, dodging feels out of place, the difficulties are all over the place, melee feels clunky and shooting feels off. Overall it feels like I'm playing a Resident Evil Remake.Puzzles are arguably better than the original, at least functionally, thematically it's a different story. The coin box puzzle is in the lobby of the apartment building rather than in someone's room, and also holds a random key with no explanation. Although it didn't make much sense in the original they at least explained it with a note on the door rather than it just being there. This goes on throughout the game and pretty much applies to every puzzle that transfers over from the original. Everything relating to sound is an improvement to the original, with a few minor complaints.Although the story sticks to the original all the way through, it is my biggest complaint with the remake, especially with how they handled the characters and certain scenes relating to them.Maria's whole character is butchered. When she is introduced in the original the music that plays is mysterious and cold. Here it's sleazy, sensual, and distracting, which does not fit the scene at all. Maria puts her hand on James's chest rather than putting his hand on her chest, which subtracts from her flirty and playful nature. She references Born From a Wish which will for sure be DLC down the line similar to Separate Ways in the RE4 Remake. I hate the Pyramid Head chase sequence in here, in the original you're completely unaware of his presence until you see him behind Maria. There is a sound cue beforehand but you're not sure what it could be until he shows up behind Maria. Here he has a huge entrance, there's a zoom in on the door, a sound cue, and a cutscene where James spots him. The corridor is breaking apart, you have to jump over an obstacle, and for some reason Maria is always in front of you. The three times I've played the game so far I have never once made it in front of her, which is just odd.Once you reach the elevator the camera is steady, both James and Maria are silent, there's no desperation present. In comparison to the original where the camera shakes, they're calling out each other's names, James is pushing every button possible on the elevator, and once Pyramid Head kills Maria he pulls her away slowly.The scene in the Labyrinth is also much, much worse here. Maria talks in the same tone, where as in the original she speaks in a manner similar to Mary when needed. I don't know if this was a problem with the actress herself or the director, but I can't understate how inferior this scene is in the remake.My final complaint is the final letter reading. I don't have another word for it other than soulless. Mary keeps the same tone throughout. Her final line sounds like she's just reading the script. In the original it sounds like the actress is about to burst into tears. They also cut my personal favorite line in the game ("I can't tell you to remember me, but I can't bear for you to forget me.") for some odd reason. This is a common theme throughout the remake, where they cut a line that is extremely important for no apparent reason.That's it for Maria, which is the one I have the biggest problems with.My first play-through I thought it was Eddie that had the best execution, but after replaying both games, it's pretty much a completely different character. When you first meet him in the original he rarely faces James, here he is scared when James enters the room and is looking down at the floor ninety percent of the time. He also asks James to accompany him, which I find odd as in the original most of the time Eddie evokes this odd feeling that something's not right with him. Here the way he acts it makes me pity him, which is the complete opposite of how he made me feel in the original.When you meet him in the theater listening to his conversation with Laura is pretty much optional, which again I find odd. Eddie also mentions that he doesn't think the cops followed him there rather than him mentioning he ran away from them. He is also no longer eating pizza but rather eating a large tub of strawberry ice cream with his hands, which I guess does a better job at demonstrating his gluttony. After Laura runs away and James asks Eddie to come with, Eddie responds, clearly hurt by their previous interaction by telling him "Now you want me to come with you?" His boss fight is where I think they really mess up. When he starts repeating to James what the guy he killed said, he gets all up in James's face, which made me a little confused as to what he was doing even though I had played the original before. Once again Bloober decided to cut the crucial line that James asks Eddie, "Eddie have you gone nuts?" which causes Eddie to snap at him and initiate the boss fight. Here Eddie just goes "You're just like the rest of them" and snaps at James. I do like that they removed the first part of the fight where you fight him in the small room and that scene where James dodges the bullet.My biggest gripe with the boss fight is the fact that they removed Eddie's "Let's Party!" before the boss fight begins.I did manage to actually enjoy Eddie's new character, however, I still think they screwed up by changing him in the first place.I think they did a far better job with Angela, my only big complaints are her voice acting and her model. Her model is not for the reason you might think, it's because in the original she looks MUCH older. Angela looks like she's in her late-thirties and I'm pretty sure it's deliberate, here she looks her age. Her voice acting is also not that great here. I think her voice fits and once again I don't know if this problem lies within the actress or the director.Otherwise Angela was great and much better executed than expected.James is the same as the original, he's just more talkative during gameplay, which I really don't like.Laura is the only character that I think is a genuine improvement over the original. She's a lot more mocking of James here, which I do like. My only complaint is her scene in the Hospital, but it's not with her, more with how they handled the scene in general. In the original Laura leads James to the room and the player has little to no reason not to believe her. Here it's clear Laura is lying and they show the door where the Flesh Lips is with an ominous sound effect, reinforcing the fact that she's lying.Another very minor complaint is a disconnect I felt with her model and voice in the last scene. She sound sad but her model looks oddly normal.Again, these are pretty minor complaints and I believe Laura is the only character that genuinely improved over the original.Overall I still think Bloober did a great job, even with all of my complaints. If the original is a 10/10 this is a 7.5/10, which is much higher than I ever expected. My only major complaints is how they handled the story, specifically Maria's character and any scenes involving her.

_childDocuments_.review: While Bloober Team did some things right, I cannot recommend any game polluted with Woke identity politics (i.e., made for a "modern audience"). They designed Maria's outfit to be more conservative in appearance, which conflicts with her character's personality. They also purposefully uglified the faces of all 3 women in the game, Angela looks like she has the mumps, and Mary looks like a cross between a human, a frog, and a chameleon. Not only are the women's faces ugly as hell, but their design is such that they look artificial. They don't even look like real people; they look intuitively fake or artificial, and it completely ruins all of the scenes with them. It's not even that they are unattractive, per se; rather, it's that I cannot even look at them without seeing "Identity Politics" designed into their faces. I look at them and I see ideology placeholders, and it rips me out of immersion.As others have mentioned, Bloober Team also did a poor job with emotional facial expressions. Aside from a few moments wherein James shows some decently believable expressions, the characters' faces look flat. An exceptionally jarring example is the scene when the little girl is supposed to be upset, screaming and crying, yet her face is nearly entirely expressionless.With all of this being said, Bloober Team did do some things right. The game-play mechanics are responsive and fluid. The scenery/environment and monsters, they really knocked out of the park! The details in the environment are really spooky and beautifully designed, and the monsters are true to the original game, only upgraded graphically... so, they're creepy as hell. I can't give enough praise for this, as it makes the rest of the game, when James is away from the Identity Politics Models, I mean female characters, exceptionally immersive and enjoyable to play. I've really enjoyed exploring this upgraded rendition of the town of Silent Hill. They also did a phenomenal job with the sounds in this game. The music, ambient sounds, and sound effects all contribute well to the immersion, dread, and anxiety as James finds his way through Silent Hill.So, in the end, the Silent Hill 2 Remake is a mixed bag in a very polarizing way. It is at once the best and worst of what they could have done. It leaves me feeling conflicted. As I play, I go between loving the experience and getting pissed off and frustrated, depending on whether James is alone or interacting with the women characters in the game.If you can play the original Silent Hill 2, I'd recommend skipping this remake and starting there. The original has aged well. It, too, has beautiful art, making the dated graphics look great even today, and the original does better with the narrative cut scenes, character design, and cinematography. Then, if you love the experience of the original, keeping in mind what the remake entails, decide from there whether you want to play the remake.
