_childDocuments_.review: IN DEPTH NEGATIVE REVIEW AHEAD (I tried to be fair, and stay away from irrational expectations or complaints, I am open to discussion)But first: This game is great! However, I cannot recommend this experience over playing the OG one.The graphics and the general scenario art direction is amazing, and its a beautiful game to look at. And the combat is fun enough to be entertaining, for a while. But when it concerns to matters of story telling, acting and pacing, this game falls flat. My main grievances with the game are the next ones:TOO LONGFirst of, some scenarios (like the apartments, or the streets at night, to name some) have been unpleasantly revamped to be way longer. Too long in my opinion. Over extending the space between story telling elements or puzzles, making the pacing awkward and slow. I understand some people may like this, I found it, personally exhausting. Because of the next point.COMBATThe combat has been revamped and made much more fun and involving than the OG. However, this has been hindered by the abuse of the amount of enemies in levels. 397 is the most that I have seen in internet posts, and its not too far from my personal 377. In the original you will hardly go over the 100 mark unless you are actively seeking for combat. This is also related to the next point.Enemy AIThe enemy AI is very fun to fight against. However it has the negative aspect. Due to the inter-connected arrangement of the map, where every room door can be opened by you and the enemies, you are pretty much forced to fight every enemy in your way in closed scenarios, or have them follow you around for quite a while until eventually you get out of their detection radius. This means that, in the worst cases, running away from enemies can get you trapped by up to 4 enemies in a room. Forced combats were also a staple and a tool used in the OG to put stress on the player. But many of the encounters were also staged to give you a chance to ignore them if you wanted.STORYWhile there are some welcomed additions, specially regarding Angela and Laura, most enviromental story telling changes, and changes related to Eddie, don't hit the same notes. Which is specially frustrating because:ACCEPTABLE VOICE ACTINGLaura and Maria voice actors fail to deliver what one could consider the correct notes to give a similar tone to their interactions with James as in the original. While Mary is really well done, Maria feels too different at times. Laura also behaves different, while in the OG she gave the vibe of an 8 year old, here she behaves and talks more like a 10 or 12 year old, which really takes me out of the experience. Angela and Eddie VA did a great job, and probably Angela was the most benefited character of the changes, along with James, who is surprisingly perfectly voiced and acted. SILENCE PLEASEThis Remake is never quiet. Either its your radio going crazy all the time cause there is an enemy every 5 foot steps, or ambient music or sounds in EVERY room, there is rarely a chance to bask in the uncomfortable silence of the abandoned town. Even the enemies are so noisy that you can hear them gurgling and babbling from three rooms away. Suspense is therefore almost unexistant bar some moments where the devs where explicitly looking for it. While Akira Yamaoka is a genius of ambient design, he may have underestimated the value of another tool in his sound and musical arsenal: Silence. DELUXE EDITIONThe additions are well worth the price (its just a couple of dollars more). Its just, I think they could have been put better together, specially the art book, and probably could have charged more for them instead. I know a OST album is coming out with everything. So I probably would have just bought that instead. In general its a great game, if you can forget the original exists or you prefer a more action focused game, its an amazing experience. Its visually impressive, and fun to play. However, it does have a different vibe from the original with different dialogues, extended or extra scenes, more locations and combat, the game could even be viewed more as an "Alternate reality scenario". But this is not a replacement for the original. Make with that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: Bloober Team indeed managed to surpass expectations and deliver a very solid remake. I'm no Silent Hill 2 purist, mind you — having played through the original only a handful of times, I consider this remake a clear improvement on all fronts: the atmosphere is still there, the fog looks the best it's ever been, the over-the-shoulder camera angle makes the game much more immersive. The combat, probably my main point of contention with the original game, is much improved upon since 2001. People might say jank was part of the charm — and maybe back in the day it really was, — but nowadays I much rather fight the actual enemies on screen than controls and the combat system itself.Speaking of which, enemies are much more agressive this time around, encounters being much more visceral and thrilling. Especially the Mannequins that employ cunning and will try to hide, flank and ambush you. Boss fights have more gravitas to them and now feel like an actual event: they are either expanded upon or turned into a set-piece.As for the story, all the beats are there and the overarching plot remains intact — it's everything in-between that has been changed and expanded upon: previous key locations are now easter eggs, while the real puzzles lie elsewhere. A mere speedbump in the original game they are now a centerpiece of a particular area or section of the game, a real highlight in the remake. The town itself now features a lot more nooks & crannies to explore with lesser puzzles to solve along the way. Some new character scenes were also added to provide a little bit of context.With the (possible) exception of Maria, all of the character performances I found to be great, especially James: Luke Roberts did a fantastic job prividing his character with emotional nuance, fleshing him out and adding some depth to his drama. Maria, however, is a hit or miss in this version: they went for a bit of different direction with her, which can either make or break the character for some. As an aside: to be completely honest, I was never a fan of the original VO. I won't say it was bad — just not my cup of tea. To make an apt comparison: where the original felt like a David Lynch production, the remake feels more like a David Fincher thing. Take that as you will, but it's a win in my book.All of the aforementioned additions and improvements made the game markedly longer to get through with my first playthrough clocking in at around 13 hours. You can easily add about three to five hours more if you plan to explore every corner of the town religiously, or have trouble figuring out what to do next. Which I doubt, as the game provides nice signposting and hints to help steer the player in the right direction without being expressly in-your-face about it.Overall the remake leaves a great and positive impression, but if I had to nitpick, as with the original the later sections, like the Prison and the Labyrinth, are still a chore to get through. The Prison is clearly the worst offender given its enemy density: it is the most action-heavy section of the game which soured my impression just a tiny bit. Somehow the devs never seem to quite escape the gung-ho throes of modern game-design. You can't just explore — you have to go commando at some point and it's always the worst. And I can't say there was too much spare ammo lying around to warrant this many enemies...As for the elephant in the room, the game's performance, I found it to be manageable in 1080p, medium-to-high rendering preset and DLSS set to performance. On my 2060S it hovers somewhere between 50 to 60 fps with dips into low 40s here and there. It's clearly not as optimised as Capcom's recent remakes, for example, yet still agreeable enough to actually play.Nitpicks and performance woes aside, I'd say the game is a pretty solid 9/10. Your milage may vary depending on how sacred the original game was for you, but to me it felt like a worthy reimagining of a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, no use in beating around the bush. I honestly don't recommend this game, at least not at full price. This is really disappointing to me as everything I read and saw regarding this remake looked very promising. What I found however is another developer trying a little too hard to "improve" the formula and refusing to recognize when something they designed does not work, or at least not well.What am I talking about? Well it's the combat. No, I am not wearing rose tinted glasses, the original Silent Hill 2 also had some pretty lack luster combat, it was there, it was serviceable, but it was bland. The remake however, goes to far in the opposite direction by trying to make combat a primary focus of the game, if not THE primary focus. My gripes are as follows:1. Enemy aggression is way too high. Enemies in this game are ACTIVE. I mean really active, there is no more sneaking or playing it safe. You are fighting, and you better like it, because it's the majority of the game.2. So many enemies. If Bloober wanted to make the combat encounters intense, that could be fine, if it weren't happening constantly. There are so many enemies now, it just becomes desensitizing.3. The actual combat system is a clunky mess and the game does a very poor job of teaching what you are actually supposed to do. There seems to be this cat and mouse system where you are supposed to hit an enemy a couple times, then back off, rinse repeat.... except when that is punished for...reasons? Sometimes enemies just have input reading levels of response time where they use an instant follow up attack after you perform a single swing. I don't want to say it's unavoidable, but the game does nothing to teach you how to avoid it. From a new player perspective, it just feels like they wanted to back in intentional damage as part of the game. This is kind of silly because in a survival horror game, it's all about conservation of hard to find items. Now it has become more of a smoke if you got em scenario, just chug healing drinks and fight through the awful combat. Also, the whole system seems to be about movement, but you are constantly fighting hyper aggressive enemies in tiny spaces where dodging and running don't really work. Makes no sense to me.Overall, Bloober seems to be very proud of their combat system, as they force you into it as often as they can, however, it just isn't enjoyable to me. I like that they tried to improve things rather than do a 1:1 remake, but I would prefer eve the old bland stiff combat over this mess.The most painful part of all of this is that the rest of the game design is quite good. The atmosphere and sound design is superb. Graphically, it feels right for the most part, and the game does a good job of capturing the old feeling of each of the memorable areas from the original. I know there are some complaints of performance, and yes, there is stutter here and there, but it is nowhere near as bad as people are making it out to be. I am high susceptible to any kind of stutter or frame pacing issues, and this game doesn't really bother me.That being said, I really hope there is some plan to tweak the combat, as it's just a little too clunky and forced for my taste and is fouling an otherwise great experience. Some have suggested that I put the combat to easy, but I honestly don't find it difficult, it just feels cheap, so doing so would be more of a bandaid than a true fix.

_childDocuments_.review: The Progenitor of the Survival Horror genre!When I played the original SH2 almost 20 years ago I remember feelings of darkness and despair while surviving all the trials that this town was throwing to James. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing the main story, I genuinely must say that I seriously hope this game wins the Game of the Year award. _childDocuments_.review: Bloober told us "shut up and watch" and provided one of the best horror experiences in gaming. In my time playing this genre since the PS1, this has been one of the few titles that has genuinely given a sense of dread in the best way possible. Sounds are masterfully mixed and purposefully hard to discern from the music. Encounters feel meaty and have this desperation in the way James stomps on the corpses to try to keep them down. I fell in love (and **** myself) when an enemy disappeared in a commonly trafficked corner early in a location and the rest of my hour was spent panic checking for a jump scare that never came. The brilliance of it being the game rarely telegraphs itself but balances that line of keeping it's scares from feeling cheap or undeserved.Enemies are far from the only star of the show though, as the game heavily and successfully relies on its incredible atmosphere to carry it. A lot of people have talked about the graphics but the real standout is the faithful recreation and detail in the art direction and lighting to the point just walking around silent hill feels like one of the most authentic small towns in a video game I've seen. The more intimate locations such as apartments, bars, and hospital feel distinct and leverage darkness to maintain that sense of claustrophobia. I could continue to gush about the obvious improvement to James as a character and the storytelling, but the only negatives I have is some of the boss fights feeling lackluster in gameplay (the updated designs of Masahiro Ito are still incredible though) and the camera being difficult in some moments, but these are relatively minor complaints.Do yourself a favor and get this instant classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the original which I got to play in it's original release:If you are looking for a carbon copy of that with just super modern graphics this is not the game.Silent Hill 2 Remake does it's own thing by adding new puzzles, small extra areas and jump scares while containing the original game in it. Motion Capture technology finally gives us realistic human characters who do a fantastic job. You will not see the uncanny faces done by scratch from the original but real people fitting their age, removing the uncanny but adding a fantastic layer of realism through real humans being our beloved characters. Maria in particular has more life to her than ever, playing with James mind and feelings way more than just being hot , she is perfectly expanded compared to the source material. If you have been playing horror games constantly since the original release of the greatest games of the survival horror genre in the PSX/PS2 era and developed a natural resistance to horror, the atmosphere will remain being great, but the game won't be really scary. Now, if you are new to the genre, be it because of your age or never tried horror games before, this is probably gonna become a stable of 'If you wanna be really scared and paranoid play this'.Combat has been improved compared to the original but at the same time suffers from it: dodging may be weird for a SH game and when you meet a new enemy and you don't understand their behavior, you can easily get beaten down to almost no life. In normal difficulty is quite common to be out of bullets, out of meds and on low health if you had a hard time with a section. Running this time around is not adviced as monsters does not reset in connected spaces compared to the original. Ironically, the lowest difficulty is closer to the normal difficulty of the original. A good thing is: you can switch enemies difficulty in the game if you are having a hard time. Is not the same for puzzles. They remain cryptic and twisted, even the new ones are rather elaborated and fair. Every new addition doesn't feel out of place and boss fights are fantastic.In terms of technical performance, I play on a very high-end pc and I did suffer some slowdowns and a single UE5 crash. This may be due to the lack of a day 1 patch. Still, this is probably the best remake we ever had for the genre and probably the best opportunity Silent Hill has to show it's horror masterclass to new generations since the original release 23 years ago.  If you are on the younger side and you are old enough to try the genre, be ready to be fueled by nightmares, is a great introduction to what the genre can do.A minor issue that may help everyone: the game tends to default to Dualsense or Dualshock when you are using a controller, you can select your controller from the options menu. I'm using a Xbox One wireless controller and I had a hard time when the game prompted me to press X until I checked the options.Update: I finished the game on Standard/Standard difficulty. While some parts at the beggining may feel slow and that go for too long, I can't but recommend this game with my whole heart. This is the best the series has ever been with the best boss fights we ever had. An over abundant amount of consumables to my liking maybe, but the last bosses were fantastic and challenging for a regular survival horror experience. Despite the minor performance issues (Really, disabling Vsync and Ray Tracing does wonders for it at the cost of fidelity, UE5 really needs to improve the engine) everything was nearly perfect. It does not replace the original, but it pays homage to it in a way that both games are 'mandatory' in my list of horror games that are must play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Silent Hill franchise since I was a kid. This series means a lot to me. Initially when I heard that arguably the best game in the franchise was getting remade I was sceptical. However, Bloober team have pulled of the unexpected. This is quite possibly the BEST remake I have EVER played. Game play wise this takes what was great about the original Silent Hill 2 and RAMPS it. The atmosphere is great, the fog and darkness always leaving you wondering what's just around the corner. The fighting system was also a great improvement, I always felt that the fighting in the original silent hill was a tad too easy if you knew what you were doing, in this the timing you need and the precision as well is a welcome addition. The puzzles have all been good. I won't say mind numbingly hard, but at the moment I've only started a medium/medium play through and the puzzles have all been straight forward to an extent and certain twists on classic puzzles from the original were a very welcome addition.The sound design and music has been a massive highlight. The sound design adds so many different layers to this. Akira Yamaoka is known for going above and beyond within this franchise and he has done so again. The general atmospheric background tracks really do help escalate your emotion throughout it and at the correct moments the tense feeling you should be feeling when you are exploring such dank horrible places. The classic tracks that have been remastered and re-recorded too are a very welcome addition. It points when you're feeling tense it brings a sense of nostalgia but with the new arrangements a whole new level to familiar but different. Overall I would rate this game as a MUST play for any die hard horror game fan. Even if you've never played a Silent Hill game before I would even go as far as to recommend this as a really good starting point.

_childDocuments_.review: After exploring the streets of Silent Hill and the narrow spaces of the Woodside Apartments, I wrapped up my session at 4 a.m., feeling my initial faith in Bloober Team remains intact and I'm essentially convinced they have accomplished something truly remarkable. I found their surreal and abstract horror in Layers of Fear intriguing, while their approach in Blair Witch was not only terrifying but also emotionally resonant - a faithful extension of the original film.Initially, Bloober Team demonstrated a clear passion, respect, and understanding for the delicate source material that made the original an indisputable masterpiece in 2001. Moreover, they approached the remake with great care, remaining responsive to critical fan feedback and implementing tangible changes over time.The remake maintains a great deal of the artistic integrity that defined the psychologically pioneering original while also impressively modernizing the gameplay. The existing content has been significantly expanded and altered, establishing new locations and added narrative elements, implementing various aspects that undoubtedly enhance the overall experience.Silent Hill 2 appears to be a remake executed admirably; it might very well be considered the remake of 2024, potentially even the top horror game of the year. And frankly, it's about damn time the stagnated and mishandled Silent Hill franchise finally reclaims its rightful place at the top of the hill.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I had serious doubts that "Bloober Team" would be able to handle such an ambitious task as the remake of Silent Hill 2. The pre-release trailers only added to my skepticism about the final product quality. But fortunately, and to my great surprise, they managed to get almost everything right. The atmosphere, sound, and graphics are all done at a very high level. However, there are also some drawbacks. For some reason, all the cutscenes are only in 30fps. The combat system in the game is frankly weak and serves a purely functional purpose. I also can't help but mention the extremely mediocre optimization and the presence of stutters on absolutely all platforms. As soon as the stutters are fixed, the Silent Hill 2 remake can confidently claim the game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: The lights are flickering above me, and I'm squinting so hard my eyes might as well be shut. It's quiet now save for my heavy breathing - the stabbing sensation in my side is a constant reminder of why I give people a wide berth.  I came here - I'm not sure why, if I'm being honest. Compelled? Captivated? Coerced? It really doesn't matter now, I suppose. My time here is running short. I just wanted to see her one last time, just to tell her... just to tell her I'm sorry.Silent Hill 2 (2024) is a remake of the critically acclaimed game of the same title, way back in the forgotten, fog-shrouded time of 2001. And it's excellent. It's pitch perfect. Bloober Team had a Sisyphean task, and they somehow pulled it off - staying true to the source material, modernizing it, and dare I say improving on some antiquated game design of yesteryear. There's reverence here, for the original: throwbacks to lines that didn't quite fit the new voice direction, puzzles that were guilty of moon logic relegated to glimpses of the past, etc. And this title wouldn't be so excellent if not for the work not just of Bloober Team, but the original Silent Hill Team... Virgils guiding their Dantes. Do I have any issues? TEENSY, baby issues that I'll lay out here, right now: OPTIMIZATION, and I don't care for how enemies lock on to James like they're enemies in the original Demon Souls.That's it, really - I was a little frustrated on the last boss because sometimes it's a pain in the butt to pick up consumables unless you're looking at them just the right way, but those are my gripes, and they could all be addressed in due time.From the moment you start this game, it feels like such an intimate journey... it almost plays like a film, with the art direction and scene direction. Slowly, deliberately, the town of Silent Hill unveils itself to you - brimming with mystery, with horrors, and with lost souls. It's such a narrative game that I struggle to say much. Yes, it's two decade old piece of art, but I hope people are able to go into this as blind as possible and just experience it for the first time.This is more gush than review, but... the way James updates the map is just so damned immersive. I love the sound design - it is OPPRESSIVE, like there are insects scurrying and skittering around in your head. I hated myself for rushing around a corner, spying a health item I desperately needed, only to get clocked by an enemy just waiting around said corner. The town is rich with assets, notes, storytelling through environment, vistas that are breathtaking, claustrophobic depths... it feels, pardon the pun, alive. Dirty, desolate, depressing, but very much alive.I played it on the highest difficulty, myself - and if you're a seasoned survival horror vet, I would recommend it. By the end of my, like, 18 hours with the game I was as exhausted as my James. I was HURTING for supplies, and every little health item or bullet I found usually came with the caveat of 'I got this, but at what cost?' But there's nothing wrong with playing on a lower difficulty and just enjoying the story, for the story's sake. You won't be locked out of anything, as far as I'm aware.In summation, imagine being tasked with - I don't know, recreating Guernica, in the spirit of Guernica, in 2024? Or being told you have to rewrite 'The Exorcist' for a modern audience while remaining true to what made it so memorable, so iconic in the first place? Picture having to improve upon something so tight and refined and consummate that it just isn't really possible; whatever the time, the budget, the talent... you are probably not going to improve on 'the wheel.'Bloober Team did just that. They took a 23-year-old game, inserted it into some kinda Willy Wonka device, and managed to make the essential version of a beloved, survival-horror classic... which is selling them so incredibly short on my part. I wouldn't go so far as to say it replaces the original, but it is certainly the best way to play this game now, for a modern audience with modern devices. If I were to force a comparison, Bloober Team did for Silent Hill 2 what Peter Jackson did for The Lord of the Rings. Are people going to be disappointed? It's 2024, there's someone furious right now that a hurricane wasn't a destructive as was promised. That doesn't take away from the fact that this is a twisted, beautiful nightmare I loved beginning to end - one I'll carry with me, always.... It also helps that I took an embarrassing amount of screenshots.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: When I was playing The Medium, I couldn't help but to think the game was heavily inspired by and very reminiscent of Silent Hill, and given a great track record of Bloober team, they seemed like an ideal candidate to create a SH game. And what do you know, right?SH2 is not only a faithful remake with countless small details only fans would notice and appreciate, but also a damn great game regardless of its roots! They took the idea of 20+ year old horror, and built a new experience upon it. The game stays true to the original by having the same locations, enemies, weapons, and, of course, the story and main characters, but also improves upon every single aspect of the gameplay. It's not just a SH2 with a better visuals, it's a SH2 with better gameplay too.No more fixed camera, no more janky controls, no more horrible running sequences: Bloober team managed to modernize the presentation, but underneath it all there's still that feeling of dread and mystery the original SH2 has. Basically, this remake follows the same formula as the Resident Evil remakes: modernize the gameplay and visuals, but leave everything that the players love.And it shows, as it is probably the best game from Bloober team (and I already loved Observer and The Medium), and one of the best remakes ever made. Whether you are a fan of Silent Hill series or just a horror-adventure aficionado, you should definitely play this game.P.S. Soundtrack by Akira Yamaoka is amazing. He made the new versions of all the songs we love: Theme of Laura, and Promise sound completely fresh, yet still so familiar and nostalgic. But regardless, even if you didn't play the original, SH2 has probably the best OST in videogames this year.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is an atmospheric bukkake and I'd recommend it on that alone. It's unlike anything I've listened to or played before. Every footstep, water drop, door creak, wind gust, paper flap or light flicker will always make you second guess if you're actually alone in the room or not. James' voice acting and performance is so great and adds to the already great atmosphere. He will breath uneasy when scared, limp when hes hurt, pull his weapon out when he knows a monster is near, grunt and swing at enemies as if his life depended on it (because it does.) I was never interested in Bloober team before, but now they are definitely on my radar from now on. Atmosphere is super important to me in video games, and I gotta say, they absolutely nailed it in this game. Not to mention, I ACTUALLY feel scared and uncomfortable playing this game for long periods of time, which I haven't truly felt towards a game since the original Dead Space back in 2008. I can officially add this game to my list of best horror games of all time (that I've played), competing with Dead Space and Resident Evil. I really do hope Konami lets Bloober remake more silent hill games as I have not played a single one before coming to this remake. If they bring the same passion for horror they had for this game to their future titles (Cronos/any future silent hill game), then we are eating good af

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to leave a negative review considering the atrocious performance even on my still decent PC, but couldn't do it because the game itself is phenomenal. While the original is still the better (best) game, this one might be the best horror game I've played. I too thought that the game looked awful when the first trailer released, but now I don't regret money spent, even though I've never paid more than $20 for a game before. It's that good. Some things could've been done better like some cutscenes, with cutscenes like those with Angela looking a bit low budget, and some just not having that same delivery like in the original. Combat and bosses are a definite improvement, maybe toning them down a bit would be good. Puzzles on normal difficulty are not too hard which I'd consider a good thing. Finally the world and the atmosphere were for me completely different than in the original, and while not as good, they still nailed the horror vibe similar to something like a first game. Overall great game, but I highly recommend you to first try the original.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no need to discuss the merits of SH2 as a game, so I won't. I think this is a great game and well worth your time, but not at $70. It lacks the replayability of other games in the genre and the combat isn't strong enough to sustain multiple playthroughs unless you're a diehard fan. After you beat the roughly 12-14 hour game in a first playthrough, you unlock NG+, which contains only one new weapon, several new endings tied to new collectibles and visual filter modes. But the game, while great with MUCH improved combat over the original game, is still very basic, doesn't evolve whatsoever and is rather easy. But that first playthrough is a great experience and the new weapon is fun enough to MAYBE speedrun a second playthrough if you want to see one more ending and get some more achievements.Bloober did a great job and this game is equal to the original in almost every way, though it does some things much better, while maybe a few things slightly worse. Get this at $50 and it will be one of the best survival horror games you ever play. In the off chance you never played and don't know the story, it's incredible and go in blind for as long as you can.Now, this game is on the DEI detected list. If you don't want to support the game for using the consultant group Hit Detection, respect. Konami and Bloober should know better, DEI kills game potential. I will say, however, that this game doesn't suffer from DEI nearly as much as you may have been led to believe. Angela's model is fine, she looks exactly like one might expect given what she went through and what she represents. Maria is more complicated, but she still dresses in a skin tight leather dress, her VA is far better at sensuality, and there's an entire new scene with her basically pole-dancing. Bloober should have included her original dress as an unlockable skin, which is also a complaint of how little unlockables there are in the game in general.TLDR: Great game, poor replaybility, Bloober gets a W, DEI sucks but doesn't effect this game to the level you might expect. Buy on sale at $50(or less).
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the original Silent Hill 2. Nor does it really feel like it's trying to be, the game does not feel like it's trying to be as surreal or lynchian as the original game was. If you aren't down for that. This remake may not be for you. I personally, enjoyed it a fair amount. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the Silent Hill franchise, having played the games from 1 all the way to Silent Hill Shattered Memories. I was very excited about this game, and my girlfriend gratefully purchased it for me. Things were promising, definitely captured the heart and soul of the Silent Hill Franchise. The graphics, soundtrack, and sound design were amazing. It wasn't just a cash grab in terms of aesthetics; the story/graphics people really cared.HOWEVER, the game is MARRED with glitches, screen tearing, and random crashes. In particular, when you reach Woodside Apartments (near the very beginning of the game), the game CONSTANTLY crashes when you open the door to the Courtside yard. You can literally not progress. This is the first game I have ever encountered a game-breaking glitch that does not allow you to progress. This is sort of the gaming trend where they rush out a game to meet an arbitrary deadline (i.e. October/Halloween), and then they will probably say "Oh, we will patch things later." It's only been a month since the game was released to the public, so perhaps they will address this soon., and I hope so. But having the audacity to charge 70 USD for a game that you cannot play is a microcosm of the gaming industry. PLEASE wait several months/when they discount this game before you purchase it.EDIT: I finalllyy got the game to not crash every time I opened the Apartment door. What you HAVE to do is 1) uninstall/reinstall the entire game, and 2) under the Steam Properties, add launch flag: -dx11. Apparently this has only worked for some but not a lot.I still standby the review: the visuals were great. The innovation/building from the original game was great. But in the end, it has to be a GAME that is functional, and it is marginally functional at best. I reached the Brookhaven Hospital and randomly,  I've not been able to move at least three times, the stuttering, the clear loading of enemies (when you leave and reenter the area, the dead bodies rise and ragdoll onto the floor). Great visuals, poor gameplay design/optimization.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. But it isn't giving you exactly what the original did. In fact, this remake is exactly what I thought it would be: better gameplay and atmosphere but worse voice acting and a soundtrack that has been 'remixed' with inconsistent results. Now I'm going to list a bunch of problems I had with it, but understand that I still *liked* the remake quite a lot. I just don't agree with people saying that this is the title people should play to "jump in" to the series. Great game or not, there is no excuse for Konami refusing to put the original games on Steam. THIS IS NOT A REPLACEMENT! The original is NOT obsolete! So f*cking port it to Steam already!So, now for my gripes.The ending letter is in my opinion vastly inferior to the original. I was waiting the entire game to see this letter and I can't be more disappointed. They changed the wording! It used to be perfect, and now Mary rambles on and ends with a very different message for James, one that seems so stereotypical and filled with platitudes, compared to the original's which sounded so unfortunate and tragic and *real*. Remake's letter can't make me cry like the original one does, without fail, every time I listen to it again.For the soundtrack, the original composer Akira Yamaoka returns for an encore. However, his shift in style and progression as a musician has been incredibly obvious over the years when you listen to the music he has made since 2001 when SH2 came out. A lot of the songs are the same but remixed into a new style, sometimes  still with the original samples that he no doubt had to dig out of his old 90's samples bin. I just preferred his original style. The song 'Theme of Laura', for example, which is the end credits scene for the 'Leave' ending, is so much better in the original compared to the version we get here. It's strange considering the trailer for the remake from a year ago had a much more faithful rendition of this particular song that seems to be absent from the finished product. 'Theme of Laura' in particular is Akira Yamaoka's personal favourite song from SH2 as he has himself said, and it has many different versions, but the one Bloober chose to include is clearly just a type of 'live rendition' rather than something I expected Akira actually intended to be the end credits theme this time around. Others like 'Laura Plays the Piano' and 'Heaven's Night' have had been so majorly altered that I think they are simply worse than the original in every single way, despite using the same samples from the same original library. There is an obvious trend of Akira Yamaoka removing synths this time around and trying to include more live instrumentation, especially strings and drum loops, which he himself no doubt performed rather than using a digital synthesizer. It may be technically more professional to do it this way, but something about his old synth-heavy style is just better to me—the original games' soundtrack was created almost entirely with Akira Yamaoka sitting in front of a computer with a simple USB-port keyboard, an electric guitar, a microphone, and an audio synthesizer program loaded with cheap digital sample libraries from sample groups like Bizarre Guitar which he literally walked across the street from Konami's headquarters to buy discs of. Now I'm sure he has an entire studio to himself and so much more advanced technology, so I don't blame him for feeling 'guilty' about how low-tech and simply the original soundtrack was composed, and I understand he wanted to 'do it more professionally' this time around. But something was lost along the way.So I humbly ask Konami to allow the original soundtrack to be restored with DLC similar to how Resident Evil 4 also included this option (and please let it be free this time, Konami, you can be better than Capcom). Otherwise, the performance of the game is uniquely terrible in certain areas, especially once you reach the Woodside Apartments and ESPECIALLY any time the game transitions to the Otherworld. It can't even maintain 60 fps with DLSS at 1440p with an RTX 3080 and ray tracing off in many indoor areas. Ray tracing, when on, also very barely seems to change the image at all but still costs you a good 30% of your performance. I noticed later in the game for example in the bowling alley that the image looked identical with ray tracing on or off, almost as if the developers just forgot to add in specific ray-traced lighting to many individual areas of the game. Shadows look strange and I think there are bugs with certain settings because the Shadows setting does literally nothing but still takes a good chunk of your performance away. There is no way to turn off chromatic aberration! I had to play with a headache the entire time if I was in a bright area! Actually, the graphics settings are kind of the bare minimum, so I imagine most changes will instead be done via engine.ini edits in the game files and with mods.I'm not complaining about Maria's new outfit, but there's this point where she literally holds up her old outfit on a hangar and asks you if she'd look good in it. Of course, she doesn't put it on. I was just waiting for her to say "not in a million years!" like Dante. What a d*ck move, Bloober Team. Also, having beaten the game, I can confirm you do not unlock the outfit for a new playthrough. Well that sucks. Also, why are some of the patches on James' jacket missing? Is the flag of the USA really too controversial to be included this time around?The ability to block from the original has been removed. I know, I know, tiny gripe, most people don't even realize you *can* block, but the real problem is that James looks so silly ducking and weaving like he's a 'The Last of Us' protagonist. Actually, he controls almost exactly like in that game, with his melee weapon just instantly teleporting to his hands when he starts swinging. I didn't care too much about this from a gameplay perspective but I would have liked a button to switch to the melee weapon proper. Also, James will put away whatever weapon he's holding after a few seconds without combat, which I think is kind of stupid considering he's never really 10 feet away from another Lying Figure trying to spit acid in his face, so why is he always putting his weapons away? It also I think looked cooler always carrying a weapon in the original, and avoids the problem of weapons materializing in his hands whenever he starts aiming or initiates a melee attack.The game has a lot of cut stuff from the original that they include in these little 'memorials' where you interact with the environment and a green static flash appears on the screen, along with a musical cue, to let you know the developers remember what it was they altered. It's fine, I guess, but some of them are particularly egregiously missing, especially the one in the Lakeview Hotel where James puts on a headset to listen to a recording of himself arguing with Mary's doctor about her condition. You still find the equipment, but you can't use it, only getting the green flash. That's weak. Oh yeah, and Eddie no longer eats pizza in the bowling alley, but you can find the pizza box there and James will even say the line about eating pizza with monster around, though Eddie is no longer in this scene. Green flash. Hurray, I guess?I guess it's mostly miniscule nitpicks from here but you get my point. The biggest problem is by far the soundtrack remix, followed by the voice acting changes, followed by everything else. Again, the game is still really good and far better than anyone expected from the guys who made The Medium, but I can't overstate how important it is to play the original and see where I'm coming from. A lot of the magic is in this remake but some of it isn't, and even that small amount of magic lost is too huge of a sacrifice to truly recommend you play this over the original. I'm still thumbs-upping this because it is worth playing for series vets. That's all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are interested in the survival horror franchise, this game is an  game for you to play. Even for players familiar with the resident evil franchise you can experience gameplay similar to that of Resident evil 2 remake with the combat. Do not expect James Sunderland (Main character) to be some sort of Leon S. Kennedy because he is NOT anything like Leon. Story-wise this game excels at telling a story that will absolutely leave you in awe. With unforgettable side characters and amazing dialogue scenes to really have you captured in the Silent Hill world, I  you that you will not be disappointed. Unless you are some miserable person who doesn't enjoy anything then you're on your own. Also beware if you are not a fan of puzzles in games this game might not be for you but, it does not hurt to try even then there are always guides to help you if you can not solve anything on your own. Just try not to rely too much on guides as that kills the fun of all the puzzles you have to solve. They really captured the essence of the original beautifully even enhancing much of the game with updated graphics and gameplay. This remake does a wonderful job at recreating the original while also putting it's own twist to please the modern audience. With callbacks to the original while adding new scenes to improve the story even further this remake does not disrespect the original at all. I never doubted bloober team can fumble with this game and I was right to where I would even say personally I enjoy so much more than the original. Bloober team never fell short of any expectations of this game for me but, some incels may say otherwise over their garbage opinions over how a woman would look in this game but, do not listen to any of those garbage reviews talking about how Maria lost her charm or Angela doesn't look good anymore to justify any negativity they have over this game. This game is not a 1:1 remake but, it is extremely close not deviating from the story at all but, instead improving and adding things that make the story even better. The puzzles I'd say are still as fun and challenging as the original while also adding new puzzles to make the game feel refreshing. _childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, let me tell you that this is probably the best Silent Hill game we've got since SH4. Bloober was so close making this game a true successor to the original you wouldn't believe it. Of course, they had to ♥♥♥♥ it up here and there, and the questionable choice to include a garbage DEI firm did not help either, but overall it's a pretty good game.So, the remaster suffers from three horsemen of major ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥:1. Everyone sees how trashy character faces look in the game. I refuse to believe that it's incompetence on the dev's part. I mean James looks alright, and I can give a pass to Laura too. But the others don't look like real everyday people at all. Eddie looks like a regular at McDonald's now (Yes, he was fat in the original too, but not THIS fat) and the women have wider jaws and bigger heads than the protagonist. The worst offender is Maria: As a man, I refuse to believe that any fellow man's dream woman looks like her. She looks like one of those confused LGTV fans. It's most likely where the "inclusivity firm" did the most damage.2. Censorship. You either make a faithful retelling of the original, or you change important stuff in your remake. You can't do both, especially when it comes to changing key scenes in-game. Aside from the famous PH-mannequin scene, they've changed numerous key scenes and sadly made a lot of them worse. I'll drop another one here:  It's a lot worse than the original and nowhere near as dramatic. Also, they changed the dress of the only character they shouldn't have touched and didn't do anything to everyone else.3. Forced Combat. It is a mixed bag. On one hand, the combat itself is serviceable and works mostly well. It's clunky as it should be and sells the fact that James is just a random dude trying to survive. BUT, there is way too much of it in the game. It's Silent Hill, supposed to be a psychological horror, not an action-packed RE4 clone. Unlike the original, You have to fight most battles here, so it gets tedious after a while. Also, it has QTE grab mechanics...Thankfully the brilliance of the original story still shines in the remake and they even added a lot of small details to it. There are new places to explore and new stuff to find. You can see James writing down important stuff on the map and breaking windows and windshields to salvage stuff. It adds to the atmosphere a lot. The graphics are nice, the fog is probably the best fog I've seen in a video game so far, the decay and rust really sell the other world's depressing mood. The monster design is great too, thank god they did not let any DEI cockroa- I mean consultant near Pyramid head. Akira Yamaoka didn't disappoint this time either, the music is phenomenal. I think the acting is well done too, it's rocky in a few places, but the original had some bumpy acting too here and there. Some characters might feel a bit off to the seasoned veterans though.Overall, it's a pretty good game, that only misses the mark by a few "manjaws" and a hint of censorship. I can easily recommend it though. Don't buy it for 70 bucks, no game is worth that much. Especially when it had the DEI firm's rotten claws around it. Buy it at a slight discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Silent Hill 2 done by the team that made the Resident Evil 2 Remake.  That's SH2R.  In some ways it enhances the original, in others it misses the mark.  Overall, not worth $70.  Wait for a sale.Ideally, SH2R would have been 5-8 hours long and $40, like the original.  A much more compact and potent experience.  But they wanted to charge $70 (or even $80 for deluxe) so they had to stretch it out.===Changes from the original that hinder the remake:- Combat and the camera make this a more action focused game.  The same thing was done to RE2R.  But SH2 is about atmosphere, which is lost with the new camera.  Don't believe me?  Check out the fixed camera mod for RE2R.  It changes the feeling of the entire game.- SH2R is too long.  I know you can speed run it, but on your first playthrough you want to take it slow, look at everything, let the gloom sink in.  Stretching the game out turns it into a slog.  In the original, you'd finish the game in 5-8 hours and then instantly want to play it again to see the other endings.  In the remake, you'll finish in 17-22 hours and then want to uninstall.  Keep in mind this isn't Parasite Eve, with a ton of unique monsters.  There are 5 enemy types (not including bosses).  Fighting gets VERY repetitive and boring.===There are MANY glitches (but to be fair, the devs are working on these):- The game LOVES to stutter.  There are mods that can fix this.- During combat James can end up on a low surface he normally can't get on (like a bed or couch).  Since you can't jump down, you have to reload.- You can get stuck if you save in the wrong place.- The save/load menu system is buggy.  Sometimes there are multiple rows highlighted.===And some minor nitpicks:- Turning the entire screen red when you're hurt like CoD is dumb.  It completely ruins the immersion.  Luckily, there's a mod to fix this.- There's a weird issue with model scale.  Like old cars that should be giant instead barely coming up to James' chest, or newspaper boxes that are as tall as James.  Seems the asset teams weren't communicating world scale very well.- SH2 takes place in 1993 (or possibly early if you go by what the original devs say).  Yet every rundown old car has modern seat belt latches.- The dog ending is missing the slide show, so the growls in the song won't make sense.- The shadows look bad, even compared to the PS2.  They don't react correctly to your flashlight.  This happens with or without ray tracing.- I have never seen a VHS player pull in a tape like a slot load CD player before.

_childDocuments_.review: Blooper team has done it again! the abouslute madmen! They remade Silent Hill Homecoming with all its problems just with Silent Hill 2 story tacked on. Removal of all the fun extra weapons (no bonus scenario for great DLC bait too!!!). The original is free, has a fantastic remaster, and takes you less time to play while being a more enjoyable and well-paced experience. I wanted this game to be fun and a great way to play SH2, but sadly, it's just a very lifeless remake, although it's a very pretty one, and some of the new music is amazing. Just a shame for the very basic gameplay loop and the poor pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: A well-written psychological horror that holds plenty of suspense--not just for its ambiance--but also for its characters and respective narrative. All characters have their own individual response to unregulated feelings surfaced by unresolved trauma and are confronted with them in real-form. The protagonist is written in a way that evokes uncertainty and conflict in what surrounds his motivations; a feeling that is supported by the viewer witnessing a person who seems aloof and not exactly in his right mind--often not even sure of what he wants. I do not think that the narrative would have been nearly as impact-full if it didn't take place in a horror setting. Both James and the us share this vulnerability in giving a permissible means to peer into his psyche and can find various physical manifestations by which a feeling resides. In spite of the stuttering issues (which hopefully can either be mitigated or fully resolved through some performance patches) it is a great game with a thought-provoking story.

_childDocuments_.review: Depression is back yet again.I cannot even express how happy I am with this remake and I hope Konami realize that there is still a lot of people that love and wants Silent hill games to come back to life and with enough time and budget it can be a successful title. So far in my 8 hours of playing I am enjoying every second of it just in general exploring , the story , the graphics, stunning monsters and the game continue to keep me on edge from time to time. I hope that after this beauty we will receive new silent hill games or perhaps another remasters / remakes of the old ones. _childDocuments_.review: Teaming up with the Bloober team, Konami pulled off a delightful surprise with the Silent Hill 2 remake, catching me off guard in the best possible way.On the whole, Silent Hill 2 captivated me with its stunning visuals. The enveloping fog and the ominous darkness of the other world are instrumental in crafting an immersive and chilling atmosphere. The game's dark aesthetics add depth to its compelling narrative, which is further enriched by a stellar voice cast and Akira Yamoaka's haunting score that accompanies every scene. The acting was phenomenal from the stars, and the character models are almost pinpoint accurate from the original character models. I loved James' redesign better than the originals. Maria is just as attractive in her new skin, even though I wish they could've made her attire a bit skimpy as it's James' fantasy. Angela had the most controversy due to her character's portrayal, but it didn't bother me. There's even a mod to slim her face down, showing the community's dedication to the game.It's a bit disheartening that Silent Hill 2 had to adopt the over-the-shoulder perspective, a common feature in modern horror titles, instead of the dynamic camera angle, a unique aspect of the original. Bloober could have truly excelled if Konami hadn't played it safe.The combat has been modernized to fit over the shoulder, and it works well, especially with melee. The dodging is smooth, and the combat is refined, so the player has to strategically watch the monster's patterns before battering up. I do wish Bloober would have given us more melee options, excluding unique melee weapons like the Chainsaw and Great Knife, which are powerful but limited in use, giving players more options. One thing Konami did right compared to Capcom's modern Resident Evil titles (excluding Resident Evil 1 Remake, which was perfect) was not cutting content. "Hear that, Capcom?" Konami and Bloober's team did NOT CUT any content remaking Silent Hill 2; instead, they expanded the areas, making the game longer than the original.For those who have yet to play Silent Hill and would love to delve into the series, this game is a great start, even though it's not the first. The game is worth your time due to the replayability and rewards you earn for completing the game such as fun head skins for James and filters to add a fun way to play each run. I'm excited to see what Bloober and Konami have for future remake installments. A definite 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I dive into praising the remake I will let the cat out of the bag first. Performance is extremely questionable, on 1440p with RTX 4090 and Ryzen 7 7800X3D and maxed out details with raytracing and DLSS set on Quality, I'm hitting 90fps on average, 120 if I'm lucky. Stutters and traversal microstutters are very heavily present, there's no option for frame generation either, cutscenes or at least the cutscene character animations are capped to 30 fps, making transitions from cutscene to gameplay extremely jarring (a uncapped fps mod update came out with the game's official release and this is now fixed). While I applaud Bloomer for making this gorgeous looking UE5 game 34GB, I just can't overlook its technical issues. Digital soundtrack having only 10 tracks and not featuring classics like Theme of Laura and Angel's Thanatos is extreme crime, even the original 2001 album on streaming services has 30 tracks, so I don't understand the decision why is this short soundtrack a part of deluxe edition.  Being done with the rant for now, I must applaud them for the work on the remake. It is very clear how much they love and respect the original source material, from simple nods and references to nearly identical recreations, this remake is overflowing with passion. Bloober should be proud of themselves for this faithful recreation of a beloved classic. While it does not replace the original, it is just as good and can stand alongside it on the pedestal. Atmosphere is unmatched and sound design simply impeccable, followed by amazing motion and voice performance by the actors. Some cutscenes might feel overly cinematic with the head shots, instead of focusing more on the camerawork. Soundtrack while fantastic has less of a presence than the original, thanks to much more dynamic soundscapes of the town and cinematic scenes, but you are guaranteed to recognize the iconic tunes when they play. Having finished the game with 100% completion, It is very safe to say Bloober absolutely nailed the impossible and achieved something that I hope is only a beginning for more exciting things to come. If Silent Hill 1 Remake is next on the list, I will be there to fully support it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry to be a lone voice in not appreciating this one, but seeing what Capcom have done with their RE re-makes I think Bloober missed a chance here. There are some changes from the original of course, but by and large this is pure 2001 game design. I hope you enjoy searching near identical rooms for keys and other trinkets, as you'll be doing a lot of that.On a technical level this is VERY Unreal Engine 5. The lighting is fine I guess, it's typical UE5 with plenty of super low res ray tracing jittering and some light bleed. But it works okay enough. The world geometry is fine too, it gets the job done but there's nothing here to really blow your GPU up. Characters however are almost universally poor, they're just poorly modelled and the facial animation is super basic. I know Bloober isn't a huge team, but this falls way short of Capcom's RE games.Then there is the stuttering, so much stuttering. It never goes away for more than a few seconds, it's relentless, and this is n a 4090. The base frame rate is okay enough (with frame gen), but frame delivery is so unstable it rarely looks smooth. So again, all very Unreal engine.  To add insult to injury the game has an elevated black floor which can't be fixed in the settings, so if you're on an OLED, you're out of luck.This isn't a bad effort, and if you love the original and can overlook the usual Unreal Engine problems you'll probably have a good time. But for me it fell short.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is my favorite game and Silent Hill is my favorite horror franchise. I had given up hope after Konami had gutted their games division and turned Silent Hill and Metal Gear into pachinko machines. When they first announced the new projects, including the remake headed by Bloober Team, I had a very negative outlook. Instead of letting my beloved franchise stay dead, Konami was going to desecrate its corpse to milk every penny. Even so, I still had to play the remake. It's my favorite game, so even if the remake was bad, I still had to play it. After finishing my first play-through, I owe Bloober a huge apology for ever doubting them. They did such a good job with everything, I am completely over the moon. They brought Silent Hill into the present day with phenomenal graphics and sound design without compromising anything that made the original great. Bloober took care to preserve the art design of the original while adding incredible detail to the environments, making Silent Hill look the best it ever has. They've basically doubled the content of the original game, but it doesn't feel padded at all. Everything flows naturally and all of their additions fit into the story while also expanding it. I had fears about cut content, but Bloober managed to stay true to the original game and remixed things in a way that it still felt fresh to me. They also added a bunch of Easter eggs and fun references to the series. The voice acting and cinematics are also phenomenal and carry a lot of emotional weight. The combat is simple, but it feels satisfying and effectively made me feel like I was fighting for my life. Other than some minor nitpicks and performance issues (mostly thanks to UE5), I don't have anything but praise for this game.The original game is still a masterpiece in my eyes. Some aspects of the the original were a product of the time and are lightning in a bottle that can't be replicated. Even so, I think this remake is also a masterpiece. It's the best Silent Hill game in the past 20 years and it's my favorite survival horror game in recent memory. For me, it's better than RE2 Remake and is up there with REmake as the best remake of all time. My gut reaction is to want Bloober to remake the other games; but my gut isn't right in this situation. I hope Bloober works with Konami to make a brand new Silent Hill. Even if they don't work on Silent Hill again, the love and care that Bloober put into this remake gives me faith that they could make a truly amazing original game of their own, better than anything they've made before. Hats off to the devs, don't believe any of the hate! You made me happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake is a masterful reimagining of a survival horror classic, delivering an unforgettable experience that will satisfy both veterans and newcomers alike.From the moment you step into the fog-laden streets of Silent Hill, the atmosphere is utterly haunting. The improved visuals are jaw-dropping; the detailed environments, lighting effects, and character models truly bring the town to life in a way that the original could only hint at. The sense of dread is palpable, with every shadow and eerie noise pulling you deeper into the unsettling mystery. The updated sound design is a triumph—whether it's the creaking of a distant door or Akira Yamaoka's chilling score, the audio keeps you on edge at all times.The gameplay has seen significant improvements while still staying true to its roots. The overhauled combat system feels smoother, with more fluid movement and better camera controls, making exploration and encounters with Silent Hill's grotesque creatures much more immersive. Puzzles retain their signature psychological twist, challenging your mind without being frustrating. The developers have done a fantastic job balancing modern mechanics with the tense, deliberate pacing that defines survival horror.The narrative remains as gripping as ever, with James Sunderland's tragic journey through Silent Hill brought to life with enhanced voice acting and motion capture that elevates the emotional weight of the story. The themes of guilt, loss, and redemption hit harder with these performances, making the game's harrowing moments even more impactful.There are very few flaws here. Some fans might find the changes in pacing or the modernized controls a departure from the original's charm, but I believe these updates enhance the overall experience without sacrificing the core identity of the game. The only minor critique I have is that some areas feel slightly more linear compared to the original, but it doesn't detract from the overall immersion.**Verdict: 9.5/10**  Silent Hill 2 Remake is an essential experience for any horror fan. It retains the psychological depth of the original while offering a fresh, polished experience that proves the power of great storytelling in gaming. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Having seen the final gameplay trailer, I went into this with cautious optimism. Silent Hill 2 is a game I replayed multiple times and one that has always managed to completely engulf me with its athmosphere. But there were always certain aspects of it (combat and bosses) which were annoying and thus distracting from that experience. My hope for the remake was that it will keep the athmosphere and emotional hits, while improving the dated aspects of original.After finishing, I can say that it most certainly has. It is very hard for me to find faults with the remake. The only two things I can possibly think of as flaws are stutters when loading new area, and the hospital which in its length became tiring. Other than that, the game is just as athmospheric and absorbing as the original, and now also delivers more tense moments - on the hard difficulty it is just challenging enough without being frustrating, which was another issue with the original - by the end of my original playthroughs I was always swimming in ammo and healing even on hard. We were also rewarded with some new beautiful Akira Yamaoka tracks and ambience, which are just as impactful as the original's soundtrack was when I first played it. James's VA did a phenomenal job and how well this portrayal of James ended up being was one of the most positively surprising things for me. Maria is also way more of a likeable character and I loved her interactions with James. Laura was another positive stand-out. Angela and Eddy were also solid.Fantastic way to experience Silent Hill all fresh, thank you Bloober for the chance to feel lost alone and sad in this foggy town again.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 (2001) will always be praised for being, objectively, one of the best video games ever made. Two years ago, we were given the somewhat controversial news that Bloober Team (creators of Layers of Fear, The Medium, and Blair Witch) were given the impossible task of remaking this classic with the same coat of paint as the Resident Evil and Dead Space remakes. I was honestly never doubtful of this project and thought all the trailers leading up to its release looked great, and I'm happy to report they exceeded my expectations!This is an incredibly faithful remake, or rather, re-imagining that literally copies some cutscenes one-for-one and adds a few extra story beats. It doesn't completely overshadow the original, but it's such an obvious love letter that was handled with extreme care. Each of the six main characters were well written and performed extraordinarily well. It feels like they studied the source material, but were still able to create their own version of each character that still fell in line with the original.Every area you know and love still remain but are completely fleshed out. Even the town of Silent Hill has more spots to explore in the opening hours of the game and sets the tone for the type of puzzles you'll be dealing with throughout your journey. The town feels very 'lived in' and the fog is just as intimidating. Each enemy type is still here and even some new ones show up every now and then. The boss fights feel MUCH better, when compared to how cumbersome they were in the original.With all of this praise comes some small gripes - while I do LOVE each area and puzzle has been extended, Silent Hill 2 Remake comes with some pacing issues that I really couldn't look past. When the story beats are few and far between, you'll be traversing an area for about 2 hours with absolutely zero dialogue or cutscene that adds to James' story. It's really not terrible and might be more of a preference thing, especially considering the nature of this games story and underlying meaning. Speaking of story, I also think maybe one or two story elements weren't quite handled the way I would have wanted, specifically one of the final scenes in the game. Again, it's really a preference thing after years of watching retrospective videos on why some cutscenes were directed the way they were, so it's a bit sad to not see them handled the same way here.I played this game pretty slowly and clocked 18 hours in my play through. With two additional endings and a new game plus, I can absolutely see myself playing this for years to come.Silent Hill 2 (2024) is a very faithful and modernized re-imagining of a beloved PS2 title. I think Bloober Team took its critical response to heart and spent some much needed time polishing something they probably could have released a few months after the first trailer. Combat and boss fights have been completely transformed and are much more engaging. I do feel like parts of this game were padded out a bit too much so it would have been nice if a few of them had been a bit more streamlined, but this was such a fun experience and an almost must play for fans of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully done remake. Graphics are incredible, performances are stellar, atmosphere is sublime, ambiance and score are legendary, and gameplay is perfectly awkward & befitting of James' predicament. Areas have been massively improved since the original in terms of emphasis for exploration, well designed horror/scares, and balance between quality-of-life improvements, new gameplay elements, and respect for the preexisting lore and design. New endings are awesome too, and completing NG+ with the chainsaw was absolute joy. My favorite areas & moments definitely include the heart-wrenching havoc of Brookhaven Hospital, the trepidatious trek through South Vale's Otherworld, and of course the lamenting and laborious lengths of the abyssal Labyrinth. Overall, excellently done. I can't wait to see if Bloober Team get the chance to remake other additions in the Silent Hill franchise, and if so, I'm definitely gonna preorder!

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll start by saying this is a good game and largely respectful of the source material. However I'm giving it a thumbs down for the following reasons:- Lots of stuttering, typical for UE5 but this game is worse (think the worst case scenario from Dragon's Dogma 2 when you were in the city, but consistently throughout the game)- In many areas I'm not cracking 60fps, while my hardware is a 4090 gpu with an i4900k- There's no health meter but rather a red border as you start to lose health that gets increasingly distracting (I feel like this could've been done better, but it's a style point)I probably would've given this a positive review, but some questionable design decisions are what's keeping me from doing so, for example:- Angela is SOOOO ugly, her chin is horrifically square and isn't faithful to the source material. It's such a weird face that it's actually distracting with scenes that contain her. Why not just be faithful and have a higher jawline? The "modern audience" that wants uglier women doesn't exist and they're just eye sores and distracting- The uglification of the women is even more odd, because the main protagonist arguably got better looking. So just why?- The Company hired "Hit Detection" or whatever the DEI consulting company was to help them on this (a less virulent version of Sweet Baby). God knows why they needed a DEI consultant on this game, and perhaps it explains the inexplicable design decisions wrt AngelaHad they hired Sweet Baby I'd not have spent the $80 buying the pre-order deluxe edition as that any game that associates with that stain on the industry will never get my cash.Overall I do feel like this game is worth the money. it's got great graphics, atmosphere that's faithful to the original and better than any recent Resident Evil, and way better than Alan Wake 2 which is the same genre.  So if you're a fan of the genre or want a top tier horror game this month, then this is the best AAA title on the market right now IMO.Thumbs down in protest to hiring a DEI consultant, the design of Angela and the performance.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: Blames Blunderland 2-2: The Returnening.Silent Hill 2 is a 3rd-person survival horror following the classic gaming tropes the genre is known for. Silent Hill was the 2nd biggest pioneer of Survival Horror with Resident Evil being the 1st. You navigate mazes, shoot monsters, collect supplies and solve puzzles. The bread and butter of the genre.It's probably one of the most well-known story in the gaming zeitgeist, but I'll still sum it up for good measure. You play as James Sunderland, a broken man searching for his wife Mary in the town of Silent Hill. James' wife died 3 years prior to the events of the game, however, he receives a letter from Mary beckoning him to meet up in their "special place". Knowing that their "last vacation" spot was in Toluca Lake, James enters this foggy and seemingly abandoned town, searching for answers... Silent Hill was a town dominated by a cult who worshiped demons and devils. A certain event that happened before Silent Hill 1 made the town collapse on itself and was largely abandoned by its residents. It is not a good place to be wandering around alone...On the graphic side, it is a well-produced experience. The town of Silent Hill never looked better. They worked really hard to recreate South Vale. There's a lot of abandoned objects and clutter. Everywhere you go, you can see they looked back twice and added further polish. The character models look really good, both for humans and monsters. The human faces aren't as god-tier as Death Stranding, but it holds up.In the sound department, Akira Yamaoka came back in the fold and remixed some of the old SH2 songs, as well as adding new ones. The OG SH2 soundtrack is basically legendary, so it was crucial to have him back in the remake. The voice actors are great and don't stray too far from the original's emotional scope. Yes, they've taken  liberties at certain parts, but it's still within the given context. The sound effects and ambient sounds are top tier, it's a crime not to play this with headphones.To kick things off, I'll talk about things I didn't like that much.If there's any harsh criticism I'd have for this remake, it would be what they did with the Otherside. In the OG version, the transition to the Otherside was really subtle, except for the hospital. Also, the OG version of the Otherside wasn't a hellish rusty bloody metal landscape. It was mostly just "over-decayed" liminal spaces. In the remake, they took the "mainstream" Otherside of SH1, Homecoming and the 1st movie, and plastered it in places where there wasn't really an Otherside in the original. A quick example would be the Appartment complex, the first "main dungeon". Woodside part is normal, Blue Creek is Otherside. However, the OG version wasn't all that, Blue Creek felt like it was just a very decayed and condemned part of the appartment complex. The original SH2 was a moody, sleepy, dreamy and ghostly experience. The remake has taken the same route as the recent Resident Evil remakes, focusing a little more on cinematic action. The transition from fixed camera angles to forced over-the-shoulder camera further drives in that point. The remake is a lot less "psychological horror" and lot a more "survival action horror" so to speak.You had more freedom of exploration before. Not just outside in the street but on the insides as well. A lot of streets now have sinkholes which block paths that were once open. Main "dungeons" like Appartment or Hospital now have 500% more locked doors. After playing the game a couple of times, these changes become apparent. Still open-ended to some extent, but more linear than the original.To drift back into a positive vibe...They did not butcher the story. It is an extremely faithful retelling of the original. As a matter of fact, they added a little more cutscenes that wasn't there before. I was expecting some things to be removed but they've delivered on this front. The same can be said about the areas you visit. Despite being a little more linear, all areas from the original return and some of these got expanded a little more. I'm actually impressed by that.In the original, the combat was slow, janky and goofy. The combat in the remake is a lot harder, so much so that we now have a Dodge button... Enemies are numerous and aggressive. Unlike the original, getting ganked in the remake can mean a quick death if you don't react accordingly. You don't have an aiming lockon here, so you better make each shot count as you will find a lot less ammo than the original. Also, you can't "pause" the game to recover health, you have to chug your Estus live during combat.I liked how the remake remixed the entire game and made it longer and confusing than the original. They removed some of the old paths as well as a bunch of old puzzles, but added new ones instead. They've been able to shove my expectations aside and keep me surprised while still being faithful to the original's main path.All in all, this remake is a great way to come back from the dead. Perhaps a little too "mainstreamified" for my nostalgia goggles. We've been running on fumes for too long, and finally we got something substantial that I think all fans can like in some way or another, while also disliking it for what's missing from the original or its altered gameplay hoops. It's a great link to the past and it gives me hope for this forsaken franchise that has been stagnating for more than a decade.Technical stuff: Use -dx11 launch command for better performance.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is one of those games you can't really escape the hype from. There is a good reason people remember it so fondly and still talk about it 20 years later after it's release on the PS2. It's a damn good game. The remake is a faithful retelling of the story with changes to gameplay and moving some of the puzzles around while taking out others. That said, it's still very much able to stand next to the titan that was the original game. My only gripes of this game was the melee combat. It felt extremely floaty to use and the soft camera lock proved difficult to use it sometimes in tight hallways. However, the enemies you first go up against aren't that terrible to fight and when you get to the point where you start coming across enemies that would be a threat to you with melee, the game has already given you enough ammo to use. My other gripe is the performance. This is your classic UE5 traversal stutter game where you can be running a smooth 100 FPS and then drop down to 20 because you entered a new area or your shaders crapped the bed. Not to mention for whatever reason in the patch I played on (1.0.4) there are two very specific mirrors that TANK your framerate. For whatever reason when I looked at them I would go down to single digit FPS and could barely play the game. Forcing the game into DX11 fixed that issue but made the overall game worse to look at. Classic UE5, eh?
