_childDocuments_.review: Game bugs out when ghost step activates. I can use the inspect and inventory buttons but can't move or open main menu etc. This has happened so many times that I have been completely put off playing.Edit: Not just ghost step, there are a number of triggers that disable movement and can only be resolved with a force close, resulting in the loss of a run. This becomes more and more common as the game progresses and things such as killing enemies with burn are introduced, I currently cannot pass the final stage due to this game-breaking bug.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: really fun modern feeling roguelike, starts off a bit slow but once you unlock the meta progression systems it gets really fun. I think that the first stage is kind of a barrier to new players and that the chip system should be unlocked earlier otherwise the first stage might funnel players out of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: The Land Beneath Us is a turned based roguelite where you control the game's pace. It seems simple at the beginning but quickly ramps up and forces you to recognize your enemies and their patterns. While there's a story and some mystery around it, I wasn't captivated, the writing is not to my taste and I did find myself skipping a lot of the dialogue. The music is also pretty good in specific instances and atmospheric most of the time. Overall it's a solid roguelite with a cool concept and some defined progression with zones to beat increasing in difficulty by introducing new gameplay mechanics. I don't know about replayability yet as I haven't beaten the main story, but it seems to be oriented around increasing the challenge level of a zone and beating it multiple times. I love that the meta progression is challenged based for unlocking new skills and weapons, it keeps the game interesting and worth exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! Reminds me of into the breach with the puzzle like combat. There's a lot of depth with this game and the roguelike elements are well implemented in both the gameplay and the story. Looking at videos I knew id find the game fun, but damn im surprised by how into the story im getting. Well done devs
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: - While not having many system like other Rougelike like FTL, this one make up for it with sheer number of random drop pool.- There are only 2 types of drops, the weapon and the relic. At first it's repetitive with you getting same item almost every run. However, once you get to level 4 the random pool for each of them starting to get big and it's a lot harder for you to get the item you want, hence, making it more vary between run to run.- Item unlock in later level also has various extra ability in them, making it more convincing to get the one that synergize with each other. This make you rely even more on RNG, which is good in Rougelike game.- The map itself seems to be random but it doesn't affect much as your run relies heavily on drops.- Play at your own pace, go slow plan out your skill or rush turn smack things with weapon.- Enemies in later level will have huge attack range, and spawn a lot. Being turn base doesn't make the game 'easier' as you might think. Some planning is required.- You also have ability to teleport but you have to use it wisely, So more planning is required.- Generally, you don't have to learn/memorize the enemy attack pattern (like in Crypt of Necrodancer, for example). You can play it by ear and react to what being thrown at you, it's turn based, you have lots of time.- I mean.... it's a Rougelike, you come here for the gameplay. So... anything will do- There's no issue with both of them other than you might want to keep the master volume at the default 50, as this game is LOUD,- Think of it as a skill. To activate it you have to move in series direction specify by the chip.- While it's an interesting concept, this kind of "hit arrow following the pattern" is more suitable in something fast pace with limited time for decision, like in rhythm game.- You also don't need to hit the direction consecutively either. You can hit 3 out of 4 and hit other direction that's not the 4th one and the "combo" will still be alive. You can hit other direction for some turns and then hit the last 4th one, finishing the combo, and the skill still activate. Which honestly, defeat the purpose of it being presented like a "combo".- Yes, it start boring. As I keep mentioning, the first 3 level is kinda boring. I almost stop playing because of this. Mainly it's too easy and don't making you "rage quit enough", which Roguelike typically should does. This is due to.... (next point)- Your random drop pool is still small leading to you getting same item every run. The item itself also not having anything special isn't helping either.- The enemy also weak with small attack range and there are only few of them.- I feel like this "baby level" should be shorter.- So... I suggest, just try to make yourself get through this first 3 levels. Give the game a chance, it will be better once you hit level 4.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Great alternative take on traditional roguelikes. Tweakable difficulty (think the heat system in Hades) for runs after the first clear. _childDocuments_.review: At the easier levels, you can do whatever and still win.Once you turn up the difficulty by adding in the modifiers, you'll need to have at least some idea of what you are doing.Combat feels nice.If I could change something, it would be the option to disable some weapons after unlocking them, maybe a toggle to turn off certain achievements. _childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I played a ton of demos during Steams Next Fest. This was my favorite game I found. This one is really special and its a great price. It's a turn-based roguelike such as Into the Breach and Crypt of the NecroDancer.The kit customization is really interesting. Here's an example of a kit I enjoyed: Enhanced Break Limit (When under 40% health, +15 dps +40% crit chance) + Stacking Edge (+10% crit dps per crit hit per room). Once I was riding the edge of life and death, I was cranking out massive damage and I felt POWERFUL.It's good. Play the demo. Once you beat the first boss, it unlocks a ton of customization and extra mechanics.EDIT: 10 hours of gameplay later, I'm SUPER into this game. Very challenging, very satisfying, very relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a unique twist on roguelite turn-based action, bringing in mechanics where you move at the same time as your enemies, but with multitude of weapons to play around with for hours. The graphics, while first looking pixelated, is extremely smooth and nice to the eye and is basically a full sprite high-res with some filter over it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I reached to the 4th boss and played many hours during the demo.In my opinion, this game is a hidden gem with intriguing gameplay in many aspects. It combines turn-based strategy with roguelike elements, featuring a core mechanic that innovatively improves tile-based movement and simplifies the complexity of the turn-based genre. What makes this game particularly interesting is that it's turn-based strategy, but players can control the pacing, which fixes the pain points of turn-based where sometimes we don't want to spend time thinking but rather waiting for the game to resolve its processes. This feature prevents boredom or wasting time during waiting periods.Then, the weapon system, integrated into each cardinal direction within the tile-based movement, creates gameplay that relies on positioning for both attacking and escaping simultaneously. This also fosters a variety of strategies, such as synergies when working with relics, or using weapons in one direction to move enemies towards another direction to set up combos. After unlocked the chip and teleport systems, these are the game changer that's make player have so many option to play. Whether in safe way to kept teleport as a great escape or play higher risk by using teleport warp to get closer with target enemy then all in with everything to maximize damage. Furthermore, the chip system itself relies on direction pattern that progress when player move along the target direction to increase the depth of gameplay and enabling even more diverse combos.Pixel art style and its combination with 3D scenes and VFX with pseudo pixel art but It looks good and unique at the same time. However, some of the animations are too rough, slight low frame and details that could be improved.The story and world setting are interesting and too many reference and gimmick that refer from movie and etc, that's make it look interesting and fun to read. About the story and characters part which facing conflicts that keep us engaged. Character emotions are portrayed vividly, but it seems there's a slight lack in the pacing and narrative tools, which hinders the storytelling from reaching its full potential. It would greatly enhance the experience if more emphasis were placed on this aspect.This game is worthy to play that will give you the fresh and new experience for the turn-base strategy & roguelike. Especially, It very incredibly addictive and surprisingly fun. For those who have played turn-based strategy games and feel bored, I would recommend giving this game a try. It offers a unique experience that sometimes feels like an action game and guarantees that it will not disappoint you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda addictive. I like how the game just boils down the complex mechanic into just 4 button and that's a lot of fun.Even though the game stated as its turn-based the game doesn't make you feel like it's slow at all. Fast-paced as if it was an action game. The weapon combination is unique that you'll have to think about where to put it and how to position yourself.The enemies design and level design are incredible that they gave me a tense sometimes.Highly recommended if you are rogue-lite fan!
_childDocuments_.name: The Land Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game. Try out the demo and see if it appeals to you. If so, the game is that, just more of it. So for this review, I'll just focus on the negatives.1) The controls are awkward. I don't know why it's "U" to pass and not, say, spacebar. You can rebind them, it's just a weird set of defaults. Also, no real mouse support. It's pretty much all keyboard controls. 2) You also don't appear to be able to save a run in the middle of one, and if you quit out you lose your progress for that run. Might have been great if I had been given a warning when I had to do something while I had a run going.3) Enemy AI is very basic. It's possible to leave an enemy to walk in circles on the other side of the map while you just heal yourself to full over and over using a chip command.4) The writing is terrible. It tries to be funny and fails miserably. I'm just skipping the story at this point. Having a computer constantly go "UWU" at you is not my style of humor.Even with these issues, it's still good. Art is fun, enemy design is solid. Expect 20-50 minutes per run. Lots of different strategies, lots of playstyles.(EDIT: now that I'm about 10 hours in.. it gets a little unbalanced near the end of the game. You feel overpowered due to the metaprogression like having a chip that heals you to full every time you use it, but one mistake and you get stunlocked into instant death. I've had 2 runs now end because I got hit a single time and fully stun-locked into losing my entire health bar, triggering the relic to revive me to full, and losing my full health bar again without having an action. Pretty feelsbad.)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm not rogue-like and turn-based gamer, but it TOTALLY FUN!This game make me start interest Rogue-like and Turn-based againGameplay very simple, Easy to play but still hard to master.At 2nd hours I felt game content struggling but after I played for 4 hrs It still have a lot more content need to unlock that's worth to play!It's really fun to keep playing!

name: Mr. Run and Jump
detailed_description: In this electric 2D platformer, help Mr. Run and Jump defeat the terrifying Void and collect all the Power Gems from the Realms of Color! Joined by his trusty pal Leap the Dog, the duo must venture through a dazzling and dangerous world, dodging countless enemies and conquering hundreds of fierce platforming challenges to save the day! Mr. Run and Jump draws you in with precise level design, free-flowing gameplay, and formidable challenge. Silky controls encourage players to run, jump, dash, double jump, and roll to clear levels with style, making it a speedrunner’s dream. Collectibles hidden in tough-to-reach spots demand players use their wits as well as their dexterity. Dynamic Assistance options allow players to set the level of difficulty they want. No matter how you play, Mr. Run and Jump offers engaging gameplay options to players of varying skill levels and approaches. Key Features Precision Platforming: Bound over obstacles, dodge deadly enemies, and collect all the power gems before it’s too late! Realms of Color: Each world has its own distinct style, with a beautifully illustrated visual aesthetic bursting with vibrant neon graphics. A Dangerous World: A wide variety of treacherous enemies, each with their own patterns and personality. Hours of Entertainment: Challenging levels, collectible orbs, and Time Trials offer 30+ hours of gameplay. Save your Dog, Save the World: Experience an original story of a transformed world, a devouring Void, and all the wonders of the Realms of Color.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that it's so expensive, because the game is really quite good. It has tight controls, a lovely retro aesthetic and packs a real challenge towards the end of the game. If you're looking for a polished platformer that does everything well, this is definitely worth it on sale.Check out  for more recommendations!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very tight precision platformer, the design is top notch and it feels great to play all the time. It's just relatively short, especially for its price, but there's the whole time attack mode that I haven't touched a lot that can make the game last even longer -- you'll probably be done 100% of the game (minus time attack) in around 10 hours. More or less depending on your skill.The game does a really great job of introducing new mechanics and stuff to avoid every level and fully using them so you get comfortable later on if you get the same obstacles. The levels are really well designed.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: So much to love here. It's all my retro-nostalgia desires stuffed in one package then jolted with a bucket of rainbow-neon-flavor. Much respect for the Ms option on the character name too. Not overlooked. Getting into the game, its straight forward running and jumping at the start. What makes it addictive is that I'm finding a puzzle aspect to a lot of it. You can't just Mario-your-way through the later stages and obstacles or you will die. A lot. Instead, you have to think about what - jumping, leaping, diving, bouncing, wall-jumping - combo will get the job done. Otherwise you will be doomed to death and the loop that follows. Achievements in the game are fun and easy to snag for the most part. Love the time mode too, though I wish there was some online component so I can see how I stack against the rest of the world. The story is super light, so that won't get in your way of blitzing through each stage on your way to the finale. Overall, loving my time with the game and wanted to support the developers with a quick review. I hope it continues to deliver as I play more!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Great precision platformer with smooth movement, feels very polished. I would say the whole game is really fun to play through, even the Dark Realm since it provided some new platforming challenges. I feel satisfied after 100%.With there only being a jump and an 'action' button, the simple controls are a blessing and a curse. It leads to occasional wrong jumps or dashes that can make you rage, yet allows you to glide though stages if you're up to it. Definitely the hardest thing to do is getting platinum time trial orbs on all the levels. Some of them will make you want to punch a hole in your screen. A couple of the platinums took me over 3 hours to achieve. Each Realm has usually one level that's really hard to get the platforming right for the platinum (especially 2-1 and 6-3), but then the other levels are more generous on the timing in case you mess up a bit.Hope more people find this game and play it. Would love to see more of Mr. Run and Jump in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: "Mr. Run and Jump" is yet another of literally thousands of console ported 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.This one has particularly bad graphics and is part of a slew of questionable business moves from Atari by dumping ancient re-hashed home video console games from the 1980's onto Steam as nasty, ridiculously overpriced cash grabs, and this is no exception (although this game was never actually published on the 2600... it's still 2600 tier gaming at its worst). Like all platformers this is just running and jumping... the concept predates Metroidvania and other more "interesting" platformers, it's shallow even by platformer standards, and 2D platformers themselves are an old, thankfully dying, obsolete genre.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The game features extremely lazy, minimalist "art", of the type you normally expect to see in low effort Flash/browser games and mobile apps.  Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game, having the graphics phoned in like this isn't going to result in a high quality, visually impressive game that PC gamers are used to seeing.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 14 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected."Mr. Run and Jump" has the preposterous price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Grand Theft Auto V", "7 Days to Die" or "Stellaris".  Or if you like platformers, Hollow Knight.  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.The $25 price tag for this shallow garbage is almost a deliberate insult to PC gamers.  When I saw the price I thought there was some defect or some kind of joke going on, but apparently Atari are dead serious, they want $25 for pure garbage.  Even Russian asset flip money laundering scams offer more than this junk does.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were not forced to collect most of all the blue coin orbs then this game would be way too easy. 8/10 Game play7/10 Visuals2/10 100% Completion Last Level of dark world felt easier than red world void.I'm giving this a no recommendation to anyone who is new to platforms as this game expects you to know everything once your halfway through world 2. _childDocuments_.review: This game rules. Tough precision platforming with lots of close shaves. Individual sections are often very difficult the first time you encounter them but become learnable as you repeat them for time trials. The movement in this game is really smooth with some well-tuned Mario-style abilities. High jumps, speedy long jumps, double jumps, air-dashes. There's something about the long jump > air dash > double jump > air dash combo that really feels like Mario Odyssey to me.I really dug this game! I recommend it for folks who are in to this type of difficult platformer. Gathered 100% orbs in a little over 20h.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pure platforming *BLISS* - imagine fusing the 2D precision gameplay of Celeste with 3D Mario's moveset, and this is pretty much what you'd get. It's not perfect, but any flaws I could mention are minor, and I could count them on one hand. Short of a full-game speedrun timer (Which I'm surprised isn't present, given the type of game this is - maybe one could be added in an update?), the only thing that could possibly make this game better is mod support for custom levels / gimmicks, and honestly that's wishful thinking. Point is, this game is an absolute *MUST-PLAY* if you're a platformer fan - what are you waiting for?! Go buy it already! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style, and possibly my favorite intro to a platformer ever! I completed all of Violet and the Void level, I really enjoyed the rush there and it would take me a while to get all the collectibles while being pushed through the level. The player assistance was very helpful as well, and it blacks out the collectibles so no cheating!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic platformer that has a very appealing style. I love the retro/neon feel, the soundtrack and FX, and the game itself. Very fun with an 'old-school yet modern' kind of feel to it. Another win for Atari, who seem to be on a roll lately cranking out a bunch of new classic titles.There's just one thing to be aware of.. the difficulty level is -sky-high- (!!) I mean, I am an experienced platform game veteran since as far back as the 80's and I was still dying constantly, even on the early stages. The game gives you infinite lives and for good reason, because you will be dying a LOT. 'Mr. Run, Jump and Die' would have perhaps been a more fitting title (!)Seriously, it gets real challenging real fast and will definitely put your platforming skills to the test. It almost feels like it was designed for experienced gamers and expects you to have a certain level of skill. But it is a lot of fun and definitely something I will keep coming back to play. Another smash hit for Atari!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: This game was almost a 10/10 for me. I would have been willing to overlook the shard collecting but then I got to Dark World and well that's when it goes steeply downhill. Up to Dark World, I collected every Challenge Orb, Shard Orb, and Time Trial Orb, not completely a terrible task but it is a bit pain-staking at times. The Void Levels and the Time Trials were probably the most fun because that's how the game feels like it was meant to be played; GO FAST! Not as a collect-a-thon... -_-The Good:Great Neon Aesthetics! Great Music! Smooth controls! Really fun platforming and level design (prior to Dark World). The Challenge Orbs were challenging but felt doable. The game itself feels like it would be a very fun any% speedrun for sure! Definitely worth playing if you like the genre! Without Dark World, the game is a pretty solid 9 or 10/10 game for me!The Ehh:The Shards. The amount you had to collect in each level ranging anywhere from like 100 to OVER 400 is just too much especially when a good portion of them are out of the way to get. But again, I was willing to overlook this until Dark World happened. The Platinum times for Time Trial seem a bit too unreasonable, granted I didn't try to get more than a few platinum's, but even from just looking at some of the times required for a gold, seeing that you have to go even faster than that by probably a decent margin doesn't seem worth it the effort. Too bad there's an achievement locked behind getting platinum in every level. The Time Trial Leaderboard seems like it could be improved a bit. Doesn't even show you which time is yours or show your best time when you hover over a level. Only one save file??? I'm really tempted to speedrun this game but with one save file, having to delete all my progress to start up a new save isn't ideal. I mean I guess I can copy the save file, but that's a bit inconvenient and I'm also lazy lol. The Bad:Dark World...what were they thinking??? So let me say first, I did enjoy many of the screens in Dark World. However, a larger number of screens were frustrating due to tight choke points and just awful cycling of obstacles, which too often moved at lightning speed so I found myself just giving up and using the Super Star from assist mode which I had turned off until Dark-2. The very first Challenge Orb in Dark World-1, I counted had a 3-cycle pattern against an 11-cycle pattern... this is very bad. If I didn't manage to cheese it with 2 pixel perfect jumps then probably would never have gotten it. Most of the Challenge Orbs in Dark Work were still actually fun and reasonably challenging. I managed to get 7/12 of them. 3 more of them still seemed okay but at that point I had just given up and didn't feel like putting in the time to get them since the other 2 I was completely clueless on how to approach them. Plus I stopped trying to collect the shards after Dark-1 so there was really no point. Also the fact that Dark World-Void is locked behind 120 orbs is unfortunate. I think it would have been a better decision to have to collect all the orbs from the pre-Dark World levels to unlock Dark World then you just play through each Dark World level to unlock the next OR just nerf the hell out of Dark World.TLDR:Game feels great and is a lot of fun BUT...Shard collecting sucks. Wish they weren't in the game.Challenge orbs are mostly fine but unless you are getting EVERYTHING, then there really is no point.100% is a nightmare, don't recommend going for it.Platinum Times seem a bit unreasonable.Dark World is mostly absurd, which is a shame because it does have it's moments.Don't even peak at Dark World. PERIOD. Pretend it's not even in the game.Other than that, super fun platformer!  Overall, it's still really a fine game and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I would 100% recommend a play-through for sure! I feel like I got my money's worth but...maybe wait for a sale... XD
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Mr. Run and Jump is a pretty tough game, but super fun to play and is pretty simple. Run, jump, collect gems, get to the end portal and move on to the next world. It looks great and I love the music too! Some of the power-ups I couldn't quite get, but I'll come back to try again. I want to pet the dog!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Mr Run and Jump is exactly what it says. It's a very difficult parkour game that pulls no punches. Similar to Meatboy but less gruesome. It also has nice quality-of-life helps for when you are having difficulty with a particular section. This is well done, similar to the newer Mario games where it makes help available but doesn't force you to use it. Overall a great game from what I've played so far, probably one of the best of this kind of game that I've played. I have been playing it on the Steam Deck with very few issues, slowed down just a tiny bit on a couple sections but not so much it hurt the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: While I am personally not the biggest fan of Platformers (my skills have degraded as I've gotten older), Mr. Run and Jump seems like an interesting concept, especially for people who enjoy super-precise platforming gameplay. I need to give it a few more hours before I decide if I want to keep playing or not but I feel pretty comfortable recommending the game to someone who enjoys this type of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: A slick retro platformer with a beautiful neon graphics. It plays partially as a puzzler as you attempt to figure out what combination of your movement techniques will both allow progress and snag you those sweet sweet shards and orbs. The feel of classic platforming bleeds through with every jump, roll, and leap; especially when using a controller. I mean, you could use a keyboard but why? Regardless, the game delivers a variety of techniques and a collection of levels and challenge zones that will push your movement precision to the next level.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight! True to its name, there is a lot of running AND jumping. Truth in advertising seems to be a relic of the past, so it's nice to see the game's promise fulfilled.Shenanigans aside, I'm having a lot of fun with this so far, despite being pretty bad at it. I had to take a break while playing because my hands started to hurt! The game asks you to pull off some tricky maneuvers, but it's nothing unreasonable with a little practice. It has a great soundtrack that's catchy without being too repetitive or annoying. The visuals are fantastic and filled with neon awesomness. It reminds me of Pac-Man Championship Edition DX Super Turbo Alpha Hyper Fighting or whatever the hell the full name of that game is. It's like playing a neon sign and I love it.I'd say the best summary of this game would be that it's similar to Super Meat Boy, except this game doesn't hate you, your family, your friends, and all life on Earth. It's just a fun, reasonably challenging running and jumping game where you can wear a top hat, a bow, or go bare headed and everything is made of neon goodness. I can't wait to get carpal tunnel trying to complete the game and get as many of the achievements my skill level allows!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Does what it says on the box, that's for sure. You run and you jump, more running and jumping than you can shake a stick at. Now go fetch that stick as you chase your dog through crazy dangerous environs. The visuals are beautiful, but don't get too distracted staring at them, because when they say precision platformer, they mean it! You will die and you will die a lot from every wrong jump or step.Anyone who likes this type of game will enjoy this for sure. The controls are very responsive and smooth, the jumps, dashes, and double jumps are varied enough to keep you on your toes trying to figure out which move to use to weave through the traps. And it's plenty difficult for those that like that, honestly a bit too difficult for me at times, but there's nice optional features that help people like me out with checkpoints and invincibility stars, which is a really nice touch (don't worry, you purists can turn them off).
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: If you are dying for a platformer game because you have played them all of them then I would recommend this game; otherwise, I would suggest putting this on the wishlist. The challenge is there. I think one button is trying to do too much making controls a little odd at times. The graphics and theme is nice. I do not like how when restarting a level trying to collect all the shards that the previously collected shards at there.  I do see the care that was put into the game and it does have polish. This is a tough one to rate. I will just put a copypasta.I am a 45 year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Summer in 2023 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Mr. Run and Jump is a gorgeous looking game utilizing simplistic design and color choices to make a very challenging and rewarding puzzle precision based 2D Platformer. The music is catchy and matches the visuals nicely. If you're a fan of something like Super Meatboy or any other fast paced 2D platformer you'll be right at home here. I was a fan of the previous Graphite Lab release, Hive Jump, so I was more than willing to give this a chance. I'm definitely going to be picking up another copy on my Xbox Series S. Looks like Atari has a charming little winner here.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: If you like platformers and speed running, this game is a must have. The controls are immaculate with how fluid and precise they are. I have not once found myself blaming them for my downfalls. That's not to say this game is easy though. It is a very challenging title that I would liken to Celeste and Super Meat Boy, and wouldn't be surprised to see Mr. Run and Jump attain the popularity of those titles. Each world introduces new obstacle types to overcome that accumulate as you progress through the game. The levels are designed in a way where you can speed through them or take your time and pick up various collectibles and learn the layout. These can be used to unlock various things such as a final world or hats you can give to the main character. You can also choose to have "Mr. Run and Jump" be "Ms. Run and Jump", or drop the Mr/Ms entirely to be "Run and Jump"! While the gameplay is solid, the sound/music and neon aesthetic are another strength. Each world is split into four levels and has a color and theme. For example, the first four levels are part of the violet realm and features well-parallax'd hills and clouds while you traverse a meadow of flowers, covered in various shades of purple. The second world is composed of various shades of blue and features an industrial theme with crates, pipes and bolts. All the levels have been visually pleasing to play through and has an up-beat vibe. For those looking for a well-done story akin to Celeste, that's where this title might not live up to some player's expectations. There is a narrative that helps players understand a bit more to the games lore, but it's not a journey of self-discovery. This title places a focus on gameplay, sound, and visuals.If you're into challenging platformers or want a new title to speed run, I cannot recommend this game enough. Disclosure: I did technically receive this for free, but through winning a speed run contest that was held for their demo. I have no affiliation with anyone involved in creating this game. If you're interested in my contest entry, it can be found here:
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Man this really feels a bit nostalgic for good platformers. And with a name like "Mr. Run and Jump" you BETTER really nail the running and jumping mechanics. And I think they truly did. The controls feel really good. Levels are well designed, and collectables are located in a wide variety of places, with plenty of side (optional) areas, encouraging replayability for completion.I did get a copy of the game for free, but I am definitely having fun and looking forward to playing some more.
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played a massive amount just yet, but a straight up recommendation from me to anyone that loves precision platformers. The game really gives you two ways of playing this which I like and usually do myself, where you try to collect everything on the first run which is usually slower, but then when you unlock time trial you go all out speed. I quite like this design and makes me want to go back and do the trials.Decent amount of content for the priceEDIT: A level editor to make your own maps and share and play others would be sweet but I know that would be lots of dev work
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

_childDocuments_.review: In this electric 2D platformer, help Mr. Run and Jump defeat the terrifying Void and collect all the Power Gems from the Realms of Color! Joined by his trusty pal Leap the Dog, the duo must venture through a dazzling and dangerous world, dodging countless enemies and conquering hundreds of fierce platforming challenges to save the day!
_childDocuments_.name: Mr. Run and Jump

name: SteamWorld Build
detailed_description: Join the SteamWorld Build Community on Discord! About the Game One final landrush! The planet is dyin', Astrid, and it's dig or die trying! That mine under our town is sitting empty, and wouldn't you know there's rumours of ancient tech down there that might help us out of this predicament. Round up the posse, circle the wagons, and let's get to buildin' a new home! Collect resources above ground and ores down below so we can get those wealthy bots in here to help us build bigger, and we can get the heck out of here! As your borders expand, new steamfolk will find their way to you! Every bot is crotchety in their own way, and it's up to you to keep them steaming along. Barter to boost efficiency, keep goods flowing to and from the mines and keep everyone happy to make them work their darndest and hardest. Stare into the abyss long enough and it might just stare back... we're going looking for riches and something down there doesn't want to share! Have gun, dig gravel, and make sure the mines don't collapse upon you as you defend yourselves from the creepy crawlies that lurk within... Break ground on a bustling SteamWorld town, inspired by the Old West. Keep your steambots from getting cranky by ensuring their complex needs get met Dig deep and spread wide to produce resources to aid your search for ancient technologies Defend your mine from the creepy varmints that lurk deep below your town Trade resources at the local train stop Five distinct maps littered with secrets for the discerning SteamWorld explorer to find Developed from the ground up for both mouse and controller, whichever takes yer fancy Four difficulty levels, including a sandbox difficulty for when you just want to Build!

name: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg
detailed_description: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg Digital Deluxe Edition In this set: - The main game 'Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg' - Full original game 'Atelier Marie Plus: The Alchemist of Salburg' included! - Gust Extra BGM Pack - 'Another Look' Costume Set （Set of 33） Note: 'Atelier Marie Plus' is a port of the original version. You can play the game with the same feeling as when it was first released, in modern graphics, and in the same language as the main game. Costumes from the 'Another Look' Costume Set can only be utilized for characters that have joined your party. Free DLC - Accessory '25 Glasses' - Atelier Series Legacy BGM Pack About the Game At the Royal Academy of Magic (the Academy for short), Marie is failing in her attempts to study alchemy. One day, she is given an atelier by her professor as part of a special graduation exam. In order to graduate, Marie must complete an item that will impress her professor. But first, Marie must strive to improve her alchemy skills, collect ingredients, and earn money to hire adventurers and buy recipes and utensils... Add all of that to the synthesis, battles, and quests she must undertake, and it's clear that she has a lot to do before she's ready for her exam! It's up to you to choose where to begin! Work hard to graduate from the Academy, but be sure to enjoy yourself along the way. Features of the Remake: - Updated graphics! Marie and friends brought to life with the latest technology! Character designs and event illustrations have been revamped, and 2D animations have also been introduced in the remake. In addition, there are now 3D models of characters and stages, so players can enjoy seeing cute mini characters while they move around the map and explore. - Atelier series origin, adapted to modern times and made more playable! While maintaining the simplicity and flexibility of the original version, the tutorial and navigation of the game's features have been expanded and improved. The methods of moving around the city and collecting items in the field have also been modified to meet modern-day demands, ensuring that the remake is even more comfortable and easier to play. - New elements added to further enhance the game experience! Fans of the original version of the game, along with newcomers to the Atelier series, will be delighted by the variety of new elements that have been added to the remake. With the new Unlimited Mode, which allows you to play at a more relaxed pace, and the addition of new events that enable interactions with new characters, you can further enjoy the world of “Atelier Marie.”

_childDocuments_.review: it's quite fun and comfy! if you're coming from atelier sophie and/or ryza, you'll notice that the combat and alchemy in this game is much more basic. atelier marie also has the series' trademark time limit, although there is an option to turn this off for a more leisurely playthrough if that's what you'd prefer.not too far into the game just yet but i haven't run into any issues. the game looks and runs great and the soundtrack is amazing as always. i was surprised that the chibi style models fit in so well with the game, too. all in all, a faithful and lovely remake of the original 1997 release. i would recommend atelier marie to anyone looking to get more enjoyment out of the series!let's hope koei tecmo brings the other older titles back for a remake, too 🙏EDIT: just finished the game last night; i think if you allow yourself to take your time with it, then you will receive a lot of enjoyment out of it. five years is plenty of time to do a lot (i reached 81% event completion and almost 100% item guide). it's a very addicting game ;_;
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg

_childDocuments_.review: *Deluxe Edition, Played on Deck*First and foremost, this is a game for people who like the Atelier series as a whole, and not just specific entries. There is quite a lot to like here. +Multiple difficulties+Completion library, including events list with unlock parameters+Great remixed music+Adorable 3d models and animations+First English localization of original Marie Plus (in deluxe edition)The cons are not many, but can be irritating.- Performance is weirdly bad on less performant rigs. (If on Deck, use Low settings, 720p, +FXAA @ 30hz)- Flickering screen? Set Window option to Borderless- Mystification around progression mechanics remain, and the original implementation of the time limit can still be quite painful - one battle takes a day, gathering a single time takes a day, crafted items are made one at a time and are not replenished after use. Given this, the overall game length feels much shorter than newer Ateliers.Recommended to play twice - once with the time limit and once without.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes, but with a LOT of caveats.  Judge carefully what you want out of it before deciding if it's worth a purchase or not.Atelier Marie Remake is a remake, visually and QoL related, to the very first game in the series originally from 1997.  There are a massive number of very dated mechanics and systems, so it may not be appealing to all players.Graphically the sprites are in a chibi style, and the terrain has a cartoony look.  Thankfully it doesn't have a lot of the obnoxious plastic toy look (at least on high graphics settings) that is popular with most other chibi style games.  Music is decent, it's Atelier, but there's less of it here than other titles.  Sound effects are fine, and feel like any modern Atelier title.This game is based around the time limit, though the remake allows you to turn off the time limit (at a cost of some events not showing).  Turning off the time limit allows you to get all the character events.  You have 5 in-game years to craft an item with a high enough grade to graduate.  There are assignments from your teacher that have individual time limits, the structure of the assignments help guide you toward the final goal and give it a structure that players of Escha & Logy, Rorona, and Mereru would be familiar with.  They're mini goals that help split up the daunting "how do I even get there?".Time passes extremely quickly.  All travel takes time and money (to pay your party members, as in Rorona).  Every single gather takes a whole day.  Every combat takes a whole day.  Returning to the atelier from the field takes time, and even returning to the atelier from TOWN takes a day.  You can only get money by completing villager requests, by completing your assignments, and rarely by defeating bandit type foes or bosses.  Money can also be made by selling ingredients, but most of these will be more necessary elsewhere.  This makes money much more difficult of a resource to manage than any later game, where typically it becomes a non-issue late in the game aside from duplication costs.Combat is very simple, you have items, basic weapon attacks, and special attacks for each character.  Characters can also use crafted items like bombs or found items like Uni.  There's a speedup animations option, and an autobattle.  Just be aware that the autobattle will use MP consuming skills, so if you're conserving that for an upcoming boss, you may wish to manually control.  There are no support actions like in later entries in the series, so combat is very simple without a lot of strategy or optimization available.Crafting is weird.  There is no quality or traits present, but the general structure of the crafting system is there (where you can build items that can be used to build stronger tiered items).  This makes making some powerful items a chore as you have to make lots and lots of low tier items but without the benefit of concentrating traits or boosting quality that you get in later games.  One particular character specific goal  took nearly 1½ seasons to create, that's nearly 5 months on the calendar for a SINGLE item!Story is barely there, you are a bad student and get a special chance to prove yourself in a hands-on basis.  Character events are present and related to friendship (also similar to later games up until Ryza's series came out).  You won't be able to get all character events in a single playthrough with the time limit on, there simple isn't enough time.  In unlimited it's possible.  That said, characterization is really slim, nearly everyone is really shallow.  It's unfortunate, but this was the first game in the series and it improved a lot through time.Finally, it's short.  I finished in 9 hours, and I did a good bit of extra stuff before hitting the 5 year limit.  There's replayability to get different character events or try for different endings.  The way endings work is also very antiquated.  Unlike many other classic/older Atelier games, you don't get a choice of which ending to trigger.  Instead, there's a tiering of endings, one of which is hitting level 50.  If you do so, you are locked into one of a few endings and all the others that feel more interesting are unavailable.  This is frustrating since you'd have to replay and make sure NOT to hit 50 to get that ending.Overall, it's a fun trip back to the origins of the series, but with a very dated set of systems that may be frustrating to some players.  The pros are a comfortable romp through the world, with simple combat and decent exploration, and the beginnings of what you would see in later installments.  The cons are a simple crafting system (for Atelier) without the sense of optimization that they typically would have, a barely there story and shallow character events, and a quite high pricetag for what you get.  Long term Atelier fans would probably like it once, but breeze through and no play again as it doesn't let you craft yourself to demigod status.  Those looking for a first Atelier game should absolutely look elsewhere, Escha & Logy, Lydie & Suelle, Ryza 1 (Secret Hideout), and maybe Sophie 1 (though I disliked Sophie 1) would be better starting points for what makes the series what it is.  Finally, if you want a quick and fun little RPG to play, this might work for you.  The time limit mechanic might be an issue to those who haven't played an Atelier game, and this has one (even though you can turn off the limit, you still have to finish the assignments in 5 years and quests and character requests often have time limits).

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is how you make a remake. Atelier Marie is the first game of the Atelier series and it was pretty bare-bone compare to what the series has become today, but still was pretty good in 1997. But this remake is what I actually call a remake. You know games that were remade exactly the same as they were, and sometimes with even less feature, well this game is the opposite. Okay, it is still a pretty simple game as it was back in the day, but man, you can walk around Salburg instead of just selecting were you want to go. There is actually an explanation about what to do in the game instead of hoping to have the paper guide you were suppose to read in your playstation 2 CD box, and the story is actually better displayed than it was with the original. The graphics are for some an issue, but not for me and I love to see the 2D characters moving their lips and bodies when they talk, Would have love to see that in the Arland series. There is also a lot of new events, yes they aren't voice, but I understand the difficulty of assembling the crew from 25 years ago again, and there is some of those none voice events in the ryza series, so not that big of an issue if you ask me.Overall, the game is exactly what a remake SHOULD be. New graphics, more things to do, more options, more clarity, and overall just more enjoyable. I highly recommend this game if you want to experience the first Atelier game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loved the original, I love this too.Here's a bunch of pros about it:+Fantastic remake of the original's music, with the option to use the old BGM if you want.+All the characters are great and have their own arcs and stories+Slightly easier than the original, so you don't die 15 minutes into the first quest.+Tutorials and added guide/manual features so you're never lost +Super easy to keep track of the events so you won't miss any that you wantThe main draw of Atelier Marie is that it's a simple, comfy game. It's not hard to get a grasp on the systems, the combat, or the exploration. It's relatively short (15-20h on a blind run), and the different endings can make you want to play it a second time, perhaps with a different party. The character stories are quick and straight to the point, with no wasted time.That's why it's so good. A JRPG that respects the player's time. Wow. '97 was a crazy time!Oh, and the port is great. Gust really has been knocking it out of the park with these PC ports and I'm proud of how far they've come since Sophie PC. Great time to be an Atelier fan.Honestly, I'm gonna be mad if they don't do this for the other older entries.These are fantastic and absolutely deserve to be played, and this remaster brings it up to modern day standards without sacrificing any of the charm the original had.P.S. If you're worried about the "time limit" you can reach the win condition in the first hour of the game, so you can do whatever you want in the remaining years without worrying about a bad end. Even the hardest ending still left me with over a year left of free time.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a nice chill game with very low stakes and simple game mechanics.Given that this is a remake and the fact that there isn't that much content in the game, I don't think the price tag matches what is provided by the game. Unless you got a really good deal on a sale, I don't really recommend this game just due to the price.Knowing what I know now, I would hesitate to buy this game even at $15.There are a lot of great older Atelier series titles available on this platform. Try one of those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Marie was the very first title in the long-running franchise, and this remake is a VERY faithful adaptation of the original. If your only experience with Atelier is the more modern entries (Arland onwards), then you'll find Marie to be extremely rudimentary in a lot of respects. Synthesis is as simple as having the necessary materials on hand then making the item. The recipe list is also very small, among other things. There are some unique quirks this game has that the other games don't, such as hiring party members to be able to adventure with them, or having a "Knowledge" stat to increase Marie's ability to synthesize and come up with more complex recipes. The world of Salburg isn't terribly fleshed out, but there are a fair bit of event scenes for all party members, and you'll be able to see their stories unfold as you progress through the game. It is nice to see.Older games like this have the issue of being cryptic in a lot of ways, but thankfully the remake added a "Story" tab to the menu that shows you a list of every single event scene in the game, and how to trigger them. You can sort by character, and understand when, where, and how to trigger each of these scenes. It's a very nice addition to have if you wanna get as much story as you can.The only other things the remake truly adds is having explorable environments in both Salburg itself, and gathering areas; in the original, you solely navigated menus to move from place to place ala point n' click adventure. Certain events that were chance-based menu prompts are now full-fledged minigames you can play, which is also fun.But as a whole, Marie Remake is pretty much the original game with a fresh coat of paint and QoL features for all intents and purposes. I do believe it is still a fun romp you can get enjoyment out of, especially if you're curious about the world of Salburg. However, considering a single playthrough is only 6-10 hours, the $50 price point is pretty steep, so I recommend you pick this up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg

_childDocuments_.review: Better off waiting for a sale. Took me 6-hours to get to a near finished game. Half way through the events take a nose dive and slows the game down quite a bit. Newer Atelier games fix these pacing issues.That said, I am aware that this is a remake of an older game, however, that doesn't excuse it being sold for $50.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Marie Remake: The Alchemist of Salburg

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Marie Is the remake of 1997's first Atelier came and the first time coming to the West. The deluxe version also comes with the original game, bonus outfits(just recolors) and a lot of Atelier and Koei BGM music.The game models are all chibi style but somehow it works rather wall, with visual novel style cutscene with regular character models.Graphically it is quite well done with a good amount of color and flair. The Steam Deck is not verified but it does work with some slight slowdown during some combat. Soundtrack is great classic Atelier. Being the first Atelier series game the alchemy is super basic so if you were expecting alchemy like in the latter series you might find it lacking. Game also has the usual timed mode, how the series did things for quite some time and an unlimited mode if you don't want to feel pressured. Every gathering, every battle, every alchemy item takes time so you want to plan accordingly. Combat is pretty basic as well being the first game and you can recruit adventurers in town that have their own stories as you gain friendship with them. During my time so far I've ran into no bugs and performance has been perfect. _childDocuments_.review: Atelier is finally back to its roots. And now, over 25 years later, we finally have the chance to play the game that started it all.Now I know this series is known for being incredibly comfy, but I think this might actually be the comfiest Atelier game I’ve played - which is ironic given that the release brings back the time limit system that more recent Atelier games had dropped. You start the game and are immediately given five in-game years to beat it. Every action you do adds to the internal time.This sounds stressful and I was tempted to choose the option at the start of my save to completely disable the time limit - a new feature - but honestly, the time limit is extremely generous. I managed to get the game’s true ending with over an entire year to spare. So those worried about the time limit thing - it’s really not that big of a deal.Which brings me back to why I find this game comfy in spite of this artificial deadline. That being literally everything else in the game compared to other Atelier titles. Combat is simplified, crafting is simplified, exploration is simplified - everything takes a bit of a dive in terms of complexity. This is where Atelier started and it’s really just the basics on display here.And honestly? I kinda liked it. I still love recent Atelier games with their challenging combat and super complex crafting systems, but it’s nice to kick back and play a bite-sized version of the series I love. Is it easy? Absolutely, but I also can’t deny that I had a lot of fun crafting every single item, maxing out my reputation and knowledge, and unlocking event after event in the story - which the game makes immensely easier by actually providing you a checklist of things to complete before an event can be viewed.The story is not really anything special, but it doesn’t do the Atelier classic of going overboard and losing itself as it progresses. The pacing stays relatively steady throughout and might even be a bit too slow, but it makes for a nice change of pace regardless. There are also a bunch of different endings to unlock as well, encouraging multiple playthroughs.The game can be completed in roughly 5 or 6 hours. There’s definitely more to do if you’re going the completionist route and want to get all the events, but even then, I had a pretty good chunk of them by the end of my first playthrough. For how simplified the game is, this short length kinda matches that change, but it’s definitely something to keep in mind if you’re used to the usual 30+ hour Atelier experience.Otherwise, I had a good time with the game. There’s a ton of stuff to craft, the characters are fun to get to know, the combat is straight to the point, and it just radiates that charm I’ve come to love from this series. I had zero issues here. No framerate dips, no stutters, no bugs, no nothing. The game worked flawlessly out of the box at 4k 144fps and didn’t require me to jump through hoops to change basic settings like past Atelier games have. I played through on a controller, but mouse and keyboard also works here (even in menus) and has bindings that actually make sense - so props for that too.Atelier Marie Remake is a nice little bite-sized Atelier experience that exemplifies just how much this series has grown while also being a fun little play in itself. It’s very simple compared to other entries in the series, but that lends it its own charm in a way and I had a lot of fun casually playing through it. I wouldn’t say it’s the best choice for series newcomers, but if you’ve already tackled Ryza and maybe a couple others, then give this one a shot.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I received a copy of this game by KOEI to use for streaming purposes.Atelier Marie is a beautiful game that is very cozy and relaxing to play. It is quite simple in mechanics, and therefore it may feel different than the other Atelier games. However, I believe that since it is simpler and the time limit can be turned off, that the game would be a pretty good entry way into playing the series. Across the several hours that I've spent on the game so far, I never felt too pressured about the time limit. I was able to play at my own leisurely pace, enjoying the character interactions and dialogue. Furthermore, as I was using it to stream, I found that it was easy to continue interacting with my chat and genuinely just had a lot of fun just sitting back and going about Marie's daily tasks. I don't typically replay games very often because many of the rpgs I have are quite time intensive, but as Marie is on the shorter end, I can see myself replaying it to see events that I missed. However, I definitely understand that the short length may be a detriment depending on what you're looking for, particularly if playtime and story length factors into the most important parts of a game for you.That said, the art is certainly gorgeous, and the environments are very beautifully rendered. The chibi models are very cute and don't feel out of place. I also have high regards with the music and options that were present in the BGM pack. There's a lot of fantastic music to listen to! The game feels very clean with a nice UI. Just as an overall experience, I think the game is  wonderful to play! I really hope they'll make more remakes and continue this trilogy!

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Marie Remake delivers a very high quality experience with a lot of QoL options, improved visuals and controls for a modern game. Gust did an excellent job preserving the first game of the Atelier series and it's origins with this remake 26 years later. I really hope they keep making more remakes at this level of quality.Atelier Nendoroid it is. Very cute character designs that look a lot like nendoroid figures, beautiful 2D menu designs and Live2D animated character portraits during cutscenes. The environments are also really well done and colorful.The overall combination of visuals in this game is perfect and gives it a very chilled back and relaxing look that the series is known for. I really appreciate the Live2D assests and I hope they use more of it in future titles.It also looks like they are using a new game engine in Atelier Marie Remake. It looks different than previous games, and better in some aspects. I wonder if they're testing the waters with this new engine for their next main Atelier game.Definitely the most impressive part of this remake. The soundtrack is really good and there is a big variety of music.The Atelier series is known for it's excellent soundtrack, but I personally think Atelier Marie Remake is one of the best of the series. All tracks are great and contributes heavily to make the world much more immersive.The soundstage and instrumental separation in the tracks are on another level and definitely above the average music we listen everywhere. Either they have used high quality recording equipment or the mixing engineer is really good. It feels special.It's the usual gathering + alchemy + combat that we already know from the Atelier series, but in this game I'd say everything is simplified because it's a literal remake of the first game of the series. It is where everything began and it did not have as much complexity as modern titles do.But even though, I had a really good time playing it and it never felt boring. There is always new stuff to do, new recipes to unlock and new story events to follow. The game is very short clocking at around 7 hours to beat, but I think this play time is ideal for what the game has to offer due to it's simplified structure and progression. The 7 hours is good time and there are multiple endings, so if you're up for more there's always multiple NG+ runs.Controls are also really good, fast and smooth and there are a lot of QoL additions like turbo during battles, menu shortcuts, quick reload, map overlay, and a lot more that makes the gameplay really smooth, satisfying, relaxing and stress free.Excellent PC Port. Runs incredibly smoothly at 1440p 60fps Max on a RTX 2060 Super. Very stable frame rate and absolutely zero issues during my entire playthrough. I don't think I have seen a single frame drop.The settings menu is also good, it has all the options you'd expect from a good PC Port. I think this marks a new era for Koei Tecmo PC Ports. If their next games are going to run as smoothly as Atelier Marie Remake runs, the future looks bright for us PC players.Atelier Marie Remake is an excellent remake that does literally everything right. It stays true to the original and brings a lot of QoL additions to make the gameplay even better. It is a very fun game to play that delivers the original experience while adapting itself to the modern game world.The visuals are really beautiful with nendoroid-like character models and Live2D animations. The soundtrack is also amazing with a very unique high recording quality that definitely makes the game a lot more immersive.It is a really good game and an example of how to make a good remake. Gust definitely delivered a high quality experience in this one preserving the series origins. I think all Atelier fans should play Atelier Marie Remake once.The only thing to note is that it is a very short game, so I'd recommend getting it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Absolutely needs to be purchased on a sale, otherwise a really great, albeit easy and short, game.Like most people in the west my first outing with the Atelier series was Atelier Iris as the first trilogy was not localised in Australia. Really excited to play the game that kicked off the franchise that spawned one of my favourite childhood games. Hope they continue the trend and remaster the Iris trilogy as well! The gameplay of Atelier Marie reminds me of a simpler version of the later Mana Kehmia spin offs. You are a student given 5 in game years to become a master alchemist. Each action takes up a day and you must also account for travel time. You need to create an item of at least 6 stars of a possible 8 by the end of your playthrough. New areas open up as you progress and talk to townsfolk. Combat is a very simple turn based affair and you can choose to gather using either a more modern 'wander around an environment and look for items/battles' or the original simple gathering where you are randomly given either items or a battle. There are multiple endings based on how well you do as well as multiple characters to befriend and level. In the limited time you have you will be lucky to fully level up more than a few.I had heard that the reason this game was not originally localised outside of Japan was because it was to difficult and unforgiving for western audiences. Armed with this knowledge I decided to play on normal and found it very easy once I had gotten the hang of things. So much so I had already completed all bar two objectives before they were given and completed the remaining two with months to spare. It has decent replay-ability for the two best endings (I had not completed the philosophers stone as there was one item you need that only appears on one day of the year and I missed the other as I didn't fully level the main character's defacto best friend).All in all I had a truly wonderful nostalgic yet new experience with this game. Which is a feeling the new more slice of life/friendship simulator style atelier games just don't give me.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend getting this game on sale. It's main flaw is that it's very pricey for what this game is, but otherwise I have had a great time with Atelier Marie Remake.Atelier Marie Remake is a full remake the first game in the Atelier franchise and thus is closer to the older type of Atelier games rather than the open world design of the modern ones. Crafting, gathering, and socialising with characters is the heart of the game. Though a combat system and boss battles do exist, you can easily get to the basic ending by avoiding enemies. Atelier Marie is short and simple, good for providing a relaxing wholesome experience, but I don't think the price would be worth it for those looking to have a meaningful, in-depth, playthrough.My first playthrough was on Normal Mode (timelimit) and I honestly recommend for others to try playing game in that way as well. As long as you don't accept quests you would not be able to finish, you are going to be absolutely fine and progressing forwards towards an ending. In fact, I would say this game is MORE fun with a deadline in place to trigger all of the social events when the Exam is marching closer and closer.  Don't worry too much about missing out on something either, as Atelier Marie's story is relatively short (10 -14 hrs) and has New Game+, meaning a second playthrough would flyby very fast if you only read the events that you have missed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes by F A S T.  Both by its length, and passage of time.  As someone who's played through 3 trilogies of Atelier games so far (I still need to play Dusk), it's so odd seeing the time mechanic here, and see time pass so fast.  One gathering attempt causes an entire game to go by.  So your actions do mean more, but alchemy is waaaaay more simple.  It's really interesting.  I'd absolutely play more games like this, but I think I do ultimately prefer the modern Atelier formula.  The music is great as always, the live2D character portraits, and the fun minigames are just the cherry on top of this quaint little Atelier game.  I think it could reasonably be one of the better entry points into the series with its length.

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Marie is a straightforward game where you can choose between normal or endless mode. Crafting items in your cauldron requires learning recipes, and some items can be easily missed if you're not attentive enough. Time is a significant aspect, with days, months, years, and seasons passing. In Normal Mode, you have five years to learn and brew as many items as possible, requiring efficient time management as gathering materials takes time. Events prompt you beforehand, and missing them can be stressful. The Endless Mode offers fewer time restrictions but still has some time-limited jobs. Overall, I enjoyed playing the game.Combat in Atelier Marie Remake is pretty simple and easy to understand, and you can speed it up to finish the combat faster. However, you don't have the ability to control what Marie and her friends are going to use. These tactics are very useful against common enemies, but when you fight a boss, I wouldn't recommend this type of approach.One of the things I love is when I spot an enemy, giving me the option to avoid them or prepare myself to have an advantage in the first round of combat. This is a big plus for me, not only in that aspect, but also because the monsters themselves are very cute and each monsters have their own skills. Some of them are harder to defeat, but that might be because you haven't yet met the certain level requirements for that particular area. So be very mindful of that, as it could lead you to die, lose days, and some of your equipped items, especially reducing your friendships with your companions who have been with you.You can have multiple companions that you can choose throughout the game, but in this part, they are more like hired companions. As usual in the Atelier series, you befriend these companions by either helping them with tasks they ask you to do or going on adventures with them. The higher your friendship level with them, the easier it becomes to hire them. You will also unlock some events specifically for each character. I highly recommend trying to befriend them, but that's all I'm going to say regarding this.As I've mentioned above, this game is pretty straightforward, and the story itself is not something that will stick with you for a very long time, but it's enough to keep you playing. I wish there were more to say, but apart from the characters, you get to know them, learn their backstories, and try to learn as many items as you can within the 5-year time limit to become an alchemist. Sadly, that's all I can say.I don't have anything against the controls; they're pretty easy to remember, and there is no confusion compared to other games that had some bad ports. Not to mention, this game has very simple controls. However, when it comes to Steam Deck, it's not yet verified, and if you are planning to play this game only on Steam Deck, you may not have a smooth experience as the game runs mostly around 28-30 fps.Do we already know why we want to try out this game? Well, of course, it's because of how beautiful the visuals are and how pleasing the game is to look at. You cannot avoid noticing the cute animations in this game; everything is so gorgeous, from the characters to the monsters and the world itself. It gives you a straight fantasy vibe. The dialogues are all in a visual novel style with beautifully drawn anime characters. Each character looks distinctly different from one another, making them uniquely special. Their transitions in the 3D space resemble the characters but are slightly different due to their chibi form.I was impressed by the quality of sound and the level of detail of sound effects in the game. It feels polished and rich with beautiful ambient sounds during conversations and throughout combat. The voice actors deliver compelling and believable performances, despite the fact that it was completely voiced in Japanese. I generally prefer it to be like this, especially if they are anime. However this might be a problem for those who prefer dubbing, and doesn't want to read subtitles.The music, in general, is very lively and feels fresh at the same time. However, I couldn't find a particular piece of music that stood out to me. This game really brings back old memories for many, some good, and some bad. Now let's talk about the CONS in this game. You can finish this within 10 hours. As I've said, the story is very simple. Since this is a Remake, be aware that the main story hasn't been changed from the original. It still holds the classic story, with updated visuals and improved gameplay. Don't expect the same level of details you'd see in other famous remakes, but it's great to see this franchise get the love it deserves and be brought to newer platforms.if you are the type who love to explore areas, this might put you off, as some areas feel a lot smaller than I was hoping, and there's not much to explore, making exploration feel somewhat bare and limited. Despite this criticism, I can say that a lot of love and attention to detail has been placed in the world, refreshing the look and bringing it up to par with newer titles from this franchise. I honestly wish there was more to explore, like dungeons and hidden areas, to make exploration more interesting.Companions feel a bit less fleshed out, lacking more depth in befriending them. Combat elements where they could easily participate in combos to aid you are non-existent. Although I understand this is a remake of the old title and my expectations might be a bit off the chart since the old game did not include this, still, these quality of life elements would have enhanced this title a little bit in my opinion.The variety of monsters is pretty limited, and I really wish there were more. I also wish there were more areas to unlock, to be honest.The lack of a calendar in the game makes managing your time and days a bit more difficult, as I'm used to monitoring and checking the calendar in such games. For a new player to this franchise, it might feel a bit confusing since it's harder to keep up with what's going on with the overwhelming jobs and events you have to do in a timely manner. You are prompted that the event or job will end before it happens, although it would be nice to be able to check beforehand.Despite my criticisms of this game, I still think it's a lot of fun, and I personally recommend playing it in Endless Mode. If you don't mind a little bit of challenge when it comes to time limits, I do want to warn you that it's not as relaxing as you expect it to be.However, if you prefer the normal mode, expect to feel pressured and stressed during the first hour and the last months before the exam.Despite its simplicity, short and straightforward story, and overall gameplay, you can't neglect the fact that this is a decent remake that many will enjoy.As for our review, we'd like to rank this game as "" and believe it's a perfect game to start this wonderful franchise.
