_childDocuments_.review: Before I even get into why I don't recommend this game in it's current state, I would like to make it abundantly clear that all the negative reviews from people who dislike the fact that the game has wipes, are written by people who have absolutely no idea what they're talking about, and you should ignore them completely. This game, along with any other game where the sole purpose is to go out and loot the best gear/materials, and then use that loot to do map events, would all be dead within a month if they never reset. Where would Rust or Escape from Tarkov be if they never wiped their servers? In game economies are DEPENDENT on a constant wipe cycle. What makes all of that even more hilarious is that I find the issue with Once Human to be the exact opposite. The game holds you back into a set progression timing with its "Phases". Phases last a week or more. For the first 7 days on any server, you straight up can't even access the second HALF of the map. I played for about 18 hours or so when I hit the progression wall. Phase 2 isn't even available for another 3 IRL DAYS! So my options are either keep running the same map sites I've already ran over and over for the exact same resources that I already have plenty of, or just stop playing for several days. If this game was just straight up Rust style constant PvP, I would understand limiting everyone's progression so things don't get lopsided (although there are better ways to go about that). But it's not. There are some servers that are PvP oriented, but most of the servers are PvE, with an OPTION to elect to do PvP events. Meaning most players never fire a single shot at another real player. Ever. So why in the actual F, are they limiting anyone's progression? 7 days per phase and 6 WEEKS per wipe?!?!?! Good god man, 700 pop main Rust servers are dead after 72 hours. How long could you honestly hope to hold a gamers' attention for? Now imagine trying to hold that attention and get that gamer to come back and play more after waiting 3 days for the next half of the map to even open up lmao. And then of course waiting days and days for the next phase after that, and the next etc etc. What a ridiculous concept. All that being said, Once Human does have very good core mechanics, and an extremely solid foundation to build off of. They did a lot of things right at the base level, and thats more than a lot of devs can say. No BS, all they would have to do is remove the phase system completely, rework the wipe cycle to a more reasonable time frame, and set up a staggered server cycle. As in one new one starting every couple of days, etc. The biggest problem Facepunch (Rust) continues to have to this day is the lack of fresh servers. When you have a 2 hour queue every time your weekly servers fresh wipe, and then that same server is dead in 3 days, sitting basically dormant for the next 4 days until wipe, that should be a clue for Facepunch to rework their server system. But it's been years for them and they don't bother. So will Once Human devs make the necessary changes? Probably not, but hey ya never know. I'm also very aware that Once Human isn't exactly the same game as Rust and EFT. This game has more of a story driven MMO thing going on. Which adds some cool aspects to it. I'm just making those comparisons for the wipe/sever mechanics. I've been saying for years now that the future of any game in the greater "Open World" genre is 100% going to be PvE with optional PvP. It's the only way to bring a massive crowd of people in, instead of just a niche audience that enjoys hardcore survival, or another that enjoys nerfed table edges and fuzzy teddy bears in a safe PvE world. You have to have both if you want success in 2024 or beyond. Once Human devs already started with that concept at the base level. Which as I said is such a good start and can only be improved upon. Beyond integral to have that from the get go. Remove time constraints first and then all you have to do is keep adding things, map sections, events and areas for more PvP and PvE, etc. Standard live service game things at that point. This game could easily be everyone's next 5000 hour game with proper management.

_childDocuments_.review: The start of the game feels nice. Then about a hundred hours in, you start to realize that there's nothing more to the game than what you've already played up to that point. You max out your gun, the unique armor that boosts it, a 4-setter and a single offpiece. You build another gun. Then another. You end up having an optimized loadout for all content in the game. And from then on, the only thing you can do is make the easy game easier. You travel to a Hard server seeking some level of challenge. You get nothing but HP bags, and faster-ticking satiation and water meters. Your house breaks for the 8th time after a random update. Your truck vanishes when it was doing nothing else aside from making alcohol for you next to your house. Your vending machine vanishes with everything in it, and you get nothing back, not even an apology. Support ignores your tickets. Your house breaks again.Maybe there's new content. You sign up for this cold wilderness survival map - to find the content-filled map you started with is now replaced with swathes of empty space with more verticality. Now instead of driving for 3 minutes to access 15 minutes of looter shootering, you drive 15 minutes to access 3 minutes of looter shootering. The guns you built in your first playthrough are still the same guns, still ideal. You've rebuilt your house at least 3 times across 3 servers at this point, and you stare at the half-done construction site. You realise you're going to build it again, everything you build will be deleted again in 4 weeks, and something will inevitably break again. The only thing that will surely work well in the future is the next RNG cosmetic box, from which you most likely will not get anything at all, unless you pay enough money to purchase Fallout 4 eight times over.You give up, purchase the Fallout series, and finally get a storyline and changes in gameplay, and then look back. Has the experience in Once Human really been worth the time you spent in it?And you realise you knew the answer all along. Only the first 100 hours was ever worth it. Beyond that, you were hoping for something to change when nothing ever could, the way it was set up. And so, nothing ever will.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote previously a positive feedback. But I have to take it back now after being through season two.Ignore my review, if you are a pro min max "git gud lol" type of  gamer with a lot of time at your hand. As a semi-casual PvE player (I play a bit more than casual players usually do), I can't recommend this game to people who can't play 24/7 and focus on min maxing your gear by grinding, hoping that the goddess "random" of loot will be kind and drop what you need.The game starts nice and great. The base building is great. Almost similar to Fallout 76 or Valheim. The pet system is nice. The world and lore is awesome. I even love the graphics.The story and quests are great and easily doable by normal non-pro gamers...  until   you reach the story line quests LEAH and Forsaken Giant.You can't even choose to do those on normal difficulty. You have to do them on level 60 Pro difficulty, which is extremely punishing and frustrating if you are not perfectly min maxed gear-wise with a specific cookie cutter build for each of those dungeons.And those dungeon-quests belong to the main story line. They are not just some random loot dungeon you simply can skip without missing out on the story experience.If you can't complete/clear these, you simply cannot finish the story line and miss out on that experience.The same goes for the Prime Wars. If you missed out on the low level ones for whatever reason, you are practically locked out of the higher level Prime Wars. And later on in the season people usually only do high level Prime Wars and you can't really get in there anymore. End of story. My free time is extremely limited and too precious for wasting on a game that in the end keeps frustrating and burning me out. That's why I am not continuing this game after the second season. Maybe later, if they make the pro mode for the story content on the last story dungeons optional and allow a normal less punishing difficulty, I might give it a try again and change my review. But as it is now, it's just a bummer for me as a non-pro gamer.My advice to the Creators:There are better ways to stroke the ego of pro gamers without disappointing your casual and "semi-casual" gamer base by locking them out from the full story line experience.Score Boards, titles, cosmetics or offering servers that are marked "Pro Super Hard or whatever", so the pro gamers do not have to mingle with us pesky non-pro gamers.Some players just want to play the game and enjoy the story, lore, quests and base building, where you did really a great job. You could even make a lot of money with base building cosmetics catering to casual and semi-casual players, who are not all too much into endless grinding dungeons over and over in hard pro whatever mode. They are usually happy with normal mode and maybe at some point with an optional hard mode. This way you can cater to both player bases.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it is hard to tell this is a free to play game. Yes there are microtransactions, but the quality of the game is pretty impressive for a free game. If I find a free to play game I actually enjoy, I spend money on the battle pass, and other cosmetic items which I did for this game. Normally when I start a free to play game, I spend a couple hours on it and eventually end up uninstalling. I have been unable to stop playing this game during my free time. There is something very compelling about the game in general. I will go over some of the main things that draw me to the game.Survival/CraftingThe construction, crafting and other survival elements are awesome. Combat is pretty simple unfortunately but there are scenarios you find yourself in that are quite challenging.CombatThat being said, the combat, even when simple, is quite satisfying. The world is filled with quite a lot of enemies so perhaps it is a good thing that much of the combat is so simple.MountInstead of a mount, you make a garage that you can build a motorcycle in. Eventually as you advance in your skills (in a tree a lot like the standard survival game tech tree) you can build a car, and ATV. I assume there will be more options but I have not discovered them yet. Driving is really satisfying and not difficult, yet not quite as simple as a standard mount in a game like WoW, or ESO. You wont go flying off your motorcycle if you hit something, but you do end up damaging it and will need to repair it. Each vehicle also has multiple upgrades, and paint/skins you can discover and I assume buy if you like. A lot of stuff in the game is only available from discovery which is cool.HousingThe construction in the game is really great. A lot of games have done a good job on this the last few years. The base works similarly to Fallout 76. I have not discovered all of the different materials yet, but there is a progression as you would expect (i.e. wood to stone to steel etc).Security in your home is serious however. You do not want to leave it too exposed. There are certain things you do that cause multiple monsters to storm your base and they will destroy everything. I did not realize they could destroy your house, and although I won the siege, 75% of my home was gone including my furniture and crafting tables. The items in the containers will remain in a drop bag so you will not lose your inventory from the destruction. It was honestly really neat to see it be vulnerable. There are options for defense like fences and gates... I assume a stone wall would do better against the monstrosities that storm your base when starting a purification (I am not going to explain what that means, but when you get to that point, dont just start it willy nilly).You can relocate your base every 10 minutes without penalty. It might cost something small but I havent noticed. You also can upgrade your base to make it larger. But you will need to find an open enough space to fit it because it is persistent housing on your server - so other houses are still there even when the owner logs off and finding a large open space is not exactly easy. A conan server is like this, but the populations are small... this is an MMO so a lot more houses (Chimerland wtf ever it is called, Pax Dei but done in a Fallout 76 manner) Although you can move servers it seems but I have not tried that yet. But relocating is easy.Skills/LevelsSo leveling up is based on XP as you can imagine. And like many survival games, there are points you earn to learn more technologies. It is not the best layout for the tree, but its not horrible. I think Conan Exiles has an easier to method when researching skills and techs. When you play you will understand, but it is fine. There is more than just tech, there is of course a few ways to increase your power. From skill points in different fields (crafting and combat for instance) to learning how to build higher ranked gear, and also upgrading the quality of the gear as well as modding them.PetsThe only "pet" I am aware of are little robot guys that mine and/or collect resources for you. Mining silver ore seems to produce these guys as a part of the loot. Do not ask me how to deploy them - I have not figured that out yet as I am going into this totally blind. But it seems very useful as you go through resources quite quickly. But thankfully they are not hard to get.I really enjoy the game so far. I think it is well worth the time and effort. I have played virtually every recent and classic survival game and I have grown tired of most of them after 5 to 8 hours. Conan was awesome but it did nothing to hold my attention. Myth of Empires, Bellwright, Soulmask, Aska (which I do like despite losing interest) Enshrouded, Palworld are the recent games I have played in this basic realm... all have great qualities and strengths, but they lack something that keeps me interested. This game has me excited and interested. I only stopped tonight because my @$$ is getting tired.If you like survival games this is well worth a try considering it is free to play.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, neat concept with a poor execution and a very boring grind loop with a hey every 6 weeks we soft reset but you can use points to bring stuff back you have earned from previous seasons, to do the grind to 50 loop again. If you are an avid gamer this game was not made for you. This is made for people who enjoy comfort in repetitive loops and content. Like how Blues Clues back 20 odd years ago used to run the same episode daily for an entire week so that people who let the TV Eldritch horrors have contaminated the world and special meta humans who can harness rather than twisted by this stardust material seems like a neat setting. However its incredibly underused and just means all the grotesque enemies are just stringy goop monsters and zombies. One early on event has footage of the apocolypse play on a big screen and the horror being shown wills its way into the present as it exists outside time in the footage, but its a generic big tall thing with several weak points to make it fall and you will kill dozens of these every level. The bus with legs is a moving lootchest you can do once per day per bus, and each area has multiple leg busii in them. A few mimic type enemies that jump scare you while looting. The other devitations are cutesy little pun-pun kobold type creatures that automate base functions for you or provide a buff while they are active, which is annoying because food/ingots made by them don't stack with normal items even if they don't have a bonus due to them being seperate items in game code, a very telling coding error where there are multiple permutations of boiled/purified water you will be constantly drinking or crafting but if you do X Y Z you will have incompatible stacks that work due to a tag system.  The majority of the weird horror is expended in the first hour and becomes a mix of minecraft, fallout 76, Rust and Destiny. But as it merely mimics these games it has no real voice of its own. Enemies are not very varied and only the wolves which coordinate to stalk and attack you have any sort of decent AI, most things just run or shoot at you mindlessly often with a generous 2-3 second grace period to aim/melee them. There isn't even that many quests for a MMO; there's literally a stop on grinding aka controllers not being readily available.Overall, after spending countless hours, you get bored super easily.----After 250 hours on August 2nd, 2024My only review change is a thumbs up because they're constantly trying to fix stuff. But how I review this game is:While the game is fun, they really make the easiest things the most difficult. --After putting in 124 hours. As of July 22, 2024Once Human has the potential to be a great game. It's currently plagued by numerous issues that need urgent attention.Bugs Galore After Patch: Initially, the game seemed promising, but post-patch, it's been riddled with bugs. These bugs range from minor inconveniences to game-breaking issues that severely impact the overall experience.Missing Housing and Territory Movement: The game has significant features missing, such as the ability to access housing or move territories. It's been a week since these issues surfaced, and there has been no communication or updates from the developers, leaving players in limbo.Lag Issues: The game suffers from persistent lag issues. Whether it's during peak times or off-peak hours, the performance is consistently hindered by lag, making the gameplay frustrating and often unplayable.Server Problems: The server is always full, yet it feels dead. This paradox is frustrating as there's either a lack of players or they're dispersed in a way that makes the game world feel empty. Additionally, fixing one server issue often leads to another, creating a never-ending cycle of problems.Tedious Reward System: The reward system is overly complicated, requiring multiple clicks to claim rewards. Navigating through four menus to claim a single reward, then repeating the process for others, is unnecessarily time-consuming and tedious.Lack of Clear Instructions: The game lacks clear descriptions and instructions for players, particularly for complex features like Prime Wars. Understanding that Prime Wars is cross-world or connected-worlds and not tied to one specific world within the server is crucial, yet this information is poorly conveyed.Poor Housing Mechanics: The housing mechanics, especially snapping, are horrid. Building roofs or house walls is a struggle as the snapping feature barely works as intended, making construction a frustrating task.Blueprint system requires some rework - where gold/legendary gear is only available to the Wish Machine. And the only currency is locked behind weekly tasks - with limited availabilityWhile the game is fun. It definitely needs some polishing

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... 317 hours of playing and i really enjoyed the most part of them to be honest. So why the heck am i giving this game a negativ recommendation?!?Simply because of the season system.This game has so many great things to explore, to discover, and ... to fall in love with. But it also has a great neckbreaker. The current season system.You're spending a month in order to level up, to get the epic gear you've aimed for, in order to build your perfect home, in order to tame your desired creatures during the current season. You've also spend hours in order to farm the needed and "allowed" ressources in order to completly rebuild your house just like they've promised.But than... the season change occurs and the most important thing you'll get... is a new unofficial title and name."Sisyphos". You know that poor ancient greek king that treated on Zeus and was forced to push the same stupid rocks upwards to the pitch only in order to watch them rolling back down and had to start all over again and again?Well welcome while walking in his shoes...You'll get a total of 20k points in order to tranfers items from your last season, to the new season.Things like weaponblueprints, blueprintparts, mods, furniture formulars and so on will carry over for free.But what doe's that actually mean?Nothing else that you have to start over again from the scratch in order to be allowed to use them again. All things that you've allready earned before within the game.Let me explain this a little bit more in detail.You've managed to really get 3 legendary weapons and a full set of of epic / legendary armory during your season. Now, you have 20k points available in order to transfer all these items and all the other stuff you own to the next season. Nice thing so far.But... transering only a single legendary weapon to the next season, will cost you 10k of these points.Do the math, 3 weapons, 6 armorparts. 10k each and you have a max of 20k. Also, every other single ressource, deviant, and so on will cost you points. To make it even more worse... even if you carry over these items, you won't be allowed to use them unless you've leveled up again to lvl 40-50. Same, count's also for your weapon and armor blueprints. You are not allowed to use and craft them, unless you've achieved the required level again.So basically, you're forced to waste a good part of your next season only in order to be allowed to use those things again, that you've allready earned. It's getting even worse. If you keep in mind how much ressources you've allready spent in order to raise their calibration level. Cause don't forget... if you carry that blueprint over, manage to upgrade it via the wish machine... it will have no affect on your current weapon. You'll have to build and upgrade it again from the scratch. Same counts for armor parts.Same count's for housing and taming creatures. You've spend so many hours in order to get the things right the way you want them to be. Only in order to see, that you are not able to carry them over par on par just like promised and you wanted to. Actually, you are forced to play with a "wannabee house" untill you've earned all those memetic shematics again -wich you allready had- in order to get your "real" house back.So actually, i still think that Once Human is a nice game worth of a shot by everyone during your first season of your personal gaming. Also, i think that this game has great potential to last on the market as one of the best f2p survival games.But as long as they are not willing to change the current season system, or come up with alternative servers that allow you to carry over all of your achievements, items, level and so on... this will be a very tough run for this game. And... i won't even speak 'bout the  policy problematics we have to deal with here.So after 317 hours of actually playing this game, my conclusion is... Netease did a good job on presenting a new survival game. As long as you are willing to accept all those strange policy agreements regarding personal information 'bout yourself and all the people you are connected with via, Facebook, Instagram, Discord and so on...You'll get a very good game during the first season you participate in. But right after that, you are simply forced to waste hours and hours again only in order to be allowed to use equipment, weapons, armor and housing installations again, that you have allready gained and earned...So... no matter how sorry i'am bout it. but i simply can't give this game a positive review right now.I see the potential, i see all the lovely work that has been put into details and i really appreaciate it.But as of now, it's literally a one season wonder cause many people... will turn their back upon this game after the first or second season change the've been forced to.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The Vegas buffet of zombie survival crafting mechanics. Terry Pratchett once wrote of Nanny Ogg, that her cookbook escaped litigation because stealing from one place is plagiarism, but stealing from lots of people is ‘research’.This is so true of Once Human (OH) it’s kinda sad. The game has no personality of its own, if you’ve played any MMO’s, any survival games, and have generally played other games, then OH is going to be pretty boring. It’s got no truly unique mechanics, nothing really new to bring to the table. It’s a microtransaction riddled, half finished, fairly unintuitive, and mostly uninteresting game. That’s not to say that it’s a  game. It isn’t. It just isn’t anything new, not even a recombination of mechanics in an interesting way. It feels like the devs played a bunch of other games and wrote out a list of mechanics then enjoyed and then stuffed them into a sack.So let’s take a look at the best and the worst I’ve encountered so far. I know some folks who are playing OH at the moment. I’ll keep knocking around and playing until we’ve met up and I can try the group mechanics. See if it improves the game any. But for now this is a general no from me. OH just doesn’t do anything well enough, and isn’t interesting enough to have my attention.So who is OH for? If you’re a really casual player, you might enjoy the gentle nature of the game. If you want to try a bunch of mechanics out, see what you enjoy then look for the inspiration and go play that for a better experience. However. If you’re looking for something complete and satisfying, this won’t scratch an itch. This isn’t a great story, the combat isn’t worth mentioning, the exploration is flawed, and the world in general is both empty and too busy. This game is a jack of all master of none.As I mentioned before, this isn’t a bad game. I just don’t recommend it because the facets from the games that inspired it are just done better where they’re focused on. If you like those games, you’ll also find things here you enjoy too, because it works both ways. I hope this does well enough, and gives people an eye into mechanics they might otherwise have not tried.   with reviews by genre. In case you want to find more games, or even reviews, like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The monetization is egregious and the gameplay is mediocre.Let’s start with the monetization:-Two battle passes-A monthly subscription for in-game currency-Cosmetics for your house, clothes, weapons, vehicles, and more. Many limited to bundle sets that cost over $30 each.-In-game items that absolutely DO impact progression and are inherently pay-to-win on PVP servers.Now the gameplay and presentation:-It feels 1.5 years away from release. It’s a barebones map and collection of systems with very little to do. The dungeons are all roughly the same fight. All the enemies are reskins of eachother in each zone. The world itself does not at all match the aesthetic of the trailers. It looks like any generic Ubisoft or call of duty open-world. The locations are copy-and paste identical repeats of each other.-The gunplay is serviceable.-The gameplay itself is entirely rooted around gathering resources and crafting. The gunplay and questing is secondary, and only exists as a means to get materials. It is incredibly grindy. You will spend 70-80% of your time chopping trees and mining the same ores hour after hour.-The writing is terrible, and the voice acting is poor. You may as well ignore the story, the game hardly has one.

_childDocuments_.review: Once HumanGame crashes upon reaching the main menu after finishing "Loading." A blank "UniCrashReporter" cmd appears for a short moment before the entire game closes itself. My PC surpasses almost all of the recommended specs and is above the minimum specs.No error code, all recommended solutions; FPS limiting to 60, FPS limiting to 120, forcing DX11, forcing DX12 did not work. Verifying game files did not work. Manually removing UniCrashReporter did not work. Manually forcing an update by removing the game's Documents folder did not work, disabling in-game overlays did not work. Restarting my PC did not work. Someone claims you have to flash your BIOS, but a video game shouldn't require BIOS flashing just to get onto the main menu.My temps are fine, my resource usage is fine, this is not a problem with my PC's specs.I, quite literally, cannot figure out what the hell is wrong since the game doesn't give any error codes or indications of what went wrong at all, merely a blank command prompt that closes itself and the game after two-three seconds.-----EDIT-----I finally got the game to work after formatting my PC for my yearly clean-up.Once Human is a third-person action-shooter-survival-crafting-base-builder-pokemon-collector-PvPvE mess. From what I understand, it's basically Rust, but with more of a focus on PvE, with PvP being side content for those seeking it. You traverse a map, clearing out hostile camps and doing story quests, while returning to base to drop off resources (and occasionally to grind a few select resources) while building up your little fort.The game itself is... Fine? The setting didn't particularly appeal to me, for as spooky as it tries to look in the trailers, most of the game is basically just running and driving around in a pleasant daytime while occasionally shooting silly looking Z-list creepypasta characters.For a F2P game, it's perfectly fine. Enjoyable, even. But it's not particularly groundbreaking, nor did anything take ahold of me. Shooting is fine, base building is fine, crafting is fine, everything is fine, but nothing seems to 'stick' for me. The main cast seem a bit stale, the areas all kind of blend in together after a while, and the enemies are very, very repetitive.This may be because I went on a PvE-focused server, but in my experience PvP typically doesn't improve these sorts of games for solo players.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed Feelings: Improvements Made, but Issues RemainI initially had a very negative experience with Once Human. The game felt like a total scam, especially when I discovered that all the time and money spent on grinding and cosmetics were tied to a single server. Switching servers meant losing everything—progress, purchases, the lot. It was frustrating to say the least, especially in 2024, where cross-server progression should be a standard feature. It came across as a blatant cash grab, and I wasn't shy about calling it out.However, the developers have since made some improvements. They’ve updated the game so that some cosmetics now carry over to the next season, which is a step in the right direction. I've been playing regularly and found that this change makes the game more enjoyable.That said, there are still significant issues. New players can’t join my server, making it impossible to invite friends unless they start on newer servers. Additionally, if players below level 5 and inactive for over 15 days were automatically kicked, it could free up more space.Another major gripe is the customer support and Discord community. I encountered an issue two weeks ago where my tier unexpectedly dropped from 4 to 2, despite being fully calibrated. I reached out to both customer support and Discord, but my concerns were ignored while the moderators focused on events. This lack of response was incredibly frustrating, and I had to grind all over again to regain my progress.Overall, while the game has its merits and is improving, these ongoing issues prevent it from being a fully positive experience. The game is okay, but there's still room for improvement—particularly in customer support and community engagement.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignoring the inability to transfer progress through server and the (maybe potential? "chinese spyware", the entire concept of the game is pretty good, the game feels like a mix between pubg and some casual survival, open-world game, though that also has it's flaws for example:- enemy a.i, the enemies practically don't move unless you're in hugging range within them, and actually getting hit by one could be comparable to a miracle.- bosses, the game's bosses are essentially just bullet sponged which MAYBE have some sort of invulnerability phase in which they're immune (although that's just more annoying than not with how easy they are), and as a general rule of thumb, most bosses (at least ones i fought) are insanely cheese-able, you can just go on a ledge/hard to reach area and completely avoid all melee attacks and most ranged attacks which are affected by gravity.- speaking of bullet sponges, the game somewhat forces you to run a slow, high damage weapon because the average weak enemy requires for dumping half a mag of your mp7, making auto weapons only good for bosses due to their consistent dps.Now with the minor(-ish) issues out of the way, it's time to adress the elephant in the room, which is not the data collection, but the game optimization.This game has absolutely TERRIBLE optimization, and i mean TERRIBLE, the game's pc requirements are absolute worthless info, as to reach a STABLE 60FPS, i had to set every graphic setting to low (that is with a geforce 3060, i5-11400F and 16gb) now my specs aren't the best, but they're a bit above the recommended, so with those specs you'd expect at least a stable 60fps at medium settings.Continuing the topic of awful optimization, the game is cpu-heavy, for no reason (although it might not be that and just the awful optimization) i've heard of multiple people just getting their cpu usage maxed, straight to 100%, which overheats the cpu (you'll most likely be genuinely able to feel the heat, turning your pc into a straight-up radiator/heating unit.The game also tends to just semi-crash at seemingly random intervals, you can just move your camera, switch weapons, do any action and the game will just freeze for a good 10-30 seconds, going back to the last 2 issues, this has not happened to me, but i've heard that people's pc's would just straight up crash after running the game (for possibly too long), funnily enough, the person defending this game so hard (speaking of asmongold here) also had a pc crashing experience with the game, just playing the game normally and suddenly his pc just crashed, nothing more, nothing less.TL;DR - this game currently is a pc hell as if it doesn't (allegedly) spy on you, then it will crash your pc, and if it doesn't do that, it'll max out your cpu and turn it into heating unit. the subpar, maybe pretty decent gameplay isn't worth the torture you bring to your pc just running it.(Also, this is irrelevant but the game takes legit 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to get into a server and start playing, loading any special areas isn't good either as it takes 10s-1.5m to load an area, aka a dungeon, event, etc...)

If you can follow that one simple rule, you may play this game.It has all of the ingredients of the typical explore/gather/craft survival game, with some spices borrowed from science-fantasy RPGs. The setting is unusual for survival games, as is the amount of variety in the extensive map. There's a lot to do. The base building is decent. The character customization is weeby but a lot easier on the eyes than, say, ARK's hideous characters.  No private servers means public servers jammed with the dead bases of players who set themselves up and then stopped playing, but at least you don't see spawn points walled in or the other horrors of most public survival game servers. Absolutely worth trying at this price point so long as you have self control, and probably worth coming back to in six months to see if they've developed it into having enough depth to be worth sticking with.

If you're wondering why, here are the reasons:1) For money, you can break the mechanics of the game - cheat.How did I figure this out?Very simple! Having pumped up my character to the maximum level, having spent a huge amount of time sharpening things, and having almost completed all the seasonal content, I encountered the following situation:During the event with capturing a passing car with a jellyfish (at the time of this event, the PvP mode is turned on, and other players can prevent you from completing it), some character ran up to me, who was dressed according to the latest "fashion word" in items that cannot be knocked out, they can only be bought, these are items from the "Neon" collection. Well, dressed and dressed, no big deal, I've fought very beautifully dressed characters before, - I thought. But this character was not just dressed beautifully, but he also dealt damage through walls, obstacles, and any textures, not just damage, but killed with the first shot, which is impossible - this must be colossal damage! Not a single boss in this game could kill me with one hit, not to mention the players. The character moved super-fast: I went through all the dungeons and bosses, was in a very large number of teams and many people know me in this game, but I have never seen anyone move so fast - by the way, it's interesting, because I have never seen this player in boss sieges either. Having fallen in this position about 10 times, practically without getting up (because this player killed me almost immediately as soon as I used adrenaline), I left the battle, deciding that this was just one case out of many, nothing to worry about, maybe there is still room to pump up your character, though the problem with one-shot kills bypassing textures is, of course, extremely unpleasant. But not even an hour passed before I was banned, forever, and the reason is - you won't believe it, and I'd rather ask "Dear player, Thank you for contacting us. After a careful investigation, our team determined that the behavior relating to your account violated our policy. Therefore, your account will remain banned. We remain committed to ensuring a fair and healthy game environment for all of our players. Thank you for your understanding. _childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for Once Human, but my experience has been a bit of a rollercoaster, and not the fun kind. I’m running an RTX 3070, 32GB of RAM, and a 5600X at 4.5 GHz on a 2K monitor, so I expected smooth sailing. Instead, I’ve been hit with some serious performance issues.First off, using DirectX 11 seems to yield better performance than DirectX 12, which is surprising. You’d think the newer tech would run like a dream, but nope! DirectX 12 gave me DLSS, which should have worked wonders with my GPU cores, but instead, it runs worse than FSR. I had to disable any upscaling technology just to get the game to run at a playable 30 FPS, which is a bummer.In the tutorial and the first area, I was actually impressed; the game was running at a capped 120 FPS (thanks, V-Sync!). But as soon as I hopped into the main game, things took a nosedive. The FPS dropped to a more acceptable 60-80, which I can live with, but then I entered the city, and it plummeted to a staggering 20-50 FPS. It felt like I was playing a slideshow instead of an action-packed survival game.I’m using an NVMe SSD with Windows installed on it, so I know it’s not a storage issue. Everything else on my rig runs smoothly, but Once Human feels like it’s struggling to keep up. It’s frustrating because the game has potential, but the technical performance is holding it back. I really hope the devs can optimize it soon because right now, it’s a mixed bag.If you’re considering jumping in, just be prepared for some serious tweaking to get it to run decently. Here’s to hoping for some patches!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the average quality cutscenes and quests-interface, we evolve here in an atmosphere and a background with rich and immersive settings, with interesting dungeons and bosses: this game takes up all the good ideas of the last decade (with a very "TheSecretWorld" bestiary/background) organized by "seasons". Everything is almost ideal until we understand that the end of a season (6 weeks) is purely and simply a complete reset/wipe of the servers: exit all the equipment (from farmed components to max-upgraded equipment => we go from lvl50 to lvl1 dropped in the starting zone: everything has to be redone in the exact same context and content.It is nevertheless possible to recover some items with "points to spend" but for maxed equipments, 2 will be enough to siphon-off the entire amount available. Obviously we have to wait to have the required level to use them anyway. It's the same for housing, which will also have to be redone entirely : even if you saved your installation, you will need all the components and skills to rebuild it.A F2P with good quality, but limited content, which can be summed up as a Sysiphean activity of doing and redoing in the same form, in the same environment, with the same content every 6 weeks.Impossible to talk about end-game PVE (despite 175 hours of "discovery" play, didn't have time...) but in my opinion, cause of the seasons, we are here on an investment out of reach of the majority of players who have a real life : O.H. seems resolutely intended for openworld PVP fans and those for whom investing lot of time in a progression destined to be erased after a few weeks is not a problem.I really wonder how NetEase is supposed to make money with a such concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Experiences with Once Human: Way of WinterAfter logging into the scenario, I was really excited and surprised. The new weather system is interesting! The tutorial from my dear friend V was simple and easy to understand: first, gather some clothes, as you do. Then, explore the world and soak up the atmosphere—it felt really good! But soon came the first letdown. The servers are still running poorly, with rubberbanding when driving and getting stuck in structures. Graphics stutters and freezes too, but okay, I can deal with that—it's been in every scenario so far. So back to focusing on the good stuff: making the apartment nice, looting points of interest, doing quests.But then, something quickly became obvious: the poor storytelling and the truly poorly designed quests. But hey, it’s supposed to be a survival MMO-RPG-sandbox-building-grind game, so I guess that fits. Played through the first phases, killed a few Chaoswavers, only to find that there's just no worthwhile loot dropping for all the effort. But hey, we’re used to that too—and the first Chaoswaver fight was nice, to be fair. I’m explicitly saying first here. Then I checked out the new and revamped dungeons and tested the new leather mechanics. All okay so far. Or, well, not really. How are we supposed to farm mods in the new dungeons? They take so incredibly long unless, of course, it's ex1, etc. And the endgame? Basically just farming mods, collecting deviants—the grind we know. All in all, an okay scenario, I think.But then I noticed more and more issues that no one seems to talk about, or that everyone mentions, yet they're never fixed. I’m not really one to question design philosophies, but someone really must have said in this scenario, "Let’s see how much we can annoy players so they DON'T play our game." So, I’m going to list what doesn’t work or REALLY doesn’t work and will still try to offer alternatives. Even if no one with any influence on the game ever reads this, it’ll make me feel better.•	Toxic players and the tower mechanics: Why are players who aren’t in a hive allowed to claim spots at towers by just placing a tent or their whole base there? And then they wall in other players with "F*** Y**" written on the walls? Why not just say: Only hive friends can build here, others get a notice to move their spot. A fair system that’s easy to implement. Tents should have no impact at all and should just be able to be built over.•	The thermal tower and the weather: First, why wasn’t this tested? 90% of the skills either don’t work or work partially. What’s the purpose of the tower except to get crafting and gathering perks? Shouldn’t the tower be there to keep the temperature within a livable range? The only sensible thing was to crank up the temperature in hot areas to boost the perks of devices. I thought the last phase would make it generally colder or hotter so you’d actually have to use the temperature feature. And then, why have talents that improve turrets or defend against Chaoswavers if the Chaoswaver is so poorly designed? If it spawns near your base, your base is gone anyway—no matter what skills you have at the tower. And then the cleansing: who designed this? Enemies spawn at the edge of the buildings, at the furthest possible point, sometimes even INSIDE buildings. And then the loot for all that stress—what the …? Suggestion: enemies should spawn to attack the tower, not structures. You could then build real defensive measures, not just ones against CW that are useless anyway.•	The Chaoswaver: Who on earth designed this? A boss so massive, spawning stationary over bases, with spawn points only assigned weeks later? You probably lost 90% of players who uninstalled because of this design. No mechanics other than “Shoot at one point.” And yes, don’t bring weapons with status damage. Bases nearby get wiped out; loot gets stolen, and you plan to fix it only in December? Phase 4: The laser that destroys everything should’ve been the feature to finally use the Gatlins. But that doesn’t work because no one can get a Gatlin up there. Suggestion: The Chaoswaver could have had stationary points on the map, one in each zone. When it spawns, the whole zone could get a -/+10 degree temperature malus, so the tower has a purpose. No-build zones around the boss, with a 15-minute spawn announcement so people can prepare. Then add a few more mechanics besides standing there and holding the left mouse button. The shield in phase 4 was a good idea but could be implemented better to make use of the Gatlins on cars. And decent loot, 3-5 CW a day, and everyone would be happy.•	Resource overload: This has always been odd. The map is full of ores, plants, and animals. Gold and silver in abundance, with no need for resource scarcity. Points of interest littered with chests and loot. Can’t take two steps without spamming F. Suggestion: make loot scarcer, focus on essentials. That way, you’d actually be happy when you find what you’re looking for. The blueprints for house decor should be convertible into new, unfound blueprints.•	Mobs are too easy: The enemies feel more like decorations and give no sense of danger. After the meteor shower, wouldn’t there be more mutants on the map? Suggestion: More enemies in zones with loot! Give them real mechanics—not just shields or immunities. More sounds and individual movements would add to the immersion. NPCs should have moods and be more integrated into the story.•	Quests and storytelling: The quests are incredibly poorly designed, and there are far too few of them. If you have so few, they should at least be well-told. The main story is also weak, and the end sequence is buggy—I still haven’t seen it. Main characters in the story are so bland and emotionless. Suggestion: Either drop side quests altogether and make the EP grind enjoyable, or add more well-told quests. The main story should be epic and leave you with emotions.•	Sound and music: Music 0/10, environmental sounds 2/10, weapon and item sounds 1/10. The sounds just aren’t immersive enough. Suggestion: Other MMOs and sandbox games show how crucial atmosphere is. Use more dynamic sounds, realistic noises, and environmental details.Conclusion – My Opinion:Overall, you’ve done a great job, but there are still many issues that need to be addressed, or the game will fade into obscurity. The servers need to be stable, players shouldn’t log in only to find that everything they’ve collected has been stolen. Integrate the Eternal Land more meaningfully into the main scenario. Improve immersion (sound, voice, story), and you’ll have a game that stands out.Best regards,nfs.oNe.Kalle

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is quite entertaining and has plenty of content, but this game has a major issue, and it's the way servers work. They will create a server and people can create a character until a character limit is reached, then another server is created and so on; once a server it's full then it's full and no new characters can be created. The problem with this system is that the game is not really designed to reach endgame quickly; it takes about 40h to get there if you follow the expected method, which is completing the map's settlements. Sure, you can rush a new character to max level, specially if you play with someone else, but it is not how the game expects you to play. To put things into perspective, right now there's 140+ servers in the EU region and most of them are stuck at Low population because these reached the character limit and people have stopped playing. Personally I'm stuck on server 28 with a lv50 character and no one to play with; I'd have to create a new character and invest about 20h just to get that character deleted at the end of season. All that progress I made on the server is pointless and will have to start all over again. Idk man, something tells me they made a big design mistake that has no easy solution. As it is now I can't recommend the game for this reason. Nonetheless, one could argue this has been an issue mostly because the game is new and a lot of people simply wanted to try it, so way more servers than necessary were created. My guess is on next seasons the playerbase will stabilize and we will see fewer servers with higher population. But still, getting your character deleted at the end of season is not good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely my biggest disappointment of 2024. It started off as one of my favorites, the new player experience was great and my first time playing through the original scenario was amazing, it brought all of my friends together and we built houses on the same island and had a great time, the build system was fun and creative, boss fights were fun, silos (dungeons) were really cool. I had so much fun going on loot runs for furniture schematics and prints for my walls/floors/ceilings. It was great.Then comes server reset. Everything you collected is lost to a soulless 'eternaland' that barely has a reason to exist, you're forced to restart from level 1 with only a very limited pool of resource to bring over items from your stockpile in eternaland, this amounts to maybe one weapon, some of your deviations (pokemon-esque homies that support your base and fight with you), a drill and a chainsaw. Basically nothing, and the slog of re-leveling through the same scenario is just sorta sad and boring. Then, the lootcrates. This game is very glitchy and feels unfinished in many ways, and the fact that new lootcrates drop at an astounding rate compared to few and far between content patches or bug fixes, is kinda gross. That said, the lootcrates also feel really aggressive, unfriendly, and unrewarding vs how much money they expect you to pay for them, and obviously they lock all the best cosmetics behind them including some really crazy fun housing and furniture items, if you like base building this really sucks. It feels very exploitative of the dedicated playerbase. Ill make a comparison, I've spent an unreasonable amount of money for cosmetics in games like sea of thieves or STO, SWTOR, etc, and never regretted it for a moment (ish). If these items were not locked behind a really nasty gambling system and just straight purchase options, I probably wouldn't have had as much an issue, but as it stands its really uncool. Seriously the lootcrate gambling makes hoyoverse games look benevolent.Then I thought, well, I'll try it again when the new winter scenario launches. Hated it. The map is really pretty and well designed, but it is empty and lifeless with very little actual content, its a bug ridden mess at a level that makes this nearly or entirely unplayable at times, and its just not fun. The heat/freeze mechanics are kinda bland and more annoying that anything else. So yea, I can't really recommend the game based on the overall experience I had. It's free, so it could be fun for a jump in and clear through the Manibus scenario once, but that's really it. PVP scenarios are even more awful than the PVE. It's really sad, I had high hopes for this game and did truly make some great memories with friends before we all just gave up on it, but I don't see it getting any better without some serious, serious work. Wasted potential at it finest. Maybe I'll check it out again in a year or two. Probably not.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game, also very flawed.Positives:No pay to winGreat art directionSolid storyOpen world stuffAbility to share base with friendsBuild varietyNegatives:Building system that will make even grown men cryLackluster PVEAwful PVP (multiple contributing factors)DesyncServer performanceClient authoritative"Did you hear that?"I spent over 500 hours across multiple accounts and servers, 160 hours on a PVE server to find out that the PVE server exclusive content, "Prime War" is utterly disappointing boss fight where players roll up, place rocket launcher turret, shoot a boss with some explosives, shoot a boss with some weapons and disperse.Moving on to a PVP server with multiple accounts to minimize unlucky RNG, the PVP is badly structured.While open world PVP is possible, it relies on both parties opting in to PVP status every 5-10 minutes as it automatically turns off, with no incentive to turn on PVP.Other then cargo event which is present on both PVP and PVE servers, the only meaningful PVP is territory battles, which is completely broken and barely even playable. If you happen to be able to even get in in the first place (because bugs), you need to build a defensive structure to protect your terminal, while the enemy clan and anyone else can destroy your building and kill you as you build.When the battle officially starts, you cannot build and the enemy can just drive their vehicles thru your structure (before it loads on their device) and destroy it from the inside with no counterplay, this isn't a bug btw. it's just how the game is coded. They can also shoot and kill you thru your defensive structures as long as their internet/PC is slow enough not to load these structures.In all this, there is never an incentive to actually fight, just hold W and throw boom at structure until the territory terminal dies.Oh and did I mention that after respawning the enemy cars are invisible for long enough to drive up to or inside your fort?This game had a lot of promise, but it was terribly fumbled, especially after playing Undawn (their previous game) which had both PVE and PVP content many times better, I'd even say the PVE was amazing for what it was, unfortunately that one was p2w and the game died as soon as that created large enough power gap.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Fallout 76/Rust/Palworld with an eldritch theme. The game servers are all hosted by the game company and they go through server resets every 40~70 real life days, however there is carry over progression between server resets. You start back on level 1 and need to get most resources, but you have 'points' to carry over your best and rarest gear and resources. There is PVE & PVP servers. They are adding new servers/regions/storylines over time. A new server in a new world with new content and new mechanics can feel like playing a different version of the game. I'm really excited about this future of this game.Monetization is done through rather expensive cosmetics. If you can afford them or your don't care, it's not an issue. There is a battle pass too that offers cosmetics on the cheap.It's also way more fun with friends, but I found my friends for this game while playing. I found the community to be really fun and helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game.The gameplay is quite simple but exploring and looting each POI on the map feels good.Difficulty, levels and skills are well balanced. You can optimize your gear according to your play style by switching weapon types (SMGs, melee, ARs, ...), weapon attachments and weapon mods.Except little hiccups in basebuilding (like snapping or clipping), claiming your territory (almost) anywhere on the map and building your own home is both accessible, rather furnished - if you're willing to spend time on it - and satisfying as you can use Deviants (= pets) or machines to automatically farm for you.Graphically, the game is OK but the horror/creepy atmosphere is some places can really be captivating.The game's business model is not Pay To Win at all as the paid contents are purely cosmetics (emotes, character skins, weapon skins, ...) and most of the current Season Pass resources are available in its free version.There are some errors in the game's localizations but it is still really understandable.Most importantly, Devs listen to the community and act accordingly : they seek solutions with the community and just communicate on the issues they're facing .The game has a really huge potential and it's ... free to play, what are you waiting to test it ?

_childDocuments_.review: I am a GFN Ultimate subscriber and impatiently waited for this game to release. It was put up 24 hours after the original release to Steam. My opinion, this game has a lot to like and so much fun content for free. It was well worth the wait. I play with a warband from a different game but I have to say, I have enjoyed the lone wolf looter/shooter aspect of OH almost as much as working with the warband. When the warband does get together there is a noticeable lag periodically. Is there a bug here and there? Yep. Less than I thought there would be actually. That’s really the only thing negative I have to say. Having experienced many previous broken games this game was much closer to finished than many that have come before on release. Since release, the devs have been super responsive about server issues and have also banned a stupid amount of hackers. OH did not let down the hype. _childDocuments_.review: It is a “number go up” game, but it’s not bad. It could just be the right game for you, if you’re looking for something new to grind. It has a nice blend of different genres that is not really present in any other game. It’s got decent progression, fantastic base building, some build crafting, it’s easygoing, approachable, etc.To me, it all just feels kind of pointless – grind for the sake of grinding, be weaker in new zones just because your weapon is lower tier, repeat the same activities over and over again for percentage power increases. Add on to that that the combat is dull, the gameplay loop is boring, and the endgame is repetitive. The 3 most important parts of a grindable game are not that enjoyable, so not really worth it in my opinion.+  is what is addicting about the game. You unlock higher tiered gear as you progress through the story. You want to see your character get stronger (even if only just on paper), get better weapons and gear, see what the endgame is all about, make a build, craft the final base structures, etc.+  is probably the best part of the game. Lots of different pieces to let your creativity run wild and make some really cool looking bases. + Base “” element was a nice surprise. Beef up your base with turrets, barricades, traps, to defend against waves of enemies for some weekly Starchrom extraction.+ Good . Very nice looking game overall.+ Lots of good  elements to make your life easier.+ Abundant basic resources that don’t need to be grinded to be able to build and craft. Although endgame resources definitely do need to be farmed.-  is pretty boring. Go to a settlement, visit every building, press Q to mark objects, press F to collect everything, find a couple of crates, and do this for every single location you visit.-  is just a grind fest, doing the same things over and over again (which is standard for these grind games, to be fair). Farm mods, farm Starchrom to buy gear blueprints, farm blueprints to upgrade those blueprints, farm certain materials needed for upgrades. And all that for incremental percentage increase that you probably won’t even notice.-  is not very engaging. Zombies barely move at you, enemies with guns mostly miss, bosses have 3 attack moves, endgame enemies are just bullet sponges for which if you don’t have the right build, are very annoying to deal with.- Cost of making a new build – you farm Starchrom to be able to purchase the end game blueprints from the Wish Machine. Throughout my playthrough (just following the story, doing some side challenges, NOT doing the weekly extraction from base defense) I had enough Starchrom to make 1 build. It was a Shrapnel build and it cost 28k Starchrom for 4 Gear Set pieces, 1 Key Gear piece and 1 weapon. Now if I want to try a different build, I have to wait potentially weeks until I can afford it.- Servers  every 6(ish) weeks. Yes you keep the most important currencies, yes you can extract a VERY limited number of items from Eternaland (for example 2 guns OR 4 armor pieces), but everything else gets wiped. You start at lvl 1 with unexplored map again, have to re-do all the settlements, re-grind all resources to get your base the way it was, etc. It’s just grinding for the sake of grinding. - Server issues – can’t change servers without creating a new character, can’t join servers that have reached a character limit, so joining your friends may not be possible. Over 200 servers and most of them are dead – mine is, I can’t find people to play activities with. Some server merging is in dire need. Maybe all of this will fix itself as the playerbase stabilizes, servers push into new scenarios, and inactive players don’t end up joining new servers.- Dozens of different challenges spread around multiple menus that are annoying to access. All the different challenges are there to give you a feeling of accomplishing something, fulfilling a checklist, getting that dopamine drip when you earn rewards.- Dozens of different currencies to get and keep track of for various vendors.-  is fairly generic and forgettable, wasn’t that engaging to get into. A lot of side missions are not voice acted, which makes them harder to care for. - Expensive  with standard skins being $20 USD, more premium ones $30, cool house building blocks $50. And they just introduced an extremely predatory loot box, where the featured skins would take 100’s of dollars to unlock.

_childDocuments_.review: **** THE OBVIOUS ****People are super paranoid when it comes to chinese developed titles, you can't deny that hasn't been a factor here.Equally true, Netease has a bad rep for scummy practices, predatory monetisation strategies and security issues.**** THE GAMEPLAY ****I played through CBT 2 & 3, the game structure and gameplay loop has largely remained the same throughout, with tweaks here and there to variables like damage, gathering speeds and amounts. The game felt hard in CBT 2, far too easy in CBT 3.I think the focus for difficulty is more on the late game hive content, and hard modes of bosses (that require teams of 4, at LVL 50, and LVL 60 respectively.)The loop is nice, you build a house, you fill it with useful stuff, you explore the map and collect materials, you fight monsters with cool designs, you loot chests for better gear, and once you've collected what you need, you go home, craft what gear, weapons, food, health items you need and head out again.While you go, you collect "deviants" which are base automation creatures, which help you with combat, gathering and other things.The goal is to fight a "Transcendent" an instanced area boss that requires more skill and resources than the usual fodder, and is the level cap for that area, the initial fight is soloable (if you have the correct level) the following fights are not. Once defeated, a new section of the map unlocks and you start again. Collect, farm, build fight.You even get access to a bike, car, AWD, truck, and eventually a lorry.Progression feels real as you move from area to area, each new map section unlocks a new base materials (Copper, Iron, Aluminium, Tungsten etc) and enemies and bases feel a little more challenging as you progress through the map."THERE IS NO PAY TO WIN!"Ultimately yes, its all cosmetic, there appears to be blueprints available in the wish shop, but i haven't explored these myself as they cost 8000 currency and i don't have enough. However, all players have access to the same pool of blueprints."BUT THE SERVER WIPES?!"The game world and season progress resets, its not exactly difficult to navigate the season and with a good enough prep and sending enough materials to eternaland it'd be even easier. The devs are planning scenarios, which are a sever wide set of goals players work towards, the season is time gated so that everyone progresses equally.****FINAL THOUGHTS****Game is good.Game is free.Game is not stealing your data.

_childDocuments_.review: [Updated Review After Experiencing a full season and server transfer]This game has been a lot of fun, and grabbed my interest in a great way due to its stylistic elements and impressive visuals. CUSTOMIZATION:The character customization has come a long way, though some of the best hairstyles are still trapped behind buying a season pass and unlocking them, making them inaccessible to people who don't have as much time to waste on a single game as myself. The body types and facial features can be from realistic to silly, and I enjoy that, though I wish for the ability to change the eyeliner colors, more eye types, and more free hair for starter players. Being able to share your purchased cosmetics between your characters was a very needed update, and makes it feel more worth it to get them. The buyable costumes are mostly very attractive and well designed, though sometimes the difference between the masculine and feminine versions are a little unnecessary.BASE BUILDING:Though starting up a territory in a new server as a fresh player can be a little hectic, the ability to pick up your entire base and move it easily is a great feature I've come to love. However, the need to reunlock all your memetics and gather all the materials over again after a season transfer made me completely give up on getting my original base back. It's just not feasible to spend that much time on the base each season and also do everything else you need to. The addition of more homesteading elements is a great one though, and I can tell that the devs are paying attention to the userbase that is playing this game with a 'Sims but with monsters' mentality by giving more to do on your territory. But again, if the need to start from scratch territory wise isn't fixed for next season, I may never be able to really play with it, so I am really hoping for them to develop a better plan. COMBAT: I enjoy the variety of combat options, but am desperate for more melee. I want more swords, more bow options, and stuff that lets the people who want a character who doesn't rely on guns to shine! Hell, give us some brass knuckles so players can brawl with the monsters! The customization of weapons is very fun though, and the variety of guns is very diverse. It's enjoyable to add skins, stickers, and charms to your favorite weapon to make it your own, and I have no real complaints about the guns and their use, just wish for more options for a melee-focused build. DEVIATIONS/ENEMIES:The enemy designs are my favorite part of this game. They are beautiful, scary, interesting, and sometimes downright spooky. The devs definitely put all their effort here instead of the human NPCs, who are mostly forgettable in comparison, and I don't particularly mind that myself. Mitsuko being the only NPC with a more striking design makes sense from a story perspective, and the game focuses primarily on combat with the deviated enemies. So even though the NPCs could be more interesting, I'm not too bothered by it. The friendly deviations you can meet are mostly very cute and interesting, and fun to see running around in your territory or in battle with you. LEVELING/PROGRESSION:Initial leveling of a character feels pretty good, not too grindy, lots of interesting side quests to keep you occupied between big story missions. But please, fix the season problem, I beg you. There was clearly an idea behind the setup, but it was not executed in a way friendly to players. This season is already half over, and I've not even been able to retrieve all of the 'leaking sources' from my first season. I have arguably way too much time to play games, so people who play less will never be able to do it, which is completely unfair to them. The time and effort spent on leveling and completing quests, the memetics you unlock, the loot you find, all are things that people don't want to lose when they start a new season, and it's definitely hurting the game's userbase a lot. If this problem was fixed, I would have no big issues with the game at all, but this problem is BIG.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: The game visuals are gloriousCons: Nothing beyond the visuals are glorious.TL:DRAll in all, it's got a decent premise, the story line isn't bad, but the game is crippled by it's mechanics and structure, can't recommend.The game gives you the fairly standard mechanics of health and stamina, along with food and water. The game also gives you multiple currencies to manage, Time-gating, low to no server population, no significant social options, and no permanance.So, you have marks (from season achievements), Starchrom (various single payouts, time locked events) Energy links (mobs drops, achievement payouts), and good will of fellow players (vital to anything). The last is not an official currency, but due to the leveling system and the way perks are handled, also something to be tracked and built.Leveling itself is easy, new gear every ten levels, with a bit of a difficulty spike when you're moving up a tier of gear. You end up spending a level or so, killing stuff that's a tier above your gear to get the parts you need to make new armor/weapons. Servers run for 2-3 months, then reset, when they do. _childDocuments_.review: Once Human immerses players in a bleak, post-apocalyptic world where survival feels genuinely tense and engaging. The dark, eerie landscapes filled with mutated horrors create an atmosphere that pulls you in, making every exploration feel dangerous yet rewarding. The game’s combat system is flexible, allowing players to experiment with different weapons and builds, keeping the gameplay dynamic and personal to each player's style.Pros:- Immersive, haunting environment- Wide variety of combat builds- Regular updates and a strong developer community- Free-to-play with no "pay-to-win" elementsCons:- Grindy progression and repetitive endgame- Time-gated resources slow down the pace- Seasonal wipes reset progress, frustrating long-term players- Poor optimization with performance issuesWhile it shows promise, Once Human’s reliance on seasonal wipes and lack of late-game content make it hard to stay invested long-term. Still, it's worth a try for survival fans who can handle a few frustrations.Message to the Developers: Please reconsider the Seasonal Wipe feature. Although it adds a level playing field, it frustrates many players by resetting progress every few weeks. This can lead to player burnout and ultimately result in a loss of dedicated players. Addressing this issue could greatly improve long-term engagement and player retention.

_childDocuments_.review: Spent plenty of time in their character customization as it was quite nice and while missing any interesting hair colors (hair dyes, plz plz plz) it was rather robust and had plenty enough to give me nearly too much time to toy with making my character my own. Height slider is awesome.The downside is after stumbling out of the creator I had to scoot and do the daily life stuff and when I came back, booted up the game and went to jump back in I was greeted with "Server overloaded, queue position 141, est time 5 minutes 11 seconds". This just will not do. I couldn't even get into the same server as all my friends are on, and now I can't even toy around in the tutorial? Thankfully it's a free game and I hope they have some kind of plan on how to make it so people can actually play alongside their friends more easily. Or get into the game without having a five minute wait timer.Not recommending this as it is, wish there was a "meh" option.Edit - 07/14/2024I've been enjoying the game and I feel there's more than a few things that really, really shouldn't even have existed as a problem within the game. Why aren't you able to just swap character across servers? You can literally traverse separate "worlds" within a server, example: Manibus PVE01-00040, World 9. You can then go to a teleportation point and then choose "World 6". The fact you can't move character from server to server seems completely foolish.The next major issue is one that should NEVER have happened in any manner of MMO game. Locking my purchases to the specific server I was playing at the time? What's that? Did you jump on a cosmetic outfit because you really enjoy the look? Or maybe you mix-and-match to have a unique look all your own! Well, too bad, if you decide to leave your server and make a new character to join your friends you will find yourself bereft of all purchases made on different servers - on top of seasonal progress is ALSO linked to the server you played on. Why is this design even a thing? Who let this get beyond product review or playtesting? This is basic nonsense that should NEVER have been an issue.But - what about the gameplay? Is it fun? Is it challenging? It can be. I'm an absolute fool for open-world exploration. I love finding interesting things and discovering hidden details. The game has a decent loop for this as each area has hidden chests and mini-objectives for each point of interest. Gunplay can feel sluggish at times, weapon-swapping hitches in high intensity situations, movement is alright. The grind isn't atrocious and building stuff isn't too bad. They took plenty of notes on making it easy to jump into and yet a deep end for people looking to make their dream mansions.Do I recommend this game? No. Not without people educating themselves extensively on what needs to be fixed. I hope they do remedy these things. I want to be able to play with my friends without completely restarting all my progress. I want my cosmetics and battle pass to carry over as well. These two things are crucial to my enjoyment and thus I can't recommend the game until these issues are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 solid game you can take at your own pace. Only complaint is lack of performance optimizations, but those will come with time. Easy to drop in and play. Game depth and end-game progression will satisfy the min-max player "itch". World is big and areas clearly show you what materials you can get in that area taking out the guess work. Game is great for people with time constraints. You can log out anywhere and continue right from where you left off if you have to step away except a few instanced missions. You can accumulate resources passively while offline to offset your irl commitments. Seasons: A lot of people don't like this; Neither did I, initially. Basically, every 6 weeks is one "season". After this season is over, your character will be reset to level one. ALL IS NOT LOST!!! Materials/gear from that prior season goes into a vault. In the new season, you will be able to carry over all important end game currencies into the next season with the option to use in-game currency to pull items from your vault into that current season. Main story/side mission progress is saved across seasons.IMPORTANT MENTIONS:NOT PAY-TO-WIN!!! PREMIUM BATTLE PASS TRACK IS FOR COSMETICS ONLY!!!YOU CAN'T BUY THE IN-GAME CURRENCY TO USE THE "GATCHA" SYSTEM, IT MUST BE EARNED IN-GAME!!!YOUR BASE CAN BE SAVED FROM PRIOR SEASONS AS A BLUEPRINT AND CRAFTED IN THE NEW SEASON WITH LOW QUALITY MATERIALS!!! YOUR ENTIRE BASE CAN BE MOVED FOR FREE EVERY 10 MINUTES!!!ANY BLUEPRINTS AND THEIR RANKS YOU OBTAIN IN THE LAST SEASON STAY UNLOCKED PERMANENTLY!!!TERMS OF SERVICE: IN COUNTRIES LIKE SOUTH KOREA AND CHINA, YOU ARE REQUIRED TO LINK YOUR GOVERNMENT ISSUED IDENTIFICATION TO ACCESS ONLINE SERVICE GAMES!!!THIS PART ON THE TOS IS APPLIED ONLY TO THOSE COUNTRIES THAT REQUIRE THIS!!!IF YOU ARE IN THE UNITED STATES, THIS DOES NOT APPLY TO YOU!!!This game reviews would be overwhelmingly positive if people were actually reviewing based on the game itself and not the misleading opinions of people who don't check their sources or even put time in to thoroughly get a feel for all the things Once Human gets right. Truly a sleeper that will only get better over time. I'll be here enjoying every step of the way.

I haven't convinced any friends to play due to varying reasons, so I haven't had the luxury of being able to experience the co-op nature that this game can bring. The building could use a little smoothing out -putting on roofs can have a high failure rate sometimes- and the fighting could be ramped up a bit in the beginning of the game. As I played, I would tell anyone about my missions—how the squad worked together, how they fought back against impossible odds. oh the excitement, a spark of joy I hadn’t got in a long time. The game gave me a sense of purpose, a chance to be a hero, even when I couldn’t be one in my own life. For hours and hours, I'd immerse myself in that world, and for a while, the pain would fade away.To the creators of Once Human: Thank you. _childDocuments_.review: Nearly missed my fishing trip because I got sucked into this game upon first launching it.At first, I was kind of like, "this is going to be another Chinese Ark/Rust clone." but after looting my first container, I went, "hmm, there might be more order to this game after all."While the game does borrow elements from both games, I would probably compare it more to Fallout 76. You own a base and you add furniture/items to it over time. However, in this game, everything is wiped every 6 weeks. This means you should not be attached to anything you've built or own as it will be removed from your possession. This is done to declutter the servers as, you'll quickly realize, there will be barren player homes as you walk past them. Unlike Fallout 76, your base remains long after you've logged off. Also, unlike Ark or Rust, this game does have a storyline with cutscenes and an evolving narrative. As annoying as it sounds, it does help set the atmosphere for the game. It feels somewhat sci-fi esque, but it also feels modern. They nailed the mysterious atmosphere/design.Base building is also a lot more in-depth than I anticipated. You can modify the finest details of your base, from the desks/carpets inside to the wall paper and the plastering of the ceiling. This allows you to really make your house your home.At the current time of review, I've played for about 2 and a half hours. It was long enough for me to decide whether or not I'd stick with the game. And, if you are good at inferences, I think you'd know my experience was a generally positive one and I am indeed sticking with this title for the long haul. I cannot wait to see where this game goes!
