_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:Mechanics & Control: The game offers a vast map and diverse crafting options, encouraging hours of exploration.Challenge & Fun: The current enemy AI is too simplistic, reducing the challenge and impacting the fun factor.Innovation: While the open-world concept isn't new, the execution with various crafting options keeps it interesting.Graphics and Audio:Visual Quality: The graphics are detailed and impressive, especially the lighting effects and environmental design.Soundtrack & Sound Effects: No specific mentions; the soundtrack and effects are adequate but not outstanding.Story and Characters:Narrative: The plot has potential but is described as rather superficial for now. More depth could be added in future updates.Multiplayer/Community:Online Modes: Not extensively tested yet, but there are reports of connectivity issues that could disrupt the multiplayer experience.Value for Money:Cost-Benefit: Given the open world and numerous interaction possibilities, the game seems to offer fair value, assuming technical issues are addressed.Conclusion:Once Human is a game with much untapped potential. It offers an intriguing world and appealing graphics but suffers from technical shortcomings and overly simple AI. It might still be worth a look for fans of open-world survival games, especially if future updates tackle the existing issues.Overall Rating: 7/10Pros: Vast open world; impressive graphics; engaging crafting system.Cons: Weak AI; technical issues; lack of depth in some areas.Recommendation:For players who appreciate a rich and visually stunning open world and are willing to overlook some technical flaws, Once Human might be a worthwhile investment. However, fans of challenging strategic combat might prefer to wait until the AI is improved.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games I feel that has captured the massively multiplayer aspect of housing correctly.  Yes, there are ton of houses everywhere and some look ugly, but it's nice having player housing in the actual game world that doesn't feel instanced.  Plus seeing players running around, jumping in and helping out, etc.The survival aspects are okay.  The game could have gone without them and did just fine, but it's okay they are part of it.  It may matter the harder the game gets.I love scavenging, which it seems I can specialize in if I want to.  Get more loot, materials, etc.Game world is great, story is okay, nothing mind blowing.  Enemies are quite unique.The UI and menus as a whole.  They are designed to confuse the player and cause them to spend money.  There are a bunch of events, microtransactions, passes, etc.  It's meant to cause confusion. Each time I played over the course of a few days, I found some reward I neglected to claim.  It's over the top.Oddly enough there is too much loot, even though I like that kind of gameplay.  It's just all loot to be loots sake.  Find iron ore to eventually get tin ore to eventually get the next ore.  The problem is I had a dozen or so storage boxes in my house, which ends up not being fun at all to have to sort and maintain.  It wasn't bad, but it wasn't good either.The gacha mechanic is overplayed at this point in games like this.  I already play one gacha game, and luckily it doesn't make it feel like a full time job.  This game does.  I feel like I need to log in to keep the currency coming in.Attempted to come back in November 2024 and it's a confusing mess.  Multiple scenarios, more confusing things thrown the player's way, and just more ways to scam the player.  Overall, the presentation is done poorly when it comes to explaining the scenarios, currency, and many other aspects of the game.  Combat is straight forward, but the rest of the game is not.  It's not worth the effort to figure it all out when it feels more like a job than a game.  I feel like it will get worse as more scenarios are added.I like the game, I think it's great, but as a live service free to play game, it's meant to swindle me of as much money as possible.  So who knows if I'll keep playing.  I haven't spent anything so far, and I wish it was a full priced game with all of these cosmetics and other items just unlockable as I play.I finally uninstalled.  I still think the game is decent, but I'd have to quit one or even two of my other long term games to play this.  Unfortunately, those I consider to be better.I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things.  Keep that in mind when reading my reviews.  If I do not have a complaint, then the game must be special!

_childDocuments_.review: A Refreshing Subject Matter in the MMO Space.I had heard nothing about this game until the day before it went into full release, but I figured why not try it out? I’m really glad I did because it offers a lot of gameplay that I find very enjoyable.The story itself has me intrigued and wanting more to understand what exactly Stardust is, who brought it into the universe, and what the end goals of Rosetta are. Not to mention our character’s role in it all. The monsters are very inventive and interesting to look at with their “cosmic horror” twist and the bosses are ACTUALLY fun to fight. That alongside all the nice base building, rate of skill improvement, and deep gear upgrade system makes this for a really big contender for one of my favorite games of the year.There are some small tweaks the developers could work on such as a polish on the quest dialogues cutting short every once and a while, small performance hiccups when interacting with others in the open world, and just some polish on the building system, but those are all very minor in my books. The developers corrected some of my bigger issues in just the first 24hrs of the game being out.I’m really looking forward to playing this game into the future to see where the adventure leads! Would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, listen up you lot! I've just spent an ungodly amount of time playing this game called Once Human, and bloody hell, it's actually not half bad. In fact, it's so good it makes me wonder if I've gone soft in the head.First off, the customization is mental. You can tweak every bloody thing about your character. It's like playing God, if God were obsessed with nose shapes and eyebrow thickness. And just when you think you're done, they throw in a mirror so you can keep faffing about with your looks. It's brilliant!Now, they say you should play with friends, but let's be honest, who's got those? Don't worry, you sad lonely bastards, you can still have a blast on your own. It's like a party for one, minus the embarrassment and regret the morning after.The action's pretty nifty too. You can swap between first and third person faster than I can down a pint. And the loot? Bloody hell, it's everywhere! You'll be tripping over guns and armor like they're empty beer cans at a football match. It's fantastic!The crafting system's a right treat. It's so easy, even my nan could do it, and she still thinks the internet is a fishing net. You can pick up your entire bloody house and move it if you fancy a change of scenery. It's like The Sims on steroids!But listen, it's not all sunshine and rainbows. The building can be a right pain in the arse sometimes. Trying to put a roof on is like trying to solve a Rubik's cube while drunk. And good luck finding resources - you'll be driving around like a headless chicken, probably breaking your vehicle on every pebble in the road.Speaking of vehicles, they're about as sturdy as a chocolate teapot. You'll be repairing your bike more often than you ride it. It's like they've never heard of shock absorbers.But you know what? Despite all that, it's still bloody brilliant. It's free, it's fun, and it's less likely to give you a hangover than a night out with your mates. So what are you waiting for? Get in there and have a laugh! Just don't come crying to me when you can't figure out how to build a sodding roof.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. A time sinker, if you will. The graphics are astounding, and the gameplay feels fluid (although some bugs appear here and there). I've only sunk in a few hours in this game but those hours were pretty enjoyable. There's so many things you could do in the game, so I had a lot of fun exploring.It's main flaw for me, personally, is the server wipes (it's the main reason why I was hesitant at first to touch this because I don't like knowing that I'll lose all my progress after a designated time). This has probably been mentioned so many times before, but I think it's dumb to implement the server wipes on PvE dedicated servers (it's understandable in PvP). You're not really competing with anyone in PvE so there's no reason for the server wipe. Not to mention, people who take their time in the quests will probably feel demotivated to continue when their progress is erased to the beginning even though they haven't finished the quest lines yet.I kind of get the reasoning for the server wipes but I wish the devs didn't implement that on PvE. It's also pretty ironic that the devs claim the server wipes exist to not pressure the players to keep up with other players, but the time limit before server wipes is more than a month, so players are pressured to grind hours to no end just to finish events. (The Eternalands exist to apparently keep your stuff and buildings built at the end of season but its mechanics still confuse me).Overall though, I really do recommend people to try this game at least once. Play through the game before a season ends or start when a new season begins and forget about the server wipe for a bit. It really is a fun game, you might even find it enjoyable enough to keep playing even though you lose all progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by saying although this is a positive review, I would still ONLY recommend it at least for a week's worth of fun, if I could post a neutral review I would, Warning, WALL OF TEXT, TLDR at bottom.Firstly, the whole journey from 1 - 50, it's great, exploring new areas, completing town anchor missions, looking for morphic crates and doing silo/boss missions, all while learning new things to build your base up and activate the defense part to defend and earn starchrom, all amazing, haven't played a game so much in a long while, this really captivated me and I even lost time and sleep over it, super fun.But that's where it mostly ends, everything else late/end game I find is just super bad or just so limited and time gated it feels more like one of those facebook city building games where you wait 15 hours for single upgrade to mostly achieve nothing, i'll make some bullet points with issues I have with the end game in no particular order.1. Prime Wars - Needs an overhaul, the whole scoring system to get your chests is a pain, resulting if hundreds of spammed wall structures (They need to be destroyed for you to score), the silver shield on every boss that stops all damage that isn't explosive (Very expensive, especially Biomass missiles) and then to top it off, if you fail and waste biomass rockets, you get nothing and if you win, you still need controllers to open the chests otherwise the loot sucks.2. Controllers, an item needed to get full loot from every single Silo, Dungeon boss, Prime war chest, basically anything worth while needs controllers, they're way too hard to get, a low chance on low spawn rate public events just isn't good enough, at a minimum they should be x1 - 3 per public event 100% of the time.3. Starchrom, ah yes, the currency you need to get blueprints through the gacha system, and the ONLY way to get any good blueprints, extremely limited currency, you'll get a bunch at first but then it'll come down to barely 4 - 8k per week, mainly from your cortex base defense but that's limited to 40 per week (4k starchrom max), keep in mind, you can outright buy blueprints (8k for a single legendary BP) and that's just to get your base weapon, there is TONS of blueprints to get and it costs even more blueprint/frags to upgrade them all, it would literally take hundreds of thousand of starchrom to get everything, and you're limited to 4k or so per week, with no other way to farm it, feels awful, you can't try new builds out or test any new weapons, so if you find your build you made during 1- 50 isn't working your basically boned.4. Dropped Legendary Weapons, useless, no other use other than a few materials and it's calibration, you can't repair dropped weapons because they don't belong to you, so any hype or excitement dies straight away upon finally getting a drop, they need to rework this system, make them way rarer but let us repair them.5. Acid, A dropped material, except almost everything worth while late game needs acid, from ingots, gunpowder for ammo and many other things, you simply don't get enough off it and takes forever to farm.6. Durability, Goes down way too fast, do a single prime war or a dungeon or 2 and your off to repair, isn't so bad a first but you soon realise it burning through your materials, really needs to be tweaked so I'm not repairing every 10mins, this also applies to your car/bike, this thing is made of paper, you'll be repairing this CONSTANTLY, even trying to drive safely, the roads are janky and you can't avoid damage.7. All there is to do END game once you're 50 and have done your base is basically MOD farm, all dungeons, silos, bosses result in more mods, worsened by the fact you need controllers to open any crates/crystals for loot at the end of the dungeon thus limiting how much you can do when it's the ONLY thing to do at the end.8. Specializations, You get these every 5 - 10 levels, can't remember exactly but getting them is complete RNG, some of them are trash and some are BEYOND broken, these can literally make or break your life in Once Human from making gold ingots to having the ability to make Acid without the need to farm, there's no way to reset these outside of a highly limited once per week reset and there's ALOT of them, needs to be changed so we can reset with Energy Links (In game normal currency)9. Seasonal Resets, yes there's resets, it will reset your level and wipe your base/map/materials farmed while keeping things like blueprints, on a survival game, really doesn't suit being there, hope it gets tweaked later.TLDR: It's a amazing game held back by way too many limitations and time gated content, it's amazingly fun for your first 7 days or so depending on your pace but then it dies off end game, without almost nothing to do you will be stuck waiting on weekly timers and resets to get anything meaningful done, highly advise you play it very sparingly and hope they change some of the games biggest issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a really fun game. But they limit the number of total characters that can be made on a server instead of limiting how many players can be on the server at once. This creates a huge problem long term.Not only does it mean you can NEVER join your friend's server if it hit it's character limit. It also means if anyone quits, like the tons of people who check out a F2P game then bail after a couple weeks, they all continue to count towards the server character limit for every server they made a character on (up to 10). Those servers will still be considered "full" even if they only have 3 active players who don't even share the same playtime.Eventually all current servers will be dead servers that are filled with people who no longer play or who switched to other servers. New servers will need to be made for the influx of new players and you'll have to keep switching to those servers if you want an active server. But once you've made characters on 10 severs you'll never be able to join another server again. And those 10 servers will all eventually be dead servers.This will especially be a huge problem in a couple of weeks as the gaming tourists, who are trying a game cause it's free and new, eventually wander off and leave a slew of dead servers on their way out.I really, really like this game and think it has huge potential. But until this issue changes I can't recommend the game unless you just want something short term.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a review from someone who has played the game for 870+ hours logged on Steam.The game start off good after the initial release, mainly during the first server. No major game breaking bug, mistranslation here and there, but forgiveable for a newly released game. No significant lag except for Prime wars.But the overall direction went to a totally different direction with major lag in all part of the game. Prime war? still lag. Silo, monolith dungeon? Lag. Solo Silo, Monolith? Lag as well. Running around the map? Lag as well. Some build is not viable due to significant lag. More and more translation error as well.All while these major issues are still in game, the dev release 3-4 paid loot boxes. Note that the game are only in the 2nd round of the season and a season only last for 6 weeks. Don't get me wrong, the gameplay is fun, hence the 800+ hours, but I wouldn't recommend anyone to start playing it in the current state. Despite the lootbox, it's not a P2W game. The theory crafting in the game is fun, and albeit locked behind the Starchom in-game currency (can't buy with real money), you can still make a number of different builds, which I have tried at least 15-20 possible builds.The base building is fun, but it's also one major reason for the lag, as mainly noticeable in the Blackfell area due to the trucks and the building on top. So, overall, it's a good and fun game, I would not recommend anyone to start playing it at the current state. You'll lose interest quickly with all the lag, and will definitely have bad impression with the mistranslation and the frequent bug. Watch the dev/community reaction on the lag issue, and see if it has been solve before trying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the censorship in the game chat is probably something you will notice first about the in game chat feature.  Their moderator team(if there even is one anymore its probably some ai driven software at this point) will mute you on a whim from anyone deeming your message in game chat distasteful and report you which can lead to permanent chat ban on one server however you can chat willy nilly on another server no problem.  It seemed as if I couldn't cross-server chat at first but I was able to get with a friend externally of the game and confirm that my messages to them did not appear at first until they logged out and logged back in and checked our chat log, so my messages from my alternate server character were able to be received by my friend on the server I had been permanently chat banned from on my main server character.  I was not banned from playing cause I was not cheating however I must be permanently chat banned and for quoting a line from a movie I like that someone took offense to or they personally didn't like me, I don't know because I was never given any details other than their generic issuance of the chat ban which they call being muted.  As a result I cannot A:mark items such as chests or crates because it posts in team chat "I marked a spot" B: I cannot chat with my hive, in team chat, warband chat, nor direct message anyone from the same server i was chat muted/banned on in addition to being muted in world chat. C: Once muted there seems to be an automated generic response from the moderator team expressing that I "violated" the terms of the games policies(if they are even reasonable to begin with, I don't spend time reading EULA if this game even has one) and will remain muted. There's no appealing it in reality and they don't tell you for how long in game, apparently they publicly "humiliate" the players who have been banned or muted by posting their player names on their official site I guess? I'm not sure but I get NO genuine communication from anyone from support when appealing my chat ban. Also, watch what you say about China, I'm willing to bet the CCP has their hands mixed in with NETEASE's hands and blended in to look the same, collecting more data off your PC that they aren't supposed to, though I'm no computer scientist nor code expert but would love to know if there's unusual code within this games coding.  The vehicle physics do not adhere to what you'd expect in the real world, full speed and accidentally clip a parked car and you bounce off it like a tennis ball, tumbling in odd ways through the air.  The user interface is not very friendly.  They did well with the character models but failed miserably when it comes to the look of the environment.  Half the objects are floating.  Objects that are floating damage your vehicle as you glance it with your vehicle.  Often simple functions don't work such as trying to join a team from another team or even look at the descriptions of the mods for your gear without them flashing away instantly.  The lag during public events was atrocious at first but they cleaned it up quite a bit however it still lags if there's 40 people and your there.   Their cosmetic loot that looks cool such as the pyro glide paint for your motorcycle, is RNG.  So your not guaranteed anything cool.  I've heard of people spending 300$ and got garbage loot out of the crates. DO NOT SPEND MONEY on this game, you will most likely feel burned.  The reporting system is garbage, you get 80 characters to report another player, so you cant really describe in detail the situation and what happened, you have to kinda talk cave man, grunts and whooping sounds for NETEASE to understand you.  Its fun with respects to working with other people.  The story-line is un-cohesive and hard to follow given the dialogue doesn't follow the subtitled text of which you cant remove. Their deviants push you around your own camp while your using a bench for supplies or weapons/armor.  You cant join your friends if you've joined different servers at different times because if the server is full then your friends cant join you and they only give you 5 invites for friends to a server that is full, if its full.  The list goes on, toxic people in chat, people bullying as you would imagine happens everywhere.  Cheating has been watched and addressed though as far as I've heard and as far as this company's let us believe.  However their Latency booster jargon, bs if you ask me. Don't buy that.  Honestly, the only reason I am going to continue playing this is because I've made a few friends on the game that enjoy the game and I enjoy their interaction, that is it. It all seems the same go some where, shoot stuff and things, collect things and stuff to maybe find a blueprint fragment that might upgrade one of your weapons if your lucky. _childDocuments_.review: Got to level 24 and decided to call it there. I think it could be good one day, but it feels a bit too "lets throw everything at a wall and see what sticks." Too many mechanics that are barely thought out. The gear grind is fine, the monetization system is a bit too hectic and the performance is subpar even on a RTX 4080. I think the biggest problems I have with the game are:1. Too many checklist type missions and areas, crates are annoying to find and don't really feel worth collecting until later in the game.2. 6 week wipe cycles make me not want to invest time into the game let alone any money. Why would I want to continue progressing the story or my character if things wipe? That should be an opt-in only. 3. Enemy AI is downright abysmal, even though there are some very unique enemy designs, they play horrible and don't react to you.4. Zones are repeated way too frequently and very quickly you will see the same area again, not as much variation as I would hope with such a large map. 5. There's a better game for each of the systems that this one is trying to do, and I would much rather play those instead. Overall, I more than likely won't continue, and I am not sure if the devs will be able to solve these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its moments of fun, especially in the early stages, but it falls short in several frustrating ways. The six-week server wipe cycle is a nightmare—it would be amazing to have a server that doesn’t wipe at all.Then there are the bugs and quality-of-life issues. For instance, locking keybinds is one of the most baffling decisions. If you’re making a game for PC, allow players the freedom to customize their controls—forcing a preset system is incredibly frustrating.Driving mechanics are another weak point. Even with max upgrades, vehicles feel clunky, and getting kicked out of your car or bike just because you drove through a shallow river is infuriating. Building is equally frustrating, with a clunky system that’s hard to manage.There are also gameplay limitations that make things unnecessarily difficult. For example, fighting a boss solo while still in a team is impossible—you’re forced to drag your friends into it, even if you just want to chat with them. The StarChrom shop has its own issues, like being unable to refund gear if you accidentally purchase the wrong item after a certain time.Finally, the game’s complexity can be overwhelming for new players. Without looking up optimal strategies, it’s easy to miss out on important benefits, which creates a steep learning curve that’s far from welcoming.This game has potential, but these issues make it hard to recommend in its current state. Ect Problems

_childDocuments_.review: At this point i'm four seasons in, i've played Manibus Novice, Hard, Prismverse Clash (PvP) and now Way of Winter 2 weeks in.Am i hitting burnout? Sure, i've had my fun with this game and while i want to continue playing, it's grinding me down with how little has actually improved of the core game.Don't get me wrong, the developers are putting in good effort to fix bugs and introduce QoL, new features that are cool but the problem is they always come half-baked and bugged laden, the newest scenario WoW is the biggest culprit with so many buggy map locations that include things like lava that can repeatedly kill you till you relog, invisible floating water bubbles that can also chain kill you, many poorly made geometry meshes that are glitchy to walk on, a handful of ziplines that lead in to dead ends making you fall off if you go on them, glitches bosses like Servitor that locks when with more than 1 person (They just fixed this, thankfully) and core issues like many new items not being available on the vending machine to trade and plenty of items not available on this server like apples causing people to use whatever method they can get their hands on to obtain them (Silver axes).The new tower function is just poorly thought out, it's easy to place one down and reserve a location (Which is a whole other bag of worms) But you can't control who places what inside, you also can't toggle oil or pollution fields so if one person sets it to research when no one wants it, you're done. the defense is also poorly done and i dread when the Chaosweavers spawn because it's just going to result in bases being wiped left and right due to poor spawn locations.But all this isn't even what the main problem is.There's little to no horizontal content at the end game, and buildcrafting basically just amounts to slotting the two obvious weapon and unique armor pieces together with the obvious mods and not much else, it's too inflexible and lacking in depth. These two things can keep a game going for ages, yet Once Human lacks them desperately, it doesn't help that in the recent update they introduced two new weapons with unique keywords for existing keywords but only they have them and the new uniques are basically made to function only with them.They NEED to update and re-balance older weapons to interact with new keywords, the builds need more depth other than more stats.As for horizontal content, they're in between a rock and a hard place, you don't want to make it required because that will drive away casuals, but they are reluctant to add cosmetics to normal events and silos etc because that's where they make their money. I personally think they should keep the wacky and out of norm cosmetics to the shop while feeding us normal, setting fitting cosmetics from gameplay. We should also get weapon attachment paints and potentially wraps, even colours for a potential dye system would be great.That's another thing- This game has an outdated cosmetic system that feels like it's a decade old, there is no actual dye system to change clothing colours, and the slots for cosmetics are limited heavily not allowing players to express themselves fully, i for one would be far more willing to purchase skins if i could change their colour to what's desired.Anyway, i do not recommend this game for those looking for something to keep coming back to season to season, there's little here other than the hampster wheel of buying more weapons for starchrom and following the potential powercreep. However if you just want to step in for a season or two of fun, go ahead, the game lasted that long for me and i had my fun, so you probably will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, I like to write reviews for games I feel are worthy of a review for either negative or positive. With that being said I think it's best to give my honest review of the game so far. Do I recommend this game? YES!! Here is why I think you should take a look at this game.- Lets start off with the character creator- the games character creation system is very well put together with all the things that you customize it's very fun. My only criticism is that the presets are all the same thing slightly. You can change it by customizing and playing 3 hours in the character creation system. But I think more presets would be nice. ALSO WARNING your character does not save if you plan on switching servers. Just keep that in mind. - Combat and kinda gameplay elements- this game with the melee combat is amazing the animations are fluid, the weapons feel weighty and overall I wouldn't expect a free to play game to have this much attention to detail in it's elements. It's not just the melee combat that feels good, movement in the water feels organic. Gun play in the game I feel could be better, there is some issues I personally find with it such as it not feeling quite right. There are two gun types that feels really good and that is the shotguns and hunting rifles. Those weapons feel really good to me anyway. The crafting system and getting materials for crafting is very fair and isn't super grindy which for a causal player like myself I love it. There is even little robots you can get that will get resources for you so you can enjoy other aspects of the game. Speaking of which.The world- The world and aesthetic of the game is so different from the typical survival game formula and I love it, like this is personal basis for sure but I am so sick of all the cookie cutter survival games with the settings and what not. I really enjoy the visuals of the game and whole world just feels lived in and it isn't dry. The one downside is that there is always bases everywhere but if you find a spot where there isn't really any bases it's very nice. Overall I just like the world it's cool and different. There is some elements of cookie cutter survival game in this game but it's not that bad. Base Building- The base building I wish there was more cosmetic options for the building materials personally like there is wallpapers and stuff. Some other options that are locked behind a paywall to get cool skins (which I did pay for) I just wish there was more free things. However if you like building houses in the sims this feels pretty much the same and there is a free camera so you get every angle. Which is so helpful. Story- The story from what I have played so far is pretty good I have no complaints really cinematics are really cool, I really like the soundtrack in the game. I am not that far in with the story though so I can't give it a full rating but so far I am not complaining. My overall thoughts on the game and response to other criticism: Overall I think I would rate the game a solid 8/10 I like it a lot there is some things I wish that were improved but it's not making me not want to play the game. I think the game is great and fun mainly for a causal player who likes survival games but hates the grind. This game just feels fair to players like myself. There is a lot of concerns people have from the ToS & EULA but if you actually read it. It only affects Asian countries so you should be fine if your playing literally anywhere else. Anyway if you made it this far in my review your probably hating your life for reading this but these are my thoughts on the game. Also if you find it helpful give it a rating so I can find validation for writing this. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Negative reviewing a game because it runs bad or is boring is one thing, spreading blatant misinformation is another. After reading through the privacy policy, they do have some strange practices, including needing to email their support to have them not distribute your info anymore, however the info they will have is limited. Everyone trying to make you believe the boogeyman is stealing your identity is misinformed. They saw "government issued id" and closed the privacy policy without ever getting to the "where laws require" part of the sentence. Your government id is only needed in areas where the law requires it to verify age, for example china. They cant get any information from you that you dont give them, or else this game would be a trojan, and steam would not allow it. The geolocation and ip part of the privacy policy is most likely used for their anticheat to ip ban cheaters, and the hardware serials part is most likely used for performance metrics, which nearly any online game company does. As for the crypto miner claims, i dont have any comment on that. That being said, i started the game and it maxxed out my cpu power. That might just be my computer being total dog, but scanning with my antivirus yielded no spooky results.Edit 1 (54 minutes play time): After reinstalling the game and giving it a second shot, the game booted up perfectly fine, with no excess draw from my cpu. At time of edit here's my current review. So far the selling point I've seen for this game was enemy design, and boy did they keep true with that. A lot of the enemies designs incorporate basic objects such as brief cases, flood lights, scarecrows, ect. I haven't seen much variety, however I'm sure that comes with more time as i play. Mini boss/Large enemies have dynamic weak points that trigger a stun animation and reveal more weak points once broken. The weak points are fairly obvious, with the ones I've seen being glowing purple sacks that count as head shots when hit. The combat feels intuitive, with melee combat being very heavy, though not overburdening as you can cancel attack animations with dodges at any time. Melee feels fluid with attacks being very momentum based, including allowing a shoulder bash when sprint attacking. I've only gotten my hands on the crossbow as a ranged weapon, but it feels good to aim both in third person and the optional first person aiming mode. The exp system feels on par with the rest of the game, with tech trees being very well outlined and intuitive. Base building feels very bare-bones at the moment, but again I'm sure that will improve as I progress through the skill trees. The only issue I've encountered with my limited playtime is base spot competition in PvE servers, with a lot of the land being dotted with bases, however that comes with the public servers in most games ie Ark. The exploration feels pretty nice, and so far the set pieces feel pretty fleshed out. Obviously draw your own conclusions about the game, whether you try it out yourself or watch youtubers play. TLDR; They cant get any information you dont give them, so dont give them any passwords, logins, or social media accounts and you dont have to worry about anything. Play the game if you want to, just be cautious. That goes for anything you do on the internet. Games fun tho, I do recommend for those who like these types of games. Review is negative to get it out to more people so they arent dissuaded by all of the people crying wolf.

_childDocuments_.review: I FOUND THIS ON YOUTUBE FROM A BIG YOUTUBER NAMED IGP SO THANK HIM FOR THIS INFO!!!!I want to clear up some misinformation regarding the privacy policy for Once Human that has a lot of people concerned currently.Firstly I want to say I totally get freaking out about it because it may be worded in a way that is alarming. Even I asked for clarification just to be safe because I didn't like what it seemed like it could mean, but now it makes much more sense and I'm here to get rid of that concern for you as well.As part of the privacy policy, it lists off all the potential pieces of information it may need. This list includes things like passports, government issued IDs, contact phone numbers, etc. It states the purpose of this information would be for things like age verification and correction of personal information, and only when required by law, so it depends on where you live if those things are ever required and even then it's not just because they are asking, it would be required by law for them to do so.But the key here is that it specifically states "recieve from you" as in the pieces of information you specifically provide to them on your own. The game and the company do not have the ability to just find your driver's license, passports, etc when you agree to their terms. It doesn't work that way.This is unfortunate because once you read it understanding this it makes complete sense and really it's actually pretty light on data collecting compared to many other games and companies, but now the internet is just spreading this nonsense without fully understanding it. But that's the way it is lolEither way, even after clarification, if these terms make you uncomfortable, you do not have to agree to them at all. That's entirely youre choice. But i just wanted to make sure everyone understood they aren't just getting full access to every piece of sensitive personal information you have.Also that "crypto-mining" claim is just absolutely absurd and there is no reason anyone should believe that nonsense lmao**From the Once Human team on Twitter:**"Dear Metas,Thank you for your attention and continued support of Once Human. We are truly grateful for all your feedback!We would like to take this opportunity to address concerns we’ve seen regarding the game’s privacy policy and confusion about the use of the NetEase Launcher.Once Human takes our users’ data privacy very seriously. We would only use personal data if we have a legitimate legal basis, such as providing requested services or acting with your expressed consent. We will only use your data lawfully and reasonably and in accordance with local legal compliance requirements, while practicing the data privacy principles such as data minimization, purpose limitation, and transparency. We appreciate and welcome any and all feedback given by our players to help us improve.Some players have expressed concern about the NetEase Launcher. This game launch platform offers broader access to games published by NetEase Games. Like some of our industry peers who run multiple games simultaneously, we hope that the launcher can provide convenient access to multiple NetEase's games for our users. However, please note you would only be required to download the launcher if you download Once Human from our official website. Players who play the game from Steam or Epic will NOT need to download or use the launcher.We sincerely apologize for any confusion or uncertainty experienced by our players. We hope this clarifies the above and please rest assured that we will continue to maintain a transparent, player-friendly gaming environment, not only because it’s required by law, but also because it’s the right thing to do.If you have further questions or concerns towards our privacy policy or game-related issues, please contact us at . You could also check the FAQ  for more detailed information.Once Human Team"

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human is a standout in the crowded genre of survival crafting games. From the moment you step into its post-apocalyptic world, you’re greeted with a unique blend of action, survival, and MMORPG elements that keep you engaged for hours on end. The game’s setting, revolving around an alien infestation, offers a refreshing twist compared to the usual zombie or nuclear apocalypse scenarios.One of the most impressive aspects of Once Human is its creature design. The alien organisms, known as Deviations, are both bizarre and fascinating. These creatures can be captured and used in various ways, adding a strategic layer to the gameplay. Whether it’s using them in combat or having them assist with base chores, they bring a delightful unpredictability to the game.The crafting and building mechanics are intuitive and rewarding. The ability to repair and upgrade your weapons and armor adds depth to the gameplay, encouraging you to experiment with different gear before committing resources to crafting your own. The game also supports both solo and multiplayer modes, making it accessible for all types of players.Visually, Once Human is stunning. The environments are richly detailed, and the creature designs are both grotesque and captivating. The game’s atmosphere is enhanced by its sound design, which perfectly complements the eerie and often tense moments you encounter.Overall, Once Human is a must-play for fans of survival crafting games. Its unique setting, engaging gameplay mechanics, and beautiful visuals make it a standout title in the genre. Whether you’re a solo player or enjoy teaming up with friends, Once Human offers an experience that’s both challenging and immensely satisfying

_childDocuments_.review: It has come to my attention that they intent to wipe everyone's progress every 6 weeks and call it a rogue like. There is nothing, NOTHING about this game's mechanics or game play that screams rogue like at all. I'm going to continue playing under the assumption that they will come to their senses and not delete everyone's progress. If the game is the exact same after the wipe and their rogue like "seasons" is some superficial bull crap, I'll never touch this game again.Now for the game itself:There are interesting boss fights, some of the side quests are actually fun and have good rewards. The POI's (Points of Interests) are overall very well done. The base building and crafting are serviceable, the deviants that you can put around your base are cute and a fun addition. Combat is alright, could be a bit tighter but open world multiplayer shooters all share that problem. Enemy AI isn't great, their responds time or radius is laughable "did you hear that" as you brutally smack down the guy next to them. (Side note: It's rather strange that your melee weapon feels more powerful than the literal guns you are shooting but that's whatever.)I've only encountered a few dynamic events, the one where it became heavy thick fog and zombies started to rise from the ground stands out as a neat experience. I would encourage for more dynamic events, they are fun. (except for the PvP ones, there was this truck and when I got it to a halt a jellyfish started to attach itself to me and I had to hold it but then a level 50 player showed up and one shot me, that wasn't fun at all. PvP has it's place but I had no idea I was getting in a PvP event in the middle of a PvE zone)In conclusion: If they continue with their seasonal resets, play 1 "season" to experience the fun and interesting content this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 11/22/2024: Played this game on release and honestly, for a free game this game had me absolutely shocked at how much fun it was. After playing it for a while, it did become a bit repetitive but I still enjoyed it for the most part. The lag was almost non-existent in the first month but gradually got worse as the weeks went on, eventually becoming kind of irritating during world boss battles.  I still feel this game is worth playing because it is fun and  unique, however, more recently there have been a few cheaters on there and I don't know if that's why the game has heavier lag issues than it did on release or if that's just server issues in general, but, they're both problems that need taken care of if they want this game to thrive...which, from my knowledge, they're working on it so that's good! Overall, the game is fun but it definitely needs to focus less on the 300 dollar loot crates and more on optimization and lag. Otherwise, this is a solid game that you can pop on for a couple hours, loot and shoot, decorate your base, and then hop off. The different scenarios are nice. Something for (almost) everyone. I'll probably come back to this game in a few months to see if they've made any more improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Once Human is a beautifully designed game with deep mechanics and dynamic content, perfect for dedicated players, but may be too time-intensive for casual gamers like myself.I played a good amount of time on Once Human. This is a very well-designed game. The visuals are stunning, and the mechanics are both deep and engaging. The game's design shows great thought and effort. There are tons of skills, missions, equipment, gear, weapons, buildings, and variants to collect and progress. The public events and seasonal updates keep things fresh and exciting.As a casual gamer, I struggle to dedicate time to Once Human. The game feels like it needs a full commitment to keep up. There's an underlying sense of FOMO for the whole game. Plus, the wipes and new seasons bring constant changes. This is great for players who can dive deep. But, it may not suit someone like me. I want a more laid-back gaming experience. I prefer lower stakes for missing a few weeks of gaming sessions.It's a bummer. I'd love to explore Once Human more. But the constant updates and need to keep up make it a tough commitment. For those who have the time and enjoy a game that evolves and grows, this is definitely a fantastic choice. Unfortunately, it may not make my regular playlist. This game is perfect for those who desire depth and complexity.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and decently put together but if you play a decent amount of time you'll be out of things to do and waiting. Locking elements of the season week by week is silly and allows you to just forget the game and not come back. Then there's the resetting every season, who wants to go through it again? Game needs a re-do on how seasons work to be fun. $50 for a building preset is insane even if you can use it on up to 4 other friends' bases (many folks don't have friends and would be fine with a cheaper version they can't share.  The transport system with teleporting around is so overly complicated that it will just annoy you, especially the cool-down to your friends' bases, unnecessary. Should just be instant.A LOT of players seem to join a new server, then make a bunch of alt accounts to friend them and use their bases as jump spots, further taking up slots on a server. And if people get bored, they can't be replaced and that server will just suffer if it loses enough people to do weeklies. Oh and you have to be there right when weeklies reset or no one does them.Interesting game, it was fun until I learned it all. It reminds me of Fallout 76 without anything to collect with plans or new things to your base, just unlocking and waiting. Like New World, server configuration choices will hurt the player base and drive folk away without a way to visit other servers at the very least. Sucks when you run into a friend playing, chance you're on the same server is zero.

_childDocuments_.review: Review: Once Human (Updated 27th Sep. 2024)Positive Points:Building System: The building mechanics have seen significant improvements, and they’re now close to perfection for a base version. It provides a solid foundation that can be further expanded upon in future updates.Season and Change System: The implementation of the season system is impressive, although the seasons could be a bit longer. The changes in the environment and gameplay tied to these seasons add a dynamic layer to the experience.Overall Gameplay: The game itself is quite decent. While graphics aren't a top priority for me, the visual elements are adequate for the experience. The gameplay and controls meet expectations, similar to other games in the genre—nothing groundbreaking, but nothing overly complex either.Storyline: The storyline is decent for this type of game, though it leaves a lot of questions unanswered. I’m eager to dive deeper into the lore, but reading through the available content doesn’t offer much clarity on the game’s backstory and events.Negative Aspects (Not Deal-Breakers):Repetitive Gameplay: As it stands, the gameplay can feel repetitive, but I’m hopeful that this will improve with future updates and content patches.Community: The in-game community is generally good, but as with any online game, there are some trolls and leechers that can detract from the experience. It’s not a huge issue, but it’s something to be aware of.Critical Negative Aspects:Developer Responsiveness: It’s disappointing that the developers seem uninterested in community feedback. Despite numerous bug reports and suggestions, it feels like they aren’t paying attention. It’s clear that they demonstrate a lack of interest in addressing important bugs, and many suggestions simply end up ignored.Content Development Focus: The developers place a heavy emphasis on cosmetic items for both houses and clothing. Legendary-quality clothing is hidden behind loot boxes with abysmal drop rates, which feels like a customer-unfriendly strategy aimed at maximizing profits rather than enhancing the player experience. Recently, they introduced the Electro Bash Self-Selection loot box, which could cost players up to €600 if they wish to collect all the included items. The manipulative nature of this system strongly resembles gambling, especially for younger players. I’ve reported these loot boxes to local gambling authorities, as the signs of gambling mechanics are blatantly clear. Supporting a developer is one thing, but this level of greed is simply unacceptable.Performance Issues: Since the last major update in September, server performance has steadily declined. There are delays of up to 5-6 seconds before enemies finally drop dead. Additionally, I’ve experienced situations where enemies are dead for over 10 seconds, their corpses despawn, and I still receive ghost hits from nowhere, which is extremely frustrating. The severe server issues also make it very difficult to effectively use builds like Unstable Bomber, Frost Vortex, or Shrapnel.Development Priorities: It’s incredibly frustrating that the developers seem to be putting 0% effort into real game development and 100% into loot boxes and other cash shop items. Instead of meaningful content or bug fixes, they continue to prioritize monetization, leaving the game stagnant and unbalanced.NPC Issues: NPCs have been glitching through walls since CBT 2, often moving without making any noise, which breaks immersion. It’s frustrating that such a fundamental issue hasn’t been addressed.Severe Concern: Support SystemCustomer Support: The support system is, in my opinion, severely lacking. Given that this is a live service game, strong support is crucial, but it’s been a letdown. Payment issues are ignored, and other problems receive generic, copy-pasted responses. The support system is chaotic, and they even demand a rating after every single interaction. Having worked in customer support for over 15 years, I can confidently say this is the worst I’ve encountered.Final Verdict:Due to the current state of the game and the developers' increasing focus on manipulative loot boxes and cash grabs, I’m giving Once Human a strong thumbs down. The game is not only suffering from a lack of meaningful updates and performance issues, but it also seems determined to exploit players through expensive gambling-like mechanics, as demonstrated by the Electro Bash Self-Selection loot box. This latest system crosses a line, and I firmly believe that it should be shut down.

name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition
detailed_description: Relive the glory of Stronghold, the original BAFTA-nominated real-time strategy game, with this new definitive edition of the classic 'castle sim'. Witness the game that started it all, carefully rebuilt using the source artwork, remastered music, returning voice talent and veteran developers of the first entry in this legendary series. UNITE A BROKEN REALM Welcome to the fractured, war-torn frontier of medieval England. With the King betrayed by his treacherous lords and a realm on the brink of collapse, take control of scattered forces and reunite your kingdom against the monstrous Rat, Pig, Snake and Wolf! Strike down each villainous Lord in missions ranging from breaking sieges and capturing enemy castles to building epic fortresses and repelling enemy assaults. Test the limits of your strategic mind with castle assaults and grand banquets in military and economic campaigns. Dive into classic RTS and city builder gameplay now elevated with remade graphics, community requested features and remastered music from series maestro Robert L. Euvino. Gather resources, construct mighty castles, protect your townsfolk, manage your gold, raise armies and wage all out war! A LEGEND RETOLD Building on its 20 year legacy, Stronghold: Definitive Edition features two classic campaigns told across 26 missions, alongside fresh single player content in the form of a new narrative campaign designed by Firefly Studios founders Simon Bradbury and Eric Ouellette. Exclusive to the definitive edition, this new 14 mission campaign sees players march across the devastated English hinterland in search of Sir Longarm's captured kin, before venturing beyond the story in a challenging new historical 'Castle Trail' of 10 unique scenarios. With remade artwork, a higher fidelity soundtrack, full Steam multiplayer support for 8 players, Steam Workshop, modernised gameplay and more, Stronghold: Definitive Edition is the ultimate way to experience the game that started it all. Your kingdom awaits! NEW FEATURES ZOOM INTO NEW VISUALS remade by the original artists with improved animations, textures and lighting. REMATCH CLASSIC VILLAINS as you hunt The Rat and The Snake in a challenging new 14 mission campaign. BATTLE OLD FRIENDS on Steam with 8 player multiplayer support and extra maps on which to wage war! RELIVE HISTORY in a new Castle Trail with 10 challenging siege scenarios and famous historical fortresses. LOSE YOURSELF in a remastered soundtrack, with fresh recordings from some of the game's original voice actors. CREATE, SHARE & ENJOY new Stronghold community content with Steam Workshop support.

_childDocuments_.review: It's 2001, you come back from school. It's Friday, so you have a free evening. You launch Stronghold, the new game of the little-known company Firefly Studios. The game runs with 20 FPS at best on your Pentium II 233 Mhz. Sometimes it's 15 FPS or lower when there are more units on the screen. But it doesn't matter, the important thing is you can just run this great game on your computer. And now, 22 years later, the magic returns. For me, it's a perfect remaster. No big changes, some small QoL improvements, a new campaign, new maps, improved textures, flying cows in high resolution, improved map editor. And integration with Steam Workshop, which already become a source of nice new maps (anyone else remember this site for original games?  And more FPS this time. The finished remaster (looking at you Konami) with already announced updates for a reasonable price (looking at you Konami again). Totally worth buying. And already waiting for Stronghold Crusader Definitive Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Stronghold 22 years ago on its debut release, and as I sit here now reviewing the Definitive Edition I can’t help but feel immense pride to see Firefly Studios still actively flourishing – in the first 72 hours of release it had sold 100,000 copies and had a peak of 9,672 concurrent players on Steam.Firefly was originally conceived in 1999, consisting of just two co-creators Simon Bradbury and Eric Ouellette, who spent their first two years together creating a game that aimed to merge both the City Builder and Real-Time Strategy genres. They accomplished this in 2001 with their first release – Stronghold, which released to critical acclaim and commercial success. The game became a surprise hit and due to its popularity led to several sequels including the fan favourite Stronghold Crusader in 2002. Both of these titles use a 2D isometric game engine which is comfortably the best way to experience the series, the Definitive Edition uses the Unity engine as a wrapper for the original game. The Stronghold series has been tried and tested over the years through different pathways, however sticking close to the original blueprint is what makes it (in my opinion) most grand. A blend of British charm and replayability made this series such an instant hit, combined with innovative castle building and visuals. The Definitive Edition enhances the original experience with remade artwork, modernised gameplay, high fidelity sounds and workshop support. The visuals are so crisp and smooth, like rewatching an 80s/90s program in HD. It’s absolutely fantastic. I will never tire from watching routine work processes in Stronghold – let’s take the art of making bread: watching workers harvest wheat crop, who then move the wheat to the keeps stockpile. The young workers then take the wheat from the stockpile and transfer it to the mill. Once flour is milled, the young workers take the bags of flour back to the stockpile. The bakers then pickup the flour and transfer it back to their bakery, where you’re able to watch them create food for the castle, before being placed into the local granary for storage/consumption. What I’m describing is the absolute charm of the game: watching the beautiful synchronisation of routine jobs throughout the castle is nothing short of scintillating and it is through this charm that makes the game richly excel. The Definitive Edition includes a new 14 mission campaign, along with a new historical ‘Castle Trail’ which sets 10 unique scenarios to delve into. The campaign itself was fine, I preferred the Castle Trail as it proved to be more challenging (I’m looking at  Heuneburg) nonetheless my entire experience so far has been incredibly rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: Look, it's a pretty old game. I'm writing this review for you guys - not the game or devs. I'm writing it in the hopes that on those days when you just don't feel like playing the latest AAA (or indie) trending game, you might consider giving this classic a try. It really is worth the chance, and if you can get it for under 10 bucks, it's a steal. And I truly think most people will like this one a lot.Like strategy games? Like City/castle builders? You need to buy and play this if you never have. And if you've played it in the past, you owe it to yourself to play it again. Is it the type of the game that will be your top ten favorite? No, probably not. But it absolutely will give you dozens to hundreds of hours of fun. It's virtually bug free, being from the era when games were completed before they were released. Everything works. Maybe the UI isn't super modern, the graphics (although updated since the original release) are mediocre, and the music is... the music is better not mentioned. The story line is lighthearted/silly and relatively simple. You're not going to find any masterpieces of story writing, or outstanding characters that you think of fondly 10 years from now. That's not what this game is, and it doesn't try to be.What this game is, is a very straight forward city/castle sim and strategy game. You gather resources that you use to build your defenses, your industry, train troops, and keep your peasants happy. Nothing is super complex about the systems. There's no research trees, or requirements you need to reach to unlock things  (though the campaign unlocks new buildings, resources, and weapons as you progress). Build wood or stone walls towers and gates in any design you wish. Make multi-leveled defenses, and employ designs that are segmented and redundant to help fend off waves of enemies. Train archers, spear men, mace men, pike men, crossbowmen, swordsmen, and even mounted knights to defend your castle and settlement. If that's not enough break out the siege weapons like catapults, trebuchets, ballistas; and traps, boiling oil, and war dogs.Some of the missions have you go on the offense, taking a limited number of troops and engines and assault the enemy, but for the most part, you're the one building and defending (in the campaign.) Additionally, there are some extra campaigns that add some newer features, buildings, and challenges - new maps, new tactics, and dozens of more hours of game time. If you decide you just want to design and build your dream castle and throw endless enemies at it to see how your design fairs, you can do that too. I hope that if you decide to give this one a chance you find it as much fun as I did. It really is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original game, then you will probably will be buying this. But would I recommend this game to a newcomer? Absolutely not. And here are the reasons why:The good:* Original campaign in its full glory is still good and unique, every mission feels different and the new textures made it even better.* Auto market got added to the game, which is massive QOL improvement.* Troops can now be trained more than one at a time with ctrl and shift clicks, which is really good.* They added additional animated character for DLC campaigns.The bad:* DLC campaigns are done very poorly, the story does not progress in logical order. One of the first missions in rat campaign gives you all of the units you want and then you start going backwards from there. And it surprisingly felt that way for all of the 4 DLC jewel campaigns. They did not listen to their playerbase feedback about it.* DLC campaigns lack cinematics of your opponents, the enemy troops just keep coming without any taunts like in original campaign, missed opportunity.* The scripts in DLC campaigns are bad, because there is none...* DLC campaigns did not take into account replayability. The maps are small and your castle can't be placed on different locations, which makes the games play exactly the same all the time.* Lots of the maps in DLC campaigns were actually running from point A to point B, it was overused and miserable experience. Putting hundreds of wolfs on the map while they are bugged and your troops wont even attack them is not considered fun.* New maps felt unbalanced and untested, mostly dull and boring, that you don't even want to play again through again.* New economic missions are actually really heavily combat oriented. They did exactly the opposite of what they were supposed to do.* Bugs from original game are still not fixed and quality of life improvements from crusader are not brought over. For example, you still can't click on items on your stockpile to easily open market.* No skirmish mode. They told from the beginning, that they would not make one for this game, but they should have, even if it took longer and would have made the game higher in price.* Multiplayer is literal 1/10 experience, don't even think about buying this game to play with friends.* No new additional items added to the game, everything is exactly the same from gameplay wise. They could have added some new items only for DLC and kept the original campaign as is for the sake of keeping the gameplay exactly the same for it.* Second castle trail maps were done in a way that you actually can't go through the walls at some locations, which is clearly because of laziness. Instead of making some weak points harder to attack, they simply played with terrain so that you can destory the wall, but can't go in from that location. It was used in multiple castle trail maps.* The newly added animated character always had the same animation, made it dull. And he was used mostly in the begging of the mission at the same time when you are told "Place your granary", which overlapped and felt like another untested product of laziness.* Still no hiscores in the list of missions, so you have no idea how well you did in them afterwards. Doesn't tempt you to replay and do better than last time, another missed opportunity.Summary:The graphics changes and some quality of life improvements they did were good, but the new jewel, economic and castle trails maps were quite poorly done. I have seen a lot more meaningful community made maps. It feels like every new map was done in a hurry and they felt boring and dull.

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasure it was to walk down memory lane with Stronghold: Definitive Edition. Even more refreshing to see the game with improved graphics. High definition indeed.Those familiar with the first need no lengthy explainer. As a veteran Stronghold player, I make note of some of the changes made which are either an improvement or hindrance (in my opinion) to the game.For starters, the mass train/buy/sell at the barracks/market using click+Shift is a handy tool, as is left click+Ctrl to copy+paste existing structures. Similarly, zooming in/out with the mouse wheel saves having to right-click all the time. The option to magnify/minify the minimap is another good addition to S:DE. It is only a pity that you can't zoom in the game up-close, so as to better appreciate the remastered sprites, as they are quite well done.Perhaps the best feature is the doubling of the unit/building limits. Firefly mentioned they might (fingers crossed) increase it even further. Still, some things remain unchanged, and I'm not referring to the game mechanics. The AI still takes a while to respond with taunts or insults after defeating them in the campaign. We should also have been able to click+drag for the killing pits as we do with the pitch ditch, since individually clicking can become annoying.Firefly also ought to have enabled building when paused, which, although not a feature in the original Stronghold (instead first introduced in Stronghold Crusader), would have been useful instead of having to slow down the game speed.Speaking of, I noticed that S:DE's game speed, even at 90, is comparatively slower than the original game. Whether this is due to the reworked system or otherwise, I cannot say. Meanwhile, I was amused to discover that Firefly removed the old bug (for a lack of a better term) wherein if you have full tavern coverage which gives you 8 popularity, you can still retain peasants without food/taxes as the no food penalty was -7.Concerning the DLCs, I must say they are excellently designed, and the pricing quite affordable, even for those whose currencies are not as strong as the pound. The missions to capture the keep or to reach the flag at the other end of the map are especially challenging. Even holding against enemy sieges can be nigh impossible. The only drawback is that save for one mission, you can't build moats, while training knights are limited to two or three missions. I gather that S:DE has been well-received, and moving forward, I hope that Firefly will eventually be able to include maps bigger than the current maximum size of 400x400. I imagine that for a game over two decades old now, this should not be too much of an issue.Though they've said they won't be providing mod support, considering that this is a Definitive Edition, perhaps some modders with the know-how can do so of their own volition. Most importantly, many players, including myself, fervently hope that a Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition may come to pass. Perhaps with the Extreme version included as well. But only time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Not long ago I was talking with a friend and the name Stronghold came up in conversation, and no more than a few days later Stronghold: Definitive Edition was announced. Our surprise was tremendous, and of course I had to play this edition. FireFly Studios once again puts us at the head of a kingdom, in this strategy and castle sim game, with robust and polished mechanics over the course of twenty years, which in my opinion stand out from the rest of the titles in the genre. This version adds a new game mode, an additional campaign, Steam Workshop integration and multiplayer, among other things. Honestly, it's a great game, and if that wasn't enough, they already have content planned for the future.Starting with the classic campaign, we’ll be located in a fictional medieval Britain, and we’ll be put in the role of a feudal lord fighting for the unification of the country. We’ll face a series of missions of progressive difficulty, and the plot will be told to us little by little. Among challenging and varied objectives, we’ll be introduced to the iconic main enemies: The Rat, the Snake, the Pig and the Wolf; and overthrowing them one by one will be our goal.On the other hand, the new campaign is recommended for veterans of the franchise, and will take us through the fields of a devastated England while we seek to free a fair maiden. This story presents us with new and challenging missions that will test our tactical and resource management skills. Perhaps for some it will be interesting to see the difference between the old and modern direction, and I can say that even separated by so many years they feel very cohesive; as far as I saw, of course, because the truth is that this campaign is pretty difficult for me.On the gameplay and accessibility side, the game has modernized some things, like controls (blessed WASD) and quality of life aspects, but beyond that there are mechanics and details that, for me, make Stronghold stand out and separate it from its peers. For example, here it’s not enough to just build barracks and hire units, no; in this game you have to hire blacksmiths and fletchers to prepare the weapons, then take them to the armory and then hire the relevant unit. It seems a bit complex and can be a bit irritating under pressure, but it's a bit more realistic and I like it a lot.Another thing that I have always found wonderful is that stone walls not only serve to protect our buildings from enemy armies, but our units can also climb them and defend from the heights. Ballisate can also be built on towers, bracers can be placed for archers to rain fire on infantry as well as to ignite the pitch fields, and we can even place units with oil pots to burn alive those unfortunate enough to get close to the walls. As you can see, the game revolves a lot around sieges, so there are not only measures to defend these fortresses, but also to attack them. There are units that make it easier for others to climb the walls, such as soldiers carrying ladders or siege towers, classic catapults, or trebuchets that can even throw cows and leave a very lethal cloud of pestilence (and a very beloved detail of the franchise, as strange as it may sound). It's a game that really provides an experience focused on the conquest and defense of castles, very tactical, and it feels great.For those who are already familiar with the saga, this edition also has a new game mode: the "Castle Trail", a chain of ten missions of siege or defense of historic castles, and extremely challenging. We also have an improved map editor, Steam integration for multiplayer (which I admit I didn't get to try, because I couldn't find a group the times I tried), and the Steam Workshop to download maps created by the community. I downloaded a very cool one of Minas Tirith! Although I was beaten to a pulp.I can't leave without talking about the audiovisual section, since they made an effort to give it a more modern and detailed look, like the interfaces, but without losing that "old school" vibe so special of the saga. And the music was updated with higher fidelity tracks, which I also appreciate since I really love the melodies that have adorned these games over the years. I understand they also brought back vocal actors from the original Stronghold, a very nice touch.In closing, I wanted to say that it has things that really stuck with me from the first time I played it, who knows how many years ago, and Stronghold: Definitive Edition took me on a nostalgic journey that made me relive those moments, back to when I played it on my brother's PC and in simpler times... but I'll stop there before we all get depressed. The charm of Stronghold is back stronger than ever, and it shows that it was a good game twenty years ago and still is today. I think it's a nice entry point into the RTS genre, and certainly recommended for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with this game. It was one of my first video-games. It holds up so well. Sure I may be a little blinded by nostalgia, but the core gameplay is still *really* good. Same way StarCraft (1) is very dated at this point but still holds up super well. Now is this game like starcraft? No. It's very slow paced, and could best be described as a castle defense and siege scenario game. Skirmish matches came in crusader (which I desperately hope gets the definitive edition treatment, the HD is just zoomed out), so sadly as far as I know you can't skirmish against the AI. There are plenty of scenarios and battles which are essentially near enough to a skirmish that I find it satisfying. The graphics are obviously dated but incredibly charming. It's that late 90s early 00s 3d-like sprite art style that doesn't so much look ugly as it does stylistic/dated (you can tell the map poly counts are very late 90s lol). I think it looks good. I haven't even touched any of the community stuff yet. Suffice it to say there's more than enough content here for the money. If you have nostalgia for the game, it's a must buy imo. If you're just an RTS fan, you might enjoy it. Like I said it's very slow paced compared to most RTS games I find. If you like castle builders than you'll probably enjoy this, but it is heavily combat focused in most modes. It's a good game. If it at all looks interesting to you from the screenshots and gameplay trailers, go for it. You won't regret it (and if you do you'll realize long before the refund timer is up I'd guess)

_childDocuments_.review: +Sound Design, 10/10 You dont have to visualize much as this game makes excellent use of your ability to HEAR whats going on, sound effects a distinct, and you can tell whats going on without needing to see it; this is what developers should be shown and forced to listen to as a lesson on how to do excellent sound effects.+User interface controls are excellent+Custom campaign is excellent, there are no skirmishes, its mostly defense missions and siege missions, which I enjoy.+This sound track is phenomenal, i don't think ive played a game that goes this hard on the flute and clarinet, Castle Jam by Robert L. Euvino is a must listen to if you want to hear what some of the best composed music that encapsulates the medieval era.+Balanciing your economy with Alcohol, Religion, and "Good things" to be able to raise your taxes is just such a fun gameplay loop on the economy side to help you earn constant money so you can afford your army. The amount of people a tavern can provide alcohol to is limited, so 1 tavern wont provide as much benefit to your popularity if you have 60 people vs 30, so the solution is to build two tavens, this example shows that as your castle increases in size so does the need of buildings to accommodate the extra populace; lest your popularity increases will drop.-Pathing is a little bad at times but hey its from 2001, get over it.TLDR: Brilliantly designed game with ASMR soundtrack, brilliant U.i, beautiful sprite work, tons of availible content for seige or defense lovers, no skirmish mode so if you want that go play Stronghold Crusader.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this definitely takes me back to the good ole' days of this game, however, Firefly needs to do some more work. I feel really bad giving this a bad review but the game needs to be fixed. I will be happy to change my review once the product owner and dev team fix a few things and add some additional features. Here's what Firefly needs to do in order to give fans a Minimum Lovable Product:1. Multiplayer games ABSOLUTELY NEED TO SHOW PING - we are almost in 2024 and playing games with people far away. Showing ping will prevent us from starting games with laggers/bad connections. That is a quick patch/fix and will improve the experience of many players. It may even solve the lag issue if we prevent it in the first place.2. Allow buildings to be placed where peasants/soldiers are in the space. Modern RTS games allow this and it shouldn't be too hard to code an update.3. The developers need to figure out why there is still bad lag and drop outs even after recent patches. There are many RTS games where this isn't an issue in 2023 so please figure it out and investigate. A re-release means you actually work to re-release and modernize code. If the lag is a player host issue, figure out a way to improve the code and make it more efficient.4. Multiplayer staging screen should show map download progress indicator to both players and admin5. Multiplayer needs more options as to what is permitted/not permitted. It should allow the admin to turn on/off mangonels, onagers, certain infantry weapon classes, walls, etc. otherwise everyone is just working off of honor system/a gentlemen's agreement6. Multiplayer needs to add an option of PT (Peacetime) in the game so nobody can attack until X min (20 min, 30 min, 60 min, etc) I love the game but you can't just put out a game 20 years later and try and collect holiday gift money without "modernizing" the experience.
