_childDocuments_.review: I was having a conversation with some friends recently about games that you could potentially dump hours into and defend from the influx of digital pitchforks of the internet, but there was a catch: the game had to be considered “not great.”  It’s easy to defend your Halo 3’s or your favorite Final Fantasy, but it’s a much more interesting conversation when you have a game like Syphon Filter: The Omega Strain that was critically panned as average and honestly doesn’t play well, but dammit, I love the game and I will fight people who seek to slander its name.  These games are always a weird anomaly, especially for reviewers, as how do you punch down on a game you are for the most part enjoying?  After putting around 10 hours into it, RKGK is taking me down this very interesting road.RKGK at its core is a collect-a-thon platformer with speed-infused techniques and combat.  Each level has a whole bunch of collectibles, objectives, and enemies to set up your next few minutes however you want to spin it.  Your main objectives are to find Mr. Buff’s, the evil B Corp’s head honcho, controlling screens and slathering your graffiti of choice to rid Cap City’s citizens of the mind-controlling schemes keeping them in check.  Valah’s movement and weapon of choice is the same paint used to deface the drab and deterring environment, as you’ll slide, slice, and dice through terrain and enemies alike to reach Mr. Buff and end his reign of terror.Cap City is broken down into 6 areas, with around 5 levels and a boss fight in each.  Levels are packed with things to collect: mainly graffiti cans to spend on murals and coins to increase your points and to spend on customizable items.  The couple dozen graffiti pieces that you’ll tag through Cap City are such a visual treat.  The different styles and ideas that come to life with the 3D-tooled pieces are eye-popping in their visual aspect and are sure to wow in a few places.  Tagging screens throughout the stages net you necessary progress to grant you access to boss arenas, and completing level objectives nets you Ghosts, which are a special currency that can also be found in secret areas within levels.  These are used alongside coins to unlock a multitude of items like outfits, graffiti pieces, different spray colors, and much more.  I really enjoyed the little easter egg nods to popular pop-culture pieces within the different colorways for Valah’s outfits and the fact you can mix and match “premium” Ghost-bought outfits with color-changed coin-bought outfits: something that should be doable in more games.Levels start small to grasp the basic mechanics and grow to some pretty hefty stages in regards to verticality and specificity.  Combat is simple, revolving around hitting with ground or air attacks, but enemies will restrict the moves you can do against them to avoid button-mashing every enemy.  Combo-ing multiple moves together, collecting items and defeating enemies, will put Valah in Defacer Mode: a special mode that allows you to move faster and can also truck any enemy that stands in your way so long as you don’t take any damage.  Defacer is key for the speedier objectives which we’ll go over later.The issue with platformers that introduce a quality of speed within their repertoire is that their game can feel awfully slow when not always in 4th gear, and RKGK suffers from this.  The initial run of the game’s levels is more focused on spraying graffiti, collecting coins, and finding the hidden secrets throughout, and this style of traversing the levels can feel molasses-like in its pace, making 6-8 minute levels feel like full-length episodes.  Combining this with a rather forgettable plot, the short campaign, which can be completed in around a movie’s time if done expeditiously, absolutely drags throughout the first run and is a tough sell to drudge through.This hits even harder with some of the later levels and bosses.  The interesting mechanics of some levels get drowned out with the need for absolute traffic jams of enemy placement.  There are objectives necessary to defeat a certain number of enemies or to collect every coin in a level but you’ll run into a few spots where your initial thought is, “Nuh uh,” and proceed to go back to it later.  With enemies that become invincible if not dealt with within a certain amount of time to constantly shooting enemies to adding in the normal grunt work and slapping them all together is not a test of skill but more of patience as the death tolls will get higher when the odds are just mercilessly stacked on you.  The final boss is guilty on a grand scale of this and is not a boss that I’m wanting to go back multiple times to master.But once you get through the initial campaign, learn all of RKGK’s movement tech, and toss aside the need to see the game through to its ending: there are points where this game absolutely clicks.  The time trials provided on each level are intensely gratifying when you hit the near-perfect lines needed to obtain the gold ranking, and putting together a top-of-the-line run to achieve an S rank is a breath of fresh air knowing you did everything needed on the level at a blistering pace.  Just taking each level in, learning a good path, and just nailing it makes you wonder why RKGK added the collectibles to begin with when the sense of speed when doing everything right is up and beyond better than its initial approach.  This second level of gameplay almost, almost makes the first part worth it, but it’s also immensely frustrating that this amount of quality in terms of mechanics and pace is buried behind what’s at surface level.In my opinion, RKGK is not great.  There’s a problematic line between adding many things and doing them all okay when you could shave off the edges and polish what could be great, and the game as a whole carries a heavy burden with the stuffing of genre staples.  But I can’t shake the urge to learn another level and try to high-tail it as fast as my fingers can allow me because getting S Ranks is a drug I didn’t know I needed.  Come to think of it: those small, fleeting, colorful moments surrounded by the melancholic mediocrity enveloping it all is very on the nose if you ask Valah and her time in Cap City.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the concept and the design of the main character, but it never really comes together.  It's less than the sum of it's parts.The characters, writing and presentation is aggressively boring.  The movement is pretty wonky and slippery.  Once you adjust you can get a good flow going but it never becomes all that fun and I rarely felt that zen you get from the best arcade or platform style games this one models itself after.It's not a bad game, but I really cant recommend it.  It doesn't excel at anything and there are much better games to spend your time and money on.  I'd really like to see the devs take another crack at this idea though.  Maybe this could have been a good game if theyd been afforded more time or money to further refine it.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really needs that neutral review. I don't wanna sht on the game, it's not bad per se, but man is it boring. I for one have seen more then enough and I'm refunding.The style is cool, music is cool, but the gameplay is just booooring. _childDocuments_.review: Game's fun. A mix of a lot of different platformers like Solar Ash, Jak and Daxter, Super Mario Sunshine. What it ISN'T is like Jet Set Radio. At all. Yes, you paint graffiti... but you don't really. Not like in those games. Even simpler than JSRF which removed any directional input. Graffiti is simply an art style choice and an objective; You will collect spray cans throughout each level and if you have enough cans to "complete" that particular graffiti it is one button press and you move on. Regardless, it's still fun, still has cool art and all that. I'd say boss fights and anything where combat is forced really bogs it down though. You spend most of your time avoiding enemies and just navigating around them to spray graffiti which usually destroys all the enemies in an area. Boss fight sections often have waves of enemies you need to get through and they're just increasingly annoying as you go. I understand their inclusion for a change of pace but it's still just more annoying than anything to deal with. Main game is fun. Boss fights are not.Interested in this as a speed game but wondering what tech will be found for movement because the "fast" movement the game wants you to do (surfing and spamming paint) isn't fun.There's also tons of content here as far as completionists go. Every level has speed, enemy, coin, graffiti, ghosts, deathless, and S rank goals. It will take dedication I probably don't have to complete the game with S rank on every level.Customization is cool but I wish there was more of it. As it is, most of the customization is palette swaps of the default gear or joke costumes which just aren't my style. I typically don't play games for their story and this was no different. Nothing really pulling me in. Don't feel bad if you wanna skip all the cutscenes.the important bit is that the moment to moment gameplay is fun and addictive and it plays great on a keyboard. Don't let the man tell you to use a controller. You'll do great. I spent a lot of time in this review talking about what I don't like, and the easiest way to put it is that I liked almost everything about the game except for this stuff. Had a blast. Constantly wanted to keep going. 3D platformers are my favorite genre and this didn't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game designed around movement and flow, they sure do love to put things to slow you down; whether it's the frustrating jumping which halts a lot of forward momentum or enemies that you have to stop and kill...this, plus the final boss being quite possibly one of the most frustratingly designed experiences I've ever had, I cannot recommend this game. I finished the story but as a result, don't meet the requirements for a refund otherwise I would've done so. Perma-removed it from my account, as I never want to see it or think about it again.
_childDocuments_.name: RKGK / Rakugaki

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda like the 3D Sonic games, and yes, I do mean that in a bad way.When you can get into a flow, it feels pretty good, but the level design far too frequently throws momentum killers in your path that really put a damper on things. There are also a lot of hidden items in the levels which require you to slow down and explore, but again, this feels like it's in opposition to the fun part of the game. I'm sure they'd like for you to play each level several times to find all of the hidden bits and improve your score/time, but the levels and mechanics just aren't engaging enough for me to want to do that.I feel a bit bad about giving this the thumbs down as it's not awful by any means, but I think most people will end up feeling disappointed. With a bit more polish and some rethinking of the level design, this could have been great, but I just don't think it quite hits the mark. If you're a platformer fan, maybe give it a try when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: RKGK / Rakugaki

_childDocuments_.review: So this may be more of a neutral review but steam doesn't have that. I just beat the last boss and wanted to talks about some of this games strengths and flaws. Generally the game feels alright. The running, jumping, dashing, and sliding are all in a pretty good spot. I think some of their level designers did a really good job as well as most of the levels are pretty well crafted. They stretch the content well by having 3 general objectives for each level. Collect everything (this is strict, getting 999/1000 coins is a failure), time trial, and S ranks which is a combo of the previous 2 (but much less strict, for example a level with a 1m gold time trial can still give you full time score bonus for a 5m time. You also generally get 99% of the points for getting 99% of the coins.) Now for the flaws of which I think the biggest one is enemy design and hit boxes. Engaging with enemies feels terrible. Your dash attack come outs late, so its not uncommon to swipe through an enemy, get hit and take damage, and not kill the enemy. The spray paint swipe feels like it has a nebulous range as well. There is an enemy that looks like a little bomb, and if you try to ground swipe it you end up getting hurt (somehow, I guess your spray paint cloud is part of your body). So you have to use your downwards aerial attack against them, which btw doesn't work against the enemies with top shields that they are next to sometimes. I think if every instance of these two enemies was replaced with the default enemies the game would be better for it. Another annoying example is the enemy with damage bubble around them. When you get near them they pull it in then do an big aoe burst, after which they are left vulnerable. This is super slow and feels awful. You can try and kill them while the bubble is pulled in, but that feels like your dancing around invisible hit boxes and also feels terrible. It would be great if instead of this slow dance with the bubble they just charged up an aoe when you get near them encouraging you to deal with them fast. I could keep complaining about other enemies but I wanna move on to a few other minor points. One is grinding on rails... its slow and boring. Sometimes they have you do stuff like jump and grapple to another rail or attack a box on the path, but other times you just get to put the controller down and take a sip of water as you wait for it to go through a little spiral at a set speed with no way to speed it up. Another thing is finding all the collectibles can be a drag. Sometimes you get to the end of a level and its just like oh you missed 3 coins go do the whole level again or possible backtrack for a few mins (tbh I haven't tried backtracking really). Alright I've complained enough. Don't let this prevent you from getting the game if you think you'll like it cause its not like there is really an overabundance of 3d platformers. Just know that its not super special. I might actually go S rank a few more of the early levels, and if they fix up the enemies I'd actually make this a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: RKGK / Rakugaki

_childDocuments_.review: While its presentation is overall stylish, and the colours are bright and dopamine inducing, I was really disappointed in the gameplay. While the Graffiti bombs are gorgeous, actually bombing it requires only a left trigger, and is an afterthought to the rest of the platforming gameplay. Which leads me to my other complaint, the movement needs polish. Traversal and motion feel like they're from 2002, where the player character can face only 8 hard locked directions. It feels okay at best, and there's no sense of flow that these kinds of games generally thrive on. I love the look of this game, but overall, the game feels shallow and I can't see myself coming back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix the aesthetics of Jet Set Radio and mix it with the bonus stages of Super Mario Sunshine? Rakugaki is what you get!  In the game you play as a teenage girl named "Valah." She is part of a group called "Rakugaki" who goes against an authoritarian by the name of Mr. Buff. Valah's objective is to traverse throughout the city and restore the livelihood by tagging sections with graffiti. The story is about as deep as a puddle of mud. It's not entirely original. The story is fairly similar to games such as Jet Set Radio and De Blob. Also, some of the dialogue was pretty cringe at times. The story is probably the weakest element of this game. It exists, but it clearly serves as an explanation for the game and nothing more.While the story won't grab, the presentation of this game absolutely will. The art style is reminiscent of Jet Set Radio. The game conveys a bleak oppressive cyberpunk setting, while Valah must paint bomb the city with color. The colors are loud and vibrant. It's truly visually a feast for the eyes and the artwork the first thing about the game that caught my eyes. While the music wasn't as memorable as the artwork, the techno beats did keep my adrenaline pumping throughout each level. As much as I like the art and music of the game. What good is all of that fluff if the game itself can't match in quality?Fortunately, I think Rakugaki mostly delivers on the game play side. While Valah would fit in to the Jet Set Radio universe, she controls very differently. In the game, Valah can jump, double jump, dash, and slide. When you press down the shoulder button, Valah can use her spray paint to glide across the floor. This helps with traversing the stages quicker. When jumping, she can use her spray paint to float across the air. This helps when clearing large gaps in between platforms. Think of it like using the jet pack like in Mario Sunshine. Controlling Valah is intuitive and easy to do. If you were expecting something similar to Jet Set Radio, you may be disappointed, as this game plays as its own thing. Throughout the game, you traverse multiple sections of the city. Each section of the city is broken up into roughly 5 stages each followed by a boss fight. The levels are structured fairly linearly. The point of each level is to get from point A to point B while tagging TV monitors, collecting coins, and defeating enemies along the way. At the end of each stage you will be graded on how well you did. The time and amount of deaths generally calculate the outcome of this score. At first, I thought this game started off easy for me, but steadily the game ramps in difficulty. Throughout the game, you can choose between "modern" or "retro" difficulties. I am not sure what those difficulties mean, but "retro" is the correct choice. So I played on retro mode. The first handful of stages started off easy enough. It helped me understand the controls and levels themselves were simple to navigate. Valah's move sets almost make the game too easy at times since you can correct a jump a few times in the air. I was almost getting bored that is until I hit the later sections of the game. By the later sections of the game, this game tests your platforming skills considerably. Before you know it, you will be jumping over shifting platforms, dodging lasers, and fighting enemies all at the same time. While the difficulty felt fair for the most part, there were certain times where I felt the game amped up to BS levels. Maybe I just suck at the game, but I swear the camera doesn't always keep track of everything that's happening. In the game the camera doesn't automatically adjust the players perspective at times and for the most part I would have to adjust the camera manually. This usually wouldn't be a problem, however, there were moments where an unseen enemy or bullet attacks me out of the blue to know fault of my own. Also I felt the depth perception was a little off. There were times where I swear that I could clear, but for whatever reason I just did not. Maybe I just need to get my eyes checked. Thankfully these cheap death moments are brief, and when I died it mostly felt like it was my fault. If you play this game, you may rip your hair out in frustration.Another criticism I have with this game is it feels like it's trying to be a type of game to speed through, however the level design seems antithetical to that premise. As I stated before, the levels are structure fairly linear, however the levels do branch out to alternative pathways. In order to complete the levels 100%, you must paint bomb several TV monitors throughout the stages. Some of these TV monitors will be hidden. This wouldn't be too much of a problem, but you really must go out of your way and explore these stages. Also these branching pathways confused me at times. There were certain points in the level where I scratched my head and asked myself "where do I go?" Another issue, there will be times where you will find yourself screeching to a halt only to wait for a foot hold to appear. It's similar to Crash Bandicoot in that regard. For the most part, these are minor gripes and do not happen often, but they do break the flow of the game at times. Overall I enjoyed my time with Rakugaki. I don't think it's going to set the standard for all 3D platformers to follow, but if you are craving for another 3D platformer with kickass artwork and a bopping techno soundtrack, you should give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'm going to recommend it since it's pretty fun for what it costs and what it is, but it has some issues that prevent it from being anything  than "pretty fun". Before I get into it, full disclosure; I have a 13% Clear save file and have just beaten Boss 2.: I have completed the game with a note below.Positives first, the visuals are bold and vibrant. The 3D animated graffiti effects are brilliant and feature a ton of really cool looks. They're probably the best aspect of the game.The music is also quite nice and contributes to an appropriately frantic feeling that pervades certain areas.The lead character is cute and has a few outfits to unlock. The movement is precise enough to allow for tighter platforming moments; I feel like difficulty scaling is often difficult to design for faster platformers so allowing multiple modes of travel allows them to simply switch to the tighter, but slower options to navigate these sections.The plot is light and goofy, which is definitely a positive since it allows more time to be spent on the core gameplay.The flow mechanic they introduce is a great idea because it rewards skilled play and encourages the player to do a little more than the bare minimum at least. The characters attacks don't require the character to stop completely to do which is definitely a plus and enemies shields stand out from their reddish designs from far away allowing the player to plan out the most optimal ways to dispatch them while spending the least amount of time.A TL;DR for the Negatives is, the game really lacks that feeling of "Deep" design that (in more polished games) creates a feeling of interconnectivity that brings the entire experience together, and some aspects of the presentation are weak (both understandably and not-so-much).The weakest aspect of the game is probably (unfortunately) the character controller. There's a level of tightness to the movement that feels pretty inappropriate. Dashes, slides and (to some extent) jumps all have fairly fixed values that are very rarely affected by things like environmental elements (like slopes), prior speed or additional inputs. The player is also locked into things like rails and certain other sequences until they end. This is another thing that harms player expression a little. The ability to pick up a bunch of speed by sliding downhill, and to keep more speed when you jump (possibly by holding or not holding the slide button?) really would have helped. Most games in this subgenre give the character some kind of skating mechanic for this reason.: After completing the game, it's pretty clear why the controls are so tight as it becomes super precision-based later. I feel like people probably won't expect that from this game, but I think that's fine actually.The graffiti walls are also a strange design element, since typically in platformers this is the sort of element that would have:A) Required a movement challenge (even only if very slight) to unlock instead of just pressing a trigger button. Imagine if there was a mechanic you had to perform and like, different kinds of walls that required you to clear a kind of micro puzzle to access while moving.B) Would have a bit more prominence in the design of the game overall since it's a core aspect of the character, possibly tied to some kind of progression.As far as the presentation goes, the voice acting is serviceable and the cutscenes are told via VN style portraits. This is fine, since its a smaller title. What's weirder though is the menus ( and other secondary and tertiary elements) have very few animations and supporting sound effects. Hitting a checkpoint just kind of plops some plain text onto the screen, for example. The levels also have the limiting factor of having to exist in a relatively set location and draw from a pool of similar-looking assets. The city streets, entrance to a facility, and the innards of said facility all look uncannily similar. Although, given its a smaller title it probably wouldn't have been possible to have a ton of discrete level assets.It's a decent game with some issues. Despite everything I still think fans of the subgenre will like it. It's cute and I plan on finishing it. Even though I haven't beaten it yet, it's not difficult to imagine a sequel or another similar title which has more focused design.It's pretty fun, and it's a shame more people aren't talking about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this being sold by a friend as more of a “jak and daxter”-like platformer instead of some high flying momentum adhd one(as the description would make you think), so I got in thinking “okay sure.”If I had to relate this game to anything, it’s like being told Yooka-Laylee is a good successor. Yeah, remember that one?Jumps will slow down to accommodate more precise platforming, sure that’s fine, works in jak because he has a usual jogging speed and it’s designed around that. This game is designed around using your constant drift button to move faster than that jog, which *still* brings you to a screeching halt when you jump. The slide and air dash are also a fixed speed/distance unaffected by how much you lifted off the ground. So sure, just play it like a classic platformer and take more time until you learn where to optimally drift. Unfortunately the bonus goals of the game tell you otherwise, that you *can* do the first level in less than a minute. It wants to be jak and also be ultrakill at the same time. Every movement option just feels yanked from something else like a mismatched jigsaw puzzle. I was still fine with putting up with it, so I gave it until the first boss to start selling the ante, maybe teach how I should be moving better. First boss is a waiting game until he summons towers that he runs into three times. Five minutes or so of waiting in the so-called high speed platform game. You barely have to do ♥♥♥♥. So that’s where this review ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I found "Rakugaki" to be just plain cringeworthy and uninteresting. The environments are a drab repetitive cyberpunk-ish slop. Painting them over with graffiti is such a tired metaphor it's just pitiful. The main character is what a crusty 60-year old conservative would consider "hip" and "quirky". The writing is criminally bad. The main villain is perhaps the only thing about this game's world that I'd found tolerable in a better game, but he's still nothing to write home about. The gameplay is tolerable but too easy at first; and by the time it's gotten a bit harder in the fifth set of levels, I was so checked out I wished it would have just ended already. With all that, "Rakugaki" just feels desperate to me: desperate for our attention, our affection, and most of all, our money. I don't know about Wabisabi Design, they might be good people for all I know, but that sneaky Gearbox logo was a red flag. Really, nothing like a corpo mandated reactionary game about teenagers rebeling against the machine. Not that it's impossible to make good art while working for a corporation; but a "Hi Fi Rush" this ain't.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a trend emerging of indie devs trying to do their own take on a fast paced 3D platformer. While a certain Blue Blur stands as the obvious prototype for this sort of game, we've increasingly seen developers trying to create titles that are still fast, but have a very unique playstyle and moveset to them. Rolling Rascal, Penny's Big Breakaway... and here, Rakugaki - coming in with some punk appropriate flare and style.This game is a dream to speed through. Between jets, hovering and a rapid ground charge, it's been a while since I've seen a platformer feel this fluid and fast. The difficulty comes from trying to balance that with precision - you've got all the tools to control your movement, but it's easy to get overhyped and make a mistake. Still, it's a blast to play - jetting through levels, doing crazy acrobatics and dispatching enemy bots with barely a thought.The world's fun. They really go in on the graffiti and colour as a theme as you go - watching the level change is a delight. Valah’s a damn solid protag- cool to be around and gives every boss fight a feeling of 'I can do this'. I kiiiinda wish we'd seen a bit more love given to the enemies - only having Mr Buff as a named, voiced opponent means they can't really bring too much menace to things. But that's a nitpick. If you're in the mood for a 3D platformer, RKGK is worth a try.Also note - the game's got a strong suite of accessibility options if that's helpful to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I was expecting! A 3D platformer perfect for speedrunners! I love this game. Now I know this is compared to Hi-Fi Rush so I'll say this. Hi-Fi Rush does better at story-telling, combat and even the music but RKGK is much better at exploration, platforming and momentum. The fact that you're rewarded for seamlessly keeping up with movement and combos throughout an entire level and not just combat is awesome! I like the characters and voice acting too. I'm a very busy person so i can't sit and play like I wish to for long periods at a time but when i can, I'll be sinking hours into this game for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: RKGK / Rakugaki

_childDocuments_.review: So far I would recommend this, especially for people who like the gameplay of the older 3D Sonic games. This game really reminds me of them in a good way. You collect coins, grind rails, double jump, slide and so on. It also has it's own mechanics like gliding using the spray bot and the fact that you leave paint everywhere you go for example.It can feel slow in the first couple of levels before an additional power is unlocked. That power basically is a meter that fills up when you paint graffiti (quick one button press when you are near a spot for them) and as you glide through the level without getting hit. As it builds up you glide faster and at full power destroy enemies by just running them over. If you get hit it resets back to 0.I believe the idea here is to replay levels to gather all special items and get the highest rank, each level has objectives regarding this as well bonus scores if you hit specific times for completing the level fast. In that way beating the level while going slow can be easy and a bit boring, if you try to go fast and hit all the objectives you'll have more fun.Graphics are good but not amazing while the art style itself is great. The soundtrack fits with the theme and pace of the game.If I find something strange later I'll edit this, however from what I’ve seen I think the game is fun enough to get at full price.

detailed_description: CRIME BOSS Buzz JOIN THE COMMUNITY ON THE 505 GAMES DISCORD About the Game Guide two brothers on an epic fairy tale filled with discovery, loss, adventure, and mystery. With their father suffering from a deadly illness, two brothers must bravely set out to find the “Water of Life,” the one cure that can save him. In addition to the original hidden treats and rich storyline, the remake has added new secrets to be discovered. Please note: When playing the game in local multiplayer, at least one controller is required.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally released in 2013, Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons was the first game helmed by the now legendary Josef Fares, who would go on to make the fantastic  and the even more prestigious It Takes Two. Before Fares and company formed the studio that made those titles, they ended up making Brothers, which is widely regarded as a significant release for the early mainstream indie scene. I played the original for the first time last year on the Steam Deck, and loved the evening I spent with it. Its visuals, gameplay and narrative held up perfectly ten years later, and its simplistic yet brief nature ensured no moment outstayed its welcome. While I never reviewed that version, I’ll link you the brilliant writeup my curator colleague  completed for that last year. Reviewing this remake in isolation of the original is tricky. The core experience is essentially the same game, with increased graphical fidelity and quality-of-life features headlining the differences for this version. And while that means it is equally as enjoyable to experience as it was in 2013, it equally doesn’t do much to justify its existence.The remake has the same narrative as the original. Two brothers head on a journey to save their father from a deadly illness by collecting water from the Tree of Life, and encounter various friendly faces, hostile threats, and traumatising hardships along the way. The beauty of Brothers is that its story can be universally resonated with, as it is delivered largely wordlessly. You can feel the joy and pain of the Brothers just by their facial expressions and body movements, and these are areas that the remake’s improved animations really help to spotlight. I thought much about my own brother and family whilst experiencing this narrative, and those thoughts really hit deeply when you see how the game wraps up.While the original release was built on Unreal Engine 3, this remake used Unreal Engine 5, and so the leap in visual fidelity between the two is quite dramatic. Many environments are far lusher and more life-like, character models, even for those with a minor role, are packed with neat details and personality, and certain areas, especially Chapters 3 and 7, have visual additions resulting in a much improved presentation compared with what was seen before. There are plenty of cool changes that fans of the original are likely to greatly appreciate.Unfortunately, this fidelity comes at the cost of worsened performance. Despite exceeding the recommended system requirements and lowering the graphical settings to High, my frame rate was very inconsistent; some areas ran at a perfect 60fps, but it would drop to as low as 35fps in places that appeared equally as demanding, and cutscenes were strangely locked to 30fps which was not the case for the original. This isn’t a dealbreaker since Brothers is a slow-paced game, but further optimization is certainly needed.Furthermore, I don’t consider these visuals to be a blanket improvement on the original. I feel the fairy-tale nature of the experience fits the more cartoony art style better, and there are many areas where the subdued colour choices make some backgrounds appear blander than they previously did. As it stands, this is one of the first renowned indie games to receive the remake treatment, and I can’t help but feel that going down this route in the first place misses the point of a core pillar of the indie scene. Few would argue that early successful indie games like Journey or Limbo need the remake treatment because their strong art direction makes their visuals truly timeless. I never took issue with the original’s art design, so seeing it remade in this manner feels deeply unnecessary. Ultimately, I’d recommend watching a side-by-side comparison so you can make your own judgement, as they both contain aspects that set themselves apart.The unique ‘single-player co-operative’ gameplay of Brothers is fully retained in this remake. Through the simultaneous control of the two Brothers, you’ll solve various puzzles, complete platforming challenges, and defeat or avoid the occasional foe or two. It uses its short runtime to its full advantage, consistently delivering interesting gameplay scenarios like the hang-glider sequence and boat traversal, before tossing them away for other equally compelling ideas like getting to ride a mountain goat and climbing up a cliff with the help of a troll. The controls do require some getting used to, but shouldn’t take that long as each Brother only requires inputs from the sticks and a single trigger. Nonetheless, if you still find this tricky, one nice addition is the ability to play Brothers in co-op either locally or via Remote Play. While this wasn’t the intended way to experience Brothers and will certainly change how certain segments of the game feel, it is a welcome option to have. The remake also advertised improved gameplay and boss fights alongside better enemy AI, but I feel that these changes were drastically oversold, as I couldn’t notice a difference in how any sequence played out. The same applies to the rerecorded soundtrack, which at first glance, did not have any perceptible differences from the original score. I also question what the developers meant by ‘new secrets to be uncovered’, as I found no interactions or easter eggs that weren’t already present in the original. The only ‘additions’ I identified were two achievements which are nothing but extensions of existing ones in the base game. Finally, there are some neat extras that you unlock after completing the story, namely an art gallery showcasing the character and environment redesigns, and the original’s developer commentary. Overall, fans looking for new gameplay reasons to re-experience Brothers will not find much on offer here.It would be disingenuous of me to rate the Brothers remake negatively because of the existence of the original. A lot of effort and polish went into recreating this classic indie title, and I found it equally enjoyable to re-experience on my beefy main computer as it was to play the original for the first time on the humble Steam Deck. Yet, it would be equally disingenuous of me to recommend it simply because it is shinier and newer. Personally, I am baffled that this remake exists in the first place. At least a couple of years of effort was put into rebuilding a 3–4-hour game in a new engine, completely redoing all of its assets, rerecording its soundtrack, and advertising its release. Meanwhile, the original exists on essentially every platform known to man including mobile, and still looks good and plays well to this day; why couldn’t they have pushed and advertised updates for that version in a similar vein to what Valve did to Half-Life last year?Ultimately, I could only recommend this remake if you meet at least two of the following criteria: A – You haven’t played the original, B – You prefer how this version approaches its visuals, and/or C – You want to play the game in co-op. Outside of that, the remake is just not worth it unless via a deep sale. While there are some neat changes, nothing is substantially improved to the point where I’d say this is the definitive way to play Brothers. I have no hesitation in saying it is the most unnecessary video game remake ever made, and I don’t think much would have been lost if the original was the only version that existed.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original back when it came out and this remake still holds up the magic from the first. The game is beautiful, as well as the story. This game is still just as short as the original, not really adding much of anything "new" to the gameplay and story itself. Although the story is beautiful and moving, it didn't create as much emotional turmoil for my () playthrough of the game. I purchased it for the nostalgia and beautiful graphics. Like my title suggests, if you are like me, save your money. If you are new to the game, please buy it as it will be worth your time.While this game is definitely playable by yourself, it does not come without its frustrations. The gameplay is fairly unique in that you are controlling each brother with a different joystick and trigger buttons for their actions. Some of the solutions aren't outright apparent, but for me personally it didn't take too long to figure out the puzzle. The game will definitely be easier when played with a friend, which I would recommend if you are not confident in your skills with difficult puzzle-like gameplay. As stated in some other reviews, if you are not adept at figuring out those puzzles it will become frustrating for you very quickly.The gameplay is very short. While Steam says I played  for 4 hours, about 20-30 minutes of that was spent on a combination of chore break or snack break or phone call. I purchased this game on release day with it being on sale for $16; it has a regular price tag of $20. With the original version of the game being $20 as well, I think it is a fair price tag for the graphics upgrade it received. I also only managed to complete 7/14 of the achievements available on a "blind" playthrough. The rest of the missed achievements seem easy enough to go back and accomplish on another playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is inferior to the original for a couple of reasons. 1: this is a single player game. adding co-op is misguided. i would advise against playing co-op, because the controls are part of the narrative, and it doesn't have the same impact if you would play it in co-op.2: the new visuals are a little uncanny. it looks technically higher quality, but the charm of astyle of the original is lost. kind of like how the Halo CE anniversary update kind of fails to replicate the original artistically.3: the cinematics i think ruin it. it was better without the cinematic cutscenes. it feels like they were trying to improve something that didn't need to be improved.Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is one of my favorite examples of video games as an art form. the remake does not capture the brilliance of the original. just play the original version.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah.  The original is stylized and still looks amazing.  This just lacks much in the way of an individual personality, and I find it tough to look at in motion with all the artifacting or whatever's going on with the graphics.  Also the paths don't stand out as clearly during gameplay.  Won't spoil, but there were also unnecessary changes to the way a key npc was introduced that make the environmental storytelling a bit weaker.  But most crucially they changed the bittersweet, subtle, yearning background music to something happy and cinematic and oblivious.  It feels much less immersive and iconic to me, it's a tone killer.My opinions are from playing this level by level alternating with the original.  I didn't get past two before I really started to dread playing the remake's levels, which is why I'm writing this.  I'm still going to play the whole thing through because this is one of my favorite games of all time and I want to see what else is different, so I'll update if my opinion changes, but for now I'm disappointed overall and can't recommend the remake period. Edit: Ok I finished it.  Cons:-More missing atmosphere, replaced with music (the music gets better).-Glitchy animals messed with the vibe of two different sequences for me, and it was so hard to see the warning to avoid a certain hostile that I just assumed there wasn't one until I got to the same spot in the original.-Multiple puzzles were made longer and/or harder to do.  I found this engaging in some cases and frustrating in others; it's a con for me because one of them adds a whole cutscene to explain how to avoid messing up.  No.  Let me be careless, kill me, and restart the puzzle instantly please, it's just as effective as a lesson and doesn't make me watch the cutscene again.-Glitchy shadows and models.  I think they updated it to be a little easier to look at on Steam Deck but I still have a LOT of weird graphics nonsense. -Further confusing layouts (why is everything so dark??).  I am convinced the environments in the original just look better period, the visuals are more cohesive and appealing and particularly the water is much prettier.  Whatever corners they cut work within their limitations; the remake just tends to look like hi def textures got slapped on for the sake of hi def (with the exception of a location at the very end which I found very impressive).-Some minor to major changes that seem to be in the vein of "let's make it more realistic," overlooking the fact that this is clearly a fairytale world with unrealistic logic at every turn, there's no need to shoehorn in realism.  -There's this very specific conflict towards the end that may take you a few tries to figure out (unlike me, who is definitely very good at video games and didn't forget how to play this part).  In the remake, you are aided in this effort by a long, unskippable cutscene that wasn't in the original, which is there to tell you something the original didn't take nearly this long to convey (because the remake makes it deliberately more confusing for the sake of drama, thanks, I hate it; it does not have the desired effect my fourth time watching).-Co op mode is a neat gimmick, but if you play it that way the first time, then (unless they've managed to account for this in some way I'm having difficulty imagining) I think you'll miss out on the game's most iconic moment.Pros:-Some extra voice bits got added in a spot where they were lacking in the original, I thought that was nice.  There are some other little attentions to detail that prove some passion went into this.-Extra animations in the cinematics with more dynamic angles.  I found these mostly unnecessary and a little melodramatic at times, but they don't radically change anything and the ending applies them really effectively. -The ending was easily the best part of the whole thing, I had exactly one minor gripe because of course I did, but there was also an altered sequence I liked so much I wish it was in the original.-Still can't recommend it, but I don't regret buying for the fun of playing them both side by side and getting into my emotions about the story again. tl;dr: Letdown.  Play the original if you haven't.  If you already have, play the original anyway, it's the superior experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to replay Brothers with my partner who never played the original. I should have waited for some reviews before purchasing the game. So many game breaking bugs that ruin the co-op experience.I have a Nvidia 2070 Super with updated drivers and there was some stuttering in the early videos, some pixel glitches with reflections in the water, my partners screen went black 10 times during game play and we had to restart the remote play, she even decided it was easier for me to just stream the game in Discord than having to keep restarting the remote play, and the final section of the game doesn't work in co-op, you need to be in single player mode for the controls to properly work. Clearly not enough Q and A testing :( The graphics are mostly good, the soundtrack and story are nicely done and the main selling point of the game. I wish the developers would have added new content instead of just a graphical update because I always felt the original game was too short and had potential to be better.  If the developers fix the bugs, than the remake will be the best version of the game. I only recommend you buy this version for single player, co-op does not work properly!!!

_childDocuments_.review: The sole purpose of the game's release was to make money. Unfortunately, the game was not finished before its release, and it is riddled with bugs. Playing the game can be quite frustrating due to these issues. I have reached a point in the game where I cannot progress any further because I am unable to move little brother at all.It's disappointing to see a great game name being exploited solely for profit. The supposed "remake" is nothing but a money-grab, with only one extra achievement and marginally improved graphics compared to the original game. It's unacceptable that they are charging the full price for such a minimal upgrade. Some parts are better visible in the old version (e.g. ropes that you need to climb).I enjoyed playing the first game and disregarded many bad reviews before buying this "remake", hoping to experience the same story with improved graphics. However, in the end, it turned out to be a huge disappointment. I do not recommend anyone to waste their money on this game. Instead, play the old version, or not even that.

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons offers a visually upgraded experience without altering the core gameplay or narrative elements that made the original memorable. While the gameplay remains unchanged from the original, the remake introduces the option to use a second controller for cooperative play. This feature can enhance the experience for those who wish to share the journey with a friend, reflecting the game's themes of teamwork in a more interactive way.Visually, the remake is a feast for the eyes. The environment design has been significantly enhanced, with improved lighting, models, better hair physics, and more detailed facial expressions. These upgrades breathe new life into the game’s world, making it even more immersive and engaging. For newcomers to the game, this graphical overhaul provides a more polished and visually stunning experience, allowing them to fully appreciate the game’s richly crafted environments.However, if you’re already familiar with the original or have a less powerful computer, the remake’s enhancements might not be as critical. The original game still delivers the same emotional impact and narrative depth with a lighter system requirement, making it a viable option for those who prioritize performance over visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed my playthrough of Brothers, and I have to say: I really do think people have been a little too unfair on this one.  The art style is indeed a little bit changed from the original vision, but I still believe it's close enough that you really understand and get the idea. The gameplay itself too is perfectly preserved - clearly the game logic is the same, and that's how it should be in my opinion.The game also does add co-op with multiple controllers. This is a little odd how for some reason one controller is one analogue stick, and the other is the other stick, and honestly I hope they fix this in a patch (you can also fix this with a bit of Steam input tweaking), but apart from that it plays solidly enough and is really enjoyable in a couch co-op setting. That's exactly how I enjoyed it this time. Is the game originally designed for that? No. Does it really matter? Not really. Just enjoy the game SP or co-op, whichever way you personally prefer.I really enjoyed Brothers, and I'm a big Josef Fares fan. It's honestly a breath of fresh air to play his games: they're full of quality narrative moments and atmosphere, and not about the typical collection of pickups or collectables that most modern games are about.If you enjoy this, make sure you also check out the mighty A Way Out, and the even more (almost perfect) It Takes Two. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: My most recent playthrough of the original Brothers was back in late 2021 and it still felt like an enjoyable game that has aged well. Yet here we are in 2024 having a remake of the game on our hands. A remake that primarily focuses on the graphics. A remake that - in all honesty - does not make the game any better. Thing is, the visuals in the original game, with their bleaker palette, created the otherwordly, magical and at the same time unsettling atmosphere that made me love the game in the first place. This is something that is completely amiss in the remake with its colorful and somewhat cinematic graphics. The remake feels modern, yes... and at the same it just feels mundane. Whatever little gameplay there was, now feels simpler as well, resulting in an oddly unsatisfying experience.So if you haven't played Brothers before - I strongly suggest you start with the classic version. If you are a fan of the original game (or - in a broader sense - of all games by Josef Fares), you'll probably want to have this in your collection, but definitely not at a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original and saw Josef Fares's journey from Brothers a Tale of Two Sons, A Way Out, F the Oscars Declaration and the highly successful and critically acclaimed It Takes Two.Josef Fares had nothing to do with the Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake, this has been made by a different studio, he just signed the go-ahead and that's ok for someone to do it.I 100% both of the games but unfortunately this is a massive letdown.It's not a remake, it's barely even callable a remaster.It's the same game with better graphics... but it just looks like it. All textures are upscaled and then covered by blur.My beefy system and GPU is running vents at 100%.Sometimes the Physics engine is bugged as I had a tortoise that wouldn't drop or struggled to slide down.I truly feel there is nothing better in terms of gameplay and story than the original version.I guess it's easier to do online co-op now cause of Steam Remote Play and being able to play with 2 controllers. Although I had issues with that, as he either had a black screen or no game world audio.But if you play this single player it will take a long time to get on with the controls.All in All, I recommend getting Brothers a Tale of Two Sons Remake only if you haven't played the original title, but if you already got the original, there is nothing new or better here.As someone said,  - Shout out to Underdrill for this statement.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with some positive stuff:-The original game is still on sale, this is an amazing move by everyone involved and in this day and age where original games get delisted all the time when a remaster comes out I can only praise this situation.-Game was sold at a huge discount for owners of the original, and even without this discount the game is only 5 more dollars (excluding sales of course, in sales the original is usually sold at around a 2 dollar price)-The game has finally received a patch that lets you change graphics setings! This doesn't change the new art direction that much but now you can optimize if you don't have a beast PC and you can remove a lot of visual blur with those new settings.-It includes the director commentary of the original game, which is an amazing watch on the original vision.Now I do not recommend this Graphical Remaster because the only thing this version adds is a "coop mode" that supports a second controller, you could always play coop with one controller if you wanted but coop was never the intended way to play (something the game even states when you pick coop which I find strange).And the new graphics, while they can look good in some very specific moments, have completely messed up the character design, art direction and for some reason they also changed the cutscene direction as well. (I find all those 3 changes inferior to the original vision).So now what would make this game a recommend then? What would appease the fans?I think the possibility to switch between the original art and cinematic direction would be what is needed.If this was an option this would be the definitive experience and well worth the price, but now I can only recommend that you play the original, and if you're looking for a coop game by the same team please play It Takes Two instead, it literally has all the coop mechanics of Brothers and more and was BUILT for coop.

_childDocuments_.review: for everyone out there saying this remake is a soulless cash-grab; the remake’s going for $16 with it’s current introductory offer, practically the same price you would currently get the original for. the remake’s a carbon copy of the original with a much more vibrant and visually astounding look harnessing the capabilities of unreal engine 5. a faithful remake everyone was hoping for. the original had a unmatched aesthetic with a low saturated colour palette meanwhile the remake makes every every colour pop out more and make everything simply more mesmerising to look at. I for one found myself appreciating the meticulous environments of this game more significantly than I ever did with the original. I say this as a player for whom the nostalgia plays a big part while comparing both sides.I remember playing the original on my iPad when I was around 10 ten years old and recently revisiting it in the past year. the unorthodox nature of the game just fascinated me, controlling two characters at a single time while each character having an almost equally significant role. me, and players alike of the original have always wondered what it would be like for the game to have strict co-op features similar to joseph fares’s other titles such as “a way out” and “it takes two”. the remake delivers, the game marketed a co-op mode and it’s here. a fully functioning co-op mode, the game’s designed to be played by a single player but players do have the choice of either playing it single player or co-op. I can’t help but notice that the clunkiness of controlling two players as a single player is still somewhat evident. meanwhile, the co-op mode feels way smoother. remote play, I wish it was present but it isn’t. I feel like there was definitely room to implement something similar to “friend’s pass” from it takes two or remote play in general via two players owning the game. granted, there’s the difference of different studios working on these games. however, surely the technology to implement this feature isn’t that complicated. there’s also the argument of not enabling remote play as a choice since the game’s not designed to be played that way since co-op mode’s an additional feature granted on the behalf of the community. I can’t support this argument since this is a remake we’re talking about, I don’t think it’s unjust to say that these demands could have been met in 10 years. again, the base price of this game is $20; $5 pricier than the original which is a very reasonable price to sell the remake at. I anticipated a much higher price, the developers had a clear opportunity to rip the audience but they didn’t. I strongly recommend brothers ‘24 to new players and players of the original alike. I wasn’t bereft of the impactful feeling the original notioned while playing the remake.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake that we didn't need but I'm still cool with it existing because I really like the original game. The story, where two brothers go on a journey to save their father, remains the same, but the graphics have been noticeably upgraded. The world looks sharper and more vibrant, with better lighting and detail. The remake doesn’t change much but polishes what was already a touching adventure. It’s a great chance for both new players and fans of the original to experience the story again. 8/10 (Great)

_childDocuments_.review: Be honest. Have you ever played a game that brought you to tears?I mean really to tears?I remember playing the Original in 2015 and it was an emotional Rollercoaster.After completing it ... i was still, i was ... thinking about what i played.Thinking about the whole Story and of course the Ending.As i said before: An emotional Rollercoaster.And ... here we go again.Welcome to BROTHERS - A TALE OF TWO SONS REMAKE!This is the story of two Brothers on a journey to help their father.At the beginning of the story the father got ill and his sons bring him to a healer.The problem is, he know a way to heal the father but it will take a very long journey.The sons already lost their mother and don`t wan`t to loose their father, too, so they started the Journey.The Gameplay is the same as in the Original and that is totally okay. You can play with Keyboard, but i highly recommended a Joypad.With it you controll the 2 Brothers at the same time. One with the right half and the other with the left half of the Controller. The same time! Most of the parts of this game you must do Teamwork with the Brothers to get through the it. That sounds a little bit complicated, but it is very easy to control.At the beginning it may take a little Time, but believe me, you are shortly into the Controls and then you can enjoy the game and it´s story.And this Time with a Friend if you wish. Local Coop or Remote Play. Your Choice. The Graphics are really wonderfull overworked. At the beginning it is nothing special. You are in a small village, with some people, normal village life. But the more you play, the Scenerys are getting better and better and you can see how much work it is in this game. I don´t wan`t to spoil, that is something you must see by yourself. The World of BROTHERS got many nice details and all the characters are very well animated. AAs i said before, really wonderfull.And that goes also for the amazing Soundtrack. Really wonderfull Music to totally dive into the World of the BROTHERS.I highly recommended buying it, too. 25 tracks for just 4,99. Brothers also have his Achievements, 2 more then in the Original, but these are special ones. Each one stands for a little situation you must find and master. For example, you have to make a special person dancing, or helping a Turtlemom to get her Babys back. Very nice done.So what can i say.This is a wonderfull Remake. Approved Graphics, the amazing Soundtracks and this damn, damn, damn emotional Rollercoaster Feeling.Yes, this game did it again. I have had some tears in my eyes, again, and i´m not ashamed of it.This is more than a game. It´s like a movie or like a book. You follow the story and you laugh and cry with them. Each chapter you wan`t to know how it is going on. You can`t stop. And at the End of the Game you sit there, thinking about what you have experienced. A very big Thanks to the Developer and publisher for this "upgraded" experience.It was really, really awesome.Again.So dear Reader, if you like a great story with wonderfull graphics and amazing music, this is for you.If you are really emotional, don´t forget the tissue. I promise you ... You will need it.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2013 Starbreeze Studios was in a weird position. They had lost several key team members in the years prior and in 2012 released Syndicate, a game that wasn’t well received. Releasing a small downloadable only cinematic platformer title was not something people expected of them at the time, but Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons was a success that made people trust the studio once again. Pitched and directed by Josef Fares, who has since worked on purely cooperative titles A Way Out and It Takes Two, it was a very curious attempt to create a “single-player coop” kind of game. That used its simple yet inventive controls to tell a wonderful fairy tale (in the classic dark but hopeful way) story that evoked emotions through basic interactions.The game has been re-released and ported numerous times since then and now, over 10 years since release, it got an almost shot for shot remake of the game, similarly to Like a Dragon: Ishin! from last year. This remake aims to be a new definitive version of the game and while it doesn’t quite succeed to be that at the moment, the game at the core remains amazing.This game is a very simple, but very well told story of a journey two brothers undertake in order to find magic healing water to save their father. Being a cinematic platformer at core, you could expect the controls to be quite simple. And you’re right, but they do have a twist – you directly control both brothers, with each of them having a dedicated analogue stick and action button to perform the necessary contextual action. Which, of course, means that it plays best on a controller. The game is balanced around this idea and while you should expect moments where your characters start running into walls because your brain starts mixing up which stick controls which character on screen, it usually works really well. The obstacles brothers face and the solutions they must come up with remain fresh throughout the whole (relatively short) game. And from time to time you also get completely optional little interactions you may engage with.Remake changes almost nothing about how the game works and how the levels are laid out. There are a couple of minor changes and you’ll probably notice them only in a side by side comparison, but as far as the gameplay goes, it’s basically the exact same game. Sadly, this means that the final big action sequence has a chance of being as finnicky as it used to be before, while having as poorly placed checkpointing as before. But since the game played really well originally, it makes sense to not change anything about it.What has been updated is the visual side of things. Moving from a small downloadable 2013 Unreal Engine 3 game to a modern and seemingly slightly higher budgeted Unreal Engine 5 title, the visuals get a huge boost. Not that the original game looked bad – due to its art style most of it still looks wonderful today. But a lot of the scenes in the Remake looks absolutely incredible while retaining the original visual intent. In fact, the new version is visually far more varied, with every chapter having a more distinct look to it. Due to all this added fidelity, cutscenes have been reedited to feature more close ups and dramatic camera movement than there were in the original. It’s not a question of “higher fidelity means better”, of course, but it is nice to see that none of the intent and emotion has been changed, while taking full advantage of the updated look of the game. Though, it must be said that a few of the late game cutscenes, and even one character, have been redesigned, but in a way that I found welcome.The move to the cutting edge and also still somewhat rough UE5, however, also means a lot of potential issues that the original version doesn’t have. People with older hardware, for example, will most likely have performance issues. But even on newest hardware you will notice problems. The picture often looks over-sharpened and noisy, depth of field occasionally misfires, the selected shutter speed for motion blur in cutscenes makes the scenes look laggy… There are also occasional bugs – for example, I once completed a chapter only to somehow die (I think) during the ending cutscene and after the cutscene finished, to be reloaded back to the last checkpoint.Luckily, any and all issues I’ve seen with the Remake are fixable, as long as the publishers are ready to support and improve game. While the updated look and feel of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is, in my opinion, worthy of becoming a definitive version of the game. Especially since now it also has developer’s commentary and coop, just like some of the later re-releases of the original game. Granted, I don’t think playing this game in coop is a particularly good idea, but it’s nice that the option is there. If you have the original game and considered replaying it – you won’t miss much if you replay the original again, especially if you have an older system. But if you have not played Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons before, Remake is probably a better option to go with, if your system can handle it. Whatever your choice will be, the game itself is still wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I played co-op with Xbox controllers. It was a considerably short game over all, but we thought it was fantastic, albeit a bit heart wrenching. In truth, I never played the original game myself, but I don't particularly get all the negative reviews about the Remake. Concerning the objections to co-op play, I personally feel like it was an amazing addition! Otherwise, I'd have likely never played it or come across it. I don't play solo games often. My preference of game play is either with my wife or our small group of friend that game together. My wife and I looked over the bonus content for the game after completion (In truth I'm not sure it was available prior to completing the game or not - if so I wouldn't view it unless you are up for some serious spoilers), and watched the entire commentary video from Josef Fares. We noted we missed quite a few things and achievements in our play through. We had one crash in our play through. Otherwise everything ran great and it was a beautiful and touching story. There isn't a lot in the way of combat, but my wife and I have played through quite a few puzzle games, and we don't mind that ourselves. If I had to compare it to a game, I'd say it is a lot like a 'choose your own adventure to some extent. There are puzzles you have to make use of both brothers to complete, along with challenges, and a few bosses, but ultimately you don't attack the bosses directly per se. You work together as a family would to over come the obstacles in front of you. The game is unique like many of the other games Josef Fares is involved in. My wife and I were ecstatic to add another game of this caliber to our collection. So long as you are fine with the fact that it is a short adventure, and you enjoy games similar too it, I suspect you'll love Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the title this is not a remake. It may say that in the title but it isn't. The only difference this has from the original is "better graphics," cinematic cut scenes, and a new coop feature so you can play it with two controllers instead of huddling around the keyboard. Also I've heard from other negative reviews that there are many bugs and glitches although I personally haven't experienced any so far. If you have the original or the original is cheaper don't buy this game. The only reason I'm gonna be playing it is so I can play it with my wife.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded as it doesn't support ultrawide in 2024.It's literally a setting in Unreal Engine "AspectRatioAxisConstraint=AspectRatio_MaintainYFOV" and yet the game doesn't support it nor allow changing it through the config. The aspect ratio is locked at 16:9 with pillar boxed black bars at all times, and it even has letter boxed black bars during cutscenes (Vert- FOV), so double black bars.The game started in fullscreen exclusive and forced 1920x1080 and started an infinite loop of resolution changes on my monitor. I couldn't get out of it if not by pressing ALT+F4.Additionally, the game has a lot of graphical glitches (green pixels), though it's seemengly fixed by toggling HDR off and on? I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: i cried 11 years ago and i cried again after playing this little emotional roller coaster of a game. its shows just how important music is to a game when there's no real "language" but you can still feel it through the music and emotions of the characters the games controls can take a few minutes to understand but once you do it just clicks really nicely. the game features a nice section of puzzles that aren't hard and offer a nice mild level of difficulty as does the whole journey there's nothing that really stumps you so you can just progress through it at a nice relaxing pace. as for the remake i find the new graphics pretty darn beautiful sure its a totally different take on the original art style but it works in its own way (imo) unreal engine shines nicely on this game and the new added details make the the game come to life kinda like a stop animation style. the game is a nice length at around 3-4 hrs depending if you explore the areas and interact with people and objects so for the low price the game is i highly recommend it. only gripe i have is the game can have some very minor stutters and performance could be better. but man in 4k maxed out on an oled with hdr on it totally shines and is a beautiful experience and with that said i rate this game a 9 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is the same great game you remember, but rebuilt in Unreal Engine 5.  Aside from a few quirks, such as brief texture pop-in and a few stutters, it looks great and plays well.  The quirks only showed up in the beginning and seemed to sort itself out as the game went on.The updated visuals enhance the game, and the re-worked cutscenes help sell the great story even more.  Some cutscenes are 60fps while others are 30fps; a bit jarring, but maybe a patch can fix it along with the quirks.I don't think you need to run out and buy it; playing the original still holds up and will work for most people.  The remake is mainly for higher end PCs with NVIDIA 3000 series graphics cards or later (or AMD equivalent).  I have an RTX 4070 and a 12th gen Intel i7 CPU, and at 1440p with high settings and DLSS set to Quality, the ran smooth at a locked 60 fps.  I would also highly recommend using HDR if your monitor/TV supports it as the game looks noticeably better with it on.The remake is nice to have, and if you own the original you get a discount.  Whether you play this or the original, it's terrific and the story will stick with you long after playing.If you're interested, you can check out my video review of the original:

_childDocuments_.review: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons Remake was great not only for those wanting to revisit the now eleven year old game, but for people like me who never had the pleasure. Sure, the original is still available to this day, but it never came to mind until news of the remake, so why not start there? It was beautiful in terms of visuals and mixed the fantastical with darker themes, sometimes at whiplash speed. It was easy to fall into the wholesome trap only to be reminded of tragedy seconds later. For this reason I didn’t entirely like the ending, “bittersweet” didn’t even begin to cover it. I still feel bummed out.For solo play the controls took some getting used to, but moving the characters individually yet simultaneously with each having their own unique interactions was pretty good—I also appreciated the other little details, such as the little brother being slower.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I cannot reccomend the game at the current state it is in. No UltraWide screen support and there are several issues with various graphical artefacts on water surfaces and hair textures when the camera is zoomed in up close. Also quite a lot of other bugs, not just graphical rainbow like artefacts and flickering. Performance is not that good aswell, needs a bit of work on the optimization side..It has a nice initial introduction launch price, on top of  -20% sale launch price, they even give you an additional 3.20 € discount for owning the original.But for reasons I described earlier, I cannot reccomend it. The original also looks quite nice, even after a decade. The remake has this weird brownish and yellowish tint/filter.*Edit 3.3.2024curently there is a temporal fix for those that want to play the game in an Ultrawide resolution made by RoseTheFlower Works fine, but you have to run the game in a borderless window.*Edit 28.11.2024even after 8 months after release, they still haven't added the Ultrawide support, but they fixed the various graphical bugs and artifacts . However the game is incredibly taxing to run, even with RTX 4090 and 4K resoluition its unplayable without DLSS on, I think this is a pattern with all the games running on UE5 unfortunately. Without DLSS the game barely is able to reach 60 fps. With DLSS set to quality the game runs from 80 - 140 fps, it fluctuates quite a lot. It's mind boggling considering how the game looks and what is on display here.I love the original, it was one of those games that was personally one of the best games in 2013, but that year some really legendary cult games came out (The Last of Us, GTA V, Tomb Raider, Metro Last light, FC3 BLood Dragon),so it had a really tough time among these games, but to me it still holds a special place in my heart after all these years and I prefer it to this soulless remake, which I haven't played through yet for various particular reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: edit: 7/24/2024 I got a brand new high spec PC and was able to finish the game, thankfully this time it didn't crash after the sequence of rescuing the girl. I still experienced some lag but that was only for the cutscenes and transitions. I would still recommend the original game over this new one, as pretty as it is.as of right now i physically can not complete the game, it refuses to load into the next area after i rescue the girl. i was looking forward to the release of this game as i've played the original (exact same game, just updated onto unreal engine 5) i wish we could take slightly different paths in the game, change a small part of a story and give us two different endings at least with the choices we make as the player, instead of being forced to go down one line.i wish i could not be disappointed in this game, it's visually stunning and the soundtrack is beautiful, both accompanied by a grabbing story that forces you to continue playing with anticipation and curiosity of what happens next. though controlling the two brothers takes some getting used to, which may deter people from playing with how weird it feels to play as both.
