_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 specifically is a very memorable game to me. I first played the Portable version on PSP and, even with a lot of downgrades of the original (and some QoL from Persona 4), it managed to affect me in a very emotional and thoughtful way of many different aspects of my life.Because of it, I followed this franchise from that point on and played many other Persona and SMT games, most of them were indeed a great time/experience, but not a single one managed to hit me like 3 did.But even with my personal bias and attachment to it, I will try to give at least an honest to good review about positive and negative aspects of this "Remake". Please take all of it with a grain of salt.Pros:-The models are amazing. They really did polish everyone, not only Soejima's Art style improved, but his anatomy as well. If you compare to Persona 5 models, the new ones are less uncanny than the previous game.- The Soundtrack is top notch. Atsushi Kitajoh managed to create not only beautiful arranges from the originals made by Shoji Meguro, but  with the return of the legendary Lotus Juice on the rhymes, they managed to outclass Mass Destruction. It's going Down is perfect in a way that hits you with a dopamine rush when you hit shadow advantage and, if you time it correctly, hit an all out attack at the peak of the song. Color your night still gives you a "Persona 5" vibe, but you can still "feel" it belongs to Persona 3. The entire soundtrack likes to work on small leitmotifs here and there to make you feel attached to the atmosphere of the game, and when you hit the final part + the credits song you get a kind like "nostalgia" punch on your gut together with the really emotional ending.- The Battle system is even more balanced and comfortable than the previous Persona games. The party members skills got buffed, the addition of Kouga and Eiga spells balanced the Light/Dark elements. The Navigator system AND Baton pass equivalents got balanced/nerfed to improve the all in all experience of the game, not to mention since you're fighting shadows, you can't have a spoiler of their weaknesses from the Velvet Room fusion/Recruiting them on ambush.- Tartarus got a INCREDIBLE revamp. The original and portable versions made Tartarus only looks the same thing with different color schemes each Name Floors, but on Reload each one has it's own vibe/environment/random seeds to make the Immersion and experience way better- The addition of Link episodes with party members and, even with some story relevant characters made the experience even better for newcomers and P3 Veterans. They even added some special situations that were exclusive for certain Versions of the game (one from P3FES and another from P3Portable FemMC route only)- The addition of Theurgy Skills made the gameplay even more interesting, putting the Fusion Spells the protagonist had on Theurgies (and not requiring you to have the Personas on the party all times) not only balanced the use of it, but also made it even more interesting to complete the Compendium- You can now choose to date a female Social Link or not. Compared to the original, you were obligated todate the girls and even had the risk of getting a reverse arcana if you got caught cheating or ignored them for a long time- Reverse Arcanas now are way harder to get, In my entire gameplay, I didn't get a single one, so I think the only way now is purposely choosing a rude/stupid option on the Social Link interactions, which brings me to the next topic- Voiced Social Links improved the Visual Novel part of the game, making you feel more attached to them.- Better HUD/Aesthetic design than the previous games.Now with the Cons:- The game feels way more easy than compared with the original and other Persona games, sure, it takes more time to "break" than Persona 5, but the few cases I got a game over were on two specific battles and against the Reaper because a friend on Discord kept insisting for me to beat it on level 35~50. Even with all the QoL and balance on some mechanics, Theurgies really help to mitigate or even brute force some bosses/challenge battles. - You can't change Tartarus Theme like the FES/Portable Version, which is a shame because after a while it gets really boring to hear the same arranged for more than 200 floors.- The game does gives you more options, but you still have the same time limit from the previous games, so, unless you follow a guide or is a veteran, you can pretty much fail to get all Social Links on the first play through(Veteran's Advice: focus on the School Social Links since you can't do them on weeks before exams, exams and school vacation+near the ending)- The Social Links are a hit or miss for the community. Either you hate them, or you love it. So I highly avoid discussing about that online.- Some Link episodes are miss able and even unlocks some specific Personas to fuse, so if you don't make them or lose one, you're pretty much screwed.- Not having the "Answer" and "female MC" route makes the fan base debate if this could really be the definitive edition of Persona 3, but they already confirmed on making a future DLC for The Answer Episode, so, only time will tell.- Tartarus has few Designs for each Floor Section and some are either extremely short, or stupidly big with a big NOTHING on them, so after a few times, you just ignored them and just look to the HUD on the left side.- The Artbook and OST DLC's are a scam. You cannot access them unless booting up the game SPECIFICALLY for each one, meanwhile Steam has a built in MP3 player for games with Soundtrack for years already. This is probably a terrible decision from Atlus/Sega to avoid people from pirating it or spreading on the internet.I highly recommend this game for both Veterans and newcomers, and I can assure that this game was a test/base for the future Persona games (possibly 6 or another 4 Remaster)Elizabeth's Megidolaon out of  10 would cry for the 7th time with Memories of You playing in the credits

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really enjoyed my experience with Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 Royal. I also really enjoy parts of this game. Like the other modern Persona games, there is a certain rhythm to how you organise yourself between clearing floors in Tartarus, spending time improving your social links, and improving your stats. This game in particular also has a unique feel to many of the social links. A lot of the characters feel more grounded and compelling in the way that real people with their own struggles that they work to overcome are.That being said, Persona games work by balancing the quality of their school life visual novel and dungeon crawling RPG elements. In my opinion, Persona 3 Reload fails this. Never before has the dungeon crawling in these games felt like punching the clock. It is fully just "what if P5 but only Mementos?" but even then it doesn't live up to that because at least mementos gave me a reason to take the time to explore it other than gaining XP and because the story wants me to. I tried upping the difficulty to spice things up but that just means that every now and then I get crit and die in an otherwise winnable fight. This is especially annoying as, unlike in P4, I'm not just sent back to the floor entrance, no I'm sent back to the Tartarus entrance. It's a slog on normal and it's a slog on difficulties higher than normal.Now, the school life side is still very solid and the dungeon crawling is occasionally given pops of pure fun so I'm gonna stick with this game and see it through to completion but that's really because I think I just latch onto big RPGs like this. As for if you should buy it though, I'd recommend it if you're a persona fiend like me. Otherwise, the other two mainline persona games on steam are better options (especially P5R).

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever had the feeling, that something you see, read or hear in a piece of media is so accurate, so innately relatable, that it might as well have been made for you? I felt that way when playing this game. As many of my fans may know, I live in Sao Paulo (Brasil #1), a town that's very similar to the game's setting with it's scenic views, beautiful public spaces and shirtless men with revolvers. So I think it's almost unnecessary to tell you, that when I first spotted Tartarus, I immediately thought: "Oh, I've been here before!", but then, afterI crawled through all 627.000 floors of it, I realiezed something: Tartarus isn't actually a 1:1 scale replica of the part of town I grew up in, it's a metaphor. A metaphor for the unending struggle of the brazillian citizen against a corrupt regime, trying to put him down at every step. Knowing this, I understand that the game might not be as immersive or breathtaking to most people, as those of us who were fortunate enough to be born into the paradise of Brasil, but I sincerely hope everyone else can at least come close to the uplifting experience I had while playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I experienced Persona 3 FES for the first time 6 years ago. While I enjoyed my time with Persona 4 and Persona 5, the story, characters, messages and themes of this game felt especially powerful. As with the other Persona games, your character chooses how to spend their time every day for an entire school year. Who you hang out with affects your relationships and combat-related abilities. I've always felt that Persona 3's themes in particular add more weight to this gameplay loop.What I love about Reload is that expands on what made Persona 3 special instead of shying away from the heavier themes. Linked episodes, study sessions and dorm hangouts are all welcome additions that show more sides to our main characters even when things aren't so serious.Tartarus got a major overhaul in Reload. As someone who found the original Tartarus tedious, Reload Tartarus added enough variety and new mechanics that I thoroughly enjoyed the almost roguelike gameplay. The combat animations and battle music are a treat to experience. Theurgy is a particularly fun new mechanic that the writers did a great job interweaving into the lore. A few Theurgy, however, do feel overpowered. For experienced players, I don't think Reload will satisfy your difficulty itch but for most players I think Tartarus will be a casual and fun experience that doesn't overstay its welcome.The voice acting and graphics also got a major upgrade which only make the most iconic scenes hit even harder. Making social links fully voiced for the first time in the series added a lot more impact than I expected.For me the main appeal is the story. Persona 3 is a character drama first and foremost. Even as ominous events happen in the background, the focus is always on how the main cast reacts and changes. So immerse yourself in this world day by day and enjoy the journey that is one of my favorite stories ever!

_childDocuments_.review: It's good.*Gameplay-wise (fighting), it's probably the best of the main Persona titles.*The level design of Tartarus is interesting, but I think Persona 5's puzzles made P5 somewhat better at that. As a note, one of the levels is very bright and colourful and very hard on the eyes; the white level too is kinda hard on the eyes, though not as much.*Story is probably the best, though kinda unrelatable compared to P4, but also grimmer and with much higer stakes (P4 golden gets there too but it's much lighter and doesn't feel as scary). Way better than P5, which I never appreciated with their whole theme of 'adults are so bad and unhelpful, we teens are the only hope to fix things' (repeated ad nauseam).*The characters are OK. No weird mascot character like P4's Teddie or P5's Morgana (though I liked Morgana). There is a dog and there is a robot, but the characters are for more serious and integrate better. Relations flow ok.*Romances (and S-links specifically) are as bad as every other Persona. As per usual, somebody whines to you and you listen or fix their problems somehow and then it's love / friendship forever. Problem with this has always been that it's never mutual. They never care about you nor ask anything about your problems - in the main storyline it happens somewhat, but not in the romances or link.Btw, romances are all straight and every girl falls for you. Children want to marry you, Teachers want to date you.*Voices are great, I played with Japanese voices*I felt the UI was somewhat worse than P5; maybe I don't remember it all that well, but there's a lot of clicking and when you gain a point in one of your stats it's soooo slow; can't skip that part much, have to click and click and click and wait and click and by the end when everything is maxed out that's just pure wasting time. Btw, still as annoying as ever, not telling you when you're gonna max your stat and one of the stats (Academics) levels way slower than the others.*There's no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minigames like fishing and all achis are easily attainable (maybe not getting all S-links maxed out in the first playthrough, but that's easy enough 2nd time).*Ending, which was spoiled already to me by everyone (I never played the original P3) sucks and I hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: While yes I recommend this game I do want to point out how this title compares to the other numbered Persona games you can get on Steam.First graphically this is better than P4 Golden, but not as good as P5 Royal. So:1. P5 Royal  2. P3 Reload  3. P4 GoldenNext since this is a Persona game there is the inevitable party, banter, cohesion, friendship aspect. I'd say this is the weakest of the three titles you can get here. Now this isn't to say it's bad, but it doesn't have a sense of comradeship P4 and P5 has. The order of those is:1. P4 Golden ( Light years ahead of the rest)    2. P5 Royal    3. P3 ReloadThen the actual story itself. Again all three are good stories but I think this one may be the weakest. P5 I felt had an amazing story and reason for doing what you're doing. However here it can leave a little to be desired. The order for those are:1. P5 Royal   2. P4 Golden    3. P3 ReloadCombat is essentially the same as they all have a procedurally generated dungeon-esq area to grind. All three have Personas to fuse so there isn't a clear runaway from these.The length of the game however feels the shortest of the three. Now understand it's a Persona game so it'll still take a while but you'll get moved along at a fairly decent pace.Lastly is the highschool events, vacation events, classroom events, and social links. All three have tons of social links to fill out but outside of social links there is hardly much to do at all. The order for extra events is:1. P5 Royal   2. P4 Golden   3. P3 ReloadAll in all I"d recommend but honestly not for full price. I got it on Steam Summer Sale and have been pleased but for a 60-70 price tag I don't think it's worth it. But if you're an Atlus Fan and Persona Fan you'll definitely want to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload brings a stunning and nostalgic overhaul to the beloved classic. With its beautifully reworked visuals, refined gameplay mechanics, and an enhanced user interface, it feels both fresh and familiar. The emotional depth of the story and the unforgettable characters remain intact, while the new features, like voice acting for every line of dialogue, elevate the experience. The fusion of daily life simulation with turn-based dungeon crawling keeps players engaged, making it an immersive journey worth revisiting for both longtime fans and newcomers. Overall, P3R is a fantastic remake that captures the heart of the original while modernizing it for today's audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 was my first experience with the MegaTen franchise back in 2017 and I instantly fell in love with it. Naturally, after completing the game, I tried my hand at the earlier entries; starting with Persona 3. The story really piqued my interest and I was really excited to get back to fusing Demons in the Velvet Room. However, I found it hard to keep engaging with the game due to it's archaic systems and graphics, so I dropped it about 3 months into the game's school year.Fastforward 7 years later, I picked it back up with Persona 3 Reload and the game is astounding. From what I've played the plot seems pretty intact and faithful to the original source material. Although, the pacing early on is a bit slow and sometimes story elements are a bit all over the place, the game really finds its groove during the month of July. Every Social Link is unique and exposes the protagonist to their daily struggles. I especially loved The Sun Arcana Social Link and his journey to come to terms with his own fleeting mortality. Every one of them is very impactful and a real joy to experience.On a another note, the new dynamic UI elements really help to liven the game up and bring it to par with Person 5's UI design, all while giving it it's own unique and distinct flair. The sound design is also on point by reorchestrating the original tracks that made the game special and by adding some new one's into the mix. The new "It's Going Down Now", "Color your Night" and the remixed version of "Changing Seasons" particularly stand out. In my eyes, the Persona soundtracks still stand leagues above the rest.Combat is still amazing with the Press Turn/1 More system that keeps turn based battles fast paced and engaging all while rewarding strategic thinking. There's not a lot more to say on the matter.In short, Persona 3 Reload is nothing short of a masterpiece. With an amazing visual style, great combat, fantastic soundtrack and a moving story to boot, it certainly holds a very special place in my heart and might as well have cemented itself as my new favorite game in the franchise.10/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I never got to play this game when I was younger, but being able to experience the modern adaptation of this game with quality-of-life and game play overhauls makes me optimistic for the future of my favorite game series. I love the story, art, and feel of this game... and it reminds me of how Pokemon (when it was good) would release modernized versions of previous games. Between the hype in the community and the quality of the game getting better and better, there is no doubt this game series is in an absolute golden age. I am hoping that some of the feedback received can be applied to improving future iterations of the series much like how the implementation of agile played a huge part in improving the seemingly flawless Persona 5 into Persona 5 Royal. KEEP EXECUTING THIS:1. After 5 different installments into the series, all confidants and their social links are voiced (except the hermit, but it adds to impressiveness considering you are texting the hermit the entire time).2. Staying true to the original concept of the franchise makes be believe Altus is among the most humble of studios. My favorite part of the franchise is the element of psychology that connects you with the characters in the game world. Finding your place is challenging, but being able relate to Carl Jung’s persona archetype system each game really adds value to the game as well as the team’s reputation. Compared to many modern studios, Atlus stays true to the dynamic between its original business model and value to the consumer. 3. Graphics. I don’t really need to say much about this because it’s iconic, but the UI designers are extremely talented. When I was at SCAD, most game art majors would reference persona as the most iconic art in any series of games. AREAS OF IMPROVEMENT:1. The game can improve on a few elements... Outside the main cast, it would appear many of the NPCs are lifeless. This is one of my biggest issues with this game, and by far it is the most noticeable in the club. 2. Some quality of life updates from Royal were neglected. I really enjoyed being able to negotiate enemies, and I do realize that this is a remake of Persona 3... But I can't help but feel it was still something that could have been added. This does not quite take away from the experience of the game, but I am hoping that future installments of the game can have the negotiation tactics in the series. 3. It starts off extremely slow, and while it picks up later, usually hooking in the viewer is crucial to story telling. I realize of course this is a remake, so I am hoping the next installment in the franchise can have a quicker tutorial than prior entries.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't planning on buying the game to be quite frank since I already own it on the PS2. In the end, I decided to get it since my partner was interested in it. So I ended playing with it myself and I have a couple of things to say. Firstly, I think ATLUS is extremely greedy to charge $94 CAD for a remake that doesn't have new content in it. Even when the game was on sale, it took me some convincing to decide to get it even though it wasn't for me initially. In the end I think it was a bit overpriced even if it was on sale. Secondly, the copy I bought 45$ back then on PS2 included the FES segment with Aegis. To my surprise, I've realized that now this part of the game that was included with the base game is now a $47 CAD dlc. So, in reality the remake costs $140 CAD. That's absolutely insane. I remember a time when I started to stop liking Squaresoft as a company and started considering ATLUS like the new golden standard for rpgs. Now, I'm starting to see ATLUS the same way I used to see Squaresoft back then. Don't get me wrong, it's nice to see this game with improved graphics, but those graphical revamps don't justify the insane price ATLUS is currently proposing. On top of that, they propose dlcs for costume. Yeah, it's just cosmetic in the end, but when your single player game that is a remake of an old game is already over 100$, maybe you should take a chill pill on the dlcs. Another negative point is that you have to deal with denuvo. Additionally, I personally think the soundtrack was better in the previous versions. This might be nostalgia, but I don't like the small modifications they've made on some of the tracks. Nothing game breaking, but it's a bit annoying. I wish there was an option to select the old ost in the options. Really, the worst aspect of the game is the insane greed of ATLUS. If you don't mind denuvo and if you really want the game, wait for a sale; it's clearly not worth paying full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is a breathtaking re-imagining of a beloved classic, bringing a new layer of depth and complexity to an already great game, a story so connected with reality and filled with raw emotions. It manages to stay so grounded for a story about exploring the human psyche despite its existing in a medium that tends to be chosen for stories that are the complete opposite in that they are as far from reality as you can get. Every Character, Yukari, Junpei, Mitsuru, Akihiko, ♥♥♥♥♥ and Aigis get their own character development throughout as well as having to face the reality of Persona 3 Reload's finale and how they will choose to live on after these events. A soundtrack that is so well written and composed that many consider that you are buying a soundtrack with a game rather than vice versa because it is that good with remakes of old tracks from persona 3 that sound new and fresh and new songs that fit in perfectly such as "Color Your Night." Social links are a staple of the persona series and they don't disappoint here, with a rich cast of side characters as well as having additional scenes for the cast that weren't in the original game, giving you a break from the tower of Tartarus which has had many quality of life changes added helping the flow of the game and keeping it from becoming stale. A masterclass example of a remake done right.it’s an unforgettable journey through the depths of the human psyche and learning to face death... a must play for any fan of the series or those looking to start.

_childDocuments_.review: It is worth throwing out there that my entry to the series was through Persona 5 Royal so my views are very much colored from my experience with that game.Persona 3 Reload is a fantastic game with a pretty great story (not without flaw but we will get into that) but I couldn't help but think to myself that the tower of Tartarus concept is outdated and it really feels that way when you play it.As far as Persona games available on steam, I'd still recommend 5 first to a newcomer, then I'd recommend this. I don't think 4 golden is for me as I have abandoned it on several attempts whereas when I played P3R and P5R I made it a mission to play them through from start to finish in very short amounts of time.To start, the story, characters and day to day of Persona 3 are all great. However when contrasting to 5 you can tell that some of the things are outdated. From what I am aware of, your social skills that you level up only impact in Social links with three individual people, not to mention there are only three, so by the time you max them out a huge chunk of evening progression feels lost (thankfully, unlike 5, they have dorm mate hang outs that both give nuggets of story, can unlock potential upgrades for partners and grant items or consumables). The unforunate byproduct is that it feels like your afternoons suffer from decision paralysis of who to spend time with while your evenings are largely barren.As far as social links go (for P5 players, these would be the same as your confidants), the stories are really tear jerking. I felt especially moved during Maiko's storyline [spoilers] in which she talked about her parents current divorce - which viewed through the lens of a child makes it all the more heartbreaking... my only hang up with this storyline is the fact that it leaned into a child confessing to want marry the protagonist which made me feel very uncomfortable[/spoilers], as well as in Akinari's storyline [spoilers] which follows a terminally ill young adult trying to come to grips with his pending death - him creating a children's story that served as a fantastic metaphor for his character as well as the protagonist really got to me emotionally and by the time his story came to its full conclusion in the epilogue i was in full blown tears[/spoilers]. In addition to that, the story with two late additions to your team was also a story highlight [spoilers] The story of Ken Amada and his parents tragic death paired with Shinjiro Aragaki's tragic tale of not being in full control of his Persona made for a great twist that I didn't see coming. Shinjiro was one of my favorites throughout the storyline and when his story was tragically cut short (and in such a poetic way in the bossfight i might add) it really made tear up [/spoilers].But it's not all praise however, my most major criticisms of the game lie in the hands of the games primary antagonists - this whole section will be wrapped in spoilers [spoilers] I like the idea of Strega as a whole, but they largely felt under utilized and explored to me. I would have really enjoyed it if they had mirrored their team to be opposites of SEES. Chidori being a noted counterpart to ♥♥♥♥♥, and Takaya an obvious counterpart to the protagonist, why not add an additional two that could be paired against Mitsuru & Sanada? Jin felt like a largely nothing character who just looked up to Takaya, but Chidori had a very interesting arc and her end was another high point for the game when her Persona fused with Junpei. Unlike Chidori who had a great character ending, Jin's felt like wasted time and Takaya's felt wrong to me. Junpei should have been FILLED WITH RAGE upon seeing Takaya and had to either be stopped or convinced to stop or maybe even an option to let him finish Takaya - Takaya was responsible for the deaths of Chidori AND NOTED SEES MEMBER AND CLOSE FRIEND TO SANADA AND MITSURU, SHINJIRO ARAGAKI! Not showing their mixed emotions and just turning the other cheek felt wholly wrong, especially given Takaya's lethality. It felt to me like they wanted him to witness the final battle and it didn't feel earned.Beyond Strega though, my biggest complaint with antagonists would have to lie squarely on Ikutski's shoulders. I had a bad feeling about him just because of his callousness towards certain things, but otherwise didn't expect him to be wholly evil and responsible for a lot of the problems. For him to be introduced as a villain, only to be killed off minutes later in a cutscene felt SO OUT OF LEFT FIELD AND ANTI-CLIMACTIC that i can't help but just feel like it was shoehorned in to give Mitsuru some misplaced character development. [/spoilers]In summary, the game is great, It has many of my favorite Persona moments - in certain ways it has the best of what Persona has to offer - but it isn't my favorite of the series and I have many of own gripes that drags it down from being a perfect release to me. The story is there, the dark themes are there, but the execution of certain character arcs, and some subpar, outdated, repetive game mechanics made what otherwise could have been a masterpiece into a great but flawed title.I would recommend Persona 5 Royal to any first time player of the series over this, but if you are looking to scratch the itch and aren't intimidated by some heavy topics and themes, this is a great use of your time and will provide at least 65+ hours of entertainment...

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the exclusion of the female main character from Persona 3 Portable will forever render this game a 9/10. If it weren't for that, this would be a 9.5/10. You'll see what I mean). - It's easily the easiest Persona title to date (compared to Persona 3 FES, however, I'm not sure that's a bad thing). It's Persona 3 with the Persona 5 upgrades to combat. Theurgy is fun but fundamentally overpowered, similar to Showtimes. You can make crazy Persona combos relatively easy with the amount of boosting abilities added to the game. - Now... with all my misgivings out of the way. Persona 3 has the most intriguing story of the entire Persona series. It is engulfed in fascinating symbolism that adds incredible ways of interpreting the story, should you know the stories of the figures the cast's Personas are based on, as well as the attributes of the tarot that they are categorized as. This level of story telling, combined with the unique atmosphere and message it conveys, makes it stand out as an unforgettable, authentic piece of art. It's worth your time, and this title is easily the most accessible way of experiencing it.

It's a faithful remake that captures the essence of the original while offering a visually stunning and engaging experience. So as a long time Persona fan, this time I decided to complete it at least once. Was it worth my time? Yes. Will I ever play it again? No.Despite some of the best main characters written and a visually aesthetic redo, the title becomes extremely repetitive in the long run. The characters you build Social Links with are mostly unrelatable and their story arcs fall flat compared to other Persona titles, which is on the other hand to be expected from the predecessor title. Tartarus exploration has been made very fluid, however the current Major Arcana system will result in extreme over-leveling, making me wish I had played the title on higher than normal difficulty on the initial run. The OST is an absolute joy, which is no surprise. Main Story wise, it is unfortunate that the pacing in 3 does not rise to the same level as 4 and 5. There were times I felt that plot twists were completely unaddressed, or characters were almost unfazed by the events. However the Story is still overall solid, albeit predictable in some aspects. Fluid and fun combat and beautiful UIs stand out as the best aspects of the title.Despite some disappointments along the way, I am glad I finally finished the title. Thank you Aigis, I can now close my eyes, indeed.

Technically yes, this game does not differ from the original. It has some added elements from the two later variations Persona 3 FES and Persona 3 Portable such as some additional gameplay, but overall this is a very similar game to the original. However, this is still a lot of more content added to the story in this version that no other version had. There’s simple things like a bunch more spoken dialogue and new mechanics added that were introduced in Persona 4 and Persona 5. However there is some new story content added. Nothing major that changes the plot of the game, but it just adds to it. Personally, despite P3 being my favorite in the franchise, I was never too attached to the characters. I thought they were interesting sure, but none of them were super memorable to me. The added story content added a lot of characterization and context for characters that, honestly looking back on it, really needed it. Some of the characters that I thought as forgettable before are honestly some of my favorite characters now. This by far is my favorite version of P3, the only downside is that I do wish the female protagonist from P3P were included so that this would be the definitive version of the game. _childDocuments_.review: So my experience with this game I'd say is pretty unique to most, which is also why the reasoning for my rating is likely different from most. For context, I was saving money around launch so I was not able to buy this game day 1, more importantly before day 1 (this is important later). My friend however, who I happen to library share with, DID pre-order the game. So, during the time he wasn't online, I was on the game. I made about 60 hours of progress. Then, recently, I finally had enough money to work with to buy the game myself. Slight issue, he got the Premium Edition, which has all the DLC. I didn't like any of the DLC, but I was just planning on not using them. Unfortunately, as it turns out, once you make progress WITH DLC, you are now FORCED to use that DLC or else be locked out of your save file. Luckily, I just had to buy the Premium Edition so I could keep my save file. Except the ACTUAL problem is that tiiiiiiny little detail I mentioned earlier. Remember when I said my friend pre-ordered the game? That means he got the pre-order exclusive DLC, the P4G BGM set. You know how I had to buy the game after launch? That means that that DLC isn't purchasable at all. Now I load into my save file, and I'm locked out of my save file because I don't have the P4G BGM Set. Atlus, do tell me, why is my save file locked behind music? What is so important about this music that it requires me to RESTART MY WHOLE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PLAYTHROUGH BECAUSE I CAN'T LISTEN TO IT IN-GAME?! To review, I borrowed a pre-ordered copy of the game from a friend's library, and now that I bought the game with my own money, I cannot access my 60 hour save file because I do not have the pre-order bonus exclusive DLC that is not purchasable anywhere in the store. I would have totally gave this game a glowing review because it's legitimately a great remake of a great game, but because of how the game treats DLC (that imo shouldn't have been a thing at all, they add nothing to the experience and feel like they're there just to pull on some kind of nostalgia strings), I am now locked out of all my progress and must restart my playthrough, thus I'm giving the game a bad review. These DLC are just plain stupid, but locking me out of my save file? That's scummy.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Persona 4 and 5 Royal, I was shocked to see that Persona 3 Reload did much more for me in the 47 hours I played (first playthrough) than either of the other two did in 78 and 113 hours respectively (I even replayed Persona 5 after finishing this game just to see whether I was misremembering an actually great story from P5R... I wasn't).I think the best way for me to recommend Persona 3 Reload is to discuss what I disliked about P5R (having revisited it) because the two are very similar in a lot of ways. To me, P5R's biggest weakness is its philosophical thinness. The majority of the game is like a college kid who talks about Marxism in a cool light because it's hip and "modern" and therefore correct.. without trying to ponder over why libertarianism exists in the first place. Scratch that, it IS exactly that, but set in a high school setting. The game mostly subscribes to the "greed is bad" view without looking at the positive outcomes of semi-corrupt governments and big companies today like Tesla (even though the people at the top might not be what you call "ideal comrades"). To be fair to P5R, I enjoyed the last part against Maruki but was quite disappointed in the "true ending" rationale against Maruki's vision; the thieves basically just say "I'm happy with this reality, so boohoo Maruki I'll do what I want, I don't care that it might cause suffering for lots of people". I myself believe that a far more pragmatic argument against Maruki is the dilemma problem: if two people want mutually interfering outcomes, like say, there's a war between countries X and Y and I want X to win while the other person wants Y, then who decides what's the right choice in terms of making either of us happy? And if you then say that we could just avoid war altogether, then what about, say, nationalistic sentiments and imperialistic desires? Why should a person like Maruki then get to decide that a person's nationalistic / imperialistic sentiments are wrong? There are countless more examples like this on even simpler bases. It should be noted that since Maruki's power could eventually be arbitrary as per the game, he could arguably just become God and herald infinite unity across the world (but then this discussion turns meaningless; more productive would be the assumption that Maruki doesn't want to change people's wishes, which would be coherent with the last dungeon's "testing room" logic).Persona 3 Reload, in contrast with what I just described, is a cogent and coherent piece that combines the stylistic elegance and modernity of P5R with a vivid depiction of the human struggle of death, of yin and yang. It is a wonderful story that, unlike P5R, mostly avoids platitudes and does not stretch its rhetoric to political infinity for the sake of sounding modern / politically correct. Additionally, P3R's ending is easily one of my favorites of any game I've played and will stick with me for a while, at the very least.This is a game I can easily recommend to anyone who desires an intellectually stimulating story set in a mechanically and stylistically charming atmosphere, and not the other way around.

Battles, though turn based, are quickly resolved and very satisfying. I know I’ve been hesitating too much when I hear more than a minute of one of the various battle themes.Speaking of — the music is great! It has been living in my head. I play it at work as background music while I wait to dive back into Tartarus. Very catchy stuff here. All in all, a beautiful game with an intriguing mystery and a satisfying game loop. I would particularly recommend it to people who, like me, love turn based RPGs but have tried and failed to be gripped by the series with other installments. Serious fun and thinking to be had here.

The new voice acting is awesome, with performances that capture the personalities and emotions of the characters perfectly. In Conclusion Persona 3 Reload successfully revitalizes a beloved classic, making it accessible to a new gamers while offering plenty of reasons for fans to dive back in. The combination of visual enhancements, gameplay improvements, and new content makes this remake a must-play for JRPG enthusiasts. Whether you're experiencing the story of SEES for the first time or revisiting Tatsumi Port Island, Persona 3 Reload is a compelling and emotional journey that should not be missed.Enjoy Persona 3 Reload!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the persona series for a while now, but in no means an OG fan from the late 90s. I've played persona 3 on the PSP, portable on the Vita, and FES on PS2, and can concretely say this is the most whole, most "fun", and most rewarding rendition of the classic Atlus formula of remastering older games with modern QOL adjustments and snazzy aesthetics."Reload" is different. It has branching paths, alternate narrative breaks, and surprising elements that will keep the seasoned Persona veteran on their toes. That being said, Reload suffers from Persona 5 Royal's gameplay balancing system, where there is a chance that you may be overpowered without grinding too much, even on the harder difficulties, which is something that didn't exist in the older games. However, this only applies to the hardcore veterans of the series, and to new fans the challenge posed by the normal running of the game will be sufficient. The fully-voiced social link interactions throughout ALL the ranks further humanises our favourite characters, and I believe the new VAs breathe some much needed life to some of the stilted dialogue of both FES and Portable. In general, the gameplay is smooth and buttery, dungeon exploration is not AS repetitive as in FES; and certainly Tartarus' new look is at least something interesting. However, not being able to change the song during dungeon-crawling is a definite downside, depending on your preference. Paying for the Aigis expansion is a big letdown, which I'm hesitant to pay for something that was already included with FES, but that's Atlus for you.tl;dr release Aigis episode for free pls

_childDocuments_.review: If you remake what is, debatably, the best video game ever made, it’s really hard for people not to be extremely critical of every single aspect of it. Even with some sloppy changes to the narrative presentation and somewhat misguided (poorly executed) attempts at fixing the battle system, a remake of Persona 3 is still “Persona 3” boasting the best cast of characters in the medium, and one of the best stories. The version you play is really up to your taste and how you view games.If you're a person with love for video games in your heart and you have the maturity and patience to realize sometimes enduring dated systems might be worth it for getting the genuine experience intended by the director and staff, you should play Persona 3 FES for PS2. If you can run this, you can run PCSX2. If you like video games but care more about a game being "fun" and "not obtuse" and want to play a JRPG with a great story play Persona 3: Reload. There’s a lot of changes in this version that come from modern sensibilities regarding cutscene presentation and gameplay elements that feel like they completely miss the mark, but it is a lot more pleasant to actually sit through due to massive quality of life changes and more content to fill in downtime, while also removing a lot of tedium. It boils down to games as art vs games as pure entertainment I guess. Just whatever you do DON’T play the god awful PSP version of the original that’s been ported to consoles/PC. That’s the worst of both worlds with terrible presentation and balance changes intended to fix the gameplay that don’t really work. Please dear god just don’t dismiss FES just because you can’t control your party members and decide to play the version missing half the cutscene graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is an amazing "remake" of the game that defined why the SMT Persona series has become wildly successful.The story, characters and setting all remain the same but a few of the more modern changes presented in Persona 4 and 5 have been applied to Persona 3 here. One of the greatest changes is being able to directly give your party members orders in combat as well as the introduction of "Theurgies" that act as special attacks that each party member can activate. These Theurgies each charge faster based on individual settings/requirements for each party member. The basic Persona combat structure of matching weaknesses to enemies and triggering "1 More" attacks to chain downed statuses to go for All-Out attacks remains in place.The game's style still looks amazing and the menu work in these games remains second-to-none. No one makes stylish menus like Atlus does.A few negative remarks, mostly surrounding sale practices or removal of content that I'm personally not as upset about :"The Answer", which was added to the FES version on the Playstation 2 is going to be released separately at cost as DLC. I'm not as upset about this as others given the amount of additional work that needed to be done art and asset wise to the base game. If that practice doesn't sit well with you, I would say you should wait for a "complete edition" or a sale on both.The Female Protagonist and all associated social links/interactions from the PSP re-release of Persona 3 is not an option here. I also understand that it would've been a significant amount of work to add this in as an option and it would be nice if it would be released to this version so it can be the "definitive" version of Persona 3 going forward, but there has been no indication this content is coming to the game.Overall, for the price, I still think this game is a great way to either re-experience a classic JRPG in the modern era or experience for the first time where most of modern Persona owes its legacy, charm and style. I recommend the game wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Persona series, I couldn't be happier with how Persona 3 Reload breathes new life into one of the franchise's most beloved entries. Atlus has struck the perfect balance between honoring the original's charm and updating the experience for modern players.The visuals are stunning, with the upgraded graphics capturing the game's dark yet hopeful tone. Tartarus has never felt so atmospheric, and the character designs shine with new polish while staying true to their iconic looks.Gameplay improvements are another standout. The updated combat system, inspired by later Persona entries, adds depth without straying from the strategic core of the original. Quality-of-life enhancements like improved navigation and streamlined mechanics make this version more accessible than ever.The re-recorded voice acting adds fresh energy to the beloved cast. Every interaction feels richer, and the new scenes provide deeper insight into the characters, making the story even more emotionally impactful.For fans like me, Persona 3 Reload is not just a remake—it's a love letter to the series' legacy. Whether you're reliving cherished memories or experiencing the Dark Hour for the first time, this game is a must-play. Atlus has delivered yet another masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: This was my second mainline Persona game after playing Persona 4 Golden back in 2020. P4G is one of my favorite persona games, and I did find myself constantly comparing this game to P4G, even if I didn't mean to. The activities in Reload weren't as extensive or exciting as in Golden, but the key parts of any Persona game were all here, all of which I loved. There were times that exploring Tartarus felt a bit like an unnecessary grind, eventually I got into a pretty good rhythm and enjoyed all of my ventures into its many many floors.The biggest strength of this game is its cast of characters, which have to be one of my favorites from any game that I've played recently, possibly even more than Golden if I'm completely honest. I genuinely enjoyed all of the time that I got to spend with all of the characters on this game, which culminated in one of the most beautiful and bittersweet endings that I've experienced in a game in a long time. _childDocuments_.review: also includes a short rant about minor UI and OST stuff.TLDR; If you don't mind the missing content (FEMC and The Answer) it's the best way to experience Persona 3, but it might not be your favorite Persona game. It is definitely a lot more forgiving than the original, P4G, and in my opinion even P5 and P5R. While it is still not a game I would say is possible for a newbie w/o a guide to 100%, I can imagine someone who came from the P5 craze and who is familiar with the systems to have an easy or manageable time doing so. There were some changes with dialogues in certain scenes but I think it's still overall faithful to the original. Yeah you can nitpick some Aigis or Akihiko lines or whatever, but overall the characters are still the same to me. (except Yukari; her VA is way less '♥♥♥♥♥♥' with her delivery of lines which made me stop hating her)Ok honestly, without revamping it I do not know how you can beat the Palaces in P5. Yes there were quality of life reworks like your party members don't get too tired and then become unwilling to continue with the dungeon-ing and there are clocks around to replenish HP and SP for some fragments and of course controllable party members. All they did was make the climb up less stressful, not more fun. Also there's no Ryuji insta-kill passive equivalent here, so you will take longer to farm up.THE CRIT BUFFS ARE INSANE JUST BUILD ONE PHYSICAL DMG MACHINE AND ONE ALMIGHTY NUKE.Theurgies are a cool addition that (I think) add some more depth to the combat that isn't 'superficial.' What I mean is that it doesn't become obsolete late game like ailments or whatever because bosses are just immune. The party members get stuff like a partywide charge/focus/heal or a magical attack with 'severe' motion value of their element. Since lategame fights are more buff/debuff centric this mechanic ages rather well.The Velvet Room is basically the same thing with the P5 installments but stripped down (it just has dyad and special fusions and fusion search). The personas don't have traits anymore (I will miss Vitality of the Tree).I have nothing bad to say about the UI except the wallet in the pause menu. It just looks like an MS Word text box and looks so out of place, how did that happen?! Why is there an extra menu upon entering the Velvet Room before seeing the fusion screen???? Just put me straight there and make me exit by pressing C (on PC) and X or circle on Dualshock controllers. Why do the border floor teleporters give me no choice but to return to the first floor????????The OST in my opinion is an overall upgrade from the original. The exceptions being Iwatodai Dorm and Mass Destruction. For both of these songs my main gripe is the vocals. In my honest opinion they were better off untouched, the unique tone of the Iwatodai Dorm vocals were part if its identity for me. The sharp vocals of the original Mass Destruction were part of the appeal to me as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game genuinely saved my life, it taught me how to recognise I have OCD which pushed me to experiencing Derealization episodes (Which is where you believe life isn't reality, pretty much it's like living through hell itself).I was deadset on unaliving myself the next time I had a Derealization episode, there are 2 characters called Takaya & Jin throughout the course of the game taught me that I suffered from intrusive thoughts as apart of my OCD and ways to calm it down. I still do struggle with my OCD, but ever since I played Persona 3 back in 2022 I haven't had a Derealization episode since. Even though most people dislike Takaya and Jin because they lacked depth in the original, the minimal interactions I had on this game are the sole reason Persona 3 holds a special place in my heart. If you struggle with intrusive thoughts or OCD, I believe this game is worth a shot to see if they'll resonate with you. Here's one quote in particular that is spoken by Jin that stuck with me the most: "Don't be bound by the past, don't look to the future. Simply live in the moment". I applied this quote to myself, instead of fixating on my intrusive thoughts I opted to just focus on what's happening currently in the moment and it actually calmed my OCD down. I didn't know I had OCD back then, but for some reason unknown to me at that point it calmed me down. After in-depth researching regarding OCD I now know why. You push out intrusive thoughts, they'll come back harder. If you try to argue with the intrusive thought itself, you make it stronger and worse. So why did this quote in particular be the thing that got me to deal with my OCD? Because you have to fight the thought with a specific thought that doesn't dissect the intrusive thought or ignores/pushes it out. So let's say I have an OCD impulse that goes like "I have to check every reply to hate me", by telling myself to not fixate on the future and just simply live in the moment I have dealt with the thought in a way that hasn't strengthened it. I don't argue with the contents of the intrusive thought and just deal with it as a concept, if that make sense. There's plenty of other quotes that stuck with me because of these 2 characters, I am forever grateful that this game got remade to breathe new live into these 2 new characters. While people still aren't a fan of Jin, some people have became a fan of Takaya. Having my #1 comfort characters being liked by people is honestly one of the best gifts to ever been given.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't experience any version of Persona 3 until I played this one, so I was pretty blind to just about everything Reload was going to offer. My first game in the SMT series was Persona 5, and I eventually played Persona 4 Golden, meaning going into P3 Reload, I had the context of what the series used to be like compared to what it's like now. This game was marketed as being a version of Persona 3 that would be more accessible to people who started their Persona adventures with P5, and after having played it, I can see what they were going for.In essence, it's the same kind of gameplay you'd expect from Persona; you hunt down monsters by exploiting their weaknesses in turn-based combat, you acquire new abilities by interacting with your hot anime friends and by combining creatures you've collected, and you stop some god or godlike figure by the end of the game from destroying the world. In Reload, there are a couple of quality-of-life changes they made to the battle system that makes it flow like how it did in P5 Royal, like giving the player the ability to Baton Pass ("Shift" in this game) to other teammates to knock down more opponents. Everything feels a lot flashier than what I assume the original game(s) felt like, which is one feature from P5 that I appreciate seeing return. As far as the setting and characters are concerned, it feels like they didn't try to update anything at all, but that's coming from someone who never had context for what it was like originally. Personally speaking, the setting felt weak and a fair few of the characters felt weaker; I understand the importance of maintaining everything plot-related in a game that's meant to tell the story of Persona 3 with a fresh coat of paint, but if they did translate everything 1-to-1, then I don't think I liked this setting as much as I did for those of the later two Persona games. Character archetypes that were present in all three games that I liked before didn't feel as enjoyable in this game. For example, the archetype of the right-hand man who's kind of a doofus but has a heart of gold; I loved Ryuji in P5, but it was hard for me to like Junpei for most of this game. There's also the archetype of the first female teammate who learns the ropes with you; Chie was awesome in P4, but Yukari never really stood out in this game. The world you can explore is pretty small, too; you only get six major hubs for fast travel, with usually only one room to walk around in and explore. I also really didn't enjoy how apathetic the protagonist was, or at least how often apathetic dialogue choices appeared for him.Despite how I felt about the characters, I did find myself really enjoying the voice acting. Several of the VAs felt like they were perfectly portraying the character they were acting for, rather than simply reading off a script. Not to mention, every Social Link is practically fully voiced, unlike in P5 where only one or two parts of a Social Link have any prominent voice acting. It all helps to keep you invested in the characters and the plot. I was also impressed by the lip flaps on both the character models and the portraits that appear next to the text boxes; they move depending on the volume of whatever sound is being played at the moment, meaning the characters' mouths are fully open on vowel sounds, half-open on stuff like "s" sounds, and closed when the actor is between sentences. It's a pretty cool detail.I didn't find myself enjoying the plot or the music as much as the other two Persona games I've played, but much like the characters, that kind of thing is subjective. The themes of death and loss were pretty prevalent in this game, so it makes sense why the characters were overall a bit more melancholy than the later games, and why the plot didn't have that many surprises lying in wait. For instance, because I had played the other games before this one, I had assumed Takaya was a Shadow version of Ikutsuki due to his stark fashion differences alongside similar builds, hair length and yellow eyes, but that guess never proved true. I did make a different guess about one of the characters' motivations, and I was not surprised when it was confirmed. Overall, I enjoyed the game. It's exactly what they were going for when they wanted to Persona-5-ify Persona 3; they maintained the major elements of what made the original game what it is, but updated the gameplay and graphics enough to allow newer players to comfortably experience the world of that original game. I would almost certainly play a Reload-styled remake of Persona 4, if that's on the table for future releases.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve finally managed to experience the game for all it has to offer, and I have a lot to say. My journey into the Persona franchise started back in 2019. 	I was rambling on about JJBA to a friend of mine when he whipped out his phone and showed me a gif of the MC from p3FES shooting himself. I thought it was the funniest ♥♥♥♥ ever and immediately wanted to know where it was from. After being told about the game, I immediately went looking for a way to play it. The only ps2’s in my house were both Japanese, and I didn’t feel like learning another language just to play a game, nor did I have the time. We also had a ps3 lying around, but I was a broke high school student so its not like I had money to throw on games. Leaving me to settle with the only choice I had left, emulation. It got the job done. I was playing p3FES in all of its low res, polygon glory. 	It was nothing like I had ever experienced before, sure I had my fair share of turn- based combat before, Mario and Luigi Partners in time, Chrono Trigger, but nothing to this extent. The way the personas emerged from each character was simply enthralling. Its combat was fun and engaging, even though I had a rough time understanding it at the start. The social school / sim aspect was something also new to me. Going around the city, talking to the other characters, learning about their goals and aspirations, wants and needs, desires and fears, absolute peak. I remember being introduced to Kenji, dude was something. Took you out to grab a bite, then started, with no filter, telling me how much he loved older women…from that moment on I knew that this character was the best, and I immediately went about ranking him up, he’s my very first max social link I completed in the entire franchise. Bro knows what he wants and has great taste, what can i say, he’s just like me fr. 	Sadly my little zoomer brain could not be entertained by the game for long, i found most of the plot dumping boring and even the combat, as much as I loved the animations, got tedious for me.Finally after the Chariot Arcana boss fight I dropped the game. It wouldn't be until the winter of 2020 that i would return to the Persona franchise, but not to complete p3fes, I had a new entry that caught my eye, the pc port of p4g, currently only playable on the ps vita. 	I spent hundreds of hours in that game, combing over each and every character, min maxing my personas, grinding out social links or simply just listening to the amazing soundtrack as I explored the town of Inaba. That game changed me, and as silly as it sounds, gave me a reason to keep on living. I don’t cry that often, I'm not fond of shedding tears, I don't like the mess they cause and the feeling I get in my chest as it tightens. However, as “Never more” began playing over the final credits of p4g, I couldn’t stop the waterfall. Since my completion of p4g, I have played through:P2 IS P4 AUP5RP5 StrikersPQPQ 2Which leads me to now, the remaster of p3, p3Reload. This game is amazing. I feel that since I've had the chance to both grow and mature since originally starting p3fes, I have come to love the dark and somber tone of this game.It’s made me reflect on how I use and spend my time. We all have a clock ticking, and once it reaches zero, it's over. Maybe you believe in the afterlife, maybe you don’t, but in the end we all run out of time. That doesn’t mean we should fear the end, but embrace each and every day that we have. Meet new people, try new things, connect with those whom you may have not seen in a while, call your parents, go and see them, that’s the message I got from p3r, go out and enjoy life. tl:dr Go out and touch some grass.

_childDocuments_.review: Best game to have ever gamed. But seriously though, here’s a review.Before this game came out, it felt like almost everyone was hoping for it to fail. _childDocuments_.review: I still have the original Persona 3 on disc for PS2 (and the PS2 to play it on).  The Reload version keeps the characters we know and love, as well as the plot and the dialogue of the original game (although the dialogue has been tweaked a bit - just smoothing rough edges more than a major rework), but it adds in greatly updated graphics with a stronger 3D feel, as well as adding a lot of new content.  The battle system is still recognisably the same one from the original game, but it's been tweaked with what Atlus has learned we liked from the newer games as well - the major differences I'm spotting so far are: there's a lot more treasure drops from Shadows; there's a lot more objects to gather; and they've added in a version of the Baton Pass system from P5 (called "Shifting") to increase the ease of dealing with difficult shadows.  Other little tweaks include definitely confirming the voice you hear in your head announcing your bonds is your attendant.   I'm looking forward to finding all the other little tweaks they've made to the game as I keep going through it, but so far, this Reload is definitely a positive experience.(Dear Atlus: could you maybe Reload the original Persona and both bits of Persona 2 for those of us who are real lore junkies?  Please?)

The only Persona game I played was Persona 5 back in 2020 on the PS3 (i didn't have a PS4 or a PS5 at the time) and I loved it! it lead me into the world of Persona but i fell out of it after I finished it and didn't really return to it. I did get Persona 5 Royal but at the time i had a pretty bad computer so i couldn't play it. I eventually bought a computer last November that is literally a beast so i got to run games I've wanted to play in a long time. This year my best friend got me into Persona 4 and Persona 3 and i have to thank him for it. So if he's reading this, thank you very much for getting me more into a franchise I deeply love and appreciate more. Anyways as for Persona 3 Reload, this is a fantastic remake that I love to death. It's like if Persona 3 got the Persona 5 treatment in terms of polish with it's art style, menu, character portraits and more but still having the things that old fans like. This game is gorgeous and is the most beautiful game i've played with an anime style hands down. In terms of 2024 releases, this is my GOTY and I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ what you say.While i do prefer Persona 4's social links, Persona 3 owns up for that in story and Aigis (without giving spoilers) has one of the best social links, not just in Persona 3 but in any Persona game. Makoto (The Protag) is the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I absolutely love him for that and he's also my favorite Persona Protag hands down. The music is absolutely great but songs like Mass Destruction is just butchered and lose a lot of charm of what made the original great. I've listened to both of them back and forth and the original is just better in every single aspect. But Color Your Night, Memories Of You, Changing Seasons are absolutely fantastic and I will continue to blast it to death in my free time.The story is just fantastic. I've never been the type of cry at video games. I've teared at games here and there but only 2 games have made me full out break down, which being Red Dead 2 and now recently: Persona 3 Reload. Everything from start to finish, you don't want to put that keyboard (or controller) down for a second! Every character is fleshed out and makes it hard to spend your time with one specific person. Persona 3 Reload's combat has the best combat UI though.Overall: Persona 3 Reload is a absolutely fun and a gorgeous remake and has entered my top 3 video games of all time. A fantastic game that is an experience everyone should enjoy. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know how I should begin writing this, but here it goes. I used to always watch my cousin, who owns a PS2, and I was really interested when I saw him playing Persona 3 FES. I was around 10 years old at the time. Of course, I played some of it but never finished it. Then the time came to have my own personal computer, which is good enough to emulate PS2 games. I was really ecstatic to play P3FES that time. I remember everything about it—the songs, enemies, and battles. What I forgot was the lesson it gave me back then: to have hope while we are living, to not wish for our own death, and the main message of the game, which is still relevant today, “Memento mori.”.But first, I want to talk about the new things that were added.I really liked the added character-linked episodes, along with the voice lines for the linked episodes and social links.The character linked episodes gave the characters more depth, along with the already great character development the original story contained. My favorite and closest to my heart was Koromaru’s linked episode.The added voice lines were really vital in this remake, especially in the emotional parts of the story. It really made me cry when I heard the emotions, even though I already knew what would happen.The new Tartarus exploration is fun, and some of the new mechanics, I would say, made the game too easy, but that’s fine for me. What really mattered to me the most was the faithfulness to the original story and characters.It’s grim, right? Memento mori, “remember that you will die." Along with the ominous aura of the city and P3R’s opening game animation scene, this game is screaming “Death” as its main theme. But with death, there’s life, and with life, there are opportunities, problems, and outcomes. It’s how we deal with those things that makes our life’s journey worth taking. After all, we’re all going to die, right? Why not make the best of it and seize the day?“Memento mori, memento vivere"—remember that you will die, but remember to live. Suddenly you’ll realize it isn’t that grim anymore, that the looming death is just really a reminder that we should do the things that make us happy, to be with the people we treasure and love, to find our purpose, to find the answer to life’s greatest question.This game really changed my outlook on life, and it came back when I forgot the lessons and ideals it gave me back then. It’s funny because I really needed it right now with what’s currently happening in my life.I will forever cherish this game because of what it gave me and made me realize. It might not be the case for you, but still, I would recommend this game, especially if you haven’t played it before.I’m looking forward to Episode Aigis, also known as “The Answer," which is quite controversial, and what they would add.Thank you if you’ve read this. I wrote this on a whim, and forgive me if it is all over the place.Amazing soundtrack, story, characters, battles, and message. Easy 9/10, but in my heart it’s 100000000/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to keep this as vague as possible to avoid spoilers for absolutely everything, and just sharing my thoughts right after finishing the game.P3R definitely feels more like a slow burn when comparing it to P4G, but what really sold it for me was the final arc of the game. Although it didn't have the silly goofy characters I hold so dear to my heart found in the Investigation Team, SEES was appropriately and amazingly written for the themes this game is going for, and has its own identity compared to my pre-established notion of what a Persona game is like.Without getting into too many details, all I can say is Persona 3 Reload was a truly fantastic and possibly even life changing experience. The sound track is phenomenal and pairs exceptionally well to what is going on in the game, and I even listen to it regularly in my daily life. The characters, main cast, social links, and even random dialogues around town, are written to feel like genuine people, and it synergises with the darker themes shown. The gameplay is what you would expect from other Persona titles with some much needed quality of life improvements, so if you're a masochist like I am, and enjoy spending a ludicrous amount of time grinding, then the JRPG aspect of this game would be right up your alley.By no means am I saying this game is without its flaws, but what masterpiece doesn't have flaws imposed on to them by the biased public? Kind of a pretentious thing to say in a Steam review of all things, but I wholeheartedly stand behind that. For instance, I absolutely hated every time I got insta-killed, having to regrind numerous sections of the game, but does that take away from the full experience? A little, but I can overlook it. It's negligible flaws like that which can potentially put some people off the game, but all I want to say with this rant is to STICK WITH IT. The payoff is well worth it if you want to experience the amazing story told in Persona 3.

From the captivating storyline to the unique blend of gameplay elements, this game has quickly become a favorite in my collection.Engaging Storyline:Persona 3 Reload weaves an intricate and emotionally charged narrative that had me hooked from the get-go. The game tackles some deep and meaningful themes that resonate with the challenges of being a teenager, making it not just a game but a profound experience.Stylish Visuals and Design:One word: stylish. The animated cutscenes are a visual feast, and the attention to detail in the environments adds an extra layer of immersion to the overall experience.Innovative Gameplay Mechanics:The fusion of social simulation and dungeon crawling in Persona 3 Reload is nothing short of genius. _childDocuments_.review: Get yourself a copy of Persona 3 Reload so you can pay your proper respects to Death.The Persona series is known for a number of things, each of which come to mind when you think of any one of its entries: good story and characters, monster collecting, turn-based combat, and social simulation, with some of the most infectious musical bangers ever to grace video games. One more thing it's fair to say about Persona and the larger Shin Megami Tensei series as a whole, is that it is INCREDIBLY dense in symbolism, and most if not all regular players will agree with that. All Persona titles and the MegaTen games I've seen are extremely allegorical to Biblical and Gnostic texts and usually draw on a great deal of other world mythology as well. I believe Persona 3 is where this symbolism really hit its stride.Persona 3 is known for being the first Persona title to introduce its social sim aspects, dividing the day as a student with responsibilities and friendships to maintain from the night, where you infiltrate some rendition of human subconscious and combat hordes of Shadows. But for me, what I like to highlight about P3's contribution to the series, is the overarching theme that these systems were created to lend credit to. You've probably figured this out by now, but that theme is Death, and it is EVERYWHERE in this game.Persona 3 takes on a damn near Poe-esque level of literary totality where EVERY cinematic, nearly every piece of dialogue, and all the music reflects the game's constant rumination on Death -- dying, making the most of the time you have, facing death and uncertainty with courage, longing to connect with someone before you die, the inevitable passage of time, the coming End of Things. Every character you meet is dealing with, in some way, the possibility of death, the inevitability of death, the grieving of death, the need to be successful before death, the need to make friendships before death, the questing of what the point is if no matter what there is death, so and and so forth and so death, death, death. You are constantly bombarded with images of ticking clocks, calendars and moon phases counting down, and the reminder that you don't have time to hang out with this person AND study for that test AND go to karaoke because guess what? Death! At certain hours of the night, people turn into coffins, containers of Death. Orpheus, the protagonist's first Persona, is a Greek character who descended into the realm of DEATH. Tartarus, the tower that serves as the set piece of most of the game's combat, is the deepest part of the Greek realm of DEATH. Thanatos, one of the final Personas, is DEATH. If you stay on one of these floors of the tower too long, who comes to kill you? DEATH! In order to summon your Persona, you literally point a gun at your head and pull the trigger. Why? Because you must have the courage to face DEATH!!Someone really just sat down one day and said "I want Memento Mori, but in video game format" and Atlus figured it out.The reason I bring this up isn't to spout facts or further psuedo-intellectualize on DEATH, but to point out that if it weren't for this obsession with DEATH, Persona as it exists today would not be the same. Maybe that's why in the Tarot, Death does not represent an end of things, but instead of transformation of them... (I said I wasn't gonna intellectualize dammit). The Social Links, or Confidants as P5 calls them, exist as a reminder to develop relationships why we can, and so too does the persistent counting down of time and that limitation on what can be done in a single day. Persona 4 and 5 and, it would seem, Metaphor: Refantazio, are shaped by none other than Death.So. If you're a Persona/SMT fan, or looking to become one, Reload is a faithful adherent to the philosophy laid down by the original game: you are going to die one day, so cherish life, friendships, and enjoy as many remarkable stories as you can while still you breathe. This is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: In my original review I talked about how I had an amazing time with the game, as well as how it was my introduction to Persona and JRPGs as a whole. Since then, I spent much of this year playing through Persona 1-5 and having an absolute blast with the entire series. I finished P3R at the end of February and have now come back to play the Episode Aigis expansion, staying spoiler free of it the entire time as I never played P3FES. (While I won't comment on how Atlus has implemented a scummy form of monetization by separating this from the steep 70$ price tag and additional editions of the game, that's a conversation for another day.)Revisiting Persona 3 and getting to cap off the experience with its epilogue through Aigis's perspective as well as playing through the entire series as a whole, I can firmly say that Persona 3 is my favorite entry in the series and possibly my favorite game of all time. I've gotten to experience quite a number of deeply impactful games up to this point, but Persona 3 has hit closer to home than anything thus far. I would love to gush on and on about the many emotions it made me feel, from sheer joy to crushing heartache, but to do so would take away from the experience of the game itself. It's the kind of game whose themes and messages can and should touch your heart, no matter what. It has personally made me more aware of the kind of person I wish to be. While that road may take a very long time and will be rough, Persona 3 has been nothing short of a life changing experience. I have never stopped thinking about it since I finished it, and now I will certainly continue to think about it for a long time to come. While this has much been more a personal rant than a review, rest assured every other aspect of the game is phenomenal. It has an engaging turn based combat system, a wonderful cast of characters, gorgeous visuals and an earworm of a soundtrack. Your daily life system is a refreshing break from dungeon crawling, both main aspects of the game balancing each other out nicely. You have a ton of Personas to grind for and collect along with a bunch of other characters you can get to know and bond with, and both of those systems go hand in hand. There's a bunch here to keep you engaged just from a gameplay standpoint even if that's all you care about. I would very, very highly recommend P3R to anyone and everyone. No matter what kind of games you enjoy, there will be something for everyone and so much more beyond that.

While Persona 4 and 5 were built on mystery and rebellion, Persona 3 is a story of bonding through trauma, that I hope you won't pass up.

_childDocuments_.review: A great example for a very well done remake.Persona 3 is one of my favourite games of all time and I've waited so long for a remake that it kind of feels surreal to finally have one.It improves so many aspects of the old 2006 release, bringing it in line with modern game design aspects, mainly to Persona 5.For anyone not having played Persona 3 at all: Keep in mind that this game is very heavily leaning into its two main gameplay loops: Dungeon crawling and school activities / hanging out with people in your free time.
