_childDocuments_.review: A very good remake with some outdated mechanics that hold it back, though only slightly.The first, and perhaps most important thing about this game is that it practically oozes style from the seams. The art, music, lighting, and graphical overhaul this remake received should absolutely be praised. The look of the game has been rebuilt from the ground up to fall in line with it's edgy modern cousin, Persona 5, while still maintaining the comfy jazzy feel of the original (albeit with a remastered soundtrack which just sounds downright amazing).However, the most glaring issue is that, at it's core, this is still a remake of a game from 2006. It can be extremely repetitive at times, and some bosses are just straight-up damage sponges with no real weaknesses. This isn't to say that it's all bad, though. There have been a litany of QoL changes which truly make some of the grindy parts of the game more palatable. Some of these are brand new, while some have been borrowed from P3P, but all of them are welcome additions. I've tried on several different occasions to get into the Persona/SMT series and it's never really stuck until this game. Safe to say, I've now been bitten by the bug and will be moving on to Persona 5 while patiently waiting on the rumored Persona 4 remake.Side note: Runs at a dang near flawless 60fps on Steam Deck, as long as you have reflections turned off.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, cautious recommendation, I guess I like it more than not. Spoilers for the story unless you've played P3 and the Answer.I have played this game, P3R, it's new game plus, and now episode Aigis, in their entirety, with 300 hours in, and I feel I can write a review.  hmmm, as a persona fan captured by the greetness of P5R, and went on to play P5S, P5T...I had high expectations for P3R, knowing of its reputation among P fans. Some of my expectations are met, some fell short.The writing is perhaps the greatest strengths of any Persona game, and certainly it was the peak of P5R, and not the silly "pokemon" gameplay, nor the well crafted yet not really groundbreaking dungeons. (Oh, the crafted dungeon is only in P5, I thought they might add new dungeons in P3 remaster, but nope, its all randomly generated ones)The "RP" is more important and is better than the "G" in Persona games. The story and message is far more important than the gameplay.In P5R, I loved every single confidant (well maybe except one) and many other characters. In P3R...most of the social links are...meh, mid, generic, forgettable. Very few characters outside the main cast is very interesting, nor their stories exceptionally well written. Even in P3 team isn't that friendly to each other compared to the P5 cast. I really liked some of the P3 team, but certain others I don't really have strong feeling for. Some character's stories in P3 are great, but most of them pretty meh.Also, if you thought that most of the confidants in P5 occupied the day slot and not enough for the night slot, this is even worse in P3. With most social links being students, it has to be daytime, weekdays, no holidays, and no scripted events. I think there's only 2 night time links. Some social links only appear on Sundays! Oh, and you better make sure to do the linked episodes ASAP as well, cause they can expire really quickly. It's very difficult to go in blind and max out all confidants and character stories in your first run, before you have foreknowledge going into new game plus.Speaking of which, there's barely anything new story-wise in NG+ plus either, just some minor scenes in the first day of school, and I don't think any other scenes afterwards. I think its only there to fix up your mistake of being able to max out all confidants during your first run. Even P5R had more NG+ exclusive scenes/content. (Lavenza)As for the story of P3...I'm not impressed. I generally don't like downer stories, and it felt the MC's final sacrifice was kinda forced. I don't really like "everything is fated this way" kind of stories, I feel it's bad and forced writing. The final bass is supposedly killable, and we only know this from a very skechy and biased character. A character that is NOT Omniscient. A character that LITERALLY is the final bad boss you can fight. And after this boss fight, MC literally abandons the team to become Persona Jesus. Hmmm...I thought I was supposed to form bonds with other people and overcome the impossible together? Nope, cast them all aside in the last moment, I the MC knows best, and won't even think of trusting my friends to achieve victory together... (In Persona and most JRPGs we kill gods all the time, STFU about Nyx being any different)As for episode Aigis...for something calling itself "the answer', does it actually gives a lorewise or emotionally satisfying answer? The OG P3 ending was at least hopeful and vague enough for me to cope that MC might not be dead. He might just be passed out or just have had a metaphorical "death". "Nope", said EP:A, MC is hard dead and becomes...door-kun. Yup, tens of hours of boring not-Tartarus dungeon crawling...just for this lame revelation. Oh...and Nyx wasn't that bad all along and its actually Erebus, the "grand manifestation of humanity's grief and negative emotion" that needs to contact Nyx to end the world...somehow? What the ♥♥♥♥ ret-con is this? It makes the whole story make less sense. Door-kun will never come back because he needs to stop Erebus now, as an eternal door that cockblocks Erebus from Nyx...Unless Elizabeth from P4A is canon and succeeds in her quest to find a way to put down Erebus permanently...yeah...the OG ending was vague and good enough to need all this baggage.But I guess I'm being unfair to Reload. The mistakes in writing was done decades ago. It's nearly impossible for Reload team to fix that. I was foolish and hoped the team can retcon the story a bit, but I guess they can't. Or fix the social links into confidants quality. P5 shows the Atlus had become better over the years, and their games have evolved over time, in both writing and game QoL improvements. Some of the QoL from P5 made it, but a lot didn't, and I guess I wished for a "story QoL improvement" as well lol...Oh, and the music has always been a highlight of P games, but here it's mostly just remasters of the OG P3/P3:Fes soundtrack. I think there just only 3 original new soundtrack in the base game (Color Your Night/Full Moon Full Life/It's Going Down Now). As for Ep:A, only two new songs (Disconnected/Don't). Color Your Night is especially good. The others are...decently good. But that's all the new original music content.P3R is perfect for those that just want P3 modernized into P5R, and graphically a little bit post-P5R. But for some that wanted and expected a little bit...more, temper your expectations. P3R is a faithful remaster, but did not fix the all the flaws of P3/P3:Fes. But on the bright side, at least Atlus has been impoving over the years, showing clear evolution from P3 to P4 to P5. Not all the evolution can be brought back into P3, but they did brought a lot of it. Yes, this would probably be the best introduction to P3 for new fans, but I don't think P3 itself is as good as P4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: I played P5R first in the series and loved it to death. When P4G was released on Steam, I was excited to play it. That was when I found out that P5 was a huge mechanics and graphics upgrade to the previous games, and I slogged through P4G as a result. When P3R was announced, I got very excited to play a more stylized, modern version of the Persona game the older fans seem to hold in such high regard.I was not disappointed. The game's graphics and mechanics are very close to P5R's (sadly Technicals are missing, but not a huge deal), and the story and characters are engrossing and leave you wanting more. It took me 92 hours to complete the game in full, though I admittedly did spend a lot of time grinding in Tartarus. Every character from Stupei to Aigis was well-crafted and interesting, but Koromaru wins the title of Best Persona User Ever.Difficulty-wise, the game felt easier than P5R, since there are only three social stats to work on, and there are lots of ways to accelerate that growth. I got very close to maxing out most of my social links in a single playthrough, and I think I would have succeeded if I'd budgeted my time just slightly better. However, P3 does throw a lot more enemies at you that don't have weaknesses, especially as you ascend Tartarus. Speaking of, Tartarus is more interesting in this game than the dungeons in P4 with all the collectible items and the fancy Shuffle Time mechanics that reward you for collecting special Arcana after battles.All in all, if you liked P5, there's a good chance you'll like P3R. Where P4 focused on happy moments and P5 focused on righteous anger, P3 focuses on death, mourning, and sadness, crafting a hauntingly bittersweet tale of kids forced to take on the responsibility of saving the world.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game where nothing happens and then it all happens at once.Most of the game is just you doing pretty much the exact same stuff everyday and night. You will clear all of Tartarus in 1 or 2 attempts per month and then all you can do is go back to grind/farm in Tartarus or hang out with social links. Other than that, you can increase your social skills, but the game is pretty long and you won't have to focus so much on them, not for the first few months of the game at least.That's actually pretty nice as you can then focus on the social links and the stories that they provide, but unfortunately most of them tend to be very strange or straight up boring and if you don't care about them, then you are very unlucky.The combat is really good and so is the ui, they both go well together managing to create a very cool and pleasant experience.Most of the fighting is going to be done in Tartarus as you try to climb higher and higher. I like the 1 dungeon approach, but the fact that you can just run past all enemies and go up to the next floor over and over again is really baffling to me. I also feel like it goes on for way too long as there are a lot of floors in Tartarus.I'm feeling mixed about the music as we hear too much of lotus juice, like this time around he just had to make an appearance in almost every song possible. You cannot escape this man and how he's in the house like carpet.The visuals are really strange, some areas of the game look just fine, others look amazing and some look very flat and boring as if they were made on another engine or they just forgot to add details in these areas and they just released the game like this anyway.And that would have been OK, but they messed up Iwatodai dorm and I just cannot accept that. Iwatodai dorm is literally one of the best video game areas ever. The dorm is absolutely the soul of this game, it's where you meet with all the homies and hang out, you will see this building more than any other place in the entire game.The lounge of Iwatodai dorm  is a character of its own and it deserves respect.They made it look very bright and flat with no shadows and it just has this glossy plastic look to it. It looks and feels very wrong, no idea what they had cooking for Iwatodai dorm, but it looks like they asked Yamagishi to take care of it and look what happened.I also dislike how they had the chance to make the definitive version of Persona 3 by adding every version into one and then focus on improving everything that each version of the game brings.Unfortunately they did not do that, instead they decided to release a remake of the original game and add some improvements on top of that. Keep in mind that this game released for 70 euros with day one DLCAnd speaking of DLC, it looks like they decided to show us that " The Answer " will arrive for Persona 3 as DLC. I do not know how much it will cost, but I would bet that it would go for 20 to 30 euros max and that's terrible considering that we already paid 70 euros.The Answer was already part of Persona 3 FES, they could've just released Persona 3 Reload with The Answer in one package for the 70 euros, but they didn't. I also expect that they will do something similar with the Female Protagonist. The modern trinity of persona games is impressive. We have Persona 3 , 4 and 5. They are all great games, but they also have flaws and when it comes to Persona 3 Reload, I just cannot stand the DLC issues and the story pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best way to experience Persona 3. The visuals are gorgeous, new tracks are all bangers, there are a bunch of QoL features that bring the game up to current standards and the gameplay has also been significantly updated. The new Shift and Theurgy mechanics, combined with all the flashy UI and animations, make it so the combat always feels cool and badass. Tartarus received a noticeable glow up with some new activities to keep the climb engaging. The Link Episodes and new Dorm Activities gave some much needed ways to spend time with the SEES crew. The ending was a serious emotional punch. My only major complaint is that the Social Link schedule could be slightly reworked to allow spending time with schoolmates on off-school days and maybe shift a character or two for night-time Social Links. Because while I understand that the game stays faithful to the original, there ends up being a lot of wasted time that would otherwise make maxing all Social Links in a single run less of a stressful mess.I've played the entirety of the game on the Steam Deck. Initially the performance was less than great and I played around half of the game in 30 FPS. Over time, though, the updates made the game run pretty well at mostly 60 FPS. I can wholeheartedly recommend playing this game on the handheld.

_childDocuments_.review: God bless you all for taking your time to read this. I recently found my son playing a video game called "Persona 3." The next thing I know, they were shooting themselves in the head! The characters had what looked like guns and they'd put them up to their heads and shoot. I got worried, so did some research on the game. The guns are actually "evokers" used to call upon a 'persona." I'm worried that my son will one day find a gun and try this out, or try to evoke evil spirits in other ways. I learned that there is a sequel called Persona 4 where the teenagers call a "persona" by using tarot cards. This goes against the Lord. As kept doing research, I learned that these games are a part of a bigger series called "Shin Megami Tensei." What learned about this series is horrifying. There are games called "Devil Children, "Devil Survivor" "Devil Summoner" and "Digital Devil Saga" that are part of this series! This got me really worried about what my son was playing. In these games you summon and fight "demons." These demons look really similar to what my son was summoning as "personas. What can I do? I'm scared that if take away the games, he might try preforming these things in real life and rebel. But if I don't take them away, he'll be felling into the hands of the devil! _childDocuments_.review: Don't go into this game expecting the same experience from Persona 5. Persona 5 is miles better than this game as expected with it being a later entry in the franchise.The pacing of this game is way too slow, and the characters are shallow and dull. In Persona 5, a kid who sounded like an older man who was a gamer was one of the worst confidants in that game. That pretty much describes half of the confidants in this game. The new animations and updated style (especially with the UI) are a major improvement compared to the original Persona 3. What has not been updated is the translation from the game in 2004/2007 though where it's one thing to read it but another thing to hear them say it. What's worse is that they added a new animation where it zooms in on a character's face in the middle of a discussion breaking up the dialogue whereas Persona 5 only had this occur during the combat to not disrupt the conversations during the game. Persona 3 Portable also reinvented the game to have an option to be able to play as both a male or female character which was unfortunately taken out of this game. Furthermore, it "pay walled" parts of the game that were included in those enhanced versions. I think what has aged the worse though about the original Persona 3 is the dungeons, which have not been fixed in this game. No one wants to run through a randomly generated dungeon for half the game, especially when it is as dull as running up the same tower over and over.Do take this with a grain of salt though, I was unable to finish the game since I lost interest about 20 hours in.That being said, on Steam 90% of the reviews are positive but less than 50% of players have even finished the game, so don't take these reviews seriously. If you're looking for an entry to the Persona franchise don't start here, please start with Persona 5 R.

_childDocuments_.review: So...I'm on about 9hrs now. So far I can say that it's pretty good. It's a remake from the original P3 game that came out eons ago so the questions are, how does it improve on the formula?Well. Tbh I might actually like P5R a bit better in terms of gameplay. The UI is so overdone that it actually has screwed me over a few times. In P5R, i could navigate through every menu as fast as my fingers would allow me to. So I could do about 6 inputs in maybe 2 seconds. in P3R however, there's a severe delay between inputs so if you click 3 times in one ish seconds then the first command and the last command will be inputted but not the second which could result in a fatal misclick. I chose to play on hard difficulty and was punished cause my target switch command didn't input do to the UI's animation blocking further inputs until it was done whereas P5R conditioned me to just machinegun through menus. This UI delay has screwed me over several times. The game is basically telling you to play slowly regardless of how familiar with the UI you are. It drags out battles significantly and ofc, your other party members are totally worthless so if you die they just stand there with their thumbs up their asses, giving up on life and resigning themselves to death instead of...you know, chucking a revive at you like they can literally do at any other point while you're alive.This outdated crap is severely annoying and it makes absolutely zero sense. Bad RNG basically can end a run which is exactly what happened. The game blocked my input due to the delay, i failed to switch targets and attacked the wrong enimy and then got one shot the turn after and my useless teammates committed seppuku. In short, a lot of the major downsides are still in the game, maybe more so than before. The gameplay falls short of P5 just cause of that insane delay between actions.Now, All of the original voice actors are here. Though bafflingly enough, Atlus gave them all the finger and told them they couldn't reprise their roles and instead got to play other characters close to each character instead. Now, this actually isn't a huge problem. All but one of the voice actors are really fantastic fits to replace the legacy characters so its not a major gripe...until Akihiko opens his mouth. It's incredibly jarring to hear. I'd understand and would be totally fine with it if Liam wasn't around to reprise his role...but he is. He's Kurosawa which just makes things infinitely more jarring. What is the thought process behind this baffling decision?The music: 9/10. Lotus Juice is, ofc, still here. If they did what they did to him what they did to the voice cast, there would be blood im sure as he's basically synonymous with Persona 3.Overall, so far, It's good. my problems with this game are nitpicky. The game is crazy expensive though. I'd advise waiting for a sale. All of its DLC should be base game adds since its just recycled content from previous games and its even poorly implemented in some cases. I don't think this game is worth it's asking price ASSUMING you've already played the original. If you haven't though, then its probably very worth itThis is my 9hr ted talk.

_childDocuments_.review: Getting all social links maxed isn't impossible in P3 but it is significantly harder than P4 and P5. You don't need to follow a day by day guide but if you mess up some quick tips even a little you will likely fail. It might look like you have a lot of time but huge chunks of time are blacked out either in general or for half the links.* Always have a matching Persona* Always do school ones before outside school ones - You WILL fail if you don't do this* Always answer correctly* Never do anything except social links during the day* Don't ignore the two Sunday only ones for to long (Maya's you can do during holidays also) - I always did them first but you will miss the achievement for Sunday hangouts* You can ignore Hierophant for a long time* If you can't rank up naturally ignore them - DO NOT WASTE A DAY* You can walk Koromaru at night and he'll get you SL points* You can use the shrine early game but shouldn't unless nothing but Hierophant is available* Late game you can get points at night with the dating app for guaranteed rank up* Ignore Mitsuru when she is first available. Before the last exam nothing (school wise) except her is available and you can easily get her to 6 during that timeThe most important thing is to always do school ones first and don't focus all on one. There is a major arcana that can avoid not getting enough points but you'd have to plan out ahead to min/max but is not needed. You'll miss a lot of the optional stuff by doing this. I did not follow all my tips and maxed all but one out.Great game was well worth a replay.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really enjoyed the Persona 3 Portable first and kinda going with the expectations of losing things that it had. I can say compared to that version as far as i remember the only part that is missing is the Female protagonist option which has its own set of stories in there. Besides that tho i think that this game does an excellent job of making the same game just look much prettier AND actually does add some new story related things with main story and characters with some side things you can optionally do, which is really lovely to see. If you are a casual and newer player to the series i'd say the combat is taught pretty well, that and the other gameplay things in the game does handhold you a bit when first learning about things. As for if you decide to play on harder difficulty i can say the grind is just as long and tedious as it was on the older game but that is honestly to be expected, that only applies in combat tho, other aspects are the same in any difficulty. The newer additions to the Tartarus (The main dungeon) In both exploration feel and look is something i was concerned how they did and i think all in all it was a lot nicer in this version. The combat has a lot more features which both builds on how you can choose to play while also building on the characters themselves.I play these games in english so can only speak for that part of Voice acting but hearing a different crew at first was kind of weird since i was expecting same game but honestly now i can't unhear that these are the characters who are a part of this role. Really great match and great job. The new music added are bangers which can either be remixes, remasters or just straight up new songs. Unless you are a big fan and can't wait tho id say maybe wait for a sale at some point since its pretty pricey, even tho for the money you do get a game which lasts you easily 100+ hours or so. They did also release and expansion pass which as of writing this only added music from persona 4 Golden and 5 Royale to listen to in exploration in dungeon. I really am more waiting for the final bit which adds more story which was only previously playable in a different version of persona 3 which wasn't available on PC which is commonly known as "The answer". Huge thumbs up for me to this banger of a game!

_childDocuments_.review: loved the absurdist themes in the game. if you dig deep enough, you'll be able to find plot holes you can poke through, but i think that takes away from the game a fair bit.the use of death as a recurring motif works well with the message the game tries to bring across. the death arcana represents loss, death, and more importantly: renewal. the characters in this game experience loss, grief, and after the MC interacts with them via their social links, they have a newfound resolve to live.death, in the practical sense, is finality. everything that lives is designed to end. with such a realisation, it is easy to take a defeatist approach and sink into despair. what is the point of living if it's going to end? the game says: life contains value exactly because it is finite.it works, because existential themes are universal; they are a reflection of the human condition. there are many different responses, but the struggle to find meaning is shared. camus once said something along the lines of: there is but one serious philosophical problem, which is the decision to kill yourself or not. if anything, this game serves as a potent reminder of that.my eyes feel heavy.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/12/24I finished this game today at 8 pm.After waiting months for its release I am at a loss for words from the emotion i feel from finishing this game. This game asks and answers the question of what is the purpose of ones life, and is death terrifying? Throughout this game you see the struggle the S.E.E.S has to experience, every member struggling with mental challenges and grief. But throughout all of this every member has good in them, the idea of death is inevitable what matters is what you do during your finite time in this world. This is what connected me to this game. It's themes are so beautiful and perfectly crafted, No matter how awful the next day may seem there's something you can look forward to and fight for. You'll know exactly what I am hinting towards by the end of the game. If I could I would remove all my memory of this game and play infinitely for my first time, and even if I can't do that I an grateful I got to experience this game in its beautiful state. Overall Review: 11/10 - The most beautiful story I've seenThank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: To give some context : this was my second persona game (I did the original Persona 5 few years before) and I did the entire series after this one.Persona 3 reload is a beautiful game in a lot of aspects :Firstly, the game is litteraly beautiful with its reloaded graphics for the characters and the whole world, we have some great reflections as well as some really detailed models. The menus are inspired from the already stunning Persona 5 UIs and are adapted to the P3R atmosphere and OH GOD THE UIs are BY FAR THE BEST I HAVE EVER SEEN IN A VIDEOGAME !Then for the gameplay, this will be quite similar to how P4 and P5 are working (obviously as P3 started this type of gamemplay and set some standards for the future games) : Your day is divided into several parts (morning, daytime, lunchtime, after school, evening) and in your free time you will be able to wander in the city, strenthening your social links, shopping ...etc, but you will also have to fight for the sake of the world in a dangerous place (no spoil). For the combat mechanics, it's pretty similar to P5R, however you will have a special attack for each of your characters called "Theurgy", it's pretty OP and verry satisfying.Now for the OST part ... well ... what should I say except : "It's a Persona game, of course it has some of the best musics you will ever hear." Some of the original game OST have been "reloaded" and there are also some new ones. The whole obviously fits really well with the mood of the game and the specific moments of the story. (+ bonus for the dubbing which is great in both English and Japanese).As for the story ... again ... : "Well, it's a persona game." This one is particularly dark compared to P4 and P5, the main theme of the game being Death. The story is cruel and really sad by moments but it's always very well told with some really good plot twists, of course the game will make you think about a loooot of things, it really changes your vision of life and teaches you some really important lessons ... Also, in the story, I really apreciated the fact that the reactions of the crew were really realistic. I'm pretty sure that this story will make you cry and to me it's probably my favorite opus regarding the story and the developpement of the characters. (+ bonus for the final boss that I think is the best of the persona Series).Now for the "bad part", well to be absolutely honnest, I cannot find a lot of things I disliked except these 2 :I played the game in Hard difficulty which is the hardest difficulty when not launching in Merciless and I found the game pretty easy, I pretty much always 1st tried the bosses (I never really grinded at any point). It's not a really bad point and of course as I knew the persona series, the game surely was easier for me but I think I would have apreciated if we could at least be able to switch to merciless difficulty during a run.Now ... The actual story isn't finished at the end of the game, indeed we will have to wait this September to be able to play the DLC "The Answer" and actually finish the story. However this DLC is in a 35€ expansion pass that isn't included in any of the game premium versions ... This is I think not really cool from atus even if actually the game is totally worth this price with about 75h minimum of gameplay for a run ... you just have to be aware of that and be ready to put 35 more euros !So yes you definitly should give this game a try, it's a perfect opus to start the series !Remeber that life results from death and not the contrary...

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very solid/faithful remake with a lot of great QoL changes. Aesthetically, it's great - the menus, shop interfaces and new portraits all look beautiful. The new voice actors have done an excellent job and you can tell they really love the series. The remastered music is also excellent. I was surprised to see complaints because I think the changes are fairly minor and the newly added songs fit in nicely, despite being a little closer to Persona 5's soundtrack.(One thing to note on the soundtrack - DO NOT buy it as DLC. It's in a convoluted format only playable via its own (very dumb) Unity player so you end up wishing you'd just pirated it.)I would've loved to see the feMC route in the remake, but they've utilised several elements of her social links from P3P, and the additional hangouts with all the SEES members is refreshing compared to the original/FES. I don't feel quite as saddened because they've breathed a lot more life into the main cast. I do have to say that, as expected, they've leaned into the Flanderisation a little too much; particularly with Akihiko. It's probably not as bad as it could've been, but a lot of his new voice lines are training/protein focused which is disappointing. It's one thing I wish they'd lifted a bit more from feMC's route for.My only real complaint is that it seems way too easy compared to the original games. I started out on hard and it feels like easy mode. It's super easy to max stats, battles are easy unless you're completely ill-prepared, and after maybe the first 50 floors of Tartarus, I've always seemed to be flush with money and crafting materials, etc. If you're not new to the series, I would recommend starting on hard or merciless to at least have a bit of challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a classic Persona 3 remake on a totally different engine. All soundtracks have been remade, they've added new dorm activities to get closer to in-game characters.New "Theurgy" attacks for each playable character that can be obtained during the story. (badass animations included)You still have to climb 264 floors of the in-game tower called "Tartarus" (will take 50+ hours alone)Amazing story which is paced badly across the whole playable year. You'll have to bear for 6 in-game months to have a story pace improvement. (6 month in-game tutorial in short)They've added gardening from Persona 4 that'll help you in Tartarus exploration.They haven't added a Female Character option from Persona 3 Portable which is depressing, since it was one of the unique things this game could deliver for this time. (will edit the review if Kotone Shiomi gets released for P3R)Mostly the game is great and new improved visuals helped a lot. Persona 3 Reload is a good remake, but it could get even better if they did more than just remaking the game and adding few more small features and mechanics. I hope that the game's development isn't over yet and we'll get even more content for Persona 3 Reload. If not, I guess community mods will fix that issue soon enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my favourite way to experience the story of Persona 3. The voice actors killed it, they've done an amazing job polishing up not only the graphics of the game, but also the Quality of Life in the battle and dungeon crawling system. Its a premium way to experience the story and gives me hope that other remakes come out as beautifully from the team.There are a few areas I had hopes for that maybe down the line they'll hit, some are unreasonable, some not as much:1) Introducing the Female MC in P3P back on their first swing at re-releasing Persona 3 created an implied precedent that we'd see FeMC in the future but that wasn't he case. I would've loved to have the option to play through as her.2) The Answer though divisive in the community would be great to see in the future perhaps reworked a little bit. Many folks won't know canonically there's more to the tale told, unless the team wanted to get away from the narrative choices they made during that bonus game on the original FES version of the game.3) Far smaller reasonable thing, but there were just some moments where the clean art style took away from the scene. Its only a few times and it toned down the comedic effect, but without context of a prior version of the game these would've been fine. (i.e. Yukari's sass level has been brought down a little but, but I really like her delivery in this.)All in all, great experience, would recommend.

As well as quality of life updates, the music is the best it's ever been in the series (the new track for nighttime exploration is my favourite) and tartarus feels more involved and interesting.I've been playing on steam deck as well as desktop, and I'm really happy with the performance on both. You may notice some slight performance issues on deck at first, but that can be fixed by going into the config menu's graphics settings and turning reflections off (which doesn't actually turn off reflections, it just turns off ray tracing from what I understand).Overall, I really recommend this game to anyone considering getting it. It doesn't disappoint!

_childDocuments_.review: 🎮 Gameplay 🎮☑ Great🔲 Good🔲 It's just gameplay🔲 Bad🔲 Awful🖥️Graphics 🖥️🔲 Great☑Good🔲 Decent🔲 Bad🔲 Awful☠️ Difficulty ☠️🔲 Insane🔲 Difficult🔲 Easy to learn / Hard to master☑ Average🔲 Easy🔲 Shut off your brain⛏️ Grind ⛏️🔲 Bring over night snacks.☑ Average🔲 Easy🔲 No grind👨‍👨‍👦 Audience 👨‍👨‍👦🔲 All☑ Adults☑ Teens🔲 Kids🎵 Audio 🎵☑ Great🔲 Good🔲 Bad🔲 AwfulBugs☑ None that I encounted🔲 Minor🔲 Some🔲 Infested📖 Story 📖🔲 Great☑ Good🔲  Average🔲 Awful🔲 No Story🕓 Game Length 🕓☑  Never ending☑  Long (20-60 hours)🔲 Average (8 - 20 hours)🔲 Short (3 - 6 hours)🔲 Very short(0 - 2 hours)💰 Price 💰 🔲 Free☑  On sale🔲 Worth the price🔲 Avarage🔲 Not recommended💬 Comments 💬Description:Persona 3 Reload retains its core hybrid of traditional role-playing and social simulation gameplay, but is overhauled aesthetically, graphically and mechanically to integrate systems and features that have been introduced to the Persona series since the original Persona 3's release, specifically deriving from quality-of-life improvements first implemented in Persona 5 (2016). In addition to foundational overhauls, Reload refines numerous elements of its graphics and interface to reflect the updated presentation of subsequent entries. For story-sensitive tasks, objective descriptions have been added below the display for the date, time of day and moon phase that list actions that must be performed to progress the narrative, which is functionally similar to Persona 5's heads-up display. The map display has also been improved in function and form over the original Persona 3, having been expanded in size in addition to depicting more intricacies about the surrounding environment, and now placing markers on important locations that need to be visited for story purposes, much like Persona 5's map.The ability for the protagonist to run through areas has also been added.Positives:If you prefer turn based and not time based or free for all then you'll enjoy the remakes combat system. Normally in persona games you feel rushed. It makes you feel as if you need to go into the midnight hour asap. However in this persona game you don't feel that way. It feels more focused on the story and social aspects of the game which feels less stressful. The game has a lot of replayability. Choosing different paths, relationships, persona's each time.Negatives:If you're like me and set camra sensativity on max like a crazy person then the camra speed may be a little slow for you. While you can set the sensativity it doesn't seem to change it very much. However if you're not insane keep it default in most games this wont be an issue.I couldn't relate or enjoy the personality of most characters. Except Junpei, but in a VERY bad way. IMO one of the most annoying characters I seen in a video game. There were only a small amount of characters I did like.Final Thoughts:The game is nice for those who played the first Persona 3 and great for those who have never played it. It takes you back to a time before the changes to the series like Persona 5 Royal and focuses more on the social aspects of the game. I bought the game while it was on sale and it was more than worth it. I would recommend getting it while it's on sale but I'd be more than willing to buy the game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: this "review" is more like a discussion of "what's the difference between P3 original and reload?" than it is a standalone review of Reload. The tl;dr is that Reload is good and recommended.When remaking an old but extremely loved game, the natural assumption is that the target audience is "anyone who wants to experience the old game, but with modern graphics". That was my assumption going into P3 Reload as someone who would have had trouble going back to the original versions due to how dated they look.The reality is that P3 Reload is not made for such a person. It's actually made for "people who played and loved Persona 5 and haven't played Persona 3 but want to play it to experience its story".One must understand what the old game was to understand the difference between these two audiences. I am a more recent Persona fan - my entry (like many) was Persona 5, and I had not actually played the original. I get my information of the original purely from youtube videos as opposed to first hand experience. I was the person who Reload targets, and when playing Reload, I was shocked at how practically identical it was to P5 in gameplay. There are minor differences - social links do not give any bonuses in Reload outside of maxing them out, compared to in P5 where they give some interesting bonus every few levels. The "theurgy" attacks in Reload are basically the "showtime" attacks in P5, at least in terms of visual spectacle (they are somewhat different in gameplay since you can build and store up theurgys for use on harder enemies whereas showtimes are triggered circumstantially). But otherwise the gameplay is mostly the same.I was surprised, then, to hear that in the original P3, you couldn't directly control your party members - only the protagonist. There was also a sort of "fatigue" mechanic where you party members, after a certain amount of exploring, will be too tired to continue and leave the party for the night. I'm sure there are other differences I don't recall of the top of my head too. The stylistic reason for these was to make your party members feel more like independent people as opposed to being entirely reliant on the protagonist, which is a very interesting premise. Reload maintains some of these design choices. On certain days, certain party members will be busy and won't accompany you to Tartarus (the game's dungeon where the combat gameplay happens). In the story, party members will experience their moments of significant personal growth independent of the protagonist (as opposed to in P5 where they're directly caused by the protagonist's actions, with the protagonist being present). These are hints at the original design philosophy.However, in practically all other ways, this is just P3's story (with some minor additions/changes here and there) with P5's gameplay.  P5's gameplay is good, and so this is not inherently a bad thing. So for that, it's highly recommended. Despite this, it is a shame to lose some of the identity of the original game. When playing Reload, I found myself thinking "if this is just a graphical overhaul of P3 original then the gameplay must have been practically identical to P5 even all those years ago". Whenever a topic like this comes up, a common response in defence of the remake is "if you prefer the original just go back and play the original". This statement in itself can have an essay written on it so it's beyond the scope of this review. What I think can be agreed by all is that, if this is meant to be the comprehensive P3 experience for the new generation, it's unfortunate they didn't add the extended content that released for the original, such as the option to choose the female main character (FeMC as she's referred to by the community), or the fact that the expansion pack "The Answer" is not included but instead sold at a considerable price as "Episode Aigis" (commentary on this is beyond the scope of this review). But what is present is still more than enough for 80-100 hours of content, which is typical for Persona games but still a pretty huge amount of gameplay by normal industry standards.As stated in the tl;dr though, the game is great. The soundtrack is also amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Such fun, very nostalgic to go through this game again. Such well written, fun characters. From the very beginning of the game the clock is ticking, how much optional content you get to experience depends on what decisions you make. How you manage your time matters immensely in this game. Persona 3 Reload is not only a very strong life simulation visual novel type game but a dungeon crawler with the full depth and customization of a mainline shin megami tensei game. Love the combination. The art direction and animation in this remake is top notch. (Just wish the game had official Ultrawide support, I did have to use a mod). The visual novel life simulation aspects allow this game to offer detailed world building with side stories making this really feel like a lived in world. You need to plan around the schedules of others living their own lives to be able to finish the optional social link storylines. The writing and characters are for the most part pretty good at keeping you motivated to manage your time well enough to fully experience all of the social links. (I'm not actually sure if you can max out every social link in the game in a single play-through, I ran out of time. May require new game plus)  The original PS2 release even with it's limitations like AI controlled party members was already one of my favourite JRPGs of all time and this is all gain no loss pretty well. (Well ok I prefer the original allowing the protaganist being able to use every weapon type but that's not the end of the world). Will also say the soundtrack for this game is absolutely incredible, but if you are already a Persona fan you know it's going to be amazing. It's what you expect. Everything this game packages together brings it to the next level, what a experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Before P3Reload, I think the most of the Persona community would say the following when comparing the games or discussing which one is the 'best': "3 has the best story, 4 has the best characters, 5 has the best gameplay"; that was such a popular thing to say it outright reached community meme status. But jokes aside, it did have a lot of truth in it.With P3R, I'm expecting the majority discourse to change into people just saying P3R is the best.The story is the essentially the same as before, with only minor changes; it's about as faithful a Remake as you can make it in that regard.The characters, especially the main ones from SEES, are now given more moments to shine in Linked Episodes and Dorm activities, and romance is no longer forced when hanging out with the female links.The gameplay is slightly improved from P5R, and it's not even a contest between it and the original P3/P3FES/P3P.P3R is just so, so wonderful. It's borderline perfect.My main criticisms of it would be that sometimes it is  faithful to the original. The difference in the quality of writing between most of the old Social Links and new Linked Episodes is , the new stuff is so much better that, without context, you would just assume they just didn't feel like putting in effort on those Social Links. I was also hoping they would take some inspiration from the movies in how to present some parts of the story, but that was not the case; not that any of it is bad, quite the contrary, I just think the movies had some neat ideas that could have made their way here too. Also, the pacing could have been improved, but it still has the same problems as the original in that regard. Furthermore, there are some events/Links which are very missable, and that can be a little frustrating, especially for new players.Going back to the positives though, just to list a few:- Theurgy is beyond awesome. I almost find it hard to describe how brilliant I think they really are. And it's not just in terms of power that I mean that, either. Sometimes, it can be hard for game developers to get players to "act" how they would want, in the sense that they had something in mind when designing something, but players just don't use it that way. Theurgy is an amazing way to reinforce what they expect each character to play like. Akihiko fills his Theurgy bar when he is buffed? Better buff him a lot then. Yukari fills her Theurgy bar when healing? She will be our dedicated savior. It rewards playing to each characters strength, and goes along perfectly with their personality. I could gush about how great this is for a very long time. Suffice to say, I find it brilliant, and hope to see more similar mechanics in the future.- All Social Links and Linked Episodes are voice acted. This makes  a huge difference in my opinion. It really helps to convey the emotions of each character. Special shout-out to the best social link in the whole Persona series, the Sun.- The voice acting is great. Persona is the only series I play dubbed, and everyone should be applauded for their performances here. Special shout-outs from my side to the VAs of Akihiko, Mitsuru, Junpei and the protag. They killed it. The moments that I was looking forward to the most in the game were the pivotal moments for these characters, and the VAs did not disappoint me in the slightest; their performances were masterful. Also, I have to point out that even secondary character had amazing performances. Yuko sounded incredible, just perfect for her character. The Sun Social Link, again, was also fantastic. I could keep going on.- The songs are also all remade, and they're all either as good as or even better than the originals, which is saying a lot. - The presentation is fantastic too. So stylish. My one complaint there would be that shops don't feel as good as they did in P5R, but still, that's very minor. The rest is all as you would expect from the same developers, and it works great.I could keep going; point being, P3R is pretty accessible, and merges almost all the qualities from the previous games into one masterwork. I do think for newcomers P5R might still be my number 1 recommendation, but P3R is giving it a run for its money.Objectively speaking, I don't believe that P4G needs a remake at all, but I have to say, if this is what we can expect from ATLUS remakes, can't say I wouldn't be happy to see it. But, of course, I still would rather have them work on P6. Looking forward to what comes next!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remarkable story with great characters, but I'm classifying it as a story over a game. As for the gameplay, I had the same problem with this game as I did Persona 5, where it starts to get repetitive after your 300th encounter. Now I like RPG's and all, but my main problem with Persona games as a whole is how long they are. In most RPG's, the combat and gameplay never really gets old because the game doesn't last longer than 25 hours. What I can say about this game that I can't say about Persona 5 however, is the amount of substance within this game's story. I enjoyed this game's story and character development far more than P5's (still was great, but I thought it lacked substance in some parts). I get that this is also a remake, so this is mainly a review for the original story itself that I never had a chance to play. Should you buy this game? If you've never played the game and want to experience it for the first time, I strongly recommend it. However if you're playing it again, I would say 70$ is a lot to invest in a remake that doesn't offer too much more than the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: In our golden years, my wife and I found an unexpected source of joy and reconnection: the japanese role-playing game, "Persona 3." We've been married for over 40 years, and with our children grown up and out of the house, we found ourselves drifting apart, each lost in our own routines.It all changed when our grandson introduced us to "Persona 3 Reload." Initially, I was skeptical. The idea of remake of a persona 3 was absurt. But my wife, always the adventurer at heart, was intrigued. Together, we decided to give it a try, thinking it would be a humorous story to share with our friends.The first time we played, it was a comedy of errors. I couldn't tell weaknesses, and my wife's personas spent more time accidentally attack on herself than on the foes. But as we fumbled through the game, something wonderful happened. We started laughing together like we hadn't in years. Each gaming session became a new adventure, filled with both in-game challenges and fits of laughter from our clumsy mistakes.As we journeyed through the rich story and dungeons of "Persona 3 Reload," we began to work as a team, just like in the early days of our marriage. We strategized together, celebrated our victories, and consoled each other in our defeats. The game became our nightly ritual, a time where we could escape to a fantastical world and reconnect.Playing "Persona 3 Reload" rekindled something in our relationship that we thought we had lost. We found new topics to talk about, reminiscing about our in-game adventures during the day. Our shared interest in the game led to other shared activities, reigniting the spark that brought us together all those years ago."Persona 3 Reload" became more than just a game for us; it was a gateway to rediscovering each other. It showed us that no matter how long you've been together, there are always new and exciting ways to connect and grow as a couple. Our evenings in front of the computer, exploring the game, became cherished moments, a testament to the enduring power of love and laughter.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable remake of Persona 3, the visuals are top notch, the gameplay is amazing, and the voice acting is stellar and easily has the most voice acting of any persona game. There's a lot of features in here that add a lot of quality of life to where I feel it's easily the most accessible Persona title - provided you can get past the abysmal pacing that not even the remake could fully fix. The difficulty is pretty managable, and the game even adds a rewind feature in case you want to fix a mistake you made earlier, some might see this as making the game too easy, but I think it's a great couple of additions. My only complaint with the difficulty is it felt a little too easy, even on hard. I'll have to give merciless a try and see if that changes things though. If I had any other complaints, it'd be the occasional points where you can see corners were cut. Mainly in Club Escapade where there's very little NPC animation. Overall a great Persona title, just wish ATLUS wouldn't have put it as pricy as it is, and then sell Episode Aigis as additional DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original Persona 3, "Persona 3 Reload" is like catching up with an old friend who's gotten a bit of a makeover. Having played through it twice, I can confidently say it hits all the right nostalgia notes while bringing something new to the table.The developers really nailed it by keeping the soul of the original intact. You’ve still got the gripping storyline, complex characters, and that perfect blend of daily life mixed with mysterious dungeon exploration. But everything feels smoother and looks sharper this time around, making each moment in the game more enjoyable.Combat is as fun as ever, mixing strategic depth with quick decisions. And the Social Links? They're better than ever, deepening relationships and impacting your journey in ways that feel both meaningful and rewarding.Not to forget the soundtrack—it’s a highlight, for sure. It brings back classic themes and introduces new ones that fit right in, enhancing every scene just right. (( my fav song outdoor is "It's Going to down now"Whether you’re new to the series or a returning fan, "Persona 3 Reload" is a must-play. It keeps what you loved about the original, polishes up the rough edges, and delivers an experience that’s both familiar and excitingly fresh.Also, to honour my true love to Persona franchise I made sure to get the Playstation 5 collector edition even though I didn't plan to play it on the PS5, but I do feel that I want to thank the developer for keeping my trust and faith in their products and their games, again, I want to thank Atlus for another gem and I really look forward to play both Shin Megami Tensei V : Vengeance and Metaphor: ReFantazio!!! <3

Removing the ability to destroy and forge a persona into its own unique weapon is tragic especially since the new mechanic replacing it just sucks.I would’ve preferred the original system actually preserving the system in the remake.The new theurgy system is garbage and completely unbalanced they gutted the original fusion spell system making a easier more op and inferior version of it. (this also doesn’t include removing half of the fusion spells) what they have done to the Elizabeth Bossfight is actually heartbreaking it went from a fight that really test is your metal and strategy to how quickly can I exploit the op new mechanics to one destroy her in a few turns. (this remake not actually preserving the original game)I don’t like how bright everything is they should’ve kept the consistent dark this is especially noticeable in one of the most iconic areas in gaming iwatodai dorm.and I’m not a big fan of the new music I prefer the original.This game is so easy it’s easier than playing persona 5R on merciless. _childDocuments_.review: 8.0Persona 3 Reload is the best way to play Persona 3, but it's still not the perfect way to experience Persona 3. Is what I would've said if I hadn't modded the game (with the mod Demons over Shadows, I'll talk more about it in the review).This remake adds some of the best features of the past 3 versions, but it has many "buts" that deters it from being the perfect fusion.I'll list out everything that comes to mind from quality of life improvements -> good -> mixed, but with an *.Quality of life improvements:	- All social links are voice acted nowv and most of the game is too;	- The cutscene Direction is spot on for the big scenes;	- The battle system was enhanced due to shifting (Baton Pass) makes the game more snappier for not needing to use guard to go through all the characters, just to exploit the enemy's weakness. Now you can choose which character to attack after attacking an enemy's weakness.	- There's no tiredness mechanic anymore, hooray; 	- The Jelously system does not exist anymore too!;	- Now the Reaper will not appear in Shuffle time and will only appear after the 62nd floor, when your navigator will inform you of that and you'll need to wait some minutes in any floor after that for the reaper to come after you (importante", the reaper travels through floors now);	- You can fully control your party members; 	- The animations makes the game feel snappier;Good:	- The story is pretty good, but if you really want to experience it at it's best, go watch all the 4 persona 3 movies, they are perfection when it comes to the story and presentation. The only downside to this is that it's better to play the game first and then what the movies; 	- The atmosphere and characters mesh really well with the theme present in this work, but sometimes it seems to lack some effort on the cutscene department to really deliver the original intention of the developers for the social links and character arcs;Mixed, but with an *:	- The graphical overhaul is good, for the most part. The texturing and models are amazing, but the lighting is a bit iffy;	- The OST is still the best of all the persona games, but while the instrumentation is much better than the originals, the changes to the lyrics and pronounciation of some words caused a certain disconfort that made me mod in the FES soundtrack. Some examples: the Iwatodai dorm's music was disfigured with the new version and Mass Destruction seems wrong with the "baby" part;	- The new battle theme (it's going down now) that appears from time to time is good, but it kinda doesn't mesh well with the game's atmosphere and it takes way too long to reach it's peak (you'll probably finish the battle before reaching the best part);Mods that will enhance gameplay: 	- Demons over shadows (DOS): Replaces all mob Shadows in the game with demons from Shin Megami Tensei. This will make the game much more interesting and challenging, since the standard shadows are just boring.	- Expanded Evening Map: Let's you go to the shrine and Port Island during night time.Some fixes that you can do on your own:	-While it is pretty looking, I preffer the look of the originals and to achieve that, dial down the brightness by 3 ~ 5 presses to the left from the center (default) and use either GTAO or RTAO mod. By doing this, the game's shadowing and atmosphere will look much more like the original. In Reload, the standard Brightness is just way too bright and lacks some shadowing (that's why I modded GTAO in the game). if installing mods is too taxing on you, just adjust the brightness, it will look much better.Now I'll talk about what's good and bad in each version of Persona 3.Persona 3 original (PS2):Good:	- It's the original Persona 3 experience;	- The main character can wield all weapon types in the gameBad:	- It's the original Persona 3 experience;	- You cannot control your party members actions in battle;Persona 3 FES (PS2):Good:	- It's the original Persona 3 experience + the Answer Epilogue (Episode Aigis); Bad:	- It's the original Persona 3 experience;	- You cannot control your party members actions in battle;	- The main character can wield all weapon types in the gamePersona 3 Portable: Good:	- It's portable and easy to emulate on any old android phone;	- Now you can control the party members;	- Female main character was added, changing the story slightly, adding new social links and romance options.Bad:	- Not being able to explore the city in 3D, you can only explore it with a cursor;	- Not being able to see the characters while in a cutscene, making you wonder sometimes what is happening due to a lack of visual information.	- Not as pretty as the PS2 versions, but that's obvious.Persona 3 Reload: See the beginning of the review. Summary:Persona 3 reload was a good remake, but it didn't add anything major to really push me to buy it on day 1. Even if they added Episode Aigis to the base game, I still wouldn't think the game is Worth the full price, it needs to offer more for us that have played the original to justify it's price tag. Atlus could've done so much more to make this the definitive way to play Persona 3. they could've added a new ending, different acrivities, new areas to explore in the city, more interesting Tartarus layouts and variety. All the things I've listed now are things that they could've done that in my opinion, would've made the game into a 9 out of 10 withought that much effort. It sucks that they took out the female main character, but I do understand that it would require much more work to do all her campaing for no feesable gain (social links, voice recording, custom animations, character's behaviours and conversations with her, etc...). What I am trying to get at is that Persona 3 Reload needs something of equal footing or better than Persona 3 FES The Answer (Episode Aigis) was for the original Persona 3 to justify the buy at full price. By the way I've bought Reload at 50% discount.Or another analogy is what Nintendo is doing to their remasters on switch. For example: Xenoblade 1 has a new 10 hours epilogue, just like Persona 3 FES was, or Mario 3D World has Bowser's fury. But what does Atlus do? Sell The Anser as DLC with no further plans to do anything else for the remake and F to the people that bought the deluxe version thinking they had the "DLC" guaranteed.All in all, I will probably be there for the next Atlus game.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona has been a cornerstone of the JRPG genre alongside industry titans such as Final Fantasy.  The Persona series provides an interesting blend on dungeon crawling and life sim elements that makes for an engaging narrative and gameplay loop.Reload is my first experience with Persona 3 as a whole and I only have P5 and P4 Golden to compare it to and what a wild ride this game was.  This game had the highest stakes for our cast out of all three games and puts forward an emotional and gut wrenching plot that left me glued to my monitor until the bitter end and was one of the few games to get me to tear up at the conclusion.  I found a majority of the characters to be likable and well developed, with some notable characters being Yukari and Akihiko, while others such as some of the social links you can find scattered around the game world fell flat for me.  Persona 3 Reload however did have some of the weakest dungeon crawling of the modern series and upon my second and third runs I found myself rushing through Tartarus as fast as possible to push the story forward.  The floors of Tartarus do not offer much variety apart from an aesthetic change every so often and is just 200+ floors of rush to the exit and felt like a worse version of P5's Mementos.  The soundtrack of this game was bombastic and emotional at times, especially during the final confrontation and cutscene sequence (if you finished the game you know what I'm talking about).  After I finished my first run of the game and seeing the main menu change the background and music was a very powerful moment that left me just staring at my screen for several minutes reflecting on what I just experienced.  All in all I did find this game to be an absolute gem and is my game of the year for 2024!Achievement Review SectionThe achievements for Persona 3 Reload are not overly taxing on the players skill, but some do require a guide if you want to achieve them in your first run.  A notable achievement is maxing all social links which took me a third entire run to achieve out of a complete stubborn desire to try and do the entire game without using guides.  Most achievements you will manage to get just through natural progression and exploration however.  Unlike Persona 3 Portable and Persona 4 Golden, you are NOT required to complete the persona compendium which is a huge time saver.  Another notable achievement that has been a mainstay for the modern entries is to defeat the Reaper, which is classed as a hidden super boss.  The Reaper, whilst not overly difficult to overcome at higher player levels, will test your knowledge of weaknesses and debuffs.  With a guide I would give the achievement list around a 4/10 and without a guide just for the social links alone I would class it closer to a 6/10.Pros+Amazing Soundtrack.+Great cast of characters.+Engaging plot.+Only game to make my cry other than season 1 of the Walking Dead.+Visually stunning.+Great performance on PC.Cons-Tartarus is very boring after a first run.-Some of the villain characters I wasn't a fan of.-A few sections where I found myself skipping through entire days to get to the next plot point.Summary:  Persona 3 Reload is easily the most gripping story I have played this year and takes the 2024 game of the year spot for me without much contest so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Tartarus is so boring and easy in this game it may as well not even be there.Atlus bought into the meme that Tartarus in the original was bad, so they removed all the classic dungeon crawling elements that made it interesting, There's no dead ends at all for you to back yourself into, shadows are ridiculously easy to run from and vanish immediately after you do. All the bad changes from Portable are back to make things even easier, like being able to continue from the highest floor you reached, and even new ones like Yamagishi randomly making you invisible.It doesn't have the visual spectacle, puzzles or really any of the interesting things that P5 added to its dungeon crawling either. Also, the music is laughably terrible, and actually kind made me hate Lotus Juice since he's in like EVERY SONG. The new outfits suck and the game is so determined to sell you on them they have an entire animated cutscene dedicated to them; it's cringe. The best thing I can say is at least they didn't ruin the story (as far as I'm aware), but you may as well just play the original on PCSX2. Or play something else like The Coffin of Andy and Leyley or something idk lmao

_childDocuments_.review: The music and art of P3R are my favorite aspects of the game, both adding a lot of charm to the experience. As someone who isn't a longtime fan of the Persona series, I don’t have any nostalgia tied to it. However, I found this remake to have many outdated design choices, retaining a lot of the clunky elements from older games. There's a significant amount of repetitive content, with much of the gameplay revolving around fast-forwarding through some social links or grinding in the same areas. It's just not fun.On top of that, Atlus' brutal cash-grab with the DLCs makes it hard for me to recommend this $70 base game to others, even after finishing the main story—especially when it comes to the additional $35 DLC content.

_childDocuments_.review: I started craving for JRPGs since December and after finishing Persona 5 Royal, this game just happened to be launching around the corner. In anticipation for P3R's release, I started familiarizing myself with the PS2 FES version of the game and after getting a sense of both directions of these games, I say P3R had definitely exceeded my expectations for a remake title of a beloved classic.The remake took many aspects of the original title and basically enhanced it without trying to stray itself too far from the original. Most of these changes I would argue are improved and well implemented that made the game more newcomer friendly for those who are not familiar with the franchise. In a sense, the remake accomplished its job of trying to be a well crafted entry for newcomers and veterans.However, I must object to say that P3R is one of the many examples of SEGA/ATLUS' taken advantage of the consumer. I dislike their business methodology of selling parts of the content such as The Answer to help garner further revenue streams. P3 FES, a PS2 title from '07 was a complete package and now we're expected to purchase a part of that content down the line if we want to have the full experience of the game.Regardless, Persona 3 Reload is certainly worth the cost on its own. The narrative and its characters are uniquely interesting and no doubt you will find yourself deeply invested throughout the game. I never found myself bored nor dissatisfied during my two playthroughs and that in itself was a huge improvement after Persona 5 Royal. If you're already a fan of JRPGs and you haven't touch this game yet, I highly reckon you do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What an incredible job ATLUS did remaking this quintessential 2000s JRPG. As a fan of the original P3, I was excited to see how this would be handled, especially considering the brand new voice cast, and the similarities the art style was having to P5. Luckily, the heart and soul of Persona 3 shines in this game not only through the talented voice cast, but the re-imagined artwork, and quality of life changes this game desperately needed. Being able to control your party members individually like in P3P and P4/5 is a blessing, but the act freely AI is considerably smarter here too, allowing for so many possibilities in combat. No more Junpei casting slash attacks on slash resistant enemies. Not to mention the ability to finally romance Aigis, which you couldn't do in the original. New players will benefit from all of these well implemented features and hopefully draw plenty of newcomers to this game. I promise that this game's story will captivate and honestly change you as a person, i adored every second i spent in Tatsumi Port Island just walking around, meeting the different social links and just increasing social stats. The various new difficulty options also make this game leagues more accessible than the original, even adding options for those new to JRPG's who simply wish to enjoy the game's story, which i think is an incredible addition for those not yet familiar or who simply prefer a different approach to this type of game.This is a game absolutely full of life and soul, and i can assure you that you wont be disappointed, and this game will appeal to you in one way or another, even if you have never experienced Persona.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who already thought of Persona 3 as one of my favorite games, Its honestly very heartwarming to see it remade so well. It adds alot of nice QoL features, such as controllable party members, hangouts with the male party members, etc. But honestly the biggest achievement of the remake is making all these additions and changes, but keeping them in line with the spirit of the old game. You can still feel alot of the old games charm  reflected in how the game plays and is designed, despite them having the chance to completely modernize it to Persona 5 standards and streamline the experience, and I think the game is all the better for it. Its the perfect way to bring such a timeless masterpiece to a more modern audience without stripping out what made the game special in the first place. Persona 3 is truly a phenomenal game, and it warms my heart to know its legacy will live on through this amazing remake.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played the three newer gen personas (3 - 4 - 5) around the release of each original version - this one is easily the best remake. I'd argue this is the best game in the series in Gameplay, story, and environmental design with the reworks to Tartarus. Its not nearly as easy as 4 and 5, but it does have its downfalls in difficulty about halfway in when you finally get enough party members and you are no-longer bottle necked by SP.If you have played Persona 4 or Persona 5, Persona 3 Reload will be no different. You fight shadows to level up and fuse personas to make crazy new combination. Unlike 4 and 5 though, in the original release of this game, you could  control your party members, or which persona abilities were inherited during fusion. This was changed in the PSP version of Persona 3, and thank goodness for that.My only gripe with the gameplay is how cheesy it gets later into the game. With no spoilers - once you start getting certain physical type personas, the game becomes a joke. I played this game on Merciless (hardest difficulty) and I hardly hit the game over screen except for a few times in the beginning. I will say however, this is not like Persona 5 where enemy and ally weakness' are amplified by 3x. You deal less damage and take more, good change on that end. Its done really well in this adaption, its easily my favorite of the 3 different versions of Persona 3. The new voice actors (especially Junpei my god) really nail their characters, and I love how they added the og cast back as some side characters. Its especially hilarious when some of the VA's from the OG game start talking to their newer counter parts. The areas are given new life through all the graphical enhancements in this engine, plus all the social links are voiced and helps sell that individuals story. My one and only problem with all of these enhancements is that we do not have female protagonist. If not female protagonist, then at least giving the male team members of SEES their own social link stories.Holy moly did they ever up their game with this adaption. Tartarus used to be an absolute copy and paste dungeon in the original (and FES) + PSP Persona 3. They have since gone the direction of Persona 5 and really given some uniqueness to the blocks in the games dungeon crawling area. Each block, you will encounter small, medium, and large spaces that have similar designs and are randomly generated each day you are in Tartarus. What you find on floor 50 will not be the same the following in game day.Outside of the dungeon space, the outside city is really brought to life in this game. The areas in which a lot of your social stats and social links will be undertaken has included a lot more depth than the original games. The PSP game took a bit more of a visual novel approach to the over-world, you would not even see your character model traversing these spaces. The club in the mall area is also given more life and actually has people in it (from my recollection - in FES this area was barren with absolutely no one around). There's a lot to do with so little time, and it was a blast to sit and watch.If you enjoy turn-based JRPG's with a hint of visual novel flair, Persona has always been the series for you. In my honest opinion, this is the best Persona game Atlus has ever conceived. You are doing yourself a disservice by not playing through this masterpiece if you can afford it. If you enjoyed Persona 4 and/or Persona 5 - this game will be right up your alley. You will find something you enjoy, there's a little bit of something for every nostalgic JRPG nerd who hit their teens in the late 2000s.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. A long ride, a memorable ride. One that someday I can look back and think, "ah, twas a good time indeed."Side stories are a treat, and so are the main cast's. They were interesting to read and follow. Rather than twists and turns, the stories were mostly more like a steady hill down to depressing land. Yep, nihilism, that's the theme of this game. Things went wrong, things fell apart, slowly over time. I'd like to think of this as a slow burn, like, reaaally slow - 100 hours slow. And then the ending just burned you a little more, just enough for you to finally get a whole view of where in the depressing land you're in. I like the ending though. It freed up the knots, tied up the hanging stories, and reward you for investing into the stories. Not all stories of this caliber can land that smooth.Just want to get it out there though, the plot is so boring and cliche, even for a JRPG. The gameplay was generic. Eating rice soaked in water would be more entertaining than this. No technical issue, excellent voice acting, enjoyable bgm. I'm not a persona fan per se. I love P4G, but couldn't care less about P5. That's why I want to look at this as an independent work rather than a comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: I've clocked in over 100+ hours in this game. I've played the original, base version of Persona 3. I've played FES. I've played Portable. If there's one thing Atlus did right with this remake, it's staying very true to the original while almost seamlessly adding in new small sections of content that help add a breath of fresh air. There was obviously a lot of love that went into this remake and a big nostalgia trip for myself going through everything all over again after having spent such a long time away from any iteration of the game. They bridge the gap so you can get to know the other cast that had social links specifically in Portable's FeMC side, and implemented features from Persona 5 into 3's already existing system in a way that isn't incredibly jarring. The amount of free time you have may feel a bit tight in this game a lot more than Persona 4 and 5 for a while as you learn what you can and cannot do, but that's what New Game+ is for.A friend of mine said it best: "It's like Persona 4 and Persona 5 had a baby."While it can be seen as a downside that they don't have plans to add in Kotone as of right now (also known as FeMC), there is The Answer (Episode Aigis) that they will add eventually which helps save my overall review of the game. I hope they continue expanding upon the game with other DLC beyond The Answer. If you're looking to enter the Persona franchise, I would highly recommend this one to start off with.
