_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is an HD Remake (not remaster and not on the switch apparently) of an old beloved playstation exclusive game for modern day consoles. There are a few things missing from portable and FES that may be included in the feature, and otherwise: *HD Graphics for all aspects of Persona 3 Reload- including the environment, buildings, characters, and especially tartarus.*Shuffle time makes a return from Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden, with beautifully resdigned tarot cards and arcana burst features. *Link events for the male party members*All major social links have voice lines that weren't included in the original (and other re-releases)*Theragy attacks (which affect the protagonist too) allowing for super flashy and strong attacks that provide beneficial boosts in combat. *Oracle will boost your team's performance and ability to survive; only buffs, no debuffs. *Shift/Shifting, a new tactic in battle similiar to baton pass from persona 5 / royal enabling you to change to another party member after striking one enemy weakness, allowing you to diverse and fully utilize your party members on the battlefield for an all out attack- most of the time.*You're no longer fatigued in tartarus, but the reaper is coming for you in every single floor*Special bonuses for Merciless difficulty game play finished in new game plus+*The arcana is by which all means are revealed...*And many more featuresIn short, 9.2/10; the story hasn't changed and is about faithful to the original, tartarus, the environment, and combat have been improved significantly with 3D Graphics. There is just the issue of the missing answer dlc content, the framerate does rarely flicker, fusion attacks are gone with the multiple protagonist theragy abilities. Honestly, this is one impressive remake of an existing game, and I hope they do improve on missing issues.-It costs $70 for a HD remake of an existing game?! That might be one of the major turn downs for P3R. The dlc adds in unique personas, costumes from other games, soundtrack and artbook as other applications included with Persona 3 Reload that don't even have a quit option (alt + f4 to leave).

_childDocuments_.review: My first Persona game was Persona 5 Royal, so I can't avoid comparing them.  After reading so many people say Persona 3 has a much better story than Persona 5 (even life-changing for many), I do feel pretty let down. Overall P3R is definitely a very well-made game with mostly well-written characters and a satisfying gameplay loop, but it is undermined by real flaws.  NOTE: All spoilers are in footnotes.GameplayFrom what I can tell, P3R makes a lot of significant improvements over P3 FES and P3P's gameplay, with more stuff to do in the real world and with more variety in Tartarus.  Combat is also much better balanced, bringing in some ideas from P5 without making it a clone of that game.  On the pro side, for example, theurgy attacks are a much better version of Showtime from P5R, giving you more control over choosing which one to use, how they charge up, and how they reflect the characters.  I still wish you could skip the cutscene... but still a significant improvement.  On the con side, Tartarus is really dull compared to Persona 5's palaces.  There's almost no environmental storytelling in Tartarus, no clues as to why one level looks different from another (and why one specific section, as all my party members EXPLICITLY ACKNOWLEDGED, is physically painful to look at, so the devs knew what they were inflicting on me).  The only motive to explore it for much of the game is simply because the leader said so, and because you need to grind so you can face the monthly bosses.  I also really question the decision to add variety floors that actually make Tartarus more of a pain, such as the greedy shadows that steal all the loot and you have to guess which directions they run in to catch them, most of the time without any clues.  Later on they give you an SP costing skill that just skips that whole minigame, so I can't understand why they put that in there to begin with.  Finally, enemy variety is severely lacking compared to Persona 5.  Even the bosses you fight in Tartarus are just mixed up versions of regular enemies with no truly unique mechanics.  Thankfully combat is generally fun (and quick) and the loot flows nicely through Shuffletime, so Tartarus really isn't a terrible experience over all; it's just incredibly uninspired from a level and enemy-design standpoint.  It also gets very easy, even on hard mode, where I simply used melee focused characters, healed them with Yukari's ridiculously cheap healing, and never had to use SP items again past the midpoint of the game.  Again, it's reasonably fun because I genuinely like these characters, but I can't escape the feeling that it could be so much better.MusicMore hit or miss for me than Persona 5, but I do love jazz much more than rap (the dorm song started setting my teeth on edge after a while), so it's going to come down to personal taste for a lot of people.  A lot of the songs for running around school and town are great, though I do wonder why they didn't go harder on other aspects of the ambiance like the weather.  Rainy days would make so much sense in this game.Side StoriesThe social links are pretty hit or miss for me, like the music.  Some are great and thought-provoking, a couple are genuinely funny and made me laugh, but several of them seem pretty pointless or undermine themselves in the rank 10 conversation.*  Biggest disappointment for me with these links is that the main character is so undercharacterized it's not at all clear why talking to him is this amazing, life changing experience for all these people.  Even if you give people terrible, life-destroying advice, they discover themselves regardless and credit you as their dearest friend and savior.  Joker, in Persona 5, has much better dialogue options, IMO, and also helps turn people's lives around in concrete ways with his unique abilities.StoryYou'll hear a lot of people say this game has the best Persona story.  In fact, that seems to be a pretty overwhelming consensus on social media, from what I have seen.  It definitely is good, and much better than I have found in most video game franchises, but it's really strange to me that it's considered so clearly better than Persona 5 because there are some pretty obvious flaws.  Not fatal flaws, mind you; I still enjoyed it quite a bit, but I found Persona 5 a lot more compelling from start to finish, and I'm not even going to talk about the differences in pacing.First off, people praise the characters in this game.  Regarding your companions, I think that's definitely deserved.  I like nearly every companion in this game better than their most similar equivalent in P5R.  They feel more down to earth, less trope-y, and they have better defined and consistent development that is interwoven well with the main story, with one exception.**Regarding the villains (who are, after all, supposed to be characters too), this is definitely not deserved.  Without delving into spoilers in the main body here, I will just say there are a lot of inconsistencies in the motives and actions of the villains in this game.***  E.g., sometimes they use overwhelming force and sometimes they hold back for no clear reason.****  The plot and worldbuilding also don't feel as developed as Persona 5, but I have heard some of my questions in this area will be answered with DLC.* Maiko's story was really touching, and I felt for her, but asking to marry you just made the whole thing leave a sour taste in my mouth.  It would have felt much more natural if she said she was thankful for you because you're like the older brother she never had.  The epilogue scene for this social link is also bizarre, because the father opens his heart to you like you're a close friend then turns on a dime and starts screaming at you to stay away from his daughter.  I've known IRL bi-polar people who don't flip that fast.** Aigis is weird and creepy as a concept, and as trope-y as it is possible for a character to be.  I will never get over the idea that a scientist for the Kirijo Group decided to make a "weapon" that looks like a 16-year-old girl.  The Chairman actively highlights this problem with how he introduces her, telling the group to look for a weapon so SEES starts looking for a tank or something.  And when we met her, I literally thought, "Please don't tell me they're going to have the android learn what it means to be human by discovering emotions..."  It's the laziest version of that trope, too, like the difference between Avatar and District 9: both movies get you to sympathize with aliens, but one takes the easy road of making them attractive and perfect; the other makes them hideous and STILL gets you to sympathize, which takes much cleverer writing.  Aigis is obviously the former, not the latter.  She stands out all the worse against the other SEES members, who are actually interesting, flawed people.*** The Chairman was a huge missed opportunity.  He could have had so many interesting connections to Yukari's and Mitsuru's fathers.  He could have given an alternative, more nihilistic philosophy compared to the main themes of the game.  But instead the sum of his motives is he believed a prophecy (no clue who gave this prophecy or how) that someone would become a king (over a bunch of dead people?) if Nyx came back.  For that he was willing to live a double life for years and crucify you all, murdering Mitsuru's father.  I mean, COME ON you've got to give me more than that.**** Takaya has a revolver that he always gets perfect killshots with when he uses it, but he only uses it when the plot demands somebody die.  Supposedly he is desperate to stop us from ending the Dark Hour, but his strategy is to... shoot one of us at a time, with several months in between...  And when he fights you as a boss, for some reason he does it totally honorably without even trying the gun, even though that gun was unblockable by a couple of the most powerful persona users in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "No one can escape time; it delivers us all to the same end. You can't plug your ears and cover your eyes." This is my personal favorite of the Persona games I played. I love the story, the extremely relatable cast, the social links. The gameplay is vastly improved from portable, with quality of life putting it on par with Persona 5's gameplay. There are moments in this game that made me very emotional, and for me it hits so much harder than Persona 4 or 5. Not trying to badmouth them, because I do enjoy both games, just my personal preference. The soundtrack for this game is also my new favorite, with tracks like Color Your Night and Full Moon, Full Life that will own my Spotify Wrapped once they get added. Now one thing I will say, is I don't believe the game should be 70 dollars, unless the Answer is included. I really don't agree with it being locked behind an expansion pass, especially for those who paid for even bigger editions of the game. If I were the average player, and not a persona fanboy, I'd say wait for a sale to get the game, and hope the Answer can be bought on its own. Another disappointment is the lack of FeMC, or the Female Main Character. While it isn't the worst thing ever to not have her, the fact that her version of the Persona story isn't remade in this when it isn't too terribly different from the Makoto storyline feels like an oversight. That said the community is making a really good mod to at least have her model and new animations/music added to the game, which is wonderful. Seriously the pink ocean main menu and reimagined tracks sell it. Now final thoughts on the game, if you want a very thought provoking story about which the primary theme is death? This is one of the best games I think to tackle it, I just love the formula of Persona games. You're given a story that takes place over the course of a year. And just like real life, the days go by so very quickly. This story and these themes resonate with me more than the other two, and that's why I'll say its my personal favorite. I doubt that'll change after I play the other few, but that remains to be seen! Thanks for reading, and if you get the game, enjoy the ride. Vibe to the music, spend time with your favorite characters, and for Thanatos's sake, don't use Armageddon on Elizabeth.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played P3FES on the PS2, as well as played P3P on the PSP, clocking at least 10 runs over many of my teen years. I love this game. This remake has given it a shiny new coat with up-to-date game mechanics and much needed changes, as well as the additional of multiple useful features.However, Atlus missed the opportunity to make it the true definitive edition with the exclusion of FeMC, which I'm very bitter about as I like playing as FeMC and played most of my runs with her. On the social links aspect, some balancing was done to try and make easier, but it was still almost impossible to max all s.links going in blind. I will definitely be replaying NG+, but only with a meticulous guide for the social links.The already strong story was made even better with the polished cutscenes. Despite experiencing the ending multiple times already, I still cried as I watched the ending. The addition of linked episodes really helped to flesh out some of the characters and made the story feel more whole. I also liked the addition of the "combat" look and gear which made it feel more like a squad.The graphics were beautiful and the new models looked good. In terms of cutscenes, there was some stuttering near the end of the game but it was minimal. I liked how they tried to keep to the original art style in cutscenes too. Ray-tracing was also on by default, which caused major frame drops especially in Paulownia Mall. There was also a treasure room in the last block which had frame drops, but it wasn't too bad.Combat was fluid and many of the newer mechanics have been brought over, such as the baton pass, but also toned down as it was kinda OP. Armageddon actually has a drawback now, which I really love, as before there was literally nothing stopping you from spamming it. Really glad they also excluded the "insta-kill" from P5, as there was too little control over that mechanic. Party members' kit have been tweaked, giving you more flexibility in building your team. The addition of Theurgy was also welcomed, as it was implemented well without making it too overpowered.Weapons fusion has been changed, which I'm honestly not a fan of due to the RNG associated with it. The last tier of equipment shares the loot pool with 6 drops, instead of the usual 3 for each tier, and many of the best gear was locked behind the rarest . After unlocking the last block, I grinded Tartarus almost every night and only got a total of 2 to drop, compared to my spare 50+ . FYI you need at least 10 for 1 copy of each gear, not counting the best armour/shoes for most party members. Without save scumming, it's honestly impossible to get them all.Probably the weakest aspect of this game, there are just simply not enough days. They did good in balancing some aspects, like changing the god-awful Hermit S.Link to not take the whole day (yes it was like that in P3FES), as well as allowing us to get free S.Link points at night near the end of the game, though it was way too late for it to make too much impact since you can't rank up Day Links at night. However, due to the additional of Linked Episodes which lock some personas behind them, you're still bottlenecked by the lack of time and too many holidays.I felt that due to the imbalance between Day and Night S.Links, they should have given us some way to progress day ranks outside of school days. Are you telling me I can't get closer to my homie just because it isn't a school day? What's the point in all these S.Link points when I can't rank up? Honestly, without following a guide to the tee you are probably not going to max all the S.Links without a NG+. Ultimately this left a sour taste in my mouth as I couldn't max 's rank in the end.

And I'm glad I finished it because the plot is really good albeit I've been spoiled on like 90% of it. However, it still has issues that plagued the original. The whole fundemental dungeon crawl of tartarus is still climbing up hundreds of floors with randomly generated layouts which many people were turned off by including me but they made it reasonably quick to sprint through and the floors are more expansive. As well as the first 20 or so hours has very little story and the last couple months felt like a slog. I feel like there could have been a lot more improvements to the overall structure and pacing of its plot. The new music/rearranged tracks are generally really good though (wow big surprise for an atlus game) If you're curious on a technical front: the game graphically feels a bit off at times. The lighting in the dorm especially. Though, most floors in tartarus look nice with SSR implementation on the floor. The game has raytraced reflections but nothing special and SSR looks pretty similar to its implementation here. The 3d models are wayyy better than P-Studio's past games.  The PC port is competent at least albeit with very little settings tweaks, no shader comp step (yay UE4 shader stutters) but has good GPU/CPU performance. I had a great time with it on Steam Deck as well after a Proton hotfix a week or so after launch.I definitely recommend checking this out if you're a jrpg fan or wanting to get into Persona on sale. Atlus finds it funny to release a $35 expansion pack for content in FES not even included in the $100 edition.

_childDocuments_.review: An astounding story and an otherwise remarkable remake ravaged by a masterclass in anti-consumer practices and incompetence.'Episode Aigis', which serves as an epilogue to the base game and is a major component of the story that Persona 3 has to tell, is locked behind an additional paywall of £28.99. Furthermore, the game is riddled with DLCs which, in truth, do not contribute anything at all to the experience and you can get by just fine completely ignoring their existence, but slapping these on top of the already exorbitant £59.99 price tag for which you would expect to get a full game? It is akin to being spat on.The release itself is utterly pathetic, being riddled with performance issues, and outright preventing some individuals (myself included) from playing the game on PC. At the time of writing this review, It has been 8 months since the game has released, and these issues have yet to be addressed; safe to say, they likely never will be. (As a side note, there is plenty of troubleshooting discussion on Reddit which has led to some individuals successfully finding ways to fix some of these problems. However, these fixes are all obtuse 'band-aid' workarounds, and are not guaranteed to work for you).Circling back to the DLCs while we are still on the topic of incompetence, the actual implementation of most DLCs is inexplicably out of touch. Forgetting for a moment that they should just be a part of the base game, let us analyze the DLCs from a gameplay standpoint. The Personas start at random levels, often above where you currently are, instead of beginning at Lv.1. This is a very poor design choice seeing as the average player is not interested in trivializing parts of progression. The amusing cherry on top of all this is that these files are available in the base game files, making it possible to simply mod them into the game.What was supposed to be a faithful recreation of a timeless classic should have not been squandered like this. Persona 3 captured the hearts of many, inspiring them during their formative years by having a beautiful story to tell about the value of life and the importance of seizing every moment. Seeing it reduced to being just another victim of corporate greed and what is likely rushed development enforced by unreasonable deadlines, is greatly disheartening.Praying for the return of video game industry to a state of simply being a labor of love, where providing a complete and polished experience is prioritized above profit margins.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best game in the Persona series, a much stronger entry than both 4 & 5. Here are some of my thoughts as someone who played FES back in 2014-2015:- The cast is very strong, and all go through character development without simply being pushed to the side or having it only forced through social links (which is a common issue faced throughout 5 with its party members, with it being less prevalent in 4 due to how well the characters bounced off of each other). - Some are upset that we don't get the female protagonist from portable, and that The Answer isn't included (with a high chance of it being later DLC, which is good news) but I say that even without that this is 100% the definitive experience that Atlus said they gave us. - The soundtrack is still excellent, despite being remade renditions of all the songs from nearly 2 decades ago (all hail Shoji Meguro) and with very few songs that are forgettable or downright bad. - Even without the male party members having social links, their linked episodes managed to give us plenty more interactions to bond with them in comparison to the older games where you could only do so with the female protagonist.My only real criticisms with the game:- It's almost impossible to 100% it without a guide unless you're a god at time management or have good enough prior knowledge from the previous versions of the game to have a fully laid out plan of how to do everything (which can still be messed up due to the addition of Linked Episodes). - Some linked episodes can lock you out of fusing some of the game's ultimate personas, even if you were able to complete all social links. This doesn't lock you out of an achievement, but can still be frustrating especially if you were planning on using Orpheus Telos for the superboss.- Even on Merciless difficulty, the game itself is not that difficult. At best, it was either frustrating or annoying but not too tough save for a small number of fights. Said fights were very enjoyable, but I would love for more fights that try to keep you on your toes. Of course, this is a personal issue as someone who has been playing the Persona games for around a decade and is only recently getting into SMT (of which Persona is an easier spinoff entry of).In the end,good game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. The gameplay is highly addictive and most importantly fun. The turn-base system isn't something I typically enjoy, but this whole series is the exception for me. It's fun and really thought-provoking at times. I enjoyed the flair that the combat had, a slick type of design compared to P5R. The social link system is also really fun, learning about a bunch of new characters and having it connect to the combat of the game is really smart. The story is where the game shines tho. The characters are really well-developed and have some sort of underlying theme with them. The plot is also good with a bunch of plot twists and reveals. The message of death being unavoidable and learning how to live your life with the time you have is done so well here. The ending is perfect ;(. Music all bang, I honestly think there is not a song here that isn't good. Full Moon Full Life, Memories of You, Mass Destruction, It's Going Down Now are all highlights in the game. Voice acting too is actually perfect, only cast member I thought was a bit below everyone was Yukari but that was for some scenes. My only complaint is that there isn't much to do at night. 10/10 100% would recommend to everyone. It has a perfect story, addictive and highly enjoyable gameplay, and a banger soundtrack to come with it. Play P5R after if this is your first persona game.

If you want one of the best games persona has to offer in HD, this is your game right here.Persona 3 Reload isnt a game to me so much as it is an experience. I think its not a stretch to say this game is phenomenal, even with its flaws. And because of that its very hard to put my feelings into words for this game, half of this game is growing bonds and making memories. And the other half is fighting other worldly monsters, typical persona stuff. But where i think this game shines is the first half, a lot of these characters are very well written (except you nozomi, literally one of the worst S Links in all of persona) and emotionally compelling. Another great thing about this game is the music, a lot of the songs are phenomenal, there are some songs that are misses (in my opinion one of those misses is mass destruction). Besides the very few misses, the soundtrack is phenomenal. Its going down now is unironically one of my favorite persona songs of all time, and both, memories of you and when moons reaching out to stars (listen to the lyrics, or read em to see why) never fail to make me cry.Gameplay. ill admit, gameplay is its weakest strength. Dont get me wrong, im not saying its horrible. Im just saying out of this games many strengths, this is the least strong (still strong tho!). I found a lot of the battles way too easy (was playing on hard), i mean i literally beat the last boss without a single member going down and was bullying that shirtless fraud like we were both in grade school and i wanted his lunch money. Lastly, the story. Holy ♥♥♥♥, the story. Ive never cried over a game until this game (both original and remake). Even though i knew well in advance what happened, i still sobbed over the ending. And it wasnt just the ending either, seeing all these characters battle with the inevitable and overcome it in their own way was really poetic given the story. And the moments leading up to the climax where all your social links give you their energy was another thing that got me in the feels, made the final moment all more impact. A beautiful end to a beautiful gameHEAVILY SPOILERS UNDER THIS, DO NOT READ UNLESS FINISHED WITH GAME

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. I still prefer P5 Royal over this, because I like P5's characters more and you can really feel how the writing and game design of P3 has aged over the years, but nonetheless it feels like a really successful remaster to someone who hasn't played the original (or portable, for that matter). For fans of the Persona series or JRPGs in general, this is worth picking up. Maybe not at full price unless you're a hardcore fan of P3 specifically.The graphics are the best out of all the Persona games. Weirdly I felt like some animations were better in P5R though, mostly in in-engine cutscenes and dialogs. This game uses Unreal Engine btw, whereas P5 uses a custom engine. The part I disliked the most about P3 was the very slow story ramp-up. The first 13ish hours of this game felt like a chore at times and I would have likely stopped playing already if I wasn't set on completing this after liking P5 so much. It felt more repetitive with less choice, less variation and lesser feeling of reward for your time spent. Between 13 and 20ish hours the story seems to have really ramped up so far and that's great, because it's managing to hold my attention a lot better than in the first 13 hours. I mainly attribute this to two things. First, there is only one overarching story compared to the multiple arcs in P5, and it takes time to get going. Second, P3 only has one dungeon with (mostly) randomly generated floors, while P5 has one large hand-crafted dungeon per arc in addition to a huge randomly generated dungeon on the side. Even that secondary dungeon in P5 is more interesting to engage with compared to P3's, at least in the first 20+ hours or so (maybe longer). But it is getting better now at about 25 hours deep.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's great so far. For everyone complaining about the expansion pass, I don't really see how it's that much different than if they were to make an enhanced edition just like every other Persona game since 3. I get that the story and stuff already exists but you have to realize that The Answer is about 30 hours long. That's a lot of game development, even with an already-written story!Despite what some say, this is not "half of a remake". This is a full remake of the normal game, which is about 78 hours long. If that's not worth the $70 price, I don't know what is. Now, the people who bought the $100 version of the game should have definitely gotten the expansion pass for free, and the only reason why they didn't is because ATLUS knew that most people passionate enough to buy the most expensive version of the game would be willing to buy The Answer separately. Now that IS greedy. It's also a bit of a shame that the FeMC campaign wasn't remade, but it's not as big of a deal as some people make it out to be, and would more dev time and money for a feature that most players probably wouldn't care about. Would I rather have her? Sure! But I understand the reason they didn't bring her back.(Also, I think it's kind of funny that people get so up in arms about The Answer when, from what I've heard, most people didn't even like The Answer lol.)

_childDocuments_.review: I had played this game on ps4 before getting it on steam so my hours is roughly 130 in total for this game.I love most of this game. For me, most of the cut scenes feel like a spit in the face of the original. The art direction of the cut scenes feel lost and disorganized. certain cut scenes drag or are shot so differently they lose their original meaning. Some cut scenes are also just jarring/ worse to watch. There is also some minor cut scenes missing from the remake, instead being remade in the in game engine ruining the tone they originally set up. Some cut scenes take heavily from the movies, no clue what they were thinking. they fall flat. The removal of the tired mechanic is good and bad to me. Overall it was annoying in the original but i wanted a different take on it. Not an out right removal. The main character not being able to use all weapon types felt wrong. I'm unsure why they removed it. I wish there was better ai party member control. I liked FES and the way it forced you to play around your party. RELOAD is way too easy with the ability to control your party members. Theurgy makes the game absurdly easy as certain ones are outright broken and break the games balance even on the hardest difficulty. Key tartarus floor bosses and pitiful in both attack patterns and threat. The answer DLC was okay. Not worth the price tag personally, Same issues with cut scenes. If you don't like the grinding aspect of tartarus floors, stay away from the dlc and just watch a cut scene compilation I'd recommend reload to brand new players to the persona franchise but would recommend FES to anyone that has played at least one persona or SMT game. I like the direction the game was heading in, but the flaws and odd decisions to game play and cut scenes make some of the most memorable parts of the original fall short for me. I wish the cut scenes were given the proper justice they deserved. Most notably, the protags persona awakening scene.For all the gripes I have, the persona fusion system works exactly like persona 5's which is a HUGE upgrade for the remake. Voice acting on nearly everything makes the game brim with life. Making even the more bland/ worse social links feel worth doing. The extra content they added is good and doesn't take away from the original intent of the game and enhances the experience. Overall, i will play P3FES if i want to experience persona 3. The emotional weight and art direction works better in the original. But reload is a passable starting point, substitute, and easier to get into especially for new comers.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I enjoy the fact that everyone can now play Persona 3 with ease even on console, I cannot ignore the glaring issues with the game. Examples of these issues are the game being poorly optimized and power draining, as well as the lackluster battles and difficulty. I have been playing both portable and FES since about 4-6 years ago. Unfortunately, when I play reload, I do not get the same feelings or emotional payoffs from playing this so called "REMAKE" of p3p. I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone that I want to show the beauty of Persona 3 to. They will not feel nearly as connected with these characters or story as I, or anyone that played FES or portable, were. The cut-scenes and music do not work well in tandem with the environment or the story. Characters feel happier, like persona 4, but this contrasts the setting of the game. While the addition of linked episodes seemed positive at first, the inclusion turned out to be not only a waste of time, but also a new way for the writers to regurgitate the same information at the player that once was a part of the normal story. Now the player can end up missing or skipping dialogue and character development all together. This change makes it harder for new players to have a reason to pursue other main party characters. I have watched over 4 new players to Persona 3 bench all of the team (except the girls) because they don't care about the characters that lack social links. When I first started seeing game-play of reload, I thought that it look way easier that the original with the inclusion of baton pass (shift). Little did I know, all of the team would get special moves that not only can't be blocked or nullified, but can't even be resisted. These moves do severe damage to any enemy including the full moon bosses. New players will never understand the struggle or fun while having to think out a strategy for a certain bosses. When Persona fans mention the white table, new players will have no idea why they had no trouble with it. This creates a big disconnect with old and new players for the future of this game.Reload also took its fair share of features that should be apart of the base game, a big example besides the answer is fusion spells, one of the best reasons to keep old personae updated. The game only has seven out of the original eight-teen spells. The main excuse being redundancy, this falls apart when you have played the original, most of the spell helped in certain situations and they helped fill out team setups. I won't say much about the music because that's more up to personal preference, what I can say is that from a story perspective the original tracks all work better. There is not a single reload track that outmatches the original's storytelling ability with it's music alone. The lack of options to switch or use other games soundtracks that in the "remake" is shocking. It wouldn't even be the first time that Atlus has done something like that, even in Royal you could change BGM with costumes (they were dlc in P5) while reload forces you to pay for barely any music what so ever. A possible switch between p3p or FES music would make the story drastically better.I do not respect reload as a remake nor as a way to tell P3's story, I cannot and will not ever recommend reload to anyone interested in P3. I truthfully believe that some teams at Atlus can do good like SMTV vengeance. If only the same passion and love could go into the persona series I would be happy. I walk away from reload learning that I need to vote with my wallet and not my hope.PS. Answer DLC is just stupid there is no excuse.

_childDocuments_.review: The first play-through of any Persona game is one of the best experiences you can have with the medium. Just absolutely adored my first play-through of this remake. Atlus, please add 'The Answer' to this! I may have finished the game but I never want to be done with it. While not 'mechanically' as good as Persona 5 Royal, the characters and story are, in my opinion, leagues above the parties and social links in that game or Persona 4 Golden. Some of the changes made between this remake and the original FES version of the game are great quality of life changes. At first I was conflicted about the removal of fatigue because I thought this removed a degree of strategy that made the original FES version challenging and also encouraged you to experiment more with different party compositions but I ended up using a large variety of party composition anyway due to the new additions. One of these additions was the inclusion of the 'shift' mechanic. 'Shift' functions the same as 'baton pass' from Persona 5 but without it being nearly as overpowered due to you being able to 'shift' your 'one more' to another character if you hit an enemy weakness or get a critical but without it adding on a damage multiplier the more characters the turn 'shifts' to in a row like in Persona 5. This meant that team composition was highly important, especially in hard fights, because you ideally want to shift to who is going to expose another enemies weakness but you may also want to use that extra turn for buffing/nerfing other combatants and I was way more inclined to experiment with this than just going for the 4 in a row baton pass to kill any enemy. I play a lot of turn-based JRPG's and take it from someone who has experimented a lot within the genre that this is definitely worth the price of purchase. I pre-ordered it because I'm a fan of the series and had buyers remorse moments after pre-purchasing but I can assure you that feeling was very misplaced. If I had to rank this in the 'modern day' Persona series, the ranking would go something like this:Persona 5 Royal (as much as I ragged on it's baton pass mechanic, I think it's other unique mechanics are brilliant and it added an extra 20-25 hours of extra game-play on top of making great changes to the original release)Persona 3 ReloadPersona 5 Persona 3 FES (having an extra whole chapter of game-play, even if I still can't do direct commands for other party members, is worth more than choosing the gender of the protagonist and utilising a clunky isometric point-to-talk mechanic.Persona 4 Golden - It may be the bottom of my list but it's still a great game!If you are even a casual or passing JRPG fan, do yourself a favour and get a copy of this fantastic remake!

_childDocuments_.review: Memento Mori, Memento Vivere Remember that you are mortal. Remember to live.Combining an overarching theme that everyone will have to confront later in their life alongside an exceptional gameplay loop as players balance controlling social aspects during the day to craft stronger personas for dungeon crawling at night to earn money to improve said social aspects in the day. Immerse yourself in its stellar soundtrack centered around a strong leitmotif of bonds and death. Experience it all through the immaculate UI design with as much subtle theme and foreshadowing as the OST itself. Persona 3 Reload is here to show us how this genre-defining title once left in indelible mark in JRPG history and is capable of doing so again 18 years later.At the end of your journey, I truly hope that you will find your answer to life. As the best girl once said, "You don't have to save the world to find meaning in life. Sometimes all you need is something simple, like someone to take care of." Here's to a brand new day.

_childDocuments_.review: The wind... It feels so nice... I admit, I'm finally noticing the beauty of spring. It's WonderfulAnd yet, without exception, each and every season will come to an end.We fought side by side... We faced the world's end... And now... Fighting for what you can change... And accepting the things you can't.Nothing on this earth lasts forever. Every life will one day fizzle out... That holds true for all of us. And as soon as you come to terms with it, you realize something. You see what really matters... And find out what it is that gives your life meaning.When I learned that I wasn't strong enough... I was tormented by it. Now I understand why.Protecting others is the duty I was given... But to me, it was more than an obligation. At some point, it became something I wanted to do for myself. Once I decided to try and prevent the Fall... something inside me clicked.When I thought about how I might never see you again... That's when I first understood... what mattered to me the most. _childDocuments_.review: Ah, finally, the game that kickstarted the modern Persona series. Having previously played 4 and 5, I was excited to dive into this game and see what I had been missing. Every Persona game has so much to experience, and it’s always an enjoyable adventure.The aspect most people seem to love about this game is the story. After completing it, I can see why. It’s the strongest of the Persona games available on modern platforms. The game tries to tackle some heavy subject matter. So much of the game is focused on one’s impending death and what it means to live a meaningful life. The conclusions the game reaches feel satisfying and well done. I also thought that the game’s willingness to let certain characters die kept the story interesting. Oftentimes, I feel like games dance around the idea of letting major characters die and are afraid of killing fan-favorites. Persona 3 doesn’t care and just lets it rip. It helped me feel invested, and I appreciated the frank treatment of death.The game’s emphasis on finding meaning in life ties in well with the social link system. The acclaimed “making friends” system got its start in the original edition of this game. In some areas, it is all too obvious that this was their first attempt at things. Some social links seem to go nowhere for the first 7 or 8 ranks, only for the character to suddenly have some epiphany at the very end. In the later games, the links have arcs that are interesting to follow. Not every link follows this rule, of course, and there are some that I greatly enjoyed experiencing. Characters such as Akinari and Hayase are standouts in this regard. The game certainly doesn’t bat a thousand, however. I also appreciated the game’s addition of “linked episodes,” which fleshes out party members that didn’t have a social link in the original version of the game. That helps add some depth to each party member and expands on their character and motivations.The gameplay takes heavy inspiration from Persona 5. If you’ve played that game, then you know what to expect. The turn-based combat mostly revolves around finding an enemy’s weaknesses and exploiting that to get All-Out Attacks for massive damage. Additionally, the 1 More/Baton Pass system returns (renamed Shift, in this iteration). Perhaps I’m jaded from experiencing this system several times over, but I didn’t find it as engaging as I’d found other games in the series. It felt like I was treading on old ground. There is very little done to innovate in this regard. However, I suspect that this may be an issue unique to me. Atlus seems to have taken the approach of “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.” Most players – especially first-time Persona players – will probably have no problems with this system. If you’ve played them all, though, you may find combat boring after a while.Unlike other entries in the series, this game does not have unique dungeons. Instead, it has a single, massive dungeon called Tartarus that you slowly explore over the course of the game. Tartarus is far from an interesting locale. It’s mostly flat, featureless corridors with a different art style every dozen floors or so. The game seems to use slight variations on a few different floor templates. There are no puzzles to solve or hidden areas to uncover. At the start of the game, it’s not so bad, but it begins to feel grating and repetitive by the end. Future games in the series improved on this by giving each dungeon a unique theme with some quirks or exploration elements integrated. Persona 3 is unfortunately shackled to the design choices of 2006. It’s not a horrible experience, but given that you’re spending so much time there, it is disappointingOverall, this game, while a little rough around some edges, is still good and worth your time. The gameplay has been modernized, and the visual style has that trademark Persona flair that so many people adore. There’s plenty to enjoy here for both series veterans and newcomers. 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: I play this game on PS5 most of the time. I have over 480 hours on it so far and I think it is amazing. This review is being written before The Answer Epilogue releases, so there will be no information on that. I played the original Persona 3 once, Persona 3 Portable several times on both sides, and Persona 3 FES countless times but I can safely say that Persona 3 Reload is the best way to experience Persona 3. The changes made allow newer players to feel more comfortable in this new entry while still giving them a bigger challenge than Persona 5 Royal did (not that that is hard to do). There were a lot of people worried that it'd be too close to Persona 5, but I think it did a phenomenal job of keeping Persona 3's themes and design style while making it modern. The graphics are great. There is amazing use of lighting in the Dark Hour and seeing your characters reflected off of Tartarus' floor was a welcome addition. My review from now on will be more about letting you know the types of changes they made to the game, so that you can decide for yourself whether you think it's worth buying or not. I won't go over everything here, as a lot was changed.Starting with the biggest thing,  Many tactics were removed because of this, but some still exist if you want to play with AI party members. The Shift mechanic was added. This works like Persona 5's baton pass, but it doesn't give any bonuses for using it. Party member's Personas have received many changes. The light-user and dark-user have been reworked to include the new kouha and eiha skills added in Persona 5. Yukari no longer misses every shot. Yes this deserves its own mention. Global crit rate increase. It's not large, but it is noticeable. A new super-skill type called a Theurgy was added. I'll let you see what these are. New skills were added. Some fusion skills didn't make it over to this game, but the feature still exists through a new system. The Shuffle Time system was reworked. Orgia mode was reworked. New passive abilities called personality traits were added. These are for your party members. They work like Persona trait skills do in Persona 5 Royal, but they're assigned to the character rather than a Persona. Again, there were a lot of changes and I won't go over everything. While each block keeps the same themes they had in the original game, they all look, play, and feel very different. Breakable objects were added. They work like the Chained Desires in Mementos from Persona 5. New Twilight Fragment feature was added. Twilight Fragments are items you can find on the ground, in the new breakables, obtained from quest rewards, and from Elizabeth when you rank up Social Links. While there is technically an infinite amount in the game, I'd advise against wasting them as it gets very tedious to acquire large amounts as the game progresses. New locked chest contains higher quality items but requires 1-3 twilight fragments to open. Items obtainable from chests were reworked. New chest added that contains equipment bases. Gold Shadows were reworked. When leaving the entrance of Tartarus, you can choose to go directly to the highest floor you've gone to like in P3P. The clock from FES' Epilogue and P3P returns. It now consumes Twilight Fragments to restore your party's HP and SP. Monad has been completely reworked. The Paradigm Door does not return. I'm covering a lot in this section. It's mostly just things that pertain to the overworld of the game. Characters and places will email you, like the IM app in Persona 5. Going to the nurse's office to try medicine can only be done the day directly going to Tartarus. On weekends or days off, you can return to the dorm without time advancing. The Inari Shrine from P3P which allows skill card duplication has returned. Accessories have been moved to the Police Station, and Le Blue V has been reworked into a skill remembrance place. This works like the confession booth in Persona 5 and allows party members to remember skills they learned in the past. The Antique Store no longer uses Personas. Following P3P, it instead takes gems you collect from Shadows and heart items obtained from nurturing Personas. You can trade gems and equipment bases for weapons, armors, items, and skill cards. Part-Time jobs have returned from Persona 3 Portable. Shops are open at night like in P3P. Like Persona 5, you can see available social links from the map screen and if they are ready to rank up or not. The dorm's laptop behind the counter can be used to spend time on various computer software purchasable from two new shops. These vary from adding/enhancing mechanics that you can use in Tartarus, to permanently increasing the protag's stats, and increasing social stats. There is now a garden on the rooftop of the dorm. Koromaru's walks have been changed and have much better rewards. Social stat points obtained from activities have been adjusted. New "Rewind" feature allows you to rewind time back to the last five times you saved. There were two major social features that they added in this game, the first being Dorm Hangouts, and the second being Linked Episodes. Dorm Hangouts are events where you can spend time with the members of SEES on their own doing things around the dorm. You can manage the plants in the garden, make food, read books, and watch movies. Each of these types of hangouts will give you a different reward. Hangout with a character enough and you may see a change in their combat style. Linked Episodes are P3R's version of the male social links included in the Female Protagonist route of P3P. Throughout the game you'll be able to experience limited-time events that progress through a storyline for each of the male party members of SEES. Each event will be available for multiple days, but if you miss one character's event then you will not be able to continue with that character's future events. Think of these like limited-time social links that  aren't tied to an Arcana. There is a reward for completing all of a character's linked episodes. To clarify, the requests I'm talking about are the ones received from Elizabeth at the Velvet Room entrance. A lot of the rewards were changed for requests and new requests were added. There is no longer a limit to how many requests can be taken at a time. Many requests that previously had deadlines no longer have deadlines. Item scavenging quests were removed. Special weapon quests have been changed. The new weapons are much easier to acquire and come from specific sources, no longer relying on RNG. Many Personas were reworked.There are new rewards for filling out the Persona Compendium.New Personas were added to the Compendium. Some Personas received Arcana changes. Fusion recipes were changed. Social Links still feature the same characters, though some of the dialogue and options have been changed. They removed the forced romance paths in the romanceable social links and removed the jealousy feature present in the original game. You can see what rank you are with a character without needing to talk to them or checking the social link page, which is a nice qol change. Probably the biggest change to social links is that I ran out of space in the review

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 is a game that a lot of people hold very close to their heart, and I'm one of those people. It's a great RPG with wonderful writing and a bittersweet sentimentality that lends it a surprising amount of weight. The game has had many rereleases over the years, and Reload has firmly become my personal favorite version of the game. It's a great starting point for anyone interested in Persona or Megami Tensei.Reload is significantly different than the other versions of Persona 3, and while other versions have their own good things going for them, I think the additional story content added to Reload makes it my favorite. The life sim elements in the Persona games tend to exhaust me, but I found Persona 3 Reload to handle them the best out of every title so far. My only real complaint with Reload is that I think it's absurdly easy. While the game is overall very engaging, the combat never really feels very challenging on any difficulty. The optional superbosses are hard, sure, but most of the game is a cakewalk.I'm surprised by how nostalgic this game made me. Especially towards the end, the art direction for the final environments of the game and the wonderful guitar rifts used in the music, really brought back the spirit of PS2-era Atlus.

_childDocuments_.review: persona 3 reload is a... hard game to review.this IS persona 3 we're talking about, i love the main characters, the simple yet underlying complex story told all at once, and aigis might be my favorite character of the whole series.(and yes, i really like the new soundtrack)that said, it's still a game, and a remake nonetheless, so i have some things i wanna complain on:1. while i did enjoy the new hangouts and mini social links, i think this remake is far too constrained on being faithful to it's source material rather than trying something more with it, this remake could've been a LOT more, but instead it chose to do the exact same thing as it's PS2 counterpart, and as a counterpart the game still feels like it has the PS2 limitations in mind. and the whole time i kept wondering "i spent $70 dollars on this, and i could've just played FES again..." 2. also, the majority of the social links... kinda suck. or i don't really care for.3. they could've done a LOT more with tartarus, the same way they did with mementos in P5 -> P5R (i miss you, ryuji's insta-kill) and it kinda frustrates me they chose to handle it like this.4. it still has the same problem as FES, that when you max your social skills and your social links at night, you have NOTHING else to do on nights. this is a little mitigated by the dorm hangouts but it gets old really quicklybut when all is said and done, it's still a really meaningful experience and i had a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The Persona series is one of the greatest series gaming because of its simple but engaging combat, it's interesting use of relationship mechanics, it's great storytelling, and its overall handling of mature topics. Persona 3 Reload is a great example of what a remake SHOULD be, much like other top-to-bottom remakes like Final Fantasy 7 Remake, and the Spyro Trilogy Remake, etc. Even at the increased price of 70 dollars, it is vastly worth it. You will more than likely get 70 hours out of it, and the storytelling is great in its own right to warrant the price. I will also always recommend Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 Royal.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload takes what made the original release fantastic, then gives it a huge quality of life makeover while keeping the core elements intact. The father of modern Persona games gets such a big glowup with the models and animations, and while most of the original voice actors got replaced, (I think the only one who stayed the same was Aigis) the new cast is insanely talented. By the end of the game I preferred the new voice actors over the old ones! This is further emphasized with the voice acting of ALL RANKS for the social links. The voice actors were not the only thing that got replaced, as many of the existing songs got the same treatment, though this time to varying degrees of success. For example, I much prefer the original version of Mass Destruction over the new remastered version. But as if that wasn't enough we also got a plethora of new tracks, the centerpiece of these being "It's Going Down Now." Thank you Lotus Juice for bringing your A-gameWhile the models are crisp and sharp, on the personas I just can't help but feel like I prefer how they looked in Persona 5 more. The animations however are fluid, and you don't need to look any further than Yukari's Theurgy to experience this.Speaking of Theurgies, this mechanic is one of the quality of life changes that adds a new layer of options in the game. It's now also easier than ever to keep party members leveled and gear with the inclusion of Monad passages and the clock. The changes to mechanics are felt the hardest when it comes to Koromaru and Ken. But my favorite inclusion to this game are the brand new Linked episodes that let us spend time with the Members of SEES that aren't proper social links such as Junpei and Akihiko. Disappointingly however, the fan favorite FeMC from the portable version of the game does not make a return, and "The Answer" From FES is going to be released as DLC. I understand that it would have required significant more recording time, but it's sad to see her get no love. Another thing that I wish could have made it into the game were more boss battles akin to Persona 5's challenges. Overall I consider this game a must play for JRPG fans, and especially Persona fans. I give this game a 9/10 for sure and am looking forward to the Episode Aigis update.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a remake and updated version of Persona 3. Among the new-gen Persona games, 3 is my favorite, and I had a good time playing it, although I already knew most of the story. + Main story that keeps the players on their toes as it unfolds.+ Fun JRPG battle sequences with a mix of daily life balance.+ Stylish UI, Art direction, and music.+ Some parts of the story are updated and so is the gameplay's quality of life compared to prior versions. - The Dungeon exploration can be repetitive (but still doable for me.)- I said earlier that some parts of the story are updated but only minor details and non-major interactions are added. The majority of the story is the same as the older versions. Returning players may find it repetitive aside from updated graphics and visuals.- DLC selections on costumes are not as varied as Persona 5. And the choice of bundling some miscellaneous DLCs with episode Aigis is questionable.For the first-time players of the Persona series, I would recommend the 5th game more but if you like a more sad and serious theme or want to explore more of Persona games or just JRPGs in general then I would totally recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part P3: Reload is nearly a one-to-one remake of Persona 3 OG, but with a huge visual glow up and a re-recorded soundtrack plus an additional new battle theme when you surprise attack an enemy alongside the new opening theme. The game just really pops visually and is beautiful to look at, also if you have a modern GPU don't be afraid to increase the internal rendering resolution, it's worth it, trust me. That said additional quality of life features alongside the now standard stylish persona menus/ui from modern Persona make this experience feel even more fresh. While I believe the current main cast who has done the voice-over here is all new they all sound very similar to the OG performances from the PS2 (In a good way) so it's not totally jarring hearing characters you've probably known and loved again for people who enjoyed FES or even P3P back in the day. I haven't gotten far enough to see more nuanced differences, but I have heard that they sort of splice the best parts of FES and P3P's additional content here into one cohesive package alongside a bit of new stuff that's non-intrusive to the spirit of the original game. From what I can see the story hasn't changed much if at all (Which is great, P3 doesn't need to really change in that regard). Sidenote, but thank god for direct commands now finally existing in P3 outside of P3P which I couldn't get into. And being able to have shuffle time feels nostalgic in a sense too in terms of end of battle bonuses. While demon negotiation is undoubtedly cool that for me at least feels like a gameplay mechanic that belongs to SMT moreso than Persona.Overall it seems like a lot of care went into this project and is a way to give a beloved entry the fresh coat of paint it deserves. Definitely feels like a celebration of Persona 3, and now newer persona fans particularly those who jumped in with 5 can see why P3 is as cherished as it is for older Persona fans.  While I know some P1 and P2 fans are desperate to get their games remade like this I also hope Persona 4 gets the "Reload" treatment one day too. While P4G has aged relatively well for a late PS2/Vita game it still shows its age today, and could really benefit from the modernization treatment that P3 has received.All my rambling aside I definitely recommend JRPG fans give this a try. Those who slept on P3 for awhile because it was too "old" for them now have no excuse to ignore this great game. The only issue for me is that under certain conditions this game can crash. I feel like part of it is the 120fps setting for some reason doesn't properly work out of the gate. But when I've kept the game at 60fps with Vsync enabled I've mostly had no issues. Just thought this was worth mentioning. Hopefully there are some patches on the way with all the error reports Atlus are receiving to eventually get rid of all crashing issues/bugs (Make sure you save often) regardless of the mix of graphical settings you choose. Also the Denuvo inclusion sucks but is to be expected, hoping that down the road it's removed after the main sales time frame is over whenever that is.P3 is grossly underrated and I'm happy that it has finally gotten the love and attention it deserves with "Reload". Like I mentioned before it's basically a visually glowed up one-to-one remake with modern bells and whistles, so the fact the core gameplay loop and cathartic narrative still feels relevant today is a testament to just how good P3 was when it originally came out.

"SEES" tries to hunt down Shadows and investigate what the "Dark Hour" is. As you play you learn more about it and begin to understand it, while getting new members for the team!Persona 3 Reload is a game that as turn-based JRPG, Dungeon crawler, Visual novel all in one! You have confidants that help you and can help you in your playthrough, You can spend time with them and even date them. You can buy gear from a , You can spend time grinding for levels or just going straight through the game. There is plenty to be doing and there is no way that you have "free time" to be wasting.The music is done fantastically. This is my most favourite soundtrack from any game ever made. I listen to the P3R music pretty much daily. I don't get tired of it, Just like P5R, It makes me want to listen to it more! It's no longer a surprise that a game like this has such fantastic music. Soundtracks such as "It's going down now" and "Color your night" are done very well! Unfortunately due to "tiktok overuse" "It's going down now" was overused and it doesn't have the same feeling now, That doesn't take away from how great it is!So far, I'm actually enjoying it. I don't get too much time to play games like this anymore. If i had more time, I'd have 100%'ed it just like i did with P5R!I also heard there is a DLC that you need an expansion pass for.. which kinda sucks but i've heard great things about the DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good remake. There are some issues that persist like the writing in the social links being inadequate compared to the likes of Persona 4 & 5, and the lack of a female route that was in Portable is a bit of a missed opportunity. But the quality of life updates, new events, graphical overhaul, and the fully voiced social links and new voice acting are very good and mostly make up for those factors. And the story still holds up extremely well with its cast of characters and narrative events/elements.But the biggest issue is that this game is ridiculously expensive. £60/$70 for this game is already pushing people’s tolerance when considering other big releases these days, but having to pay an additional £30/$35 for a standalone expansion pass that contains important story details  is a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ move. Like I anticipated it being released after the initial release but it being this expensive as well is just pure greed.On top of the other day 1 DLC in this game makes it just egregious. It’s what gaming executives like to do – ruin games for everyone for the sake of unsustainable profits.The price tag hangs overhead like Tartarus during the Dark Hour which is a shame because this is a very good game and a very good remake with lots of details and improvements. They have been doing this for a while now and I don’t want to see ATLUS follow the likes of EA, Ubisoft and 2K anymore. The egregious DLC and expensive price tags, plus re-releasing games like with the upcoming Shin Megami Tensei 5: Vengeance at full price has to stop. But they won’t because executives are going to continue pushing, and we will continue to buy them anyway.As someone who genuinely likes this game and this franchise it annoys me to ‘not recommend’ this game. It just stings quite hard because this isn’t a complete remake to begin with. And I’m part of the problem buying this game at full price. Don’t let yourself become part of it as well. TLDR: Very good game, but it is way too expensive to recommend right now. Wait for a good sale for the base game and for the expansion pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 is a timeless classic and this remake improves on it in nearly every way. Tartarus and the handful of lazy dungeons, while still among the worst in any SMT game, are nicer to play and navigate now due to the quality of life changes like the Jump-Slash as well as the significant increase in graphical fidelity. Also, the game is near 100% voiced now  so the story feels so much more alive than before and while I think replacing the original English voice cast was folly, I do think the new guys did a pretty great job at it. As for the soundtrack, the remixes genuinely trade blows with the original and the new additions along with the new singer are quite good and Lotus Juice is as corny as ever on his Sonic Adventure Knuckles rapper type beat but I won't hate. My main complaint with how things have changed in the remake is that the game balance is a bit suspect. Physical (especially slash) is broken beyond belief now to the point I think that magic builds outside of the Almighty Affinity are Pointless. In addition, the game even on the highest difficulty is not very hard, certainly quite a bit easier than the original, but that being said all of the new additions and mechanics introduced and inspired by Persona 5 make the game far more fun to play than the original ever was. The introduced Persona 5 battle mechanics include a toned down version of the baton pass system, the addition of damaging light and dark affinity spells, among other more minor additions. Notably missing are the technical combinations as well as the Nuclear and Psychic elements, which I think should they had been included would've been a nice buff to the seemingly under-powered magic builds in this game, but I understand their absence as too many mechanics can feel clunky. 94/10 but im a die hard SMT fan so idk done yapping
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload successfully revives a beloved classic with modern polish while retaining the core elements that made the original so impactful. This remake enhances the visuals, bringing the vibrant world of Tatsumi Port Island to life with stunning, detailed environments and character models. The art direction stays true to the original, yet feels refreshed, adding depth and flair to the game's unique style.Gameplay-wise, Persona 3 Reload maintains the balance between daily life simulation and dungeon-crawling RPG elements that fans adore. The social aspects—building relationships, managing time, and navigating the emotional highs and lows of adolescence—are intact, delivering the same thoughtful character-driven narrative. The combat, now smoother and more refined, introduces quality-of-life improvements, while maintaining the strategic depth that fans expect from the Persona series.At its heart, Persona 3 Reload captures the game’s original themes of life, death, and the search for meaning, with the added benefit of modern-day advancements in design. Whether you're revisiting this iconic title or experiencing it for the first time, Persona 3 Reload offers an engaging, emotionally resonant experience that stays true to the spirit of the original while pushing the boundaries of what a remake can achieve.

_childDocuments_.review: Although if tends to change depending on the day you ask, I would say Persona 3 is my favorite game in the Persona series, and one of the best games the Megaten series as a whole has to offer.  I grew up with it, it introduced me to the larger SMT series as a whole, and it's left its mark for over a decade. When I found out it was finally coming to modern platforms as P3P, and I saw how terribly Atlus had treated it,  I lost any hope that I'd see Persona 3 brought to it's full potential. Then one day, a trailer for P3R leaked on Atlus' Instagram.I had no faith in this remake at first. The trailer looked nice, but with a lot of disappointments back to back from Atlus, (and the gaming landscape at large) I refused to get my hopes up, keeping my eye on it from a distance. I went in with low expectations, expecting a butchered cash grab, but within the first few hours, I was suprised.There's no need to exposit further, Persona 3 Reload blew me away. While I'd still hesitate to call it "the definitive version of Persona 3" It absolutely stands up with FES. The team went above and beyond here, from the presentation, to the game play improvements, both big and small QOL. The new voice actors to a magnificent job, with all of the social links hitting so much harder than they did before, and SEES translating perfectly, feeling perfectly like themselves, even with the new content. If I had to go for minor complaints, I miss the tired system. It was fun trying to minmax your time as much as possible, and if you knew what you were doing you could exploit the positives and negatives that came with it. And while now your Academics feels a bit harder to max out than it used to with the extra study time, the sizeable upgrades and reworks to Tartarus make up for it. Honestly, I'm just happy to have gotten to experience a fully realised version of a game that is so fundamental to me. If you haven't experienced a Persona game before, this is a perfect starting place, and if you've played them all before, I can't recommend a revisit enough. Persona 3 Reload is a brilliant diamond in the unfortunate sea of remakes that make up most of gaming's release cycle now, and I couldn't be happier. Here's hoping this shining mark of quality continues into Atlus' future releases. 9/10.

name: Strayed Lights
detailed_description: Strayed Lights is an immersive action adventure set in a wordless, dreamlike world of corruption and shadows. You are a nascent light on a journey to free yourself from the grasp of shadows surrounding you. Key Features of Strayed Lights: Battle endearing creatures deformed by their emotions, shift your colors to repel their attacks. Experience a tightly-crafted cinematic experience through art and emotion, with not a word of dialogue. Explore the fractured lands of Strayed Lights, from luminescent forests to canyons, caves and lands of bewildering mist. Scored to a haunting, atmospheric original soundtrack by Austin Wintory. RESTORE YOUR LIGHT Play as a newborn flame torn by shadows. Progress in a hostile world on a quest to restore your light by facing your inner demons and helping beings along the way. Unlock new abilities as your light brightens. PACIFY YOUR ENEMIES Find your siblings who went rogue, each deformed by a specific emotion. Battle these monstrous forms and pacify the emotions that control them. Face your inner demons taken form to hinder your progress. SHIFT COLORS TO FIGHT Face creatures torn by shadow in fluid and rewarding combat. Repel their attacks while shifting between blue and orange to match their color and overcome them in vivid finishers.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the first three areas as of writing this. Amazing atmospheric game with challenging combat. You match colors with the enemy and parry their attacks. The games platforming elements are solid, but when you jump on a latch it takes a while for your character to pull himself up which breaks the pace of the otherwise fast running. Loads of collectibles which actually make your character stronger so they're an interesting initiative for everyone and not just completionists. The boss battles is where the game really shines though, Shadow of the Collosus/Asura's Wrath vibes, which I absolutely love. Soundtrack is mostly atmospheric with some upbeat music during boss battles. The game follows a set formula. Cutscene points your character in a certain direction? Turn around for a collectible. Two or more different paths to take? Check them all out for collectible. At the top of a jumping puzzle? Gives you view of a collectible so better jump down to get that first. My absolute biggest gripe with the game is that the sprint button is on a face button of your controller, B by default. This sucks because the movement feels great but you constantly want to turn your camera for, you guessed it, collectibles. This makes you play with a claw grip and I don't wanna relive my 2000s Gears of War days. I'm getting old and my finger hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent action-adventure game with great visuals, unique color-swapping parry system, and a relaxing soundtrack.  The combat system was somewhat fun, but barebones as you do not get any new combat abilities throughout most of the game. Enemy variation is at a minimal with the same encounters but sometimes mixing up the enemy type. Energy orbs hidden throughout the world can be collected to increase your energy efficiency but the game has no backtracking system once a level is complete which is personally a negative for me. The boss fights are the standouts here with adrenaline pumping fight sequences combined with neat mechanics. The game is also rather short as it can be completed between 3-6 hours depending on difficulty. [7/10]
