_childDocuments_.review: The Art style is absolutely gorgeous and the gameplay is quite good.The issue is that the campaign is pretty short (8 missions, when they are all available. As of writing it's 4 missions so barely 8hours of gameplay), and that skirmish mode is all all the game has to offer.. with a MAJOR issue: the time it takes of AI turns is absolutely horrifying, even during the first few rounds of a new game with nothing on the map. I'm talking 2 min waiting time versus 10s playtime (one army so a couple clics and your round is done), for repeated turns. It's not playable like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm neutral on this but going thumbs up due to wanting to see more from this studio. They have a really great idea here and a really fun battle system. Art style, character art and the story itself are all well above average. Would love to see another game without the negatives.Those negatives are big enough to almost out weigh the good. One, the game is far, far too short. The skirmish maps can alleviate some of the replay but I am a big story/campaign player so skirmish maps don't do much for me. The big negative for me is with the small number of story missions, several of them short, too many of them are on some kind of "timer." Defend for x turns, expecting I can explore after but instead am rushed off the map immediately. Reach location in x turns. Leaves very little time to explore the map and find all the fun stuff. The last mission, just wow. What an awfuuuul miss on that level design. Huge map and no way to enjoy exploring it with a rushed, anti-climatic ending. None of this may matter to you, but timed missions, especially half of a short story mission roster, are a huge turn off to me.In spite of all of this, the game is still worth the entry fee. Barely. The studio seems to have some great talent and a good concept here. Hopefully they can make another game, longer and without the timed mission contrivance that just sucks the fun out of a terminally short story campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: For a strategy warfare game it's fundamentally hideously broken in it's imbalance. Basically one faction (Crusade) can take territory and when they do, it's more or less permanent. When you take their territory they lose nothing and you get nothing. This is because when they take your territory they destroy it and make it partially impossible to rebuild it, while absorbing it's power into their main base. Which can move lol. So when you fight this faction you can't afford to lose a single location, while they don't have to worry about losing locations at all. It is a MASSIVE fundamental problem, especially since you might only have like 4-5 locations in a small game. In order to play this competitively you have to perma ban Crusade, leaving you with only 2 legit factions. Pretty bad. The game play seems to be designed more for single player with no though to the implications of how rediculously overpowered the Crusade iwould be in multiplayer/skirmish. This is simply not viable outside of campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Too many down-votes from people with very minimal time actually playing the game.This is a game being developed by a small group of game developers.  Yes it's been in development for 4 years, but the content that they've been able to provide in that time is actually wonderful, even for the price point. Based on what this game already offers, and the plans to continue developing and adding more content, it's absolutely worth $40 if you enjoy the 4X genre. Especially if you know how ridiculous other 4X games are with their $20-$30 DLC packages for the most minimal content updates. The artwork and music are wonderful. The story and voice-acting is great as well. I was actually surprised by the story and how interesting it was.  I'm excited for more chapters to open up in the future.I see complaints about tutorials.  No, this game doesn't have a tutorial and it doesn't need one.  The encyclopedia in-game offers explanations for every bit of information you'll need as you play. There have been difficult and confusing moments in the story, and with that come my only complaints so far:Please add a x2 or x4 speed to combat, or a skip feature.Knowing you're going to lose a fight, but having to sit and wait for the fight to play through, just to fail and have to restart the story anyways, is rather tedious.Other than that the game is great.I'll update more once I dabble more in Skirmish + Multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Ive got about 8 hours in(5 offline). It sucks to give it a non buy because its so well polished, it really is, and I looked forward to it. Many games even AAA dont get this kind of clean AI that this team built and going forward hopefully they take that skillset in to their next game BUT and this is about as big a BUT u can have while gaming, its simply not that much fun and for $30, some even paid $40, its not even close. This is a great looking Phone Game IMO.It feels like your just playing an interactive book, choices in the way you go about the maps are largley inconsequential. You do not really control combat, which could be fine but it just feels like its a phone game that looks too good so it was made for PC. The Economy is super slow, the heros are where the game coulda been saved but there skills and upgrades are few and boring.Its a good team of devs, they do care, but this game in the end simply isnt fun and thats the number 1 thing you have to hit.Just crazy how well polished this game is from UI to the Audio but the formula was such a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! The art is gorgeous and a spin on the homm battles with real time autobattles that you influence by position and mid fight abilities. This game is EARLY ACCESS in a true sense. _childDocuments_.review: The core mechanics are decent, but the game doesn't do anything so far that gets me really excited about them, while having a lot of little quibbles that up to making the experience very annoying.1. No breakdowns of tooltips in battle combined with an awkward time even seeing the limited unit info it gives.2. No after-battle breakdown of what your units did, which combined with the former makes it very hard to actually get meaningful feedback about how your units and enemies did.3. Abilities you cast mostly have like 1/5th of a second delays and it's somewhat hard to read who's in the aoe, which combine to mean you'll constantly be trying to squeeze 2 or 3 units at once into a buff spell and then be disappointed when one of them sneaks out of it at the last milisecond, which might be unit-killing if it was an invuln spell you badly needed on your frontline.4. Enemy heroes spam their own abilities with no ability to see what they do mid-battle. Oh they... did some sort of glowy buff on their guys. Man, sure glad this isn't some sort of strategy game where I need to react to what my enemy does and try to think about things!5. I'm only partway through the 3rd of 8 story scenarios, so all I can just say is that there hasn't really been anything that tickled my fancy yet. The 2nd one was a mostly-no-base mission that had a lot of strategy game design sins of "if you don't do exactly what the developers want you lose instantly" which sucks a lot when you can't actually easily, you know, check which enemies can move where... which is vital info in a strategy game...6. The heroes you see seem to mostly have a very obvious type of unit they're meant to be used with - like literally, they just have "give all units of this type +2 power" or such. And the smallish size of armies means you'll probably be doing a lot of battles in a row with a near-identical strategy. Cavalry charge then use the heal buff on your massed cav. Summon luminant swords into the enemy ranged units while protecting your tarpit infantry from enemy charges with the invuln buff. There's definitely choices to be made in army comp, but they aren't nearly enough to carry the entire game, since each hero has like 2-3 buttons you can use in combat that mostly really just are used one way (target enemy squishy unit with this, target your own engaged unit with this, target a big clump of wounded friendlies with that, all on simple cooldowns) so constantly mixing up and tweaking your composition is the only chance the game had to be engaging, and it just... isn't enough.Despite all this the game isn't retally frustrating to play moment-to-moment or anything and I can definitely see myself giving it more of a try in hopes that the mechanics get more nuanced later on in a way that'll make it feel meaningful. But so far it just seems to be dying a death-of-a-thousand-quality-of-life-cuts in the process of not really doing anything sufficiently impressive with its premise.Character art is pretty snazzy tho. Ox best horse.

_childDocuments_.review: Because Songs of Silence presents itself as more than your average auto-battler, you expect deeper, more tactical decisions, but sadly, it misses the mark in establishing any sort of cause-effect game loop indicative of the genre, boiling down instead to mindless troop-mustering and troop-mashing.The art, sound design, and environments--all top-notch. Where it falters is in its lack of strategy. Your best chance at completing each mission is to pick on the little guy, to snowball one location at a time until you're able to sweep the map. There's really no reason to deviate from this strategy, and in fact, you're punished if you do. Taking risks--just for the sake of spicing things up--often results in lost troops, lost special units, and lost time, with nothing to show but frustration. Worse still--in some missions, you aren't even offered the opportunity of choices. You're ordered to move your hero from one area to the next, reading lines of dialogue as you travel, and if you deviate from the path, you lose. The game plays itself in many ways, but in these moments, the charade becomes painfully obvious. In the end, your decisions feel inconsequential and your time wasted. Can't recommend the game as is.

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence sings a strong first note. From its captivating soundtrack and hyper-stylized art nouveau-inspired visuals, to its committed high fantasy voice acting performances and unique approach to RTS combat (one that involves auto-battling and deckbuilding), SoS makes immediately clear that it takes itself seriously and so should you... regardless of how many throwaway Angry Birds mobile games its developer made in the past.  At this stage of Early Access, Songs of Silence sports half of its 10-part narrative-driven campaign, and each mission is stuffed full of fun worldbuilding lore that revolves around “the Silence,” an all-consuming black (red*) hole blob thing controlled by a fanatical cult called the Crusade that’s determined to... uh, not super sure to be honest. Your world is split into two realms—one of light, one of dark—and the Silence seems intent on gobbling both of them up in order to restore balance somehow? (“Are we the baddies?”) What I do know is that you’ll battle the Silence as both Lorelai, a reluctant heiress to the light realm throne of Ehrengard, and Akard, a spunky prince trapped in the crumbling Dark realm. A number of interesting side characters both help and hurt you along the way, and each features a committed voice actor. All in all, I consider the game’s story a strength, and I’m excited to see its second half.  Though it blends a number of genres, Songs of Silence is a classic fantasy 4X at heart, meaning you’re here to build up your base and blow up baddies (oh wait, that’s a 4B). To do so, you’ll use a combination of cards, of which there are three types. (1) Blue strategy cards are used to build and improve your settlements, castles, and temples, each of which will gradually level up, in doing so giving you more resources per turn like gold that you’ll use to play (2) gray troop recruitment cards. After assembling a hero-led army, you’ll lead said army into interesting auto-battles that you can dramatically impact through your deck of the third and final cards, (3) red cards. These buffs, debuffs, heals, shields, attacks, and retreat cards are all linked to timers and can be played anywhere on the battlefield, which turns an otherwise uninteresting, hands-off auto-battle snoozefest into an often frantic all-hands-on-deck adventure. It’s not a perfect system, and the level-capped campaign missions means you’ll accrue new cards at a snail's pace. Still, it feels like an evolution in RTS combat and I want more of it. Equally impressive are the game’s single-player objectives, as each campaign mission has its own fun flavor. You’ll go from the good ol’ 4X conquering of an entire map, to charting a sneaky, stealthy path through enemy territory using the game’s stealth mechanic, to defending your castle from an unending siege of Silence. Each map has its own little surprises and side quests, too, including an adventure mode that pits you against powerful monsters in exchange for powerful rewards. But, while Songs of Silence handles its core mechanics well, it’s clear the game is still missing significant polish. In addition to missing or incorrect text here and there, not to mention a hefty helping of visual bullshittery, I encountered a game-breaking battle bug that necessitated a full restart... not of the battle, but of the whole program, because for some miserable reason the game won’t let players access the menu during combat, meaning you’re stuck watching the bitter end of every battle gone wrong before you’re given the opportunity to reload.  But these faults seem fixable and are pretty easy to forgive on day one of Early Access, especially when the rest of the game is so darn fun to look at. While the actual in-game textures and lighting fail to live up to the dozens upon dozens of eyepopping unit designs done in that gorgeous art nouveau style, I’m still giving SoS a strong “4/5” for Visuals. The soundtrack, meanwhile, is well done if a smidge too repetitive—would love to see more music added by 1.0, because what’s here is quite good. The sound design, meanwhile, needs some work, preferably starting with an annoying "mooing" sound that plays every five seconds while organizing your army.  That brings us to overall value. I beat the game’s five missions in about 12 hours, then tossed a few more at the skirmish mode, which includes a multiplayer option. My video review posted before the publisher announced the game's price, and I think it's on the very upper end of what's reasonable at this stage of Early Access. So, after averaging up our micrometrics, Songs of Silence gets an aggregate MEGA score of 3.71/5 (full scoring breakdown, from “Plot” to “Sound,” available in video). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence combines storytelling, heroes (strongly reminding me of Warcraft III), strategy auto-battle, deck-building and map driven strategy into a certainly unique 4X game.If anything, SoS is a very beautiful game. It is rare that a hand drawn art-nouveau style fits in with in-game 3D content, but SoS does this very well; adding lots of tiny details that match the artworks' filigrane brushwork (although the battles often come out way too pastelly and bright). Combined with the music (which does a good job at setting the mood, but never grasping unnecessary attention), the game feels comfortable and homey right away.The UI feels polished, sparse and not overloaded at all, although the control scheme still has some rough edges. The game looks great on an ultrawide screen, but in-world chat bubbles are misplaced.The Gameplay is spread across a few levels - battles, cities and the world map at the very least. As far as I got until now, the story is well written and goes into fantasy name-dropping mode pretty fast (the glossary certainly helps).The tutorial left me fending on my own pretty soon, which gave me time to experiment strugglingly, and fail miserably a couple of times. Hero respawning prevents you from having to save and reload constantly.I have no idea how big or deep the game will be later on yet, but I did enjoy the first few hours.Being as impatient as I am, I guess I'm missing a fast mode.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game.  Battles are great, the card system is fun and the art is just beautiful. However.  While I can recommend this game, the 4x element to it, the building of bases, AI and AI camps and heroes from all 3 factions need balancing.  A lot of it.  They also need to rework how to obtain heroes.  Sure, 1/2 Skirmish wins, not a big deal but the 75 STOLEN loot chests? Goodluck.  Not unless you 1v1 a friend and just steal from each other.AI will literally sit in the same spot for the entire game if you're a crusade player.  Thousand Armies? They will constantly take back cities you just took instantly.  Crusade doesn't need to worry about.Heroes are either so good or so bad.  A 2/2 Thousand Army Paladin is grossly under powered vs a 2/2 Crusade hero.  Healing from moment to moment needs a buff.  Unless you got lucky and got a healing card from a hero or from the city level up (because its random) you may struggle with keeping up with everyone.  Healing is so slow.  Even then, when a heal card pops up, it competes with other strong cards and feels so lame to toss them away never to see them again.It's clear they pushed out the 1.0 without balancing in mind. The polish is really good and while I understand why, it makes the first impression harder to enjoy when so many things are just not balanced and it makes it even harder to stay when everything is set up for your failure if you're trying something new or rolling the dice.Would purchase as a sale product.  Not full price as of 1.0.

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a beautiful and unique addition to the 4X strategy genre. The game combines deep tactical gameplay with fast-paced autobattles, all wrapped in stunning art. The presentation, music, and voice-acted story create an immersive experience that draws you in from the start.The gameplay in Songs of Silence stands out with its innovative battle system. The intense, real-time battles require strategic thinking and quick decisions. Setting formations, using tactical orders, and deploying divine interventions keeps each encounter fresh and exciting. The inclusion of cards representing unique actions adds another layer of strategyThe visuals in Songs of Silence are a feast for the eyes. Inspired by the Art Nouveau movement, the game breaks away from the typical drab and muddy look of many strategy games. Each unit and environment is rendered with care, making the game a joy to look at. The atmospheric soundtrack composed by Hitoshi Sakimoto, known for his work on Final Fantasy Tactics and Valkyria Chronicles, complements the visuals perfectly and enhances the overall experience.For Polish players, the translation seems to be well-done, making the game accessible and enjoyable for a wider audience.The text boxes could be a bit bigger for better readability of dialogues, they can only go up 120%. The rest of the ui is fine, but some of the small texts feel like they could be bigger for improved readability.The price is a bit steep in some countries, but it is well worth it for this quality of a game.One of my problems with Civ 5 / VI is the ability to discern the types of units. If not for their icons and description I'd have trouble telling apart the unit types. It's an issue of most 3d rts games in this style. Same thing is here, but the units don't have their own icon above them. As a new player of this game I am having trouble telling units apart based on their view. It would be really great if those units had a symbol or a health bar + their name. I understand that this makes it less stylyzed / cluttered, but it would help me play the game quite a lot; even if it was optional.Kinda hard to get a grasp at first, I'm sure that this will improve over time. There are many good tutorials for it.Overall, Songs of Silence is a standout title in the 4X strategy genre, offering a fresh and visually stunning experience that strategy fans should not miss. If you like homm3 and enjoy shiny graphics in the style of Civilization VI you will enjoy it.I'll revisit the review once it is out of Early Access, it's a work in project title that looks like a masterpiece in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, after a fair amount of playtime I'm happy to say its got so much more going for it too besides good looks. Lots of strategic considerations on the campaign map and a surprisingly large amount of tactical options in the auto-battles. When two armies clash they will automatically attack each other without intervention but during the battle you can heavily manipulate the outcome with many different spells and abilities, some of which are game changers and very satisfying to use. I really like this system as it keeps the game flowing at a good pace, very important consideration if multiplayer is your thing. Its also means you can finish a full game in one evening which in a genre where the average strategy game can take multiple days is very welcome.For those with concerns about this being in early access and being unfinished there is a surprising amount of great content already in the game. The campaign is always getting updated with new chapters and the skirmish mode allows you play all factions. There is a sturdy unlock based progression system in which completing various missions will unlock new heroes and features. I think its done very well and you can unlock the hero of your choice in a relatively short timeframe. The devs are very active within the community and always listening to feedback, one look in the official discord makes this obvious. I think this game has a very bright future and I can't wait to see the overall response once it hits full release. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun idea inspired by homm and confidently taken into its own direction.After completing campaign(skirmish, but not mp) my impressions are:-Amazing art and design together with animations, smaller details like change of city visuals when you lvl them up is even more noticeable in such art style-Campaign, altho in terms of main story did not impress me, lore was quite cool behind the factions and the world. (also, its voice acted for yall that always skip homm walls of text), not that long but if you explore properly its a fine length -Maps themselves are cool as you can approach them differently, miss or uncover hidden ~side~ quests and secrets, meanwhile decisions on these maps actually have an impact on the outcome, there is strategy behind moves -Interesting mechanics of the game itself, mix from different games that feels right for this genre (hiding in forests, marching stances, neutrals actually making hideouts from abandoned cities etc.)-Battles themselves are engaging and def have a strategical element from positioning to active cards, cards have various cool effects that actually can turn battles outcomes, factions have unique gameplay both outside and in battle, only 3 factions but well distinguished plus a bunch of neutral factions to utilize from, also with their own quirksSome factions are stronger early game, others late game, good differences in play style and behaviour Music is well done and authenticYou can actually unlock a bunch of different heroes and gameplay additions through just playing the game, nice touch Now things that I wished were better or available:More rpg elements behind heroes and army, more cards, more map interactables Would make it more fluid to be able to move units leaderlessCities that can be managed and developed beyond just hiring units, trading and artifactsMore polish in terms of optimisation (tho nothing deal breaking) Altho voice acting is there, its hit or miss sometimes, I feel like they wanted to make this chill for this type of genre, not too loud and emotional but overdid it on some parts (also damn if you wanna put voice lines between every enemy turn, make it more fluid so it doesnt slow down the pace, but good for skip option). Tho I do like that enemies have something to say and things are vocally interactable across the board Some more UI elements for clarity like buffs to power etc. (to see changes in stats above max) Pretty good and exciting prospect for a first game (afaik)I hope devs expand on it and develop further, potential is there
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing for some time. Art is amazing! Never seen anything like this tbh. It's up there with the likes of Hades or Transistor.Gameplay is also good. Not a great fan of auto battling - would love to be able to control each unit myself but nontheless, the flow of everything is pretty smooth & slick.Story seems solid. Indulging and interesting for sure.If you know what you're doing, you'll overpower anyone in skirmish or multiplayer
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly huge potential, art style is stunning and I love the general themes of the game RTS/Cards/4x stuff all fun and games. Literally until chapter 2 in which you are introduced to the stealth mechanic which just removes all the fun and adds a ton of stress. You will just being saving and loading hoping you can salvage the mission to ultimately realise you cannot win and should restart for the 3rd time.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I've given this game a decent shot but it seems kind of shallow and tedious despite pretty graphics. When I completed Mission 3 I thought "nice, the game is finally starting to open up a bit and let you play around with the units" after a couple of on rails missions that were a bit of a chore to play through. Then immediately you're swept away from the first non-linear segment of the game to play a new faction.  You're dumped in a big map and told you have to go collect refugees from its 4 corners with your 2 and only 2 heroes, while enemies appear from outside the fog of war to attack your towns and reduce your already meagre resource income. The new faction's lower tier recruitable units are absolute dogwater, taking 2 upgrades applied to the tier 1 unit to become decent, you can only bring the better units into your army when your 2 and only 2 heroes are in the town and the tier 2 unit you need to upgrade to begin to get half decent units slow your army's painfully slow world map speed down. It goes without saying the game is an autobattler and combat grinds down your units while healing is slow and requires staying in towns unless you spend a significant chunk of your meagre income to provide 20% healing to an army. The game isn't crazy hard or anything, I'm pretty sure I could beat this level if I cared enough but it's just tiresome and there's better stuff out there to play. The campaign is only 8 missions long and out of the first 4 missions only mission 3 wasn't crap.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a great visual aesthetic and sound design; battle sounds are punchy and the music slaps. The grand strategy elements are toned down to complement the auto-battler aspect of the game which makes it a great entry point into this genre of game. The story and cutscenes are also visually pleasing and the medievel aesthetic combined with the apocalyptic presence of the Silence makes you feel immersed and part of a lived-in world. The game is easy to pick up and play due to the simple auto-battler and easy to navigate UI and that is by far the best part about it. There is still some complexity to the game with the unit tags and various other buffs and debuffs but it is never overwhelming. The multiplayer is also a cool addition although having all the races and classes for generals would be nice to have from the beginning.  Get this game if you want to play Total War without stressing out over the nitty-gritty and just have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderfully beautiful and brilliant game, Such a cool art style with very interesting gameplay. I am only half way through the campaign but can see Skirmish and Multiplayer right around the corner with all these interesting units you can unlock to make the playthrough different. Well done! _childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: What I like: The art of this game is gorgeous. I love to look at every single character illustration. The voice acting and narration is very good, a nice additional to the game.What I think the game lacks:1. Progression: Progression in this game feels quite barebone. You level up your heroes, you get to choose a few new ability cards or building cards, which does not feel rewarding, but predictable. Every hero progresses similar to each other, they also have level cap to them each campaign, so you can spend hours battling without getting stronger.  I would like to see more options to upgrade our heroes/ units, introducing stats upgrade and unique abilities, weapons, armours, artifact etc.2. Strategy: Despite being a turn-based strategy game, there are little strategy involved. I often find myself stocking up on units, spell cards and power my way through everything, which gets old really fast. The army formation doesn't provide new or creative ways to position your units, but the same old, melee in front, range in rear. No penalties/cost for using spell cards, which mean trying to spam spells as soon as the cooldown is over is your best bet.3 The world: The whole gameplay is basically who can captures the most towns and cities. There are little things to do besides that. The world feels empty with no points of interest. You just to travel from city to city on a straight line and pay zero attention to the pretty landscape around. Terrains also provides no strategic value to the whole battlefield. The pretty artstyle drew me in but as a strategy fan, I would say no to this game sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obviously a labour of love. Everything from the art style, card system, soundtrack, voice acting and mission design (as far as I can tell so far) has been done with great attention to detail and is very enjoyable. To be honest, I am not at a stage in my life where I can spend endless hours learning complex game mechanics, so I really like the "easy to learn, hard to master" approach that seems to have been implemented here. It's deceptively simple on the surface, but I found myself contemplating my next move and thinking about things I hadn't considered at the outset. The price is a little high, but otherwise I highly recommend it and look forward to seeing where they take it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty solid turn based strategy game. It feels a bit like a mix between Dominions and Heroes of Might and Magic, and if you like either of those two games, you'll probably like Songs of Silence too.Complexity-wise I think it's a bit more difficult than HoMaM, so at first it needs a bit more time to get into, but it's by far not as complex as Dominions.I, personally, was looking for a Dominions-like game that is a bit less of an investment (time-wise), and I'm happy to have found it in Songs of Silence.By the way, I'm playing on Linux, with Steam Play Proton, and the game is running great. I would expect it to run just as well on the Steam Deck (though I haven't tried it - I prefer the big screen for strategy games).
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I love it!The art style is simply fantastic, the campaign engaging and having a Total War style game without taking me hours to complete a single fight is awesome. I do not have as much time anymore to play as I had and Songs of Silence scratches my strategy itch just perfect! Thanks to the devs for this!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a fantasy 4X strategy game for PC and consoles with rich tactical gameplay, dynamic auto-battles, and a deep story. Inspired by art nouveau, it breathes new life into the classic strategy genre. With a detailed single-player campaign and various local and online modes, it promises hours of fun.The game impresses with its immersive soundtrack, unique visuals, and innovative mix of RTS and deckbuilding. The narrative-driven campaign is full of lore and interesting characters. Though it needs some polish, Songs of Silence’s visuals, sound, and gameplay make it a standout for strategy fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend this but with some caveats:The story leaves a lot to be desired. I started skipping scenes very quickly due to how long the characters take to speak their lines and lack of interest in the dumb decisions the characters were making. The theme and world building is really well done though so I still connected with the world despite skipping all the dialogue.During certain missions it feels like you need to very specific things to win, things you won't know to do on your first attempt. This was only for 2 campaign missions but they were not very fun and just felt out of place.During dialogue you can't do inputs like selecting or ordering characters. Sometimes the dialogue is just some dude saying he'll kill you but you gotta sit there for 5 seconds waiting for the dialogue box to go away which isn't bad once but in mission 8 there's dialogue at the start of each turn so you just keep sitting there waiting to be able do anything. (Dialogue boxes can't be skipped but speaking cutscenes can)It's an auto battler, it can only hold your attention for so long because the second to second gameplay is not super engaging. I enjoy the genre but after an hour or two I just need to do something else.Great art, fun gameplay most of the time and I like the character abilities/cards. Buy on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: YouTube Link:Songs of Silence is a new released, story-driven turn-based strategy game that blends auto-battler mechanics with exploration, military conquest, and rogue-lite progression. Offering a unique mix of familiar mechanics and deep strategy, the game challenges players to build kingdoms, manage resources, and develop heroes for a satisfying, tactical experience.The real-time battles, which incorporate auto-battler elements, add a layer of decision-making that requires careful card selection and timing. While initially, I found the lack of direct control over each squad of units a bit off-putting, the strategic depth of planning each move and predicting outcomes kept me engaged and invested in every match.The game features two main modes: Campaign and Skirmish. The Campaign mode offers a story-driven adventure, following Queen Lorelai as she journeys through a land consumed by darkness in search of a new home. Skirmish mode, on the other hand, offers single matches with customizable settings that can last for hours, giving players the freedom to test their strategic skills in a variety of scenarios.At its core, Songs of Silence is a classic good vs. evil tale, but its challenging mechanics, fast-paced battles, and tactical depth make it a standout for those who enjoy strategic gameplay. Though it may not be for everyone, those who embrace its complexities will find it a deeply rewarding and immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty hard to review this Game. It got me divided into loving it and hating it.Let's start with the good Things:- very nice and original Artstyle and Graphics - Finally a new Way of Strategy-Game with lots of new Ideas and Mechanics - A lot of Worldbulding and Story, espacially for a Strategy Game- Not basic Strategy but acutally Challenging for PlayersBut what are my issues with the game? First of all, you don't get much explanation about the rules of Combat or anything else. You have to figure out by yourself how everthing works in the game. That can a little frustrating when you get totally smashed and dont know why. At the Moment, theres is not that much content in the game. The campaign is not finished and the mutiplayer is pretty empty.But at conclusion despite all the Frustration i got from the Game, its worth it. But it still needs a lot of work before it can be called a complete Game. Don't Buy now, except you are a Hardcore Strategist. All others wait a little bit longer, when more content ist available.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, albeit buggy strategy game. So first off the good, I love the artstyle... and so far I like the story. It also has pretty great sound design and I've enjoyed the voice acting. Now I mentioned bugs? Well first of all, the most common and annoying one I've noticed is sometimes a unit will just stop doing anything mid combat. I've had a unit just go to a corner and stop there doing nothing until something gets to them in melee. If I'm lucky it's a flying unit and I can just reposition them to get them out of this weird stunlock but if not I have to wait for an enemy to run up and engage them, not ideal. And the second one, which I can't tell if it's a bug or just a poorly coded feature but... you can get ambushed by enemies that you end your turn next to. Like you'll be able to see them when you end your turn and yet somehow immediately after they can ambush you, which stuns you whole army for the first few seconds of a fight and can be a big deal if you're against an evenly matched group. There is an ambush system for hidden enemies but I'd argue if I can see the enemy when I end my turn right next to them they shouldn't be able to become hidden and ambush me.That being said I've enjoyed my time with the game so far, though I'm curious to see the replayability when I get through the story. I did see the "skirmish" mode but I haven't tried that yet! All in all it's not a greatly expensive game, so if it appeals to you I think it's worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Why am I paying $36.00 for a game that has locked content? And I don't mean content that will be released in the future, I mean factions, warlords, and units that are locked in skirmish and multiplayer mode until you find them in the campaign to unlock them. Or you can optionally play 54 games of skirmish to unlock them. I ALREADY PAID FOR THIS CONTENT, I don't need to jump through more hoops to have access to the game content.Also, the Encyclopedia is a pain is the @$$. Why do I need to go to the encyclopedia and individually manually click well over 300 entries of things I've already seen in game, to make the notifications go away.I also understand that the game is in early release, but the campaign is completely disjointed. The story is pretty bad, but the biggest problem is that at the beginning of every new chapter, YOU DELETE ALL THE UNITS IN MY ARMIES and then give me a generic bare bones army to rebuild all over again. This is why there feels like there is no continuity between chapters.The biggest deal breaker is that the Skirmish and Multiplayer mode content is locked and has to be unlocked through "achievements". This should not be, I already paid for the ENTIRE GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, the skirmishes give a lot of replayability. I wish the unlocks in the encylopedia were less repetitive. _childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: WOW! Not what I was expecting, but still WOW!Songs of Silence claims to be a strategy game and it is, in a way. Checking the screenshots, it reminded me on classics like HoMM. With a world map where you strategically move your armies, conquer cities and have tactical fights against enemies. But boy, was I wrong.Although you're still moving your armies across the land, you cannot recruit an arbitrary number of them, at least not in the campaign. This makes it hard to have a "support army", that just recruits units and transports them to your mai n armies. But that also makes a single army so much more valuable. And also defeating an enemy can be so much more costly, if you lose units (damaged units will recover over time if you're in a city).I like the way cities are getting conquered. Unlike other strategy games, you first have to lay siege on a city. Depending on the skills of your army and the defense of the city, this is either quick or quite long (the longest i had were 6 turns). And the longer the siege takes, the more likely it is that your army is getting attacked and has to retreat in order to reinforce. But if the siege is successful, you have to fight whatever unit was in garrison and/or the enemy army that is defending the city.And now to the - for me - most controversial part: the tactical fights. Unlike other games, your army fights by itself. In the beginning, you have little to no control over how a fight evolves. Although you can place your units on a tactical grid and yes, that already has an impact, it's far away from the tactical depth of a HoMM or AoW. That is, however, not necessarily bad.In HoMM, AoW or other games of that genre, I often used the auto-combat option when I knew I'll win anyways. The only fights I did by hand where the hard ones. To turn the tide of a fight, Songs of Silence gives you abilities that slowly load up and can be activated. The more experienced your army is, the more abilities you can learn and use. And with the abilities you can: direct parts of your army, resurrect troops, call reinforcements, ... There are a lot of options.So all in all, I'm enjoying the game. And yes, it's a strategy game. And it has a good story. And it's missing the micro management and I like that!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Because i like the concept of the Game i will leave a recommend for now but for the state (Contentwise) of the Early Access its quite a steep price and people that want more Content should probably stay away for now and wait till more released.I would say the current Story is around 5hours long maybe a bit more if you go for Side Missions and archivements.There are also more Archivements to unlock Heroes and Classes which can be quite tedious because its build like a Waterfall you dont unlock them all at once but rather one after another (You need to Unlock Hero/Class X (by winning 3x) and then you need to play to unlocky Hero Y and then play Hero Y to get Hero Z)Skirmishes are fun but the smaller maps are a little to quick for me because the building of your Kingdom falls short there, You can basically create a deathball and rush the enemy capital. While the Bigger Maps where right up my alley, You had a good mix of Realm building and fighting especially cause the neutral Units were alot stronger aswell, you had to think about your early game more and your resource management.I mainly play with AI and didnt try out the Multiplayer yet but i heard that the Turn system is not simultaneously and is not planned to be added except if player voice the need for it more. There are ways to limit the turn time by either 2 or 4 minutes each but in a 6 player match it can still then take up to 12-24minutes time per full Turn which might be to long for some people.I see alot of potential in the Game and hope the devs will continue with the great work and implement more Unit varity / Factions and maybe more Skirmish modes events (bigger focus on resource / realm management and of course balancing)

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite difficult to rate the game in its current version. Whilst the graphics are fantastic, the sound and music are great and the story isn't bad, the gameplay lacks depth and the user interface isn't well thought out at times.The first mission of the campaign is okay, but I don't know what the level designers were thinking with the second mission. I have to use the mouse to find out which places I can sneak into. If I click wrong or forget to play the scout card, I have to wait until my units are defeated.Unfortunately, I can't simply load the game if I already know that I've lost the battle, but have to wait for all the sometimes very lengthy animations.Using the cards in battle is nice, but gets boring relatively quickly because the heroes level up too slowly and I have to use the same cards over and over again. In addition, the melee units all feel the same, and the ranged units don't look much better. Overall, I can't intervene enough in the battle.The individual characteristics of the units and heroes are often unclear because they are not described in detail and it is sometimes impossible to understand why a battle is won or lost. In addition, I can't get any more information within the tooltips, but always have to open the unit screen again and even then I only get vague information about what the individual abilities actually do.I also hope that the city building gets fleshed out a a lot more, just upgrading cities feels really not enough for a 4x game in 2024.The price is clearly too high for the content currently on offer, EA version should really be cheaper when so much is missing.Nevertheless, I'll give it a thumbs up in the hope that the developers will improve the game soon.  I will change the review to "not recommend" if the next couple of updates don't improve on the points I mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice strategy game, you can either concentrate on strategy against AI, friends, or enjoy it along with a deep story in the campaign maps. Cards mechanics are really interesting and do make a huge difference: each hero has his own so you each match can be built different if you try all different heroes.Besides this graphics and music are stunning, very different from classic strategy games. _childDocuments_.review: I have under an hour but had to give this an initially positive review just based on the fact they are doing something different. Taking risks in the gaming industry is not easy. Too often studios look to emulate successful games rather than take a risk on trying something new. By mixing the 4X style world with AFK battles and card mechanics you get something that feels entirely new. BTW, there is no way to talk about this game without mentioning the art which is simply gorgeous. I would gladly buy a hardbound book featuring the art of this game. I will update this review as I go but at this point I would buy it just to support the developer for doing something this creative.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem that I highly recommend. The gameplay mechanics are intricately designed, rewarding every ounce of strategic thinking and planning, ensuring each move feels deeply meaningful and satisfying. The campaign draws me in quickly, and the accompanying story remains thrilling throughout. The races are diverse in design and offer a sense of familiarity that adds to the overall richness of the experience. I've been thoroughly engrossed in its campaign mode and the compelling narrative of the main hero.While the game may pose a challenge for novice players, its thoughtful tutorial system ensures a smooth learning curve by providing helpful prompts along the way. Additionally, although the abundance of information, including detailed card descriptions, may seem overwhelming to some, it enriches the experience for strategy veterans who relish in-depth gameplay. This aspect elevates the game, showcasing its potential to become a beloved choice among seasoned strategists seeking immersive strategic combat experiences.What truly sets this game apart is its immersive sound and music. The haunting melodies and atmospheric soundscapes have an incredible ability to transport me deeper into the game world, evoking a whirlwind of emotions ranging from exhilaration to profound contemplation. I was so impressed by the musical composition that I couldn't resist delving into the credits to discover the mastermind behind it.Additionally, the artwork is simply breath-taking. Every landscape, character, and structure is brought to life with meticulous attention to detail, immersing me fully in this vibrant world.

_childDocuments_.review: "Song of Silence" is a wonderful strategy game from Chimera Entertainment. The game impresses with its well-thought-out gameplay and captivating storyline. Visually, the game looks stunning. Beautiful backgrounds and stylish animation create a cozy atmosphere that invites players in. Thanks to the developers for the Ukrainian localization — it’s very important for us.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a beautifully crafted strategy game that strikes a balance between challenge and tranquility. Although it offers an array of multiplayer options, I find myself most drawn to the campaign, where I can immerse myself in its world while enjoying the fantastic soundtrack. The game has an almost cozy feel, blending Art Nouveau-inspired visuals with calming, atmospheric music that makes even the most intense moments feel oddly soothing.Despite this cozy veneer, the gameplay is still strategically demanding, rewarding careful planning and attention to detail. The storyline is well-written and engaging, it stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the other quality games in the genre. With the upcoming 1.0 release promising additional content, I’m excited to see where the game will go, even though I still have quite a journey ahead to complete the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing that made me want to support this game is the absolutely stunning visuals of it. This is not just a game this is a piece of art. For some there might be to much of explanations but then you are free to click away. And also revisiting the instructions directly from the map, I personally find very important. Also I like how within the rounds also the enemies do not necessarily move every round. this gives time to heal and think through the next moves. Until now I´d say it is a rather slow paced game, which for this specific game I like. It also gives you time to explore all those precious details, read through all the lore for the different characters and cities. Also the "small talk" of the characters here and there between the rounds is nice, as you get to know the heros and their backgrounds . I think if you are new to the genere and are appreciative of the artistry in both visuals and acoustic you´ll enjoy the game.  Sure might not be 100%  on point yet, but it is early access and I´m looking forward for it evolving.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game!The campaign made it easy to get into the gameplay and it is fun to follow the story, explore the maps and run into little sidequests.There are many mechanics to explore and using them to your advantage to turn the tides is very satisfying. It feels like every situation has a solution if one knows the synergies of unit abilities and hero skills well enough. Even when a very large enemy army is coming, it is possible to choose battles with advantages to wear it down slowly or even achieve a victory by exploiting its weak spots. Do not underestimate the power of good supply lines! :DOn top of that, there are a lot of different factions and heros, allowing for different play styles. They are unlocked by playing matches with different heros (check the quests in the encyclopedia!).I also really like the world. I hope we will see more content/games taking place in it!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I had about 30 hours in the demo and beta playtest in addition to my 4 hours of early access release.The game is really great in my opinion, but surely not for everyone.This game stands on its own. Its not like Heroes of Might and Magic, Civilisation or Total War. I saw many people comparing these. It has elements of all these games, but it puts them together in its own way.The campaign currently consists of five missions and it will teach you every relevant mechanic of the game.The missions will let you play different factions and leaders and there is some great mission variety.The narrative is rather engaging and has some very high quality voice acting through voiced actors and the narrator. It has (like the rest of the game) a lot of detail to it. For example when failing a mission, you will get a small outro-sequence, telling you what happened after you failed. I found this a great detail. Way better than just a screen wich tells you to reload.You will explore a map with different locations wich you can explore and conquer.Each location can be enhanceed with one building, where each building brings different strategic advantages.Some tough choices have to be made, because you cant build everything that you would like to.some thoughts to be considered are:Wich troop-lineup do I want to field into battle?How can I ensure a supply of fresh troops?How can I secure my spoils of war?When two armies meet, the battlescreen will open to fight an Auto-Battle. Because of this careful deployment of your troops is crucial. During battle you can influence it with a wide array of battlecards. All units have multiple abilities and will fill a specific niche in your army. What I noticed very happily is that the AI uses its battlecards very well too. A big improvement since the demo.In general it is very well thought out.Everything is just one or two clicks ahead. At first it can be a bit confusing that you do everything via playing cards. Recruit a troop? Play a card. Pillage a city? Play a card. Level up your hero? Play a card.But once you get the hang of it, it will become second nature.The game runs very well and is very polished for an early access game.- AI doesn't act the best on the world-map- the overall balancing needs more work (although I understand it is impossible to perfectly balance over 100 units)- as with other 4X games, the end of a match can be a bit anticlimactic- too many unit abilies wich do nothing (for example fear feels like it has no impact)- WHO PUT THIS PRICE TAG ON THE GAMEIf you like the art, you are into careful planning and like to build a lot of unique troop-lineups, I think the price is justified for the game.  With the campaign and skirmish matches, there is a lot of content. You can feel the love and detail that went into this game.

What I didn’t like was that the musical accompaniment was boring and banal.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a lot of potential very Songs of Conquest esque intro. Skirmish is a great game mode as well with a very different style of play then the campaign. Class options in that game mode bring a lot (that said it does not seem to work properly in its current 1.0 state as I have unlocked some classes that don't appear in the class selection).The gameplay loop is there and a very unique almost rts (maybe RTT is a better genre to place it as) auto battler wargame with card mechanics is fun with a lot of depth through a Master of Magic/Age of Wonders sized unit selection for their respective factions. I definitely am excited to see more units and classes added to the game over time.One thing I really would like to bring to attention is the voice acting is something notably good.Cons include while the manual is great, some explanations and in game dialogue are poor, or rather lack clarity, for instance during the tutorial campaign they say bring both armies to fight the capital of Frieland and that is simply not possible. One army can weaken the defenses while the other can actually bring them to pitched battle but to combine armies for a siege is impossible. This is also not really a design flaw but I imagine in a MP setting it can be exploitable to make nigh indestructible cities through this.Definitely a game to look forward to if you are not into early access games. Would not say it feels feature incomplete but it does feel like the whole picture does not feel there yet. Would recommend for strategy game lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style alot. And as a veteran Total War player and some other games, this game is hitting sweet spots. Alot can be added (more sandbox, factions, lore, missions etc,) and improved, but Developers seem to be on top of things, so let them cook. If it helps them, for what its worth some specific points of feedback. Maybe some or all are or will be adressed. -When, how and why my armies and units can heal should be more clear in the UI. I know it has to do with Supply, but even when I get that its not clear how much it heals. Like add a part on the healthbar showing what is healed next turn.- I want to compare units, with holding shift and hovering over another for instance. Why is tier 2 unit beter then tier 1? - Unit tooltips/more info on what they are and do. I can see "ward 1" or something, but I was not able to find out what it does very well. Perhaps the unit UI is a bit to fancy at the cost of clarity.- Building upgrade info. I could see that my settlements could be upgraded, but could not see very well (or at all, dont remember) how much my income there would go up. made it hard to determine how long earn back the investment would take (for instance).- The cards in battle user experience. For me, it was a bit much to take in per card. like 2 or 3 cards are about to become available, and then I have to hover one, read what it does again, read another on, and the third one. it takes to long and I have a timepressure feeling. I guess what could be nice is to have much clearer indications what the cards main role is. Blue = defensive, red = Attack etc, purple = spell. and for the retreat card...- hide the retreat card or take out of hand. Not sure about others, but for me in times of intens combat a few times i was close to play the retreat card. - Not sure if this is already looked at, I dont like how battles begin instantly and I quickly need to read the cards again. A pre battle screen where I can see the deck/hand and both our army positions. Not change those, I think its nice you have to preplan those.- Alot of the points above, for me, boil down to the UI being not clear and actionable enough. Its good looking, it has the right size etc. But just not the info I wish to see and places I expect to see it.Also died on the first attempt of the second mission lol, which was a bit too hard and unclear for my tastes, I beat it though. But I read you have already made several adjustments there. Appreciated and should prevent from people quiting early on in frustration (or out of shame).Keep it up, looking out for more!

_childDocuments_.review: The negative comments and votes are mostly wrong from people who have only played like 30 minutes.This game has depth, every unit has like 5 different stats that you can play arround, every hero has like 3 different abilities and its fun to build either well composed armys or just go full oxen storm flying across the whole map :DThe art is very beautiful, the voice acting is on point and the city building elements are interesting, but there need to be more stuff you can build without "wasting" a heros ability for it. _childDocuments_.review: The art, music, voice acting, and particularly the story, are all fantastic. The gameplay is serviceable, though it's lacking substance and could use some tweaking. There are times when the 4X and combat can drag on. The only agency players have during combat is to cast from a limited set of abilities every few seconds, usually as soon as any of them come off cooldown. This can make combat feel a bit boring and repetitive. Some of these abilities don't feel impactful, and other times they aren't at all necessary to determine the outcome of combat. As of the first patch, fast-forwarding though these fights is possible which helps alleviate these issues.I had a fairly good time playing through the four campaign missions available in early access. The start was slow, but I found the factions and lore compelling. The store-telling is particularly noteworthy. Dialogue is rich with world building and delivered with great voice-acting. Many discussions happen automatically after a fight and do not interrupt the player. The quality of the story is enough for me to return for the v1.0 full campaign release.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game. Have played through full 1st campaign mission on PC and 15 turns or so on Steamdeck.If you are a player that players Total War games, but autoresolves almost all the battles (in my timepoor mid-30s, this had become me increasingly) then this seems to offer scope to develop into a more streamlined, narrower scope version of this experience.- I think the user interface needs more attention - often was moving armies around when i wanted to drill down on their makeup etc- Not my game, but were i the devs I'd be focusing more attention on the campaign and less on skirmish/MP- I have no issue with the price, and would suggest that just because something is EA doesn't mean you should get a discount. Selling it to you at 25% of cost now, means they cant sell it to you at actual cost when they finish the game. I guess it was only mission 1 so maybe its toned down to ease people in, in 40+ turns of procrastinating the AI only attacked my settlements twice both times inside the first 15 turns or so, despite me leaving settlements with no garrisons in within vision range of their units.  in will update if this changes with further experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of HoMM and tactical strategy games, I find it frustrating that the game makes it so difficult to understand precisely what is happening during gameplay. Essential information is scattered across numerous tooltips, and there’s no combat log to review actions or outcomes.While I noticed that 'Making combat more readable' is listed on the roadmap, there aren’t any specifics about what that actually entails. It’s puzzling that improving combat readability wasn’t a priority before launch, especially for a tactical strategy game. Given what was offered in 1.0, I don’t feel confident that the game will eventually provide the information that I'm looking for.To make matters worse, the developers have stated that mod support isn’t planned, so there’s no hope that the modding community could step in to address these issues.I will say that the game is visually stunning, and the lore is genuinely intriguing. I really wanted to enjoy this game, but the same level of care and attention to detail wasn’t applied to the tactical combat. For me, that’s the most important aspect of a game like this, and it ultimately fell short.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game - lots of fun. The writing lays it on a bit thick with religious conflict, but you can wade through it. I wish the interface did a better job of streamlining game play - both by surfacing information more clearly and requiring fewer tedious clicks. The campaign is on-rails, with each chapter being a complete reset which kind of makes previous chapters feel pointless and disconnected (to the point I didn't finish). I understand how that makes balance and narrative easier - but it comes at too great a cost. But that is just feedback, I enjoyed playing and the people who made this game are awesome and I want to give them a high-five! Wonderful game, and I'm glad I took the time to play it. I am also playing during early access, so if you are in the future that is even more reason to give it a try because I have confidence that if the game is this good in early access then it will truly leave a mark at full release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been much of a fan of the "heroes of might and magic" style of game despite trying hard to get stuck in. I just seem to bounce off hard as some of the mechanics just never clicked for me.This game though, was like a glove. Having troops auto battle with your influence being card abilities subjective to the leading hero of your army and moving the battles to real time is a game changer. There is a pause button of you want to fiddle with spell ranges and such but i've never gone off 1x speed. This helps keep the flow of battle up although does decrease tactics just by inherent design of auto battling.The factions are distinct in how they play and what they're good at on the field. I like the settlement system even if it did take a bit of getting used to.All in all, I am exceptionally happy with this game and i think people who are into auto-battlers and/or grand strategy games should give it a go. I think if you are a HoMM gamer then you might find it too shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept of the game way more then the game itself. The campaign is kinda boring and restricted, no fun allowed. Artstyle is great but it comes in the way of visual clarity.Skirmish is by far the strongest part of the game but the gameplay-loop is tedious. You can't really push hard since you can only do one attack per army, this also leaves the army open for ambush. What this tend to do is force you to turtleup and wait for resources in order to build stronger tier units and then stomp the AI. There is also no diplomacy and a hard cap on the number of armies. The balance feels off, low/mid tier units can't do much and even if you try to swarm the foe the casualties will be too great and the replenish after battle is too slow. Something thats really lacking is buildings, you have the core upgrade and then one extra depending on what resource you want and thats it.Really wanted to like this game but i just can't.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to give a neutral review but at the current state I rather say "no".The idea and concept of this game is nice and the campaign makes some fun. Until mission 4 (more later).You have different factions and different heroes. You have units like archers, knights etc. And "stone paper scissor" like you have units which are better or worse against some enemies (e.g. units with spears do more damage against knights). Usual strategy as in other games.I had some fun until mission 4: The 3rd faction is just bad and feels useless. You can have 3-4 units more than the enemy and you get ez slain. In some fights, the enemy could cast multiple spells (cards I guess) while not even one card of my hand is ready.I played a random mission with bots and even there: You are gone around turn 3 or 4. Your hero has lvl 2, while the enemies are lvl 3-4. How? I mean: I fight 2 enemies with 4 units (hero + 3) and 2 units die.. So you have only your hero and 1 (dmaged) unit left.Another note about the 3rd faction: The first 2 can "just buy" units or summon units in your city. The 3rd faction requires to "level up" your units. You buy useless civilans for gold. to move them across the map to another city where you can uprage them to "better" units like soldiers (better in quotes because they're weak and die anyway). Just a few units can be bought direcly. This leads to waste a lot of movement point to level up your herop or heal the units in a city just to fill up your squad again..So in summary: The game has great potential. I like the style of graphics/paintings. I wonder how the campaign continues. The roadmap looks promising, but for now the balancing (espeically the 3rd faction) is definitively ruining this game for me. The different enemies are looking interesting, too.And I would love some improvements of the controlling of this game. As example: The game gives you the hint to adjust the formation of your units before a fight. It would be great (maybe as option) to change the format before the fight starts.For now (I know it is early access) I can't recommend it but it looks promising.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10It's a great game with lots of fun mechanics, but it's missing some things that would make it perfect. The story is above average with a world I'd like to know more about. They've done such a great job with laying foundation for a world that can multiple series to come. The game play is addictive, but frustrating at times. There are many instances later in the game where you are pin holed to play one way for the entire chapter. It moves the story along, but would be nice to have flexibility with strategy. Why it lost points:-Voice acting is hit or miss. The main characters are pretty good, but most of the side character acting is mediocre at best. That coupled with dialogue that seems extended and drawn out makes the game feel more tedious to listen to than entertaining. This is very apparent in later chapters where enemies have to wheeze between each...and...every...word.-Clarity of objective and tools. Early in the game the tool tips and descriptions are clear and perfect. As you get farther along, the utility of instance buildings and units become very unclear. This can lead you to play almost an hour or more before realizing the game wanted you to focus on a specific strategy revolving around a new mechanic given late game. That makes the game feel more repetitive and restrictive than challenging at times.-Lack of card diversity. The cards used for battle and city setup are essential to the strategy, but there aren't many unique cards per character. It would be nice to have more skill specific cards revolving around each character's strengths and weaknesses. As it is now, cards are mostly the same and unlocked at different character levels. It makes the gameplay dynamic in the beginning, but more dull near the end as each character has the same group of cards.Overall, amazing game especially for the price and time. I think with some minor tweaks it will be much more enjoyable to play the storyline. As far as replayability, I could see the multiplayer being fun, but the lack of card diversity make it less personal when it comes to strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're seeking a strategy game that prioritizes engaging gameplay over complex empire management, with simplified combat mechanics akin to a strategic rock-paper-scissors for unit placement, and is set in a beautifully rendered world rich with lore, then I recommend this game.However, if you're looking for a strategy game that delves into the intricacies of empire management, diplomacy, and resource gathering, this might not be the ideal game for you.I'm currently playing through the single-player campaign on the hardest difficulty, and it's providing a satisfying challenge. I've had to make numerous strategic decisions about unit composition and where I send my heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a Stylish and Polished combination of a few different strategy games.  Fusing a Total war map, Heroes of Might and Magic Hero/army management, and an Auto-battler/Card system, its juggling alot of things at once.  Draped over all of it is a fantastic Visual style with a unique fantasy aesthetic.  The current campaign offers eight missions, introducing a number of the games mechanics. I didn't find the writing anything exceptional, but the voice acting is done well and nothing stands out as too obnoxious.  There is a wide range of content to unlock for skirmish and multiplayer, with a huge range of hero classes and specialties.    I find that while the game lacks significant depth in any of the areas its exploring, it does a good enough job of tying it all together to warrant a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: There is something immensely charming about this game, something that makes it more than the sum of its parts. There is the strategic layer reminiscent of the Civilization and Endless series, there are the battles that are echoes of auto battlers, and a card ability crafting to make sure that you remain engaged during the battle. The artwork is evocative and beautiful, making every interaction feel premium in a wonderful way.You can dial up the difficulty for a greater challenge, or you can tune it down to enjoy the story in the campaign and take your time exploring the world and familiarizing yourself with the world and units. Overall it is a very enjoyable game and a very nice take on the genre!

_childDocuments_.review: First off the game is gorgeous so full marks there. Other then that there are some issues. This game's campaign reminded me of warcraft 3 which is a good thing but unfortunately instead of having a campaign for each faction you get 8 missions that blends a few together and the final missions are an unfun slog. MIddle of mission 8 on challegning and the concept is nice but the execution is aggravating. Combat is an autobattler which is nice so you dont have to do heavy micro.ProsArt - Top tier for this type of titleTurned Based - Personal preference since I like being able to stop at will without issue.Overworld leveling Card system - This is where you get some meaningful choice in your campaign choose between being able upgrade garbage tier units to elite cav or make any location a fortress that can heal and depost loot. Could of really done some cool stuff with this to increase replayability. Meh- Story. Standard endtimes affair. Not bad but not interesting- Units. While there are a host of units, there isnt really build diversity just ending up spamming the same high tier units and ignoring the rest. Not unusual in games like this but should be mentioned- Battle cards. Couldnt decide whether to put this in bad or not. The concept is good but they vary wildly in usefullness. When you level you can also pick battle cards which vary from useless to broken. The upgrades also vary from useless to meaningful. Ex Stun a group for 6 to 9 seconds with a shorter cd yay! vs units get +5 instead of +4. Stun duration is deadly. +1 is just technically an upgrade. Some of the Overworld upgrades are also hot garbage EX 80 resource to 75! You'd need to halve the 80 to 40 for even consideration but even then youll be swimming in resources at a certain point.Bad- AI. The AI is braindead. Im pretty sure they are just set to attack move. You can win 100% of the missions your allowed to build a base by making one hardpoint(fortress) and leaving a character there while the AI endlessly suicides into unwinnable battle vs a garrison+ your army. This leads tiresome battles while your other character goes to try to win the mission.- Mission structure. Outside of the base building missions there are the survive or do the thing missions. Incredibly aggravating. Most of the level up overworld cards are useless here making your limited levels pointless. Needlessly putting crucial units to survive in garrisons or in reserve. You are given two heroes on these missions you can only usefully use one so you have to stack the one hero and leave one sitting in a corner.Overall They game isnt bad. Its visually splendid and if they tweak the AI and combat there is real potential here. I enjoyed leveling the hero getting overworld cards that helped me jumpstart into the missions. It made the choice feel relevant. Unfortunately missions just devolved into make a fortress and watch AI suicide against it

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is fantastic, I think it has great potential to keep a series going. It's kinda like if Heroes of Might and Magic and Total War had a baby. I love it and its been a long time since I've played anything like those two.Here's my thoughts of the first 7 hours.- The soundtrack honestly is my top positive. I love it, it's a great mix of heroic and magical, I'm not a conductor by any stretch but they did a great job with the music.- Combat is good fun, love the use of cards etc but can be a bit repetitive and sometimes 'spammy'I wish there was a skirmish campaign with some RPG elements or even rogue-like as the card system can already potentially add that. I also wish there was an easier way to support your army 2v1 like in Total war, currently I believe you just retreat one army and attack with the other. However, that could just be user error or intentional by the devs. There's honestly just a good nostalgic vibe that I cant explain, but theres a demo so try it out! I wish more developers did this! what a great way to let people dip their toes before diving in (obviously can refund but still)

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence joins an incredible rooster of stylized War Games to drop recently; Songs of Conquest, Age of Wonders 4, Symphony of War, Unicorn Overlord  Graphics:Songs of Silence has an art direction that is easy on the eyes due to a ink and water color shader with vivid colors chosen by someone who understood color theory.I think Songs of Silence is the prettiest girl at the ball. Battles:The auto battles are beautiful to watch due to animation that looks better then Total War animations. Battles are engaging to watch due to fantastic hp/dmg pacing of random numbers. Best of all your given a hand of cards to play to turn the tide of the Auto Battle.   I think Songs of Silence has the best battles because its an auto battle that you can shove like a quarter machine. Overworld Map (4x portion):Closer to Unicorn overlord then Age of Wonders. Seems very simple but serves the purpose of filling out armies so you can get back into battle.  MusicSeems a bit over the top but its growing on me. StorySeems to take its milieu pretty seriously, I haven't played enough to say if its interesting or good. Difficultly:Seems to be very hard.Replay:Has a Campaign, has skirmish, has multiplayer, I would say there is a ton of game for the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great strategy game. Mixes in elements of deck building with TBS/RTS and Auto Battler aspects. Art style is really nice. Has an interesting single player story and good skirmish modes. The game also has RPG elements with levelling up your characters. You will have to make strategic choices when you level up for example do you pick a new card you can deploy in battle, or do you instead pick an economy card that will help you on the world map stage, or do you skip both of those and instead power up a card you already have in your deck. Overall, I'm really enjoying it. It feels unique and refreshing. I don't really like deck building games so this game actually impressed me. It gives me enough of the RPG and RTS elements that I like in games that I can get onboard with the deck building aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a refreshing and unique entry in the turn-based strategy genre. Its mix of tactical battles, faction variety, and immersive worldbuilding makes it stand out.The gameplay is easy to pick up but offers plenty of depth for those who love to strategize. Each faction feels distinct, and the blend of narrative and mechanics adds extra layers of engagement.Visually, it’s stunning, with an art style that’s both beautiful and atmospheric. The music perfectly complements the game’s tone, enhancing every moment.If you’re a fan of strategy games and want something that feels fresh but familiar, Songs of Silence is definitely worth your time
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game with fresh, in depth worldbuilding. Gameplay is fairly simple but is more focused on strategizing before fights than mid-fight management. A few bugs/instances of typos in descriptions, but genuinely has not impacted my experience much. Really just buy it for the art/lore/gameplay and the rest falls in place.
