_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a very beautiful game and it has immense potential to be taken to the next level with more content and features. Really enjoyed my time with it and I can see it becoming a very beautiful franchise for people to relax and roll out their imagination. As a game developer myself I'd love to see this game reach that potential and enhance its experience and I even offer my support if needed, as a Presentation | Senior UI Artist.I tried to compile a list of features, options and items that could add to the experience, from my play time with the game:1. Lighting: adding multiple types of light fixtures, maybe of different materials, medieval torches, candles, lanterns or procedural string lights that could be attached to pillars, fences, or gates2. Walls: Wooden beams textured, similar to outdoor cabins, possibility to have pergolas or just pillars stretching out on a patio, ability to build walls with the same looks and aesthetics as the walls (e.g. Tudor style, fully windowed walls that can be used in building something similar to a greenhouse3. Roofing: Maybe creating a sims like roof tool, Different textured roofs, like thatch, shingles, wood shake, clay tiles, turf. Ability to extend each end independently to another (one end could be hipped, one end could be gabled, also allowing a certain variation like a Jerkinhed end). Also decorations would be really cool: roosters, Northern weather vanes, rain gutters, bird nests.4. Doors: Doors with windows, more styles and materials: such as metal, rounded, windows on the sides, ability to set height or proportions manually.5. Windows: more style families, matched with doors, more control on the outcome, maybe a menu to pick the style, with the same ability to set height or width manually.6. Decorations: a menu just for this, even if the object is random, a predefined family of assets could really help. Either by size, type or by having a scatter tool method like the flowers but for rocks, pebbles, sand, grains, plowed fields, different types of grass for example or various objects, leaves or fruits under a tree, snow or ice on winter maps. 7. Floors: we need a tool that only does floors or terraces or walkways. Even if it's just pebbles, rocks or stone walkway, various styles can come in handy and have an automatic railing with various styles that can help a pergola look.8. Fencing: Various materials like metal, twigs, picket. Various gates to pick from with procedural resizing, mini borders that can act as fences(made of little rocks, or small trunks, hedges).9.  Other suggestions and improvements:- the ability to detect the type of item just by clicking it (having to continuously select items to delete them can be really finicky)- ability to hold shift for a perfectly straight wall, road or fence.,from point A to point B- ability to hide UI in photomode- remove size lock for buildings- add a duplicating, copying styles, items or paths tool. Like an eyedropper thing maybe- more types of trees, different shapes, accessories like swings or lights- add the option to place animals or animal items (chicken coops, cows, dog houses, birdhouses, bird baths), people and people doing various actions (plowing, gardening, cooking, tending to their house, painting, building something, with a simple looping animation)- add more type of terrain tools: being apple to create a hill instead of a rock formation, or creating a stone formation to begin with, a tool for flattening already existent default terrain- ability to add rocks in the environment, like the edge of a lake or a mountain - ability to add decorative boats or people fishing on water surfaces, maybe even fountains or waterfalls- adding fires: like fireplaces, camp fires, carriages with horse and fire next to it, tents - ability to rotate round buildings/towers: sometimes the pillars don't align with something you have under/top of them, a rotating tool for them too would be awesome- edge screen navigation where you go up by just having the cursor at the screen edge- decorated archways: with grapes, roses, flowers, various greenery like ivy- specific decorations and items: cathedral/castle types, beams, arches, shields, tower tips, clocks, monumental pillars, weapon assets like canons or trebuches, drawbridges, banners of various size and colors, armors10. Packs: to easily deliver most of these assets and improvements, I would suggest going with something like packs, delivered every certain time frame, even buyable if it helps the developers. You could really take this to the next level with various packs that include maps and new objects each with a different theme. Off the top of my head I'm already thinking about a few:- mountain pack, with cabins, firs, autumn weather or winter, chalet type of thing- medieval castles or cathedrals to address the goth fans- farmhouse pack, with animals, items and barns, maybe carriages or herds of sheep and cows- american frontier pioneers: wide plains with carriages, camps and cowboy items, desert and wild west context- seaside pack: with an island with sandy beaches surrounded by the sea, coconut trees, palms, tiki items- international packs: like Italian Tuscany, Burano - Venice, British Cottages, Japanese gardens and houses, French Provence, Swiss Chalet, Norse cabins with the aurora borealis at night, Indian or Arabic palaces, dutch tulip fields with windmills- licensed packs in the future maybe: like Lord of the Rings' the Shire or Rivendell, Harry Potter's Hogsmeade, Peter Pan's Wonderland, Narnia, Aladdin, various Pixar worlds.Hope to see this game grow even more and offer its players the world they always wanted to build their imagination's worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little sandbox game. It is simple and easy to get the hang of. It is a little limiting but not as limiting as you may think at the start. The more you play the more options you'll find, so be creative. It only starts being a little limiting when you start making bigger builds. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely builder game that at first appears overly simple without including instructions. But don't be deceived, discovering how the building elements can be used is a fundamental intent of the game and encourages creative experimentation. Uncovering the 'hidden' mechanics of the game is a joy and delight. The game has great potential for expansion without changing the basic mechanics too much; differing water levels, waterfalls, changing tree height and size might be a challenge. Other options would likely be readily achievable - choices of trees (conifers, fruit trees) or plants (vegetables), choices of building cladding (i.e. thatched roofs, log walls), choices of path paving, choices of walls (hedge rows). Maybe one day all of the above options will come true but for now it's an impressive gem. Nicely done.

_childDocuments_.review: Me as fan of TS4, Spore, House Flipper 1-2 and Townscaper, just couldn't get past it. My fastest purchase for all my 11 years in Steam (so much cool so I bought Cozy Contrasts Collection).Medieval architecture has never been so simple and meditative. Put blocks, squeeze and stretch them, attach to each other. It's almost the same as creating diaramas irl, just your crooked hands aren't spoiled nothing and get dirty in paint and epoxy. Just one thing is missing in Tiny Glade for me - copying similar configured objects or created by several pieces like it was in Spore, for example, to have similar towers in your castle or houses in town.One day I'll wait for Paralives, and then my casual soul will reach a peace.

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god this game is legitimately so good. I love the graphics, the sound, the general vibes this game gives off. It feels so cozy, and its just so enjoyable to play.My only "gripe" is the lack of things like copy-paste, being able to manually place props, etc etc. BUT besides those teeny tiny things, this game is legitimately so fun. I love taking photos of the things I've made, and being able to go FIRST PERSON is just incredible!Tldr; Game is incredible. If you love cozy, calm, quiet building games, this is for you. If you're looking for complete control over your stuff, that doesn't exist here (unfortunately or fortunately depending on your perspective), but you do still have a lot of control.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most relaxing game ever made, after Placid Plastic Duck SimThere are a fair few features I'd like to see, like multi-building selection, ability to create your own holes in walls and buildings, more building decorations, bridge modules separate to other building types, much higher building limit for both terrain manipulation and building height, bigger spaces to build, and a bunch more customisation options for decorations, rather than the game randomly deciding where to put them.I get that this isn't supposed to be in depth in any way, but you get a certain point when building and think "argh I wish I could do that one thing!"
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, and this is very much 'more of the same'. A very relaxing and zen game, no stress, no pressures, no resource management. Just soothing music, easy to build structures and sheep. And ducks too!I do hope that more building options will come in time, i.e. bridges, but that's just me being greedy :DIt is a fantastic way to wind down in an evening after a busy day and let my imagination build a fantasy styled house, which I can then use the photo tools to get some really great shots of.*EDIT* So I've found how to create bridges of sorts, it's not perfect as you can't create arches [or I've not stumbled across this yet], but it does allow for a lot more interesting building options.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is the most satisfying art game you could ever play, it manages to blend in all the details to everything you place and you have absolute full control to how you want to design your landscape. The devs also made sure to add in a Daily Theme mode to give you some inspiration on what you want to build.Very chill and laid-back game, hopefully there will be more content to fill out on what you can really do.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love it. Seriously. Your boundaries are that of your imagination. Potentially, you can create anything you so desire - in reference to the buildings and landscape. No missions to complete. No enemies to fight. No timer. It's just you and your imagination. It's relaxing, and takes you into another world created by your mind - even for just a little bit. Want a cottage? Go for it.  Want Dracula's castle? Try and create that too. Just create what your heart desires. I wholeheartedly recommend this little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It has finally happened. A single player, intuitive, adaptive movement, non-pay-to-win, non-resource gathering game that has basic building blocks are crafted into everything from Toy Spiders to Castles from Hamlets to City Skyscrapers.I remember when another game like this was released. Blocks that you could pick up and move. It was such a success. But that game does not even come close to what can be created in Tiny Glade.Tiny Glade is anything but tiny. It is simply astounding in what it allows a player to create. There is no rush. No time limits. No goals. It is relaxing and your imagination determines what you build. Your terrarium as you decide what to put and where items should be placed. There are daily themes. And week-long themes around holidays.Oh, how I have longed for this kind of game within the myriad of crappy horror games, jRPGs, MMOs, first person shooters, servers that lag, rage quitters and games where people need to be in the top 10 to get better items. Mahalo to the Creators and Developers of Tiny Glade: You have created a masterpiece of item manipulation.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade: A Serene Masterpiece in the World of Building Games!Tiny Glade is a gem of a building game that effortlessly merges creativity, relaxation, and exploration. From the moment I started, I was captivated by the tranquility and charm of its design. Every aspect of the game radiates calmness—from the gentle soundtrack to the smooth, intuitive mechanics. It truly is a game where you can lose yourself in the beauty of creating, and the learning curve is both enjoyable and rewarding.What stands out most for me is the freedom you have to manipulate the terrain. Whether you're creating a forest village or a sprawling castle, the sheer variety of paths and options makes every session feel fresh. There's always something new to discover, and the way the game encourages creativity without pressure is wonderful. The ability to shape the land around your builds brings a whole new dimension to the genre, and I'm constantly amazed by how immersive it feels to watch my creations come to life. The daily themes are also soooo good at fostering creativity and ideas!Another big highlight is the Tiny Glade community. They're warm, supportive, and always eager to share ideas, tips, and creations. As someone still learning the ropes, it's been such a positive experience to be a part of this community. I feel welcomed at every turn, which only adds to the enjoyment of the game.Of course, like any game, there's always room for improvement. While I love the flexibility in building, I do wish there were a copy-paste feature for structures—this would streamline the process and make large-scale creations a bit easier to manage. Additionally, deleting parts of a structure can sometimes affect multiple layers, which can be frustrating when you're trying to refine the details of your design. Despite these minor limitations, the experience remains unparalleled.In all, Tiny Glade is a must-play. The calming atmosphere, limitless creativity, and supportive community make it the best building game I've ever played. I can't wait to see how the game evolves as I continue to explore its endless possibilities.Sending love!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to write a review for a game that is so simple. But that's the beauty of it- the game is simple in scope; that is, there is no grind, no unlockables, no timeframe. You are free to design your own towns and villages as you see fit. You are given all the tools, and it is your job to lean how they work, how they interact, and how to utilize them to your full effect.A time waster, in the best way possible. Grab a hot chocolate, wrap up in a blanket, and let your imagination take the lead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: If you saw the demo of the game, you've seen everything the game has to offer. I was expecting this game to be a very simple experience, but I assumed we would have a little more to work with than just the demo. Even as I write this, the store page is showing me a video of someone building a gargantuan castle. At least from what I can tell, that's not actually possible. The map areas are too small to do huge builds like cities or large castles.The game could use tooltips on the various buttons as well. I get that they probably want us to discover things, but it's hard to talk about the game and understand the basics when nothing is labelled if you hover over it.I'd also kind of like to see the ability to draw on walls/floors. When I initially saw the paintbrush icon, I got excited that I could maybe paint on walls like I was drawing with a crayon or something. Nope. It just lets you change the material that the buildings are made out of.The game feels like it's in early access and for the full price, I'm not sure I can recommend it unless you watched the demo and you really think what you saw there was worth the price. I hope more gets added to this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Downloaded the game 2 days ago and am still obsessed! I already clocked 9 hours and it doesn't feel like that at all. I really love the cosy vibes, no pressure from anything - it's doing exactly what I had wanted from Sims 4 Cottage Life. Just all the time for building the most beautiful scenes without any hassle. The tools just easily match up so things look even despite building the wonkiest houses, if that's what you're going for. And they are still adding features! I really hope for some Halloween inspired additions, like mushrooms, tree stumps and gravestones. That would be amazing.The patches are "tiny" but honestly big enough to build an entire village with a lake. And each map is automatically saved, so you can easily jump around between builds. And there's a daily surprise map for extra inspiration.Definitely recommend for all build lovers.

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for a long time (I accidentally saw it on TikTok and immediately added it to my wishlist). I spent some time with the demo and eagerly awaited the full version release and I was not disappointed. The graphics create a beautiful, fairy-tale atmosphere. You can truly relax with this game, there are no tasks or goals, just you and your imagination. The available options allow you to build both fantastic, imaginative lands and more realistic medieval buildings.While there are a few things I feel are missing, considering the game is only a few days old, I’m still very satisfied. Overall, I recommend it to anyone who wants to relax, escape everyday stress, and enjoy building beautiful cities. The photo mode is a lot of fun. You can walk around your buildings, position the camera however you want, and take stunning photos.I hope to see some updates in the future, including:• The addition of wooden textures for buildings (currently, there are only stone, brick, and plastered walls). I would love to see nice board paneling and some mossy old planks for a witch hut.• A copy/paste option! to save time from repeating the same actions and be able to focus more on exploring new ideas.• More variety in bridges (such as smaller hanging rope bridges, drawbridges, etc.).• Different types of lighting (torches, garlands, bonfires, etc.) to add even more magic to my creations.• More general environmental decorations, not only randomized seeds from doors and windows.• The ability to place water on higher floors (ideally, allowing you to create waterfalls ❤).• More fun elements to fill up the water – like boats, driftwood, etc.• A direct element for making easy stairs, as creating them now is quite tedious 😃.• More flexibility in breaking elements into smaller fragments—for example, creating roofs and walls with holes, so you can achieve that old, crumbling building vibe and set walkable pathways through and inside them.I will definitely be spending a lot of time with this game and am excited to follow its development.To the devs, thank you very much, and I wish you all the best with the game’s success!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Gamifying creativity the cozy way.When I first started playing the Tiny Glade demo I felt constricted by the small area I got to build in, but still had an amazing time experimenting with build styles and getting to know the tools. Even in the demo, I felt this game was right up my alley.Then, on release day, I felt paralyzed by the size of the full sized glades - it took me some time to even get started on my first project. Once I got the ball rolling, I found myself in a flow state of pure creative bliss. The game has taken me by storm, and I can't say anything bad about its simplicity in design, art style or polish. However, I do have some suggestions for the devs when it comes to tools and features to consider adding:1: Placeable furniture/prop nodes that you can “reroll” like you can with windows. As an example, placing a prop on a grass field, then clicking on it to get a picnic table. Moving it to the beach could turn it into a fishing chair with a rod resting against it. Placing it on the wall of a building could make it into windmill sails.2: A clone shape/size tool. When building symmetrical buildings that aren't as small or large as you can get them, it's difficult to get the shapes to be the same dimensions. I wouldn't like to be able to clone entire builds, but one shape at a time seems like it would be helpful.3: A mass color tool. Marking several windows or doors and setting their color all at once would be a time saver.4: The ability to move/freeze the animals (and maybe future NPCs) to set up your photos.5: A slider for leaves/snow.To conclude my review, here's my score: 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 3 hours, am hooked. This is going to be perfect for those days where I want to be creative but have no braincells. Proper cosy/relaxing gaming.I've barely scratched the surface of the assets but first thing I noticed is how INTELLIGENT the mechanics are; there are some very good Quality of Life features, just little things like flags close together create bunting, putting a 'window' on a flat castle roof will create a trap door, climbing ivory and other details will adjust around windows and doors as you move them, putting flowers on top of water will create lily pads etc. There are too many examples for me to name and I'm still finding more. Honestly if you told me the game engine was AI I'd believe you. If a small indi studio can craft this level of intelligent/responsive design then really it should be bog standard in the industry at AAA level. I hope a lot of studios take inspiration from what Pounce Light has done here for future sandbox games as this makes many existing sandbox/city building games now look very restricted in what you can accomplish.I think the daily challenge feature is a really nice touch too. There's no pressure but it's a great place to start if you're stuck for ideas.Having said that, the game isn't perfect. There are a few things I'd love to see;- People/more animals roaming around. The sheep and ducks etc are very cute but creations do feel like they're missing a little spark of life. Some townspeople roaming around idly would add a lot to the environment.- More asset choices. Arguably I may not have found everything yet but things like farm fields, flower variations, bridges and placement of small decorative objects outside of the ones that randomly spawn with doors/windows would allow a lot of variability.- More building styles. To be fair the existing building blocks are pretty customisable you could probably make anything if you tried hard enough, but it would be nice to have more to work with so you could create for example a Japanese style diorama etc. - More maps. You have a few to choose from but more variety is never a bad thing! Especially if we can get some larger ones too to spread out a bit more.For £10 this felt like a bargain, going to be a nice way to chill out and pass the time now and again!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Tiny Glade because it offers such a cosy, slow-paced (or whatever your pace is), creative gameplay - it is a great choice for showing your imagination and de-stressing. No time limit for anything, and you are done when you feel so. I can very much see this game becoming a popular choice among every group of people. I am not particularly creative, which is why I appreciate daily "challenges" to get me started and explore it even more. I love finding little Easter eggs, and this game brings me just that, + it gives me the chance to explore what I can make work.The art style is really beautiful, honestly best word to describe the game is cosy. I would love to see more options added throughout time. I would love to see: - more animals- more flower and tree choices- ability to make farmland- ability to create an actual bridge (curved bridges, please? :D)I am sure I will think of some more things, but that is it for now, after about an hour of gameplay :)I also wanted to add that the game is made by two developers, who made their own engine using different technology, as it is so custom made. The cons can be that it doesn't offer too many variations (yet) of fences or walls, landscaping. But you can still explore what you can do with it, and I have seen amazing creations by now (someone literally made Saurons tower, Disney castle, a whole city). _childDocuments_.review: Have been involved in playtesting this game since last year. Got in excess of 300 hours in it. I obviously love the game but here's the "Townscaper warning":If you're on the edge about getting the game, take seriously what it says about "doodling" and "sandbox." Much the same way that I tell anybody interested in Townscaper to take it seriously when it says "more a toy than a game."The game's not going to give you any directions. It's like Minecraft stuck in Creative mode. If you have an idea and you're willing to put the creative effort into making it a reality with the tools you have, great! For a lot of things the procedural engine will allow for creative solutions to be found. If you want to place down a house and immediately recognize "Ah yes, Tavern." then you might be out of luck. It's up to you to make that building look recognizable as a tavern, however you might try to accomplish that. Again - Doodling. It's free-form. I can turn on Tiny Glade, click all the buttons, place all the objects, go "That's like a dozen things at most!" and turn it off again. The same way that I can pick up a pen, put it to a page, draw three squares and a triangle and get bored. You really have to bring the motivation to be creative yourself.The same thing that makes the game relaxing and cozy and stress-free for some, make it boring, limited and uninteresting to others.Castle doodling sandbox with no management of any kind. I can't recommend enough that you take those words seriously.Lovely devs, lovely game, game is so much more versatile than it seems! I've spent 300 hours in it throughout the playtest and the demo. If you're happy doodling and/or learn to think outside the box, you can do a lot more than the basic building blocks let on. If you need some sort of motivator that gives you a *reason* to build or if you want the convenience of a city builder with prefab buildings that are instantly recognizable, Tiny Glade won't be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively simple yet in depth no strings attached builders need to be more of a thing, then they are. Look I have nothing against resource management building games but they are always exceptionally good at doing one thing, limit your building creativity, as practicality has to take priority over just shear creative fun.I stumbled on this by pure chance and I am glad fate willed the encounter to happen. The game isn't flawless but criticism I'll be leveling against it are very minor and really do nothing to undermine it. However lets start with the good points. First off, the lack of resource management and the freedom to explore creative building free of the shackles of resource limitations makes for a very relaxing and engaging gaming experience. Next the cute whimsical art direction of the game, further adds to its charm and sense of tranquility. Lastly the variety of building options and the ways you can blend them really create a vast amount of creative potential for users to explore and capitalize on.Moving on to the criticism. The game lacks an sort of good in game guide or tutorial to help players understand how to use the tools fully. Now this doesn't undermine the gameplay much since there is an "undo" feature so any missteps or need to do some trial and error aren't overly problematic. Still I don't think a user should have to resort to such crude methods to try and figure out what everything does fully. Hours later and I'm still stumbling on to features I wish I'd known where a thing so I could have made use of them earlier. Next the game has no manual save feature, which I don't like, as leaving things up to auto save seems needlessly risky especially when you're working on on something for hours. Furthermore the game is not very clear at when the auto save is even saving, it tells you when you want to exit that the session will be saved but in between that and when you start its anyone's guess when its actually saving and I can't help but worry that if it only ever auto saves on a shutdown that a single 2 second rolling blackout could undo hours or work just like that, if the game gets closed unconventionally. Lastly this is more of a personal suggestion rather then a criticism, larger build areas would be nice. I think "Tiny" is being taken too literally when it really a measurement of comparison (eg: a pebble is tiny in comparison to a boulder but its massive in comparison to a grain of sand). I'm not asking to be given an build area big enough to build a mega-city spaning 100s of square kilometers. A glade itself is simply just an opening within a forest, its size is vague at best. Anyway just  putting it out there that having a larger build area would really be icing on the cake.To wrap things up I will say with out question that I highly recommend this game and mentioned points of criticism really do not rob the game of the amount of creativity fueled enjoyment it has to offer and the asking price is fair given the amount of creative potential it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game really excited and wanting to like it, but especially for $15, I'm coming away feeling quite disappointed. Pros:- The sheep are very cute- The art style is very charming- It does allow you to build things quite quickly, and I found the controls fairly easy to adapt to.Cons: - There is very, very little variety. If you want to build a cozy cottage or an Arthurian-esque castle, great. If you want to explore anything outside that aesthetic, you're out of luck. - The number of details you can place yourself are limited to flowers, lights and flags. There are other detail items the game will randomly generate in, but you can't place those things yourself. - There's some extremely frustrating limits on how much you can customize things. If you don't like the piece of laundry the game generated outside your window, that's just too bad. If you want a banner with a specific design on it, you just have to keep placing and unplacing it until you randomly get the one you want. You have the control to change colors. That's it.- You cannot customize interiors. At all. The game will allow you to place doors which you can enter via camera mode, only to be met with the depressing, unfinished and unfinishable inside of your otherwise delightful build. If I'm going to be completely unable to do anything interesting with the insides of my buildings, then please don't give me the false hope of being able to enter them. If this was a $5 or $10 dollar game, I would be like, "you know what, fair enough. whatever." But for $15, I'm left feeling like I wasted a few bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very relaxing and simple. You can create anything from small shacks, to serene villages, as well as massive castles. _childDocuments_.review: So far I love this game. The graphics and lighting are really calming and so is the music. Every time I play it, I find out a new way to create. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I think the simplest thing I can say about Tiny Glade is that it gives you exactly what you paid for. It's just... exactly what it says on the tin - a delightful and creative experience making cozy little environments.But there's more I want to say, because (much like when I'm playing the game) I keep realizing that I'm not quite done yet.Firstly, this game is beautiful and yet runs really, really well. My wife's laptop, not a "gaming machine" by any means, can still run it pretty well. On my computer, it runs near-flawlessly. And this is all directly post-release, I should add - they've been adding fixes consistently since then, and it already ran so well!Secondly, I feel like something has to be said about the massive success of this game as a tool for fostering creativity. I've played a lot of simulator/builder sort of games, and yet never before have I felt this free in my creative goals. I've made four complete glades so far - a small village with a wizard's tower, a large city with an imperial palace, a cozy farmstead in the snowy countryside, and a spooky mansion in a dark forest. And I'm completely satisfied with all four, because they all turned out exactly like I wanted them to.This game is delightful and I'm delighted whenever I play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly cannot recommend this game. The design options are incredibly limited and it still feels like it's an early access game. You get two types of windows (which have doors attached) or a third door type available only by putting a path under it. You can't put decor down yourself, it is attached to the windows. So if you wanted to put a random sign? Nah, it has to be close to a wall. You do get lanterns and flags, but it's just not enough. There's a trick where you can make the house flat, put a trap to generate decor, then put another flat house over it and try to make it a courtyard, but again that's really limiting. Everything is tied to the walls or the windows so everything you make is just going to be a generic medieval village or town. There's some impressive castles, but again it's really limiting. You can't even change the light of the windows, so if you want something dark and spooky with purple lights (like the lanterns)? You can't change the bright yellow light. This game still feels like it's in early access. Full release should have had new building types, more window types, and an option to put down decor yourself. I know that it's about the "procedural effect" but it's just frustrating and limiting for no reason. By the way, you have to play gacha with the decor and just click on the windows till you get something you like - you can't control what it gives you. So if you use the square window, it'll change the window AND the decor near it. At the very least just give me a "decor" button and let me cycle that separate from the window. You can't even make a waterfall! The vegetation brush is just bushes. You get the same trees according to the map and you can't even put down logs. It's a good game and it can be fun, but it's just limiting for no reason and IMO not worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for calm and relaxing building! Very laid back and easy to navigate, super cute graphics! Could use some more variety for certain aspects in my opinion, like rotating build items and being able to move doors\windows to a more specific area. But the free-form build style also creates an easygoing feel to the game! Super cute and cozy! (Pet the sheep!!!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I love how easy it is to make something feel and look cozy and warm, I like how things connect together and procedurally generate props and clothes and all those kind of things BUT, I just feel the game is missing somethings that'd make it alot better...- The game is missing some sort of "open world" type level, all the levels are small enclosed areas where I have to make all the terrain myself which I don't want at all, the challenge of building around the terrain you're given is what i really wanted in this game I want to build a viking village around a lake, a castle along a coastal area or a farm village around a stream but you can't you're limited to this tiny little flat area, it's like if Minecraft was only superflat, it'd suck.- Building sizes is something I wish was more custom, currently just rectangles that i can make bigger/smaller nothing "abnormal" without faffing about adding more buildings to the current one, maybe a sims like mode where you can pull and push walls however you like making them angled differently at different lengths.- Small details is something this game does but doesn't do that well, I enjoy all the little procedural bits that spawn around but I wanna place them myself, I want the streets to have carts, tables, chairs, etc.. not just be an emtpy dirt path.- I think the game is also lacking different textures, the path is just dirt and that's it.. no cobbled paths, gravel roads, tiles, wooden planks its just dirt. This aswell as being able to place farmland areas or hay/mud areas for animals to make it all feel more alive and lived.- Foliage is almost a non existent thing, I really wish there was more to it but that's it, there is one type of tree and a sparkly magical looking plants you can place and that's it, no twisting ivy on the walls (that's placeable by the player), no bushes or flowers and no rocks or stones or even short grass or wheat fields, hopefully it's added and expanded in the future.- The different colour swatches is also a feature that's lacking no wooden buildings/roofs, only a few brick colours and not having a way to make a building look more worn or aged is something I'd love to see added.Overall I like this game and recommend it but I'd also say wait a bit to see where the game goes as I think it can be alot better than it currently is, after you have build a cute little area it feels kinda dead, no life other than the sheep or ducks and no signs of life either, nothing in the streets or fields, nothing growing or moving (other than chimneys) I just wish the game felt more alive :3Oh and little wooden bridges that spawn when i drag a path over some water would be nice

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely, 100%, highly, omega, super duper, 3 times over, chocolate milk with whipped cream and a strawberry on top recommended!, theres a daily "map" so to say that gives you a theme and a prebuild sample which you can work off,  heres one for example (20 min simple build) in which you can see some things that are possible, but believe me when i say, i am VERY smoothbrain, theres so much you can do, and im only scratching the surfacethings id love to see added though, are L, XL, XXL map sizes, being able to just drown yourself in a single project for months on end would feel so cool, another thing id love to see is a random doodad button, where based on ground type you get doodads, grass and sand will give you haybales, farm equipment or things like that, while if you put it on bricks, youd get blacksmith tools, stone benches, ect ect, clicking next to a sand road will give you wood benches and maybe some other thingsthese are the only things that i can think off that id love to see added, there is nothing bad about this, i honestly cant think of anything, just dont go expecting unlockables, achievements, objectives, managementits just point and clock, and design something from scratch (as you can see in the video, i have another one thats meant to be a towncentre, the video is called glitch in the matrix to give you another example of whats possible)hope this helps you all, if you want to chill, relax, just sit back and let your brain wonder off, this is something youll absolutely love!, no handholding either, experiment to learn more of whats possible, though the big cathedrals on youtube do make me wonder, how? _childDocuments_.review: What can I say that others haven't already? Not much. This game is the closest I've ever seen come to perfection in only days after its initial release (and I have hundreds of games to compare it to). The concept is simple and it is extremely difficult to build something that isn't beautiful. Every setting is as gorgeous as the next and the random starting points are a really nice touch (from ruins to basic buildings and even a central town square here and there). We get it on the TV screen so we can 'ooohh' and 'aaaaahh' at each others' Tiny Glades (especially at sunset when all the lanterns and windows begin to glow). _childDocuments_.review: This game is perfection. If you prefer games that give you peace, this is the one. It's so beautiful, and simple in the most perfect way. _childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a breath of fresh air in the world of gaming. If you’re looking for a relaxing, no-stress experience, this whimsical diorama builder is an absolute gem. 🏰🌿The gridless building feels incredibly organic, allowing you to doodle cozy cottages, enchanting castles, and charming ruins with ease. It’s like watching your imagination come to life as the game fills in the details of your creation with its beautiful procedural touches. Every glade feels like a peaceful sanctuary, and with no management, combat, or objectives, you can simply lose yourself in the creative flow.The atmosphere is wonderfully cozy, and the sense of calm that comes from crafting your own little world is unmatched. It's a perfect escape from the fast-paced nature of most games. Highly recommend it for anyone looking for a relaxing, creative outlet. ✨If you're a fan of building games or just need a peaceful break, Tiny Glade is a must-play!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eagerly awaiting the full release of Tiny Glade, and I’m happy to say it doesn’t disappoint. While I wouldn't necessarily describe it as a traditional game, it shines as a creative tool—a calm, soothing experience where you can build to your heart’s content, whether it's a castle or a quaint village.For storytellers who don't need the complexity of DnD map makers but still want to visually convey their ideas, Tiny Glade is a perfect solution. The simplicity and ease make it ideal for sharing the scenes playing out in your mind without the hassle of more in-depth tools.The music is gentle and relaxing, setting the perfect tone. Being able to interact with the cute little sheep and ducks adds a delightful charm to the experience.One of my favorite aspects is the outdoor focus. If I want to design interiors, there are plenty of other programs that cater to that. But in Tiny Glade, you can play with minimal placement restrictions—there’s no grid, and objects can clip into each other, often resulting in fun, unexpected shapes. Experimentation is encouraged!The screenshot modes are a blast too—having a first-person mode was an unexpected but welcome feature.That said, there are areas where I hope to see improvements, and I really hope the devs continue expanding on Tiny Glade, even if it's through DLCs. For what’s offered, I think the price is very fair.- A copy and paste tool is sorely needed. There have been multiple times where I needed to recreate the same-sized building and had to fiddle around.- Stacked buildings should snap or "group" together better. When I adjust terrain later, only the ground-level buildings move with the terrain, leaving the rest in disarray.- A dedicated stair tool would be a game-changer. Right now, building stairs between different levels is tricky and frustrating.- Building area size feels restrictive. I understand the limitations may be there to accommodate lower-spec computers, but even when trying to scale down my castles, the space feels too small. I get that this goes against the “tiny” in Tiny Glade, but an option for larger building areas would be appreciated.- While the lack of a grid is freeing, a toggleable grid would be nice for us perfectionists who want precision when needed.- Round windows and resizable window options. While building a church, I found the largest window sizes weren’t quite enough. Having the ability to resize or add larger windows (maybe even stained glass) would be amazing.- More textures—especially wooden and small-brick wall options. Being able to add custom textures would be a fantastic addition.- A cobblestone texture for paths feels like a missing piece.- Glass roofs or skylights would be a beautiful touch for certain builds.- More variety in trees and flowers, particularly evergreen trees like pines.- While I’ve seen people request more furniture, I think the focus of the base game should remain outdoors. That said, a big bell to add to church or castle builds would be a nice touch.- Fairy lights and hanging lanterns would add a lot to the atmosphere—similar to the creative use of flags and bunting we already have.- Additional environments, like a beach or island-themed area, would be a lovely expansion.Overall, Tiny Glade is a delightful and versatile creative tool with huge potential. I truly hope the developers keep building on this foundation. I wish more "building tools" on Steam worked as intuitively as this one. If you're someone who loves to create without being bogged down by limitations, I highly recommend Tiny Glade.

The style of Tiny Glade is gorgeous, the controls are intuitive, the camera mode is extremely well made, the features that exist currently provide multiple use cases for making structures. This is one of the few games where I kept music on. Also, I feel as though the price is reasonable for the creative potential. Oddly, the game I can relate this game to the most is a hybrid of minecraft and townscaper.Feedback for the game (to be updated as I play more):  Could you possibly add a function to change the colour of the water (e.g: different shades of blue, green), provide another form of lighting apart from the lantern, a grouping function and a copy/paste feature so that something that has a certain style can be repeated easier.Additionally, make a performance mode so that it could possibly be run on older hardware as well (unsure how viable this is). Other general suggestions include: increasing the height limit for ordinary structures without it 'floating' above the ground, different sized building areas (maybe customisation between a set range), trapezoid building structures, railway lines, tree size slider and possibly a way to dig into the ground, similar to planet coaster or something.I would highly recommend for anyone who wants a relaxing game to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible building experience.Even if you're not very good at building, the system itself more than makes up for it, making even a single box placed down in a field look charming and alive. The procedural generation is an AMAZING technical achievement. For such a complex building systems, the low number of bugs is honestly shockingly. I was predicting the system to be a bit of a mess, but it holds up very well. I cannot stress enough what an amazing job the devs have done to get what seems like a deceptively simple game working so well. Building is easy and rewarding and the end result is a ton of fun.There's no 'point' except to build (no resources, tech trees, etc), so if that doesn't appeal to you you will probably not enjoy it, but for anyone who enjoys building this is an unmatched experience. There is a level of learned skill involved, which makes it a rewarding experience. Small things like figuring out you can use wall lamps to make street lamps, learning you can turn windows into doors, that you can join windows and doors to make them bigger.... There's so many small and rewarding moments like this in the game.The only critiques I have:I wish you could ctrl+ click when on a certain build system to delete, for example being in road placement mode and then hitting ctrl to move to road removal mode. Switching manually over to the destroy tool every time is annoying, though it does have a very decent 'undo' and redo system to make up for it, so it's not awful. Just something that will come into play more once the game has been out longer and people get into more advanced builds.There's a season option, but you have to manually change your save game file to switch between seasons. I'm assuming there's bugs associated with this. but it would be nice to have a seasonal change option in-game.Either way, I can see myself playing this for a very long time, even without changes. I highly recommend it for anyone who is interested!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Once Tiny glade dropped as a free demo, I tried it out and Immediately got hooked! Now that we have full access.. omgthis is game is amazing. I feel pressured a lot in a lot of games due to the action element, or the inventory management.. but if you slack in those things you don’t get anything done.. this game is the opposite. You have full range to do whatever you want. It’s so intuitive and easy to make masterpieces that are one of a kind and lead you to wanting to build more and more! This is a must have game for ANYONE! It’s easy, fun, colorful and beautiful! Stress free and amazing! 10/10 game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a dream come true.Tiny Glade, which just launched today, is an absolute dream come true for anyone who cherishes the freedom of building and relaxing, reminiscent of the beloved sandbox mode from ''Stronghold or Stronghold Crusader''. From the very first moment, the game captures a sense of creative liberation where you're free to build, shape, and perfect your own little world without the pressures of resource management or impending threats.The attention to details, the music the camera mode... everything is there.Tiny Glade allows you to focus purely on the joy of design. Whether you're crafting winding stone walls, cozy cottages, or scenic pathways, every element comes together harmoniously. There's no rush—just a calming sense of flow. The serene atmosphere, aided by the soft pastel colours and peaceful music, makes it feel like you're building in a dream.It’s therapeutic and meditative you’ve ever dreamed of peacefully building without constraints, this game is the perfect escape.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I have completely fallen in love with this game. As someone who played the old versions of SimCity back in the day, I feel right at home (except there is even LESS jeopardy in this one). It's very pretty, fun to learn and creative. It will EAT your spare time if you are of the right mind! OK, long-term, it may pale, because it is limited in scope; but for the price, it's an absolute steal. System requirements: If, like me, you have an older-spec machine, it is still worth downloading the free demo and giving it a try. It will run on my elderly desktop machine running Intel 530 graphics but, as the developers warn, it's a bit slow and occasionally misbehaves. Still had fun with it, even then. Runs nicely under Intel IRIS on a newer laptop.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: such a beautiful and wholesome game. this has quickly become one of my favourite games to play and do projects on. i cant wait for future updates with a bigger area, more things to design with, more colour swatches and i would absolutely love the idea of maybe interior on day. some games should really take a page out of tiny glades book with making a nice, beautiful and creative game
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXACTLY as described.It's a tiny builder.I'm marveling at my little 1-3 building castles with ponds and ducks and trees while I look at others building grandiose towers filled with architecture.  It has stuff for everyone...including a photo mode that is gorgeous.Also, it runs great on the Steam Deck by default.  If you've played KB/M-controlled games on the deck before, this will come naturally to you, and the controls work very well.It's very chill, and the tutorial drops you in your own plot to continue on - or you can choose different scenarios (one of which cycles daily).I love it, it's a great calm creative game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I am not much for building games honestly. They entertain me for a few hours, but I quickly move on. There is something so magical about this game: from its whimsical aesthetics to the satisfying sound effects as you smoothly place builds, walls, ponds. As the wandering sheep and ducks pop up on your screen, it encourages you to just take a moment and appreciate the game's beauty and character. As a perfectionist, it is hard to get into building games and shut that constant inner critic up because I am not building a replica of the Notre-Dame from day one like everyone else, who showcases their elaborate masterpieces. It is healing to find a game that allows you to just create without that inner critic springing into action, leaving me perplexed. Why am I suddenly okay with existing as an imperfect architect in this game? The way the game slows you down and encourages you to just breathe and enjoy the flow is something really special that few games manage well in my experience. It doesn't feel frustrating; rather, the peace and naturally soothing aesthetics of the game feels safe and comforting.This turned into a deeper review than I initially set out to write, but I hope some of you who relate to these experience can find some comfort in this game the same way I do.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: What a unique and charming game! The mechanics are great, visuals are absolutely beautiful and aesthetically pleasing, great camera mode. What can I say - Pounce Light, you created a true masterpiece! Congratulations to everyone involved in the creation of the game! And thank you for making the game available on Geforce Now, really appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is an adorable world-building game. You can add water, trees, walls, and all the while, sheep, ducks and fish join you. You can even pat the ducks and sheep!I'm so glad I bought this game! I'll definitely return to it when I feel the inspiration strike.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Very Relaxing, No stress!Great game to just let your mind go and to let your creativity set loose. This game you don't have anything to bother you, no foes or enemies, no resources gathering, just your creativity, unlimited resources and that great feeling of freedom to do whatever it is you want!This is a game to switch out of busy mode onto a careless loose mind, great for one of those post long day at work, activity and to just build to your heart's contempt! and you can always pause the game and just take a brake and stare at your build for as long as you want.Highly recommend  if you are in a relaxing and creative freedom kind of mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is the most beautiful cozy game I've ever played. plus SHEEP! It’s also incredibly satisfying when I place a window (or door, path, etc) and a random object appears. I love moving buildings around and the plants/vines change, too. It’s “just a building game”, but it feels alive and unexpected things happen during your building process (like I’m still discovering how combining certain tools/object placements can get different results).
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute, and is part of the general growth of cozy games with no objective and no purpose other than letting whatever comes your way take shape in front of you, because, let's face it, the world is stressful enough and sometimes we just need something creative without direction. Some people are doing amazing things with the limited tools and palette available to them, but even for those of us who are less creative (or creative in other ways) there's lots of new discoveries and synergies of the items and tools in the game that make it interesting to play. There are some things that I wish they had. I wish they would integrate some more capability for keyboard controls, copy/pasting or mirroring in order to duplicate objects.  More construction lines would be handy, though this might start feeling like "work" (especially for those of us with CAD background).I also wish (and hope) they come out with more free-standing items and decorations that we can put down outside of what will randomly generate through the procedural nature of the game. I would like to place farm field/garden field plots in addition to the cacophony of flowers that get dropped, the ability to change the roof material from tile to thatch, fruit trees, and decorations. For example, I was jokingly making a witch's hut in the swamp and it would be fantastic to put down some more harvest-themed items around it for October. Maybe sometime soon!I've gotten into other recently published cozy games but I think that Tiny Glade may be my favorite right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It is an extremely relaxing game that made me understand what people who have played Minecraft for years feel—without the frustration of crafting and so on! I searched for days to finally find something so juicy, relaxing, and rewarding. And here it is — no losing, no winning, only pleasure. PS: if you use 3D graphics tools or engines, sometimes you will miss some features. But it is okay, you can do the best with what the game provides, and it's a challenge of its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So I bought this and played with it for almost two hours and got a refund. The lack of even simple modelling tools (think xyz references, global/local centers, copy/paste, etc) was a frustration. However the game stuck in my head so I rebought it and played with it most of yesterday. I'm still slightly boggled by the lack of copy/paste or basic modelling tools but the game does have its own charms. I hope that the devs see how many are asking for simple tools like copy'paste etc and add them to the game.If they don't the game still has a certain ability to create interesting things but manually placing lots of objects they have to create from scratch every time will burn most people out eventually. I would also like to see more small pieces to use to fill out the models. I would recommend the game anyway as it is a stress free way to model things without getting into the steep learning curve of modelling apps.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a grown man. I listen to black metal. I work in a metal workshop. And I built cute little towns and castles in Tiny Glade.What a lovely little game with a unique building engine that just works. I've played for over 10 hours now and in that sense would say it is definitely worth the money, but it would need something... I would love for tiny people to just start living and doing things when you build. Like get out and start working the fields or something. Somethign to make the towns feel more alive, but I realise what an ask that is.But perhaps have a little more options, different windows, a shop building style, perhaps more customisations. But as it stands, this is a beautiful game with a lot of potential. Very therapeutic and I can't wait to see what future updates bring.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It performs like a dream thanks to its custom engine, the procedural generation does a great job of letting you resize things, and the music and aesthetic are great. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This does exactly what it says it does. It's a cutesy little diorama maker. Very easy to use, fun to use.There are a bunch of cute little secrets to discover, too. Some buildings interact differently with water, for example, and making a really short building with no roof will make a very pleasant bridge. Having two roofs intersect at an angle will often make a bird's nest appear. It's lovely.The closest thing I have to an "issue" is the wanting of more. More architectural styles. Some wooden buildings. More flowers. More window shapes. Porches, little decorations like wells, etc etcIf this looks like something you want it almost definitely is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I already love this game so much! I played the demo the day before release and immediately wanted the full game. At first it seems more simple than expected, with only so many tools I thought there wouldn't be that many options, but gosh was I wrong! There's so many little things that can affect a build so much, my only complaint is that they aren't always told to the player, I just stumbled upon some of the starting builds that helped me figure it out. I did really like learning that way, poking around to see what works is quite fun, but I kind of wish at least it was clearer how to find that stuff out. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I'm easily overwhelmed by city-builders, base-builder games. You have to collect resources. You have to achieve goals. If you make a mistake, it can cost you. Even games like The Sims, it takes me forever to make even a small town, building each house one by one and trying to give it some personality. Usually I end up giving up, or losing interest half-way through.This game is different. I quickly found myself building a scene, a house, a village, without even thinking. It's intuitive, relaxing, and effortlessly charming. If you want to undo something or change it on the fly, you can. No pressure whatsoever. The building is somewhat limited by nature--you can't place down individual animals, or certain decorations, or choose what type of flowers grow, etc--but I think this largely helps the building process by constraining choice. I place down a building, and the game pops in a little bush, some boxes with farming tools, maybe a line of laundry. I don't have to worry about hand-placing everything, it just comes together on its own.A lot of fun packed into a tiny price tag!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the demo! Bought the full game, Lovely, cozy graphics and sounds. Good UI. The game has  a couple of improvements possibilities:Every new game doesn't start with a clean building area. There are always buildings, etc. when you start a new game. You first have to delete everything before you can start your own building projects... It's annoying... But once that is done you'll have a lovely relaxing and fun cozy building game! Would love an option to start with a clean building area, though.There is no proper controller support. I like to play my games with a contoller (on a big TV). ...And not all handhelds have trackpads. Yes, you can "hack" something together... But that's still isn't great.It really is a tiny glade. Not medium sized or large. Would love to see options to build a large town on a large area.Nevertheless, this game comes highly recommended for those who love relaxed building!

_childDocuments_.review: It is indeed a game that has no mandatory objective. Playing it makes you feel free with various landscaping aspects. The type of maps that can be built are all up to player. No directions, no setting goals just the player and map - for start maps there are also tiny addings to give a chill vibe-. What I am waiting for the next patches (or DLC's maybe) is new little decoration elements (farm tools, barrels, plants and trees), new tools to snap height of a wall for instance (tools to make it easier to built symmetrically), different types of architecture such as Japanese or Chinese or even maybe Ancient Greek architecture where glorious temples can be built. For the last is people, because I would like to give life to the space that I created. Tiny people wandering around the place doing some daily tasks would give vibrant and dynamic gameplay to its players. What I am really invested in this game is landscaping. I really loved the coziness of it. So basically, it is game you can enjoy without a stress or doubt. And its price is really worth it that is all I can say without a second think.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a delightful game that invites you into a whimsical world of nature and creativity. At first glance, the game’s charming graphics and soothing soundtrack set a relaxing tone, making it easy to get lost in your own little serene glade. The core mechanics revolve around creating your own small town in a glade where players can plant flowers, grow trees, and attract adorable wildlife. The controls are intuitive, allowing for smooth navigation and interaction. If you can think it, you can probably do it. The way in which this game promotes creativity in a serene environment allows you to simply get lost in the tiny world you're building. By far one of the core components of the entire tiny glade experience. The art style is vibrant and enchanting, with each element beautifully designed. The animations of the animals and the gentle sway of trees add a layer of life to the glade (don't forget to give your sheepys head pats!). Complementing the visuals is a calming soundtrack that enhances the overall experience, making it perfect for unwinding after a long day. Both of these elements combine to give this game a truly unique and serene vibe. Don't forget to try all the different camera modes! Tiny Glade is a breath of fresh air for simulation game lovers. Its charming aesthetics, relaxing gameplay, and encouragement of creativity make it a worthwhile experience. Whether you're looking to unwind or go crazy and indulge in some creative building, Tiny Glade offers an experience that will accommodate any taste. Overall, it's a delightful addition to the gaming world that deserves a place in your gaming library.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a breath of fresh air in the world of city builders. If you're looking for a peaceful, stress-free experience where you can let your creativity shine without being bogged down by complex mechanics, this game delivers. With its intuitive, grid-free building system, you're free to craft stunning castles, cottages, and picturesque landscapes that come to life with charming, spontaneous details.The game thrives on simplicity—drag, drop, and watch as the environment evolves around your choices. Whether it's a bay window forming from placed windows or an archway appearing in a stone wall, Tiny Glade constantly surprises with its delightful attention to detail. I lost track of time as I tinkered with different designs, creating everything from humble hamlets to sprawling castles.The visual charm of the game is undeniable. The soft, pastel palette and fluid animations give everything a storybook-like feel, and the changing seasons and day-night cycle add an extra layer of magic. Watching ducks paddle through ponds and sheep lazily graze is strangely therapeutic.However, Tiny Glade's strength is also its limitation. While the game is a fantastic tool for relaxing and casual creativity, it doesn't offer much depth in terms of building variety. After a few hours, you might feel like you've seen most of what it has to offer. Hardcore city-builder fans looking for intricate mechanics or more customization options might find it lacking.That said, Tiny Glade doesn't aim to be a complex sim. It's the ultimate ""—perfect for winding down after a long day or just zoning out and creating something beautiful. If you enjoy games like  and , this will feel like a cozy blanket of creativity.  In conclusion, Tiny Glade offers a charming escape into a world of miniature creativity. It might not be for those seeking complexity, but if you're after a cozy, artistic experience where you can unwind and let your imagination flow, this is the game for you. Fans of relaxing, creative sandbox games.

_childDocuments_.review: After giving it a solid 80 minutes of play here is my opinion.-----------------------"The good"-Graphics are really nice, I'm running a GTX 4070 with Core i7-14700K. After beefing up the settings, my frames start dropping. I find that around 4.0 quality is the sweet spot for me.-Easy to understand interface. Simple, smooth, easy to get to know.-Small file size is always nice as it can just sit installed and have no reason to remove it for something else then come back later ect ect.-For those stuck with ideas, they have weekly templates to start from that you can edit in your own way which helps save some time. For someone like me, I always get stuck in the begining of a project and constantly start over and over. Plus it helps to know what can be done.- Day/night cycle with lock, sun rotation. Helps when you are trying to find the right effect for lighting.-Summer, winter, fall and few other seasonal types to choose from. Winter is pretty nice looking with snow flakes floating around the screen.-------------------"The bad"The biggest concern is "CUSTOMIZATION"More options should be available in terms of size. Your buildings "without stacking/rotation" can only be so large, small, wide.No option to customize where little objects appear. It also seems like you have no choice "where" they appear.From what I see there is only so much you can do with trees, and flowers. No option to change their apperance really.Only one road type. how about cobble stone, or different types of sand?Water is too simple, should be an option to clear out lily pads. Control the depth too would be nice.I read somewhere that borders aren't an issue, but from what I see there is infact a border. Maybe I missed something...------------Conclusion.Perhaps I am being too harsh on a game that just fully released. I am hopeful and optimistic that the devs will update and add features and more customization options. I also only gave it 80 minutes of play, so I could have missed something. But unsure.If your looking for something simple and a way to kill time. Sure go for this game! it looks great and as I said its easy to use.But there are tons of sandbox/builders like this that are alot further along in the ways i described that don't require a learning curve like Unreal engine or Blender.I used programs such as FlowScape which covers alot of what I described in my complaints.With a game like this, Options and customization are tremendously important especially when you want to create something nice and worthwhile. 5/10 but would still recomend for the good reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning, this is more of a toy than a game. There's no objectives or challenges to overcome, just a blank canvas and a set of tools to build with. But what a canvas!What's here already is excellent, and more than enough to justify the purchase. Castles, towns, churches, you can build away to your heart's content and most things will look pretty good out of the box. The art style is chunky enough that your manually placed windows will usually look fine even if they're not perfectly centered. The camera is intuitive and the controls easy to learn.After a few hours building a small castle town, I've had a blast, but also have a few items of feedback for the devs:- rectangular buildings could use more edit options. tweaking the buildings into parallelograms would be great for handling corners & more unusual building shapes. I also wish we could get gables as an option for the stone siding like we do on the tudor-style siding.- It would be cool to get ruined bridges working. Right now, using the delete tool turns rectangular bridge sections into walls, which is fine, but walls are locked to the ground so you can't have a suspended section of ruined bridge.- I was hoping that doing a circular section suspended over another circular section would make a gazebo, but it ends up looking more like a platform on pillars. This one would probably be a lot of work to implement, though.- It would be nice if terrain could be adjusted down as well as up. Carving out valleys is a bit cumbersome right now, as you have to effectively erase them into existence, and can't adjust them the way you can adjust the surrounding elevation. It also feels like you should be able to paint terrain over water, rather than needing to erase the water to raise the land back up.- Paths are always on the ground, so you can't really draw paths across bridges or atop rectangular wall sections. It would be great if pathing could be painted onto building rooftops and balconies. This would open up a lot of options, from multi-tiered stairs to steep ziggurats to something approximating that gazebo.- on a related note, it'd be nice to get the option to widen doors as well as change their height. Right now it's a bit awkward trying to paint paths under the wall to get just the right door/arch width. It's a little unclear how wide it needs to be to turn from a door into an arch, as well--would be cool to make this a toggle by clicking on the door.- I hope to see more decorative pieces added in the future! Flags and lanterns are a great start, but it'd be cool to get braziers, fountains, statuary, and so on.- agricultural themed areas are a little sparse as well. You can make a great barn and silo, but there is no crop painter option. It'd be cool to get rows of wheat or cabbages, as right now it's restricted to flowers and trees (which can make pretty orchards). Beehives would be a fun addition, too.I'm loving this so far, and can easily see myself losing dozens of hours to this in the coming months. Really well done!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to people who know how little there is to do in the game. There's VERy VERY VERY little here. If you take the time to learn how flexible many of the mechanics are, and you hyper focus on tiny sections you can find yourself having a good time. The tilt shift function for photography is nice. I recommend this cause its nice and chill. Just know how little there is here. Very Very little. Even the space they give you to make a diorama is minuscule.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The attention to detail and polish on this is very impressive. It's incredibly simple to create very detailed villages and is relaxing but rewarding at the same time. There are no objectives or gameplay other than building whatever you want. A castle fit for a princess, or maybe a vampire, a small English village, huge city. Your imagination (and textures) are the limit.You can tell the game is made with passion and care, everything is so well polished and pretty complex looking buildings can be made with ease. No tutorial is really needed and it's impressive how much you can achieve with so little time.My two biggest wishes are the ability to furnish indoors, and more textures, otherwise I can see myself getting a bit bored of it after approx 10-20 hours. Although that is still pretty good value! If there was a way for the community to mod this I can't even begin to imagine some of the amazing creations people will come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: As a man of grounded action, fast-paced playstyle and competitive multiplayer. I have never been so appeased by a sandbox/building game ever since Townscaper. _childDocuments_.review: This was easily my most anticipated game of the year, among all the garbage thrown out there by AAA studios, this game is a breath of fresh air and it's baffling no other studio thought of developing a game like earlier.The fact that they give you just a few elements to work with, basically boxes and cylinders and let you discover the combinations you can achieve with them is priceless and will allow you to get so many AHA moments.That being said, there are some things that frustrate me and I think it's mandatory they get fixed in a patch or DLC pack or something. The first one is the terrain modifier, you can't really create a castle on top of a mountain (like let's say the Orava Castle) because you can raise the terrain only by a few floors height. Not sure why you aren't allowed to play more with terrain.There's also no way of doing slopes or slanted platforms, which would be very useful when working with different elevations. Also, no stairs implemented, other than manually placing a box for each step and trying to manually align them every time, which gets old and boring pretty quickly if you have a stair with 10 steps or even a circular staircase.Then the fact that you can't create asymmetrical roofs, like a Shed or a Sawtooth roof is quite frustrating, it feels like such a huge loss after all the work that has been done to create so much freedom to combine shapes. I can't imagine it would be hard to implement since the basic mechanic is there already, so I really can't find any reasons to why this was left out, because it would add a crazy amount of diversity to the game.I'd also love to have a lot more elements and I'd be happy to buy a pack of more variations of let's say windows, or doors. Or maybe the ability to make the chimney wider, maybe combine 2 chimneys like you can combine 2 windows and get a wider chimney. There's so many examples of huge wide chimney on chateaus and castles that again, I literally can't understand how this feature was left out.Then maybe the ability to make flags bigger, taller poles, or different types of flags when you click on them, not just changing the emblem.Also the tips of the pointy roofs, would be awesome to get different designs for that as well, maybe a cross for the church, or even a small statue, again, there's a ton of examples of this in real life.Other than that, the game has a great building base and I guarantee you haven't encountered this amount of building freedom in any other game before, so I totally recommend trying it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is honestly one of the cutest and most relaxing games I’ve played in a while. Big kudos to the devs for nailing that cozy, peaceful vibe! The building mechanics are super smooth and just feel right. No matter how you place the pieces, everything blends perfectly with the environment—it's like magic how seamless the structures and nature come together. Definitely gives off this whimsical village charm.That being said, there’s still so much room for this little gem to grow! I’d love to see more animals roaming around—deers grazing, squirrels darting through the trees, and even birds chilling on rooftops would make the world feel even more alive. Maybe even some farm animals to really bring out that rustic, village-life vibe. And more decorations, please! Benches, tables, cute little market stalls—anything that adds personality to the villages we’re crafting.Oh, and villagers? That would be a game-changer! Just imagine people walking around, entering their cozy homes, and living their little lives while you’re still building the village around them. It would really make everything feel more dynamic and alive.The potential for DLCs is huge too. A forest-themed DLC with more wild animals, or a coastal village expansion with boats and docks—there’s so much that could be added! Right now, though, the game can get a bit repetitive after a while, especially if you’ve built a few villages already. But even so, it's totally worth buying if you’re into chill, creative games.Overall, Tiny Glade is a fantastic start, and I can’t wait to see how it grows!

_childDocuments_.review: From castles to small hovels. Palaces to forts. You name it, you build it. The ammount of customisation is also very nice. Everything renders beautifully. No matter how much you build, the game does not seem to have an issue with it. FPS stays good and you don't have to wait for anything to load.
