I'm not sure exactly what to call it, it's not cartoony, but drawn, in a way.I think DnD players will also love this to create their worlds for players in Tiny Glade.I could say a lot more, but I just wanna play. _childDocuments_.review: Lets start of with the important part. I really like this game and im glad i bought it. But i wouldn't recommend it to any of my friends at this state. There are not much options for building, round and square buildings, a fence, a wall, windows, a path, water, flowers and trees. That may not sound like a lot for a game that doesnt do anything besides building, but here comes in the cool thing about this game: . It has a lot of options by customizing and combining the existing features. There is no bridge in the game? just put some water, take as building, make it as tiny as possible and take away the cealing. Now make it a long rectangle and your done. Want to make a fence door? build a small fence and then put some dirt under it, which becomes a door when combined. Not only do you feel smart comming up with new things to creativly combine these features, it also is so relaxing not having tons of options in one huge UI.A lot of combinations do nothing interesting, or do nothing at all. -Flowers and Tress have no variations. I cant set the hight of them, i cant click on them to cycle through options like we can with windows, and most importantly i cant even use the brush tool on them. They could become cherry trees, rose bushes, etc.-Flags cant be set to have a variable hight when placed on a roof- If i rise the ground and then place water on it i cant create a waterfall, the ground is automatically lowered there (probably the most disappointing missing feature)- I cant cycyle through variations on fences, only colours- Theres only one kind of lightsource, a lamppost. Its cool that you can change colour of the light, but thats about it. Torches are heavily missed, and hanging chandeliers aswellAnd i am sure there are more interactions like these missing, i encountered them after only 2 hours of gameplay. I really hope they keep developing, because it already looks like my most favorite game of all time. Sadly playing it for only a couple of minuts reminds me, why it isnt.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Tengo Project reimagination of their older works, this time being Pocky and Rocky/Kiki Kaikai for SNES. Much like Wild Guns Reloaded and The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors, Pocky and Rocky Reshrined takes its source material and revamps it for modern day systems, adding in new mechanics that don't detract from gameplay, additional characters that offer new playstyles, and beautiful updated art to flesh out the original sprite work for a larger screenspace. It's still a challenging arcade style game that doesn't keep the barrier of winning too high, but leaves room to improve and master its stages. If the gameplay in motion interests you, it should be right up your alley. And if you're already familiar with Pocky and Rocky SNES, there's a slew of twists and turns to make things fresh again.As an aside (as others have noted), the Steam version is essentially the equivalent of the uncensored Japanese console versions; no weird censoring on Ame-no-Uzume, which is neat. Unrelated to that, the game even supports Playstation button icons if you happen to be using a Sony controller through Steam.I'd say the only real downside to the game is that there's no dedicated online co-op support. That being said, there's Steam remote play which (sort of) makes up for that. It's not as perfect as actual couch co-op, but it's an option.Overall one of my personal favorites, clearly a product of passion alongside the other recent Tengo Project remakes and worth playing. Here's hoping The Ninja Saviors sees a Steam release too.

_childDocuments_.review: The text limit for Steam reviews is pretty strict, so I'm challenging myself to write this succinctly!I think this game is decent, but I have caveats for anyone on the fence about buying it:Pocky & Rocky Reshrined is not simply a remake of the SNES Pocky & Rocky.  It's both a remake and a sequel in terms of its mechanics and the scenario, the game you're playing.  I say this because Pocky & Rocky Reshrined will likely be a pretty frustrating Story Mode because the crux of the story is that the main villain travels back in time to defeat Pocky.  The way the game motivates this particular aspect is by restricting you from having your special abilities.  That's the twist in the story, that by obtaining the blessings of the gods, Pocky is able to use abilities that she didn't have in order to turn the tables on the antagonist, Black Mantle.That's all well and good, but I think this story is otherwise fairly threadbare, relying on homages or references to things most people won't have any concrete knowledge of to begin with.  Not only that, Pocky is incredibly frustrating to play as, she's fairly weak compared to other characters and her shot types don't seem to strike a good balance between coverage and precision, ever.  For casual players who are just looking to survive, this means that you're going to find yourself playing as a character who never feels like she has enough power or utility to really dispatch enemies efficiently.  Pocky is a character where you have to have very strong fundamental skill.  That's just to say, even if you don't care about being "the best" at the game, unfortunately the game is putting you in a position where you're going to take a bit of a beating whether you like it or not.Players more invested or familiar with shmup mechanics should feel right at home; however, with Pocky & Rocky Reshrined.  Upon getting through Story Mode, you unlock Free Mode and, upon unlocking the 3 secret characters in story mode, access to other play styles by which to try to approach the game.The scoring concept is based on farming for score and, in my opinion, is probably the least interesting aspect of the game.  I, at some point in time, had the number two score on the leaderboard for a normal playthrough... but that kind of run is very dry.  The game actually, from the outset, has a design trick to try to implicitly suggest that "This is how you score well", by placing a 300 coin shop in the middle of Stage 1.  The only way to get the money for this shop is by staying in one area and killing waves of enemies then picking up the money they drop.  You would then, theoretically, look for profitable areas to score.  Maximizing bonuses by not getting hit, thus making bombs, shields, and extra lives all spill over into high point collection.I'm just going to be up front, the distinction that players make between, say, video games and pachinko, mean increasingly less to me as this kind of design normalizes.  Scoring is the least interesting thing to me about a video game, ironically, I just learned how to do so because it's important to actually know the subject matter you're engaging with.  In doing so, I'm going to say right now, this is the least compelling part of the game, but unfortunately the one that got quite a bit of consideration from the developers.I won't go further into that, but getting a 1CC casually is pretty fun.  At a 30 dollar price point, I think that most players who just want to run through a game and have a good ol' whimsical time should be well serviced.  It may do well for you to wait on a sale at that.If you're the type of player who feels that what a game communicates is very important to the experience, I would suggest skipping out on this game.  Otherwise, it's a very good looking, pleasant sounding experience for those who like shoot em ups.  Those who have never played this kind of game, if you find frustrating experiences off putting, take that into consideration because this game is not something I'd call "easy."

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect. 10/10. No notes.The spritework is really fantastic. I love the music, and each character really makes you play the game in a different way. They're all fun though Hotaru has my heart. Accessing co-op is a little obtuse, but there is a cheat code to unlock it immediately if you're trying to jump right in with a friend.The game is hard, but very fair. I never feel like I'm dying because the game decided to end me. lol. Failures stack and game overs are generally the result of not being mindful enough when approaching problems. Definitely pays to have some old school sensibilities when jumping into the game, but I have both seen the game over screen on the first stage and completed the game on normal without continues over the last 48 hours so it's not impossible to go from being terrible to sitting on the leaderboard.Definitely pick this one up. Arguably the best $30 I've spent this year and may very well be my GOTY to be honest. I'm a bit smitten.

_childDocuments_.review: A game so nice I bought it twice (on Switch and Steam).I'm really glad most of the original team was able to get together to make a new installment in this series. They really knocked it out of the park. My only major complaint... Is that I want more of it! It's rather short at only eight stages total and it took me just over an hour on my first (solo) playthrough. A few more stages would have been very welcome, not only for the enjoyment but also for helping pad out the rather overly ambitious and chaotically-paced story.It's also really weird that co-op mode needs to be unlocked rather than simply being available from the start. _childDocuments_.review: an amazing remake of an overlooked SNES gem!gameplay is super fun! it plays like a shooter with powerups an all, with the special mechanic being a melee attack that can reflect attacks. it's very difficult, but you make a lot of progress with each continue! there's multiple characters you get to play as that have different abilities and shot effects.the game looks absolutely amazing. perfectly brought up-to-date while retaining a nostalgic retro feel. there's so many cool animations in this game!one of the only real issues with this game is that you need to beat the game on singleplayer mode to unlock multiplayer. there is a cheat code that unlocked the multiplayer mode, though. it is also pretty short; even with how hard it can be you can beat the singleplayer story in 2-3 hours. the multiplayer/free play modes offer the most replayability, with some difficult steam achievements to shoot for if you want a challenge. that's about all, though.absoultely recommended! it can use all the love it can get!

_childDocuments_.review: A reimagining/sequel to a fantastic SNES game, Reshrined maintains and enhances the qualities of the original. Hard mode being genuinely hard, it's been a while since I felt such a sting and it's all the motivation I need to really master every stage and character. 5 characters to be exact with 3 being new, they all possess unique traits and abilities to make them valuable. Co-op is accessible in Free Mode which is unlocked by Story completion or a code one can easily find online.This is nothing if not love and care from Tengo Project, 3 old developers from the earlier days of gaming who still GOT IT!

_childDocuments_.review: I first discovered this series while going through MAME roms years ago but quickly fell in love with it. It's a classic 80's arcade coin eater that plays as a top down shooter.Reshrined is an HD remake that plays exactly like the classic game down to the incredibly hard and ruthlessly punishing gameplay. While the game is plenty of fun to grind through with infinite credits you're going to be fully aware that you suck the entire time as you struggle your way through each stage, inching your way to the finish line. The rigid 8 way shooting combined with small projectiles means you can open yourself up to being hit quite easily. There's a dodge, and some subtle tricks like using your melee to deflect bullets but everything moves fast so you need good reactions or a great memory.New to the game are 2 characters, some new attacks, and some new stages which are all cute bells and whistles but these are going to be more appreciated by the pro's who can make the most of them. Needless to say this is a very authentic remake and its no wonder that only 2.7% of players have the 'no continues' achievements for each character. If you're looking for a fun cute arcade action game you may end up discovering a tough as nails grind fest! Fun with friends but alone you're in for a long fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Pocky & Rocky Reshrined

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game was hard for me shows that I'm really bad at this genre, but that doesn't take away the fact that I liked this title. I knew the first game of the series as "Kiki Kaikai" (it's title in Japan), it was until know that I discovered that this is a remastered and additional version of Pocky and Rocky from the SNES, and I liked it :DThe music (specially the theme from stage 1), the power-ups, the characters selection, Free Play mode, Very Easy Mode (even with this I was losing, and again, I'm a complete noob at this game), the graphics (the movements were really smooth!), and the fun backstory.Knowing that this is one of Taito's greatest games, makes me feel like I have a great game in my library, and even though I suck at this game it's really fun to play :D
_childDocuments_.name: Pocky & Rocky Reshrined

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Natsume's previous SNES remake , it improves on the original in many ways, and would have been a lovely little top-down shooter if it weren't for the fact they chose not to revise the original's outdated control scheme. I don't care about 'not staying true to the original' - I care about enjoying myself playing a video game, and playing one like this without twin stick controls is like playing an FPS without mouse look. And if that requires rebalancing the entire game, then you rebalance the entire game.

name: GYLT
detailed_description: Shape your fears… Fear the shapes. Set in a creepy and melancholic world, GYLT is an eerie story mixing fantasy and reality in a surrealist place where your nightmares become reality. Hide from terrible creatures or confront them as you find your way through the challenges of this wicked world. Live the story of Sally, a little girl living in Bethelwood, Maine. Her life is not easy, and it has become even worse since her little cousin Emily disappeared. After being chased by a group of bullies, Sally is dragged into a twisted version of her town where her fears and worse memories are presented in a wicked and very real way. Main characteristics: Narrative adventure game with puzzles, stealth and action. Get to understand the world surrounding and discover the mystery behind Emily’s disappearance. Decide to either face the creatures or hide from them, in the same way you’d face or hide your fears. You can avoid being detected by creatures, you can build strategies to distract them, through sound or visual lures or by attracting them. Soundtrack by Cris Velasco.

After being chased by a group of bullies, Sally is dragged into a twisted version of her town where her fears and worse memories are presented in a wicked and very real way. Main characteristics: Narrative adventure game with puzzles, stealth and action. Get to understand the world surrounding and discover the mystery behind Emily’s disappearance. Decide to either face the creatures or hide from them, in the same way you’d face or hide your fears. You can avoid being detected by creatures, you can build strategies to distract them, through sound or visual lures or by attracting them. Soundtrack by Cris Velasco.
short_description: Shape your fears… Fear the shapes. Embark on a journey where you face your worst fears and are confronted with the emotional impact of your actions in this narrative adventure game with puzzles, stealth and action.

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts off with a warning for sensitive content regarding to bullying, it then opens up with a scene where our protagonist is literally gettin bullied by a bunch before she descends into a silent hill kind of world. The storyline tackles the issues within a grade school setting, combined with a gameplay where you're alone, cornered, scared and trying to navigate a bleak world while avoiding enemies trying to hurt you and it essentially gives the same feels of getting bullied.I like this game in particular, maybe because I can relate in a way. I was bullied a lot growing up while moving from school to school and there is really no clear way of getting out of it: * I don't fight back > I just get bloodied up and spent my time at home trying to hide the bruises, cuts and my busted lip from my parents.* I tried fighting back > I beat one up, then many more will come back to beat me up more angry than ever and then I come home with much more injuries to hide. * I tried being friends with so called cool guys > nah it's just not me* I tried being friends with kids that are being bullied as well > I wanted to see the perspective from different people in same situations on how they cope with it and I wanted to help too so it always end up in me fighting for them but then they just ran away and left me to get beat up lol! I expected them to call help at least but it never happened, not their fault anyway.* I didn't tried asking for help from the grownups because I'm really friendly and I don't want people to avoid & hate me for being a tattler and I also prefer figuring things out on my own so you can blame me for that. * I could've tried to be "invisible" but I didn't because that is not who I am, I wanted to be lively and make everyone around me smile & laugh even if it meant I would also attract the attention of bullies.  It's a struggle. Showing courage isn't always enough to ward bullies off, I've beaten up many of them through the years and eventually built up my own rep but it just ain't the same in the movies where they just respect you right after, well some did! but there are also rare instances when a bully attempts to do some serious harm either on you or to anyone/anything important to you the moment they felt vulnerable so if avoiding them is an option, take it! When all is said and done, I came to realize that Bullies are just weak minded individuals, not worth it and thus I didn't really harbored ill wills. Yes it hindered my life for a stretch but it is what it is, On the other hand I saw plenty of people change for the worse, therefore the matter should always be treated seriously. My Point is, there is no exact way on how to avoid being bullied but just like in the game Fighting them straight on or Stealthing your way is always the key to make sure you don't lose the fight! Results may vary but the worst thing to do is letting them do what they want because it only makes them stronger!I hate very simple gameplay & I hate stealth and GYLT have both of those! I still love the game as a whole nonetheless because it just has this adorable charm and as mentioned before, a relatable storyline that portrays courage and grit. The puzzles are okay, most are easy but there are a few instances where It took me some time to figure out where to go and what to do.The visuals are neat, the atmosphere & music are nice and the superb voice acting brought so much life to the characters! (there are only 2 actually, ok maybe 3) The loneliness, distraught and fear is really felt throughout the story, Sally is awesome! After playing GYLT, I think the real life bullies symbolizes the monsters in this game. They strive in the dark world where they fuel their desires with inflicting fear upon others but crumbles the moment someone exposes them to light. I love this game, I find it wholesome! ★★★★☆Lastly, for anyone out there: If you experience bullying at any point in your life, my advice in most circumstances, go and talk to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Babys first survival horror. Originally a Stadia exclusive, that got a second chance and for the most part it delivers. It's sort of a more kid friendly Alan Wake (mixed with some Silent Hill, if it was made by Tim Burton, where you explore a nightmarish version of your school, in search for your missing cousin. It's a very forgiving and casual survival horror overall, you will never run out of batteries (your way to defeat enemies) or health since they are all over the place, the enemies will quickly lose interest in you if you run and hide and you will pretty much always have everything maxed and still have half a dozen more to pick up if things go south, and honestly it seldom does. The enemies are seldom a threat and you can dispatch or avoid them pretty easily. It's pretty much only the bosses that will give you any challenge at all, and even they are pretty easy when you understand the mechanics. This is not a bad thing, it's probably a very good first introduction to the genre, just don't expect to be challanged if you are a veteran.The amount of collectibles in each area are also clearly marked, and if you are close enough they will be marked in the map. Just make sure you collect everything before the "point of no return", because the only good ending require that you have found and saved all "Inhabitants", otherwise you are given a choice between one depressing and one awful ending that are both pretty horrible, and kind of goes against the theme of the game. I kind of hate when games does that, when the "secret" ending is the true ending. But overall, a few missteps aside, Gylt is a pretty solid game. Happy that it got a second chance after Stadia.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game on launch and 100%'ed it on my PS5, and now I bought it again here on Steam to support the developers and tell ya'll to go and buy it too!Gylt is neither revolutionary nor perfect, but it is a little kid friendly Silent Hill x Alan Wake horror game, that is full of heart and charm. Initially launching on the ill fated Stadia, the game got another chance here on Steam and PSN, and if you're anything like me - someone who likes things that mix various genres and don't fit into one specific category - then you will love this indie gem.The game is relatively short (took me around 12 hours on PS5 cuz I like to take my time and explore), but playtime - although a widely discussed topic - should in my opinion be of no concern if the game is good and the story it wants to tell fits within that time. Like how a 12 episode anime can be just as- or even more impactful than a 52 episode anime. It is all about how effectively you use the time given.With that outta the way, while it doesn't add a whole lot of extra hours to the clock, Gylt comes packed with lore to unravel and secrets to find, in the form of diaries, portraits, birdcages etc, making sure that you have a reason to look around extra carefully if you are the completionist type. My first time around I swore I had looked everywhere, but still my index told me I had missed a whole heap of things, that I then had a blast going back and trying to find (afterall, it ain't fun if it's too eas), as I loved navigating the world and the mc Sally who is very fluid to control.On that note, keep in mind that until a certain point before end game (the game will be very clear about when this is), you can ALWAYS go back to previously visited areas in case you missed something!I was looking forward to Gylt after hearing it was gonna get re-released, and although various luke-warm reviewers initially discouraged me from dipping, I took the plunge anyway, and I am very glad I did!Again, Gylt doesn't revolutionize or do anything remarkable that you haven't already seen before if you are seasoned in the action/adventure/horror genre, but what it does it does extremely well; from the sombre but colourful graphics and cartoony artstyle that gives the game a visual identity all its own, to the atmospheric soundtrack, the well-done voice acting bringing the characters to life, to the polished gameplay where you run around the city- and school premises, fighting off shadow creatures with your flashlight, and choose to be either sneaky or aggresive about it.For what Gylt offers, $20 is more than reasonable, and I hope we see more within this universe!

_childDocuments_.review: GYLT is the latest game from Tequila Works (of Deadlight and RiME fame), that thrusts you into the role of Sally, a young girl looking for her lost cousin Emily. The game takes place in a town where everyone has vanished, save for the monsters that roam the streets and inhabit the buildings. The gameplay is a mix of stealth and puzzle adventure, with elements heavily inspired by Alan Wake with the use of a flashlight against enemies and more often running or hiding from enemies than facing them head on. I found some of the monster designs to be pretty good and there’s a couple legitimate creepy moments in the game. I’d also like to highlight the game's use of light as an indicator of where to proceed next, which felt organic in the sense that it wasn’t holding my hand but I also never felt lost as to where to go.I found that the story and messaging had their heart in the right place, if not a bit wrought. I enjoyed my time with GYLT, and while it did not bring a ton of new ideas to the table, I think it executed what it set out to do fairly well. While I’m not sure I’d recommend this at full price, I think it should definitely be on everyone’s radar during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of Little Nightmares, Alan Wake and Silent Hill with a nice Pixar art style but terribly boring gameplay. You play as Sally, a young girl looking for her missing cousin. You will have to go through a ghost town to find her. The story is full of clichés and moral lessons about children being bullied and yadayada. Gameplay is linear, you explore each new location, trying not to be spotted or using your flashlight to kill patrolling monsters, while also collecting items needed to solve puzzles and remove obstacles from your path. There is very little variety of monsters so you will get bored soon and their AI is horrible too; they can barely detect you and if they do you can just run until they return to their patrol position. There are some "boss fights", unfortunately very simple and boring. To unlock the true ending you also have to find all the collectibles, which is annoying. Standard endings are predictable and disappointing. I'm trying to think if there's anything good besides the graphics, but there really isn't. If you have 10 year old kids, it's fine to let them play this game, but RiME would be a better choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Gylt is a former Stadia exclusive which is essentially survival horror in a Pixar-esque world with similar mechanics to Alan Wake.Gylt takes place in a nightmare version of the main characters school as she is drawn into a dark world while looking for her missing cousin. You must look for your missing cousin while surviving the horrors of the world and uncovering why both of you have been drawn into this dark dimension full of monsters. The gameplay loop of Gylt involves exploring various parts of the school campus, dealing with monsters via stealth or using the games combat system of using your flashlight to evaporate enemies. There are occasional puzzles most of which feel a little confusing and out of place compared to the core gameplay these are the weakest aspect of the game. There are also a few boss fights with special mechanics which are without a doubt the games strong point in terms of boss and boss fight designs.Visuals and audio are strong here, the game looks good and crisp and the game is fully voice acted with creepy dialogue from the monsters.There are lots of collectables to get outside of the main story and multiple endings, I'd estimate it would take 6-8 hours to do everything. For the price this is pretty good value and very reasonable.While I have lots of praise for Gylt here the sad fact is while this is good, it's not a memorable horror game it won't go down in history and as long as you go into this expecting something functional, occasionally scary but ultimately quite generic except for the monster design then you'll enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game. The level design and the graphics are good. The performance is excellent. I had all the settings maxed and stayed above 130 fps. No skips or stutters, no loading screens. I usually don't like stealth. But the devs realize that in order for stealth to be good, the enemies have to be a little "dumb". Yes the A.I knows where you are, but they have cues that will make them attack. Cues like running, your flashlight or if they actually see you. In other games you can be 50 ft away, dead still behind cover and they'll go "I heard something". That type of stealth isn't fun imo.Combat isn't bad. It would be better if she had a stick or something. I'd like to be able to jump. Without spoiling the game, why'd I do all of this to help, and I stay behind. The other option would be worse. There's a camera transition that made me think I fell off the platform. And there's a unique camera angle that was fun once I realized I wasn't the enemy.This is worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Amazing art style reminiscent of 'horror' cartoons masterpieces like Coraline and Paranorman, enviroments,  characters and monsters are beautiful to look at and wonderfully animated+ Precise and tight controls that allow the game's various system to flow effortlessy, being it in combat, stealth or exploration+ Simple yet charming story that tackles various traumas that can affect children and adults alike, child bullying is evidently the most explored of them, yet loneliness, paranoia, hopelesness are all touched upon in a classy and well told wayCons:- While it does not hinder the value of experience per se, the difficulty is quite low, anyone with a bare minimum knowledge of survival horror will find no problems in handling the game's enemies and resources- On the short side, around 7 hours for a fully complete run with all collectibles found, yet the game never feels like its padding its runtime, Gylt its all meat and no fat- Overabundance of resources, it would have been nice to have a few less flashlight batteries and health kits around to make stealth slightly more prominent, i'd say 20% less of both would have done greatGylt has been a very pleasurable and unexpected find, a small yet beautifully crafted survival horror game that follows young Sally in her journey to find her cousin, disappeared in a shadowy, twisted reflection of their hometown where, akin to classics like Silent Hill, your traumas take form and wish only to harm you.The game has been clearly made with a lot of love, the voice acting for Sally is top notch, i encountered 0 crashes, 0 bugs and 0 gameplay annoyances in my entire run. If you ever wished for Coraline to be a videogame then playing Gylt is the closest thing you can have.Reccomended 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Although I remember seeing something about this game back when it released on Stadia, I really didn't pay very much attention to it. At long last, following  (another Stadia exclusive that I didn't get to until much later),  has finally arrived on Steam. And it's pretty good!I tend to enjoy most stealth games, so perhaps I'm already the target audience for this type of thing. As usual in stealth games, your protagonist Sally can hide in shadows and distract enemies. Taking on many enemies at once is a bad idea. The enemy awareness meter, although simple, is sufficient. The game has this cool Alan Wake-style light vs. dark thing going on, where Sally has a flashlight that she can focus to "burn" 2-3 particular spots on an enemy to dispatch them. She also has a "flash" that recharges over time that she can use to stun enemies. She can also jam the flashlight into the backs of most enemies to instantly destroy them. However, both her flashlight executions and flashlight focus eat a lot of battery power. Luckily, there are batteries absolutely everywhere, and the ones that you don't pick up are marked on your map. An odd aspect here is the game's insistence on telling you exactly what you can do with batteries (and inhalers) do every single time you pick them up. You'll get quite a bit of exposure to these tooltips.The aforementioned inhalers heal Sally, and these are also all over the place (and marked on your map). I'm not even sure I can recall a time when I had less than four inhalers (Sally can carry a maximum of five). Although the batteries and inhalers could have introduced a bit of a survival horror aspect to the game,  just isn't difficult enough to create this tension in the player. What's odd here is that you later get a fire extinguisher that, although it requires time to recharge, never actually runs out of whatever compound is inside. This can be used not only to extinguish fires (duh), but can also help you solve puzzles, navigate through steam leaks, and freeze enemies!Don't get me wrong - there's still a lot to enjoy here. I thought the shadow version of Bethelwood and the school environments were compelling and lovingly crafted, and I enjoyed this "Silent Hill 2 for kids" vibe that the game had going on. The game is ostensibly about the bullying of Sally's little cousin Emily, and the enemies say amusing things like "I smell loser!" to drive this point home. Certain doors are also locked with these eyeball stalks that follow Sally around, which seem to echo Emily's feeling that everyone is always looking at her/judging her.Another aspect of the game that I loved were the "inhabitants." From time to time, Sally will locate a ball of something called "blood quartz." She can use this blood quartz, one for one, to free individuals in the shadow town that have been turned to stone. These individuals have been trapped in the town, and upon their release Sally is rewarded with a diary entry that explains the circumstances that led to their gorgon-ification.Unfortunately, this brings me to the aspect of the game that I liked the least - the ending. Gylt is one of these games that features multiple endings. Whether you receive ending 1 or 2 depends only on what choice you make at the end, while ending 3 requires you to So, I can recommend Gylt for the environments, puzzles, enemy designs and gameplay, but not for the fact that it implicitly suggests that  I had a much higher overall opinion of the game prior to the ending, but still came out of it with a net positive impression.

_childDocuments_.review: - If someone were to see a still shot of Gylt with no HUD, they could be forgiven for assuming that they were looking at a frame from a Pixar film. Or at least Dreamworks' best impression of one. There is a conspicuous absence of moms with dumptruck asses. In any case, the game's characters feature the exaggerated cartoon features like oversized heads and tiny noses that you'd expect to see in films like those- In contrast to the visual style used during gameplay, cutscenes take on the form of short comic book stills. I actually really liked the artwork in these plot interstitials. In addition to punctuating the action and providing a change of pace, they seemed like a savvy alternative to prerendered or in-engine options. In addition to looking nice, they avoid awkward loading screens or weird transitions- Although they weren't all bangers, some of the settings deserve special praise. Two that really stick out in my mind are the school library and the arcade. Props to the art and level design teams for their work on those. They didn't make the game much more fun to play, but I did find myself fairly engrossed when I was sneaking my way through those areas- It's a relatively non-violent horror game, so expect all the musical tropes that would come from something a little spooky with a YA bent. Tinkling piano, ominous strings, thundrous percussion, and a single kid from a children choir serving up a lot of "Oooohs" and "Aaaahs" set the stage for most of Gylt's action- Although this is a horror title taking place in Maine, you can disabuse youself of the notion that there's anything Stephen King-like in the game. Gylt's story is far less creepy or violent than anything he'd write- Instead, you take the controls of Sally, a young girl in her early teens. Not too long before the action of the game, Sally's younger cousin, Emily, moved to her town. Unfortunately, not terribly long afterwards, Emily went missing without a trace. The game opens with Sally wandering town putting up missing posters until she's chased into the woods by bullies- To make a long story short (and avoid spoilers), Sally eventually gets magically transported to a mysteriously altered version of the town, where she catches a glimpse of Emily. She also meets a mysterious old man with a penchant for nighttime sunglasses wearing who urges her to track down her cousin, though his motives are unclear. As you make your way through the creepy New England setting, you'll be thwarted by an army of monsters that you'll either need to dispatch or avoid if you want to save Emily- The story wasn't particularly interesting, and nothing that Sally does or says of her own volition ever feels very motivated. Sally herself isn't much of a character in her own right. She's just a little girl who apparently has no interestests, identifiable personality traits, friends that you see, or family that you talk to besides Emily. In fact, there's only 3 characters, and the other two may as well spend maybe a collective 5 minutes on screen. The main story is also a somewhat half-baked very linear affair, just being a string of "go to X do Y" objectives. Additionally, you only get to make one moral choice at the end of the game, and the decision basically makes itself (unless you find all the collectibles to obtain the true ending)- Although the vibes are overtly ominous and the set dressing evokes most of the spooky goodness you'd expect from a horror title, Gylt is simply not very scary, even for the younger audience it appears to be targeting. As a kid, I read things like Goosebumps, Fear Street, and Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark, and those could probably still raise the hair on the back of my neck more capably than this game did. There are a few creepy moments moments scattered about, but none of them were able to elicit even a shred of fear or dread- With the free camera 3D perspective, gloomy settings, and snarling monsters, Gylt really does look like a survival horror title, but the gameplay feels more like a stealth action game. Hell, take a look at any room, hallway or street in the game, and you'll immediately notice that unusual number of waist-high boxes for you to crouch behind- The closest gameplay comparison I can think of is Murdered: Soul Suspect. Like that title, you spend most of your time sneaking around enemies due to your limited combat options while trying to solve a mystery, pilfering collectibles, and occasionally find yourself wandering into a boss fight with a gimmick or two that pulls from your limited set of abilities. Come to think of it, that is also a not-very-scary horror game that takes place in a moderately sized town in the northeast US- I had a hard time finding consistency in the stealth gameplay with respect to how capable enemies are in detecting you. Most of the time, the monsters are oblivious. I could get close enough to breathe on them if I was crouched and behind them, and even when directly in their line of sight, I still found I could often get fairly near before they started chasing me. However, in a few sections like the Arts Center, it feels like they gave all the monsters binoculars- Beyond crouching and trying not to be seen, your only other stealth ability allows you to throw soda cans at enemies. Although it works fine, the implementation feels clumsy since I don't think there's any other throwables. As a result, this game's town has the highest vending machine:human ratio this side of Tokyo- Combat is notably limited. Early in the game, you get a flashlight that you can use to Alan Wake your way out of trouble, and not too long afterward, you find an upgrade for it that'll allow it to do enough damage to kill enemies. It can also perform a stealth kill if you can get close enough behind an enemy to execute it. Later, you'll also find a fire extinguisher that is virtually identical in function, but freezes enemies rather than blinding them. I confess that I didn't use combat much beyond what was required for achievements. As an aside, there is a no-kill achievement that I managed to earn, but you can exit to the menu immediately after earning the kill achievements in order to maintain your pacifist run's integrity- There are a number of collectibles in the game, including journals, red gems called blood quartz, strange ashen statues of humans alled "Inhabitants", and, um, ghost canaries. Be sure you find all 6 canaries, otherwise you'll miss out on the last journal, bloodstone, and inhabitant in the secret room they unlock. If you don't get that last Inhabitant, you won't see the true ending- I managed to 100% the game, and I didn't enjoy it enough to consider replaying it in the future- I remember this game getting announced as a Stadia exclusive back in 2019, and I recall being a little annoyed. Imagine my excitement, then, when it was finally announced for Steam last year! Unfortunately, it's just not a very entertaining or engaging game. I compared it to Murdered: Soul Suspect before, but at least that game had some mildly interesting characters, a more involved (even if still not great) narrative, a fun "campy" vibe, and more interesting set pieces. Gylt isn't totally without merit despite the litany of complaints I aired. It runs well, controls well, and looks like a nice modern indie title. Unfortunately, I walked away from my experience feeling a bit disappointed by how by-the-books it was- It ran really nicely on the Steam Deck, at least, so it has that going for it: If you really want to see what Tequila Works can do, go try out Rime. Gylt feels like a nicely polished indie title that promises a creepy good time but delivers an underwhelming Are You Afraid of the Dark? experience

_childDocuments_.review: Game Review:SPOILER ALERT! THIS REVIEW CONTAINS EXAMPLES FROM THE GAME! DO NOT CONTINUE READING IF YOU DON'T WISH TO KNOW THEM BEFORE PLAYING!1. Setting & Theme: The dark, gloomy autmosphere of the game really helped with the overall experience. It was well-made and did include details to express the theme of one's past and the expression of being bullied. As someone who has been bullied in school, and as someone who saw others get bullied, I felt a stab in my chest at some parts of the game, be it if I collected diary entries or if I watches the design of the game; Mean writings on the walls and the wooden dolls depicting acts of bullying. Still, having stuff such as fully functional soda machines did feel a little comical at times. 8.5/10 stars.2.Gameplay: While using inhalers to heal and fighting monsters with a flashlight and a fire extinguisher (which somehow freezes enemies solid) was a fun concept, the game felt pretty easy once you've gotten the option to really FIGHT back. Some elements that make horror games immersive and exciting is the risk of danger and death. It was pretty good at first, but after you've gotten the upgraded flashlight, you could just pretty much stand and fight most enemies with ease, barely even dodging or running away from them since they stumble after detroying each weakspot. While having the option to kill enemies isn't bad, it should come at a risk of sort (for example, if the flashlight were to overheat or consume more light, that would make players think twice before they just decide to kill everything). Without such risk, and with the game having no difficulty settings, it felt dull at times. Not to mention that stealth-killing an enemy consumes around 30% of your battery, while killing an enemy head-on - only about 5%. Don't bother sneaking around, since you can just kill most of them. Some of the boss fights were also, to be blunt, quite lame, especially the one at the auditorium. You could bath in that monster's light for 10 seconds before actually being in danger. If you've just finished Amnesia: The bunker on hard mode and are looking for a similar nightmarish, challenging gameplay experience, this game might not be for you. 6.5/10 stars. Story: I knew what I was getting to after reading the into message, but the story was pretty straight forward. Bullying has been around for many years now, be it in games or movies. The only real major twist that was experienced was the fact that Sally (the protagonist) was ALSO mean to Emily, at least by being ignorant. This is also something that you can only know if You've discovered the underground secret room. And speaking of secrets, discovering the diaries from the people who died down there explains some lore about the mining company and how people lost their mind while digging there. Even after reading all the diaries, I still have many questions as to how that parallel universe works? And how do the big bosses (who are named after emotions and feelings that one would experience while being bullied) change depending on the person? Sally wasn't the only one there, so how do the rest of the people see it? 7/10 stars.4. replayability and length: The game's length justified its price. With no difficulty settings, no post-story challenges and secrets, your depended on getting all collectibles in the game to play at your fullest. And while the game does have different endings, only one of them had a special condition of getting all the ticket pieces, which you can actually do even after completing the main storyline through an option in the main menu. Imagine if the game itself has choices that affected the ending, This could have made people actually replay the game just to find out how to get them (or at least how to make a video online guiding others). 7/10 stars.Overall, I would reccommand this game. I had fun with it, but after getting all collectibles and knowing there is nothing left after, I'll be moving on to the next title.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a simple stealth game with good graphics, don't wait. Pick this up NOW..Gylt was a Stadia (Yeah, that dead gaming concept) exclusive that moved over to everything after a short stent. You play a the older sister looking for your missing younger sister who just started going to the same school as you. For some reason, there is a parallel city that she was trapped in with several other town residents. If you are looking for a game with excellent graphics, I would not put this on the top of the list. Do not get me wrong, the graphics are great and the level of detail is outstanding. This game was not designed to look like Horizon Zero Dawn. The comical animated style brings a sense of childish wonder mixed with a terror of silent hill. Heavy attention was paid to when they designed the feel of the environments.Moving over to the music. I will be short. It is simplistic to the point where it gets the atmosphere and tension where it needs to but no further. On the plus side, although repetitive, it is not overly loud nor is it annoying.  Controls are simple. You pick up a few items that you would normally find at a school. These items will be used to clear pathways and deal with the monsters. As the game is more stealth than anything, usage will be more for traversing the multiple sections.The game has multiple endings so there is room for additional play-throughs. In conclusion, if you have fatigue from all those hardcore games, definitely pick this up. It is not very long but have simple intuitive game-play with a satisfying story!
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Good- Well-written characters with compelling voicework; engaging atmosphere; mechanics are simple but enjoyable enough for the short runtime. Bad- The story needs to be fleshed out; the level design can be pretty linear, making puzzles easy; combat mechanics don't have much depth. Thoughts- Despite its many shortcomings, GYLT is a passable adventure that retained my interest throughout its campaign. Sure, the mechanics aren't anything new or particularly innovative – but they serve their purposes for the relatively short runtime of around six hours. The story also has an exciting premise but falters due to a barebones structure and poor pacing. GYLT might be worth a try if you find any of this interesting, but it's passable if you aren't particularly piqued by anything on offer.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! I was drawn to the game by the character design and Little Nightmare vibes, but this was no copy knock off this was a game true to itself. Puzzles and combat weren't hard so can be enjoyed by those who want to enjoy the story, maybe a hard mode update in future for those who want a challenge. The environments and characters were unique, accompanied with the music it made for a memorable experience - especially the creepy mannequins! There were a couple spelling errors in the diary notebooks and 2 of the achievements popped early but they are simple fixes. I'd love to see some DLC covering the background of the rock people or playing as Emily and her journey. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, probably best story driven, action, puzzle horror title so far this year, without counting all the remakes. Back tracking, puzzles, combat and world design are great. World feels twisted like Evil within or Little nightmares, combat is a bit more complex then Alan Wake. I would like if developers add difficulty so we get less batteries  or less hp recovery items. I was mostly maxed out most of the time.  Other then that this game is a breath of fresh air for a genre. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little spooky stealth horror adventure game for all ages. If you're a fan of Alan Wake, Coraline, or Little Nightmares, chances are you will love this title. I adore the art style especially. Would love to possibly see an update that adds fully rendered cutscenes, as the still images kinda took me out of it every time they showed up, but I also understand its an idie team and its not really a big issue at all. I won't spoil anything, but great art, great story, great music, and great gameplay. I absolutely see myself returning to this every once n a while for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting story the moral of which is connected to values like respect and self-sacrifice. More generally, you want to keep playing …

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is like a cross between Luigi’s mansion and The Last of Us. I love it. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Immersive, creative, creepy, exhilarating, heart-breaking, mind-bending, wow. Difficult enough to provide the player with a decent challenge, but not nearly break-your-controller frustrating (aka, good for novice/intermediate players). Solid depth of lore/backstory, complex enough to not quite get it off the rip (had to watch an explanation video afterwards but just to tie a few pieces together that I didn't catch on to- Pay close enough attention while playing and you will). Been compared to Alan Wake, which I have not played so I can't say, but figured I'd mention it in case that helps anyone else. Took me quite a few hours to complete, although I would put myself in the novice/intermediate category of player, as mentioned previously. Overall, definitely worth the money, great experience, would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable survival horror action adventure game, with a good story, atmosphere, and art style, and fun combat and stealth gameplay. Puzzles are pretty simple, not much challenge there but also won't frustrate you and make you look up a guide. Obtaining all collectibles isn't always that easy though and there's plenty of reasons to explore thoroughly.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hours in but I can already tell this is going to be one of my fav SP games of all time. Right up there with Alan Wake. It has a great atmosphere and story. I really loved everything about it and I really hope they make a second one, I would buy it in an instant.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: A really good hidden gem here. It has a little bit of a 'Little Nightmares' feel, but from a 3D perspective in that it shows a twisted world from the point of view of a kid. I thought the game did a really good job of showing familiar places, but making them eerie and surreal. The story and characters were also great, keeping me interested all the way through. The gameplay, which involves a lot of sneaking and puzzle solving, was fine. The combat was well balanced with the flashlight, which makes enemies feel dangerous. Overall a great game

_childDocuments_.review: If you love "Little Nightmares", then you're gonna enjoy this one for sure.Story is interesting and feels good, the gameplay is just 10/10 and the world build is really nicely made. _childDocuments_.review: So far the game has been quite the experience. I am not normally one for scary games so I thought I'd dive in on this one since it didn't seem as scary on the outside. _childDocuments_.review: Enter a hauntingly beautiful world in 'Gylt', where fear and bravery intertwine in a mesmerizing tale. Developed by Tequila Works, this atmospheric adventure keeps you on the edge with its gripping storyline and immersive gameplay.Embark on the journey of Sally, a courageous young girl exploring a mysterious, eerie town to find her missing cousin. The game seamlessly blends puzzle-solving with stealth mechanics, keeping you engaged at every turn.The striking visual design coupled with a haunting soundtrack creates an ambiance that lingers, immersing you deeper into the narrative. 'Gylt' delivers a mix of emotions, from fear and tension to triumph and empowerment, leaving a lasting impression.With its captivating narrative, atmospheric world, and compelling gameplay, 'Gylt' stands tall as a testament to the power of storytelling in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this game. It's definitely a "dark" game rather than straight up "horror". No jumpscares, no gore, the "monsters" are almost cute. It felt weirdly nostalgic to return to some childhood memories and exploring the school grounds. The graphics are incredible!Puzzles were all enjoyable, nothing too difficult. Only thing I struggled with was how sensitive the flashlight is, and if it's even slightly "off" from what you are hitting, it might not do it's job. I assume this will be fixed in the future though!The game itself reminded me of Alan Wake, Silent Hill, Little Nightmares, with some Alice Madness Returns mixed in. Overall, a wonderful game that I will definitely recommend to other people!
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: In the most endearing way possible, this is baby's first horror game. I loved the story, I think the topic that the story covers is handled with grace, more grace than many other studios have done in the past. It isn't going to pull any wild twists or turns on you, nor is it challenging, but it's well-written and has a ton of heart. Absolutely worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I got this copy included in a fanatical bundle & so glad I did. I never would have played it on Stadia since it was an exclusive but with this port I got to. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice small gem. Short but well built. Extremely pleasant graphics and well organised atmosphere, with slight 80s vibes. I didn't like that the story is pretty obvious shortly after the beginning (could have been some kind of a twist if done differently...)  but still enjoyable.Less than 7 hours to 100% it.For ultrawide users: the game is Vert- but if you use the usual Maintain_YFOV trick you can restore the correct FOV without any unusual fisheye effect and cutscenes are also scaled properly.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Gylt was a pleasant surprise to me. I initially thought it would be a game for children, but I was mistaken. Gylt showcases beautiful graphics with meticulous attention to detail in the art style that enhances the game's immersive nature and captivates players from start to finish. The search for Sally's missing cousin, Emily, drives the story forward, and the game successfully explores themes of guilt, fear, and friendship. The beautiful relationship between Sally and Emily is a significant aspect of Gylt, adding depth and emotional resonance to the game's narrative.It's worth mentioning that Gylt is remarkably polished, no glitches or bugs, providing a smooth gameplay experience. Additionally, all achievements can be unlocked without any issues. Gylt offers three distinct endings, including two bad endings and one good ending. The game allows you to obtain these endings without replaying it entirely; you can return to the campus after completing the game to collect any remaining items.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!I played the whole game in one sitting (just under 6 hours first playthrough) and had to play more to get the collectables to get the secret ending.The story, the graphics, level designs and gameplay mechanics were great. It was a good balance on everything.Had an Alan Wake feel to it at some moments.I know some people have gotten annoyed and complained about dead ends in the game, but they are usually people who don't really enjoy or go for collectables in games, which is what some of the dead ends in the games were.If you use the map by looking in your backback with TAB, you can easily work out where you need to go next for the story or where you haven't been to find the missing keys etc for progression in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but....The game it's good, but it's not comparable to RiME.The story it's heartwarming and the levels design are good enough. Visual style it's appealing while technically not so up to date, which doesn't actually worsen the quality of the game. Completing the full game finding every object takes some time which it's actually nice and accounts for about 10 hours.Sound wise, the music it's pretty awesome, just on par with RiME even though the later had some more memorable themes.The downside of this game it's the game mechanics itself. They aren't bad, but they are very repetitive. You haven't much to do but hiding over and over. I appreciate some stealth levels but in this game it's all you get. I would have preferred if the game mechanics changes a bit from level to level. There is also another thing that quite annoys me, and that's the extremely easy difficulty level. While not every game has to be a Dark Souls type, it's frustrating when you reach one of the few simple puzzles and suddenly you get the protagonist talking telling you exactly what the "puzzle" it's about. Puzzles are already extremely simple to have those kind of hints right when reaching one. I preferred RiME kind of puzzles and game mechanics by far.Obviously, GYLT and RiME are not the same game, but they do come from the same studio and this one feels like a step back in terms of quality.The game it's still good enough to put some time on it so I definitely recommend it but try to get it on sale. Because, even though the game it's not expensive, for the short life spam that it offers and the repetitive game mechanics, I feel it's worth a bit less than it's normal price.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting horror game, even though the art style is cartoonish/cute the subject matter is pretty heavy, as it deals with school bullying and the effects it has on children. Which is also what makes this game quite unique for a playthrough, because you dont see too many games touching on this subject of matter. Gameplay wise, this is a stealth action game, think an easier Metal Gear Solid. The story was what really kept me going, I was surprised by how polished this game is. Total game time is about 5 hrs 30 mins to 6 hours. I recommend this for someone who enjoys horror and interesting storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This was my favorite Stadia exclusive so I was really excited to see it finally come to other platforms. I picked it up the second it went live on the store and I do not regret it. 7.5 hours later and I've got 2 of 3 endings, all the collectibles, and just have 9 more achievements to wrap up.To me, this game has a story that reminds me of Sea of Solitude, environments that remind of The Evil Within 1 & 2 with a little bit of Obscure thrown in, the cutscenes remind me of Deadlight (which was also by Tequila Works so that makes sense), and when you put all that together you get a fairly compelling horror game with a sad story. I really, really love this game. I loved it on Stadia and I love it even more now. I'm definitely going to buy the physical Collectors Edition for PS5 to add to my collection (the front of the CE looks like Sally's backpack !!!)Anyway, I got off track a tiny bit with the physical there but if you like games like the ones I mentioned above, definitely check this out. It's got exploration, stealth, puzzles, a great story, etc. I really think you'll love it if you give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawless. Just a classic game. Great story, graphics, and sound. Gameplay is good, but nothing too innovative. It's an adventure horror style with some light puzzles. The map is nice and you'll probably find most collectibles with a few left after you finish the game. Using a controller was perfect (it was the Stadia exclusive game, thankfully it could move on). Good length too. Perfect performance on Ultra, zero crashes.After you finish the main story you can go back and finish collecting stuff if you'd like.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a masterful use of atmosphere, audio and level design to scare people without any cheap crap like jumpscares or gore. But this game manages. Incredible atmosphere, good story and well-acted protagonist more than make up for this game's simplistic stealth gameplay.The only thing I really didn't like is that you need to get all the rock people collectables to get the good ending to this game and those are really convoluted to obtain. For example you need to get 6 birds with your flashlight and that opens one unmarked room in the main building second floor without any prompt, cutscene or any indication that it happened. And afterwards you need to go to courtyard to the statue and activate the plaque to get to another one. And then you have to do some map cheating with the elevator to get a third hidden one. Without a guide there is no way players can be expected to figure something like that out by just exploring the level. At least most enemies don't respawn... When you make collectables this convoluted to find you should never make them have a significant impact on the story.Otherwise, I highly recommend this game. Just read a guide on all the rock people locations before you proceed to finale (you'll know when).
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Gylt is a good niche game: its got slight horror, puzzle, and combat along with  wonderful characters that gives a compelling people to root and feel sorry for. Only two characters have names in this game where as the rest our done in single entry journals that do a wonderful job in giving us a idea of what these nameless characters were like.Monster design is quite nice and simple, there's not to much going on and it works for this game.Spoilers AheadBosses, while interesting, do not have proper boss fights. Only one boss is actually fought and you fight him twice. There are two others, a stealth boss and a escape boss. the stealth one you can just ignore stealth for the most part if you have the healing to get through.There is a implied Fight or Stealth in most encounters but your resources are so plentiful that you would save yourself so much trouble by just fighting through everything.My biggest gripe is that the true ending requires you to get at least three  complete sets of collectibles that require each other for completion.I also hope that we can get a sequel to learn more about the dangers of the mountain and to either deal with them or bury them cause even though you escaped the evil the evil is still very much there. Its almost next door for crying out loud.This is a game worthy of trying out, i played it do to seeing a little bit on Superhorrorbro so if the devs wanna get games like this known they should check out you-tubers who play specific types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: People are drawing comparisons to Alan Wake and while I see it on a surface level, this isn't that at all. Nor is it as good as Alan Wake. - M+KB Lock-in is enabled by default. I don't think it is advisable to turn this off but then you lose some significant gameplay. Having it off also disables your crosshair from being red when aimed at a weakpoint so now you aren't sure what to "shoot"- AI placement and detection is questionable. The distraction and detecting leaves me a little confused but that may just me not having enough time in the game. With the distraction soda can tutorial, the enemy is placed in a questionable position. I threw the can to distract it and hid further along its path. Where I hid, the monster can detect me and there are no soda cans around. Turns out I can just run to the door and it'll sense but not detect me, even though the placement, how its facing, and the indicator all showing that if I come out then I'm screwed. - The AI (I don't think) can't see anything past its "zone". If there is an enemy patroling a specific hallway, if you are in a connecting room and you can stare at him through the window without him caring. The environmental design people drew blinds right next to the window but left the window completely bare. - The environmental and level design in my opinion is the worst offender for it being made that way because "video game". Looks completely unnatural and out of place as an actual real world location. - Less said about the writing in the story, the better. The overarching story is interesting but the actual storytelling from the writing and the environment leave something to be desired.I'm not entirely knowledgeable on the staff from Tequila Works but some of these issues seem to stem from a developer's first game. I know it's their first game as that studio label but not sure where Stadia got their employees from when they asked for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: When Emily is bullied at school she runs away, and her cousin Sally is out looking for her when she stumbles into an otherworldly place that seems to manifest the darkest thoughts of those it traps. As dark forces confront her will she be able to overcome them and rescue her cousin who is trapped too? Or is it all in Sallys mind, borne out of guilt (or GYLT if you prefer) for failing her?GYLT is essentially a young adult version of Silent Hill smooshed up with elements from Alan Wake, such as light being your main weapon against enemies and including some fairly generic chase sequences. In terms of the graphical style and narrative content it is very tweenage, with a cartoony Tim Burton-esque look to it and themes that are somewhat childish in nature, because its...uh..about children and for....uh.....children.Soooo, yeahhhh....not all that for anyone who isn't a child....This isn't like Coraline where its for the youth but is warped enough to be unsettling for adults.  This is pretty toothless, with simple combat, simple stealth, and basic set-pieces. Where it is more involving is the puzzles, which, whilst not head-scratchers, are pleasantly involving, and although I don't find it particularly rewarding as a story or experience, I'm not the age group its intended for.This isn't going to be Silent Hill 2 and that's okay (no sex-ee faceless but busty nurses here for those thirsty players ignorant to their meaning!), but you just have to know what you're getting isn't for adults. With game-play that's been done better elsewhere, and a life-lesson that's distinctly pre-teen / teen in its level, this is nothing more than an okay way to spend a few hours. Considering the generally high craft on display here that might be a harsh assessment, but it's an honest one, so there you go.Is it badly written? No. It won't win any awards but its not cringe because of the execution. The "message" is a worthy one, it's just nothing new to me and is at a level where you'd hope I've learned it by now, considering I'm old enough to have one foot in the grave at this point. Unless I happen to live to around 300, in which case I have one-sixth of a foot in the grave....(do the maths as to my age....)Bullying is bad m'kayyyyy?! But as the world gets ever more "woke", what exactly is bullying? Is it disagreeing with someone? "I like the colour blue" "I think blue is sh*t and that red is a much better colour" "Whah! Whah! You hurt my feelings disrespecting the colour blue, stop bullying me with your anti-blueisms. Respect my truth or reveal yourself to be a hater" (or some-such  bull-sh*t)"Get f*cked you snowflake!"It honestly feels like the world is one step away from such moronic entitled thinking, where everything the individual  believes and feels must have worth to it. Soon there might be a day where calling a flat-earther a "f*ck*ng idiot" is offensive, even though it's merely stating a truth you feel after formulating that opinion based on....um.....the scientific fact that the earth is round, and that to think otherwise is an indication of mental illness or massive stupidity. As an adult you get posed philosophical quandrys such as: an out of control train is hurtling down the tracks towards a switching junction, and ahead on one side is a woman with a baby in a pram, and on the other side is a group of people. You can give it a twist and say that the group is all old folks who have already lived a good portion of their lives,  thus adding in another moral question about ageism when it comes to worth, but essentially the point is whether the needs of the many outweigh the few and which side will you pick.In this game you are a bad person because you are emotionally immature....as a child yourself...and apparently DESERVE to be stuck FOREVER in an an evil dimension because you...uh...didn't want to play with your much younger cousin...?? Oof! I know life can be cruel, but that's a bit harsh considering it's natural to put away childish things as you mature and as such grow apart from your siblings. Because you didn't defend her from the bullies you are a bad person and DESERVE to be stuck in this horrible supernatural place FOREVER!!!! I mean, that's pretty harsh too, considering that your character isn't that old herself and gets bullied as well. But no! She's a piece of sh*t because she didn't either (a) get her head kicked in too, or (b) know that (as a child) she should be dealing with things that are generally overseen by adults. On the one hand you can understand Emily acting like a child, because she is one, but on the other hand:  She is a whiny little sh*t and honestly seems like she's destined for a life of prozac even before the bullying (which, to be fair, is horrific) and being "betrayed" by her cousin because she was moving away from her with age (which is bull-sh*t entitlement on her part as an immature kid)I get that these are the trials and tribulations of youth, those growing pains as we evolve into adults that are hopefully more reasoned and intelligent beings. But the truth of it is: The world just gets darker and deeper, and the "horrors" (such as it is here) of childhood pale in comparison. After, what? 30,000+ years of human development? People are still sh*t to one another no matter how old they are. Funnily enough, this isn't something the game feels the need to address....You even get an achievement called 'violence isn't the answer', which is very zen, yet sadly as a species that statement is a crock of sh*t when looking at our past, and..um...the present...and....er......our future. And also you earned this achievement by committing lots of acts of violence, so whilst it may not be the answer to bullying (reality seems to suggest that it very much is the answer) it was certainly quite helpful when it came to defeating demonic entities.According to this game, all we have to do is be "good to one another" a la 'Bill & Ted' and everything will be A-Okay. So: the next time you get bullied, try being nice to them. And then, when that doesn't work and they become emboldened by your perceived weakness, you realise that VIOLENCE IS THE ANSWER and you do your best to beat the sh*t out of them instead of getting beat-up yourself.  Here endeth the lesson when we're not in the la-la-land of twee make-believe that is young adult entertainment. Is it right to fight fire with fire? No (unless its an actual fire and you're burning things to make a fire-break). Will you stop being a victim? Probably. Until lobotomies become a cure for why people have been so sh*t for thousands of years, it's naive to think that a species which still has a primal pack mentality doesn't require alpha displays of power.This game has a very simplistic view of morality and personal responsibility, and as such is rather underwhelming by its conclusion. As entertainment it was a passable, somewhat enjoyable experience, but as a deep and thoughtful examination of the human condition.....well....that will depend on your age range as to its "complexity" in that regard.It's got a plucky, emotionally tortured young heroine! (female empowerment of the yoof!!) It's spooky and ookie and fwightening! (scary!!) It deals with "heavy themes"! (but then has nothing to say about them beyond neatly packaged outcomes for dramatic purposes) When you add it all together with the fairly average game-play it becomes a bit "meh!", but overall it did enough to hold my attention, so I give it a positive with some *coughs* caveats involved.  Bare in mind that I am a jaded arsehole and am perhaps being unreasonable about "a bit of fun", but then again: If you are doing a game about serious themes such as terrible bullying, doesn't it then invite more examination as to its worth? This has nothing to say, and given the topic, never could. Its not frightening or especially amazing as entertainment either. For the price its alright for a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Optimization seems to be a bit bad.  While the game runs rather gracefully it certainly puts a lot of pull on the CPU which feels kind've strange.  Obviously based on my hours played here, I did not finish the game.  Ultimately the puzzle aspects left me scratching my head trying to figure out how to solve at times, and I didn't want to jump in and out of Youtube to try to figure them out. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: GYLT is a very safe product that lacks depth in any department, be it gameplay, story, or else.It handles player with kid gloves, never forcing you to think about anything too much. The story is bland and characters, of which there are only three, are boring and uninteresting. The main protaginist is typical stoic character, the "villian" is misunderstood and simply needs love, and Guide is there so that the protagonist knew where to go, and to remind the player the motivation to go forward.The setting sometimes tries to be nightmarish and otherworldly, but majority of the time it mimics real world locations, be it classrooms, prison cells ect. There are only few locations where you get to appreciate the twisted nature of the world. Praise where praise is due, the graphics are very detailed and very snappy and pleasing to the eye. If you interested in exploration of topic of bullying, you will find none here. The game "shows" bullying through mannequins doing bad things to other mannequins, simply depicting as much as possible scenarios, throwing them at the player in a hopes something will stick. It's all straight forward with no nuance, and with how much these situations are depicted, considering the person who manifests these are ~10 years old, absurd. And the bullies are monsters. Thank you game, very cool.Speaking of game and its gameplay. Game allows the player to eirher sneak or fight their way through. Sneaking is ruined by rudimentary gameplay, mondane locations and aggresive UI that constantly shows AI awarness, rendering any sence of suspence obsolete. That leaves the player with more fun gamestyle of fighting, that the game also promotes by showering player with ammo and healthpacks. Despite very limited variety of enemy types - there are four monster types (not counting bosses), two of which you actually fight - they provide just enough engagement to vary the slog of playing this game. Enemies can dodge, hide their weak spots, rush you, teleport, and their attacks are dangerous. And even though I had to disable auto aim to have some fun, two and more monsters provide a good challange.That being said, enemy design is completely unfit for this game, specifically the level structure. Enemies usually patrol a small area, they cannot croutch and leave the floor they are standing on. But their locations often have many vents or highgrounds, which allows a player to simply camp monsters while they are dumbly stand right infront of the vent or small highground you may find yourself in. Vanquished enemies dissapear from the world, and that makes the locations feel empty afterwards. Puzzles are easy and straightforward, and at some point it made me realise that the game does not want the player to think, it urges you forward, but it also doesn't trust you with interesting puzzles as to not suspend your progress. This game is what happens when you take an interesting topic of bullying, streamline the story to be as simple and safe as possible, and put it on gameplay rails that are both easy and flawed, And while the graphics and high detail may attract few players to try it, I cannot see this game being a topic of discussion, fading away into obscurity not as some hidden gem, but as a very mediocre product.
