_childDocuments_.review: I feel that i need to shout this in all caps:YOU DO NOT LOCK THE ONLY DECENT ENDING BEHIND COLLECTING RANDOM GARBAGE, are you kidding me?!I could understand if it was plot-relevant diaries or something. It is not, you can miss them to your heart's content.  Instead here is what you need to do:- Collect 10 red rooks- Put 10 random (and I mean random) souls to rest using aforementioned 10 red rooks- Collect 6 birds.Some of that stuff is hidden in some asinine moon logic places. You do all that and your ending will be just abrupt and unsatisfying, and not, you know, infuriating. And that even not touching the fact that this game moonlights as anti-bullying PSA, with disclaimers and everything, and fails miserably at it. I'm serious, implications of the "normal" endings are insane, ill-advised and very irresponsible, just shy of The Medium and The Suicide of Rachel Foster (mostly because the subject matter is a little more tame). I'd recommend playing it with the achievement guide from the very beginning.The game itself is alright, I guess. It's like Silent Hill for the beginners. It looks mostly good if you don't count very rough comic cutscenes, The pacing was tight before it did a nosedive due to 1,5h of garbage collecting.I can VERY cautiously recommend it at 75% off or more.===================================================Is it just me or the grandpa in this game really looks like old Postal dude?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hesitant thumbs up.  More of a middle thumb, really.This game, overall, is passable.  It plays as it should, it looks okay and it sounds okay (ish).The thing is, I don't agree that the story is anything to write home about.  The themes here are very common at this point and there are other games that talk about them more adeptly.  Gylt has far too many moments of contrivance and clunkiness to tip over into "great" territory.On the technical side of things, this is yet another game built in Unreal that ships without DPI awareness.  If you are running your monitor with display scaling, you will have to edit the executable's compatibility flags.  This is something that can be easily fixed with a simple project setting toggle, but SO MANY Unreal developers miss it.The game is also strangely demanding despite not looking like it should be.Finally, the game has these pointless motion comic style cutscenes.  I say they're pointless because the game also contains real-time cutscenes that are fully voiced and animated.  The motion comic sequences are also heavily compressed, which sticks out like a sore thumb in 2024.Ultimately, this is an okay game to play through if you get it on sale, but you shouldn't pay full price.  You definitely shouldn't now that we have no idea where the money's going.

_childDocuments_.review: I do highly recommend Gylt. I was expecting some kind of adventure toonish-like kind of game but I found a entertaining, disturbing, creepy and fun horror game to play. The story was also surprisingly good: finding and reading the documents is really worth it. Overall a great surprise and will love it if you like horror, exploration, stealth and good story.

_childDocuments_.review: GYLT is a really good, beautiful and emotional horror, adventure game with so much to love and this is one of those types of horror games that's perfect for kids to play, but they have to be 10 and 11 as this is a great way to get them into horror, okay the story.The town of Bethelwood an old mining community located in Maine is where are little girl named Sally lives, unfortunately Sally's life is not easy dealing with bullies and generally just growing up, but it has become even worse since her little cousin Emily has disappeared having been missing for a month. Desperate to find her, Emily spends every day putting up missing poster flyers even when all hope seems lost and everyone has given up hope, but after being chased by a group of bullies Sally is soon dragged into some nightmarish and weird version of her hometown where her fears and worst memories are brought to life and twisted into a wicked monstrous forms, but all is not lost as she has found her little cousin, so despite the danger decides to save her and perhaps they can both escape this hell.Alright the likes, the story is absolutely fantastic it's beautifully written as it delves into its themes of bullying, depression, isolation and peer pressure and so much more, it feels like if Silent Hill was written by Ray Bradbury or Katy Towell, it just feels beautiful and heartfelt and almost made me cry. The graphics art style is really good and beautiful it has this stop motion feel to it like Coraline and ParaNorman, especially when it comes to its character designs. It also has incredible uses of color, scenery and character designs and just the overall design of the graphics.The levels in the game are really good it mostly takes place in a school and some of its surrounding areas and they are all incredibly well detailed from little potted plants to an arcade and generally the bizarreness of this twisted school, it's all incredibly good and quite visually distinct and makes you just want to stop, stare or just explore and see everything.The characters are really good, we only get three but each one is very well written, like Emily as she feels like an actual 7-year-old girl going through a difficult time in her life, Sally feels like an actual 11-year-old girl who's trying to be seen as mature but is still a little kid and you just want to hug them both.The mysterious old man is also well written as he has this mysterious air to him and you don't know if he's a good guy or a bad guy, but you do get a sense that he's trying to help and he's just very old and sad. The enemies and bosses are really good each one has their own unique design that really ties in with the story and it's themes, I think my favorite enemy has to be the dolls as they're really creepy looking with pretty good voices.The gameplay is really good it takes some inspiration from Alan Wake I.E using a flashlight to fight off enemies or sometimes distract them or blind them in order to get past them as you go around, explore and solve puzzles. The puzzles are very good, it’s all most all environmental puzzles and some wire puzzles, they can be quite tricky but not to the point where it's frustrating, it just takes a little brain work.The music was good with plenty of great haunting soundtracks that just takes you back to movies like Coraline. The voice acting is good not one character gives a wooden performance, each one is quite good. My favorites has to be the old man and the doll enemies, the dolls even those they has a few lines are repeated it's actually quite nice to listen to and the old man’s voice acting you could really hear/feel how sad, tired but still trying to help.The atmosphere is pretty good nice and spooky for first time players as you're wandering around dreading what's going to come out and get you. The notes are very good it really paints an interesting picture about the town and how this all started and there's also plenty of room for a sequel. Now then is the game scary, kind of yes but it’s mostly a general spookiness, sort of like Coraline or some of Ray Bradbury, RL Stine and Katy Towell’s works, we have the right level of scariness that kids and adults can enjoy.Alright the dislikes, now I would say this game is perfect, but there is a problem there's this game breaking bug that I encountered in my first playthrough for some reason when I was far in the game my stuff disappeared like all the notes and stuff, also the enemies like the eye stalks just reset, at first I didn't really care but then when I tried to meet the old man to get access to the mine, but I couldn't go through the main door due to the fact that the eye stalks were behind it that I destroyed previously and I could not fix it and was locked out of completing the game, so I had to start the whole game over. Alright then now that I told you all this GYLT is a really good, beautiful and emotional horror, adventure game with so much to love, with it absolutely fantastic story, really good characters and a really good and beautiful graphics art style.So I highly, highly, highly recommend this game you will definitely enjoy it, it's also the type of horror game I could safely recommend kids playing it granted they have to be 10 and 11 years old but still if you want to get your kids into horror games this is a good starting point sort of like introducing them to Ray Bradbury, RL Stine and Katy Towell’s works to get them into horror literature.

What's also weird is that this game was using 100% of my GPU and made the fans spin at max speed. I've never heard my GPU become so loud before with any other game. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: You play a young girl named Sally looking for her cousin Emily who's been missing for sometime. After being chased by some bullies, she tries to get back home but realises her town is destroyed and everyone is missing but strangely Emily is at the school. I had a great time through this, it's very well polished, the story was great and the voice acting was fantastic. I loved the little dialogue Sally says though-out the game and I made me jump a few times. Loved the art style and design of everything, it's so well detailed.Unfortunately, while I enjoyed the game and everything it offers, the game-play was simplistic. There are only four enemies in the game and it is very easy. The game follows modern day gaming trend where you have an awareness icon, item to distract, enemies can see you only at a certain distance (even if you're standing in their line of sight), enemies patrolling one area back and fourth or standing still in a certain location, stop chasing after you reach a certain area, no backtracking (only for collectables), follow the directed path given to you and very simple puzzles.I get it they wanted to tell a story but it is a horror game. I mean the game is liner but they still put an X on your map to tell you where you need to go, they don't let the player figure it out or even give an option to turn it off. Kinda feels like the developers were worried the game would be to hard or gamers wouldn't buy it and made easy for everyone. To get around you have your stealth and have a torch to fight back with. Considering how small the game is I wish they made the enemies much harder and opened up the game to travel different areas and paths to get around instead of holding your hand. You play as a young girl in a nightmare, so it would of made sense to only take a few hits and to be chased down, making the player find alternate routes because of how dangerous it is.There is no replay value apart from collectables and endings.Another thing that I didn't like is, they have real-time cutscenes but for some odd reason they use these still images as story content as well. Like they made the 3D scenes but realised they need more content or they ran out of time and just decided to do the images instead. It's jarring because there are some emotional scenes but you don't see the character animating these emotions you just get images which really ruins and takes you out of it.As I said, I did enjoy this game and do recommend it but it does have some missed potential. I hope they make another horror game like this but give options, open it a bit more, stop holding the players hand - let them figure it out, backtracking, and consider more survival horror gameplay. Playing the game I can saw these type of things in Gylt, would love them to go further with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a stealth puzzle adventure game with a mental health story. It isn't really a horror game but more of a psychological thriller. The three endings are almost a let down after playing 7 to 8 hours. Still, it is fun to play and I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about an American mining town in which there is an alternate dark reality and you have to light enemies with a lantern to damage them. Yes, I'm talking about  Gylt.Story is pretty straightforward, and the game poses little challenge. It is a bit like Alan Wake but without the guns, just light the enemies to kill them. And with added stealth mechanics that fit great in the game. But there is plenty batteries and inhalers to comfortable traverse the game without having much problem. Puzzles are also quite easy, no Silent Hill piano puzzle here.Art direction is quite good, and although the game is not a graphics exhibition, it looks quite good. Music is good when it sounds, that is not quite often, most of the time you will be hearing only ambient sounds. And well, the ending is a bit disappointing: there are 3 endings and even the good "secret" ending could have been a bit more crafted.Anyway even with its flaws, I think it's a good experience for a 6-hour game. The stealth mechanics are fun, the story is plain but takes on an interesting topic and not being too long, it does not get repetitive or boring.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: "GYLT" really draws you in with its gorgeous, creepy visuals that'll remind you of "Little Nightmares." It’s a short but sweet horror game that packs in everything you’d expect, like sneaking around, using your flashlight to stun enemies (total "Alan Wake" vibes!), exploring secret spots, and solving puzzles that aren’t too tough. It took me about 7 hours in total to collect all blood stones to unlock the alternative ending.But the story? It feels a bit off to me. The game tries to set up this big reveal where you, playing as Sally, are supposed to realize that you’re actually the bully, and you need to make things right by saving your cousin, Emily. However, it doesn't quite land. Throughout the game’s seven hours, we see Sally busting her butt to find Emily, dealing with bullies herself before Emily disappears into this creepy, "Silent Hill"-esque place. And once they're both in that nightmare world, Sally’s trying super hard to save Emily from all sorts of monsters.Then there’s this weird old man who accuses Sally of being a bully and sort of manipulates the whole situation, (I feel like he tried to emotionally manipulate Sally to sacrifice herself) which feels pretty unpleasant. Honestly, Sally comes off more like she’s also a victim rather than the bully the game wants her to be. The title "GYLT" implies Sally is wracked with guilt all through this journey, and yes that how she feels, but let’s be real—a true bully wouldn’t be feeling that guilty in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This game hooked me from the start, with the story and its thick atmosphere. But it's very short (I don't even have 8 hours registered on Steam), and as you make progress questions start to pile up. You find books containing "lore", but they mostly only repeat the questions, not answering them. When you finally reach the ending you'd naturally expect some answers, only to be disappointed.The gameplay is extremely simple and linear, with enemies that you either can kill with your flashlight, or avoid completely by sneaking. There are some easy puzzles here and there too, and that's it. It's good, but not great.Maybe the problem lies with me, being an adult playing children's games (because I try to find different games, hidden gems). But I'm not sure my kids (who span the right age, I guess) would think it's that great either.So... Should I recommend or not? I guess it's all about price. On sale for less than $10 maybe, but not otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright I guess..And it does look adorable...but in the first two hours, nothing really happened. I'll give it another go soon to make sure I'm not wrong about this one, but all gameplay segments felt like filler between little tiny cutscenes that just send you to the next level. _childDocuments_.review: a fairly standard stealth adventure game with light horror elements. It might spook you a bit for the first hour or so, but mercifully this is one of those modern horror games which don't try to scare you so much as unnerve you. Which is much better and the game does so wonderfully.All of the gameplay elements, the stealth, the puzzles, etc are all a bit undercooked. None of it's bad but none of it's particularly good, so most of your enjoyment will have to come from the story. which is actually pretty good. The game is on the shorter side so it doesn't need to parcel out its story sparsely, with frequent cutscenes that don't drag on beyond what's needed. You'll also be reading journal entries from various characters that further explain what's going on with your cousin and what's happening in the town.replayability is low however, apart from a few collectibles and different endings there's not much to the game. As afformentioned the gameplay is not particularly enticing by itself, so you can expect to be done and through with this game in a single playthrough. Which will take you about 6-7 hours. The are no difficulty modes or new game plus modes and the endings can be selected at the end and thus dont require seperate playthroughs.Some advice for your playthrough however, the 3 different endings are good, bad and secret. The good ending is not particularly satisfying, so unless you're going to watch the other endings on youtube like me, i suggest you to carefully collect all the clay people collectibles. There's about 10 total in the game. Don't worry too much about getting everything in your first go as you can backtrack later and you'll get a warning before the final stretch begins.Final rating: 7/10, its good but i'd wait for a sale unless the game really appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Surpassed my expectations. I love the way our character is animated, great OST, smart ways of guiding the player so that we don't get stuck or waste time, the voice acting in french was good, variety in settings and enemies, simple but enjoyable puzzles, nice graphics like an animated movie, no bugs. It's cute and creepy at the same time. The only thing I didn't like much were the drawn cutscenes and the fact that the main theme was treated in a way that is too cliché and americanized. But all in all, very good surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 .If you looking for an  alternative to a plague tale ,evil within, silent hill, outlast and resident evil  ,maybe it's a good choice to try this game.However,make sure to BUY IT AT SALE.In this game,a little girl Sally has to find her missing cousin Emily in a wired place and make a way to get both of them out of here.  Obviously Sally is  not a super soldier , so most of time you have to rely on STEALTH to avoid or stealth kill monsters .Also ,it feels good to use camera 's beam and fire ectinguisher  to fight back when it's necessary.Those  two weapons are also the tools to deal with puzzles, wich are quite easy and fun.Although ,players who have experience with  school bullying  may find this game traumatic ,so make sure not push yourself.And I have to admit it's quite hard to agree with some contents..And this is also the reason that  I may not recommend this game to kids.Overall , this game is fun and the art is cute ,the gameplay is satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Tackling a sensitive subject this game tries to empathize and transpose the player into a world imagined and derived from a place of refuge imagined by a bullied person.Very good overall story, hidden gems all over the place and a world full of "monsters" where you need to find your way around with courage and help your missing cousin who desperately needs your help and care.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually pretty enjoyable for a number of reasons: First, the designs of the character and enemies are very Tim Burton leaning, and the graphics overall are quite good. Secondly, there's tons of collectibles to locate as well as lore bits/diaries that give insight onto the events unfolding; I found the lore bits to be well written. Thirdly, the game is quite optimized and I didn't experience a single bug/glitch/frame drop during my entire playthrough. Lastly, the gameplay is a bit simple, but it doesn't overstay it's welcome which makes the story all that better. I'd say the game is more narrative driven, but regardless of the simplistic gameplay I enjoyed it all.Would recommend! Also, who the hell is the OLD MAN?

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple Alan Wake-style game that lasts about 5-6 hours to 100%. And do please 100%, the story is actually engaging enough to care about what happens to the characters and the true ending is the only one that isn't massively depressing, so please unlock it.Game play is solid, the graphics are way better than what you'd expect from a budget title, and even the cost-saving comic-style cutscenes have their own charm. _childDocuments_.review: Very much love this version of childfriendly horror. One might think that means a fun cutsie halloween like experience like Luigi Mansion 3. But no, not at all. This game is more like the book series "Scary stories to tell in the Dark". Subject matter and visuals that are creepy and unsettling, but not so much that kids would be traumatized for days after. In other words, scary and serious enough that kids would be able to appreciate the thrill of fear the way adult horror media does for adults. And its brilliant. We need more movies and games like this.In terms of gameplay, its again, approaching that level of survival horror that isn't too taxing but enough so that you can tell if you were careless you would feel it. Its what easy mode should be in any game; not a braindead mode, but a mode that you have to take seriously but can easily enough bounce back if you got sloppy. But I will give one criticism to the gameplay. Due to the nature of the aim mechanic, being like og Resident Evil 4 with the laserpointer, the crosshair provided doesn't always line up to where the flashlight beam is aiming for combat or puzzle uses. With no option to turn off crosshairs, you just kinda have to learn to ignore it. Small thing, but still notable.  In terms of story, I LOVE that it feels so much like Silent Hill. So much so, that this game could EASILY fit in the Silent Hill universe with very VERY minimal changes to background lore that doesn't even need to be found. Unless you want the best ending.Thumbs WAY up on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got that big, "Indie game that's a metaphor for depression" vibe going on. _childDocuments_.review: Overall GYLT is a really nice and a bit creepy 3rd person action adventure game with some puzzles, a bit of stealth, relatively easy combat and a few boss fights. I wouldn't call it horror since it's not too scary overall.Level design is nice, controls work well, performance is good, puzzles are fair and well designed and the combat and stealth parts aren't too easy, but never frustrating. It feels like a good mixture of Little Nightmares, Alan Wake and Stray.There's just one thing i didn't like at all: To get the good ending you have to find a lot of optional collectibles which is a bit frustrating, especially since the game doesn't give you a warning and the chance to say "no, i still have things to do" when the last mission starts. But you can get back to the campus in freeroam mode after finishing the game, collect the missing items and finish the game again to get the good ending (that's how i did it). But i still think this isn't a prime example of good game design since the game doesn't warn you and getting the collectibles requires a lot of backtracking an possibly a guide to find some of the better hidden items.But overall i'd say: Really good game! Not a masterpiece, but except for the "finde certain collectibles to get the good ending" it's at least good in everything it does.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: for $20 it was pretty good honestly. I'm not too good with puzzles but I only got stuck once or twice, the rest was pretty self-explanatory. some aspects of the gameplay are pretty annoying (one specific boss battle requires being stealthy while moving to various objectives but then seems to punish you for moving at all? not sure if I was dealing with it wrong or what.)they give you various ways to deal with enemies, which is pretty cool, but once you've gotten used to the gameplay it seems the easiest way is to just start gunning them down instead of being stealthy. they introduce various ways to "counter" this and force you to stealth but it ends up being annoying at times.the story/worldbuilding are honestly really awesome, I was able to predict a lot of things but I still had a lot of fun with it. the atmosphere is pretty spooky and fun. I actually enjoyed finding the collectibles because of how they expanded on the world and its characters. I also managed to find about 80% of the collectibles myself (which is a plus because I am very stupid and also very lazy, and some games go too crazy with hiding stuff.)they were very, VERY generous with items (healing and battery), it got outright humorous just how many extra things were laying around on the map that i didn't need but it was a good call, because on the off-chance that you managed to run out of items i think you might be screwed actually, depending on where you were lmao.there are multiple endings, but they make it really simple to go back and get different ones, thankfully. there are also apparently different achievements for beating bosses with no hits (i managed to get one on my first blind playthrough) and beating the game without killing any enemies (how????) so the replayability is there for anyone who.... feels like doing that? the stealth is way harder than just killing enemies so you won't catch me replaying the game for that lol.all in all, i'd say, if you can't decide whether or not to buy this game, watch the trailers or some gameplay online, just to see what you're getting into. the gameplay is basically the same through the whole thing so if it looks like fun, i'd say try it! if you're looking for an extremely challenging horror game, this may not be for you (unless you decide to play through with no enemy kills), but if the story seems interesting to you and you're interested in something comparatively chiller than other horror games out there, definitely give Gylt a shot :)

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story. It really hits close to home for me as I was bullied relentlessly in middle school. It felt like no one would ever stick up for me. Close friends didn't help or mention it. Teachers ignored it and pretended like they cared but never actually helped. I ran into the guidance councilor's office crying once... just to have her kick me out and tell me to get back to class...I'm almost 30, now, and I have a tough shell... I confront things head on and I don't take anything from anyone... Push before they push you... Its not a good way to be. ... If you see bullying happening... please help stop it... doing nothing leaves scars that won't heal on their own.As for the game, itself:Great stealth mechanics, movement is fluid, controls are intuitive (though space for crouch is an odd choice, but you get used to it).A great survival horror game that had me panicking at times, but not so scary that it was hard to push forward.o.o ...but those manikins are pure nightmare fuel...

If you want to spend 10 hours for mild horror, light puzzles and some action, I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: My review will not be comprehensive, just what I've enjoyed and a disclaimer for how you may want to approach this game if you want to enjoy it. Other reviews have gone into detail. I'll only talk about the most important aspects to consider when looking at its mixed reviews.Is this game worth buying? YES.Should you play all of it? NO.Is this a bad game? NO.Is this game filled to the brim with time-wasters? YES, but you're not forced to waste your time.Ubisoft treats their Assassin's Creed games post-Syndicate like they're pseudo live-service games. That means videogames mostly filled with a lot of filler. The game isn't as focused on assassinations as pre-Origin titles. In fact, you'll have more fun with the combat. The combat is the best of any AssCreed game, bar-none. The movement and animations have been the most fluid since AssCreed Unity, and although you will not need to go stealth often, the stealth aspect is fleshed out, just not as fleshed-out as Unity.The problem here is that there aren't much in the way of enemy variety to warrant playing anything other than the main quests. Resist your urges, choose the options before you start the game to remove as much of the HUD and indicators as possible, and ONLY DO THE MAIN QUESTS UNLESS YOU NEED TO LEVEL UP. Your goal here is to remove as many distractions as possible. This is the game's main problem: there is too much of everything.The loot, the sidequests, and the skins are mostly superficial at best. So if you want to have fun, and I can't believe I'm saying this, play only what progresses the story and the amount of sidequests necessary to continue the story. If you're the type of person who enjoy the grind, then there are hundreds of hours of gameplay loops for you to enjoy.In terms of performance, my experience was positive. For some context, I'm running an Radeon RX6600, Ryzen 5 5600G and 16GB of standard-speed RAM. I was able to run the game at 1080p on HIGH with over 60fps.

_childDocuments_.review: Free weekend was a chance to revisit the game on my new computer - I believe they had done because of the great delay to get this title onto the Steam Marketplace. I originally played on console (ps3) so getting to see the stunning 4K graphics was a treat. It goes without saying that the series is not entirely historically factual; This does not mean history buffs cannot enjoy the series. Norse mythology is worked into the story, like the other two previous titles (Origins & Odyssey) that had mythology elements worked in - unlike the other titles prior which worked to develop the overall story arc to the series. This was not my displeasure with the game, although I can imagine someone who is upset with history revisionism would not take kindly to the creative liberties in retelling the norse mythology tales. Then again, history revisions come from the ill-informed or those of ill-intent; With all the various nuances with each retelling of classic norse mythology tales - this game has an entertaining take on the binding of the wolf Fenrir, with the chapter spent in Asgard as Odin, whilst the protagonist were under the influence of a shaman's ritual.I simply did not like the repetitive tasks. In particular, raiding, which is the definition to go viking, or rather the raiding is where viking literally gets its meaning - The Vikingr would go viking. In this game, it's used as a means to gather resources to upgrade the buildings of your clan's settlement. The annoying part is how it is incorporated, to have raid locations across the open world map and also just three other locations for River Raids that are their own separate map. That design is okay, but it means that there is one large map with a finite # of raid locations (unlocked as you level up) and there's a few other small maps for the river raids - which are intended to be farmed for an indefinite length of time. Again, it's not this design that is annoying, but the infuriating fact is that the resources gathered from raids on the large open-world map are used for upgrading your settlement; and the resources gathered from raids at the separate maps are only used to upgrade the ship for those exact river raids, so in reality you would only do the optional river raids if you didn't want to partake in the other available content. The design of these raids, in particular, was a disappointment for myself - as a fan of the series that looks forward to each release since the original game was available.Additionally. The challenges, to complete for your 100% achievements, are near impossible on the easiest difficulty. They are not for the faint of heart, yet to accomplish them would be a feat with no reward. The other last thing I can note of my disdain - the previous 3 titles followed a formula with many of the same game mechanics; I'd hope that the release of Mirage slated for 2023 is not any more of the same, along with the next title to take place during feudal japan - which may people are looking forward to since the series was essentially playing a ninja, so now the series finally visits that time period where they can plan a big grand game incorporating those ninja themes into the game mechanics. Like, can I ever play an assassins creed title where the free-climbing isn't broken? In this particular title, you can easily get caught up scaling a mountain or simply trying to climb into a window. The only complaints I hear of the series would be Ubisoft Connect - the developer's own proprietary launcher. I'm uncertain why this is of pain to some, but in my personal experience - the bother is that you need to have the separate login credentials for the Ubisoft Connect account; This is a bother, personally for myself, because managing multiple passwords can get out of hand very quickly - so to forget that password and to be unable to retrieve the account would be a great misery for anyone without the funds to purchase the games' licensing once again to be used. For example, there's the Ubisoft connect account on my console - but I couldn't happen to recall the proper login credentials, so I was stuck creating a new Ubisoft connect account on my computer for use with Steam. I'd imagine this can get out of hand if you wanted to purchase a license on your Steam account - but Steam would prevent you from completing the purchase because the first purchase was tied to the Ubisoft Connect account you cannot log into.Although that is all speculation - I'm certain you can find a more critical take of Ubisoft Connect and STEAM from some blog on the internet.

_childDocuments_.review: For the purpose of this review, I'm going to compare AC Odyssey with AC Valhalla. If you like either or neither, please understand this is simply my own experience, and am well aware each person's experience may be different.AC ODYSSEY:There is a fundamental flaw with the game, and is the reason why I couldn't finish it. The levelling system: Each time you level up, you have to upgrade your gear, but you can never collect enough resources to upgrade them before you level up again. You could just swap it out for lower tier gear that you find all over the place, but you get attached to your current gear and just can't part with it. You end up with an inventory cluttered full of useless gear, and have to dive into your inventory every 5 minutes to compare the next weapon you picked up, then scrap it if it's not able to compete. I'm a perfectionist, and this absolutely drove me mad to the point where I just had enough. The levelling was also pointless, because most enemies just scale with you. So it was just a pointless illusion with no real reward for defeating enemy, and just an absolute chore. I would welcome a mod the slows down levelling so you can just for once enjoy a piece of gear you picked up for less than 30 minutes.The Enemy AI: As stated before, the AI just levels up with you. So if you're level 30, but you have a level 10 sword, a wild pig will probably kill you. You never feel like you've grown powerful, but rather just in an endless loop of  trying to stay ahead of the AI levelling. I honestly couldn't care if it's a real AC game or not, I just want a fun, immersive open world experience. But even I was dumbfounded how you can't assassinate half of the enemies because their level is too high. Sneaking up and assassinating an enemy is completely a pointless feature and seems it was just added to make it seem like an AC game. It's simply not fun, and a very badly thought out system.The World: The world was absolutely beautiful. The colours were so vivid, and the islands/continents were massive. The seas were far and between so you could go off sailing with your crew and cause mischief on the seas. I love the naval aspect of both AC Odyssey and AC Black Flag. I could just stare off in the distance and be captivated by the ancient architecture marvelling at what man was capable of building so many years ago. The world designers did an excellent job at captivating ancient Greece.The RPG: I did quite enjoy the RPG elements of the game. I was blown away when my decisions had consequences, and regretted my decision once I found out what the consequences were later on. I love these types of surprises in games though, and think it was a good decision to introduce into the game. However, the side quests were simply rinse and repeat, and eventually just became boring after a while. Because I have this obsession to do all the side quests in an area, I felt trapped again in an endless loop, with no fun being gained from the experience. They should really put more thought into side quests instead of just doing the usual fetch, kill this, find this etc. quests. I don't want side quests removed, because I want to just get immersed in the world and not actually have to care about the main quest, but put more effort into it.AC Valhalla:The Levelling System: So why am a ranting on about Odyssey? Because it was an absolute sigh of relief when I found out you can stick with the same weapons throughout the game and only have to level them up once in a while. The skill tree is much more fun to work through, and the armour classes all have a unique personality. Now I can just enjoy the game without having to compare gear every other second because you don't get bombarded with it. you also level up much more reasonably, and it's more affordable to level up your gear.  AC Valhalla is no longer a chore and you have more control on how you want to shape your character.The Enemy AI: Most enemies can be assassinated, making stealth a viable option once again. I could go for a more stealthier build, and it felt more like a traditional AC game as opposed to Odyssey.  The bows are a bit OP, being able to 1shot kill almost any enemy by aiming for their heads. This could do with some refining, with perhaps introducing this later down the skill tree so it feels like you have to earn it.The World: This is probably my greatest let down with this game. Instead of vast oceans, you are now stuck with small rivers  that you can navigate between with your longboat, with no naval combat whatsoever. Everything felt more compact and much smaller. I felt claustrophobic playing this game, worried that at any hour I would have explored the whole map and get bored. The colour palette is dull and smudged. Something is just off about it. I know it's England where it's constantly raining, but it just doesn't look realistic. It just looks like a blurry smear across your screen, The darks are not dark enough, the brights are not bright enough. I don't mind lower res graphics, but the contrast, colours and atmosphere needs to blend well together. Honestly on both games it's just off, but for this one particular it frustrated me to no end to the point where I had to download ReShade and tweak it for hours so that the world looked more realistic and less blurry. I head to seriously push up the "lumasharp" and tones to make it look less like a watercolour painting and more like a photo. Ubisoft needs to scrap whatever engine they are using because it's awful. At least it can be saved if you use a good ReShade preset.The RPG: Honestly, this game didn't feel much like an RPG to me. None of my choices in the dialogue seemed to really make much of a difference, and there isn't much side quests, only "encounters", which was obviously ripped of from RDR2. Encounters are okay, but I would have liked some more variety in side quests in the game. New Features: Being able to raid with your clan is a breath of fresh air, and it really is impressive having such big battles happening at once on your screen, with you being a part of it and helping to influence the outcome. I hope they don't scrap it in the next AC game, but rather improve on it, but with Ubisoft you never know. Having a settlement is also a nice feature, and I enjoyed watching my settlement grow and in turn improving my dominance over the landscape. It wasn't what I was expecting though. I though you could go out over vast lands and build settlements where you choose and decide if you want to upgrade them. Instead, you only have 1 settlement you need to work on and being in the same location so long really gets boring over time.Conclusion: Both games have their shortfalls, and I wish Ubisoft took the good features from Odyssey and incorporated it into Valhalla. If I were to pick between the 2, I had to say Valhalla is better, because it's less of a chore and more like a game, but I can't help but miss the vast open seas, massive continents and beautiful architecture from Odyssey. I guess people complained about the side quests, so instead of fixing the problem, they almost completely removed it from AC Valhalla instead. Ubisoft just can't seem to get the formula right, and it's sad because they have the potential to make epic games, instead of just average games.Side Note: I didn't experience any bugs or crashes with this game. There was one instance where instead of blocking the character from going any further, the character could just run up the road out of sight of your screen. It was actually just really comical watching your playable character run off screen up the road. I almost couldn't get her to come back as I couldn't see where she was.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a lifelong fan of the Assassin's Creed games, I have to say that AC Valhalla is quite a different direction that the franchise has taken. But is that really a bad thing?Veering off the long-beaten path, Valhalla presents an absolutely massive open-world map with breathtaking landscapes, and even additional realms of travel beyond the base-game's area (various trips to additional nations, locations, etc). This is quite a stark change from the founding games, and one that has been progressively added to since AC Origins. Another stark difference of Valhalla is the divorce between the traditional combat and stealth we've always known. No longer are the days where stealth is a requirement for an Assassin's Creed game. Now, you are a brute of a viking with a big, heavy ax, and subtlety is not exactly your strong suit. These two major changes were enough to scare off many AC traditionalist, but to put it frankly? The tradition AC format was getting old. How many times can you creep through a building and stalk rooftops to pounce on some dude until you get bored. For me, it was 15 years. I, for one, love the chance that has been made (so far) and look forward to the new face of the Assassin's Creed. Lets hope they don't f*** it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla, the latest installment in the long-running franchise, takes players on a Viking journey through medieval England. While it does have its moments of glory, this game falls short of its potential, resulting in a mediocre experience that fails to live up to its predecessors.First and foremost, the storyline of Valhalla lacks the depth and intrigue that made previous Assassin's Creed games so captivating. The narrative feels disjointed and often fails to engage players on an emotional level. It's clear that the developers attempted to blend Viking mythology with the established Assassin's Creed lore, but the execution feels forced and contrived, leaving the player feeling disconnected from the characters and their motivations.Furthermore, the gameplay mechanics in Valhalla leave much to be desired. Combat, which should be a highlight in a game centered around Vikings, feels clunky and imprecise. The hit detection is inconsistent, and the controls often feel unresponsive, leading to frustrating moments during intense battles. The stealth mechanics, which have been a staple of the Assassin's Creed series, are watered down and lack the depth that fans have come to expect.The open-world exploration, while visually stunning, quickly becomes repetitive and tedious. The vast landscapes of England offer breathtaking vistas, but the side quests and activities quickly devolve into repetitive fetch quests and uninspired objectives. The lack of meaningful variety and engaging content make the exploration aspect feel like a chore rather than an exciting adventure.Technical issues also plague Assassin's Creed Valhalla. The game is riddled with bugs and glitches, ranging from minor visual hiccups to game-breaking crashes. These technical shortcomings further disrupt the immersion and enjoyment of the game, leaving players frustrated and disheartened.On a positive note, the graphics and audio design of Valhalla are top-notch. The detailed environments, character models, and atmospheric music create an immersive setting that captures the essence of the Viking era. However, these positives alone are not enough to salvage the overall experience.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a disappointing entry in the franchise. It fails to deliver a compelling storyline, suffers from subpar gameplay mechanics, and is plagued by technical issues. While it has its moments of visual splendor, they are overshadowed by the game's many shortcomings. Die-hard fans of the series may find some enjoyment in Valhalla, but for newcomers and those seeking an exceptional gaming experience, it falls far short of the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start by saying this is a long game, a very long one at that, if you're looking to 100% Valhalla you have to know that it took me 300 hours. It's pretty fun and the map is huge with lots of beautiful landscapes to explore but try to complete it as you go or you're gonna be left with a huge map with lot's of things to do once you finish the story, which is long as well, not bad but just long, by buying this game you're getting a lot of content, so try to enjoy the variety of missions and objectives the game gives you.I didn't feel it got as repetitive as Odyssey, which I loved too, but it's definitely another beast of a game. The gameplay is similar and stays the same for most of the main story, the DLC however, gives you tons of new abilities, the Rogue-Like one is pretty cool too. Regarding the story, like I mentioned before, it's long but really engaging and with a few twists here and there, I liked how they tried to keep it a bit more grounded by making Eivor dream the god sequences, and the settlement mechanic was a nice addition, seeing Ravensthorpe grow with the help of the resources obtained at the brutal raids, it also made Eivor more "human" by getting the help of his clan instead of doing everything by himself. Like with Odyssey, the Hidden Ones story isn't the main theme and more like a background threat, which only became truly relevant by the time Eivor's viking saga was complete. I wouldn't say this is a good Assassin's Creed game, having played all up until this one, if you are a hardcore fan of the series I don't really recommend it, there's barely any lore about the Hidden Ones or the Isu, so might as well watch a video recap for that, as a Viking game tho, this game is great, and I do recommend it. Which is why I'm giving it a thumbs up. I am also happy they finally added achievements to this, I got it on Uplay when it came out and completed it there, but also got it here once they released it to complete my collection, would be great if they added the Uplay achievements here for the old games but I'm sure that's a lost cause, I hope Ubisoft adds them for future games though.

_childDocuments_.review: I've already put about 150 hours into Valhalla on another account, so ignore my 'hrs on record.'Valhalla is a weird one. As an RPG it's probably one of the best I've ever played. As an Assassin's Creed game it falls more in line with AC: Rogue but on an acid trip. The story is phenomenally good, only surpassed by Odyssey in my opinion. The is a ton of lore, more than most AC games. The voice acting is as good as you could possibly get, along with facial animations and portrayed emotions. There's literally nothing bad I can say about Valhalla's production quality, it's what AAA game development should strive to be.The combat in valhalla forces you to go melee, which is a shame, although the melee combat is fun once you get the hang of it. Bow combat is heavily nerfed compared to odyssey and lacks the same kind of mindless fun you can have being obnoxiously stealthy. The more in-you-face combat matches the Protagonist's personality.It's a little mind-boggling to me that Valhalla has such mixed reviews. While it's not a traditional AC game, we can only hope that Mirage has the same level of production quality and sheer amount of story content as Valhalla. I've seen many saying Valhalla is repetitive, yet out of all the games in this franchise, Valhalla is probably the least repetitive, aside from raiding monasteries. 15/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a dissapointment in everywayAs a long-time fan of the Assassin's Creed franchise, I had high hopes for Assassin’s Creed Valhalla, but after spending countless hours in this game, I can't help but regret buying it. Ubisoft has turned what could have been a great Viking adventure into a drawn-out, bloated, and lifeless experience.First and foremost, the length of the game is absolutely unnecessary. Ubisoft has padded the game with an endless list of fetch quests, useless side missions, and tedious grinding that doesn't feel rewarding. Instead of focusing on meaningful content, Valhalla is stuffed with filler that only serves to artificially inflate the playtime. I’m all for open-world exploration, but when 80% of the game feels like busywork, it’s a problem.And then there's the story—or lack thereof. Valhalla arguably has the worst story in the entire Assassin’s Creed franchise. The narrative is disjointed, dull, and lacks any emotional depth. Eivor is a bland protagonist, and the Viking setting, which had so much potential, is squandered by uninspired writing. There’s none of the intrigue or historical depth that made previous titles great. It feels like the Assassin’s Creed identity has been lost in favor of trying to be a generic RPG.To top it off, Ubisoft’s downward trend continues. Year after year, they seem to care less about delivering quality and more about milking the franchise with microtransactions, repetitive content, and lifeless worlds. Valhalla is the perfect example of a game that prioritizes quantity over quality, and it shows.In the end, I regret buying this game, and I can only hope Ubisoft listens to its fans before it’s too late. Unfortunately, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a game that has overstayed its welcome, and not in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed AC Valhalla. It is a fun game, the combat is a step up from odyssey even though the visuals are a slight downgrade. The beggining has some very harsh sound compression but it does get better pretty quickly. This games biggest strength is also its biggest weakness though and that is its episodic story structure. While this makes the game very easy to pick up and put down, there are also four or five too many of these arcs and the main overarching story really only connects to 3 or 4 of the 20+ episodic arcs that can be found throughout the game (all which span multiple hours), due to this the game can feel repetitive at times. The sidequests are very different than in previous games, they are short and while the game will tell you where to start them there will be no markers from there. You will have to listen to NPC dialgogue and figure things out on your own. This is very strange at first if coming from previous titles however I enjoyed many of the short and more lighthearted journeys that can be found throughout the game. Overall I thought that the main story was entertaning but was very dissapointed by the ending and final boss fight. England is gorgeous to explore, and as someone who has played both the original and newer AC games, I would say that this is a worthy entry to the series. However, like many I am ready for a game where you get to play as an assassin again. I am looking forward to Mirage. I wish that they would make a game set during the first civilization where you can play as adam and eve. This game even sets up some very good ways that they could tie the story into the overarching franchise with some very unique ideas as well as brilliant story telling moments. Either way, long story short I would give the game a 7.5/10. It is a ubisoft openworld game and isn't much different than the other newer AC titles. If you liked those you will probably like this and if not and you aren't a fan of ubisoft games don't buy this. Anyways hopefully this helps give you an idea of what you are getting into with this game!

_childDocuments_.review: (updated review at the bottom)Where I'd like to recommend this game I really can't, and before I go on I did not jump into this viewing it as an assassins creed game.I bought this yesterday after playing it for 30 hours during the free weekend, I'm enjoying it simply because I like vikings and nordic lore (though Ubisoft has butchered a lot of actual history of the vikings to make it more "PG") another thing is do not go into this game expecting any semblance of historical accuracy.The combat is enjoyable though janky at times and the world is enjoyable to roam around and explore. I'm not very far into the games story yet though as I've been going off and trying to beat raids and world bosses while being extremely under levelled for it so it takes a hot minute, though I will say the story so far is interesting but not "amazing", it has an "it'll do" kid of feel to it, I don't feel particularly invested yet. The voice acting a lot of the time is meh and the music could have been so much better, I've found myself loading up viking themed playlists on youtube and switching the in game music off. The game does not feel like a AAA title when it comes to the voice acting, sound design and music in my opinion, I don't know if its just nostalgia but I feel like the ac games with Ezio had 10 times better voice acting and music, overall I feel like there is a lack of passion behind nearly all the dialog I've heard so far.Most of the core things I've found to be fine and the game is decent, but its the underlying sh*t that is bringing my opinion way down. For example I use the berserker armour because I'm going for that berserker raider look and I've been using this set since I started playing the game. Now any normal person would assume that these armour sets and weapons such as the berseker stuff where fully part of the game, however as I just discovered, if you switch to offline play on the Ubisoft connect app (which is a pain in the ass btw) the game removes all the the online related items you have, once you go back online it will re add them however all upgrades you made will be removed and the sets are reverted back to their base forms. This is extremely annoying, 1. because I feel like I've just been robbed and 2. I'm playing on nightmare and every upgrade is important. Other issues are numerous crashes during raids that then reset your progress, again especially annoying on nightmare because a raid can take upwards of 20 minutes (for me anyways because I'm under levelled) It took me almost 4.5 hours to beat one high level raid because the game crashed each time I was close to completing it. Something I would have done for the raids is having opening each major chest as a checkpoint so if you die or the game crashes you don't have to restart the entire raid from scratch (this obviously isn't needed on easier difficulties but would have been nice for nightmare and I mainly would have liked it due to the crashes that fu*ked 6 of my runs) I could say more but I wont, in short ubisoft continues to f*ck their players and not care about their games and it not longer surprises me.If you want a half way decent viking game then go for it but only ever when it's on a sizeable sale, like 60% or more. However I would recommend waiting for another free weekend and trying it out for yourself, I don't think this game is anywhere near worth €60 let alone €140 for the complete edition.This is one of those games I will finish but wont really remember down the line.(Update) I'm roughly 85 hours in and I still can't recommend this, in fact rather than waiting for a sale for it I'm almost more inclined to say steer clear of it all together, for a few reasons. So far I will say that the story has been getting better but I still feel very unattached to most if not all the characters so far, and though I'm about 85 hours into the game I still have a massive chunk of he story left, from what I've been told I'm apparently not even half way in yet. Though the story is improving it's about the only thing I can say has improved since I first wrote my review. The exploration, raiding, item fetch quest bollocks and most of the other core loops of the game all feel extremely repetitive at this point and unrewarding and I still have loads left of it I'm going to have to do before finishing the game. I've encountered several fetch style quests where you must gather a certain amount of items to then get a reward once all are gathered and the most bull one out of all the ones I've done was one is asgard. The player has to gather 30 Ymir tear stones, this in itself isn't difficult just very time consuming as you have to run literally all over the map to find them, now since I've played the older games I believed the reward for such a time consuming quest would be a cool weapon or armour piece and from reading some reddit posts about this quest I was not alone in my thinking, however, the reward for a quest that took me probably 4-5 hours to complete was a mere 5 skill points, 5 skill points for my almost 5 hours of play time when I had gotten 5 times that amount from just running around the map. I was extremely disappointed after completing this but it was an eye opener and set the standard for the rest of my experience with the game so far. The majority of quests in this game have basically no reward making it feel like a waste of time or like your time was just robbed from you for even bothering, you could invest a good chunk of an evening into something only to realise the reward is a common item or just some silver and a pat on the back.The worst thing though has to be the near constant crashes, and I mean constant. This game for some reason just hates running through steam and I can only surmise that that is due to the uplay launcher it forces you to use. I've seen many posts online about how badly this game runs on steam since I've purchased it, saying to not purchase it through steam or epic and just get it from the uplay app directly and it runs fine. These crashes have been my biggest issue and anger inducing problem with this game, just today the game has crashed more than 15 times, I have done so many file verification checks I've lost count and the crashes seem completely random. Sometimes I can get a good 3 hours with no crashes and then just like before writing this update review it crashed, I then relaunched and 10 minutes later it crashed again. So in summary, terrible gameplay loop, super repetitive, unrewarding and feels like I've wasted my time after completing most quests, story is ok and seems to improve and is the only redeeming quality about it, sound design is still awful, the main protagonist isn't good and feels for lack of a better word just very meh, the map is to big and could have been half the size and packed with triple the amount of content, story is to damn long and lastly if you gonna get 1. get it on sale & 2. avoid getting it on steam cause it's unstable as ♥♥♥♥ on here.

_childDocuments_.review: Post-Review Edit: I have to change my stance to "Not Recommended." While the game itself was good, the game-breaking bugs and constant crashes have meant I am struggling to rush through the end of the main story with zero enjoyment. Unconscionably shoddy work for a AAA game developer, though I've come to expect nothing less from Ubi$oft.The ever-evolving Assassin's Creed franchise meets the Viking Age. The game has a lot of high points, the occasional frustration, and even a few downright awful experiences. Though I've played most of the series, most of my comparisons are with Odyssey as they are the most similar.The Good: - Fairly interesting, if very long-winded story - A great refresh to the combat system from Odyssey which makes fights a bit more engaging - A few fun side quests to stumble on in the world, including some that aren't marked. Gone are the epic 5+ long quest arcs in Odyssey, replaced mostly with scripted encounters with England's odd country folk - Several new worlds to explore broken out into individual quest arcs ala Atlantis in OdysseyThe Bad: - Frustrating parkour that seems to have taken a step back from Odyssey. It's difficult to balance ease of movement and complexity, but there are so many times where Eivor would yeet himself off towers or refuse to jump on a ledge that was a couple of feet high - Stealth. It works, sort of. Isn't necessary at all for 99% of the game, which I suppose makes sense because you're playing a viking raider. But for the 1% of the time where it's needed (see: Mastery Challenges below), it turns the game into a horrific slog of save scumming. Odyssey had a nice balance and I often switched between a stealthy and juggernaut approach. I never use stealth in Valhalla unless I absolutely have to. - A reach that extends its grasp. There is a LOT of content in the game, most of it quite good. However, I believe this good content could've been made great if they focused on a few major components rather than cramming so many things to do - The leveling system. It's not horrible, but the massive web that is the skill tree is both daunting and inconsequential. Once you get the few hugely advantageous perks (dual wielding 2 handed weapons, health/damage on kill etc), it's a slog to go through the tree and assign the constantly awarded 2 skill points. And what does "+3 weapon damage" even mean? The stats don't seem to be very intuitive.The Ugly: - Bugs. Game breaking bugs, unfortunately. In my first 20 or so hours, the game had crashed 10 times. That's 10 more times than my nearly 200 hours in Odyssey. Once I had that sorted, it very recently started freezing on menu screens after just a few minutes of play which requires me to restart my PC every time. Fingers crossed I find a fix, as I'm only about 75% through the story. - Raids. Now, on its surface - I like raids. The first dozen or so you do are pretty fun, and they are varied enough not to be immediately boring. But having to do raid after raid after raid to build up your settlement, only to have an entire questline specific to far-flung raids gets old. Until they're fairly upgraded (by, you guessed it, doing RAIDS!), your Jomsvikingr suck and constantly get downed, limiting your progress in each river raid. - Speaking of bad allies, AI is absolutely horrible. Friendly AI is mostly useless, charging into battle get killed constantly. Enemy AI is even worse - seeming to always know where you are and where you're going.  - Mastery Challenges. These suck, aren't fun, the other issues above make them much harder than they should be, and not in a "git gud" way, but in a way that something out of your control can cause you to easily lose the challenges. - Somehow, the worst of this lot is the sound that Eivor makes whenever he stumbles or runs into something. If I wanted to hear Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor make his infamous noise, I'd watch Home Improvement re-runsAll this being said, I like the game. I'm a sucker for massive open-world games that let you play how you want. While Valhalla doesn't necessarily let you play how you want all the time, it does it enough to keep it interesting. If it weren't for the bugs, I'd give this a solid 8/10. Without a handy resolution to these issues, I would still recommend the game with the caveat that the issues I have are widely reported and you may be in for a frustrating experience even outside of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece of a game.If you experience random crashing in the game, I'm here to (hopefully) save your day.I too experienced random crashing with this game, but eventually found the fix after extreme patience and persistence. There are a ton of suggestions online, all of which did not work for me, that is why I feel obligated to share this fix.My epic random crash fix (for NVIDIA cards):1. Download and launch the latest version of NVIDIA Profile Inspector2. In the "Profiles" drop down, select "Assasin's Creed Valhalla"3. In the main window, scroll down until you see "rBAR - Feature" and change its value to "Disabled"4. Select "Apply changes" at the top right cornerThat's it. You can now close NVIDIA Profile Inspector.Important: Whenever you update your GPU driver, the game's profile will be reset to default and you will have to repeat the steps above.I hope my fix saves your day. This game would have been unplayable for me if I couldn't find this solution and had it crashing all the time, which would have been a real shame.Last comment. Even with my solution above, the game will still sometimes crash. However, it is no where near as frequent as before the fix above. An unfortunate minor annoyance that I had to overlook.

I really tried to love it... and I can't.on paper this game has so much cool things such as funny world events or environmental puzzles, but they give you nothing more than fixed amount of XP which is meaningless because there are no actual levels in this game and skills mean nothing. I also tried playing on the highest exploration difficulty with no quest markers, hoping it would give me some challenge. and yeah, for some quests the "unguided" objectives mode really works, but there are so few of them.for some reason, the bird does nothing in this game. it was a core gameplay feature for origins and odyssey, in valhalla you literally can forget about it's existance. it's just a tool for seeing your waypoints and sometimes a circle of investigation area. it doesn't mark your enemies or battle opportunities - all of that moved to odin's sight - a pulse version of eagle vision with marked things lasting for about 2 seconds so you end up running and pressing sight pulse button all the time.gear is pointless too. devs went for a "dark souls"-like system where you have a lot of armor sets that slightly difference in stats and you can grade every piece from 0 to 10 quality. but these stats mean nothing and you end up just wearing armor that looks cool. I don't even know why they added a transmog because you just can wear armor itself, it has no impact.the only pros are visuals and music. this game looks insane with all the weather effects and clouds (and excellently optimised tho, it runs in smooth 60+ fps all maxed out on my laptop with rtx 2060 while origins had huge fps drops and stutters in big cities), but it's just so empty and soulless. combat is bad, stealth is bad, parkour is slow and buggy. there are so much buttons and abilities that controls are a mess even if you spend an hour trying to make your own control scheme (I made a guide on this and it still does not work sometimes, but default controls are even worse).

_childDocuments_.review: As the Assassin's Creed franchise begins to expand to encompass the entirety of human existence, spanning great swaths of time to give small playgrounds of unique cultures and people, the gameplay itself has managed to keep itself surprisingly similar to previous iterations. In fact, playing an assassin's creed game is a bit like trying a new word processing software. You know they all basically do the same thing as the other ones, but some things are easier and some features are more cumbersome than the others. You're not going to be surprised, it's not that kind of thing, for as different as the Vikings were from the Greeks and Spartan it feels kind of like the same thing. If you like it, you like it. If not, it's easily passed by.Vikings are cool so I feel like I got something out of it, but not much more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont' care about achievements; the game is a disappointment anyway. Awful graphics, poor performance, horrendous HORRENDOUS story. Quests are lazily put together with no thought to narrative depth or nuance. Any time there is a spot to explore the protagonist's conflicting interests as a leader, raider and a member of the assassins, the writers hastily rush past it.Gameplay is extremely repetitive. The UI is gross, and while the combat is decent it's filled with overused finisher animations that interrupt the flow and ♥♥♥♥ with the camera. Fortress raids are unbelievably samey. Once you do one you've done them all. I forget which one I've done and sometimes raid the same fort twice. There is little, if anything, connecting this game to the larger Assassins Creed framework. The developers make it very clear that this is a loot-chasing, low attention span, dopamine troll; every side quest description promises "loot" and "rewards" and not a meaningful story.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRIt doesn't feel like an Assassin's Creed game, but you might enjoy it if you pretend it doesn't have that legacy in it's name.I wanted to enjoy it and it even gave me the itch to re-watch the Vikings TV show but in terms of playing it, it just isn't very fun if you're looking for an "Assassin's Creed" experience. They tried to dumb down the parkour controls (functionally even Assassin's Creed 2 - Revelations felt better) but all they did was make it feel jank as you try to get through moving through the environment. The world looks great, the story is somewhat bland regardless of the fact it should be enthralling to raid Britannia in medieval times, it falls so short in it's attempts to capture my attention. I'm also not a fan of the combat nor the combat AI as you do raids, your allies will just lose focus or your enemies will, truly incredible for this to even be a problem.It's not terrible but I wish they just didn't try to even make it an Assassin's Creed game and just made it a full on viking game because it doesn't feel like an assassin game, You are a viking through and through regardless of how much you'd like to be an assassin, regardless of how many stealth perks you spec into or try to focus on, nor is the world designed purely for stealthing around and clearing camps with wit, you're more likely to give it up and just deal with the detection combat.I don't know how this bodes for upcoming Assassin's Creed games as they claim they'll return to the golden days but my beliefs that they can falters as I tried to get into this one. Every aspect of this game other than the world design feels like an after thought.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla can best be described as a 'shallow titan'.  In short, this game is massive, without a solid story to support the entire run-time of this 100+ behemoth.  With that said, there is a plethora of worthwhile side content to enjoy along the way.  The dev team has also perfected the placement of viewpoints along the map, and tied the game's story in well with the exploration; effectively minimizing backtracking.  As is the case with many releases, Valhalla's writing fluctuates in quality, with some arcs providing more engaging stories and characters.  Ah yes... Characters.  There's not a whole lot of good ones in this game unfortunately.  Some standouts are Basim, and Sigurd.  Most characters fall into some form of archetype, such as the young beta male king-to-be, the great warrior going mad, or the old king ready to die.  It is quite disappointing there aren't more well-written characters to get invested in, especially because the game's theme of loyalty is well portrayed with many of these generic archetype-bound 'characters'.To the game's credit there are some cute fan-service tie-ins to the lore to be found, though they are removed from the main-narrative.  Right... The Lore.  Valhalla, as was the case with Odyssey; relegates the Assassin's to a side role, with all mentions of the Hidden Ones being absent for 20-40 hours at a time... a few times.  Some, like myself may not mind too much the shift in focus, though it is a shame having lost great amounts of time with characters capable of carrying the game's disjointed story.I liked Valhalla.  I like the twists, exploration, viewpoints, mysteries/wealth/artifact system, and even the settlement system.  What I didn't like is how little substance the story had, and aside from two cut-scenes, how little your time spent in the world really matters.  Great potential, a decent ride, though not worth your time.

But it's still another step in the right direction for Ubisoft.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. I had previously played Origins and Odyssey. While I still preferred the other two, I still enjoyed this one a lot. Even though there are no steam achievements, they still exist in UbiConnect. There are also an additional set of goals to go for. So I didn't find the lack of achievements displayed on steam to be a hindrance. This game is even longer than Odyssey even if you go for all of the side quests in both games. I will point out that there are some crashing issues. Though I found it wasn't very often and mostly they were within the DLC. I played nearly 200 hours before I got my first crash (despite playing on a machine that far exceeds the recommended requirements). It can get annoying, but I also realise others have this issue worse than I did. The story-line is fine. But as with Odyssey and Origins, the scenery is beautiful. I am also from England, so some of the scenes and locations were particularly interesting to look at. I played nothing but Valhalla between July 2023 and October 2023. That is how engrossed I was. I would recommend this game. It's fun to play and the side quests were interesting. Smack my Bishop!

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun... for the first 30 hours.My positive and negative feelings are parted like sea before Moses when it comes to Valhalla. Without playing newer, more rpg oriented Assassins Creeds from Ubisoft I've decided to give this one a go. So for me it was a breath of fresh air into the series. But even with that, I've quickly gone to notice how Ubisoft instead of putting more quality into the game, decided to put as much mediocrity as it could.Talking about the story, it sucks because it has some good points to it. Both beginning and ending segments of the game were great. It’s the whole bloat in the middle that pissed me off in the end. There are many quests and characters in there that should have been side contents but are shoved in as part of the conquering and pledging to the lands of England. And it doesn’t help how much quests are build to go from point A to B,C,D,E,F and to even later points of the alphabet sometimes. Many of quest threads have mostly set amount of objectives, so you better won’t be going in expecting just 2,3 missions/locations to go, usually it goes around 8/9 per pledge.Characters again have some good and bad sides to them. I believe Norway looked amazing and we should have much more game time set in there. England is nice but not very assassins creed-like, 80% of the map is either open fields of rivers. Jesus how much clutter can you get into this game is incredible.I have finished this game with decent % of completion, synchronized all viewpoints, done all tombs of the fallen, done all the caves for excalibur, done a few river raids, completed side quest of Asgard, completely finished the roguelike mode. _childDocuments_.review: A Saga of Vikings Rich in History, Yet Not Without FamiliarityRating: ★★★★☆ (4)Assassin's Creed Valhalla plunges you into the harsh yet beautiful world of 9th century England through the eyes of a Viking raider, and it does so well. The game offers a wealth of content and introduces several new features to the franchise, but it also falls into some familiar patterns that can make the experience feel somewhat repetitive.The world of Valhalla is vast and full of life. The rolling English countryside, majestic Norse fjords, and towering Saxon fortresses historical detail are evident in every facet of the game's environment, immersing you fully into the games Viking era. The narrative is another strong point of the game. Eivor's saga is filled with interesting characters. The interweaving of historical events and personalities, along with elements of Norse mythology, creates a rich tapestry of tales that will keep you engaged for hours on end.In terms of gameplay, Valhalla introduces several new elements to the franchise. The settlement building aspect adds a nice layer of progression, giving a tangible sense of growth and development. The revamped combat system, with its emphasis on dual-wielding and brutal finishers, fits well with the game's Viking theme.However, the game is not without its drawbacks. One of Valhalla's most noticeable issues is a sense of repetitiveness. Despite the large map and multitude of activities, many of the quests and events start to feel very similar over time. The game also leans heavily on familiar mechanics from the franchise's previous entries, which can lead to a sense of deja vu.Additionally, while the game's combat is brutal and satisfying, it can feel clunky at times. The AI also lacks consistency, switching between being ruthlessly efficient and oddly passive.Overall, Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a solid addition to the franchise, offering a captivating look into Viking history and culture. While it does suffer from repeats and a few gameplay issues, the strengths of its world-building, narrative, and new mechanics make it a journey worth embarking on for both veterans and newcomers to the series.

For the first 40 hours or so.But then it just... keeps going. And going, and going. I'm 131 hours in to a (fairly completionist) run, and there's still a third of the map left to explore. I shelved the game when the repetition started to outweigh the fun parts.I recommend turning the difficulty up, and playing only the main story lines (and the Niflheim bits). But if you ignore the excess content, I think there's a really fun game at the heart of this.
