_childDocuments_.review: Ok so most of the bad reviews on Steam can be summarized thusly:1. The game was buggy for me (yes, it also crashed for me a few times, and loading times are quite long)2. Ubisoft integration in Steam is awful (yep, no question)3. Lack of achievements (I personally don't care about this stuff)4. Map too big/game too long/too repetitive (I loved the size)5. Too much bashing, not enough sneaking around (I loved both bashing & sneaking, but admittedly, in the early phases of the game there is more bashing than sneaking. By the end, it's the other way around)Not since AC Black Flag have I been truly sucked into such an immersive and deep world in the AC franchise. I was a bit disappointed at AC Odyssey, but with Valhalla I really loved nearly everything about this game, and found myself playing just a biiiiit longer than I would have liked. The storylines, the characters, the side-quests, the environment, the challenges... pretty everything was well-done and compelling. As a bonus, the normally-tedious VR aspect of AC games is quite minimized, and not such a buzzkill as in other titles.I don't deny that there are some *ahem* technical issues with this game, esp. on Steam, but as a true escape to another world, I'm willing to forgive all of that.

_childDocuments_.review: I am only 10 hours into this game, but I highly recommend it. The graphics and scenery are absolutely beautiful, I think it is a noticeable improvement from Odyssey. Odyssey has very idealized graphics, whereas Valhalla adds realistic shadows and lighting that make me feel like I am there myself. I find the combat mechanics fun and it pays off for you to learn different strategies for different opponents and situations. I like that most missions include a group of vikings who go along with you rather than doing everything alone, and fighting for the clan feels more rewarding that just being out for myself. Others have complained about the skill system but I am ok with it. You get frequent skill points that give you a tiny boost here and there and then every 6 or so points you get something more noticeable. This lets you fine tune your character more precisely, and is honestly just a different way of doing things. The type of skills you see in Odyssey are renamed "abilities" and you find them in books of knowledge as you explore. Some may not like the change, but I have no problem with it. IMPORTANT FIX READ THIS: I was super frustrated at one point because the game kept crashing and I could make no progress. I googled forever and found that I need to turn off UbiSoft's in-game overlay and I have had no more problems since. From the main menu go to "UBISOFT Connect" and in the settings it mentions "enable in-game overlay" or something like that. TURN IT OFF. Some people had to reinstall the game and change the setting first before playing or continuing a game. Once that is fixed it is a fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: A game that needs a middle-rating really, but ultimately it is something I would only recommend for those who are AC completionistsThe scenery is great, the gameplay is decent, but the story is flabby and in desperate need of an editor to cut the fat. After about halfway, I stopped even looking at side-quests and hunting down equipment - compared to Odyssey where completing armour sets was a vital part of your desired build, here the set perks are negligibleThe skills and abilities are mostly useless, with only a handful worth using, and the skill tree/web is a poor design choice which becomes annoying to use as you hunt and peck for a perk worth having without wasting pointsThis is a big step down from AC Odyssey, which I loved. Much of the time, Valhalla felt like a chore, with some highlights but not enough to justify even a sale purchase unless you are wanting to follow the over-arcing AC story. It's not such a bad game that I didn't complete it, but it's not a game I'll remember fondly either, lacking both the charm and mythical interest of Odyssey, and overall having a dour nature

_childDocuments_.review: Tried this out during a free weekend.My rig is ageing now (i5-4670K CPU @ 3.40GHz), and I did have some technical issues which will bias this- controller recognition (had to fire up Steam, which fired up UPlay, and xbox controller sometimes worked fine, sometimes set to fairly useless "Hybrid mode" which I then couldn't change)- one crash in my 5 hours of gameplay, right in the middle of the first boss fight (progress was saved though to its credit)Reasons to buy- exploring, discovering, and raiding as a viking in this time period looks and feels fairly 'authentic' - I'm not terribly learned in this period, but there is acknowledgement of a living world of real kings, tribes, and places. It did manage to bring the history to life- raiding at least starts fairly open ended and fun!- looks like plenty of places to explore Reasons to avoid- slow and slightly cliched start made me want to skip through most of the first two hours- still suffers from a familiar feeling with many of Assassin's Creed instalments - a lot of bloat and unwanted bits (busywork that doesn't add much, dull cutscenes and character exposition, futuristic present day stuff) which I personally wished I could cut away to enjoy the good bits- if you're on older systems, 100GB+ install and slow loads (I accept could be addressed with a more modern SSD)

_childDocuments_.review: I finally did it. I completed the worst Assassins' Creed game. Fully, with all DLCs and their collectibles.There are so many things wrong with this game. It doesn't mean you can't enjoy it. Well, you can, but... Compared to the previous few entries - this game overstays its welcome for more than 150 hours.I think maybe the first 50h or so are decent. You experience new things like raiding, a bit different combat, new characters, areas and locations. And then you hit a brick wall of repetitiveness, wokeness, very mediocre writing, constant stupid puzzles plastered all over the world. It just sucks the fun out of the game and out of you. This game becomes like a job you despise.There are a lot to talk about this game, but I'll just throw some random thoughts about it. So.Once you get to England after tutorial in Norway, you get that big map with many different areas to conquer. You can only choose to do 1 out of 2 or 3 at a time, It's all good and dandy. You go to new area, go to the leader, help him to become the king or whatever of that land and be done with it. You have to do that more like 10 times or so. Every area has it's own story and mostly its own characters. You forge new alliances, it's cool. It's like you are preparing for the one big battle at the end. At least I though so, but the very end of the story is so badly written, so badly done, so disappointing that everything you did felt so F pointless at the very end. And the story just ends. Ha. What a f. Terrible. Most region stories are very forgettable and with 0 intrigue. Most cities are the same. Basically mud and wooden houses everywhere. Only Jorvik was a fun city to explore and memorable.I only liked Ivarr as a character. He was the only one that was unpredictable, had charisma, good lines and was genuinely funny. This game lacks funny moments/dialogues. Everything feels very "by the numbers" from start to finish. The main character, Eivor, is just as bland as blank page. He (I played as male, like a true viking) lacks charisma. He feels shallow. Not interesting. Even though he talks and talks and talks, but in the end - it's just like a fart in the wind. Even Sigurd, who is just an annoying c*nt, has more personality than Eivor. If Eivor was like Ivarr... Imagine 200h of Trevor from GTA 5. This game would have been such a f*kng hit and a cult classic for the ages. But nah. What we got is a sterile character without any personality.Itemisation in this game is terrible. I didn't even need to change my armor set... not even once from start to finish. Every item and their bonuses are so meh that I didn't even bother. The same can be said about weapons. You find what you like and stick with it till the end of the game. You can max out all the skill tree. It takes some time, but what's the point of having a skill tree with small passives if you can get everything?... At least AC: Odyssey had a simpler skill tree which achieved the exact same thing in the end, and it was much less annoying to unlock skills.Power level is also whatever, there is no difference in damage done if you are power level 200 or 400. All the combat feels exactly the same throughout the whole game (damage-wise), maybe only your damage reduction gets better the more passives you unlock. At least that's how it felt to me.Then there is that mysterious order and their members.. ooo... spoooky.... But nah. You only encounter like 2-3 of them in the main storyline and all the other ones (like 30+ of them) are just random NPCs you kill if you find their clues. That's it. Hunting the order members sounds really cool, but the way it's done is just abysmall. It was just slapped like a s*it on a wall and left hanging without any meaningful purpose.And my biggest gripe with this game - various challenges (collecting flying tattoo papers (0 fun),mysteries (extremely short side quests that can be done in 30 seconds most of the time - 0 fun), 10 anomalies - (unending climbing puzzles that overstays its welcome as soon as you encounter them), Hallucinogenic mushrooms and its puzzles - (2/10 fun). _childDocuments_.review: Overall~18/20☼ Graphics ☼5/5♬ Music ♬4.5/5☯ Story ☯3.5/5⚔ Gameplay ⚔5/5Comment:Assassin’s Creed Valhalla has been a captivating journey into the history of the Vikings and Norse mythology. The game has provided me with a profound understanding and adventure into this historical era. The combat system is exceptional, with execution animations that offer fascinating visual effects. The Norse music, traditions, culture, architecture, and history are effectively portrayed, immersing me in the Viking era.However, there are areas where the game could improve. The design of the wars of conquest during the game’s story is one such area. The grandeur of these wars of conquest is often reduced to what feels like small-scale wars due to the limited number of soldiers. The repetitive and monotonous procedures of these wars of conquest are unsatisfying. For instance, the final war to conquer the last territory of England only showcased the leaders of the allies  in the cutscene, with none of their soldiers appearing. Even the army camp was quite small, which made the atmosphere feel awkward and not intense or strong enough. This issue is prevalent in other conquests as well, failing to effectively convey the scale of the battles to the player.  The second half of the main story seems more unclear and disjointed.Additionally, the game’s setting in old, primitive England results in mostly uncolonized and undeveloped land. This makes the scenery and visual impact comparatively weak when contrasted with the vibrant landscapes of Odyssey (ancient Greece) and Origin (ancient Egypt). The mythological storyline and scenarios also seem weaker compared to these previous titles.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice looking and I love the setting. They caught the atmosphere spot on. Old England folk talk is perfect, and there is a lot of content you can do anytime on the side (like Asgard storyline or a certain Roguelike sidestory as Odin), great stuff. Certain ‘blue’ side-quests were also a great laugh. The auto-pilot for horse and boat is also nice (even though it's bugged sometimes too). Actually want to get dice to play their version of it IRL.  RPG doesn’t really matter in this game, choices are kind of irrelevant. Charisma is only a part of a small minigame and unlocks like 4 options in the whole game. Getting a better horse is possible just by 6 purchasable upgrades. Raven is also completely useless, only for sight-seeing. Got a Unique weekly free item, that was OP for the rest of the game. Never understood the bad name it had for its length. Since when is a longer game bad? Well you learn by practice. It reminded me very fondly of the terrible design of Mafia 3. You start a region, you finish quests like: fetch, go&kill, go&destroy, and a lot of following of NPCs, until you can get to a big interesting battle / scene at the end. Region done, good job,  There is a try to differentiate the gameplay by stuffing the main storyline with every single tiny feature (fishing, flyting, drinking, dice, etc.) but the rest is just this repeated design and you have to suffer it through on about 15 regions.  Just finished it and already I don’t remember most of the characters. There are Yellow Pages worth of names. They’re presented every few minutes, you will get lost in it too, I’ll bet.  Collectibles. Most of it is just a wall you need to blow up by a bomb hidden somewhere around. That’s it. The whole design. Since half the game, whenever I saw such a wall, I left. If they only cut those fillers for each region, made them half the gametime, focused gameplay to quality over quantity (added achievements to steam) and fixed the well full of bugs it has, it would be a great game.  I ended up speedrunning since like 70 hours of playtime to call it a day and move to Mirage. Ain't no way I'm going into DLCs. Still recommended due to the points mentioned above, and the fact that until like 30-40 hours I was generally calling it a great game. = Worth to stop and observe, photomode the crap out it = Has it’s bright moments and very fun features, everything gets repetitive by time = Good enough, apart from like two shanties not memorable = Might have to upgrade = Openworld bosses are challenging, the rest not at all = Unreachable 100%, don't even try if you want to see your kids grow up = Some arcs were great, some were not needed at all, so yeah, varied =  = Crashes, Critical blockers … it’s got it all. The longer I played, more critical the state got. = You like Vikings? Then good. You like proper AC? Then not good. = Now why would you do that? You’ll be happy if you’ll finish it once.

_childDocuments_.review: I've barely scratched the surface of this title, even at 27 hours, but I must say it's a real treat in the AC franchise. There's a lot of the Ubisoft bloat that's in just about all of their games, and it can be quite overwhelming a lot of the time. I will say though, the vast amount of activities you can take part in is very refreshing. Orlog is a blast. Flyting is fun. The drinking games bring you back to the days of house partying with your friends. And just when you think you done all there is to do, you construct a new building in your town and boom, new activity to go off and tackle.The Viking aesthetic is absolutely a gem to the series, and England has to be one of their best maps to date. You really get to live out your Norse fantasy here conquering a new land. Plus the fact that when you go into towns here, you have to disguise yourself or people will get frightened and run away is *chef's kiss*. Gives a new approach to the idea of trying to blend in like in older titles.My only real gripe with the game is that it will randomly crash from time to time. Not sure why? Probably a bad patch, and I'm sure it will never get fixed. Thankfully though, the game auto-saves regularly enough that even if you get a CTD, you don't lose much of your progress at all. I do have a second gripe, but it's just universal with Ubisoft as a whole. STOP with the micro-transactions already! I'm glad it's mostly cosmetic, but gating resources behind a paywall is a pretty gnarly move. Granted you can get resources in-game simple enough, but they make it just minor enough to be sort of irritating when it comes to some of the upgrade progression. More reason to get out and explore though, right? (I'm talking resources for upgrading gear early on. This has no effect on later upgrades, nor does it effect the progression of your settlement.)I definitely recommend really anyone to get their hands on this title, but I would say wait for one of Ubisoft's big sales so you can grab it for real cheap along with the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it, even on sale. I bought the Complete Edition for 65% off ($49USD)I thought it was an awesome deal because I usually LOVE the Assassin's Creed games. Been playing since the very first one. Even when they were bad, I still enjoyed them. Something about AC always brought me back.But Valhalla, I don't know how to describe how bad this game looks and feels.If you're thinking of buying it because you enjoyed the smooth combat of AC: Odyssey, you should reconsider.If you're thinking of buying it because you loved the impressive graphics of AC: Origins, you should reconsider.Assassin's Creed: Valhalla lacks everything that made previous titles fun, beautiful, or even playable.It looks terrible, the graphics took a MASSIVE step down from AC: Odyssey, closer to AC: Revelations era. The shading is awful, the lighting is full of awkward edges all over character faces.This game looks visually like AC: Revelations/Brotherhood got lower res textures of AC: Odyssey/Origins.The intro was so gross looking I couldn't focus on the story at all. It just looked unnatural.The combat is, at best, stiff. It doesn't have the fun back and forth that AC: Odyssey/Origins did. While I enjoyed old AC combat, the newer games definitely stepped it up. Depending on the difficulty you choose, you can really come away with some satisfying action sequences.But this game, Valhalla, feels so lifeless and hollow it's truthfully hard to believe it's real.I can't fight in this game without being miserable. I want more direction to help with what in the world I'm supposed to be doing. Like the main character is shown with a sword and an axe, all the cutscenes have an axe, but then the first time you fight you have a bow?I just cannot rationalize spending any money on this game. It's clearly a rushed out, unfinished hunk of junk meant to sell based on its name. It carries none of the merits of the previous games.Like I said, I bought the AC: Valhalla - Complete Edition for $50USD and it's still NOT worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: My long Viking journey has come to an end since I started it on the prompt of my girlfriend (who is fascinated with historical cultures). I must give it the devs for accomplishing another world that has its richness in world building (IMO) along with maintaining standards in writing. The action RPG trend has been carried on since Origins and Odyssey, is less than half of what Assassin's Creed has been known for. Still, the gameplay style is up for variety between melee, ranged and stealth, thanks to the skill tree system that allows you to adapt your preferred playstyle.For what it's worth of the Viking saga part, I took for what the AC franchise offers, merely in the sensationalized setup to make the adventure extra interesting, if yet ridiculous at times. While I am bearing with some pretentious dialogues and characters, the stories in the mainline and on the side are mostly engaging. Even many side quests gives a plentiful treat of cultural easter eggs.Yet, after over 160 hours of playtime, Valhalla is also riddled with collectibles that make little sense other than giving minor challenges with rewards that are of little to no significance (curses and chasing tattoo designs barely mean anything to me). Even money is hardly a thing to worry about, even when finding countless junks that I haven't bothered to sell on a regular basis.If Valhalla had its fluff of fat trimmed to save at least half the hours I spent on it, it would have earned at least 4 stars. Still enjoyable for the action and the stories, overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 7.5 of 10 but I recommend getting  it in a sale with all DLCsPros+ tons of content. Maybe too much. I am near 130 hours and haven't even started several DLC quests. There is so much to do and to explore. I read that some people needed 250 to 300 hours to finish all quests, all markers  incl. DLCs and do a 100% collectible run. + I really enjoyed the journey. Conquering England with all the Arcs and quests felt sometimes strechted, but overall it was a fun experience.  + the Mystery Quests implemented as "world events" are unique and a good concept. + Raids with your NPCs are fun+ The Skilltree allows many incremental upgrades+ I enjoyed the fighting even if it is repetitive after so many hours.+ The enviroments and graphics are nice. Unfortunately this game lacks Raytracing, it would have added to the immersion and setting.+ The different weapons are fun trying out, they felt like they all served a different style of fighting.  Cons- This wasn't a game designed around beeing an Assassin. Stealth gameplay unfortunately is boring and non-fluid. Assassinations take too long and are clunky.  I prefered the fighting action.-  Storywise the Sigurd and Eivor relation was interesting, but really early in the game something happens (I won't spoiler this)  and this storyline doesn't really continue for like 50 or 60 hours of gameplay because of all the territory grind and tasks.  This feels diconnected, and especially The Order does not find a place here, too much fragmented stuff imho.Another 30 hours later after "beathing" the main story and having done the final missions I was left with some answers (AC lore Fans might appreciate it more), but I had some new questions after the "ending".- One of the great activities in Odyssey was clearing forts. The Valhalla locations are somewhat lacking compared to the forts in Odyssey.- The "finding chests and treasure"- stuff gets more and more annoying after 20 hours. After that I did only bother at all when it was about Books of Knowlege. The most infuriating moments were the "treasure is inaccessible until a main story or mystery sequence" ones. This a really bad  design.- I liked Kassandra in Odyssey more than female or male Eivor, but that's a personal taste.

_childDocuments_.review: A massive viking adventure mixed in with Norse mythology. Personally, its my favorite AC game.The story of Valhalla is about family, loss and change mixed in with mythological and mystical elements akin to other AC series games. Eivor, the protagonist, is also incredibly well written and acted out. The scale of the game can be overwhelming or boring to some, but for me its perfect. Tons of stuff to do and places to visit. The journey starts from Norway and has you travelling to England, Ireland, France and then some (don't want to spoil). Combat feels punchy and satisfying with tons of ways to adjust difficulty to your tastes. The game also has one of the best soundtrack ever created in my opinion, have been listening to it regularly since the game first came out.On the technical side, the game looks absolutely stunning and runs excellent. One of the best implementations of FSR to date.Before it came out on Steam, I had over 180 hours of playtime. The saves transfer over as well. Good to see Valhalla on Steam!

_childDocuments_.review: I have around 240 hours in this game on Ubisoft, and I can confidently say that this is one of the best games I played in 2020. Valhalla iterates and improves on Odyssey in so many ways, and it's designed to reward the player for really engaging with the game.The open world design is better. The gloomy English landscape isn't as pretty as Greece, but exploration is more thoughtfully planned with unique encounters everywhere. Combat is great; the mechanics go deeper than Odyssey with greater rewards for skill and attention-paying. I do think there's still a lot of room to improve though.Valhalla also has a great story - it's rich with lore and the writing, at its best, really shines. It's unfortunate that the England storyline doesn't hold up quite as well as the rest, because most people think it's the primary narrative of the game (since the other plots are quite nuanced) and conclude that the story is bad.The only bad thing I can really say about the game is that it's quite meaty and a bit diluted in places, which means you have to spend more time in the world before you can get to the really good bits - the endgame story, Forgotten Saga game mode and Dawn of Ragnarok DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the game keeps randomly crashing I can't honestly recommend the game.However, the game is still good enough for me insist on playing despite the crashing so they are clearly doing something right.The aestetics are masterful as always and the combat seem to have improved since assassins origin. The raid system seems very fun and interesting, however this feels like the least assassins creed entry in the franchise. The main character doesn't feel like an assassin, and the story also doesn't portrait as such, at least not to the point that I'm at. There are some cringy identity politics shoved into the game, like how the main character can be a man or a woman somhoe, or how apparently the vikings don't really get biology and they keep sending woman to battle. The christians in the game seem to suffer from the same issue. Every time I attack a soldier and woman noises come out of the armor I find it very amusing.The village building aspect of the game has a nice feeling to it, however, like everything, it has a heavy stereotypical vibe to it. The vikings are all a bunch of brutes, including the woman, who drink a lot, have feasts, and like to burn vilages to the ground because it is fun. They all feel like indestructible superheroes that can't be affected by anything. Battles are like going to the park, there is no danger, no emotion, nothing heavy about it, just cartoonish excitment.And for some reason the cristians have a ton of random monasteries everywhere for you to pillage, because f cristians I guess. Apparently all cristian villages are called moasteries, idk. And apparently they stock all their wood and supplies in massive golden chests that need multiple people to open. But we don't take the chest made of solid gold, just the raw building materials inside it. The game talent system is the most interesting one so far, very misterious and cool to navigate. Overall the game feels very gamy, with all the realism in the art being countered by a very cartoonish and forced composition. It doesn't feel like a functional world, it feels like a playground where you play viking. Oh and the sidequests so far have been strangely cringy, no idea why. Stuff like helping a couple get aroused by destroying their house because they are into viking raids...

_childDocuments_.review: I'll warn you about two things right off the bat: First, I can't call myself a hardcore Assassin's Creed fan. I played most of the titles in the series, but only a few went to the end, and the two previous parts of the modern "RPG trilogy", Origins and Odyssey, did not hook me at all. Therefore, on the one hand, I am not an expert on lore, and on the other hand, I look at the series with a more or less fresh, not yet blurred look, because I am not tired of the gameplay formula of the last parts.Secondly, I liked Assassin's Creed Valhalla more than I expected. I did not expect anything outstanding against the background of the last game and, in general, did not get it, but still I was pleasantly surprised. The only question is whose merit it is: Ubisoft Montreal, which took up the mind, or the writers of the Vikings series, whose homework the studio wrote off.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I can't stand it anymore. I need to write a review of this game and try playing one of the earlier games. Overall Game Score: 38/100Before I begin: This game has left such a sour taste in my mouth that I refuse to purchase another AC game, ever again. The problems with this game are both it and with the company behind it and it's clear they will not improve but decay. I'm not wasting money on the mindless 'developments' I can already foresee in this series's future. If you're reading this, I advise you to only purchase the earliest games for a quality experience. The audio in this game is good. The white noise of the ocean and surroundings is well done. The music is relatively decent for many locations. The weak link is the voices. The voice acting itself is often good but they aren't great because the dialogue they're given is dreadful (we'll get into that). Visuals are the greatest part of this game and that's not saying much. It doesn't have a heavy impact on your PC and plays well even on Very High settings. I won't get too much into it, however, but the FPS in the game isn't what it should be and plenty of other players have gone into it in much greater depth, so give their reviews a read too.Okay, positive stuff out of the way, let's dig into why this game is dreadful. There's so much to unpack. The game tries to do too much at once. It's quantity over quality. You can do so much in Valhalla, it's absurd but it's obviously going to lead to problems with dozens of unfixed bugs and controls not working like they're supposed to. You want to stab forward? You'll stab 90 degrees to the right at random. You want to dodge somebody's attack? Sometimes we'll listen to your inputs and sometimes we'll move you in front of the enemy attacking even if a split second ago you were rolling out of range of that attack. The more I play, the more I found the inputs get more complex and the lack of polish becomes apparent. (Shoutout to 'Redwall' for teaching me to parry when under-leveled, using a buggy system and to accept death comes for all, multiple times). The story in Valhalla is terrible. It's one of the weakest points of the game. Loose ends everywhere, illogical moments that lead nowhere, events that literally could be cut from the story because they do nothing for it and dialogue that feels like it starts and ends randomly at times. I feel like I'm watching inexperienced actors who forget who their character is meant to be in each scene and were whispered their lines just before it. Characters also don't appear to behave as they should, given the setting, being weirdly sensitive or dull at times that don't match with what they're going through. Furthermore on the writing part, historical accuracy is down the drain. The game says it's 'inspired' by historical events. Try more like they did a five minute google search and then just made up the rest. I get it's a work of fiction but the game acts like it's 90% based on reality when it's more like 15%. Honestly, the writing team should be fired immediately. Whatever group of writers put this mess together are not people I would consider writers because their incompetence shines so brightly, I can feel my eyes burning from a room over from where my PC is. I just can't let this go, can I? The modern day story line is terrible too. I think it's about time Ubisoft stop babbling in the corner and just get rid of the modern day story line from AC games. I've checked and a lot of people absolutely do not care about Layla or that part of the game. It's also incredibly frustrating to be in a viking world only to be dragged into the modern world to be reminded this character you don't care about exists. It worked fine in AC 1, 2 and maybe even 3 but I'd say after Black Flag, this just needs to stop. Nobody cares about the modern day view anymore. Ubisoft Connect is so poorly managed, I think some people would take malware over it or even see it as malware. Also, Ubisoft has plenty of time to pump out new releases but clearly not a single employee to fix bugs in their old games like Valhalla or even older games like the 'Kenway Fleet' bug from Black Flag...you know, the game that came out...about a decade ago? There's only two more things I want to point out and I bet it'll be relevant for Shadows in the near future too. This is the most IMPORTANT part, so I hope you survived my rambling to here. It's clear to anybody with a three digit IQ that the company is farming attention through controversy. Not getting into that can of worms but it's highly unethical and sickening. They've also proven with the design of specific characters in this game that they may be, how do I say this, 'people lacking empathy, moral integrity and a well-polished set of ethics'. Certain characters are given certain stereotypes based on certain characteristics that prove the developers see certain humans as 'lesser'. Furthermore, the developers have been actively engaging in censorship, so if you thought you had any credibility left, Ubisoft, that's cute. The second important point that I hope people remember going forward with future releases is that this game has been designed to be predatory of your time. It's manipulative. You're encouraged to take rivers everywhere, where they'll flash glowing points where you can raid constantly, making you want to spend time doing so. They've made the settlement construction based on finite resources you can only get from certain locations so if you want to build up your base, you need to hit all of them for raw materials. You won't be told clearly that some structures in the base don't give you access to something that's important or fun (like some buildings being purely for cosmetics), encouraging you to spend MORE time hitting specific locations. The grind in this game is designed maliciously. They want you to play as much as possible, to the point where instead of an open world where you can strike anywhere and do as you please, it's more like you're somebody in a viking costume with a shopping list and the promise of candy for checking off everything on the list. Thank you for reading all of this. I'm sure I missed some other problems but I think I've said enough to prove that this is not worth your time and money. Please do not feed a company that deserves to starve and do not support creators that actively help feed companies like this. There's a deep-seeded rot in Ubisoft, only when their sales tank will there exist even a slim chance of digging it out.

_childDocuments_.review: great  game so far, if a bit split between being a viking game and a stealth assassin game (a concept of opposing themes and playstyles that the franchise has struggled with for a long time), but at least both styles of play are excellently tuned so it doesnt bother me much.  the stealth play is tight and clean and fun, and few things in this franchise have been more satisfying than rowing up to an outpost/village with your longboat full of warriors, blowing your horn and raiding all you see.  i hear what people have complained about the game being almost too big. im only a little ways into the plot so far and i dont mind a long game, but the map is HUGE, and vast portions of it are essentially empty (if beautiful landscapes) with little incentive to explore it outside of missions. but as this is essentially fully optional, it also doesnt bother me much, with fast travel and a horse and a ship to help navigate more quickly.my biggest complaint tho, is how unstable it is. i dont mean that its full of bugs and stuff, for the most part it actually runs silky smooth even on full ultra settings (aside of course from the ubiquitous control issues that have always plagued the franchise, such as jumping to your death rather than to  that obvious ledge right there in front of you, or up onto a fence when you just wanted to run past it, etc), but it DOES hard crash on me at least once (often several times), nearly every session! and given that the game has so many unskippable intro splash screens, and it always takes nearly a minute to check for addons every time you load the game, combined with not too bad but still long enough overall loading screens, when it does crash, its several minutes before you can get back into the game again, and this is very annoying and frustrating. it would be much better if you could just skip the stupid intro screens like you can with most other games. but no, you have to wait on them every time, and having to wait on them 2-10 times every play session eats into valuable playtime, and given how long the game reportedly is, this will add up to literal HOURS of wasted time in the long run...still tho, its a solid addition to the franchise so far and i will definitely enjoy playing it  through to the end.EDIT: i was able to find an easy guide that helped tweak some system settings, which has helped with the crashing (a known and common issue with the PC version of the game). it hasnt completely stopped the issue, but it has helped. it still crashes too often, but its better than it was...

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh thsi is my fav AC game so far. Comparing it to the Odyssey they improved a lot of game mechanics and story mission. The game does not feel so overwhelming like the previous one did. The custom village idea is 10/10 imo. Many new mechanics, like eating, leveling up mount's stats or even beeing able to finally !OPEN DOOR!People say its a long game, that takes even more time to fully finish the prologue. I dont see it. It was rly smooth for me. The story is catching and easy to follow. I LOVE that they "hide" map marks now, allowing me to better relax, instead of chasing every single question mark on my way, which was draining in previous games. Now even short 5min activities i find on my way are an adventure.  The mini games are super fun - i always participate whenever i have a chance - dice game is my fav! They got rid of a ton and ton of usless iteams we were getting from every dead body in AC Origin and Odyssey... They even reworked the numbers. Instead of collecting 173649924 coins for another usless weapon upgrade, they made it simple - we need 10-40, but we collect 1, sometimes maybe 2 from loot. Feels more real. They also got rid of the mercenary system!! (biggest + tbh)I know many people hate on skins in new AC games, but i have always been fan of those. The cosmetics in Vallhala deff are the peak so far (there are collabs as well! <3) I dont buy them, but collecting exotic currency from around the world is enough to get you what you want. I feel like noone talks about it, but you can easly get every single cosmetic skin for free, if you are patient enough. Ive got almost all of them in previous game, its much more rewarding too!Fans of the "old" AC games might feel cheated on, since its not a game about...well... assassins. Its a great viking game, with a great "follow-along" story. The game has brotherhood background with i would say - around 10% quests following that topic. The rest is pure viking expirience. _childDocuments_.review: AC Valhalla is a very broken game, and a very long game. I've put in 300+ hours according to Ubisoft's REQUIRED terrible launcher. Here's what matters.Gameplay: 6/10. There are some fun moments to be had here, but they are marred by the incredible jank, particularly in combat. Plays sort of like darksouls, without good hitboxes. The controls are responsive enough, but by no means tight. It feels very floaty and "hit with pool noodles" for a lot of weapons. We won't get into the hilariously unfinished execution attacks or buggy enemies.Story: 3/10. Honestly, I dont play AC games for the story, but this one was particularly boring. I couldn't care less about it. Arrive in England, conquer England. The end. There's some tacked on Animus stuff, but at this point who cares? The developers clearly didn't.Dialogue: 2/10. There are some good moments, but holy hell. As a writer myself with a focus on dialogue, much of this was very painful. It essentially boils down to: What is happening right now? The characters say exactly that. Repeat. No nuance whatsoever, mostly pure pain with some rare gems. Good (or impressively terrible) voice acting can't do much for bad writing.Visuals: 9/10. It's very pretty. Many people care about graphics, but I am not one of them. I prefer a polished, fun game. That being said, even my old grumpy ass appreciated some of the stunning landscapes (particularly in Norway.)Open World: 6/10. Holy hell is this big. That's about it.  It's gigantic, but not particularly meaningful. But they went BIG.The Verdict: If you like a huge gigachad-sized map that's very pretty, with an absurd amount of barely meaningful collectibles, you'll like this. You'll need to get past the janky combat and impressively boring story and writing, though. The game might actually be better if you skip all dialogue and simply smash and loot.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla. A typical Ubisoft game. A so called Ubisoft Original. A great open world bottlenecked by a "storyline" that's okay-ish at best but why did i hit the recommend button? Most likely because there is still no neutral review option on Steam.As i previously mentioned, the open world of AC: Valhalla is fantastic. There is no shortage of serene landscapes, astonishing pieces of architectures and vivid cities. In one moment you're daydreaming in colorful fields with a chill spring breeze down your neck and moments later you're knee deep in gloomy, disease-ridden swamps. Green forests, tall mountains, freezing cold regions as well as crypts: This game's design is incredibly diverse and exciting. I must admit that i'm not really into ancient nordic history and mythology yet Ubisoft has created a world that's simply breathtaking even for modern gaming standards. In addition to that, the environment is filled with some minor world events like in Red Dead Redemption 2 and some small yet fun activites like tabletop games, drinking duels and flyting competitions. The gameplay is not really much different to the previous Assassins Creed titles. As a matter of fact the mechanics feel not much different to those from Origins and Oddysey. The enemies in Valhalla are wide-ranging but have been mostly taken over from the mentioned earlier titles in the series with a few new yet neat additions. Some enemy types are archers, brutes, swift lightweights, pikemen and the new pyromancers. No worries though, every one of them feels unique and do offer an own arsenal of attacks and weaknesses. You, as the protagonist, can choose between light or heavy axes, greatswords, hammers, daggers, shortswords, a variety of shields,different bow types and plenty more. There is a playstyle suited for everybody. Furthermore, the skill trees aren't just simply base stats improvers but contain entire new attacks and animations that can be used as an advantage during combat.As someone who played both AC Origins and Odyssey i was kinda afraid of the non-stop grinding that took the fun out of both games for me. Luckily, the gear and weapons do not have any level locks anymore! Yet what remains are level-locked regions. Sure, you can move to those regions at any given time but you'll get mauled by wolves because they're a much higher level than you. Okay, maybe it's not that severe but enemies will be alot stronger than you even though they're the exact same ones as in the other regions. Instead of farming XP you'll spend a great amount of time gathering materials for your own settlement in order to build new buildings such as vendors or stalls. A similar feature was introduced  in AC: Brotherhood. If you plan to build your own collony be ready to raid settlements with your crew and if you plan to improve your armor prepare for a search through the entire world as the crafting materials are in hidden containers throughout the map. They are marked on the (mini)-map though once you come close to them! Why did i put the word "story-line" in quote marks earlier? That's because there is no real storyline. Rather a dozen of major side quests that will lead to the grand final. Those are linked with each other but you can choose the order as you like. Thus there is no real main antagonist but plenty of minor ones. The below average story line with its shallow and stereotypical characters is definetely the number one weakpoint of AC Valhalla. At least half of the time you spend helping out other settlements and each region has its own unique story arc. Moreover, you can choose Eivors gender and between a few hairstyles and tattoos. Most of which you have to purchase with ingame money at vendors. Just like Kassandra being canonically accurate in Odyssey, i recommend playing as male Eivor. In my opinion his voice actor did a fantastic job.Remember when Ubisoft removed crossbows from a game because they were not historically accurate? Those times are no more: AC Valhalla feels like a fantasy game with glowing weapons and colorful skins. Eivor is walking around in heavy plated knight armor. Aren't assassins supposed to be light on their feet? This game feels like anything BUT an Assassin's Creed. Ubisoft being Ubisoft, there are plenty of microtransactions. Microtransactions.. in a full price singleplayer game.. sigh.. I guess we have to thank Bethesda for its horse armor DLC back in Oblivion. The good thing is that they're clearly optional and don't affect the story. The bad thing is that they simply exist. Even single player gaming is becoming a money milking industry with Ubisoft and EA being the pioneers... but should you buy it? The answer is pretty simple. Do you like the Ubisoft open world formula? Did you enjoy Origins and Oddysey? Do you like free roaming and exploring? Then go ahead, this game is worth the price. Do you want to enjoy and concentrate on a fleshed out storyline with unforgettable characters and decisions? Make sure you  stay way clear from this title. A great game that focuses on an amazing storyline around the nordic mythology is God Of War, which is a unique masterpiece. For achievement hunters it is crucial to mention that the Steam version doesnot have any achievements and trading cards for whatever reason. However, there is a pretty decent photo mode which i personally enjoy very much!Feel free to share your thoughts on Assassins Creed Valhalla down below.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to express the level of rage and disappointment that Travis Scott's so-called "Utopia" album has left me with. It is an absolute trainwreck of a project that utterly fails to live up to any of the hype or expectations set by the artist himself. From start to finish, this album is a nightmarish disaster that should be avoided at all costs.First and foremost, the production is a chaotic mess. It feels like a jumbled collection of random sounds slapped together without any rhyme or reason. There is no cohesion or artistic direction whatsoever, making it nearly impossible to enjoy any of the tracks. It's like Travis Scott threw every sound he could find into a blender and called it music.But it's not just the production that's a disaster. The lyrics are equally terrible, if not worse. Scott's attempt at being deep and introspective comes across as nothing more than pretentious rambling. It's as if he believes throwing in some vague references to his struggles will automatically make the album meaningful. Well, newsflash, it doesn't. Instead, it just feels forced and insincere.Furthermore, the guest features on this album only add to the mess. It's almost as if Travis Scott chose artists randomly from a hat without any consideration for how they would fit into the overall sound. The collaborations feel forced and unnatural, and some artists are wasted on tracks that do absolutely nothing to showcase their talents.And let's talk about the lack of innovation. Travis Scott was once praised for pushing the boundaries of hip-hop and rap, but "Utopia" is a giant step backward. It's filled with generic trap beats and clichéd auto-tuned vocals that have become the bane of modern hip-hop. There's nothing fresh or exciting about this album; it's just a regurgitation of tired tropes.

_childDocuments_.review: ********** MAJOR ISSUES, READ THE UPDATE ***********I'm not recommending that people play this game for a very good reason... Crashes and major bugs are that reason.The game itself is enjoyable and I had already completed my original play-through on PS4 when the game first launched. I completely moved all my gaming to PC and have never looked back at consoles. Valhalla was fun when I played through the entire story originally, but the bugs are so bad that I don't want to risk anything happening to my PC. I bought this game last week ( 12-9-22 ), after the initial download and boot up I got about 2 minutes of gameplay before it crashed. After reading about issues it was recommended that all graphic settings be turned down. I went to relaunch the game and it was asking me to download the entire thing again...? Okay, I thought that was really strange, the game crashed and somehow deleted itself. I restarted my PC and what do you know, the game is back. I launched the game again and got about 30 minutes of play ( turned graphics down to medium ) before it crashed yet again. Okay, I guess the graphical settings need to be a potato quality to run on a high end PC. I go to relaunch and the game is asking to be downloaded again. I decided to search my storage and saw that my D drive was missing, with only the C drive showing as available. I restart the PC and guess what, the D drive is back. I launch the game again and turn the graphics far lower than they need to be for my PC. I get 2 hours of play time and it crashes yet again, and like every time before my D drive is missing.I'm not sure what would cause this as I can't seem to find anyone else having this issue, but the game crashes are somehow causing some kind of corruption on my new 4TB NVMe. M.2 SSD. The 6 months I've had this SSD, I have never had a single issue with it, Valhalla is the only game that has ever caused this issue and it scares me enough that I'm just done playing it until the issue is fixed.******** UPDATE ********Developer suggested I start a support ticket which I did. ( Case number 17556852 ). The rep asked for my MSINFO text file along with my DxDiag file, which I provided. Rep said that they would need to escalate the issue as it couldn't be resolved over chat and I completely understood that. I get an e-mail shortly after the conversation ( BTW I waited 2 hours in queue to chat with support ), and the e-mail says per the initial conversation that my $800+ newer NVME M.2 SSD is somehow at fault for the crashing when it was only Valhalla that caused this issue of my disappearing drive. This support rep said I should replace this drive and try the game again LOL. Not on your life, I'm not risking another $800 drive to try this game again. We even had that conversation in chat when they asked why I didn't try to re-download the game on to my  C drive. I said I wasn't willing to risk another drive.So basically the developer response has been less than helpful, I wasted 2 hours of my time to try and provide the suggested info for the rep to say they were escalating this, just to close the case and say my drive was faulty when everything points to this game crashing that caused this.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game. The viking setting feels okay, clothes, weapons, scenes are good. Villages, towns, feels lively. Graphics are good.  At first, raids feel... raidish, and later they feel rubbish. Learned fast that raids are seriously about running in, getting the 1-4 big treasure box, then leaving. If you don't die, you will always succeed. Big sieges are even worse in this, you just have to rush to objectives, then everyone will advance. You can literally fight forever if you don't go objective, enemy spawns out of nowhere constantly. Oh and when you advance, suddenly your teammates are already fighting in the area, which was inaccesible by them a few seconds ago :D Abilities are unlockable, but you can win the game without them (I only used 2 frequently, but just to advance faster).  Skills matter until you reach around power level 140, you just have to learn to parry and dodge, some skills boost them, if you learn those you can beat enemies with 100-200 level higher then yours. Items can be found, they add buffs, but not much, and not worth the effort. I finished the game with upgrading the basic raven clan set, and 2 axes I got at the begining of the game. I can say the story is just as fluctuating between bad and good, as the gameplay. The real world story is close to non-existing. It continues the ac3-odussey storyline, but you will only know 2 times that a world exists outside animus.  Eivor story is also a bit messy, his/her personality switches randomly, which can be okay, because of the main plot, but his/hers gender does that too, even if you fix it to one, there are parts where he just suddenly becomes she for a cutscene, or just the beard dissapeares :D In terms of morals, it's very twisted, It's hard to justify the things we do. I mean, how can we be the good guys, while we rob every military building and monastery in England? Also I find it funny that you can only kill soldiers, and order member, if you start killing civilans, the animus well desync. Didn't know vikings were such nice people. Side quests (world events) only good to boost exp and power level, but doesn't add much, some are fun, but will get tired of other activities fast. Pledging territories have the same quest structure: go there, talk some, go talk at some other place, get attacked, talk at another place, oh evil somewhere, free some people or get something, get back, assault a fort or monastery, we are friends now. The bigger assaults just doesn't feel bigger, because there won't be more soldiers, just your allies as unique soldiers, but they do as much as common footsoldiers, fighting in the background with not doing anything else. It's just feels like a low budget historical documentary. You can only loose them if the story has in it. The Order of the ancients (later in time templars) are a bunch of burnt out common folks, you won't even meet most of them, just when you found enough clues, they have close to 0 impact on the world, it's like ubisoft didn't have the time to add them to the world properly.  Some of them at least has proper story, i would think that the 5 most important ones, but not :D Sigurds part in the story, and his character developement is shallow too, he is just there, doesn't do much while Eivor does everything, then gets mad for a while, then he gets well. In the begining and in the end he has crucial part, other than that, he is just a guy traveling around having a god complex. In overal the game is okay as a viking game, for an AC game it's not really. Characters mostly blunt, plot is weak, story is pointless many parts. Fun to play for a time, but it gets boring after a few territory pledge, and some quests are annoyingly slow. Get in when the price is lower.

_childDocuments_.review: I will give it a positive review, if only for the sheer amount of work on display. Saying that the game is huge is an understatement. Sadly though, it's not a good direction for the series, probably why they changed the gears with the new Mirage entry. I finished the main game in equal parts entertained and exhausted. Then I started ragnarok dlc and got even more exhausted. But then the other two dlcs are actually better paced and generally better than the main game. The ending is fine but it's no odyssey. The prologue is what actually is really strong.Now seeing that the game has mixed reviews is actually super accurate, cause mixed is what my feelings are towards this game. Another problem that should've been immediately apparent to anyone in the first brainstorming session is that a skyrim/kingdom come-like rpg in the viking dark ages might be a great idea, however the same cannot be said about an AC game because the one thing that everyone immediately think of when you say Assassin's Creed, is climbing on tall beautiful architecture. This obviously cannot be done in rural areas. This is what happens if you pander to idiotic fans rather than trust your years of experience and education. I would rather trust you, the ubisoft that gave me Unity, to choose a region and period which you think might fit the core gameplay loop, than change the gameplay loop and make it a witcher-lite just so you can satisfy some cretins. Thing is, for some reason I still thing Ubisoft has the chops to pull a great 15h perfect game. God knows they got the money and manpower. They came pretty close a few times in the franchise.The final sieges of each region are fun. The overall story arcs are generally good but in 100 hours, of course it feels diluted as hell. There are some leaps in logic, in the story, but the dialogue is actually quite good so it kinda balances it out. They took from god of war the thing were someone tells you stories while you sail your boat but they are extremely boring and not related to anything happening. The pesudo-nemesis system is still here and it's more token than ever. The mythic beasts from odyssey are back but is more backbones and token than ever. The equipment revamp they did after odyssey is worst than ever, and I ended up using the same weapon and clothes for all my playthrough + dlcs. The base management idea is good, and it really ends up feeling a little bit like home but it just lacks things to do and interesting conversations to have. You build and upgrade it and eventually more and more people start living in it but it would've benefited from a system akin to Fire Emblem/Midnight Suns. If you want me to get used to something and feel like home in an area, then make me spend time in it. Preferably quality time and not dumb busywork, anyway.The game is way too easy as it is so the best advice I can give you is don't do any markers on the map. These are really boring anyway. Just try to bee-line the main arcs.Oh, I really like the protagonist. I mean the female one. The male one really is dragging down the experience. So if you buy this, just play with the woman. If it helps you sleep better, know that it's cannon anyway.I suppose at this point I should mention that even without dlss and raytracing, the environments and lighting effects look great and the game runs smoothly. The cloud looks noticeable like ♥♥♥♥ and the characters design and animation look early last gen. Little to no bugs. Unimportant glitches here and there are present but nothing to nitpick about. All in all, for this colossal a game, one could say it is bug-less.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla, the only assassin's game that does everything but be an actual assassin. This game is terrible at stealth, the spotting and detection mechanics are horrendously implemented and barely function. Enemies will spot you in an instant before you can react if they find a body and will spot you from miles away. Hiding in bushes barely works as enemies dont even have to check them to already notice youre in there. Enemies will notice an arrow hitting the ground and will find the exact spot from where it was shot no matter the distance. Assassinations bug out on ledges and sometimes lead you to missing your kill. Enemies will detect you if youre above or below them no matter the angle as if they have eyes on the tops of their heads and the soles of their feet. Ledges are poorly done and if you move to close to them your character decides to jump down, as i continued playing the game i noticed that this got worse and worse as Eivor would jump down from larger ledges, this and the poor assassinations on ledges led to me dropping right on top of enemies. The combat system seems to have been dropped half way through as the ideas- skills- weapons- all seem well planned out but the actual combat is just bland and boring spamming, the ai never really tries to fight back and when it does it usually decides to break through blocks or become very predictable. The only thing enjoyable about this game is the graphics and detail on weapons and armor, other than that the stealth is sad, the combat is poor, and the story is written by 16 different writers without any connection with each other. Oh and dont get me started on the quests, you can barely figure out what quest to do first which leads to weird storylines and poor context. A horrific successor to origins and odyssey that brings shame on the AC Title series.I loved ac origins for its exploration and combat mechanics and loved odyssey for its vast map with so many missions and content, Valhalla could have been the holy grail created by the feedback of the last two games but instead it is in my opinion, a game with lost potential.

_childDocuments_.review: A disappointment to the Assassin's Creed series, even by the standards of their recent games. Initially, I'm annoyed by the lack of steam achievements, which the previous games have had.The combat cinematic are repetitive, and way less smooth than any previous game, which really sets a new low for the franchise. Though I can't put my finger on it, the general movement and climbing also feels very clunky. The intro to the game was breaking new barriers... for how boring it was. To top it off, it felt very devoid of emotion. Maybe they wanted a stoic viking, but that doesn't help me connect with the character.I've known Assassin's Creed to be the franchise to go to when you want a cinematic combat experience, but this game really shows how much they've strayed from that. Syndicate was the last game for good cinematic combat, and Black Flag was the last game for good story and atmosphere. Every game since Black Flag almost seems to be competing to be a bigger joke than the last.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Achievements were just released for Assassin's Creed: Valhalla on 7 October 2024. So I think this is a good time to offer my review of the game. Having completed it twice. The steam achievements are backwards compatible. What I mean by this is that after 8 October 2024 anyone who opens AC: Valhalla from Steam gets all their previously-earned achievements added to their account.Okay, on to the review.AC: Valhalla was released on PC and consoles at 10 November 2020. I first played and completed the game in early 2022 on the Xbox Series S console. I really enjoyed that play-through and I completed AC: Valhalla in under a month without buying any DLC. Although, there was a game-breaking bug to do with (spoiler!) fighting an antagonist, Dag. Let's call it the "Dag Bug". The Dag Bug was even more painful given that it would still break the game even if you loaded an old save. I think the bug just subsided one time and I was able to make a save past it, in a very fortunate moment. The Dag Bug didn't appear on the PC version by the time I played the game for PC. Again, I really enjoyed the game; the experience, the graphics, the atmosphere of the world of vikings, the mechanics, the voice-acting, and the lore.I enjoyed AC: Valhalla so much that I decided to buy the game again when I saw a great deal. This time on PC rather than console. And I played with an Xbox Series X controller which works perfectly for PC. In July 2024 I saw a deal on Steam for the Complete Edition of AC: Valhalla and all its DLC for just £30 (€35.83 and $39.22). That was one hell of a deal and I took it. The deal was so good, look at this: at the time of writing the game alone is priced at £49.99 (€59.72 and $65.36) and the Complete Edition is £116.99 (€139.77 and $152.96).AC: Valhalla is really good for the experience, the graphics, the atmosphere, the mechanics, the voice-acting, the lore. And probably more stuff that just isn't coming to mind right now. I played and enjoyed AC: Origins (on Xbox 360) and I would say AC: Valhalla is even better than AC: Origins. Which is a tremendous feat.Again, this is my second time playing through AC: Valhalla. This time with the Complete Edition, which includes all the DLC, so I have loads and loads of game-time with this. That suits me well because I love having loads of game-time with a really good game.For me the game in the Assassin's Creed universe that AC: Valhalla was trying to one-up would be AC: Origins. And I believe the developers hit the nail on the head.What a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a beautiful game that simply feels too big, and too empty. To start, some good points. Valhalla is stunning. Travelling across viking-age Britain, you get to encounter a number of moments that encourage you to just stop and stare. The combat is also not terrible. Though it doesn't feel as tight as previous entries, it still is pretty fun. Now for the negatives. Assassin's Creed: Valhalla feels huge, but also empty. Though there are things to do sprinkled about, they all feel the same, and the amount of progression earned feels pitiful. Combine that with a system that necessitates levelling up, and it just feels slow, glacially slow. The perk system while levelling is also horrible. Much like previous entries, levelling up unlocks abilities... sometimes. Between each ability is 5-6 points of stat boosts, that don't feel like they do anything. An example might be +1.5 ranged; what does this mean? Who knows! The game also retains Ubisoft's characteristic jank, with floating characters, and all the rest. Finally, despite the massive world, it feels like their is nothing to collect. While some may have disliked the amount of throw-away armour is Odyssey, Valhalla goes in the opposite direction, with minimal armour or gear to collect, discouraging exploration. The cult, which returns, doesn't even always drop gear, making even defeating them feel pointless. I have yet to try the DLC, partially due to frequent crashes, but for the main game, it just lacks the charm of the previous entries, making it hard to recommend. Also, no achievements. Not a deal breaker, but a disappointing omission nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a game that unequivocally screams 'Vikings' from start to finish. If you're content with immersing yourself in the world of Norse warriors, breathtaking landscapes, and epic boat journeys, then this game is tailor-made for you.With Assassin's Creed Valhalla, you'll get to indulge in Viking forced down your throat – from executing stealthy assassinations amidst historically rich locations to embarking on exhilarating raids on unsuspecting towns. Did I mention Vikings? Yeah, I guess you're also a Viking.While I can't deny the allure of the game's stunning graphics and the palpable atmosphere of the world, I must confess that I find myself more drawn to the exploration aspect rather than the storyline. There's a certain satisfaction in charting uncharted territories and discovering hidden secrets, especially when every corner of the map is steeped lazily with "Viking" lore.In essence, if you're seeking a gaming experience that's all about Vikings, Vikings, and more Vikings, then Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the game for you. Just be prepared to lose yourself in a world where every aspect of gameplay "revolves" around the legendary Norse warriors. Vikings. Before you buy, please watch Spongebob Squarepants, Season 6, Episode 4: Dear Vikings/Ditchin'; you will then, and only then, understand Assassin's Creed Valhalla. Truthfully, I barely recommend this game, as anything more than it is. Vikings.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the warning at the beginning of the game that the plot is purely fictional, it's laughable how Ubisoft loves to pretend they "value history" and try to keep their games from delving too deep into fantasy. However, their so-called "control" only seems to apply when it comes to references that might be deemed too harsh or cruel by today's standards.This so-called adherence to historical accuracy becomes glaringly hypocritical when you can't even kill the head of the Order of the Ancients. Historically, he was a complete ***hole , and deserved it, but apparently Ubisoft thought otherwise. Yet, all that historical accuracy goes straight out the window when you start building your settlement. Suddenly, modern agendas are shoved down your throat, and the only thing missing is a transgender character—though maybe I just missed that.You've got everything else: Islamist Arabs as best friends, a Chinese merchant, Native American hunters, some African kid with a New Jersey accent—why not throw in a few more clichés while we're at it? And let's not forget, this is all happening in the era of Scandinavian raids in the 8th-9th centuries. But who cares, right?To be fair, the main plot isn't entirely drowned in this nonsense, Then there's the main game map, where every large location has a fragment of "animus memories" or some other garbage. THANK THE GODS it's not mandatory, but if you're aiming for 100%, prepare to have your immersion shattered as you're forced to play as that strong, independent heroine from the beginning, jumping around on mirror cubes like a circus act.The storyline itself is well done—up until the end, that is. Your decisions? Your opinions? They don't matter. No one gives a **** about your choices. And those last few missions? A symphony of script impotence and sheer cretinism. Played as a man? Too bad. Suddenly, you're a female character in every video and scene. Don't want to fight  No one cares, go eat ♥♥♥♥.And let’s not even talk about the ridiculousness of the Asgard memories. From the first visit, it’s painfully obvious who everyone is just by their expressions and mannerisms. But of course, your character remains blissfully ignorant for another 98 hours of gameplay—brilliant.This game could have been great, even phenomenal, if Ubisoft had just cut out all the Assassin's Creed trash and focused on the main character's story, his settlement, his dreams of other worlds, and Odin's wise counsel. But that's asking too much from Ubisoft, a company that can't make a good game without cluttering it with assassins and animus.

_childDocuments_.review: It is definitly not one of the best Assassin's Creed games.Still, I had a lot fun playing this game.- Good story- Good graphics- The Zealot system is way better than the endless bounty hunter system from Odyssey in my opinion- No naval combat like in Odyssey (which was fun at first but felt like a chore later)- Flyting is a fun new idea- The return of "Assassination Opportunites" in "Wrath of the Druids". I kind of wish that they were included in the base game and the other DLCs, as it made stealth way more fun.- Instant assassination with the hidden blade. In Odyssey, even with full upgrades, there were a lot of enemies that were not insta-killed by the spear assassination. This was very frustating, so I was happy that I did not have this problem here.- There are almost no fully fleged side quests. There are a lot of small mysteries, but they all take like 1-5 minutes each and don't offer a lot of side story- The stone cairns range from ridiculously easy to ridiculously hard- The map is a bit to big for its own good- The endings of the DLCs are a bit lacking- Very little incentive to do things the stealthy way.- Some bugs here and there- There is a ton of collectible stuff. Depending on the region it ranges between an okay amount and absolutly ridicolous. Some things require you to gather other stuff in order to complete it. There are a few things I did not complete because of this.Like I said in the beginning, it is not the best, but also by far not the worst Assassin's Creed for me (the absolute worst is "Rogue" for me).Definitly worth checking out when on sale in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather than go with quality, Ubisoft went with quantity. There are so many side quests and at least 50-60 hours of main story. But it isn't a compelling story. There's not a lot to him, which is a shame since Odessey's MC was great and actually had depth. Lots of bugs especially with the arena type game mode for medals. They made stealth very optional/ obsolete and combat a lot of fun, so all I wanted to do was run around and fight everyone. You also have the ability to customize how much damage you do, how much damage you take, and how much health enemies have. I personally loved that addition. I had a lot of fun with the rune system, and there were a lot of different abilities to choose from. And there is no more getting garbage armor or weapons anymore, like in Odessey. All armor is part of sets, and all weapons can be fully upgraded. The environment is beautiful, but a little too spread out for my taste. Though, much better than Mirage. I haven't played the Siege of France DLC yet but I have played the other two. The Wrath of the Druids was alright, and the Dawn of Ragnarok is horribly boring and long.If its on sale, I would definitely recommend picking it up. At least 80-100 hours of gameplay without DLCs

_childDocuments_.review: This is my last assassins creed game most likely. While i still enjoyed the present day story, Eivor's story is really drawn out and started making me not want to play another hour. This is definitely the longest game in the series and has a lot of bloat in the story. The main missions stretch on seemingly forever and when you finish an arc, a lot of the time it doesn't feel like anything has changed in the world. Also there is a few thing that never get explained to the player and you're just expected to accept them      Gameplay wise this game can be really unfair (especially if you play on hard) in the beginning but after you get some skills and abilities it becomes a breeze. Part of the problem with the difficulty is the settings, as you can customize them to your preferences but they are options like enemies get more health and you do less damage, healing heals less. I ended up turning down the difficulty after the 50 hour mark because every fight was getting tedious and it never felt like my damage was going up. A weirdly cool feature in the game is how much is saved on the map when you do stuff, like sabotaging siege defences will be saved for a few hours. The unfortunate part of this saving is that bodies will stick around in places and make guards angry at you for them. Another gameplay problem is the "no killing civilians" rule as you can find yourself accidentally killing people during a building fight because the people run around the combat and your wide swings insta-kill them.   There is a lot that annoys me in this game that they dropped the ball with it feels. The SHIP is barely required and raiding is entertaining until you realise that they struggle against basic foes. The game gives you pretty much no equipment for the beginning and when you have figured out what works for you it starts to trickle a few items at time that now need more resources to upgrade them, making me not want to touch them until I was getting bored in late game.      The WORST offense though is the character of Eivor, or more specifically the fact that the game is made expecting you to be the female version. There is so much dialogue and subtitles in the game that refer to Eivor as a woman that it begs the question of why even leave the option to be a male in the game. Hell even in the endgame there is a note that confirms that Eivor is suppose to be played as female since they refer to  which is placed beside the name Sigurd Styrbjornsson to show you the proper naming convention for if the character was the son of Varin.I can't give this game a good review as it suffers from being the longest story with so little payoff, you play through 18 arcs and so many of them are boring (you are going to be playing kingmaker a lot). The combat is decent but you fall into questioning if you want to pump up the difficulty at the cost of how long its going to take to fight. World map is best part and running around this time period is a blast for me personally, but the map starts to feel annoyingly big when you are trying to complete missions. The game was fun for the first 30 hours but started to become a slog that i just wanted to finish. 4.9/10, wanted to enjoy it but just feeling burnt out from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Captivating Saga of Viking Adventure, Though a Departure from Assassin's Creed RootsAssassin's Creed Valhalla takes players on an epic journey through the tumultuous world of 9th-century England, immersing them in the rich tapestry of Viking culture and conquest. As a departure from its predecessors, Valhalla ventures further into RPG territory, offering a vast open world teeming with activities, exploration, and the brutal yet captivating life of a Norse warrior.From the breathtaking landscapes of Norway to the lush fields of England, the game's environments are meticulously crafted, breathing life into the world of Vikings with stunning attention to detail. Whether sailing across stormy seas or scaling towering mountains, every step feels immersive and awe-inspiring.The narrative of Valhalla is a gripping tale of ambition, loyalty, and betrayal, weaving together the personal journey of Eivor, a Viking raider seeking glory and revenge, with the broader conflict between the invading Norsemen and the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. The game skillfully balances historical accuracy with the fantastical elements of the Assassin's Creed universe, creating a compelling narrative that keeps players engaged from start to finish.Combat in Valhalla is visceral and satisfying, allowing players to unleash a variety of brutal melee attacks, ranged assaults, and stealthy assassinations. The revamped skill tree system provides ample opportunities for customization, allowing players to tailor Eivor's abilities to suit their preferred playstyle.One of the game's standout features is its robust settlement system, where players must manage resources, construct buildings, and forge alliances to strengthen their Viking clan's foothold in England. This adds a layer of strategic depth to the gameplay, as players must balance their ambitions for conquest with the needs of their burgeoning community.However, despite its many strengths, Assassin's Creed Valhalla may disappoint fans of the earlier titles in the series who were drawn to the more stealth-focused gameplay of games like Assassin's Creed 1, 2, Brotherhood, and Revelations. While stealth remains a viable approach in Valhalla, the game leans heavily into its RPG elements, placing a greater emphasis on exploration, combat, and player choice.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a sprawling epic that delivers a captivating journey through the Viking age, filled with breathtaking landscapes, engaging storytelling, and satisfying gameplay mechanics. While it may stray from the traditional formula of the Assassin's Creed series, it nonetheless stands as a worthy addition to the franchise, offering a fresh perspective on the age-old conflict between Assassins and Templars amidst the backdrop of Norse mythology.
