_childDocuments_.review: First off, I am a huge Sierra fan and a fan of my buddy Steve from Infamous Quests who worked on this game. In another start off shout out, thanks to Steve for a key to the game. Now if that is too much bias for you, please feel free to go find something else to do. I won't mind.  I teach engineering at the local community college, you can't possibly ignore me any better than my students.I have really enjoyed this game. I haven't gotten all the way through yet but I have found many of the pieces and I'll need to go back and replay to do a better job. I've managed to get myself killed, robbed and lost so in true Sierra fashion, I'm having more fun messing up than doing it right!This is a fun twist on a classic. The graphics are enough to move the game along but work so well with the text to give it that old time feel. I like the use of the music and the control system is easy and natural. Can a game feel both new and old at the same time? With Roberta Williams at the helm, it most certainly can. If you are a fan of the original, you should play this game. If you like old games, you should play this game. If you are like my kids who like their games with all sorts of weapons both real and made up, loud bangs and possibly nasty zombies, you should still play this game to see how that all got going.  I'd write more but I have more to do so I'm getting back to it! Great to have Roberta and Ken back in the game business.

detailed_description: Become a party legend with The Jackbox Party Pack 10. Start Your Party The celebrated franchise returns with 5 new party games in 1 hilarious pack. Reunion? Work Party? Hanging with pals? There's a game for everyone and every occasion, from strategy, drawing, trivia or music! Play with your phone or tablet - no special controller required. Games support up to 9 players and 10,000 audience members. Ready to take things global? All Party Pack 10 games can be played in English, French, Italian, German, or Spanish. Choose Your Game Tee K.O. 2 (Drawing, Writing): In Tee K.O. 2, return to T-Shirt Island, where the most hardened warriors in the world compete in a deadly fighting tournament. The drawing finger–not the fist–decides the victory! FixyText (Writing, Teamwork): FixyText is the Wild West of text-editing. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR is that Pack 10 will still be great to play at parties or with friends over streams, but $35 is a bit much unless you're a returning fan. The fan favorite returns with better drawing tools/better customization, the ability to redraw someone else's art, but unfortunately with a lesser final round that asks player to button-mash on what they think should win instead of a typical voting system. At the end of the day, it's still Tee K.O. at its core which is a great drawing game; However the chance to implement a scoring system that rewards good art and slogans, and not just who was lucky enough to be sent the best stuff, was a sorely missed opportunity. A trivia game solely fixated on questions about the specific year or era certain events happened. Restrictive on paper but they do a great job keeping things fresh by constantly changing up the format of the questions. Unlike Trivia Murder Party or Fibbage, Time Jinx is straight trivia with no other elements players can excel at. If you like trivia then this is a very well paced game, but there's little else on offer if trivia isn't your thing. You're all sent a message on the screen , and then on your device you all simultaneously write a response to said message. Beyond other players voting for what words they liked the most, there is essentially no structure to this game. It goes on for 3 rounds with no gimmicks to shake things up, and the end result is always unintelligible word salad. Even the game's great presentation can't salvage what is the equivalent of 4 people all jumping in a public Google docs, and hammering away on their keyboard. If there's any game worth buying pack 10 for, it's this. Dodo Re Mi is a rhythm game very much in-line with stuff like Rock Band or DDR. There's an impressive number of songs, a great variety of instruments, the music itself is super solid, and the ingenious  sync system assures all players will always be in-tune with the music even over streaming. Dodo Re Mi is so good it could be sold as its own stand-alone title. Easily the most complicated in the pack, this is a social deduction game where you're assigned a secret role  and need to deduce who else is in your assigned group. There's a single "outlier" each round that will not fit in with the other assigned groups. The inclusion of the outlier is why players shouldn't flat out state who they are, since the outlier could be you, and if that's the case, you need to realize that ASAP so you can blend in afterwards. A very interesting concept albeit poorly paced; And players who don't answer, or enter jokey submissions, are actually rewarded since it reveals nothing about themselves whilst they take in all the information of their opponents. The Jackbox Party Pack 10 might be the most experimental pack to date; And in the case of Dodo Re Mi that risk was definitely worth it. Regrettably that's one home-run in a pack that is otherwise a bit rough. My friends and I love playing Jackbox so I can still see myself booting this up plenty for the next couple of weeks; But given a few months, the only games I can see myself revisiting is Dodo Re Mi, and maybe Hypnotorius for its intriguing premise. This has the highest retail for a Party Pack to date, and I could only recommend it for its asking price of $35 if you're like me, love Jackbox, and just want to play the new games.

_childDocuments_.review: It brings me absolutely no joy to say it, but it's plain to see. This is likely the worst Jackbox we've gotten in years. I don't want to overdramatize this review, but I've always looked to this series as a really big part of my social circle, Jackbox nights are one of the few things that can get everyone in the same room together without fail, and with the previous 5 or so constantly building and improving upon each other, getting something this blatantly rushed out and poorly done feels like a bit of a slap in the face, and it makes me worried about where the future instalments are headed, and if they'll even be worth picking up.Anyways, lets run through the games. Normally, I'd highlight the 1 or 2 games that are the standouts of this pack, but honestly, there isn't one here. There's only one sequel game in this pack, Tee K.O. 2, and its... disappointing. New to the pack is... 2 new font options, the ability to make your shirt a hoodie or a muscle-shirt, and a worse final round? Tee K.O. was one of my favourite games from the series, and it still is, but there's no reason to play this one over the original. Of the four new games, we have a lacklustre coop rhythm game, another trivia game, and 2 things that barely qualify as games at all. We'll get them out of the way first.FixyText might as well be Wordspud 2. It's that bad. You and your friends are split up into 2 teams. Each team takes turns getting text prompts, and answering them all at the same time, with no backspace button. Being in a team doesn't really matter, you aren't really working together, and points are awarded by the other team picking funny words in your text wall. We played this one a few times, and never really got much out of it. Hypnotorious is just as bad, its labelled as a social deduction role-play game, but the rules are non existent, and the whole premise is flawed at the core. You each get a person or thing, and have to answer questions as whatever you were assigned. You then have to put yourself into one of 3 categories with everyone else. Everyone belongs to 1 of the 2 categories, with the third being for the odd one out in the group. You don't KNOW you'er the odd one out, so lying doesn't really work, you don't know what the categories are outside of hints that are either too obvious or say nothing, and everyone gets the same amount of points in the end anyways? We tried really hard to get this one, but after hours of modifying our own personal rules, we just couldn't make it work. We got a flawless victory every time, and we usually had it by round 2. It goes nowhere, and by the end it just sort of happens, no one feels anything, and you just kinda wish you were doing something else. Every Jackbox pack has 1 or 2 throwaway games that you play once and don't really try again, but they're all still playable. These are just confusing at best, and frustratingly boring at worst.The other 2 games are Timejinx, and Do Re Mi. Timejinx is a trivia game where you guess what year something happened. Its pretty much just Guesspionage but with years instead of percentages. Trivia games are always Jackboxes weakest showings, and this is no exception. Do Re Mi is just any one of those cookie cutter mobile rhythm games you can find anywhere for free, but you all of your scores are combined at the end. If you like rhythm games, it definitely is a rhythm game. The songs aren't much, beating the boss at the end takes way too long and just feels arbitrary, and there are a lot better options out there for playing rhythm games with your friends. I really like the idea, but like everything else in this pack, it just lacks any polish. Jackbox has been on a yearly release schedule for awhile now, and its starting to catch up with them. This is the 10th one, it should have been a big milestone, a celebration of all of the awesome games that they've made, a monument of this cool series that noone else has really been able to replicate, but instead, it feels like a cheap cash grab they threw out for the sake of it. They bumped the price up again on this one, and really, I think aside from Party Pack 1, this is probably the worst one they've put out. I wouldn't bother picking it up, even if you're a huge fan of the series, wait for a heavy discount if you HAVE to play it. The good entries are so endlessly replayable that this model is completely unnecessary, and its really disappointing to see something this bad come from a series that I've admired for such a long time. 2/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I own every single pack of Jackbox and host weekly nights for my community. Over the years I get a feel of whats great and what's... Not so great. This pack is not so great. Putting aside the bug issues I'm just gonna break down game by game just the issues of it.Fixty Text:This game from the initial trailer left me confused on what exact was the concept for this game. Once I finally figured it out the concept eats away at what Jackbox is suppose to be. The whole goal of Jackbox is to play with a large amount of people but having 4 people tackle a prompt at the same time is so chaotic. It feels like a weaker version of job job that just takes the mad lib part and goes no where with it. Having more people hurts how the game flows. The only time me and my group enjoyed it when it was 4-6 people but even then got a little too much.Tee K.O. 2The first game was a great note but the real question is do we need a sequel? What does it add? New avatars, 3 different types of clothing, and a new 2nd/3rd round. The new addition of the 2nd round was great and I loved the idea of remixing one of the old drawings. The final round however is just terrible. I understand they didn't want to have a simple vote and wanted to spice things up but bringing back spam tapping from bracketeering was not the right option. If you make a sequel of a previous jackbox game then there needs to be something new to be done or built upon. We get less shirts in the final since they removed the streak system which yeah that gameplay element was not the best but maybe add a feature allowing the audience or players to vote for their personal favorite at the end of a round for a 2nd contender. TimeJinxProbably the least egregious game in the pack. I personally love trivia but everyone else doesn't enjoy it that much. I find it interesting when a game can balance that to make everything enjoyable. Comparing to all the other trivia games it doesn't really stand out that much. Sure I still enjoy it but I rather go play Trivia Murder 2 party or Fibbage 3/4 for a more engaging experience. I really don't have anything to say about this one which that in itself is an issue.HypnotoriousThis game was probably the most controversial when testing it out. Some people liked it but the most just despised it. People couldn't get the concept, fully understand how to answer the questions, or enjoy themselves. It feels half baked like the game is relying on player engagement to do all the work. That isn't a bad thing but if the layout isn't clear and there isn't anything engaging in the process it all falls flat. Between the bugs involving the outlier no one really knew if they were winning or losing even if they paired up in the correct group. Since there is no final game leaderboard everyone is left clueless how one of the random players won including them. Out of everything in this pack this game needs the most reworking and is not fully fleshed out.Dodo Re MiI wanted to leave game for last because it's probably the best game in the pack. Sure it's just guitar hero but it takes that simple idea and brings the best with it. While it got some push back from my group a majority enjoyed the game and the only real discontent was bugs or how some of the sound charts are made. The only drawback besides the bugs/some chart placement? I want more songs, I want custom songs, I want more from this game cause that's how fun it is! I will state again this is probably the best game out of the pack.Despite liking one of the games I cannot recommend anyone buy this pack. On top of they raised the price for a pack that is worse overall then a majority of packs. Maybe on par with the first part packs which says alot. I hope the team take this with a grain of salt and maybe rework some of the games in this pack but I highly doubt it. Please add murder trivia 3 next year

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best pack. Jackbox 10 offers improvements on some previous games, but with various questionable game mechanic choices, bugs, and no clear homeruns, the price ($34.99) is hard to justify.A wonderful improvement! The game design feels really fresh and music is spot-on. Compared to the previous Tee K.O., there are more garment options, there is less focus on the presenter, and the drawing UI is more intuitive. The game is shorter than the original which is a really good choice.A decent game about history that doesn't go too deep. Plays like a variant on Guesspionage – but more fun. Round 1 involves guessing a year, which is a kind of lazy trivia history enthusiasts will enjoy. Round 2 is about matching social fads to recent time periods, which is accessible to non-history buffs. The final round gives you a curious historical event, but something is wrong with it and you have to correct it. Game rounds don't seem too long. In the negatives we have a game that is pretty limited mechanically, which doesn't make you want to replay it too often.What do you get when you allow four people, whose delete button has been taken away, to edit a shared message simultaneously? That's right. A bad game.The art style is nice and the music is inoffensive. However, nothing can fix the fact you end up with garbled message with either illegible nonsense or constant raunch. Worse still, you have to wait for the narrator to read through it in a cringefest.The rounds lack variety, and four-player teams are probably just too big for effective funniness.The one redeeming quality for streamers is that Jackbox finally introduced a 'Kick Player' button on the mod screen – but that's something they should have added to many other games long ago.An original, new music game that's pretty awesome! Pick a song, grab an instrument, and try to hit the right keys when a dot reaches the horizontal line (as in a lot of other rhythm games). It offers various difficulty levels per instrument, ranging from a single to five buttons – so even the most rhythmically-challenged gong player can go wild. The replay of how everyone did together can be hilarious, and the game's epic rendition of Row, Row, Row your Boat deserves an ovation. Special thanks for adding musical screaming, a fast food cup, and Doug as musical instruments.A jumbled mess. Hypnotorious tries to be a more layered version of Who Am I, adding social deduction and hints. The game rules are very unclear despite the tutorial, and its mechanics seem to have little relation to who wins. Do we purposefully stay super vague, or just blurt out what we are? Can we lie? It seems like this game is lacking guard rails.As if that weren't enough, the game feels incredibly long. At this point I'm not sure if there was a miscommunication and the devs accidentally added too many rounds.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll go over each and every game me and 6 of my close friends have played really quick. All of us played the previous jackbox party pack games (excluding 1 & 2) and we were really looking forward to this pack but were unfortunately let down by how the games were.Two out of five games were worth playing as the chaos fit our group. Fixytext is the best game of the bunch as the ridiculousness and vulgarity that can come from the game is perfect for us. DoDo Re Mi, while it is one of the least interactive games from all the party packs is genuinely a joy to play due to the thrill of actually surviving despite picking difficult instruments.Besides that, Hypnotorious is confusing yet not bad at all. Our group enjoys it but it's a mess of a game, too confusing and the tutorial does not do a good job explaining.Tee K.O. 2, the successor to our group's 2nd favorite drawing game (right behind Champ'd Up) is arguably worse than the original. It lacks the spirit of Tee K.O. and while the new fonts and shirt options are a fantastic option, there is something that's missing to keep it together. Maybe due to the new narrator (no offense, she still did a good job), the new contenders... it doesn't work. Sorry.I liked Timejinx but it's just a guessing game. When I want to play a Trivia game, I'd rather play Trivia Murder Party. It's the base of what all trivia games Jackbox should be going off of.Lastly, the price is TOO MUCH. 35 bucks is unfortunately not worth at all for one/two good games (debatable). Huge let down, one of the weakest party packs they released so far and in my opinion, the only one I'll refund. I will give the next one a try and hope that our feedback from review across the internet could improve the future ones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 10

_childDocuments_.review: For the tenth game, I do recommend it but... it DOES feel like more effort could have gone into it.Tee K.O 2 was an instant hit with all of us. It improves on literally EVERYTHING from the first one. A new bracket system that helps elevate more stuff and prevent favouritism, more options, more fonts, and overall more ways to play! Even our most avid certified Tee K.O haters loved it.Hypnotorious was a huge surprise for us all. I admit going in that it did not seem great, but we were completely thrown for a loop at the concept of it all. It's ♥♥♥♥♥ It but without knowing who's the outlier and categories. It was a smash hit with us all.Dodo Re Mi (to me personally) was a chaotically fun ride although it definitely was a mixed bag among my group. Instead of just a regular tutorial, the game gives you a tutorial that you play as a group, which is a great addition! It's basically Guitar Hero but with more instruments, hilarious out-of-sync playing, and a great way to make the new hit single: "All I want For Christmas is You but very off key"Timejinx is the trivia game of the pack that actually has an interesting twist: you go through history and try to guess about things in time. You also get to go through time loops, mistaken timelines, etc. My friends loved this game, but I was very much an outlier as I very much was meh towards it.FixyText is easily the least favourite (or almost) of my group of lovely pals. It has a very great concept that is ruined by sloppy execution. The "tutorial" explains the wrong aspects of the game and we had no idea what we were doing. The game also actively encourages screwing over other players, which is counterproductive to the entire game of creating funny text messages and especially when you have limited characters.Also the price hike was not appreciated. Overall, not a bad pack nor the worst as some have claimed, but it's a far cry from what it should have been for the tenth game in the series.I feel like that this game shows that we really need some sort of Jackbox hub game similar to the Master Chief Collection where we can buy the individual minigames that we want rather than having to buy a whole set of five to play only a few.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played and loved every Jackbox Party Pack up until this point. At most, a pack will have 1 game that doesn't fit my group's style, and that's perfectly acceptable.  This is a totally different story. The games are shallow and lack any reason to play multiple times. I genuinely hope the next release is better, this is the first time I've ever refunded a Jackbox game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only Jackbox game I would actively not recommend, primarily as it is the only Jackbox game I have ever played which has bugs in it.In Fixy Text we had players type things that never appeared, and cursors typing stuff in places we had not selected. There are also issues with the keyboard popping up inconsistently.Hypnotorious does not work properly for low player counts as the structure of the game does not work! There is no point switching jars.Dodo Re Mi whilst by far the best game in the pack (about 10/12hrs of my playtime at this point is dodo) this is also problematic. Older phones struggle to run this smoothly, and even modern phones (Samsung S22 Ultra & iPhone 14) struggle to run this without jitters and lag.TimeJinx we enjoyed and was a pleasant break from the bugs/issues but wasn't exceptional. TeeKO 2 is just TeeKO with more options.I love Jackbox games, and I hate to see one being released as a rushed buggy mess. I would much rather they skip a year if they do not have the content ready, than release a sub-par collection of bugs. Lets gets back to the level of polish we had on the previous instalments.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there's not much I can say, as there will definitely be a new patch coming out.It's sad that the release build is so raw. This build was created at the end of August.Every single game there has bugs, some of them causing to game or lobby crash.Starting from TeeKO2, where the final round can be interrupted for no reason, and continuing with FixyText, that may just not render the thing...Lots of graphical bugs, like dissappering lines from drawings in TeeKo2. It's not like first drawer made a circle with two dots, and other one finished it. TeeKo just deleted most of details from first and second artist. And during the round, some elements of the drawing even were out of the T-shirt after some animations played. Blue blinking screen in Hypnotorious - a minor bug, but still noticeable.Ensless timers in Hypnotorious, ignoring whole input (ofc not every time) in DodoReMi, long delay between final shirt and credits in teeko2, disappearing or non-appearing text in FixyText... And a lot of other things, that could be listed there...I just don't understand why Jackbox Games made this. For example, a game with a million audience Geometry Dash announced that the release would be in October and recently they posted that they had to move the release to November. Everyone is upset, but understands the reason why.I understand that there will be an update coming out soon with bug fixes. But at the time of public release, there are a lot of them. And I totally understand people who complain about the high price.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Packs are never games that I would recommend my friends to buy, simply because it's a "one person pays for the friend group" type of situation, as all party games should be. With that being said, knowing that not everyone has to purchase it, I can safely recommend this for long time fans of the Jackbox Party Packs. Do I think the increased price is a bit of a turn off? A bit, but the games are unique and enjoyable, and I always have a good time playing them with my friends. At the end of the day, that's all that matters to me for party games like this.I see a lot of people stating that it's the worst party pack. And honestly, my perspective on this franchise makes it a bit hard to add an opinion on that. Regardless of if I agree or not, I do think that the developers, if they expect to get away with asking for more money, need to listen to the fans who are upset. If the next installment comes out under their yearly release cycle, and it also gains "mixed" reviews from their audience, they'll start losing their community bit by bit.If you haven't purchased a Party Pack yet, this would not be the first one I would recommend. Not by far. However, if you have been purchasing them over time like I have, there isn't that much of a loss here. Small price to pay for the memories I get in exchange. But that's just me.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 10 is the newest one and sadly… it isn’t as good as the older packs. Multiple games seemed half-made during release, and while many got updated… not all issues were solved. As a pack, it isn’t extremely bad… but it’s not really good either.The worst game is definitely FIXYTEXT. When we saw the trailer for this game, we were excited, but sadly, this game isn’t really good. It’s basically a shared Word document where everyone’s typing chaotically at the same time, and then they choose the craziest words made. The idea isn’t bad, but there’s nothing more to it. If they added something more than just the typing, it would have so much potential. But it’s simply bland, and after a few playthroughs, it’s pretty boring honestly. And it also was extremely bugged. Many people got their full answers deleted, and nothing they wrote was submitted for some reason. This game… if we can call it a game, is just a failure, sadly. Yes, you can have some fun with it, but it gets old quickly, and the bugs make it horrible. (2,5/10)The other weak game that has issues is TEE K.O. 2. I am sad to say this because the original Tee K.O. is a great game, but this one isn’t really… that good. While it adds some new things (new kinds of shirts, fonts of the texts, etc.) that are fine, it also introduces new mechanics that make it worse than the original. And the final round that is literally just really fast clicking… that change wasn’t a good idea. Not only that, but this game is also bugged for some reason. The timers and transitions don’t work properly. After the time runs out for the drawing part, we had to wait for around 4 minutes once and then usually about 1-2 minutes the other times we played this. I have no idea whether it was loading or what was going on, but even though they kinda repaired this, the waiting is still there, and it’s really annoying. Still… it’s Tee K.O., so it’s fine even with the issues. (5/10)Next one is the trivia game TIMEJINX. It isn’t bad; I like the idea of trivia about history, time, and all about it. The minigames in it are really creative, and it’s overall very innovative and a good concept. One issue I have with it is that it’s the easiest Jackbox trivia game ever to cheat in. Finding the year of some historic moment on the internet in 20 seconds is rather easy. Then there’s this other thing. The name of this game is TIMEJINX. And if two or more players guess the same year, it tells them "JINX." But it doesn’t do anything else. I mean the "JINX" moment is literally in the name of the game… but it has no effect on the gameplay? Why was it implemented in the first place then? This detail just doesn’t make any sense to me and is really weird.Overall, this game is pretty fine and fun, though. It has a fast pace, runs smoothly. (7/10)HYPNOTORIOUS is the second-best game in this pack, and it’s REALLY GOOD. It’s harder to understand. During the first playthrough, expect everyone to be kinda confused. But once you find out what to do, it’s fun. It’s a game I replay a lot with my friends in this pack. One thing that annoys me is that for some reason, there isn’t a final leaderboard – you just see the winner and not the other rankings. Also, while the idea is really creative, I think they could have done a bit more with it. It’s very good, but there’s something missing to be GREAT. (8/10)But a game that is not only GREAT but almost PERFECT is the game that single carries this pack – DODO RE MI. It is a very experimental music game, basically the first game of this kind that Jackbox has ever made. But it was so worth it. The game slays extremely and is very fun to play. It was great on release already, but they added more songs and instruments in it later, which adds additional content that makes it even better. Where the other games are missing something and seem half-baked, this one is a well-made masterpiece. I would give it an 11/10 if I could honestly. It’s great and a well-deserved (10/10)Overall:The average of game scores is 6,5.The quality went down for sure. Where other packs have weaker games, this one has trashy games. The average games of this pack also have more weaknesses than the average games in other packs. And while Timejinx and Hypnotorious are good, they‘re missing something in them. The only game everyone is fully satisfied with is Dodo Re Mi, and honestly, the pack is only worth buying because of this game. If it had another mediocre game instead of Dodo Re Mi, I wouldn’t buy it and wouldn’t recommend it.Also, this pack is more expensive than the other ones so… this price for worse quality makes it even worse. I think it is worth trying out still, but honestly… for full price don’t buy it. Don’t. Wait for a sale, and then it can be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: THIS PACK DOES NOT OFFER GREAT VALUE! PLEASE DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME IF YOU AREN'T FAMILIER WITH JACKBOX! PLEASE CONSIDER BUYING JACKBOX PARTY PACK 7 IF YOU ARE INTERSTED IN THE SERIES AND WANT A GOOD VALUE PACK, OR BUY THE JACKBOX STARTER PACK WITH THE 3 MOST POPULAR GAMES IN THE SERIES, ITS ALSO GOOD VALUE!I fell in love with the jackbox series all the way in pack 4, bought every pack after that because I not only was excited for each release but very thrilled for the possibilities of new times with my friends, and Jackbox allowed me to make a ton of meaningful connections.HOWEVER, this is the first jackbox pack I truly cannot recommend, and I really feel like the quality in these games has been dwindling since Jackbox 8, Jackbox 8 was my first jackbox pack where I felt disappointed but still had fun with the overall selection. Jackbox 9 was a nice step up and a hope things could be good again, but alas, this pack is lackluster, with 2 games being great (TKO 2 and DoDo Re Mi), one okay game, (Time Jinx) and 2 stinkers, (FixyText and Hypnotorious). Honestly this review is less of a review of the pack and more just feedback for the devs, if you are reading this as as someone considering buying this pack, please don't, it will give you a bad impression on the series, I would suggest buying Jackbox Party Pack 7, which is fantastic, or the Jackbox Starter Pack with the 3 most popular games in the series!If the devs are reading this, please, I truly say from the bottem of my heart, this is not from a place of malice, I still bought the pack because for me TKO 2 and DoDoReMi make the pack personally worth it for me as I do not own pack 3, and own the squeals to all the other games from Jackbox Party Pack 4-9.Please, please, please Jackbox Games, if you need more time to innovate and push out these games, then please do, OR, play it safe and simply make the next party pack (Pack 11) or even something separate from Jackbox 11, and make 4-5 sequels of games the community has asked for. Or take a controversial game (Bracketering), and think of ways on possibly turning that inconsistent concept into a great one, something seriosuly needs to be done to improve more on the formula of Jackbox because I can't support a company who does not listen to their community and push out another mediocore pack like this one. And I haven't even mentioned the several bugs you have not fixed in this pack. Your guys quality for you packs has always been great but not here. And we as fans appreciate you expanding on language barriers, such as me being able to play these packs with my family that only speaks spanish, but I am honestly baffled by how this pack turned out, and I hope Jackbox can find success and fortune once again such as with Party Pack 7, which honestly has yet to be surpassed in its value even after now with three new packs to the roaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox is such a great franchise, but it has been on a significant decline since Jackbox 6.  9 was dissappointing, but still playable.  Unfortunately, this 10 year anniversary really felt like the developers were struggling to even want to create a game, none-the-less compete with the past.  All of them are pretty easy to get bored of real fast.  I didn't think I'de actually not recommend a JB party pack, and sadly, it makes me consider ever buying from this franchise again.  I really hope they  actually attempt to create a competitive and fun group of games like they used to, rather than really lame knockoffs like the singing bird one which doesn't even work right to begin with... and that is the best on on here.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't understand a lot of the reviews I'm reading, I find myself disagreeing with most of them.  All the games people rate as being "Bad" are honestly some of the most fun I've had.  Is it up to the standards they set for an anneversary game?  No.  But it still is a good pack in my opinion.  Here's the ranking I would give:1. Tee KO 2As a fan of the first TeeKO, I went into this with some bias.  But the game delivered on everything I wanted, from adding more options to the shirt, being hoodies and tank tops, it gives more variety if you decide to purchase the shirts made.  Having the ability to go back and add to the not used images is a really fun concept.  I can understand being upset that this game feels like a cut and paste of TeeKO, but it's still the most fun game in the pack in my personal opinion.2. HypnotoriusI was worried this was going to be bootleg 'Push the Button' when I first saw it, where the whole point of the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ among us.  But I was pleasantly surprised!  The game is a little hard to get the hang of at first, but once you get a handle on it then it gets really fun.  Having to not only figure out what categories, which category you and your friends fit into, and who is the outlier makes for a fun game that rewards you for problem solving.3.  Fixy TextThis game is fun when you play it with small keyboards and big fingers.  The genuine misspells are what really get the group laughing, it can be a lot and the layout is a little annoying and the humor is not up to the snuff of other packs.  But it is still a fun game.4. TimejynxThis game is like murder trivia but on easy mode.  Most of the questions aren't that hard and as long as you guess in a general area you'll be fine.  REMEMBER THAT LOWER POINTS ARE THE WINNERS, it got me and my friends on the first go through.  All in all, not much variation, just a trivia game with a semi interesting twist.5. Dodo Re MiI do not get why this game is ranked by a lot of people as the best in the pack... It is unique, sure, but it is such a niche game.  Maybe it's because I can't process visual stimuli fast, but this game is genuinely my least favorite.  Having to have the sound come out of your phone if you're using it is annoying.  The browser version disconnected my friends from the lobby when they tried to press space, and half the time it wouldn't let us play the damn game.  You  can say this was playthrough exclusive an I should give it another try, but this game is miserable.All in all, is this the best pack.No.Is this the worst pack.Also noIs this an adequate game to be the 'big anniversary pack' that costs $35?Once again, no.It's an ok pack, the games are fun enough, but it is completely up to you if you want to spend $35.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything's either unfun, or competing for my time with an older game:   Much as I've been buying these games the moment they've come out for three years now, Jackbox 10 is below the bare minimum for me. The only good thing I have to say about it is that I think the games play quicker than previous ones, which meant I could try all 5 before refunding it. _childDocuments_.review: Most of this pack borders on okay. Fixytext is an okay game that can be funny, but isn't that much more involved than opening a Google document. Hypnotorius has a fun concept, but is ludicrously unbalanced. Timejinx is a fun year-guessing trivia game, who's scoring system means that it's fairly fun even if you suck at trivia (like me.)Tee K.O. 2 is a really good side-grade to the original, offering a usually less funny bracket-style tournament structure, as jokes can get stale when you've seen them multiple times. I'd argue it's a bit better than the original, the ability to take a design and draw over it is a fun new concept that helps when you're running out of creative energy after drawing 2 t-shirts without a prompt. The drawing tools are also improved, carrying over improvements from Champ'd Up, and an eraser for some reason.Dodo Re Mi is the star of the show, and easily the best game in the pack. If you're getting Jackbox 10, you're getting Dodo Re Mi. It's basically a multiplayer stepmania rhythm game (think DDR or Osu!mania) featuring some original music, some public domain covers, and some other Jackbox themes. You'd hope they'd be good, and they really are. The Public Domain ones usually have some sort of twist, like a Rock cover of In the Hall of the Mountain King, a dubstep cover of Flight of the Bumblebee, or the most extra Row Row Row Your Boat cover you'll ever hear. There's multiple difficulty options, ranging from Really Easy (1 key charts with one note every 4 beats level easy) to Really Hard (Can really be as hard as they like, and usually are stupid difficult even for a someone who is decent at Rhythm games, like me.) This makes it a great party game, even for those who are less experienced in Rhythm games, while still allowing for challenges for more experienced players. The game also keeps track of the parts you've perfected, which requires full combo-ing a part with only "Perfect" notes. The game is very forgiving for what it considers a Perfect note.Basically, do you want to spend £30 on a Rhythm game with a bonus Tee K.O. 2 thrown in? Probably not, I just wanted to show how much I like Dodo Re Mi. It's one of my favourites alongside Champ'd Up and the Tee K.Os

_childDocuments_.review: Played the new pack last night with friends in what's become an annual tradition. Was a bit nervous cause we weren't huge fans of last year's pack (9), but this one was all hits for us. We had an absolute blast and the Jackbox team knocked it out of the park. We did a ranked-choice voting after we played all 5 games and for our group of 9, the order was:1. TeeKO 2 -- way out front, but we've always loved this one. My only critique here is that apart from some quality-of-life improvements, it's structurally exactly the same game. Would have loved at least an option to add some extra modes or something. But the quality of life improvements do go a long way: letting you get a head start on the next drawing if you finish one early, letting you iterate on one of the previous drawings in the second drawing round, and improved drawing tools overall.2. DodoReMi -- my personal favorite of the bunch, as a rhythm game player. Actually pretty impressed with how well this works, I was skeptical a game like this would be possible with the input lag inherent to using phones. But the 4-3-2-1-tap-tap-tap sync system works well and actually feels really fun and satisfying. The amount of instruments you can pick for each song is massive, and full of hilarious choices like screaming that feel very in Jackbox's wheelhouse. We loved that everybody could pick a difficulty that suits them. My only critique here is that the presentation of the band members takes way too long and I wish I could skip it. The playback itself is fun to watch but having to watch it after a long presentation drags it out a bit. But still, very impressed with this one, and it's quite beautiful as well.3. FixyText -- Almost tied with DodoReMi, our group generally loved this one. We're the type that tends to get a little high and riff on jokes. I feel like this one would not be as good with coworkers or family, since most of the funniest bits involved typos and profanity, but it made us laugh a lot. I do think it'd be better if it were only 2 rounds rather than 3 though. The inability to use backspace was a brilliant choice that made for some of the funniest moments. Presentationally, this was our favorite game of the whole pack, the graphics and aesthetic are beautiful and we repeatedly commented on it.4. Timejinx -- We still enjoyed this one but it was a drop off from the last one. I wish that they'd sometimes go for much larger date ranges to pick from. Guessing the exact year feels pretty hard. But there was enough going on and enough new modes/suprises to keep this one pretty fun, and it's nice to have a more cerebral trivia experience in here. Less of the jackbox-style humor than other trivia outings, but still a good time.5. Hypnotorious -- For the two rounds of this that we played, it always became fairly obvious who the outlier/imposter was. It's a neat concept, but it kind of requires players to play in a particular vague way to make guessing the outlier hard, and there's no way for the game to enforce that. I think it would have been better if they gave us prompts to play as actual people rather than objects/songs, because I think that would have made the answers possibly more ambiguous? To be clear, we still enjoyed it and I can imagine us trying it again, but it was last in our ranking.On the whole though, we all agreed that there were no real duds, and we had a blast playing them all. I'm sure we'll be giving them all a spin again soon. For us, this felt like the best of the last 3 packs.

_childDocuments_.review: Man.I love Jackbox games. I play weekly with a group of 6-10 adults for a few hours, it started during COVID and we're keeping it going. I own all the party packs and it seems like each pack has one or maybe two solid games that we revisit often, but this is the first party pack that didn't have a single good game in it.I'd say the "best" game was the new version of TKO, but even that didn't really add anything meaningful in terms of game-play.  The rest of the games were huge duds for our group.  All around disappointment for this party pack and no where near any sort of value at the $35 price point.I'm pretty shocked by how unfun the games were...I guess I'm too old now to be the target audience, because I assume they did extensive play testing prior to rolling these out. Edit: After some additional playing, some further comments:The strongest in the pack, but not really a big improvement from original TKO. You get to choose different shirt types now (T ♥♥♥♥, tank top, hoodie) and you can now choose a font for the slogans, but really that's about it.  No points for giving the winning drawing or caption though, only the person who combines them. There is no more "streak winner" either, so the winner is the combo that receives the most votes, at the end.  They also added a "spam click this button to fill the bar and choose the winner" at the end, which was a bit of a turn off for our group.I can't stress how idiotic this game is. The premise of the game is fine, but the fact that everyone  can put the cursor anywhere within the message, type whatever they want, and there is no backspace or delete means every answer devolved into meaningless gibberish. This seemed like a cool premise, a "find the impostor" type game but either the voting is bugged or maybe we just don't understand the rules. We played it three times and the impostor, who was correctly identified by the group all three times, still won the game. By a lot.This was probably the best received game in the pack, my group loves trivia. But what we don't really like is randomness injected in. (We love Trivia Murder Party, but at least that's somewhat controllable randomness)  In all our games, the person who was the most correct and led the game in the initial rounds ended up losing to a catch up mechanic, where the people in last place (bottom three, in a 7 player game) were given clues so obvious that they may as well been given the answer.  My group hated the Wheel trivia game from Pack 9 for the same reason. I know this one gets a lot of positive reviews, but it was a dud with our group. The game is a Jackbox version of Guitar Hero, but the majority of our players play on a browser on a PC, not a phone or tablet and clicking was incredibly difficult and burdensome. (I could see this being much easier on a touch screen, but have not experienced it.)

_childDocuments_.review: All of the hold so many memories with my friends and this one continued that trend. I've played all of the games included in this pack and they were all really fun! is the remake of a very popular Jackbox game. It holds up as better than the original by adding new ways to design how your shirt looks like. New features like being able to remix a pre-existing shirt is a fun addition that builds off of jokes and makes them funnier. is a trivia game about years throughout time. Jackbox is nothing without trivia games so it was good to see this pack had a new concept for one. is a funny text message writing game where multiple people are adding to a text to make it funnier. It's very funny to see the ways that people transform the message of the text into something else. The addition of not being able to delete anything means you have to get creative with typos. is an amazing musical teamwork game. Jackbox has had some phenomenal music in some of their games throughout the years so it just works perfectly that we get a game about music. It's very fun to work with your friends to survive songs while playing a wide range of silly to nice sounding instruments. The lobby music is somehow up as one of the most beautiful songs I have heard, the backing vocals are just so beautiful. Many really nice quality of life features appear in this game too like being able to easily join, leave, and transfer the host privileges without having to restart the lobby. If you play multiple songs everyone's overall scores will be shown at the end of the session, a very cool feature. is a very complex game where you really have to use your head to figure out what is going on. This game feels similar to "♥♥♥♥♥' It" from Jackbox Party Pack 3 but instead the faker/outlier also doesn't know who the outlier is. You can get some funny answers out of this game but it really comes down to using your brain to organize who belongs in what category.Overall I think this pack is amazing and definitely in the top best Jackbox Parry Packs. I do wish the other games shared the quality of life features that Dodo Re Mi had with joining and leaving lobbies though. It would also be cool for Dodo Re Mi to have custom songs as it's such a fun game but that is okay also.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Jackbox party pack that I don't think is worth the price. Don't get me wrong, there's fun to be had from all of these, but there are only 2 games in this pack that I think are worth their respective prices.Tee KO 2 is a pretty good sequel, all things considered. I actually like the new bracket style of voting for the regular rounds. The only thing that drags it down is how the final round is just a button mashing contest between two sides, which is not only anticlimactic, but can also be very unfair. I wish the winner was decided by vote or something in the final round as well.Time Jinx is a trivia game all about history. I don't think there's anything wrong with that, but as someone who is not a history buff, I get bored of this game very quickly. All it takes is one answer off by 30 years or so, and you've basically lost the game. The scoring system is off, the skill gap between history nuts and non-history nuts is too big, and I really think it deserved more features or depth.Fixy Text is probably the most uninspired game in here. You're given a small text, and you and your friends type nonsense all over it. I think word salad can be funny, but it's significantly less funny when you yourself are making it or watching your friends slowly build off of the text.Dodo Re Mi is actually a really good rhythm game, and feels like it got an entire pack's worth of thought and effort into it. There's tons of songs, tons of funny instruments for your birds to emulate, a difficulty option when picking your instruments, and is an overall great game that I come back to all the time.Hypnotorious has so much potential that it hurts. It's fun on paper, but it's unbalanced, the scoring system is abysmal, and you need a ton of niche pop culture knowledge to know some of the roles you get given. Under all that, the core gameplay is still some fun. It's just bogged down by so many flaws that I can't help but call it the worst game in the pack.I don't think this is the worst pack you can buy out there. I think Tee KO 2 and Dodo make the pack worth getting on sale. But $35 for 2 good games and 3 duds is just not worth it in my opinion. I got it while it was on sale, and you should too. Since this pack is still alright.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been testing out this game and wanted to share my thoughts on it. I played it on a stream with some friends a couple of nights ago and unfortunately, I found the game to be quite underwhelming. Although I bought the game while it was on sale, it still seemed overpriced. This game is not one of the Party Packs that I would choose to play on a night of games with friends. To simplify, here is my mini-review of each game and how it went for me while playing with a group of 6 players:Tee K.O. 2 ( 3.5 / 5 ) ★★★☆☆--------------------------~ This game is fine, it was really quite in my group after the first round, jokes on tee's started to get dry, some of the new additions are awesome, like the new avatars based on past Jackbox games, being able to choose between Tee / Tank /  Or Hoodie is awesome, you also get to choose a different font when making a shirt. I honestly think i prefer the first Tee K.O. over this game, just not a whole lot changed and honestly the soundtrack isn't as energetic as the first game. The final Round plays a lot like Bracketing from party pack 4, two of the finalist tee's are presented, then all players tap on the shirt they want to win the most as much and as fast as you can, after the battle completes, the Winner is declared, and that's Tee K.O. 2, pretty solid title, don't hate it, but not much has really changed since the first addition. Its alright. Timejinx ( 3 / 5 ) ★★★☆☆-------------------------~ This is a very tame trivia game for Jackbox, the object is simple, try and guess when did a event take place on a timeline, for example "When was Apple established?" 1960-2000, then your score is judged based on how close or how off you were to the actual year, points count up like golf, meaning the lower your score i s the better. They shake somethings up like photo-shopping out a landmark in an actual IRL place in the world and you and friends need to guess where in the world it takes place or whats missing. Overall, not a bad game, but very tame if you're expecting the likes of Trivia Murder or Fibbage, a lot of the comments in this game were "WHat!?" and "No way!" or "What the ♥♥♥♥ even is that?"FixyText ( 2.5 / 5 ) ★★☆☆☆------------------------~ I'm sure someone has made this comparison already, but this is basically just making a jumbled message with friends, so its basically Google Dox the Game. There is a theme to vote on before the beginning the game, but, most players just ignore the theme and prompt and just type whatever is funny. which is where this game falls flat.  To score points, players vote on their favorite words that other players have typed, your instinct is probably to tap on whatever made you laugh, so a lot of it was stuff like " PEE PEE POO POO" "♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥, ASS, BUTT" you get it.. and that stuff is only so funny so many times. This goes on for three rounds with no changes at all, then a winner is announced aaaaand that's FixyText. Its OK. Dodo Re Mi ( 4.5 / 5 ) ★★★★☆------------------------~ If there is a game worth checking out in this pack, this is definitely hands down the best one. This is essentially rock-band but with up to 9 players, this its self could be a stand alone title, so many songs and instruments to unlock and experiment with. This is a very chill and laid back type game, there wont be a lot of banter or talking, but that being said, there is nothing wrong with a chill game like this. Its not everyone's cup of tea though as some of friends found it boring after just 2 rounds. This game is great in my opinion, but this game alone i cant recommend you buy pack 10 just to experience this. Hypnotorious ( 2.5 / 5 ) ★★☆☆☆------------------------~ This is the first game where my group of friends got agitated and started to actually argue and point fingers saying that were playing it wrong. But i really just think that no one understood how to play this game. The concept is simple, you and your friends are given a role which will then fit into 1 of 3 mystery category's and the catch is one of you is an Outlier but the twist is, no one knows who the outlier is, not even the outlier knows that they are the outlier which is admittedly a cool concept. But it drags way to long, the game is played in 2 rounds and those just drag! I like the games visuals but i don't know if id rush back in to play this one. --------------------------------------------Over All Score of Party Pack 10 ( 3.5 / 5)   ★★★☆☆--------------------------------------------And that's Pack 10. A mixed bag as i said and i can now see where the mixed reviews are coming from having experienced this game for myself. If you really want to try this one, hop on a stream and play for free LOL or, wait till the game goes on sale like i did. The asking price is way to high in my opinion, you could almost buy 2 Party packs for the price of this game. Unfortunately i feel this game is just going to sit in my library untouched, i just cant see myself going back to this one.

_childDocuments_.review: All Jackbox Party Pack games are the sum of their parts. When a new one come out, it's not just if the games inside it are good, but better or on par with what came before it. Truthfully there is nothing in this pack that outshines the others which you could be playing instead.T-KO 2 does nothing to improve itself from the original besides new art and music, along with the ability to choose your 'type' of shirt (Putting a dent in the name given they are no longer always T-Shirts). It's a format that if you jump back to the original, nothing is different save the ability to re-draw one previous drawing, which while funny isn't selling this as its own independent game, and the last round which is oddly a 'mash the screen' victory rather than a vote when nothing truly changes.Time Jinx, while an okay trivia game, wears down quick as it is nothing general knowledge compared to say, the Wheel or Murder Party versions of a trivia game. Focused on dates and decades, it's rather bland. There's only so many times you can enjoy 'When did this happen' before it gets old - that is, most likely after one round of it.Hypnotorious is a game about lying, but not to the extent of ♥♥♥♥♥' It because the odd one out doesn't know they're precisely that. This also comes into the problem that you have to know what it is you are assigned, otherwise your round is practically done. While it isn't every single time, we've had more than once somebody say 'I don't know who this is' as it pops up on their screen.FixyText was not particularly interesting. It's two teams 'answering a text' in the form of a prompt given with the twist being that everybody can type at the same time and there is no ability to back space. Like Time Jinx, it gets old very quickly.Finally the best game of the bunch is probably their most original - though it isn't an original concept. DodoReMi is a rhythm game much in the vein of Rock Band where notes come down a track and you tap the screen to play and build combos. It's a great game, hence why there are so many clones out there, but it isn't going to be original other than its with up to 9 people all playing a track from 'easy' three note instruments to five note ones with far more intensity. Fun, and you'll enjoy it if you enjoy those games, but the song selection does get old rather quickly.Overall the price of this game to you is one weighed against 9 other games with clearly better choices. It's hard to say 'Let's play Jackbox 10' when you can easily go to other titles with the precious hours you have with family. Pick it up if you want to add it to your list of things to choose from during the evening, but know there are better titles from this same company you can buy instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, none of the games are good, and the scoring is completely gameable if not incoherent across the whole pack.The trivia game of this pack. You guess the year associated with some prompt (assasination of JFK, for example), then you receive 1 point for every year you are off. Lowest score wins. However, the acceptable ranges of years differs wildly between questions; the first question might give you a range of 1990-2010 but question 2 gives you a range of 1600-1700. This means a large inaccuracy in question 1 might score similarly to relatively close guess for question 2. There isn't a ton of variety either, as the final round is only superficially different !!!! The final question will be something like "1000 years ago we landed on the moon", and they want you to write 2969. This is worst game of the entire pack, both conceptually and practically. You're divided into teams and everyone on your team answers a prompt simultaneously. You can move the cursor around and interject into your teammates' sentences, creating misspellings and new phrases. Then the opposing team places votes on their favorite words. There are 2 huge problems with this: 1) the opposing team can refuse to vote, giving you less points, 2) you are awarded bonus points for words constructed by 2 different players. This means that I can place a single character in each of my teammates' words and rack up tons of points. This alone basically guarantees that I win no matter how the opposing team votes. This is intended to generate freeform jokes like Quiplash or Job Job, but really its just an incongruent mess where the "hilarity" is just a bunch of typosA social deduction game where everyone is assigned a secret object/occupation/etc. You're given questions to answer in-character. The goal is to find which other player has an object most similar to you. There is one outlier, so one person will not be paired. It ends up very drawn out and repetitive. We had more fun answering the prompts in absurd and vulgar ways than actually playing.Basically the same as Tee KO 1 except you can change the font or put the drawings on tank tops and hoodies. Wow!!!!!! The final bracket is just a contest to see who can mash the fastest.Didn't play the rhythm game so can't comment. I don't see how it could save this pack.Flops all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox Party Pack 10 is a real test with these party packs. It's a test of what new experiences will work with your friend group, what will work with your phone and what works generally as a gaming concept.I was able to play the >3 player games a couple of times each, before a significant update on November 15, 2023. Rating each of these packs requires a breakdown of each game, so here's what we thought of the 10th one in the series.Fixy Text was loved by everyone, but me. I believe this is where the device bugs hit the hardest. It's an interesting design that is kind of like Job Job and Quiplash from other packs. The fun lies in how interesting, creative and funny your friend group is, with some minimal support from the game. The game provides some prompting, but doesn't rely upon it, so role-playing elements depend on the group you're with, unlike Roomerang or Hypnotorious from this pack. I experienced a lot of bugs while playing, including my cursor and typed letters being randomly applied in the text message, making me a chaotic disaster to play with. Everyone else really loved freestyling text messages with minimal prompts and having their wit acknowledged by others gifting them points.Tee K.O. 2 was a hit among my friend group, and this has definite quality of life improvements over the first. My problems with the first one are mostly resolved in this one, you can re-use text and pictures that weren't used in previous rounds. However, I really didn't like the last round re-using the shirts we've already made and won with - our group really enjoys the surprise and hilarity from introducing new shirts, but this is a new favourite of ours despite this issue.Dodo Re Mi is a highlight. It's Guitar Hero for your phone, which I'm very surprised hasn't been done yet. It can be played solo or with one other person, and has been incredible fun just for my partner and I to play through. It's what we've spent the most time with and had the most connection to from both myself who has mastered most Guitar Hero games and someone who has never played a rhythm game before. This could have been an entirely standalone game with the amount of work going into it. However, my Samsung A13 really struggled, often skipping, lagging and freezing during the game, or having inputs not recognized or seen, but that's probably all on my phone model.Time Jinx is a decent trivia game that is something closer to Guesspionage than a You Don't Know Jack or Trivia Murder Party. It makes good use to contemporary popular cultural historical events for trivia questions. It also has decent for rubberbanding for players who either struggled to remember timelines or guessed poorly. It's fun and interesting, albeit not as much as their other trivia games.Hypnotorious could potentially be the weakest one of the pack. It relies heavily on the group's roleplaying ability, which mine isn't good at, but also has a somewhat confusing premise and prompting. Our group will have to revisit it, but some of them did enjoy it.The November 25th update seems to resolve some issues and improve games somewhat, but I have yet to try. This isn't the weakest of the Jackbox Party Packs, but it's far from the strongest.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly as a long time supporter of jackbox it's just been going downhill for a while and this is the weakest entry, yet. Tee KO 2 is the only standout and it's virtually identical to the first only with slightly better drawing mechanics and 3 shirt types.TimeJinx is the worst game to ever exist in a Jackbox party pack and that's saying something. Just outright awful. They took the worst part of trivia, knowing the exact year of things, and made that the whole game.The bird game is fun and silly and addicting but overall a 6. Just a mild distraction that's not nearly as good as the other rythm games out there.The texting game is probably the best one IMO. it's just pure chaos in a good way and if you and your friends have a similar sense of humor you can come up with some hilarious texts but overall it's a 7/10.And the brainwashing game is also a 7/10. _childDocuments_.review: This has to be the buggiest Jackbox game ever. Games will just stop working midsession, and it's frustrating how often this happens. Don't buy this one, it's easily the worst one. The games in this pack aren't the greatest either.Tee KO 2 is fine until the last round becomes a mash fest, and IMO deciding something over who mashes the screen more is just never fun.TimeJinx is okay? But it's like the easiest trivia game ever.FixyText gets old fast, but it really depends on the people you play with. FixyText has no structure, is super buggy (sometimes points are attributed to you to words you didn't even touch), and the chaos it provides is better utilized by other Jackbox games that require typing like that (Mad Verse City, Job Job, Quiplash). The bugs on this game in particular are too numerous to be unnoticeable. The text doesn't live-update well enough and lags several seconds behind and the game can stop mid-session. All the games work but there are some glitches that need to be fixed and they should be patched ASAP! DODO RE MI SHOULD NOT BE PLAYED REMOTELY OR OVER A STREAM! IT SHOULD BE PLAYED IN A ROOM! The massive out of synchronization with the game is very troublesome.  Now im going to go through each game from Greatest to Least.-----------------------------------------------------------------------FIXYTEXT:This is the most fun game in the pack! It's drunken group texting and it is a riot and one of my newest favorites.Gather your group and pick a phone category and make your own replies as the party splits into groups and re-engineers a reply text. You can't backspace or delete. You have limited characters and it sort of works like (X) Twitter. very fun I laughed my head off.TEE K O 2:It's more TEE K O with more variety, with added fonts and shirt styles (shirts, v-necks and hoodies) The end game is a bit weird but still fun. The game doesn't provided a link at the end of the match like the previous game for the shirt gallery the shirts to buy end up on your device and you buy them from your device. Very fun if you like history and very easy to play.Hypnotorious:This game is a bit confusing but once you get the idea, it is fun. You figure out who the outlier is and accuse them if there are any outliers and receive points that way.  very fun DO NOT PLAY ON A STREAM OR REMOTELY. BEST PLAYED IN A ROOM TOGETHER WITH A GROUP.Dodo Re Mi:This is the worst of the pack due to the technical nature of this game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm probably extra nitpicky about this game due to the price increase and being a long time fan of the series but please bear with me during this reviews. It kind of pains me to rate this negatively. ** ALSO IMPORTANT: I think I found a bug in Time Jinx. The non-impostor always has a line on its mouth like a puppet. Unless its intentional, it's a dead give away to the right answer. Happened to me 3/3 times it popped up ** Okay back to the actual review. The price change actually made me super upset. I suspect it has something to do with Epic Games since the price is 29.99 on there and 34.99 on here; but the increase in price is not budget friendly. As a college student this was price I wasn't that happy to pay. But I did shell out. Why? Three reasons. 1.) I've been a fan of this series since 2016, when there was only 3 party packs. I've been getting every release since, I bring out all the party packs during family parties, or on discord calls, or hangout sessions with friends. I even got hyper fixated on this series for a while and got to visit the Jackbox table at PAX East 2019- I even bought pins (which I sadly lost). And reason 2.) Tee KO 2. Me and probably many other players have been highly anticipating this to be a headliner title; and I've kind of been waiting for at least four years, hoping during each spring/summer the dev team would announce the games this title would be on it. And the time is finally here!! As I'm writing this review I currently havent played it, but I love everything about it. Reason 3.) I got a good discount on this from a third party official site. Well, a good discount for a launch title not a good discount for a game/game on sale. But I saved a bit of money so Im at least happy about that... Also another thing I'd like to add is that with this price point change, nothing about the game got changed either. at the very least I wish and I hope in the future that the devs would consider adding trading cards and badges to these games again!! It's something I've really been missing these past few years. And I think that this is a good time to bring it back for us considering the changes.Now I'm going to dive into the game itself and I'm aware of how nitpicky this may sound but I'm going to list the things I do and don't like, and maybe some improvements that could realistically be made. Starting off with the menu, the introduction was funny, but the actual menu itself lacks soul that the past party packs have been delivering. We are met with the hosts of the five games in a room with each other. I love the room itself, its filled with all the previous games and its cute. But the hosts inclusion is weird. All of the art styles conflict (due to the artstyles being different in all five games) but due to this it feels like they were all inserted last minute and without thought. And I know thats not the case. If we look at other recent games, such as Jackbox Party Pack 8, the menu is stylized and everything matches each other, while looking aesthetically pleasing. Or a menu that always stands out to me, Party Pack 7; its creative uses of 3D models looks so good and its definitely my favorite menu out of all the packs. I hope that in Party Pack 11 the menu will be similar to something seen in 5-9I haven't gotten the opportunity to play every game yet so I will edit my review when I'm able to properly play them, it's only fair. But I will write about the ones I have played so far.I'm quickly including a part about Tee KO 2. I sadly havent been able to play it yet, but I suspect I will not have any disappointments about this game. I got so fanatic when I realized all the characters were going to be from previous games. And I nearly squealed of happiness when the Quiplash mascot was chosen to be the yellow guy. He's my favorite and I always choose him in Quiplash 2 and get so excited if I'm able to randomly get him in 1. I'm also very happy that the captain from Joke Boat and the host from Roomerang made it. If a dev actually reads this entire review (or rant at this point) what are their pronouns? Genuinely curious- I don't know how to refer to them.Time Jinx: Before I start my review... for the love of god I know it's probably part of the pack formula but WHY is there always a trivia game in each of these packs? After a while some of them feel pretty boring and I tend not to play them after the novelty very quickly wears off. I would be actually kind of happy if a future pack didn't include one. I will say this game does a good job with actually having novelty, but I think I will get sick of it quickly. The host has a cool design, I like her. The topics of the questions vary enough to where it isn't all pop culture... but the only other topic is just history. Also in terms of achievements its pretty hard to grind for the 1984 achievement. I'm sure that's intended but it was a little frustrating that it was all left in the hands of RNG.Fixytext: I will give this game another chance with a bigger group, but my first and only round of it was completely unenjoyable. I did not like the chaos of collaborating on text. It went in as many directions as there were people playing (3). I was kind of getting tilted at this game and I was irritated for most of my play-through. I wish there was something else to this game like having the computer judge the texts or having individual answers and vote on those instead.Dodo Re Mi: I really like this game actually. This may be biased of me because I love rhythm games and often play them, but I think this is not only a creative use of phone/smart device/PC controllers but also the potential that a party pack game can rise up to. So far I've only played by myself, but I imagine a room full of friends playing this game would lead to a delightfully noisy room. My two nitpicks of this game are as follows. 1.) I wish the recap of the band part could be skip-able. Or at the very least if you're playing solo. 2.) This isnt a problem for me personally, but I think it's a bad decision to leave a lot of the songs behind locks that are grindy. Having to complete all of the beatmaps for different songs, sitting through the (what feels like) five minute long credits, or playing like 20 songs total to unlock more songs is something a causal player isnt really going to achieve during their sessions. Which the audience for party packs is primarily causal players, am I right? It just feels like maybe a little bit of an oversight.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 10 is another very solid pack in the series and a huge step-up from the disappointment that was last year's pack. Tee K.O. 2 is an even better version of one of the greatest Jackbox games making this one of, if not the best Jackbox game ever made. (10/10)Timejinx is another one of Jackbox's iconic gimmicky trivia games and it's easily one of the best. The game is extremely simple yet extremely fun if you love trivia. The gimmick of the timeline is super unique. (8.5/10)I wasn't looking forward to Fixytext, but it is great. It's so chaotic yet, so fun. (8/10)Dodo Re Mi is a Jackbox version of a rhythm game and its a fine attempt at one. I'm already not a huge fan of rhythm games but it was executed as well as a Jackbox rhythm game could. (6/10)I was most excited for Hypnotorious and it was kinda disappointing tbh. It's kind of a mix between Faking It and Roomerang but I'd rather just play one of those. The concept of the game is good but doesn't really work that well in exectuion. It may be fun with a lot of people (I only played with 5) but I wouldn't recommend with smaller groups. (4/10)One thing that kinda sucks about this pack is the price increase. If you didn't know, Jackbox packs were originally $25 but then $30 became the norm. Now, packs are going to cost $35 which kinda sucks. I am ok with it because it isn't TOO much of a price increase and I know Jackbox Games only releases one game a year. But, it's kinda lame. Because of the price increase, I can't recommend this pack over better packs like 3, 7, and 8.TLDR: Pack is very solid but price is higher than other, better packs.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this pack, although as a pack, it isn't the best.**While most of the games in the pack feel a bit hit-or-miss, Dodo Re Mi is a masterpiece that more than makes up for it.**FixyText is alright. It creates a lot of chaos, which can be good with the right groups. The text to speech at the end of the round is fun, especially if simply typing in garbage. However, there isn't much in it to make it very repayable in successive sessions.An overall upgrade to the successor. The shirt UI is nice to work with, and the ability to continue off from a previous shirt adds something new. However, the core gameplay doesn't change much.A masterpiece of a game. Everything feels well thought-out and highly detailed. The background music is great, the playable songs are fun, and the many instrument choices add a lot of variety to each play.- The ability to quickly switch out players. When a player closes a tab or loses connection, they are also removed from the game's lobby. In addition, the host player can be easily changed as well.- Great customization and accessibility options. Players can remove animations, incorrect sounds, or decide to unlock all the content if they so choose.- The song selection UI is great. It is easy to use and also changes based on screen size for faster selection when possible. My only gripe is that there isn't a way to preview a part of the song.- Instrument selection is also easy and lets players of different skill ranges to find instruments that can work. The song preview is also nice. I also appreciate the ability to rebind notes on desktop devices.- The syncing method is very nice and satisfying, a good way to resolve latency issues in streams.- The actual note UI is quite nice and responsive for the most part. However, it is somewhat graphics heavy and can lag some devices. I've also noticed that what appears on the player's screen doesn't always match the final outcome.Time Jinx is a trivia game about time and history. It's got a few different kinds of prompts. The prompts are also decently challenging. Not a bad choice if you want a time-focused trivia game.This one is not great. For a hidden role game, for new players, it is really not obvious at all at what one is supposed to do to win. Until the end of the first round, when a major concept of the game is revealed. This means that players who have played before have an advantage. Sure, there is a second round of the same thing to make up for to initial confusion, but I think that a single short round with a better explained premise would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: As it is at the moment, I can't recommend this instalment of the series. As a chronic Jackbox player I feel that this entry into the franchise is the weakest one yet. It's also hard to justify spending £30 given the overall quality of the games. As is usual, some games are better than others, but the disparity in quality is the strongest yet. Do Do Re MiEasily the best of the pack. Some of the instruments were hilarious, and the harder instruments were manic but fun. Trying to 'beat' the levels was a good challenge, and the option to play the song back is welcome.TKO 2More of the same from one of my favourite entries in a previous pack. Perhaps not enough has been done to improve upon the original, but if it ain't broke etc. Features such as changing the clothes and font add some quirkiness. Feels more like TKO 1.5TimejinxA fairly inoffensive trivia game. Feels like a free app you'd play for 5 or 10 minutes for a quick laugh.FixytextThe potential for creating funny words is all this game really has going for it. Bugs-a-plenty on our devices, such as some deletion allowed and words not being entered. If these were fixed it could be decent, but overall it's unsatisfying with a confusing premise and anticlimactic finish.HypnotoriousThe worst of the pack. Not well explained, strange execution, some glaring bugs and issues (giving players the wrong hints etc), and just not fun. This one could've easily been sacrificed for more effort put into the other games.If the price was reduced by 33% or so, I'd probably pick it up, with the hope that the more glaring issues and problems would be fixed. As it is, avoid it and pick up an older, more well-received pack.
