_childDocuments_.review: Another banger of a pack from Jackbox Games.Tee-KO 2 is more of the great stuff. It takes the better drawing system of Champ'd Up and puts it in the Tee-KO format. It also adds hoodies and tank tops, new fonts, and an option to edit a first round drawing in the second round.FixyText is probably the best game in the pack. It's like if Word Spud was good. I don't know how to explain it, frankly, but it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. You'll be crying laughing from the sheer chaos.Timejinx is trivia with a time gimmick. A decent trivia game worth coming back to, with a nice focus. Not too difficult, so even if you're stupid you can still enjoy it.Dodo Re Mi is a rhythm game, which somehow works really well. As far as rhythm games go it's kinda meh, but it's unique enough with the party gimmicks to make it a blast, and has a real addictive quality to it.Hyptonotorious is a social deduction game that's frankly too difficult, and requires four people to play. Good luck finding a large enough group of smart people to play it. I know I can't. The idea is pretty neat, at least.Overall, 4/5 great games, and even the worst still has a charm to it. A lot better than some of the previous packs. Makes the price increase sting a bit less?

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't buy for full price (nor any jackbox, to be honest) but I don't get the hate for this one. FixyText is awful, granted, and Tee KO 2 is Tee KO but again... The other three minigames, though, are the most fun my friends and I have had playing Jackbox in some time. Timejinx was a BLAST! Trying to pinpoint when exactly X thing happened is a fun twist to trivia instead of choosing from a pool of choices and the theme of the game is very fun. Hypnotorious is a bit hard to grasp at first, but when you get the hang of it it's extremely fun! Plus the "traitor" also has to find out whether he is the traitor or not, so it's more of a coop game than anything else and I really enjoy it. And Dodo Re Mi is a blast, which is a statement everyone seems to agree with. I recommend this jackbox a lot, ngl

_childDocuments_.review: The 10th installation of the Jackbox Party Pack series is a pretty decent one! Amongst my group of friends, we found TimeJinx to be the most enjoyable game - you can suck at trivia and still do pretty well in the game since the answer format is a time range with respective scoring rather than a singular option. We also enjoyed Tee K.O. 2, as it basically improved upon the masterpiece that was Tee K.O. with new drawing tools and different clothing/text options. The game that followed was FixyText, which we honestly loved because of its chaotic nature as multiple people are typing together nonsense in the same prompt (also, the text-to-speech readback makes it even better). Dodo Re Mi was a fun rhythm-style game, but kind of got old quickly. Finally, I sort of understand where the creators were trying to go with Hypnotorious, but it just fell flat for us and became this pack's "throwaway" game.Overall, this party pack is above average and has a handful of entertaining and interesting games! If the group you are playing with enjoys time-based trivia, silly drawings, chaotic wordsmithing, and rhythm-style games, then I recommend picking up this pack!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good despite the price increase, but some of the games could have a little MORE. But that's probably because Dodo Re Mi has SO MUCH effort put into it.Timejinx: Interesting trivia, fun even for those who don't LOVE trivia!Fixytext: Wordspud, but good! It's definitely hectic, and fun. Go crazy when playing this game, it will be fun.Tee KO 2: Tee KO, but with even better music and small improvements. It feels more like an update than a proper sequel though, which is unfortunate.Hypnotorious: My personal favorite game of the pack, but it feels unfinished. I feel like there's supposed to be a bit more to the end of this game, but the base concept is so great that it's very enjoyable.Dodo Re Mi: The proverbial, and literal, golden goose of the game. If you enjoy rhythm games, this is essentially 70% of the pack's content/value! Many different instrument options, and a whole lot of replayability.-TL;DRThis pack is solid. There are no bad games, but some games aren't as good as they could be.Dodo Re Mi is 70% of the value, so you better love rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm posting what I put on the Jackbox subreddit here since I think it warrants a review and should be seen by more people.The pack overall is… not good.When my group played TeeKO2, it was literally just more of the same, with more drawing options (although I didn’t notice any way to change the size of the drawing tool). We had to stop early in the game since one of us got kicked out and couldn’t rejoin. Also, a player should not be able to vote for themselves. I thought this was like a weird glitch when it was a thing in TeeKO, but now I see this is intentional. Why?Time Jinx is worse than I thought. It is literally just “pick a number and see if you are right.” if you know history then this is a cakewalk. It goes on for a while like this and when I realized this, it got boring. Also, the fact that getting a jinx does absolutely nothing is extremely disappointing. The lack of like an intro to the game makes it really awkward for me, it just jumps right in (I don’t have tutorials off and didn’t skip any instructions). I don’t even think the host introduces themselves.Fixytext is literally just typing in a Google Doc with the backspace/delete key broken and calling it a game. The majority of the time players will just ignore the prompt and do their own thing. This isn't really a game in my eyes, it's practically on the same level as Word Spud.Dodo re mi is also not that good. the fun comes from the garbled mess your group creates and that’s honestly not that fun in theory or in practice. we would skip the replay of the song and the results would just awkwardly say “eaten” or “survived” and our group didn’t care. we just wanted to see who did the best and who was the winner, which is only truly revealed when you quit the game. I would hate to see this game played in an environment that has poor connection.Hypnotorious was the one I was looking forward to the most and, unfortunately, isn’t that well executed. Our group struggled to get into similar categories. For example, my objective was “a sleepy bear” while the person with the same category was “Genie from Aladdin” (the category was “lives in a cave”). This also felt like it went on forever and it killed the mood when we found out there was a second round, so we quit.Overall, this is not a good pack from our perspective. Nothing to do but wait for the next entry in the series I guess…It sucks that I have to give a jackbox game a negative review since my group typically loves jackbox games.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems worth it so far for the two games I HAVE played in this pack.FixyText is your classic word salad game. Backspace and Delete are banished. your goal is to reply to the texts sent to some valley girl with whatever BS gets them to stop. You have four categories of texts to reply to and three successive texts to deal with. But each reply text can contain a word or phrase from your reply, a sin you will have to answer for. For example, there was a HR reply that asked 'can you confirm what is '♥♥♥♥♥♥'?. What followed was a Liar Liar/SOAD-esque litany of double entendres from me, my sister and her friend. Glorious if your friends are funny already.DoDoReMi is an ambitious game that turns your phone into a rhythm game controller, you try and match the inputs on screen to the beat. However, it has problems on mobile Firefox and can errorscreen out on certain devices. Difficulty is fine, rhythm game fans will have fun, as each song is split into four 'acts' and the third act is always 'throw notes at the wall and see what sticks'. More people will push the threshold for scoring further away, so everyone has to try and pull their weight. This one is fun, but if your device hard crashes or has problems, you can't join back in for obvious reasons relating to the difficulty of syncing the beatmap.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time officially reviewing a Jackbox game as a long-time player & a fan of the franchise. This is also the first time that I have to say that I CANNOT fully recommend this pack, especially not at the price that it's asking for & this is in consideration of their recent patches of the game. It is impressive that it took up to 10 packs for me to finally say this, but I'm concerned that this yearly-release model may continue to harm the quality of JB games in the future.-INDIVIDUALLY-Tee K.O. 2: While this IS in my opinion an upgrade from the original Tee K.O. & I do personally prefer the bracket format, I can also see why people might miss the gauntlet style of voting from the original as well. Generally, I do feel like this sequel is better structured & doesn't feel like it drags out as much as the original sometimes did. I do wish however that the art & the text were more adjustable & didn't feel like they were sometimes too scrunched together. I've found that the bugs that plagued this particular game have been mostly fixed, although some improvements could still be made.FixyText: Even after this game has been patched, I still can't find myself fundamentally enjoying this one & my stream friends mostly agree that this particular game is a bit of a mess. We're not entirely sure of how or why, but it feels like more often than not certain text messages just don't appear on-screen at all or they're very delayed. Not only that, but it's way too chaotic & nothing stops players from typing out complete nonsense (AIHFIUSBHBKJHABXABXA, etc.) & there's not really a strong enough criteria for why players should vote certain words over others. WordSpud feels more put-together. Sure, you could say "well, it's more fun with the right people", but you can say that about ANY game. This didn't work.Timejinx: Probably the best [new] game in this pack, albeit very basic/very challenging for people that don't cheat. My only personal complaint in this game is that for a game called "TimeJINX" the JINX-es don't mean that much in the grand scheme of things. No bonus points or events. Nothing. It's more just a "Oh...that's neat & coincidental..." thing. Bugs that I noticed with Timejinx have been mostly fixed from what I'm able to tell, though this game didn't have many issues.Hypnotorious: Oh boy. Probably the most polarizing game here. I like this game, conceptually, but execution-wise this game does a very poor job explaining things. This is the same issue I had with Nonsensory from Pack 9, even though I liked that game. Why explain that you can double-down points halfway through the game & not at the start? Same with this game. Why only explain the whole jar assortment thing in bits & chunks & not right from the get-go? Also, while I appreciate JB trying to add more flavor by having players award points while applauding during reveals, this makes certain aspects of the game null-&-void when somebody could just win based off of those votes alone. For that matter, why can't we see the scoreboard after Round 2 is over? Some people LIKE seeing those, you know. Like FixyText, kind of a mess. Before this game got patched, Hypnotorious would crash often. It SEEMS to run OK now. This doesn't change the messy layout.DoDo Re Mi: A fine rhythm game, though sometimes a little laggy. I don't really have much to say about this one, although I can see why for some people this game by itself makes the pack worth it. That isn't the case for me. I do like the fact that you can play this game solo without needing other players as well & that does help this game stand out a little bit.OVERALL tl;dr: For the 10th pack (basically an anniversary pack), this should've been better than what it was. I don't get the price hike. Wait for this to go on sale before purchase. Not an awful game, but needed better quality control. There needs to be hefty consideration for the development of future JB games/packs to come. These can't start feeling rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda get where the negative reviews for this game are coming from, but I don't 100% agree.Yes, this is NOT the best Party Pack Jackbox has released. When you think about getting just a Party Pack, get 7 or maybe 3, these are the two almost everyone agrees on to be the best of the best. That being said, JPP 10 is NOT a bad game. If you love Jackbox games, you will have fun with this pack, HOWEVER:- The game was released unfinished. Not unplayable at all, but had some bugs and some missing features and I do get why people are angry about it. The production quality has really increased over the course of the last couple of packs, releasing a new one with 5 new games each year is insanity. I'm always happy about new Jackbox, but I can wait half a year or even a full year longer, if it increases the quality. I personally had not encounternd a large amount of bugs, but some functions were not 100% working as intended for sure. However, it seems like the latest patch got rid of most issues and even added some new content, which is very welcomed, but that we had a month to get those fixes is really frustrating, especially when you think about...- the increased price. I understand that the production quality got a lot higher in the newest packs and I do agree that the newer ones are worth more than like JPP 1 or 2, but given the state this game was released in, this was kinda disappointing.- The games itself aren't peak Jackbox, but in my opinion, there is much fun to be had with them. This point is very subjective tho, so take the following reviews for the individual games with a grain of salt.The games:Tee KO 2:Sequel to one of my favs in the franchise, and a good one! The new additions are nice, espacially the option to choose the font is really funny, however I wish there were more options. The new bracket structure also enhances the game by a mile, because seeing the same shirt over and over again was kinda lame.The game does provide a few enhancements compared to its prequel, but also doesn't offer that much new, but I like it.TimeJinx:It's a pretty straight forward trivia game, nothing really special about it. I was kinda disappointed with this one, not because its a bad game (it's not!), but because this isn't nearly as creative as former Jackbox trivia games. It's solid, but just so standard and the time hopping theme doesn't contribute that much. Also for some players, some of the special rounds were a little counter-intuitive.It's alright, nothing bad here, but also like I already said: very standard.Fixy Text:This one's strange. It's some of the best fun I've had with a Jackbox game ever, but also... it's barely a game? You could literally play a bootleg version of this just with Google Docs, but still it's so funny and I kinda love it? This is not an outstanding game technically, but for me personally it kinda is? I don't know, it's very stupid and very stupid fun.Dodo Re Mi:Yeah this one's a banger. It has so much content (even got more content with the update) and just the fact that you have actual progression in a Jackbox game ist kinda sick? And if you don't want to unlock everything (even though I love it), you can literally cheat and unlock everything from the start. Gameplay-wise it's kinda very basic, because it's just Piano Tiles, but that you all contribute to one piece is just really cool, the instruments are hilarious and the songs are just bangers. I might want to add a minor criticism: Because you're all tapping on your own device, there is little to none player interaction during the actual gameplay, which is the main reason most people play Jackbox in the first place, but listening to the final piece together is really funny. Also we had some issues with the web controller while playing. There were a few disconnects and the website was sometimes lagging, which is kinda terrible for a timing-based game. As of now, I can't confirm if the update has fixed the issues or not, since I wasn't able to try it yet.Still my point stands: That one's a banger.Hypnotorious:My most anticipated game, and I think it's good, but it has some major issues. The concept is really cool and I think it works well, that is if all players are familiar with how the game works. Unfortunately, this is probably the worst tutorial I have ever seen in a Jackbox game. There is no reason why to gatekeep the very important fact that there is outliar until the start of the second round, it really makes no sense. Also I still don't fully understand how the final vote works and how exactly points are awarded, which is just bad. Again, I don't know if the update fixed some of these issues, but I really hope so, because otherwise this game is really fun and creative. I have read in the patchnotes, that at least the hint system got finally fully implemented, it was very confusing at first and just made the game feel unfinished. One more piece of criticism: Please give us the option to play just one full round instead of two, would be nice for a shorter game.So that's the Jackbox Party Pack 10. It's good, not the best, but still a good game. I will just mention one more thing, because it always bothers me with Jackbox: Please give us more option to customize a game. Give us more setting options, please! Like how many rounds will be played etc. I have to admit that this game does have more settings options, but they are still very limited. It's not as bad as in some of the older packs (Push the Button really needs customizable settings), but I don't get why they are so extremely limited.That's it.I had fun with it.I will probably have even more fun with it in the future.Yeah.Dodo Re Mi bangs.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I have overall positive thoughts on the Pack as a whole, but it's definitely more mixed and certainly not as strong as I feel about Packs 7 or 9Tee K.O. 2 is pretty alright—I do prefer the original for its characters and aesthetics (and, admittedly, the host), but the new garment options and matchup format are upgrades, outside of the final roundTimejinx is not for me in terms of gameplay, as someone whose weakest subjects are history and pop culture—it's my least favorite trivia-type game for sure, but its music and sound design are amazingFixyText is one of my favorite games due to the hard rules it can implement outside of a Google Doc, and I personally see a lot of incentive in the text base; it gives you substance to build off of and inspires you on what kind of wackiness to write aboutDodo Re Mi is lovely! Its soundtrack is killer, among the best for an individual Jackbox game, and I'm impressed with how organically they made the gameplay work. Some complain about the game making you feel "detached" from each other, but that's honestly an upside in a livestream environmentHypnotorious is my favorite game from this pack—It's admittedly hard to grasp at first, but I think once you do a game, you can REALLY have some fun with it if you like social deduction and analysis!!(I've only had 0.3 hr as the host but i've played the games for much, much longer as a guest)

_childDocuments_.review: Every game in this pack is very surface level and boring. This is by far the worst Jackbox pack because there's not one redeeming game among them.Tee K.O 2Fine, but pretty much the same as the first. A few extra colors, some extra shirt shapes, and new avatars (recycled from other Jackbox games) aren't enough to make it feel fresh. The streak system is removed in favor of a bracket, which is theoretically more fair but we found it less fun. The final round relies on spam tapping to vote which is just annoying.Fixy TextThe scenarios are so bland that the player-generated texts have to stand on their own, which they don't. The humor relies on random, out of context typing and since there's several people typing at once it's impossible to craft a punchline with intentionality.TImeJinxGuesspionage but worse because at least that has a social deduction aspect. You just guess the years of historical events and that's it. The answer is revealed and everyone goes, "huh." and moves on.HypnotoriousEach person gets a character and has to respond to prompts as if they were that character, then sort themselves into buckets based on which responses they think go together. Responses are not allowed to be very long, so they're pretty shallow and you have to be purposefully obvious. You only get two choices for which character to be, so it happened multiple times that someone got something they weren't familiar with and had to wing it. For one round our buckets were "noun" "verb" and "adjective" which required us to somehow guess the exact titles of the medias each other's characters were from. Couldn't tell how points were being assigned and the winner felt random.Dodo Re MiThis one was a letdown because it could have been great but it's too glitchy. You're basically playing guitar hero on your phone, but the notes stutter and lag and the sound didn't play consistently on any of our phones, so it's impossible to keep up even on the easiest songs. Our playback was a cacophony. The score system is punishing despite this, and the birds getting eaten every time was upsetting.I knew as soon as we were done playing every game that we would never pick it up again, so I asked for a refund. Disappointing from a studio that's usually so consistent. They needed to workshop this one more before they released it. Hopefully it's a fluke and the next one is better.

_childDocuments_.review: When looking at the other reviews for this game I was surprised to see people being so negative. In my opinion this is a very strong collection of Jackbox games. _childDocuments_.review: My bad, I HAVE to write a negative review to this Party Pack.I really like party games, and I think Jackbox games have always been very fun to play, or even just to try.This 10th party pack was a delusion for many reasons, with the main reason being that it costs too much for what it offers. The price increased, while the general quality of the minigames decreased, and also the development support to the games highly decreased.This is not the first time I'm reviewing this game. I'm updating my review because latest update to this game made some minigames (almost) unplayable (again).I'll write a small review for each minigame, based on my experience for playing this pack with my friends, giving a score for each minigame and finally the score for the whole Party Pack.TEE KO 2: (Score: 1/10)More a "TEE KO 1.5" than a "TEE KO 2".We tried it just for curiosity. We didn't like at all the first TEE KO already, we knew this wouldn't have been different. The game is basically the same as the first one, it just has a few more tools for drawing. Nothing different. Not fun at all, pretty boring. We never played it anymore.I don't understand why they thought there was the need to fill this spot with another TEE KO game, this space could have been filled with a new funnier game with new mechanics, instead of a copy-pasted one.TIMEJINX: (Score: 7/10)This game was for me the real surprise of this pack. The only game of this pack worthy of being played on repeat. A trivia based on getting as close as possible to the correct year of a given event, with a few variations from a round to another. The gameplay is very well done and studied, it works really well and it's funny.This game would be a 9.5/10, but one of the latest updates ruined it. In the final round, everyone gets a -40% bonus, regardless of their answer and position in the time bar, ruining the final score.Also, the narrator is pretty boring in this minigame, she always says the same things and slows down the gameplay. I would add the choice to skip those parts to speed up the game a little.FIXYTEXT: (Score: 3/10)Should be a 0/10, it's a 3 just because of the few exhilarating moments it gave to me and my friends.I had high hopes for this game, but it ended up being the biggest delusion of this pack.Very cool and fun idea, very fun gameplay mechanics, but awful execution.It had a lot of potential, this is the most cahotic game and could have been very exhilarating, it is mostly frustrating instead.The game was very buggy when first released, it was unplayable basically. Now it has become playable, but still too buggy to be played peacefully.Each game there is one of the players who can't write anything, or if he tries to write something the only things that are written are letters and new lines, ending up ruining the game for everyone.Despite of the bugs, the conversation inputs seem really uninspired and boring to play with, except for some of those in the "Spicy" category.The character limits doesn't give enough space to play when there are too much players. It's ok to limit characters to avoid having too long messages, it's just that it's too low right now.DODO RE MI: (Score: 5/10)Each player has to play a weird instrument on his smartphone, and then as a final result the song everyone was playing will be played again with all instruments played by players to hear the whole result. Not the most original idea of gameplay, funny if you play it just a couple times, very boring if you try to go on playing it more.This game was a complete mess at first when it was released. A few updates made it work properly and made it enjoyable.When I read its description, at first I thought this game would have let me play some famous pop songs, the songs you're able to play are instead just classic songs, mostly well known, and you even have to unlock them by playing more. It would have been funnier to play other kind of songs too, other than just classic music.HYPNOTORIUS: (Score: 8/10)Other than Timejinx, the only funny game to play more than once in a lifetime in this pack. Each player gets assigned a character (or animal, or anything in general), and player have to understand, by the end of the third round, which players belongs to their same category, and who's the anomaly and belongs alone to a category. Very funny to play, good mechanics. It is maybe a little too long, since the game is repeated two times, I would have cut it just after the first one and then let the players decide if they wanted to play more or not.Instructions aren't very clear, each time I play this game with someone new who hasn't played it yet, I have to stop and explain myself how the game works.I had to play a whole game the first time before I could understand completely how it works, and still I find pretty unclear how points are assigned to players. I also find the points system being wrong, since it's more a coop game than individual game, but despite of the score the game is funny to play.The latest updates made the hints useful to better understand the categories, while when this game was just released I felt they were kinda useless.Total score of this Party Pack: 4.5/10For being a pack with only two decent minigames and three unplayable or boring games the price is set pretty high. With Timejinx fixed it would be a 5.5, with Fixytext playable it might even be a 6/10, but right now 35€ to play just with Timejinx, rarely with Hypnotorius and never with the other three minigames are really too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly surprised by the low ratio of positive to negative reviews compared to the other packs, because appart from the price change, this pack doesn't really stand out from other packs.Seeing the reviews and the concept of the game, I was prepared to hate this. I expected it to be a similar joy killer as joke boat. The game turned out better than I expected, but it's still the worst game in the pack for me and I doubt I'll play it again any time soon. It just doesn't really have any meat.To be honest, I wasn't the biggest fan of the first game and similarly, not a big fan of this one either, but I know it's a general fan favorite, so it's pretty likely that it's a game you'll enjoy, even if I didn't. If you like drawing games, this is the game for you in this pack.A solid trivia game, fun for a few rounds. It doesn't have a very strong hook that sets in appart from other trivia games, but there is also nothing holding it back.This game is a bit more complex than your average jackbox game. Players will be split up between a few categories that are linked with each other in some way. While players don't know their category, each gets assigned a person or item that belongs to their category and needs to answer questions as their character in order to give enough clues to find the other people that belong in their category. The catch is that 1 player is alone in their category and isn't told this, so you need to be.careful of how much you share, so people can't easily tell that you're the odd one out.It's my personal favorite game, provided I play with people who have a taste for something more complex like I do.That said, I have to admit that this game has a glaring issue: the scoring and voting system just does not make any sense whatsoever and generally has terrible feedback. It's a game where you kinda need to focus on the journey and not the destination. The winner might as well be arbitrary.Also, the tutorial is just really bad...This game stands out above the rest and you can tell that a lot of work went into the making of this game. It wouldn't surprise me if this game is the main reason behind the price increase of this pack. It has nice selection of songs and instruments. You are able to choose your personal difficulty with your instrument choice, each with an appropriate risk-reward for your score. And it has a genious "tap tap tap" feature that allows you to sync up with the host even over large delays due to streaming for example.In my personal jackbox ranking of the 10 packs, this one managed to end up in 4th place

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda surprised at the mixed reviews this pack's getting. After a few plays I genuinely think it's among the top packs ever.-Tee K.O. 2 is exactly what you think it is. A welcome update to one of the best Jackbox game ever.-FixyText is a weird one. It's probably terrible for a group of casual acquaintances, but great with a group of people who know each other well and have lots of experience riffing off of each other. Each time I've played this it's created at least one running gag for the rest of the night. It's one of those games where the group has to 'provide their own fun,' which I know isn't for everyone, but good dumb fun for those who can.-Hypnotorious seems to be getting all the hate, but I like it. I think trying to figure out what the categories are and who belongs where is a good time, but I'm not sure why we shouldn't just blurt out who we are immediately? I get that the outlier needs to figure that out and then hide the fact that they're the outlier from the group, but statistically you're probably not the outlier, so why not just force them to out themselves? I've probably played well over 60 social deduction games of various sorts, and while I like the mechanics here, not sure about the meta-game though. -Timejinx is a trivia game. It's kinda like the card game Timeline, but not as good. No real discussion is fostered by the mechanics and it isn't going to change anyone's mind about trivia games. It's a trivia game!-Dodo Re Mi is probably the best Jackbox game since Murder Mystery Party. It's a riot with a bunch former Rock Band addicts and sounds silly as hell when everyone's jamming in the same room. I think this game would lose A LOT of it's charm if played virtually via Discord or something, but it's a blast in person. Also, being one of the few (only?) true co-operative games makes it a very welcome addition to the Jackbox line-up.I really like this pack. I've played it a few times and it's a big hit with every group I've played it with too. I do think most of the games here play best in person, and a few of the games, namely Dodo Re Mi, Hypnotorious & FixyText, would all suffer greatly from being played virtually, but overall I highly recommend, especially if you have long running Jackbox nights.

_childDocuments_.review: A new year, a new pack! Starting off: I have heard some sad, but justified criticisms about this pack, mainly with bugs. (Those'll be quashed soon, and they haven't tainted my experience.) Despite that, I think there's gold in here, and these are mighty fine pieces of gold. (I should say while I have played it for myself, the majority of the time I spent playing it was with others.)Here are my summaries:Tee K.O 2: I think it's a good improvement of the original, featuring quality of life features and changes to how shirts win the rounds.FixyText: Chaotic would be the best word to describe it. Chaotic, good fun. Though I'll admit that chaotic isn't everyone's cup of tea, but listening to the sentences is worth it imo, heh.Timejinx: It might get repetitive for some, but I think this was a really good trivia experience with a lot of charm. (Same goes with a lot of the games, not just in this pack.) I like it's time travelling aspect a lot, and appreciate the variety in the questions.Hypnotorious: Admittedly a bit confusing, though I can see what they were going for here. Trying to figure out who belongs and who doesn't, this is one of those games where I have to play a bit more to form more words, but I think as of now; It's alright.Dodo Re Mi: The highlight of the pack for me, from it's ambitious concept alone. I still can't believe they pulled it off so well. Like, daaang. You could tell that they put a lot of work in this, and it shows. From the songs and the instruments alone. If there's anyone that can make a song like Row, Row, Row Your Boat sound cinematic, it would be Jackbox's music makers, heh.I think Pack 10 is a very good pack, despite it's bugs.I'm hoping people will come around to it once the patch comes around.

_childDocuments_.review: Tee KO 2 is ok but its only marginally better than the original. The other 4 games range from mid to godawful. Time jinx is actually pretty ok but nothing special.This is probably in the bottom 3 worst packs theyve released. Cant believe they thought they could charge an extra $5 for this. I think they should stop doing yearly releases and just release more polished packs, I feel like the last 4 have been increasingly full of bad games.

_childDocuments_.review: Another year, another Jackbox, and it is a fun time as always! Tee K.O. 2: Wow what an improvement! Feels a lot better and the changes they made with the bracket system, more options for fonts and shirt types, and changing already made drawings in the last round are all amazing improvements! Time Jinx: Super fun trivia game! I like all the types of questions it asks since the game is able to leverage anything from history. Honestly, I think this might be my favorite game from this pack.FixyText: Fun game although in my experience typing has been clunky because my phone tends to try an auto correct but since you can't back space in the game it causes problems, so maybe turn off auto correct if you phone does that for this game. Anyways, this game got a lot of laughs and is pretty simple. I'd say this was my least favorite of the pack but doesn't mean I didn't have a good time!Dodo Re Mi: Surprisingly really good! Didn't know what to expect going in with a rhythm game coming from Jackbox but I actually really like it! Make sure to tap when they tell you to tap because if you don't it messes up everything entirely since the device you are using needs to by synced. The only other problem I have had in this game was that with some of the holding and moving at the same time sections, the game would sometimes just stop registering which I thought was weird. Otherwise from those instances, the game works very well and the song selections so far have been quite good.Hypnotorious: Good deduction game! I really like the concept it has and had a lot of fun trying to decipher who was the odd one out. Only thing I would say is that so far I feel like it has been a little too easy to figure it out but that's only with a few sessions so far so maybe I haven't experienced the game enough. The game concept and the fun me and my friends had was amazing!Overall good party pack! Maybe not the best one ever but Jackbox is always fun and I love playing these games every year! I always recommend these games for a fun time!

_childDocuments_.review: Price was raised and quality was lowered. My group found the set of games pretty bland, there wasn't a standout game like there usually is. I have at least one game on every other pack that we come back to.TKO 2 - Strictly worse than TKO 1. No charm, very barebones, and the final round was made worse. The only good change was adding hoodies/wifebeaters which adds to the amusement with a well timed use of oneFixytext - AI doesn't give you enough to work with, basically gives you one sentence and then you have to all create all the ideas/comedy yourself. I don't get how this game even made it through development, it's just Job Job but significantly worse.Hypnotorious - Pretty decent game but confusing at first, if your group understands the premise and can make good blurbs it can be fun but once again this game relies purely on the players, doesn't give you much to work with at all.Timejinx- Solid idea but feels a little more basic than some of the other trivia games in the past, like you are almost never playing this over trivia murder party, it's just strictly worse.Dodo Re Mi - seemed fun if you liked guitar hero back in the day but theres not much more to it beyond that, you just all separately play guitar hero and then see how bad everyone ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up at the end, and it is difficult so thats probably the only funny part. Probably the most unique/effort game that had potential at least.So yea, for 35 bucks definitely not worth it. Wait until sale at best.

_childDocuments_.review: Woof. Almost hard pass: Tee KO 2 is almost PERFECT, almost every change I wanted was put in EXACTLY as how I wanted! It's easily one of their best individual games ever.But the rest. Oh my gosh. I really hope they fix some of these. I refunded it. You can see us play it here =/    I can't recommend it for the full $35, but once it's on sale for $15~ I'll get it just for Tee KO.TimeJinx is okay. If you like trivia, specifically exact-ish dates of historical events, it's great. I wish it had a no-dates mode, the later rounds are fun but much of the score comes from exact date rote memorization, my least favorite thing from school. 4/10Fixy Text is a disaster. It's not a fun one like jobjob. I get what it's trying to do, but it doesn't work. Everyone types at once and picks a cursor spot, and the result is kind of just garbled nonsense. It'd work better if you could only change cursors once, or if you could stop someone else from typing as your 'power' instead. Or...something. It's just not very fun even after you get the hang of it, everyone just types random crap.People vote for funny words, so it's best to just spam funny/offensive words based on your crowd. Scoring would be better if you had to pick consecutive words to reward people who managed to fill out a coherent thought. 2/10Dodo Re Mi is just Guitar Hero. It's unplayable on mouse and the tutorial of all things is extremely hard. We just quit. The other games can be fixed with SEVERE changes, this one cannot. 0/10Hypnotorious is one of those "everyone has to play the game EXACTLY right for it to be fun" games. Your first play of it will be a nightmare. You can either be funny or play it right, and I don't like games like those. 1/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is buggy. Know that right now. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to buy a Jackbox game, this one is mediocre at best. FixyText can be buggy, DoDo Rei Me crashes on my phone so I cannot say anything about it, and Hypnotorious is hard to understand and play right. The other two games, TimeJinx and TKO2 are very good! I recommend instead of Party Pack 10, getting 3 instead. _childDocuments_.review: Only voting negative due to the increased price along with poorer performance.Tee. K. O. 2 fixes my main gripe of the original (the music), and does exactly what it needs to as a sequel to Tee. K. O. I may not like drawing games all too much due top not being a good mobile phone artist, I can at least have fun with the game. FixyText is an absolute blast with my group, no real complaints other than the questionable voting system. Right up there with JobJob for best games. TimeJynx is a trivia game that makes it a bit more bearable for those who hate trivia by being more laid back compared to something like Trivia Murder Party. The golf-style point system is unique for a jackbox game, with the credit being a fun addition to help level the playing field if somebody is opff by an odd 30 years for a previous question. Dodo Re Mi is good as a rhythm game, but I'm biased as a rhythm game enjoyer, so your milage may vary. Holding out on an update to add more songs if anything. In my opinion, Hypnotorious is the dud of the pack by far. It's a good concept with frankly poor execution. The main issue with the game is that it drags on for so long. So much so that it is consolidated to just 2 rounds. At least other 2 round games like Tee. K. O. make up for it by making the players feel more involved rather than just answering prompts vaguely before having everybody pick an odd-one-out. Wait for a patch or two at the very least before buying. And maybe a salw while you're at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe people are pooping on possibly one of the best packs of the franchise (is it worth 35 dollars is a different story)I think this pack has the best charm aspect/ art design of any of the packs by far. It for sure does not have the best music though, even though it is good. Onto individual ratings:Tee K.O 2: gosh they really did improve this game it used to be a 6/10 imo but the pacing improved, the drawing improved, the customization the charm all improved. I didn’t really like the spam tapping last round though but hey what can you do. Recency bias and allowing the creators to vote on the shirts are still things that irk me about the game. Solid 8.5/10TimeJinx: One of the better trivia games for sure. Very fast paced so you don’t get bored, includes pop culture + history, and the side minigames were cool . Obviously drawbacks of it being a pure trivia game and not pacing too much variety in gameplay and I don’t understand what the jinx thing does like I guess you both chose the same answer hooray? I think the scoring system is super fair because there are some rounds where they take off certain percentages so it can even out the playing field but not coddle you too much so people don’t feel hopeless in last place. Would revisit. 7.4/10Fixytext: Absolutely hilarious the no backspace is so funny and the fact that you can move around your cursor and add to/interfere with other people’s sentences. The scenarios were so funny I think it had my favorite art style too. Only think is that I wished they changed which people were writing in each round (the groups) 9.8/10 (might become an all time fav). The complaint is that it ends up being a jumbled mess but if that's not what you were expecting going into it then idk what to say. THATS THE POINT! its supposed to be messy and you can see in real time how it all goes wrong. If you can't find the fun in chaos then stay playing quiplash and fibbage for the rest of your life. We'll have the actual fun. Hupnotorius: challenging in a good way, makes your brain think but not like too hard there’s only 3 categories which keeps it relatively simple. The hints are a good addition and the fact that  the outlier doesn’t know who they are is yet another layer. very creative concept probably one of the most well thought out social deduction games yet. I wish we could see each other’s answers from previous rounds and I wish the timers were longer esp for discussing the outlier ( that can be done in settings though) 9.2/10This is yet another social deduction game that goes over people's heads. You can't understand push the button, you can't understand weapons drawn you can't understand hypnotorious. "Oh you have to find a balance as to how much info you give away its too confusing" LIKE THAT's THE PURPOSE OF THE GAME??? I think we've seriously lost the ability to think and the only social deduction games people can play now are mafia because it relies almost completely on chance and people don't have to use their brains. do do re mi I just find too subjective to even rank. I like rhythm games, I like this. If you don't like rhythm games, you won't like it. Simple as that. Overall: 9/10 (should've been $25)

Even with everyone playing honestly with vague but relevant hints, there just isn't nearly enough there to ever revisit.The final round to Tee K.O. 2 is clearly meant for streamers in mind, as it just draws out unnecessarily for groups of friends, and is a very strange change to the original with no added value.FixyType has some potential but seems worse than other word games from earlier packs.Timejinx is one of the weaker trivia entries, and seems like a downgraded version of Quixort from the previous pack.Dodo Re Mi is an OK rhythm game, but it seems to miss inputs frustratingly. _childDocuments_.review: It's great, but not the best, especially considering the price increaseI'm surprised there wasn't a new YDKJ for number 10 but tee ko is amazing, I will now go over each game individually. Tee Ko 2: It's just better tee ko in most ways, better art tools, better voting system, plus references to many other jackbox games which is fun. However, there are some downsides to it, mainly (in my opinion) worse art, and the removal of a really good narrator. Also its very minor but they totally forgot to add the karasutengu as a spirit.Timejinx: Fun trivia, but not too special. It feels weird that the jinxes do nothing considering it's in the name, but it's good.Fixytext: It's pure chaos but pecking hilarious. It was the group favorite when I played but it will very much depend on your group. When I played with another group I hated it because it was bland with their humor style.Hypnotorious: Cool in concept but abhorrent tutorial and way too many game breaking bugs. One person got permanently signed out, we paused it to talk for 3 minutes and it froze. Probably fun if you play a few rounds and nothing breaks, but not really worth the effort until they fix it and improve explanations.Dodo Re Mi: I love it, but most don't. Very fun both single player and multiplayer, mostly to see how bad you fail.Overall: Good pack but with a lot of glitches. If this was any other pack it would probably be fine but this is disappointing that it is more expensive than previous packs, and also the big double digit milestone. I wouldn't recommend getting it as your first pack but it's a good addition to your collection otherwise. I feel like most games were experimental in this pack which is fine and good but it feels like a pack that some will hate because of that. It has a similar issue to 4, where most people I've played with only like 1 of the games plus Fibbage. For me this game is better than 4. Not amazing for a party pack but still a good game that I definitely recommend, there's just a lot more bad to say as the good is just "it's very very fun".       TLDR: 2.355/Pi

_childDocuments_.review: My friends and I have been playing Jackbox together almost every Saturday since spring 2020. Collectively we own all of the packs. Every pack has at least one or two games that aren't that great, but the majority of the games are either amusing or become fan favorites. The golden games are what make the packs worth keeping and playing. I am absolutely grateful for the hours of entertainment provided by the previous packs as it got my friends and I through some really difficult times and they continue to bring us together regularly to laugh until we cry.That being said, I am really sad that this pack only has one game that we enjoyed. Not sure what went wrong here. ~The new TKO didn't have enough updates to make it more fun than the old one. The things I am sure others besides myself wished for (other than an eraser) were not included to make it a better quality game. ~Time-Jinx was just.... what? I don't think the fun part about trivia is remembering dates or doing math. But maybe that is just me. I love trivia, but this just sucked the fun out of trying to remember things.~Hypnotorious was just too darn easy to figure out who is the outlier. While our answers were fun and we had some good chuckles, it was just too obvious too quickly who the was the odd one out. Like an easier and less fun version of Push the Button.~Dodo Re Mi... gosh this could've been good. Maybe it was just me... but was there a way to make the tutorial not absolutely freaking bonkers difficult? What a terrible way to teach anyone a game... by making them feel discouraged and frustrated. We then tried Row Your Boat and it was also pretty difficult. I suppose it is better played on a phone or tablet, not a PC screen with a keyboard but sheesh.... not fun enough to return to, that's for sure.~Fixy Text was the one we all agreed was fun. It was chaotic and goofy and we had a good time playing. I am sure we would play the heck out of this game had there been more games worth returning to.So that wraps it up. One game wasn't enough to convince me to keep the pack, so I refunded it. Despite my disappointment I will remain hopeful for when 11 rolls around.Edit: Despite refunding it, my friend re-purchased it for me, just so we can play fixy text. So Jackbox got their money instead of mine.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the Jackbox Party Packs, I've had the pleasure of enjoying every installment, except for the latest release, Pack 9. Coming into Pack 10, I was somewhat hesitant, having felt a sense of repetition with Pack 9. However, I'm thrilled to say that Pack 10 exceeded my expectations.This latest edition doesn't just rehash the same old games with different aesthetics. Instead, it brings forth innovative new games that inject a fresh dose of excitement into the franchise. The developers have taken the essence of what made the previous packs enjoyable and spun it into a collection that feels genuinely new and exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly kind of shocked this entry is as controversial as it currently is? I will agree with the upped $35 price tag being a bit absurd, they shouldn't have raised the price when considering very little here is of such quality to warrant it. Buy this on a sale or check other stores like Green Man Gaming. But at the same time, I think Party Pack 10 has more than enough good games here to make this a better entry than most of the newer packs have been, I sincerely disagree that this is the worst pack when 6 and 9 had more duds than this does.Tee KO 2 admittedly makes up a  of the value for my group when the first is easily one of the best games Jackbox has ever had, and this is just more of it with more options. FixyText will definitely be dependent on your group of friends, but the sheer chaos of it reminds me quite a bit of Talking Points from Pack 7; if your group is good at making up random garbage that actually makes all of you laugh, it will be a good time. Timejinx is a much more interesting take on trivia than the other trivia games in this series has been, enough that it's a very fun time but I do wish questions didn't repeat so often; there needs to be more questions than what the game has at least around launch right now. Dodo Re Mi I feel like is the reason why the price was raised higher than usual because the sheer number of songs and options here is genuinely insane, but the value of this game is going to really depend on how much you and the people you play with like rhythm games. It's definitely a little buggy and it's not like a hyper polished actual full game like other real rhythm games, but it's been the game my group has spent the most time on playing so far.The only real stinker here in the entire pack is Hypnotorious, to such a degree that I question if anybody actually playtested this thing. It's a deduction game which Jackbox isn't new to, but this one is so incredibly badly explained and moves at such an insanely slow pace. I've played this game with two different groups, and both of them audibly groaned and stopped playing early right after we realized we only played one round and not a full match. Having dud games isn't new for Jackbox, it's basically expected for every entry at this point, and at the very least I'm happy enough with every other game in the pack that this makes 10 one of the better newer entries.I wouldn't recommend this to someone who hasn't bought the other Jackbox games before, get the starter pack if that's the case. For everyone else, know your group of friends and decide for yourself if the types of games here sound like a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited 11/14. Original review at bottom. Pack 10 is a good showing, and I feel is leagues better than Pack 9. However! I don't think that justifies the price hike, especially when the pack was practically unplayable at launch due to a myriad of technical issues. These have since been (mostly) fixed, and now that my regular group has actually played the games I can give an earnest review.I like pretty much every game in the pack! The weakest IMO is Timejinx, and that's mainly because I don't care for trivia and neither does the group I play with, but all the same it's got neat gimmicks and we had fun for the couple of rounds we tried. Hypnotorious surprised all of us with how much we liked it. The other reviews have not been kind to it, but we found the concept neat and inventive and we had a lot of fun talking out our clues and category guesses. It's definitely something we'll play again. I feel like having a game be two rounds was kind of overkill, however; a single round is a nice little contained experience and we were all quite surprised when the game just kind of... kept going after the first one.Tee K.O. 2 is a solid sequel! I like the added shirt options and colors, but at the end of the day it's still pretty much the same game. Which in itself is a bit disappointing; I feel as if they could have done more. My biggest complaint is that the cute yokai are (mostly) gone, replaced by other jackbox mascots. DoDoReMi clearly got most of the attention and dev time. It's a multiplayer rhythm game-- one of the hardest things to make! And they pulled it off! My group had a blast with all the different instruments on offer. It's definitely something we're going to be coming back to. I'd recommend playing it on mobile instead of your desktop, though one of my friends used Joy2Key and a USB guitar hero controller to play and it rocked for them.I've seen FixyText get a lot of hate but it clicked really well with my group to the point where we'd rank it up there with Job Job. It's semi-cooperative, semi-competitive, and the text message narrative framing gives it all a lunatic bent that leaves us in stitches every round. For us, at least, it's the standout of the pack. ___Original review 10/21:Fixytext is really fun, Tee K.O. 2 is somewhat of an improvement, but we weren't even able to play Hypnotorious because it kept breaking on the very first round, with nobody getting a prompt. Overall this is the most unstable launch for a Jackbox game I've seen. There were numerous graphical oddities, lines not rendering etc. with TKO2 and Fixytext still drops a few players' input every round. I'm going to try the pack again in a week or two to see if any of the issues are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10There are enough good games in this pack to warrant a purchase, although I would argue that the price is a little high for the level of innovation this game-pack presents, compared to earlier entries in the series. This pack is only as good as the sum of its parts, and thus I shall review each game separately:T.K.O. 2: More T.K.O., this time with other clothes than t-shirts, as well as the option to take earlier drawing and changing them. It is an improvement but a very small one. A patch, if you will. 6/10Timejinx: A quiz-game about what year cetain events occured. You are often given a range in which a certain event has occured and tasked with guessing as close as possible to the correct year. The closer you get the less points you get (and like golf, fewest points at the end wins). There is rubber-banding, which is uncompetetive, but this is The Jackbox Party Pack, who cares? I like this game, it is nothing groundbreaking but it is educating and entertaining nonetheless. 8/10Fixytext: One of the best drunk games I have ever played. You are tasked with replying to text-messages. But everyone gets to write anywhere in the text and there is no delete or backspace. This causes chaos. Nonsense and chaos, but a great time with tons of laughs. 8/10Dodo re mi: A rhythm game. Imagine Tap Tap Revenge for iOS. Then instead of pop-songs and electronica you have mainly music from other entries in The Jackbox Party Pack-series. Sure, you can play weird instruments but why is this a game in a The Jackbox Party Pack? It does not fit. 5/10Hypnotorious: a mafia-style game in which you are given a role and is tasked to group it with other people . Bu answering questions and discussing you group each other into categories and get points if you have grouped yourself correctly. It is slightly confusing, as it is not clear if you should collaborate or compete. Why should you fool each other and be secretive if the game rewards you for group-mentality? It is okay, but lacks structure and goal. 4/10All in all, this is not as bad as people make it out to be. I have had fun here and ill probably have some more fun. However, wait until the price goes down, this is not worth full price. With ten entries, there is just not enough new things to warrant a purchase if you have played the nine games that came before this.PS. Achievements are not too hard to get, for the 0.01% of those of you who care.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally buy Jackbox games on release, but I would probably have waited for a sale if I had a good sense of what all of these games were going to be. Tee K.O. 2 is Tee K.O. - It's fun, it's silly, but it doesn't do what things like Quiplash sequels have done to revitalize the game in a new way. Fixy Text is Nothingburger - I really don't get the point of this game. There's no goal, there's no fun gimmick, it feels a little like Job Job without the entertaining addition of making your opponents remix the words to make sense. Don't love this one at all. Timejinx is Best - Super fun trivia game, I really enjoyed the new hooks and switch-ups they do to the questions to keep things fresh. I think Jackbox really excels at trivia games in general, but this one might be one of the best. Hypnotorious is Convoluted - It's still an impostor game like Faking It, but with a lot of confusing steps. They don't make it super clear there's an impostor who needs to fake it from the beginning, so we ended up wasting a game while we quickly figured out there was an odd one out. At the very least it's easier to play from a distance than Faking It was. Dodo Re Mi is Not For Me - It's a rhythm game you play with friends. I am not a fan of rhythm games to begin with and this one doesn't really do anything else. Even an addition like sabotaging your friends or facing off for bonuses would make this more interesting. All this being said, the previous game was better overall and cheaper. Still worth a play, still a good time, but wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Jackbox games fan but, as sad as I am to write it, this is not a great party pack.Jackbox previously made a really great game called T.K.O. and they have remade the "sequel" in this party pack. It changes some mechanics slightly but I'd hardly call them improvements. You're able to draw 3 shirts at once instead of waiting for the timer breaks, for example, but then you're left waiting for a much longer time while everyone else finishes. The host is weirdly aggressive and monologues in a way that doesn't hit my funny bone personally, and it messes with the game's pacing. If you're excited to play T.K.O. I'd highly recommend playing the original in Party Pack 3, it is better in nearly every way.Timejinx is fine but I don't feel it's very exciting for general audiences. The core play loop is being presented with a piece of information, and guessing what year it happened. It's pretty slow-paced compared to most other Jackbox games. If you're playing with a group of history buffs, I could see it being more interesting, but it's still a hard sell.Hypnotorious is an interesting concept but I feel they failed on execution. You are assigned a category, basically, and you have to guess who else was assigned a similar category. The core play loop is answering prompts about your category, and guessing who is in which category together. You have a few rounds to figure it out as a group. I've found it difficult for people to understand, and many people are left confused even at the end of the game. I don't find it fun personally, even among people who understand the game.Dodo Re Mi is like guitar hero for Jackbox. The core loop is actually pretty okay -- If you've played any rhythm game, you understand the concept -- But I just don't like it for this medium. Most Jackbox games are played on phones, so you're left tapping without any tactile feedback in those cases. For others playing on keyboards (or similar) it's enjoyable. I don't have a superb time playing it though, personally, and would rather play most other games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 10

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't the best party pack yet. I would probably put it in the upper half of them though. In the end, like the rest of the party packs, there are hits and misses. If you want more Jackbox games, this is a solid pickup I think. It feels overall fairly unique with some different takes on returning ideas. If you're just starting to get into Jackbox, I would personally look more towards other packs. Ones like Party Pack 7, 8, or 5 may be better served there. Personally, here are my thoughts on each game:Tee K.O. 2: This is just Tee K.O. with upgrades. More shirt options, a different bracket style, and trading off the yokai characters for Jackbox Series characters. I think the drawing and shirt QoL changes were a plus. The bracket is a little less interesting. There's only one winner for each bracket, and the final battle being press-based is only really cool for streaming. For the players I've done it with, it's been more annoying than fun. I personally preferred the unique theme from the first one rather than 'a bunch of Jackbox characters.' But as the flagship game, I understand it.Fixytext: This is probably my personal favorite. But I also admit it has serious flaws. There's a lot of fun in messing with the text in real time with others. But glitches just not letting people type have been fairly common. And you have to just ignore the scoring for this one. Given the groups are always the same, it leads to situations where one player running away with their group means they just win even if the other group is full of stronger players. In the end though, I find it a ton of fun.Timejinx: This is the most straightforward trivia game I think Jackbox has ever made. I don't think it's for me, but a lot of players I've played with enjoy it. It's a little like Quixort turned into a non-team game.DoDo Re Mi: I personally like this one, but I've also found it incredibly polarizing. A lot of people are thrown off by the tutorial, which switches difficulties between easy, normal, and hard and gives a bad impression. The button controls also takes time to get used to. But I've found people warm up to it after playing a bit. Some still hate it though. So it's going to be very different from person to person.Hypnotorious: This reminds me a lot of Weapons Drawn. A really interesting idea that feels like it has a rough execution, and it feels like it goes on too long. I've had a lot of people be surprised that there was a second round at all given how long the first one lasts. The deduction element is interesting, but I've found it hard to really get a grip of the categories personally. I think this an interesting one and may get better with the right group as you play it more. But at the moment I'd say it's the weakest of the pack despite having some good concepts.

_childDocuments_.review: i was intitially very worried about this pack’s quality which wasn’t helped by the reviews, but after playing it for myself, this is far from the worst jackbox pack. now lets slow down a bit. is it the best? no. is it in the top half? probably not. is it worth 35? definitely not, and i think that’s the main sticking point for many. the price increase is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but outside of that, this is a mostly solid selection of games. i also wanna really quickly go over the bugs in this game. i didnt run into any while playing and it sucks if you do, but from what ive heard, all the bugs people are bringing up are bugs ive encountered in other packs. they arent exclusive to jack 10. not sure why theyre being brought up now. Tee K.O. 2 does a few things better and a few things worse than its predecessor. on the better side, the nee drawing tools are welcome additions. i like that you can make things other than t-shirts this time, and i think, at least for the first two rounds, the tournament style is better. as for the negatives, the final round is much worse. i dont know why it isnt just… a vote. i guess that wouldnt be climactic enough? either way, i know for a fact someone in the group i was playing in was using an autoclicker, and if your final round can be cracked open like that, its time to return to the drawing board. this is a nitpick im aware, but i also dont like how they got rid of the animals from the first game. it gives this one less personality. ill rate the games outta 7 ig.4/7Timejinxthis is trivia where you pick a year and then do trivia involving years and it works on golf rules so whoever has the lowest score wins. this was just really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring and it felt like it went on for an eternity despite not being that long.2/7FixyTextthis is a rough one. its like id they took word spud, mixed it with civic doodle, and called it a day. theres no cohesion to this one. it doesnt even have a final round. all that ends up happening in the end is you get left with a sentence that makes no sense. speaking of making no sense, the voting makes no sense either. you just vote on words. worst game of the pack, easily.1/7DoDo Remii was worried about this game in this pack, and yeah i didnt love it at first, but ive come around on it a bit. theres a lot of content in this one which definitely adds value to the pack. my main concern, being the latency, also wasnt an issue given that they actually programmed around that, so its pretty responsive! its a really great game! 7/7Hypnotoriusi didnt fully understand this one at first, but now that i do it was a fun enough time. id say its the second best game in the pack in fact. its got a lot of structural problems though, so know that when i say second best, i mean it was the one i had the second most fun with. in hypnotorius, everyone is assigned a role and has to find other people assigned a role thats in the same group as them. you do this by studying people’s answers to the various prompts. one person is the outlier, and you have to figure out who that is so you can single them out. depending on who got in the right groups, and depending on if you caught the outlier, you get points. person with the most points wins. its a little difficult to understand, but once you do its fun enough. my issue comes down to the scoring. it doesnt make any sense. the outliers seemed to get massive points, even if they were caught because they were in the right group. which i should add, the game said they got 0 points for. the game also felt like it was dragging a bit by the second round. its not a fast game at all. it was still fun and i liked the discussion in it specifically, but i totally get why some dont like this one very much.5/7pack 10 took a lot of risks. it is a very experimental pack, and one that i totally get why people dislike. however, i think there is still value in this pack. dodo remi is great, and hypnotorious and tee k.o. 2 were still fun, even if they arent as good as they could be, and i do respect this pack for being taking risks more than i would if it didnt. im happy it exists for that reason, but this is not the pack they shouldve increased the price for. its overpriced for the time it released which is something i cant really say about any other party pack. i cant recommend this as a first pack. youre much better off getting packs like 3, 6, 7, or 9 first. however, if you do own at least a couple of the prior packs, give this one a shot. its better than 1, 2, or 5 for what thats worth.18/35

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR6/10. Barely a pass for me, get it on sale, I don't think it's worth the price increase.Dodo Re Mi. The best of the pack and it's not close. Instant hit with my family, some of the most fun we've had with Jackbox overall. The range of difficulties for instruments made it super accessible for my easily overwhelmed mother that typically struggles with the more involved games. Failing is still very funny, as it should be. Only issue is it can get laggy sometimes. 9/10TeeKO 2. Silver medal here, I like the bracket format over the old gauntlet. I also like the eraser addition instead of just undo. My biggest issue I have is when playing with a mouse, going outside the drawing box then back into it when you're trying to fill in colour, your line doesn't stop when you pan back over the drawing even if you've let go of the mouse button. Also small issue with typing slogans, occasionally in the middle of typing the entire thing erases and you have to do it again. I like the hoodies and tank tops. 7.5/10TimeJinx. Finishing the podium here, but kind of underwhelming. It's VERY simple, it's literally just guessing years for most of the game, assuming you don't actually know when things happened in history. It's kinda cool when you do get a guess exactly correct, so that's a small plus. I wish the JINX part actually did something instead of just being an "oh, cool, we said the same thing" moment. It isn't BAD, but it's a little too basic for me. 6/10Hypnotorious. This game is (or at least WAS, before patches) a total mess. In the first few games it's completely confusing on what you're even doing. Not knowing if you're the Outlier or not seems stupid to me, not only cuz it just adds more confusion, but also if you're near the end of the round and you THINK you're the outlier, do you just... Have to not contribute anymore if you don't want to be found out? Like just copy things someone else says or something? It's dumb, I don't like it. Also the points aren't explained and it just seems like a random person is the winner every game. 4/10FixyText. This game just sucks, but worse than that, it's boring. I don't even know how to describe how not fun this is. You all just... Type nonsense in a text box, and the other team votes on the "haha funny words" and that's how you get points. I don't know what they were going for with this, because no one even pays attention to what we're supposed to be replying to, it's just write whatever nonsense or offensive or stupid things you can think of to get votes. Word Spud is genuinely better in my eyes. 2/10.Price increase isn't justified with these games feeling a little unfinished, or just glitchy and buggy. Get it if you're REALLY interested in one or more of the games, but otherwise I'd wait for a decent sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely loving this pack, Bought it first day and we loved every game.TKO 2A wonderful sequel to the first game, fixing all the issues with the original along with adding a bunch of extra customization options. Definitely worth just for this.FixytextIt felt like an alternative to Job Job, with the same type of humor involved. I absolutely loved this one, but it was really annoying to have your stuff deleted because two people were writing in the same place at the same time, you could never tell when it happened.HypnotoriousThis one was fun, but I never understood what the developers wanted you to do. It felt like we were working as a team, but the outlier made it seem like a social deception game, but you never knew if you were the outlier or not, and chances are if you knew, everyone else did too. Felt like a fun game but without a good direction.TimejinxThis was a fun one-off trivia game that we had a blast with when we wanted something to do while waiting for the lobby to fill up. _childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed it overall but this is probably one of the more middling Party Packs. Not bad but not one of the first I'd recommend checking out especially considering how good the previous 4 packs are. If you're a longtime fan I can still recommend this but otherwise wait for a sale down the line.Tee K.O. 2 is a better Tee K.O. with all the nice drawing tool improvements from Champ'd Up. Having a tournament bracket setup for it is good. The final round tap fest is kind of dumb though. Not a massive improvement over the first though so I can't call this a "MUST PLAY" or anything. The OG Tee K.O. and Champ'd Up are still good alternatives to this. Still a pretty good time though. Timejinx is a very solid trivia game with an awesome scoring system and a solid trivia format. Kind of reminds me of Guesspionage in some ways with how you're guessing years. Not better than Trivia Murder Party though if you want a more pure trivia game. Probably the strongest game in the pack overall but again not quite a "MUST PLAY" like Trivia Murder Party or Fibbage but if you love trivia games, you can't go wrong with this.Fixytext can be surprisingly funny with the right people but your group NEEDS to embrace the text chaos. Can be a bit too aimless but had a surprisingly good time with it. Not amazing but pretty good. Great presentation.Dodo Re Mi is a decent little rhythm game but I'm not really much of a rhythm game guy so I don't have much to say about it. My group had a solid time with it though. Hypnotorious was the game that I was the most interested in going into the pack and I'm sad to say that it just isn't very good. The game has a horrendous tutorial which doesn't establish the key outlier mechanic until you're halfway through your first round and it's just a very confusing game for most people that I've played with. The game needs to give players more direction for how much we should give away about our roles because even after 3 full games we still didn't really have a good sense of how to play this thing. That combined with some pretty bad pacing for a Jackbox game, this whole thing ended up as just kind of a mess to play. Might be good with the right group or maybe some house rules though.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 10 is honestly pretty good, way better than 9, though it is not a powerhouse pack like 7 4 8 though.Tee KO 2 is just a flat out improvement to the previous game which is good because Fibbage 4 being worse scared me. But yeah no some of the biggest changes if if you finish a drawing early, you can start the next one there and then. There is also a slight layer function and more colours and the way the voting works as in who fights who is tornament style which is way better than the streak thing which needs a bit of luck more than just being a funny shirt. I will say the slogan issue is still there and they did remove different sizes (but again there are 2 layers to play with now so kinda works out) but yeah this is just a better Tee KOThe Second Round gimmick of being able to edit a persons bad shirt is also a great addition tbh Time Jinx is pretty mid and easily the worst of the pack. Honestly the way the questions are asked and the types of rounds are actually really neat and creative, what sucks is that every question is just a history based triva question which yeah. Imo jackbox trivia games only really work when the trivia is generalized or if it is so out there that it isn't. Where as this one has some general knowledge but it is mostly "what year did thing happen" or "which thing is the odd one out of this decade"Again the way the game handles the prompts is the best out of all the trivia games but content wise very limiting in a negative way Fixy Text is actually decently funny. Way better than what I thought it  would be. Half the people type stuff together (without an undo button) and the other people vote on what words within the text are the funniest. It plays better than what the preview made it seem to be. I think all the other good comedy games you can think of in Jackbox are probably better such as Talking Points, Job Job, Quiplash etc. But this is still a good/funny one and it is actually unique and not like how Joke Boat and The Rapping one are practically the same game just with a different themeHypnotorious has a really fun gimmick, I sadly can't give a proper review as our group not only didn't understand the rules fully, but also one of the people left mid game. But from what I gathered, it is a mix of lying but also working together to figure out who the odd one out is. Also it is pretty fun but I will need to test it again because yeah, our session was kinda borkedNow Dodo Re Mi is a horrible jackbox game.However it is actually just an amazing stand alone game.The rhythm part actually works surprisingly well, even with someone across the other side of the planet. And each instrument has 2 different sound options and each song has a bunch of different parts. What is real nice and kinda in the Jackbox spirit is there are different instruments for different levels of skill so even people bad a rhythm games can join along. And there is a bunch of songsWhy it sucks as a Jackbox game though is firstly this is a game that really only works well on PC, so that whole phone thing doesn't work at all. Also the game is, similar to a rhythm game a just play until you get board. Which if you get people that want to actually play rhythm games, then great. But Jackbox are kinda meant to be generic so something like this just doesn't work. I couldn't imagine going to any party and whipping this out. But I had one of the rhythm friends with me and yeah I am def gonna play this game with all the rhythm gamers as it is a thing that all of them can join and is a collaborative effort. Like unironically I wish this were a stand alone game, it would be way better like that and I would buy itOverall pretty decent, put it above pack 6 but below 8. If you can afford it I would buy it but maybe wait a bit as it is still a little buggy and might go on sale later
