_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to say that this year's pack is kind of a bummer. The obvious thing that will drive returning Jackbox fans away is the massive jump in price, last pack was $29.99, but I really didn't care since I had a 20% off coupon. I excitedly bought the game... and man what a disappointment this was. Being the pack to jump two digits, I was not expecting how buggy the games got. For instance, in Dodo Ri Mi, playback would sometimes not count notes which would end up ruining perfect combos and what not. Jackbox Games if you're reading this, and I don't think you will, take this Pack's negative reviews as a lesson for the futureEh it's okay... I wasn't a fan of the original, nor do I even care for the sequel. I do like how the drawing tools were greatly improved.Another okay game. It is the most laid back... and we're talking about TIME TRAVEL.  Of course I wasn't expecting Trivia Murder Party wackiness but wow is the hostess really chill. I like the questions being all about time and stuff.Word Spud but better??? Not by a long shot, but still better. This game best simplifies as a Google Doc game. You and your friends type. That's it... I did not see any reason to go back since the game is a bit... too chaotic for my liking.When Jackbox Games revealed this game, I thought it was going to be Zeeple Dome 2 but I was wrong. The game syncs everyone's game up with a simple countdown and then you're off. I wasn't much of a fan of rhythm games but I think I'll consider playing more after playing Dodo Ri Mi. The renditions of the classical music + jackbox classics really spice up the gameplay. The only negative gripe I have is that the website app will sometimes lag and even freeze if you're device sucks. Other than that, pretty solid rhythm game.It's not good. I like roleplaying games and the idea of being someone or something you aren't while answering questions is pretty fun. The horrible thing about this is that everything is confusing. You aren't told how scoring works, the outlier game mechanic happens at the end of the first round and some people/things are very obscure.

_childDocuments_.review: I got into Jackbox starting with the 7th entry and tried each ensuing one after that. 10 definitely feels like the weakest game I've tried by far. Tee KO 2 is a proven product and FixyText was fairly funny when you have several people - albeit still a bit weaker than some of the simpler comedy text games like Quiplash/Job Job. From there though, the other games are fairly average if not downright bad.Timejinx is fine, though it's hard to say if Jackbox has ever really nailed the trivia genre. Maybe I missed something in the earlier entries, but the party style they tend to go with seems overly complicated for what could be a pretty enjoyable trivia game. The categories for questions often feel a bit too niche, not just in this game, but in every trivia-oriented game I tried from JB. It's an oddly way-too-specific answer every time despite the categories still often being grounded in pop culture. I guess my issue is that the games don't really feel like they give you a chance most of the time to be rewarded for decent general knowledge like you'd want trivia games to do. That's maybe a bit biased though.Dodo Re Mi, for as much as people seem to talk it up in reviews, fell very flat for me. Latency issues seem to screw over a lot of players, and the songs they initially give you aren't remotely interesting. This again could be chalked partially up to preference as I'm not a big music game guy, but something about rhythm games having to be played wirelessly via phones for most people doesn't feel like a good combination.Hypnotorious is a full-on flop. Terrible game with an unclear end goal. It is never obvious what the game wants you to really do, and how it determines a winner is poorly communicated. It's extremely confusing to play and leaves players struggling to figure out just how secretive or cooperative they need to be - players have to fight themselves to really find any enjoyment. Not really worth the time.The game just isn't worth the increased price tag. It's fine for Jackbox fans that will buy every game to add to their library, but it definitely feels weaker than most entries in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of mixed feeling reviews around this game but after putting a lot of hours across all the other games this one still lived up to the classic excitement they bring as well, if not surpassing it.Breaking it down game by game:FixyText is pure chaos and such a dumb funny game, even if it's just repeating random copypastas we still enjoyed this game.Hypnotorious caused so many arguments as to who belongs together. This game will end friendships lol. Timejinx is one of the best trivia games Jackbox have put out, ranking for me just under Trivia Murder Party. Adding in the percentage bonus for getting multiple questions right really keeps the game competitive.Dodo Re Mi while being considered a Rockstar/Guitar Hero clone is still an absolute blast, the tutorial is rather hard but after that it gets easier with other very funny "instruments" available. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Four of the five games in The Jackbox Party Pack 10 are really good, but the instability at launch was not welcoming, especially with the increase in price. If you like rhythm games though, consider picking this up for Dodo Re Mi alone. And heck, Tee K.O. 2 should be more than enough to buy this game.The Jackbox Party Pack 10 has by far the most interesting game lineup throughout all the Party Packs so far. Going through each of them to give my thought.This might be a shocker for some, but  might be my favorite game to play out of all the five games. I usually don't play or like mastering rhythm games, but I find Dodo Re Mi to be one of, if not one of my top classic games for a variety of reasons. Song selection is fair, yet I really enjoy the feeling of playing each instrument per song and then watch our insane performance. I always want to make sure we beat the plant together, and every time we fail, I would always have a chuckle or two from playing. The sync at the start was a very clever idea to have, especially when playing over a stream that has really bad latency. That being said, a lot of performance issues have been noted by players. I used a Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 3, but not every person owns a smartphone capable of being able to hit every note perfectly. I'll note this later when I get down to performance, but practically speaking this game works good for the most part. One time we managed to make a really bad performance of The Wedding March, and we somehow survive the entire song. I think with that in mind, Dodo Re Mi is one of the best games Jackbox has developed, but if flaws were addressed, I think it would help address other people's concerns with the game. Regardless of these issues, this game is awesome, and I am patently watching for the modding scene to take ahold of this game.I was not sure with  when I saw gameplay of it. One of my biggest concerns were the new bracket layout replacing the "new challenger" approach and the final round being Bracketeering, but after giving it some playback, I really think this game does manage to overmatch the original Tee K.O., but just slightly. While Tee K.O. 2 has very improved tools to draw and such, I really find it annoying that the pen has no width setting. Similarly the eraser also is stuck to one width. I really like the new and improved tools but I think this game needs to allow me to adjust the width sometimes. Other than that, the gimmick to redraw someone else's drawing is so cool as well, but I also think this game should at least credit the original artist. The final round, while it involves tapping or clicking a lot on your vote is actually done way better than how it was in Bracketeering, because this is the final round and you cheering on your vote is really exciting! With these great changes done with Tee K.O. 2, i think this game is better than the original, and even though the Yokais aren't around anymore, I feel comfortable knowing the only character worth playing with is Alien from Push the Button. is a very nice addition to the trivia game genre. Unique for a game this type, you want to make sure you get the least amount of score as possible, or risk acculuminating points based on how far you were off from a year. If you got too much points though, the "side-missions" help reduce it as much as possible. As a big history nerd, I really like this game. A lot of the questions were tricky to solve, but if you know your basic history, it should be fun to play this game. I personally like how quirky the host is with giving stats that may or may not be the right answer during "TimeLoop" and the dumb changes in history during "TimeFix" is also a blast to behold. I initially really liked this game, though it has since dropped a bit to third upon my further re-evaluation of Tee K.O. 2, given that there are better trivia games out there to play, especially Fibbage. This game is just guessing years and standard trivia, which can be great if you don't like cryptic questions, minigames, or chance, but I feel like they're more interesting than this game. It's not bad tho and hell I would play this game to death, just not the best one out there. has an intriguing and fun concept. You are assigned a secret role that must then be used to answer questions said by the host. Then you have to group you and the other players together in jars. One player is secretly the "outlier", or does not belong any particular group, but you or the "outlier" will not know who it is until the accusation stage is set up. I do enjoy Hypnotorious for all I know, as the game requires a lot of deduction of your fellow players to find out if you belong or if you're the "outlier", and it is especially a blast to see other player's responses. This game does drags on for a bit, and having no indication of the scoreboard or how scoring works in this game is a bit baffling. Plus, the categories can be confusing at best, hence why I modded categories in. Despite this, Hypnotorious has grown on me and I really enjoy this game at its finest. That being said.... Visuals, sound design, and music cannot save this game. All this game boils down to is typing the dumbest responses and then voting on what words were "interesting" or "funny". FixyText's formula does not hold up well to multiple playthroughs. I can enjoy tapping notes, answering trivia questions about time, craft the funniest shirt, and shout excessive on who is the "outlier", but when it comes to this game, it is just so boring and so easy to win. Co-author points have to be the most broken system in this entire game. By hijacking someone else's words, you can take some of the points that the other players would have earned. This is a strategy that has made me win this game over and over again, and yet I have no fun playing this. The text-to-speech reading it is funny, the words other players type out can be funny, and the credits are...interesting. But I do not think this game is all that good, and if we're considering if this game is better than Word Spud, it is, but not even that good of a game to overmatch Word Spud. And after the game literally bugged out on the first message, this game's bugs do not make me want to play this game anymore.Overall, The Jackbox Party Pack 10 has a lot going for it, and I like 4 of the 5 games included. That being said, the early issues at launch didn't really help that much, especially now with the new price of $35, the first Jackbox since Pack 5 to see a price increase. Is it worth it? I don't know. I received this product for free by Jackbox Games, so I have no right to talk my opinion on how this should affect me, but I do know many aren't appeased with this price change, and I can understand. Dodo Re Mi brings in a fresh new idea that Jackbox hasn't dipped in the waters before, and many aren't happy that the tutorial section is hard or they aren't a fan of rhythm games. Timejinx is an okay trivia game, Hypnotorious is tedious, and FixyText is bad. Meanwhile, Tee K.O. 2 has a lot to go through if it wants to eventually dethrone Tee K.O., and many point out that Tee K.O. 2 hasn't changed enough. But while I think some of these reasons are valid, The Jackbox Party Pack 10 is a solid experience. While I might mostly play all but FixyText from now on, I think this is my 4th favorite pack in the entire Jackbox Party Pack series.

_childDocuments_.review: Great collection of games, some better than others as usual.Tee K.O. 2: You know what it is, and it's still good. Probably the strongest contender in here, no pun intended. It's a lot faster than the original too!FixyText: I had a lot of fun reading mumbo jumbo from a bunch of goofballs in the same Discord. You get to help write a message together and it usually devolves into degeneracy and concern very quickly. Kudos for having robot voice read everything afterward, really makes the game.TimeJinx: I learned that I know nothing about history or time periods and for being bad at it alone should be grounds for calling it bad, according to gaming journalism. However, this is also fun and slightly educational! Probably my second to last pick in here though.Hypnotorious: While I want to say this one's interesting, with five people it feels a bit lacking. I could see it working a lot better with eight. You all get randomly assigned roles that belong to one of three categories with one of you being sus as an outlier and not fitting in. You get asked a series of questions to answer as what you are and attempt to group yourselves together based on said answers. There's trickery to be had, but again, with a small group, this one looses its luster easily. Probably the least likely one for me to play in here.DoDo Re Mi: Do you like Friday Night Funkin or Flash Flash Revolution or Dance Dance Revolution or any other rhythm game? This one's for you and it works great. Mostly lagless thanks to syncing up your device before each song and it only takes three seconds. Play various instruments and make horrible incoherent bird music that may or may not get you eaten by a carnivorous plant. As an added bonus, you and your friends can download whatever cool music you make afterwards. My friends and I spent most of our time on this one, surprisingly, when we had intended to play more Tee K.O. 2. It's just that much fun, and super simple to jump in, play, and be done with when you're on a limited amount of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just say this: I think this pack is alright, and It does have problems, but I don't think it's one of the "worst packs"Before anything else let me just get my opinions on each of the games first before anything:Tee K.O. 2: A nice improvement on the original, better features, but I do wish more was done with it. (I also dislike the final round's mashing gimmick)FixyText: While my least favorite game in the pack, It can still be some chaotic fun. The concept is great, and the mechanic of not being able to delete is funny, but could've been done a bit betterTimeJinx: I'm not a trivia guy, but this game is pretty good. The fact that it's based on when events happened and not what happened during those events makes it more unique, and the side missions are fun too. Good Game, just doesn't appeal to meHypnotorious: The most controversial game, to most it's confusing. But to me, it just takes a bit to learn. It's a lot like weapons drawn or bidiots in that regard. I absolutely love the concept and the game can be super fun with a group of people who have a basic understanding of the game, but I do understand the criticism to a degree.DoDo Re Mi: The most polished game, It's a great guitar hero inspired little rhythm game, I see my self playing this one by myself a lot. A very cool game, and one of the best of the packTo me, the games aren't the problem, It's one: the bugs, which are annoying, but will hopefully get fixed in a upcoming patch, and the price hike. I find this a little dumb, but I do understand that things get more pricey overtime, but I think this should've stayed at 30$. Overall, Is it amazing? no, Did it live up to expectations? no not really. Is it a terrible pack? No not at all. I see myself coming back to this one from time to time, and there are definitely worse packs, I do hope the bugs get fixed. I would really only recommend to someone who already has like 4 or 5 other packs. (unless your like me who bought it on release day for some reason)

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic as always. (I guess this is how I justify the financial cost of owning almost all the packs now).TKO has got some great additions and quality of life changes making TKO 2 the obvious choice to play over the original. Dodo Re Mi is another breath of fresh air for the series and is great fun (plus it works with more than 8 players so great with large groups).

_childDocuments_.review: While I do think the price hike is very disheartning, I cannot deny that this was a pretty good pack. Definitely some new favorites in my group.Tee K.O. 2It's pretty much exactly the same except with updated tools. The tap battle at the end is a cool new feature though! I can't say anything bad cause they already knew they had a perfect game, it just needed an update. Our play through was very buggy at times, not using the outline tool right or kicking us out a bunch, but it was launch day and that's to be expected. I'm sure it'll be patched very quickly.TimeJinxMy group pretty unanimously agreed this one was a skip. There's better trivia games and there's better guessing games. I will say there's nothing outstandingly wrong with the game. It has a good mix of formats and it never felt like anybody had a super strong lead (that lasted long anyway lol). Might be some people's cup of tea but not ours.FixyTextThis game was so much fun, we went back and played it twice! The absolute chaos of trying to write together but also write better, funnier, things is mindblowingly hilarious. Picking the categories really gives the game a fresh coat of paint between playthroughs. This game and Tee K.O. 2 make the entire pack very worth it in my opinion.Dodo Re MiI was pleasantly surprised by this game! We didn't think any of us would like it but we all ended up adoring it. It had the most votes for favorite game of the pack. There's so many songs and instruments and you can really customize the game to your experience. I love how the scoring works and the sync is very good (unlike some other games *cough* Zeeple Dome *cough*).HypnotoriousVery mid hidden roles game. The tutorial is confusing and the premise is not very clear. None of us really enjoyed this game and agreed we probably won't play it again. Made me kinda sad cause I was very excited about this one from the trailers!Overall, I feel like the pack either hits HARD or misses wildly. But I will always recommend anything giving Tee K.O. 2, it's nice that there's other great games to go along with it!

_childDocuments_.review: I love every party pack, but I have to say that all of them have at least one game that isn't quite as good as the rest. There's no game like that in this pack. Each game is interesting and fun, with its own interesting flair that makes it stand out from any other game! They're all really fun and replayable and even if you don't have any friends both Dodo Re Mi and Time Jinx can be played singleplayer so there's no excuse not to play this game!! The only downside is that the variety in these games may not be the best for people looking for their first pack to buy, as it doesn't have as many 'iconic' games as, say, Pack 3. Although at the time of this review the game is about 2 days old so that could change. This game is so worth it though, and you should definitely get it!!

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 10 was one of the most hyped up packs being a celebratory pack, but admittedly, I do have a few criticisms with it and I think it could have been a lot better considering the hype, but there is still value here regardless.Tee K.O. 2 does expand on the original greatly adding features I very much am glad to see though I do wish the original yokai returned as playable characters but making this one full of Jackbox characters is still fun.Timejinx expands on the trivia genre even further with a pretty neat concept of guessing the correct year something happened along with other different categories. It isn't my favorite over games like TMP or YDKJ but is still fun.Dodo Re Mi is one of my favorites being a new take on rhythm-based games using music Jackbox themselves has done. No song in the game is licensed either so the game is safe from things like copyright. It's not perfect by any means and it's not for people who don't care for rhythm games, but it's addictive and fun. Hypnotorious is a hidden identity game where everyone plays a certain role and has to group themselves with players that have a role similar to theirs while also trying to find the Outlier who has their own category and because the Outlier isn't actually told they are the Outlier in advance, it adds to the fun as it could even be you. That said, this isn't a game that has aged well for me because the scoring system is very skewed and the moderation for this could've been better.FixyText is my least favorite of this pack because I did enjoy being chaotic with it to start but it does eventually become a one-joke game with the limited categories and simple premise. Especially since it can descend into just typing gibberish or excessive profanity with no real point behind it. The moderation for this game also needed more work. I do like the aesthetic and music a lot though!Overall, I do have my issues with this pack. Maybe even more so considering that it was hyped up to be a celebratory pack and the games simply needed more work and polish. I still have fun with this pack and do recommend it. But I do think it could've been better crafted.

As for the games in the pack, TEE KO is a classic game, having that come pack with not only T-shirts but hoodies and muscle shirts, makes it all the better. * I do miss the other Announcer though.* The Texting game is a bit bugged at the moment, we cannot get passed the 3rd stage because the game just breaks. _childDocuments_.review: Genuinely the best entry to the party packs in the past few years- there isn't a single 'bad' game, they're all very entertaining with the small group of friends I tried it with (yet to play with a bigger group) and all games play to their strengths perfectly. Despite the slight price increase compared to other packs, I'd definitely recommend this one over some recent entries.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 10

_childDocuments_.review: Played some with the wife, 2 games which play 1+ players; Timejinx and Dodo Re Mi. Timejinx is a fun quiz game in the same vein as Guesspionage. Dodo Re Mi is the game we played the most, this is a rhythm game like DDR, Guitar Hero etc. It's very good, however, the super hard difficulties can be particularly difficult if your phone doesn't seem to be responding quick enough to the cues. I can't tell if this is an internet issue, an issue with my phone, or a software issue. My phone certainly wasn't responding to multiple taps at once which is required on this difficulty. Anyway, other than that, it is a lot of fun and I highly recommend giving it a go!

name: AQUA KITTY UDX
detailed_description: AQUA KITTY UDX blasts onto Steam in this enhanced Ultra Deluxe Edition including an epic Dreadnought mode! You and your team of milk mining kittens have overcome a fear of water to drill down under the ocean seabed and begin extracting vast reserves of what seems to be naturally forming full-fat milk. Get ready for fast-paced submarine action, defending the kittens from disruptive mechanical sea creatures. PLEASE NOTE - Buying this game also includes `AQUA KITTY - Milk Mine Defender` at no extra cost! In the game you can choose from 3 different main game modes: CLASSIC - The regular game mode, clear waves of robotic sea creatures whilst protecting milk mining kittens. There are 4 sea areas, each with a large boss enemy at the end. Work your way across the map via any route you prefer. ALSO try the special Infinite Espresso challenge level, where there are no milk pumps to defend and the enemy waves just keep on coming! ARCADE - This is a twist on the main game mode, with the addition of gems you collect and use to buy upgrades. These upgrades persist across levels. DREADNOUGHT - The newest game mode is set deep underwater where you must fly through huge multi-screen enemy dreadnought ships, weaken them by blasting parts off to expose the shielded weak point, and then destroy the core!!! (all whilst trying to free imprisoned cats!) Some of the enhancements compared to the original Milk Mine Defender game: Extra Bosses (one per sea area). New Dreadnought mode with 13 increasingly humongous dreadnoughts to battle and destroy. Improved visuals such as new parallax scrolling skies and other enhanced graphical effects. Rebalanced gameplay. Please note - The game is best played with an Xbox or PS4 controller, as controllers with analogue sticks give the most precise movement control. Keyboard control is also supported. Mouse control is not supported.

DREADNOUGHT - The newest game mode is set deep underwater where you must fly through huge multi-screen enemy dreadnought ships, weaken them by blasting parts off to expose the shielded weak point, and then destroy the core!!! (all whilst trying to free imprisoned cats!) Some of the enhancements compared to the original Milk Mine Defender game: Extra Bosses (one per sea area). New Dreadnought mode with 13 increasingly humongous dreadnoughts to battle and destroy. Improved visuals such as new parallax scrolling skies and other enhanced graphical effects. Rebalanced gameplay. Please note - The game is best played with an Xbox or PS4 controller, as controllers with analogue sticks give the most precise movement control. Keyboard control is also supported. Mouse control is not supported.
short_description: AQUA KITTY UDX blasts onto PC in this enhanced Ultra Deluxe Edition including the epic Dreadnought game mode!

_childDocuments_.review: me and my friend played the original a long time ago. the characters, sprite work, and music are all great. it's a bullet hell shoot'em up. you're locked from looking left to right so its tough to get around enemies below or above you. there's a ton of upgrades and levels that make the game more interesting though and if you're interested then try it out!!!
_childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, what's going on? Apparently everyone who owns the original gets the UDX for free. That's great.And secondly, the UDX turned out great after all -  there is fullscreen support and the game is not so easy to beat. And there is a nice soundtrack too, where the filter reminds me of the SID filter - although it is certainly a different kind. All together it's a nice upgrade!
_childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: Original was very much worth the small price. This version adds the Dreadnoughts which is a mode i actually enjoy more than the original. No need to constantly save cats being taken. The mayhem on Dreadnoughts is off the charts as you try to make enough room in the narrow areas inside or near the target ship while enemies constantly try to get you. There is some death star trench run level of desperation sometimes when you are sooo close yet so far from the killing blow. Have not even tried Arcade mode yet but with these 2/3 already it is well worth even full price.  Yes my game hours is not that high yet but i am basically reviewing a game that i know well from before with some extra spice. Just be prepared to restart again and again. Perfect game basically when you got 15 minutes of extra time so why not try again to beat yet another level. Also if global/friend high score tables are your thing there is plenty of room at top for people who play 2-player.
_childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: Played the original a long time ago.  Looks like this is a fixed-up version of it, but I never had issues in the first place.  That said, the devs appear to have given it away to owners of the original so I'd say that if you're looking at this for the first time, pick up this version instead.If you don't know what Aqua Kitty is, it is very much an updated clone of arcade classic Defender.  Protect your civs on the ground by flying around a wrap-around map that has tons of things to shoot at.  You must manually choose which direction you face, of course, just like in Defender.  Unlike defender, there's a progression system at play.In short, fun arcade-style shootbang game that won't break your wallet.
_childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the original a looong time ago on release, it never worked. This version works perfectly. Super cute.Cap your FPS to 60 via rivatuner, nvidia control panel, nvidia inspector whatever. Devs are working on it though.If you don't hit your full res you need to go to the .exe and override high DPI settings for application.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment the game runs at super speed and also has the timer going at twice the speed unlike the original so i can safely assume that this is unintentional, i do however find it adds an extra layer of difficulty to the game so when this is all said and done and patched out eventually i hope they actually add the current buggy super speed as another difficulty as i'm just having way too much fun with it

As of today 5 anti-malware vendors on VirusTotal think the current version may be malicious.McAfee and Microsoft are not reporting the currently released version as malicious which, according to the forums, appears to have stopped the game from being blocked by default on many Windows installs that rely on Microsoft AV.Here's the VirusTotal report:Intezer reports that up to 8.51% of the main Aqua Kitty UDX exe may have code genes in common with TeamViewer.-----July 2023 Aqua Kitty UDX review (thumbs down rating):The (July 2023) version of Aqua Kitty Ultra Deluxe is detected as a coin miner and other types of Malware by Microsoft, McAfee, and 7 other antivirus vendors.Earlier this month they had this issue and updated the game to a new version with the same coin miner / malware issue.See the virustotal report:

_childDocuments_.review: I received this updated version free since I own the original.It's what it says on the tin: Defender with kitties.There's multiple modes in this new version. They added "dreadnought mode" where you have to destroy a bunch of structures making up the inside of dreadnoughts while dodging infinite waves of enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Surprised to find this on my account years after I played a fun little arcade game about cats and submarines.It's a remake of the original, worth the revisit if you're like me and forgot about it.The extra game mode is a great addition and it can be tough so be sure to bring a friend in, props to whoever came up with the idea, it's fun!

_childDocuments_.review: So Guys... I already bought "Aqua Kitty" a long time ago and enjoyed it a lot. Now the new UDX version is out as a separate game and not as the usual paid DLC. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game some leeway because it's obviously meant to be a fun little title created as a passion project by a small team. _childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking amazing!!!. It was so fun to play the classic game in dual kitty mode with my youngest daughter. Unfortunately, she moved off with her mom. Anyway, I somehow got UDX for free - I guess from when I bought the classic PC version. Even though the classic version was GREAT and had the super amazing Sound Track by Electric Cafe  , I still wanted the UDX version. It was a while before the authors make UDX available on PC and now I got it for FREE!!! _childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: Great update to the original game "Aqua Kitty Milk Mine Defender". The game is very reminiscent of the classic arcade game by Williams named "Defender". The difference is that in the game Defender, you fly around in a spaceship stopping and destroying aliens from grabbing humans off the planet. In Aqua Kitty UDX, you're stopping any number of adversaries from grabbing your milk miner kitties from the bottom of the ocean.This game has captured that classic arcade feel that many games try for but few achieve in my opinion. The game is addictive. These devs have done a great job of combining crisp clean pixel art with that classic arcade style gameplay.The game is a 2D continual side scroller that is in an underwater environment. You play as a kitty in a submarine, protecting your milk miners on the bottom of the ocean.  There are various power ups and enemies to deal with while you're protecting your miners from being taken.  You fight your enemies in waves that get progressively harder with progressively different enemies to fight.This update has Classic, Arcade, Infinite and Dreadnought modes. Each mode brings its own twist on the story and is a great way to introduce the game in 4 different ways. Nice upbeat music and sounds makes this as enjoyable to hear as the game is to play.I already had the game Aqua Kitty Milk Mine Defender and loved it.  Anyone who previously owned that game received the updated "Aqua Kitty UDX" for free. As I loved the original game from the start, I felt a need to give the updated UDX some love as well.I had no problems playing the game with my Logitech gamepad.  Nice enjoyable game for the casual player or bullet hell enthusiast alike.
_childDocuments_.name: AQUA KITTY UDX

_childDocuments_.review: Aqua Kitty UDX blasts onto Xbox One in this enhanced Ultra Edition including an all new epic Dreadnought mode. Get ready for fast paced submarine action, defending the kittens from disruptive mechanical sea creatures. Play co-op or solo, the milk must flow. [Xbox.com]

name: New Star GP
detailed_description: NEW STAR GP is the arcade racing game where every decision counts - on and off the track! You take control of your own motorsport team, guide your team’s technological development, plan your race strategy, take the wheel, and drive to victory! With a simple but deep gameplay experience and appealing retro visuals, NEW STAR GP puts you in the driving seat for every twist and turn as you manage and race your team through decades of racing, from the 1980s all the way to the present day! STUNNING RETRO VISUALS Beautifully rendered retro looks and a driving retro soundtrack that bring back fond memories of the iconic racing games of the 1990s. CHOOSE YOUR RACE STRATEGY! A pick-up-and-play arcade driving experience that has more depth than you think. While anyone can take the wheel and have success, those who want to truly master the game will want to make use of tyre choice and wear, component reliability, slipstreaming opponents, fuel load, and even pit strategy. Anything can happen in races, from catastrophic component failures and dynamic weather changes, to tyre blowouts and multi-car pileups. START YOUR CAREER IN THE 80s Compete in GPs, Elimination Races, Time Trials, Checkpoint Races, and one-on-one Rival Races. In between events, choose how to upgrade your car, or which staff perks to equip: from sponsored car components to faster pit stops. When you’ve won a season, progress to the next decade of racing and face a new set of opponents and challenges in a brand new car! RACE ICONIC LOCATIONS AROUND THE WORLD! Race a myriad of events across the decades at some of the most iconic racing locations around the world. Earn rewards for setting personal bests! CHALLENGE YOUR FRIENDS IN SPLIT-SCREEN MULTIPLAYER! Enjoy the game with your friends with a fun split-screen social multiplayer mode. Play with 2, 3, or 4 players, choose your car, driver, handicap, and play mode, and any of the tracks to compete on. Points carry over from event to event, so it’s as easy to play one race as it is to play a whole season of racing together. WRITE YOUR NAME IN THE HALL OF FAME! Can you beat competition from all over the world to clock the fastest Hot Lap time? Outpace your opponents’ ghost-cars and claim your place on the Steam leaderboards! JOIN OUR DISCORD

Play career mode and work your way through decades of racing while upgrading your car and your support team... or chase high scores in championship mode on your own or in split-screen with up to three friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 1994 my Dad ran out and bought me a copy of Virtua Racing on Sega Genesis for my birthday. I never realized how expensive and complicated it had been to get it at the time, but I played the game to death and I still remember how it made me feel.  Joyful, engaged, and excited. This game is more complex and advanced, but it makes me feel the SAME way I did playing Virtua Racing. The game itself is arcadey, with light simulator elements such as tire/fuel pitstop strategy, car development, and team management. The graphics are bright/colorful, the music is upbeat, engines sound excellent, the courses are similar enough to real locations but without some of the issues associated with same (Monaco, Imola/Monza), and it is clearly a labor of love from the developer. I'd like to give a big 'Thank you' to New Star Games for this engaging and enjoyable racing game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! The work put into the career mode makes me joyful to experience. Racing is fun to do and fun to strategize with, and the career itself is so well done. I'm halfway through the 2000's season and I can say for sure that New Star GP is one of my favorite racing games in a while. For F1 fans who would like something to play that's not as focused on simulation driving, this is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: First game in a long time that I had pure fun playing. Pros: right level of challenge and balance between hardcore and casualCareer mode is engaging and detailedTracks are exciting to race roundCar detail and customisation is ok, for a simple indie game it’s actually very goodInterchangeable weather conditions!Progressing through the eras of f1 is a nice touchCons (nitpicking): some off track events in career are repetitive, but some can sometimes really disadvantage you ahead of a race! Overall, this game is a love letter to f1 fans, particularly those who may be disenchanted with the current f1/codies series. Pick this one up and give it a go and just have fun, it runs beautifully on the deck too. I’d give the game a 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: "If you finish first..."The Good:Only two hours in, halfway through the 1980s season this is already one of the greatest racing games I've played.  The feel of the racing strikes a perfect balance between arcade and simulation.  It's very easy to pick up and play but in order to be a successful racer, you'd have to take into account the racing line, brake zones, and drafting behind opponents.  The great thing about the career mode is that it's not just about building up your car with upgrades but also building rivalries and relationships it really helps immerse you into the drama in the world of sports.  The old school 90s look of the game ain't half bad either.  Also, the difficulty so far feels tough but fair on Pro difficulty.  It really forces you to earn a podium position and oh boy can the AI make it difficult, get ready to try to pass racers who cut you off and brake check you at every corner but it makes taking the podium so much sweeter!The Bad:Can't say anything bad about it so far, except maybe the lack of online multiplayer is a bummer.  Also had minor glitch that replaced my career mode character with one of the arcade mode characters but was nothing a quick restart didn't fix.The Ugly:Would have been nice if the career allowed for qualifying laps.  I get always starting in the rear is a staple of old school arcade racers but still, I'm not a fan of that concept."...you win the race."
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play as much of this as I could so I could get a good idea of the difficulty, and I think I have played enough of this now to make an informed review. The game difficulty starts off quite easy and it is not really a problem to finish first in most GPs in your first year. I was a bit worried that this game would be too easy, and this trend did carry on for another season before things started getting more challenging. There are two difficulty levels which you choose between at the start of your career and these cannot be changed once you have made your choice. I chose the normal difficulty, so I would imagine choosing pro would mean a much more difficult path through the decades. There are five seasons organised by year, starting in the 1980's  and finishing in the 2020's. With each decade comes faster cars, better upgrades, more difficult circuits, and better opponents. When I reached the 2010 season I struggled to finish races let alone win the championship, but your upgrades and cash are carried over to season two so you have a head start. The racing is arcade based and there are lots of things happening that you wouldn't see in a sim. Collisions are quite forgiving and cutting corners doesn't penalize you too much apart from slowing your car down if you veer off too much. Your car does sustain damage but it takes quite a battering before it starts effecting your drive. If you crash into walls on tight circuits or hit too many opponents you risk the danger of tire blowouts, gearbox malfunctions, and brake failure. All of these things can be repaired in a pit stop, but obviously the pit stop will take longer. Whilst you are in the pits, you can put on new tires, fill your car up with gas, and make any repairs necessary. These are all decisions you need to make. You don't have to change tires or repair your car, and sometimes these are valid decisions. If you find yourself limping over the finishing line with a broken gearbox and no brakes, but won the race because you refused to go in the pits when your pit crew told you, then that can be very satisfying. There are perks which you gain from winning cups in challenge races, like beating a challenging lap time, winning an elimination race, racing around the circuit in reverse order, and racing through checkpoints before the time runs out. If you do well in these you receive cups, and when you have enough cups, a perk is unlocked which you have a choice of two. Placing your perk in a slot can give you a nice advantage, but you'll soon find that you have more perks than slots, so will have to decide which perks suite your driving style, or whether you want other perks, like benefiting the team. There are a lot of perks that give you an advantage in lots of areas, including faster pit stops, earning more money, getting the option to restart a GP, keeping your team happy, or generally making your car faster or handle better. Some of these perks are better than others, like being able to restart your GP. This perk is the best perk to get but it is only offered to you half way through the season, but it does stay with you if you need to start a new season. You have a team of workers which you need to keep happy. They all have a happiness rating and making decisions effects this rating. Usually, any decision will make one faction happy and the other side unhappy. You can pay for morale boosters, which is needed now and again, but generally it is not too much hassle to keep everyone happy. Now and again, you'll be offered new staff from other teams, and if you can afford them and you think they are better than what you have, you can hire them. Each person has certain attributes like "Gets on with people", or "Is easily pleased" and these are color coded in a traffic light system. It wasn't really clear how these attributes effected your team however and I tended to just go for workers who had the most green attributes. Winning races earns you prize money which you can spend on upgrading your car in areas like handling, acceleration, top speed, braking, and efficiency. There are several tiers and they get more expensive as you upgrade, and unless you do more than one season in a decade it is unlikely you will earn enough money to fully upgrade your car, so choose the best upgrades for your driving style. If you are low on money and do not have enough for an upgrade, there are temporary boosters you can buy from other teams that last so many laps, and can be the difference between winning or not. I absolutely loved the racing. It is so easy to get completely engrossed in the proceedings, The tracks are all faithful representations of existing tracks, although you may be racing on a short circuit or the full circuit. There are driving line and speed indicators to help you navigate the courses and a small map. There is an option to rewind if you crash and try again, but this will have a negative effect on trophies won and money earned, so generally I just started again. As you travel through the decades you really notice the difference in speed and handling, and those upgrades really make a difference too. Opponents can be very aggressive and swerve in front of you to block an overtaking move. If you hit an opponent too many times, they may complain afterwards, and unless you apologize to them publicly, they become a rival of yours and will behave even more erratically than before.  The cars feel realistic and the driving feels satisfying and rewarding. Some of the crashes were a bit odd, but then again this is an arcade game not a sim. I was quite impressed with the depth of management involved in the game and it gave it an extra dimension, rather than just racing. Nothing is particularly difficult to manage but your decisions will have an effect on the outcome of a race, whether that be a choice between soft tires or hard tires, or a one stop or a two stop strategy. There are lots of little choices to make throughout the game, and a few strange events that crop up now and again that are either amusing or potentially lucrative like stopping an opponent from finishing on the podium. Apart from the career mode, there is also an option to create your own championships with up to four people participating with lots of customization options, and a hot lap mode where you can compete on leader boards and race against your ghost. There is a lot of content here. I would estimate over thirty hours depending on how competitive you are.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the racing game I've been waiting for.As someone who has done my fair share of sim racing, NS GP is a breath of fresh air. Underlying the arcade-y racing is a physics and handling model that you can sink your teeth into. If you enjoy finding the optimal racing line, picking your breaking point, experimenting with how to ride the curbs - that's all there for you, and it feels amazing. That said, NS GP doesn't demand any of this! You can absolutely just focus on approximately following the racing line and avoiding collisions, and still have a blast.So far, career mode seems equally fun and accessible! It takes many conventional race management game systems (part upgrades, staff, dilemmas etc) and gives it a distinct New Star Games flare. Each race weekend has a number of fun and re-playable events that allow you to get acquainted with the track before jumping into the Grand Prix event, which can only be played once. I love this structure, and appreciate how the extra events don't just feel like busywork (like how practice sessions do in other games).Overall, I am thoroughly impressed with NS GP, and can't wait to continue following its development!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Slipstream and Horizon Chase Turbo and Hotshot Racing and so forth...but THIS is the one that's finally scratching the retro racer itch for me. Totally into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised by how fun this is.Don't be fooled by the looks. This has more management that EA's F1 game. Really cool with the pit stops where you have do a lot on your own. Then there's hiring team staff, decision making etc...Wasn't expecting that tbh. "SADLY" the handling is too arcady to really compete with F1. But the npc drivers have some agressive lines and won't make it too easy to get past, which mitigates the handling model. So there's fun to be had on track as well. All in all, it can't replace EA F1 but some of its ideas are great. Wished these 2 games could be merged into one.Absolutely recommending New Star GP. (Obviously great on the Steam Deck as well)

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun racing game in a generation, New Star GP expertly blends exhilarating retro-racing with an in-depth, dynamic, and lengthy career mode.Most modern racing games have a singular focus on realism at the directly proportional expense of fun and engaging game design.  Thankfully, things do seem to be pulling in the opposite direction as of late, as there have been several polished and fun arcade racing games in the past several years.  But nothing in this new wave of retro, arcade focused releases holds a candle to New Star GP.The racing itself is top notch here.  Easy to handle but difficult to master, as you need to account for things like fuel weight, tire and component wear, weather changes, and pit stops (which are handled as a simple minigame).  And the star of the show is the aggressive and dynamic AI, as each race forces you into toe-to-toe battles around fun, bite-sized versions of real life circuits.  Races play out differently in nearly every attempt, as the AI is impressively tuned to race you as hard as it can.The meat of the game is the lengthy and addictive career mode that has you racing through five decades from the 1980's to the 2020's.  Each decade has 10 race weekends, each with a different combination of events (time trials, checkpoint races, reverse races, elimination races, rival races) and finally a GP.  Winning grants you "BUX", which you spend to upgrade your car.  You also have a crew of three (pit, commercial, and engineer), each with a different set of unlockable perks that you attain through winning races.  This crew is randomly assigned to you when you start, and each member has different personality traits.  You will also have to manage your relationships with the team in order to extract their maximum value.  Simple choose-your-own-adventure style prompts give the player a fun amount of choice that lets them craft their experience off the track.The combination of these systems allows for amazingly dynamic racing throughout the career.  Here's an example: my commercial manager doesn't respect the pit crew, and at one point early in the season, clumsily injures my pit manager after dropping a box of supplies.  My pit manager is then out for two GP's with an injury, meaning that pit stops are slower.  I know that the track I'm racing wears the tires faster than others, so I should plan on two pit stops, but this isn't ideal with slower pit times.  As I start the race, I'm then informed that there is a 30% chance of a component malfunctioning, but I can't afford the repair because I just increased my car's acceleration to account for the tight turns and lack of straights.  To top it off, the forecast calls for rain in the middle of the race, which may throw a another wrench into my pit strategy.This might sound overly complex, but these are actually simple systems that interact in highly dynamic ways.  The developer has tuned these systems to near perfection, ensuring that nothing is cumbersome or overbearing, and that everything contributes to extracting as much fun as possible from the game.  It's honestly quite the feat of game design, and unlike anything else I've experienced in racing games in years.My only criticism would be that the dynamic difficulty scaling takes a bit too long to challenge the player on "normal" difficulty, so "pro" is the way to go if you play racing games regularly.  There is serious challenge there as you progress through the decades.On top of this is a customizable "Championship" mode that allows for local coop (an amazing rarity), and sees the player design their own set of races, setting the conditions and difficulty.  There seem to be a few more options in this mode as well, including difficulty, realistic damage, and AI buffs.  The performance of the game has been perfect across both Steam and Xbox in the time that I've put in.All of this is to say, New Star GP is easily the most well-designed and fun of the recent crop of arcade racing games.  If you've longed for a game that combines fun, exhilarating arcade racing with a best-in-class career mode, you found it.  I can't recommend the game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I’m only 30 minutes into this game, but I would like to give an honest feedback already. I went through the tutorial and qualifying, and had my first GP race. Controls are simple, finding the perfect racing line is not. Let me back up a little: I LOVE racing games. But I am not a sim racer. I like to play on controller, or even a simple non FFB T80 racing wheel… but now I own a steam deck so controller it will forever be. I have played officially licensed F1 games, and any game that has GT3 or IndyCar. I started with automatic gear shifting and then worked my way into manual in order to “feel” the car better. I always keep the racing line on because on a screen type can’t get the same feeling and awareness of a real track… but you better believe I push the boundaries of that red line. My teenage sons also enjoy racing games, but they seem to enjoy the more arcade style. Back to my GP race: by lap 4 I have pushed my way through the pack to P2. I’m approaching Gilles Verville who is battling a back marker, VER goes left on the inside, so I take the outside line using a little push to pass turbo, hoping I can carry some speed into the next corner. VER reads my play and squeezes the back marker into me, throwing me into the gravel trap. I was furious… but laughing hysterically. I’ve never been so mad and so happy at the same time. This game is fantastic!  I only have two complaints that prevent this game from being 5 stars. 1: I would love to be able to build my own tracks, and with the simplicity of these graphics I think it would be easy to implement the racing line for NPC. I don’t even want to share them online, just locally recreate the legendary Long Beach circuit that Indy runs on in a 4 player battle with my kids. 2: if it’s possible to add an advanced control scheme to allow for manual shifting. I know the physics are simplified but I just love downshifting into a corner and hearing the sweet spot. Other than that, well done devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everyone, as it’s a bit repetitive and you’ve seen almost everything the game has to offer in the first decade apart from the faster classes and a few of the locations. But played in short bursts, New Star GP is one of the best racing games I’ve played in a hot minute.While not super in-depth, managing your team and making decisions are engaging little interactions between races, and picking pit strategies and accounting for grudge-holding opponents or other mishaps on track means racing is rarely straightforward. People say there’s not much here for the price but I think $30 for the nearly 20 hours I put in is well worth it, and if you’re looking for a decently chunky little racer without any of the open world trappings of the current racing game landscape, you can do so much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I had in decades with racing games. Because it breaks everything down to the basics: just run and win. _childDocuments_.review: This game would just be a decent arcade racer, but the upgrades, the progression, the multiple track variations, and how the game helps creates a story through it's news articles, failures, and the rivalries system makes this into a unique game that really captures the enjoyment of F1 racing. The AI does a reasonable job of being able to battle on track and stay side by side through corners. The main weakness of the AI is that it is usually slower in pit stops (even without the player using any of the perks that help improve your pitstop speed), and they're especially slow on pit entry, which means you can usually gain 3-4 seconds on most tracks quite easily just by having better pitstops. The AI also often commits to a 2 stop strategy, and while it takes a bit of time to get the tyre selection and fuel loads right, on a lot of tracks, especially with a reasonably upgraded car, you can often manage a 1 stop race, which is a huge advantage even if you're not faster on track. I've also noticed some times that even though I've messed up my strategy, pitting on the last lap the cars behind me will also pit, even though they should be able to make it to the end. I believe the AI is programmed in a way that means they will copy your pit strategy to try and keep up with the better, fresher tyre. But with only 1 lap remaining, this means you often get a free pit-stop, when they should really get the track position, especially since you leave the pits with cold tyres. This doesn't always happen though.Tyre management is a lot of fun, with the tyres wearing out faster when you touch the kerbs, and becoming more damaged if you run off the track. This means you can try and make a 1-stop work by avoiding the kerbs. Fuel management can be fun too, if you've realised you've underfueled the car and can't make it to the end, you can lift and coast to effectively manage fuel consumption. Fuel weight significantly effects the performance of the car, so trying to minimise how much fuel you need can add a lot of lap time.Some perks are objectively better then others. Sponsor perks mostly suck, while perks such as the one that lets you have better control when you run off the track allow you to get away with some really drastic cuts on certain tracks, or the perk that gives you extra fuel when you run out once a race, which means you can run with much less fuel for your final stint, and generally gives you a large performance edge.The AI does appear somewhat adaptive in difficulty. Towards the end of my first season, the AI drivers at the front of the pack gained a lot of pace, which meant the final 2 races were a genuine challenge.You can crash your opponents out pretty easily, and there isn't a massive disadvantage to this, since they only really get mad at you and start trying to hit you and race you harder if you talk trash about them in the post race interview. This means if a faster car is overtaking you, a lot of the time you can just put them into the wall.Overall, it's a very solid game, and while a bit more content would increase it's value a lot, as far as arcade racing games go, I'd say it's up there in quality. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: One of those times that I wish Steam had a "neutral". Like, I can't fault it because it works, but it just isn't for me.I mean, lets break this down. £24.99 is the same money for Le Mans Ultimate, though I would argue this works better out the box than that game, but its a mere price comparison so here's to document my experience;Career mode plays like this; You have car. You can get money to upgrade car by doing 2/3 lap events at a track. Car stat numbers go up when you upgrade. Car becomes superior. You win. The game rewards you putting the numbers of your cars build up versus skill. I play a lot of racing games, I think this is the part that mostly broke my interest - My skill at racing was not rewarded because either my car is that much better because I grinded the events to get money to make it better, or it was inferior meaning that I would watch everyone vanish on the straights. I struggled to do the Race 2 elimination race because my car just didn't have the acceleration, but as soon as I upgraded it... suddenly there was no issue. Handling physics are... brake only on really tight corners. Else go flat out or ease off the accelerator. You have so much grip even on hard tires its like you stuck glue on the tires. Watching the videos of this game on the steam page you'd think that you'd have to brake more or whatever but no, its just dramatic effect. You can really push hard almost all the lap and suffer no consequence.I was able to win 3 of the 4 career races that I did before I got bored merely because I did the 1 stop strategy and just abused the places the AI goes slowly - certain corners (example is Turn 3 at the Vienna track the AI just brake test mid corner while you can go flat out easy), entering the pits (they seem to really slow down and you can just breeze past them when they do this). The AI themselves are uninteresting. They don't provide a challenge so much as they are just numbers that you either have or have not surpassed. Or they get "annoyed" with you and will literally run you off the track. The idea of having to go through 5 more GPs in the career, replaying the same track 2/3 times before doing the GP was honestly just not my idea of fun. The only reason I lost 1 race was because I tried to Lando the last lap when it went wet. I managed to stay on the track but the Wet Tires driver overtook me because he had better grip. Note, I was playing the career on Pro and was not even breaking a sweat to win races. By Race 4 I was winning by 15 seconds over 2nd place.I don't know, maybe I missed the point of the game. I just liked the idea of having some AI to race against in a championship mode. It just didn't make for an enjoyable experience playing.Finally - The controls are fixed. I prefer my racing games playing the right stick accelerate/brake and was annoyed I couldn't change from the RT/LT. Or my rear/left/right camera views to see around me on A/B/X ... none of the controls can be rebound on the controller but you can do it on Keyboard. Not that it mattered, I didn't need my normal finesse to play the game as the handling was super arcadey which I guess is the idea. They're mostly responsive enough though more responsive when you upgrade your car... so. There's that.TL:DR If you like a racing game against the AI which is more chill than challenge, with a game that references tracks, locations, cars from Formula One, I suppose you'll enjoy it. I find £24.99 a bit of a steep ask for what it is. I know New Star are good for it considering their mobile games are cash grabbing micro transaction horrible messes (you ruined New Star Soccer guys :( ) and this honestly feels like it would play fine on a phone rather than being a PC game, at a £4.99 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it took more inspiration from the F1 Netflix show than actual F1 and honestly it makes for an incredibly engaging career mode where you juggle the wellbeing of your team and your reputation as a driver. The racing itself is intense and arcadey, with just enough simulation thrown in to make it still feel like you are undoubtedly driving an F1 car.The real star of the show here is the driver AI which adapts to both your skill level and driving style. If you race respectfully and carefully, other drivers will admire you and will yield to you in the turns and straightaways. If you cause a crash or even ♥♥♥♥-talk other racers between events, however, you'll make enemies that will drive defensively, cut you off in turns, and mock you as they pass. If you've got a nemesis on the track you'll know about it because they'll make your life hell at every opportunity!Performance-wise, the game runs great, even on steam deck, and maintains a solid FPS throughout. I haven't encountered a single bug and my only complaint is that the UI can be confusing to navigate but overall I'd highly recommend this game

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite good, but not for long term play.  The AI cars are very aggressive as you get on in the game which would be bearable if you didn't always start last (no matter where you are in the championship) or if you could have races that are longer than 6 laps.As it stands the starting at the back all the time and the short races mean that on the higher difficulty you don't have time to be patient and race, you just end up barging like the AI do which all gets a bit silly.Shame as there is a lot of good things in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Most engaging career mode I've played in a racing game in some time. I've played 2 complete seasons now expect to be playing a lot more. The way choices are presented to the player allows for a really interesting and complex career mode that doesn't feel confusing and is easy to play without looking through a million menus before every race, but there's still plenty to min/max if that's your thing. The driver relationship mechanic that lets driver's be anything from "admirer" to "nemesis" is really fun and adds a lot even during races. Having a nemesis pass me and then show a kissy face emoji as they go by really gets me involved in caring about how the AI are doing in a race. There already seems to be way better content here in EA than most big racing games have at launch. I would like to be able to see more detailed results (unless I've just missed that feature) for previous races but the fact that that's the best criticism I can come up with shows the quality of the rest of the game. The driving model itself feels quite basic but engaging. Driving isn't hard but isn't easy and the AI is unpredictable and engaging. It's very easy to get absorbed in a 1v1 battle against an AI for an entire race at higher difficulty. It feels really precise on controller in a way that allows me to spend more time in close-quarters battles with AI. Trying something like that on controller in most formula-style racing games is a nightmare, so I'm really glad to have this awesome package for when I just want to race and enjoy myself.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best F1 style arcade racing games ever made but it has some issues/missing features:-No number of opponent setting, always 10 which can't be reduced/increased.-No rear-view mirrors but good arrow indicators if opponents nearby/behind you.-No qualifying sessions, always start at 10th place (except in career mode but only if use a perk). -No race restarts in career mode (except if set a perk before the race). -No crew photos in career menu, except when you get messages from them, making it more difficult to relate to who's who.-No proper button used for upgrade screen: X button (on Xbox controller), instead of A which exits menu.Nevertheless it has:-Great custom championships option.-Great controls and settings to turn on/off: damage, weather, pit stops.-Great option of choosing the pace of the race based on eras (from slow speed 1980s to super fast 2020s with progressively higher top speeds & acceleration for each era).  -Great quick 1min or less lap times with pit stops around every 4-5laps which make for some fun, epic and strategic fuel/tire option races at higher lap counts (up to 99 laps).  -Great camera options, from a full cockpit view to a zoomed out forward angled top helicopter perspective. -Great and unique career mode with crew happiness levels & perk bonuses that depend on text scenario questions/decisions between races.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surprisingly in depth racing game. I thought it was just going to be Virtua Racer but there's a career mode spanning the last 4 decades of racing, with rivals (you can ♥♥♥♥ on other drivers and stuff) and the more they hate you the more aggressive they get and can do stuff outside of races, car upgrades, other teams upgrade their cars as the season progresses and quite a few tracks. You can rent car improvements off other teams and if they like or dislike you the price can go up or down. There's changing weather effects in the race and a forecast that isn't perfectly accurate. Car parts can wear and break and there's tire heat and stuff but it's not like I was expecting where all tyres wear the same, it changes based on cornering directions and breaking and stuff so they can wear at slightly uneven rates.My main gripes are there's no marker to say 'this is how much fuel you need to do a lap when pitting so you have to do test runs to ballpark it, but after 2 trials and 4 laps of the GP you might forget 'was it 3 lines or 4?' You can pick a strategy and automate the process but I find a custom one is always much superior because it lets me do a one-stop strategy on soft tyres, not the mandatory hard otherwise.The other gripe is about the morale of your staff, you're always pissing someone off, its unavoidable, whoever you pick gets a boost and whoever you don't gets a hit. So it becomes less about picking the response you want to over what you need to, sometimes there isn't even the right response, like one race I spun out and came 3rd or 2nd or something and it says 'who was to blame? pit crew or commercial!?' and I'm like  but I can't pick that and blamed the most happy group, and why would it  be commercial?I'd give it an 8/10. The driving is simple enough even people who "hate all vehicle games" could enjoy it but complex enough to still be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is everything I have ever wanted in an arcade F1 racer. I have played a few of these Virtua Racing/Daytona USA esque games but they all just seem to lack a certain character, charisma, and charm. New Star GP does not have this problem. It actually does a really good job of distilling and gamifying the ins and outs of the sport. The story mode has fun choices throughout that allow you to curry the favor of your team, forcing you to manage them in a way where you are keeping them happy. What happens on the road doesn't stay on the road, as cutting off or crashing into opponents can cause them to build a rivalry with you, including what you actually say in interviews about them. This will make them more aggressive and faster so you have to manage your slings and arrows. The graphics here are superb, putting modern flourishes on a very low poly visual style that give it this wonderful, playful, and colorful aesthetic. The sense of speed is not up to the degree of something like the Codemasters/EA F1 series, but as you go you do upgrade your vehicle. However, it still remains exciting on the more corkscrew oriented tracks, and the car doesn't turn on a dime so you are expected to understand when to brake, although it is far more forgiving here than in racing sims.One baffling choice to me was the absence of a manual gearbox. I actually don't mind ultimately that I am driving automatic, it just adds to the more casual approach, but c'mon - even Virtua Racing had this feature, and it just adds a sense of depth and control to the driving ultimately. I think the developer was going for a more arcade oriented focus here, but since the game goes to such lengths to include pitting, tyre types and fuel management, it is a really disappointing choice to not include this. Not to dwell on it forever but - argh, please, add a manual gearbox. This is by far the best Virtua Racing inspired game in the bunch, by a longshot, and it would be even moreso were a manual gearbox present here. The sound of the cars is alright, but the winner here is the music. This soundtrack is...wonderful. I won't name names but there is one particular VR clone I was really excited about a couple of years ago and its soundtrack was just abysmal and didn't fit the tone of the game at all. This is corrected here in SPADES. This is a brilliant soundtrack that really captures both the arcade racing feel, and it's hard to extrapolate, but I get the feeling sometimes I am watching an old tuner VHS of some kind. Just really fantastic stuff all around, and they have the default mix all wrong here - the sound effects should be defaulted lower so that the soundtrack can shine through. The artists here obviously worked VERY hard to create the soundtrack for this game, and its a real kick in the face to have it drowned out by default the way it is. Anyways, my nitpicks are really minor. I really, really adore this game. It could certainly use a couple extra things but I am extremely satisfied with this purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I Cannot begin to say how brilliant this is!Simple yet absolutley engaging from the get go. _childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good amount of depth in a fun arcade racer package, nuanced with some realistic sim-style characteristics. Well worth picking up for any F1 fan, and it is a great casual racer that plays well on the Steam Deck as well as a PC.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral-positive. (Edit: This was a "negative" review but that looked kinda ridiculous with my 50h+ in the game. That was for 100% completion, and you could maybe do it in less if you're a little more efficient than I was.) Overall it feels like it's 90% finished, so it could do with a lot more polish / attention to detail, but when it's good it's really ****ing good. Get it on 50% discount or better - the original launch price does not reflect the quality of content contained within, and it could be interpreted as saying a lot about the developer. Don't get me wrong, this is a good game and the driving itself is great, but I have the hours in this game that I do despite everything else rather than because of them.It seems that the monthly patches have ceased, which concerns me somewhat. Not due to any game-breaking bugs, but just polish really: the presentation is very slap-dash, the UI (including *some* of the "English") is incomprehensible and make no rational sense until you get used to it, extremely slow pit AI, and it mentions social media when you're racing in the 80s/90s championships......so the sort of things that an update should fix. They're all relatively minor issues, although some are less minor than others. Small issues just add up if there's enough of them, y'know? On a subjective level, I also find the Wii-ass graphical style a bit of a turn off but it's not even done particularly well from an objective standpoint, and everything needs more of a colour gradient generally.Some reviews criticise the AI, especially later on in the career mode. There is some truth to it being borderline suicidal at times, but it's pretty easy to antagonise half the grid to the point where they would rather you lose than they win, and I bet that's the reason for those reviews. It does react to things like clean driving and the opposite of that. The thing is, if you keep your driving relatively clean, then the AI will while racing you too. The AI does also make mistakes, which is fine for a racing game... and also pretty funny when they're ahead of you. You can pressure the AI into making a mistake if you don't have space to properly overtake. The racing is the core of this game and it does it incredibly well, with the only racing issue being that the AI is absolutely awful at pitstops. It doesn't really know how to handle changeable weather conditions either, but I think that might be because the wet weather tyre is OP and is perfectly valid in "damp" conditions, however the AI doesn't know that.The main menu has the sound of a redline-revving V8 blaring, like it's about to explode, and is not a great first impression. If it was revving through the gears, it might sound alright! For a while I thought that was part of the music, and so I thought the music was trash. The music itself is okay, sort of standard 2020s indie racing game music (meaning sythwave inspired), but it's not exactly a soundtrack you'd buy. I personally started putting my own music on in the background after the first season.Plenty of effort went into the handling models, as should be the case in racing games, and the way the game does pitstops should have EA taking notes for the official F1 games, but everything else has an air of "yeah whatever, that'll do" about it. New Star GP is a good game (see my hours) but it ultimately feels like a beta. When you get into a battle with 1-2 other cars for meaningful positions, with drivers who "respect" you or better, New Star GP is wonderful. The game could be a summary of everything great about Formula 1, and it almost is.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably one of the first few people that have completed all the achievement and the career.
