_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is a fascinating blend of racing simulation and arcade racing, offering a multi-layered experience that keeps players engaged on multiple fronts. Here’s a detailed look at what makes this game stand out:Gameplay and MechanicsNew Star GP strikes an odd yet intriguing balance between a racing sim and an arcade racer. The car handling is a mix of sim-style precision and arcade-like accessibility, making it enjoyable for a wide range of players. The game features a variety of perks that you can equip to enhance your car’s performance, such as better slipstreaming, increased earnings from races, faster pit stops, and improved off-track handling. These perks add depth to the gameplay, encouraging players to drive strategically and aggressively.Management and RelationshipsOne of the unique aspects of New Star GP is the management of your pit crew and teammates. Your team members can be sidelined due to injuries or other issues, adding a layer of realism and strategy to the game. Additionally, the relationships with other drivers are dynamic and impactful. Drivers you collide with will become more aggressive, and continued collisions can sour your relationship with them, affecting their behavior on the track.Track Variety and Car PerformanceThe game boasts a surprising number of track layouts that keep the racing experience fresh and challenging. Each track tests your skills in different ways, ensuring that the gameplay never becomes monotonous. However, the car handling, while good, leans more towards an arcade feel than a true simulation, which might disappoint some players looking for a more realistic experience.Challenges and DownsidesOne of the main challenges in New Star GP is the uphill battle against rival cars, which seem to be fully upgraded from the start of the season. This can make early races particularly tough until you can afford to max out your car through strong performances or clever pit strategies. The tracks, while well-designed, are not exact replicas of real-life circuits, which might be a letdown for purists. Additionally, the cars, though they get faster over time, never quite deliver the raw acceleration and speed of real F1 cars.Performance and PortabilityThe game runs smoothly at a steady 60 FPS on the Steam Deck, providing a seamless racing experience. It’s also available on the Switch, making it a great option for on-the-go gaming without the need to carry around the bulkier Steam Deck.Final ThoughtsOverall, New Star GP is a highly enjoyable game that successfully combines elements of both racing sims and arcade racers. Its multi-layered gameplay, dynamic relationships, and strategic depth make it a standout title. While it has its downsides, such as the arcade-leaning car handling and the initial difficulty curve, it remains a must-play for fans of games like Virtua Racing and Super Retro GP. If you enjoy a mix of simulation and arcade racing with a strategic twist, New Star GP is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I'm really glad I didn't review too soon, this throwback arcade racer is mint. There is so much in here (some of which that wasn't on release) and it is a super-satisfying, pretty deep and good value game with so much love put into it, which is exactly what I like.While obviously a massive homage to Virtua Racing in look and style, it does a great job of adding all the modern bells and whistles you want from any retro salute like this, with a lengthy and pretty deep career, the sim elements you DO want in like tyre wear and pitstop strategies, and none of the stuff you wouldn't when looking at this game cold.  There are several modes including multiplayer but I reckon that 90% of us just want to play this for its old skool vibes but with modern production and content, of which there is plenty; at least 15 hours of variety and challenge before you have to repeat yourself. And like I said, you can tell this game was made with love. Brilliant art and music styles (with plenty of fan-service) and a properly thought-through structure and progression system. It's actually quite magnificent, and the best thing is that, right now, there's not much really like it.  A cracker

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the style, the music, and the racing, but most of the other mechanics in this game were annoying.In career mode, you are constantly trying to purchase upgrades, but you also have to spend money to prevent parts from breaking, stop perks from being disabled or keep your staff happy. But they surprise you with these emergency requests right before a race, so during the entire career playthrough, I could never afford any of them and always suffered broken parts during races or had to miss out on hiring better team members.There are perks you unlock, like a faster boost or getting more money from races, but you always get presented with a selection of perks, and buying a perk from one person makes the other unhappy, so I picked the perks that would keep people happy instead of the perks I wanted. Each level in the career mode had a different set of perks, so you couldn't use the same perks you had already unlocked and had to unlock the same perks multiple times.The physics in this game can sometimes go crazy. Sometimes, when other AI racers made contact with me, my car would fly into the air like it was doing a sick skateboard trick. There is a rewind feature, but you're penalized if you use it in most racing modes.There's not much car customization, but there are a lot of tracks. _childDocuments_.review: Perfect mix between arcade and simulation where you drive in different decades. Since this is in early access, some of the features are not available yet.The driving experience is a hybrid of arcade driving with mechanics available only in simulations. You'll need to think about fuel, tires, damage, and pit stops in particular. And on the arcade side, you get a turbo that recharges after each lap and three rewind options. Tires lose durability and the performance depends on weather. Because it can start pouring in the middle of the race, you should drive into the pit lane as soon as possible because the wrong tires won’t work right. You also don't want them to go red and blow up. Fuel is another thing that requires smart choices. It constantly runs out during a race and you will eventually have to go refuel. However, with less gas in the tank, all of the car's stats improve, so there is some risk-reward involved. When you enter the pit, time does not stop and nothing happens on its own. You need to act quickly by selecting the appropriate items and holding down the refueling button. The first few stops will most likely be slow because you don't know where everything is, but it will improve with time. While these mechanics are always present in the game's career mode, the championship typically removes them or turns them on in challenging races. Championship is a bunch of cups where you can take your favorite car. There are no restrictions and all perform the same. Sadly, most of it is locked because of early access.The career is where the fun happens. First, you make a driver from a reasonable set of options (you can't delve into every last detail) and select the colors for the car. You begin in the 1980s and work your way up to the present. Each decade becomes more difficult. Despite the fact that the game lacks licensed vehicles, it does a fine job at making them look appropriate for the era.A decade has ten racing locations with various events such as elimination or checkpoint races. You can start with these smaller events or go straight at the main even. However, while smaller events can be repeated, the major race can only be played once. Each event has a number of goals. It's a good idea to make an effort because getting the best result earns you two types of rewards. The closest thing to a game's currency is Bux. It allows you to improve parts of your car, which is necessary if you want to stay competitive. Each part can be improved multiple times, and additional bodyshells can be unlocked.The second award is cups that are linked to your crew. You get to choose one of the two people after earning five cups. What's intriguing about this is that each comes with a very useful perk. You might gain more bux per race, enable limitless rewind, or even totally automate pit stops. The catch is that there is only room for three individuals - or two more if you use bux to unlock the spots.Another interesting feature is how people think of you. This is noticeable on the track when you receive emojis from other drivers. For example, a tongue sticking out as they overtake you or a furious face when you hit them from behind. They might remember this and decide to come at you in the next race. This is also important when it comes to staff. Following a race, a difficult situation may arise, forcing you to choose a side. As a result, you will have one happy and one unhappy team member. If you irritate someone, they may leave your team.

_childDocuments_.review: As expected with New Star Games, it's another absolute Banger.I love the idea of separating the classes between the decades and all the facetes of career mode work really well.You can sometimes tell that it's in Early Access, like how the music settings reset every time you start the game, but those moments are way less frequent than my experience with other Early Access games.I'm really looking forward to experiencing the newer decades as well once they're finished and hoping that one can design their own championships and race with their own settings in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of games nail the handling and driving feel of racing games (this game included), but very few nowadays manage to capture everything around the driving that makes a game great and stand out from the others. This game does and I love the detail and love put into this game, including the driver rivalries, post race interviews & moments with your crew. They all matter and change how other drivers race you or unlock new perks for your crew to help you in races.The sound design is great I love how the engines sound, the cars feel really fun and have a variety of options for upgrades and bodies, and the tracks are beautiful and vibrant. The tracks are loosely based on their real life counterparts so if you are familiar with them from real life you will be able to pick out layouts and track side scenery that's taken from the real thing.I am with other reviewers, I would love to see this dev team make a game like this for other racing disciplines like touring cars, rally, stock car, even motorcycles. Definitely recommend, even at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Having done every significant event and having raced a full season, I can confirm that this game is amazing— not amazing for an indie game, amazing, full stop. The team behind this must really understand racing. I only wish I could change difficulties after starting a season, but other than that, I can't really complain about this game. It's a great mix of arcade and sim racing, it's fun, it's lite, it's cheap.This game feels great, looks even better, and might just be the best in its genre.It is not too difficult, and there's a rewind function should you need it. There is a meaningful upgrade path, and a little managing to do when it comes to the team.There's a couple of events in every country (besides the GP), and 10 countries per season.Pit stops actually matter, as do the weight and tyre-wear of your car at any given lap. There's plenty of angles to choose from with the camera, and they all look great.Ah! And unlike with , you don't have to be online to play offline. What a novelty!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding love letter to old school arcade racers of the 90s, and F1 from the 80s through today. This does for F1 what Art of Rally did for Rallying! The driving may firmly fall into the "Simcade" category by design, the career mode has enough depth and tongue-in-cheek moments to entertain for days and weeks to come. The official F1 game is just that, but I suspect most of you would have much more fun playing this, I certainly have, and I'm a fan of hardcore racing sims. I hope the devs make enough to add even more eras to the game, as one of you put it in the discussion forum, adding even earlier eras of F1 to this already robust title can only be a great thing! 10/10 even at full price!

_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 2 hours in an I adored every minute.If you want an easy to pickup simcade feeling racer, buy it!It's a great game for bringing the feel of big F1 racing and all it's minutia into small sharp fast events without needed to learn everything to do with motor sport. The tutorial is litterally 2 minutes and explains everything you need and after that you're planning tire strategies based on weather, based on how long the track is. You're running practise laps to see how you can get better and where you can gain the edge. And even before that you have other evens along side each GP to warm you into the race.The handling physics are right where they need to be, being very simple but still feeling rewarding to drive and feeling like you always have control, no tap drifting nonsense, just you, a steering wheel and two pedals.Honestly so far the only thing I wish was in, was a manual gearbox option, but that might just be me.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time for the value. I highly recommend playing on pro, although an arcade-based game there's a still a learning curve.With that in mind, I do have some criticisms (mainly posted hoping the devs see, I can live with them):- Pro mode in some cases feels like I need to cheese the AI by overtaking them as they slow to a snail's pace during pitting in order to win. Suggest relaxing the difficulty a little and forcing the player to pit slower so you can't power full throttle into the pits- The buffs rivals gain are too strong, in some cases they're just outright faster in a straight line by a significant margin than my fully upgraded car. (Their advantage seems to be somewhat track dependant so maybe it's my skill, or their benefits are worth more on some track layouts? Azerbaijan was hell for example)- Leading on from the above, I feel forced in GPs to take the perk that lets me restart. One small mistake, or just not playing efficiently enough on every sector causes them to run circles around you. Most of the time the deciding factor is whether you have a good starting boost- Leading on again, reduce the randonmess of timing starting boost (encourages using the restart perk every time) and reduce the boost given to counteract- Maybe it's just me, but brake damage gives me major anxiety. I wish the threshold of damage after which the brakes can be replaced in the pits was lower. The strategy of trying to conserve my brakes it fun though!- Sometimes the game crashes when I've been tabbed out, or randomly starts on my second monitor.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who prefers arcade racers but doesn't mind a bit of sim-like racing every now and then, this might be one of my favourite racing games of all time.The actual racing is phenomenal, striking a perfect balance between arcadey fun and sim-like precision. The career mode is a similar story, giving you a good number of choices in how you build your car and team without being overwhelming like the official F1 manager games.And if you have any trepidation about buying games in Early Access, rest easy knowing that this game will hit 1.0 in March 2024 (edit: it was March 7 to be exact). The game in it's current state is extremely polished, and I suspect the finished version will be more about content updates than any gameplay fixes.This is New Star Games' magnum opus, the ultimate culmination of all the ideas and concepts they've been developing over the years. So what are you waiting for? :P

_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a surprise, wasn't expecting it to be so good, especially as a Steam Deck player (60fps, sips the battery, no fan noise and vibrant visuals).Highest compliment I can pay it is that it actually plays how your head remembers the old 90s classics do, but when you revisit them you forget how far things have moved on and improved. So this has simplified arcade handling but nuance with kerbs, slip streaming, racing lines, course elevation. It starts easy but the adaptive AI starts to kick in after a while and the opponents get a lot more aggressive. On top of the lovely visuals and handling it adds in a really nice lite management and upgrade system, plus an in race pit stop strategy (which requires 2 hands to change tyres and refuel and is fun under pressure to get right).Really really solid even in initial EA, and can only get better over time.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Just pure and simple fun - This has become the latest addition to my couch games collection. I ran through the beginner championship with a friend and so far I am very happy with my purchase. _childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I can safely say this is one of my most favourite racers of all time. I love the arcade vibe, great handling and sim elements without it actually controlling like a sim racer. People use sim-cade as a descriptor, but New Star GP is completely it's own thing. I love it.Course design is instantly memorable and ramp up nicely in difficulty at a perfect rate. The adaptive really kinda kicks in by the 90s GP's, but going back to replay the 80s GP's really is much more difficult the second time around - I have placed second many times, haha!The pit stops are incredibly fun - I love trying to get as much done with my left hand as my right hand fuels up the car. This is a great way to make pit-stops engaging, and the never, ever become a chore.Actually, the whole game is full of those minute details, nothing is slip-shod or extraneous. This game seems to have *serious* depth hiding under a bright and cheery veneer. I've gotta give a big shout-out to the amazing soundtrack. Totally catchy, with a mix of Drift Stage-style synthwave and rocking Japanese-style 90s racing rock. In fact, I'm getting F1 Challenge vibes, a classic SEGA Saturn racer. New Star GP is in the same ballpark, but much more polished and fleshed out. Having played for a while now, I'm hoping that more music is on the way, since it tends to repeat quite often. It would be REALLY GREAT if the different decades had era-appropriate music. I'd be more than willing to contribute some 90s dance jams if the devs are open to it! I'm pretty good with a Korg M1 soft-synth ;)Visuals are fantastic, but I'd love some sort of in-game AA toggle. I've noticed a couple of micro-stutters here and there, but most of the time is smooth sailing. There's a ton of charm here, for sure. Love the Tokyo track with it's cherry blossom trees.Controls are almost perfect. I feel that the steering controls could definitely be smoothed out a bit, whilst retaining the super-responsive feel they already have. Minute movements are totally possible and slick, but the move from minute movements to full steer could be smoothed out for sure.Please keep it up, this game is truly the best racer in an age. It uses the Formula 1 template to add meaningful depth to an arcade racer. It's just so much fun.I am completely enamoured, and I cannot wait to see how this all turns out when it leaves Early Access. It's so polished already, where can it go from here? I'm excited to find out.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time in 33 years some small team called New Star Games has perfected the right combination between Arcade and Simulation.Granted the game is more Arcade than Simulation, but apart from going fast and avoid crashing you have to strategise and think. Like how much fuel you put into the tank as you stop to pit (my first race has me pit twice because i didn't fill enough to prevent being overtaken, and i finish with half of the last bar left. It's thrilling), when to change tires, and how you need to manage relations with the others (basically don't piss other teams, give them pay bonuses if you can't elect to choose them, and...9.5/10. Would want an anime update because i can't really stand beady eyes. Then it'll be 10/10. Probably i'm just kidding.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I am so glad I bought this amazing game. I am more than positively surprised by what I really liked:+Very good career mode with lots of variety+You have your own crew+You can unlock and activate perks+Custom Championship against AI or together with friends against AI+Very cool tracks+Cool weather effects like heavy rain, lightning and thunder+Cool soundtrack+Very good controls with the controller (tip: set the steering a bit more sensitive)+Hot lap mode, whoever drives the fastest lap can move up the leaderboardWhat I didn't like so much:-No difficulty level selectable in career mode-Restarting in GP mode only possible with a perk-small bugs here and there in career mode, like for example that I suddenly have a different paint jobMy conclusion:This game is a big surprise, it's incredibly fun to play career mode with the 80s, 90s, 00s, 10s and 20s F1 Cars.Hopefully the game will continue to be updated with lots of bug fixes and lots of new content, buy it, you won't regret it, especially not during the sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not too many hours on this game /wink but can confidently say i love it. _childDocuments_.review: Great arcade racer with a robust career mode and enough strategy elements to make it feel somewhat sim like, despite being quite the opposite. But New Star GP is the perfect racing game for Steam Deck that I have been looking for, and i expect to put quite a number of hours into it. 140 hours later, I was right.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the 30 dollar price tag for sure.  The game has some decent gimmicks like a bare bones nemesis system, hiring staff, and car upgrades. It has a ton of fun tracks, with many having corners inspired by the real-life GP circuits.  My G29 wheel works fine, having just the minimum FFB to bring the wheel back to center... which is all you need really.  My only gripe is the AI blocks a little too much sometimes, and we need more drivers on the grid maybe? Highly recommend this game to any motor racing and/or F1 fans
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful concept, finally it's like having a Virtua Racing 2 or 3.  But the interface is like a bad dream, you'll have no idea what you're clicking. and every time you move in the  menu a tutorial box pops up that expects you to remember a bunch of text instead of practicing whatever function in real-time.  And the interface says "You can turn off the HUD driving line in options", except I looked and there is no option for that in the Interface.Also while tributing Virtua Racing, the devs created a bad artistic clash by using inappropriate typography, inappropriate rounded driver fingers (in first-person cockpit view) instead of square-ish fingers, and inappropriate annoying 'realistic' engine sound while nothing looks 'realistic' otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: great racing game. its the classic look of 1993 sega virtua racing but it plays like a solid sim. the perfect balance of realistic physics and arcade pure fun. a difficult game play and feel to pull off but new star racing pulls this balance off perfectly.(update)NO your mind is not playing tricks on you, your car is becoming more ragged as you drive it to the extreme edge. there is a lot of physics and mechanical models in this game. far more that you can see but you can feel and experience them. the "Era" or decades of the racing brackets is pure genius. its a fun arcade racing game in "1980" but its a full fledged racing sim at "2020" extremely FAST!!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP contains all the trappings of a modern-day racing simulation wrapped up in a marvelous presentation of stunning 4K visuals that make the 80’s look much better than they really were.  Just seeing those polygon panels that make up the curvature of the rear tires brought back instant memories.   Everything is so crisp and clean, and my 4090-equipped PC was able to deliver a fluid 120fps for single player and 60fps for two and four-player split screen either locally or using Steam’s Remote Play Together.  It is all too easy to approach this game from an arcade play perspective, but once you dive into the expansive career mode, New Star GP takes on the depth of the more serious competing titles.New Star GP is the complete racing package, delivering insane amounts of fun and increasing challenge while maintaining that flawless 80’s/90’s arcade aesthetic with its bold and colorful info overlay during the race to the incredible menus, garage, and pit crew interface.  I was impressed the game could have this much sophistication while maintaining a consistent level of arcade purity for both solo and split screen racing.  This is arcade racing perfection at its finest.Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade-y as far as controls being very forgiving and tight and things like boosts that re-new on each lap, but with sim touches like tire wear/choice, gas usage, pit stops. There are vehicle classes (decades) and upgrades you can purchase, and mild RPG like elements (keep your different crew members happy and you'll get certain perks). Split screen works great and you can set it up how ever you want, and a player can even get a speed boost handicap, great for racing with my kid! All around a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the cute condensed circuits that mirror the real life ones, they seem to keep the recognisable features while giving a completely new experience. I love the career mode, progression, and effort that has gone into it. It nails the more arcadey feel that this game is going for.I dislike that restart for GPs is locked behind an arbitrary perk slot, which doesn't even offer a distinct advantage, and can also be circumvented by restarting the game. I don't think hiding the restart button adds any value to the game, it's just kind of sucky. Need for Speed Unbound did something like this, and the game suffers heavily for it.The difficulty also seems to vary a lot between game modes on the same race weekend and I'm not sure why, that does affect my enjoyment a little.I am really impressed that the game has managed to make alternate strategies viable on what is a 6 lap simulation, something the real simulation games have never managed to work out (not that they really put any effort into trying). I also really like the different decades and that they feel quite different to one another.It would be kind of cool to see this game more developed to see what else it could be, such as adding harder difficulty for AIs, adjustability for lap count, possible qualifying etc. I wonder what other game modes could also be fun to have if it leaned more towards the arcade side of racing, like what would a game mode that focused on the demolition aspect be like? Or what about one more focused about tyre/fuel management like the real games do in practice sims?
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game has almost everything I would want in an open wheel arcade racer! The classic graphics look good, the in-race strategy is a lot of fun to work through on the fly, and the variation in race modes keep it interesting. I'm definitely looking forward to the release of more content, it'll be a racing staple in my game list for a long time.I do wish the car handling was either slightly adjustable or skewed more towards oversteer instead of understeer but this is a very minor complaint.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to just rip ass open over some things in this game until I got them figured out and actually got playing. Damn it, I like this game. The racing is fun, it's not stressful, it keeps you interested with the advancement and the knock off names to historic drivers easily click in your mind. The game is great, but I gotta rant about a few things. So just a bit of ass ripping.I've been married for so long I thought I had become immune to loud noises. Shut the damn intro music off or tone it down! Or let me choose to turn off all music at all times. My ears can only handle so much screaming. The ease to leave the game Drives Me Nuts when I are just moving around championship mode and just stumbling around at the start. As for on the track. Yellow means CAUTION, switch out the yellow arrows to either white boards, or green flashing lights in some corners. Every single time I see a little yellow box with an arrow my brain goes "that's a caution anywhere else". I should check that I received this product for free since it was a gift but I won't. The gifter was pretty bummed when I was raging a bit about getting into the game, and the music volume and some controls but once I got passed it I enjoyed the hell out of the game play.Oh, and if your controller is not working, make sure other controllers for other games aren't plugged in, my flight stick was making me rage when I couldn't figure out why my PS5 or Steam controllers wouldn't work.Back to good stuff. the 80's is where I am at in the game and it's a blast. The look of the cars is spot on. As for racing, the pitting is really cool, makes you pay attention. Want to undercut? It's there to do. Want to play the fuel game? It's there to do. Bumping doesn't total your car like other racing games that want that full sim experience (looking at you F122/23). The curbs are fun to use, the car really pops off them and you can see plenty of suspension travel and it does unsettle the car a bit. Your braking makes a difference on the brake rotors, your cutting the line, cornering a bit aggressively, does burn the tires up a bit. The devs have hit a good spot of some arcade action style racing but with some sense of realism of keeping your car in check. You can bin it a bit and not total the car out. The AI is all over the place skill wise which is fine, I'm sure it gets harder as you progress but the tongue out when you screw up and get passed is a nice little touch. Some AI are fast, some are back markers. Rivals is fun, it's nice passing one. The RPG portion with team principals, managers, commercial and pit guys you need to keep happy is a good start. Managing your bux to build a faster car is nice, it's basic and quick and not all out in depth taking you spreadsheets to decide what works and doesn't. Go fast parts go fast, brakes brake better and suspension and tires hook you up.If I had to buy it, I would, it's a great start to what can be a really fun game to play. I hope they keep progressing and pushing out content. This game is a great way to blow off some steam after a long day, race a bit and have fun.tldr: 10/10 go get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: good game, dev did well.  lot of camera angles, you can play it like a top down if you please, or sit in the cockpit.  there is a career and a championship mode, as well as races you can make any length.  the driving is well done, the speed feels nice, hitting the curb and accelerating out, all feels better then you'd expect for such a "simple" game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game - I like my racing games but I'm not hardcore so this has the right mix of elements to keep me entertained without having to worry about all the fine details.  The racing itself is great, very much arcadey but that's what I like, and the handling of the cars is just right for me.  The graphics style is also brilliant, takes me back to the 80s and 90s.  Other people have mentioned that the relationships part is a little annoying which I tend to agree with - but that's what you get with New Star games.  Can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fun F1 style game. Always been a big fan of the New Star Games developer with Soccer and Cricket on my phone and when i seen this was getting released i knew I had to get it.Drive style is fun with the added boost makes the racing very interesting. The likeness to names and tracks is refreshing and enjoyable. If you want a simple but fun F1 experience then this is definitely it!Only wish would be for a difficulty setting as it does seem a bit easy at launch but I can imagine this is in the pipeline.Looking forward to more updates in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A really encouraging and promising Early Access debut that works flawlessly on Steam Deck. I've always wanted to play an old school F1 racer that had all the fun of the sport without the picky licensees/FOM/FIA toning anything down. New Star GP has all that in spades including cheeky soundalike drivers, brilliant 80s and 90s inspired cars and decisions about day to day racing which are fun without being too impactful.£14.99 for the Early Access build as it stands is good value and really excited to see how the game evolves from her. Really hoping dev adds more tracks, a more detailed career mode, the ability to actively sabotage other drivers/teams before the race and more types of retirements.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This old-school style arcade racer will appeal to anyone who has fond memories of Virtua Racing or F1 Grand Prix. It is much more advanced than those games of course, adding some strategic elements to it. The graphics, ui and controls are very good, gameplay is fun. The game runs perfectly fine on the SteamDeck too.The developers are in continuous communication with the players, and are open to feedback and comments, which is a big plus always.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for the price, wasn't expecting much initially as it is early access but my lord this game is packed with content that makes the game both immersive and entertaining all while in the signature low-Poly arcade style. If you're on the fence I would definitely buy this game as it will only have more and more content as time goes on. Yes there is probably a few bugs being worked out and a few mechanics needing to be included, but other than that, this game is a hidden gem and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Game does not support my racing wheel. To make it worse, you can't change the bindings on your controller. _childDocuments_.review: Great little fun game, jts just missing a few little touches to justify the price;battery charge via braking - not per lapmore cars on the trackmore laps better event/race management and selectionsonline play manual gear changeit could be the better F1 game, even with the arcade graphics, if it went down the sim management side a little more. other than this, its a fun little racer
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid arcade racer but but it does start to feel repetitive relatively quickly. I only made it through one of the five decades, but I already felt like I'd seen most of what the game has to offer. Still giving it a recommendation because I enjoyed my time with it, but I was hoping for a bit more.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become one of my favourite games to play on the deck. Really nice balance between casual and more intense. Long campaign with decent challenges to get to know the tracks.Fantastic for local multiplayer, can tweak difficulty of AI, tracks and handling/speed of the cars to suit different skill levels. Competing for championships gets tense and addictive soon enough.My only gripes are that there's no online MP, the settings menu is a bit bare, and AI GO SO SLOW IN THE PIT LANE that you can do cheaty overtakes there every time, but what's here is worth full price if you're looking for a more 'fun' f1 experience. Still get that feeling from weaving a few corners together perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Hope you enjoy having a mandatory stick deadzone and twitchy, instant steering snap-back. For a driving game supposedly made to support gamepads, it is not very fun to drive with one... and for some reason this cannot be customized!Developers: not everyone has blown out bad quality gamepads with 2mm stick drift, and some people like to control how the car turns. This should not be something that needs to be said in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: You can't restart or retry races in career mode, but the computer cars may foul or cheat their way to victory.  You're supposed to use a reverse time gimmick that some other company innovated, but it wasn't fun or sensible when it was done then or now. The game also suffers from giving you penalties when you do well.   Congratulations you get +1 this but also you suffer -1 that.   You're just altering not improving your character/team.   IMO It's not as fun or as deep as many of the other reviews suggest.   They do go out of their way to tell you it's early access,  and I'll gladly change my review if they turn this into something more fun, but for now it's a thumbs down.

It's easier to quit through task manager, than searching for the quit button in game. Nothing to customize your controller settings. The Oppents think they are driving formual 1 tanks. And so onImho it's not even worth with 40% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game enough especially if you're a fan of other New Star titles.I've been saying on a keyboard which is more than suitable but you can use a gamepad or apparently it does support a wheel.Physics wise it's very arcadey but satisfying with a whole damage and Tyre wear system. Absolutely love how it feels although Tyre wear should cause less grip earlier on as really they are only unbearable when they are about to blow.Career is basically multiple race weekend with various mini races to get you up to speed with the track and then a proper GP that scores you points in the overall championship.You can upgrade your car through earning cash through out the weekends.The difficulty in the game is something I'm still figuring out, it's not difficult during the first era and I've only just started the 2nd era so it's still to be seen however the dev has said their is an adaptative difficulty so make of that as you will.There is a RIVAL system which is perfect, basically crash into or annoy a driver enough and they will defend and attack VERY hard which definitely makes some races more difficult than they should be but that makes it so much more exciting.Overall I can't wait to see how this progresses but it's an absolute gem at the moment My wishlistDifficulty optionsDurability on partsTeam name customisationMore customisation overallRanked Online multiplayerFor difficulty options I'd love to see these:Damage, so reduced all the way to simulation.AI difficultyReduced and increased part failuresReduced and Increased Tyre wearAnd basically just anything else that could be adjusted

Would be nice to have other options to toggle as well.Fix these things, and it's goat racing game, absolutely perfect for the steam deck. As of now, an absolute slammer on sale, and will surely get better with time.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun arcade racer, but I feel like the AI is just programmed unfairly.  Once you get behind 5 or 6 seconds from a leader it just seems like you cannot catch them no matter what.  Even using the boost which should be a pretty cheap way to get there, but just useless. _childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Looks kinda cute and there's a certain wit to the game, but unfortunately it completely fails at what it wants to be: a racing game. Now, maybe I'm just not getting the 90s games homage, but the least I can ask for is *racing*. All I get though is teabagging. The AI can't seem to pour out a bucket of water, and despite the bulletpointed "adaptive difficulty", that just never changes. I went 13 GP into the career and unless I manage to run out of fuel or hit the inside walls too often on Cote d'Azur, I dump the AI by 15+ seconds at every 6-lap race. I would complain about how the AI doesn't even seem to change the finishing order between themselves a lot, and how I'm not sure why the game doesn't go for 2-car teams and slightly larger grids, but if you're running away that hard it doesn't even matter.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Has a ton of potential, and I bought it for the Virtua Racing vibe... but the controls are too touchy for me unfortunately.  They are like a light switch, either on or off.   But if I see thats fixed at a later date I will come back as the game looks pretty neat.I am saying NO to recommend it... but keep in mind the controls may not bug others... so its up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was something else. Seems all the people into it are more into the team building management part of the game. The actual driving falls short from what I wanted. All I was expecting was something in the ballpark of Virtua Racing but this is extremely basic, more like you generally guide the car around the track and match the corner speed to what is expected. No physics model to speak of at all, arcade or realistic.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but almost everything about it annoys me. There's two good things about this game, for starters it runs great on Linux through proton, but that's more of a nod to proton, and second, the amount of texture detail in the splash screen in contrast to the rest of the game gives me a good chuckle, likely unintentional. Now for the bad, the menus look like it was pulled from a mobile game, the noises your pit crew dude make are stupid(awkward phoned-in voice overs from the devs would at least be endearing), the arcadey nature of the game paired with fuel and tire strategy is perplexing at best, doubly so when there is no manual transmission option, and don't you even think about cutting a corner, because this arcade game is serious business and will slow you down. It sucks that I can't get past all this to experience the effort that was put into the career mode.I went into this expecting Virtua Racing, but with more courses and extra stuff, but what I got was a $30 mobile game. Guess that's what happens when all the reviews I watched were from easily impressed switch-guys who have been stricken with the faux-nostalgia cancer of thinking low poly games equal good.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game's core career mode concept of starting in the past and working your way forward through time to the present day is something I've always wanted from a NASCAR game. F1 is obviously the exact opposite of that, but it's still cool to see someone finally make this type of game. It's also exceptionally rare for an arcade racer to have a proper career mode, so that's doubly cool. I don't really vibe with is the flat textured graphical style, but that's entirely subjective. The multiplayer is a little confusing, my friend and I had a hard time getting a lobby set up, and we didn't know that you have to unlock content in multiplayer because the game doesn't tell you, so we wasted a lot of time trying to figure out how to change the track layouts. We both bought the game mainly for career mode though, so it's not that big of a deal, just something worth mentioning. Oh yeah, the game actually has wheel support too, but there's no FFB, just centering spring. I don't think a game like this needs FFB at all, but I know for a lot of people that's a deal breaker, so there's your heads up.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to learn, fiendishly difficult to master, brutal on the joints in your fingers if you play for long enough with a controller, this is '90s sim/arcade hybrid racing right out of a PS1 game or the old Virtua Racing family of arcade machines. But it doesn't coast on nostalgia, even if you're way too young to remember the '90s there's a lot to love even in the present day. A change of pace from the full-sim F1 or Assetto Corsa experience or a "daily driver" in its own right, there is a LOT to love here. One of the best games I've played in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Retro graphics that look good and work extremely well at high frame rates, and fast paced racing with an addictive career makes this one an instant classic. The game has character and atmosphere that is lacking in many higher budget and higher fidelity racing games, and the player is presented with good racing action with meaningful strategic choices despite the short length of the races. Good stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Quite funny in naming people and circuits. Personally prefer this over the hyperrealism of other racing games. Only annoyance I could find is having to re-do an entire season before progressing to another era in carreer mode. I get that that's sort-of the game, but I'd like the option to just re-do the races I didn't finish in first.It's not really a game for the big race-game fans, but a silly little racing game for those who just enjoy playing a silly little game from time to time. 6/7 would reccommend.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooooo good. Controls rock and the racing is fun. The graphics look awesome but what surprised me was how great the audio is. The sound of the race cars, the track ambience, and the music are superb. The simple car upgrades and the team management is fun too.There’s a few things I wish this game had, but I don’t think it’s getting updates anymore. A replay mode and a photo mode would be nice. Manual gearbox would be fun too. The writing is funny, but it would do well with some additional lines to make it less repetitive. BUT!! It’s really really fun. I am glad I bought this video game :3
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great racing game that captures a lot of the thrill and the amazing moments of F1 racing.Not too arcadey - but certainly not a simulation. As a non-wheel racing gamer, this was just the right mixture.The career mode is fun and it's really enjoyable to go through the decades of F1, even though the "difficulty increase" throughout the decades feels more forced than needed.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent F1 game in the same vein as Virtua Racing from the 90s. If you remember that you'll like this a lot. Especially given how well the computer controlled NPCs are programmed to respond and block, tail, and evade you. Also the little emoticons that pop up above the NPCs gives you a good idea of how they're driving/responding to how the race is going.  Ironically better programmed that a lot of supposed triple A racing games, where not a single one tries to cut you off, almost like they're too embarassed! Whereas here they'll tailgate into corners, touch fenders, and even have spectacular blowouts midway through the race and you have to avoid their cars which have subseequently spun out. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Man.... i gotta say, this game took me completely by surprise. i think i discovered this game from some random youtube video and decided to give this a shot, especially since it was on sale. Let me just say this game wowed me! This genre of retro racers sadly has been cursed with developers not delivering on whats promised or being stuck in development hell or games getting cancelled out right. But this game, im glad saw the light of day. Its polished, its straight to the point, its got depth and inspiration from modern games, its surprisingly lengthy and cars have some levels of customization. This was totally worth every penny and if these devs take on another racing game ill absolutely keep and eye on it, Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun, an engaging combo of retro-esque graphics, recognisable yet legally-distinct-to-real-life tracks, and a surprisingly in-depth career mode - permanent and temporary upgrades, staff management, car wear and damage, and AI that will fight back if you hit them into the wall one too many times through a season. It's a bit on the easier side if you have experience with racing games, but if the microtransaction-riddled hellscape of modern big-budget racing games is getting you down, this is a great game to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is a very good looking and sounding Arcade type racing game. It took me a few hours to get used to the steering and braking using my x box controller. I have just finished 99/99 laps of Naples GP and that gave me lots of experience of the steering and how the car behaves and pitting and fitting new tyre types and re fuel and servicing the shocks and engine and brakes.Also the weather changes and it looks very colourful and lots of gorgeous detail, like the on screen map of the course and the lap time and caution messages to warn me I need to pit and re fuel or change tyres.I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS GAME FOR A ARCADE TYPE RACING EXPERIENCE.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. One of the most fun racing game I've played in years. I enjoy the arcade physics; there is a lot of depth to them.It's a great pick up and play game, you can just hop on for a race or two.They did a great job with the tracks. Each track has a unique feel that carries over from the real life track.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: 55 hours of solid entertainment in the hardest difficulty. Got this game because I had a bad F1 itch and I'm still saving up for good sim racing gear, this definitely scratched that F1 itch. Fuel and Tires make a difference in the outcome, teaches F1 strategy, great physics, reminds me of the Early F1 games that I used to play as a kid. Great game to practice proper racing line, and reflexes as well.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches that Virtua Racing aesthetic itch, with a nice layer of upgrades on top. Also features team social dynamics that are a bit weird, like you get an option of going to the cinema with the commercial manager or the pit boss and one of them is gonna get pissed and might leave the team if too unhappy... weird, but charming and manageable. Very arcade-y handling, but in a good way. Lots of races and different types of events too, not just GPs. Recommended especially for Deck owners, it's a great 15min at a time game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic arcade style F1 game, that has a surprising amount of depth to it. I love this game since I find Codemasters F1 games to be a lot more fun on wheel, and have been looking for racing games that are designed for game pads that still have some level of depth to it. Really love how you can feel the car become sluggish with higher fuel loads, or how you lose grip as tyres or the bodywork degrades. The rival system is also a really awesome addition that makes it so other drivers you bump wheels with on track become more aggressive to you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I like racing games, used to play sims but now I just want to play arcade racing from time to time without a sweat. This game is good for that. It can require some skills and knowledge if you play on pro difficulty. But there is also normal difficulty which is quite simple to beat. There are also rewinds if you are too bad :) Maybe this game is not for tryhards. - Car handling is basic but I like it in general although there is no manual gearing. There is a speed boost that you can use- You can upgrade your car in the career mode- There are also perks that you can also use that can improve slip streams, starts and whatnot.- You doing pits and choosing pit strategy here- Circuits are mini versions of real tracks, so you can recognize some corners- There are quite a lot to do in a career mode (although I'm not used to play for long in one game and I playing short sessions so for some it wouldn't seem a lot maybe).- In the career mode you obviously racing gran prix but without qualification (you are starting last), there is also few more mods like: hot laps, check points, elimination mode that goes before gran prix and will prepare you to it kind of.- There is also hot lap competition with real players I believe but I didn't try it.All in all - nice racing game to chill, have fun and also have some challenges if you will.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is a near perfect blend of arcade racing with a sim mindset. While sparse in some areas, it is well fleshed out and considered in all the right places. 4 player couch co-op is so much fun! Somehow my friends and I were evenly matched despite our varying skills at racing and/or video games. Online multiplayer would beyond the Hot Lap mode would put this game on another level.I would love to know more information about the mechanics of the game be it in the descriptions menu or a wiki. On this note, more flexibility in setting up championship races would also be cool. Things like saved racer profiles, keeping rain on for the whole race, number of cars on track, and a reverse version of both short and long tracks would be great. The ability to modify tire deg. would also be blessed. Sometimes I want to race 20 laps but I don't want to pit 7 times on softs.The campaign menus are a bit un-intuitive but I got used to them. Some more flexible car/helmet customization would also be cool. Think bare-bones version of Forza. All in all this is a fantastic game and will keep you booting it up for some casual fast laps well into the 10's of hours after you've finished the Campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, the graphics are fun, it's light. It's not an intensive game to run, i'm currently running it on my Windows PC, BUT also on my Mac M1 using Crossover. Runs a treat, with my configured 8BitDo controller. I'm only talking career here, I have never played a racing game before in my life, for real. I wanted to pick up something light to have a story mode on. So everything below here is career based. I'm currently 10 hours in, and have just begun the 2000 season (So probably 40%? Through career)The decades as season progression is great, it makes sense. I really like that with the phone call tunes changing and the vehicle chassis changing, fantastic little elements in there.It's easy to pick up and play, there's not much confusing mechanics/buttons to remember. You don't need to know any technical details to play the game. Heck, I didn't and it's great to play. The modes are fun and keep it fresh for each map, in each season. The driver relationships are great, these should be involved in the phone call options. Where you can choose to hang out/do something with one of the other drivers, if you look at F1 motorsports (Real life that is), those drivers are friends and some are rivals. So yeah, introduce them into the phone call options a bit more to build/reduce relationships. Customisation is fun, I wish there was more sponsorship decals really, because F1 cars are plastered in decals. With so many helmet styles in player customisation, probably worth clicking/selecting the helmet styles to open another sub-menu which tiles into squares, with a small thumbnail for each design. There's too many to flick through one at a time and I would've forgotten the number or design I liked without having to scroll through -aaaallll- of them again.Things for the dev to work on so far, the 1990 season, Canada, Quebec track. Exiting the pit lane forces the player to break as it's on 'auto-pilot' until dropping you off to face a barrier. Nah. No. That shouldn't happen, something needs sorting out there. A player shouldn't have to break as a first instinct coming out of the pit. Auto-drive it past the first bend maybe? Because you can't change the track or release them from the pit sooner, that defeats the object of it being like the tracks. Qualifying... I get it's a light-hearted formula' genre game. But starting 10th every time sort of sucks. A perk get's you to 9th but is really useless with other perks being better and boosting at the start to pass 9th anyway. I think there should be some time trial to qualify and then the perk could be remade to +1 starting position to whatever you qualified for. And it could also be random, you could qualify and not know other's times and at the end there could be some % chance that a player beat you. (So you're not always 1st qualifying and 1st winning as that would get boring)Other than that though, i'm seriously loving this game. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: really cool f1 racing with some light management elements. there's staff that provide buffs to race day, on the track or in the active pit lane, or engage with your  sponsors to boost your income. the racing is tight and responsive from the jump and steadily gets faster as you progress through the decades kind of like mario kart CC difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun Arcade F1 Racing game. I love how it gets more difficult after your first season in each decade. The AI becomes more advanced, some AI drivers admire you and wont drive dirty, some AI despise you and will ram you to ruin a podium position. Some AI drivers suddenly get the car upgrades they need and leave you 6 seconds behind with no hopes of catching up. There's tire changing, parts repair, and re-fueling in the pit stops. You have to be wise of when to pit, how much fuel you're carrying, tire conditions, weather. It's all a lot of fun and somewhat immersive after you get your first season out of the way. I would love to see the Devs make a Rally game with the team management from this game and maybe more upgrade/downgrade options for your car, and see their take on snow and muddy roads. I think they would crush it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Hi everyone,Should this game be in your Steam collection ? YES and a thousand times YES !.I haven't encountered any bugs. The graphics are great and the gameplay is incredible, I have a lot of fun beating my own times / playing in career mode or custom championship.This game is well worth the asking price, the quality is impeccable, the cars from 1980 to 2020 and the sound is top too, the circuits are quite detailed, the developers are attentive to updates .There is already a lot of content but I hope that, in the future, there will be even more!  American competition ? karting? Manager mod ? nascar ? more race ? i hope.I'm a complete fan and I admit that I'm probably not very objective, however I really don't have any faults to highlight, it 's just a VERY GOOD game !Buy it for dozens of hours of fun against decent AI and players from around the world !!!Have fun ! sorry for my basic english !
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbridled unmitigated good fun. The racing is not SUPER technical but it's really rewarding. Definitely you don't need to be some sim racing guru to play it and pretty much anyone can pick up a controller and have a great time. But as someone who DOES own a full racing rig and is really into my driving, I also still find it really fun and a blast. Basically, New Star just really know what they're doing and this is definitely worth the money. Would be great to see some online multiplayer in there, too, any maybe some longer endurance racers and definitely some harder AI. But honestly even just for a casual pick and play it's really great.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I must say this all I wanted for a arcade racing game for my steamdeck. Not overly complicated, quick and action packed races, tire wear, pit stops, easy to learn but hard to master. I wish more people would notice this game. As a motorsports fan, I'm actually surprise how long I took to notice this. This game is amazing. Props to the devs, you made something special here,
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: When i booted this game up I really had no idea how damn hooked I'd get.I played the whole first campaign of races and came to 4 hours later realizing this game was probably the most fun i'd had racing in a long time, if not ever.Controls are less sim, more arcade; however theres light sim touches light improved parts, managing the team to get money/pit stop/engineer perks.Cannot recommend enough.Scratches the F1 Itch SO GOOD
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches all the right itches. It's a great racing game without being too far on either end of the Arcade/Simulator spectrum. The cars feel fun to drive and are quite responsive. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, you'll see the headlines between a few races here and there and the content is pretty funny. If you find that EA's F1 is a bit more than you can stomach on the Simulation side, this game tones it down to a digestible level. They start you off with very little complexity and then steadily increase it.I would say i'm surprised that this isn't more popular, but this game doesn't have actual online multiplayer - which, to me, is likely a large contributor to its lesser popularity. However, it does have split-screen PVP which can be hard to find these days, especially for PC games.If you enjoy racing on your own, pick this game up. It's worth every dime.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly pretty great. It is F1 racing for casuals. And with that in mind, it features something that is missing in a lot of other racing games - FUN! I've just been having pure fun playing this. Hats off to the team. I'd love to see them come out with a GT3 racing game just like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the price of entry. Incredibly underrated.My rival started getting madder and madder at me because I bumped him ONCE on the first GP. Fast forward 5 GP's and he challenges me to a 1 on 1. He loses badly. In retribution, he repaints my car the night before the final into a beautiful white/pink which I took 1st in. He finished the season with 0 points.Mustachioed prick lmao. Everyone else on the grid admired me.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are finicky at best. The pit stop could use some reworking. The idea of a boost is fun but takes away from the F1 simulator aspect of things. I like that the AI tries to 'defend' the corner but not much is done for when they're 'attacking' the corner. The pit-stop strategizing seems to have little to no effect or any real benefits for one or the other in the end. Slip-streams shouldn't be a perk but just an overall aspect. Overall, a fun game to pick up, mess around with, and practice racing lines when you're bored, but, not something I can see myself sinking tons of hours on.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Big time recommend from me. It's kind of like a rogue-like f1 arcade racing game. The meta game (game outside of the racing) is cool, the way it sets up different events for each race weekend in career mode is really fun. The racing is a really nice blend of simulation and arcade, and introduces some light f1 racing strategy in a fun way that's easy to learn even if you don't follow the sport. The local split screen is great too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game for F1 fans that just want to zone out and relax. Literally the only 2 complaints I have is that the 2 eras I played had the exact same engine noise, and there is no option for manual shifting (which would be amazing if the devs add it). Otherwise a genuinely fun game for something so simple
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I own Horizon Chase Turbo with Sena. I think it would be the same so I did not need this game.For fun I also own Hotwheels.I must admit that all three games are fine. Even if you own Horizon Chase Turbo, you have in New Star GP (1) the Pit management and (2) much more detailed circuits and in more numbers (than Horizon Chase Turbo) (3) without headhaches (In Horizon you can soon become sick if you play to much due to the game speed on screen). New Star GP remains an arcade game with a mini simulation touch.(4) Another big advantage : this is easily playable without any jerk on an old PC (7 Years old) using an NVidia GTX 1060 6GB RAM, on triple screen configuration (3 x 2560*1440 aka WQHD) using Apple Cinema LED Diplay at 60 Htz refresh rate.(5) More important : this is fun. Do you need a simulation game after a hard day's work ? For my part no. I just need to relax without any hassle.(6) Graphically speaking, this is really top, an arcadish look but this remains pretty to look at.Developpers said it was compatible with a Logitech Wheel. I own a G29, this is not ideal since you cannot set up the wheel in game (OK I could use Logitech profiler but developpers instructions would be welcome...) and you are forced to use the keyboard in menus. Use a gamepad, this is what the game is designed for (keyboard is never needed). WIth Microsoft Elite 2 gamepad, this works flawlessly.Purchase the game for 20 € max, then you make a profitable investment.Sole regrets : a) the game needs an update since the game asks you to use A button instead of X button in menus, so it is not 100% perfect.b) the impossibility to select a circuit and to do a race out of career mode (in solo mode, unless I have missed something). You need to enter career mode to play it but once done, this is over you cannot start again, you have to play the 9 other races of the season..., only then the circuit becomes playable again in solo mode.c) The rewind mode is not clear even with a pad (you click on a button for Rewind, then you have toi use the mouse to go back exactly where you wanted). I would have preferred a button to restart a race, period.But this is a funny game which will bring you fun even on low end hardware (even if a 7 years old PC is not totally obsolete).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixture of elements that work better as the sum of their parts. Each of the aspects of the game is greatly simplified, but that allows for a fun and engaging experiecing that you can pick up for a little while or for a long sitting. In essence, in this game you act as the manager of a F1 team and also as their driver, so yuo execute everything: from upgrades to the car, to the overtakes on track. But since none of it is really complex, what sounds complicated in turn is very easy and fun.I love that you can trash talk other drivers and then they will mad with you and try to crash you (Nigel Mansgwen who?), or you can have a respectable rivarly with them. I also love that with the upgrades you do feel the car being faster and faster throughout the season, which also adds a bit of difficulty spike.Perhaps the aspect I like the least about the game is the driving. It's fun and arcadey but I almost never feel in danger during the races. The opponents are very slow, and I can end up winning a GP by 20 seconds. Perhaps this was my fault for choosing the normal difficulty rather than the Pro one, so developers should add the option to change difficulty once you start the carreer mode!!!All in all a fun game that's perfect on the Steam Deck (and I will probably get it for my phone as well lol)
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to racing games, I mostly play management/sim style but have played a few where you are driver like this (Circuit Superstars and Project Cars come to mind).  With that in mind, I'm not judging the management/development part of this game since it's obviously very simple in an arcade driving game like this.The steering is super easy which I appreciate, and even on the harder mode it's pretty easy to do well.  The game looks okay, and if you're looking for an arcade-y open-wheel racing game, you could certainly do worse.  Don't expect much depth, and do expect arcade-style action (there is a boost button and a rewind button), but I've had some fun with it.  This will probably be a steam-deck game for me for short plays, but if you like arcade racers then it's worth a shot (preferably on sale - I got for $17.99 which feels just a bit high until I think about how that wouldn't buy a McDonalds meal, and then it seems like a fair price :-P).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hell of a lot of fun and I enjoyed playing this - this is my first time with the game and true first impressions (  ).Glad I brought this and if you like Virtua Racing, you are going to love this on the PC.Controls are really good, game is really good and it have a lovely mode that eases you into how it works with the tutorial.My video does not show the current patch that released, it was recorded a day or so before that.
