_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: its fun, the controls are tight and upgrading/customizing your car is fun despite lacking depth. supposedly there's adaptive difficulty as you play through the career but im not seeing any improvement from the ai.after three races, i stopped doing the events and racing the track blind. im still blasting everyone. i dont think the ai even uses boost.so .. knowing you're gunna win every single race with little to zero resistance makes this a no from me. even the neat features like dynamic events and perks and stuff kind of fall flat, they're not as cool as they sound.id keep this game for 9.99 or even 14.99 but i paid 17.99 on sale and im considering refunding it, it's definitely not worth the full 29.99
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: You should know that by being a racing driver you are under risk all the time. Being a racing driver means you are racing with other people and if you no longer go for a gap that exists you are no longer a racing driver because we are competing, we are competing to win and the main motivation to all of us is to compete for the victory, it is not to conserve for a fifth or sixth place.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this a try on the strength of the endearing retro visual style, and found a deeper open-wheel racing game than I expected, while being thoroughly accessible. Altogether, a breath of fresh air in the circuit racing genre.The driving, set to some great original music, feels good and definitely leans toward arcade racing. For instance, while real-world F1 cars have a Kinetic Energy Recovery System that provides a short-duration burst of power, the equivalent here works much more like your typical boost button. There is a racing line displayed to guide the player. And while crashes will damage the car and impact performance, they're far more forgiving than in the really diehard racing simulations.But what surprised me is how, without any of it seeming like a chore, the game works in details like fueling, tire, and pitting strategy. And racing team management, which is accomplished with a very intuitive menu interface. Feeling, even to someone like me who has never engaged with a racing team management sim, just like something you naturally do between races.At the moment, I'm dominating the early GP races in the career mode, which spans from the 1980s to the 2000s and from what I've read, may be expanded further. While I've largely been relying on an aggressive one-pit strategy, the game has already cautioned me that the difficulty is adaptive, so the better I perform, the more competitive other teams will get on the track and in the paddock. Reflecting rather well the automotive arms race that is classic F1 racing.This also means that, quite surprisingly, I find myself investing more in my crew and less in upgrades to the car. Building a team to last, rather than squeezing every last drop of performance out of the car to pad out my margin of victory. Which is very much not what I expected going in. But it was a pleasant surprise to find such depth in a game with these lovely retro arcade visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely banging game. I bought this because of the positive reviews on a whim and was not disappointed. I love the arcadey physics but with pit stops, fuel loads, tyre wear and all that it still gives the feeling and relative flow of an F1 race. The championship mode is great.The tracks are incredible, despite being unique they are still excellent representations of the actual tracks, with certain corners, whole sectors, or even just a vibe being so accurate to the game. And playing at my home track you could really see the attention to detail in the tracks.I hope this game gets the support it deserves, I can see this game and these devs building a strong community. Hopefully there is plenty more to come out of this game and these devs!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For the same price as Le Mans Ultimate, you get a proper, fun game. Which LMU isn't. Seriously though, despite it's unashamedly arcade style, New Star GP has everything that should be included in 'real' sims: Full Career mode, hotlaps with leaderboards, and individual championships.Then there's the management side: hiring and firing staff, and trying to keep them happy (an impossible task), press conferences and full customisation of cars. The rivalry idea is fun: if you trash talk an opponent in the press conference, or run them off the road, they'll come after you in a big way. All in all, a great title that every sim could learn from.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: having loads of fun with this. great little f1 game that simulates all the aspects of that type of racing, from crew management to sponsorship to pitstops in an arcadey and quick, non time consuming way (eg: short ~6 lap races but the tires wear out in only a couple laps)my one major gripe to the devs: make the dials and mirrors in work in cab view!!!!!super lightweight on memory and graphics as well so great for low budget low spec which i appreciate greatly
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic racing game. The art style is fun and the game's atmosphere is really upbeat thanks to the soundtrack. The overall experience with a controller is pretty flawless. I am using a Logitech F710 wireless.The game play is simple, gas, brake, go. FYI, there is currently no manual transmission option as this was designed as an arcade racer. I know, arcade racers do sport MT but, that where this game is and seems like it will stay. I'm good with that, if I want more realism i can play one of the racing sim games I have. Where this game becomes more is in the perks you select for your crew, managing your winnings to upgrade your car and be prepared for random events that pop up. Pit strategy also plays a role. Will you select hard or soft tires? How well can you handle your car on a full tank? Handling deteriorates with a heavier fuel load. Also, check the weather before a race, is that rain on the horizon? When should you pit to switch to wet tires? Also, can you hit the gas at the right moment to have a perfect start off the grid?If you are looking for a fun and simple F1 racing game, this is the one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, everything I want in a retro racing game.  It plays and feels like a 1980's racer game but is so much better with career mode, upgrades and smother but retro graphics.I absolutely love it.  I am half way through the first season in the career mode.  I can't say enough about how awesome it is.  I have only played on arcade settings and don't know if I care to try realistic since arcade is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game all round. Makes you feel like Ayrton Senna!Nice meta game with fast pace chunks of progression and fun little decisions to make between events. Very nice graphics, giving that proper Virtua Racing vibe through and through. Polished and quick loading so the action never lets up. Plays wonderfully on the Steam Deck too. It’s very arcadey (obviously) but you still need to drive it properly, just that it’s quite forgiving but none the less satisfying for it. The complexity is pitched perfectly for the aim of the atmosphere of the game, with enough depth and nuance to the handling and the races without being frustrating or feeling dumbed down. Very nicely done. Nice selection of events to mix it up (with changing weather + puddles that you need to adapt your strategy and driving to, as well as look after your tyres and consider the best time to use the KERS boost) and confidently presented overall. Above all, it’s just plain FUN and I’m excited to progress through the next years in the game and see how it pans out. I have not even arrived at “Monaco” yet in the first year (and there is TONS more content here to explore) but I felt completed enough to write this review, so it must be good!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I want to refund this game so I can buy it back at full price because they deserve my money.  After a few hours of this (and 36 seasons Retro Bowl) I don't know if New Star Games gets me, or just gets gaming in general.  They definitely hit that sweet spot of an easy learning curve, but enough depth to keep you coming back.  It's hard to put your finger on exactly what New Star does so well, but there's something fundamental that they understand about what makes games fun that so many companies miss.  It's that magic that Nintendo captured during the Wii era:  yes, you can make phenomenally good games that are wildly technologically inferior to everything else out there.  I absolutely hate the low-poly aesthetic of the mid-90's graphics, but somehow I don't even notice it when I'm playing, because it just fits.  Everything about the game is polished and considered.  Every element was clearly chosen and created by people who actually play games, not a bunch of boardroom clowns with marketing degrees.  I haven't played EA's F1 (the most common comparison), but I'd way rather be playing this than Forza.  Sure, Forza wins the beauty contest.  Hundreds of cars...but how many are actually enjoyable to drive?  Hundreds of tracks...how many are actually fun to race on?  And don't get me started on the train wreck of a menu system, seasons (welp, it's winter again, guess I'll have to wait till next week to play), broken physics, and awful grinding.  I guess the moral of the story is that something simple, done correctly, is vastly superior to something complex, but done poorly.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game!After hundreds of hours in the official F1 games, as well as Motorsport Manager and its mobile variants, I think I finally found a new kick. Sure, New Star GP is no simulation but it’s still a lot of fun. The game combines driving with managing your own F1 Team through the decades. You start in the 80s and work your way up to the modern era of F1. The driving is not very challenging but mistakes are punished, so it’s quite appealing still and can lead to occasionally exciting races. The AI is not helping sometimes, pulling unforseeable (and also quite illegal) moves but all in all the racing is fun. The other part is the management aspect, which you could describe as F1 Manager LIGHT. It’s not very deep but you can I.e. determine strategies, upgrade your aero, engine, suspension, or even do occasional publicity stunts with the help of your public relations manager. While we are at the point of crew members, they can provide the team with helpful perks, that make your racing easier or earn you more money after a victory. All in all this is a really fun game, that will surely keep me playing for the next 20-50 hours. It’s also very light on resource consumption, so it can run several hours on the steam deck. Tl;dr:Can recommend this for every arcade racing and gp team management fan.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it a lot so far, there are not many good arcade racers out there now and this is a good one. I like the aggressive AI and the general feel of the game gives me nostalgic flashbacks to the early Micropose Grand Prix series, which is no bad thing. I'm only two hours in and although I'm enjoying the game, a full price of £24.99 I do wonder if it is priced about £5 too high. I bought it on offer at £14.99 and at that money it is definitely fair.Improvements on my wish list are, in the following order: 1) Online multiplayer 2) Bigger grid sizes in a race/bigger circuits to accommodate them.   3) More intelligent/gambles from AI on strategy.  4) The ability to change the names of teams and drivers
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Really really fun! Delivers on being a retro styled arcade racer with a lot more depth than I was expecting. The more I play the more I'm sold on the game.If i had to have a gripe it would be for more cosmetic customization for the cars in a future update (like sponsorship text color or helmet colors). Would also love to change difficulty during the career mode, I realized after one season I needed to switch to the higher difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Arent the devs of Wreckfest going to be upset that these devs stole the AI programming?Seriously though, its a fun update on a retro style arcade racer. Enough depth to the in-between-race choices to keep you engaged and the races can become chaotic enough to make you want to get back to the in-between stuff before you tear your hair out in frustration over the ludicrous AI shenanigans. Balanced...as all things should be.Its fun having decades of cars that actually feel dynamic in their era, 80s feel planted but a bit slow, 90s ultra-fast and slightly unwieldy in a fun way, etc.Will it satisfy hardcore sim racers? Shut up, nerd. Pick up a controller and embrace this arcady break from soul crushing realism and actually have some fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Love when games balance "sim" aspects into an arcade base, this game brings that together with an entertaining career mode where you manage your team and sometimes watch chaos ensue as well a custom championship mode for replay value afterwards. Basically you can kick back after a long day but still feel like you are actually racing, nice presentation, has some pit strategy mixed in, and best of all it's funny. Full recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I had been looking for a good racing game for a long time and there just weren't that many good options (imo) until this one came out earlier this year. It is exactly what I was looking for and been one of the games I pick up to play whether I have 30  minutes, or a few hours. The racing is fun, and goes to show that you don't need an exact replica of real life to get the excitement of a good race. It's fairly arcadey, so if you're more into the sim aspect, it's probably not for you, but there is a surprising amount of depth in the main game mode, and with only 6 laps per GP, it makes you want to do just one more race. Highly recommend - have not found a game by this dev that I do not like yet.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Very good arcade F1 career game. In career you go through 80s cars, then 90s and all the way to 2020. There's a multiplayer race option but it's only local or with Remote Play Together.The races are quick and the gameplay is very simple and sometimes silly - in a good way. You will be able to recognize all the tracks and they have multiple layouts. To upgrade your car you not only need to do the GPs but also side events. For example an elimination race, checkpoints time trial, reverse track race, etc.All in all I would recommend this. Plays very well also on Steam Deck. For $30 it is a bit steep. I got it for $18 and I'd say it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a refreshing game, it has a surprising amount of depth to the gameplay. Most importantly though, it's never boring.I love all the on track action, the short races with pit stops, the fact that tire temps, wear, and fuel weight is simulated.There is just so much packed into this game, worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Believe the hype from the reviews, this game is insanely fun. Think the arcade thrill of Virtua Racing with a great campaign mode that lets you upgrade your car, manage crew, unlocking perks, weather such as rain, and pit choices such as tire and fuel strategy. Multiple camera options is the cherry on top. Definitely worth a purchase. With that said, be prepared for the difficulty to rise considerably as you progress further.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game It's already one of my favorite racing games of all time. It's EXACTLY what I was looking for in an Arcade Racing game. A surprisingly good amount of depth in a fun arcade racer package, nuanced with some realistic sim-style characteristics. The career mode is great with progression through different eras and building rivalries with the AI characters (who have comically similar names to real life F1 icons), and there is a nice focus on car development and team management to boot too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is more than just a racing game, it's a celebration and a heartfelt tribute to the world of Formula 1. It's clear that the developers are fans themselves, and their love for the sport is evident in every aspect of the game. It's the game F1 fans deserve, and it's an absolute joy to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, defnitely recommend. However for the devs just a couple things to make it a bit better. Unfortunately right now there is no manual gearbox so a setting for that would be great. There is also no option to change the bindings for controller. Fixing those two things I believe would make it pretty much a perfect game.Thank you New Star for never failing us xoxo
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Amazing Idea. The cars and gameplay are insteresting and a lot of good Ideas. But pleeaase... seriously? reverse races? It´s a anti-pattern for racing games, even arcades. Worse on a f1 one... is a signal that's something is wrong. You got one race more of gameplay time for track... in a incredible horrible event, with the AI hitting you all the time, bad pit entrances and exits and you even won't give me 100% of the credits for the race if I use flashback? Now if the AI hits me in a corner that surely was not made to be run in that direction in the last lap I need to restart the entire thing. Great. Let´s do it like 10 times, shaw we? Every...time... It became the type of event it´s not fun to do. I'm a completionist but I'm gonna start skipping those or I will stop playing the game.And the crew is like the most needy and tiresome ever. Play it for laughs then if you must but in the way it is now is just bad. It´s better than before, but surely it has space to improvments. Like events and bonuses. Not only well paid adults in a winning team crying and leaving all the time.This game is too good to have such idiotic problems. Please Devs, keep the development. Would love to have manual shift for the gears too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Something strange happens in this game: it happens that you might like rough steering.I asked for a refund twice because the steering didn't convince me and today I repurchased it for the second time (bought for the third time) and I am convinced that this steering is perfect in this game. I never thought I would like On/Off steering.I never even thought I would like turbo in a game.No element of this game was placed by chance, everything comes together beautifully. Nothing is out of place.Everything is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little arcade F1 racer with suprisingly good handling and depth. The main things i like about it:- presentation.- sound design.- how the career mode is set up.- you can upgrade your cars and the upgrades are noticable.The main things i dislike:- nemesis system isnt implemented in a fun way.- perk system is due for a qol fix, its kinda unclear how it works at first.- the addition of a perk that allows GP restarts is a serious negative point for me, this takes away from the immersion in a big way, i really hate it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fun racing & management game with just enough simulation elements to make it immersive and challenging. One thing I've always loved about New Star Games is their approach to teaching new players: the tutorial is built into the game so you can learn as you go. No need to read walls of text or complete a separate tutorial "mission" beforehand.At $30 it's not the cheapest game, but it's worth it. Many different tracks and racing eras to explore (even though I'm mainly a fan of the 90s - yes, I'm getting old).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Pretty good, Very grippy physics. Pit strategy is kinda interesting but feels extremely rigid as in 99% of the time it's pit on laps 2 and 4 or once on lap 3, It's almost never a good idea to try to push an extra lap. I feel like it would be a bit more interesting if there were 7 laps and there was a bit more pit strategy flexibility maybe adding medium tire compound would help. Tracks are based on real life tracks which I found charming.I don't think it's perfect but it's a very solid and unique arcade racer with light management aspects which is quite enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY fun. I like how you progress through the eras. I like how  its realistic, but has some details that arent. The only thing that I dont like is that if you go off the track, all your speed is gone. You can go from 150 to 75 in a second. This also happens when you are fighting someone and you barley dip a tire in the grass. But, overall, the game is very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome hommage to Formula 1 - you feel how much love has been put into this game, I really love it! The tracks are so greatly designed, that you know very fast which original track it should be. Same for the fake drivers - very funny! :)The only thing I hope to be worked on is the difficulty. Started with the normal difficulty, the first season was way too easy. Won every race by more than 20 seconds. Hoped that the second season gets more difficult, but same for the first race. So I started a new career in the pro mode and well, it's not that harder. Winning is pretty easy, now with around 5 to 10 seconds in front. It still makes a lot of fun to me, but would be greater if the races were more challenging, as the rest of the game is soo great!Some little bugs / general things:- KI drivers are breaking / slowing down for the pit entrance, where I can simply go full speed into the box. This is one big problem regarding the easiness of the game I guess, because every pit stop you can save a lot of time against the KI- Saw some cars crashing in the box in rainy conditions- Tyres: Wet tyres in dry conditions didn't feel like a time loss at all. Of course this is an arcade game, but I think the tyres in general could influence the cars behaviour more
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fun retro looking arcade F1 racing game that looks simple on the surface but has some deeper mechanics that you wouldn't expect. Such as damage, fuel weight, a nemesis/rival system, crew choices, random events during the seasons, interactive pit stops, wear on parts other than just the tires, and dynamic weather. It's not perfect, but I can't think of anything that it's "bad" at.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of Super Monaco GP on the Megadrive and also F1 Exhaust Heat on the SNES. Loving this game, very fun to just pick up and play and very reminiscent of arcade racers of old. Highly recommended. It could do with a bit more pace though and a sense of more speed, without boost, the cars can feel quite slow, but the visuals are just so awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice arcade racing game with an unexpected depth in racing and strategy. Its more fun to play than most auf the current racing games with a good humor.Its still in development and im excited for the upcoming addations. I hope there will be some more mechanics for racing, the career and more general content.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Played this one at the Gameforce Indie-boot and immediately purchased it afterwards!It not only brings back the feeling of the original Grand Prix 2 all the way from '96 but also incorporates today's features like events, upgrades, crew interaction etc.Enjoying the Early Access and looking forward to what's next to come!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game does so many things right. I love the graphics. They take me right back to the 90's arcades when I played Virtua Racing and Daytona USA. Driving is great. You can upgrade your car. Career mode is awesome. There's just enough sim (fuel, tires, pitting) to feel like real Formula 1/2/4 without taking away from the arcade aesthetic or gameplay. The game is so polished I can't even tell it's early access.My one gripe is my comms chief is mad at me and about to quit the team because I didn't take her to the movies, and honestly I'm not sure what that has to do with racing.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, loving it so far. Great mix of retro arcade style racing plus management. Loving the graphics styling and the racing is really fun. Really easy to pick up for short periods which I love as I often don’t have time to game for long periods. Can’t wait for the future updates but even now it’s well worth the purchase
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Can't wait to see the finished product! Even in just the first 2 playable series this game is addicting fun. Brings a fresh arcade feel to open wheel racers while still having rpg levels of depth that you'd see in main line titles. This game is woefully underrated and is easily one of the best games I've played all year
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, it is a fun little arcade racer to enjoy alone or with friends.The artstyle is perfect, a good resemblance to the old arcade racers on the arcade machines.The car handling is clean and intuitive, there is a good weight to the cars.Damage model is simple but does the job.Pit Stops were implemented well with a minigame.There is a really big track selection with manyy different layouts of many iconic racetracks.The career mode is better than the one on the EA F1-Games, ngl.Overall it is an already great game with good ideas and great potential. The roadmap looks really promising.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Its a really fun and cute arcade F1 game and i´m excited to see whats to come but holy *#%& the ai is annoying its so aggressive a lion in heat wouldn't come to close to it they just ram you of the course and cut in front of you where you cant do anything except crash they really need to implement a penalty  system.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Works best on controller, full support for a xbox one controller. Also, lower your sensitivity settings for steering.Fun game, it is challenging, you have to watch both fuel and tires, and AI is really defensive.Reccomend to play it in cockpit mode.It feels like a sipler version of the F1 games, it even has some team managing involved.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For those with a craving for racing games that can balance Arcade with a little bit of simulation, I would highly recommend this game. If you grew up playing Virtua On this game will hit just the spot. So with the ambitious Roadmap they have ahead it only makes me happy that I've found this game and I'm more than glad with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Add replays!  Night time races with lights would be cool too.  Option to go back and change you helmet/looks. More paint options would be more fun too, car numbers, etc. Problem:  I got a DNF on Adriatic Sea GP and it won't let me try again. Awesome game! Hope to see lots of add-ons n updates! The pits makes it fun. Glad I decided to get it! Hope to see some improvements tho
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, good fun.  Very much like the retro arcade race games of the late 90s and early 2000s but with slightly updated graphics.  Thats not to say it looks or feels old, it just replicates it well.  Race physics and AI are fun and challenging too.   Enough depth to make it the career mode fun without being overly detailed and somewhat tiresome like the F1 games.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun Racer with way more depth than expected. Pit Tactics are especially fun.The Crew Management Part is the one like the least so far, as it is really hard to keep the mood up, imho the Team should be happy when i win race after race and not moan about perks not being used. But we'll see, we are in early access after all.Coloring the car and the race tracks changing over the time periods is also fun!Also the game runns on every potatoe that can run unity, nice!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Love the thing to bits. The game is a casual version of the codemasters F1 games, with a carrer mode, letting you upgrade your car as the season goes along.It's just short races of 6 laps, but it garantees you can pick up and play for a bit and still do 2 or 3 races.The AI is surprisingly decent. They try to close the door when you approach to make an overtake and they actually give you room once you're side by side with them, so it's already better than the F1 games in that department.It's on the easy side of things, even if you choose the pro difficulty the AI drivers will have little chance if you're just an average racing game player, but I wouldn't increase the difficulty too much. Love the artstyle, it remind me of that old arcade game Virtua Racing. I wish it had some special long duration event, like LeMans or Indy500.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: As a 90's kid growing up watching the likes of Senna, Prostell, and Mansell on the TV and pretending (poorly) to be them on Pole Position, Final Lap, and finally Virtua Racing at the arcade, I'm blown away by New Star GP and the work that's been done with the early access version.The presentation is great as well as the gameplay, but it's the attention to detail that sets this one apart in my book. One can tell the cars and tracks that inspired what's in the game, but the team has taken care to tweak things for entertainment value (ie, no super long flat out straights yet maintaining the look and feel of circuits) and added in touches between races to keep things interesting in team building decisions the New Star team is known for. All my gripes are small and inconsequential, but he's a couple to put on the back burner- unless I've missed it, can you edit your helmet and appearance after the initial setup?  My bald guy needs a cap :)- Could there be another way to distinguish tire compounds other than the pirelli style bands for the 80's and 90's cars?  Maybe white vs. yellow lettering?  Just picking nits :)Beyond that, really looking forward to the next updates
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I started following this game when it was first teased in the Retro Bowl and Retro Goal subreddits, and I'm pretty pleased that I did. It's a good game at release and I think if it wanted to, it has a solid base of game play mechanics to implement a manager mode or even be more realistic in some of its driving. Highly recommend if you just want to chill and race. A few cons that I have noticed so far:I'm not a racing guru, and I haven't consistently played a racing game in years, but I felt the races were easy once you made it past the pack even if you haven't upgraded your car or used your rewinds. The battles with other drivers were fun during the few short minutes you stay racing with them.it is *really* difficult to break your car, I tried a few times and I couldn't get it into the red or break any of my parts. I also noticed that even if you run out of fuel, I was able to still complete an entire lap going at 60 MPH. I could stop entirely and then start accelerating again, but 60 MPH was the cap until I refueled. Another note: it'd be helpful to know how much fuel = 1 lap when fueling.Due to the graphic design of the game I also kind of find it hard to see the end of a road just due to the textures, and this also makes spotting the pitting lane a pain sometimes. These problems are exemplified when you use the driver POV camera.Pros:Cool driver events and relations. Keep your team happy or risk having someone leave and their perks with them, the random events that can improve relations or give you funds, just the all around flavor of them even if it's an event that gives you nothing, it's pretty cool.The idea of managing your relationship with other drivers is still kinda barebones and isn't like the old NASCAR games just yet, but I was able to pretty clearly notice when a driver liked me or not -- if they liked me I could pass easily and if they didn't I'd have to undercut them because they were always blocking my path. It's fun. Also, seeing driver events such as their gearbox breaking down mid-race or seeing news about a certain driver not being able to have topspeed potential due to engine problems before the race was AWESOME.The overall racing gameplay is solid, again I'm not a racing guy so I don't have a steering wheel or anything like that but using my dualshock 4 everything felt responsive and I was pretty happy with it overall.The Eras is a great idea and moving from the 80s to 90s was awesome.What you pay for this game is pretty much worth it, especially with this dev team and their tendency to expand their games past their original goals once completed.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is the F1 97 Arcade Mode with beautiful and highly detailed retro graphics, an excellent soundtrack, accessible high grip downforce driven gameplay that is superb for a 1980s-2010s Formula One/Indycar arcade title.Era driven seasons with different car specs and tracks, a wide variety of parody race drivers with their own personalities, likes, dislikes, and skill levels. Your crew similarly has the need to feel wanted and appreciated, and will resign if they feel like they are being mistreated. Wide selection of upgrades for your car and some team buffs, some light management features with interviews and team decisions to make. Dynamic and randomised weather makes pit stop strategies a critical element of every race, which could make or break your chance for the top of the podium. Some AI issues right now with rivals overly willing to turbo punt you off the track, and often your backstage choices or lack of can mess up your team management, but this should be addressed in time.Excellent wear and tear damage model with everything from your suspension and brakes to gearbox and spoilers that will degrade as a race goes on, especially if you hit too much of a curb or into the gravel. Doesn't feel like crashes harm you that much mechanically, only making the punting rivals even more annoying as they can get away with just a slight loss of speed, while you are spinning through the gravel trap and getting your car components worn down extra fast.Fantastic feel, tracks based on real world counterparts, and a surprising amount of depth for a arcade based pad racer. More games should be this accessible while still having this amount of complexity to them. Some humour, great music, beautiful scenery and lots going on during a race, really makes the stadiums feel alive.One of the courses looks a bit phallic, so there is that, too.Is it perfect? No.Is it incredible? YES. YES. ALL THE YES.8 Green Starting Lights/10 Grid spots.Vroom.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For those looking for a faithful low wattage (for steam deck folk) homage to classic F1 racing, this looks to be the one! Seems to have quite a few features on this day 1 review, with visible tire degradation, dynamic weather with water pooling, and even tire strategy (though no mediums!).The tracks are - um - inspired by real life tracks, with quite a few to chose from, though I've not unlocked them all. Ditto for the cars, which are grouped by decade. While I've not played this on my wheel, it's a beauty on the steam deck! I'll match this one up with any recent licensed option.One minor issue, love it or hate it, there seems to be annoying orange smoke popping up at various spots on the track.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Verry cool Game i love it. <3things that i miss is a difficulty setting because at the beginning it´s a bit easy.i like this Rivalry feature and the NPCs (KI) are verry agressiv. its not so easy to overtake. i miss this in the real F1 game.all in all a nice little game for F1 fans. a bit like the old retro F1 games, but better. :D 10/10 i recommend<3
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review:
NEW STAR GP is the arcade racing game where every decision counts - on and off the track!

You take control of your own motorsport team, guide your team's technological development, plan your race strategy, take the wheel, and drive to victory!

With a simple but deep gameplay experience and appealing retro visuals, NEW STAR GP puts you in the driving seat for every twist and turn as you manage and race your team through decades of racing, from the 1980s all the way to the present day!

name: Halls of Torment
detailed_description: Halls of Torment is a horde survival game with a pre-rendered retro look reminiscent of RPGs from the late 90s. Choose one of many hero characters and descend into the deadly Halls of Torment. Fight unholy horrors from beyond and survive wave after wave of enemies until you face one of the tormented Lords. Strengthen your hero with character traits, abilities, and items. Create a new powerful build during each run. Explore various underground expanses and find new powerful items that enable you to venture even deeper into the abyss. Features Quick and casual 30 minute runs Old school pre-rendered art style Quest-based meta progression Large selection of diverse abilities, traits, and items, all enabling you to create interesting synergies Diverse bosses featuring unique mechanics and attack patterns Several distinct characters allowing for many different play styles Unlock and explore multiple interesting and challenging underground worlds Unique items can be sent up to the overworld and used to customize future runs Craft magical tinctures to direct fate in your favor Unlock the power of each class and combine them with your chosen character Defeat the Lords of the underworld and explore infinite growth Find rare item variants to further improve your builds Put your strategies to the test in the late game against the unbeatable Shrine of Torment Full Content List 6 stages with unique environments 11 playable characters & character marks 25 blessings that make you stronger for each run 60 unique items to retrieve and unlock 240 higher rarity item variants 74 abilities and ability upgrades 30 artifacts to customize your game experience 35+ unique bosses 70+ unique monsters 500 quests to complete 1000+ traits that upgrade characters and abilities

_childDocuments_.review: Though this is marked as Verified on the Steam Deck everything is super tiny.  Make sure you turn off the "pixelate text" option (I don't know why that's on by default, it makes the text even harder to read).  There aren't any options to scale up UI elements, text, or gameplay graphics.  Unfortunately I have to mark this not recommended unless this gets fixed for the Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent Survivors-style game that is both fun and different enough from the other main contenders in this sub-genre to warrant inclusion in your library. There is an audio issue if you have a Scarlett USB interface, but then again, the Scarlett interfaces seem to have issues with quite a few different programs these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what people are calling this sort of game now, but whatever the genre term is, it's easily the best "one of those" I've played so far. It's perfectly tuned and consistently engaging, with a bunch of unique mechanics that really go above and beyond the traditional grind incentives. I love the aesthetic and all the deliberately lo-fi animations and design elements. There's a surprising amount of content here for an early access game - or for a game that costs five bucks, which is crazy! I would easily have paid twice as much for it, no question. I'm having a great time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game and I've enjoyed my hours with it. Only complaints are the pacing of development and how specific some quests are. This is the kind of game that yearns for newer content even if it takes spiritual inspiration from games where running the same map is the norm.Quests can be a bit annoying because the majority of them are just things you unlock by playing, but there are a few you need to specifically plan for and go out of your way. I'm not the most fond of that.These are extremely minor complaints, though. So yes, a definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Torment of TimeFor the price and its EA status I really want to recommend this game but I feel I just can't, the concept is great but there is alot here regarding game design which likely wont change on 1.0 release that is on a spectrum from boring to bad.I've played many of these type of games and recently played death must die which sadly does everything better than this game from its pace to its abilities and experimentation. Its unfortunate as I do love this games tone but even that is badly done the graphics when you actually play the game in person are very bad. I get that its supposed to be nostalgic old school but it more feels like a game with a blurry filter that makes a game that has reruns in it very annoying to play. Also the animations on the sprites are total trash and this is coming from me with a degree in animation, the sorc hand animation to fire lighting is horrifically bad.The pacing of the game regarding the choice to make runs 30 minutes feels far too long it becomes boring and tedious especially given there are zero movement abilities. This is another aspect that I don't think is justifiable the game strongly feels like a simple roll or dodge is deeply missing. In other games you don't realise how much having something like that really makes you feel like you are controlling the character and have strong player agency.Once in the game I just really don't enjoy the gameplay loop it feels like no matter what the enemies are you just circle around managing your waves in a very dull manner. Most of the enemies feel like boring or annoying creatures and even the bosses are super forgettable.Something very disappointing to me even having unlocked 7 characters is how similar they all feel given how little differences and abilities there are in the game. The abilities are super disappointing like this is probably the games biggest mistake why the fk are there not more abilities ??? why are alot of abilities on the same characters why they dont fit the archtype at all... you wouldnt find this kind of thing in an old school game either. The items system is 0/10 garbage feels tacked on at the last second never do you get an item and think wow amazing its just a chore you deal with to get stronger and survive more.Overall this game makes you feel like your progressing towards something but you never actually do get that feeling you just get more disappointment for many of the above reasons and more. This company needs to seriously change this games design philosophy and throw away any barriers they have towards radical change.-Add way more (100s) abilities that can only be used by certain classes-Add at least 1 movement tech for each character-Change enemy movement-Redo the entire item system-Add a weapon system that gives each character at least 3 choices-Unlock all characters from the start-Change timer to 20 minutes-Buff the quality and readability of the graphics-Redo all bosses and keep the mobs out of their fightsIf you do all this it will be a great game added to the genre if not its not only will it stay a disappointment no one is going to grind through the hell of this game in currently its asking way to much for far to little reward via fun and fun is ultimately what we are all here for.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'm going to change my review. I (mostly) recommend the game now.I went back and played some more and got into it all over again. The problem I had before was that I went to the new content and just got destroyed. I felt in control before but now I was a newb. But I tried out the Agony system and I like it. I see the logic behind some of the changes and can see where they're going. It still feels really fun in the first two acts.The difficulty does ramp up too quickly though. When you die to swarms of enemies that have too much health it feels bad. Even if you think you're not making any mistakes, you will die to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But there's too much good here to leave this a bad review.I'll leave my old review here for transparency...____Two days ago I was forming my glowing review of this game in my head. It was better than VS I was to declare, mainly because it was harder and required more skill, and the enemies were more varied, 'meaty', and fun to kill. After the latest patch those words don't fit anymore. There are two new classes and a new zone introduced, but also new bugs. And the game moved from 'hard' to 'frustrating'. Enemies are bullet sponges, and exp gain has been nerfed.The devs seem to have misunderstood their own game. Players do not want a dark souls-like challenge requiring patience and persistence to complete. We (or at least I) want to gain power, kill lots of stuff, and make steady progress at unlocking all the goodies. I want to have fun. This is a passing dalliance, not a new part of my life. Give me a 20-30 hour ride to 80% completion and wake me up when you have DLC. Which I will buy. I have no doubt the devs will reconsider their changes, but until then I have to give this a bad review.

_childDocuments_.review: Combine Diablo with your favorite Vampire Survivor type game and you have Halls of Torment. This game is absolutely fantastic. It has wonderful progression  that keeps you coming back for more, and is just hard enough that you feel like it's challenging but not impossible. I highly recommend this game. You will not find a better value for $5 (but if you have $10, buy this AND Rogue Genesia- HoT and RG are the best in the Vampire Survivor genre that i've played).Edit: The big difference in this game and almost all the other VS type games i've played is that you control your attacks. It seems like a simple thing but it makes a world of difference imo. I think it makes the game feel much more responsive and I wish others in the genre would take note. It really is a perfect mix of Diablo and the VS genre. Speaking of Diablo... (I know I've mentioned it a ton)... the art style is PERFECT.  This game is a true gem. I cannot wait to see what all they do between now and the rest of EA.Edit # 2 (after beating alost all that EA has to offer short of some quests):-After 18 hours of play time it's safe to say I LOVE this game. Some notes for those who like the game and/or need some help to get more out of it:-Use the Warrior early and often until you unlock the well guy. -Once you unlock the Pyro guy, use him to plow throw the early stages of the Fire area and the Aqueduct, Basically I used him to unlock as much as I could until I got the sorcerer then used her and switched between her and the archer to finish off the bosses when those were my final sticking points.-Once you are able to use more items than the starter set the game really takes off customization wise.-Personally, as I said above, I found the archer and sorcerer to be the strongest late game characters when focusing on Attack Speed and Crit. -I completely ignored health/defense/health regen (health regen only because I found a torso piece that heals you for every 3% of your kills- which actually adds up extremely quick to heal you when you are destroying thousands per minute)This game is AMAZING!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I forgot to leave my review for this when I covered it last year. Better late than never I suppose!Things have changed a bunch for this game since I played it last year, the biggest is it went full release.I liked the game's more gritty style and less visual noise than the previous games of this genre (like the seizure-inducing visual noise of Vampire Survivors).The characters are mostly fun to play, although some require more work than others (looking at you Sage....) to truly be worth using. The abilities are all decent and the upgrade paths aren't too complicated (you can expect to complete all the trees by about level 90-110 on average).However, I do recommend play this game on low graphical settings and turning down transparency as it becomes really difficult towards the end-game to see through your own attacks (like the meteors). I can't say much for the music as I have it turned on but never seem to hear it so that's a null point for me (I remember it being rather ambient though).There is also the matter of the developer refusing to modernize the screen size (they have stated multiple times in their discord their refusal to fix this): the game starts in such a small window you have to spend a few seconds manually dragging it out to a larger size, assuming you don't just force full screen. Would really be useful if they added a few common screen size options (like 1920x1080) as choices. Probably my only real complaint for this game, but it is truly annoying.At the cost of $4.99 USD you are getting more than a bargain for the game and I've sunk 270+ hours into it by this point and will probably sink a few hundred more into it (they do have 500 achievements to conquer after all). The more recent updates give it even more replayability so I do suggest picking it up.While my original VOD for this is dated now, this is an example of the earlier game and is a good comparison for the game in the current state. So why not check it out :D

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I play this game on Steam Deck to fall asleep and I'm not even joking.It's incredibly slow paced and it does not captivate due to it's very shallow difficulty.----The game loop in itself is nice and 'akin' to Vampire Survivors. Lots of enemies to slay that walk towards you and pose a threat or are just meat. Gold drops which you collect. There's some 'puzzles' scattered in the maps that you may be able to solve if you can bother.What I like what this game does is the challenges that reveal over time like a skill tree - but this should be displayed more prominently when entering a dungeon so you know what task is at hand.My biggest con with this game, and that's also the reason why I play it to fall asleep, is that it's slow. It's so slow. It doesn't engage you as you walk around the map hearing the gold jingle and kill sounds, the only thing that makes my sleepy eyes open is when I hear myself getting hit. That's also when I look at the timer "6 minutes left..." so I doze off halfway while walking in a circle and wait for the boss to appear so I can put the Steam Deck away and go sleep.There's no way (that I know of, besides Cheat Engine on PC) to speed up the game. The only enemies that pose a threat are those that shoot or leave puddles on the floor (if you're half or completely asleep).I would much rather have this game be significantly harder. Brutally hard so that it's hardly possible to reach the end of the timer for the boss to appear, so that it captivates and you need to stay on edge to not make the wrong call. I dunno. I just personally find this the most boring game I've played and I've played quite a few. But it's a good sleep aid at least

_childDocuments_.review: better than vamp survivors. Here's why:Each playable class has it's own upgrades. You can pick from one of two options on each upgrade. There are over 5 upgrades for each class usually involving your sustain/defense, weapon/damage and special damage/ability. There are scrolls that allow you to pick additional spells/abilities. These will spawn upgrades of their own to pick from on level up. There are different upgrades available at different ranks for these spells. Picking the combination is up to you. When you reach level 3,6,9 with a spell/ability, you can get the upgraded version from a scroll which can upgrade multiple times if you have it unlocked, each upgrade immensely improving the ability. Defeating unique enemies drop either a chest or a scroll. A chest allows you to pick an item - which you can bring back using the well. Equipment: D2 Like equipment, you have a Chest, Helmet, Gloves, 2 ring slots, amulet slot. The different items affect your play style and what you want to focus in the run. Equipment once unlocked is accessible by all classesUsing a combination of class, abilities, and equipment, you can focus achievements which unlock more possibilities.Potion system: You can reroll abilities on level up, You can elimitate abilities in the pool on level up for the rest of the run. You can reroll abilities on scrolls. You can reroll equipment in chests. And more!Many many achievments, each with meaningful unlock.The basic gameplay is similar to Vampire Survivors. This is more in depth with combat, elements, play style, and upgrades ie damage, speed etc.Agony is actually very difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible amount of fun. _childDocuments_.review: I like the Horde Slayer genre.It allows one to dip into and out of a game quickly instead of needing to dedicate hours to playing (although i can spend hours playing these games anyway).It's also quite addictive, keeping me playing to unlock that next weapon/ upgrade/ stage/ character.I discovered Halls of Torment from a demo play-through by SplatterCatGaming, and thought it interesting enough to try out.It is one of the more fun examples of the Horde Slayer genre I have played.Regarding the above-mentioned staples of the genre, it does it quite well.In addition, I love the Diablo-esque art direction. I am fond of the darker atmosphere.The music suits the mood nicely too.This is the first Horde Slayer game where I've had to pay attention to a variety of character stats.This is because the game is designed in such a way that the base stats of each character make a big difference to the effectiveness of the stat boosts provided by the various weapons, items, and abilities.Stat boosts can work much better for some characters, and for some others not at all.I enjoy the quest-unlock record - it allows you to know what quest goals have been achieved and what other related quests can be further pursued after a particular goal has been achieved, which allows you to plan for what next quest to tackle, giving you a little bit of control over your chosen path to end-game.Aside from the general common quest-record, there is a different set of quest-goals for each character, and one for each stage.I would love to see a much larger variety of stages, enemies, weapons/items/abilities, and also hear a larger variety of music tracks, but i assume that these will come in time, as it is still early access days.Regarding some quality-of-life improvements (at the time of this review, 3rd June 2023),1) It would be nice to be able to see the character stats outside the dungeons where character & equipment selection happens - you can only see character stats after you've started a run.2) Although stat boosts for a current run are recorded inside the menus in the order they were chosen, there are some mutations to abilities/weapons that can be chosen during a run which don't show up in the stats and abilities menus, and many times I don't remember exactly what the choice i made did to the character, and it would be nice to be able to refer back to it when entering the menus.3) Some info needs to be less opaque specifically in regard to how some stat values interact with stat boosts and items (eg. base stats vs  Shrine of Blessings boosts vs in-run boosts, base stats of 0% and the interaction with percentage multipliers, and so on... ) - and related to this,if some types of stat boosts have no effect on the character's stats, it would be useful if those stat boosts did not appear in the choices offered (unless, of course, this is meant to be a feature of the game).I am having a blast playing Halls of Torment.I recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this since around when it first launched in early access, and have played every update since. The gameplay is fun and refreshing compared to other titles. The characters and playstyles are unique. Progression feels rewarding. The learning curve is fun and enticing.At 95 hours I have about 80%-90% achievement completion, and not much completion on the new agony mode now that it has been remade the in full release update.This is also an amazing game if you have a steam deck/portable device or even remote desktop. I would play this all the time using remote desktop during downtime at an old job.It is oozing with a unique 2000s RPG style which is so well made. Models/sprites look amazing and are exceptionally stylized. All of the effects are great, and they added an opacity setting for visual clarity in the full release update (or maybe a bit before, not sure). The price point is an insanely good deal for consumers. $5 for a great gameplay experience, amazing visuals, long (but not drawn out) playtime, and extra completionist content. You rarely see a deal that good now, even from starving indie devs.I would like to see ability combinations play a bigger role or have an extra mechanic. You can still of course take multiple fire abilities and add on some fire damage upgrades or equipment buffs. Something extra like having 2 or 3 fire abilities gives a buff or upgrade to fire damage or Meteor Strike and Flame Strike can combine to have meteors fly out of flame strike hits for extra damage. Just something that combines the two ideas or identities of the ability into one extra powerful upgrade/ability.I would also like to see more equipment that gives the feeling of going for a specific "build" more than the current set that is either a generic buff such as +30% attack speed or +20% movespeed. This is not bad by any means, (do not nerf this) but items that give pure general stats like this will always be more powerful in a game with some levels of chance.More environmental interactions would be really neat. The "puzzles" of each level are interesting but even things with less impact but still serve utility such as the traps from one of the agony mode modifiers, or the falling ice damagables in the ice caves level.Finally, it would be really interesting to have some sort of alteration or option that takes the idea of a character and remakes it in a different form of flips it somehow. Similar to something like the tainted characters of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. Just something more to mix up gameplay and add extra content. With the 1 million sales announcement, they said they plan to add more  content, so these may be introduced in the future.The worst part is that if you played during early access, you did not get any torment shards before full release. Torment shards are awarded after every level complete and give small permanent upgrades to characters. The difficulty curve, especially in agony mode, accounts for this gain so its a good bit harder coming from a late game save from early access. If you're still reading, why haven't you bought the game already? Don't tell me you don't have $5 for this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I so very much want to give this a thumbs up because they're this close to greatness.For context I've got 100+ hrs in Vampire Survivors and I imagine many other people leaving a review here do as well. I've put in 50 or so hours into this, unlocked pretty much everything there is to unlock at this point in EA, and have about 4 achievements left that I can't be bothered getting at this point.Aesthetically, this game is neat. They've gone after the Diablo 1 vibe, and it probably looks better than what D1 actually looks like - so hats off to them for that. Stilted animations and dialog - all good. Inventory and loot for persistent upgrades? Also cool. So far there are, like, two characters to meet and, well, that's it. If you're expecting "Stay a while and listen", you're out of luck.As for "everything else" - this game and a lot of others like it I feel have fundamentally misunderstood what VS did and I'm not sure that enough people understand this, so I'm going to tell you, because I played that game in its EA phase as well.VS at its core is extremely concerned with a slow but controlled burn for the player, in that it is strict in how characters grow from level to level, how often unique/boss-type enemies appear, when weapon ascendencies can happen and just when the sessions start to feel like they get too long or dull, VS will then offer up a variety of options and mutators to make the game harder and even speed things up. By the time you reach VS' "endgame", yes, a lot of the challenge is trivialized and it's mostly a matter of nuking everything until the time runs out, but up to that point VS does a stupidly good job of controlling the "just one more minute" tension-and-release cycle. Essays can and should be written about what that game does because I am not doing justice to how VS' mechanics overlap to create a stupidly compelling experience. It should not come as a surprise that the developer of that game used to make gambling apps.You'd think HoT would offer the same sort of progression and understanding of VS' systems, but it simply doesn't. For whatever reason, a lot of the upgrades feel pathetic, with the most expensive one (the revive) only being truly worthwhile to a run, with damage and walk speed being the big game changers a distant second. The best thing HoT does on this front is actually make the achievements system boost the XP earned, which is a cool idea... but to have 98% of the things unlocked and have that boost, and wear the +50% xp amulet and *still* not be able to ding level 100 with either the Cleric or the Shieldmaiden by the 30th minute on the hardest area despite multiple attempts? At that point I truly give up, because I think what may have happened is HoT only concerns itself with the first few minutes of play, and not the totality of the run.There are numerous QoL fixes that are (apparently) coming, such as fast restart, being able to reroll scrolls of mastery and so on, but none of are going to fix the inherent problem in the endgame's design, in that there either is none, or it's kinda just down to luck, I guess? This is apparent in the finale of each zone - each boss (or "lord") is an enormous damage soak that, once you get used to their patterns (or just invest enough in walk speed), becomes an exercise in tedium because it just a massive HP pool to drain each time. VS by contrast spends most of its time killing you immediately on the 30 minute mark until you've worked out how to beat the reaper, rather than running away from the reaper until one of you dies of boredom.Don't get me wrong: I don't regret the time spent, and maybe you'll find enjoyment out of this - but don't expect the same arc as you got from VS.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly my favourite one of these kind of games. The art and sound design, though clearly heavily inspired by Diablo are very well done and really make it feel like a game that isn't just a fiver.It's nice to have full control (toggle, both by hotkey and in the menu) over auto-aim and auto-fire. You can easily just use manual aim for the bosses and take a more relaxed approach for the regular hordes.For me the biggest downsides are probably things that'll get added/fixed eventually, but the balance isn't the best. A game like this doesn't need perfect balance, it's ok to have harder and easier classes, but some skill/item options are so clearly superior that it basically removes any choice aspect.Other than that, it could do with some sort of turbo mode, games have a 30 min timer, add a bit of time for picking things from the menus and it gets quite lengthy. Once you reach a certain amount of meta progress it gets quite easy as well, but I think that just comes down to the fact that it's still missing content.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far the best game to scratch that Vampire Survivors itch! Ok Brotato is pretty good too, but but HoT is like if Vampire Survivors was released in the early 90s, Vampire Survivors 2: Halls of Torment was released in the late 90s. It moves from pixel graphics to Diablo style! Very nostalgic feeling!Overall a fantastic evolution! Progression is really fun, and drives the player toward different playstyles without holding things back too much. The levels aren't too different from each other, but still they have a decent bit of their own identity. There's a good bit of variation in the abilities, but of course ultimately everything boils down to being a godlike damage ball in the end, and it feels good to do that!It doesn't replace the OG, and it's great to have both! The only negative thing I have to say about it is that the systems are quite opaque, it's not that easy to understand how stats affect the outcome. You hover over a line on an ability and it just says "+20% Shrine of Blessing", the Shrine of Blessing being the thing used to upgrade permanent stats like damage or crit chance. Is that +20% from damage, movement speed, or wut? Yeah I can go find that out in base, but just put all info everywhere please. Regardless, very good for a game from 1996!Wholeheartedly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I love the overall style of this game but currently I can't really recommend it. So far my time with this game has largely been waiting to see if it gets more fun, and wondering if i'm missing something or taking the wrong approach. But in the end the few hours ive spent so far have just felt excruciatingly slow, and it seems as though there's still a huge grind ahead of me before it starts getting more interesting. I have no shortage of games to play and not much free time so i'd rather just play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Just saw this game got a 1.0 release, and tons of stuff has changed. I'm happy to actually make this review positive now! They refined the gameplay loop, the tool tips actually help you understand what is going on, what stats do - or what they effect, and thank heavens they made it so you can actually see what abilities do. Outrageously strong work, and I'm happy to visit this 1.0 release with fresh eyes and new enjoyment.This game has all the polish it needed to be a great, and I think it'll be able to cement a firm place in the genre with it's graphic style, game loop, and progression!-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Survivor games are all similar, trying to find variety. This is a great game in the genre, and arguably hits all the marks I could ask for. I actually really enjoy it, have spent plenty of time in it, and plan to spend more.So why am I not recommending it? Because, like every single other game in this genre save one, there is nowhere I can go to look at what the abilities are. What they do. How they work. Know what game does allow you to at least get a snippet about the ability? Vampire Survivors. Literally the first game of this genre to make it huge and explode, and no one can copy that super SIMPLE aspect? Come on guys. Just give us a little lore book where you let us look at each ability, what type of damage it is, etc. All that info is ALREADY in the game because you programmed it to work with those specifications. Let us plan our builds before-hand. I shouldn't have to go on a deep-dive through google to know which abilities are magical and which are physical.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Vampire Survivors, buy this, its got its own thing going, its got a great diablo vibe, and its very similar to the state of VS when it first went viral, already a fantastic game, but has plenty more in the pipeline. Price is great too. The progression bosses are brutally difficult at times though, you can be cruising along obliterating all the normal mobs, then they rock up at 27 minutes and penetrate your rear end vigorously. Lots of fun and good incentive to keep grinding away. 9/10 isometric roguelike game for me. (VS is a 10, but buy them both).

_childDocuments_.review: HoT is carried by its strong aesthetics. I think almost everyone will dig the visual style, and for many people it'll be really good at pushing nostalgia buttons in the brain. This visual association I think drives the positive ratings, because mechanically the game offers literally nothing new, or even slightly novel. No significant improvements or twists are made to the Vampire Survivors recipe and indeed it has less complexity and build variety than many. Upgrades you get from leveling up are  boring fodder like extra x% crit chance or x% attack speed increases. Rarely you may get lucky with a 'good' level up upgrade choice that may offer 2 substantial stat boosts instead of one mediocre one.The meaningful upgrades are the ability drops and these only come from bosses or are spread out really far in the levels - so during a 30 minute run you really only make a small handful of impactful decisions. Even if you get the 'best' drops the runs still miss that feeling of gamebreaking insanity that the best of this genre is so good at evoking.Making this problem even more troublesome is the fact that many of these ability drops are locked behind quests so you wont even see them until after completing certain criteria. Furthermore, getting an ability drop that actually works with your current class is only half the issue - you must then also get the appropriate ability upgrade because the upgraded abilities are without exception so much better than their base counterparts. These upgrades must of course also be first unlocked via quests, and then you must hope that the right one happens to be one of the handful of drops you get in any run.This is just putting the most fun the game can offer behind too much RNG, and even at its best HoT is still just a mid Survivors clone that admittedly looks pretty sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Great time killer.  The game, on the surface, looks to have a lot of depth but that's all just a facade.  There are only a handful of abilities and traits and 2-3 branching paths for each ability to upgrade it.  The game gives you access to a few characters after you have finished their unlock conditions but after each unlock I found myself going back to the Archer anyways because it's the only class that ever gets beefy enough to kill quick enough in later levels. It's fun, for a few hours but you can see pretty much every ability the game has to offer within the first 5 hours, tops and then it's just a grind to hopefully get better armor for future runs.  Speaking of armor, the system seems lackluster with only 1-2 items being genuinely useful.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the game is fun and there's a lot of variety when it comes to characters and upgrade choices. But runs being 30 minutes long kind of kills the game for me. _childDocuments_.review: I had 6.5 hours in prelude and, against my better judgement, decided to try the EA version. Well, it's just boring and tedious. I understand it's just the first days of its early access, but I can compare it to Time Wasters (EA, lots of content, same price), Soul Survivors (EA, much more content even at demo stage, almost twice as expensive) or 20' till Dawn (different heroes with different weapons, much more interesting at its initial step). This game brings nothing new to the table, is utterly boring and grindish. For now I've played warrior, archer, fireman, cleric and warlock. Class difference leaves much to be desired, you basically have your class basic attack and a set of very similar side skills that you can pick with any hero.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts of extremely well. It is challenging and interesting. However, you soon realize that bosses and enemies aren't really "inventive". They follow very basic patterns. In addition to that, you quickly become far too powerful and just... stand. You can literally stand and nobody will be able to hurt you. Stupidly easy.That's a shame. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most addicting "survivor" games out there. It is VERY easy to lose hours to this game, and the devs are still steadily adding content. With this said, there are a handful of traits and mechanics which are not properly explained (especially in the UI) which makes the first few hours of this game very trial and error. "Force" is the most notably confusing trait on first go, so I do hope that there are better metric visuals added in the future.There are things missing which are staples from other games of this genre - most glaringly the total lack of turbo. Combined with the ramping up necessity for the first 10 minutes of gameplay, the later half of the matches can tend to feel underwhelming as you progress further through the quests. This is usually an issue with these bullet hell type top down games and long-term progression. However, I do feel that with new additions to exploration (potentially with merchants and secret areas) and with modifications available for the in game timer/speed that Halls of Torment will solidify itself as one of the top dogs in this genre.

I'm definitely looking forward to more of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches a particular itch for me. When you've got less than an hour free and wanna play a game, BOOM each match lasts a max of 30 minutes (not including pauses). When you need somethin to do with your hands while you're doin somethin else, BOOM this game is almost mindless. It's great if you have ADHD and need to pay attention to a video but need to do somethin at the same time. I use this for my studies, and it makes a world of difference. It's still being updated, and each update brings new balances and more free content. After 23 hours, I only have 59% of the achievements, though admittedly that's partially due to my predilection to use nothing but the Pyromancer. Can you blame me though? He looks like a plague doctor with a flamethrower! Which brings me to the aesthetics of the game. I love them. It's very grim and dark, grimdark, if you will, and as a massive Warhammer 40k fan, the vibes of this game resonate with me. Each new area has been visually distinct, and each item unlocked gives you more options to customize your builds. I do wish you could pull more than one equipment each level, or that the new equipment you're wearing after beating a boss counted as "retrieved," but I understand why it's set this way, and it just gives me more enjoyment time.TLDR: it's grim, it's dark, and it's fun. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to say a lot about a game that is exactly what it's look like : it's a Vampire Survivor inspired game that really wanted to look more like Diablo 2 than its counterpart.And it obviously does work, those type of game have always been closer to hack & slash than bullet hell so it's nothing surprising to see them borrowing more from them. This one in particular is extremly specific about the stats and much less about the attacks, this results in a more flexible game that usual where on the spot decision is more natural than trying hard to stick the build. There's sure archetypes and playing arround them is probably a good idea but because there's so much more option available it really discourage badly chasing one option. The interesting flipside of this is the randomness doesn't hit too hard but also it gives value to defensive options, something that's pretty rare to achieve in very stat heavy game.But having said that, it's not that much of departure either and the main appeal of this game in particular over any other one is its presentation. Now I did stop at what looked like a conclusion but there's obviously more to, there's exactly 500 achievement to unlock and a few of them does require some effort, two different mode gradual difficulty, a few different grind and I have barely foudn any artifact outside the obvious so there's a time sink element to it I haven't touched and probably won't bother too much with and while the game itself isn't extremly difficult it does seem to scale pretty viciously. Combined with ennemies that have pretty varied behaviors, none of this is a completly mindless grind while also being entirely optional.In any case, there's nothing wrong with this game that isn't relative to what type of game it is, that is to say a pretty repetitive time sink.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've played -- can't really seem to put it down.Only downside for me is the lack of ease and clarity of information provided to you. As a new player, when levelling up for the first time, you're shown things like "Force", "Range", "Area", and mousing over them in that level up menu, -- which you can't escape from until one has been selected -- it tells you to check the stat to find out what they do for you. This stat page is separate from the level up menu, and so you can't see what these things do, and how important they are for you until after you pick it, and this was my only frustration. I think being able to check both at the same time and make informed choices from the beginning would help newer players settle in faster with multiple characters. It's likely a design choice, and you might like it as it is.I love the rest. I'm going to play more now.
