_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those hidden gems of a game that I personally never saw advertised and I think Ubi did a really bad job at marketing. It's fun, self aware, occasionally 4th wall breaking. It's an open world greek myth inspired tale, heavily stylised in a very attractive way. I'd encourage people to give it a try if they like open world action-rpg games and simple but fulfilling puzzles. The story is full bodied and engaging, the characters fun and interesting, and it really harnesses the greek myths in an accessible way.

The main quest itself is very fun, but with all the collectibles, you can at least add a 100 extra hours of life to the game. I really hope they release a sequel some time. The main quest as well as all the DLCs are very fun and allow to experience different mythologies with very similar mechanics. Perhaps the only one I do not enjoy as much is "A New God", which is entirely consists of trials and I find it a very time consuming and frustrating to some extent. Otherwise, to me, this is a perfect experience and I cannot recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, very fun game. There is a large, beautiful world filled with puzzles and challenges to explore and find, or scout from a vantage point. The combat feels simple yet satisfying, the puzzles are super easy to frustrating, but doable. Gliding and climbing around everywhere is so much fun, although it takes some getting used to for gliding challenges. I really love the cartoony artwork and vivid colors. I highly recommend this game on sale only because the price difference between full and sale has been massive lately and this would be an ideal game were it not for the Ubisofty stuff in it. You get the launcher and they push some paid cosmetics at you. Other than that it has been a great experience so far with tons of stuff to do if you like upgrading your character and completing areas. The dialogue is often interesting, telling summarized version of stories from greek mythology with a goofy tone that is sometimes really funny, though often very adult oriented. _childDocuments_.review: Played on steamdeck. Wow this game is the highest possible 9 out of 10 I can give.. I had no clue this game existed.... what perfect way to wash away the sadness of beating Elden Ring. Also.. everyone says it "copies" BOTW.. like shut up.. no seriously shut your stupid mouth... no really, look at me.. shut up and stay shut up.This game has its own very strong identity.. the graphic are incredible aided by an insane Elden Ring esque draw distance.. Now combat is good and challenging, but holy dog feces do I hate the fact there is a 2 button parry.. what a cheap way to make the game more difficult.. I immediately made it a 1 button back grip button press on Steamdeck.. also I do not agree with a lot of reviewers here that the player character is slidy or stiff.. not my experience.. however I do find gliding to be unnecessarily hard to control and it's irritating how the character can start climbing stuff in the battle.. and if you try to dash and jump you usually screw it up.. and stamina seems limited at times but you can pump it up whenever with plentiful mushrooms and potions. It's also super irritating that a lot of people see Ubisoft on the cover and immediately think oh it has too much collectibles.. but those very same people have no problem with the ridiculous complex crafting and leveling mechanics of a fromsoft game... I personally found the collecting of a bunch of different elements to level up many different types of abilities to not be a grind as the world is so dense with stuff to do that you are constantly collecting enough stuff to level up something. People also complain how it's a map marker collection where you just go from icon to icon on the map.. but really you don't have to reveal the map icons, it's a mechanic if you want it but you don't need to use it.. I preferred mostly exploring on my own.. seeing stuff in the distance and going "that's cool.. let's go there" or "I don't think I've ever been there before" just like Elden Ring.I like the setting and extremely densely packed world tons.. the puzzles are good and consistently get more interesting and difficult as the game opens up. I found the humor mostly on point and entertaining.. the music for the most part is amazing though some songs or musical cues can get quite repetitive... And I said it before the graphics are increadible.. but it does sometimes look too cartoony.. while other times it looks like the most beautiful game ever.. usually when you are high up and seeing the whole world.. and at 15$ or 80% off this game was a steal. at 50$ there is still enough here to make it worthwhile and had I known it was going to impress me so much I would've gladly thrown more money at it to snatch it up. Its a beautiful, fun, funny, rough around the edges colorful adventure well worth the asking price!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! I wasn't expecting it to be so fun, but it just works in a fantastic package. This is a fusion of multiple genres, but the biggest inspirations are definitely from Breath of the Wild/Zelda Franchise and Assassin's Creed franchise. It's good fun, and I wanted more. Good news was there are 3 DLC's but each of them are very different from the base game. I've tried A New God DLC, but I could not get into it. It's basically vaults but are now called trials and they are much harder than the base game. The checkpoint system is ass, every time you miss a jump or something, you get sent back to the very beginning of a "stage." I couldn't get through it with the patience I had as it wasn't fun anymore. I then tried Lost Gods DLC, and it's very different as it's a top down style gameplay. More Diablo-esque, but it's own thing. It doesn't feel polished because the camera is very hard to adjust to after playing the base game. Since my original review, I've played through Eastern Realms DLC. It is a fantastic DLC. Very basic story like the base game, and even more bare bones as it is much shorter. I think to complete everything it takes around 8-9 hours. It had a few new puzzle mechanics which were very enjoyable. Soundtrack was just as amazing as the base game. I loved the Chinese mythology, would've loved if we had a full game instead of just a DLC.I also want to mention the fact that there are no Steam achievements is pretty bizarre, when UPlay has these achievements. It's weird, and feels almost empty without having achievements listed on Steam.However, definitely pick up the base game, as it's a solid game!I'm also a little bummed that this game won't get a sequel according to rumours. Such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of content, lots of world to explore, lots of rewards to find, though some of them are just visual upgrades and don't change your gear stats. If you're a completionist, there's plenty here to grind on, though that's not necessary to complete the game. You can just focus on the main quests. There are aspects of this game I appreciate the relative simplicity of, versus other games. For example, there is no durability system to weapons. Once you have a new weapon, it won't break, and you have it forever, thankfully. There are lots of ability upgrades, based on collectible items. There are also a lot of potion upgrades based on brewing, but mercifully no complicated recipes. The game simply tells you if an upgrade is available based on what's in your inventory. Most of the NPCs are baddies, so the world and the story does feel a bit sparse. There are however, many nods to Greek mythology, with the less family friendly parts alluded to subtly.

I would have been disappointed if I missed this and am amazed it isn't rated higher. For sure don't be scared off by the rating. _childDocuments_.review: The only cons are as follows. Lack of enemy variety, janky physics at times when it comes to solving puzzles and lack of varied tasks per map segment. Amazing value for money especially with the sale price I paid for it. I would definitely say it's worth the full asking price. My only regret was playing this game on Normal difficulty because it was too easy for me. Immortals Fenyx Rising needs to be a franchise. There's so much potential.

_childDocuments_.name: Immortals Fenyx Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising looked neat and I have heard great things, so I decided to pick it up. Unfortunately, It’s a pretty mediocre game. It is clearly inspired by Nintendo’s Breath of the Wild, but they made the smart decision to not make weapons break, which is nice to see.To start with the good, the combat is fun. It’s relatively simple, but it’s fun. You got a light and heavy attack, a bow attack, and a doge. The doge slows time if timed right, which is not anything original, but it works well and it’s fun. Enemies can feel pretty tanky at times, but you can upgrade your weapons and gear using a very confusing system that has something like 10 different currencies.The game is filled with puzzles. They are not the hardest puzzles, but I enjoyed doing many of them. The story is comedic, which I liked, but I do not find it particularly interesting or engaging. The world and graphics look good and the game runs well enough, although not what I would call great. You can explore the world, which is interesting enough, but you can also just use your magic telescope that has a very far range and sees through walls to see where the loot is, but is pretty finicky to use. The game would have been better if they did not have that and maybe made loot areas more visible from a distance, or if they just went the normal approach and showed you everything when you were nearby.The controls feel like they could have used an extra bit of polish, mainly in the gliding and climbing.There are no Steam achievements for some reason, which is really annoying, especially since it has achievements on console, but not a deal breaker for me. Cloud saves and controller support are broken, which is annoying, but this is not really a controller game, so lack of controller support does not bother me. Cloud saves not working does. They’ve chosen to use some Ubisoft system, which errors every single time, instead of just using Steam Cloud which works perfect 99.99% of the time.Every time you open the game, it spends several minutes verifying that you own that game, which is very annoying and really makes me not want to even open the game, especially when it isn’t anything amazing. The main menu greets you with a cash shop where you can buy items. I did not look too carefully, but they looked to only be cosmetics. Not the worst thing in the world, but still very annoying to see in any game, especially a game it has absolutely no place being in, like a full priced single player only game.Immortals Fenyx Rising is not good, it's not bad, it’s just mediocre. It’s a decent way to pass some time, but nothing about it makes me want to open it, so I end up playing other, better, games.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game on sale for $9 and my enjoyment has far exceeded that cost!As others have discussed in detail, this feels like a watered down AC Odyssey combined with Breath of the Wild, without breaking weapons. The puzzles are enjoyable and it's feels really satisfying when you complete a particularly challenging vault. I like the range of activities in this world as well as the systems for leveling up various stats and abilities. The first time I played, I wasn't immediately immersed in what seemed like silly cut-scenes, but after playing more, I find them charming (especially with these interpretations of Prometheus and Athena). This game doesn't take itself too seriously and is good fun after work. It's a shame that the sequel was cancelled, so I hope to complete this one as much as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: An above average game that could of been great if wasn't open world. If it just had a linear story and cut out all the filler content it would of been a masterpiece. Yes this is a legit zelda alternative but it lacks the awesome physic puzzles or robust crafting freedom of that game. On top of that we get lots of padding including a 3 hour intro/prelude and many things like double jump and basic moves like air dash locked behind a skill tree. I personally loved the puzzles but i felt like they should of just put the best parts of the puzzle temples instead of having lot of repetitive filler. How many times do have to find a hidden rock to put down on a pressure plate for crying out loud. The combat is basic as well and the harder difficulties only make the already too long game even more torturous with there cheap bullet sponge ways. I personally loved the beautiful graphics and titan quest vibes and despite me not having enough interest to finish i'll recommend it on sale. But ubisoft's open world ways really got in their way of delivering what could of been a fun little romp.  Instead it becomes just another tiresome open world game that you will never finish due to eventual boredom.

_childDocuments_.review: Clash of the Titans meets Titan Quest meets Cartoons meets Adult films meets God of War meets Devil May Cry... pretty much sums up the game. Visual - simple but very nice and very romantic atmosphere throughout whole game, made a lot of screenshots, really nice art design, eyecandy. Story - solid, despite the known Greek mythology it was about the family and really impactful in some way - shows real world problems in fairy tale adaptation, sometimes I was touched as themes as betrayal, rejection, depression, hopelessness, low self-esteem, no success etc occured. Really recommend the game for adult audience, game is not really suitable for kids despite the visual. Dialogues - between Prometheus and Zeus its interesting how they comment every action in the game, so it feels like narration is alive whole time, you dont have the feeling of being only watching main hero to progress but those characters too. But... whole game is insanely thirsty, its like writer/s were horny whole the time, other way I cant explain why this game has so much of double-meaning texts which I am not fan of, in my past life I was like that, but now its not that funny anymore, because they bring serious topics around it and I am not fan of adultery and betrayal of your spouse, its not funny and never should be taken lightly as it destroys too many lives. Gameplay - great gameplay, its fun to upgrade every time your char with powers, new tricks, never gets old, because if you do all side missions and collectibles you get better and more interesting equipment, there was always reward and game feels rewarding in terms of combat and combination of your suit/weapons, where you can be really overpowered as I was in the last 1/4 of the game, where I was really too strong and even boss fights were like 30 seconds to 1 minute speedrun shots. World - living world with enemies and animals, its all hostile but still you have sense of life and uncover something interesting. This game has really good approach as it offers variety of puzzles, mostly special tombs which are from beginning quite simple and bit of repetitive but after time they get more interesting and harder, but still nothing you cant beat after few tries. Platforming is solid, you can run, jump, climb with endurance meter and use horse/unicorn etc animals for quicker travel. Upgrades - it has some RPG elements, but its Action Adventure game in core, so yes you upgrade sword, axe, bow, armor, helmet and potions, but you dont have to be necessarily over the top to beat the game, yet, I wanted to be as strong as possible but still theres a plenty of room because I returned to game after more than month and didnt want to play it more, so I just quickly finished the game. Music - fine, sometimes good, sometimes not so special, moody. Replayability? - I would say yes, it has really catchy combat, fights are the best in the game and to me it never got old, as you upgrade over time fights are even more entertaining. Rating: Its game on its own from Ubisoft, Its epic action-adventure with really visually stunning world, would recommend if you are fan of greek mythology or epic adventure with fast paced hacknslash combat. TL;DR - Epic Action-Adventure with powers and upgrades where you kill monsters from greek mythology, got OP later, enemies got rekted.

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't have native controller support, of any kind at all on Steam. One hand, glad that they're bringing back their games to Steam, on the other hand, can't support their mediocre measures for this game.Instant refund.Edit: if you disable PS controller support from Steam settings, and keep DualSenseX running, then your controller is picked up as DS4 in the game and it works fine then. _childDocuments_.review: IFR is a quality open world game in all the right ways. It looks great, sounds nice, plays well, the UI is top-notch, the world is interesting, the characters are pretty charming, you can save anywhere and more. It’s the perfect game to pick up & play, take a break from and come back to. In terms of content, it depends on whether you do the optional stuff or not. I did everything that I encountered but I know it’s not 100% due to some Ubisoft achievements (missing about 8-9 from the main game). Steam shows over 72 hours but in-game it shows around 65 hours. I played it blindly with no concern for efficiency. I enjoyed the puzzles and the overall variety with the challenges, moves/skills and combat.Sometimes you NEED to take a break due to its open world nature where tasks can feel repetitive, lots of asset re-use and there could have been more variety with the enemies. But it’s comparable to other open world games, nothing against this game in particular. Also the game has a lighthearted and funny atmosphere with the jokes and art style. I’m not against that but not all the jokes landed well. Some involve cheating and having weird s*x kinks between gods etc. It’s a bit weird when the game is trying to be cartoony. I’m still not a fan of launchers and this is no exception, but it didn’t give me any issues at least. My biggest problem is the lack of Steam achievements. Yes, you have them in their launcher but it’s just not the same. It’s demotivating and the reason why I didn’t go for 100%. I’m hopeful we’ll still get them like with Assassin’s Creed Valhalla and we know they can unlock retro actively based on previous examples. So all that I did is not wasted, I’m planning on getting 100% when we get Steam achievements.I usually ignore games without Steam achievements and I understand if others do it but I still highly recommend getting the game. I would even say that the normal price of €40 is worth it if you like open world games. The game is on sale often though, so you don’t have to pay that price. It’s awesome being able to get such a great game for a good price. I have all the DLC, I will be playing them in order next.

It's a good looking game with fun and satisfying game play and a decent story. The elephant in the room however, is the writing. There have been some lines that got a genuine chuckle out of me, and some that made me audibly groan with how bad they were.The base game took me about 40 hours to 100% (not including the one miss-able achievement that I'm too lazy to start a new game to get because, there is no steam achievements.) and for $65 NZD i think its an alright deal, though some people might want to wait for a sale. _childDocuments_.review: I had great fun playing this game. The art style is beautiful and the combat fun. I loved exploring and solving the puzzles that are dotted everywhere. Yes, this game has the typical Ubisoft symptom of dotting the landscape with icons but, personally, I don't mind it. I think it's done better here than in most of their other games. The mini puzzles that need to be solved give a great sense of reward as some require careful observation of the environment to figure out.I also loved the vaults and the levels of puzzles they presented. There are some mild frustrations with some of them where a whole section needs to be restarted to try again after a failed attempt, which can get tedious. Overall, the vaults are brilliant in engaging the player with some longer, more complex puzzles as presented on the Golden Isle.As mentioned, combat is fun, flashy, and satisfyingly responsive. The story is pretty well done and the writing is very competent as well, with many parts having me genuinely chuckle -- rare for the video game format.I will say though, the climbing feels incredibly slow... Knowing that this same engine is used for the latest Assassin's Creed games where climbing is fast and fluid, it makes no sense. Yea, maybe they want to limit it more to fit in with the stamina system but, later in the game, when you can have loads of stamina, climbing is just tedious and I found myself avoiding it when possible. It's usually quicker going around a tall climb, than actually climbing it. Maybe that was the intention.

Ditto for the characters.The combat is very straightforward hack and slash. Honestly, I think the answer for why I don't like this game is because I'm just not interested in the progression. In Palworld (which, as another heavily BOTW inspired game, I am using as a point of comparison) the primary reason I play is to unlock more pals and grind for better gear. The difference in gear is felt in boss fights, and the Pals are cool to collect aesthetically, and are useful for helping to grind gear at the base. I want to get more Pals and better gear because its compelling.In Immortals, the primary progression is unlocked through the story. I get a quest to save Aphrodite, or Hephaestus. These characters are barely more than a few jokes, which means I don't care about saving them, and I don't really want to run around a map just to save them. To suffice, the art style is cool, but I'm so disinterested in both the story and in combat progression that I'm just not interesting in playing further. The game is just that uncompelling.Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I played the game on the Nintendo Switch, but stopped after the first Zone, because I couldn't really enjoy the game on Switch it was because of the controls, which were simply horrible on Controller, but now when I tried the game on PC I understood it's simply a bad game.After starting on PC the first thing I noticed was that the manuals for the interface and cut scenes were pretty inconsequentially designed. Some buttons with Keys on it could be clicked, some not. The second thing to notice was the heavy integration of the Store, like in all Udon'tplay games. After starting the game it was integrated in every interface. When I started a new game every cut scene needed to be skipped another way or simply couldn't be skipped... Like I said I played already on switch and just wanted to start. The first cut scene was skippable by ESC, the second by holding Space and the third was not skippable. Also the transitions between cut scenes were pretty bad where some other stuff loaded in shortly to be cancelled by the cut scene again.When I finally started into the game I realised that the game really is just a cheap console game. The textures of the environment are cheap, like some PS2 game. The animations appear cheap cause the animations start and finish what ever the player does or interacts with. For example the animations of walking do not match to walking the stairs or uphills, the jump animation does need to be finished before you can start climbing and when you jump out of water your character simply spawns jumping over the water.After continuing with the first steps the player is introduced to a special view mode to check out the landscape which has several issues. First... the camera is offset like the characters eyes are suddenly in his chest which makes it hard to glance over descents, secondly you can scout and mark points of interest and chests... through trees, through walls, through water, through literally anything without any limitation as long the zone is loaded. You either don't use the feature at all or you will always spoil stuff, whats the point of "adventuring", when you don't actually need to go there and simply "know" what it is. There are even different icons for chest content like "in this chest is an equipment piece" and "in this chest are casual materials". On PC I did not continue to play for longer than ~30 Mins and didn't continue to play the story, like the first dungeon and so on. The described above was enough for me to uninstall and refund the game. Overall it might be an alright game for console, but I do not recommend buying the game for PC, since it will just suck out the fun for adventuring.

_childDocuments_.review: Pirate Ubisoft games. They steal your money and your games, don't let them get away with it.As for the game, the writing's so bad. There have been numerous puzzles where Promentheus and Zeus will just give you the answer before you even have time to look at the puzzle. I'd say the combat is at least alright, you can't just cheese every fight using heavy attacks and dodging, light attacks are encouraged as they give you stamina so you can use your other abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't had this much raw fun in a game since I was a kid. The dialogue is great, the combat is fun as hell, and the puzzles manage to feel different and unique even though most of them use the same pieces and mechanics.  People complain about the cash shop, but everything there is attainable in the game for free (with a little time and effort, obviously). But the free stuff you get in the game from just playing it looks LOADS better than most of the stuff in the cash shop anyways. The game as a whole feels like a little bit of Spyro, Darksiders 2, and Assassin's Creed. Buy this game NOW before the sale ends. $10 for a $100 game is a steal for any game, and this one is worth WAY more than $10.TL;DR: God of War for kids, but don't let the cartoonish looks fool you. Smooth gameplay and hilarious jokes in every line, even more so if you have a good understanding of Greek mythos. Go have fun.Edit: Just got done with a 12 hour session, and lemme tell you, I think this is my new favorite game of all time. Silly, I know, but it's just so GOOD. The puzzles are FAR more varied than I initially thought, and each one is fun in a different way. They're not simple time wasters like in Genshin, where you do the exact same thing 50 different times. The story and writing is fantastic. They manage to take Greek myths, legends, and epics, and dish them out across the world in a manageable and sensible manner. I also really like that all the voice actors have greek accents. Feels good, as much as I liked John Goodman as Zeus in the disney Hercules.Also, Athena is hot.

_childDocuments_.review: "Checking for additional content..." 28 seconds every time you start the game.EDIT: Game's framerate is capped at 60 and the game says it's "native" Refresh Rate. LOL my screen is 120 hz in Geforce Control Panel and 144hz native. Nice try tho Ubisoft. We know it's a ♥♥♥♥ console port. ON TO THE REVIEW...This game's controls make me think of the jank of going back to Fable one. Animations feel unrefined and unstable, movement actions like the double jump and glide are not smooth, fall speed is whatever the game feels like at the time rather than a smooth acceleration downwards (noticeable after double jump or cancelling glide, you instantly start falling at max fall speed). Platforming segments will have you struggle not to walk off the other side of the platform since you have 10ms to react and stop pressing W.Dodging is not good. If you don't perfect dodge, you don't dodge. You get hit every time even when mid dodge animation unless you get that perfect millisecond timing. If you do, time slows down, nice, but then if they have a combo you just lost your timing for dodging the other attacks.Lots of tough enemies, good, but once you overcome the challenge of beating them you can do it again since enemies like the Minotaur are not once-off boss-like challenges and they don't get easier (at least not that I've seen) so you have to do a dark souls level fight every time you see one, or ignore all combat. To be honest, the game really punishes you for fighting unless it's for a specific objective like unlocking a chest in the area or progressing the story.Keybinds are atrocious. Glide isn't Space, it's R. Why? I don't know. Probably since double jump is in the game and they want to let you glide without double jumping. Maybe just make double jump not use stam and then let us glide with Space? And there's lots of other examples, I had to rebind several keys to get a somewhat sane control scheme. Since they don't have weapon switching, power attack is either going to be on your keyboard or middle mouse since you use right mouse to switch to bow mode. What about blocking? That's on keyboard too since there's no mouse buttons left. You have so much keybind jank in this game it makes it not fun to play.You cannot progress through the story without playing the puzzle segments. I don't really like them but I could bare it if not for the other issues.Gearing system has very little going on and I wish it wasn't even there. Items have very bad passive effects and weapons are all "perfect dodge to regen 1 hp bar" or "perfect parry to regen 1 stam bar" and that's all there is.Some of the sound effects are very muddy. The rest are merely passable.EDIT: These ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ make some of their puzzles completely waste your time. You can do the first half and then it says "You don't have the abilities needed to continue" and there's a convenient exit. They went out of their way to say "Yup the last 15 minutes of your time were all for nothing and we didn't bother pointing that out earlier hahaha ♥♥♥♥ you!". This game is shockingly bad and deserves mixed reviews at best so that other people don't buy this garbage.On the good side:* The story is entertaining and so is the narration.* The animations are very nice and some provide a solid amount of visual comedy tooI'll probably force myself to come back to this game to get my money's worth but it frustrates me more than it brings me joy.

_childDocuments_.review: Insofar Immortal Fenyx Rising feels like a chore, without the any kind of satisfaction that actual chores give you. It's an open world game with POI icons all over the place, you travel to them (mind-numbingly boring & time-wasting), do the (not particularly fun) activity at the location , get a miniscule amount of resource that you accumulate to get a miniscule upgrade, then you open the map and do it all over again.Shallow and basic, hit enemies and make numbers appear until they die, with occasional parrying/dodging. There doesn't seem to be any significant benefit to parrying as opposed to negating damage by just dodging, both just slows down time (unless the equipment has parry bonus damage). Dodging distance seems poorly implemented as it sometimes doesn't go far enough to escape attacks. All combat options(sword for quick, axe for heavy, bow for range) are given pretty early and does not evolve as you progress - thus it gets stale pretty quickly. Range attacks sucks, the guided arrows do most damage but also slows combat to a crawl. Your damage numbers also becomes ♥♥♥♥ very early in the game unless you go around doing time-wasting chores for upgrades, making enemies damage-sponges that makes boring combat last even longer.Exploration is slow, worse in the early game where stamina is limited, which not just limits sprinting but swimming and climbing distance. Later you might upgrade the stamina resource, but while spending stamina to sprint of boost glide does increase movement speed, it still takes too long to get to places - take into account how many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ POIs are marked around the map, a big chunk of your playtime is just slowly getting to places.The world is huge, and manages to feel pretty empty despite the ♥♥♥♥-ton of POI icons it litters all over the place. There's the usual open world game mechanic of climbing up a vantage point to reveal map and POIs, except in this one you have to manually identify each POI with your cursor, but 1)there's annoyingly far too many of them, 2) the identification ring isn't particularly sensitive enough, 3) most of the POIs aren't visually identifiable without the ring, thus you end up simulating a seizure and fast clicking to get as many of them out of the way as possible. I honestly groan every time I open up the map screen and see how many chore icons are on it. Quite a lot of the icons are just treasure chests or ambrosia, but I wouldn't exactly count travelling to chest or ambrosia to simply collect them "gameplay". Some of the collectibles might be locked behind puzzles/combat/platforming, but it isn't particularly engaging, as it seems to be made to be very accessible to children. Within the first few hours of the game, you would have seen a dozen iteration of box-on-button puzzles, which gets old really fast, made worse with how slow you are at pushing large boxes (in one case, pushing a dumb pearl long distance). Vaults similarly provide puzzle/combat/platforming challenges, just with a different upgrade resource at the end. Perhaps the reason the game gets old really quickly is that regardless whether you travelled to a treasure chest/ambrosia/vault POI, you're basically doing the same few activities. and always rewarded with 1/6th to 1/???th of an upgrade.I have never played Zelda:BOTW, but I have played Middle Earth: Shadow of War and I recommend that instead: it has the same tower vantage point to reveal POIs with cursor mechanic (which I didn't like then either) - except there's only 6-10 POIs instead of the dozens in Fenyx; combat's inifinitely better in depth and mechanics, as are the enemies (Nemesis system!); the upgrade tree is far more interesting, and the process of earning them is more fun/less of a chore; you can enslave orcs to your side; writing and graphics are also better...  I can't think of any aspect of Fenyx that is more appealing that Shadow of War, except if you want a more kid-friendly game (which it is), or enjoy listening to Zeus and Prometheus constantly bickering as narrators to the story, rather than hanging out with one grumpy elf-ghost.I would definitely refund this game if I could.

Just start UC, click remember my login and login and from then on forget about it. UC will boot up automatically when you start your game from steam and you just wait an extra 10 sec.. Honestly if you can't wait 10 sec you shouldn't be playing games but getting your issues sorted. _childDocuments_.review: After umming and arring as to weather or not to purchase this game, a recent sale and play of the demo changed my mind and boy am I glad I played this game.To put it bluntly, this is the poor mans Breath of the wild. The only real difference is this is using Greek mythology.I really enjoyed the art style and none of the artistic choices grew old for me in my hours of play.The combat is very simple and doesn't really require any skill. Be that as it may, it was another thing I enjoyed.The biggest turn off most people have about this game is the constant chatter between Zeus and Prometheus. I myself didn't have this issue and enjoyed the background conversations and tidbits of lore surrounding the Greek mythos. I did find that the chatter only really kicked up during story missions and relevant lore areas.All in all a fun game and worth a purchase. I can't really comment on the DLC stuff as the first major DLC bored the ever loving hell out of me after only 10 minutes of play.

_childDocuments_.review: I was approaching Fenyx Rising as a "typical Ubisoft game" or a "cartoonish Odyssey". Just finished it, and I find this statement so unfair - this is really an underrated, hidden gem.Narrative approach is clever and well-executed. The plot itself is surprisingly good. Light, but never trivial, and underneath the goofy vibes and horny jokes (which totally make sense in the light of Greek mythology), it delivers a really nice story about family and identity.Exploration is extra fun. Using "eagle vision" to mark places of interest can quickly turn the game into a boring to-do list, but you can spot most of interesting things from afar on your own, so you don't need to rely on it. And this made it one of my most enjoyable exploration experiences in recent years.Combat is really fun and smooth. Seems very simple at first, but has some surprising depth and it's very satisfying and engaging.Puzzles are great! Built on simple ideas, but impressively creative. Perfectly balanced for a relaxing game - not too easy, and never too hard to get you stuck for hours. Art style and graphics are fantastic. For some reason, trailers and screenshots don’t do it justice - the game looks much better in motion and avoids feeling overly “sweet”. Traversing a deserted kingdom on horseback, exploring colossal temples and castles with silhoutes of tormented ghosts haunting the land, brings to mind... Elden Ring. The soundtrack is also surprisingly amazing! Perfectly complements the atmoshpere and themes of the game, and fits its relaxing aura.Towards the end, looks like I've got only praises to give, and most of them are "surprising". And yeah, honestly Fenyx deserves them. Everything it tries to do, it does great, or at least very solid. It might be partly because it isn't the type of game I usually play, and I haven't played Breath of the Wild, which apparently Fenyx is a clone of, but it's easily one of the best games I played this year. It's not revolutionary in any way, but delivers something special, really stands out from other titles and I love it. Big thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is great! The combat is fun and exciting at first and slowly becomes a chore. The game throws the same 4-5 enemies at you with more and more health as you progress through the game. When you do find a new enemy, it becomes common around the world and merges with the others. When killing enemies, it gives you bare-minimum and sometimes no rewards.The first few hours of the game are magical! I had so much fun exploring Vaults and other activities around the map. Exploration rewards you with chests and some underwhelming gear but it gives you some reasons to explore. Again, after a while, they lose their charm and become a drawn out mechanic. They add very little differences between points of interests (POI) and Vaults, eventually the puzzles become time wasters.The story is a great idea but it does not live up to it. The characters are weak and act dumb. The first hour of the game made me question if the main character knew anything. The gods all act the same and are somewhat boring. They are cowards and are depressed with nothing to live for, but the main character comes in and saves the day with pitiful cheer-me-ups. However, the gods aren't themselves and that does make it entertaining. The game is told like a story with narration over it. It is a fantastic way to tell the story. It has funny lines and the voice actors for the narrators are the best in the game. Overall, the story is really intriguing and had fun comedic moments, but it was executed poorly.A few things I want to congratulate the game on are: narration, skip-ables, and humor.One of the best parts of the game is the narration! The game benefits a lot from  (Names of people talking) talking over the gameplay. They have fun jokes and they sound like best buds. They also have great tone's for different events, unlike every other character that is the same bland monotone conversation. The narration makes me stop my music to listen to every word they say.This game lets you skip every cut-scene! Story cut-scene or minor animations. It is amazing. I personally have not skipped any story cut-scene but I have skipped a lot of the boring repeated animations. Very very nice feature.The humor in the game is safe enough for most children but also hides adult humor in it! With these little additions, it makes it more fun! It made me laugh some and smile and it did not go farther than any modern PG13 film. I can only recall it saying "badass" once.A few game play mechanics I want to complain about are: far-sight, stamina, enemy attacks, and treasures. This mechanic sucks. It is a "mini-game" of sorts that makes you find all the objectives around the map. You have to look at each objective, press E and then it will show up on the map. This is terrible. There is no information on how many you can see, the indicator only shows when you are an inch or so from it, and this is the worst part of the game. Massive time waster.This game is a clone of Breath of the Wild (BOTW), no doubt, with its copying of stamina and game play. This is awesome! I really wanted a game like BOTW on PC. But the stamina in this game is a burden to play with. If I am in combat, I think it is fair to enforce the stamina drain on every action but this game forces it on you throughout the whole game. Carrying an object stops all stamina regain, unless your not moving, and slows the pacing of all the puzzles and tedious work already in the game.Some enemy attacks are truly unfair. The combat in this game is simple: block/roll then attack. The fighting is easy and not difficult, but there are moments in this game where a projectile will change on a dime and hit you or a enemy is not facing you but instant turns to attack you with an unshockable attack. It is unfair and happens every couple fights. Not a big issue but it is there.This game is fun! I really enjoyed it (still have the ending to do, but wanted to write this before hand). I have never heard about this game and luckily saw it on the day of release. I picked it up for $15 and I really enjoyed it. If you want BOTW on PC, this is a great game for it! It took me the whole game to get invested, still a little withdrawn, but I am happy with the experience I had with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to respond to some of the things I have seen in recent reviews that I do not feel are entirely accurate. 1. Comparisons to BOTW: Aside from the obvious visual style they are not even remotely similar.  This game actually descends from Assassin's Creed Odyssey and it shares many game mechanics with that game.  2. Voice Acting: the acting in this game is of the same quality of any ubisoft game and is exactly what I would expect.  Depending on your perspective that could be good/bad/Neutral.  Personally I don't mind it at all, it's pretty good for what it is.  3. Humor: The dialog and narration in this game are pretty funny.  Yes they are campy but they are supposed to be.  This game will not replace a recording of George Carlin on stage, But it's not supposed to.   It's exactly as funny as it needs to be.  Stop taking everything so seriously.  4. Ubisoft - Connect : Every Ubisoft game requires you to run their software and have an account.  This game is no exception.  Why is that a surprise to some people ?  I don't like it, it's entirely stupid and serves to do nothing but irritate paying customers and make them not want to buy Ubisoft titles in the future.  Blame Ubisoft for their stupid anti-consumer practices if you want to but it has nothing what so ever to do with this game specifically.  5. Controller support - I read a review from this month saying that Controller Support was completely broken.  That simply isn't true, it works just fine for me.  I used my Guillikit Bluetooth Controller from the first time I fired up the game and it's been flawless.  6. Too much content/takes too long to finish -  Seriously ?  Shut the hell up and go play asteroids, your opinion is invalid.  7.  Crashes : I ran into a situation where I was crashing over and over at the same area of the map.  I traced it back to the nvidia driver crashing (I was using the latest "Game Ready" driver.)  I removed it and installed the "Studio Driver" instead which is slightly older and according to nvidia more stable.  I haven't had a crash since.  Don't know who to blame for the crashing but the driver I was using just came out a week ago and the devs obviously could not have tested the game with that driver and using an older one did fix the issue.  I expect that it's a bug that will be resolved sooner or later.  I did send in several crash reports to help with that.   I'll continue to update this review as I make my way through the game, so far it's been a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: First, let's get the obvious out of the way.  This is an unabashed, shameless rip-off of Breath of the Wild in every conceivable way.  However, it's not a cheap rip-off.  A lot of time and effort went in to developing what makes this game good, and for that reason I can recommend it.  There are a few things holding back from being a fantastic game, though.First off, the combat is satisfying, with some cool combos and fun weapons.  Also, the world is detailed, the models are diverse, the assets unique, and the animations are very well done.  Those at the grunt level tasked with bringing this game to life took great care to make it high quality, and it shows.  It definitely looks like a AAA game. The problem I have, is it often feels more like the production of a corporation capitalizing on a popular game than a project lovingly crafted by passionate developers.  What do I mean by this?Well, it's obvious that a lot of elements of this game were designed by committee and doled out to various programming departments who probably didn't communicate with each other.  My foremost example of this is one of the earliest labyrinths.  It is designed to teach you how to use your newfound magnesis, err, I mean, godly power that lets you pick up objects and manipulate them from a distance.  The person who designed this particular labyrinth apparently didn't collaborate with the the overworld designer, because the puzzle in the overworld you need to solve to access the labyrinth is the exact same puzzle that's in the labyrinth, but without any tutorial.  So, by the time you get to the official tutorial inside the labyrinth you've already had to figure out how to use the powers by yourself and now it's almost laughable that the tutorial was placed here.There's a lot of having to figure out stuff yourself, too.  They drop powers on you without even telling you have them, much less how to use them.  Sure, there's a tutorial screen you scroll through, but I found myself spending a lot of time and even Google searches on how to do the most basic things.  How was I supposed to know that as soon as I got the bow I could remote control my arrows like they were some kind of drone?  Took me way too long to solve that puzzle.Anyway, I wanna get back to that overworld I mentioned in passing a moment ago.  It's detailed and brought to life with extreme precision and care, but it seems more like a collection of evenly dispersed locations stuffed chalk-full of random items.  Most of the time, it doesn't seem designed to fill you with wonder or the desire to explore, it's simply designed to keep you occupied.  The most egregious example of this is climbing up high to get an overview of the land.  Instead of getting excited about the places you might be able to visit from your breathtaking vista, you're invited to scan the entire area with a tool and muck up the horizon in every direction with decals of where each power-up and pick-up item you can find is located.  It undermines the desire to explore and turns travel into an exercise involving an itemized checklist.  It has every mark of corporate game design all over it.  This is a shame, too, because the overworld is beautifully crafted and the locations a delight to look upon, and this game could have easily become so much more with the correct vision and guidance.But, there are advantages that come with big corporate game design, and that's deep pocket books to bank roll things like 100% voice acting for most of the characters.  And to be sure, the voice acting is top notch, all the actors did a fantastic job.  Unfortunately, I found the writing pretty bad, the story bland and uninteresting, with no personal stake for the main character.  Because of this, most of the cut scenes seemed filled with unnecessary and sometimes cringy dialogue, redundant information, or without a lot of direction or purpose.All that being said, though, they did copy one of the greatest games of all time, and not only did they do a good job in copying someone else's homework, they added a lot of fun things to the mix.  Perhaps, if Breath of the Wild didn't exist, I might think of this as a fantastic game.  But after seeing what a truly great game can do with a better version of its idea, Fenyx falls  short of achieving the same level of greatness, but it's definitely worth the full $15 I paid for it on sale.  I'd probably even pay more.

_childDocuments_.review: Really, this game is quite amazing for what it is.  It is trying it's best to have an open world like Zelda:BotW, but have more to do it in than BotW offered.  To be clear, I am not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on BotW, it's an amazing game.  But so is this.  It's not as thoughtful, it's doing its best to lean more towards humor, and it's successful.Throughout the adventure, you will often hear the continued tale and discussions between Zeus and Prometheus.  It's funny and heartwarming.  The tale is meant to show Zeus he is a bad father while saving humanity and preventing the Titan called Typhon from killing the gods and taking over the world, remaking it in his own image.  The Voices:  The voice acting is truly great in this game.  Everyone is speaking English (in the English version), but they have thick Greek accents and it adds more levity to it as they discuss the various transgressions that Zeus has committed against his own family.  At one point they are talking about Herakles and Zeus interrupts asking "why are you saying it like that?".  To which Prometheus responds by saying, "Because that is how it's pronounced".  The joke here being that everyone refers to the Greek Hero Herakles as "Hercules", which is a Romanized version of the name.  It really leans hard into it's Greek roots and I truly loved that about the game.  Nor is it filled with the fluffy, childish version of Greek Mythology, it's the gritty kind of Greek Mythology with all the nastiness they contain, and all the wonder as well.  You also come across and regularly speak to the likes of Hermes, Hephaestus, Ares, Athena, and Aphrodite, all of which are excellently voiced.  Story:  Story is fine.  It was never going to win any awards on this front.  It wouldn't be a game about Greek Mythology if it wasn't your basic heroes journey story.  And it is that in spades.  A man/woman (you get to choose what Fenyx is), who is a shield bearer and story teller, but no great warrior, must come to realize that he/she is a hero because that is what they need to be.  Who they were will mean something to who they are becoming, but a hero is someone who is called to duty and answers when the call comes, not necessarily someone who is born warrior.Gameplay:  This is where the game really really shines.  As the game goes on, you will unlock more and more powers to fight in a world that is becoming ever more harsh.  The map is riddled with gateways to Tartaros (think the puzzle dungeons of Zelda:BofW).  And these are a lot of fun.  You always get from them a piece of Zeus's lightning bolt which is used to enhance Fenyx as the game goes on.  You also expand the health pool by finding Ambrosia around the map.  The combat is exciting, it is on the ground and in the sky, and the ever broadening of Fenyx's abilities really opens up what you can and cannot do in the world.  Some of those same abilities will also enable you have an easier time solving all the puzzles around the world.  Each one of the aforementioned gods will need to brought back to their full godhood through what are essentially trials on Fenyx's heroes journey.  They also grant blessings which can enhance your gameplay in subtle ways.  For example, Ares blessings will enhance combat, even adding a new combo stage to your combo meter.  These things can change what weapons you decide to use.  Each weapon does something different.  Perhaps it improves the damage your sword does.  But there are others that will restore health when you reach a new combo stage, while others may offer enhanced stun for a few seconds after a perfect dodge.  All the equipment works like this.  You can forge your equipment to enhance the bonuses and do more damage or give better defense.  All equipment, when enhance to level 4, will unlock another bonus you get for using it.  All the upgrades are to gear slots, and not specific gear, so you don't have to worry about enhancing all the swords, your upgrades count for all swords/axes/armors.Beyond Tartaros, the world is riddled with challenges that each offer further enhancement to Fenyx.  They unlock more weapons/armors, or offer more upgrade materials, or offer cosmetic changes to equipment you already have, or Coins of Charon.  The coins are vital as they are used a currency to upgrade your powers.  Some will offer a charge to a godly weapon ability, others though will enhance the ways you can navigate the world or the battle field.  For example, you get the Wings of Daidolas, but one of the first abilities worth getting is the one that allows you to glide faster and use less stamina.  Herakles Gauntlets allow you to move heavy objects, but an enhancement not only allows you to pick up heavier blocks, but pull enemies towards you, or you towards enemies, on the battle field.The map is absolutely massive.  Each God is in a certain part of the world, each section of the map is very different from each other.  Aphrodite lives in an incredibly lush, natural land.  Athena resides in a beautiful but more developed area with many large temples and landmarks.  Hephaestus lives in a land that is more barren, as befitting a god that uses a forge to make things.  It's littered with broken down automatons.  Ares land is blasted by War, barren, and really only has half destroyed structures besides his massive keep.The game does support ultrawide and run great for me.  It's a huge world and it feels even larger at 5120x1440.  All of this is delivered by consistent frame rates.  The draw distance is pretty impressive because at points you are high enough to see every inch of the Golden Isle, and it all looks quite good in my opinion.  Also, there is a day/night cycle and it feels like a different world at different times of day.  In the northernmost land, at night, you will see Aurora Borealis in the night sky and night will also offer a few combat challenges that only become available at night.All of this is great, it's easily a 9/10 game for me.  It's compelling and fun to play, nothing feels forced.  There is one downside though, and that is Ubisoft Connect.  When you start the game it will always "Check for more content...", and this will always take 30-60 seconds with no way to shut it off.  Hermes main point in the game, besides comedy relief, is offer to lighten your burden of Electrum (real money currency for the game, which only offers you cosmetic or shortcut items).  As soon as you get back to home base, his first inquiry is about you spending Electrum.  It's an annoying live service thing they added to an otherwise fantastic single player game.  You can get Electrum by doing daily or weekly quests, but it's really immersion breaking to hear Hermes offer to let you buy some premium skin or crafting gear goody bag.I did not play the DLC, the reviews overall were disappointing for them so I didn't really feel a need or want to do them.  The main game also offers a New Game + option, which I may come back to at a later time.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is a hard one to review given it's age. But I hope you have the time to read it. For one, this game was not released in 2022. So the release date can be confusing in the steam store. The original release date is December 3, 2020. I did play this on more than 1 platform hence I'll be reviewing on this platform given it's state today and with the Steam Deck available on my hands. I will say that the lore of this game does require you to understand the world of mythology. Especially Greek Mythology in order to get some of the character back stories. But these stories are mostly well known if you've ever been out of high school. Thus, there's expectations that you know them. Hence that's the only requirement you actually really need to know to have a good laugh on the comedy of things.Undoubtedly this game is a blend of Assassin's Creed and Breath of the Wild which was only exclusive to the Nintendo Switch (not anymore thanks to the community hehehe...). And as an avid Open world type of player, I will say this was a joy to play on with the comedic effect in place giving it a nice touch for those who like comedy. If that's what you're looking for then this will not disappoint. Game content, open world structure, points of interest, etc. are just a good experience in this game. None of the points of interest are pointless. Actually, each one has it's point of progress for your character. Treasure chests, Zeus' Bolts, Ambrosia, Charon's Coins, and etc. are all part of progressing your character's strength.HOWEVER, I will say that character customization is RESTRICTED. It's not as vast as AC Odyssey for that matter. You can choose what to upgrade but once you hit the end of each tree, you pretty much realize that everyone will hit this point once they get to this point as well. Thus, there's no point in customizing play style. You have what you have and the only thing that can make things unique to your playthrough is just which gear you choose to use. Oh and the gear is mostly visual. You'll notice it when you complete at least 1-2 sections of the world map.Enemy variations could do better though. I notice almost all enemies are the same. Even bosses don't have much uniqueness to them once you face them. Kinda a bummer at part but once you face crowds, I do hope you have DMC skills in your hands cause they can be pretty annoying. Just a lack of unique enemy design. Puzzle designs are interesting but there are puzzles that are annoying. There are points in a puzzle where, in your head, it's so easy to solve but for some damn reason the game makes the puzzle difficult to solve and there's no solution skip to these terribly designed puzzles. For one, there's a PINBALL puzzle where you have to basically pinball a fireball into a hole... which borders some luck that relies on the Physics engine of the game. Another is a jump the ball into the other side of the platform which also borders some luck and precise timing in order to get the ball to the other side. In other words, there are puzzles that are not straight forward in solution despite the solution having some randomizer to take effect. Even though you're standing in the solution, the game basically forces you to pray to the Physics gods to solve something ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ basic into the equation. And yes, this is the weakest part of the game. The puzzles. Innovative, but annoying. I decided to split this review into two parts. 1 for the PC and the other for the STEAM DECK. Why? I won't lie, I have pretty badass PC but my experience with both is just SIGNIFICANTLY different. If you plan to play on PC (at this time and age), I really do hope you have an AMD GPU. This game just crashes randomly and quite commonly on my Nvidia PC with the latest drivers. I tried 537.xx drivers and it still crashes. Discussion forums have also said to downgrade your drivers down to 528.xx but I say.. ♥♥♥♥ it... To do all that for one game is NOT RECOMMENDED. I genuinely do not know who's responsible for a fix to the random crashing but I 100% absolutely can confirm that this game crashes commonly in 2024 and no it's not my hardware as I can literally play all my other games without crashing. It's only this and mostly other Ubisoft games. Does it suck? yeah... it sucks. But this is all I can say about the PC review. It's bad and unfortunately makes me want to switch to the other device I have to just play it... and speaking of which... For a game that's older than the deck itself, I will say this game was NOT optimized for the Steam Deck. Hence don't expect it to be. I did the numbers and had at least 5-10 hours of gameplay on this in the deck and will say that my experience was WAY better than my PC (which has an RTX3070 btw). Game doesn't crash (unless I smash my deck with a hammer), decent frame pacing (not perfect frame pacing, just decent), highly acceptable quality, and completely comfortable to play on. Just one issue, you need to set your controls to gamepad mode manually. I don't know why but that's how it is. Concerning the FPS, it does drop a lot at medium settings at 800p. Hence it's not perfect 60 fps but it's at least better than having it crash every now and then. It goes down to about 40fps and lowest I got is 30 fps so you might want to stick to NSW framerate if you know what I mean. But it does hit 60 fps at certain sections. Either way, devs never made any optimization for the deck so you'll just have to make do with raw performance as stock. If and only if you want to, you can try using 3rd party upscalers such as FSR if you want to make it really hit 60fps flat. I don't need to say it but I used SteamOS for my experience and not Windows so you know exactly m experience. This game is definitely 7/10 for me. I wouldn't give it a decimal point higher given the flaws of the game. But hey, it's a better game than a lot of other games right now. Recommended if you really like open world game and comedy. I would only say that you shouldn't play this on an Nvidia PC because of the crashing issue that it has. But if you have a Steam Deck, fire away. It's the best alternative experience to BOTW from the NSW without sailing the 7 seas.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game to (almost) 100% on Stadia (RIP) and I REALLY liked it there - gorgeous world, solid combat, fun puzzles and exploration, nice itemization. It's *heavily* inspired by Breath of the Wild, but that's really not a bad thing here. Especially since it does away with a lot of the things that annoyed me in BotW, such as weapon durability and cumbersome crafting. I even liked the story - it's silly, yes, but at least I found it memorable; that's more than I can say about many other games these days.If you look at other reviews, you'll see two recurring complaints - that you have to use Ubisoft Connect and that each time you launch the game it spends a fair bit of time on "checking for additional game content", whatever that is. These are real problems and are indeed annoying, but overall the launcher thing is just a one-time setup, and the "checking" stage is 35 seconds - which is exactly 33 seconds too long for my taste, but I'm willing to wait that long once per session.As for downsides in the game itself, my main complaint is that it has a "survey" mode that allows you to detect (and mark) points of interest on the map, which really take away a lot of the fun inherent in the exploration. The game does a decent job of also making these points of interest visually distinct, though, so I highly recommend just never using the "survey" feature and instead relying only on pure exploration to find these points of interest. Yes, you'll probably miss a bunch of stuff, but you'll have much more fun exploring!Oh, and one more thing - while I really like this game, I don't recommend the DLCs at all. Stick with the awesome main game.

But hey, it's pretty and the characters have a little soul. so I can't blame the art aspect. The controls are solid, though RB/RT (R1/R2) for both melee weapons that you have to press ALL THE TIME feels awkward and clunky when holding an average controller.Most puzzles are simply NOT FUN or rewarding when the dumb obscure mechanic is stumbled across to solve it, and are there to pad the game. Creativity is not rewarded.The Daily challenges and microtransactions in this Single-Player FPS are disrespectful and out of place. But I played the latter half of the game on nightmare, the highest difficulty. I expected *some* amount of challenge, but the final boss battles only required roughly 4 health potions (and 1-2 attack/def potion). For reference, you have 20 of each in the end-game.- After you get off "tutorial island", you unlock 3 dlc-preview quests. Although the game doesn't tell you this until you're inside one of them, and they look identical to other main story quests. While they give you a predetermined "loadout" of powers, potions etc, they still expect you to do them towards the end of your gameplay. But one of them **is located in the tutorial zone**. 2 of the godly powers can be used for mobility purposes, but chances are you haven't acquired them in your playthrough yet, let alone have never had any reason to use them for mobility. So here the game is throwing one of the hardest "challenge runs" in the game at you with little warning. Just a tiny warning or something in the quest description would've helped a lot.- This might mainly be a keyboard issue, but the "godly powers", 2 of which are used for mobility, are always hidden behind at least 2 button presses: you have to hold down one key to bring up the menu, and then one extra button press to perform the action. With the default binds it makes sense: 1-4 is mapped to potions, and they're also used for godly powers. but even if you map them to something completely different that doesn't share a binding, you still have to hold the context button. When you're asked to chain 2+ godly powers in a row, *and* also have to use a stamina potion in the middle, it feels extremely clunky, and is easily messed up. There's no "stance" or anything tied in to holding the context button, you can instantly use it. So there's 0 reason to not allow it on PC.The nitpicky:- The way you reveal objectives on the map feels kinda "meh". You're supposed to use it from high up above, but there's no line of sight requirement or anything. So you can just awkwardly "scan" a wall until your cross-hair reacts and you can reveal something. I guess this is a band-aid fix due to some objectives being placed in caves/cliff walls where most people might not scan for stuff.- Small anti-frustration measures in "vaults" (Usually puzzle areas) would have gone a long way. Why does dying to a laser reset you waaay further back than if you'd died by falling off a cliff? (yes, even if you do not have the hp to "recover")- Inconsistencies in how godly powers interact with physics objects, namely spheres. The Dash + uppercut does absolutely 0 to a sphere, but the hammer sends it flying. This mechanic is used in a total of **two** vaults in the entire game, and I was stuck for 5+ minutes, because I only checked with the abilities I use often: uppercut and dash. These didn't affect the sphere, so I figured none of them did. - Small stuff like this crops up all over the place, where some things are granted pages in the tutorial pages, and some are even on-screen prompts. But mostly things are not explained. I'm fine with experimentation, but there's such a weird arbitrary line of what's described and what isn't.- Not being able to rotate "in place" while hovering. More than a few "deaths" took place due to that.- I didn't touch the real money shop, but I did browse the one where you could do "dailies" to get a currency to be spent on cosmetics. I genuinely do not get why there's a week long timer before it changes. Do they expect people to stick around in this game for more than like... 4 weeks, ever? I took a rather completionist approach, and did practically everything available in the "main land" (minus the 5th zone, was getting a bit same-y at this point). If I didn't, I could probably easily shave off 25 hours of my runtime. Despite my long lists of complaints, they are mostly nitpicks. Had a good time, that was somewhat interrupted by small frustrating moments, which does drag down the score a fair bit.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising is an incredibly well made game, completely undone by the decisions made at the top level, and it is a shame.  IFR is an open world adventure taking place in ancient Greece, steeped in the lore of the Greek Gods.  Its cartoony graphics, and much of its gameplay seems inspired by mashing together traditional Ubisoft "climb the towers" open world traits, and Nintendo's Zelda Breath of the Wild.  That is a pretty solid combo!  The game looks fantastic and feels great, it is clear there were many talented people involved in making the game.  At the macro level, the problem with the game is that it can't decide what it wants to be, and in trying to be everything to everyone, completely loses its way.  This manifests in a number of ways, the first thing I noticed was how mixed up the narrative is.  The game is framed by a sequence between Zeus and Prometheus, where they are discussing you, the human that is their last hope, and your adventures.  As they speak about the adventures, you experience them in realtime, doing hero things and interacting with others characters.  There is a massive tone gulf between the two viewpoints.  The Zeus/Prometheus parts are written in that Pixar all ages sort of way, where it would be appropriate for a young person, but there are winks and jokes for the adults too.  It doesn't always hit the mark, but it is not terrible.  The writing in the parts you are actually experiencing is unbearable.  It is seemingly written for children, the dialog is utterly banal, and the tone is inexplicably goofy, even when dealing with deadly serious matters.  Every conversation with Hermes and the other Gods that you rescue is painful, and the vast majority of the attempts at humor fall completely flat.  It is a totally fine thing to make a game for children, only aimed at children, but based on both the Zeus parts, and the marketing for this game, I do not think that is Ubisofts intention, and if it was and was known, I would not have bought and played it.  Gameplay-wise, the game has tight controls and feels very good in both exploration and combat.  Again, taking its cues from Breath of the Wild, you can glide long distances over the open world, and climb most any surface, as long as you have enough stamina and stamina potions.  The game world manages to feel both overstuffed with tasks and empty and devoid of life at the same time.  The enemies just seem to be magically "there", they don't feel like they actually reside in the environments.  The tasks you complete are engaging at first but there are so many of them stuffed into the map that all of them eventually feel like a chore.  The combat is excellent, but by the time you are halfway through the game you have unlocked all your powers and moves, and have fought all the main enemy archetypes so much that combat becomes a slog as well.  It feels like the enemies, and especially the bosses, could have been more challenging and interesting, but were dialed back a bit to keep the game accessible to everyone.  There are Zelda-like shrines scattered throughout the map, some of them are combat arenas but most of the them are puzzle based.  They range from boring to miserable.  The worst offenders are the ones that try and use the physics engine in a BOTW-like way, and frankly, the game is just not made for it.  There was on puzzle where you have to hit a switch to make a spot on the ground spring up and send a large stone ball rolling over it up onto a ledge.  I tried to do it at least ten times and couldn't get it to get all the way up there.  It would get very close some of the times, and not close at all on others.  Eventually I got it by doing the exact same thing I had been doing the whole time.  That is unforgivably bad game design.  Many of the puzzles involve getting a box or a stone block, and getting it somewhere else without it breaking.  There is nothing enjoyable about them.  I stopped playing IFR at the 20-ish hour mark, I think I was 65-70% done with everything.  I had really enjoyed the first few hours of the game, but it got to the point where almost everything in the game felt like a chore and I couldn't stand it anymore.  I also want to note that the Ubisoft does a very poor job of releasing their games on Steam.  Not having Steam Achievements and not using Steams cloud infrastructure are terrible decisions, and forcing me to use Ubisoft Connect makes me want to avoid Ubisoft games in the future whenever possible.  3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever want to play The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild but you don’t own the necessary Nintendo console? Ubisoft got you covered.The story: The game has actually two stories. One is Zeus seeking help against the monstrous Typhon and Prometheus starts to tell him the story of Fenyx, a shield-bearer who tries to lift the curse of the petrified humans and step out of the shadow of her heroic brother. To do so she needs to restore the Olympian gods to their former glory.  While Fenyx story is more serious Prometheus and Zeus act as light-hearted commentators, often pointing out what kind of horrible father Zeus is and what terrible stuff the Greek gods did according to mythology.The gameplay:  It is a mix of combat, exploration an riddles. Each activity gives you different kind of materials to increase your health, stamina, upgrade your skills or your equipment. Each part neatly meshes into the others. Combat is surprisingly fun. Try to keep you combat multiplier high by skilful evade enemy attacks. The game also offers a new game plus mode which lets you upgrade your character further.The graphic: Vivid colours and lush landscapes, especially in Aphrodite’s domain.  Plus Fenyx, who is canonical female, looks like she is right out of Disney’s latest animated movie. I was seriously waiting for her to turn out to be a princess.The problems: Boy, where to start? There are a lot of small things and feels it like bad management decisions are to blame:Personally I think all the negative reviews here don’t do the game justice and are more due to the rejection of Ubisoft.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: The game is Zelda-inspired. However, quite a few problems emerged across my first 18 hrs of gameplay (clearing 2.5 regions out of 6). Lack of interactions between the character and the world, it still has the shape of the previous AC open world games. Bad physics, it is very hard to turn around airborne, and sometimes items don't drop at supposed location when trying to solve a puzzle. Repetitive gameplay like most other Ubisoft games. Getting 3 items across the map, push a ball from A to B, shoot an arrow across a few specific location blah blah blah. The puzzle is only hard for the sake of it, like you have to start all the way back if you miss a point during a platformer challenge, or a switch to open a door is hiding god knows where (I suspect they want to prolong people's game hour that way). The puzzle can give you a real headache combining with the game physics problem I talked about before. Solving a puzzle in Zelda makes you feel smart and proud, solving a puzzle in this game makes you feel whoever design these is stupid. Pros: Fun dialogue and cute graphics. I like how Zeus is ranting about everything when Prometheus is ranting about Zeus. The other gods are also quite funny (they are the only motivation I am still playing).  Very good combat system. The rewards from all those repetitive puzzles are quite helpful instead of some trash items in AC Odessey or Hogwarts Legacy. You also don't have to spend tons of time upgrading an individual item.In general: One of the better games from Ubisoft's industrial assembly line, gameplay wise consider it as a way better version of Hogwarts Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ubisoft, home to Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and... The Legend of Zelda?A few months ago, Ubisoft introduced The Crew Motorfest, and watching the presentation made my face flush with embarrassment, even though I have nothing to do with it! They shamelessly and unscrupulously stole the Forza Horizon formula, without bothering to change the concept or artistic style; it's a blatant copy-paste with a different name. I don't know how they haven't been sued. I feel the same way about Immortals Fenyx Rising; it's a copy of Zelda Breath of the Wild, though not as shameless as Motorfest. At least here, there's a different concept, a distinct world, and variations in gameplay. It's one of those titles that went under the radar, perhaps a hidden gem? It is, in my opinion. I didn't play it initially because it was a bit expensive, and I'm wary of Ubisoft products – you never know if they'll be good or utter crap. So, I let it pass until it went on a big sale recently, and I bought it. I'm having a blast; it's incredibly fun and even challenging, especially with the puzzles. The art style is beautiful, the world as well, and the story is laid-back and enjoyable, without too many twists. I'd give it a well-deserved 7/10, and it's a shame they canceled the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game thus far. Definitely one of the better games Ubisoft has released for a while now. _childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising continually impressed me with the creativity of its design. The world, the characters, the gameplay, the enemies, the story, the music, and especially the puzzles are so full of thoughtful, clever creation. It is truly special and is among my favorite titles of all time.One complaint I see is that "tHeRe aRe tOo mAnY PuZzLeS". The puzzles are a big part of what this game *is*. They're really not too difficult, but are apparently far beyond the limited capability of some (often rude) players. The puzzles are truly interesting and fun which sets them apart from so many puzzles you see in lots of other similar games.The biggest valueless complaint I see often is that "It uSeS ThE UbIsOfT LaUnChEr". I don't love launchers either, but to ding this title because of that publishing mechanism is stupid. Many other Ubisoft titles have similar useless "reviews" for the same reason. It says nothing of the game itself which is what I want to know about when I read a review. It's like a one-star review for something on Amazon because the shipping was slow.  Immortals Fenyx Rising is an excellent title that is interesting, compelling, and fun. It is worth your time..
