_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play Zelda ; BotW, but I don't own a Nintendo console. Many people compared this one to BotW or very close to it and some comment even tell better than BotW.IF this is as close people tell, then BotW must be pretty bad. I don't recommend this game for 80 CAN $. I got it on sale for 15 $. For 15 $ this is a good game.PRO :+ Story is good+ Animation great+ Voice acting+ Narration and joke+ Greek mythology lore is goodCON :- The character move like a RPG in the early 2000's. Feel like it is hovering instead of walking. This is noticeable mostly when you are on rock, concrete or climbing. For a 80 $ game, this is not good.- Stupid ''Radio Tower'' thing for discovering the area. For god sake Ubisoft, be original for once.- Everything is about fetching your upgrades. (Like in Zelda I guess). If you want to upgrade your health, stamina, gears, mount, etc. You must find it. This is very tedious and pretty much got 20 hours of running around and 6 hours of real gameplay. This is a cheap way to add false hours to a game. Some people will argue that this is like Zelda, but I don't care. Not a reason to copy 100 % a game and Ubisoft got enough experiences in video game to do something better.- Mounts are all the same, just a horse with stupid recolours. This is a lazy way to add more stuff in a game. You even got mounts with wings that they cannot use. Just because this is only cosmetic. - Scaling system ; Maybe this one is not a CON for many peoples, but it is for me. The enemies get stronger as you get stronger. This mean you never get the feeling to become actually stronger, because everywhere is always scaled to your power level. Feel like your progression of running around for hours and hours is for nothing. Except for the stamina. - I didn't get any in game crashes. Many comment talk about that. Everything is running pretty smoothly. But I do get a problem when I close the game. IF I exit the game with ''Exit to Desktop''. The game will close but Steam will still mark it as running. So I cannot start any other games or even close my computer because it is saying a program is still running. The only way to close my computer was to override it (holding 3 sec the power button). The solution I found was to exit to the main title first, then exit to desktop. Pretty annoying.NEUTRAL :- Puzzles are too easy. I put that as neutral comment, because it depend of people. They could put some very easy and more challenging puzzles, but they didn't. The challenging one are about that you don't have the necessaries Godly Power. This is not a challenge, this is a prerequisite.Overall :For a 80 $ game (92 $ with taxes), this is a fail. Don't get it full price.I got it on sale for 15 $. For that price this is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello friends! Today i will review the game Immortals Fenyx Rising. This game has some issues on steam, but if you can get it to work, it works very well. It is a open worldgame similiar to other ubisoft games, except this one is more greek mythology related. It features a hero who must save the gods and lands from evil. There is also a decent story the game follows when saving the gods, and some twists and turns. Many puzzles are also in teh game, so you can play many puzzles througth the game. So if you do not like action rpgs with lots of puzzles, you may wish to avoid this game. Also, seems the current nvidia driver version causes lots of issues with this game. A poster on the forum says using a older version driver can fix this issue. You can see the information here on the driver version to rollback to which is driver version #528.19. If you wish for them to have a permanenet fix, i suggest people contact nvidia and explain the issue with the current patch with them and this game to have a long term fixing solution.Other people have reported crashing in the game. Although i did not personally experience crashing inside the game, i do have issues when closing the game. The crashing could be related to the steam overlay and the cloud saving, as i think this is the issue that is causing them. I have contacted ubisoft connect support about this issue too. Anyways,here are my pro and con list for the game. Crashing maybe also caused by settings from nvidia/amd settings, so the player may have to fool around with them to find the best solution to the crashing issues.PROS:- A story based around greek mythology.- Lots of side quests to do.- Many collectibles to find.- Lots of puzzles.- Controller support for my logitech f310.- Legendary beasts and mythical monsters to find roaming the open world.- Ability to go wherever you want in the open world.CONS:- Some technical issues associated with the game, such as the currrent nvidia drive causing crashing, and other things. This can cause everything from crashing or not properly shutting down correctly.- Many individuals are mad there is not achievements on steam. You can achievements being connected to ubisoft connect and on their platform, not steam.- Some people have said their controllers are not working. I am using a f310 logitech controller fine and it worked right away with no fooling around.- Some of the quests feel repetitive and doing vaults almost feel the same. Also many puzzles in the game.- This requires ubisoft connect to play, and i see this as a negative.- A in game money store in a single player game. Usually these are only cosmetic, but they also have upgrades to stuff in the game. This takes real money to buy this stuff.NOTE: To fully enjoy the game with the dlc's, there is a certain order you should play them in. The order is: The main game (beat it), then play A new god (beat it), then playThe Lost gods (beat it). The eastern gods should be treated as a seperate entity as it features a new hero and new places. Make sure to play eastern gods last.Do i recommend the game? Yes, if you can get over the bugs in the game and can actually play it. It is quite fun action rpg with many many puzzles. If you do not enjoy puzzles though, avoid this game at all costs. If you like the full base game, consider getting the DLC's as they add more storyline to the game about fenyx. Make sure to follow my method of playing above or else the story will be out of order.

_childDocuments_.review: So... this game is basically Zelda meets Ubisoft open world.  Its cartoony and fun spots, its tedious and repetitive in others, and they managed to throw in a snow level just for fun... Collectibles are everywhere, there are tons of chests to find and open, but most items are just cosmetic or are supplies to make/power up other things.  There is a good mix of fighting and puzzles, though some of the puzzles are a bit contrived, especially when they are platformer puzzles.  The flying in the game is really gliding, and I was disapointed that there wasnt more to it.  there is no fine elevation control or Arkham-like manouverabilty, its just glide, or fast glide.  not a fan of the stamina system, as everything takes stamina and so until the endgame, you are pretty limited as to what or how long you can use the skills.But, I did enjoy the game.  TO be honest, I was going to quite when I finished the second God region (Aphrodite), as the fetch-quest collect-a-thon was getting to me.  The Items weren't that great, enemies get repetitive...  but I decided to play through Aries area next and thats when the charm really started to grow.  in terms of story and characters, the interactions get better as the story progresses.  it is a basic Greek myth story where Zeus is the bad father, Hermes and Aphrodite are snarky, but with Aries, Hephestis, and Athena, they balance out better.  There is a lot of Greek myth here, and its inserted well in little challenges and puzzles.Overall, its a fun game.  It is repetitive in the usual Ubisoft way (climb that to open up the map!) and its not as inspired as a good Zelda game can be, but it is solid.  I dont know if I'll play it again, but if you like the open world set-up, if you like a fair take on Greek Myth, and don't mind the usual Ubisoft tropes, Give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I will help this game out a bit because it honestly deserves more love. I picked it up upon completing Assassin's Creed Odyssey. Devs took a lot of inspiration from AC series and BOTW Zelda, there's no doubt about it. As to why you SHOULD give it a go despite a lot of people complaining about Ubisoft Connect... read below.- BAD: If you want to play Ubi games, you have to install their official Ubisoft Connect app. I've had UPlay then Ubisoft Connect since Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag, and it's something that you need to launch in order to play the game online. Yes, it's not always reliable and takes forever to open - but it NEVER crashed my games or made them unplayable in any way. The more Ubi games you play, the less of a big deal it becomes, because you automatically launch it and don't really think about it.- The GOOD thing about it however, is that the app has a Rewards system, which means that through completing weekly challenges (that are optional) you end up earning credits on the Connect app, which then can be exchanged for cosmetic DLCs such as Legendary/Epic skins in game, weapons, mounts, armour, sometimes additional missions in game, etc. Ubisoft Connect offers you free adds-on as well.To sum it up: Yes, installing extra apps is annoying, but no, it shouldn't ruin the gaming experience in overall.(Based on over 100 hours of gameplay accumulated on Epic Games and Steam together - finished the game and replaying it for the 2nd time)+ Combat is easy to learn, lots of combos to master, different weapons to choose from, different modes of difficulty meaning that you can enjoy the story and explore the world at your own pace or go hardcore and choose to die to everything that moves.+ Soundtrack is fantastic. Period.+ All the characters are likeable, and may I say that Zeus who co-narrates everything in the game... is so cringe that it's so good. He throws around dad jokes at every opportunity, and a lot of them hint at the Greek mythology and how he screwed everyone over. I mean, there are moments when I just want to quit the game because of that fella. But he still cracks me up in a good way.+ The humour may not be everyone's cup of tea, but the whole game feels like a joke at times, and it's not meant to be taken seriously. There are a lot of memes and references to other media as well.+ The world is filled with Vaults of Tartaros which are basically domains of varied difficulty, that include mini boss fights, a lot of platforming, and tons of puzzles to solve. I personally love those, because they are the most rewarding part of the game.+ Completing Daily challenges awards you with weapon skins and materials used for ascention; Weekly challenges give you coins that you can use as in-game currency to buy cosmetic DLCs (microtransactions). That means that you can either pull out your wallet, sit back and enjoy sets of skins OR put in some effort, grind for the coins and then exchange them for the same items for FREE (mind you that in the second case, those skins appear in the game randomly and you may need to wait for them a bit longer). - strictly technical issues. The game itself is fine.- Controllers are not supported for this game for some reason. Whilst a lot of people prefer a keyboard/mouse, I am not one of those people and to make it even worse, I use a PlayStation controller. Because yes, I like Sony more.Thankfully, Steam offers controller support so all you have to do is choose which layout you want to use for the game, and just play. Ubisoft, git gud.- No Steam Achievements. I mean, come on u guys. You gave us achievements for Origins and Odyssey then you just gave up. We Gamers like to collect those on Steam. Don't ask why, we just do. So please copy pasta them from your app to Steam. Make your fans happy again.- The game is very resource pack heavy. It can lag even on low graphic settings. But I will blame it on my old potato PC and partly on the game being POORLY optimised.- Ubisoft Connect throwing a tantrum every now and then asking me 1000 times to log in then not recognising my password and repeat. I once tried to log on too many times in a row and my account got locked. Upon contacting Ubisoft customer support I was told that I have to wait 24 hours to log in again. It could always get worse than this, right? :)The game is 90% off on sale now, so grab it and give it a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: IFR is an open world action adventure title with environmental puzzle elements. The game takes places in a massive world based on ancient Greek mythos with you playing a mortal character named Fenyx on their quest to ultimately face Typhon and save their brother. While Greek mythology plays a massive role in the game's world and storytelling, there is a lot of of tongue in cheek humor that uses modern humor tropes and oddly enough very subtle and sometimes not so subtle modern references. A great deal of this is told through some great narration from Prometheus as he tells this story to Zeus, with some great back and forth banter. IFR is broken down into several categories of gameplay: Open world exploration, traversal, combat, and puzzles. The open world exploration borrows a bit from other Ubisoft titles in how you open up parts of the map by seeking high vantage points in certain locations to scan the area. Something seen in titles like the Far Cry series and Assassin's Creed. Once you have uncovered a section of the massive map, you can even go into a focus mode and visually scan around for key spots that range from chests, other items, enemies, puzzle areas and more. The world is massive and ripe with key spots for all sorts of open world explorers to enjoy. Seems there is always something new to discover. Traversing the map comes in many flavors outside of your normal walking. Equipped with the powers of the gods, Fenyx can move about in many various ways. Using the strength of Herakles Fenyx can move massive blocks to allow for big stepping stones to reach higher areas. Fenyx can climbs mountains. Fenyx can double jump and even soar through the air equipped with the wings of Daidalos. They can tame wild creatures to use as mounts. And more. There's no shortage of ways to move around the massive world. For those who are impatient there is of course a nifty quick travel option from the map for some previously explored spots. Now some of the traversal sadly comes at a cost, as it does use up stamina. So you won't be climbing or soaring for an endless period, but with upgrades and potions it can seem that way. Combat would be the key factor into also having the action tag on this title. And there's plenty of it. Combat to me at least feels very similar to the newer Assassin's Creed titles, such as Origins. You have ranged combat with Fenyx's bow, melee combat with 2 weapons, both a sword that dishes out quick light attacks, and a heavy attack thanks to a meaty axe. Attacks from the melee weapons can be chained, and thanks to moves like a dodge and parry that gives you an advantage, combat never seems too difficult when enemies are in the right skill range. Ranged combat also comes in 2 ways. you can either aim and shoot normally with arrows that shoot in an arc, which is fine for closer ranged combat, or you can guide the arrows in slow motion thanks to the power of Apollo's arrows. In all honesty this actually negates standard aiming for ranged combat as Apollo's arrows are much easier to use and are seemingly endless since they just recharge after a few seconds once depleted. Lastly, you have puzzles. IFR is definitely not short on these either as there are puzzles scattered all over the world. This part of the game reminds me a lot of Breath of the Wild. If you're not a fan of action oriented environemtal puzzles, this might be a game you may want to skip, as this takes up a huge chunk of the game and is also mandatory in some parts for progression. If you've ever played Breath of the Wild, you'll feel right at home in this area. When I say environmental puzzles, what I mean is that the puzzles use parts of the enviornment in a lot of cases. And there's a lot of variety in them too. From your basic block pushing puzzles to puzzles that have you shooting cleverly obscured targets with Apollo's arrows, to puzzles that have you using ball rolling physics, and a lot more. Puzzles can be found outdoors in the open world which usually lead to treasure or other things, but are also contained in their own "dungeons" much like Breath of the Wild. Being a fan of BotW, I quite enjoyed these parts of the game. All in all, the whole definitely is greater than the sums of its parts, and in terms of gameplay, IFR is neatly packaged into a grand adventure with lots to offer. IFR does not try to go for the photorealistic look as seen in other massive open world Ubisoft games and instead goes for a more cartoonish look that actually works well given the overall tone of the narrative. Some parts of the game offer a bright and cheery colorful look with sprawling grassy and foresty areas surrounding by calm blue waters, and a colorful skybox, while others will look more dreary and wartorn with darker hues. there's several different biomes to showcase the variety in overall aesthetics. Makes for some great screenshots for sure! And luckily Ubisoft tossed in their photo tools as seen in other titles to make for some amazing looking snapshots. Character models also look fantastic. the overall look is still cartoony, but fits the visual tone of the game quite well.As for performance, well, mileage may vary. I am personally playing with an RTX 2080 Super, i7-9700KF and 32GB of Ram on an SSD. I am also playing on 3440x1440 ultrawide monitor. (Yes Ultrawide works great in this!). Running the game at default settings I encountered a ton of stutter. More so in cutscenes, but still somewhat during actual gameplay. Lowering the settings did not do me any favors except in increasing FPS. I was still getting a lot of stuttering. After quite a bit of trial and error in settings I managed to get the game in a very stable state without any stuttering, and still having settings at max in most options. I'll post in the comments what settings I am using for anyone curious. Either way, if the game auto detected settings based on my configuration, it did a poor job. Luckily it runs fine with some settings changed. I've heard quite a few people complaining about the same issues in this regard, and to those I will say just keep at it. Play around with the settings and find that sweet spot. While you won't have music blaring at all times, it does kick in at key moments, and is mostly fitting for those occasions. I would not say any of the music is entirely memorable, but it's good enough fill in those spots where it's truly needed. Most of the time you'll have your ears filled with serene ambiance instead as you explore the world. with some softer music kicking in too while exploring every now and then, kind of going back and forth to remind you its there. The ambience though is glorious. Walking around you can hear the wind rustling through the trees, the occasional sounds of wildlife and more. It's never truly quiet, but also never too much. Voicework is also superb. It never overstays its welcome, but when it does pop up, it's a thrill to hear. Especially from the narration itself. Is it worth it? Absolutely. Despite being heavily downvoted for some very petty reasons, the game itself is amazing. Fans of open world action adventure titles will love this. Breath of the Wild fans will love it for the puzzles also. It's a great amalgam of different ideas brought together in one solid package. Pros + Aesthetics + Narration + Combat + Powers of the gods + Tons of secrets and puzzles for explorers +  Great use of ambient soundCons - Has optional microtransactions (does not impact gameplay luckily) - No achievements yetRating 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Breath of the Wild or if you have and you want to scratch that itch, this is an interesting take on that formula. But, the wholly unnecessary integration of Ubisoft's platform and microtransactions are a big whiff. Do I recommend this at the $60 price tag? No. The Gold edition when on sale for $10? Absolutely a big ol' recommend.The upgrade system for abilities and gear in IFR are a solid positive for me when comparing to how BotW handles progression. (No weapon durability, hooray!) Improving gear also feels solid, as there are different resources used that you gain in different waysThe underlying banter between Prometheus and Zeus contributes a nice audio backdrop reminiscent of a Borderlands game. But the overall game story plays second fiddle to all the little snippets of Greek mythology scattered everywhere."The" drawback to this game is the same double edged sword shared by BotW. It's too open. It seems that there is a definite ideal path you should follow for the game to keep yourself adequately challenged by enemies and terrain. The game allows too much freedom in straying off the path which results in a bad time of finding challenges that are incredibly difficult, but theoretically possible. However, another advantage to IFR over BotW is that IFR overtly tells you "this area might be too difficult right now".
